Translation to English:

To the provost of Caminensi. When it is requested from us, etc., up to: consent. We confirm to you and through you to your church, by apostolic authority, the villages, enclosures, and revenues of Lubin with all their appurtenances, as you justly and peacefully possess them, and we fortify them with the protection of this present writing, etc. etc. Dated as above.

REGESTO:

Gregorius IX papa preposito Caminensi villas, clausuras, et redditus de Lubin cum omnibus pertinentiis suis, sicut iuste possidet, auctoritate apostolica confirmat. 1230, [date unknown]. [place unknown].

**Translation to English:**

To the people of Benevento. Just as a mother cannot forget the child of her womb, we, who desire the prosperity of your city's state, love you as special children and carry you in the heart of Jesus Christ. We are making a diligent effort so that your city may breathe in the desired peace and progress with continual advances, as it has been afflicted by continuous troubles. Given at Rome, at St. Peter's, on the Nones of December, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Beneventanis significat se diligere eos tanquam filios speciales et efficacem operam dare, ut urbs eorum pacem et incrementa assidua consequatur. Datum Romae apud Sanctum Petrum, Nonis Decembris, anno primo pontificatus nostri.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man, the Count of Holland. Since you have taken up the cross to follow Christ, denying yourself, we, as much as we can with God, wish to show you reverence for Him. If there is any sentence of excommunication pronounced against you after you have undertaken the journey of pilgrimage, we revoke it from the fullness of our power. Given at Rome, at St. Peter's, the 10th day before the Kalends of June, in the second year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro comiti Hollandiae, qui crucem suscepit, sententiam excommunicationis post iter peregrinationis revocat. Datum Romae apud Sanctum Petrum, X Kalendas Iunii, anno secundo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Prague. Since, as we have learned from your report, certain canons of Prague and prelates of your diocese have violated the interdict you pronounced against that diocese by rashly celebrating divine services in interdicted churches, disregarding the prohibition made by you under the penalty of anathema, we grant you by the authority of these presents full power to deprive them of their benefices and otherwise punish them according to canonical statutes. Given at the Lateran, the eighth day before the Kalends of August, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Pragensi concedit facultatem canonicos Pragenses et praelatos eiusdem diocesis, qui interdictum violaverunt, suis beneficiis spoliandi et alias puniendi secundum instituta canonica. Datum Laterani, VIII Kalendas Augusti, anno tertio (pontificatus).

**Translation to English:**

To the Chapter of Bremen. You have humbly asked us what should be done concerning the bodies of the dead who were buried by schismatics at the time of the schismatic and reprobate Wademar, and concerning the priestly vestments with which they were buried, as well as the altars on which degraded priests have celebrated. We briefly respond to your inquiry that we do not believe that, for this reason alone, such buried bodies should be exhumed, nor that such vestments need to be blessed again, nor the aforementioned altars reconsecrated. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Honorius III papa Capitulo Bremensi respondet, quod corpora sepultorum a schismaticis non exumanda nec indumenta sacerdotalia benedicenda iterum, aut altaria reconsecranda sint. Datum ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the provost and chapter of Kamień. When it is requested from us, etc., up to: consent. The freedom which secular princes have granted to you and your men, as you justly and peacefully possess it, we confirm to you and through you to your church by apostolic authority and protect with the support of this document. Let no one, etc., of our confirmation, etc. But if anyone, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the Ides of March, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa preposito et capitulo Caminensi libertatem, quam principes seculares eis et hominibus suis contulerunt, auctoritate apostolica confirmat et scripti patrocinio communit. 1227, Id. Martii, Lateran.

**Translation to English:**

To the podestà and all of the city and diocese of Nicterine. By the authority of these presents, we command you that, until we fully decide concerning the duchy itself, you shall attend to the noble woman, the wife of the late duke of Spoleto, regarding those matters which pertain to the court from your city and its county; the rights of bishops, clerics, and churches being preserved in all things. Given at the Lateran, on the 7th Ides of January, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa potestati et universis civitatis et diocesis Nicterine mandat, ut nobili mulieri, uxori quondam ducis Spoletani, in iis quae ad curiam pertinent, assistant, iuribus ecclesiasticis servatis. 1229, Ianuar. 7, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To all the faithful of Christ established throughout the diocese of Bremen. Since our predecessor, Pope Innocent, of blessed memory, to suppress the treachery of the infamous Waldemar, declared his lay supporters excommunicated, and the places that received him subject to sentences of interdict in his presence, we, following the footsteps of our said predecessor, denounce the supporters of the aforementioned Waldemar as excommunicated, and the places that receive him, as long as he is there, are subjected to ecclesiastical interdict. Given at the Lateran, on the 2nd Ides of April, in the second year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa universis Christi fidelibus per Bremensem diocesim denuntiat fautores Waldemari excommunicatos et loca ipsius receptoria interdicto subiecta. 1229, Apr. 12, Laterani.

Translation to English:

To the same. The beloved son, the noble man Louis, Count of Looz, who is bearing the cross, has humbly petitioned us that the sentences of excommunication and interdict, which our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Trier, has promulgated by apostolic authority against the noble man W. of Holland and his supporters in the dioceses of Utrecht and Liège and their lands, demanding justice, we should deign to strengthen with apostolic protection. Therefore, we command your discretion through apostolic writings to uphold those same sentences as...

Regesto:

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Treverensi mandat, ut sententias excommunicationis et interdicti, quas contra W. de Hollandia et fautores eius in diocesibus Traiectensi et Leodiensi promulgaverat, apostolica auctoritate confirmet. Datum apud Urbem, anno pontificatus IV.

Translation to English:

To the Chapter of Bremen. Since your church has been severely damaged in many ways by the reprobate Guademar, you have humbly asked to be allowed to sell the revenues of two prebends of the aforesaid church, out of twenty-four prebends in total, to repair the church's roofs and recover what the said Guademar pledged from its goods, and to relieve other necessities. Especially since you are putting forth greater diligence and care to supply the lack of canons. Therefore, acceding to your requests, we have deemed it fit to grant this to you for just two years. Given at the Lateran, on the 2nd Ides of April, in the second year of our pontificate.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa Capitulo Bremensi, ut, ob ecclesiae damna per Guademarum reprobam illata, proventus duarum prebendarum per biennium distrahere possint, concedit. 1228, Apr. 12. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Magdeburg. Considering the fervor of devotion you bear towards the Apostolic See and recognizing the labors you and your followers undertake for the expansion of the Christian faith, we decree by the authority of these presents that the land in Livonia, which you and yours, by your expenses and labors, convert to the faith of Christ with His help, shall be subject to the metropolitan jurisdiction of the Church of Magdeburg. Therefore, no one etc. shall infringe upon our constitution etc. But if anyone etc. Given at the Lateran, the 6th day before the Kalends of May, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Magdeburgensi terras in Livonia convertendas ad fidem Christi sub iurisdictione metropolitica ecclesiae Magdeburgensis constituendas esse decernit. 1227, Apr. 26. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the citizens of Benevento. Since from long past times the city of Benevento has enjoyed such liberty that anyone, as long as he is free, who chooses to reside there and swears an oath of fidelity to us and the Roman Church, should be regarded by all as a citizen, by the authority of these presents, we strictly forbid anyone from presuming to compel those who pass to reside in that city to return to abandoned dwellings. Therefore, let no one, etc., of our prohibition, etc. If anyone, however, etc. Given at Rome, at Saint Peter's, on the calends of December, in the fiftieth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Nicholaus III papa civibus Beneventanis inhibet, ne quis eos qui ad Beneventi incolatum transeunt, cogere praesumat, ut ad habitationes relictas revertantur. 1278, Dec. 1. Romae apud Sanctum Petrum.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man R., son of the late illustrious Duke of Spoleto. With the intention of advancing your interests as far as we are able with God's help, we have held a diligent discussion concerning the matter of the Duchy of Spoleto with Blertuld, your brother, and we have made sure that what was agreed upon between us and him be put into writing as a precaution. We are prepared, with the Lord's help, to bring this to fruition when you arrive, provided that you, on your part, are ready to observe what has been agreed upon. Given at the Lateran, 7th Ides of January, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro R. ducis Spoletani filio nuntiat se cum Blertuldo, fratre eius, de ducatus Spoletani facto convenisse et paratum esse conventa ad effectum ducere, si ipse ea observare paratus sit. 1229, Ian. 7, Laterani.

Translation to English:

To the Abbot of Saint Gall. For the enhancement of ecclesiastical honor, the insignia of dignities have been devised, which the Holy Roman Church distributes with fitting generosity to individuals and grants to devout sons, as it deems worthy. Therefore, considering more kindly the merits of your probity and the devotion you are known to have towards the Apostolic See, we grant you personally the use of the mitre and ring out of apostolic kindness, decreeing that you may freely use them in processions, synods, and principal feasts. Let no one whatsoever, etc., of our concession, etc. But if anyone, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the 7th Ides of April, in the first year of our pontificate.

Regesto:

Gregorius IX papa Abbati Sancti Galli usum mitrae et anuli in processionibus, synodis et festivitatibus praecipuis concedit. 1227, April 7. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the Chapter of Lodi. It was presented before us on your behalf that, although it was forbidden through apostolic letters for the supporters of the Milanese, under the penalty of excommunication, to enter the land of the Pavians hostiley with the aforesaid Milanese, your citizens, although they did not enter the land, still declared those Pavians as enemies in a public assembly after the aforementioned prohibition. Therefore, you humbly ceased from divine services, beseeching that, since peace has been reestablished among the aforementioned citizens, we might henceforth deign to grant you the license to celebrate. Therefore, commending your devotion in the Lord, we command you through apostolic writings to freely celebrate by our license, provided no other canonical impediment stands in the way. Given at Alatri, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of October, in the second year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Capitulo Laudensi concedit licentiam celebrandi, post pacem inter Mediolanenses et Papienses reformatam, dummodo impedimentum aliud canonicum non obsistat. Datum Alatri, XVI Kalendas Octobris, anno secundo.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Raynald. We have kindly received your beloved brother, the noble man B., who came into our presence, and after diligently hearing and having a careful discussion about what he proposed on your behalf, we are prepared, as much as it is within our power, to bring the matter to completion. However, your brother was unable to complete what was necessary on your behalf. Therefore, having been informed by your brother's report about these discussions, if you accept the terms of the discussion, prepare both the persons and the resources necessary for the completion of this matter, and personally come into our presence, so that the matter may be accomplished, because we, as much as it is within our power, will be ready to bring it to completion. Given at Ferentino, 2nd day before the Kalends of October, in the second year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro Raynaldo mandat ut, postquam tractatus cum germano suo habitus sit et ipse terminos acceptaverit, ad suam praesentiam accedat cum necessariis ad negotium complendum. 1230, Sept. 30. Ferentini.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Würzburg. Since those who, setting aside the fear of God, shed the blood of your predecessor, the late Conrad, Bishop of Würzburg of blessed memory, are known to thirst for your blood as well, we, striving to block the path to their wicked desires, grant you by the authority of these presents that when our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Mainz, your metropolitan, holds a council or meeting in a place reasonably suspect to you, you are not obliged to personally attend such a place against your will but may instead supply your absence through prudent and honest messengers. Through them, you will be informed of the matters arranged in said council or meeting, and you shall humbly receive and observe these as do the other suffragans of the Church of Mainz. We decree any sentence which the aforesaid archbishop might unjustly impose upon you, contrary to our concession, to be null and void. Let no one, therefore, infringe upon our concession and constitution. If anyone, however, shall attempt this, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the 4th of August, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Herbipolensi concedit ut, metu inimicorum suorum, absens per nuntios ad concilium ab archiepiscopo Maguntino convocatum se repraesentet, decreta tamen observans. 1229, Aug. 4, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To B., Dean of Bremen. On behalf of our venerable brother, the Archbishop, and our beloved sons, the chapter of Bremen, it was humbly requested of us that, due to the prolonged and constant hostility which your church has endured until now and is still enduring, and is believed to endure in the future, no canon of the same church can be secure about what he possesses. They asked that we consider you kindly, so that you may, with our permission, retain two prebends, one of which you have in the church of Bremen, and the other in the church of Monastery, so that you may not fall into poverty, which, as they assert, would greatly harm the same church. Therefore, inclined by the prayers of the said archbishop and chapter, and wishing to grant you a special favor, we concede that, unless another canon law prohibits you, you may freely retain the aforementioned prebends. Given at the Lateran, on the 2nd Ides of April, in the second year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Honorius III papa B. decano Bremensi concedit, ut prebendas in ecclesiis Bremensi et Monasteriensi retinere possit, propter hostilitatem quam ecclesia patitur. 1218, Apr. 12, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the Abbot and convent of Belbog. When a request is made to us, etc., as far as: agreement. We confirm and grant by apostolic authority, and with the protection of this present writing, the tithes of Trebetowe, which were granted to you by our venerable brother, the bishop of Camin, with the consent of his chapter, out of pious consideration, and the villages of Belbog and Cholm with all their appurtenances, revenues, and other goods, bestowed upon you by the noble men Bozlao and Kazimaro, dukes of Pomerania, with pious liberality, as you justly and peacefully possess all these things, as is more fully contained in their authentic documents. Let no one, etc. etc. Given at the Lateran, the 16th day before the Kalends of April, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa confirmat abbati et conventui de Belbog decimas de Trebetowe, villas de Belbog et de Cholm, redditus aliaque bona eis concessa, auctoritate apostolica communita. 1227, Mar. 17, Lateran.

**Translation to English:**

To the Abbot of Saint Hubert of the Diocese of Liège and the Deans of Saint John and Saint Martin of Liège. Since we have commanded the observance of the agreement amicably entered into between our beloved sons, the noble men L., Count of Loon, and William of Holland, concerning the abduction of the noblewoman Ada, wife of the same count, as well as Holland and other lands belonging to the same count by right of his wife, with the mediation of the late Philip, Marquis of Namur, then bailiff of the county of Flanders, and confirmed by oaths given by both parties, as is more fully contained in our letters, we mandate by apostolic writ that you ensure the said agreement, as it was prudently made without malice and voluntarily accepted by both parties, is inviolably observed by ecclesiastical censure, with no appeal allowed. If not all of you can act, then let two of you proceed. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Honorius III papa Abbati Sancti Huberti Leodiensis et decanis Sancti Iohannis et Sancti Martini Leodiensibus mandat ut compositionem inter L. comitem de Los et Willielmum de Hollandia super raptu A[de] uxoris comitis auctoritate ecclesiastica inviolabiliter observari faciant. 1217, Dat. ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Paderborn. Our beloved son Conrad of Boffesem came into our presence and humbly requested that, for the honor of God and the solace of the sick and poor, he wishes to build a hospital in the place called Huxaria and make it subject to the hospital of the Holy Spirit in Saxia, seeking our permission to construct and build a chapel therein and to have a cemetery and a personal chaplain for the benefit of the sick and poor. Therefore, commending his pious intention in the Lord, and respecting your fraternity, we command you by apostolic writings to grant him the requested permissions, as you are the diocesan of the place, without prejudice to others' rights. Given at the Lateran, on the Nones of April, in the second year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa [Nomine] episcopo Padeburnensi mandat ut Conrado de Boffesem licentiam concedat ad hospitale in Huxaria construendum, sub hospitali sancti Spiritus in Saxia, cum capella, cimiterio, et proprio capellano pro infirmis et pauperibus. Datum Laterani, Nonis Aprilis, anno secundo pontificatus nostri.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Prague. Our beloved son L., a priest and pastor of the church of Prascoles, appeared before us and humbly confessed that, in Bohemia, up until the general council, it was an ancient custom for clergy in holy orders, even priests, to contract marriages de facto and live in such unions. He himself was born of such a union, and he requested that we mercifully dispense with him concerning the orders and benefice he has already received. Therefore, sympathizing with the labors the priest endured in coming to the Apostolic See, and considering that those who confess voluntarily should be treated more leniently, we confidently command your brotherhood through apostolic writings that if this is so, and if he is not an imitator of his father's incontinence and no other canonical impediment stands in the way, you may dispense by our authority concerning the benefice and orders he has received from mercy, which exalts over judgment. Given at Rome, at St. Peter's, on the 11th day before the Kalends of December, in the first year of our pontificate.

---

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Pragensi mandat ut dispense cum sacerdote de Prascoles, legitime progenito ex contubernio, circa beneficia et ordines susceptos, si paternae incontinentiae non fuerit imitator neque aliud canonicum obsistat. Datum Romae apud Sanctum Petrum, XI Kal. Decembris, anno I pontificatus nostri.

**Translation to English:**

We have received your letters of devotion with paternal kindness, and we have diligently examined their content, commending your fidelity with worthy praises in the Lord, since you act as devoted and faithful sons of the Roman Church. Concerning your request to know our will, that is, whether we wish you and your other friends from Lombardy to swear an oath of fidelity to our dearest son in Christ, Frederick, the illustrious King of Sicily, elected as Emperor of the Romans, if you are requested by him, we have decided to inform you through the present letters that if the other citizens of Lombardy have sworn oaths of fidelity to the said king, we shall tolerate for the sake of your peace, that if you are requested by him, you may swear to him, provided, however, that the fidelity and rights of your holy Roman Church, your mother, are preserved in all things. Given at Rieti, on the third day before the Kalends of September, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa potestati et populo Alexandrino mandat, ut, si cives Lombardi regi Sicilie Frederico fidelitatis iuramenta praestiterint, pro pace sua sustineat eos, si requisiti sint, praestare, salvis fidelitate ac iure Romanae ecclesiae. 1230, Aug. 30. Datum Reate.

Translation to English:

Letter to the Lord Pope. To the most holy father and lord Honorius, by the grace of God, the supreme pontiff of the holy Roman Church, Roland, by divine mercy and apostolic approval, Bishop of Ferrara, sends the reverence of his devotion. Let your holiness know that I have excommunicated the occupiers of the castle of Medicina and their supporters, the citizens of Bologna, according to your mandate, and have subjected the city of Bologna to ecclesiastical interdict. By your authority, whose cause is special, I have firmly ordered the Bishop of Bologna through my letters to proclaim the aforementioned occupiers and their supporters as excommunicated throughout all the churches of the city of Bologna, and to ensure that the interdict is observed inviolably until due satisfaction is provided.

Regesto in Latin:

Honorius III papa Rolando Ferrariensi episcopo nuntiat se occupatores castri Medicine et fautores eorum cives Bononienses excommunicavisse et civitatem Bononiensem interdicto supposuisse, mandans episcopo Bononiensi ut excommunicationem denunciet et interdictum observes. Datum Laterani. [The date should be calculated based on the pontificate year provided in the original document, which is not fully given here, but assumed to be during his pontificate, 1216-1227.]

**Translation to English:**

To the provost, dean, and chapter of Bremen. As your church has in many ways been ruined by the unworthy Guademar, we, wishing to provide for it with fatherly care, and inclined by your prayers, by the authority of these presents, forbid that your archbishop, whoever he may be at the time, assigns in fief to anyone the tithes, comities, and advocacies pertaining to the aforementioned church when they become vacant, to the detriment of the same church. We also grant you permission to freely redeem the tithes pertaining to the church from the hands of laymen. Given at Rome, at St. Peter, on the 6th of the Nones of May, in the second year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa preposito, decano et capitulo Bremensi prohibet ne archiepiscopus, qui pro tempore fuerit, decimas et advocatias ecclesiae Bremensis in feudum concedat; concedit etiam eisdem decimas de manibus laicorum redimere. 1244, 2 Maii, Romae apud Sanctum Petrum.

**Translation to English:**

To the provosts of the greater church and of Saint Peter, and to the dean of Saint Saviour in Utrecht. Considering the zeal of faith and the fervor of devotion which our beloved son, the noble man W., Count of Holland, demonstrates in both intention and action concerning the matter of the Holy Land, as is fitting, we have decided to grant him the twentieth of the ecclesiastical revenues of Holland, Zeeland, East Frisia, and his other lands to support the Holy Land. Therefore, we firmly command your discretion by apostolic writings to assign the collected twentieth to the envoys of the same count, whom he will choose for this purpose, removing any obstacles of contradiction and appeal. If it has not yet been collected, gather it with the aforementioned envoys and confer it to them, restraining the contradictors by ecclesiastical censure, appeal set aside. If not all of you can act, then two of you, etc. Given at Rome, at Saint Peter's, on the 12th day before the Kalends of June, in the second year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa maioris ecclesiae et Sancti Petri praepositis et decano Sancti Salvatoris Traiectensis mandat ut vicesimam ecclesiasticorum proventuum Hollandiae et aliarum terrarum ad subsidium Terrae Sanctae comiti Hollandiae assignent. 1228, Mai. 21, Romae apud Sanctum Petrum.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishops of Prague and Olomouc and the provost of Regensburg. It has come to our attention, through our dearest son in Christ, O., the illustrious king of Bohemia, that the nobleman T., his nephew, who had taken up the sign of the life-giving cross on his shoulders and had set his face towards going to Jerusalem, turned aside to the field of Sempnar. There, joining with certain sons of iniquity, he treacherously occupied a certain castle of the king, rashly acting against his oath, through which he does not cease to devastate the goods of both the king and the churches. Therefore, we command your discretion through apostolic writings that you compel the aforementioned nobleman, by ecclesiastical censure after prior warning, and without appeal, to restore the said castle to the king, as he ought. Given at the Lateran, on the 15th day before the Kalends of February, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Pragensi et Olomucensi episcopis et preposito Ratisponensi mandat, ut nobilem T., qui castrum regis Boemiae proditorie occupavit, censeant ad restitutionem cogere. Datum Laterani, XV Kal. Febr., anno primo pontificatus nostri.

**Translation to English:**

To the Patriarch of Grado: You are to admonish and persuade the crusaders who are planning to cross from the port of Venice to the lands of Jerusalem, as well as the sailors who promise to transport them, to make every effort to land at Damietta, where the Christian army is located. You shall proclaim, by our authority and removing any obstacle of appeal, a general sentence of excommunication on both the crusaders and the sailors if they go against your admonition. Fulfill our mandate in such a way that you may please Him for whose cause this is undertaken, and that we may be able to commend your diligence in the Lord. Given at the Lateran, 10th Kalends of February, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Gradensi patriarche mandat, ut crucesignatos et nautas, qui ad partes Ierosolimitanas transfretare disponunt, moneat et inducat ad applicandum in Damiate, sub excommunicationis sententia si contra fecerint. 1229, Ian. 23. Datum Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To all princes of Germany, both ecclesiastical and secular. Although we have not received any letters from you through our beloved sons, the Abbot of St. Gall, the Dean of Speyer, and the noble man, the Marquis of Montferrat, messengers of our dearest son in Christ, Frederick, the illustrious King of Sicily elected as Emperor of the Romans, nonetheless, from the accustomed providence of the Apostolic See, we send you our writings, earnestly exhorting your community that, as it behooves the members, the honor of the head should not falter, and that you might powerfully and manfully assist the said king, as you have done thus far. For we ourselves aim, as much as we can with God, to his exaltation. Given at the Lateran, on the 9th of April, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Latin Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa universis principibus Alamannie, tam ecclesiasticis quam mundanis, scribit, hortans ut regi Sicilie, electo in Romanorum imperatorem, assistrent. 1227, Apr. 9. Laterani.

Indeed, we do not believe it is hidden from you that, although the brothers of the Hospital of St. John and the Knights Templar have heretofore and still are notable defenders of the orthodox faith among other Christians in the world, their hearts are so inflamed with the fire of the Holy Spirit that they not only continually fight the Lord's battles, ready to receive the crown of martyrdom, but, having become servants of the poor for Christ’s sake, they devote themselves to the ministries of hospitality, tirelessly performing works of piety, by which they not only gain the favor of the King of kings but also endeavor to rescue Christ’s faithful offering them kind assistance from eternal damnation, preparing for them a dwelling in the heavenly palace.

Yet, to prevent these brothers from escaping the fire of purification, the devil has stirred malicious tongues against them, so that some returning from overseas have blackened their reputation to such an extent that unless their innocence had shone like gold in the furnace at a time of necessity, upon hearing the rumors and murmurs of the slanderers, we ourselves may have been compelled at times to suspect them wrongly. Thus, we have deemed it necessary to declare to your community that when we caused an inquiry in the regions of Jerusalem to ascertain whether the outcry that reached our ears was justified, it was more clearly reported to us by our venerable brother, the Bishop of Albano, legate of the Apostolic See, and others, that the aforesaid brothers, among all other athletes of Christ, are managing the business of the cross with all fidelity and diligence, giving generous aid to the defenders of Jesus Christ from the alms of the faithful; and if the Hospitallers and Templars did not make the expenditures they do daily for serving knights, crossbowmen, and others useful for fighting, as well as for the poor, the army at Damietta could not in any way remain, since each of the afore-mentioned houses, as we learned from the same bishop, supplies daily necessities to nearly two thousand persons and seven hundred mounted troops.

We therefore urge and exhort your charity in the Lord, commanding you by apostolic writings to consider any rumors and murmurs against the aforesaid brothers, if any should reach your ears, as frivolous and fabricated, and ensure they are commended in your usual manner, preaching their innocence in your churches every Sunday and feast day, knowing for certain that the good you do for them will not perish, but are presented to the Lord, the giver of reward, through the hands of the poor, so that you may receive a hundredfold and possess the beatitude of eternal life. Given at the Lateran, on the eighth day before the Kalends of December, in the third year of our pontificate. In the same manner, letters have been sent to many others.

To the Archbishop of Salzburg. Enter into the chamber of your heart, and there diligently question yourself whether you would endure with an even mind the things that you have done to us, if they were done to you by your subjects. For as W., a monk of the monastery of Saint Lambert in Carinthia, which is said to belong directly to the Roman Church, has long since shown us by his complaint, you, while the matter of elections concerning him and Wolcher, a monk, in the said monastery was pending before the abbot of Runa and his fellow judges delegated by the Apostolic See, had him arrested with tyrannical violence in the church, heavily wounded, and thrown into prison, while the church itself was plundered of horses and other goods, so that he might be forced to desist from pursuing his rights. And while he was so detained, for the correction of his excesses, which you insinuated were various and numerous, you obtained apostolic letters, concealing that he was held in chains, so that under their cover you might more freely rage against him. However, when he sent his procurator to your synod to oppose the consecration of the aforementioned Wolcher as abbot while the case was pending, you nonetheless presumed to bless him as abbot after a legitimate appeal was interposed by the said procurator, while the matter was still under judgment, and to pronounce a sentence of excommunication against the said procurator without any prior warning, causing him to be disgracefully expelled from the synod, and to be treated dishonorably by your attendants, although he was a subdeacon. Moreover, since the said monastery, as stated, pertains specifically to the Apostolic See, you, usurping undue jurisdiction therein, pronounced a sentence of excommunication against certain monks following a legitimate appeal to us. And when we directed our writings to you on these matters, as we deemed necessary, you, adding fault to fault and contempt to contempt, scorned to receive our letters, which you certainly should not have done, even if we were in a lesser office, especially recalling that affection of charity which we showed you before our promotion. See if you have acted as befits an archbishop, see if you have kept inviolate the obedience promised to the Apostolic See! That this rebuke may suffice for now, we command your fraternity by apostolic writings to remove the said Wolcher completely from the prelature of the aforementioned monastery within a month of receiving these letters, and to lift or declare null the sentences you pronounced against the said subdeacon and monks, since the said monastery is claimed to be exempt and the appeal is said to have been legitimate, and allow the cause of the said elections to be concluded without hindrance before the aforementioned judges, restoring to the said church what was taken from it. Otherwise, know that we have instructed the abbot of Crehmsmunster, the provosts of the house of Saint Florian, and Matshe of the diocese of Passau by our letters, that if you cease to execute our mandate, they, by our authority, shall carry out what is above stated concerning the removal of the aforesaid Wolcher and the lifting of the sentences you pronounced against the said monks and subdeacon, removing any obstacle of appeal or contradiction, having ascertained the truth, and instructing the aforementioned judges to proceed in the case, notwithstanding any contradiction, according to the form handed down to them, to hear the proposals from both sides regarding the plundering of the said church and to decree what is just, removing any appeal. Given at Ferentino, Kalends of September, in the second year [of the pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Salzburgensi mandat, ut Wolcherum a praelatura monasterii Sancti Lamberti amoveat et sententias in subdiaconum et monachos relaxet, causamque electionum sine impedimento permittat terminari, sub poena interpositionis legatorum per nostras litteras. Datum Ferentini, Kalendis Septembris, anno secundo.

To the Bishop of Metz, Chancellor of the Imperial Court. Your brotherhood, as we believe, recognizes the prerogative of love with which your mother, the Roman Church, has embraced you, opening the door of her goodness to you so that she has deemed you worthy of being honored with a certain singular grace among others. Moreover, you must hold firm that we have anticipated you with such an abundance of love that we are concerned about your honor and gladly think about those things which concern your advancement, which is why the Apostolic See and we ourselves have confidence in you, that recalling the sweetness you have tasted from it, and considering that more and more of the dew of its blessing will be poured upon you if you remain in its devotion, you should carry the affairs of the Roman Church in your heart, and even procure them without our prompting. Gregorius IX papa episcopo Metensi mandat, ut terram comitisse Matildis Raynaldo Munaldi, subdiacono et capellano, secundum regium mandatum restituat. Datum apud Urbemveterem, Nonis Augusti, anno quinto.

To the illustrious King John of Jerusalem. We have heard that you have withdrawn from the regions of Damietta and have gathered your forces and come to the city of Acre; if you have done so with the intention and consideration to counter the incursions of the pagans infesting those regions and to thwart their efforts, we commend your foresight in the Lord, especially if Christians from that region are so troubled that they seem to be in need of such help. However, it would not befit royal magnificence, while others fight for the Christian faith, for you to rest in idleness or be occupied with private matters. We certainly cannot believe, as some dream, that you wish to move arms against the kingdom of Armenia, as we believe that there is such prudence in royal serenity that you clearly see how much danger, harm, and confusion could result from this for the faithful in the eastern regions and for the entire Christian people, and how much you would render yourself odious to the Apostolic See and all the faithful if now, with the forces of the whole Christian world being shaken for your aid and that of the Holy Land, you were to prefer particular interests over common advantage, which cannot be successfully promoted unless the common good is first advanced. Although we trust that you, prudently considering these things, will avoid attempting anything that could cause the entire effort for the Holy Land, which the Christian people have undertaken so far, to be lost and frustrated, yet we strictly forbid you, by the authority of these presents under the penalty of anathema and under the protection of divine and our grace, to move arms at this time against the Armenians or any other Christians. Instead, strive to ensure that the entire overseas Christendom remains in unity, and dutifully heed our venerable brother, Plelagius, Bishop of Albano and legate of the Apostolic See, who has frequently commended your valor to us in his letters, endeavoring that the common business of the Christian people may achieve the desired outcome by the Lord's bounty, after which you may more diligently and usefully attend to your particular benefits. Otherwise, however much we love your person and wish to show deference to royal dignity, we could not, however, defer to you or anyone else against the common good, indeed against God Himself. Given at the Old City, on the third day before the Ides of August, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

To the Archbishop of Salzburg, the Bishop of Kym and the Abbot of Holy Cross of the Cistercian Order in the Diocese of Passau. After a lengthy delay at the Apostolic See by our venerable brother, the Bishop of Prague, regarding a dispute between him on one side and the illustrious King and Barons of Bohemia on the other, concerning tithes, ecclesiastical jurisdiction, the immunity of churches, and several other matters pertaining to ecclesiastical freedom, for which the King and Barons are excommunicated and his kingdom is under interdict, finally, with the procurators of the King and Barons present before us, both parties freely committed themselves to our arbitration. After a long discussion with our brothers and the parties themselves about a settlement, with the parties disagreeing on a few points of the proposed form, behold, the noble Dalebor, the chief justice, and Martin, the King's cupbearer, as well as Marcuard of Dechin and Divis of Prachen, castellans, and Habra, the procurator of the noble Bleneson, castellan of Budisin, arrived on behalf of the said King and themselves, urgently requesting that we send the aforementioned Bishop to the city of Vienna, belonging to the noble Duke of Austria, affirming that with the Bishop present, the King and Barons could be easily brought to concord, and they would exert diligent effort and effective work for this. They also swore under oath that they spoke with the King's and Barons' special mandate and would faithfully work for peace and concord, safeguarding the Bishop's person like their own, both in leading him to the aforementioned city and returning him to our presence, should concord not be achieved. Therefore, complying with the requests and the urgency of the aforementioned nobles, we decided to send the Bishop to the said city, so that with the Lord's assistance, this dispute may find resolution. Thus, we command you by apostolic writing to personally go to that place, or closer if necessary, to the borders of the kingdom, and to admonish the King, to whom we write concerning this matter, that he, according to the promise of the said nobles, shall come to the said place with some of the barons authorized by both the barons and nobles of Bohemia. Prudently and diligently, you shall contribute your efforts to restore concord among them. If concord is achieved through your mediation, and it is secured with sufficient and appropriate guarantees, you shall lift the sentences of excommunication and interdict. Otherwise, ensuring the Bishop returns to us safely as promised by the aforementioned nobles, you shall command that the sentences remain observed inviolably until due satisfaction is rendered. Given at Viterbo, March 20, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin**:

Gregorius IX papa mandat archiepiscopo Salzeburgensi, episcopo Kymensi et abbati Sanctae Crucis Cisterciensis ordinis, ut controversiam inter episcopum Pragensem et regem ac barones Boemiae super decimis et libertatibus ecclesiasticis componant, episcopo ad Viennam misso, concordia reformata excommunicationis et interdicti sententias relaxent. Si vero concordia non fiat, episcopum incolumem reducant. Datum Viterbii, XIII Kal. Aprilis, pontificatus anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To N., Bishop of Tusculum, legate of the apostolic see, and to our beloved son, the subdeacon and chaplain Alatrinus. By the common counsel of our brothers, we mandate you with the present authority that you diligently ensure that the capitulars, which we send to you enclosed herein, are formulated into public laws in the royal name, with the sentences preserved under suitable words, and sent back to us fortified with the royal seal, to be solemnly published under the imperial name in the Basilica of the Prince of the Apostles on the day of coronation. Furthermore, prudently and cautiously endeavor to investigate and understand the royal mind and intention, both about avoiding the union of the kingdom and the empire and about the aid to the Holy Land, clearly impressing upon the royal ears that it seems he has clearly acted against his promises and privileges, as he has procured the election of his son, crowned King of Sicily, as King of the Romans, and has summoned the prelates and magnates of the kingdom to the imperial crown and demanded and continues to demand oaths of loyalty from them anew, through which the aforementioned union seems to be pursued to the detriment of the apostolic see as well as his own posterity; whence many are justly amazed. You should stress the necessity of the Holy Land, as the matter demands, indicating to the royal majesty how the confidence and hope of that business depend almost entirely on him after God, as it is clearly evident through the envoys and letters of the legate, prelates, and barons of the Christian army, and how we have urgently called him to the crown specifically for this cause; and you should add that unless the Christian army is magnificently supported in the imminent passage, there is without doubt a fear that the aforementioned business of the Holy Land may be utterly dissolved. Whatever you may be able to understand on these matters, ensure to faithfully inform us as soon as possible. Given at the Lateran on the 4th day before the Ides of November, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Tusculano et subdiacono Alatrino mandat ut capitularia in leges regias redigantur et de statu regni et subsidio Terre Sancte investigent. 1231, Nov. 10. Datum Laterani.

Translation to English:

To the Archbishop of Salzburg. Your praiseworthy devotion and honorable intention lead us to support you as a noble and illustrious member of the Church of God with the favor of the Apostolic See. We should not unreasonably grant your requests, which are known to contain not only the advancement of your church but also the salvation of the flock entrusted to you. On your part, it was humbly requested of us that, since you wish to provide your church, in which regular canons exist, with a learned man in theology according to the constitution of the general council, who can both teach them and minister the word of God to the clergy and people entrusted to you. Since it would be unfitting to join or rather set a secular person over religious individuals, because an ox and a donkey should not plow together nor a garment be woven with linen and wool, we might deign to grant you the license to appoint Brother B., a monk of the monastery of Hausen in the diocese of Augsburg, to this office, of whose knowledge and piety you are fully aware. Therefore, favorably granting your supplications, we grant you, whose fraternity we fully trust in the Lord, the requested license. Given at the Lateran, on the 7th Ides of February, in the sixth year.

Regesto:

Gregorius IX papa Salzeburgensi archiepiscopo licentiam concedit ut magistrum B. monachum de Hausen ad docendum et ministrandum verbum Dei in ecclesia sua assumat. 1232, Febr. 7. Laterano.

**Translation to English:**

To all archbishops, bishops, and faithful Christians established throughout Germany. The king, the son, descended to the lowest as he emerged from the secret of the father into the public to serve, so that, under the guise of our mortality, the potter was seen on earth and conversed with men, preparing the ascent to the highest for his subordinates. He finally did not shy away from insults, nor did he withdraw from injuries, but offered himself to the cross and willingly gave himself up to sufferings, so that he might cancel with his blood the record of our servitude and abolish the law of temporal death with eternal death.

Truly, those invited to Christ's table, if they wish to consider what is placed before them, might prepare similar things themselves and gird themselves not just as those already signed with the cross, but others as well, for the service of the cross. However, we sorrowfully report that some from the empire, both lesser and greater, are believed to have turned their faces away from Jerusalem, to which they seemed to have directed themselves, since they have neither pursued the vow they made nor shown any readiness to do so thus far.

Therefore, wishing to provide for their salvation and the aid of the Holy Land, we have decided to set a fixed term for them to begin fulfilling their vows to the Lord. But not within that or another term, which we have extended, have they, with few exceptions, fulfilled their promised pilgrimage duties, nor have they shown any signs of fulfilling their vow. Hence, they have incurred the sentence of excommunication, which we have ordered to be proclaimed against such individuals according to the statutes of the general council. What will these individuals demand gratuitously from their inferiors when they do not fulfill what is owed to their greater and creator, what they have willingly offered and are now altogether due?

Because many good things are often given to the unwilling, and coercion is sometimes beneficial, since the sentence of excommunication is medicinal, we command you by the authority of these presents to generally denounce such individuals as being bound by the chain of excommunication, except for those whom a just impediment clearly excuses. But because we seek not the binding but the loosening of souls, we have provided by a pious deliberation that if any of these seek the benefit of absolution, they may be absolved by you upon receiving the oath to comply with the commands of the Church, which we wish to impose under the obligation of the given oath, that on the feast of the Blessed Benedict next or before, unless detained by a just and evident impediment, they undertake the journey to aid the Holy Land and pursue it as the Lord grants.

However, we do not wish to conceal from you, the crusaders, that, as we have heard, unless some cross over in the March passage to the aid of the Christian army, a grave danger, which God forbid, might threaten them, nor would it be easy to resume such a great undertaking, which has had prosperity thus far with the Lord guiding the process, from the beginning with an uncertain outcome. Given at Rieti, Kalends of October, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa universis archiepiscopis, episcopis et Christi fidelibus per Teutoniam constitutis denuntiat quosdam de imperio, excommunicationis vinculo subiacere ob vota crucesignatorum non persoluta, et mandat ut si petierint absolutionem, iuramento recepto, absolvendi sint. Dat. Reate, Kal. Octobris, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To Frederick, ever august Emperor of the Romans and King of Sicily. We do not believe that any Roman pontiff has ever held a more sincere affection towards any emperor than we have for the person of your highness, as you may have been able to perceive through evident proofs and will continue to perceive, with the Lord granting, throughout all the days of our life. Therefore, if there was any difficulty or deficiency in providing you with the imperial fodrum, it is most grievous and troublesome to us, nor can it in any way be imputed to us. For as you approached the regions of Tuscany, we expressly commanded all the cities under our dominion to offer you the procurement or fodrum liberally and gladly, and to ensure that no one dared to contravene our orders, we took care to send there our beloved son Alatrinus, our subdeacon and chaplain, who is no less devoted to you than to the Roman Church, indeed he is entirely yours, so that everything might be decently accomplished through his diligence. And because, according to the tenor of the privilege made concerning this matter between the Church and the Empire, this fodrum ought only to be requested through the envoys of the Roman Church, Roman emperors do not have the right to demand such procurements or fodrum through Maritima or Campania, since they do not pass through those parts when they come for the crown or when they return to their own lands, and if any have ever received them while yearning to invade the kingdom of Sicily, it was not by justice but by violence. Even if this were a debt, it ought nevertheless to be requested by envoys of the Roman Church, according to the tenor of the aforementioned privilege. However, we, not observing these things concerning your person but wishing to extend all honor liberally to you from our own, directed our beloved son, our cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo, R., who is united to you in special affection and devotion, and who governs all of Campania and Maritima, instructing him to ensure the fodrum and all honor are provided to you diligently and attentively. And behold, having received your majesty's letters, we have given orders to the same cardinal through our writings to make such provisions that everything may be fully provided to you, so that no deficiency may be found, declaring to your highness that we do these things not out of obligation but out of special grace and sincere affection of charity. Given at the Lateran, on the 11th of December, in the fifth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Friderico Romanorum imperatori fodrum et honorem ex caritate non ex debito per cardinalem R. Sancti Angeli exhiberi mandat. Dat. Laterani, III Idus Decembris, anno quinto.

Translation to English:

To Frederick, illustrious Emperor of the Romans, ever august, and King of Sicily. Our beloved and faithful citizens of Benevento have brought to our attention through complaints that your bailiffs are demanding and extorting from them duties on land, pledges, tolls, forest rights, marketplace fees, and pasture rights, and are troubling them and especially those who once belonged to lands under your rule, in many ways. Since we hold the city of Benevento in special affection among others which belong to the jurisdiction and property of the Apostolic See, and since it is protected against such exactions by the privilege of you and your ancestors, we earnestly ask and request your majesty to cause your bailiffs to cease their harassment of this city. We are prepared to provide a complete measure of justice to anyone who has a grievance against our faithful subjects residing in the aforementioned city. We ask you to reaffirm and keep inviolate the privileges that your ancestors and you have granted to the city in respect for us. Furthermore, since the noble Thomas, Count of Acerra, is ready to seek justice before us if he has a grievance against them, you should forbid him from harassing the city but instead pursue his rights judicially in our presence. May you ensure, in these matters, that our requests are heeded, so that we may justly commend the devotion of your highness. Given at the Lateran, on the 14th of May, in the fifth year.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa Friderico, illustri Romanorum imperatori semper augusto et regi Sicilie, mandat ut balivi eius a vexatione civitatis Beneventane cessent et privilegia a parentibus suis et ab ipso indulta serventur; item comiti Acerrarum inhibet ne civitatem ipsam molestet, sed ius suum coram sede apostolica prosequatur. 1231, Maii 14, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man, the Duke of Saxony. Since the arrogance of the wicked and the wickedness of the arrogant have multiplied to such an extent that, without distinguishing between holy and profane, they impiously persecute the churches, sacrilegiously seizing their goods, it is necessary that those who have received secular power from the Lord of the ages should firmly oppose such wrongdoers. By correcting the unruly with justice and consoling the pious faint-hearted, they may thereby earn merit before God and render their power gracious before men. Therefore, as our beloved son, Master Conrad, our chaplain and penitentiary, the elected bishop of Hildesheim, has shown us in his petition sent to us, many in those parts, having cast aside divine fear, not only recklessly revel in the goods of his church but also publicly plunder them as robbers. We earnestly ask, instruct, and urge your nobility through apostolic writings that, as a Catholic man, you support and defend the same church favorably, and powerfully and openly assist the elected bishop against his wrongdoers, so that he, serving the Lord in quiet freedom, may offer favorable sacrifices of praise to the Lord for you. May the God who hears the prayers of His servants and we ourselves be able to commend your devotion rightly. Given at the Lateran, on the 9th of September, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa, nobili viro duci Saxoniae mandat ut ecclesiam Hildesemensem, cuius bona diripiuntur, foveat et defendat contra malefactores, auxilium praestando Conrado electo Hildesemensi. Datum Laterani, V Idus Septembris, anno sexto (1232).

**Translation to English:**

To the provost and chapter of Northhausen. When it was formerly intimated to our ears both by our dearest son in Christ, Frederick, the ever august Roman emperor and king of Sicily, and by certain archbishops and bishops, that your church had so collapsed in the hands of certain women then residing there, who were living the life of secular canons and were called canonesses, that it did not seem that it could be easily restored while they remained there, at the request of the emperor himself and many others, we entrusted to our venerable brother, the archbishop, and our beloved sons, G. the dean and V. the provost of St. Mary's of Magdeburg, the task of instituting a provost with a college of secular canons in the place, after consulting our venerable brother, the archbishop of Mainz, the diocesan of the place, who was said to have given his consent, with the women of that place first being suitably relocated to other appropriate places. Recently, the same archbishop and his colleagues informed us by their letters that they had suitably relocated the aforementioned women to appropriate and accepted places, except for one who impudently attempted to resist this arrangement and said she did not need apostolic grace for her relocation. As a result, you were instituted in the above-mentioned church according to apostolic mandate, and we were humbly petitioned to deign to confirm their process with apostolic authority. Therefore, we confirm the process duly and prudently carried out according to our mandate by apostolic authority and strengthen it with the protection of this present writing. Let no one, therefore, infringe upon our confirmation. If anyone should do so, etc. Given at the Lateran, 5th Kalends of June, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa preposito et capitulo Nortusensi confirmat quod post relocationem sororum, secundum mandatum apostolicum, instituti sunt in ecclesia cum collegio canonicorum secularium, et processum a G. decano et V. preposito Magdeburgensi rite factum auctoritate apostolica roborat. Dat. Lateran. V Kal. Iunii, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishops of Halberstadt and Hildesheim, and to the noble men H., Duke of Saxony, Count Palatine of the Rhine, Count of Ascania, and the ministerials of the Church of Magdeburg. We express our gratitude and acceptance for, as we have heard, you have bound yourselves by oath to confer mutual assistance to procure and preserve peace in your lands, so that the people entrusted to you may dwell in the beauty of peace and in abundant rest. Therefore, commending your discretion with worthy praises in the Lord, we mandate you through apostolic writings to observe this oath, as it is lawful and honorable, in such a way that you preserve your conscience unblemished before God and your reputation intact, and that you may be deemed prudent by others. Given at the Lateran, on the sixth day before the Kalends of July, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopis Halberstadensi et Ildesemensi et nobilibus viris H. duci Saxoniae, comiti palatino Reni, comiti Ascaniae et ministerialibus ecclesiae Magdeburgensis mandat, ut iuramentum pro mutuo auxilio ad pacem in terris suis procurandam, licitum et honestum, taliter observent, quod conscientiam apud Deum et famam illesas servent. 1232, Iun. 26, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To Conrad, Scholasticus of Mainz and our Penitentiary. Our venerable brother, the Bishop of Albano, legate of the Apostolic See, and our beloved sons, the entire Christian army present at Damietta in the service of Jesus Christ, have informed us through their messengers and letters that now, more than ever before, the Holy Land requires greater and more mature assistance. With many returning to their homes from those parts, the Christian army has become exceedingly diminished, so much so that unless it is quickly reinforced with new soldiers, they will not dare to attack the land of the Saracens, and may scarcely be able to defend what has already been conquered. They also fear being left in the hands of the enemy, to the eternal disgrace of all Christ’s faithful and the perpetual loss of the small portion of the transmarine land still held by Christ’s faithful. 

In addition, to bring joy to you and others who hear this, know that our dearest son in Christ, Frederick, the illustrious Emperor of the Romans and King of Sicily, recently, on the Sunday preceding Advent, received the imperial diadem from our hands in complete peace and tranquility. In full devotion, he publicly took upon himself the sign of the cross, fervently swearing with a heartfelt oath that, God willing, he will cross the sea in the coming month of August to aid the Holy Land. Our venerable brother, the Bishop of Metz, Chancellor of the Imperial Court, and our beloved sons, the noble Duke of Bavaria and Warner of Boland, steward, along with other marquises, counts, and barons from Germany and Apulia, more than four hundred of them, and with them a large multitude of knights and foot soldiers, having openly received the sign of the cross, have vowed to cross the sea in the coming March to aid the aforementioned land. Therefore, it is expedient that those signed with the cross and those to be signed hasten without delay to cross the sea, so that with assembled forces, they may, with God’s help, more easily, as we hope, overcome the enemies of the Christian name. 

Given at the Lateran, on the fifth day before the Kalends of December, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Conrado scolastico Maguntino mandat ut notificet Christianos crucesignatos et crucesignandos de necessitate succursu Terrae Sanctae, exhortans eos ad celerem transfretationem in subsidium. Insuper, Fredericus imperator et multi nobiles crucesigno recepto in subsidium Terre Sancte transire devoverunt. Datum Laterani, V Kal. Decembris, anno quinto pontificatus.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishops of Turin and Vercelli. Our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Milan, has brought a grave matter to our attention: that A., the ruler of the people of Milan, along with the people themselves, wickedly conspired against him, because he strives to uphold ecclesiastical liberty. They presumptuously dared to place him under ban. Although a sentence of excommunication has been pronounced against them for this reason, they persist in their hardness of iniquity, not only failing to correct what they have rashly attempted but also not fearing to lay ambushes on the life of the archbishop himself. Since we do not wish to tolerate such an absurd abuse of rashness, we command your fraternity by apostolic letters to solemnly publish the excommunication pronounced against them, with bells tolling and candles lit, on every Sunday and feast day in places where you see fit, and ensure, by our authority, that it is strictly observed until they make due satisfaction. You must also strictly prohibit any city from presuming to appoint one of them as a ruler, nor should anyone dare to assume the governance of the city of Milan, nor engage in any conversation, commerce, or contract with them, if they wish to avoid a similar sentence. Given at Alatri, Kalends of June, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Taurinensi et Vercellensi episcopis mandat ut, ob conspirationem contra Mediolanensem archiepiscopum factam et excommunicationem latam, eam campanis pulsatis et candelis accensis publicent et observandam curent, ne quis Mediolanensibus in duritia persistentibus rectorem assumat aut cum eis colloquium habeat. 1232, Iun. 1, Alatri.

**Translation to English:**

To R., Cardinal Deacon of Saint Angel, Rector of Campania and the Maritime Region. Our beloved son in Christ, Frederick, Emperor of the Romans, ever august and King of Sicily, has sent us certain letters in which he seems to convey that he has not been duly satisfied concerning the collection of the fodrum in Campania and the Maritime region. He claims to have sent his notary, Master John, and Stephen Tiniosum to Campania and the Maritime region to collect this fodrum. We believe your prudence makes you aware that such fodrum is not owed to the Roman emperors by the people of Campania or the Maritime region, as they have no obligation to pass through those parts except for matters related to the Kingdom of Sicily, to which we or our subjects are not obliged to provide assistance. Even if some of them have sometimes extorted this fodrum when eagerly rushing to invade the kingdom, it was done not by justice but by force. Moreover, if this fodrum were rightfully owed to the emperors, it should only be requested through the envoys of the Apostolic See, as established by the privilege concerning such fodrum made between the Church and the Empire. Therefore, we command your discretion by apostolic letters, prudently and diligently explain all these matters to the Emperor, and inform him that we have ordered the fodrum to be given to him in Campania and the Maritime region not out of obligation but as a special grace and sincere affection of charity, advising him not to incline the ears of his imperial majesty to those suggesting otherwise in these or other matters, for he should trust our benefactions more than the deceitful words of others. Furthermore, have the fodrum collected in Campania and the Maritime region by your envoys and delivered to the Emperor's envoys, so that what we began to do out of liberal grace may be liberally completed. Given at the Lateran, on the third Ides of December, in the fifth year of our pontificate. A similar letter was written to Alatrino, our subdeacon and chaplain, until: the words of others.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Honorius III papa R. Sancti Angeli diacono cardinali, Campaniae et Maritimae rectori, mandat ut fodrum per Campaniam et Maritimam colligi et imperatoriis nuntiis exhiberi faciat, non ex debito, sed ex gratia speciali. 1221, Dec. 11, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

Letter to the Lord Pope. To the most holy father and his lord H., venerable supreme pontiff of the Holy Roman Church, from his devoted son in Christ, L., by the grace of God Duke of Austria and Styria, due and devoted obedience with filial reverence. Because of the benevolence and grace of your paternity, which has looked upon my smallness more abundantly and familiarly than upon the other princes of Germany, I have firmly resolved and still resolve to always be faithful and devoted to you and the Roman Church. The indignation you have conceived against me, because I refused to affix my seal to your instrument, greatly burdens me. But let your paternity know for certain that this was not done out of malice or lack of devotion, but because a certain clause contained in it greatly terrified me: namely, that I, my wife, and children should bind ourselves under penalty of excommunication not to act against what was contained in the same instrument. Therefore, I humbly beseech your clemency to wholly remit in God any rancor and indignation you have conceived against me. For whatever the king and princes may wish to do for the honor and exaltation of the Roman Church, I will in truth not only not hinder, but, God willing, will strive to apply effective effort to promote the same to the best of my ability. Furthermore, I inform your paternity that upon my return from overseas, when I was in your presence, the deposition of Master Arnold, the former dean of Prague, was famously discussed in your court, and no one there doubted it, to the point that even some clerics of your court asked me to confer the benefits that the same Arnold held from me on them. Upon my return home, I found such rumors that the Archbishop of Salzburg and the Bishops of Passau, Regensburg, and Eichstätt, by your mandate, had declared the said Arnold deprived of all offices and benefits, and judges delegated by you instructed me, by your authority, to present suitable clerics to the churches the aforementioned Arnold held from me, which had also been vacant for a year or more due to my absence, which I did; and two of my chaplains were canonically invested in these churches through my presentation, and they have now peacefully possessed the same for two years or more. Therefore, I humbly beseech your clemency in the Lord, not to intend to restore the aforesaid churches to the mentioned Arnold to my and my chaplains' prejudice and grievance. For if it pleases your liberality, you may provide for him in another way without scandal and more fittingly.

**Regesto:**

Honorarius III papa, dilecto filio L., duci Austrie et Stirie, significat se indignationem suam propter negationem sigilli remittere, cum id non ex malitia sed ex timore clausulae factum sit; rogat etiam ne ecclesias, quas capellani ducis per biennium possederunt, Arnoldo decano Pragensi restituat. Datum Perusii, VII Kalendas Martii, anno pontificatus tertio.

**Translation to English:**

To the illustrious King of Sicily, elected as Emperor of the Romans. It is unnecessary for us to express in words how purely and diligently we have aimed and continue to aim with steadfast purpose at the exaltation of your highness, because the very exhibition of our actions abundantly expresses and demonstrates this; hence we justly marvel that, what we rightfully request from you, we obtain with such difficulty. For when we had instructed our venerable brother, the Bishop of Metz, Chancellor of the Imperial Court, to ensure that the land of the late Countess Matilda, which pertains to the Roman Church, be surrendered in our name to our beloved son Alatrinus, our subdeacon and chaplain, and when we learned that the said Alatrinus was not in agreement with the chancellor, we made efforts to send our beloved son Raynald, our subdeacon and chaplain, to the chancellor for this purpose. The latter, however, detained him for a long time with various promises and, for whatever reason, did not have the land surrendered to him. Therefore, we have seen fit to earnestly request and exhort your highness, urging you to fulfill what you promised with royal privilege, confirmed by the subscriptions of the princes and your other letters, by ensuring that the said land be freely surrendered in our name to the aforementioned chaplains or to one of them, should both not be able to be present, considering that if you were to violate your promise in such a small matter, it would be unbecoming of royal highness and could also lead to the presumption that, having violated your promise in the least, you would not keep it in the greatest matters concerning the church. For this reason, we earnestly entreat again that you make provision in such a way that for your exaltation, which we not only wish but also desire, you render us more willing from among the willing and more prompt from among the prompt. To this end, we also willingly exhort your highness to those things by which you may be able to please God more earnestly, and we solicit your royal highness that, since the vice of heresy is said to have greatly increased in Lombardy, as is evident from the wicked statutes that many cities of that province have issued against the Church of God, you decree and cause to be kept something worthy of royal majesty against heretics and their supporters and harborers, and that you generally annul those statutes, inasmuch as the chapters arising from the root of heretical depravity are attempts against ecclesiastical freedom, and command them to be abjured, so that the faithful, seeing your zeal for the faith and the Church of God, may rightly rejoice, recognizing through your deeds that you have received the sword from the Lord for the praise of the good and the punishment of the wicked. Given at Orvieto.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa illustri regi Sicilie, Romanorum imperatori electo, mandat ut terram comitisse Matildis Alatrino subdiacono et capellano nostro resignari faciat, et hortatur ut contra hereticos in Lombardia statuta condat. Datum apud Urbemveterem.

**Translation to English:**

To all the faithful of Christ who will inspect these present letters. The immensity of Divine kindness, bestowing virtues to grant rewards, rejoices in receiving even little in return from its faithful, so that they may thus merit grace from grace, and in a happy exchange receive eternal goods for temporal ones. Therefore, since the church of Saint Maurice of Magdeburg, whose foundations were laid by our venerable brother Hugh of Ostia, bishop, and our beloved son Leo, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross, then legates of the apostolic see, rises with noble structure and so costly a work that its resources do not suffice for its completion, we ask and exhort you in the Lord, enjoining upon you for the remission of sins, that you provide necessary aid from the goods bestowed upon you by God, so that the said work may be successfully completed through the help of your support, and that you may earn eternal rewards through these and other works of piety which you do by God's grace. We, however, relying on the mercy of Almighty God and the authority of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul, mercifully relax forty days of enjoined penance for all truly penitent and confessed who devoutly assemble at the said church on the day of the solemnity of its glorious martyr Maurice or even within the octave, intending to provide assistance for the completion of the aforementioned work. These letters shall be valid for a period of up to ten years. Given at Alatri, 17th May, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

For, although the king and his barons, through special envoys, once swore before our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Mainz, and later confirmed this oath before you, brother of Regensburg, and our beloved sons, the abbots of the Cistercian order of Ratisbon and Würzburg, delegated by the Apostolic See, to leave the rights of our venerable brother, the Bishop of Prague, and his church intact, as the king himself has informed us through his letters, now, as the aforementioned bishop has humbly presented before us in the presence of the abbot of Walsassen, whom we had appointed as executor over this matter, and the king's envoy, they are persecuting him and his church in manifold ways, appointing and removing, or rather imposing, persons in his churches at will, and preventing him and his officials from exercising ecclesiastical jurisdiction.

They also refuse to pay him tithes, under the pretext of a wrongful custom, which should rather be called corruption; and they not only refuse to return the fruits of ecclesiastical property and other things they had unlawfully taken from the bishop while he was staying at the Apostolic See, as well as the taxes they extorted from his people, but they have also recklessly invaded and are said to have alienated certain lands of the Prague church and other churches as well as some of his own properties, which he had possessed peacefully for a long time before he set out for the Apostolic See and had assigned to the Prague church for a certain debt, thus infringing upon the privileges of the churches. 

Moreover, they knowingly associate with the excommunicated, do not allow schismatics to be punished with due penalty, and those who have been stripped of ecclesiastical benefits due to their crimes, they do not allow the revenues of these benefits to be withdrawn. They also expel from the kingdom the clerics who present letters of citation or deprivation to the schismatics, forbidding anyone in the entire diocese of Prague to dare to receive letters from the Apostolic See or the bishop that mention sentences of interdict or excommunication. They do not permit clerics and the bishop's envoys to leave or enter the kingdom freely. Not content with these actions, they demand and extort thirty denarii from clerics at tolls or customs, although only one denarius is demanded from a layperson. They frequently extort large sums from religious houses under the pretext of any army's passage.

Although we and those delegated by us have frequently admonished them thoroughly about these matters, they have never been able to be deterred from harassing the bishop and the Church of Prague. Therefore, although we wish to show deference to the aforementioned king as an eminent figure and to the barons sent by him, since deference should not be shown to people against God, to whom it is owed against all humans, with the counsel of our brothers, we firmly command you, by apostolic writings, to prudently admonish and effectively induce the king and the barons to provide suitable satisfaction for the damages inflicted and the fruits withheld, as well as the injuries caused to the aforementioned bishop, and to refrain from harassing him further, once they have provided appropriate pledges or sureties. If, God forbid, they refuse to heed your admonitions within two months, we declare that they will henceforth be subject to sentences of excommunication and their entire land to interdict, which you shall renew daily on Sundays and feast days, ensuring their strict observance by bishops, church prelates, and all neighbors, removing any appeal, until returning to their senses, they may deserve the relaxation of these sentences. If not all, etc. Given at Rieti, 2nd August, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

Oh, how much we desire you in the presence of the Most High, oh, how much in the eyes of men, so that before Him, your conscience may observe whatever is integrity, and before them, your reputation incurs no notable disrepute. Indeed, he who loves much fears much. Hence, it is no wonder if we fear for you and for ourselves regarding your delayed progress as assistance to the Holy Land: for you, lest through the insistence of so frequently repeated delays, you incur the offense (God forbid) of the most powerful king. For us, lest by the ease of such extensions we seem to have left the cause of that supreme pontiff who offered himself as a sacrifice to God the Father on the cross for the salvation of the people, to negligence. 

However, you still insist that a fourth delay be added, not considering that one summoned by three edicts, if he scorns to come to judgment, can be reproached for contumacy.
