Given at the Lateran, on the 16th Kalends of April, in the first year (of our pontificate).

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Coloniensi et suffraganeis eius mandat, ut subditos suos ad subsidium Terrae Sanctae animet, crucesignatos iniungendo ut transeant in instanti passagio, alios vero ad suscipiendam crucem vel conferendum in eundem subsidium exhortando. 1228, Mart. 17. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To R., cardinal deacon of St. Angel, legate of the apostolic see. Our beloved son in Christ, Frederick, the illustrious emperor of the Romans, ever august, and king of Sicily, has urgently requested that the cities, castles, and other places belonging to the empire in the regions of Provence and the kingdom of Arles, and specifically those which the late Raymond, count of Toulouse, held from the empire, be restored to him, whether they have fallen into your hands or those of anyone else owing to the army assembled to eradicate heretical depravity from those parts, or whether they may yet fall into such hands. Surely, we do not believe it has escaped your memory that we have repeatedly instructed you through apostolic letters that we desired those lands to be purged of heretical depravity while preserving the rights of the empire intact. Therefore, even though the emperor's request does not diverge from our intention, and we do not wish to diminish the rights of the empire but to enhance them, we have decided to defer such restitution until it becomes clear to us, through your report, which lands belong to the empire in those regions and all the circumstances of the matter. We wish and we command, by the authority of these presents, that you retain the lands pertaining to the empire under your and the church's control, ensuring they are diligently guarded by bishops and other prelates of the churches, who shall keep these lands safe, respecting the rights of the emperor and the empire, maintaining loyalty to the emperor and the empire, so that when we have learned from your report the facts of the matter, we may ensure the rights of the aforementioned emperor are restored to his envoys or appointed officials without jeopardizing peace and faith. Given at the Lateran, the 10th day before the Kalends of December, in the eleventh year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa R. Sancti Angeli diacono cardinali, legato apostolice sedis mandat, ut terras imperio pertinentes in Provincia et regno Arelatensi in sua et ecclesie potestate retineat, donec per eius relationem plenius constiterit de circumstantiis. Datum Laterani, X Kalendas Decembris, anno undecimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of the Monastery of St. Michael of the Cistercian Order, in the diocese of Halberstadt, and to the provost and dean of Halberstadt. As it was presented before the Holy See by the dean and convent of the Quedlinburg Monastery, directly subject to the Apostolic See, that after the monastery had been recently deprived of the support of an abbess, they invoked the grace of the Holy Spirit and unanimously and canonically elected the provost of the same place as abbess, humbly requesting that the election held for her be confirmed by apostolic authority. Therefore, following the form of the letters which our predecessor of good memory, Pope Honorius, had arranged to be sent, we expressly command you by apostolic writings, that after examining both the election and the elected, if you find the election canonically celebrated for a suitable person, confirm it by our authority, and cause the blessing to be bestowed upon the elected in our stead. If all of you cannot be present to execute these tasks, let two of you nonetheless carry them out. Given at the Lateran, the 4th day before the Kalends of April, in the first year (of our pontificate).

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati de Lapide Sancti Michaelis Cisterciensis ordinis Alberstadensis diocesis, preposito et decano Alberstadensi mandat, ut electionem preposite monasterii Quindelimburgensis in abbatissam, si de idonea persona canonice celebrata sit, auctoritate apostolica confirment et benedictionem vice sua impendi faciant. 1227, Mart. 29, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop, the Greater Provost, and the Dean of the Holy Apostles of Cologne. Since we have received under the protection of Blessed Peter and our own the beloved sons, all the crusaders of the city of Cologne, who, kindled by zeal for faith and devotion, have assumed the sign of the life-giving cross and proposed to set out for the aid of the Holy Land with their families and all their goods, which they presently possess reasonably, we decree that once they begin their journey overseas in the upcoming general passage, all these things shall remain whole and undisturbed under the defense of the Apostolic See, until it is most certainly known about their return or death. We command by apostolic writing to your discretion that you do not allow them to be troubled by anyone against the tenor of our protection and constitution, compelling their undue molesters by ecclesiastical censure, with appeal postponed. Given at the Lateran, on the Ides of November. In the same manner, it is written to the bishops of Zurich and Ratzeburg. Given at the Lateran, on the 16th day before the Kalends of December. In the same manner, it is written to the Archbishop, the Greater Provost, and the Dean of the Holy Apostles of Cologne for the cross-bearing clerics of the city of Cologne. Given at the Lateran, on the Ides of November.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo, maiori preposito, et decano Sanctorum Apostolorum Coloniensium mandat ut crucesignatos civitatis Coloniensis, sub protectione apostolica receptos, ab omnibus molestiis tueantur, et molestatores per censuram ecclesiasticam compescant. Datum Laterani, Idibus Novembris, anno pontificatus XI.

**Translation to English:**

Gregory, etc., to the same concerning the office of preaching entrusted to him. We commend your diligence in the Lord, which you carefully apply to tracking down the followers of heretical depravity in the parts of Germany, since this kind of pestilence, the more it secretly spreads, the more gravely it demolishes the Lord's vineyard among the simple. Because you will be able to proceed more effectively to abolish heresy from those parts, if some are called by you to share in this diligence, we strictly command you by apostolic writings, that you, having taken to the same diligence those whom you know to be expedient, diligently and vigilantly inquire about those infected with heretical depravity in the aforementioned parts, so that by those to whom it pertains, the weeds may be rooted out from the Lord’s field. Given at Anagni, on the 12th of June, in the first year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa eidem mandat ut, ad heresim in partibus Theutoniae abolendam, assumptis quos noverit expedire, diligenter inquirat. 1227, Iun. 12, Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

Gregory, etc., to Frederick, illustrious Emperor of the Romans, ever august, and King of Sicily. Let your serenity know that the leaders of the Lombard Society have humbly accepted the terms of the concord, which was established between you and the same society through the apostolic see, and concerning this, they have sent us and your excellency letters in accordance with the form sent to them by the apostolic see, written by a public notary and fortified by the appending of various seals, the tenor of which we send to your highness enclosed under our seal. We will send the letters themselves, which are addressed to your highness by them, to you through a suitable messenger, as we have not deemed it fit to entrust them to the bearer of these presents. We therefore ask, exhort, and beseech in the Lord your imperial magnificence, that, as you are bound and as befits your excellency, you magnificently and powerfully gird yourself to liberate the land in which the Lord Jesus Christ willed to accomplish the salvation of the human race, from the hands of the impious, with His assistance going before, knowing that we have signified this by our letters to the cross-bearers stationed throughout Germany, and have diligently enjoined them to prepare themselves to pass over with you in the imminent expedition, and have commanded the prelates to zealously exhort their subjects to strive to aid that same Holy Land. Given at the Lateran, 17th March, in the first year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Frederico, illustri Romanorum imperatori et regi Siciliae, significat rectores societatis Lombardie formam concordiae per sedem apostolicam ordinatam acceptasse, et hortatur ut se accingat ad terram Sanctam liberandam. 1228, Mart. 17. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz. Since we previously instructed you through our letters to collect all the revenues and incomes of the Church of Worms and send them to France, to Troyes, so that our beloved son Matthew Widonis Marroni and his Roman fellow citizens might be satisfied for the money the Church of Worms owes them, and because, as we have understood, its revenues are so meager that the said church could scarcely be freed from its debts over a long time, we command your fraternity through apostolic writings to take care to bind these revenues and to more earnestly exhort and induce the prelates of the churches, canons, and other clerics of the city and diocese of Worms, as well as the citizens and vassals of the church, to help in this matter. If necessary, you are to compel the Jews, both of the city and the diocese of Worms, by cutting off their communion with the faithful, without any chance of appeal, in order to collect up to the next feast of the Resurrection of the Lord one thousand six hundred and twenty marks, including the four hundred and thirty marks already collected, and deposit them in a safe place. You are to promptly inform us once the money is collected, so that the said Romans may be quickly satisfied of the money owed to them and the church itself may be more easily freed. Given at Rieti, on the eighth of the Ides of July, in the ninth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino mandat ut proventus Warmaciensis ecclesiae colligat et mittat, ad satisfaciendum Matheo Widonis Marroni et sociis civibus Romanis de pecunia debita; mandat etiam clericos et Iudaeos compellere ad collectionem marcorum per censuram ecclesiasticam. 1235, Iul. 8, Reate.

**Translation to English:**

Gregory, bishop, etc., to the Archbishop of Salzburg. Our beloved son, the noble man, the Duke of Austria, has shown us by a petition he has sent that, while he was in the region of Lombardy—where he had been called by our dearest son in Christ, Frederick, the illustrious ever August Roman Emperor and King of Sicily, to discuss aid for the Holy Land—the Bohemians, hostilely invading his land, presumed to plunder and burn it. Therefore, Henry of Cuning, the duke's minister, whom he had left to guard his land, resisted the enemies with all his might, accompanied by the aid of soldiers obeying him, forcefully entered their lands, and there carried out burnings and plunders. Hence, the said duke humbly petitioned us, that although the said minister and his associates, unjustly provoked, seem to have done nothing wrong by legitimately defending themselves, because it is the way of good minds to acknowledge fault where there was none, we should absolve the aforementioned minister and his followers from the bonds of excommunication, if they had perhaps incurred it, especially since the same minister is prepared to send, at his own expense, four knights who otherwise would not have gone, for aid to the Holy Land. Wishing therefore to grant the requests of the petitioner while maintaining the rigor of ecclesiastical discipline, we command your fraternity by apostolic writing, that once he has fulfilled the aforementioned conditions, you bestow the benefit of absolution on them according to the form of the Church, imposing on them penance appropriate to the quality and quantity of their faults.

Given at the Lateran, the third day before the Nones of April, in the first year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Salzburgensi mandat, ut Henricum de Cunring et socios eius, a duce Austriae propter defensionem contra Boemos invasores commendatos et forte excommunicationis laqueum incurrentes, absolvat, si quattuor milites in subsidium Terrae Sanctae mittat. 1227, Apr. 3, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz. It was presented to us on your behalf that, when, as you had received in mandate from us, you proceeded to the church of Worms, you diligently admonished the prelates of the churches, the canons and other clerics of the city and diocese of Worms, as well as the citizens, vassals, and Jews of the church, to aid that same church by collecting one thousand six hundred and twenty marks by the feast of the Resurrection of the Lord just passed, with four hundred and thirty marks already collected, for the payment of debts which greatly burden it. They, however, contemptuously refused to do this and resorted to a frivolous appeal, which you deemed baseless and empty, and you pronounced a sentence of excommunication upon them. But the said prelates and clerics, stubbornly disregarding the sentence, presume to celebrate divine services while excommunicated, to the peril of their souls and the scandal of many. Therefore, lest they may boast of their obstinacy, we command your fraternity by apostolic writs to ensure that the said sentence of excommunication, as it was reasonably pronounced, is inviolably observed until due satisfaction is made, removing the obstacle of appeal with our authority. And if any might wish to make satisfaction, you shall grant them the benefit of absolution according to the form of the church, and with the clerics who have thus celebrated returning humbly to your command, you may mercifully dispense. Those, however, who persist in their obstinacy, you shall chastise with canonical discipline. Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Nones of June, in the eleventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino mandat ut excommunicationis sententiam contra prelatos et clericos Warmacienses, dictam ob contemptum colligendorum debitorum ecclesiae, inviolabiliter observet et contumaces canonica disciplina castiget. Dat. Laterani, II Nonas Iunii, anno XI.

**Translation to English:**

To the Abbot of Prémontré. Those things which are providently ordained for the utility and peace of the churches must be fortified by apostolic authority, so that they are observed with greater diligence. Indeed, it was proposed on your behalf before us that a dispute arose between you, on one side, and the provosts of St. Mary of Magdeburg, Gratia Dei, Liezeka, Brandenburg, Havelberg, Rasceburg, Ihericho, Colebethe, Rothe, Quedlinburg, Widda, Polethe, Gramonorwe, and Temenis on the other side. The dispute was regarding your assertion that the aforementioned provosts were obliged to convene annually at Prémontré for the general chapter and to obey the common statutes of the order, and several letters on this matter had been issued from the Apostolic See. Eventually, with the mediation of the cantor of Metz and his colleagues, delegated by us, you, brother abbot, and the opposing party willingly and amicably reached a certain form of agreement before our venerable brother Conrad, Bishop of Porto, legate of the Apostolic See, which you requested to be confirmed by apostolic authority. Therefore, granting our kind assent to your petitions, we confirm the agreement itself, as it was prudently made without deceit, willingly accepted by the parties, peacefully observed hitherto, and fully contained in the letters made by the bishop and the aforementioned judges, by apostolic authority and fortify it with the protection of this document. Let no one violate our confirmation, etc. If anyone, however, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the 13th day before the Kalends of May, in the ninth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Honorius III papa abbati Premonstratensi mandat, concordiam inter eum et diversos prepositos factam, qua isti annualiter Premonstratum convenire debent, auctoritate apostolica confirmat. 1225, April. 19. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the Patriarch of Aquileia. Because many, blinded by their own malice, fail to discern between the sacred and the profane in this world poisoned by evil, and thus irreverently extend wicked hands to seize ecclesiastical goods more boldly, finding few who will wield swords on behalf of the church against them, it is our duty to oppose the power of the just against the malice of the wicked, lest we seem to abandon the rod of sinners over the lot of the just, for we are bound to correct the restless and console the fainthearted. Indeed, our beloved sons, the dean and chapter of the Church of Civitate in your diocese, have humbly besought us that, since the same church is exposed as if among lion cubs, who are not content to squander its goods prodigiously unless they seize them like robbers, it is so torn apart by injuries and plundering that, diminished in many ways, it fears incurring irreparable harm unless it is suitably aided. They asked us to commit the provostship of the same church, now vacant—concerning which, as was proposed before us on behalf of the said dean and chapter, it consists only of temporal matters—to you, hoping, as they assert, that the same church would be usefully governed by your power and diligence. We have decided to commit the said provostship to your defense and governance, acceding to their prayers, earnestly advising your fraternity and by these apostolic writings commanding you to prudently observe our and their intention, as is fitting, and to strive to govern the same provostship in such a way that you may deserve the divine and our grace more abundantly and that we may rightly commend your diligence. Given at the Lateran, on the 7th Ides of December, in the ninth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa patriarche Aquileiensi preposituram ecclesiae Civitatensis, in temporalibus vacantem, ad gubernationem et defensionem committit. 1235, Dec. 7, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the archbishops of Nicosia and Caesarea, and the abbot of Mount Olivet. The Count of Tripoli, who, for his various and diverse excesses, should have lifted his gaze to that highness, at which Peter is recorded to have burst into bitter tears, is instead sunk into the deep sleep of oblivion and entirely swallowed by the abyss of despair, receiving no discipline, feeling no pain even when struck. Among other publicized excesses, he violently took Antioch and the castle of Antioch, which the venerable brother of ours, the bishop of Albano, then legate of the Apostolic See, had entrusted to the brothers of the Hospital of Jerusalem for safekeeping, and a house they had in Tripoli, incited by diabolical rage, he had one of them flayed and another, it is said, killed, aside from cruelly and dishonorably treating some of them, inflicting heavy damages and injuries upon them. Hence, this bishop, for these and many other evident reasons, pronounced the sentence of excommunication against him and those who favor, accompany, and participate with him which was subsequently approved by apostolic authority. But he, like a sinner who scorns, having fallen deeply into the mire of vices, utterly disregards this sentence, and, detaining what he has taken without offering any satisfaction for the damages and injuries, does not seem even to consider returning to the command of the Church. Therefore, so that he may be aroused by us to reconsider his salvation, who for seven years has ignored the aforementioned sentence, we instruct your discretion, etc. Given at Rieti, 3rd of the Kalends of February, in the 10th year.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa Nicosiensi et Cesariensi archiepiscopis et abbati Montis Oliveti mandat ut comitem Tripolitanum, qui Antiochiam et castrum Hospitalariorum violenter occupavit atque contra sententiam excommunicationis per septennium contempsit, ad mandatum ecclesiae redeundum excitent. Datum Reate, III Kalendas Februarii, anno X.

**Translation to English:**

To the Podestà and commune of Rimini. We have received a serious complaint from our beloved son, I. de Macreta, a citizen of Modena, that Ariminus de Bonfiletto, Bucca de Ferro, and certain other citizens of Rimini laid an ambush for him when he was managing the governance of your city. They made a reckless assault on him with the intention of killing him, inflicting serious injuries, because he had captured and handed over to the emperor certain of their daughters, sisters, and female relatives who were manifest heretics, to be burned, and was trying to include the imperial law recently enacted against heretics in the statutes of the same city. Therefore, not wishing to ignore the injury suffered by the same I. for the zeal of the orthodox faith, we have decided to admonish and exhort your entire community, commanding through our apostolic writings that you make satisfaction to I. and ensure that satisfaction is made by the aforementioned offenders. You should do this in such a way that he rightfully ceases his complaint and others are deterred from attempting similar actions. Otherwise, we instruct our venerable brother, the bishop, and our beloved sons, the provost and the primicerius of Arezzo, by our letters to compel both you and the aforementioned offenders to provide appropriate satisfaction to him and to reimburse the expenses he has incurred, through ecclesiastical censure, without appeal. Given at the Lateran, on the third day before the Kalends of March, in the eleventh year of our pontificate. It is written that the constitution on the two diets issued in the general council notwithstanding. If not all—, you brother bishop—. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa potestati et communi Ariminensi mandat ut I. de Macreta civis Mutinensis, ob iniurias propter zelum fidei orthodoxe a civibus Ariminensibus passo, satisfaciat, alioquin per episcopum et prepositum Aretinenses ad satisfactionem compellantur. 1237, Feb. 27, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Sabina, legate of the Apostolic See. We have carefully understood how that person desires an army to be led against another neighboring land, so that through fear they might be able to induce their people to comply with their will. However, since an enemy is more often feared when he is at the front rather than at the back, and nearer rather than farther, for which reason they should be more justly terrified if the battle line is directed against their own land, we firmly command you by apostolic writ to proceed directly, boldly, and steadfastly against that person if they so desire, as your prudence may find expedient according to the nature of the business. Given at Perugia.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Sabinensi episcopo, apostolicae sedis legato, mandat ut, si persona ilia voluerit, contra ipsam directe procedat secundum negotii qualitatem. Data Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To the provost of the main church and the deans of the same church and of St. Stephen in Mainz. Because it was unworthy for our beloved son G., formerly elected of Osnabrück, to be deprived of ecclesiastical provision, who had been removed from the administration of the Osnabrück church and did not have any benefits for his sustenance, since he had long awaited in great humility at our apostolic see imploring grace, we, with the advice of our brothers, deemed it necessary to provide through certain prelates of churches and their successors as well as chapters, giving them our letters with mandates so that our venerable brother, the bishop of Osnabrück, would provide him with one hundred marks of pure silver, the bishop of Utrecht with twenty-five, the bishop of Münster with twenty, and the abbots of Herzfeld, Wildeshausen, and Corvey with thirty, with each of them providing ten annually, half at the feast of St. Walburga and the remaining at the feast of St. Martin each year to be given to him or his procurator, as long as he lives, according to the contents of our letters. The chapters of the main and the St. John's churches in Osnabrück, Münster, and Verden shall receive him as a canon and brother, assigning him prebends if they are presently vacant or when they first become vacant in those churches, and each year, until they become vacant, they shall provide him, whether present or absent, with as much as a resident would receive from his prebend, and shall deliver it at the aforementioned dates. Therefore, we command by apostolic writings to your discretion that you compel the aforementioned bishops and abbots and their successors as well as the aforementioned chapters to this, if necessary, by ecclesiastical censure, removing any obstacle of contradiction and appeal, notwithstanding the constitution made at the general council concerning two diets. If not all, etc. Given at the Lateran, 11th January, in the eleventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa preposito maioris ecclesie et decanis Maguntinis mandata dirigit ut G. quondam Osemburgensis electus beneficiis ecclesiasticis provideatur a prelatis et capitulis diversarum ecclesiarum, sub censura ecclesiastica, 1237, Ian. 11, Laterani.

**English Translation:**

To the noble man Henry, Count of Zuerich. We once believed that you would recognize the great and serious stain you have rashly placed upon your reputation by capturing our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of Denmark, your lord, by breaking the bond of loyalty. We hoped that, moved by apostolic rebukes, you would follow our exhortations and release the king freely, thereby erasing this stain through the remedy of swift satisfaction. However, disregarding your reputation and completely ignoring our pleas and commands, you extorted from the king, through violence, an oath to give you his sons as hostages and to pay you a certain amount of money, severely burdening him in this and other matters to the grave prejudice of the aid for the Holy Land, for which he had solemnly pledged himself before his capture, as well as to the serious injury and contempt of the Apostolic See, to which his kingdom is known to be subject by tribute as a mark of special authority, and to which his special devotion binds him. Therefore, since we neither wish nor ought to overlook such a loss to the Holy Land's aid and such contempt for us and the Roman Church, we admonish your nobility, we beseech and, under the invocation of divine judgment, strictly command you by apostolic writings to return the hostages and money you received from the said king without difficulty and not demand from him the remaining balance of the money. Fulfill this apostolic exhortation and command in such a manner this time that you demonstrate by your actions that you possess the fear of God, and that the Apostolic See may regard it as pleasing and acceptable. Otherwise, besides the divine vengeance which we predict will come upon you for such wickedness, we shall proceed against you spiritually and temporally according to the severity of your malice, so that, by the Lord’s authority, the punishment will serve as an example to those to whom your guilt was a scandal. Given at the Lateran, on the 9th of June, in the tenth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro Henrico comiti de Zuericb mandat ut obsides et pecuniam, a rege Dacie extortos, sine difficultate restituat et residuum pecunie non requirat, alioquin contra eum procedet spiritualiter et temporaliter. 1236, Iun. 9, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To E., Abbot of Middelburg of the Premonstratensian Order.

You have informed us that, although we have instructed you to collect money pledged by the faithful or otherwise allocated for the aid of the Holy Land in the territories where you preach the word of the cross, compelling the holders to restore it under canonical constraint, our venerable brother, the Bishop of Cambrai, and the noble Duke of Brabant, by virtue of certain letters granted to them by the Apostolic See in the recent passage, claim the money belongs to them and have almost entirely received it within their territories and are not ceasing to demand the rest. Moreover, the Templars, Hospitallers, and some others have received some of this money; therefore, you have requested instruction on what you should do about this.

Therefore, by the authority of these presents, we instruct you to compel the aforementioned bishop and others, by the same authority, to either fully assign the money to you to be converted for the aid of the Holy Land or, within a suitable time limit which you shall set for them, to send us apostolic letters claiming the money for themselves. Meanwhile, ensure they diligently preserve the money, and inform us of the amount of said money, removing any appeal, so that after examining these letters, we may do what is right in this matter.

Given at Tivoli, on the 12th of May, in the ninth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa E. abbati de Middelborc Premonstratensis ordinis mandat ut episcopum Cameracensem et alios compellat ad pecuniam ad subsidium Terrae Sanctae convertendam sibi assignandam vel litteras apostolicas mittendas, quibus pecuniam vendicare contendunt, infra terminum praefigendum. 1235, Maii 12, Tibure.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Passau and his fellow judges. The beloved sons, the dean, Eweradus and Hermann the archdeacons, the vicedominus, and other canons of Regensburg, who have come into our presence regarding the matter of the election or, more accurately, the intrusion of the provost of Regensburg into their church, have humbly petitioned us. They requested that, since the provost, daringly assuming himself elected, has unlawfully assigned certain benefices to himself which he could not lawfully claim, and has converted some into his own use, and moreover, some of their goods have been illicitly occupied by certain canons of Regensburg and some other clerics and laymen, we would, with paternal care, provide for these matters. Therefore, we strictly command you by apostolic writings that, whatever you find was rashly attempted to their prejudice pending this cause, you restore to its rightful state; and if there be any contradictors or rebels, subdue them by ecclesiastical censure, dismissing any appeal. If not all of you can convene, then let two of you proceed accordingly. Given at Anagni, the 13th day before the Kalends of July, in the first year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Pataviensi et coniudicibus mandat, ut temeraria intrusione prepositi Ratisponensis pendente causa revocata, res in statum debitum reducant, contradictores per censuram ecclesiasticam compescendo. 1227, Iun. 19, Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbess and convent of Jouarre. In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. I, Faro, to all those both in the future and present. Indeed, I, bishop of the church of Meaux, send greetings and love, which is in Christ Jesus. It is the duty of prelates to extend the authority of the holy rule, indeed the dignity of the holy church, by the privilege of rank, for the increase of the holy and catholic faith with such salutary observance entirely prolonged, etc. etc. For recently, King Dagobert of the Franks, specifically the son of our most glorious lord King Chlothar, and Childegarius, bishop of the city of Sens, Audebertus, bishop of the city of Paris, Madegigilus, bishop of the city of Tours, and many others, both friends and our prelates, came to our presence, requesting under the protection of the holy faith, that we recognize the church of Jouarre, which Ado, son of Autarius of Soissons, had built on his own land, yet by the work of his brother Audoenus, referendary of the aforesaid King Dagobert, in honor of the blessed mother of God Mary, etc. etc. This was done and confirmed in the monastery of the Holy Cross in Meaux, in the year of the Incarnation 618, in the third year of Pope Martin, in the eighth year of King Dagobert of the Franks, in the eighteenth year of Constantine, son of Constantine, seventh indiction. This was given on the day before the Nones of May. Signed by King Dagobert of the Franks. Signed by Childegarius, bishop of Sens. Signed by Audebertus, bishop of Paris. Signed by Regniesilus, bishop of Troyes. Signed by Aigutarius, bishop of Noyon. Signed by Faro, bishop of Meaux. Signed by Chagnelmus, count, etc. etc. etc. Bertoldus the chancellor wrote and subscribed.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Faro, episcopus Meldensis, abbatisse et conventui Iotrensi notificat ecclesiam Iotri sub protectione fidei sancte a rege Dagoberto et aliis episcopis recognitam fuisse, quam Ado filius Autarii opere fratris sui Audoeni in honorem beate Mariae genitricis Dei edificaverat. To Frederick, illustrious Emperor of the Romans, ever august, and King of Sicily. To Emperor Frederick. Since we, with fatherly compassion, sympathize with all those suffering injustice and diligently pursue the grievances of individuals as our office requires, we must address more carefully the troubles and losses inflicted upon travelers, especially those coming to and returning from the Apostolic See, and ensure the public roads are secured properly. This is because such action is known to benefit the entire Christian populace greatly, as was done by our predecessors and more diligently pursued by us. We solemnly bind all violators of the roads and their accomplices with the chains of excommunication thrice a year: on Maundy Thursday, the feast of the Ascension, and on the consecration of the Basilica of St. Peter, in the presence of all people gathered from various parts of the world. But Tancred of Campelio, like a son of Belial, disregarding what is proper, recently allied with many of Bertold's knights, captured numerous individuals, both from our household and others, coming to and returning from the Apostolic See. He led them through remote paths, forced them to go to Campelio, and subjected them to severe injuries before sending them to Bertold in the middle of the night. Bertold, with damnable presumption, had all their letters obtained from us examined and made a general announcement before the assembled officials, without grave injury and contempt for the Apostolic See. It is hard to believe this could have occurred without your connivance, especially as Bertold, who dared to attempt these nefarious acts, is said to be your special envoy and publicly declared that Tancred had received from you a special license to violate the road against certain persons. In this, your imperial dignity is greatly diminished, for you are obliged to correct the unruly, not to support them, and to pursue malefactors and oppressors of the innocent. Neither are you ignorant of this, nor can we ignore the grievous injury inflicted upon the Church. Since nothing affects the Church's status more than depriving travelers and pilgrims of security and attempting to violate its authority in letters, we have deemed it necessary to urge and admonish your serenity to correct such an enormous excess with swift amendment. Thus, the rightful ability of pilgrims seeking the benefit of prayers and the oppressed seeking justice should not be denied by anyone's rash audacity. Otherwise, since we cannot leave these acts uncorrected, we shall consider how to proceed in correcting such grave excesses. Given at the Lateran, 12th Kalends of August, in the 19th year.

To the illustrious Louis, King of the French. We call upon as witness Him before whom all things are laid bare, that we love your person with sincere affection and aspire fervently for your and your kingdom's honor and status, retaining in memory and having almost always before our eyes that special bond of love which united us and your father, the late Philip, King of France, with mutual affection, and the sincere devotion which the Apostolic See has always found unceasingly in him and in your other ancestors, Kings of France. We hold firm hope and confidence that you will not depart from the footsteps of your ancestors but, by their laudable example, will always remain firm and steadfast in devotion to the Apostolic See.

Nevertheless, in these times, you have acted quite contrary to our hope, for although we have repeatedly asked and requested you in our letters as a special favor to extend the truce between you and the illustrious King of England, you, ignoring our prayers and requests, have violently occupied some lands of that king, despite our appeals and also disregarding the decree made concerning peace or at least truce to be observed among all Christians, especially among the most excellent princes. As we have reminded you, we made this decree at the conference recently held between us and our dearly beloved son in Christ, Frederick, the ever august Roman Emperor and King of Sicily, and consequently, you have neglected the care of the business of the Holy Land, for which the aforementioned decree was made.

You have done these things, and we have remained silent, deferring to your highness and hoping that our patience might inflame your devotion towards us and provoke you to comply with our will and prayers. Although you have not yet cared to comply with our hope and expectation in this matter, nevertheless, we do not cease to hope for your devotion, but promise ourselves firm confidence in it, since both your innate clemency and the memorable memory of your ancestors assures us of it.

We further appeal to your highness with multiplied prayers, asking and exhorting you in the Lord Jesus Christ, as much as we can, that you restore to the said king his lands, which you are known to have violently invaded, and that you agree to appropriate truces with him, lest, if you resolve to do otherwise, the aid to the Holy Land, which by your ancestors and by the power of your kingdom was especially accustomed to be advanced, now seems to be hindered by you, and this may harm your reputation and salvation, and we, which God forbid, may be compelled to despair of your devotion, of which, although we have already so often experienced the contrary, we cannot but hope. Given at the Lateran, in the month of February, in the ninth year.

We have carefully listened to what your letters contained and what your beloved son, Master Roffredus, your envoy, proposed to us verbally concerning the arrangement of certain churches in Apulia and the matter of our venerable brother, the Bishop of Catania, as well as the absolution of the Count of Tripoli. We have entrusted our response to the first two matters to the mouth of the said Master, who can fully report it to your highness. Regarding the absolution of the aforementioned count, let your excellence know that the envoys of the count requested things clearly contrary to law and the customs of the Roman Church. Although we are always willing to heed your requests as far as we are able according to God, we could not accept the envoys' petition. Your prudence should not take offense at this, as we believe you do not wish us to disrupt the order of written law and established custom. Although the count has rendered himself undeserving even by the mere administration of justice due to many reasons which are not convenient to recount now, we have decided, in view of your intercession, to entrust the entire matter to good men under this condition: namely, that the count should swear in their hands to abide by the mandates of the Church concerning the matters for which he was excommunicated, make amends for manifest offenses, and provide suitable assurance to abide by the law concerning doubtful matters. Upon fulfilling these conditions, he would be granted absolution, and consequently, the doubtful matters would be examined and decided according to the order of law. We have kindly offered all these things to the mentioned envoys through our venerable brother Hugh, Bishop of Ostia, and our beloved son, Guala, Cardinal Priest of the title of St. Martin, and Gregory, Cardinal Deacon of St. Theodore, through whom we made sure to hear the envoys carefully, since it is not customary for the Roman Pontiff to admit excommunicated persons to an audience except through an intermediary. However, the envoys refused to accept what was offered, claiming they had no mandate for it. As we mentioned before, we could not grant what they asked, as, where justice is concerned, there is no room for favor at another's expense. Nevertheless, we are ready to assign the matter according to the prescribed form whenever requested, always prepared to heed your highness's requests in this and other matters as reason permits. Given at Rieti, 24th January, in the tenth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Fridericum Romanorum imperatorem certiorem facit de impossibilitate absolvendi comitem Tripolitanum ob petitiones contra ius et consuetudinem ecclesiasticam, proponens conditiones sub quibus absolutionem obtinere posset. 1237, Ian. 24. Apud Reate.

Translation to English:

To all the princes of Germany. It is more fitting to weep than to report that Emperor Frederick has abandoned the overseas matter, for which the Church and the Christian people have long labored and toiled. Therefore, not deferring to the man who has brought this disgrace upon the cause of Christ, we have proceeded against him, as is more fully contained in the letters we have sent to the prelates of the churches. However, although we have been so deceived by him in whom the Church had placed its hopeful trust regarding this matter, because the hand of Him, whose cause this is, and who grants glory to His name when it pleases Him, is not shortened, and since it is better to hope in the Lord than in princes, we have firm confidence in Him that He will show us the way to proceed successfully in this matter. Since the perfidious pagans, seeing the faithful thus disheartened, are likely to assume greater audacity, it is necessary for us to rouse mighty and Catholic men to meet such danger and relieve our disgrace. Therefore, since the Lord has granted you life and all that you possess, which you ought to render to Him in return, we earnestly urge and beseech all of you to prepare your minds to vindicate the land occupied by blasphemers of the cross, consecrated by the blood of our Redeemer, and to be all the more courageous as the necessity is seen to be greater, so that your devotion in this matter may be evident in action, and you may more fully obtain divine grace and the favor of both us and the Roman Church. Given at Anagni, October 8th, in the first year of our pontificate.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa universis principibus Alamannie significat Fridericum imperatorem negotium transmarinum deseruisse, hortaturque eos ut contra blasphemos crucis animum preparent et terre Redemptoris occupate vindicandam operam impendant. 1227, Oct. 8. Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the illustrious King of Denmark. Your petition presented to us stated that Henry, Count of Zwerin, your vassal, captured you and held you imprisoned, and extorted from you an oath to pay him a considerable sum of money and, in the meantime, give your sons as hostages. Therefore, you humbly entreated us that, since the fulfillment of your solemn promise made long before your capture, to magnificently aid the crusade for the Holy Land, would be entirely hindered by this, and since the amount of money exceeds your means, you should not be compelled to pay it, as no one should be driven to impossibility, and since the oath was extorted from you through fear and manifest force, and thus you are not bound to observe it, as things done through fear or force should not stand, and since by capturing you the said count broke the bond of fidelity, for which you are not bound to keep faith with him, since faith should not be kept with one who does not keep faith, we should deign to absolve you from the said oath for caution. We therefore, for the aforesaid reasons, and because we are admonished by the prophetic voice to dissolve the bonds of wickedness and untie the oppressive bundles, to let the oppressed go free, and to break every yoke, absolve you from the oath extorted in such a manner and everything that is known to have followed from it, as an oath should not be a bond of iniquity but a support of justice. In testimony of this absolution, we have deemed it fit to grant these letters to your devotion. Given at the Lateran, the sixth day before the Kalends of July, in the tenth year of Our Pontificate. In the same manner, a letter was written to the Bishop of Verdun and the Abbot of Luna of the diocese of Verdun to similarly absolve the aforementioned vassals of the King from the aforementioned oath for caution. We therefore command that you prudently and effectively advise the said count to release the King’s vassals from this oath, compelling him to do so by ecclesiastical censure, postponing any appeal if he does not heed the warnings. Given at the Lateran, the seventh day before the Kalends of July, in the tenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa regi Daciae significat se eum ab iuramento extorto, quo Henricus comes de Zwerin captum coegit pecuniam dare et filios obsides tradere, absolvisse, necnon mandat comitem moneant ut iuramenta dictorum vasallorum remittat, et si non acquieverit, per censuram ecclesiasticam cogatur. 1237, Jun. 26-25. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To Frederick, illustrious ever-august emperor of the Romans and king of Sicily. Among the countless and immense concerns, which we can bear more than we can express, as we, while presiding over the universal Church, both govern and are governed, we are burdened no less by the weight of servitude than we are exalted by the honor of dignity, our spirit is especially troubled by the fact that the matter of the Holy Land, contrary to our hope and almost the entire confidence of the Christian people, has thus far been suspended from the desired outcome anticipated by all, which was expected for a long time to be promoted by you after God as effectively as swiftly, since you publicly committed yourself to this by a solemn vow and notable profession, as your serenity can fully recall, which, to spare your honor, it is not fitting for us to recount. However, although you seem to have disappointed us and the universal Church, besides the offense to the divine majesty, we, wishing to care for your salvation and spare your reputation, have decided to grant your supplications, despite many murmuring and clamoring against us and our brothers: "Behold the men who want to cover others' infamy with their own disgrace!" Therefore, so that what is contained in the letter presented to us might be effectively completed, if it is given from above, as you voluntarily offered and it was accepted by us and our brothers, behold, we have provided to send to your presence our venerable brother P. bishop of Albano and our beloved son G. cardinal priest of the title of St. Martin, men of proven virtue, conspicuous honesty, and eminent knowledge, whom we and our brothers embrace with a special prerogative of love and grace, as pillars erected in the house of the Lord and stars shining in the firmament of the Church, having fully entrusted them with the office of legation, so that what has been diligently deliberated on the aforementioned matters might receive the strength of full perfection and be made clear by solemn publication. Wherefore, we earnestly ask, beseech, and urge your imperial majesty, that you may receive them, or rather us in them, kindly and treat them honorably, and strive to execute purely and sincerely what is contained in the aforesaid letter, which we have entrusted to them under our seal, so that, proceeding in truth with Him who is the truth, you may appear to redeem the preceding negligence, and render yourself and us excused before men, knowing that we have given them full power both to receive the oath and to pronounce the sentence of excommunication and to proceed further therefrom, as in. Given at Rieti, 15th Kalends of August, in the ninth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorii IX papa Fridericum, Romanorum imperatorem, hortatur ut negotium Terre Sancte promoveat et plenam potestatem legatis suis concedit ad iuramentum recipiendum et sententiam excommunicationis promulgendam. 1235, Iulii 18. Reate.

Translation to English:

In the year of Our Lord 1226, in the 14th indiction, on the tenth day from the end of November, in the city of Bologna, in the palace of the bishopric, Lord Bocatius Bremma, Lord Robert of Concolezo, Lord Ubertus of Marnate, Lord Ardicio of Ponte Caralo, Lord Guillielmus of Oliana, Lord Guillielmus of the Gate, Lord Ubertus Viscount, Lord Aicardus of Formivica, Lord Auliverius Henrici Gerardis, Lord Oldradus Pocalodus, Lord Guillielmus of Solarolo, Lord Guillielmus Lazaronus, Lord Deutesalvi of Cremona, Lord Guidrixius the judge of Scaperlis, Lord Johannes of Cremona, Lord Rustigellus the judge, Lord Spinabellus the judge, Lord Ubertus of Maltraversii, Lord Fredericus of Pascipovre, Lord Scanabicus of Arimondo, Lord Mariscotus Johannes of Mariscotus, Lord Henrigetus Hugonis Regaite, all rectors of the society of Lombardy, the March and Romagna, in the name of that society and for that society appointed procurators: Lord Bocatius Bremma, Lord Mudalberg the judge, Lord Guido Mainerio, Lord Guillielmus of the Gate, Lord Ubertus Viscount, Lord Guido Boncambii the doctor of laws, Lord Albert of Muso, Lord Guido of Cole of Saint Martin, Lord Bartholomew of Vidoro, Lord Guido of Marzan.a, Lord Senzanomeb of Achillicis, Lord Obizzo of Hugonibus, Lord Rizard of Rodengo, Lord Guillielmus of Campidello, Lord Castellanus of Caffaris, Lord Peter Bicherius, Lord Huguicion of Bondonis, for making peace and concord, and everything necessary or useful for this peace and concord or for this peace and concord, concerning the discord or about the discord which they have with Lord Frederick, ever August Emperor of the Romans and King of Sicily, or which Lord Frederick the Roman Emperor has with them; and they promised to consider as ratified and firm whatever the said procurators or the majority of them will do regarding the aforesaid matters and for the aforesaid matters. Regesto:

Innocentius IV papa notificat rectoribus societatis Lombardie, Marchie et Romaniole procuratores constitutos ad pacem et concordiam cum imperatore Friderico II componendam, anno Domini 1226, Bononia.

**Translation to English:**

To Frederick, the illustrious emperor of the Romans, ever august, and king of Sicily. The concern of your highness has not unreasonably requested that the cities, castles, and other places pertaining to the empire in the regions of Provence and the kingdom of Arles, and specifically those which the late Raymond, count of Toulouse, held from the empire, and which have come or may yet come into your hands or those of our beloved son, R., cardinal deacon of St. Angelus and legate of the apostolic see, or into the hands of anyone else on account of the army assembled to eradicate the heretical depravity in those parts, be restored to you. Therefore, let your serenity know that we, who do not wish the rights of you and the empire to be diminished but rather increased, have told the aforesaid cardinal in person, while he was present before us, and subsequently have instructed him by apostolic letters, that we wish that land to be purged of heretical depravity while keeping the rights of the empire intact. Although your request does not diverge from our purpose, we provide that such restitution be deferred until we are made more fully aware through the report of the legate himself of what lands in those parts pertain to the empire and the circumstances of the whole matter. We have currently instructed the cardinal through our writings to retain in his and the church’s power the lands that pertain to the empire, ensuring they are diligently guarded by the bishops and other prelates of the churches, who will guard those lands while preserving your rights, maintaining loyalty to you and the empire, so that when we are informed of the aforesaid matters through the statement of the aforementioned legate, we may ensure your rights are restored to your envoys or appointed officials without jeopardizing peace and faith. Therefore, let the imperial circumspection patiently endure this delay, necessary for the matter of peace and faith, which, as it is now newly established in those parts, could be uprooted by a small disturbance. To prevent this from happening, your devotion ought to wish for and our diligence should strive to guard against it. We have also sent our writings to the legate and the people of Massa regarding certain castles said to be held by the faithful of the empire and to be harassing them, and receiving their men to the prejudice of the empire, as we have seen fit, and we shall ensure, either by writing again or by sending our own messenger there, if necessary, that your faithful have no just cause to complain about them. Given at the Lateran, the 22nd of November, in the eleventh year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Friderico, illustri Romanorum imperatori semper augusto et regi Sicilie, significat restitutionem civitatum, castrorum, et locorum ad imperium pertinentium in partibus Provincie ac regni Arelatensis, quae occasione exercitus contra haeresim in manus cardinalis legati devenerunt, differri, donec pleniora ex legati relatione cognoscantur; interim eadem in potestate ecclesiae retinenda mandat. 1237, Nov. 22, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

*Form of the letters that Lord Frederick the Emperor should send to the leaders of the Society of Lombardy, the Marches, and Romagna.*

Frederick, etc., to his loyal leaders of the Society of Lombardy, the Marches, and Romagna, and to the entire society, his grace and goodwill.

The cause of the discord that recently arose between us and you, because it seemed to bring an impediment to the business of the Holy Land, we have placed entirely within the providence and disposition of the Lord Pope and his brothers.

Having fully understood their provision on this matter, out of reverence for Jesus Christ and the business of the Holy Land, we remit to you all and singular, from our innate clemency, all rancor, malice, injuries, and offenses, and all bans, constitutions, sentences, and ordinances, which we have made or imposed by ourselves or through another, or by another on our behalf, against your society or any member of that society, cities, and persons thereof. We utterly revoke whatever has followed from them or because of them, and specifically the constitution made regarding the university and students of Bologna, restoring entirely and in every respect all and singular who seem to have been harmed on account of any of the aforesaid, to their status and reputation, remitting all infamy and penalty which have followed from any of the aforesaid, so that those things done by them in the meantime, notwithstanding the aforementioned, may obtain the strength they ought otherwise to have obtained.

Moreover, we receive your cities, places, and persons into the fullness of our grace, and we grant them firm peace, especially to the Marquis of Montferrat, Milan, Piacenza, Vercelli, Bologna, Faenza, Alessandria, Turin, Lodi, Bergamo, Brescia, Mantua, Verona, Padua, Vicenza, Treviso, Cremona, Ferrara, and the Counts of Biandrate, and other places and persons of the same society.

We will also cause those captured on account of the aforementioned discord, with their goods, to be restored, and other things captured or detained on account of this matter.

Furthermore, we will have letters made patent on behalf of our son, that he will hold this peace and concord firm and secure, and that he will remit to you all rancor, malice, injuries, and offenses.

For full certainty of this matter, we have ordered these present letters to be made according to the good pleasure of the said Lord Pope and to be marked with the seal of our majesty.

In the same manner, it should be written to the Lord Pope with the words suitably altered.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Fredericus imperator rectoribus societatis Lombardie, Marchie, et Romaniole significat se discordiam cum eis ortam, quae impedimento negotio Terrae Sanctae videbatur, in providentia domini papae posuisse, et universis remittere rancorem atque offensas, restitutis civitatibus et personis societatis in plena gratia et pace, captivos et bona restituendos promittit. Dat. apud locum, tempore expeditionis.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Colocensis. Blessed be God, who often deigns to bring forth good from things that seem evil, and to turn to advantage what is feared to result in loss. Therefore, as it has been wisely provided, through our diligent efforts with God, the peacemaker, cooperating, for the discord which arose between our dearest son in Christ, Frederick, the illustrious Roman emperor, always august, and king of Sicily, and the Lombards, and as the same emperor prepares magnificently, as befits imperial excellence, to cross over in the coming August, diligently preparing a multitude of ships and other things suitable for such a great undertaking, as we have gladly heard from his solemn envoys and letters, and as the clear evidence of the matter, as asserted by those who have seen it, more clearly manifests, hoping that God has arisen to judge His cause and to restore Jerusalem as in days of old, we have decided to renew the mandate which you formerly received from the Apostolic See to preach the cross, earnestly soliciting and exhorting your brotherhood, and through apostolic writings commanding you to diligently carry out the office of preaching assigned to you, inducing both great and small with careful exhortations according to the prudence given to you by God, that in the coming August, when the general passage has been proclaimed, they may provide their assistance to the said Holy Land in all ways they can. Moreover, effectively admonish those signed with the cross that, with obstacles removed, they may cross in this passage, and if necessary, compel them through ecclesiastical censure, unless obvious necessity excuses them, removing the impediment of appeal. Given at the Lateran, the 11th of January, in the eleventh year. In the same manner to the bishop of Geuriensis. In the same manner to the bishop of Hildesheim. In the same manner to the abbot of Saint Truiden. In the same manner to Master Conrad of Marburg. In the same manner to Master Giles of Brabant, a preacher of the cross. In the same manner to the abbot of Bebenhausen. In the same manner to the abbot of Morbach. In the same manner to the abbot of Aldenberg. In the same manner to Master Arnold, a preacher of the cross. In the same manner to the preachers of the cross assigned throughout the province of Cologne. In the same manner to the preachers of the cross in the province of Mainz. In the same manner to the bishop of Winchester.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Colocensi mandat ut officium predicationis crucis renovet et exerceat, crucisignatos exhortando ut sublato impedimento transeant, et si necesse fuerit, per censuram ecclesiasticam compellat. Datum Laterani, III Idus Ianuarii, anno XI.

**Translation to English:**

To the rectors and people of Gaeta. We have kindly received and carefully listened to the beloved sons John, called Cabot, and Peter Bulgamin, your citizens and messengers, men of prudence and discretion. Since we hold sincere affection for you as a father to his sons, and therefore attend willingly to your interests as if they were our own, we have endeavored to heed your requests wherever we could with integrity. However, we have decided to retain in our hands the administration and duties of the city's tolls and the borough of Molarum, along with all the rights and revenues owed to the court, intending to provide for other matters at an opportune time in a manner beneficial to you, while safeguarding the honor of the Church. We therefore admonish your community through apostolic writings, commanding that you strive to always progress from good to better in loyalty and devotion to the Apostolic See, so that you may increasingly earn its love and favor, and that we may favorably assist you in your needs. Given at Perugia, on the 19th of June, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorii IX papae rectoribus et populo Gaietano administrationem baiulationis et plateatici civitatis, cum omnibus iustitiis et redditibus, retinere et admonere ut in fidelitate sedis apostolicae proficiant. 1230, Iun. 19, Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To Frederick, Emperor of the Romans. A wail, a lamentation, and a terrible cry have reached us, grievous and dreadful, from the churches and clergy of the kingdom of Sicily and Apulia. For you, raging against them in unjust ways beyond what can easily be expressed, afflict them with countless torments, plundering and extorting their goods! This is in manifest insult to the Redeemer and grave injustice to the universal church, not to mention the contempt for the apostolic see, bringing disgrace from those who reproach. Since we cannot tolerate these actions without risk, we, who though unworthy have been appointed as Christ’s vicars, are committed to defending justice and ecclesiastical liberty, and are willing to expend ourselves for this purpose, trusting in recompense from Him who blesses those who endure tribulation for justice's sake. We earnestly warn and encourage your imperial highness to restore fully all that has been taken from the churches and ecclesiastical persons, and to cease entirely from their harassment, having regard for your honor and salvation. Otherwise, so that we do not show favor to man over God, we will proceed on this matter, God willing, as is fitting. To this end, we send our beloved sons B. and R., Friars Minor, to you, in the hope that perhaps at last you might heed our salutary admonitions, which you have thus far all too recklessly ignored. Given at Rieti, on the Nones of May, in the second year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Friderico Romanorum imperatori mandat ut ecclesiis et personis ecclesiasticis regni Sicilie et Apulie ablata restituat et ab eorum vexatione desistat, alioquin procedet. Misit fratres Minores ut eum admoneant. Datum Reate, Non. Maii, anno secundo pontificatus.

**Translation to English:**

Gregory, bishop etc., to the leaders of the Lombard League. We are astonished and cannot sufficiently express our amazement, that despite the Apostolic See, with fatherly affection intending peace and order in your province, has endeavored to mediate the discord arisen between you and our dearest son in Christ, Frederick, the illustrious Emperor of the Romans, always august and King of Sicily, and when both the Emperor and you have freely and absolutely placed the entire matter into its care, it has made provisions regarding this matter which undoubtedly promote the welfare of the province, and has given you apostolic letters instructing you to diligently uphold what has been decreed on your part, and further, to send your sealed letters, written by a public hand and bearing the seals of yourselves, the noble Margrave of Montferrat, and any cities from your society, to both the Apostolic See and the said Emperor by the first Sunday of the past Lent according to the form transmitted to you. However, you, though long awaited by the Emperor's envoy, who sent letters as instructed by him, have not cared to fulfill what was commanded, trying to excuse such negligence and contempt through certain simple envoys and pretending certain frivolous and unsuitable excuses. Therefore, our predecessor of blessed memory, Honorius, rightfully rebuked you and instructed and strictly ordered you by his letters to do what seemed necessary. Since, however, our said predecessor has meanwhile departed from this light, we have been appointed, though insufficient, to the duty of Apostolic service, lest perchance you wish to excuse yourselves by the occasion that the mandate of our same predecessor expired with his death, we have decided to renew it, strictly ordering by apostolic letters that, as you hold dear the grace of God and ours, you should send letters according to the aforementioned form, which have now for the second time been sent to you enclosed under the apostolic seal, to us and to the same Emperor, all excuses and delays ceasing, so swiftly that it cannot reach the knowledge of the same Emperor, either that you have delayed the sending of these letters for so long, or that you have been written to so many times about this from the Apostolic See; and meanwhile, nevertheless, with the diligence that the urgency of the time demands, you should prepare what you are obliged to do for the aid of the Holy Land, lest you appear to give the Emperor an excuse to delay the aid of the Holy Land, and thereby provoke God and men against you; knowing that if we perceive you as scorners and deceivers of God and us in such a great matter, we see nothing else remaining than to call upon heaven and earth against your insolence. Therefore, take care to fulfill our command in such a manner that we, who loved your province with sincere charity while we were in a lesser office, may rightly grow in love for it. Given at the Lateran, 6th Kalends of April, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa rectoribus societatis Lombardie mandat ut, neglecto mandato predecessoris Honorius III de mittendis litteris ad ipsum et imperatorem Fridericum II, illud innovetur et celeriter expleatur. Data Lateranis, VI Kalendas Aprilis, anno primo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Caesarea. He requested that the sentence of excommunication, which our venerable brother, the Patriarch of Jerusalem, at the demand of justice, pronounced against Frederick, the said emperor, be made to obtain due firmness, as the nobleman G. de Monte Acuto, a crusader, humbly asked us for this. Therefore, we firmly command you through apostolic writings that you ensure the said sentence of excommunication, as it was reasonably pronounced, is observed with our authority under the firmness of apostolic obedience until appropriate satisfaction is made. Given at Perugia, on the 10th day before the Kalends of August, in the third year of our pontificate. The same is instructed to ensure that the sentence of excommunication, as described above, is observed to the end. Our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Nicosia, humbly requests us.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Cesariensi mandat ut sententiam excommunicationis in Fridericum imperatorem, a patriarcha Ierosolimitano iuste promulgatam, observet. 1229, Iul. 23, Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Metz. Since, as we have learned, your bishopric is burdened by such a great weight of debts that, unless some remedy is provided, it is feared that extreme desolation may imminently befall it, we grant you by the authority of this letter the permission to retain the fruits of the benefices of your diocese that are vacant for a period of three years within five years, with the exception of priories, provostships, and abbeys, to be converted into the reduction of said debts, provided that in the meantime you appoint suitable vicars to serve the churches in which these benefices may become vacant. Therefore, let no one infringe upon our concession, etc. If anyone should, however, etc. Given at Perugia, on the 8th of November, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Metensi episcopo concedit, ut fructus beneficiorum suae diocesis vacantium, prioratibus, preposituris et abbatiis exceptis, per triennium retinere possit ad debita extenuanda, vicariis interim idoneis faciendis. 1230, Nov. 8, Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To the rectors of the Lombard League. Having been frequently requested with insistence by Frederick, called the emperor, to accept him as ready to return to the command of the Church, we have carefully examined a certain document submitted to us on his behalf. And because we have unwavering confidence in your loyalty and devotion, we intend to honor you as special sons, we have decided to send this document to you, so that, with your counsel understood, we may proceed in the matter according to the honor of God and the Church and the peace of its followers, as we shall see fit. Therefore, we earnestly ask and admonish your discretion, mandating through apostolic writings, that after understanding it thoroughly, you inform us of your counsel; knowing for certain that your mother, the Church, will never abandon you, but will strive to provide beneficially for your peace and tranquility in every situation as for her own. Given at Perugia. November 10, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa rectoribus societatis Lombardie mandat ut, scripto Friderici imperatoris diligenter inspecto, consilium suum sibi transmittant, promittens ecclesiam numquam eos deserturam. 1229, Nov. 10. Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To the provosts of the greater church and St. Mary's at the Steps, and the dean of St. Mary's at the Steps of Cologne. Our venerable brother, the bishop of Würzburg, had once informed us that certain bloodthirsty men from that region, along with their accomplices, had impiously killed his predecessor and relative of blessed memory, Conrad. They, along with their entire posterity, were justly punished as the severity of the crime demanded. Yet, they did not show remorse but became even more rabid in shedding innocent blood, attempting to kill the uncle of the murdered bishop and his successor. Consequently, he was forced to desert the city of Würzburg, and as their goods were passed on to others, they, along with their sons, accomplices, and friends, sought the blood of the bishop, who is a relative of the aforementioned bishops and their successor in burden and honor, to avenge the loss of their properties. Therefore, it was not safe for him to approach the city or diocese of Mainz because the said malefactors belonged to the diocese and family of our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Mainz. Thus, we, unwilling to expose such a man to the swords of the wicked, granted him the indulgence that he should not be compelled to come personally when summoned by his metropolitan, the said archbishop, to a council or other matters, but should present himself through solemn and suitable envoys, especially since the same had been granted to his predecessor by the apostolic see, as he claimed.

However, the said archbishop and the chapter of Mainz sent us letters of complaint that the bishop, on false and frivolous pretexts, was trying to withdraw from obedience to the church of Mainz. For he excuses himself, asserting that he neither held nor holds any of the bishop's bloodthirsty enemies or those complicit in the murder of his predecessor in his town or house. He also added that the bishop has often visited Mainz, Worms, Frankfurt, and other nearby places he claims to suspect, without fear, having Theodoric of Mainz, one of his predecessor’s murderers, as a special secretary and friend. Wherefore, the said archbishop humbly supplicated us that, although this might have been granted to the bishop’s two predecessors for some reason, still, we should not allow the continuation to lead to consequence, and prudently revoke the indulgence the bishop often extorted from us through false inventions, so as not to allow the church of Mainz to be diminished. Therefore, lest we seem to grant favor to one to the detriment of another, we instruct your discretion through apostolic writings to diligently inquire into the truth of these matters. If you ascertain that the bishop can safely approach the church of Mainz, revoke the aforesaid indulgence, removing any hindrance of appeal. Otherwise, permit him to use his indulgence, yet not transferring it to his successors. Witnesses —. If not all —. Given at the Lateran, on the Nones of June, in the tenth year.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa maioris ecclesie et Sancte Marie ad Gradus prepositis, nec non decano Sancte Marie ad Gradus Coloniensis mandat ut inquirant an episcopus Herbipolensis tuto ad ecclesiam Maguntinam accedere possit, et si sic, indulgentiam ei concessam, ut personaliter non veniat, sublato appellationis obstaculo revocent. 1236, Iun. 5, apud Lateranum.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Tournai, and the abbots of Vacellensis and Cambron of the Cistercian order in the diocese of Cambrai. The beloved sons, Master Baldwin of Barbenzon and John of Louvain, clerics, messengers and procurators of the noble man, the Duke of Brabant, who has taken the cross, appeared in our presence and humbly requested on behalf of the said nobleman that, since he is believed to be seventy years old and unable to fulfill the vow he made due to his infirmity and the frailty of his body, we mercifully deign to absolve the aforesaid duke from the said vow. However, we, placing special trust in the Lord in you, to whom full faith concerning these matters can be given, strictly command you by apostolic writings to personally approach the same duke or summon him to a place to which he can come without danger to his person. If you ascertain that he can personally fulfill his vow, you shall urge him to prepare himself as is proper to pursue the aforesaid vow in the upcoming March passage. If necessary, you shall compel him by ecclesiastical censure. If you find the same duke unable to undertake his pilgrimage in person, you shall compel him, by ecclesiastical censure, removing any appeal, to send forty suitable knights with the necessary and sufficient expenses in the upcoming March passage, to serve in the aid of the Holy Land during wartime for an entire year, as described. It is to be ensured that he is not absolved from the aforesaid vow in the meantime, unless he sends the knights as previously described to the aid of the aforementioned land. If not all, etc., two of you, etc. Given at Anagni, on the sixth day before the Kalends of August, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Honorius III papa episcopo Tornacensi et abbatibus Vacellensil et Camberonensi mandat, ut, inspecta impotentia ducis Brabantie votum suum personaliter exsequendi, eum moneant vel cogant ut quadraginta milites cum sumptibus in subsidium Terrae Sanctae mittat, nisi personaliter exsequi possit. Datum Anagnie, VI Kal. Augusti, anno pontificatus primi.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop, Dean, and Archdeacon of Reims,

We had hoped that the provosts, sheriffs, and other citizens of Cambrai, once admonished, would soften their hardness, but instead, they persevered contrary to the expectation. Struck, they do not grieve, and being contrite, they refuse to accept discipline. We fear, therefore, that their affliction might be desperate, becoming incurable as it has become insensible. But, lest their corruption, which God forbid, infect others by example, we are compelled to use the sword of rigorous vengeance against them. For when our venerable brother Godfrey, Bishop of Cambrai, had previously excommunicated the provosts, jurors, and sheriffs of Cambrai for unjustly ringing the bell to banish a certain cleric and forcibly entering the house of a canon of Saint Gaugeric, and when they, after being canonically admonished, refused to make amends, he extended this sentence to one hundred and forty citizens of Cambrai who had acted under the counsel and authority of these leaders. This sentence was confirmed in one part by R., Dean of Saint Paul, and his co-judges, and in another by I., Provost of Saint Lambert, and his colleagues delegated by us. Eventually, because the people, empowered and encouraged by them, spurned the admonition and request to make amends, he bound them with a similar sentence, which was confirmed by I., Dean of Amiens, and his co-judges delegated by the apostolic see. However, not only did the people fail to repent their obstinacy, but they also added iniquity upon iniquity by persistently harassing the said bishop against their privileges. He obtained apostolic letters addressed to the Bishop of Noyon and his colleagues on this matter, who, proceeding lawfully in the case, pronounced a sentence of excommunication against them due to their obstinacy. As their obstinacy increased, this excommunication was solemnly published throughout the province of Reims and at the fairs held in the provinces of Reims and Sens. Yet, those who should have returned to the one striking them, treated the hammer as if it were mere chaff, and they have not yet bothered to make amends. Some of their envoys approached the apostolic see, requesting the benefit of absolution on behalf of the community, but because they were unwilling to provide satisfaction or security, they left without absolution or permission. Therefore, so that a sharper penalty may sting those whom penitence has hitherto not pierced, we strictly mandate you by apostolic writings to renew these sentences solemnly throughout the provinces of Reims and Sens and the fairs held in these provinces on every Sunday and feast day, making them be avoided more strictly by all as excommunicated persons. Also, any clerics who presume to communicate with them or to celebrate divine services rashly, shall be struck with canonical penalties, with no hindrance from appeals. If not all of you can... Given at Rieti, on the fourth day before the Nones of October, in the tenth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo, decano, et archidiacono Remensi mandat ut sententias excommunicationis contra cives Cameracenses ob contumaciam et delicta innovent, et clericos communicantes poena canonica feriant. 1236, Oct. 4. Rieti.

**Translation to English:**

To the authorities and communities of all the cities and castles in the March of Ancona. The kindness of the Apostolic See prudently considers the merits of individuals and is accustomed to bestow greater grace upon those whom it sees burning with greater fervor in their devotion to it, so as to strongly encourage the devoted to its service and provoke the indifferent. Therefore, to duly reward the late Azo, Marquis of Este, for the many and great services rendered to it, and to bind him more closely to its devotion, it freely and absolutely granted the March of Ancona as a direct fief to him and his legitimate heirs, saving certain services to the Apostolic See, which are more fully set forth in the privileges made on this matter for the said marquis and the illustrious memory of Aldobrandino and the dear son, the noble man Azzone, Marquis of Ancona and Este, his sons, who were lawfully invested with the said march.
