Although we have retained the said march to our hands for some time, as the age of the said marquis and the state of the time required, yet, as the said marquis has now, by the grace of God, reached the age and has the capability and integrity to prudently govern himself and his affairs, we have freely restored the said march to him as it was granted by the Apostolic See to his aforementioned father and brother, and as is more fully contained in the aforementioned privileges, with the counsel and consent of our brothers, after receiving the oath of fidelity anew from him, and we have solemnly reinvested him with it through the banner. Therefore, we firmly command your community through apostolic letters, that you receive him gladly as your marquis and lord, offer him the oaths of fidelity without any difficulty, and obediently and faithfully serve and attend to him, responding fully regarding all the rights and claims belonging to him, knowing that we have instructed our venerable brother, the Bishop of Forosimphroni, through our letters, that if any, which we do not believe, show themselves difficult or rebellious in this matter, he compels their presumption, after due warning, by ecclesiastical censure, removing the obstacle of appeal. Given at Rieti, on the third day before the Kalends of December, in the tenth year. In the same way, it is written to the barons and knights established throughout the March of Ancona. In the same way to the bishops, abbots, and other prelates of churches established throughout the March of Ancona. In the same way to the authorities and people of Jesi. In the same way to the Bishop of Forosimpro. In the same way to the authorities and people of Osimo. In the same way to the authorities and people of Ascoli. In the same way to the authorities and people of Fermo. In the same way to the authorities and people of Monte Rubiano.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa potestatibus et communitatibus civitatum et castrorum in Marchia Anconitana mandatum mittit ut Azonem marchionem Estensem ac legitimos heredes eius in rectum feodum marchiae Anconitanae recipiant et fidelitatem ei iurent, eique in iustitiis et rationibus respondeant. Si qui resistentes fuerint, episcopus Forosimphroniensis per censuram ecclesiasticam eos compellat. Datum Reate, III Kalendas Decembris, anno decimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the rectors of the community of Lombardy. Amidst the various worries and innumerable and immense occupations that burden us beyond our strength, we think most urgently about how the merciful Lord may have mercy on Zion and Jerusalem, in which He deigned to work salvation with us and restore it as in ancient times, specifically by liberating that land from the hands of the pagans and restoring it to Christian worship, which He dedicated with His own blood. We must remove every obstacle and take away impediments and cut off the matter of arising contention as much as we can. Since, therefore, discord has recently arisen between our dearest son in Christ, Frederick, the illustrious emperor of the Romans, ever august, and king of Sicily, and you, due to the enemy sowing tares, and it is expected that from you, among other provinces subject to the Christian name, great help for the succor of the Holy Land may be hoped if, with the Lord's help, concord is reformed between you, and on the contrary, it is feared that its promotion might be impeded if peace is not reformed, it is necessary for us, both because of the above-mentioned and also since, although by insufficient merits we are constituted as vicars of Him who named the peacemakers as sons of God and whose prophetic voice called the feet of those who preach peace beautiful, to work by all means possible to settle discord and unite your hearts in the bond of peace and unity of spirit. Now, since the same emperor, out of the devotion which he owes to the Church and the desire with which he aspires to the aid of the Holy Land, concerning the reform of concord between you and your supporters on one side and him on the other, has submitted himself to our good pleasure of will through his letters and the venerable brother our archbishop of Regensburg and beloved sons, the master of the house of the Teutonic Order and R., professor of civil law, whom he has specifically sent to our presence for this reason, giving, moreover, by his own letters in command to all his faithful that no one should presume to disturb any of you working at court for such concord, but rather that they should provide them with secure conduct in going and returning, as you can clearly see from the tenor of those letters which we send to you: we, therefore, ask your entire community and exhort you in the Lord, by apostolic writings commanding you that on the coming feast of All Saints, you send some prudent men, sufficiently instructed in the name of your community to receive our mandate, concerning the making of said concord and other matters which are known to pertain to the peace and quiet of your whole province, to our presence, not considering that the beginning of this discord seems slow, because, if it increases, as the fire is in the beginning gently, with difficulty, yet extinguished when rotten, so it could not be removed without serious losses of things, dangers to bodies, and detriment to souls unless thwarted at the outset. You should carefully and effectively ensure the fulfillment of our mandate so that your province, which we, due to the eminent merits of its assistance, magnificently, as often as necessary, intend to honor, grows from strength to strength every day, becoming more gracious in our eyes and those of our brothers. Given at the Lateran.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa rectoribus communitatis Lombardie mandat, ut discordiae cum Friderico imperatore sedandae operam dent, mittendo viros prudentes ad recipiendum mandatum apostolicum super pace cum imperatore reformanda, attendentes ad pericula discordiae augendae. Laterani, anno pontificatus.

**Translation to English:**

Frederick, Emperor of the Romans, makes it known to all that he has assigned to Hermann, Master of the Teutonic Order, the Castle of Celi, Rocca of William, Rocca de Bantra, Rocca Praesentiani, Rocca of Saint Angelo de Rupe Canina, Rocca of Monte Dragone, Castle of Atina, and Petra de Tocco as security, under the condition that within eight months, under the form contained in the peace treaty, he will provide a guarantor's caution. August 7, 1230.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Fridericus II Romanorum imperator universis notum facit se Hermanno magistro Teutonicorum castra et roccas varias in securitatem assignasse, sub condicione cautionis fideiussoriae infra octo menses secundum tractatum pacis praestandae. Datum VII Idus Augusti, anno Domini MCCXXX, apud [locum non indicatum in textu originali].

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man, the Duke of the Venetians. With the affection of the usual love, having received your envoys, namely the beloved sons B. Falletr. and Jacob Accottant., wise and discreet men, we have summoned both the people of Ancona and those of Osimo and Recanati to our presence, granting the aforementioned envoys full and gracious audience and understanding what they took care to propose before us. Because the alliances that were made here and there in the Marches were to the prejudice of the Apostolic See and also to the detriment of the reputation and safety of those who made them, we, as justice demands, dissolve these alliances and absolve all who had sworn regarding this from the bond of their oath, and indeed, we have decreed that they are not bound. Moreover, this should not be troublesome to you but rather acceptable, since you are a Catholic man, devoted to God and the Church, loving equity and justice with your citizens among others around, and accustomed to observing seriousness and modesty. Indeed, since we do not wish, nor should we wish, to subject the ports of our land, which belong to the right of the Roman Church, to another's power or to entrust them to others for management, we have retained the bank of Recanati and Humanate in our hands, intending to dispose of it as we shall see fit. However, since we hold your person and the city of Venice in special affection, desiring your exaltation and the benefit and growth of that city, you ought indeed to trust that we, with the Lord as the author, will so provide for this that you can be even more devoted and ready for the honor of the Apostolic See, your mother. Wherefore, we earnestly admonish your nobility, asking that you entirely renounce the alliances made with the people of Osimo and Recanati, and withdraw the illicit agreements regarding this; for it is not expedient for you to harm the Roman Church, which considers you a special son, in its honor or justice, nor, God forbid, incur the detriment of your salvation or even obscure your name. Given at Perugia, on the 12th of October, in the second year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro duci Venetorum mandat ut societatibus cum Auximanis et Racanatibus initis renuntiet et illicita pacta remittat, societates in Marchia prejudiciales dissolvit, et omnes a vinculo iuramenti absolvit. Data Perusii, IV Idus Octobris, anno secundo.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishops of Rimini and Brescia. Since we have entrusted the duty of eradicating heretical depravity in the province of Lombardy to you, brother of Brescia, and to our venerable brother, the bishop of Modena, and since the latter, wishing for a long time to carry the name of the Lord Jesus Christ before the leaders and peoples of the Prussians, has been earnestly requested by the faithful in those parts, we have, by the counsel of our brothers, decided to send him there, so that the people who are still walking in darkness may see the great light by his ministry, with God as the actor: lest the work of eradicating the aforementioned depravity, which has been happily begun, be left unfinished due to the absence of the bishop of Modena, we have taken care to substitute you, brother of Rimini, in this matter, in whose zeal and prudence we have certain trust. Therefore, we command your fraternity by apostolic writings, that you proceed manfully and steadfastly in this matter, having only God before your eyes, confident in the favor of the apostolic see wherever it seems necessary. Because in the city of Brescia, a kind of domicile for heretics, these heretics and their supporters have recently burst into such madness that, with armed towers against the Catholics, they have not only destroyed certain churches with fire and ruin, but also presumed to blasphemously proclaim from these towers that they excommunicated the Roman Church and those following its do

**Translation to English:**

To the provosts of Halberstadt and Borslo of the Mainz diocese and L., canon of Halberstadt. It has been made known to us by our venerable brother, the bishop of Schwerin, that a dispute arose some time ago between him and our venerable brother, the bishop of Havelberg, concerning the boundaries of certain parishes. Eventually, the said bishop of Schwerin agreed to a compromise with the provost and his colleagues of Schwerin, with an explicit agreement inserted in the compromise that everything should remain in the state it was before the compromise was made, and that the matter should not be taken to another court until it could be resolved by the arbitrators.

However, the aforementioned bishop of Havelberg, having obtained letters from us against the parish priests of these parishes concerning these boundaries to the provost of Crevese and his co-judges, without any mention of the said agreement, managed to have himself inducted into possession of those boundaries after an appeal had been legitimately lodged with us by the same parish priests, without citing or informing the said bishop of Schwerin at all. Later, while the compromise was still pending, he procured other apostolic letters against him regarding the same boundaries to be sent to the provost of Arnesse and his co-judges.

But when the said bishop of Schwerin objected against the bishop of Havelberg, claiming that as long as the case was pending before the arbitrators, he could not, due to the explicit agreement, be sued, and that the bishop of Havelberg had obtained various apostolic letters to different judges concerning the same matters without mentioning the previous ones or the lodged appeal and the course of the trial, and because the aforementioned judges would not admit his objection, he appealed to us, and sent the scholastic of Schwerin to pursue it. But when he brought back certain letters that were too suspicious, the bishop did not use them, as was fitting, and therefore the matter has remained unresolved to this day.

Wherefore, since the time appointed for the appeal, as the said bishop of Schwerin asserts, has now elapsed, he humbly requests that, notwithstanding this, since he has not been negligent in its prosecution, we order that if anything has been presumed against him after the appeal, it be revoked, and that you proceed with the matter. Therefore, we command that if the premises are established for you, you are to revoke to its proper state whatever you find to have been rashly attempted to the prejudice of the said bishop after the appeal was lodged by him, and remit the matter to the arbitrators; otherwise, remit the parties to the examination of the aforementioned provost of Arnesse and his co-judges, condemning the appellant for exceeding the law; the passing of time notwithstanding, if it is established that through no fault of his own he was unable to pursue his appeal within the lawful time. Witnesses —. Given at Rieti, on the Ides of January, in the eleventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa provostis Halberstadensi et in Borslo Maguntine diocesis ac L. canonico Halberstadensi mandat ut, auditis querelis inter episcopos Zuerinensem et Avelbergensem de terminis parrochiarum, negotium ad arbitros remittant aut ad provosti de Arnesse iudicium partes dirigant, tempore appellationis elapso non obstante. Datum Reate, Idibus Ianuarii, anno XI.

**Translation to English:**

To Frederick, illustrious Emperor of the Romans, ever august, King of Sicily. There are various reasons that should lead your discretion to show favor to our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of Denmark, regarding the harsh circumstances he is known to have fallen into due to the treachery of Henry, count of Zuerich, his vassal. First, as you know, the king stood by you at the exhortation of the Apostolic See, diligently and at an opportune time, aiming at your honor and exaltation. Second, there has been a bond of amicable alliance between you and the king, as we have seen contained in your public letters fortified with a golden seal. Third, although the law of nature generally demands that man assist man, there is a special duty whereby a knight is bound to help a knight and a king a king, so that which makes him honorable to others, he may honor in kings royal majesty. Therefore, since the aforementioned count has, while holding the king captive, extorted from him an oath to provide hostages of his sons and to pay a certain amount of money, we have deemed it necessary to earnestly ask and encourage your serenity to wisely consider the malice that the count has shown against the king as not only grievous due to the act itself but also because of the precedent it sets, and to see it as wholly detestable, and therefore not suitable or expedient for the count to find favor with you, as he has by his example encouraged vassals against lords and subjects against kings. Compel the count with the power given to you from heaven to return the hostages and the money he has already received from the king and not to presume to trouble him over the payment of the remaining sum, disregarding the portion of the money you are said to be owed, as the divine bounty has so opened its hands to you and surrounded you with such abundance of wealth and other goods that it should not be needful for you to stain your glory for a little money, which in comparison to your honor and reputation, you ought to regard almost as dung. Thus, heed our admonitions in this matter so that others, led by your example, may understand how much regard should be given to royal dignity, and, by the illicit gain snatched from the jaws of the aforementioned count, may fear to attempt similar actions, and the king himself, prompted by this favor, may be bound to you by the bond of perpetual devotion, and we may justly commend in the Lord the providence of imperial majesty. Know that unless you heed our honest prayers and exhortations in this matter, we will not be able to fail the said king, suffering so open an injustice, not without great detriment to the aid of the Holy Land, to which he pledged himself with solemn promise before his capture, and not without injury and contempt to the Apostolic See, to which his kingdom is known to be tributary. Given at the Lateran, 9th June, in the tenth year. A letter in the same manner has been written to the bishop of Porto, legate of the Apostolic See, with words suitably changed, to effectively advise and lead the said emperor to this.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Fridericum Romanorum imperatorem monet ut Henrico comite de Zuerich vassallo perfido adversus regem Daniae iniuste agentes compellat restituere obsides et pecunias, nec ulterius super residuis eum molestet, contempta pecunia. 1236, Iun. 9, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To R., our subdeacon and chaplain. Holding firm hope and full confidence that you should carry sincerity of devotion and purity of faith towards the Roman Church, your mother, and be a zealous guardian of her honor, we have decided to confidently entrust to your prudence the custody of the fortress of Bantro, having received an oath from you that you will diligently and faithfully guard the aforementioned fortress in the name of the Apostolic See, along with the servants of Campania or other faithful to us, who are bound by an oath of fidelity to the Roman Church and to diligently guard the same fortress for its benefit, and that you will freely resign it to whomever and whenever we wish, according to our mandate, which we will communicate to you through a messenger or by letters. Therefore, we command your devotion through apostolic writings, instructing that you take the necessary caution and diligence in this matter, and take such care for the Roman Church in this regard, that nothing untoward may happen to us from your custody, but that the zeal of your solicitude, devotion, and faith may clearly appear in effect, so that we may be obliged to hold you in grace. Given at Perugia, 5th day before the Kalends of September, in the third year of our pontificate. In the same manner to the abbot of Cassino and to R., his brother, our subdeacon and chaplain, for the fortress of Cassino and the fortress of Janula.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa R. subdiacono et capellano suo committit custodiam arcis Bantre, sub iuramento fidelitatis ad Sedem Apostolicam. 1229, Aug. 28. Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To Peter, Infante of Portugal. By the inspiration of the spirit of salvation, you have conceived of the noble idea to take up arms and serve in the cause of the bride of Christ. You have devotedly offered yourself, with His grace guiding you, to pursue the vows inspired in you, with the hope of His support. You should rejoice with spiritual exultation and offer a sacrifice of praise to the Giver of all good things, as you have been chosen among so many kings, princes, and faithful sons of the Church, to follow Deborah, seated under the palm, or rather ascending the palm, into battle against Sisera, who has shut himself off from true joy and is, unfortunately, consigned to the pains of hell. He has become so dull that he does not feel the bitterness of the sword’s spiritual strike, nor does he even blush to return to the one who strikes him to be healed by salutary confusion. Instead, he persists in his malice with a hardened mind, having forgotten God’s mercy without which he becomes inglorious, or rather nothing. Your devotion brings the joy of internal and eternal happiness, as you, anticipated by the largesse of divine gifts, have turned the left side of temporal substance into the right by offering it for the Church’s aid, to deliver the people of God from the yoke of unjust servitude. To both you and those who will come with you, we grant remission of sins, so that, as you have generously offered, you may quickly proceed with a multitude of knights to the aid of Christ’s bride, to serve the Lord under the leadership of His army with blessed Peter. Given at Perugia, on the 4th of June, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Petro infanti Portugaliae remissionem peccatorum et exhortationem concedit, ut cum multitudine equitum ad subsidium ecclesiae quanto citius properet, militaturus sub beato Petro. Datum Perusii, II Non. Iunii, anno pontificatus nostri III.

**Translation to English:**

To the rectors of the Lombard League. We marvel and are not sufficiently able to admire that, when we, with paternal affection, aiming at peace and the welfare of your province, sought to mediate in the discord that has arisen between you and our dearest son in Christ, Frederick, the illustrious Roman Emperor always august and King of Sicily, and the Emperor and you both freely and absolutely placed the whole matter under the guidance of us and our brothers, we have decreed, concerning this matter, what is undoubtedly expedient for the advantage and stability of the same province, and we have given you commands through our letters that you should strive to keep intact what we have decreed on your part, and that you should send us and the Emperor your open letters, written by a public hand and fortified by the attachment of the seals of you and the noble man, the Marquis of Montferrat, and of any cities of your league by the first Sunday of Lent just past, you, after having been awaited by us and the Emperor’s envoy, who sent letters on this behalf according to what we wrote to him, have not cared to comply, attempting to excuse such negligence and contempt through some simple envoy, claiming that the document in which the said form was written fell into the water and was so damaged that it could not be read, and in support of this claim you sent us the page in which the aforementioned document was enclosed, on which we do not intend to express here what we noted. Surely it was not prudent of you to offer such an inappropriate excuse, and thus provoke against yourselves the Roman Church, the Emperor, and Jesus Christ himself, whose service, namely the aid to the Holy Land, could easily be hindered by this. Therefore, dismissing your petition for delay, which you sent us through another envoy, of whatever kind you pleased, we command and strictly urge your discretion by the authority of these presents, that, as you hold dear the grace of God and ours, you shall without any delay or excuse send us and the Emperor letters according to the aforementioned form, which we now also send you enclosed under our seal, so swiftly that it cannot reach the attention of the Emperor that you delayed sending these letters for so long, nor that we had to write to you about this again, and in the meantime, with the diligence that the urgency of the time requires, prepare what you are obliged to do for the aid of the Holy Land, lest you seem to give the Emperor occasion to delay the aid to the Holy Land, and thereby provoke God and men against yourselves; knowing that if we perceive you to be in such a matter scorners and mockers of God and us, we see nothing else remaining except to call upon heaven and earth against your insolence. We have sent to you for this purpose our beloved son Guala, a brother of the Order of Preachers, the bearer of these presents, who, as we have clearly known, loves the state and tranquility of the same province and has frequently taken care to intercede with us on its behalf, through whose report you will be able to know more fully how grievous and vexing such a manner of delay has been to us and our brothers. Given at the Lateran, 10 March, in the 11th year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa rectoribus societatis Lombardie mandat ut litteras secundum formam praescriptam sine dilatione ad se et ad imperatorem mittant, monens ne Terrae Sanctae succursum morentur. 1238, Mart. 10, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

Gregory, bishop, etc., to the noble man, the duke of Austria. The sincerity of your faith and the merit of your devotion demand that we, loving you as a devoted son, should look after your peace and strive for your honor and benefit. Beyond this, because your commendable devotion is evident in many ways, you, once fired with zeal for the faith, undertook labor in your own person for the honor of the Church, defending the crucified against the reproaches of the blasphemers, and you did this laudably and powerfully on behalf of the cross in the lands beyond the sea. From your recent communication, we have also learned that many of the nobles of your land, having taken up the sign of the cross, have devoted themselves to the service of the Holy Land, and many more of the other rich and powerful have conceived this pious intention and are ready to cross over in the next passage. Consequently, although you may thus be deprived of a great part of your soldiers, because you ardently desire the promotion of this said mission through its actual completion, and now showing the devotion which the Lord has inspired in you regarding this, you do not wish to impede so great a good and necessary work. Instead, you asked that provision be made for you by the apostolic see, so that you may be able to encourage those signed with the cross and those to be signed for the aid of the aforementioned land more freely, as you will be able to do it more securely, when a special provision has been made for you in this matter. Wherefore, inclined by the prayers of your nobility, we, welcoming you in this devotion and procuring the mission of the Holy Land, receive you, with your land and all goods which you reasonably possess at present, under the protection of blessed Peter and our own, and fortify you with the support of this present writing. Let no one at all, therefore, infringe upon our protection. But if anyone should, etc. Given at Velletri, on the 13th day before the Kalends of November, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro, duci Austriæ, qui pro negotio crucis laudabiliter laboravit, terras suas cum bonis sub protectione beati Petri et nostra suscipit, ut securius crucesignatos animet. Datum Velletri, XIII Kalendas Novembris, anno primo pontificatus nostri.

**Translation to English:**

To the people of Sorano, our faithful. Since by God's grace you have been brought back to the loyalty and dominion of the Roman Church, your mother, to whom it was undoubted that you belong, by which you now exist not as children of the bondwoman, but of the free woman, it is fitting and proper that the Apostolic See provides for your needs, as it mercifully customarily looks after the welfare of its children. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, inclined by your supplications and with the counsel of our brothers, we receive you and your city, with all the goods which you rightfully possess at present or may in the future obtain by just means with God's help, under the protection of the Apostolic See and ours, and we fortify you with the safeguard of this present document. We have also provided that the aforementioned city, while persisting in the loyalty to the Roman Church, be retained henceforth in its domain, granting you the liberty which the cities of Campania have, with half the services, namely in wheat, wine, foodstuffs, iron, nails, and shoes, and all gifts commonly called "salutes," and other just dues owed to the court, while maintaining the mandate of the Apostolic See. Let no one at all, therefore, etc., infringe upon our protection, provision, and concession, etc. But if anyone, etc. Given at Perugia, 29th August, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Populo Sorano fideles suos sub protectione apostolicae sedis et sua suscipit et civitati eorum libertatem civitatum Campaniae concedit, servitiis mediatis salvis. Datum Perusii, IV Kalendas Septembris, pontificatus nostri anno tertio.

**Translation to English:**

To the podestà and people of the city of Castellana. Since it is clear that your city is part of the patrimony of Saint Peter, as is evident from many privileges, although imperial power sometimes unjustly usurped this dominion by force, since you prudently recognize that it is in both your interest and ours to be subject to the Roman Church, you have turned to us in faith and devotion, having taken oaths of fidelity to us. We wish, as is fitting, to favorably nurture you as special sons and faithful ones in the sweetness of liberty. We take your city and persons, with all your goods and rights, within the city and outside — namely, the county, bishopric, and others which you reasonably possess at present or may justly acquire in the future with the Lord's help — under the special protection of Saint Peter and ourselves, decreeing that this city shall forever be held within the domain of the Roman Church and defended by the Roman Church in both matters and persons, like other faithful ones of the patrimony, never to return under another's rule. We also confirm and strengthen by apostolic authority your liberties and laudable customs observed up to now, which other cities of the patrimony enjoy — namely, in electing and appointing podestàs or consuls, judges, chamberlains, notaries, merchant consuls, and all other officials, by whatever names they are called, and those who make municipal constitutions or statutes by which you are governed, provided nothing is contained within these against the Church and ecclesiastical liberty, and also the authority to exercise full jurisdiction in the city and beyond over you and yours, both in persons and matters, as you justly and peacefully possess all this, and other things you may justly acquire in the future with the Lord's help. We confirm these by apostolic authority and strengthen them with the protection of this present writing. Let no one, therefore, etc. But if anyone, etc. Given at Perugia, 19 May, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa potestati et populo civitatis Castellane civitatem et personas cum omnibus bonis et iuribus sub protectione ecclesiae Romanae suscipit, libertates ac consuetudines confirmat. 1230, Perusii, XIV Kalendas Iunii.

**Translation to English:**

Form of the letters which the Lombards must send to the lord emperor. To their most serene and excellent lord Frederick, by the grace of God, the most invincible emperor of the Romans, ever august, and the most illustrious king of Jerusalem and Sicily, from the rectors of the society of Lombardy, the March, and Romagna, and the entire society itself, his faithful servants, prompt and faithful service. Among other things that the lord pope has ordained and established, as his letters have declared to us, he has most piously decreed, by the providence of his brothers, that we, to the honor of Almighty God and His holy church, and for your sake, should provide your excellency with four hundred knights for the aid of the Holy Land at our own expense for two years. We should make peace with the cities, places, and persons adhering to your majesty, firmly preserving it, and remit all rancor, malice, injuries, and offenses, and revoke all bans, constitutions, sentences, and ordinances that we have enacted or imposed on cities, places, and persons adhering to your majesty, and whatever has followed from them or because of them. We shall also restore the captives who were taken because of this discord, with their goods, and other things taken or detained because of the same discord, so that those adhering to your majesty will do the same and observe it towards us. Other captives are to be restored according to the law of the empire when you decide to send your legat

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Lyon. The prayers of the faithful, containing piety within themselves, especially when they seek liberty, which is a favorable thing, should be pursued with appropriate support, and we are obliged to provide apostolic protection to them. Therefore, although we might have been initially hesitant regarding the petitions presented to us concerning the liberty that the noble man G., Count of Forez, your nephew, is said to have granted freely out of piety to the people of the village of Saint-Rambert and its parishes, namely Bonzon, Chamble, Saint-Cyprian, and Saint-Just, which belong to the monastery of Saint-Rambert, we have been made more certain of this grant through your and the count's letters, and having approved the devotion of the said count, we have graciously decided to agree to the petitions.

Furthermore, as we have learned through the same letters, although nothing of right belonged to the Counts of Forez, your ancestors and those of the said count, over the people of the aforesaid village of Saint-Rambert and the said parishes, nevertheless, due to the custody of those places which they had held from ancient times, they often imposed heavy tallages on the people of those places, against God and justice, and inflicted other undue burdens upon them. However, the aforementioned count, inspired by pious affection, lamenting past wrongs and desiring to prevent future grievances, to prevent the abuse of such from becoming custom and practice, with your counsel and assent, as you are their diocesan, for himself and his successors, has renounced the said tallages and burdens, granting full liberty to those places and people, and binding himself with an oath that he would never go against it; he also decreed that his successors and descendants should swear a similar oath.

And because men are prone to evil rather than good, and many imitate the vices of their predecessors rather than their virtues, as charity cools day by day and the iniquity of many abounds, he wished, by apostolic authority, for what he had piously decided to be done to be defended. Wherefore, he humbly supplicated us through his letters to grant that, if at any time he or his successors presume to violate such liberty, the Archbishop of Lyon, whoever he may be at the time, should, unless suitable redress is provided by the violator within a month after admonition, subject him to excommunication and place the county of Forez under interdict until proper satisfaction is made.

You also indicated to us through your letters that the aforementioned count, after having a diligent discussion with you about preserving the said liberty, thus wished to have it defended and so to be kept. Moreover, stating that you know more fully about this matter and the state of that land, and that it involves no small ecclesiastical benefit and contains a great work of mercy, you humbly requested that the supplications of the count be accepted.

Therefore, we command your fraternity through apostolic writings that you protect the said liberty and immunity by excommunication against the persons of the Counts of Forez and by interdict against the said county by apostolic authority, which authority we also wish to be extended to your successors. Given at Rieti, the third of the Kalends of September, in the tenth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa archiepiscopo Lugdunensi mandat, ut libertatem et immunitatem hominibus villae Sancti Ragneberti et parochiarum suarum concessam tueatur per excommunicationem et interdictum contra comites Forenses, extensione huius auctoritatis ad successores archiepiscopi. Datum Rieti, tertio Kalendas Septembris, anno decimo.

Translation to English:

To the Archbishop of Lyon. When Frederick, the so-called emperor, with the confused business of the Holy Land, allies with the Saracens and other infidels to trample upon the Roman Church and overthrow ecclesiastical liberty with all his might and main, we have confidently called upon you for the aid of the church, as you are bound by oath to assist in defending the papacy and the regalia of Saint Peter. But you, who should have assumed the spirit of fortitude out of love for virtue and zeal for ecclesiastical liberty, so that nothing could alienate you from the love of your mother (the Church), have thus far neglected to come to its aid, not considering how easily you could be justly accused of the vice of ingratitude, loss of reputation, and evident transgression. Therefore, to justify such an offense with swift amendment, we earnestly beseech, advise, and exhort your brotherhood, commanding strictly by apostolic writings in the virtue of obedience under the obligation of your oath, and enjoining in the remission of sins, both yours and those who come with you in service to the church, that without delay, with a suitable force of warriors, you hasten to come to us in person, to serve the Roman Church so wholeheartedly that you may earn merit from your duty, and we may be bound to reward your devotion with worthy thanks. Otherwise, know that we have instructed our beloved sons, the abbot of Saint Victor, the dean, and Master John, the archdeacon of Paris, through our letters to compel you to this by ecclesiastical censure, with no appeal allowed. Given at Perugia, IV Kal. Oct., in the third year of our pontificate.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Lugdunensi iniungit ut, ob confoederationem Friderici imperatoris cum infidelibus contra ecclesiam, cum exercitu venire festinet ad defensionem ecclesie Romane, sub comminatione censure ecclesiastice. 1230, Sept. 28. Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To the archbishops, bishops, noble dukes, marquises, counts, and other princes of Germany, both ecclesiastical and secular. We recall informing you previously that our dearest son in Christ, Frederick, the illustrious Roman Emperor, ever august and King of Sicily, was magnificently preparing, as he had informed us through his letters and envoys, to liberate the land where our God and Lord Jesus Christ deigned to mercifully operate the salvation of humankind from the hands of the infidels. We had decided to retain for some time our beloved son, the master of the House of the Holy Mary of the Germans, who was hastening to the regions of Germany to procure aid for that land, because his diligence was crucial to us, both for other great and arduous affairs and especially for settling a certain discord that had arisen between the Emperor and the Lombards. Since, by our efforts, with God, the author of peace, cooperating, a salutary provision has been arranged concerning this discord, and the Emperor himself is preparing magnificently, as befits his imperial excellence, to cross over there in the coming August, diligently preparing a multitude of ships and other things suitable for such a great undertaking, as we have joyfully heard from him through solemn envoys and letters, and as it is more clearly manifested by the evident fact, as asserted by those who have seen it; therefore, hoping that God has arisen to judge His cause and restore Jerusalem as in former times, we ask, admonish, and beseech all of you in the Lord Jesus Christ, and by apostolic writings we command and enjoin it upon you for the remission of sins, that, inflamed with zeal for faith and devotion, for the love and fear of our Redeemer Jesus Christ, as well as for the honor of imperial majesty and the empire, you prepare yourselves for the aid of the Holy Land, so that those who have already taken the sign of the cross and others whom divine grace will inspire may be able to cross over, with God as their guide, in the coming August, when the general passage is proclaimed, to the praise, honor, and glory of the Christian name and the remedy of their souls. The said master, who devotes himself entirely to this undertaking and now comes to you after overcoming other affairs and impediments, we commend most zealously to you all, considering it superfluous to explain or commend to you his prudence and diligence concerning the business of the Holy Land, since his commendable deeds make themselves abundantly known and commend him. Given at the Lateran, on the 11th of January, in the eleventh year. 

In the same manner to the archbishops, bishops, noble counts, and barons established throughout Hungary. In the same manner to the illustrious King Andrew of Hungary, up to "restore," you, who long ago took up the sign of the cross and vowed to fight for Him who fought for you on the gibbet of the cross, we ask, admonish, and earnestly exhort, and likewise exhort through the shedding of the blood of Jesus Christ, that you prepare yourself in such a way that in the coming August, when the general passage is proclaimed, you may be able to cross over with God as your guide, to receive grace in the present and glory in the future. The said master, etc., up to the end, with the words suitably altered. In the same manner to the noble landgrave of Thuringia.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopis, episcopis, ducibus, marchionibus, comitibus et principibus Theutonie mandat ut ad subsidium Terre Sancte, una cum Friderico imperatore, se preparent. Commendat etiam magistrum domus sancte Marie Theutonicorum pro hoc negotio. 1238, Ian. 11, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Salzburg and the Bishop of Regensburg, Chancellor of the Imperial Court. Since our dearest son in Christ, Frederick, the illustrious Emperor of the Romans, ever august and King of Sicily, has committed himself to provide a certain assurance requested by the Church for the observance of the peace reformed between him and the Church, we admonish your fraternity by the authority of these presents to ensure that you procure the receipt of the assurance from the prelates and princes, whose names we are transmitting to you in writing, according to the form which we are sending enclosed under our seal. Given at the Lateran, on the 16th of January, in the fourth year of our pontificate. These are the names: [names of prelates and princes]... In the same manner as above is written... to the Bishop of Vercelli and the elected of Milan. These are the names: [list in Tuscia, Lombardy, and Romania]. 

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Salzburgensi et episcopo Ratisponensi mandat, ut a nominatis prelatis et principibus cautionem recipiant ad formam sub bulla inclusam, pro pace inter ecclesiam et imperatorem Fridericum servanda. 1229, Jan. 16. Datum Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To Frederick, the illustrious always august Emperor of the Romans and King of Sicily. Since it was arranged in the form of peace agreed upon between us and you that for those matters which came to be observed in the peace treaty, you would provide a surety within eight months, and due to supervening impediments this could not be fulfilled, we do not wish you to suffer prejudice from the lapse of the elapsed time. However, you should now strive to fulfill the aforesaid matters, as the time for providing such surety is now running for you. Given at the Lateran, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of February, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Friderico, illustri Romanorum imperatori semper augusto et regi Sicilie, mandat ut, non obstante impedimentis supervenientibus quae cautionem fideiussoriam differre fecerunt, adimplere studeat quae in tractatu pacis inter eos ordinata sunt, cum iam tempus cautionis prestande currat. Datum Laterani, XIII Kalendas Februarii, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz and the Bishop of Bamberg. The sincere devotion that our dearest son in Christ, Frederick, illustrious Emperor of the Romans, ever august and King of Sicily, is known to have towards God and the Church, compels us to strive with diligent study and careful diligence for his tranquility and peace. Therefore, since he is zealously moved by faith and devotion to liberate the land where Jesus Christ, King of Kings and Lord of Lords, deigned to accomplish the salvation of humankind mercifully, as befits imperial magnificence, we support him so that he may better fulfill this pious and beneficial purpose. We have taken him and his son's persons, along with the Empire, the kingdom, his rights, and his people, under the protection of Saint Peter and our protection, strictly forbidding anyone from daring to invade, diminish, or disturb them in any way, but rather that they may remain free and undisturbed under the special defense of the Apostolic See and the archbishops and bishops until his return. Wherefore, we command your discretion by apostolic writings, that if any, with reckless daring, come against our prohibition and presume to invade, diminish, or disturb in any way the honors and rights of the emperor, which he holds within the bounds of your metropolis, brother archbishop, you shall compel these presumptuous individuals, from wherever they may be, to desist from their presumption and make due satisfaction for their presumptions, by excommunication upon their persons and interdict upon their lands, removing the appeal, as often as you are required. But if not both, then one of you — Given at the Lateran, the 13th of January, in the eleventh year. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Salzburg and the Bishop of Gurk. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Besançon. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Pisa and the Abbot of San Antimo in the diocese of Chiusi. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Reggio and the Bishop of Aquino and the Elect of Bari. In the same manner to the Archbishops of Arles and Embrun; except in that clause, where it says within the bounds of your metropolis, brother archbishop, which to the Archbishop of Pisa and the Abbot of San Antimo, it says in Tuscany. Similarly to the Archbishop of Reggio and the Bishop of Aquino and the Elect of Bari, it says in the Kingdom, and to the Archbishops of Arles and Embrun, it says in the kingdom of Arles. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Esztergom. Within the bounds, etc. In the same manner to the Bishop of Winchester. In the same manner to the Archbishop and Provost of Genoa. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Cologne and the Bishop of Paderborn. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Bremen and the Abbot of Stade. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Trier and the Bishop of Metz. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Ravenna and the Bishop of Parma. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Milan and the Bishop of Novara. In the same manner to the Patriarch of Aquileia and the Bishop of Padua.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino et episcopo Bambergensi mandat ut Friderici imperatoris honores et iura, sub speciali protectione sedis apostolicae posita, ab invasoribus defendantur per excommunicationem et interdictum, si quis ea invadere presumpserit. 1238, Ian. 13. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the illustrious King of Sweden. The kings of the earth offer the most gracious service to the King of Kings, who sympathize and grieve when the bride of Christ suffers persecution, and during times of persecution clearly demonstrate that no one is to be preferred before God. Indeed, if the said emperor, ungrateful to God and men, repays iniquitously the apostolic see with evil for good, insult for honor, and hatred for love, not content with maliciously perverting the business of the Holy Land, now eagerly aspires to trample the universal church by all means he can, and to subvert ecclesiastical liberty, considering almost everything lost to him that the bride of Christ obtains in freedom or honor, and wickedly thinking that if he could oppress the Roman church, it would be very easy for him to conquer other kings and kingdoms, he has proceeded to hostilely occupy the patrimony of Saint Peter. There he has, through Raynald, son of the late Conrad, formerly Duke of Spoleto, his vicar and minister, invaded certain lands of the apostolic see by corrupting their inhabitants, with priests and other clerics wickedly mutilated by Saracens. Wherefore, seeing and grieving that Frederick’s wicked pride, ever rising, is not halted until justice may confront and meet it, we take providential care, with divine assistance, to set the right hand of the apostolic see against his malice, having gathered three armies for this purpose. But since these cannot be accomplished without heavy expenses, to which the resources of the apostolic see are not sufficient, we have confidently decided to seek your assistance in these matters as a special son of the Roman church, affectionately asking and earnestly advising your royal serenity that you trust what our beloved son, Master Simon, our scribe, of whose providence and sincere faith we fully trust, will propose to you on our behalf, believing it as if spoken by our own mouth, that you may strive to fulfill the same in such a way that you make the Roman church meritoriously obligated to you, and we may be able to respond to you with grateful reciprocation. Given at Perugia, on the 12th day before the Calends of January, in the second year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa illustri regi Suetiae mandat, ut cum auxilio pecuniario subveniat adversus Frederici iniustam superbiam, quae hostiliter occupat sedis apostolicae terras, hortans ut credat quae magister Simon ex parte papali proponet. Datum Perusii, XII Cal. Ian., anno II.

**Translation to English:**

To Archbishop Regino. We had hoped that, as you promised us in person, you would ensure the return of the possessions taken from the Hospitallers and Templars, but now, having first been deprived of what was taken, they have been newly despoiled of other possessions, as their lamentable complaint has revealed to us. Therefore, as we are sending our beloved son, the Abbot of Casemari, to the imperial presence because of this, we urgently ask and admonish your fraternity, by apostolic writings, to effectively intervene with our dearest son in Christ, Frederick, the illustrious Roman Emperor, ever august, and King of Sicily, so that he may restore all their taken possessions, in such a way that we can justly commend your diligence. In the same manner, to Archbishop Capuano. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Regino archiepiscopo scribit, ut apud imperatorem Fredericum interponat partes suas ad restituenda Hospitalariis et Templariis ablata. 1237, Apr. 11, Datum ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Tournai. Since by the duty of the apostolate entrusted to us, we are bound to uproot from the Lord's field the thorns and thistles choking the crops of virtues, we neither wish nor ought to tolerate the vice of usurious depravity, which causes a loss of goods and endangers souls, from which scarcely anyone infected with such corruption abstains. Indeed, it has come to our attention that some people from Cahors and certain other foreigners residing in the town of Ypres presume to engage in public usury, in contempt of divine law and to the peril of their souls, as well as the scandal of many, since, as it is said, the locals are not at all permitted to do this. Therefore, lest others who keep their hands free from such depravity be infected by their contagion, we firmly command you by apostolic writings to restrain the aforementioned usurers of the said place, both foreign and local, from the often-mentioned depravity of usury, in the manner described, by the penalty enacted against usurers in the Lateran Council, removing any appeal, and to enjoin all and each of the sheriffs and the community of the said town under the same penalty not to have any commerce or participation with them, nor even to dare to shelter them, unless they have ceased from the often-mentioned depravity. Given at Perugia, 30 January, in the third year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Tornacensi mandat, ut Caturcenses et alios alienigenas in villa Iprensi commorantes, qui fenerari praesumunt, compescat, et scabinis ac communi eiusdem villae iniungat ne cum eis commercium habeant, nisi desinant a pravitate usurarum, sub poena in Concilio Lateranensi statuta. Datum Perusii, III Kal. Febr., anno tertio.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Milan and Brother Guala of the Order of Preachers.

Would that the Lombards had never offered themselves to our service, would that we had never hoped for any help from them, for we could have sufficiently attended to the honor of the Church in other ways, except that, not wishing to withhold a helping hand from them, we acceded to their supplications and promises. But while we were managing their cause effectively in foreign lands, while we were restraining the impetus of the enemy eagerly aspiring to their extermination, behold, the Lombards delayed the promised help so much, not to mention how they served those whom they had sent in the service of the Church, that the enemy, having gathered strength, is growing powerful, unless he is quickly opposed by a strong and powerful hand, because a fire that is not opposed easily spreads into an unquenchable conflagration. Therefore, lest the said Lombards appear to put their hands, which they ought to have extended to mighty deeds, under their armpits to their eternal disgrace of confusion and not be able to extend them when they wish, if now they cease to will while they are able, we urgently ask and admonish your discretion, commanding by apostolic writings, that you excite and earnestly strive to induce, those whom you see fit by all means possible, enjoining them in remission of sins, that pursuing their own interest manfully, they may come to our aid without any delay with as much force of warriors as they can, because if we still have it in due time, we hope in the Lord that the enemy will not prevail but will fail. Otherwise, you can safely protest to them that they will be able to blame themselves, not us, if we shall have taken care to provide for the honor of the Church in another way, with the Lord's help, abandoning the deserters. Given at Perugia, on the 7th Ides of October, in the third year of our pontificate.

---

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Mediolanensi et fratri Guale ordinis Praedicatorum mandat ut Lombardos, qui auxilium in bello promiserant sed distulerunt, incitent et inducant ad celerem subsidium, innuendo remissionem peccaminum, alioquin se aliter provisurum. Datum Perusii, VII Idus Octobris, anno pontificatus nostri tertio.

**Translation to English:**

To the master and brothers of the Militia of Christ in Livonia. Those things which are established by judgment or concord, etc., up to: to be fortified. Therefore, etc., up to: with consent, the composition that was amicably made between you on one side and our venerable brother, the bishop of Leal on the other side, concerning certain lands, with the mediation of our venerable brother, the Bishop of Riga and his colleagues, as it is more fully contained in the letters drawn up thereon, since it was done rightly without corruption and voluntarily accepted by both parties, we confirm by apostolic authority and fortify it by the page of this present writing. Furthermore, for greater clarity, we have decided to insert the tenor of those letters word for word into the present documents. It is as follows: Hermann, by the grace of God, Bishop of Leal, to all who read this letter, greetings in Him who is the salvation of all. We wish it to be known to both future and present that, upon the counsel of our venerable brother, Lord Albert, Bishop of Riga, and his church, as well as the pilgrims and citizens of Riga with the brothers of the Militia of Christ, according to what is contained in their authentic document, we have made such a composition, to wit, that they and their successors may hold about half of our episcopal region in civil jurisdiction to be possessed perpetually with churches, tithes, and all temporal emoluments, namely the land of Sackcle, Normecunde, Moeche with its appurtenances, and half of the land of Weigele, saving to us in all things spiritual right. In those lands, therefore, they shall establish suitable persons through their churches and present them to us for investiture. For these lands, they shall render to us no temporal service or anything else, except that they shall continually fight for our bishopric against enemy incursions and obey us in spiritual matters, and when, by reason of the episcopal office, we visit their churches, they shall furnish us the necessary expenses. Moreover, we will leave the river Emevike free, or we will grant them half of the king’s fishing weirs; and lest anyone bring malicious impediment against them on account of this our concession, we forbid it under the threat of anathema. And so that our action may obtain perpetual strength, we have caused this charter to be written and fortified it with our seal and that of the lord Bishop of Riga and his church. The witnesses of this action are: Lord Albert, Bishop of Riga, and John, provost of Saint Mary in Riga and his convent, Albric, prior in Duneminee with his brothers, Rothmar, our brother, Thomas, priest in Luneburg; vassals of the church of Riga: Count Bruchard of Alderiberg, Daniel of Lenwarde, Conrad of Ikescule, John of Dolen; pilgrims: Fredelmus of Poch, Theoderic of Escherde, Lubert of Nordorphe, advocate of pilgrims, Helmold of Luneburg, Henry of Lith, John of Bekeshovede, Eugelbertus of Tisenhusen, Jacob of the City; citizens of Riga: Luoderus, advocate, Bernard of Deventer, Albert Utnoerding, and many others. Given in Riga, in the year of the Lord 1224, 10th Kalends of August. Therefore let no one, etc., confirmation, etc. If anyone, etc. Given at the Lateran, 4th Ides of December, in the 11th year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa magistro et fratribus militiae Christi in Livonia compositionem inter eos et episcopum Lealensem super terris, mediantibus episcopo Rigensi et collegis, confirmat. Datum Laterani, IIII Idus Decembris, anno undecimo.

Translation to English:

To the Bishop of Paris: Since charity, which does not seek its own, considers nothing human alien to itself, anyone who loves charity can rightly deem whatever threatens the universal church as their own concern, and should not spare themselves where they can avert a common danger, lest they appear to prefer private interest over universal benefit. Indeed, the Roman Church is now situated in such a predicament that it seems driven to one of two alternatives: either to defend itself and the universal church, supported by the faithful with the Lord's help, or to allow itself and all its members to be, God forbid, trampled and subjected to severe servitude, with the said Emperor wickedly conspiring against God and the church, miserably confounding the affairs of the Holy Land, and impiously amassing forces with the Saracens and other infidels. Therefore, seeing and lamenting that the Emperor's wicked pride and proud wickedness always escalate unless restrained by the barrier of justice, we have deemed it fitting to oppose his endeavors, lest he who provokes to wrath be exalted. Relying on your sincerity in the Lord with full confidence, we earnestly ask, urge, and exhort your fraternity, by apostolic writings, strictly mandating in the virtue of obedience and under the obligation of an oath, and promising remission of sins, both yours and those who come in service of the church, that as you hold divine and our favor dear, remembering that necessity tests kinship, you endeavor to come to us personally with a fitting retinue of warriors or send them without delay, intending to serve the Roman Church from the heart, so that you may earn your due merit, and we may owe it to reward your devotion with fitting gratitudes. Given at Perugia, September 30, in the third year of our pontificate.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa Parisiensi episcopo mandat, ut personaliter cum exercitu ad ecclesiam Romanam veniat, aut mittat, ad resistendum conatibus imperatoris qui contra ecclesiam insurgit. 1230, Sept. 30. Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To the same (recipient). The more malicious and slanderous people burn with a greater desire to slander, even wickedly twisting right things to damage our and your reputation, the more carefully you should guard your sincerity, lest you give those people a reason to unleash their slanderous tongues against both of us, as it is fitting for you to be a zealous protector of the reputation of both. We have indeed understood that you intend to compel those in the kingdom who have adhered to the Church to cross the sea, that is, to exile them, as it appears to you and others, as if you might be induced to do so from lesser affection. Therefore, lest you seem to seek an occasion against them and, consequently, sharpen the tongues of detractors against us and you, we affectionately ask and earnestly advise your imperial highness to desist from such an intention, on this occasion. Dated as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa eidem recipienti (Imperatori) affectuose rogat et monuit, ne eos de regno qui ecclesie adheserunt in exilium relegare intendat, ut linguas detractorum adversus utrumque non acuere videatur. Datum ut supra.

Translation to English:

To the same. We have received with gratitude the letters of imperial majesty presented to us by our beloved son, the abbot of Casemaria, and have diligently understood them, rejoicing in the Lord that you exhibit the due affection of sincerity towards us and the Roman Church, through which you gain the grace and favor of God and men, and you effectively exhort us to your successes. However, having understood what the same abbot proposed to us on your behalf by word of mouth, being occupied with many matters and especially with the business of faith, we could not have appropriate deliberation on these or other matters in the City. But since, as it is believed, our departure from there will not be delayed for long, you can then send your messenger to us, who by explaining your intention to us will bring back to you our fuller response. In the meantime, confidently comply with those things which the aforesaid abbot will propose to your gentleness on our behalf by word of mouth, certain that we gladly accede to your wishes as far as we can with due propriety. Given as above.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa dilecto filio .. abbati Casemarii gratulatur ob litteras imperialis celsitudinis acceptas et hortatur ut nuntium mittat pro responsis plenius recipiendis, inter alia occupatur negotio fidei. Sine loco et data certa (data ut supra).

Translation to English:

To the abbot of Saint Nicholas of Furnes of the Premonstratensian order, to the provost of Lee, and to the dean of Furnes of the diocese of Morini. On behalf of the aldermen and the commune of Ypres, it was presented before us that, in disputes arising between laymen against laymen of the same place, to be resolved by secular judgment, B. and certain other clerics of the same place in the Morini diocese make actions be ceded to themselves by some of those laymen either as a gift or for a price, so that they might draw their adversaries to ecclesiastical court and gain profit from such transactions, while those laymen, worn out by the labors and expenses imposed by the same clerics, are forced to settle with them or cede their rights. Since the jurisdiction of the aldermen is thus being circumvented, they humbly implored us to provide apostolic circumspection over this matter. Since the cession and purchase of lawsuits are legitimately prohibited by sanctions, and they are also odious because they seem to arise from the source of greed, we strictly command you by apostolic writings, that by our authority, you prohibit the mentioned clerics from buying such lawsuits or receiving cessions; and if they presume to do so, suppress them from such presumption through ecclesiastical censure, without appeal, when the truth is recognized. If not all of you are able, then two of you— Given at Perugia, the fifth day before the Kalends of February, in the third year of our pontificate.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa abbati Sancti Nicolai Furnensis, preposito de Lee et decano Furnensi mandat, ut clericis Morinensis diocesis prohibeant, ne actiones litium a laicis emant vel recipiant, et si presumpserint, per censuram ecclesiasticam compescant. 1229, Jan. 28. Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Milan and the Bishop of Brescia. Grave complaints have reached us for some time now, concerning you, brother bishop, and our venerable brother, the Bishop of Modena, to whom we entrusted the responsibility of eradicating heretical depravity from the province of Lombardy. In the city of Brescia, which was said to be more seriously corrupted by this depravity, you wished to publicly order the council of Brescia to destroy certain houses where heretics had lived and openly preached after expelling them. M., the vicar of Gerard, a citizen of Modena, who then held the governance of the aforementioned city, along with the consuls, some nobles, and others of the city and diocese of Brescia, refused to listen to you, and boldly opposed us by manifestly allying with the said G., who, on account of his crimes, was excommunicated from the ecclesiastical community and was a known supporter of heretics. They stubbornly adhered and supported these heretics against our prohibition, defiantly rising against God and the church by openly receiving heretics into their homes, fortifying towers against Catholics for them, and aggressively fighting against them. For this reason, by our authority, you pronounced a sentence of excommunication on them. When we understood the audacity of their presumptuousness, we directed our letters to you and our venerable brother, the Bishop of Rimini, regarding the penalty to be inflicted on these presumptuous individuals. Recently, upon you and the noble men, Count Raymond of Mosi, and Raymond of the Hugonis, Tetoccio of Tetocci, Frederick of Lavello Longo, Matthew of Gambara, John of Minervio, Ottolino Meleghette, and Bonaventura of Walando, appearing before us, these noble men earnestly tried to excuse their own faults and those of the absent, asserting that the city of Brescia has been divided into factions for a long time, as is well known. They humbly requested that we deign to relax the aforementioned sentence and revoke the mandates expressed in the letters directed to you and the aforementioned bishop of Rimini. Moreover, the noble men Guido Grosso and Bonoldo de Bonoldis, citizens of Milan, whom the podestà and commune of Milan especially sent to our presence regarding this matter, respectfully petitioned us to take due care for the peace of the aforementioned city. Even though these men who dared to attempt such things have undoubtedly gravely offended, the church should not close its bosom to those who return but rather open it. We have arranged for the benefit of absolution to be granted to the aforementioned noble men who personally came into our presence through you, according to the form of the church, and we have decided to entrust the absolution of the absent to your prudence. Therefore, we command your fraternity by apostolic letters that, after receiving sufficient caution from them, you grant them the benefit of absolution. Then, according to the terms of the aforementioned letters directed to you, brother bishop, and the bishop of Rimini, punishing them by demolishing the towers that fought against the church and Catholics and executing other matters contained in those letters. Yet, considering the offenses of each with prudent deliberation, you may moderate the penalty for the less culpable and aggravate it for the more culpable, as you see fit, ensuring that the churches are adequately compensated for the damages caused to them on this occasion. If there are any among them whose offenses are particularly difficult and severe, you shall send them to the apostolic see to be absolved, and you shall inform us by your letters of the nature of their offense and the penalty that seems appropriately inflictable on them, so that, instructed by your report, we may better do what needs to be done. Given at Rieti, on the Ides of July, in the tenth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Mediolanensi et episcopo Brixiensi mandat, ut, accepta cautione, nobilibus quorumdam excommunicatorum beneficium absolutionis concedant et exsequantur poenas in eos, qui in civitate Brixiensi hereticorum fautores fuerunt, moderantes. Dat. Reate, Idibus Iulii, anno decimo.

To the Abbots of Alderspac' of the Cistercian order and Heidenheim', and the Provost of Speinshart of the Premonstratensian order, of the dioceses of Eichstätt and Regensburg. The beloved sons R., Dean, and H., Scholasticus of Regensburg, on behalf of themselves and the greater and wiser part of their chapter, have informed us through a petition that their church, recently deprived of the solace of a pastor, found the ministerials of said church claiming to have the right to participate in the election of a bishop. They sought to be admitted to the election alongside the chapter. When the chapter convened on the appointed day to elect, the ministerials, presuming to vehemently insert themselves into the election, rashly nominated the senior provost of Regensburg as bishop, demanding with threats that he be given to them. Their fury was so inflamed that many of them would have incurred the danger of death if not protected by the citizens. Eventually, the ministerials deceitfully offered hope of peace to them, and while they remained under such expectation, the said provost, not considering that he had been nominated through the abuse of lay intrusion, with a few canons, during a time when others were asleep, entered the church as bishop, usurping the pontifical chair, and having the bells rung, publicly proclaimed himself as bishop of Regensburg, and thus intruded, conducts himself as their pastor, to their significant prejudice and grievance, for which they were compelled to appeal to the Apostolic See. They humbly requested that we deign to recall this cause to us, lest, if it be entrusted to others, the day may be postponed, to the grave detriment of the church itself. However, Ulric, the procurator for G., elected as bishop of Regensburg, opposing in a public hearing, presented letters stating that when the chapter convened on the first day appointed for the election to discuss the election of a future bishop, and could not agree due to the insolence of laymen, they unanimously set another day and hour for the election. When the elected one and the greater and wiser part of the chapter, having arrived at the appointed place and time, summoned the aforementioned dean and his party, so that, as they had agreed, they would convene with them to discuss the election of a bishop, and those did not care to attend nor to excuse themselves in any way, the greater and wiser part of the said chapter, which had convened with the elected one, fearing the insolence of laymen and seeing the grave danger of delay threatening the church, unanimously elected the said elected one as their bishop and pastor by the grace of the Holy Spirit. But the said dean and his supporters, some of whom had elected the said elected one, opposing his election against justice, appointed some in minor orders against the established and ancient custom of the church, and promoted some to holy orders, and even unlawfully received into the chapter someone released from obedience and another publicly infamous for monastic apostasy, not without fraud and prejudice to the said elected one and his party. Wherefore it was requested that we deign to write to certain discreet persons who might inquire into the election, and if they found it canonical, to have it confirmed by our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Salzburg, his metropolitan. Since it has not been established to us concerning the premises, we command that, having called those who should be summoned, you hear the case, and having sufficiently instructed it, remit it to our presence, setting a term for the parties on the octave of the coming Epiphany, on which they may present themselves before us in person or through fit procurators to deliver a judicial sentence by the authority of God. If not all, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the third Ides of July, in the tenth year [of our pontificate].

Regesto:

Gregorius IX papa Abbatibus de Alderspac' Cisterciensis et de Heidenheim', ac Praeposito de Speinshart' Praemonstratensis ordinum mandat ut vocatis qui fuerint evocandi causam electionis episcopi Ratisponensis audiant, et sufficienter instructam ad sedem apostolicam remittant, partibus terminum prefigentes. 1236, Jul. 13. Lateranum.

To Frederick, abbot of the monastery of Saint Mary in Alchinghen, and to his brothers, present and future, who have professed a regular life forever. New remedies are required for things that are newly recognized, and it is advisable to vary cures according to the diverse and varied ailments. Indeed, our venerable brother, the bishop of Augsburg, your diocesan, has recently informed us through his letters that a certain monk of yours, instigated by the devil whose works he was performing, stole certain privileges granted to your monastery by the apostolic see and handed them over to a certain knight; whose castle, after being captured by his enemies and all goods taken away, returned these privileges to you without the seal, through those into whose hands they had fallen. Although you felt great sadness and grief over this, the said bishop, compassionating your great loss, humbly begged us through the aforementioned letters to renew these privileges. You also, dear son abbot, came to our presence, presenting to us one of those privileges, namely that of Calixtus II, and a transcript of another, namely that of Innocent II, with considerable insistence of prayers, similarly petitioned that provision be made for the monastery concerning such a great danger. Therefore, considering that it should be advised for you, since this was believed to have been attempted to the greater injury of the monastery, and considering furthermore, both from the said privilege of Calixtus and a certain writing found in the register of the aforementioned Innocent, that the said monastery had been offered to the Roman Church by its patrons, namely Countess Berta and her daughter Lenugarda, along with her husband Conrad the Marquis, and their sons Henry, Otto, Theodoric, and Theto, according to the aforementioned privilege of Calixtus, which we found to be true on parchment, in writing and style, with the advice of our brothers, we have deemed it fitting to grant you and your monastery the present privilege, adding certain other common chapters of the monks.
