To Calippus de Ballach to recognize the path of truth. The celestial height of counsel and the immense benevolence of the most high God, etc., as in the letters that are directed to the Sultan of Damascus, which you may find in the eleventh quire of the sixth year, up to the end. In the same manner, it is written to the miramamolino. Given at the Lateran, on the 7th day before the Kalends of June, in the seventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Calippo de Ballach mandat ut viam veritatis agnoscat, simili modo ut in litteris ad soldanum Damasci scriptum est. 1233, Mai. 26. Laterani.

Translation to English:

To the same. If, God forbid, you may not wish to accept what we are sending to your highness through our beloved son, Master I. of Capua, our notary, and through letters, we advise and request your Highness to observe the form of peace which we are having presented to you through him, and, after compensating for damages and removing violences, to not delay in appointing arbitrators, who, together with others chosen by the church, will proceed according to the form of the aforementioned peace, ensuring not to offend by yourself or through others in persons or things those who adhered to the apostolic see during the time of discord until the matter is concluded by the arbitrators. Given as above.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa regi (vel principi) monitionem mittit, ut formam pacis observet et arbitros dirigat ad negotium finiendum. Data ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To all the faithful and vassals of the Church of Cologne. It has come to our attention, etc., as above until: they presume, we command by apostolic letters to your community that, since you are bound to defend the Church of Cologne by your own means and should consider its danger as your own, you should powerfully and faithfully assist against the aforementioned wrongdoers of the church and the archbishop himself, so that the title of sincere faithfulness may shine forth in the aid of defense, and that you may thereby earn praise and grace. However, we do not wish that the process of inquiry, etc., should be delayed. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa universis fidelibus et vassallis ecclesie Coloniensis mandat, ut contra malefactores ecclesie et archiepiscopo potenter fideliterque assistant. Datum ut supra.

Translation to English:

To the Patriarch of Antioch, legate of the Apostolic See. Some time ago, as we recall, in order to remove any cause of contention between you and our venerable brother, the Patriarch of Jerusalem, and to avoid scandal, we instructed both of you to be content with your respective legations within your patriarchates, exempting the kingdom of Cyprus from either's jurisdiction regarding this matter. Therefore, we command you that, whether or not the aforementioned mandate has reached you, you are to be content with exercising the legation office within your own patriarchate. Given at the Lateran, on the 10th of June, in the seventh year of our pontificate.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa Patriarchae Antiocheno mandat ut in suo patriarcatu legationis officio contentus existat, contentionem cum Patriarcha Hierosolymitano vitans. 1233, Iun. 10, Laterani.

Translation to English:

To Masters Hugh of Reims and I. Barat, archdeacons of Châlons, and G. Goin, canon of Reims. Since we have decided to entrust you with the matter of inquiry against our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Cologne, with specific instructions, we command you to diligently admonish and urge the same archbishop, before all else, to wisely consider his own salvation and reputation by providing himself the remedy of resignation; and if he decides to proceed with this, you should accept it on our behalf. Ensure, however, that the prosecution of the matter is not delayed by such admonition. If not all [can proceed], etc. Given at the Lateran, 13th of the Kalends of May, in the seventh year [of our pontificate].

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa magistris Hugoni Remensi et I. Barat Cathaulonensi archidiaconis et G. Goin canonico Remensi mandat, ut archiepiscopum Coloniensem monere studeant, ut cessionem faciat, et si factam duxerit, eandem vice sua recipiant. 1233, Apr. 19, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

Letter from the King of France to the Lord Pope. To the most holy father in the Lord, Gregory, by the grace of God, supreme pontiff. Louis, by the same grace King of the Franks, sends greetings and reverence in the Lord, as much as is due and owed. May your kindness know that we no longer have the counsel to guard the land beyond the Rhône, which is in the territories of the empire, and which our dearest friend R., then legate of the apostolic see, entrusted to our bailiff to guard. We make this known to your paternity through the present letters. Done at Lorrez-le-Bocage, in the year of the Lord 1233, in the month of March.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Ludovico regi Francorum scribit, eum certiorem facere se non habere consilium terram ultra Rodanum custodire, quam sedis apostolicae legatus balivo eius commisit. Actum apud Lorrliacum, Martii 1233.

**Translation to English:**

To the Rectors of the City. Since efforts have been made for a long time to restore peace between the Romans and the people of Viterbo, and now, by the grace of God, peace has been restored among them, we fear that, through the machinations of him who is the author of discord, this peace may be disturbed by certain sons of perdition. Therefore, wishing to consult for the salvation of souls and avert future dangers, we bind with the sentence of excommunication all those who disturb this peace and those who presume to rebuild the Castle of the Monastery or to construct any building there by the authority of Almighty God and the blessed Peter and Paul, and by the power granted to us of binding and loosing. Given at Anagni, 10th of August, in the seventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Rectoribus Urbis mandat ut omnes turbatores pacis inter Romanos et Viterbienses, et qui Castrum Monasterii rehedificare vel aliqua edificia ibidem facere praesumpserint, excommunicatione innodentur. Anagniae, 10 Augusti, anno septimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the communities of the county of Luna. Since it is beneficial for the health of souls and bodies that the bonds of impiety be loosened and oppressive bundles be removed, we command you by the authority of these presents to dissolve the conspiracies which we have heard you have formed to the detriment of the Church of Luna. Fully provide for all the rights of our venerable brother, the bishop of Luna, upon his return with our favor, showing him due and devoted reverence, so that you may find him favorable and us gracious in your times of need. Given at the Lateran, on the 7th day before the Ides of April, in the seventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa communitatibus comitatus Lunensis mandat ut coniurationes in preiudicium ecclesiae Lunensis destructas venerabili fratri Lunensi episcopo, redeunti cum gratia pontificia, de iuribus suis plenarie intendant. 1233, Apr. 7, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To H., provost of Passau. Having appeared in our presence, you humbly asked us that, since you were forced to incur a debt due to being robbed by Eberhard of Porta, a knight, and his accomplices of the diocese of Freising while on your way to the Apostolic See, we might mercifully allow you to pledge your ecclesiastical revenues for up to two years to pay off this debt. Inclined by your devoted prayers, we grant you by the authority of these presents what you have requested, provided that the Church is not in any way defrauded in the duties of your provostship because of this debt. No one, therefore, should infringe upon this concession of ours, etc. If anyone should dare, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the Kalends of July, in the seventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa H. preposito Pataviensi, qui a militibus spoliatus fuerat, concedit, ut redditus suos ecclesiasticos ad biennium obligare possit ad debitum persolvendum. 1234, Kal. Iulii, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Ravenna and the Bishop of Arezzo, and to all abbots, priors, and other prelates and clerics of the churches established in the cities and dioceses of Ravenna and Arezzo. Since our beloved son Iaquintus, our chaplain, etc., as above in CCCCXXXVIIII...

(Note: The text is incomplete, so the translation is based on the provided portion.)

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Ravennati et episcopo Aretino necnon universis abbatibus, prioribus et aliis ecclesiarum prelatis et clericis per civitates et dioceses Ravennatem et Aretinam constitutis nuntiat se Iaquintum capellanum suum misisse. [Data et locus nescia obscurae sunt].

**Translation to English:**

To the elected Bishop of Chur. It has been humbly requested of us on your behalf, since your election as Bishop of Chur was canonically celebrated and properly confirmed by our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Mainz, your metropolitan, and since the Church of Chur is burdened with a heavy debt, that we might grant you the permission to retain, at least for a certain time, the benefices you had previously obtained canonically. Therefore, inclined by the earnest prayers of our most beloved son in Christ, Frederick, Emperor of the Romans, who has petitioned on your behalf, and with the aforementioned facts being true, we grant you the authority, by the present letters, to receive the fruits of those benefices until our pleasure permits. Let no one, therefore, infringe upon our concession, etc. If anyone should attempt, etc. Given at Rieti, on the 13th of July, in the eighth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Honorius III papa electo Curiensi facultatem concedit retinendi beneficia canonice obtenta ad percipiendos fructus usque ad beneplacitum, ecclesia Curiensi debitis gravata. 1224, Iul. 13, Reate.

**Translation to English:**

To those signed with the cross against the heretics of Slavonia located in the regions of Hungary. The Holy Roman Church, etc., to cherish. Since you, inflamed with zeal for the faith and devotion, have taken the sign of the life-giving cross and proposed to proceed to Slavonia against the treachery of the heretics, we, inclined by your just petitions, receive your persons with all the goods you reasonably possess at present under the protection of Saint Peter and ours, decreeing that once you have undertaken this journey of pilgrimage, all these things shall remain intact and undisturbed until it is most certainly known about your return or death. Therefore, let no one infringe on our protection and decree. If anyone, however, etc. Given at Perugia, 17th October, in the eighth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa crucesignatos contra hereticos Sclavonie sub beati Petri et sua protectione suscipit, statuens ut bona eorum integra maneant donec de eorum reditu vel obitu certissime cognoscatur. 1234, Oct. 17, Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Trier. Wishing to provide for the indemnity of the Church of Cologne with paternal care, we have firmly forbidden our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Cologne, from contracting any loan without your consent and agreement while the matter of investigation is pending. He is neither to dare to alienate nor to infeudate nor to mortgage any of the immovable goods of that church. Moreover, we have decreed that he be suspended from the administration of temporalities should he act contrary to these instructions. Therefore, we command you to solemnly publish this prohibition and suspension throughout all markets and places where you deem it expedient. Furthermore, if the Archbishop presumes to act against this, the church itself is not to be held liable for the payment of any money on account of this, and such a contract is to be considered invalid. Given at the Lateran, on the 30th of March, in the seventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Treverensi mandat, ut inhibitiones et suspensiones archiepiscopo Coloniensi firmiter iniunctas publicet, ne absque Treverensis archiepiscopi assensu mutuum contrahat vel bona immobilia alienet, sub poena suspensionis a temporalium administratione. 1234, Mart. 30. Romae, apud Lateranum.

**Translation to English:**

To the authorities and people of Jesi, a spirit of wiser counsel. We do not deny that we are deeply grieved that, not content with your own rights, you have, as we have heard, recklessly abused divine and our patience, extending your hands presumptuously towards the rights of our court. And as if this were not enough, etc., as above up to: manifest. And because the Roman Church did not sufficiently correct you for these things, as the quality of the fault demanded, in order to call you to repentance through patience, because of this the repentant, etc., up to: burdensome, with the excommunicated Auximans, conspiracies, etc., up to: to receive. Otherwise, etc., up to: in orders, that you, the authority and counsel, should publicly announce the excommunicated throughout the whole diocese of Jesi and neighboring parts and make them be more strictly avoided by all as excommunicated, and neighboring churches should be interdicted to you, etc., up to the end. Dated as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa potestati et populo Esino mandat ut excommunicatos per totam diocesem Esinam et partes vicinas nuntient et tanquam excommunicatos faciant evitari. Datum in loco, anno pontificatus eius octavo.

**Translation to English:**

To the provost and chapter of the church of Brandenburg. Considering the just petitions... with consent, we confirm to you by apostolic authority the villages, allods, possessions, rights, and other goods granted to your church with pious and provident liberality, both by our venerable brother the bishop of Brandenburg and his predecessors, as is more fully contained in the letters of the said bishop, as well as by noble men, the Margraves of Brandenburg, and other faithful Christians. We also confirm the liberties and immunities reasonably granted to you by them, and the ancient and reasonable customs of the aforesaid church as observed up to now, as you rightly and peacefully possess them, etc. for greater security of the aforesaid church, we have deemed it appropriate to insert verbatim the tenor of these letters in the present ones. Which is as follows: In the name of the holy and indivisible Trinity. I, Sifridus II, by the grace of God, bishop of the church of Brandenburg... etc. 

**Regesto in Latin:**

Honorius III papa preposito et capitulo ecclesie Brandeburgensis villas, possessiones, iura aliaque bona a Marchionibus Brandeburgensibus aliisque concessa, item libertates, immunitates et consuetudines confirmat. Datum Lateranii, XVIIII Kalendas Ianuarii, anno septimo pontificatus.

**Translation to English:**

To the Provost of Saint Blasius in Brunswick. Since you are said to have been canonically and unanimously elected as Archbishop of Magdeburg by the beloved sons, the chapter of the church of Magdeburg, we grant you the dispensation by the authority of these presents, so that, if this is so, it may be lawful for you to minister in temporal and spiritual matters according to the statutes of the general council, until the election made of you, if it is to be confirmed, is confirmed by the Apostolic See. Given at Anagni, the 10th day before the Kalends of October, in the seventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa preposito Sancti Blasii in Brunswich concedit dispensationem ad ministrandum in temporalibus et spiritualibus, donec electio ad archiepiscopatum Magdeburgensem per sedem apostolicam confirmetur. 1233, Sept. 22. Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the nobleman H[ermannus], landgrave of Thuringia, who has taken the cross. Observing diligently the affection of sincerity, which we believe you possess towards the holy mother church, as your ancestors had towards her, and the zeal of your faith, by which you have been fervently moved at the preaching of our venerable brother, the bishop of Hildesheim, and have taken the sign of the cross against heretics, we deservedly pursue you with the favor of special love and grace and cherish you with paternal benevolence. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, inclined by your devout supplications, we place your person, persisting in the devotion to the church, along with your family, land, and all goods which you reasonably possess at present, under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, granting that they remain whole and undisturbed as long as you piously decide to attend to this kind of business. Let no one violate our protection and decree, etc. If anyone, however, etc. Given at the Lateran, 11th February, in the seventh year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa [H[ermanno] landgravio Thuringiae crucesignato mandat], ut personam eius cum familia, terra et bonis sub protectione beati Petri et sua ponat, manentibus illis integris et quietis. 1234, Feb. 11. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man, William, Count Palatine of Tuscany. We are pleased to express our gratitude for your devoted service to the Apostolic See by bestowing upon you the favor of our grace, so that the more you perceive yourself to be esteemed, the more you may be encouraged to frequent acts of devoted service. Hence, because you have undergone many labors and expenses in your diligent and prompt service to the Holy Roman Church, your mother, for the reverence of the Redeemer, and are eager to accomplish what we can rightfully consider to be pleasing, we, with the counsel of our brothers, receive you, Countess T., your wife, and your children, who remain faithful and devoted to the Apostolic See, along with all your goods, under our special protection and defense and that of the Apostolic See. You, on the other hand, receiving the fortitudes of a steadfast spirit, should effectively persevere in the defense of the Church, as you have laudably begun, having firm hope and confidence that we will not allow you to be overwhelmed by the waves of adversaries, with the Lord's help. Therefore, let no one break our protection and defense. But if anyone should attempt to do so, etc. Given at Perugia, on the 5th day before the Kalends of October, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro Willelmo comiti palatino Tuscie, uxorem eius et filios cum bonis omnibus sub protectione sedis apostolice recipit. 1234, Sept. 27, Perusii.

Translation to English:
The Lord, contemplating plans of peace, whose spirit rests only upon the quiet and humble, detests dissensions and battles, which bring dangers to souls. Therefore, those who diligently and solicitously work to bring discordant parties back to harmony perform a service pleasing to God. It has been made known to us through our beloved sons, the dean and the scholastic of Bremen, that in the archdeaconries annexed to their offices, the people, commonly called Frisians, perpetually battle among themselves as if hating rest, striving with all their might for mutual destruction. In a troubled region, no one dares to approach them to bring about peace or a truce, nor do they allow themselves to be invited to concord by anyone other than great princes or their envoys sent for this purpose, as they consider it indecent and unworthy to be led to this by others. Therefore, wishing, as we are the vicar of Him who is the lover and author of peace, that these people return to the bond of charity, we admonish you to personally approach them on our behalf. Strive to reform the bonds of peace among them, inducing them with diligent admonitions and exhortations, so that through your diligence a peace treaty may be established among them, and you may thereby merit the joys of eternal happiness. If not all, etc. Given at Anagni, January 19, in the sixth year.

Regesto in Latin:
Gregorius IX papa abbati de Ilei Cisterciensis ordinis et archidiaconis Astringie et Herlingie Bremensis diocesis mandat, ut personaliter accedentes inter Frisones pacis federa reforment. 1233, Ian. 19, Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the Patriarch of Aquileia. It would not be easy to recount the madness or the fury of the most wicked Henry of Winkenstein of your diocese, who treacherously captured our venerable brother, the Bishop of Pabenberg, and held him in imprisonment, forcing him through various securities to pay a certain sum of money, and even demolishing a certain castle of the Church of Pabenberg to fulfill his wickedness. We believe that the enormity of this crime, which has been widely spread, is known to you who are nearby. However, we, as much as we can with God, are taking precautions for the indemnity of the Church of Pabenberg, which is of special concern to the Apostolic See. We declare, by apostolic authority, that you are absolved from all bonds of oaths and other securities given to the aforementioned wicked man, insofar as the Church itself is harmed by these, and that you are not bound to their observance. Given at the Lateran, on the 7th Kalends of July, in the seventh year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa patriarche Aquilegensi mandat, ut ab omni vinculo iuramenti aliisque cautionibus Henrico de Winkenstein prestitis, in quibus ecclesia Pabenbergensis leditur, absolutus sit et ad earum observantiam non teneatur. Datum Laterani, 25 Iunii 1233.

**Translation to English:**

To the rectors of the Lombard Society, the powers, and the councils of its cities. Desiring to bring peace to the peoples and to make safe the people of the Savior, because it is our duty to ensure this for all the faithful, we have undertaken in our will to bring the concord, which we have assumed to establish by the help of the Lord between our dearest son in Christ, Frederick, the Roman Emperor, and you, to a beneficial conclusion, dismissing the delay. But because your procurators present before us did not have sufficient mandate for the individual cities of your society to negotiate as per the form of compromise, we, unable to proceed on that matter, have decided to send back the procurators to you. However, lest this matter, from which many dangers might arise, remain in suspense for too long, we command your entire body under the penalty of three thousand marks, etc., as above up to: send solemn procurators for each city of the Lombard Society, the March, and Romagna, etc., as above: under the penalty of six thousand marks of silver, etc. Date as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa rectoribus societatis Lombardie, potestatibus et consiliis civitatum eiusdem mandat ut, sub poena trium milium marcarum, procuratores sollemnes ad concordiam cum Friderico imperatore faciendam destinet. Datum apud [locum non specificatum], [anno pontificatus].

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of Rosazzo in the diocese of Aquileia, from the canon of the major church and the provost of Saint Stephen of Aquileia. Hearing the audacity of such nefarious presumption, etc., as far as it is present there. Since he did not wish to measure his strength nor enumerate virtues to see if he could commit such a crime with impunity and trample the entire body of the church, we strictly command that you publicly announce and ensure that the aforementioned nobleman and all his supporters are avoided with bell tolls and lit candles each Sunday and feast day, declaring them excommunicated. We place their entire land under the strictest interdict, such that no ecclesiastical sacraments are to be conferred there except for the baptism of infants and the penance of the dying. In all places to which this nobleman comes, as long as he remains there, you are to prohibit the celebration of divine services until, with the bishop fully restored to liberty, they offer worthy satisfaction to God and the church and present themselves personally before us with testimony of your letters. If not all, etc. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati Rosacensi et canonicis Aquilegensibus mandat ut nobilem quendam et fautores eius excommunicatos publice nuntient, terramque eorum interdicto supponant, donec episcopus libertati restitutus satisfaciant. Datum Laterani, anno pontificatus tertio.

Translation to English:

To the Archbishop of Salzburg. Out of deep compassion, which, according to the duty of our pastoral office, we hold for the church of Passau, lamenting to us incessantly about countless troubles and distresses, we have been compelled to think more strongly, given its greater necessity, about how we might provide it with a useful shepherd, especially since the canons of the same church, who had been sent to our presence on behalf of themselves and others, have not been able to agree on a single person. And when the favorable name of our venerable brother, the bishop of Chiemsee, was mentioned, and we sensed the sweet fragrance of his reputation, we were pleased with him, as if in his person he were ready to offer helpful guidance to the needy church. Therefore, on the advice of our brothers, providing from our office for the aforementioned bishop of Chiemsee to become bishop of the aforementioned church, so that we might not seem to deny mercy to the desolate church, we command that you absolve him from the care of the church of Chiemsee and transfer him to the aforesaid church, committing to him its spiritual and temporal affairs. Given at the Lateran, on the fifth day before the Kalends of July, in the seventh year [of our pontificate].

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Salzburgensi mandat ut episcopum Chiemensem absolvat et ad ecclesiam Pataviensem transferat, eius cura spiritualia et temporalia committens. 1233, Iun. 27, apud Lateranum.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man, the constable, and the barons and knights of the kingdom of Jerusalem and the citizens of Acre. The agreements made by judgment or concord, etc., to the consent, the settlement which has been amicably arranged between you on one side and our beloved son in Christ, Frederick, ever august Emperor of the Romans, illustrious King of Jerusalem and Sicily, on the other side, through the mediation of our venerable brother, the Patriarch of Antioch, legate of the apostolic see, and our beloved son, the master of the Teutonic House of the Hospital of St. Mary in Jerusalem, which the same emperor later confirmed by his letters, we, considering it ratified and firm, confirm it by apostolic authority as it was rightly and without deceit provided and voluntarily accepted and has been peacefully observed by both parties until now, and we strengthen it by the protection of this present writing. Therefore, let no one infringe upon our confirmation, etc. If anyone, however, etc. Given at the Lateran, 22nd March, in the eighth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobilibus viro comestabulo et baronibus ac militibus regni Ierosolimitani et civibus Acconensibus notificat, se compositionem inter eos et Fridericum imperatorem, mediantibus patriarcha Antiocheno et magistro domus hospitalis sancte Marie Theutonicorum, auctoritate apostolica confirmasse. 1234, Martii 22, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To archbishops, bishops, abbots, priors, deans, archdeacons, and other prelates of churches, to whom these letters may come. Among the countless duties by which we are continuously pressed, since we cannot attend to everything by ourselves, we sometimes delegate certain tasks to those whose proven faith and diligence inspire our complete confidence. Therefore, as we send our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Ravenna, legate of the Apostolic See, whose merits in integrity effectively encourage us to entrust him with our roles in difficult matters, to the overseas regions for the business of the Holy Land, we ask the entirety of your community, commanding through apostolic writings, that since the sending person can either be despised or honored in the person of the sent one, as the testimony of Truth asserts what is done to one of the least of His is done to Him, you kindly receive and treat him honorably, and liberally provide for his necessities, so that in his person you may demonstrate by your deeds the due affection of devotion towards us, and thereby render us more favorable and gracious to you. Otherwise, any sentence he may justly pass on the rebellious because of this will be confirmed by us and, by the authority of the Lord, will be firmly observed until proper satisfaction is made. Given at Spoleto, 9th August, in the eighth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopis, episcopis, abbatibus, prioribus, decanis, archidiaconis et aliis ecclesiarum prelatis mandat, ut legatum suum, archiepiscopum Ravennatem, pro negotio Terre Sancte missum, benigne suscipiant et in necessariis provideant, alioquin sententiam quam ipse in rebelles tulerit confirmaturum. 1234, Aug. 9, Spoleto.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man G., Count Palatine, [we wish] the spirit of sound counsel. As your envoys, the beloved sons Amator the knight and E. the judge, whom we kindly received, presented in our presence, you, inspired by the one from whom all good things proceed and to whom belongs all that is best, have conceived in the spirit of salvation to put forth your hand to great deeds and to serve the Roman Church, your mother, showing a ready willingness to serve in person and resources. We, therefore, confident in the power of Him who encompasses and holds all things in His hand, and considering it easy to confront the calumnies of the enemies, commend your salutary plan in the Lord, and wishing that the effect of such a salutary intention should increase the fruits of your devotion, we, with the counsel of our brothers, receive you, persisting in the faithfulness and devotion to the Apostolic See, with all your goods under our special protection and defense and that of the Apostolic See. You, indeed, receiving the fortifications of a steadfast mind, should brace yourself valiantly for your and the Church's defense, having firm hope and confidence that, with the Lord's help, we will by no means allow you to be overwhelmed by the attacks of adversaries. Therefore, no one is allowed to infringe upon our protection, etc. If anyone, however, etc. Given at Rieti, July 26, in the eighth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro G. comiti palatino commends propositum salutare et recipit eum cum bonis suis sub protectione speciali sedis apostolicae. 1234, Iul. 26. Reate.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man John of Bellino, the spirit of sound counsel. Know that it has come to our ears that you, led astray by unjust suggestion, have gravely offended our dearest son in Christ, Frederick, the illustrious Roman Emperor, ever august, and King of Jerusalem and Sicily, by not showing due deference to the imperial majesty and not taking precautions to avoid this difficult situation. Because an appropriate remedy should be applied to a wound, we earnestly advise and exhort your nobility, and faithfully counsel you, that since it is known to be more prudent, you should satisfy him through your own initiative without coercion. Do not delay in sending suitable envoys to offer voluntary reparation for the damages and injuries inflicted. For we will take care, with fatherly concern, to ensure your safety and that of yours and to restore you to his favor as appropriate. But if any doubt from our counsel might have held you back, at least willingly commit yourself to our decision and offer to make amends to the aforementioned Emperor as the Roman Church shall direct. Otherwise, since we neither can nor should fail him in justice, in which we are indebted to others, we shall be compelled to exercise the severity of justice upon you according to the office entrusted to us by God, and you may bring upon yourself the risks of your obstinacy. Given at Arrone, on the seventh Ides of August, in the eighth year.
