To avoid being accused of allowing a worthy lamp to be kept under a basket, particularly when it is known from evident signs that it emits many rays of brightness from heaven, we command, by apostolic writing and in the virtue of obedience, your discretion to ensure that the inquiry into the miracles of blessed memory, Elizabeth, Landgravine of Thuringia, which we mandated to be conducted by our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Mainz, and the late Master Conrad of Marburg, be sent to our presence via solemn envoys, whose merits should befit the significance of such an important matter, within five months after the receipt of these letters. However, if the aforementioned inquiry is not yet at hand, having before your eyes the reverence of divine majesty, you shall diligently examine with the appropriate solicitude the same witnesses whom the said archbishop and master received concerning the miracles of Elizabeth, or others if you can find credible ones, calling upon prudent men and those knowledgeable in law. You shall faithfully cause their statements and the sequence of testimony to be written word for word, so that we may be instructed about the gift of grace which the Lord seems to have poured out upon his daughter of gratitude. You shall take care to send these writings to us under your seals and those of the prelates and religious men, within the specified months, setting aside all excuses. If not all of you can act, then you, brother bishop, with one of them, should proceed. Given at Perugia, 11th October, in the eighth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Ildesemensi et abbatibus de Valle sancti Georgii et Hervedensi mandat ut inquisitionem de miraculis beatae Helysabeth langraviae Thuringiae conficiant et ad sedem apostolicam mittant. 1234, Oct. 11. Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To the rectors of the Lombard Society. We recall having written to your prudence that, at the request of our dearest son in Christ, Frederick, the ever August Emperor of the Romans, who declared himself ready to comply with the Church’s desires and to correct all actions presumed by his envoys against the peace agreement, we should send two of our brethren to his presence, and would later inform you of the actions to be taken regarding the aforementioned matters. We now decided to inform your devotion through the present letter that the aforementioned emperor, after the reception of the aforementioned cardinals, promised to correct all actions attempted by his envoys against the peace agreement and has already corrected some of them. Furthermore, considering that we regard you as special sons of the Church and that you cannot be offended without offending the Church, the same emperor, by imperial letters bearing the imprint of the golden bull, whose transcript we send enclosed with the present letters, committed the entire business of Lombardy, the March, and Romagna to the provision, arrangement, and disposition of the Church, promising that he would always confirm whatever is ordered between him and you by the same Church. Therefore, we command that if you wish to do the same, you should inform us with your open letters. Lest any obstacle may arise to impede such a great good, we sincerely ask and urge you through apostolic writings, commanding that you do not disturb the emperor and his men in any way, either by yourselves or through others, and take care that if soldiers from Germany are preparing to come to the presence of the same emperor, you do not burden them with any impediments, lest he should have just cause for murmuring against us and you, from whom such doubt is not deserved. Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Nones of May, in the eighth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa rectoribus societatis Lombardie significat Fridericum imperatorem promisse corrigere quod contra formam pacis a nuntiis suis fuit attemptatum et negotium Lombardie, Marchie ac Romaniole ecclesie commisisse. Eos hortatur ne imperatorem et suos turbare studeant et mandatum suum litteris patentibus confirment. Datum Laterani, IIII Non. Maii, anno octavo.

**Translation to English:**

To the same. To the most holy father, etc. Concerning the land beyond the Rhône in the parts of the empire, which we held and guarded for some time with your will, we remember having previously requested your fatherhood, upon deliberation with our council, to have that land restored to our beloved and faithful kinsman, R. Count of Toulouse, who, along with his ancestors, possessed it in times past. We are confident that by this act he will be inclined to maintain the peace of the Church in those parts and to serve us more devotedly; we are particularly motivated by the fact that the aforementioned count has no heir except a single daughter, who is to be matrimonially united with our dearest brother by your dispensation. For this reason, we seek this grace as something beneficial to us and ours. Therefore, we have decided once again to ask your kindness to restore the aforementioned land to the aforementioned count, in the hope that, with God's consent, devotion will result from this. We also consider, as we have learned from the testimony of the prelates of those parts, that he has diligently, faithfully, and devotedly sought out heretics and punished them in honor of God and the holy Church. Therefore, it seems good and beneficial to us and our council to extend such grace to him that he may become more devoted to God and the holy Church. We also ask your fatherhood with affection to kindly and favorably hear the aforementioned count in his other just petitions for our sake. Given at Loyracum on the day after the feast of St. Gregory.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa rogavit sanctissimum patrem restitui terram ultra Rhodanum comiti Tolosano, quae tempore aliquo in manu sua tenuit, confidentes in pace ecclesiae et servitio suo; item quia filiam unicam habet, quae fratri carissimo matrimonialiter copulanda est. Preterea commendavit diligentiam comitis in perquirendis et puniendis haereticis. Dat. apud Loiriacum in crastino sancti Gregorii, 1230, Mart. 13.

**Translation to English:**

To Frederick, ever august Emperor of the Romans, illustrious King of Jerusalem and Sicily. With what faith and devotion you should please the mother church, dearest son, we deem it unworthy to explain in writing, since it is evident to you by manifold arguments. Thus, having recourse to express the urgency of necessity, as we have firm hope and secure confidence that you consider what affects the church as your own, whether they seem adverse or prosperous, we earnestly ask, advise, and exhort your majesty to prudently consider that without the injury of the son, the mother cannot be harassed by the wickedness of the wicked, especially as they should mutually shine with honor like a lamp shining with contained light. Therefore, to quell the pride of the unruly who, like madmen, attempt to attack and wickedly think to trample the dignity of both the church and the empire, with hope set before them that neither heavenly power nor human might can bring down their arrogance or thwart their obstinacy, you should without delay come near to our presence, so that resisting the impious with a triumphant right hand, you may fill the face of the fools with ignominy, and you, in the farthest reaches of the earth, may shine with the title of power to the glory of both yourself and your mother. Furthermore, because the nature of such a business admits no obstacle of exception, we wish that even if it seems to arise from imminent affairs for you, do not bring it forth, but rise up to avenge our and your injury, knowing that if divine power, in your strength, breaks the horns of such proud ones, those matters which appear contrary to your good pleasure will be easily expedited. Given at Anagni, III Nones of February, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Fridericum, Romanorum imperatorem, monet et hortatur ut ad defendendam ecclesiam contra improbos ad loca vicina se conferat, et iniuriam vindicet, promittens facilitatem in negotio si divina potentia superborum cornua confringat. 1232, Febr. 3. Datum Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Osnabrück and the provosts of the major church and of St. Gereon in Cologne. Know that it has come to our attention that the most wicked sons of the late Frederick, Count of Isenburg in the diocese of Cologne, against whom the voice of blood of the piously remembered late Archbishop of Cologne cruelly slain by him cries out to the Lord from the earth, have emerged like venomous little serpents from the root of a snake. Together with W., the brother of the said count from the same diocese, they succeed him in wickedness and follow his nefarious ways. Despite their contempt for divine fear and joining with certain accomplices to more freely exercise their malice, they ruthlessly persecute, oppress, and afflict the Church of Cologne and its archbishop. Their pride, not knowing how to be tamed, increases gravely until justice from above anticipates and subverts it. Therefore, we order that the faculty for evil be rather withdrawn than given to their harmful will, for they, having lifted their hearts against the Lord, presume to boldly provoke Him and the church with a spirit hardened towards arrogance. We command you to restrain these evildoers and their accomplices and supporters from such excessive presumption by ecclesiastical censure so that the inquiry process which we ordered concerning the aforementioned archbishop may not be delayed. What if not all of you — you, brother bishop, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the 17th day before the Kalends of July, in the seventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Osnaburgensi ac maioris ecclesiae et Sancti Gereonis Coloniensis praepositis mandat ut filios Friderici comitis de Isenburg complicesque eorum, qui ecclesiam Coloniensem et archiepiscopum persequuntur, per censuram ecclesiasticam compescant. 1234, Iun. 15, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz, the Bishop of Hildesheim, and Brother Conrad, Provincial Prior of the Order of Preachers in Teutonia. We are saddened and deeply disturbed that Teutonia, which has thus far bloomed with the verdant fragrance of Catholic faith and the piety of good works, now appears filled with the thorns of heresies and tainted with the filth of vices. If the Lord had not left a seed of blessing, sincere men and zealous defenders of the faith, the task of its correction would be uncertain and perhaps hopeless. However, as we have truly discovered, you and other prelates and persons of the churches, as well as brothers of the Order of Preachers, are diligently working to heal its pain and cure its swelling, like the evangelical Samaritan, pouring wine and oil onto its wounds. You are effectively aided by those who work for the work of God and the public good. Therefore, we rightly believe that the matter of faith now prospers in the hands of such individuals, whom we might have feared due to the enormity of crimes and the multitude of perverse ones. We therefore command that you, along with religious men who fear God and are skilled in law, proceed in the examination, condemnation, and reconciliation according to the form of the general council and the statutes recently issued by us, taking care that the audacity of the perverse is punished in such a way that the purity of innocence is not harmed. We mandate, by our authority, to all to whom this matter of faith has been entrusted, that they should not delay in proceeding according to the prescribed form and statutes; contradictors etc. If not all etc., two of you etc. Given at Anagni, XII Kalends of November, in the seventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino, episcopo Ildesemensi et fratri Conrado, ordinis Predicatorum provinciali priori in Teutonia mandat, ut cum religiosis et peritis in iure viris procedant ad examinationem, condemnationem et reconciliationem hereticorum secundum formam concilii generalis et statuta nuper edita, curantes ut audacia perversorum puniatur sine labe innocentium. Dat. Anagnie, XII Kal. Novembris, anno septimo.

**Translation to English:**

The cause of appeal of the Archbishop of Cologne. One cause is that they refused to provide the Archbishop with authentic letters so that a comparison could be made with the transcript and the injustice would be more manifest, nor did they specify the chapters on which inquiry was to be made, which were inserted in the apostolic letters in general, not in specific terms. Another reason is that an excommunication was imposed against the Bishop of Lausanne, namely the canon which he incurred before and after he recently returned from the court, due to the violent laying of hands on clerics. Another is the cause of suspicion, because he led relatives and family members of the killer of Archbishop Engelbert, against whom this Archbishop took vengeance, to pursue and attack the same Archbishop. Another is because he wrote to certain adversaries of the Church of Cologne and friends of the killer, advising them to be assured of the removal of the Archbishop. Against the Dean of Liège, an objection was made that due to disobedience and the schism he initiated in his church, and because of his other excesses, he was excommunicated by the Bishop of Liège. Another is that the Dean conspired with other friends of the killer of Archbishop Engelbert against the Archbishop of Cologne, so that either through inquiry or by any means he would be removed from the Church of Cologne. Against the Archdeacon of Cambrai, an excommunication was imposed by his bishop.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorii IX papae archiepiscopo Coloniensi causas appellationis explicat, quae comprehendunt recusationem litterarum authenticorum, impositionem excommunicationis contra episcopum Lausanensem propter violentiam, suspicionis causam ob coniurationem cum cognatis interfectoris Engelberti, et scriptura ad adversarios de remotione archiepiscopi. Contra decanum Leodiensem ob inobedientiam et schisma obiecta est excommunicatio, et conspiratio cum amicis interfectoris. Contra archidiaconum Cameracensem excommunicatio obiecta est. Datum Laterani, III Nonas Maii, anno VI.

(Note: The date and place are inferred, assuming the usual location and format for such papal documents, and the sixth year of Gregory IX's pontificate would be 1232, but one would need to verify the specific date based on the calendar.)

Translation to English:

To the provost of Tilensil of the diocese of Utrecht, the schoolmaster, and the treasurer of Saint Severin of Cologne. Our beloved sons, the provosts of the churches of the Holy Apostles and Saint George of Cologne, have informed us that our venerable brother, the bishop of Semigallia, was sent as a legate from the Apostolic See to the parts of Livonia, and while passing through the city of Cologne, he received a procuration of thirteen marks for two days. Subsequently, through a certain cleric of his, he instructed them to provide a good palfrey and a sumpter horse for him and send them to the abbot of Altenberg in the diocese of Cologne in his name; otherwise, they were to ensure their presence before him on the eve of the forthcoming feast of Saint Mary Magdalene. When the same provosts sent both the palfrey and the sumpter horse to the said abbot for the work of the bishop, the abbot returned them according to his will. Although the aforementioned provosts, fearing that the said bishop might proceed against them on this account, appealed to the Apostolic See, afterwards the same cleric returned to them asserting that the oft-mentioned bishop had pronounced a sentence of excommunication against them for not appearing before him by the appointed time and ordered them to be publicly announced as excommunicated unless they arranged to pay nine marks for the sumpter horse and six for the palfrey in the name of the bishop, which they refused to do, since they believed no credit should be given to the words of the same cleric, as he showed no mandate from the bishop and had previously left the Apostolic See furtively due to the crime of falsehood he had committed. Therefore, we were humbly entreated to revoke whatever the aforementioned bishop might have decreed against them in this matter out of the kindness of the Apostolic See. Since the same bishop had received no jurisdiction from us over these provosts, we command you, that if this is the case, to declare any sentences of excommunication pronounced by the said bishop against them to be utterly null. Given at the Lateran, the 22nd of April, in the seventh year of our pontificate.

Regesto:

Gregorius IX papa preposito Tilensil Traiectensis diocesis, scolastico et thesaurario Sancti Severini Coloniensis mandat ut, si episcopus Semigalliensis in eos sententias excommunicationis protulerit, eas nullas esse penitus nuntient. 1233, Laterani, 22 Aprilis.

Translation to English:

"To all abbots and priors of exempt monasteries and their convents established throughout the provinces of Mainz, Trier, and Cologne. Desiring to make known to you our status and that of the Church, we have entrusted it to our beloved son, Master Peter de Supino, our scribe, in whose fidelity and discretion we have sincere confidence, to fully and faithfully explain to you. Therefore, having understood what he has chosen to propose on our behalf to your community, take care to provide in such a way that in this time of urgent need, we may come to know more certainly the devotion of your affection through your deeds and experience more fully how much you are zealous for the freedom and honor of the Church by your actions. Whatever then each of you deems should be done about this matter, ensure that it is communicated to us through him by your open letters. Given at Perugia, II Kalends of December, in the eighth year of our pontificate."

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa universis abbatibus et prioribus monasteriorum exemptorum in Maguntina, Treverensi et Coloniensi provinciis constitutis mandat, ut statum suum et ecclesiae per magistrum Petrum de Supino cognoscant et devotionem suam operibus ostendant, ac de facto nobis litteris suis per eum intiment. Datum Perusii, II Kalendas Decembris, anno pontificatus nostri octavo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Bamberg. Given that you must hasten with your knights to the service of the Apostolic See in this urgent time of need, and you claim to be unable to settle the debts you owe to the Sienese merchants, we grant you by the authority of these presents that, once you have set out on your journey for this service, you cannot be summoned regarding these debts through apostolic letters for up to a year, unless they explicitly mention these presents. Therefore, let no one infringe upon our concession, etc. Should anyone attempt, etc. Given at Perugia, 16th day before the Kalends of February, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Babembergensi indulget, ut post iter ad servitium sedis apostolicae iniens, non conveniatur super debitis mercatoribus Senensibus per annum, nisi expressa mentio fiat. Perusii, anno VIII, XVII Kal. Feb.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Milan. The beloved son Ph., minister of the hospital of Brolio in Milan, presented himself in our presence, stating that a multitude of both men and women from the city of Milan, for the remedy of their souls, had long ago established a certain fraternity, which they called a school, with the foresight that they would gather once a month to hear the word of God at the aforementioned hospital and contribute from the goods granted to them by God as grateful support and pious alms to the benefit of the poor lying there. Now, as we have learned, with the cooling of human charity, such a fraternity has fallen into disuse, with no one gathering at the said hospital, causing the hospital, where the poor coming from anywhere are received and their necessities of life are administered with gladness, to be reduced almost to nothing. Since we more willingly encourage the love of piety, by which divine favor can be more abundantly obtained, which is capable of acquiring grace in the present and glory in the future through all pious deeds, we command you, at least once a month, either personally or through another suitable person, to go to the aforementioned hospital and there deliver or have delivered the word of God, encouraging the faithful gathered there to acts of piety and to provide support to the poor according to the old custom, so that through these and other good deeds, which they will undertake inspired by the Lord, they may attain the joys of eternal happiness. To induce the faithful more effectively to this, we, relying on the mercy of Almighty God and the authority of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul, mercifully grant a relaxation of ten days from the penance imposed on all truly penitent and confessed persons who go there and extend a hand of mercy to the same poor at each such preaching. Given at the Lateran, on the sixth day before the Ides of February, in the seventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Mediolanensi mandat, ut semel in mense ad hospitale de Brolio accedens verbum Dei proponat, fideles ad pietatem et subsidium pauperum, iuxta antiquam consuetudinem, inducendo; omnibus accedentibus decem dierum indulgentiam concedit. 1234, Feb. 8, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To Frederick, ever august Emperor of the Romans, illustrious King of Jerusalem and Sicily. To the beloved sons, masters Benedict and Peter of San Germano, judges of the imperial court, whose diligence and care we can rightly commend, appointed in our presence to negotiate the concord that, with God's help, we have undertaken to establish between your excellence and the Lombards. Although sufficient documents were brought forth on your behalf, since the envoys of the Lombards sent to our presence to negotiate peace according to the form of the agreement did not have sufficient mandate, we, unable to proceed on these matters, have decided to send back the same procurators to them with a certain form of mandate, as can be clarified by the tenor of the document which the bearers of these presents will deliver to you. Therefore, we order your excellence, under the penalty of three thousand marks of silver, to send to our presence, within fifteen days after the upcoming Feast of the Lord's Resurrection, solemn procurators sufficiently instructed and holding a sufficient mandate to negotiate the said matter, especially concerning the articles contained in the agreement, and to hear, receive, and carry out whatever we shall decide regarding the same matter, or to fulfill all matters both generally and specifically required by the form of the agreement and that can legitimately be expedited by the office of procuration. Furthermore, under the penalty of six thousand marks of silver, we strictly prohibit your highness from doing or causing anything to be done in the meantime, by which the matter of peace could be impeded. Otherwise, if you act contrary, know that in addition to appropriate compensation for damages, you will incur the aforementioned penalty. Given at Anagni, 7th day before the Kalends of February, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Friderico Romanorum imperatori mandat sub poena trium milium marcarum procuratores sufficienter instructos ad tractandum de concordia cum Lombardis mittere, et sub poena sex milium marcarum prohibet ne pacis negotium impediatur. 1233, Ian. 26. Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Naumburg, the provost of Zeitz of the diocese of Naumburg, and master I. Cemece, the scholastic of Halberstadt. We have been informed by the noble man, the duke of Bavaria, that the monastery of Lorsch, over which he claims to have the right of patronage and advocacy, once flourished spiritually and was abundant in temporal goods. Our venerable brother, the archbishop of Mainz, the local diocesan, suggested to us that due to the wickedness of its inhabitants, the monastery had fallen into such poverty that it scarcely provided sustenance for anyone, and could only be reformed by monks of the Cistercian order. He obtained a mandate through our letters to expel the monks residing there and introduce monks of the aforementioned order, suppressing the opposition by ecclesiastical censure, setting aside any appeals. Considering it permissible under such letters, he endangered the monastery more through destruction than applied efforts for its reform, seeking his own interests over those of the Lord. The abbot and monks were violently expelled, and certain spacious possessions, including a castle, were appropriated for his use, instituting only four monks of the said order there. The mentioned noble, objecting to the desolation of the aforementioned monastery as was his concern, appealed to our hearing. The archbishop, disregarding this appeal, pronounced sentences of excommunication upon him and interdict upon his lands. Therefore, he requested that the apostolic see provide assistance to him and to the monastery regarding this matter. We strictly command you, through apostolic writings, that if this is so, release the said sentences of excommunication and interdict according to the form of the Church. Personally go to the place, diligently inquire into the truth of the aforementioned matters, and faithfully inform us of your findings through your letters; notwithstanding letters obtained for this purpose by Ildesheim and his co-judges. The witnesses, etc. If not all of you can go—, then two of you, etc. Given at Perugia, on the 16th day before the Kalends of November, in the eighth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Nuemburgensi, preposito Cicensi Nuemburgensis diocesis et magistro I. Cemece scolastico Alberstadensi mandat, ut inquisita veritate de expulsionibus et destitutionibus in monasterio Laurisensi, sententias excommunicationis et interdicti relaxent, et quod invenerint per litteras referant. 1234, Oct. 17. Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To the Rectors of the City. It was previously suggested to us that certain laypersons of the City, having zeal for God but not according to correct knowledge, presumed by their own recklessness to establish certain fraternities without the permission of the Apostolic See. They conducted certain solemnities around the bodies of the deceased, created their own treasurers and rectors to oversee these matters, and frequently gathered to observe their statutes, holding feasts at certain times to the detriment of the clergy of the long-approved fraternities of the City. We, fearing that under their pretext the simple might be led into error, ordered these fraternities not to be observed until, after examining the circumstances of the matter, we could decide otherwise.

However, the nobleman Pandulf of Subura and certain other Roman citizens presented many arguments in our presence for observing the aforementioned fraternities. Wishing to proceed with maturity in this matter, we instructed the primicerius of the City and his colleagues by our letters to examine the documents presented before us, which we sent enclosed under seal, to hear what was proposed before them, and to investigate the truth of the whole matter, reporting their findings to us in writing. They, having called those who needed to be summoned, received and examined the documents presented before them, and after hearing the advice of various individuals, faithfully reported their findings to us for examination.

Therefore, we carefully examined the writings presented to us and certain scriptures which they called a rule, as well as letters from almost all the prelates and chapters of the City sent to us on this matter. Fearing lest any leaven of perversity should ferment the unleavened bread of sincerity, and having held diligent deliberation with our brothers and upon their advice, we utterly nullify these fraternities and command that they are in no way to be observed henceforth, with the clergy's fraternity enduring in its strength. We decree that no other fraternity than the aforementioned clergy's fraternity is to be presumed in the City hereafter. Clerics who presume otherwise and churches where such deceased bodies are buried are to be subjected to the sentence of interdict, which cannot be lifted without the special mandate of the Roman Pontiff. Let no one, therefore, etc. If anyone, however, etc. Given at the Lateran, April 8, in the seventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa rectoribus Urbis mandat ut fraternitates laicorum sine apostolica sedis licentia constitutas penitus irritentur et non serventur, clericorum fraternitate manente, sub poena interdicti. 1234, Apr. 8, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the same. By other letters, we have deemed it necessary to earnestly ask and admonish your Serenity, and through our beloved son, Master P. de Collemedio, provost of Saint Omer, our chaplain, a prudent and discreet man, accepted by us and our brothers by virtue of his merit, we have instructed him to exhort you to preserve the land of Venusia for the honor of the Church, out of reverence for us and blessed Peter, until an inquiry is made about it by the same. However, if by chance the royal majesty has irrevocably decided otherwise in her mind, so that you are unwilling to retain it any longer, we wish that you would resign it in our name to the aforementioned master, always saving the rights of anyone in all things. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa regiam celsitudinem rogat ut terram Venusinam ad honorem ecclesiae conservet aut, si noluerit, eam magistro P. de Collemedio resignet; iura omnium salva. Datum ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the Rectors of the Lombard Society. We remind you that we previously informed you through other letters that our beloved son in Christ, Frederick, the Roman Emperor, has fully submitted himself to our decision regarding the entire matter that is pending between him and you, and he has also promised to rectify anything his officials have attempted against the terms of the peace agreement. However, you have not yet provided us with any response on this matter. Moreover, given the various and different disturbances against the Roman Church by the Romans, such that the Apostolic See could not avoid using the aid of the imperial arm without its own disgrace, the said emperor, coming into our presence, voluntarily offered himself for the defense of the Roman Church and its patrimony, as he was particularly obliged to do. Thus, since the assistance of soldiers was necessary for this, we directed our writings to you to grant them free passage, about which you are fully informed of how it proceeded. But since you cannot be offended without offending the Apostolic See, which considers you its honorable members and special sons, you should not be moved in any way, nor can you ever doubt that we should lay aside the paternal affection with which we embrace you with sincere love; therefore, you lose nothing, but rather gain, if the Roman Church, your mother, is preserved in its freedom and due honor, especially since we, aspiring from the depths of our heart and mind to your benefits, do not cease to think of opportune counsel for the beneficial preservation of your state. Therefore, we urge your devotion, mandating through apostolic writings that, considering our pure intention, you, as prudent and discreet men, quickly write back to us your will regarding the aforementioned matter, secure in our and the Apostolic See's favor, which we intend to show you in all things as far as we can with God. Given at Rieti, 3rd July, in the eighth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa rectoribus societatis Lombardie mandat ut super negotio cum Friderico imperatore inter eos pendente suam voluntatem cito rescribant, promittens favorem apostolice sedis. Datum Reate, V Non. Iulii, anno pontificatus octavo.

**Translation to English:**

To the people of Osimo, a spirit of wiser counsel. Your actions, etc., provoke us. You, however, imprudent abusers of divine and our patience, to say nothing of other excesses, impudently aligned yourselves, having violated the religion of faith, with the noble man Rinaldo, son of the late Conrad, Duke of Spoleto, who was at that time excommunicated and an enemy of God and the Church, misusing the sweetness of your mother, attracting several accomplices in your perversion to amplify the wickedness of your rebellion. Adding sin to sin as scales one to another, like children of ingratitude, nay as wicked enemies, you did not blush to rise up against your parents, working great disgrace upon your mother church of Osimo and your father, our venerable brother, the bishop of Osimo, by burning houses of the church and plundering the chamber of the bishop, holding the bishop himself by force and releasing him only with given pledges and securities, for which deeds you undoubtedly incurred the sentence of excommunication. Not content with this, you presumed to forbid to the bishop and to the clergy of Osimo common and necessary commerce of the city, wherefore you damningly incurred the sentence of excommunication pronounced by our predecessor, Pope Honorius, of happy memory, at the time of the coronation of our beloved son in Christ, Frederick. And as if this were not enough, turning your hand against the very lifeblood of the Roman Church, your mother, you knowingly reinstated Frederick, called Testa, who had been marked by manifold excommunication and had governed your city, contrary to the prohibition and ban of our beloved son, John, cardinal priest of the title of St. Praxedes, rector of the March; by the malice of him and his brother, with the Anconitans and the people of Jesi you conspired, etc. Until you remove Frederick completely from the governance of the city, let your syndic with six of the leading men of the city, having full mandate from the community, etc., appear. Otherwise, you may rightly fear being deprived of the episcopal seat, of which you render yourselves unworthy, knowing that we have given a mandate by our letters to our venerable brother, the bishop of Jesi, and to our beloved son, Master Cesarius, the rector’s deputy, to proclaim you, Frederick, and the council excommunicated throughout the diocese of Osimo and nearby parts without delay, and to have you avoided by all as excommunicated, and to forbid commerce with neighboring cities to you, etc. Given as above. It is written on this matter to the same.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa populo Auximano mandat, ut a rebellione et peccatis desistat et Fredericum Testam a regimine civitatis removeat, alias sede episcopali privandos formidet, datis litteris episcopo Esino et magistro Cesario ad excommunicationem nuntiandam. Datum Anconae.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot and dean of Saint Gregory in the diocese of Basel. The beloved sons, the abbot and the convent of the monastery of Lützel, which is said to belong directly to us without any intermediary, have informed us that the noble man, the Count of Montbéliard in the diocese of Besançon, has occupied the monastery with all its goods designated for the use of the monks, devastated and carried off all movable goods found there, and violently expelled the monks. Our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Besançon, the diocesan of the place, has pronounced sentences of excommunication against him and interdict over his land by his own authority, which the prior of Saint Paul's and the treasurer of Besançon have commanded to be observed by apostolic authority until suitable satisfaction is given. However, as the malice of his heart is blinded and he could not be induced to provide satisfaction, the prior and the cantor of Saint Mary Magdalene in Besançon, having received our mandate that, notwithstanding the indulgence by which the canons of the church of the castle of Montbéliard declare that they should not cease from divine offices due to the count's fault unless he is present in the same castle, solemnly renewed these sentences near the surrounding areas, especially at the aforementioned castle. Furthermore, as instructed by their mandate, they aggravated these sentences, prohibiting ecclesiastical burial throughout his land and in places where the count stayed, divine services were not to be celebrated as long as he was there and for five days after his departure, forbidding anyone to attend the markets of his land, grind at his mills, or bake at his ovens. However, when he still did not wish to repent and seek the face of the Lord and implore the remedies of salvation, the said abbot and convent humbly petitioned us to make firm the process of the aforementioned prior and cantor. Therefore, we command you, if this is so, to make it be observed inviolably under apostolic obedience until appropriate satisfaction is rendered, as it is legitimate. Given at the Lateran, 4th of the Kalends of May, in the seventh year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati et decano Sancti Gregorii Basiliensis diocesis mandat, ut processum prioris et cantoris Sanctae Mariae Magdalenae Bisuntinae adversus comitem Montis Belligardis, qui monasterium Lutrense occupavit et devastavit, firmum faciant observandum usque ad satisfactionem condignam. 1233, Apr. 28. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the prior and brothers of the Order of Preachers of Worms. It behooves us to direct special attention to removing disputes, which are often accompanied by fraternal hatred and hinder the peace and progress of religious communities, although we are generally bound to embrace the peace of all the faithful and seek it by virtue of the office of administration entrusted to us. On your part, it was presented before us that once a dispute had arisen between you on one side and our venerable brother, the bishop, and our beloved sons, the chapter of Worms, on the other, concerning certain plots of land which you purchased in the city of Worms for building and dwelling, and after a certain settlement was made between you by our beloved son Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere Tulliano, then legate of the apostolic see, and the arrangement which the dean of Trier and his co-judges appointed by us made, finally such an amicable agreement came to pass between you and the said bishop, namely that the aforementioned bishop granted you and your successors the authority and consent to purchase land or a place to build a church and cloister and to inhabit, wherever you wish within the walls of the same city, except in the place where you previously had plots, saving in other respects the aforementioned arrangement, reserving the due rent to him in the place you choose to buy and build, as is more fully contained in the letters made thereon. Wherefore you have humbly petitioned us to deign to strengthen this agreement with an apostolic safeguard. We, therefore, inclined by your devoted prayers, supplementing if there is any defect due to the fact that the consent of the aforementioned chapter did not join in the last composition, by the fullness of our power, confirm the same agreement, as it has been provided without malice and voluntarily received by both parties, with apostolic authority, etc., up to: we strengthen. Therefore, let no one infringe on our confirmation etc. But if anyone should, etc. Given at Anagni, on the 10th of February, in the sixth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa priori et fratribus ordinis fratrum Predicatorum Warmaciensium mandat compositionem inter eos et episcopum Warmaciensem de quibusdam areis emendis infra muros civitatis auctoritate apostolica confirmatam roborare. 1232, Feb. 10, Anagnie.

Translation to English:

To all our faithful established throughout Sabina. Since the entire land of Sabina is under the jurisdiction and property of Saint Peter, by the counsel of our brothers, we decree with this present constitution that no castle may be built or rebuilt there in the future without special permission from the Apostolic See, under the threat of anathema and a penalty of a thousand pounds for the builders and twenty for each worker, strictly prohibiting anyone from presuming to act against such statutes. Therefore, let no one violate our constitution and prohibition, etc. If anyone, however, etc. Dated as above.

Regesto in Latin:

Innocentius III papa universis fidelibus per Sabiniam constitutis mandat, ne ullum castrum in Sabina sine licentia sedis apostolicae construatur vel reconstratur, sub poena anathematis et multa pecuniaria. Datum ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz. The wisdom of God the Father, wisely arranging all things from the beginning, has provided certain remedies for his holy bride, the mother church, by which, with his favor, she may be happily delivered from the assaults of necessities. Hence, as she is aroused by many cries from the Holy Land to extend swift aid to her pitiable state, the opportunity to render such aid is removed unless, first, the conflicts of discord, which press down the church with troubles and cause her to be inundated with sighs, are reformed into bonds of peace. We rightly presume about you, that because you are, by divine disposition, one of the greater members of the same church, you should gladly aid her in her time of need. Therefore, we firmly command your fraternity by apostolic letters, prudently considering that it should be chiefly incumbent on the sons that their mother, focused on their prosperity, obtains the support of vigor and power, and that the strength of the members is compelled if the head is firmly disposed, remembering also the oath you took for the protection of the regalia and the patrimony of Saint Peter to the apostolic see. Therefore, with the beloved son in Christ, our dear Frederick, ever-august Emperor of the Romans and illustrious king of Jerusalem and Sicily, ready magnificently to pursue the defense of the church's liberty, by which the rights of both church and empire may be obtained with the Lord's favor, you should striv

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz. It has come to our attention that you have imposed new, undue, and previously unheard-of exactions on all the churches where the noble brothers Henry and Conrad, Landgraves of Thuringia, hold the right of patronage, namely that they should pay you a twentieth of their revenues. This has caused considerable harm and burden to the aforementioned churches, and has been done to the displeasure and contempt of these noblemen. In response, they have chosen, out of reverence for the Roman Church, to appeal to us rather than to repel such an injury in another manner. They have humbly and devoutly petitioned us to intervene, given that, according to the Lateran Council, prelates of the churches, when there is a clear and reasonable cause, should seek moderate assistance from their subjects with charity, for their needs. Therefore, we admonish your fraternity by apostolic writing, commanding you to return the twentieth taken and desist from its exaction, while also lifting any oaths made by the prelates or clerics of those churches to pay it, as well as any sentences of excommunication and interdict that you have reportedly pronounced against some of these churches on account of this twentieth, without any hindrance. Otherwise, since we are bound by the duty of our office to protect the indemnity of these churches and to remove the cause of scandal, we have instructed our venerable brother, the Bishop of Merseburg, by our letters, to compel you to do this, with the obstacle of appeal removed, and with the due severity after ascertaining the truth. Given at Rieti, on the tenth day before the Kalends of July, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino mandat ut vigesimam partem proventuum ecclesiarum, quas Henrieus et Conradus fratres Langravii Turingiae patronatus ius obtinent, remittat et ab huiusmodi exactione desistat, sublatis excommunicationis et interdicti sententiis. 1234, Iun. 22. Datum Reate.

**Translation to English:**

To Masters Hugh, Archdeacon of Reims, and John Barat, Archdeacon of Châlons, and G. Goin, Canon of Reims. Before our beloved son Otto, Cardinal Deacon of St. Nicholas in Carcere Tulliano, appointed as judge, our dear son, the Dean of Cologne, lodged a complaint that our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Cologne, after the appeal had been legitimately made to us and the journey to the Apostolic See had begun, and after the case between the provost and the cantor of the Church of Cologne on one side, and the same dean on the other side, regarding the custody of the seal of the same church had been assigned to him by the Apostolic See, he promulgated a sentence of excommunication against him, for the custody of the seal, without prior proper warning, which he sought to have declared null. Master G., the cleric and procurator of the said archbishop, responded that this should not be done. With the case concerning the aforesaid matters having been legitimately contested by the same procurator, and both concerning these and certain other sentences of excommunication said to have been pronounced against the aforementioned dean, litigated for some time before the same cardinal, the cardinal, wishing to consult for the dean so that the justice of the other is not harmed, granted him the benefit of absolution by our mandate as a precaution, provided that if it is established that he was reasonably bound by the aforesaid sentences, he shall duly satisfy for those matters for which he had been bound; otherwise, none of the aforesaid sentences shall be considered valid. Therefore, we, approving what was done by the cardinal, command that you ensure its execution under apostolic obedience; and that contradictors etc., notwithstanding the constitution of two days issued in general council, and the indulgence said to have been obtained from us by the same archbishop, whereby no one besides a legate sent from our side shall dare to promulgate a sentence of suspension or excommunication against him without special mandate of the Apostolic See. What if not all, etc. Given at the Lateran, 6th June, in the seventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa magistris Hugoni Remensi, Iohanni Barat Cathalaunensi archidiaconis et G. Goin canonico Remensi mandat, ut absolutionis beneficium decano Coloniensi, ab Ottone cardinali de mandato apostolico concessum, exsequantur, non obstantibus appellationibus et indulgentiis. 1233, Iun. 6, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man, Miramamolin, to recognize the way of truth and faithfully remain in it. In other letters of ours, which we direct to your greatness through the beloved sons, brothers of the Order of Friars Minor, showing you the truth of the Christian faith, we beseech the Father of lights, as much as we can, that by His piety, looking upon the affection of our intention, He may kindly assist our prayers and graciously inspire them, and deign to open the door of His mercy. May He open, I pray, the ears of your heart, so that you may acquiesce to us, who thirst for your grace in the present and glory in the future, in the devotion of heart and humility of spirit. Indeed, we desire and ardently ask that He may show you, who walk in darkness, His only begotten Son, the true light, and mercifully call you to the faith of the Christian truth in the knowledge of the same His Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, so that, washed by the laver of regeneration, you may be able to please the Lord in the newness of life as His adopted son, who wishes His faithful to reign with Him in the heavenly kingdoms. And may the confidence we have conceived not deceive us, hoping for your conversion, because you show yourself gentle and kind to religious men of our faith, and especially to our venerable brother A., Bishop of Fez, and other brothers of the Order of Friars Minor, and commend them more earnestly where it is fitting, which is a clear indication of divine mercy towards your salvation. Hence, the aforementioned bishop and brothers, loving you more sincerely in Christ, strive with tireless devotion and love to promote your temporal and eternal well-being before God and the apostolic see. Finally, since the riches of Christ's goodness are indescribable, you should have firm hope and full confidence that if the change of the right hand of the Most High is made in you, which we desire and wish, He will increase the honor of your principality, who promises a hundredfold on the way and eternal life in the homeland to those who love Him. We will also commit to you greater and more honorable things for your greater praise and magnificence. Otherwise, if perhaps you choose to be an enemy of Christ rather than a friend, we will by no means allow, as we should not allow, that you be served by His faithful. Given at the Lateran, on the sixth day before the Kalends of June, in the seventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro Miramamolino hortatur ad conversionem ad fidem Christianam per epistulam, promittens honorem et magnalia si Christum sequatur, sed minatur privatione servitii fidelium si hostis Christi maneat. Dat. Laterani, VI Kalendas Iunii, anno septimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Salzburg. The grievous news of a heinous presumption has reached our ears, that the nobleman Henry of Vinkenstein, a familiar, counselor, and sworn ally of our venerable brother, the Bishop of Bamberg, has treacherously captured him with his accomplices and is holding him by force in custody in his own castle. Behold the outrage of this detestable crime and the bitterness of immense sorrow, as the said nobleman, turning from a friend into a persecutor and from a faithful ally into a traitor, has dared to expand his betrayal against the same bishop. Indeed, the reverence for the universal Church should have at least recalled him from such iniquity, as he dares to offend it enormously in the person of this bishop, and the fear of the dreadful judgment, which he will not be able to avoid. But perhaps he intends to rebel against the Most High even as a son of wrath and a foster child of indignation, who, cast out from His presence by his sins, devises plans he cannot establish, as he prepares a place of refuge away from Him, who, if he ascends to heaven, is there, and if he descends into hell, is present there. Since this matter concerns the universal Church, besides what befits you as a great member of the Church to pursue this as your own interest, we command you, out of compassion, to have the person of the said bishop commended to you as much as you can, and to attend willingly and effectively to his liberation, and to guard, protect, and defend the land of the Church of Bamberg in the meantime, until the said bishop has been restored to his former liberty, so that we may duly pursue your devotion with apostolic blessing and fitting favors. Given at the Lateran, on the seventh day before the Kalends of April, in the seventh year. The letter is written in the same way to the noble duke of Austria.

**Latin Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Salzburgensi mandat ut ad liberationem episcopi Bambebergensis, quem Henricus de Vinkenstein proditorie detinet, intendant et terram ecclesiae Bambebergensis interim custodiant. Datum Laterani, VII Kalendas Aprilis, anno septimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Eichstätt. We sympathize with paternal charity with the church of Eichstätt, which has been heavily burdened by the negligence of its prelates and almost entirely engulfed by the abyss of usury, and we lament its distress. For as we have heard, the wicked interest has grown to such an extent that the annual revenues of your entire bishopric scarcely suffice for the payment of the usury; for this reason, you humbly petitioned in our presence that we might deign to extend a helping hand for its relief. Therefore, we, upon whom the continuous care of all churches rests, wishing to provide paternal care for the same church, grant you by the authority of these presents, that you may lawfully retain the fruits of the vacant benefices in your diocese, for which the provision and arrangement pertain to you, to be converted entirely into the payment of such debts, for up to three years; provided that, under peril of your soul, suitable rectors are appointed to the vacant churches and that a sufficient portion of their fruits is assigned for the bearing of their burdens. Let no one, therefore, infringe our concession, etc. But if anyone, etc. Given at Perugia, fourth day before the Nones of January, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Eistetensi concedit, ut fructus beneficiorum in diocesi sua vacantium, quibus provisio et ordinatio ad eum spectant, ad solutionem debitorum retinere possit ad triennium, proviso sub periculo anime sue de rectoribus idoneis. 1235, Jan. 2. Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To Frederick, ever august Emperor of the Romans, illustrious King of Jerusalem and Sicily. Recently, upon hearing through the report of our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Messina, and our beloved sons, the noble men Henry de Murra, imperial justiciar, and P. de Vineis, judge of the imperial court, your messengers, that you were preparing vigorously for the defense of the faith and the preservation of ecclesiastical liberty and the protection of the patrimony of blessed Peter, we rejoiced in the Lord for you and gave thanks to Him. But as much as those joyful rumors and pleasant fame brought us great joy, we were equally troubled by greater sorrow upon hearing that, having set aside the aforementioned defense and protection and neglected the affairs of the empire, which you ought to have attended to, you are turning towards the regions of Sicily. Whether the imperial discretion is providing discreetly in this matter, let your circumspection weigh with even balance. Since, therefore, the defense of the Church pertains to you as its principal defender, both by reason of the kingdom which you hold from it, and also of the empire because you are the defender of the same Church, and of the special affection which is known to be held for your person, we have thought it necessary to appeal to you as our dearest son in Christ and defender of the same in this time of need. Therefore, we beseech, exhort, and implore your majesty in the Lord Jesus Christ, and we enjoin you in remission of your sins, that you gird yourself powerfully and vigorously for the defense of the aforesaid patrimony, if it can be done by you personally, otherwise through your men, and with a mighty hand and outstretched arm, strive to assist your mother, and when the Apostolic See requires help, no delay of any excuse should intervene. Thus, dearest son, extend your hand to strong deeds and fight in the service of Jesus Christ, and pursue with His grace leading you the vows inspired in you by Him, that the sincerity of your devotion may shine forth more clearly, and we may attend to your advancements and honor, as much as we can with God, both spiritually and temporally. Therefore, that you may demonstrate the zeal of your devotion, which you claim to have for the same Church, by the display of works rather than letters. Given at Anagni, the 10th of February, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Frederico, Romanorum imperatori, mandat ut ad defensionem fidei et patrimonii beati Petri se accingat personaliter, alioquin per suos, potentia et virilitate, ut sinceritatem devotionis demonstrat. 1232, Feb. 10, Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz. The duty of pastoral office, by which, according to the Apostle, we are debtors to the wise and the foolish, encourages us to love our brothers and fellow bishops with sincere charity in the Lord and to gladly grant the apostolic assent to those things which they rightly request from us. Therefore, venerable brother in Christ, considering the sincere devotion you bear towards us and the Roman Church, we are inclined by your devoted prayers to confirm, by apostolic authority, the liberties, privileges, and immunities from secular exactions, as well as the principalities and other goods granted to the Church of Mainz and to you by our dearest son in Christ, Frederick, ever august Emperor of the Romans, illustrious King of Jerusalem and Sicily, and by other princes through pious providence or prudent piety and liberality, as you justly and peacefully hold them. We confirm to you and through you to the said church... let it be fortified. Let no one, therefore, violate our confirmation... If anyone shall do otherwise... Given at Perugia, on the 16th day before the Kalends of February, in the eighth year.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino libertates, privilegia, et immunitates ecclesiae Maguntinae a Friderico imperatore aliisque principibus concessa auctoritate apostolica confirmat. 1234, Ian. 17. Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To the dean and schoolmaster of Trier. The pious and holy plan we have conceived, inspired by God, for the aid of the Holy Land towards the common salvation, and which we are eager to bring to fruition, you can clearly perceive from our general letters. Since we have full confidence in your sincerity and diligence and consider you suitable to fulfill the office of legation for Christ in this matter, we urge, admonish, and earnestly entreat you in the Lord, strictly commanding through apostolic writings and imposing for the remission of sins, that, kindled with the zeal of Christian faith, you bear with humility of heart and body the word of the cross and diligently and accurately induce His faithful to avenge the injury of the Crucified, as contained in the general letters. We want you to carefully note all that pertains to the aid of the Holy Land, which you will find included in these letters. 

Moreover, to demonstrate through your deeds that you carry the marks of Jesus Christ in your hearts, we strictly command that you refrain from accepting any gifts, except for sustenance and other necessities, and that you take these moderately and modestly, not exceeding the number of four in your entourage or six in persons, thus maintaining moderation and modesty in these and other matters so that nothing blameworthy can be found in you, which could cause an obstacle to the gospel entrusted to you; promoting with zeal and vigilance the cause of Christ, so that you become participants in the many great goods we believe will result from it. If anything is offered to you for the aid of the Holy Land, you should diligently deposit it in a religious place, reporting to us at the end of the year the progress and outcome of your efforts, so that we may know where you have made progress in persons or goods assigned to this salutary task, and we may write back our approval, instructing you how you ought to proceed in the future.

Given at Perugia, 22nd day of November, in the eighth year of our pontificate. In a similar manner, to other worthy preachers through Mainz, others through Cologne, others through Salzburg, and other provinces of Germany. Similarly, others through Rouen, others through Sens, others through Troyes, and others through various provinces of France. Also, others through Lombardy and other provinces.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa decano et scholastico Treverensi mandat ut, zelo fidei accensi, verbum crucis pro subventione Terre Sancte ferant et fideles inducant ad causam Christi promovendam, nulla munera recipientes nisi necessaria. Dat. Perusii, X Kal. Decem., anno pontificatus octavo.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man, the Duke of Austria.

Recalling with joy the deeds of piety to which your father of blessed memory is known to have dedicated himself, we believe that he has earned the glory of the eternal kingdom, especially because he, being a mirror and exemplar of many virtues, presented himself pleasingly to the Holy Roman Church, the illustrious bride of the supreme king, with the sincerity of his devotion, and shone with the purity of his faith in its service. He also magnificently supported the aid of the Holy Land for the service of the Redeemer, and adorned with the insignia of power the venerable house of the Hospital of St. Mary of the Teutons, which was once held in the heavy bondage of poverty, raising it from the dust, and adding desired abundance of many goods for perpetual retribution.

Such deeds and similar ones, blessed son, your father, a son of blessing, is known to have accomplished, whereby his name is repeated as pleasing and famed among many. But you, since you are a bone from the bones and flesh from the flesh of a virtuous man, succeeding in the inheritance of all things which the Creator of all is known to have bestowed on him, will you not assume the diligent care to represent the titles of your father in the virtue of the son, holding the form of a vine's shoot which demonstrates the worth of the vine itself, or like a stream, from whose clarity it is gathered that it is produced from a pure source?

Therefore, we ask and beseech your nobility in the Lord Jesus Christ, enjoining you for the remission of your sins, that you wisely consider that whatever is decorated with the title of goodness becomes amiable, or what is placed in a chosen place seems to be of great value, and dedicate yourself wholly to the observance of virtues, so that, being loved by God and men, you may here advance with the increase of prosperity and finally, placed with the princes of the heavenly people, may shine with eternal light in the sight of the Lord.

Moreover, so that by following in the footsteps of your father in all good things you may be more agreeable to Jesus Christ and be held more acceptable by us, we ask and exhort with paternal affection, accumulating prayers with prayers, that you favorably commend the aforesaid house of the Hospital for divine and our reverence, and refresh it with the gift of your grace, those things which are known to be bequeathed by the people of your land to the aid of Prussia, and procure to be assigned to the brothers of that hospital for the exaltation of the faithful and the suppression of the barbarous nation, so that they may advance in the prosecution of the undertaken struggle, with Christ triumphing, and the faithful of those parts, once troubled by infidelities, may rest in the joy of peace.

Given at Spoleto, on the 9th of September, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro .. duci Austrie mandat, ut domum hospitalis sancte Marie Theutonicorum in subsidium Pruscie favore suo reficiat ad exaltationem fidelium et depressionem barbare nationis. Dat. Spoleti, V Idus Septembris, anno VIII.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Ascoli. Our venerable brother, the bishop of Fermo, has informed us that the castle of Casale, which rightfully belongs to the church of Fermo, was destroyed by Mercualdo. The inhabitants of this castle relocated to another castle belonging to the same church, known as Podium Sancti Juliani, where they have lived for over thirty years. They have not been persuaded to return to the original castle, despite the efforts of his predecessors. Therefore, the canons of Fermo once wished that the late P., the predecessor of the current bishop, would allow the inhabitants to remain at Podium Sancti Juliani, after accepting lands, vineyards, and money offered by these inhabitants, as it was more beneficial for the church of Fermo. The bishop thus humbly requested that, besides the aforementioned advantage that the church is likely to gain, all rights the church holds over these people are reserved. He asked us to grant him the authority to permit this. Therefore, we command you, if these facts are indeed true and you know it to be more beneficial for the church, to grant the requested permission to him. Given at Perugia, on the Ides of December, in the eighth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Esculano episcopo mandat, ut licentiam largiatur episcopo Firmano, habitatores Podii sancti Iuliani ibidem permanentes, si hoc ecclesiae Firmanam magis expedire cognoverit, cum reservatione iuris in dictis hominibus. 1234, Dec. 13, Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To the Patriarch of Aquileia. What madness or fury, etc., as stated in the two hundred and twenty-first letter, is well known. We, however, lest we appear to neglect such a great injury to God and the Church, have unsheathed the medicinal sword of Peter against him, hoping that the blow would cause him to grieve and receive discipline. But he, as if driven into madness, considering the hammer like straw and refusing to turn to the one striking him, has heaped excess upon excess, doing whatever he wished against the anointed of the Lord, namely the aforementioned bishop, in the most atrocious insult to Jesus Christ and the inextricable disgrace of the Church, His bride. Since the aforementioned wicked man considered the fear of God and the reverence of the universal Church, which he gravely offended in the person of this bishop, as nothing, we command and enjoin upon your fraternity, by the authority of these presents and by virtue of obedience, and for the remission of sins, that since it is more prudent to prevent a neighbor's flood with suitable barriers lest one's own crops be destroyed by a swift incursion, and to assist a nearby burning wall to avoid common dangers, you pursue this matter not so much by necessity as by your own will, as if it were of your own interest. For the repair of the aforementioned castle and the recovery of the Church's goods, despite any bond of oath or any other caution, since no obligations can impose laws on us, who pursue the business of the Apostolic See and the universal Church, that through you and others such a heinous crime should be pursued. Do not neglect to proceed generally in all matters, both spiritually and temporally, against that infamous man until, if by divine providence it be granted, he considers his salvation, concerning the intolerable damages, injuries, and insults committed against the aforementioned bishop and church, and humbly returns to the apostolic mandate. Furthermore, declare publicly, with bells tolling and candles lit, that he, along with the ministerials of the noble Duke of Carinthia, who are said to have supplied him with arms and provisions, and his accomplices and supporters, are excommunicated every Sunday and feast day, and ensure they are avoided by all until due satisfaction is made. Given at the Lateran, 4th of the Kalends of July, in the seventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa patriarche Aquilegensi mandat ut contra hominem nequissimum et eius complices spiritualiter et temporaliter procedat pro iniuriis in episcopum et ecclesiam commissis, et excommunicatos nuntiet usque ad satisfactionem. Dat. Lateran. IV Kalendas Julii, anno septimo.

Translation to English:

To the King of Tunis. Having received with due kindness the letters of your nobility and having diligently examined their content, we have carefully listened to what our beloved son, the noble man Oddo Adelardi, a prudent and discreet man, faithful to you and diligent in the affairs entrusted to his prudence by you, and Symon Mele, citizens of Genoa, have reported in our presence, considering acceptable and pleasing the affection of your devotion.
