**Translation to English:**

To the knights and people of Piacenza. We rejoice in the Lord and are refreshed with salutary joy, because He, who is true peace, has united various walls of discord in your city into one, bringing you back to peace through His mercy after internal wars and dangerous dissensions. Just as the sting of immense sorrow pressed us due to the countless dangers to bodies, souls, and possessions that continually arose for you from dissensions and schisms, so we are grateful that, having rejected the sower of discord and the enemy of your salvation, you have been reconciled to the author of reconciliation, your savior, returning from the wrong path to the right, from the left to the right. Therefore, desiring the prosperity and peace of your state and city, and considering the growth of your city to be the proper concern of the Apostolic See, we have specially instructed our venerable brother, the Bishop of Ascoli, a prudent and discreet man, whom we are sending to your region for the peace of the whole province, to put forth all diligence and effort for the inviolable observance of concord among you, strengthening it with apostolic authority. Otherwise, we have instructed the bishop himself to proceed by our authority against violators of this peace, setting aside any hindrance of appeal. Given at Viterbo, the 9th day before the Kalends of April, in the tenth year [of our pontificate]. In a nearly similar manner, a letter was written to the same bishop concerning this matter.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa militibus et populo Placentino mandat, ut venerabilem fratrem suum episcopum Esculanum pro concordia inter eos observanda benigne recipiant et eius monitis adhereant, alioquin ipse episcopus contra pacis violatores auctoritate apostolica procedat. Datum Viterbii, IX Kal. April. anno decimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Cambrai. Since it is fitting for him who fully devotes himself to the service of God and the Church to enjoy apostolic favor, we command that you do not allow the noble man Baldwin, Count of Namur, heir of the Empire of Romania, who has laudably dedicated himself to the services of the Church from a young age, and his goods, which he possesses in the Empire of Germany and the Kingdom of France, to be unduly troubled by anyone; restraining such troublemakers by ecclesiastical censure, setting aside appeals, notwithstanding the constitution concerning the two days issued in the general council. Given at the Lateran, on the Calends of December, in the twelfth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Cameracensi mandat ne Balduinum comitem Namucensem, heredem imperii Romanie, et bona sua in imperio Alamanie et regno Francie indebite molestari sinat, molestatores per censuram ecclesiasticam compescendo. 1238, Dec. 1, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot and convent of the monastery in Salsa of the diocese of Strasbourg. On your part, it was humbly requested to us that a privilege granted by our predecessor, Pope John, of blessed memory, which was nearly consumed by the passage of time, be renewed with the benevolence of the apostolic see. We, having diligently examined this privilege as is appropriate, have decided to renew it word for word. The tenor of the same privilege is as follows. In the name of the eternal Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ. I, the humblest of all servants of God, appointed not by my own merits but by the intercession of the most blessed Apostle Peter, Prince of the Apostles, by the Almighty to the apex of the apostolate in the holy Roman see, the teacher of the whole world. Because our Lord entrusted His own sheep, which He redeemed with His precious blood, to be fed by blessed Peter, it is evident that all worshipers of God should be under his protection, by whose patronage we do not doubt to be protected everywhere. Therefore, it is very fitting that all Christians should flock to the holy mother church and the apostolic see, so that the devotion of the people may suitably attain the effect of their creator, and the aid of pious construction in granting privileges should not be refused. Therefore, because our daughter Adaleida, the august empress, requested from us that the monastery in Alsace, above the place of her right, which is called Salsa, near the river Matra, be adorned with a privilege of the apostolic see for the redemption of the illustrious governors of the Roman Empire, namely the great lord and her dear Otto and their son likewise Otto, who was buried before the church of our blessed Peter the Apostle, and for the forgiveness of their sins and also all her faithful relatives, to the eternal praise of Christ Jesus, in honor of the apostles Peter and Paul, and that we grant it such liberty in perpetuity that its liberty may never be corrupted by any reasons, nor should an abbot be appointed over the monks serving the Lord there without their election, it is most fitting to acquiesce to her most Christian prayers and to fulfill completely whatever she justly requests. Furthermore, granting our consent to her pious desires as is fitting, we grant by the authority of this our precept to the aforementioned monastery and the brothers there fighting according to the rule of blessed Benedict what she requests and we consent by apostolic donation. By our authority and spontaneous largess, we also permit the abbot of the same monastery to celebrate the offices of mass with sandals and dalmatic, to be ordained by a bishop whom the entire body of brothers will have called. Thus we do not permit any priest of the church to have any priorate authority in the aforementioned monastery. We also prohibit him who is known to presently preside over the city of Strasbourg and likewise him who will later acquire it, from extending any opposition or dominion over the aforementioned monastery by this authority of the apostolic see, so that no assemblies may begin to be pretended there, nor any parts of the alms given for the use of the monastery by the faithful may be demanded as his own share, nor tithes nor lands nor churches nor treasures nor books nor anything granted by the most blessed empress or later offered by others may be attempted to be taken away, because the monastery is subject to the apostolic see with all its appurtenances not by the power of donation but solely for the cause of liberty and secured by the protection of the Roman see so that anyone who makes any opposition to the monastery or to those serving the Lord there, or who, wounded by miserable greed, ever claims any part of the land of the same monastery as his own, or who by any trick constrains the same monastery with his goods within or outside, shall be damned with eternal punishment, as with the help of God it is ordered by us according to the desire of the most holy empress that these things remain unshaken and inviolate for all times. **Translation to English:**

To Frederick, ever august Emperor of the Romans, etc. Those who are accustomed to fishing more fruitfully in troubled waters consider the sweetness of peace as the bitterness of death; they sow disputes and quarrels, so that they may reap bundles of iniquity and profits of wickedness from these. However, domestic enemies more effectively plot deceits, who, by corrupting the righteous works of their lords, turn light into darkness and, through certain venomous mixtures, dissolve the bonds of love that unite the hearts of princes, so that they may more freely exercise their malice when peace is wounded, malice which they would not dare bring from the darkness of fraud into the light during times of concord. Indeed, the apostolic see is frequently pricked by these goads of Satan, from which the imperial court is also not exempt. For when we wrote previously regarding a certain matter of yours, as we have understood, certain sons of iniquity, who would by no means want the Church to be united with the empire in the bond of love, sent secret letters and documents to the executors of the said matter, so that they would not proceed with its execution, falsely asserting that their letters had come forth with our knowledge. On this, we invoke the testimony of Him who knows everything, the searcher of hearts and knower of secrets, Wisdom 16, that such a scheme never originated from us, but rather, purely from their impure machination, which in the matter of the kingdom of Jerusalem you can clearly argue! And you will be able to find those who wrote contrary things to be liars in both matters. Moreover, some of your associates, believed to be enemies of the imperial peace, send letters concerning your progress, which, if truth were to stand as witness, the whole structure that the Lord has built upon you would suffer ruin and perish. However, since we have previously organized with you for a peace reform, if you recall well, to counteract these frauds, so that if anything harmful to peace regarding one or the other came to light, we would deny a hearing to the barkings of detractors from either side: we have thought it right to request and advise your serenity, that when such things about us reach your ears, you should silence the mouths of those speaking iniquity, just as we do in reverse, and inform us of what you have heard, so that truth may be known to your excellency through our letters. Thus indeed, peace will be maintained in its vigor and iniquity will lie in the detractors' heads in their attempts to harm it. Given at Assisi, 12 Kalends of October, in the ninth year of our pontificate. It is written regarding this to the master of the house of St. Mary of the Teutons, that he may prudently relate the foregoing to the emperor and more diligently induce him to this end.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Friderico Romanorum imperatori scripsit de dolo factorum et litterarum secretarum ab inimicis pacis missarum, quae unionem Ecclesiae et imperii impedire conabantur; monens ut talia auditui deneget, et veritatem per litteras suas cognosci permittat. 1235, Sept. 20, Assisii.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishops of Cambrai and Tournai. It has been reported to us on behalf of a nobleman, Herbert, who has taken the cross, that about twenty of his relatives and friends from your dioceses have taken up the sign of the cross on the condition that they would either transfer themselves for the aid of the Holy Land or the Byzantine Empire, or redeem their vows according to their own means. We command that, if they choose to redeem their vows, the sums should be fully assigned to the nobleman who is going forth for the aid of the said empire, granting them the indulgence that was granted to those aiding the Holy Land in the general council. Given at the Lateran, the 6th day before the Kalends of December, in the twelfth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Cameracensi et Tornacensi episcopis mandat, ut redemptiones votorum consanguineorum Herberti nobili succurso Constantinopolitani imperii integre assignentur. 1228, Nov. 26. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the former bishop of Modena, legate of the Apostolic See. The burden of the governance we have undertaken compels us to direct all our actions along the paths of justice, so that, by resolving the questions brought before us, we may ensure that justice is granted to each petitioner. Therefore, since our venerable brothers, the bishops of Lubus, Meissen, Cammin, and Brandenburg, frequently dispute among themselves concerning the unclear boundaries of their dioceses as appropriate, as contained in the petition presented to us by the bishop of Lubus, and because they and their churches suffer serious damages and losses from this, and even endanger the salvation of souls, we, wishing to sever such contention and provide paternal care for their indemnity and the salvation of souls, have decided to entrust this matter to your providence, in which we have full confidence in the Lord, mandating you by apostolic writs, that you personally go to the location, summon those who should be called for this, and then, with equity as your guide, prudently determine the boundaries of the said dioceses, preserving the rights of each of those bishops, and establish that each remains content with his own, so that we may justly commend your diligence in this matter; those who oppose, etc. Given at Viterbo, on the 7th Ides of September, in the eleventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo quondam Mutinensi, apostolicae sedis legato, mandat ut, vocatis evocandis, limites dioecesium Lubusensis, Misnensis, Caminensis et Brandeburgensis equitate provida definiat, cuilibet episcoporum iure suo servato, contentionem amputare et indempnitati ac saluti animarum providere cupiens. 1237, Sept. 7, Viterbii.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishops of Regensburg, chancellor of the imperial court, and Hildesheim. Formerly, it was heard that our venerable brothers, the bishops of Würzburg and Augsburg, and the abbot of Fulda, having forgotten that our dearest son in Christ, Frederick, the ever august Roman Emperor, illustrious king of Jerusalem and Sicily, has been appointed by the Lord as the defender of the Church, and whatever befalls him in good or bad fortune should be considered as concerning the Church itself, ignored the obligation of their oath to him and adhered with sworn oaths to the nobleman Henry, his son, against every man. This caused the state of the world to be disturbed by such a dangerous upheaval, which could neither be easily corrected nor eradicated by many efforts. We recall having instructed your fraternity, after diligently inquiring into these matters, if you found the situation to be as stated, to firmly command them on our behalf to present themselves to the Apostolic See within two months after receiving your admonition, or otherwise to compel them to do so by our authority, removing any obstacle of appeal. As for Dlegenhard, provost of Hougue, and Walter of Tannenberg, canons of Würzburg, who were reported to have gone to Milan against the same emperor by the order of the said noble, you are to suspend them from office and benefice and compel them to come to our presence, dismissing any appeal, through ecclesiastical censure. However, as we have heard from you, no process has been undertaken by such letters. Therefore, we, rightly wishing to prevent them from having reason to boast of such a great excess of rashness, which should be corrected with diligent correction not only in clerics but also in laymen, but rather that punishment for the past may make them cautious for the future, since if they had raised their eyes to the justice of the supreme judge, they would not have incited the son to persecute such a father, but should instead have assumed all diligence to suppress his audacity. We command by decree that concerning the aforementioned bishops, abbot, and canons, as well as concerning the elected bishop of Worms and Master Devard, canon of Würzburg, who are reported to have presumed similar actions with the aforementioned persons, you proceed after receiving these presents according to the contents of the former letters, dismissing every occasion of appeal. What you find concerning the aforementioned matters, you are to express to us faithfully by your letters within the said term. Given at Assisi, September 24, in the ninth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopis Ratisponensi et Ildesemensi mandat ut post inquisitionem super adhesione episcoporum Herbipolensis, Augustensis et abbatis Vultuensis ad Henricum contra Fridericum imperatorem, eos ad se praesentandum compellant et canonicis Herbipolensibus, suspensis, iubeat coram se comparere. Assisii, 24 Septembris, anno IX.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Hildesheim. The urgency of the matter of the Holy Land is fully known to Him who searches the hearts and minds, as we earnestly desire its liberation. Therefore, wishing that many may be girded with the glory of the cross for the physical campaign in the army of Jesus Christ, we have decided to entrust to your devotion, in whose mouth the word of the Lord is not bound, the office of preaching in the province of Mainz for the matter of the cross. And to encourage the faithful of Christ to more eagerly and willingly run to hear the word of the Lord and to come, we grant an indulgence of ten, twenty, or thirty days, as you see fit, once a week in any city, town, or village to all who are truly penitent and confessed and come to your solemn preaching. To ensure nothing is lacking for the execution of the office entrusted to you, we grant you by the authority of these presents the power to absolve, according to the form of the Church, those who have laid violent hands on clerics and incendiaries, provided they are marked with the cross and even those assuming the sign of the cross, or if according to their means they send others in their place as warriors; provided that those who are bound by the bond of excommunication for violent laying of hands make suitable satisfaction to those who suffered injury, and incendiaries to those whom they have harmed by fire, unless the excess of those who laid hands is so grave and enormous that they must rightfully be referred to the Apostolic See. Furthermore, because, as we have heard, the office of preaching, which we impose on you and others for the aforesaid matter, is hindered by solicitors, we command that no obstacle or hindrance be brought to this matter, that you absolutely forbid all solicitors present to propose anything to the people while the word of the cross is being proposed by you, restraining them by ecclesiastical censure if they presume otherwise, setting aside any appeal. By the same authority, we also grant you the power to summon the people to your preaching through parish priests, other church rectors, and even simple priests, through whom, if any wish, they may safely receive the sign of the cross. Moreover, lest the mouth of the ox treading out the grain be muzzled, it is permitted for you to receive moderated hospitality for eight persons and six horses outside your diocese for the imminent office; and any who oppose or rebel, etc. Given at Assisi, IV Kalends of October, in the ninth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Ildesemensi mandat officium praedicationis in provincia Maguntina pro negotio crucis, cum indulgentiarum concessione et potestate absolvendi manuum iniectores et incendiarios, necnon convocandi populum ad praedicationem et signum crucis recipiendum. 1235, Sept. 28, Assisii.

Translation to English:

To the Archbishop of Rouen. Since you are a son of the Church, the zeal for it cannot fail to consume you, nor can you endure the reproaches of those who scorn it and usurp its rights. We believe you are so deeply rooted in the fear of the divine name and in reverence for the Church's dignity that we do not doubt in the least that you feel its distress as your own. Indeed, we have been deeply grieved because the Romans, who ought to be special sons of the Church, have so degenerated from sons into stepchildren that they exhibit such ingratitude and lack of devotion that scarcely a spark of gratitude or devotion seems to remain in them. Wickedness has emerged from them like fat, to such an extent that they not only stretch out their reckless hands toward temporal matters which do not pertain to them but also toward spiritual matters entirely forbidden to laymen, seeking to overturn and subvert ecclesiastical freedom and to enslave the Roman Church, their mother, in every manner, provoking all others against the liberty of the universal Church by their pernicious example. Since, although this is a grave offense, the fact that this persecution has persisted for so long is an even graver example, we are compelled by pastoral diligence to bind up what was broken in them and to bring back what was cast aside, laboring among them with earnest admonitions and frequent exhortations. But they have not been granted from above the grace to accept the healing medicine for their wound, for which we have labored extensively to heal, and thus we have taken care to exercise ecclesiastical censure upon them. And because their iniquities have increased to such an extent that they neither fear God nor respect ecclesiastical censure, we are reluctantly compelled to rouse you and other devoted sons of the Church, in whose territories they commit public harm, to take vengeance upon them. We affectionately request and urgently exhort your brotherhood, by apostolic writings, strictly commanding you to wisely consider the cause in question, which is public, not private, not specific to any single person but common to all, in which it is incumbent upon you to rise to our aid, as we intend to defend not certain individuals but all universally. May you provide us with a fitting supply of soldiers or stipendiaries as liberally and willingly as possible, so that fortified by your assistance and that of others, we may, with the Lord's help, so repress their arrogance that others may not rise against God and the Church in the future, and that the sons of the Church may rejoice in due liberty, and that we, recognizing your sincerity from the affection and effect of your exhibited liberality, may embrace you more dearly in the heart of Christ. Given at Perugia, Nones of December, in the eighth year [of our pontificate]. In the same manner to his suffragans separately. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Tarentaise and his suffragans separately. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Besançon and his suffragans separately. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Embrun and his suffragans separately. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Aix and his suffragans separately. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Arles and his suffragans separately. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Vienne and his suffragans separately. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Lyon and his suffragans separately. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Sens and his suffragans separately. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Reims and his suffragans separately. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Tours and his suffragans separately. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Bourges and his suffragans separately. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Bordeaux and his suffragans separately. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Auch and his suffragans separately. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Narbonne and his suffragans separately. In the same manner to the elected Archbishop of Tarragona and his suffragans separately. In the same manner to the Bishop of Pamplona. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Toledo and his suffragans separately. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Compostela and his suffragans separately. Regesto:

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Rothomagensi mandat ut subsidium militum contra Romanorum improbitatem praebeat. Datum Perusii, Non. Decembris, anno octavo.

**Translation to English:**

"To the Duke of the Venetians. The Holy Roman Church, which embraces all faithful Christians with the affection of a loving mother in the heart of charity, ought to support and defend the devout with the special prerogative of grace, so that they may receive worthy rewards for their sincerity and others may be inspired by their example to show devotion to the Apostolic See. Since the city of the Venetians has always shown and continues to show special reverence, devotion, and faith towards the Roman Church, their mother, as is proven by certain experiences, we, inclined by your supplications, which we gladly accept, take you and the same city, persisting in devotion to the Apostolic See, under the protection of Saint Peter and our protection and fortify you with the safeguard of this present document. Let no one violate our protection, etc. If anyone should, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the Nones of December, in the twelfth year."

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa duci Venetorum mandat, ut personam suam et civitatem Venetorum sub beati Petri et sua protectione suscipiat et communiat. 1238, Dec. 5. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Henry of Ravello, imperial seneschal in Provence, [we wish] the spirit of sound counsel. We express the signs of paternal affection chiefly in this, that we suggest to each of the sons of the Church to shun what is contrary to the divine will. Therefore, since, as we have heard, you, not realizing that whatever happens to any of His ministers is considered as done to God, are heavily persecuting our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Arles, and his church and lands, along with certain others who lack divine fear, we earnestly ask and urge your nobility, commanding that you desist completely from all harassment of the said archbishop, church, and lands, and do not presume to offend the state of ecclesiastical liberty in any way, as you value divine grace. Otherwise, we have instructed our venerable brother, the Bishop of Nîmes, by our letters, to compel you to do so, after issuing a warning, by ecclesiastical censure and without appeal, with a prior reasonable process. Given at Viterbo, the 8th of August, in the eleventh year. [Also to the] authority and people of Avignon, the spirit of sound counsel; to the council and people of Arles and the noble count of Provence, that they may bring aid to the Archbishop of Arles against Henry of Ravello.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Henrico de Ravello, senescalco imperiali in Provincia, mandat ut ab omni molestatione archiepiscopi Arelatensis et ecclesie eius desistat, alioquin episcopus Nemausensis per censuram ecclesiasticam eum compellat. 1237, Aug. 8, Viterbii.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Lund and the Bishop of Roskilde. The petition of our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Danes, which was read before us, contained that there has been a grave and longstanding discord between the kings of the Danes of clear memory on one side and the Slavs on the other, from which many dangers to body and soul have arisen. On the advice of experts, it has been suggested that, to restore a beneficial peace between them and the Slavs, he should give a certain niece of his to a nobleman, B., Duke of Pomerania, to whom she is said to be related in the fourth degree, in marriage. Therefore, the said king humbly begged us to grant him permission, in our usual kindness, to proceed with this marriage alliance. However, since we are not informed about the aforementioned matters, we command your fraternity, in whom we have full trust in the Lord, through apostolic writings, that having diligently investigated the truth about the aforementioned matters, you should faithfully report back to us what you find, so that, being adequately informed by your account, we may decide what seems expedient in this matter. Given at the Lateran, January 29, in the eleventh year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Lundensi et episcopo Roskildensi mandat ut veritatem inquirant de petitione regis Danorum circa matrimonium cum ducatu Pomeraniae, et relationem fideliter rescribant. 1238, Jan. 29. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To Masters Hugh, Major of Reims, and I. Barat, Archdeacon of Châlons, and G. Goin, Canon of Reims. 

Since a complaint against our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Cologne, has reached us to such an extent that it could no longer be ignored without scandal or tolerated without danger, we resolved to follow the example of Him who, though He knows all things, chose to descend and see whether those who dwelt in Sodom and Gomorrah had acted in accordance with the outcry that had reached Him. Thus, in response to the repeated outcry, we entrusted the investigation of the said Archbishop to our venerable brother, the Bishop of Lausanne, and his colleagues, under a specific form. 

The aforementioned inquisitors, as we have learned from their letters, conducted their inquiry with the utmost diligence, taking statements from several named witnesses, and faithfully sent the collected evidence, sealed with their seals, to us, setting a suitable peremptory term for the Archbishop to present himself before us, even in his absence. 

Master G., a clerk and procurator of the same Archbishop, appearing before our beloved son Eligius, Cardinal Deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, who was appointed by us as auditor, alleged that the proceedings by the same inquisitors were entirely null, having cited many causes of grievance and suspicion, which he detailed before the cardinal. Therefore, he requested that it be declared void. 

When the cardinal prudently and faithfully reported to us and our brothers what had been presented before him, we diligently examined the causes from which the appeal arose, enclosed them with the process of the said inquisitors under our seal, and, under the threat of divine judgment, we strictly order you by apostolic writings, that if the said Archbishop can within two months from receiving these presents fully prove that the alleged causes of grievance were proposed before the said inquisitors and not accepted, and if he offers to prove them true, and having specified the causes of suspicion, asked for arbiters and was denied, and consequently appealed to the apostolic see, and proves before you any or all of these causes to be true, you should declare the process null. 

Then, inquiring diligently both into the matters about which the aforementioned inquisitors conducted their inquiry and into other excesses contained in our previous letters, send the sufficiently instructed case to us under your seals, setting a suitable peremptory term for the Archbishop to appear before us to receive what is just. Furthermore, if the said Archbishop fails to prove his case within two more months, provide him with a copy of the names of the received witnesses, before their publication, so that he may reasonably object and, if he wishes, prove objections regarding their persons, so that after the publication of the witnesses, he shall not be heard against those same persons; and after the publication of the said testimonies, provide him within the same period with a copy of the said testimonies, with the names omitted, so that he may, if he wishes, reasonably oppose whatever he deems fit in their statements; and then, after hearing the matters proposed before you, remit the sufficiently instructed case to the apostolic examination, setting a suitable peremptory term for the Archbishop to present himself before us. 

Moreover, since the Dean is pursuing the matter of inquiry by our mandate and no one is compelled to labor at their own expense, we want and command that both the Dean and you be provided for in moderate expenses necessary for the prosecution of the case from the goods of the church. 

Additionally, wishing to provide for the indemnity of the Church of Cologne with paternal care, we strictly command you to firmly prohibit the Archbishop from contracting any loans or daring to alienate, enfeoff, or pledge any of the immovable goods of the Church without the consent and agreement of our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Trier, while the inquiry matter is pending, denouncing him as suspended by our authority from the administration of temporalities should he act contrary, and declaring such a contract void. 

Since the said Archbishop is reported to have pronounced sentences of excommunication, suspension, or interdict against some while the case is pending, or to have deprived some of their benefices and goods after appealing to us, if it is established before you that the Archbishop proceeded against them in such a manner after a legitimate appeal, declare his process and whatever followed from it entirely null. Otherwise, having received from those against whom such sentences were pronounced sufficient security that they will make appropriate satisfaction on your mandate for whatever the sentences were reasonably issued, relax these sentences to caution according to the form of the Church; strictly prohibiting the Archbishop from proceeding in such a manner against them while the case is pending.

**Translation to English:**

To the rulers, communities, counts, and other barons of Lombardy. The infallible fullness of experience fully instructs and teaches you, even those nearby and distant, how sincerely we love your province and desire its peaceful and prosperous state, considering your well-being as an augmentation of the apostolic see. For we have not ceased to work for you, but have undertaken to labor for the peace of the said province with indefatigable solicitude, having many times sent legates and envoys from our side for this purpose, who, knowing and following the affection of our mind, aimed at this with all diligence and all their might. But because it has not yet been granted from above that the effort of our desire may have its desired effect, we do not cease to taste the cup of this labor, urged by the fervent love we bear towards you and the fear of many dangers which are wont to threaten souls, goods, and bodies from dissensions. Therefore, driven by this consideration, as a mother cannot forget the child of her womb, we have decided to send to your parts our venerable brother, the Bishop of Ascoli, a prudent and discreet man, believing that he should produce the hoped-for fruit as an angel of peace and counsel, namely of tranquility and salvation, turning crooked things into straight ones and rough paths into smooth ones. Therefore we urge your community, etc., as above, not to delay in proceeding. Given at Viterbo, the fourth Nones of April, in the tenth year. In the same way, to the rulers, communities, counts, and other barons of the Treviso march. In the same way to the rulers, communities, counts, and other barons of Romagna. In the same way to the rulers and people of Milan. In a similar way to the rulers and people of Cremona. In nearly the same way, it is written to the Bishop of Ascoli as far as: turning rough paths into smooth ones, so that the fruit of tranquility expected may come from your circumspection. Moreover, if any with obstinate mind should lead to resist you in this matter, since we rightly intend to pursue with blessings and paternal favor those whom you find devout and ready for your counsels and mandates, but in the rest to tolerate in no way those disturbing the cause of Christ and the Christian people, nor with us weight and weight, etc., as above.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa potestatibus, communitatibus, comitibus aliisque baronibus Lombardie mandat ut pacem et tranquillitatem provinciae procurent, mittens Esculanum episcopum ad partes suas. 1236, Apr. 2, Viterbii.

**Translation to English:**

To Arnaldo, canon of the Church of Saint Mary to the Steps of Mainz. We willingly show favor to those seeking the pearl of knowledge in the field of study, which beautifies the house of the Lord in many ways, and we grant as much as we can with God, to their supplications. Therefore, as you proposed in our presence, having been constituted with the permission of your chapter, you have devoted yourself to the study of canon and civil law for four years and have progressed commendably in it, and you still wish to continue striving: we grant you our kind approval to your devoted supplications, permitting you to continue studying law for three more years and to receive your ecclesiastical revenues during this time, except for the distributions that are accustomed to be given only to those residing and attending canonical hours, by the authority of these presents. Let no one infringe our concession, etc. But if anyone, etc. Given at Anagni, 28 September, in the twelfth year of our pontificate. In the same manner, almost...to the dean and...treasurer of Saint Peter and W. of Echeburn, canon of Mainz, up to: the faculty. Therefore, we command that the aforementioned revenues be fully administered to him according to the tenor of our concession; contradictors, etc. But if not all, etc. Given at Anagni, 28 September, in the twelfth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Arnaldo canonico ecclesiae sanctae Mariae ad Gradus Maguntinae concedit facultatem per triennium studendi in iure et percipiendi proventus ecclesiasticos, exceptis distributionibus residentibus tantum ministrandis. Anagniae, IIII Kal. Oct., anno duodecimo.

Translation to English:

To the Archbishop of Messina. The envoys of the crusaders of France, coming to the Apostolic See, earnestly petitioned us that, since they have bound themselves with a double bond of oath to cross over to the Holy Land on the forthcoming feast of Saint John the Baptist, we might incline our support to their passage at the appointed time and induce the assent of our dearest son in Christ, Frederick, Roman Emperor, to their prayers. Therefore, considering that the more... (as above in letter 284) until: unable, we have deemed it necessary to earnestly beseech the same emperor that he may submit the matter to judgment (up to: feels supported). Thus, we have deemed it necessary to request and advise your fraternity, by apostolic writings mandating you, that you effectively employ your influence with the said emperor and prudently induce him to this. But if he cannot be persuaded to this, ensure diligently that he resends to us and the same crusaders his will concerning this through his open letters, promising them counsel, aid, and favor in arranging another passage by ship and the aforementioned matters, so that we may justly commend your diligence in this. Given as above. In the same manner to the master of the hospital of Saint Mary of the Teutons.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Messanensi mandat ut apud Fridericum imperatorem intercedat pro subsidio crucesignatorum Franciae in transitu ad Terram Sanctam, et si hoc fieri non possit, curet ut idem imperator per litteras patentes suum consilium et auxilium in alio passagio eis promittat. Datum ut supra.

Translation to English:

To the noble lady of Turris. Bearing special concern for the status of your person and your land, which pertains to the Roman Church and which we wish to be tranquil and peaceful, we have arranged for you to be matrimonially joined to the noble man Guelfo de Porcaria, a devoted son and faithful follower of the Apostolic See, strong and powerful, by whose guidance and counsel the land itself can be well ruled and prosperously governed. Therefore, we earnestly admonish and encourage your nobility and command you by our apostolic writings, that you do not delay to send a procurator to our presence, who can render an oath in your soul concerning the marriage to be contracted between you and the said noble, under penalty of excommunication and deprivation of all your land, strictly forbidding, since that land is especially under the jurisdiction of blessed Peter, for which reason you should not take a suspect man as your husband, who might disturb the rights of the Church, that you do not proceed to contract marriage with anyone without our mandate or special license. Given at the Lateran, 2nd of the Kalends of June, in the twelfth year. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Turris, up to: special license. Therefore, we command, that you admonish and induce the said lady to that, as diligently as you can, providing effective help and effort. Given as above. In the same manner to the Bishop of Empuries. In the same manner to the noble man Pletro, judge of Arborea.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa nobili mulieri Turritanae mandat ut cum Guelfo de Porcaria matrimonium contrahat, sub poena excommunicationis et privationis terrae suae, sine mandato vel licentia non procedens. 1238, Mai. 31, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble woman Sophie, widow of the late duke of Miranie. As your faith's purity merits that you be regarded as a special daughter of the Church, we have deemed it fitting to be favorable to you in the pious requests you make. Since, as we have heard, driven by divine inspiration, you wish to serve the Lord, the master of virtues, in the humility of spirit and committed to works of charity, having taken a vow of perpetual chastity, we, moved by your devout prayers, have taken you and your household with all your goods, which are presently reasonably... under our protection. Therefore, let no one... of our protection, etc. If anyone, however, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the 19th day before the Kalends of January, in the twelfth year. Dioceses of Halberstadt and Mainz... under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves. In almost the same manner... we have seen fit to admit to the abbots of Sichemensis and of Wolkelderode. Therefore, we command your discretion by apostolic writings, that you do not permit the aforementioned noblewoman to be unjustly disturbed by anyone against the title of our protection; the molesters etc. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa (Sophiae nobili mulieri, relictae ducis Miraniae, personam et familiam eius sub protectione Sancti Petri et suae protectionis titulo communit ne a molestoribus iniuste vexetur. 1238, Dec. 14. Datum Laterani.)

**Translation to English:**

To Frederick, ever august Emperor of the Romans, illustrious King of Jerusalem and Sicily. We recall that we recently requested, through apostolic letters, your imperial excellence to restore the nobleman Peter Sarracenus of Andreocta, a Roman citizen, whom you had placed in prison custody as it pleased your highness, to his former freedom out of reverence for the apostolic see and us. We believed we would be more readily heard in this matter, as we hoped that you would be more strongly persuaded to this end out of affection for our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of England, your relative, who sent him to the apostolic see for his affairs. However, since if, God forbid, the liberation of this nobleman were to be hindered, a point of difficulty might arise, which would be very difficult for both us and you to rectify, we deemed it necessary to exhort and beseech your serenity once more and more intently, that with your clemency you release this citizen, who is not bound by any crime, from the chains of undue captivity. Thus, his easy release may serve as evidence that his capture did not come from the pleasure of your will. To further demonstrate the affection we bear for this citizen, behold, we are sending to your presence the venerable brother of ours, the Bishop of Florence, a man prudent and discreet, acceptable to us and our brothers by merit of his integrity, whom we advise you to receive and listen to kindly, for the more effective execution of this matter through the counsel of the said brothers. Given at the Lateran, 3rd Nones of June, in the twelfth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Friderico, Romanorum imperatori, mandat ut Petrum Sarracenum de Andreocta, civem Romanum, a custodia carcerali absolvat. 1238, Iun. 3, Laterani.

### Translation to English:

To the master of the Hospital of Saint Mary of the Teutons. Explaining the parable of the fig tree, the Lord teaches that when its branches become tender and leaves sprout, summer is near, thus preventing presumptions and removing the place for conjectures not preceded by usual signs and common occurrences. Since truth in singular and future matters is undetermined, suspicion should not disturb discerning minds, and is better repelled when past actions have shown contrary outcomes. We are compelled to wonder at the repeated suggestions in your letters that we should not proceed against our dearest son in Christ, Frederick, the emperor of the Romans. We do not understand from where this suspicion arises, as nothing in our letters urging him to restore peace with the Lombards, nor in our actions, could indicate any intention other than promoting his and the empire's exaltation, preserving the church's honor, and disregarding those who aim to depress him, as you well know. Hence, such presumptions should not be made against one who has been recognized as favorable until now. Furthermore, before receiving imperial letters, with the advice of our brothers, we arranged that our venerable brother, the bishop of Palestrina, a man rejecting the vanities of the world, desiring peace and concord without favoritism, should be sent to Lombardy to provide effective aid for peace, which you should confidently inform imperial majesty to dispel any suspicion from him. Regarding sending our venerable brother, the patriarch of Antioch, to the same location, we could not comply. However, since the emperor is said to be arriving there soon, we command and sincerely advise you by apostolic writings not to delay coming into our presence by hastening your journey to meet him, to discuss matters pertaining to the honor of the church and the empire with us. We believe, as you have intimated in your letters to us, that with God's help, you will arrange these matters with us. Given as above.

### Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa magistro hospitalis sanctae Mariae Teutonicorum mandat, ut ad praesentiam suam festinato veniat, de rebus ad honorem ecclesiae ac imperii tractaturus, cum imperator Fredericus in Lombardia mox venturus sit, sublatis suspicionibus de proposito contra imperatorem procedendi. Datum Laterani, anno pontificatus IIII.

**Translation to English:**

To Hedwig of Sebhet, widow, of the Mainz diocese. To the just petitioners, etc., up to: fulfill. Therefore, since our beloved sons, the noble men Hermann the Younger and Henry, lords of Thuringia, have granted to you, out of regard for the services which you devotedly and faithfully rendered to the blessed Elizabeth while she was still alive, the village of Werd in the diocese of Mainz, as it belonged to them, as was proposed on your behalf before us, with liberal piety: we, inclined by your devotion's prayers, recognizing and affirming this donation, confirm to you by apostolic authority the same village, as you rightfully and peacefully possess it, and we fortify it with the protection of this present writing. Therefore, let no one, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the 14th day before the Kalends of January, in the twelfth year. In a similar manner, to the provost and dean of St. Castor in Confluentia of the Trier diocese, etc., up to: he possesses it and peacefully, we deemed it to be confirmed to him, etc. Given as above.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa Hedwidi de Sebhet, vidue Maguntine diocesis, donationem ville de Werd a nobilibus Hermanno iuniore et Henrico Thuringie sibi factam auctoritate apostolica confirmat. Datum Laterani, XIX Kal. Ianuarii, anno duodecimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the knights and people of Piacenza. Although we gladly think of peace for those who are far and near and wish to quell uprisings and preserve peace wherever it is restored, according to the duty of our office, we especially desire peace for your city, as it is a special daughter of the Apostolic See. The division within it tears at the heart of the Roman Church and its turmoil has greatly troubled us. We earnestly desire peace for your souls and bodies and, if the Lord wills, true unity. Recently, hearing that peace had been restored among you by the peacemaker's efforts, we rejoiced in the Lord for you and gave thanks. However, as much joy as this happy rumor brought us about the restoration of peace, we were later gravely disturbed to learn that some among you had violated the peace accords. Therefore, with fatherly concern, wishing to provide for the tranquility of that city, which we regard as an augmentation of the Apostolic See, and for your peace, whose unrest greatly disturbs us, we have charged our venerable brother, the Bishop of Ascoli, a prudent and discreet man, in whom we have full confidence, to go to your region for the peace of the whole province. Among other tasks, we have instructed him to have the terms of peace made among you presented to him, and if he finds them made in accordance with God's will for the common benefit of the parties, he should ensure they are observed inviolably. Otherwise, he should either correct them, if possible, as he deems fitting for the common good, or strive to reform the peace accords anew. And so that he may more effectively and freely attend to these matters without any hindrance, restraining any violence and repressing all armed force, he should repel any reinforcements coming to support the parties and compel those present in the city for any party's support to return home. We further exhort and command you through apostolic letters to receive him joyfully, treat him honorably, and devote yourselves humbly and devoutly to his salutary advice, counsel, and commands, so that your devotion may gladden your mother, the Roman Church, and reveal no less filial affection than it hoped for, thereby meriting our help and favor in your needs. Given at Viterbo, Nonis April, in the tenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa militibus et populo Placentino mandat, ut illorum civitatis pacem diligentissime observent, legato episcopo Esculano ad pacem reformandam et confirmandam misso. Dat. Viterbii, Nonis Aprilis, anno decimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Brixen. When previously the city of Bergamo was divided into factions due to internal wars, they finally agreed, under oath, to submit to the mandates of our beloved son G., Cardinal Priest of the title of St. Mark, then the apostolic legate in those parts, who personally visited there. He assigned the noble man P. de Turre, a citizen of Milan, to govern the city. However, since R. de Mandello was later installed in power there without admitting P., the same cardinal pronounced a sentence of excommunication on the men of Rivola and Suardis and their supporters and followers, and placed their mother church and parishes under ecclesiastical interdict. When they then offered to strictly obey our mandates, I instructed you, that if they satisfied the injuries, just damages, and moderate expenses of P., and provided sufficient surety that they would do their utmost to eliminate heretics and preserve the church's freedom, you should release those sentences according to the form of the church. Recently, prudent men, namely John de Biffa and La. Roniaa, representatives and procurators of both the commune and the aforementioned men of Rivola and Suardis, came to our presence and humbly implored us to mercifully provide for these matters. They asserted that the stipulated salary for the power of that city is five hundred imperial pounds, which should suffice annually for himself, two judges, and a suitable retinue, and that the aforementioned P., who did not remain there for five months, received two thousand nine hundred pounds of median money from the common funds of Bergamo from the said cardinal, as we also understood from him. They stated that he was more obliged to refund the said commune than to receive more from it; while a procurator of the said noble in our presence asserted the contrary and humbly requested that those citizens not be absolved before they adequately compensated P. for the said damages, injuries, and expenses. Since we, following the footsteps of Him who wants all to be saved and none to perish, and considering that where there is great slaughter, severity must be somewhat reduced, after receiving the oaths made by them to submit to our mandates, commanded them, under the obligation of the given oath, to revoke statutes and customs contrary to ecclesiastical liberty, and that similar ones are not resumed in the future, and also to include in their statutes the constitutions against heretics issued by us, which have been presented by you. We also wish and command that on our behalf they offer you sufficient and suitable surety to obey all our mandates regarding those for which they are found bound by the bond of excommunication or interdict by our authority or the cardinal's. Therefore, we command you, that by personally going to the place, if all the above are fulfilled, you release all the sentences and constitutions promulgated by the same cardinal against them on this occasion and the obligations made to him, by receiving an oath from them according to the form of the church, and declare those whom the cardinal specifically excommunicated, along with their guarantors, supporters, and assistants, absolved from the said sentences, constitutions, and obligations, notwithstanding any letters obtained from the apostolic see on the aforementioned matters. Given at Viterbo, IV Kalends of December, in the ninth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Brixiensi mandat ut, si cives Rivolae et Suardorum satisfaciant pro iniuriis et damnis P. de Turre et praestent cautionem de exterminandis haereticis et conservanda ecclesiae libertate, sententias excommunicationis et interdicti a cardinali S. Marci contra eos latas relaxet. 1235, Nov. 28, Viterbii.

**Translation to English:**

To the Podestà, council, and people of Viterbo. The closer the city of Viterbo is known to be to us and the more it is subjected to the Apostolic See, whose marks of devotion we have hitherto especially experienced, the more deeply we regret when you commit acts by which, besides the fault of ingratitude you incur, you abuse the mildness of the Roman Church, your mother, provoking our patience to anger. You indeed know and, as we believe, recognize in your devotion, that when you were once in great peril, so much so that you could hardly breathe from your difficulties, the Roman Church, your mother, who cannot forget the children of her womb and is afflicted in the affliction of her subjects and oppressed by the pressure of her children, anxiously began to think about your safety, and finally, to return the favor of peace to you, after multiple labors, after many and grave expenses, in a way poured herself out; and later, when the savagery of your persecutors was impending, adding favor to favor, for your peaceful state and of the entire province, as your same mother courageously girded herself against them, those who are far and those who are near know fully. But you, which we report not without mental disturbance, whom, as is publicly said, and would that it were not true! a root infected with the poison of heretical depravity sprouting into a toxic shoot has bewitched, attending not at all to the benefits conferred upon you as is fitting, presumed of you

**Translation to English:**

To the leaders of the Lombard League. With the affection of customary kindness, we recently received and heard your beloved ambassadors, faithful, prudent, and discreet, who prudently set forth what they wished and sought to commit to us in your name. However, because when they arrived, our beloved son, the master of the Teutonic Order, sent on behalf of our dearest son in Christ, Frederick of the Romans, had already departed after waiting for a long time at the Apostolic See, we, being certain that you acted not maliciously but in good faith during the delay of the said ambassadors, so that those sent by you would come with the procurators of all the cities of your party, immediately instructed the said master to return. But he excused himself through letters and a messenger, saying that, recalled by the emperor, who felt himself slighted, he could not do this without a special mandate from him. We directed our letters to the emperor, urging him to once again commit to us, hoping that with customary goodwill he will embrace our exhortations and advice. Since it is neither fitting nor expedient to undertake anything that might bring hindrance or difficulty to the matter, and so that you may not be noted for malice or carelessness in this regard, we have deemed it fit to send our venerable brother, the bishop of Ascoli, a prudent and discreet man, to your regions, believing that, as an angel of peace and counsel, he should bring forth the desired fruit of tranquility and salvation, converting the crooked into straight paths and the rough into smooth ways. Therefore, we have deemed it appropriate to admonish and exhort your community more earnestly, commanding you through apostolic letters, that receiving him kindly and treating him honorably, laying aside all animosities and rivalries, which bring innumerable losses to property and bodies and dangers to souls, you should diligently and humbly attend to his healthy admonitions, counsels, and commands concerning the peace of the region, so that your mother, the Roman Church, which ceases not to labor for you, considering you its special sons, may be gladdened by your devotion and should not have to grieve or complain that it found less filial affection in you than it had hoped. Otherwise, since we have commanded peace to be observed throughout the entire Christian world for the mission in the Holy Land, and have even compelled certain princes and magnates to this end, and there should not be double standards with us, we have instructed the bishop to proceed by our authority against the disobedient and rebellious, removing the obstacle of appeal if necessary. Given at Viterbo, on the Kalends of April, in the tenth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa rectoribus societatis Lombardie mandat ut episcopum Esculanum, ad pacem regionis promovendum, benigne recipiant et eius monitis obediant; alioquin contra rebelles procedatur. 1236, Apr. 1, Viterbii.

**Translation to English:**

To the archbishops, bishops, abbots, and other prelates of churches in Lombardy, the Trevisan March, and Romagna. Would that the day might dawn and the shadows incline, and the darkness of crimes be removed from your midst, Cant. 2:17; and the storm's cloud, which has covered almost the whole of your regions, so that He, to whom the winds and the sea obey, Matt. 8:27, who converts the storm into a breeze, and who, in accordance with the mystery of His beneficent will, reserving ways to show mercy everywhere, knows how to heal the wounds of the afflicted, might grant calm after the storm. How much tribulation has long pressed upon and still presses your regions, how grievous a persecution has surrounded and still surrounds the Christian people, how your regions have been worn by harsh wars, and how monasteries and churches have been attacked by various oppressions, can scarcely be recounted in detail, which we have been given to hear not without bitterness of mind, but you have been disposed as the Lord has decreed to experience. And although the Roman Church, as a loving mother who cannot forget the children of her womb, has labored much hitherto for the restoration of peace, pressing letter upon letter and envoy upon envoy, not once but often, not with only one but with several of our brethren in order that they might join together on the cornerstone, and that land might breathe from its distresses and be purged of its contagions, yet, with the author of schism working against it, a fitting remedy could not be applied. Since, however, we are constituted as the unworthy vicars of that peaceful King who, that He might reconcile the servant with the Lord, handed Himself over to death, we willingly consider plans of peace for those who are near and those who are far away, and we can no longer, without harm to our conscience and damage to our reputation, disregard the dangers to many souls, the loss of goods, the desolation of churches, the destruction of religious places, and the slaughter of the Christian people, especially since the aid to the Holy Land, to which the Christian people aspire, is greatly hindered by this, and lest the little foxes, which spoil the vineyard of the Lord, Cant. 2:15, and the venomous serpent in its astute wickedness prevail. Therefore, wishing that this land, which has long mourned and languished, may enjoy the desired peace and that the mountains may drip sweetness upon it and the hills joyfulness, Joel 3:18, so that, yielding rain from the heavens, it may produce good fruits, behold, we have decided, with the counsel of our brethren, to send to those regions our venerable brother the Patriarch of Antioch, a man indeed prudent and discreet, whom we and our brethren hold dear and acceptable due to his fervor of devotion and the merits of his own virtues, having granted him the full office of legate. He is to know what to uproot and destroy, what to build and plant, Jer. 1:10. We therefore admonish your entire community earnestly and exhort you, commanding you by way of instruction to receive and treat the aforesaid patriarch, as the legate of the apostolic see and holding a great place in the Church of God, or rather receiving us in him, cheerfully and honorably, attending to his salutary advice and mandates humbly and devoutly, and to observe inviolably the statutes he deems necessary for the restoration of peace, the matter of faith, the preservation of ecclesiastical liberty, the correction of morals, and the salvation of souls. Otherwise, we will ratify the sentence that he rightly imposes on the rebellious and, with the Lord as our guide, will ensure its firm observance. Given at Perugia, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of June, in the ninth year (of our pontificate). In the same manner to the noble men, marquises, counts, barons, podestàs, communities of cities, and all those established throughout Lombardy, the Trevisan March, and Romagna. In the same manner.. to the Doge of the Venetians. In the same manner to the Patriarch of Grado and his suffragans.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopis, episcopis, abbatibus aliisque ecclesiarum praelatis Lombardiae, Marchiae Tervisinae et Romaniolae mandat ut patriarcham Antiochenum legatum apostolicae sedis honorifice recipiant, eiusque mandatis pro pace et negotio fidei obediant; dat. Perusii, XII Kal. Iunii, anno nono (1235).

**Translation to English:**

To Otto, knight of Liechtenstein in the diocese of Naumburg. Laudably, as we have learned, you have chosen to flee the turmoil of the world and dedicate the remainder of your life to the pursuit of penance, so that you may find peace for your soul. Therefore, in order that this pious desire may be brought to fruition with our support, especially since, as it is asserted, you have left three parts of your goods to pious places for the honor of the Creator of all, leaving the remaining part to your only son, who is still of tender age, we, inclined by the prayers of your devotion, take your person under our protection; decreeing that your son shall remain under the guardianship and defense of the Apostolic See until he reaches the legal age of twenty-five. Let no one violate our protection. Given as above. It is written on this matter to the conservators, the bishop and provost of Meissen and the abbot of Sichem of the Cistercian order in the diocese of Halberstadt. To widows and orphans, whom, etc. As we have learned, our beloved son Henry, formerly advocate of Gera, and Jutta, his widow, etc. Given at the Lateran, 17th day before the Kalends of January, in the twelfth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Honorius III papa Ottoni militi de Liechtenstein Numburgensis diocesis, qui se vitae residuum studio poenitentiae deputare elegit, ipsiusque personam sub protectione apostolica suscipit et filium eius unicum ad annos viginti quinque sub tutela sedis apostolicae esse statuit. 1228, Dec. 16, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Penestrino, legate of the Apostolic See. How we write concerning the matter of Lombardy to our venerable brothers, the Archbishops of Milan and Ravenna and their suffragans, you will be able to see clearly in the letters which we send to them. Moreover, having a certain hope and unwavering confidence in the prudence of your circumspection, we hope—indeed, we hold with reasonable presumption—that since the Lord has given you a learned tongue and the word of the Lord is not bound in your mouth, so that you know how to overcome contradictors, if you should be present at the court of our dearest son in Christ, Frederick, you will handle everything with discretion and maturity, by the grace of God, for the honor of God and the Church and the good state of the empire. However, if by chance you are not present at the same court, lest the Roman Church remains inexcusable—which the truth of the matters sufficiently excuses—, you should impose this labor, with the counsel of the archbishops and their suffragans, on our venerable brother the Bishop of Brescia or our beloved son G., our subdeacon and chaplain, or on any of their archbishops or suffragans, as you see more expedient. Be prudently cautious, so that if the insolence of detractors boils over to such an extent that the said Emperor or his people openly open their mouths against the Church, which we do not believe, you should counteract their slander with the impact of truth, like the striking of flint or adamant, so that the purity of the Church shines more clearly. Having examined the writings and letters we recently sent to your devotion and those enclosed under our seal, which contain grievances inflicted on the churches and ecclesiastical persons of the Kingdom of Sicily and some others, some of which should have been revoked within three months from the time of the warning if he was in the kingdom, and within four months outside the kingdom in Italy, and within five months outside Italy, and if he, once warned, does not revoke the grievance within these set terms, he would incur a certain penalty. With all caution and diligence observed, and after careful deliberation, if necessary and great necessity demands, everything should be brought to light, and how faith to God and the Church has been kept should be proposed in defense of the Church. You, as a man of virtue and grace, should conduct yourself in word and deed with protestation of the law and honor of the empire so discreetly and circumspectly that no just occasion for detraction may be taken against the Church from your actions. We trust in the Lord, and hope in the power of His virtue, that with Him guiding your steps, you will strive to proceed along the royal way, which will lead to the glory of God, the exaltation of the Church, and the honor of your name. Given at Rieti, 17th August, in the tenth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Penestrino, apostolicae sedis legato, mandat ut, si curiae Friderici Romanorum imperatoris interesse nequiverit, laborem super negotiis Lombardiae aliis committat et puritatem ecclesiae tueatur. 1236, Aug. 17. Datum Reate.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Como. Having long understood the atrocity of the horrendous crime, which the noble man Rodulph of Grifenstein, the bearer of the present letter, committed in the murder of the late bishop of Chur of good memory, instigated by the devil, and with the same Rodulph humbly seeking reconciliation with his mother church, among other things, which our beloved son brother Rain, our penitentiarian, enjoined upon him after granting him the benefit of absolution according to the form of the church, he instructed him to take up the sign of the cross and cross over at the next general passage established by the Roman church to aid the Holy Land, intending to remain in service to that land for a certain term. Also, it was suggested to us afterward that the delay granted to him might bring danger, and we are said to have commanded you to compel him to cross over without further delay through ecclesiastical censure, removing the obstacle of appeal. Moreover, because it was proposed by his party before us that you had pressed him to cross over within the assigned term, imposing upon him and those with him the sentence of excommunication if they did not cross within the set term, and because he could neither pack his bags nor otherwise provide for himself in necessities, we command you, that if it is so, the sentence of excommunication imposed upon him should be relaxed according to the form of the church, and you should strive to extend the term for him until the upcoming feast of St. John, instructing the nobleman not to depart from there without the special license of the Apostolic See, and that his companions should remain in the service of the said land for at least two years. If, however, he does not care to cross over within the set term, you should not delay in returning him to the sentence of excommunication with all excuses ceasing and have it solemnly published in places where you see it fitting, proceeding nonetheless against them as you see fit. Given at the Lateran, on the tenth day before the Kalends of January, in the eleventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Cumano mandat ut Rodulpho de Grifenstein, qui homicidium episcopi Curiensis commiserat, post absolutionem ad Terram Sanctam transfretare iniungatur. Si vero in termino dato non transierit, excommunicationis sententia in eum reducatur. 1237, Dec. 23, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the Abbot of Saint Genevieve of Paris. Since our beloved sons Bonacura, Jacob, and Paul, citizens of Rome and agents of the provost of Lübeck, who is assigned at the Apostolic See for managing the affairs of the aldermen, jurors, and community of the city of Magdeburg, whose envoy and procurator he is, expressly renounced the constitution concerning two days' travel established in the general council and the exception of jurisdiction, having a mandate from them regarding this matter and the contracting of a loan, lent him three hundred and fifty marks of sterling silver, as the same provost admitted in our presence, to be repaid at a certain place and time, with both the provost and the aforementioned community being jointly obligated, as is more fully contained in the letters drawn up on this matter: We command your discretion, with the assent of the same provost, that if payment has not been made to these citizens at the place and time established, you shall then compel the provost, aldermen, jurors, and the said community, notwithstanding the aforementioned constitution and exception and any indulgence they may have, which would prevent them from being excommunicated or interdicted except by special mandate of the Apostolic See, to satisfy these citizens concerning the aforesaid money with just and moderate expenses and due restitution of damages, with interest wholly ceasing, as they are bound to do, by ecclesiastical censure after a prior warning, removing any appeal. Given at the Lateran on the Kalends of March, in the twelfth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati Sanctae Genovefae Parisiensis mandat, ut prepositum, scabinos, iuratos et communitatem Magdeburgensem compellat ad satisfaciendum civibus Romanis Bonacura, Iacobo et Paulo de pecunia mutuata, non obstantibus constitutione et exceptione, per censuram ecclesiasticam, appellatione remota. 1229, Mart. 1, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To Frederick, ever august Emperor of the Romans, illustrious King of Jerusalem and Sicily. The worst still persist, who, instigated by the instigator of all evils, are attempting to stir up scandal between you and the Roman Church, your mother, who nurtured you from the breasts of her sweet milk. They improperly launch into offenses against this Church, not without the scandal of many, considering it not your concern but their own, and with the devil's suggestion, they more confidently fish as rival fishermen in troubled waters.

Recently, your officials, perhaps without your knowledge, exceeding the boundaries of their office, have presumptuously laid hands on the rights of the apostolic see, occupying by damnable presumption the castle of Acquaviva, a special possession of this Church, and holding it against its will. They claim undue jurisdiction in the March, imposing bans, issuing edicts, making prohibitions, and attempting other acts, as if such jurisdiction within the lands of this Church pertained to them.

Therefore, dearest son, consider whether these things are to be tolerated equitably, whether we can pass them over with closed eyes without damage to conscience and loss of reputation. Do not dangerously ignore in your mother what you would rightly tolerate in no one else, and do not make the faults of your officials your own through consent, as an error not resisted is approved. We earnestly ask, exhort, and urge your imperial excellence that you effectively and swiftly have these matters corrected and these presumptuous acts duly punished with severity, demonstrating through your actions that these do not proceed from your conscience, so that no reason for disturbance is left to us because of this. We, for our part, will pursue the debt of our office against these presumptuous ones, with the Lord as our guide. Given at the Lateran, 4th March, in the eleventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

**Honorius III papa Friderico Romanorum imperatori mandat ut officialium suorum temerarias occupationes et indebite iurisdictionis vindicationem emendet, significans se contra presumptores officii sui debitum exsequi decrevisse. 1227, Mart. 4. Datum Laterani.**

**Translation to English:**

To the citizens of Velletri, faithful to the Apostolic See. The ancient faithfulness of your ancestors and yourselves has long merited that your city be honored by the Apostolic See with the grace of special munificence and the privilege of singular liberty, so that the gifts granted might bring joy and encourage you and your descendants to serve faithfully. In order to inflame your hearts more ardently towards the service of the Mother Church, the late Pope Urban II, of happy memory, inscribed in his privilege granted to your city how your ancestors, of unwavering faithfulness to the Church, endured mockery, beatings, chains, and imprisonment, and ultimately, withstanding death, stood strong in mind against all adversaries of the Church. Because you have been tested in the furnace of tribulation and have often shone bright in the purity of faith like refined gold, as true branches springing from that noble and memorable lineage, you strive to follow in their footsteps. Despite facing the losses and destruction of your goods for the Apostolic See, you boldly expose yourselves to peril amid enemies. Therefore, since you stand with us in our trials, we faithfully intend to cherish you like a domestic family in the bosom of the Mother Church, to love you more earnestly, and to adorn you with signs of customary liberty. Thus, we confirm the liberties and immunities granted and the customs affirmed by our predecessors, Popes Paschal and Urban, of happy memory, and observed up to now, by apostolic authority, and decree they be observed in the future. You shall supply food for one meal to our court, and also furnish parliaments and hostings through Maritima and Campania. Following the example of our predecessors, Gregory VII and Urban, we abolish, by the authority of these presents, all customs and exactions imposed upon you by the more powerful, and forbid them from imposing burdens or subjecting you to their rule, as you ought to remain quietly and freely under the jurisdiction and power of the Apostolic See as special sons and faithful. We decree that the inhabitants of your city and the ancient boundaries of your land be kept safe from any invasion or harassment by secular power. We confirm to you, and without any contradiction, decree that you and your heirs in the future shall possess cultivated and uncultivated lands, forests, mountains, plains, streams, marshes, aqueducts, and all other possessions, as contained in the ancient privileges of the Roman pontiffs and as you have hitherto possessed them. We have thought it appropriate to note the boundaries themselves here as they are described in the privilege of Paschal: From the first side, it begins at the trench that descends from Monte Episcopi and descends to the water of Palumba and thence to the silex of Macro. He and the dear son, the elected Bishop of Pace, preferred to await the response of the said prince in this matter rather than undertake anything without his counsel, and thus they did not accept anything on this. Moreover, the same judge proposed before us that it was the will of the said emperor that certainty concerning the commitment made by the Lombards should reach him by the next upcoming feast of the Nativity of the Lord, and that the sum of twenty thousand marks expressed in the arbitration should be increased, and that the rectors and councils of the cities of the Lombard league, if they presumed to contravene our order or arrangement, should incur excommunication by that very fact, and we were arranging how this matter might be healthily concluded. To the Archbishop of Reims and his suffragans. Let us go out to Jesus, according to the apostle, outside the camp, bearing His reproach, Hebr. 13:13, so that we may deem His disgrace our own, considering the injuries inflicted on Him as if inflicted on ourselves. As He bore our shortcomings by His birth and endured pains by His death, He was made a little lower than the angels at His birth, and He emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men and found in appearance as a man; and by dying, was captured, dragged, bound, struck, mocked with blows, crucified, killed, pierced, and buried. Thus, although there is no likeness between the creature and the Creator, that we may at least render something for all He has given us, His injury should touch us, so that we might help the poor Jesus Christ to relieve the insults, Matt. 27:40, hurled at Him by the enemies of our faith, who scoff at Him and say: "If you are the Son of God, save yourself; if you can, free the land of your birth from our hands and restore your cross to its worshippers." Indeed, it is a disgrace to the Christian people that the King of Kings, who made all things, has lost the land, which is the portion of His inheritance, due to our sins, from His own seat, in which Baruch 3:38 He was seen bodily and conversed with men, and where He carried out all the sacraments of our redemption. How anxiously would the apostle cry out today if he were still in the world: "Let us go out to Jesus outside the camp, bearing His reproach." Perhaps he would say: "Let us go out Gen. 12:1 like Abraham from our land, houses, and kindred, both bodily and mystical, to go into that land once renowned and consecrated by the blood of Christ, so that with God's help, having expelled the Amorites from there, we might ascend Mount Zion with Judas Maccabeus to cleanse and renew the sacred places, adorning the temple of our Lord God with golden crowns." Christ Himself also cries out in Matt. 16:24: "Whoever wants," He says, "to come after Me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow Me," as if to say: "The battle is at hand, I prepare the battle line; therefore, whoever is Mine, let him follow Me. Gregorius IX papa, episcopo quondam Mutinensi, apostolicae sedis legato, mandat ut assumat officium praedicationis in provincia Bremensi et aliis locis ad succursum fidelium, et remissionem peccaminum concedit eis qui labori isti in propriis personis et expensis subierint. Datum Viterbii, XV Kalendas Martii, anno IX.
