Since, as it has been intimated to us on behalf of our venerable brother, the Bishop of Veszprém, he is suffering from such a severe bodily illness that he cannot personally come to the council, which we, with the Lord's blessing, plan to hold, by the authority of these presents we command you to grant him, by our authority, permission to remain, provided that he takes care to send an appropriate representative to the said council. Given at the Lateran, the fifteenth day before the Kalends of April, in the fourteenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa (Iohanni de Civitella subdiacono et notario, capellano suo mandat, ut, si episcopus Vesprimiensis gravi infirmitate impeditur, licentiam remanendi tribuat, nuntium tamen ad concilium destinare curet. 1241, Mart. 18, Laterani).

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Otto, Count of Guelders. In order to satisfy your conscience, which you say is troubled, regarding the receipt of the fruits of the tithes that you and your predecessors have claimed to receive from time immemorial: by the merit of your devotion, we grant you by the authority of these presents that you may freely receive the fruits of these tithes, provided that you spend the received or a part of them and those to be received on assisting our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, W., in the business of the Church. To no one etc. Given at Lyon, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of August, in the eighth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Octoni comiti Gelrensi indulget, ut fructus decimarum percipere possit, dummodo eos expendat in negotio ecclesiae assistendo regi Romanorum. 1251, Iul. 18. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the podestà, councilors, and community of the Genoese. The sincere devotion that we know you have towards us and the Roman Church is commendably deserving, so that we may grant your petitions as much as we can with God's will. Therefore, since due to the dangers of wars that now threaten the province of Lombardy, you cannot leave the city of Genoa and its district without risking persons and property, we are inclined to your prayers and grant by our letters that you and your citizens and men from the aforementioned district cannot be summoned to judgment outside the city and its district, unless mention of this indulgence is made, and this shall remain in effect until it pleases us otherwise. Let no one, therefore, violate our concession, etc. If anyone, however, etc. Given at the Lateran, April 28th, in the thirteenth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa potestati, consiliariis et communi Ianuensium significat se indulxisse, ne extra civitatem Ianuensem et districtum eius ad iudicium trahi possint. 1239, Apr. 28. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the same. The unwavering faith and tireless devotion, which the beloved sons, the people of Benevento, our faithful ones, laudably demonstrate towards us and the Roman Church, their mother, like sons of blessing and grace, as well as the distress and pressures they almost constantly endure, effectively persuade us that just as we embrace them with the prerogative of special love and grace, so we should follow them with blessings of sweetness. Therefore, so that our aforementioned faithful, weighed down by the blows of various persecutions, may rejoice and breathe anew in the consolation of our grace, we command that any legacies and bequests left for the aid of the Holy Land, be converted, by apostolic authority, by your hands to the use of poor able-bodied men for fighting and for the repair of walls; opposing parties, etc. And if not all, etc. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa dilectis filiis populo Beneventano mandat, ut legata et fideicommissae ad subsidium Terrae Sanctae relicta in usus pauperum ad pugnandum et in reparationem murorum convertantur. Datum Laterani, anno pontificatus sexto.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Ancozacase, a Roman citizen and signatory of the cross. It was presented before us on your behalf that the authority and commune of Monte Alto, because you refused to return to them and adhere against the Church and Catholic faith in favor of Frederick, the so-called emperor, an enemy of God and the Church, wickedly divided among themselves the possessions, lands, houses, vineyards, incomes, and other properties which you held by hereditary right within the district of Monte Alto, obtaining letters of confirmation from the said Frederick regarding this. Therefore, inclined by your prayers, we have deemed what was rashly done by the aforesaid Frederick and the authority and commune as void, decreeing that no prejudice to your right may be generated in the future by this, but rather that you may freely return to the possessions and other aforementioned properties, having obtained the ability to do so. Therefore, let no one infringe upon our decrees, etc. If anyone, however, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the 13th day before the Kalends of June, in the fifteenth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro Ancozacase, civi Romano cruce signato, acta Frederici et communis Montis alti, quibus possessiones Ancozacase divisae sunt, irrita decernit et ius eius in possessiones restituit. Datum Laterani, XIII Kalendas Iunii, anno XV.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Castellan. As our venerable brother, the Bishop of Treviso, has shown to us by his complaint, Ezzelino da Romano, an enemy of God and the Church, has forcibly occupied the castles of Asolo and Montebelluna, the fortress of Braida, and the fortress of Cornuda, as well as villages, estates, possessions, and other rights of the Church of Treviso, in violation of the oath of loyalty he owes to it. He continues to hold these occupied places and refuses to return them. Therefore, we command that if this is so, you compel the said Ezzelino, by the sentences of excommunication upon his person and interdict on his land, removing any appeal, to restore the aforementioned castles and other properties, along with the fruits received from them or which could have been received, to the said church within a month after your admonition, as he is bound to do. Ensuring that both sentences are strictly observed until due satisfaction is rendered. Given at the Lateran, the 12th day before the Kalends of December, in the 13th year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Castellano mandat, ut Ezelinum de Romano, castra et alia iura ecclesie Tervisine occupata restituere recusantem, excommunicationis sententia coerceat. 1239, Nov. 20. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the minister of the Friars Minor in Saxony. The nobleman, the Landgrave of Thuringia, and his wife, desiring to align themselves with divine grace through works of worthy penance, have humbly petitioned us to grant them a religious priest who may hear their confessions and assign them salutary penance. Therefore, favoring their pious intention benevolently, we command that you appoint one of your brothers, whom you find to be suitable, to diligently carry out these tasks with our authority. He should absolve the nobleman, if he finds him to have incurred the sentence of excommunication for the violent laying of hands on clerics and religious persons, or for arson or robbery, or if he should incur such in the future, provided that he adequately satisfies those who have suffered damages and injuries. If the nobleman's offenses are grave and enormous, he should be sent to the Apostolic See to be absolved. Given at Anagni, on the 5th day before the Kalends of August, in the thirteenth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa ministro fratrum Minorum in Saxonia mandat, ut sacerdotem eligat qui Lantgravium Thuringiae et uxorem eius confessionibus audiendis et poenitentiam imponendam deputet, cum facultate absolutionis pro violentia in clericos et rapinis, salvo gravium excessuum casu ad sedem apostolicam mittendo. Anagnie, 28 Iulii, 1239.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Arezzo, rector of the March of Ancona. Since, as we have learned from your report, some individuals in the March of Ancona who, due to the favor shown to Frederick, the so-called emperor, are bound by the chain of excommunication, wish to return to the embrace of the mother church: we command your fraternity through apostolic writings, that you, through yourself and others whom you may consider suitable for this, ensure that upon receiving from them a sufficient guarantee of obedience to the mandates of the church and that they will not further revert to the side of the said Frederick, grant them the benefit of absolution in accordance with the form of the church. Given at the Lateran, on the 18th of January, in the fourteenth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX episcopo Aretino, marchie Anconitane rectori mandat, ut quibusdam excommunicatis in dicta marchia constitutis, qui ad ecclesiam redire cupiunt, post cautionem de parendo mandatis ecclesie et non redeundo ad partem Friderici acceptam, beneficium absolutionis impendat. 1239, Jan. 18. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the Podestà and council of the Genoese. We have understood that our venerable brother, the Bishop of Palestrina, and our beloved son, O., Cardinal Deacon of St. Nicholas in Carcere, legates of the Apostolic See, have assembled at Lyon with the prelates of the churches from the regions beyond the Alps who are hastening to the council, at the place where a ship will soon be prepared for their passage. Therefore, having sincere confidence in you, as special and beloved sons of the Roman Church, we earnestly ask and exhort your community, commanding that, as you love the honor of God and the grace of the Apostolic See and ours, you hasten to meet those legates and prelates with a multitude of galleys and vessels, so that, with God's help, you may be able to convey them with their families and necessary belongings comfortably and safely. Thus, we shall be bound to commend the affection and zeal of your devotion in the Lord.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa potestati et consilio Ianuensium mandat, ut legatis et prelatis apud Lugdunum congregatis cum navigiis occurrere festinent et eos secure transportare procurent. Datum Lugduni.

### Translation to English:

To the noble men, lords of the castle of Frusino, in the diocese of Veroli. To the just petitioners, etc., as far as: complete. Indeed, from your report, we have learned that you were once unjustly deprived of the lordship, consulship, and half the revenues of the castle of Frusino by certain bailiffs of the Roman curia. Our beloved son, R., cardinal deacon of Sant'Angelo, rector of Campania and Marittima, has restored these to you by our mandate and has invested your syndic, John of Capua, in all these things on your behalf, as it is said to be contained in the public document drawn up about this. Therefore, inclined by your supplications, we confirm with apostolic authority what has been done by the same cardinal in this matter and protect it with the support of this present writing. Therefore, let no one—our confirmation, etc. But if anyone, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the second day before the Nones of December, in the fourteenth year.

### Regesto in Latin:

**Gregorius IX papa nobilibus viris dominis castri Frusinonis Verulanae diocesis restitutionem iurium et proventuum per R. Sancti Angeli diaconum cardinalem factam auctoritate apostolica confirmat. 1231, Dec. 4. Laterani.**

**Translation to English:**

To the Chapter of Ancona and the clergy of the city and diocese of Ancona. Our venerable brother, the bishop of Arezzo, not forgetting the sincere devotion and faith he has always shown towards the apostolic see, chose to endure persecutions and other temporal losses from Frederick, the so-called emperor, an enemy of God and the church, rather than veer from that devotion in any way. Therefore, unwilling to allow the same bishop, who has been completely stripped of his episcopal revenues by the said Frederick, to be forced into begging, to the disgrace of his episcopal dignity and the apostolic see, especially since we have commanded him to remain in the Marches for church affairs, we have decided to grant him the revenues of the bishopric of Ancona for his sustenance until our further pleasure. Wherefore, we admonish your community to ensure that these revenues are provided to the bishop. Otherwise, any sentence he duly pronounces against the rebellious, we will uphold and ensure it is observed inviolably until proper satisfaction has been made, with the Lord as witness. Given at the Lateran, November 7, in the fourteenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Capitulo Anconitano et clero civitatis et diocesis Anconitane mandat, ut episcopo Aretino, qui a Friderico imperatore spoliatus est, proventus episcopatus Anconitani exhibeant ad sustentationem, alioquin sententiam contra rebelles latam ratam habebit. 1241, November 7.—Laterani.

### Translation to English:

Gregory, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons in Christ, all the Lombards present and future, greetings and apostolic blessing. It is fitting that we incline the ears of the apostolic dignity more benignly to hear the desires of the supplicants, as that which is advised and sought is more fitting to be heard. Therefore, assenting to your just wishes, we give you by this present privilege the license and grant you the free power, that whenever the Roman Emperor wishes to enter the Italian region, as contained in the agreement made with the illustrious son of blessed memory, King Frederick of Constance, you may form alliances and bind yourselves with oaths and promises to preserve your rights, saving all honors and services that you ought to render to the Roman princes, who shall be at that time, by agreement or approved custom, which we do not wish to derogate in any way by this privilege. Let no man at all dare to infringe this our privilege or contradict it rashly. But if anyone presumes to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the wrath of Almighty God and the blessed Apostles Peter and Paul.

### Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa omnibus Lombardis praesentibus et futuris licentiam dat et concedit potestatem liberam societatem faciendi iuramentis et promissionibus, quotienscunque imperator Romanus Ytalicam regionem intrare voluerit, ad iusta desideria eorum conservanda, salvis honoribus et servitiis Romanis principibus praestandis. 1230, Romae.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Humanatensis. Considering the steadfastness and sincerity of the devotion and faith, which the beloved sons, the council and people of Racanatensis, are known to have observed in loyalty to the Apostolic See against Frederick, the so-called emperor, and detesting the treachery of the people of Auximanum, who damnably adhered to the said Frederick, persecuting the faith and ecclesiastical liberty, we exempt the castle of Racanate from the jurisdiction of the Humanatensis church and have decided to transfer the seat of Auximanum with all its rights and appurtenances to the said castle. However, in recompense for the rights which the Humanatensis church held in the said castle, we may assign some part of the Auximanum diocese, when we see fit. Meanwhile, wishing to make provision for you and your church as much as we can in God, we grant by the authority of these presents to your fraternity that you may collect all episcopal revenues in the said castle until our pleasure be known. Given at the Lateran, 17th Kalends of December, in the 14th year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Humanatensi mandat exemptionem castri Racanate ab ecclesia Humanatensi et translationem sedis Auximanae cum omnibus iuribus ad idem castrum, cum concessione ut episcopus proventus episcopales ibi recipiat usque ad beneplacitum papale. Datum Laterani, XVI Kalendas Decembris, anno quarto decimo.

Translation to English:

To John of Civitella, our subdeacon and chaplain. Since we have decided to instruct you to preach the word of the cross against Frederick, the so-called emperor, the son of perdition, in the kingdom of Hungary, and since several in the said kingdom have taken the cross in aid of the Holy Land, which creates not a small impediment to your purpose, we, considering that it is so much more salutary to assist the Apostolic See in this time of necessity, as it is the mother and head of faith being grievously attacked to the peril of Christendom, grant you, by the authority of these presents, the free faculty to convert the vows of those crusaders to the defense of the Church against the same Frederick, provided their consent is obtained. You may also grant them, and others redeeming their vows, the remission of sins that was granted to those assisting the said land in the general council, as long as they assign the expenses they would incur by going to the said land, staying there, and returning from there, into your hands and those of our beloved son, the abbot of Pelis of the Cistercian order, and Benedict the canon of Strigonium, to be transmitted for such defense. Given at the Lateran, February 12, in the 14th year.

Regesto:

Gregorius IX papa Iohanni de Civitella subdiacono et capellano suo mandat ut vota crucesignatorum in defensionem ecclesiae contra Fredericum convertat, si eorum consensus obtineatur, et veniam peccatorum concedat, expensis in defensionem assignatis. 1241, Feb. 12, Lateranum.

**Translation to English:**

Gregory, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons, the elected of Grado and the archdeacons of Grado and Castellanense, greetings and apostolic blessing. Since we have received under the special protection of blessed Peter and our own, our beloved son, the noble man, the duke, and the community of the Venetians, and since it is fitting for us to support with apostolic patronage those who persist in the service of the Church: we command your discretion through apostolic writings, that you do not allow the said duke and community to be unjustly harassed by anyone in their persons, goods, or lands, as long as their army persists in going to, staying in, or returning from the service of the apostolic see in occupying the kingdom of Sicily, restraining such harassers by ecclesiastical censure, postponing appeals. If not all of you are able to attend to these matters, let two of you nevertheless carry them out. Given at Anagni, on the eighth day before the Kalends of October, in the thirteenth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa electo Gradensi et archidiaconis Gradensi et Castellanensi, mandat ut ducem et communitatem Venetorum sub protectione ecclesiae existentes defendant a molestatoribus in regno Siciliae, censura ecclesiastica, si necesse sit, compescendis. Anagniae, VIII Kal. Oct., anno pontificatus XIII.

**Translation to English:**

To the knights of the castle of Frusino in the diocese of Verula. Your petition presented to us stated that a dispute was ongoing between you, on one side, and the inhabitants of the castle of Frusino, on the other, regarding a payment in money which you claimed was owed to you by the said inhabitants. This dispute was being handled by our beloved son, St., our chaplain and then rector of Campania and Maritime provinces, not by our delegation. The said rector, after understanding the merits of the case, issued a definitive sentence in your favor against those inhabitants. However, they appealed to us, and regarding their appeal, they obtained from us the concession of our venerable brother R., bishop of Ostia, as the auditor. After consulting with prudent men, he confirmed the aforesaid sentence and decreed it to be executed, as is more fully contained in the public document drawn up thereafter. Therefore, you humbly petitioned us to ensure that the same sentence was fortified with apostolic authority. We, therefore, agreeing with your requests with favorable assent, confirm the sentence providently passed with apostolic authority and strengthen it with the support of this present letter. Therefore, let no one infringe upon this confirmation of ours, etc. But if anyone, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the 7th Ides of February, in the 13th year.

---

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa militibus castri de Frusinone Verulane diocesis sententiam a rectore Campaniae pro ipsis latam, et a R. Ostiense episcopo confirmatam, auctoritate apostolica confirmat et communit. 1239, Feb. 7. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the diocese of Autun. We empathize with your monastery, which, burdened with the weight of debt, is said to be almost entirely consumed by the abyss of usury, so that hardly any substance remains for it. We grieve for the poverty to which it is known to have come. Therefore, as your petition presented to us contained, you, wishing to prevent the injury to your monastery and to avert the dangers to your people, who are sometimes killed due to such debts, and the land of the said monastery is ravaged by raids and fire, so that you may be freed from the pressure of creditors, have proposed, with the consent of the diocesan and chapter intervening, to remit a certain servitude, commonly called "mortmain," to your men of Flavigny, who are prepared to contribute to the payment of these debts according to their own means. You humbly requested us to grant you the permission to do this. We, inclined by your supplications, grant you the requested permission. Given at the Lateran, on the 8th of June, in the fifteenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa diocesi Eduensi concedit licentiam remittendi servitutem, quae manus mortua vulgariter nuncupatur, hominibus Flavigniaci ad solvenda debita monasterii. 1231, Iun. 8. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To all our faithful established throughout the March of Ancona. Having experienced the sincerity of devotion and faith, together with the prudence of our venerable brother, the Bishop of Arezzo, in many affairs of the Apostolic See, we have great confidence in him, so that with the trust placed in his industry from past dealings, we appoint him to faithfully promote and discretely manage matters in such a way that honor and benefit may arise for the Roman Church, and the elevation of the subjects may achieve happy progress. Therefore, since our beloved son, the Cardinal Priest of the title of St. Lawrence in Lucina, having recently returned from the March, must remain at the Apostolic See for pressing and arduous concerns, we have decided to provisionally appoint the said bishop as rector of your province. Wherefore, we earnestly ask and urge all of you, through apostolic letters, to receive him with due honor, indeed as if it were us, and diligently and faithfully obey his commands. Otherwise, we will consider the penalty he rightfully imposes spiritually and temporally on the rebellious as valid and, by the grace of the Lord, will ensure it is observed inviolably until due satisfaction is achieved. Given at the Lateran, on the 2nd Ides of December, in the fourteenth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa universis fidelibus per Anconitanam marchiam constitutis mandat, ut episcopum Aretinum, interim rectorem provinciae, cum debita honorificentia recipiant et mandatis eius obediant. 1238, Dec. 12, Laterano.

**Translation:**

To the Commune of Ascoli: Considering the pleasing services that you have rendered to the Apostolic See until now and continue to diligently provide, as well as the tribulations and hardships you endure from Frederick, enemy of God and the Church, for maintaining fidelity to the Church and Apostolic See, we willingly intend for the honor and benefit of your city and respond to its services with a pleasing exhibition of benefits, as far as we are able according to God. Hence, with a grateful concurrence to your prayers, by the authority of these presents we grant you that against wrongdoers who are within your city and territory, you may be able to exercise the due justice according to the order of law and the ancient and approved custom of other cities of the March. Let no one, therefore, violate our concession, etc. If anyone, however, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the 12th of May, in the fifteenth year.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa Communi Esculano concedit potestatem iustitiam exercendi contra malefactores secundum ius et consuetudinem Marchie. 1242, Maii 12, Laterano.

**Translation to English:**

To Gregorio de Montelongo, our subdeacon and notary, legate of the apostolic see. Since the Patriarch of Aquileia, for having presumed to communicate with Frederick, called the emperor, an enemy of God and the Church, who was justly bound by us with the sentence of excommunication for many reasons due to his faults, both in divine offices and in the kiss of peace and at the table, and because he neglected to publicly excommunicate the same, as he had received from us in orders, although he had decided to execute it before many, and not promptly coming to our presence, as he had been commanded on our behalf, he was tied by the sentence of excommunication by our authority: because we embrace with a special prerogative of love and grace the persons of our dearest sons Béla of Hungary and Coloman of the Ruthenes, illustrious kings and nephews of the same patriarch, granting their supplications, we command that, setting aside all things, you personally proceed to Venice or Torcello and grant to the aforementioned patriarch, once he has begun his journey to our presence, the gift of absolution by our authority according to the form of the Church, humbly asking. Given at the Lateran, the fifth day before the Kalends of February, in the fourteenth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Gregorio de Montelongo, subdiacono et notario suo ac apostolicae sedis legato, mandat, ut patriarche Aquilegensi, ob communionem cum Friderico imperatore excommunicato et inobedientiam, venienti ad sedem apostolicam absolutionis munus impendat. 1239, Jan. 28. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Esztergom. Believing you to be a man after our own heart and able to rejoice in you as a special son of the Roman Church, we have confidently decided to commit the Church of Esztergom, a noble indeed member of the Church of God, to you, hoping that, called to share in the concern, you would thus share with us the burdens in pressing necessity, so that we might boast that we have appointed a useful cultivator of the vineyard of the Lord Sabaoth and have taken up a suitable helper for us. But, which we report not without disturbance, as bearing a wound from an unexpected enemy, in the immediate necessity, you withdraw the service of your devotion from your mother church, which no persecution or sword, present or future, should in any way separate you from. Although you have sent us certain letters of excuse for not coming to the council some time ago, and we have responded to you on this as we saw fit: since, however, you have recently reiterated the same to our ears through other letters, expressing certain difficulties and dangers of the roads in these letters, since now by the grace of God the way has been providently arranged by which you and others can safely come to the apostolic see, without needing to pass through places of peril or lands of enemies of the Church, about which you can be fully informed by our messengers, we wish and by apostolic writings command you in the virtue of obedience, that according to the tenor of our first mandate you do not delay coming to the council. Given at the Lateran, 26th February, in the fourteenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Strigoniensi mandat ut ad concilium veniat, difficultatibus viarum iam provisis superatis. 1231, Febr. 26, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the archbishops and bishops and prelates of churches and to noble men and other faithful Christians established throughout the kingdom of France. The people of Siena, sons of malediction, unmindful of the many benefits they have often received from the kindness of the Holy Mother Church, have recently presumed to gravely offend her beyond expectation and merit. Therefore, so that they may be taught by experience to recognize what good can come to them through the pursuit of devotion and what evil may befall them through the vice of ingratitude, we command that you must by no means provide satisfaction for the debts of the said Sienese from now on without our special mandate, with no harm to be incurred in the future by reason of such detention. Given at the Lateran, on the 28th of April, in the thirteenth year (of our pontificate). In the same manner to those established throughout Germany. In the same manner to those established throughout the kingdom of England.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopis, episcopis, ecclesiarum prelatis, nobilibus viris et aliis Christi fidelibus per regnum Franciae constitutis mandat, ne Sienensibus de ipsorum debitis absque speciali mandato satisfactionem impendant, propter eorum ingratitudinem contra ecclesiam. 1240, Apr. 28, Laterano.

**Translation to English:**

To Bartholomew and Oddo, brothers and citizens of Perugia. It was presented before us on your behalf that the Fulignates, from Spello, Mevania, and other communities of certain castles, followers of Frederick, the so-called emperor, enemy of God and the Church, inflicted many damages upon you regarding certain vineyards, possessions, quantities of grain, and other matters. Because of this, our beloved son, Brother Bonus Vicinus, our chamberlain, has granted you the power to seize the goods of those who, being rebels to the Church, have been excommunicated by us, until full satisfaction is rendered to you, as is more fully contained in the letters drawn up on this matter. Therefore, inclined by your devoted prayers, we confirm and ratify what has been appropriately done in this matter by the same brother by apostolic authority and secure it with the protection of this present script. Let no one infringe our confirmation, etc. But if anyone, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the Kalends of July, in the fourteenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Bartholomeo et Oddoni fratribus Perusinis significat, quod Fuliginates et alii sequaces Friderici imperatoris damna irrogarunt super vineis et possessionibus; mandat et confirmat auctoritate apostolica potestatem a fratre Bono Vicino ad res capiendas usque ad satisfactionem plenariam. 1239, Kal. Iul., Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the same. Since, as we have learned, Ezzelino da Romano, the enemy of God and the Church, has been bound by various sentences of excommunication by apostolic authority due to his crimes, and has remained in them for three years and more, damnably scorning the keys of the Church: because it is fitting that those whom the fear of God does not recall from evil should at least be restrained by temporal discipline, we command that, unless he returns to the command of the Church with a willing mind, having been diligently warned by you within a month, you should strive to deprive him of all fiefs which he is known to hold from both the Church of Treviso and other churches, by our authority, and furthermore announce to him that he is deprived of them, expressly warning him on our behalf that from then on we will proceed against him as against a heretic and a despiser of the keys of the Church. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa mandat officiali ecclesiastico, ut Ezzelino de Romano, excommunicato et inimico Dei et ecclesiae, nisi infra mensem ad ecclesiae mandatum redierit, suis feudis privetur et heretici poenae subiaceat. Datum Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishops of Hildesheim, Merseburg, and the Abbot of Porta, of the Cistercian order: We rejoice in the Lord that, as we have learned, through His merciful inspiration, our beloved son, the noble Landgrave of Thuringia, and some others from his land, desiring to withdraw from harmful ways and to be directed toward salvation, have chosen to emulate the brothers known as the Penitents. They have decided to crucify their flesh with its vices and desires, so that, by serving as soldiers to the eternal King during this brief temporal life, they may receive from Him the reward of heavenly bliss. Therefore, considering it fitting that such individuals should enjoy the prerogative of special grace, we command you to assist them favorably and not allow them to be rashly troubled by anyone against their pious intention, lest they be hindered in such worthy service to the Lord. Restrain such molesters through ecclesiastical censure, setting aside any appeals, notwithstanding the decree concerning two days' journeys issued in the general council. If all of you cannot be present to execute these matters, let two of you nonetheless carry them out. Given at Anagni, on the 6th day before the Kalends of August, in the 13th year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopis Ildesemensi et Merseburgensi ac abbati de Porta Cisterciensis ordinis scribit, gaudens de conversione lantgravii Thuringiae et aliorum, mandat ut eos foveant, ne a proposito suo a quibusdam impediantur, molestatores per censuram ecclesiasticam compescendo. 1239, Julii 27, Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the matters concerning, are added. When we, sending you to Genoa for certain urgent matters of the Roman Church, have given our letters to our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Genoa, instructing him to have complete trust in you regarding what you say on our behalf, especially with regards to the money necessary for the expediting of these matters, which you will declare to him, he should not hesitate to obligate both himself and the Genoese Church; for we will ensure full satisfaction for this to those to whom it is due, keeping him and his church harmless over this obligation. We command that if the said archbishop neglects to fulfill our mandate, you shall compel him to do so by our authority, removing any appeal. Dated at the Lateran, 7th Kalends of July, in the fifteenth year. In nearly the same manner, it is written concerning this to the same archbishop. In the same manner to the chapter of Genoa. In the same manner to the abbot and convent of Saint Fructuosus in the diocese of Genoa. In the same manner to the abbot and convent of Saint Syrus of Genoa. In the same manner to the abbot and convent of Saint Bartholomew of Fossato in Genoa.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa venerabili fratri archiepiscopo Ianuensi mandat, ut plenam fidem legato papali adhibeat et pecuniam necessariam pro negotiis ecclesiae Romanae sine dubio se ac ecclesiam Ianuensem obliget; si vero archiepiscopus mandatum neglexerit, legatus eum appellatione remota compellat. 1241, Iun. 25, Laterani.

### Translation to English:
To the podestà, council, and people of Spoleto. We rejoice in the Lord that you, steadfast in the devotion of your Mother Church like an unmovable column, have not been separated by any persecution or adversity from its fidelity and service, enduring the plundering and burning of your goods to preserve its honor. Through this, you obtain the reward of eternal retribution before God and the title of perpetual praise among men. We, acknowledging that such devotion cannot and should not escape the attention of the Apostolic See, propose to recompense the affection of such great devotion with an effect of worthy retribution and aspire with eager and perpetual desire to the exaltation of your city. Therefore, because we wish at present to grant the grace we can to your city, so that you may become even more devoted from your devotion, we have decided to grant you, as you persist in the devotion of the Church, the revenues which the Roman Church holds in the diocese of Spoleto, except for the revenues assigned to the custody of our fortifications, until it pleases our will. Given at Crypta Ferrata, September 1st, in the 14th year [of our pontificate].

### Regesto in Latin:
Gregorius IX papa potestati, consilio et populo Spoletano gratulatur pro fide ac devotione erga Ecclesiam, quae eos in adversitatibus non separavit, et concedit eis redditus in diocesi Spoletana, exceptis redditibus ad custodiam munitionum deputatis, ad beneplacitum suum. 1231, Sept. 1, apud Criptam Ferratam.

**Translation to English:**

Gregory, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son, the noble Duke of the Venetians, greetings and apostolic blessing. We wish to make known to your nobility that the Church will take care and ensure that the one to whom the Kingdom of Sicily will be entrusted by the Church will swear to uphold the agreements and conventions established between it and you, as well as the Venetian community, as is known to be contained in the public instrument drawn up by the hand of our beloved son Nicholas of Ferentino, the scribe of our chamber. This is provided that those who will govern Barolo and Salpis on behalf of you and the same community at the time, will, in the presence of those to whom we and our successors shall see fit to entrust this, deliver the oath in Venice that they will not conspire, act, counsel, or consent to cause the appointed person by the Roman Church to lose life or limb, land, honors, dignities, or other goods they might have in the aforementioned kingdom, nor will they suffer harm by their capture as a person. Given at Anagni, on the eighth day before the Kalends of October, in the thirteenth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa duci Venetorum scribit se curaturum, ut is, cui regnum Siciliae ab ecclesia committetur, pacta cum Venetis servet, si iuramentum apud Venetias exhibeatur. 1239, Sept. 24, Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the archbishop and to the prior of the Friars Preachers and to the minister of the Friars Minor of Benevento. In order that the beloved sons, the people of Benevento, our faithful, may be more strongly encouraged to defend their land and not feel that our hand of aid is lacking to them, we command that you grant them, by our authority, the license to pledge our regalia up to the sum of five hundred ounces of gold, to be expended for the support of the rector and the poor able to fight, as well as for the repair of the walls of the said land, through your hands. This is to be done after having first received sufficient and suitable security from them that they will redeem the pledged regalia at the opportune time given by the Lord without any difficulty, and you will faithfully report to us whatever you have done in this matter. Should all not be able to act, you, brother archbishop, are to carry this out, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the 11th of April, in the 14th year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo et priori fratrum Predicatorum et ministro fratrum Minorum Beneventanis mandat, ut populus Beneventanus regalia pontificia usque ad summam quingentarum unciarum auri obligare possit pro sustentatione rectoris et pauperum ad pugnandum atque reparatione murorum, recepta cautione idonea. Data Laterani, III Idus Aprilis, anno XIIII.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Ferentino. The customary vigilance of the Apostolic See, which often shows benign favor to some whose merits are unknown, should be more liberally gracious to those who endure many hardships from its enemies because of the See itself. Therefore, considering that the harsh death of the late Berard of Sanctuloe, the father of our beloved sons Andrew, Cuscius, and Peter, laymen, and nephews of our beloved son Master Sinitius, our scribe, which he suffered in the prison of the late Frederick, former Emperor of the Romans, for allegedly adhering to the Church against him, gravely afflicts them, and also considering with compassion that, besides the chains and prisons of Frederick, in which some of them were held for a long time, their goods are dissipated, alienated, and wickedly distracted by their enemies, and wishing to provide some remedy of consolation, though not fully adequate, we command that you, by our authority, or through others, ensure provision for them from some lay fief or possessions usually held by laymen in some part of the Kingdom of Sicily, where they have deemed it more acceptable, without prejudice to the Church's rights—despite constitutions—; objectors, etc. Given at Lyon, 7th of the Ides of August, in the eighth year.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Ferentinati mandat ut Andree, Cuscio et Petro, nepotibus magistri Sinitiid, a carcere F. quondam Romanorum imperatoris liberatis, provisio fiat de aliquo feudo laicali in regno Sicilie. 1234, Augusti 7. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To William, procurator of the Church of Valencia. We gladly add the firmness of apostolic protection to those things granted to the churches of God, so that those fortified by our protection may remain unviolated. You have indeed presented before us that certain Roman emperors have granted to the Church of Valencia the city of Valencia with its suburbs and territory, and everything contained within and outside its limits in the entire bishopric of Valencia, namely the county, market, mint, roads, ships, tolls, fortresses, castles, villages, hamlets, plots, servants, maidservants, tributaries, forests, woods, hunting rights, ovens, mills, watercourses, fields, meadows, pastures, cultivated and uncultivated lands and the common court for handling civil and criminal matters, so that the bishop or elected representative who is in charge there at the time may exercise ordinary jurisdiction in the city and its suburbs, castles and villages belonging to the church itself, or in other places of the diocese in case of appeal or failure of the lords. Therefore, inclined by your devoted supplications, we confirm by apostolic authority the concessions made over these and other matters by the aforementioned emperors, as fully contained in their privileges, as well as the liberties and immunities reasonably granted to the same by Roman pontiffs, our predecessors, and by emperors, kings, and other faithful in Christ, and protect them with the patronage of this present document. Let no one therefore violate our confirmation, etc. If anyone, however, etc. Given at Anagni, Non. July, in the thirteenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Willelmo procuratori ecclesie Valentine confirmat et communit auctoritate apostolica concessiones et libertates ab imperatoribus, pontificibus, regibus aliisque fidelibus eidem ecclesie rationabiliter indultas. 1239, Iul. 7. Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the former bishop of Osimo, now of Recanati. To prevent a wolf from attacking the Lord’s flock and scattering the sheep, shepherds are assigned to guard them, to guide those who stray, to call back the dispersed, and to support the weak. Therefore, prelates must diligently watch over the sheep entrusted to them, lest neglecting their care, the flock is left defenseless, open to the attacks of wolves without a guardian. Thus, considering the faithfulness and devotion of our beloved sons, the clergy and people of Recanati, unwaveringly held toward the Apostolic See, and deeming it worthy that those who have merited well receive a fitting reward, we have decided that their land, formerly a castle, shall henceforth be a city, granting it episcopal dignity. Due to the infidelity of the people of Osimo, the sons of perdition, we have decreed that the church of Saint Flavian of Recanati shall become the cathedral, transferring the see of Osimo along with all its rights, dignities, and honors to it. The care of the clergy and people of this land and its diocese, once of Osimo, is entrusted to you: we command you to go to the aforesaid city of Recanati and to diligently carry out your duties as their bishop over the clergy and people of the said diocese. Given at the Lateran, on the 16th of the Kalends of February, in the 14th year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX episcopo quondam Auximano, nunc Racanati mandat, ut civitatem Racanatensem adeat, et cleri populi eiusque diocesis, olim Auximane, sollicitudinem diligentem gerat, cum sedem Auximanam ad ecclesiam sancti Flaviani Racanatensis transtulerit. Datum Laterani, XVI Kalendas Februarii, anno XIV pontificatus.

**Translation to English:**

To the judges, scabini, and community of the city of Cologne. The filial and singular devotion that the city of Cologne has had towards the Roman Church from ancient times, and still is known to have towards us, earnestly admonishes and induces us to impart apostolic favor to you in those matters which you consider necessary to request from us according to God, because we deem it advantageous to ourselves and to the Roman Church to provide for your benefits. Indeed, on your part, it was proposed before us that several, who do not fear to take the name of the Lord in vain, have been harassing you in many ways and frequently have you summoned to suspicious places through apostolic letters, places to which you cannot safely go due to the dangers of the roads and mortal enmities, so that you might leave even the most just causes undefended or sometimes are forced to undergo an unjust and damaging settlement or to redeem the harassment of the wicked. Therefore, as we wish the cases we entrust to be brought to a proper conclusion so that neither party is unjustly burdened, we are inclined by your devoted prayers to grant you by the authority of these presents, that by apostolic letters obtained against you, you cannot be compelled to go to such places unwillingly. Therefore, let no one etc. of our concession etc. But if anyone etc. Given at the Lateran, the 13th Kalends of June, in the thirteenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa iudicibus, scabinis et communi civitatis Coloniensis scribit, concedens ut per litteras apostolicas contra eos impetratas ad loca suspecta inviti compelli non possint accedere. 1239, Mai. 20, Laterani.

Translation to English:

To the Archbishop of Bremen. Our venerable brother, the Bishop of Prussia, humbly supplicated us, stating that he was liberated from the detention and prison of pagans, who held him captive, after giving hostages. Consequently, he is indebted to these pagans in the amount of eight hundred marks of money and lacks the means to free himself from such a debt. He requested that we grant him permission to receive, up to the mentioned amount, the money that those who recklessly transported iron, salt, and other necessities to aid the pagans of Prussia against our prohibition, for which the bishop himself pronounced a sentence of excommunication against them by apostolic authority, promise to provide as satisfaction for this transgression, to be converted to the aid of liberating himself and H., his brother, and Christian, his nephew, who are detained in the prisons of the aforementioned pagans. Therefore, we command you to grant the requested permission to the said bishop, as you deem appropriate, ensuring that nothing fraudulent is attempted. Given at the Lateran, on the Kalends of June, in the fifteenth year.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Bremensi mandat, ut episcopo Pruscie postulata concedat, ad pecuniam ex excommunicationis satisfactione a transgressoribus datam in liberationem suam, germani et nepotis convertendam. 1241, Iun. 1, Laterani.

Translation to English:

To the noble man E., son of our dearest son in Christ, W., the illustrious King of Denmark. It has been intimated to us on behalf of our dearest son in Christ, W., the illustrious King of Denmark, your father, that a grave discord had arisen between him and the noble man, the Duke of Saxony, resulting in many slaughters of men, the devastation of many lands, and grave dangers to souls. The said king, considering that these dangers could not otherwise be averted, agreed with the said duke that the duke's daughter, Iuita, should be given to you in marriage. Wherefore he humbly supplicated us, since the said Iuita, the duke's daughter, is related to you in the fourth degree of consanguinity, to take care with paternal clemency to provide for this matter. Inclined by the prayers of the said king, whom we embrace with a special prerogative of love among the princes of the world, we grant by the authority of these presents that you may take Iuita, the daughter of the aforesaid duke, as your wife, notwithstanding the said impediment. Let no one therefore — our concession etc. But if anyone etc. Given at Anagni, II Kalends of September, in the thirteenth year.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro E., filio regis Dacie, concedit ut Iuitam, filiam ducis Saxonie, in uxorem ducat, non obstante impedimento consanguinitatis quarti gradus, ex carissimi filii regis petitione. 1239, Aug. 31, Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Ravenna, the Bishops of Arezzo, Castello, Urbino, Rimini, San Leo, Bobbio, Cesena, Forlì, Livi, Faenza, Imola, Cervia, and Comacchio, as well as abbots, priors, priests, and other prelates of churches situated in these cities and their dioceses. Considering with paternal concern the state and tranquility of our beloved faithful of Massa Trabaria, we have appointed our beloved son, Jacinto, our chaplain, a provident and discreet man, and accepted by us and our brothers due to his merits of probity, as their rector, having fully entrusted him with the office of legation. We have decided to earnestly ask and admonish your community through apostolic writings to receive him with reverence for the Apostolic See and ourselves, treating him courteously and honorably, and to humbly attend to him as your legate. In this way, he may be more closely bound to your affection, and we may justly commend your devotion. Otherwise, any sentence that he duly pronounces against the rebellious, we will endorse and cause to be inviolably observed with the Lord as our witness until proper satisfaction is rendered. Given at the Lateran, on the 18th day before the Kalends of July, in the 14th year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopis et prelatis civitatum et diocesium Ravennatis, Aretinae, Castellanae, Urbinatis, Ariminensis, Feretranae, Bobiensis, Cesenatis, Foropopuliensis, Liviensis, Faventini, Ymolensis, Cerviensis et Comaclensis mandat ut Iaquintum capellanum suum, rectorem Massae Trabariae et legatum, reverenter recipiant et honorifice tractent. 1257, Iun. 14, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Palestrina, legate of the Apostolic See. Having kindly received your letters, we have fully grasped their content and that of the letters of our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Arles, and also of our beloved son, the noble man, the Count of Provence. We commend your diligence in the promotion of the business of faith and the church with worthy praises in the Lord. Truly, since it is fitting for the Apostolic See to follow with greater favor and support those whom proven devotion and tested constancy show to be worthy and acceptable in its regard, so that they may rejoice in having served the church and others may be invited to its service by their example, we command you to provide for the said archbishop and count and the city of Arles, who steadfastly support the business of Christ and His spouse, the Catholic faith, against Frederick, the said emperor, their open adversary, by exerting the strength of their power in their aid. From the assistance which you will receive from the prelates and churches of your legation, about which you have taken care to write to us, procure to provide and aid them as your discretion shall see expedient, so that they, continuing the cause of Christ, which they have begun to support with all their strength, may happily bring it to the desired end, with the Lord's granting. Given at the Lateran, 10th January, in the thirteenth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Penestrino, sedis apostolicae legato, mandat ut archiepiscopo Arelatensi, comiti Provinciae et civitati Arelatensi, qui contra Fredericum imperatorem Christo et fidei catholicae constantissime assistunt, de subventione a praelatis et ecclesiis suae legationis recepta, providere et subvenire procuret. Datum Laterani, IIII Idus Ianuarii, anno XIII.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Guillelmo, judge of Arborea. For the purity of your devotion and faith, you are said to be worthy of special grace with us. Hence, as we consent to your supplications, we confirm by apostolic authority that you may retain the land which you are known to hold in Arborea from the Roman Church, until our good pleasure, and we safeguard it with the protection of this present document. Therefore, let no one violate our confirmation, etc. Given at Lyon, on the third day before the Calends of October, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Guillelmo iudici Arborensi terram in Arborea ab ecclesia Romana obtentam confirmat et communit. 1234, Sept. 29. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the men of the castle of Racanati, our faithful ones of the Humanatis diocese. The effective affection of your devotion and faith deserves that we grant your petitions as much as we can with God. Considering, therefore, the fervor of faith and the constancy of loyalty which we have understood you have towards us and the Roman Church, as well as the damages you have recently suffered for the preservation of such loyalty, and through these wishing to pursue you with grace and favor, the grace and concession which our beloved son, S., presbyter cardinal of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, rector of the March of Ancona, made to you regarding certain matters pertaining to the Roman Church, as contained in the public instrument made thereof, as it was piously and prudently done, and also your ancient and approved customs and reasonable liberties and immunities, as you justly and peacefully hold them, we confirm to you with apostolic authority, you persisting in the devotion to the Church, etc., up to: we fortify. Let no one, therefore, violate our confirmation, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the seventh day before the Kalends of March, in the 13th year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa confirmat hominibus castri Racanate, Humanatis diocesis, gratias et concessiones factas a S. cardinale rectori marchie Anconitane de quibusdam rebus ad ecclesiam Romanam spectantibus, necnon antiquas consuetudines, libertates et immunitates eorum. 1239, Feb. 23. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Gubbio. In the presence of us and our brothers, it was requested on your behalf that, since the enemy of God and the Church, a persistent invader of ecclesiastical rights, attempts to occupy the castles of your church in order to attack it more severely, and since the church would be able to resist him better if, heaven forbid, he were to strengthen himself with the forces of the church against it, and since you currently do not have the means to fortify those castles to resist the aforementioned enemy, we should mercifully provide for you and the Church of Gubbio by contracting a loan for the fortification of those castles and other necessities of yours and the said church. However, when our beloved sons Henry, your brother, and John, your nephew, known as Tallentes, Roman citizens, were present at this request, having considered these needs, they offered in our and our brothers' presence to lend you five hundred Provençal pounds if we made arrangements for their indemnity. Therefore, wishing to provide for you and the Church of Gubbio in the aforementioned matters and to ensure the indemnity of the aforementioned citizens, we grant you, with the advice of our brothers, full and free authority to obligate the episcopal goods of the said church to the aforementioned citizens up to the specified amount of money due to these necessities. Given at the Lateran, on the 12th day before the Kalends of March, in the fourteenth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Eugubino concedit facultatem obligandi bona episcopalia ad civium Romanorum Henrici et Iohannis Tallentes indempnitatem, ut pro mutuo quingentarum librarum Proveniensium ad castrorum munitionem et alias necessitates Eugubine ecclesie provideatur. Datum Laterani, XII Kalendas Martii, anno pontificatus XIV.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Embrun and his suffragans. The apostolic see, as almost the entire world knows, etc. as in the first to the end. Given at the Lateran, 22nd May, in the thirteenth year. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Canterbury and his suffragans. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Rouen and his suffragans. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Lyon and his suffragans. In the same manner to the Archbishop of York and his suffragans. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Sens and his suffragans. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Tours and his suffragans. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Reims and his suffragans. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Bordeaux and his suffragans. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Bourges and his suffragans. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Genoa and his suffragans. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Besançon and his suffragans. In the same manner to all the abbots and brothers of the Cistercian order. In the same manner to all the abbots and brothers of the Cluniac order. In the same manner to all the abbots and brothers of the Premonstratensian order. In the same manner to all the priors and brothers of the Dominican order. In the same manner to all the ministers and brothers of the Franciscan order.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Ebredunensi et aliis nominatis recipientibus similem epistulam mittit, qua sedes apostolica, sicut totus fere orbis novit, significat. 1239, Mai. 22. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

Letter from the legate regarding the obligation of the possessions of Genoese churches. To the most holy father in Christ and lord, lord G., by the grace of God the supreme pontiff of the holy Roman Church, G. of Romania, your devoted servant, humbly at your feet. Brother Nicholas, upon arriving in Genoa, stated that you absolutely wanted me to arrange for the hiring of galleys, ships, and other vessels for transporting and returning the prelates and others coming to the council, with sufficient guarantees received from the community of Genoa for keeping the promises. The extent of labor and distress I endured to accomplish this with the counsel of all those you mentioned in your letters cannot be expressed in short words, since many wanted to hinder the task without whose counsel it could not be accomplished. Regarding all these matters, I could do nothing unless I first paid the community of Genoa a thousand marks for the preparation of galleys and cargo ships, which they consider in the agreement and payment, from which thousand marks I had three thousand five hundred and fifty pounds in Genoese currency, which I paid them, and two hundred pounds in Genoese currency I gave to the merchants who lent the said marks for expenses; for which marks the Genoese prelates pledged their possessions to these merchants. And I wrote to lord... Bishop of Palestrina, the legate of the Apostolic See, to pay five thousand and fifty-seven marks of silver, the fifty-seven I promised to the merchants for their salary, accounting for those thousand marks I received; and the merchants are to give two thousand marks to your envoys in France within a month after receiving them, and another two thousand marks the following month; and if this money is not entirely necessary for this task, the remainder will be used as you please. I send to your holiness the agreements made regarding the aforementioned matter enclosed with these presents. Furthermore, for the reward of all the service I have done for you and the Roman Church, I earnestly request and humbly ask that you grant me permission to depart, as I wish no longer to stay in Genoa. Recommend Master Peter of Guarcino for the church of Saint Sixtus in Genoa, for whom I have previously pleaded with you. Given at Genoa, on the 9th day before the Ides of December.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa G. de Romania mandat ut pecuniam pro naulo navium ad concilium perferendam solutioni mercatoribus Ianuensibus persolvat, et licentiam redeundi postulat. 1230, Dec. 5, Ianuæ.

**Translation to English:**

Copy from the same source by the distinguished scholar F. Thaner. Honorius, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brothers, the Archbishop of Pisa and the Bishop of Florence, greetings and apostolic blessing. Since we once instructed the authorities and people of Pistoia to surrender certain castles, namely Fossato, Torre, and Monticello with their appurtenances, which belonged to the late Countess Matilda and pertain to the Roman Church, to our beloved son, the Abbot of Septimo in the diocese of Florence, by the feast of the Purification last past, or to send suitable proxies to our presence if they had legal confidence: although they sent a suitable representative to us, the truth could not be ascertained. Therefore, we have decided to entrust this matter to you, instructing your fraternity by apostolic writing that, notwithstanding that we had already entrusted the same case to our beloved son, the Archpriest of Florence, you should summon to your presence our beloved son John, a monk of Santa Maria de Monteplano, whom we have appointed as a procurator of the Roman Church, and our beloved son the noble man, Count Alberto, who received these castles from us in fief, or his procurator, as well as the procurator of the people of Pistoia. Hear what they have to propose on both sides, and proceed in this matter to a definitive sentence, disregarding any appeal; if the parties consent, settle the case with due conclusion, otherwise remit the same to us sufficiently instructed, setting a suitable term for the parties to present themselves before us to receive the sentence. For we have withdrawn the power of transacting or negotiating over the aforementioned matters from both the said procurator of the Roman Church and the Count and his procurator. Any witnesses who are named, if they avoid testifying out of favor, hatred, or fear, you shall compel by ecclesiastical censure, disregarding any appeal, to bear testimony to the truth. Given at the Lateran, 17th Kalends of August, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Honorius III papa archiepiscopo Pisano et episcopo Florentino mandat ut causam castrorum Fossati, Turris, et Monticelli, pertinentium ad ecclesiam Romanam et olim comitisse Mattildis, audiant et diffiniant, evocatis procuratoribus partium. Si partes consensum non praestiterint in sententia, causam ad sedem apostolicam remittant. Dat. Romae, XVII Kalendas Augusti, anno sexto pontificatus.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Lund, the Bishop of Burguliano, and the Archdeacon of Lund. Our venerable brother, the Bishop of Roscild, has informed us through his petition that the noble prince, the mayor, and the people of the land of Rugians in the Slavic region of the Roscild diocese are observing a certain corrupt custom, which is to be considered a malpractice. They follow such usurious profits, which they commonly call 'poddas', wherein a creditor annually receives from the debtor a certain quantity of grain, flax, and other goods that far exceed in value more than double the money lent. Not content with this, he also receives five solidi from the debtor for his daughter, whom he may wish to give in marriage, otherwise, he cannot give her in marriage. Likewise, for any animal that the debtor sells, he must pay a certain sum of money to the creditor. If the debtor happens to die before repaying the borrowed sum, this detestable condition passes to all his heirs, such that if any of them is unable to pay, he is branded with a bundle of straw in the judicial forum and is thrown down by the inhabitants of his land and subjected to perpetual servitude to the creditor. However, since the profits of usury are condemned by the pages of both the Old and New Testaments, we have deemed it necessary to earnestly ask and admonish them, by sending them letters with our orders, to cease from henceforth observing such an abuse of servitude and to desist entirely from such usurious profits. Therefore, we command you that if the said prince, mayor, and people neglect to fulfill our mandate, you compel them to do so, with prior warning, by ecclesiastical censure, removing the possibility of appeal, taking care not to bring any excommunication upon the entirety of the land of the Rugians. If not all of you can act, then two of you should proceed. Given at Anagni, VIII Kalends of September, in the thirteenth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Lundensi, episcopo Burguliano et archidiacono Lundensi mandat, ut principem, maiorem et populum terre Rugianorum in diocesi Roscildensi inducant, ne pravum morem usurarum, quem poddas vocant, retineant, et si mandatum non impleant, eos per censuram ecclesiasticam compellant. 1239, Aug. 25. Anagnie.

**Translation into English:**

To the clergy, the authority, the council, and the people of Aquae. It was from the kindness of our predecessor Pope Alexander of happy memory, who piously considered that the city of Alexandria was constructed in honor of the prince of the apostles, etc., as above until: union. For this reason, led by the aforementioned consideration, Pope Alexander deprived the Alexandrians of the honor of episcopal dignity because, at that time, they recklessly disdained to return to the command of the Church, adhering to its enemies. We, however, considering their merits of faith and devotion, in which they have especially endeavored to show themselves agreeable to the Church at this time, have decided to restore this dignity to them out of special grace, granting them that they may enjoy it in perpetuity according to the form of the mentioned privilege. Moreover, since it is our desire that you also strive to earn the grace of the Church through acts of gratitude, we command you by these presents to desist from any persecution of that city, which is of special standing with the Apostolic See, disregarding all excuses. You shall offer no counsel, aid, or favor to Frederick, the so-called emperor, the enemy of God and the Church, and his supporters, against the Church and ecclesiastical liberty. You are to send special envoys with sufficient mandate to abide by our commands, within two months after receiving these presents, to our presence, especially since you have inflicted grave injuries upon the aforementioned city of Alexandria, in contempt of us and the Apostolic See. Otherwise, you may rightfully blame yourselves if, due to your transgressions, your city should be deprived of an episcopal standing. Given at the Lateran, on the eighth day before the Ides of May, in the fourteenth year. In a nearly similar manner, to the abbot of Saint Justine of Sezzadio? in the diocese of Aquae until: deprived of episcopal standing. Therefore, we command you to attentively advise and induce the clergy, authority, council, and people of Aquae regarding this matter and report back to us faithfully what you have done and found. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa clero, potestati, consilio et populo Aquensi mandat ut Alexandrinis episcopalem dignitatem restitutam tueantur et ab iniuriis contra Fredericum imperatorem et eius fautores se abstineant, sub poena privationis status episcopalis. Dat. Laterani, VI Idus Maii, anno XIV.

**Translation to English:**

The same king to the same (Pope). We do not believe it has slipped from your Holiness's memory that when, during the time of sweet memory of Queen Beatrice, your granddaughter, we often and repeatedly asked the Emperor, who was holding the goods that rightly belonged to her by succession, for our son Frederick, he refused to return them. We then appealed to your paternity, imploring your advice and help on this matter. To which, as befits a father of justice and the vicar of Jesus Christ, you responded with your customary clemency of kindness, stating that your counsel would not be lacking to us, further promising that you would ensure the full complement of justice would be rendered to us.

However, when the same Emperor, guided by sounder counsel, later indicated to us repeatedly that he was prepared to return the requested goods if we would take care to send him the same Frederick, whom his mother had also ordered to be sent there on her deathbed under a certain adjuration: we, considering that it was harmful to delay what was prepared, both to obtain the maternal inheritance and because we wish to have him at the service of the Roman Church, and for other most urgent reasons which the venerable abbot and religious man, our beloved G., abbot of Saint Facundus, will more fully explain to your magnificence: we have decided, with the counsel of prudent men, to send him, firmly ordering him by word and under the penalty of paternal grace, that he must, in the manner of his ancestors, the kings and emperors of Spain, procure and love the honor and exaltation of the Roman Church and always be obedient and devoted to it.

Indeed, if the same Emperor, which we do not believe, should refuse or delay to return the same inheritance to him, we extend our heartfelt prayers to your paternity, humbly and devoutly asking that you, under your protection, which we commit him to, deign to extend your help and favor to him.

Given at Burgos, on the 4th day of December, in the year of our reign.

---

**Regesto in Latin:**

Rex (nomen non specificatum) ad Papam (nomen non specificatum): petit auxilium et consilium pro obtinenda hereditate Beatricis, filiole suae, a imperatore detenta, et de Frederico filio suo mittendo. Dat. Burgis, IIII die Decembris, anno regni sui.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man, William, Count Palatine. Although the ship of Peter is tossed by the raging storms and waves of wicked people, as if by a tempestuous sea, we nevertheless hope in Him, to whom the winds and the sea obey, because He turns the storm into a breeze, that such tempests and storms, even if they can shake it, will not sink it. For the Lord, residing in it, aroused by the cries of the righteous, when He dispels the blowing winds and commands the sea and winds, will grant calm after the storm has been stilled. Therefore, wishing you to place your trust in Him, we attentively advise and exhort your devotion, and through apostolic writings we mandate you to be strengthened with a strong spirit, receiving the fortifications of a steadfast mind and bravely arming yourself for your defense, that you may steadfastly persevere in the faith and devotion to the Roman Church, your mother, being assured that if needed, the timely aid of the same Church will not be lacking to you. And if it happens that the same Roman Church returns to peace with its enemies, we will by no means leave you and the men of your county of Ildebrandis, which pertains to the Roman Church, deprived of peace. And so that you may be able to carry this out better and more effectively in affection and action, we, with the counsel of our brothers, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and support with the patronage of this present writing, your person, and those of your wife and children, persisting in fidelity and devotion to the apostolic see, together with the integrity of the county of Ildebrandis and all your other goods. Let no one therefore infringe upon our protection etc. But if anyone should etc. Given at the Lateran, on the 9th day before the Kalends of May, in the fourteenth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro Guillelmo comiti palatino mandat ut in fide et devotione Romanae ecclesiae fiduciam ponat et protectionem cum comitatu Ildebrandisco sub beati Petri patrocinio suscipit. 1241, Apr. 23, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To all the masters and brothers of the house of St. Mary of the Teutons. We are not unjustly amazed nor moved with indignation that, although we hold you and your house especially dear in the bosom of charity, and have deemed it fit to grant you and, through you, to the same house many great privileges and indulgences, you, as has come to our ears through the report of certain trustworthy persons, unmindful of our love and entirely ungrateful for our grace, returning evil for good to us, lend counsel and favor to the adversary of the church who attacks the Catholic faith and tramples on ecclesiastical freedom, contrary to the decency of regular modesty, by which you ought to exhibit filial reverence to us and to the bride of Christ, the holy church, striving to turn away the minds of the devout from the service and devotion of the same church as much as you can, and to recall them to the service and love of that Satan, to the ruin of your salvation and reputation. However, unwilling to allow the sin of such ingratitude to pass under the pretense of concealment, which would be very dangerous, especially due to the peril to souls known to result from this, we admonish and exhort all of you more attentively in the power of obedience, strictly commanding that, thoughtfully recalling our love and grace, you take care to henceforth restrain yourselves from the aforementioned actions, from which you undoubtedly incur divine and our indignation, at least out of respect for the undertaking of your religion, and conform yourselves in word and deed to the appeasements of the apostolic see and our own, so that by the endeavor of future conduct you may justly obtain the merit of abolishing past faults. Otherwise, because there are faults in which it is a fault to relax vengeance, you should know that you and your house will be perpetually deprived of all privileges and indulgences that we have granted to you and the same house. Given at the Lateran, on the 11th of June, in the 13th year [of our Pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX universis magistris et fratribus domus sancte Marie Teutonicorum mandat, ut se a consilio et favore adversariorum ecclesie cohibeant, ne privilegia et indulgentias concessas amittant. 1239, Iun. 11. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the rector, judges, consuls, and people of Benevento. Would that our desires followed their desired effect, and not because of the works of justice that we have done, but according to the multitude of His mercies, the Lord would grant our wishes, because neither would you have to endure afflictions and pressures for long, nor would we be compelled to sympathize with you over these matters for longer. Nonetheless, the fact that our and your desires have not yet been fulfilled in this regard, apart from the secret counsel of divine providence, which no mortal can comprehend, is certain evidence to you that He still intends to test you, so that your trial of faith, much more precious than gold tested by fire, may be found to result in praise, glory, and honor. Therefore, as men of courage and grace, considering diligently as is fitting how great and renowned the name of your steadfastness has become among all nations, and how much strength and glory it has brought to your city, gird yourselves and be strong sons, defending the city and yourselves valiantly, and by keeping the safer places secure, cautiously avoid those where there could be danger, assured that soon, by God's doing, you will gain glorious success from mournful calamity. Moreover, since some from the aforesaid city, as we have learned with great dismay, prompted by a diabolical spirit, intended the destruction of the same city and attempted to betray it into the hands of enemies: because the treason was discovered by God's doing and flight took the traitors from your hands, you have decided in counsel that, with all the goods of these traitors confiscated, neither they nor their heirs shall ever be allowed to return to the said city forever. We, detesting treason and traitors as is fitting, confirm this prudent statute made with apostolic authority and strengthen it with the protection of this present writing. Given at the Lateran, on the Ides of October, in the fourteenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa rectori, iudicibus, consulibus et populo Beneventano confirmat statutum de confiscatione bonorum proditorum atque eorum exclusionem perpetuam ab urbe, proditione detecta et evitata. 1241, Oct. 15, Lateran.

**Translation to English:**

To G. of Romania, our subdeacon and chaplain, legate of the Apostolic See. We find pleasing and acceptable, commending in the Lord your diligence and industrious circumspection, for the affairs of the Apostolic See entrusted to you have been laudably advanced by your efforts, with divine grace assisting. However, since we judge that sixteen galleys and as many cargo ships are insufficient to carry the prelates and their households and others going to the council, along with their necessities, we command you that, to prevent the delay of their arrival due to a lack of vessels, you take care to provide, with the counsel of our venerable brother, the Patriarch of Jerusalem, and others devoted to the church who are at Genoa, a sufficient quantity of vessels for transporting all the prelates and others. Dated at the Lateran, the Ides of March, in the fourteenth year of our pontificate.

To the same. Since, as we have learned, the church's persecutor has prepared twenty-five galleys to impede the passage of the prelates, we command you to ensure, without delay, that a sufficient number of well-armed galleys are provided to meet and escort the prelates powerfully and boldly, so that when they come, the lurking adversary does not dare to appear before them, and so they may come honorably and safely. Dated as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa G. de Romania subdiacono et capellano suo, legato apostolico mandat, ut de quantitate vasorum et galearum bene munitarum provideat ad deferendos prelatos ad concilium, ne adventus eorum impediatur propter defectum vasorum et insidias adversariorum. Datum Laterani, Idibus Martii, anno quarto decimo pontificatus nostri.

**Translation to English:**

To the clergy and people of Recanati. It is weighed in the balance of proper consideration when the merits of subjects are evaluated with fair judgment, so that a worthy reward responds to the devotion of the faithful, and the punishment of perpetual disgrace oppresses the necks of the unfaithful. For thus we raise many to the merits of virtues by the rewards given to the good and prohibit others from the audacity of sinning by the punishments of the wicked.
