Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we rightly consider that you have shown such constancy in your devotion to the Church that neither the losses of property inflicted upon you by Frederick, the so-called emperor, enemy of God and the Church, nor the dangers to your bodies could turn you away from fidelity to the Apostolic See. And considering it appropriate to honorably elevate the castle of Recanati, which we now decree to be a city, with grateful distinction, by the common counsel and consent of our brothers, we grant your land episcopal dignity, which we remove from the jurisdiction of the Church of Umana, transferring the see of Osimo, which adhered damnably to the said Frederick, persecutor of God's Church, disregarding divine fear, to the Church of Saint Flavian of Recanati, which we now decree to be the cathedral, along with all its rights, dignities, and honors. However, when it seems expedient, we may grant some part of the Osimo diocese to the Church of Umana in recompense for the spiritual and temporal rights it held in the said castle and its territory. Therefore, no one should infringe this our constitution, exemption, and concession. If anyone should act to the contrary, etc. Given at the Lateran, 22nd of December, in the fourteenth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa concedit clero et populo Racanatensi castrum Racanatense in civitatem elevare et episcopalem dignitatem terræ suæ attribuere, sedem Auximanam cum omnibus iuribus ad ecclesiam sancti Flaviani de Racanato transferendo. 1237, Dec. 22. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbots of Buch and Dorberlu and the prior of Buch in the diocese of Meissen. The burden of the governance we have undertaken induces us to direct all our actions through the paths of equity, so that, when intricate questions are brought before us and clarified, we may grant to each petitioner their rightful due. Indeed, the petition presented to us by our venerable brother, the bishop, and the beloved sons of the chapter of Kammin stated that our venerable brothers, the bishops of Lübeck, Brandenburg, Havelberg, and Schwerin, contest the possession of Demmin, Tribsees, Broda, and other castles and villages with their appurtenances, located between the river called Leba to the east and the river called Rekezsan to the west, as well as certain other possessions of the church of Kammin granted by the late Duke W. of Pomerania, the founder of the same church, with pious liberality, as is more fully contained in the letters drawn up regarding this matter. Desiring, therefore, to remove this contention and to provide for the indemnity of each party with fatherly care, we command you, personally proceeding to the place and summoning those who should be summoned for this purpose, to take care to provide a suitable delimitation of the aforementioned dioceses with fairness, ensuring that the rights of each of the bishops are preserved and that each remains content with his own, so that we may justly commend your diligence in this matter; those who oppose, etc. Witnesses, etc. If not all, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the 13th of May, in the 14th year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbatibus de Buch et Dorberlu necnon priori de Buch Misnensis diocesis mandat ut, vocatis evocandis, dioceses inter episcopos Lubusensem, Brandeburgensem, Haveldeberdensem, et Zuerinensem equitate previa provide limitent, lis super possessionibus ecclesiae Caminensis dirematur. 1239, Maii 13. Datum Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the archdeacon, the cantor, and the dean of Wrocław. The chapter of the Olomouc church has shown us by their petition that recently, with the church being vacant of a pastor, they, as is their duty, convened in the chapter to discuss the appointment of a future bishop, so that the church would not suffer from prolonged vacancy. They unanimously agreed through the form of scrutiny on Master William, their fellow canon, a noble, learned, prudent, and honest man, circumspect in spiritual and temporal matters, through whose effort the said church is believed to be reformed for the better. They elected him as the bishop of Olomouc. Although he consented to the election made for him at their insistence, Conrad, a canon of Hildesheim and supporter of Frederick called the emperor, an enemy of God and the church, procured entry into the bishopric of Olomouc through lay power. He expelled them from the church, plundered their homes, and violently desecrated its goods by breaking its doors. Therefore, this chapter humbly beseeched us to care for their protection with fatherly solicitude, as no certainty regarding the merits of the elect and the wishes of the electors can be made at the Apostolic See. They, having been stripped of all their goods by the said intruder, have miserably experienced bonds and prisons and are forced to beg in disgrace to the clerical order. Since our daily concern is the continuous care of all churches, we command you to diligently investigate the truth of the above matters. If you find that Conrad was intruded in such a manner and the election of the said Master William was canonically celebrated by a suitable person, you shall remove Conrad from the administration of the said church and confirm the election by our authority. However, if you find that Conrad was canonically elected and the election of Master William was less canonical, you shall duly annul it and grant the confirmation to Conrad. If what has been done by either party has been improperly attempted, impose silence on both as is just, and ensure that a pastor suitable for such a burden and honor is provided for the said church through canonical election. If not all are available, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the Ides of April, in the fifteenth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archidiacono, cantori, et decano Wratislaviensi mandat ut diligenter inquirant super electione facta in ecclesia Olomucensi inter Conradum canonicum Ildesemensis et magistrum Willelmum, et, si invenerint Conradi intrusionem et Willelmi electionem canonicam fuisse, Conradum amoveant et electionem confirment; sin minus, Conrado munus confirmationis impendant. 1241, Apr. 13, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To Francon of Herornedi, Canon of Münster. The sincere devotion that our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Armagh, and our beloved sons, the noble men, the counts of Thekenborc and de Marca, bear towards our person and the Roman Church prompts us to grant their petitions as far as we can with God's help. Therefore, inclined by their supplications, we command you to provide or ensure provision for our beloved son Henry, a cleric of Münster, with a prebendal or other suitable ecclesiastical benefice in the city or diocese of Utrecht, even if it involves the care of souls, by our authority through you or another. And have him received as a canon and brother in the church where you have commanded provision for him, even if there is a fixed number of canons established by oath, confirmation of the Apostolic See, or any other firm validation, or if we have directed letters for others in that church, which we do not wish, etc., to cause any hindrance. Nor if it has been granted by the same see that they are not bound to receive or provide for anyone, or that they cannot be interdicted, suspended, or excommunicated by apostolic letters unless such mention is expressly made of this grant in them, or by any other indulgence by which such grace could be impeded or delayed, and about which special mention must be made in our letters. Given at Lyon, on the Ides of July, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Franconi de Herornedi canonico Monasteriensi mandat ut Henrico clerico Monasteriensi in civitate vel diocesi Traiectensi de prebendali vel alio beneficio ecclesiastico provideatur et eum in canonicum recipi curet, non obstantibus quibuscumque impedimentis. 1251, Iul. 15, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

Gregory, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son, the noble man, the Duke of Venice, greetings and apostolic blessing. Taking into greater consideration the sincerity of devotion that you and the community of Venice have towards the Roman Church, and also hoping that you remain firm and stable in the same devotion and that you give aid and effective effort to occupy the kingdom of Sicily, which is the special patrimony of Saint Peter, we declare to your nobility by the tenor of these presents, that we will grant to you and through you to the said community, in perpetual fief, Barletta and Salpi with their appurtenances, and a free court and jurisdiction among the Venetians, as well as full liberty and immunity and the right to have consuls among the Venetians from Venetians in the kingdom of Sicily, the duchy of Apulia, Calabria, the principality of Capua, and in any other place of the kingdom which comes to be occupied with your and the community's help, after they have been occupied; provided, however, that you swear to observe all and each chapter contained in the instrument of agreement between the Roman Church and you and the community of Venetians, made through the hand of our beloved son Nicholas of Ferentino, notary of our chamber, known to be contained there, and that your successors will offer a similar oath, and that you and that community will make those who will preside over the aforementioned places, namely Barletta and Salpi, whenever and as often as they are renewed there, in Venice, and all Venetians who now live or will live in those places, and all other co-inhabitants of the same places, give an oath of fidelity to us and our successors and the Roman Church, in the presence of him or those to whom we or our successors shall have committed this. Afterwards, he or they who for the time being preside over the aforementioned places on your behalf, and all other inhabitants of those places, can offer you an oath of fidelity, our and our successors' and the Roman Church's fidelity in all things always being preserved. Given at Anagni, on the eighth day before the Kalends of October, in the thirteenth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa dilecto filio nobili viro duci Venetorum concessit Barolum et Salpas cum pertinentiis in feudum perpetuum, cum conditionibus pactis servandis et fidelitatis iuramento praestando, 1239, Anagniae, VIII Kalendas Octobris.

**Translation to English:**

To the deans of the churches of Saint Mary and Holy Cross of Hildesheim. On behalf of our venerable brother, the bishop, and our beloved sons, the dean and chapter of the church of Halberstadt, it was humbly requested of us that since the provost of Steindal, at the urging of certain nobles who devastated the church with plundering and fires, had obtained our letters concerning his reception and provision in that church, and since he harasses them in many ways using those letters as a pretext, we should, in our usual kindness, care to provide for the church in this matter. We command that, if this is the case, you do not allow the aforementioned bishop, dean, and chapter to be troubled regarding the reception and provision of the said provost under the pretext of such letters; restrain these harassers, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 12th of October, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV episcopis et capitulo ecclesiae Halberstatensis mandat, ne a praeposito de Steindal sub praetextu literarum molestentur. 1251, Oct. 12. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Eghno, Bishop of Trento, and our beloved son Bruno, Bishop-elect of Brixen. Since we have decided, brother bishop, to transfer you from the Church of Brixen to the Church of Trento, and you, son bishop-elect, we have appointed to the Church of Brixen: because the properties of the Church of Trento have been occupied by the enemies of the Church, we, with the counsel of our brothers, have decided in such a manner that you, son bishop-elect, shall hold two of the castles of the same Church of Brixen, and you, brother bishop, shall hold and equally divide the remaining properties between you, deducting the expenses of these castles, sharing the revenues of both bishoprics, until you, brother bishop, are able to recover and peacefully possess the castles, villages, and properties of your church. We command that you observe this arrangement. Given at Lyons, 8th day before the Ides of November, in the eighth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Eghnoni episcopo Tridentino et Brunoni electo Brixinensi mandat ut duo de castris ecclesiae Brixinensis inter se dividant proventus, donec bona ecclesiae Tridentinae recuperentur. 1234, Nov. 8, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Berengarius, rector of the church of Williby in the diocese of Norwich, born of Valentius Marsilius, a citizen of Florence. The merits of your probity and the petitions of the beloved sons, the captains and the party of the Guelfs of Florence, who have pleaded for you through their letters, lead us to extend special grace to you. Therefore, dear son in the Lord, inclined by your prayers, we grant you the authority by these presents, that besides the church of Williby in the diocese of Norwich, which you now hold and which has the care of souls, and whose annual revenues do not exceed the value of fifteen marks for you, you may lawfully accept one other benefice in the kingdom of England, having similar care, if it is canonically offered to you, and freely retain it with the same church—notwithstanding the constitution issued by the general council on this matter—provided that the same church, etc., is not neglected. Let no one therefore, etc. Given at Lyon, the sixth day before the Kalends of October, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Berengario rectori ecclesiae de Williby Norvicensis diocesis concedit ut, praeter ecclesiam quam nunc obtinet, aliud beneficium in regno Angliae similem curam habens recipere possit. 1251, Sept. 26, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the podestà, council, and commune of Ravenna. Restraining wickedness and defending justice is believed to be highly pleasing to the eyes of the Redeemer, but defending the Catholic faith and protecting ecclesiastical liberty is considered to be even more gratifying to God, as the human race achieves more salvation through faith, and we believe that God is more greatly honored through the liberty of the Church. Therefore, we decree that it is fitting to protect the defenders of the Church with the shield of apostolic defense, so that while we repay them with the appropriate rewards for their merits, we may invite others to the obedience of the apostolic see. Hence, as you are led by a salutary counsel to defend the faith and ecclesiastical liberty against the said Emperor Frederick, we place your persons and city, persevering in the devotion to the Church, as well as other goods that you reasonably possess at present, under the protection of St. Peter. Therefore, let no one—our letters. Given at Anagni, July 26, in the thirteenth year. In the same manner, to the noble man Paolo Traversari. Given at Anagni, July 15. To the Archbishop of Ravenna. Restraining wickedness, etc., as far as inviting others. Hence, as the beloved sons, the podestà, council, and commune of Ravenna, against the said Emperor Frederick, etc., as far as we have received. Therefore, we command that you do not allow them to be improperly disturbed by anyone against the tenor of our protection; the molesters, etc. In the same manner to the Bishop of Cervia for the noble man Paolo Traversari, etc., to the end. In the same manner to Sinibaldo, presbyter cardinal of the title of St. Lawrence in Lucina, rector of the March of Ancona, as far as inviting others. Therefore, we command that you receive the people of Rimini and all others from Romagna, who strive to defend the faith and ecclesiastical liberty against the said Emperor Frederick and have come to the devotion of the Church, under apostolic protection in our stead, and that you do not allow them, persisting in this purpose, to be improperly disturbed regarding the goods they reasonably possess at present; the molesters, etc. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa potestati, consilio et communi Ravennati mandat, ut eos, qui contra Fridericum imperatorem fidem et ecclesiasticam libertatem defendant, sub protectione apostolica recipiat, ne ab aliquibus indebite molestentur. Datum Anagnie, VII Kalendas Augusti, anno tertio decimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the authorities, council, and community of the castle of San Ginesio in the Diocese of Camerino. To the just demands of petitioners, etc., with assent, the liberties and immunities and any other privileges granted to you by the of blessed memory R., cardinal deacon of Santa Maria in Cosmedin, then the legate of the Apostolic See in those parts, we hold as valid and acceptable. By apostolic authority, we confirm them to you and strengthen them with the protection of this present writing. Let no one, etc. Given at Lyon on the 4th of December, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa potestati, consilio et communi castri Sancti Genisii Camerinensis libertates et immunitates ab R. cardinale diacono Sanctae Mariae in Cosmidin concessas confirmat. 1234, Dec. 4, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the same. Since we are sending our beloved son, Master Mathew of Babuco, our subdeacon and scribe, in whom we have full confidence in the Lord regarding his fidelity and prudence, to you for church matters and especially for the business of the Kingdom of Sicily, we command that you endeavor to place firm trust in him regarding those matters which he will tell you on our behalf, both concerning the election and appointment of powers or officials through the cities of that kingdom and bringing them into common unity, as well as other things. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa eidem mandat ut in dilectum filium magistrum Matheum de Babuco subdiaconum et scriptorem suum fiduciam habeat pro ecclesie negotiis et regni Sicilie. Datum ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the lord, council, and people of Alexandria. The mother church, the illustrious bride of the supreme king, observes such an order of discretion towards the children acquired through the laver of regeneration, that just as it sometimes corrects their excesses with appropriate severity, so too it does not cease to pursue their acts of devotion with fitting reward. Indeed, it was due to the kindness of our predecessor of happy memory, Pope Alexander, that, piously considering your city was built to honor the prince of the apostles, he adorned it with the title of pontifical dignity, decreeing by the authority of the apostolic see that, since the city of Alexandria is much larger and more populous than that of Aix, the episcopal seat should be transferred from the latter, to which it is adjacent, to the former. Over time, our predecessor of pious memory, Pope Innocent, upon the supplication of the Alexandrian people to have what Pope Alexander had providently decreed executed, moderated this statute so that he united the Alexandrian church and the Aix church, establishing, as contained in the apostolic privilege drawn up regarding this, that one and the same pontiff would govern both, holding one and the same seat in both. He also decreed that if the people of Aix presumed to act contrary to the form declared in the same privilege, unless they corrected their presumptuous excess upon the admonition of the Roman pontiff, the episcopal seat should be transferred from the city of Aix to Alexandria; and if the Alexandrians exceeded against this statute, unless they satisfied the apostolic admonition regarding their excess, the prescribed bonds of union would be dissolved. However, since the aforementioned Pope Innocent, because you at that time adhered to the enemies of the church, contemptuously disregarding his command to return to its obedience, deprived your city of the honor of episcopal dignity, we finally, considering that in these days, when through Frederick, the so-called emperor, divine majesty is offended and the Catholic faith is damnably attacked, you have remained steadfast and stable in devotion to the church, and it is carried in your affection that it may always find grateful children in you, on the advice of our brothers, have decided to restore the same dignity to your city, granting you by the authority of these presents of special grace that it may enjoy the said privilege for all future times. Therefore, let no one infringe upon our confirmation, etc. If anyone, however, etc. Given at the Lateran, 10th May, in the 14th year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa potestati, consilio, et populo Alexandrino dignitatem episcopalem restituit, concedens civitati secundum privilegii formam gaudere. Dat. Laterani, VI Idus Maii, anno XIIII.

**Translation to English:**

To the same. If it happens by the support of divine grace that you enter the kingdom of Sicily, we wish it to be lawful for your devotion by the authority of these presents, that you may be able to confer twenty-five of the prebends or ecclesiastical dignities of the said kingdom, being vacant, to devoted and worthy persons suitable for such grace and promotion of the business, and also to provide for other benefices, which may become vacant after your entry, just as it is known to be permitted to legates who are sent from our side. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa eidem mandat, ut, si in regnum Sicilie ingrediatur, viginti quinque personatibus ecclesiasticis vacantes personis devotis conferre possit. 1230, Dat. ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Strasbourg. In the Church of Strasbourg, there are said to be some beneficial statutes and approved customs, and also some other statutes and customs that are neither useful nor honorable. Since we desire the good state and prosperity of that church, we command that you confirm, with the consent of the chapter of said church and by our authority, its beneficial and honorable statutes and reasonable and ancient customs, and that you strive to eradicate from the same church the less honorable statutes and unreasonable customs, as you know to be expedient for the benefit of the church; contradictors, etc. — notwithstanding if it has been granted to some by the Apostolic See that they cannot be interdicted, suspended, or excommunicated by apostolic letters, which do not make mention of such a grant. Given at Lyon, 9th December, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Argentinensi mandat ut statuta salubria et consuetudines ecclesiae Argentinensis approbet et confirmet, minus honesta vero extirpet. 1234, Dec. 9. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Trento. The Church of Trento has long been without the solace of a shepherd, and you, then Bishop of Brixen, were appointed by our beloved son, O., Cardinal Deacon of Santa Maria in Via Lata, the legate of the apostolic see, etc., as stated above in Chapter 90 with the words suitably altered up to: "in both." Therefore, we earnestly admonish and exhort your fraternity, commanding that you, upon reaching the said Church of Trento, diligently and wisely exert yourself in recovering its rights, confronting the opponents and rebels, etc., so that you may benefit from the merit of life and provide an example for the family entrusted to you, and that we may rightfully extol your person with worthy praises in the Lord, thereby pursuing you with the favor of our grace. Given at Lyon, November 9, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Tridentino mandat, ut ad ecclesiam Tridentinam accedens iura eius fideliter et prudenter recuperet. 1250, Nov. 9, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the prior of the Dominicans and the provincial minister of the Minor Brothers of Germany. As at present the Holy Land is in need of the support of warriors, we, considering that many Frisians have taken up the sign of the cross driven by zeal for devotion and faith, and that the Frisians are accustomed to prosper in overseas regions, command that you earnestly and effectively encourage and lead all those who have taken the cross in the regions of Frisia and Norway to cross over at the forthcoming passage, as determined by you and to the satisfaction of our dearest daughter in Christ, the illustrious Queen of France, to aid the Holy Land, compelling them if necessary through ecclesiastical censure, setting aside appeals — notwithstanding any privileges of the Apostolic See or indulgences or letters obtained or to be obtained and any others by which this might be hindered or delayed and which should be mentioned in the present letter, and the constitution regarding two days published in the general council. If not both, etc. Given at Lyons, November 29, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa priori Predicatorum et ministro Minorum fratrum provincialibus Alamannie mandat, ut omnes crucesignatos de partibus Frisie ac Norwagie ad transfretandum in subsidium Terre Sancte inducant, etiam per censuram ecclesiasticam, si necesse fuerit. 1234, Nov. 29, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Seckau, the abbot of Waldebach of the Cistercian order, and the prior of the Order of Preachers of Friesach of the dioceses of Regensburg and Salzburg. The noble man, the Duke of Bavaria, has informed us through a petition that when our venerable brother, the bishop of Freising, pronounced sentences of excommunication against him and interdict on his land by ordinary authority unjustly, and after various letters were obtained from us to different judges on this matter, the aforementioned bishop obtained our letters addressed to our venerable brother, the bishop of Chiemsee, and to you, brother bishop, and the abbot of Agmund of the diocese of Salzburg. These letters instructed you and your colleagues to ensure that the letters and processes obtained through them were presented to you, compelling the holders to exhibit them through ecclesiastical censure. If the parties agreed, you were to ensure that the case was resolved by judgment or concord; otherwise, you were to send it back to us sufficiently instructed, setting a competent term for the parties to present themselves before us in person or through suitable procurators. Therefore, the aforementioned Duke humbly supplicated us, since those letters were obtained while his procurator was on his way to our presence, that to avoid the matter being postponed through evasive delays and to ensure the judgment proceeds without suspicion, we should remove two of the judges and substitute another by our office at the request of the Duke. Inclined by the Duke's prayers, we have removed the said bishop and abbot, and appointing you, sons, the abbot, at the Duke's petition, and the prior, by our office, in their place, we command that in this case, unless it has proceeded to the contestation of the suit, you should proceed according to the content of the previous letters, setting aside any appeal with due reason. What if not all —, two etc. Given at the Lateran, 17th Kalends of May, in the thirteenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Secowensi, abbati de Waltebaci Cisterciensis ordinis, et priori ordinis fratrum Predicatorum de Frisaco mandat, ut, duce Bawarie petente, causam contra episcopum Frisingensem, qui excommunicationis et interdicti sententias protulerat, sine suspitione procedere curent. 1229, Apr. 15, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

Honorius, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons, the authority and people of Pistoia, greetings and apostolic blessing. Since you do not doubt, nor can you doubt, that the land of Countess Matilda pertains to the Roman Church, which even our dearest son in Christ, Frederick, ever august Emperor of the Romans and King of Sicily, recognizing this, has restored to us the aforementioned land, it is entirely improper that you hold certain castles of this land, namely Fossato, Torres, and Monticello, occupied by your own authority. Therefore, not wishing that your city, which we embrace with a certain prerogative of love, provokes the Roman Church against itself and experiences us, whose duty it is to defend its rights, as angry, but rather desiring that you and the same city may obtain more abundantly our and the apostolic see’s grace, which promotes and exalts devoted and humble sons: we attentively admonish and exhort your community through apostolic writings, strictly ordering, that by the feast of the Purification next, you surrender the said castles with all their appurtenances to our beloved son, the abbot of Settimo of the Florentine diocese, in the name of the Roman Church, or at least, if you trust in your right, send your procurators concerning this matter to our presence. And because it would be evident, if you acted otherwise, that you delight in our grievance and contempt, know that we have instructed our venerable brother, the bishop of Florence, to compel you to one of the aforementioned actions by ecclesiastical censure, removing any appeal. Given at the Lateran, on the 11th day before the Kalends of January, in the sixth year of our pontificate. I, Vethosus, notary and scrivener of the apostolic see, saw and read the authentic document of the lord Pope Honorius III, sealed with his leaden bull, from which this example is taken, and I wrote and faithfully exemplified it here word for word, as I found it, with nothing added or removed, and therefore I have subscribed it with my own sign for future demonstration.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Honorius III papa potestati et populo Pistoriensi mandat ut castra Fossatum, Turres, et Monticellum, quae ad terram comitissae Matildis pertinent, restitui faciant aut procuratores ad sedem Romanam mittant; alias episcopum Florentinum committit ut eos per censuram ecclesiasticam compellat. Datum Laterani XI Kalendas Ianuarii, anno sexto pontificatus.

**Translation to English:**

To Brother John of Limoges, our penitentiary, of the Order of Friars Minor. Desiring to put an end to disputes, we command you to diligently inquire into the rights of our venerable brother, the archbishop, and the beloved sons, the chapter of Besançon, and the noble man John, Count of Burgundy, Lord of Salins, regarding the minting of coin which the said count has ordered to be made at Salins. You are to determine whether the aforementioned archbishop and chapter can or should prevent the count from doing this, or if the count has the authority to do so. After conducting this inquiry, ensure that what is just is observed inviolably by our authority, with appeals removed. Given at Lyon, on the 21st of January, in the eighth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Fratri Iohanni Lemovicensi, penitentiario ordinis fratrum Minorum, mandat, ut de iure archiepiscopi et capituli Bisuntinorum ac Iohannis comitis Burgundie super moneta apud Salinas cudenda inquirat et quod iustum fuerit observandum curet. 1249, Jan. 21, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To G. de Montelongo, our subdeacon and notary, legate of the apostolic see. Having learned from the report of some and from the letters of our venerable brother, the bishop of Vicenza, that he, when Frederick, the so-called emperor, entered the Church of Vicenza on the feast of Pentecost, did not stop the celebration of the mass he had already begun, we commanded, through letters addressed to our venerable brother, the bishop of Castellano, and our beloved son, Master Benedict, our scribe, then residing in those parts, that they admonish him, suspended by law from office and benefice for such recklessness, to present himself before us within a certain period; otherwise, they should then pronounce the sentence of excommunication against him. He indeed, humbly presenting himself at our sight upon such admonition, respectfully proposed in his defense before us that, since his metropolitan and certain other prelates accompanying the said Frederick were present with him at the divine offices in the same church, he, to whom it had not yet been announced that he should avoid him, did not dare to desist from the prosecution of the office already begun without shame and confusion. However, since he has long endured the penalty of suspension at the apostolic see with much patience on account of this, we, moved by our usual mercy towards him, have absolved him from the sentence of suspension, with the counsel of our brothers, and decided he should be remitted to the aforementioned church with our grace. We also desire that if any wish to bring forward something against him regarding the assignment of certain castles of the same church to Ezzelino and other enemies of the Roman Church, you should hear them, and faithfully report to us by your letters what you find concerning this. Given at the Lateran, the Nones of July, in the fourteenth year.

---

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa G. de Montelongo subdiacono et notario suo, apostolicae sedis legato mandat, ut si aliqui contra episcopum Vicentinum proponant quod castra ecclesiae Izelino et aliis inimicis assignaverit, eos audiat et facta referat; episcopum, a suspensione absolutum, ad ecclesiam remittit. 1257, Iul. 7, Lateranis.

**Translation to English:**

To the presbyter cardinal of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, rector of the March of Ancona.

Although the kindness of the Apostolic See is always intended to bless all and each of the Church's children with sweetness, it is also necessary that, just as it rewards those it finds devoted among them with suitable grace, so it punishes those who do not fear to offend God within it with just retribution. Thus, since the beloved sons, the lord, council, and people of Recanati, have shown such constancy in the faith and devotion to the Church that they could not be turned away, despite the loss of goods and personal sacrifices, we, considering it fitting that the Church's goodwill, accustomed to favor the deserving with benefits, be manifest in effect, have determined, with the advice of our brothers, that their land be perpetually honored with episcopal dignity. Moreover, their territory should be transferred from the people of Osimo, who wickedly adhered to Frederick the so-called emperor, pursuing the Church's faith and liberty without fear of God, afflicting the people of Recanati with various injuries and multiple harms. The seat of Osimo, with all its rights and appurtenances, is to be transferred. However, since the said people of Recanati, generously offering five thousand pounds of usual currency or possessions of equal value to endow the future cathedral church, promise that they will build suitable houses for the bishop and canons, we mandate you to provide, according to the prudence given to you by God, so that they make such an addition from which the said bishop and canons may honorably be sustained over time, especially since during the dangers of wars, it cannot easily happen that the goods of the church of Osimo can be peacefully possessed. Furthermore, let your discretion provide for our venerable brother, the bishop of Umana, concerning the right he is known to have had in the castle of Recanati, by granting some part of the diocese of Osimo and some part of the Ancona diocese to the church, as you may see fit, with the village of Osimo, once a city, and the remaining part of said diocese reserved for the church of Recanati. Lastly, inform us as soon as you can of what you have done regarding this by your letters of sincerity, so that we may more expeditiously proceed to grant the privilege to the envoys of the said people of Recanati who will approach the Apostolic See for this purpose.

Given at the Lateran, on the 4th before the Nones of July, in the fourteenth year.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa presbytero cardinali tituli Sancti Laurentii in Lucina, marchie Anconitane rectori mandat, ut terra Racanatensis perpetuo episcopali dignitate decoraretur et sedes Auximana transferatur ad Racanates, ob fidelitatem erga Ecclesiam et iniurias ab Auximanis passas. 1241, Iul. 4, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the dean of the major church, the treasurer of the Holy Apostles, and the scholastic of Saint George in Cologne. A mother shares in the struggles of her offspring, and a child is not free from the disadvantages of his mother. The bonds of natural affection share both in prosperity and adversity. If the bond of inherent love makes one share the suffering of another through compassion, it breaks the bond of nature if one does not share the burdens of the other. Therefore, the mother should extend her abundant support to an indigent child, and the child should exert his utmost capability to support a needy mother.

Indeed, our beloved son, the elected one of Cologne, presented himself before us, stating that the church of Cologne is burdened with such a great debt that, unless quickly assisted by the foresight of the Apostolic See, it is feared that it might be utterly consumed by the abyss of usury, to which its revenues scarcely suffice to provide a solution. Therefore, he humbly implored us to extend a hand of paternal aid to this church in this time of need, which should be sympathized with all the more because it is less accustomed to the inconveniences of poverty, being endowed with nobility and accustomed to the abundance of temporal goods.

Considering it appropriate that the members should help the head and that the churches subject to the major church, like a mother, should share its burdens, we, inclined by his supplications, decide to grant from all the revenues of the churches, monasteries, ecclesiastical dignities, prebends, and other ecclesiastical benefices of the city and diocese of Cologne, exempt churches excepted, a sum of eight thousand marks to be received over a period of six years for the payment of said debts. Therefore, we strictly command, by the virtue of obedience, that you collect it in full, imposing the burden on each according to their own means, and conserve it faithfully among you, so that nothing of it may come to anyone else, and convert it entirely through your hands to the payment of these debts, so that you may render an account worthy to God and us; contradictors, etc. We also wish that you report to us by your letters whatever you decide to do about this. If not all, etc. Given at the Lateran, the 5th day before the Kalends of June, in the 13th year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa decano maioris ecclesie, thesaurario Sanctorum Apostolorum et scolastico Sancti Georgii Coloniensis mandat ut colligant et administrent summam octo milium marcarum ad solutionem debitorum ecclesiae Coloniensis, distribuentibus onera iuxta facultates, et convertant ad dictorum debitorum solutionem. Dat. Lateran., V Kalendas Iunii, anno XIII.

**Translation to English:**

Letters from the Queen of Castile to the lord pope. To the most holy father and lord Gregory, by divine providence the supreme pontiff of the holy Roman Church, Berengaria, by the grace of God Queen of Castile and Toledo, sends the kisses of the blessed feet with filial reverence as much owed as devout. For the manifold grace which, from your abundant goodness, both I and my son have so often received from your holiness, not once but many times granted even without asking, I find it fitting to at least ascend to the act of giving thanks, though I am unable to do so adequately, while I consider your graciousness towards me and mine, while I ponder the readiness of your piety; indeed, I would prefer to express my gratitude through actions rather than words or letters. But because at present I am unable to do what I wish, not due to any defect of heart or want of worldly means, but rather by waiting for your will's good pleasure, I meanwhile return thanks to your greatness as much as I can, imploring your majesty with all the affections of my mind, that according to the devotion which both I and my son have always had and still have towards you, you might deign to indicate something to me, which may be in accordance with your will, indeed whatever may please your holiness, to be executed according to your good pleasure in all things and in all respects. I do not believe it should be kept from your kindness that the reason I do not write to you more frequently is not born of lesser devotion, but rather because of the modesty which the female sex has by nature acquired, and the reverence owed to the vicar of Jesus Christ; for the Lord knows that when I behold with the eyes of my mind the papal splendor of purity, a certain brilliance reflects back on the gaze of my mind, delaying the desire to write, and being seized by a certain awe, I almost deem it presumptuous, as in Matthew 9:20, to attempt even to touch the hem of your garment. Nevertheless, the more often I would receive your letters or a mandate, the more grateful it would be to me, and the more fully my wishes would be fulfilled. Now, however, I give thanks to the Lord that I have the opportunity, through the venerable and beloved abbot W. of San Facundo, a prudent and discreet man, who was otherwise about to come into your presence, to securely and confidently declare certain matters which I did not wish to commit to letters, who can more freely explain them to you and more broadly reveal our will. Given at Burgos, on the 5th day of December.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa litteras a Berengaria, Dei gratia regina Castelle et Toleti, accipit, quae gratiam pro beneficiis receptis exprimit et petit ut indicet aliquid secundum devotionem suam. Datum Burgis, V die Decembris.

**Translation to English:**

To the same. Because at the entrance into the kingdom of Sicily, some difficulties might arise for you due to the efforts of noble men, namely the Marquis of Flaumberg, the Count of Caserta, and other powerful figures of the said kingdom, we wish and by the authority of these presents command you, that if you see it advantageous for the Church, you entice the same marquis and count, as well as others, with certain promises, and grant some of the baronies to them or to any of them, so that they may return to the mandate of the Church and restore and assign to you the fortifications and strongholds of the said kingdom. In these matters, you should place firm trust in our beloved son, Master Matthew of Babuco, our subdeacon and scribe, to whom we have expressed our will regarding this business. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa (recipienti ignoto) mandat ut marchionem de Flaumberg et comitem Casertanum aliosque potentes regni Siciliae promissis alliciat, ut ad mandatum ecclesiae redeant et munitiones regni restituant. Dat. ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Strasbourg. Our beloved son Walter, a canon of Strasbourg and son of the noble man W., Lord of Gerolsheim, has informed us that we previously instructed you by our letters to dispense with him concerning the benefices or dignities or other prelatures, even if they involve the care of souls, up to a suitable amount, using our authority—despite the constitution of the general council. However, because the same canon is under twenty-five years of age, you have so far refrained from dispensing with him on this matter. Therefore, he has humbly petitioned us to kindly provide for him in this matter with the apostolic seat's kindness. We command that, if this is the case, you should dispense with the said canon—despite the fact that he is asserted to be nineteen years old over the obtained and to be obtained prelatures, dignities, personates, offices, and benefices, even those involving the care of souls—despite the aforementioned constitution—in accordance with the contents of the previous letters; provided that the prelatures, dignities, personates, and benefices are properly managed, etc. Given at Lyon, on the seventh day before the Ides of December, in the eighth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Argentinensi mandat, ut cum Waltero canonico Argentinensi, non obstante quod decem et novem annorum existat, super obtentis et obtinendis prelaturis, dignitatibus, personatibus, officiis et beneficiis, etiam curam animarum habentibus, dispenset. 1250, Dec. 7. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Abbot of the Holy Cross of the Cistercian order in the diocese of Passau. We are deeply troubled by the oppression of all the faithful, but in these days, a special and great sadness has filled our hearts, which, as we have learned from the letters of the noble men, the dukes of Austria and Carinthia, not without the shedding of many tears, the Tartars, after having invaded and for the most part occupied the kingdom of Hungary, drenching their swords without distinction of age and sex with the blood of all they could capture, are now attempting to invade the kingdoms of Bohemia and Germany, desiring to lay waste the whole land of the Christians and to destroy their faith. Therefore, we firmly hope, etc., as above until: in the virtue of obedience we strictly command, that through the neighboring provinces, proclaiming the word of the cross according to the wisdom given to you by God, both through yourself and others whom you know to be suitable for this task, you do not neglect to encourage Catholic men, considering that just as the destruction of the entire Christian people is sought by the said Tartars, so in their defeat the salvation of all is procured, and trusting in Him who saves the humble people and humbles the arrogant eye, to gird themselves powerfully and manfully against the said Tartars for the defense of the aforesaid kingdoms, with healthy admonitions. For we indeed grant, as above until: are granted. If any of these crusaders have been bound by the chain of excommunication for the violent laying of hands on ecclesiastical persons or for arson, provided they adequately satisfy those who have suffered injuries and damages according to your prudence, and their excess is not so grave and enormous that on account of this they should be sent to the apostolic see, we grant you the freedom to impart the benefit of absolution according to the form of the church, and also to change their vows against the said Tartars, who vowed to set out for the aid of the Holy Land or otherwise for the remission of their sins. Given at the Lateran, on the 13th day before the Kalends of July, in the fifteenth year. In the same manner to the provincial prior of the Friars Preachers of Germany. In the same manner to the prior of the Friars Preachers of Vienna, in the same manner to the provincial minister of the Friars Minor of Germany.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati Sanctae Crucis Cisterciensis ordinis in dioecesi Pataviensi mandat ut, ob imminentem Tartarorum periculum, per provincias vicinas verbum crucis praedicet et viros catholicos ad defensionem regnorum Bohemiae et Teutoniae contra Tartaros excitet. Concedit potestatem absolutionis et commutationis votorum crucis. 1241, Iun. 19, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

Conrad, Archbishop of Cologne, Landolf, Bishop of Worms, Ludolf, Bishop of Münster, and Engelbert, Bishop of Osnabrück lament the discord and promise to assist the pope if the emperor cannot be brought back to concord, which they report having written to him about; they request that Conrad, the master of the Teutonic Order, sent to the Apostolic See for peace restoration, be kindly received; they have entrusted him with the task that, if he sees any prince suitable for this matter by the pope's will, he should assume him. Conrad, Bishop of Freising, Frederick III, Bishop of Eichstätt, and Egon, Bishop of Brixen write the same on April 8, 1240. Berthold, Bishop of Strasbourg, writes the same. Conrad VI, Bishop of Speyer, writes the same. Hermann, Bishop of Würzburg, writes the same on May 2, 1240. Theodoric II, Archbishop of Trier, writes the same. Henry, Landgrave of Thuringia and Count Palatine of Saxony, writes almost the same on the 12th of July; he adds that he is in expectation until he is fully informed about the responses of the pope and emperor. Henry of Brabant, Matthew of Lorraine, Henry of Limburg, Dukes, Otto VIII of 1240, May 11. Geldern, Henry of Sien, Arnold of Los, William of Jülich, Henry of Luxembourg, Counts, and Walram of Limburg write the same as the Landgrave. Siegfried III, Archbishop of Mainz, requests the pope to incline his mercy to those things which are of peace and to mercifully hear Conrad, the master of the Teutonic Order, about these matters; he promises, if his presence is opportune, to be ready to expose himself to labors and expenses. April 20, 1240. Sibodol, Bishop of Augsburg, requests the pope to hear Conrad, elected as the master of the Teutonic Order, over the general petition of the princes and all of Alemannia and to mercifully allow the discord to be appeased; he also has urged the emperor with the other princes to incline himself to this. Otto, Duke of Brunswick, requests the pope to graciously consider the necessity of the whole world and to permit Conrad, the master of the Teutonic Order, to be a messenger for making peace; no one more suitable can be found, because other princes might render themselves suspicious to one party or another. Albert, Duke of Saxony, requests the pope to deign to join the unity of concord and allow Brother Conrad, formerly a landgrave, to be the mediator. John and Otto, Margraves of Brandenburg, write almost the same as the Duke of Brunswick with changed words.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Conrado archiepiscopo Coloniensi et aliis episcopis Germaniae gratias agit quod ad pacem inter imperatorem et ecclesiam reformandam operam daturi sunt, et Conrado magistro Teutonicorum benigne suscipiendo commendat. 1240, Aprilis 20, Romae.

**Translation to English:**

To the archdeacon of Como. We have received the complaint of the beloved sons, the primicerius and clergy, exempt and non-exempt, of the city and diocese of Milan, stating that the podestà and commune of Milan, not considering how much they have been burdened by the provisions for legates and envoys of the apostolic see who go there for the common good, and that no power has been granted to laymen over clerics, have recently presumed to impose on the same primicerius and clergy a tax of twelve thousand pounds in Milanese currency. They have been causing churches and clerics of the said city and diocese to be stripped of chalices, silver crosses, books, and other ecclesiastical ornaments by their envoys, to the prejudice of ecclesiastical liberty, the peril of their souls, and the evident detriment of the aforementioned primicerius and clergy. We command that, if this is the case, you should exhort and firmly influence the said podestà and commune not to exact this tax from them in any way, but to return what was taken under its pretext without any difficulty, compelling them to do this, if necessary, by ecclesiastical censure, dismissing any appeal. Given at Lyon, on the 11th day before the Kalends of November, in the eighth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archidiacono Cumano mandat, ut potestatem et commune Mediolanenses inducat ne collectam duodecim milium librarum a clericis exigant, et ablata restituant, si necesse fuerit, per censuram ecclesiasticam coercendo. Datum Lugduni, XI Kalendas Novembris, anno octavo pontificatus nostri.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Perugia. Since, as we have recently learned, the authorities and council of Perugia have imposed a not insignificant sum of money on the clerics and churches of both the city and diocese of Perugia, against ecclesiastical freedom, and are attempting to extort it from them, and you have ordered the suspension of the clerics' activities because of this, we, considering that due to the malice of the times something must be mitigated from severity, grant you the authority by the present document to absolve, according to the form of the Church, the authorities, council, officials of the commune, and others who imposed this money from the sentence of excommunication, which they are known to have incurred for this reason, and to assist them in some amount of money from ecclesiastical goods for redeeming their vexation, according to what your discretion deems expedient for the common necessity.

Given at Lyon, on the 14th of the Kalends of February, in the 8th year of our pontificate.

**Latin Regesto:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Perusino mandat, ut potestati, consilio et officialibus communis Perusini, qui contra libertatem ecclesiasticam pecuniam imposuerunt, absolutionem concedat et pecuniaria subsidia ex bonis ecclesiasticis provideat. 1251, Ian. 19. Datum Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Bremen. Having been informed through messengers and letters that Frederick, the former emperor of the Romans, has passed away, although it seemed highly beneficial and expedient for us to hasten our return to the City (Rome), we have decided not to return until we have properly arranged the affairs of the Roman Empire, as is fitting. This matter indeed primarily occupies our heart; we fix the focus of our thoughts on this, and we always direct the effort of apostolic diligence toward it, because it is foremost in our affections that the matter be directed wisely and concluded with commendable completion, with the Lord’s help. However, since your prudence, advice, efforts, and assistance can greatly advance and significantly enhance this matter, your presence is absolutely necessary for us: so that we may discuss its execution together with you, we wish and by the authority of these presents command you to make every effort, setting aside all excuses and difficulties, to come to us in person by Palm Sunday. Given at Lyon, on the 6th day before the Kalends of February, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Bremensi mandat, ut personaliter ad se veniat, ut de Romani imperii negotio tractet. 1235, Jan. 27. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the illustrious King of Hungary. If you are a son of the Church, indeed because you are its special son, as we hold with infallible proof, zeal for it must consume you, and you cannot endure any reproaches of those who usurp its rights with equanimity. For we believe you to be so deeply rooted in the fear of the divine name and the reverence of ecclesiastical dignity, that nothing can separate you from its love and devotion. Since your royal majesty is not unaware of the cause presently threatening your mother, the Roman Church, which is more a cause of the bridegroom, Jesus Christ, than the bride, whose name is the only one under heaven by which we must be saved, and whose enemies strive to extinguish it, every Catholic prince should rise more vigorously to aid it, as he sees the foundations and founder of the Church being openly attacked. Not only for the peace of the Roman Church but for the tranquility of all the faithful of Jesus Christ, we have provided for a council to be convened. We neither believed nor wish to believe that any difficulty would be placed by any son of the Church, especially by you, whom among other Catholic kings we embrace with the arms of sincerity, but rather through you, the lukewarm, if any, should be inflamed. Although you have seen fit to send us pleas and letters for the prelates of the kingdom of Hungary as an excuse, and we have responded to your royal majesty as was appropriate, since we did not see it as expedient for you and them, if our letters have reached you: because you recently reiterated to our ears through other letters, which we received kindly, expressing certain difficulties and dangers of the roads in those letters, we earnestly ask, advise, and exhort your royal excellence to wisely consider what is advantageous for your salvation, reputation, and honor, and not to be upset if we cannot grant requests against both our honor and yours, since by God's grace, it has been suitably provided that they can access the Apostolic See safely, without having to pass through areas of danger or lands of the Church's enemies, about which they can be fully informed by our messengers. Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Kalends of March, in the fourteenth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa illustri regi Hungariae mandat ut, in hoc tempore difficultatum pro Romana ecclesia, auxilium suum catholicae fidei exhibeat et consilium convocandum approbet. Dat. Lateran. IIII Kal. Martii, anno pontificatus nostri XIV.

Translation to English:

To P., cardinal deacon of San Giorgio al Velabro, legate of the Apostolic See. We, acceding more favorably to the requests of our beloved sons, the authorities, council, and commune of the Perugians, devoted to us and the Apostolic See, command that the castle of Castellione Ildebrandi, which the Gubbio people are said to have constructed in violation of the agreement made and confirmed between them and the Gubbio people, as it is known to have been irrationally constructed, be demolished as the circumstances demand. Given at Lyon, on the 9th of February, in the eighth year [of our pontificate].

Regesto:

Innocentius IV papa P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali, legato suo, mandat ut castrum Castellionis Ildebrandi, a Eugubinis contra pacta erectum, demoliri faciat. 1251, Feb. 9. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

Letters of testimony from the Archbishop of Genoa regarding the preparation of a fleet. To the most blessed father and most holy lord G., by God's providence the supreme pontiff, I., by divine mercy unworthy minister of the Church of Genoa, always ready as well as due in all service. Let it be known to your Beatitude by these letters that Lord G. of Romania, legate of the Apostolic See, with the counsel of the Lord Patriarch of Jerusalem and many wise men, and also with my counsel and assistance, having borrowed money from some Genoese, has so well provided for the galleys, barges, and other necessary ships that when the prelates of the churches come into your presence for the council to be held, they will find the aforementioned ships excellently prepared in Genoa. 

Letters of testimony from the abbot of Saint Stephen of Genoa on the same matter. To the most holy father in Christ and most reverend Lord Gregory, supreme pontiff of the Holy Roman Church, R., abbot of Saint Stephen of Genoa, unworthy, at your feet. With humble devotion, I inform your Holiness that concerning the agreement which Lord Gregory of Romania, legate of the Roman Church, made with the authority and community of Genoa regarding the hiring and arming of galleys and barges, as your Sublimity will see contained in the letters of the same legate, my small self was present, and the same legate labored with diligent care and solicitude always in my presence, nor could he have made the agreement better; indeed, this same was obtained with much difficulty because of certain adversaries of the Church who resisted with all their might.

Letters of testimony from the provost of Santa Maria de Vineis on the same matter. To the most blessed father and lord Gregory, supreme pontiff of the holy and universal church, P. called provost of the church of Santa Maria de Vineis of Genoa at the blessed feet. I inform your Holiness by these presents that Lord G. of Romania, legate of the Apostolic See, with much and great diligence and caution, handled the business of the galleys and barges with counsel taken from many wise and religious clerics and with me faithfully. For although some laymen of Genoa wished to impede this business, it was completed with the Lord granting it, and for this the same legate is very commendable, and we can provide good and true testimony of this.

Letters of testimony from Brother Algisius of the Order of Preachers on the same matter. To the most holy father and lord G., supreme pontiff of the Holy Roman Church, Brother Algisius of the Order of Preachers of Genoa at the blessed feet. I inform your Holiness that Lord Gregory of Romania, your legate and my venerable father and of my brothers, whatever he did regarding the galleys and barges, he did with my counsel and of my brothers, and in this business, he proceeded with much subtlety, diligence, and discretion; and with the Lord assisting, this business was accomplished, though with much difficulty of the same Lord G. and all those whose counsel and assistance he was aided by. However, I was solicitous about your business, your son and your servant, desiring to do your will in all things.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa a diversis ecclesiae Ianuensis dignitatibus certior fit de provisione apparatuum navigii per Gregorium de Romania, legatum apostolicum, consilio plurimorum et auxilio pecuniario accepto, adveniente concilio ecclesiarum praelatorum. 1232, Genuae.

**Translation to English:**

We have full confidence in the Lord regarding your person, whom we have recognized as zealous in the work of the universal church through your diligent actions. Therefore, we grant you by the authority of this letter that no executor given by the Apostolic See or its legates may proceed in your city or diocese regarding the conferment of prelatures, dignities, or ecclesiastical benefices to anyone without your consent. We decree that any attempt made contrary to the tenor of this indulgence shall be null and void. Let no one infringe upon our grant and constitution. Given at Lyon, on the Kalends of February, in the eighth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa (Nomen recipientis) indulget, ut in civitate et diocesi sua nemo executor, a sede apostolica vel eius legatis datus, absque eius consensu super prelaturis, dignitatibus aut beneficiis ecclesiasticis conferendis procedere valeat. 1235, Feb. 1. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot and convent of the monastery of Morbach, which pertains directly to the Roman Church without any intermediary, of the order of Saint Benedict, in the diocese of Basel. The devout prayers of our venerable brother, the bishop of Strasbourg, and your sincere devotion, which you are known to have towards us and the Roman Church, induce us to grant you a special favor. Since, as was proposed on your behalf before us, your monastery has endured many labors and expenses due to the current ecclesiastical affairs, we, considering this with due regard and wishing to alleviate such labors and expenses with the customary clemency of the Apostolic See, grant you the authority by these presents to convert to your own use and retain perpetually one of your churches, over which you have the right of patronage and which has the care of souls attached, whose income according to common estimation does not exceed fifty marks annually, or two of such churches together of the same value, when it happens that it or they become vacant, and to freely take corporal possession of it or them without requiring anyone's consent—notwithstanding any indulgences or letters obtained from the Apostolic See or its legates, for which it might be necessary to make express or full mention in our letters in whatever form of words, or that may be obtained—provided that in the same church, if you decide to retain only one, or in both, if you decide to retain two, there shall be service by a suitable vicar to be presented by you, as pertains to you, with a suitable portion reserved from the revenues of the church or churches for the vicar to support the due burdens of diocesan and archdeaconal procurations, and with all rights of the diocesan in other respects preserved. Let no one etc. of our concession etc. Given at Lyon, on the second Ides of September, in the eighth year. A conservator, the abbot of Saint Vincent of Besançon, was appointed over this matter.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa abbati et conventui monasterii Morbacensis concedit facultatem unam ecclesiam, cui ius patronatus habent, in usus proprios convertere et retinere, cum vacaverit, sub conditione providendi vicarium idoneum. 1251, Sept. 12, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To P., Cardinal Deacon of St. George at Velum Aureum, legate of the apostolic see. Having understood through your letters of devotion that the late emperor Frederick has departed this life, we have turned our thoughts promptly to this matter, so that, as it has long been our desire and that of our brothers, we might return to the City with God's favor. Subsequently, it occurred to us to consider whether divine providence has inspired all in the kingdom of Sicily to return unanimously to the embrace of the mother Church for the sake of achieving full peace and perpetual freedom, or whether perhaps some, instigated by an evil spirit, have wickedly conceived to oppose this with obstacles. Since clear and prudent foresight is necessary in such a significant matter, we desire and mandate you through apostolic letters to be diligently attentive in your heart, so that you may strive to investigate the full truth regarding the universal sentiment of the people of that kingdom about their return to the Church, and report to us without delay what you have discovered. For if the desirable return of those people can freely occur through the Lord's power, we might set aside the company of a large army, or otherwise, it would be fitting for us to come with powerful force, so that the malice of the rebellious may be swiftly crushed and the pious will of the devout may easily be fulfilled. Given as above?.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali mandat, ut exquirat de universali hominum regni Sicilie affectu circa reversionem ad ecclesiam, et quid invenerit sine dilatione rescribat. [Data ut supra].

**Translation to English:**

The city of Genoa, of proven devotion and tested constancy, has always fervently supported the Roman Church with sincere affections, with such immaculate purity of faith that it has presented itself reverently to serve at opportune times and has boldly risen to demonstrate the strength of its resources for the same cause. It is shown to produce greater fruits of devotion through its continual growth in greater affection. Whenever necessary, it ardently presents itself in service to the Apostolic See, unfurling the banner of fidelity ahead of other cities, tirelessly offering its assistance and motivating other cities to serve the same See more eagerly.

Indeed, having recently received your letters, we have learned from their content that although the adversity of current circumstances has deeply wounded your hearts with severe anguish, as no slight offense could be inflicted on your mother Church without affecting your filial affection, you are nonetheless spurred by an even stronger spirit against the enemies of the same Church. You rise with galleys and numerous ships and other vessels to avenge the grave injuries recently inflicted on the Church by these enemies.

We therefore commend in the Lord your steadfastness with worthy praises and render abundant thanks to you. We earnestly admonish, request, and exhort your community, through apostolic writings, to steadfastly support the Church. Vigil with tireless effort for its exaltation so that, with heavenly aid cooperating with you, the strength of adversaries may be weakened and the audacity of offenders may experience avenging hands.

And to more swiftly and usefully promote the Church's affairs in this matter, with the Lord as our guide, behold, we specially send to you our venerable brother…the Patriarch of Jerusalem, dear and pleasing to us and our brethren by the merit of his integrity. Receive him joyfully and devoutly, and treat him honorably out of reverence for the Apostolic See and us—indeed, as though it were us in him. Be sure to give full credence to him in all matters he will relay to you on our behalf regarding these affairs, effectively executing them, setting aside any pretext or delay.

For with the Lord's consent, we will endeavor to procure that which brings praise to Him, strength to the Catholic faith, and an increase in ecclesiastical liberty, and that your city may obtain special honor and benefit. Whatever you decide to arrange with the aforementioned Patriarch concerning these affairs, we will hold it pleasing and acceptable, with the Lord granting it. Given at the Lateran, August 16, in the fifteenth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa civitati Ianuensi mandat, ut in defensione ecclesiae Romanae perseveranter assistat et negotia cum patriarcham Ierosolimitanum, ad ea specialiter destinatum, fideliter et efficaciter pertractet. 1241, Aug. 16. Laterano.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot and convent of the monastery of Fossanova of the Cistercian order in the diocese of Terracina. Inclined by the just desires of the petitioners, we confirm and fortify with the protection of this present writing the place of the Old Mill with all its rights and appurtenances on the Saona River at Port Algardi in the diocese of Calvi, where you later constructed a mill at your own expense, which the late emperor Frederick, before being bound by the chain of excommunication, as it then pertained to him, granted to you and your monastery with pious liberality, as is more fully contained in the privilege made thereof. We have caused the tenor of that privilege to be noted word for word in these presents; it is as follows: Frederick, by the grace of God, ever august emperor of the Romans and king of Sicily. By this present writing, we make known to all our faithful, both present and future, that we, considering the religion and honesty of brother Peter, the venerable abbot, and the brothers of the monastery of Fossanova of the Cistercian order, from our usual grace of majesty, grant and donate to the same monastery forever in our domain the place of the Old Mill on the Saona River at the place called Port Algardi, with all justices and appurtenances, which the same mill, when it was whole, is known to have had, wishing that henceforth it be lawful for the aforesaid abbot and brothers of Fossanova and their successors to build a mill in the aforesaid place without any contradiction and to possess it freely and peacefully forever, and let it be permissible to no one to build there or do anything that may result in damage and inconvenience to the same mill. To the memory and perpetual strength of this our grant and donation we have ordered this present writing to be made and sealed with the seal of our majesty. Given at Messina, after the court held at Capua, the twenty-fourth day of the month of May, ninth indiction. Therefore, let no one etc. of our confirmation etc. Given at Lyon, the third Ides of August, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati et conventui monasterii Fosse Nove Cisterciensis ordinis Terracinensis diocesis confirmat locum Molendini Veteris cum omnibus iuribus et pertinentiis, quem Fridericus imperator monasterio ipsorum concessit, ut ipsi et successores molendinum ibi aedificare et pacifice possidere possint. Datum Lugduni, III Idus Augusti, anno VIII (1234).

**Translation to English:**

... concerning the canon of the greater church and ... the provost of St. Nicholas of Magdeburg. Our venerable brother, the Bishop of Meissen, has shown us by his petition that the noble man, the Margrave of Meissen, having gathered an army and allied himself with certain sons of iniquity, wickedly devastated the lands, possessions, and other goods of his church. He approached the village of Curiise and other villages of the said church in a hostile manner and, having taken away the goods found there, presumptuously set them on fire, with divine reverence set aside. Because of this, the same bishop, demanding justice, has promulgated sentences of excommunication against the said margrave and his accomplices, and of interdict upon the land of the margrave, because they, having been diligently warned, did not care to make amends for such damages and injuries, and so public and notorious was the excess that it could not be concealed by any subterfuge. Therefore, he asked of us that we make these sentences have the firmness of authority. We command that these sentences be observed as they have been reasonably pronounced, notwithstanding that it is known that the said margrave has been granted by the Apostolic See that no sentence of interdict or excommunication can be promulgated against his land or person by apostolic letters, nor any indulgence of the Apostolic See by which the execution of our mandate may be impeded. If both of you are not able, etc. Given at Lyons. November 30, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa canoni maioris ecclesiae et praeposito Sancti Nicolai Magdeburgensis mandat, ut sententias excommunicationis in marchionem Misnensem eiusque complices et interdicti in terram ipsius, a Misnensi episcopo latas, observari faciant, non obstante quod ab apostolica sede indultum est marchioni ut tales sententiae non possint promulgari. 1234, Nov. 30, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To William of Ripatransone, layman of the diocese of Fermo. When a petition is made to us, it is customary to consider its fulfillment. Hence, as your presented petition to us contained, the late bishop of Fermo, of good memory, under the mandate of our predecessor of happy memory, Pope Gregory, granted to you and your heirs up to the third generation, as long as they were male, certain vineyards and possessions in emphyteusis. Our beloved son, P., cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the apostolic see, considering the devotion you hold towards the Roman Church, decided to extend this grant made to you and your heirs also to females, as is more fully contained in the letters prepared on this matter. We, inclined by your supplications, confirm by apostolic authority that which was providently done by the cardinal, and we strengthen it with the support of the present writing. Let no one therefore etc. Given at Lyon, 8th Kalends of February, in the eighth year. A conservator was appointed for him on this matter, the prior of St. Venantius of Camerino.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Guillelmo de Ripatransonisi, laico Firmane diocesis, confirmat concessionem vinearum et possessionum in emphiteosim factam per Firmanum episcopum sub mandato Gregorii papae predecessoris, quae a P. S. Georgii ad Velum Aureum cardinali etiam ad feminas extendi decreta est. Dat. Lugduni, VIII Kal. Feb., anno octavo.

Translation to English:

Desiring that churches be provided with such pastors by whom they may be healthily governed in spiritual and temporal matters, we command that the provision of the church of Verona, should it happen to become vacant in any manner, be reserved to the Apostolic See. You are to interdict the chapter of the said church and all others to whom its election pertains, so that, upon the resignation or death of their pontiff, they do not presume to proceed to election, postulation, or nomination, promulgating nevertheless a sentence of excommunication on the transgressors of this prohibition. This is notwithstanding any general or special letters obtained from the Apostolic See concerning the promotion of anyone to the episcopate in the province of Lombardy or in the March of Treviso, or in any city therein, and specifically in the church of Verona, under whatever form of words or tenor they may exist, which we wish to have no force concerning the said church of Verona. Whether it has been enjoined on any legate or envoy of the same See, or anyone else by it, generally in the cities of his legation or in the province or the March aforesaid, or specifically in any of their cities or the aforementioned church of Verona, that they proceed to such an interdiction or reservation, or whether by them it has been proceeded to such an inhibition and reservation in the same church —; you are to silence contradictors, etc. For from now, we decree null and void whatever shall have been attempted by anyone against your inhibition and reservation. Given at Lyons, on the 11th of October, in the seventh year.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa mandat, ut provisio ecclesiae Veronensis sede apostolica reservetur, et interdicit ne ad electionem pontificis procedatur, promulgans sententiam excommunicationis in transgressores. 1233, Oct. 11. Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To the dean of Würzburg. Know that it has come to our attention that our beloved son, the noble man, the count of Henneberg, devoted to us and the Roman Church, was deceived by false words from the abbot and convent of the monastery of Reinesbrunn, of the Order of Saint Benedict in the diocese of Mainz, who had obtained from us, through our letters, the indulgence that they could choose whoever they wished as their advocate and defender of their monastery. However, the same abbot and convent, not without that vice of ingratitude, where evil is returned for good, recklessly abused this grace granted to them by choosing, under the authority of our letters, an advocate or defender of that monastery who was disloyal to the Church, causing the said count serious harm. We command you, therefore, that if this is true, since the abbot and convent have rendered themselves unworthy of the grace by their abuse, you or another, by our authority, revoke this concession and declare everything that followed from it to be utterly invalid. Given at Lyon, on the 3rd day before the Nones of February, in the eighth year.

Regesto in Latin:

Innocentius IV papa decano Herbipolensi mandat, ut, si abbas et conventus Reynersbrunnen monasterii advocatum ineptum elegerint, concessionem revocet et irritam faciat. 1251, Feb. 3, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of St. Gall in the diocese of Constance. Since, as our devoted son, the noble man, the count of Tokkenburg, has explained to us, he, for the defense of ecclesiastical liberty and the promotion of the general cause of the church against Frederick, the former emperor, having taken up the sign of the cross, did not hesitate to expose himself to many dangers, being wounded many times in conflicts while resisting the efforts of the supporters of Frederick and thwarting their attacks.
