We, therefore, wishing to grant special favor to him through the person of our beloved son Radulf, his brother, elected of the monastery of St. John in Turzal of the Order of St. Benedict in the diocese of Constance, command you to provide for him some abbey of the same order, which he may choose to accept, if any in the city or diocese of Basel is currently vacant or as soon as an opportunity arises, through you or another, by our authority — notwithstanding if we have written concerning similar provision in the same city or diocese for others, to whom we do not wish, etc., up to: to be generated, or if it has been granted by the Apostolic See that they cannot be compelled to receive or provide for anyone, or be interdicted, suspended, or excommunicated by apostolic letters unless mention of such a grant is expressly made, or any other special or general indulgence granted by the same See under any form, by which such provision, etc., up to: or be delayed, even if its tenor must be inserted word for word in these presents, or what is said to have been granted by us to our venerable brother, the bishop of Basel, that no one should be executor in our provisions except himself —; those opposing, etc. Given at Lyons, the seventh Ides of January, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati Sancti Galli Constantiensis diocesis mandat ut Radulfo, fratri comitis de Tokkenburg, qui pro ecclesiae defensione contra Fridericum quondam imperatorem se periculis exposuit, de aliqua abbatia ordinis Sancti Benedicti in civitate vel diocesi Basiliensi vacante provideat. Datum Lugduni, VII Idus Ianuarii, anno octavo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Elect of Passau. To the just requests of the petitioners, etc., until fulfilled. Since, as your petition presented to us contained, the church of Passau was lacking in pastoral governance, our venerable brother P., bishop of Albano, a legate of the apostolic see, wishing to provide that church with a person suitable for such a burden and honor, having diligently considered the merits of your nobility, devotion, and probity, has appointed you as bishop and pastor of that church. We, inclined to your supplications, approve and accept what has been done regarding you in the said church by the same bishop, ratifying it by apostolic authority and confirming it with the protection of this present writing. Let no one, therefore, etc., contravene our confirmation, etc. Given at Lyon, on the Calends of October, in the eighth year. Over this matter, conservators were assigned to him: the bishop of Eichstätt and the abbot of Saint Emmeram of Regensburg.

To the Chapter, ministerials, and citizens of Passau. Since, as was proposed before us on behalf of the beloved son B., the Elect of Passau, the church of Passau was lacking in pastoral governance, etc., as above with the words competently changed until: pastor, we earnestly ask and urge your whole community, enjoining it upon you for the remission of your sins, that you humbly and devotedly show and pay due honor to the same Elect as the father and pastor of your souls, and as you are bound to defend the said church, you effectively assist the said Elect against those who seize, invade, and plunder the goods of that church, and also against the supporters of the late Emperor F., dukes, counts, and barons, and others, both clerics and laypeople, of the dioceses of Passau, Salzburg, and Regensburg, when requested by him, so that he may rejoice in finding due support among you and be more strongly bound to your charity, and that you may deserve to be commended by God and men. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa electo Pataviensi nuntiat ratam habere electionem eius in episcopum et confirmat auctoritate apostolica; mandat etiam capitulo, ministerialibus et civibus Pataviensibus, ut electum tanquam patrem et pastorem honorificentia prosequantur et contra adversarios eiusdem ecclesiae, requisiti, assistant. Datum Lugduni, Kalendis Octobris, anno octavo.

**Translation to English:**

To Anselm, Bishop of Worms. Your petition presented to us contained that our venerable brother, the Bishop of Albano, legate of the Apostolic See, appointed you, brother of the Hospital of Saint Mary of the Germans, as bishop to the then vacant see of Warmia with apostolic authority and summoned our venerable brothers, the bishops of Cambrai, Tournai, and Arras, as well as several abbots, to bestow upon you the gift of consecration, as is more fully contained in his patent letters prepared on this matter. We, therefore, inclined by your supplications, hold as ratified and firm what was properly and canonically done by the same Bishop of Albano upon this matter, and confirm it with apostolic authority, granting the protection of the present writing. Moreover, we have caused the tenor of these letters to be written down word for word in the present documents, which is as follows: "P. by the mercy of God, Bishop of Albano, legate of the Apostolic See, to all those who inspect these present letters, health in the Lord. Let your whole body know that we, by apostolic authority, have appointed the venerable Father Anselm, brother of the House of Saint Mary of the Germans in Prussia, to the bishopric of Warmia as bishop and pastor and thereafter, with the venerable fathers, the bishops of Cambrai, Tournai, and Arras, and several abbots and prelates assisting us in the church of the Friars Preachers of Valenciennes on the Lord’s Day, namely, the 5th day before the Kalends of September, have seen fit to bestow the gift of consecration. In testimony of this, we have caused the present letters to be fortified with the muniment of our seal. Given at Valenciennes, the 5th day before the Kalends of September, in the year of the Lord 1250." No one at all shall etc. Given at Lyon, the 4th day before the Nones of October, in the eighth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Anselmo episcopo Warmaciensi confirmat provisionem et consecrationem ad episcopatum Warmiensem, factam a Petro episcopo Albanensi, apostolica auctoritate. Actum Lugduni, II Nonas Octobris, anno pontificatus octavo (1251).

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Strasbourg. Your fraternity has informed us that, as a zealous supporter of the Church, you, wishing to bind certain nobles and powerful people, as well as others from the city of Strasbourg and some other cities and dioceses, to the service of the Roman Church against its enemies, gave them a certain sum of money and promised to give another, mortgaging many of the possessions of the Church of Strasbourg for this money. However, some of them later did not care to assist you, and some withdrew from the service of the Church. Therefore, so that the aforementioned individuals do not gain advantage from their deceit, we have decided by the authority of these presents to grant you the right to reclaim the money given to them and the possessions granted for that purpose, or obligated in any other way, and you are not bound to fulfill the promise—despite any instruments or letters, oaths taken, or penalties added, or any other guarantees provided on this matter either by you or by the chapter of the Church of Strasbourg, whom you assert are obligated together with you. Therefore, let no one etc. of our concession etc. Given at Lyon, the Kalends of February, in the eighth year (of our pontificate).

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Argentinensi concedit ut pecuniam datam et possessiones ob id datas vel quovis titulo obligatas repetere valeat, nec tenearis exhibere promissum, non obstantibus instrumentis, iuramentis vel cautionibus. Datum Lugduni, Kalendis Februarii, anno VIII.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Como. The prior, major, and sounder part of the monks of the monastery of St. Gall, said to belong directly to the Roman Church, have shown us through a petition that recently, when the monastery was vacant of an abbot, the prior and monks gathered in chapter to discuss the appointment of a future abbot. Proceeding by way of scrutiny, the prior, the treasurer, and eight others, who formed the majority in the chapter, canonically elected the provost of the same monastery—a religious, prudent, and honorable man—believing that through his industry the monastery would be reformed from good to better. To prevent any prejudice to this election, an appeal was made on behalf of the elected to the Apostolic See. However, the minority, some of whom had no voice in the election, presumptuously attempted to elect Walter, a monk of the same monastery, completely unsuitable and unworthy. Upon appeal to our venerable brother, the Bishop of Constance, who, although having no jurisdiction over the said monastery, was overly favorable in the matter, the election of Walter was wrongly confirmed, and he was invested with temporalities by Conrad, son of Frederick called the emperor, who calls himself King of Germany, issuing an excommunication sentence against opponents and rebels, allegedly. On the other hand, it was claimed for Walter that when the monastery became vacant, the greater and sounder part of the convent convened for the election, following a diligent discussion, and elected Walter, a discreet and prudent man, evidently suitable to govern the place, as their abbot canonically. He consented immediately to the election, and upon appeal to the said Bishop of Constance, whom they claimed was in possession of confirming abbots of the monastery, the election was confirmed, rejecting the nomination of the said provost. Therefore, it was requested from us to provide a remedy. Since we are not certain of the aforementioned matters, we command that, having inquired into the truth of all these things, and having lifted any excommunication sentences issued by the said bishop against the provost and his electors or the ministers of the monastery for this matter, if you find Walter was assumed to the governance of the monastery against canonical sanctions and the election of the provost was celebrated canonically and of a suitable person, you procure to confirm it by our authority, and secure obedience and due reverence to the said provost from the monks and other subjects of the monastery. Otherwise, if you find Walter's election canonical and celebrated validly, secure obedience and reverence from the monks and subjects to him and have the blessing granted. If both elections are found uncanonical, you ensure a canonical election of a suitable person for the monastery. Meanwhile, do not allow the ministers of the monastery to relinquish the care of the castles and other properties they hold for the monastery, to prevent any harm or consumption of its goods. Moreover, to prevent the said provost from suffering loss, ensure two monks pursuing this matter receive necessary expenses from the goods of the monastery; contradictors, etc.; notwithstanding any letters prejudicing truth and justice obtained from the Apostolic See, the constitution of two days set in the general council notwithstanding, provided no party is drawn beyond the third or fourth part outside their diocese to judgment by authority of these presents. Given at the Lateran, 4 Non. June, in the fourteenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Cumano mandat ut, post inquisitionem, electionem inter Waltherum et praepositum monasterii Sancti Galli dirimat, providendo confirmationem vel novam electionem abbatem si oportet. 1240, Iun. 2, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

I. To the Patriarch of Aquileia, spirit of sound counsel. The Roman Church, your mother, hoped that, being neither ungrateful for the grace granted to you nor forgetful of the benefits received from the Apostolic See, you would not only refrain from offending it in any way, but also stand as a wall for it against adversaries. But you, not acting as is appropriate, presumed with condemnable audacity to communicate with Frederick, the so-called emperor, an enemy of God and the Church, who has been justly bound by us with the chain of excommunication for many reasons at the demand of his many merits, in both divine offices as well as in greeting and at the table, showing contempt for the keys of the Church. Although this is a fault where it is wrong to relax punishment, and leniency which does not merit leniency of pardon, nevertheless, because we hold the persons of our dearest sons in Christ, B. King of Hungary and C. King of Ruthenia, your illustrious nephews, with a special prerogative of love and grace among other Catholic kings and Christian princes, due to which we cannot deny the devotion of these kings, when according to God we should listen to any other Catholic prince, we will grant you this grace for the honor of their serenity, that, after you have set out on the journey to come to us, you may be absolved from the chain of excommunication, by which you are bound for this reason, by our venerable brother, the Bishop of Castellan, to whom we send our letters on this matter, according to the form of the Church. Therefore, by the authority of these presents and the counsel of our brothers, we command you, that as soon as you can, you do not delay in coming to our presence. Given at the Lateran, 14th Kalends of January, in the thirteenth year of our pontificate.

II. To the Bishop of Castellan. Since the Patriarch of Aquileia, for communicating with Frederick, etc., up to: at the table, and because he has neglected to publicly denounce him as excommunicated, as he had received instructions from us, although he deemed this to be executed in front of many, not even promptly coming to our presence, as he had been commanded on our behalf, has been bound by our authority with the chain of excommunication, we command you to humbly grant the gift of absolution to the aforementioned patriarch, after he has begun the journey to come to us, according to the form of the Church. You should also ensure that the form of the oath, which he will take, is sent to us word for word by his open letters signed with his seal, and your process on this matter by a personal messenger to us as soon as possible. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa, patriarcha Aquilegensi mandat ut quam citius poterit ad suam praesentiam veniat pro absolutione ab excommunicationis vinculo a venerabili fratre Castellano episcopo, propter communicationem cum Friderico imperatore excommunicato, concessa gratia propter reges Hungariae et Ruthenorum nepotes eius. Datum Laterani, XIIII Kalendas Ianuarias, anno XIII pontificatus.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbots of the Cistercian Order of the diocese of Würzburg, known as Ebetab and Bilhilthusen. You should be aware that it has come to our attention that, a few times past, our beloved son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, W., laid siege to the rebellious castles of Oppenheim, Geilinhusen, and Breghele. Some monks and lay brothers from the convents of your monasteries, who were assigned to serve the king and those assisting him, were present at this siege. Due to the pressing scarcity of food, they were forced to eat meat contrary to the regulations of your order. Therefore, because what was illicit through the prohibition of the order became licit due to necessity and, as it is said, the authority of the one who was superior there, we have decided to urge and admonish your discretion, strictly ordering that you do not impose any penalty or penance on them against their will on account of this situation. Given at Lyon, the Nones of February, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa abbatibus Cisterciensis ordinis Herbipolensis diocesis mandat ne monachis et conversis, qui propter obsidionem regis Romanorum carnes edere coacti sunt, poenam infligant. 1251, Febr. 5, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble woman Adelaide, niece of our venerable brother, the bishop of Constance. Often the Roman pontiff, who presides over all law, dispenses beyond all law, especially when necessity or evident benefit demands it. Therefore, since, as our venerable brother the bishop of Constance has explained to us, the noble man Heberard of Wade has betrothed you, who are related to him in the fourth degree of affinity, and since a marriage between you and this nobleman cannot be consummated without an apostolic dispensation, we, considering that Walter and Gozwin, lords of Henelsa, nephews of the aforementioned bishop, whom the same nobleman captured and holds imprisoned in favor of the late Emperor Frederick of the Romans, might be released to liberty because of this and the same nobleman might be brought back to the devotion of the church, inclined by the prayers of the same bishop, we dispense with you by apostolic authority that you may consummate the marriage begun with the aforementioned nobleman, notwithstanding such an impediment. Let no one, therefore, etc., oppose our dispensation, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 11th of February, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Adelaide nobili mulieri, nepti episcopi Constantiensis, auctoritate apostolica dispensat ut matrimonium cum Heberardo de Wade, cuius quarta affinitatis linea contingit, consumare possit, non obstante impedimento. 1249, Feb. 11, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To P., Cardinal Deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, Legate of the Apostolic See. Since, as your discretion is not unaware, the beloved sons, the citizens of Perugia, never deviating from the devotion to the Apostolic See, have suffered such severe damages and injuries from the degenerate sons, the citizens of Foligno, that they can scarcely ever be erased without severe penance: we, who are obliged to assist the same Perugians by sharing in their joys in prosperity and in their adversities through shared compassion, wishing to offer them the solace we can regarding these matters, deemed it necessary to advise and exhort your discretion, strictly ordering you through apostolic writings, that you should not admit any agreement with the aforementioned Foligno citizens without the counsel and knowledge of the Perugians, unless it is honorable and deservedly acceptable to them, or even to negotiate any settlement, so that the faithful may rejoice in having found grace for their faith and devotion, and the unfaithful may be duly punished for the audacity of their temerity. Given at Lyons, on the Ides of February, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali legato mandatum dat, ne cum Fuliginatibus sine Perusinorum consilio compositionem admittat, nisi eis honorabilem. Datum Lugduni, Idibus Februarii, anno octavo.

**Translation to English:**

To P., Cardinal Deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the apostolic see. By the authority of these presents, we command you not to proceed in any way with the conferral of vacant or to be vacated archbishoprics, bishoprics, and abbeys in the kingdom of Sicily without our special mandate, as it is very expedient and beneficial that such matters are handled with the maturity and providence that brings honor to the church and, with God's favor, more easily incline the hearts of the people of that kingdom towards the pursuit of desired devotion. Given as above. 

II. Revocation of conferrals or provisions made in the kingdom of Sicily by the legate or any others. For the perpetual memory of the matter. Because the kingdom of Sicily, a special possession of the apostolic see, has long endured hardships and pressures, from which, now that the one who burdened it with constant demands and uncustomary services is no longer, it begins to breathe freely. It is fitting and expedient that we, who are charged with its care, seek the relief of the desired peace, lest it be troubled by any disturbances or scandal. Therefore, as we have inhibited our beloved son P., Cardinal Deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the apostolic see, by our letters, from conferring archbishoprics, bishoprics, or abbeys in the aforementioned kingdom, we decree by the authority of these presents that any conferral or provision made by the same legate or any others without our special mandate concerning such vacant or to be vacated dignities is henceforth null and void. Let no one, etc. of our constitution, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 8th day before the Kalends of February, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Petro Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali, apostolicae sedis legato mandat ne archiepiscopatus, episcopatus vel abbatias in regno Siciliae absque mandato speciali conferat, et omnes collationes seu provisiones absque mandato factas irritas decernit. Datum Lugduni, VIII Kalendas Februarii, anno VIII.

**Translation to English:**

Letters of the prelates of Spain concerning the capture of the legates of the Apostolic See and certain other prelates. To the most holy father and lord Gregory, by the grace of God, supreme pontiff of the Holy Roman Church, I, the archbishop of Arles, and P., the archbishop of Tarragona, N., the bishop of Astorga, L., the bishop of Orense, M., the bishop of Salamanca, P., the bishop of Portugal, and E., the bishop of Piacenza, kiss the feet of the blessed. We sorrowfully report, and in reporting we deeply lament, that while we and the venerable fathers in Christ, the archbishops of Rouen, Bordeaux, Auch, Besançon, and the bishops of Carcassonne, Agde, Nîmes, Tortona, Asti, and Pavia, along with the noble Romeus, procurator and envoy of the illustrious count of Provence, and many other prelates and procurators of our and other dioceses and provinces, were trying to come into your holiness's presence in obedience and devotion, in accordance with the contents of your letters, disregarding or setting aside any difficulties, threats, and perils, on the third day of May, the ships of the Pisans and Sicilians and some others under the jurisdiction of Frederick, the so-called emperor, and by his command, opposed us. They attacked us so powerfully and vigorously, as our faults demanded, that except for us and the aforementioned Romeus and the lord of Compostela, who was hindered at Portovenere and had not yet reached Genoa, and some other prelates, namely the archbishop of Braga and the bishop of Anjou, and a few other procurators and members of the households of the prelates, whom the mercy of Jesus Christ delivered from the hands of the wicked, and some who were killed by sword and drowning, they took the rest with them, as is reported and we believe, bound in chains. Since the world is placed in evil beyond what can be conceived, and the universal church seems to be in great tribulation, unless the Lord should deign to have mercy with an outstretched arm, may your holiness consider and deliberate on how to proceed in such a crucial time of need, and command us to do what is pleasing to you, because notwithstanding any adversity, which, when faced with good intent, should be the proof of true love, not an indication of rejection, may you know that we remain in all constancy and firmness. And although, due to the many and grave offenses he has committed against God and the holy church up to now, it would be appropriate to proceed more harshly against this tyrant, yet we dare to suggest that action be taken against him with due reason according to the severity of the crime; for under his rule, the church would never enjoy peace or tranquility, especially since all princes would take example and boldness from him in this matter. Concerning the power and citizens of Genoa, we present to your holiness that, as far as we have heard and understood, they will show themselves more faithful and zealous in the cause of the church than they have shown themselves up to now. Given at Genoa, on the 10th day of May.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopis Arelatensi et Terraconensi, et episcopis Astoricensi, Auriensi, Salamantinensi, Portugalensi et Placentino litteras mittentes. Queruntur de captione legatorum apostolicorum et aliorum prelatorum per navigium Pisanorum et Siculorum mandato Friderici imperatoris, et hortantur pontificem ad agendum adversus eum ob crimina commissa. Affirmant fidem civium Ianuensium in ecclesiae causam. Datum Ianuæ, X die Maii, pontificatus anno duodecimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Würzburg. We have heard from our beloved son, the noble lord, the Count of Henneberg, that the monastery of Würzburger in your diocese, situated in the lands of the said count, which used to be affluent with temporal riches and provided necessary sustenance for a convent of forty monks, has now reached a state of extreme poverty due to the malice and dissolute life previously led by the abbots and monks there. Moreover, it is entirely deformed in spiritual matters. Therefore, the said count, fearing God and zealous for ecclesiastical propriety, has humbly petitioned us to incorporate the monastery into the Cistercian order, as he does not trust in its reformation under the current order, and he is willing to remit to the monastery a hundred marks of silver and more, which he annually receives from it as advocacy rights, for the remission of his sins. We should take care to incorporate the monastery into the said order from our plenitude of power. Trusting fully in the Lord in your circumspection, although the report of the aforementioned count should be fully trusted and his intention, emerging from the source of pure faith, is worthy of commendation before God and men, it is not appropriate to proceed in such matters without careful deliberation. We command you to diligently inquire into the above matters and faithfully report to us what you find. Given at Lyon, on the Nones of February, in the eighth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Herbipolensi mandat ut investiget de statu monasterii de Wrrawe et referat, cum comes de Hennenberg petierit ut monasterium ordini Cisterciensi incorporetur. Datum Lugduni, Nonis Februarii, anno octavo.

To the same. Regarding ecclesiastical benefices and also feuds to be conferred in the Kingdom of Sicily, as well as other provisions to be made there, and also concerning those which have already been granted by us or others with our authority, various letters have previously been issued by the Apostolic See. However, because the hearts of many might be troubled and serious scandal could arise due to the pretext of these letters, we have decided that these letters should be suspended until our pleasure, decreeing null and void anything that might be attempted through them against this suspension. Given as above. To the archbishops and bishops and beloved sons, the abbots, priors, deans, archdeacons, and other prelates of churches established throughout the Kingdom of Sicily. Regarding ecclesiastical benefices, etc., as above to the point: have been issued. However, because it is our duty to proceed on these matters and others in such a way that it may redound to the honor of the Church and provide you with worthy joy, we have decided that the aforesaid letters should be suspended until our pleasure, decreeing, etc., as above in the previous.

**Regesto in Latin:**

**Papa:** Gregorius IX

**Recipient:** Archiepiscopis et episcopis ac dilectis filiis abbatibus, prioribus, decanis, archidiaconis et aliis ecclesiarum prelatis per regnum Sicilie constitutis

**Place:** Datum Laterani

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Constance. Confident in the purity of your faith and your proven discernment, we entrust you with the authority, through these presents, to receive any nobles, others, or communities of castles, towns, or villages of your diocese who wish to return to the command of the Church. You are to grant them the benefit of absolution according to the form of the Church, provided you first receive from them sufficient and suitable assurances that they will persevere in devotion to the Apostolic See and swear due fidelity to our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, W., who will soon ascend to the pinnacle of imperial honor, and that they will openly support and assist him as their king. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Constantiensi mandat, ut nobiles et alii vel universitates diocesis sue ad mandatum ecclesiae redeuntes recipiat et absolutionem tribuat, cautione data de devotione et fidelitate erga W. regem Romanorum servanda. Datum ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To Ulric, canon of the church of Bubelsbach in the diocese of Constance. On behalf of our beloved son Berengarius, rector of the church of Ingersheim in the diocese of Speyer, it was presented before us that, when he was presented to the then vacant church by the noble man, the Duke of Austria, and Berthold of Slutheim, a cleric of the diocese of Worms, was presented by Ralph, the brother of the said duke, the true patrons of the church, to our beloved son, the provost of the church of St. Guy in Speyer, the archdeacon of the place, to whom by ancient, approved, and hitherto peaceably observed custom the institution of the rector in that church pertains. The said provost, after summoning the parties to his presence for this reason and having legitimately understood the merits of the case as befitted him, rejected the said Berthold as unworthy because he was lacking in age and his parents were allied with the late Emperor Frederick and his son Conrad against the church, and did not admit him to the church, but canonically instituted the aforementioned Berengarius in the same. Therefore, at the behest of the said duke and the noble man, the Count of Württemberg, who supplicated us on behalf of the said Berengarius, we, having ratified and approved what was prudently done by the aforementioned provost in this matter, confirm the same by apostolic authority, and we command that, if it is so, you ensure that the aforementioned Berengarius enjoys peaceful possession of the said church by our authority, either through you or another—notwithstanding any apostolic letters obtained by the said Berthold on this matter with truth concealed, and proceedings improperly held by the same letters—and to oppose any contradictors, etc. Given at Lyons, December 11th, in the eighth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Ulrico canonico ecclesie Bubelsbac' mandat ut Berengerium, rectorem ecclesie de Ingereson Spirensis diocesis, pacifica possessione gaudere faciat, confirmando eius institutionem in ecclesia contra Bertholdum, clericum Warmaciensis diocesis. 1250, Dec. 11, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

The only part we provide here is transcribed; the missing parts are of no significance to the general history of the empire. The letter is read in full in Ripolli Bull. Praed. t. I, p. 108, n. 198. Potthast, Reg. 10841. To Rusudani, the queen, and her son David, the illustrious king of the Georgians. ECCH. 4322. Admirable vessel, sun, work of the Most High, etc. That which is also contained in your letters, namely that the Tartar enemies of the Catholic faith have entered your kingdom, diminished the joy we had, and the severe damages they inflicted upon you wounded our acquired joy. Nevertheless, we have regained some exultation in that, although you turned your backs on the aforementioned enemies, you have ultimately achieved the palm of victory over the victors, and the danger of grave loss has afflicted those who dared to take up arms to your detriment. However, you should also sympathize with us, who are currently suffering many persecutions from the enemies of the faith, for apart from the Saracens who in parts of Spain and Syria attack the Catholic faith, several others, having apostatized from the faith of Christ and attacking the Church of God with whatever forces they can muster, are trying to introduce a new sect of perdition and to exterminate the faith of salvation and human redemption from the earth. But perhaps the divine will imposes these trials upon us, which sometimes allows the good to be troubled by the wicked, so that He examines their constancy and strength like gold in a furnace, and purges all rust of sin from the heart of the just through such tribulation, for the building of the divine temple does not accept stones that the hand of the craftsman has not polished with many tribulations, and bread is not made from wheat unless it is first cleansed from the chaff with the flail. For just as the just, once purged, receive eternal rewards, so the proven advance to the delights of eternal life. For the people of Israel did not enter the promised land until, after a long circuit in the desert and many victories over enemies, they were deemed worthy of entry into the same land. Nevertheless, we hope that our Redeemer, after this storm, will bring calm and will not fail to crush the adversaries of the Apostolic See under His feet. Therefore, children, cease to wonder if the army of the Roman Church does not come to your aid against the said Tartars, because the wickedness of the interposed Saracens, whom we have ordered to be attacked in the said Syria, would have prevented it, and the distances of the intervening lands, which barely allowed these rumors to reach us, would not have permitted it. We have been insufficient to come to your aid, as we labor without interruption with all our might for the defense of the Christian faith in Italy and the said parts of Syria and Spain. Therefore, since we could not help you otherwise, we decided to send our letters to your sincerity, so that you might at least know from writing our affection, which you could not know from the expected aid that we bear towards you, the indication of our love, etc. Dated at the Lateran, on the Ides of January, in the thirteenth year.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa Rusudani reginae et David filio eius, regi Georgiano, significat quod, licet auxilia militaria contra Tartaros mittere non potuerit propter Saracenos in Syria hostes et interiectas terras, tamen consolationem et caritatem per litteras exprimit. 1239, 13 Ianuarii, Laterani.

To the same. Having full confidence in the prudence, circumspection, and fidelity of our beloved son, the noble man Roger of Leucin, we have decided to entrust to him the affairs of Sicily, which particularly resides in our heart, as he remains devoted to the church. We enjoin upon him for the remission of his sins to diligently and faithfully execute it for the honor and utility of the Apostolic See, and for the good, peace, and healthy state of that land. Therefore, we command that you effectively comply with everything he enjoins upon you on our behalf. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa (recipientibus ignotis) Rogerium de Leucinio de negotiis Siciliae, ad honorem et utilitatem apostolicae sedis et bonum status illius terrae, fideliter exequendis mandat. [1231-1234], [Urbs].

To Albert, canon of Basel, brother of the noble man, Count of Habsburg. Since you, as our venerable brothers, the bishops of Constance and Basel, have taken care to inform us, have faithfully assisted them in the matter of the general church, exposing your person and possessions to many dangers, by the authority of these presents we grant to you that, due to the lack of devotion of the noble man R., Count of Habsburg, your brother, who is said to be a supporter of the enemies of the church, no prejudice may be generated against you concerning your benefices, as long as you remain devoted to the Roman Church — notwithstanding any letters obtained against you regarding this from the Apostolic See or even to be obtained. Therefore, let no one, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 10th day before the Kalends of March, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Alberto canonico Basiliensi indulgentiam concedit, ne ob indevotionem fratris, comitis de Habspurc, prejudicium circa beneficia patiatur, dummodo ecclesiae Romanae devotus maneat. 1235, Feb. 20. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Gotifridus de Hoenlachd. We have frequently heard that the Lord has granted you great wisdom, such that you delight in the love and fear of the divine name, rejecting vices and embracing virtues, and also providing timely support of favor to pious places and ecclesiastical persons. We have also heard that previously you would have willingly rendered yourself devoted to the church, if it could have been done without your disgrace and without causing you considerable loss. However, since the merciful Lord has removed the former Emperor F. from the midst, granting you, as well as other faithful, a favorable time in which you can publicly display the affection of your devotion toward the Holy Roman Church through the effectiveness of your deeds, we have thought it appropriate and necessary to affectionately request and admonish your nobility, enjoining you for the remission of your sins, that you direct your spirit toward those things by which the said church may be filled with an abundance of joy, etc., as in the letter to the Duke of Saxony.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro Gotifrido de Hoenlachd mandat ut, amotis impedimentis, devotionem suam erga sanctam Romanam ecclesiam operibus manifestet ad gaudium ecclesiae augendum. 1231, [Locum non specificatum].

To Brother Roger of Lentinio from the Order of Preachers. We wish to grant a special favor to our beloved son, the noble man Guerrerius of Squillace, and therefore we command that, upon his resignation from the farmhouse of Baropodio in the diocese of Mileto, you grant him the castle of Saint George in the same diocese as a fief by our authority, provided it does not belong to another who persists in devotion to the Apostolic See. Gregorius IX papa Fratri Rogerio de Lentinio de ordine Praedicatorum mandat ut, eo resignante casale de Baropodio, castrum Sancti Georgii in feudum Guerrerio de Squillacio concedat. Anno Pontificatus VII, [Locus non specificatus].

**Translation to English:**

To the Prior of Prüm in the Diocese of Trier. Our beloved son Rigaudus, a cleric and son of the late Arnold, Lord of Lustenges, has informed us that although we had previously, at the request of our venerable brothers, the archbishops of Cologne and Trier, and our beloved nobleman, the Count of Salm, instructed you by our letters to have him received as a canon and brother in one of the churches of the province of Trier by our authority, and to provide him with a prebend as soon as an opportunity presented itself, he has not benefited from the grace granted in this matter. Desiring to bring this to fruition and to extend it to the church of Metz at the request of the same archbishops, we command you to have him received by yourself or another by our authority as a canon and brother in the church of Metz or another church, and to provide him with a prebend as soon as possible according to the content of the aforementioned letters — notwithstanding a certain number of canons of that church, an oath or confirmation by the Apostolic See or any other firmness supported, or if we or legates of the same See have already directed letters there for others, which we do not wish to be hindered, nor if it has been granted to the dean and chapter of that church by the same See that they cannot be interdicted, suspended, or excommunicated by apostolic letters, or that they may not be required to receive or provide for anyone, and the indulgence said to have been granted to our venerable brother, the bishop of Metz, that in said church and other churches and monasteries of his city and diocese, by any apostolic letters or those of legates of the aforementioned See concerning pensions, dignities, personates, offices, prebends, and other ecclesiastical benefices, whether they have the care of souls or not, even if it is stated in those apostolic letters that any apostolic indulgence should not hinder the petitioners of those letters, may not be provided unless full and express mention is made of such indulgence and the number of received canons in that church in the same apostolic letters, or any other indulgence of ours or those legates, by which such grace may be impeded or deferred and which must be fully and expressly mentioned in our letters —; contradictors etc. Given at Lyon, 30th August, in the eighth year of our pontificate.

Papa (nomen Papae specificatum non est) priori Prumiensi Treverensis diocesis mandat, ut Rigaudum clericum, filium quondam Arnoldi de Lustenges, auctoritate apostolica recipiat in canonicum et fratrem in ecclesia Metensi vel alia, ac de prebenda provideat, non obstantibus privilegiis et indulgentiis prioribus. To the abbess and convent of the monastery of Quindelingeburch of the order of Saint Augustine, belonging directly to the Roman Church, in the diocese of Halberstadt. We might perhaps have taken vengeance on you for such presumption, if the kindness of the Apostolic See and our beloved son, the provost of Mainz, who interceded for you not insignificantly, had not tempered our resolve, for you should not be ignorant in any way that where any scruple or doubt arises in the privileges of the Roman See, that ambiguity is to be explained by none other than the Roman pontiff. Therefore, lest any further doubt might arise over that word, we wish from now on for a mark of pure silver to be understood as a pound, more kindly granting to you and those who succeed you that you pay no more than a mark of refined silver by the Cologne weight annually, provided that you do not presume to withhold the tribute of a single mark beyond the fixed term from now on. Innocentius IV papa abbatisse et conventui monasterii de Quindelingeburch ordinis sancti Augustini, ad Romanam ecclesiam pertinentis, confirmat privilegium a Lucio III papa concessum, ut marcam puri argenti annuatim solvant loco libre, sicut in privilegiis exprimitur. 1250, Nov. 26, Lugduni.

Letter of the King of Castile to the Lord Pope. To the most holy father and lord Gregory, by divine providence, the supreme pontiff of the Holy Roman Church, Ferdinand, by the grace of God, King of Castile, Toledo, León, Galicia, and Córdoba, with due service, kisses the blessed feet. He who knows all, the scrutinizer of hearts and knower of secrets, knows that with sincere desire of heart, no less devotedly than dutifully, our heart yearns for your honor and aspires to your exaltation. It is no wonder that, following the footsteps of our ancestors, we desire to the best of our ability the increase and glory of the apostolic see, which, as the vicar of Jesus Christ on earth and the representative of the true God, abundantly distributes and wisely administers the most sacred nourishment of faith to all the faithful throughout the world. Through this, we and all the faithful of Christ, both kings and others, believe and desire the growth of heavenly hope to be offered to us; for this faith, we fight and stand against its enemies, uprooting heresies and physically opposing ourselves to the assaults and conflicts of other enemies who strive to defend their errors with arms, not without grave danger. Therefore, we deem it worthy, for the name of Christ, to endure these and many other harsher things, which we have not committed to writing both because it would be long and superfluous to recount and also lest we seem to seek our own praise, so that the cord of the Lord's inheritance may be extended and the honor of our holy mother the apostolic see, through our ministry, may receive some increase, even if not what is hoped or due. For if we sincerely love the sacred Roman Church, which has always loved and cherished us in the bowels of charity, and not only when asked but also eagerly showed itself propitious towards our promotion with the abundance of special favors, we do not believe we have a reward, but indeed we consider it slight if we assist it in its needs and expose both our person and realms to any dangers for it. Indeed, we have learned from the report of many, later demonstrated to us by a papal letter, that the emperor has gravely offended the Holy Roman Church, which nourished him with care and miraculously exalted him, provoking it to such wrath that it was necessary for him to be touched by the hand of the Lord. Can a pious mother suffer, and the son not sympathize? Does the apostolic see grieve, and can the faithful rejoice? Are the limbs known to thrive when the head is disturbed? However, since the Lord does not forget to show mercy nor will he restrain mercy in his wrath, having once begun, we will speak a little to the Lord, not more anxious about uncertain outcomes of affairs than about the deed of the emperor, whom we are bound to love in many ways as much as we can with God's help, having first obtained pardon and granted permission, so that the gentleness of the father may recover the penitent son and the church not lack its champion, we would take care to intercede. To execute this more appropriately, we have recalled the venerable and beloved W., abbot of San Facundo, a man of prudent foresight and honesty, in whom we fully confide due to his prerogative of integrity, who, while on his way to visit the Roman church, was dispatched by us to you for this and other matters, so that, assured of his honesty and industry, you may confidently send him to the emperor on our behalf, if you see fit, or even return him to us with your benevolent consent in all things. For he will faithfully and devoutly execute whatever is enjoined upon him by your holiness, as we know and have already experienced in many instances. Given at Burgos, the fourth day of December, in the year of our reign.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa abbatem V. Sancti Facundi delegat ut intercedat apud imperatorem pro reconciliatione cum ecclesia Romana, auctoritate Ferdinandi regis Castellae. Datum Burgis, 4 Decembris, regni anno.

To the Duchess of Austria. The monuments of your ancestors suggest that you should honor the worship of sacred rites with sincere faith towards God and His church, and we rejoice in the Lord, as we have heard that you do not fall short of your parents' greatness but rather imitate them with commendable similarity in conduct. **Translation to English:**

To the noble man Hartmann, son of the noble man L., count of Froburg. A petition presented on your behalf contained that when the noble man H., the younger count of Kiburg, related to you in the third degree of consanguinity, had previously married Anna, the daughter of the noble man, the count of Rapreswil, there was no consummation, and later, due to the fact that the same count of Kiburg had previously contracted espousals with Anna's maternal aunt through words of future consent, a divorce was celebrated between them by the authority of the Apostolic See. Subsequently, learning that you desired Anna to be joined to you in matrimonial union, which was hindered due to the public honesty justice that arose from her previous betrothal to your relative, the count of Kiburg, we directed our letters to our venerable brother, the bishop of Albano, then the legate of the Apostolic See in those parts, containing, among other things, that if he saw it to be expedient for the church's business, he should grant you the freedom to contract with Anna by our authority, if it could be done without scandal, with the consent of our dearest son in Christ, W., the illustrious king of the Romans. Since our beloved son, the elected bishop of Speyer, proceeding in this matter by the authority of the legate, as he had received it in command, and understanding through trustworthy sources that no scandal would arise from your union with Anna and that great benefit could come to the church from it, with the advice and consent of the said king, granted you permission to freely contract with the aforementioned Anna, notwithstanding the impediment: you have humbly requested for this to be confirmed by the Apostolic See. Inclined by your supplications and those of our beloved son, the noble man L., count of Froburg, your father, whose devotion to the Roman church has been experienced in many ways, we accept and approve what was done by the aforementioned bishop and elect in this matter and confirm it by apostolic authority and fortify it with the protection of this present writing. No one, therefore, etc., of our confirmation, etc. Given at Lyon, the fifth day before the Kalends of February, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Hartmanno nobili viro, filio comitis de Froburg, confirmat quod episcopus Albanensis, legatus, et electus Spirensis, auctoritate legati, ei concesserit ut cum Anna filia comitis de Rapreswiler contraheret, impedimento non obstante, ex consilio et assensu regis Romanorum. 1235, Jan. 28, Lugduni.

### Translation to English:

To the Archbishop of Cologne. It is not beyond the hope which we have conceived of your brotherly sincerity, even though it has brought us new material for rejoicing, as our dearest son in Christ, W., the illustrious King of the Romans, has taken care to inform us and our venerable brother, the Bishop of Albano, has recounted to us in person, that you have shown such diligence in this year in the affair of the Church and the same king, proving yourself a faithful zealot of the same matter, for which we commend your diligence with worthy praises and thanks. Indeed, while it is redundant to goad the diligent and awaken the vigilant, since the former Emperor Frederick has been taken from the midst of this present life, an ease of affairs has thereby arisen which promotes the pursuit of said matter to its effect, we command that, with the Lord's help, you do not allow the opportunity thus provided to pass uselessly, but strive to cooperate with the occurrences of success that converge by divine disposition, assisting the said king as a fosterling of your promotion with tireless diligence, so that the same king may recognize you as his chief supporter, and the apostolic see may attribute to your titles the increase of future prosperity, and henceforth hold you more intimately in the bowels of charity, committing the service of your devotion on this matter to the book of unfailing memory. We further desire and command that, putting aside all excuses, you endeavor to come to us in person, to discuss usefully with us, God willing, concerning the above and other matters. Given as above.

### Regesto in Latin:

**Gregorius IX papa** archiepiscopo Coloniensi mandat, ut in negotio ecclesiae et regis Romanorum diligentiam suam prosequatur, occasione sublata per mortem Friderici quondam imperatoris, et ad sedem apostolicam personaliter veniat. — 1227, Dat. ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the illustrious King Béla of Hungary. We have heard a voice of lamentation and weeping on high, and we, embittered by many sorrows, lament that the judgment cast from heaven is now ravaging the Christian people everywhere, that the sword of the faithful is turned back upon the faithful in mutual slaughter, and that the pagan sword is cruelly raging against the followers of Christ. For the multiplied cry of the human race's crimes has ascended to the ears of the Creator of all, compelling Him, who has thus far remained silent as if not seeing, who has patiently awaited the correction of His people, to unsheathe the sword as an avenger of iniquities and to cleanse from His eyes the abominations of sins by demanding severe vengeance from the sinners. Therefore, it is necessary for all whose hearts the fear of the Lord has touched, covered in sackcloth and sprinkled with ashes, to implore divine mercy in sighs and tears so that He, who has always been abundant in forgiveness, who has accustomed Himself to be steadfast beyond all malice, may command the unsheathed sword to return to its scabbard and, pouring out His wrath on the nations that do not know Him, deign to have mercy on the people marked with the sign of His Son. Yet we hope that even if our God has begun to rebuke us with harsh reproof, He does not intend to destroy the kingdoms that invoke His name from His presence, but rather cares to rescue sinners from perpetual punishment, providing the benefit of temporal vengeance for the chastisement of our race, for even if the trial of death sometimes touched the children of Israel in the desert, the wrath of the Lord did not remain on them for long. However, even though we are gravely troubled by the oppression of all the faithful, over the affliction of the kingdom of Hungary, which we have learned with great effusion of tears from your letters was invaded and occupied to a great extent by the Tartars, our heart is filled with especially greater sadness because we have found in it signs of purer devotion to God and the apostolic see, as we have known your ancestors of blessed memory and your royal excellence to be more prompt in executing the church's good will. Therefore, placing firm hope in Him who, although He granted free entry to King Sennacherib of Assyria into the land of Israel, was moved by the contrition of Hezekiah and destroyed the multitude of adversaries in one night, we earnestly admonish and exhort your serenity and beseech you in the Lord Jesus Christ, that by trusting in Him, who saves the humble people and humbles the arrogant eye, you may gird yourself powerfully and manfully for the defense of the aforesaid kingdom and the Catholic faith, which is known to be particularly attacked by these Tartars, and take care to act all the more studiously and fervently in their expulsion, as you recognize that you are thereby promoting the exaltation of your name and honor more strongly. For we will take care to provide you and the aforesaid kingdom, to whom we cannot and should not fail in such a grave necessity, with effective help and counsel, the Lord granting it, and receiving your person and family under the protection of the apostolic see and ours, we grant to you and to all who, having assumed the sign of the cross, shall advance against these Tartars for the defense of the aforesaid kingdom the same immunity and indulgence that is granted to those aiding the Holy Land in general council. Given at the Lateran, the sixteenth day before the Kalends of July, in the fifteenth year [of our pontificate]. In the same manner to the illustrious King Coloman and Duke of Slavonia.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Bele regi Ungarie mandat ut contra Tartaros ad defensionem regni et fidei catholicae se viriliter accingat, promittitque subsidium apostolicae sedis et indulgentias similes succurrentibus Terrae Sanctae. Datum Laterani, XVI Kalendas Iulii, anno XV.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Rouen and his suffragans. The Apostolic See, as almost the whole world has learned from the evident facts, has treated Frederick, called the emperor, with maternal affection ever since it received him from his mother's womb, nurturing him with its milk and carrying him upon its shoulders. It adopted him when he was almost entirely bereft of aid and left to doubtful outcomes, defending him from the invaders of his kingdom who had cast their greedy eyes upon his lands and entered them without any obstacle of defense, and protecting him from those laying in wait for his life who, envious of his safety, tried to snuff out his spirit and erase his memory from the earth. Although fortified by the shield of ecclesiastical protection and with the cardinal Gregory of Gualganoa of the title of St. Anastasia from the Apostolic See appointed as a guardian over his person and realm for many years, he reached the threshold of maturity, and through its support, he was eventually elevated to the highest dignity. However, the diligence extended towards him, and the many toils the Church endured for his sake seem to have been lost on him, as he is ungrateful for such benefits and fails to acknowledge the good received. 

Indeed, while any offense may cause the sting of pain, it is especially grievous when ingratitude is returned for favor, and evil is repaid for good. Regardless of how much the Apostolic See has loved him and elevated him to the supreme peak of secular power, due to his offenses, for which he has been repeatedly admonished to make satisfaction to no avail, we have been compelled, though unwillingly, to act against him. For even though Adam was exalted by divine providence to a position of dignity and authority, being given dominion over all creatures of the earth, because he transgressed God's command, he received no exemption from punishment. We wish not to leave you in ignorance of what reward of retribution the Church has received from the said Frederick for the many benefits conferred upon him, hence we declare a few things among many in this present page.

In the City, he incited a grave sedition, striving with all his might to exclude us and our brothers from there, thereby seeking to demean the honor of the Apostolic See and utterly trample upon its liberty, contrary to the oaths he had taken. And when we desired to send our venerable brother, the Bishop of Palestrina, to the parts of the Albigenses to strengthen the Catholic faith there, he ordered him to be impeded on his way by some of his faithful. 

Furthermore, he does not permit the vacant cathedrals and other churches in his kingdom to be filled, to the peril of souls and their great detriment, stripping them and certain others almost entirely of their goods, and imposing undue taxes and exactions upon the prelates, religious, and other secular clergy. Also, with the nobles, poor, orphans, and widows driven to extreme destitution, his collectors' hardness and cruelty scarcely allow them to breathe. Thus, almost the whole kingdom, which is the special patrimony of blessed Peter, for which he is bound by an oath of fealty to the Apostolic See and is its liege vassal, he has reduced, as much as he could, to ashes and ruins. If, after we have admonished him, he does not correct this, we will proceed against him with the Lord as our guide as we see fit.

Moreover, he impedes the business of the Holy Land and also of the Roman Empire. Furthermore, during the time of concord established between him and the Church, he swore in the hands of the apostolic legates to obey the Church's commands. However, he scorned to fulfill the mandate received from them, not to seize, occupy, or devastate the lands of the Church or those he then held in his hands or their persons, by occupying the Church's land in Lombardy, Ferrara, Bondeno, Pegognaga, and Bondeno, seizing the land of Sardinia and the Massa of the diocese of Luni, ejecting those whom the Church had reserved for its hands, and devastating their lands. Although the legates then pronounced a sentence of excommunication upon him if he did not do as they commanded, the same held captive in prison the nephew of the king of Tunis, who had come to the Roman Church to receive the sacred baptism, and the beloved son Peter, a noble Saracen Roman citizen, sent to the apostolic see on behalf of our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious king of England, and his son.

Since he was often admonished by us concerning these and many other excesses without feeling the remedy of correction, as the sores of his sins are hardened, daring to commit more grievous offenses daily, we, unable to overlook these matters without offense to Christ, have decreed, with the counsel

**Translation to English:**

To William of Gado, knight of the diocese of Grenoble. Since, as we have heard, a serious discord had arisen between you and Yscardus of Claix, a knight of the diocese of Grenoble, and in order to finally settle this discord, you promised, under oath, to give your daughter Margaret to Yscardus, the son of the same Yscardus, as a wife. But since they are related in the fourth degree of consanguinity, you have requested the grace of the Apostolic See in this matter. Therefore, inclined by your requests and those of our beloved son, the nobleman Rudolf, son of the noble Count of Geneva, who personally pleaded with us on this matter and is said to be your relative, we dispense by the authority of these presents with special grace that the aforementioned Margaret and Yscardus may marry, notwithstanding this impediment. Let no one therefore etc. Given at Lyon, on the 8th of the Ides of March, in the eighth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Willelmo de Gado militi Gratiopolitane diocesis concedit dispensationem specialem, ut Margarita filia eius et Yscardus de Clais, non obstante consanguinitatis impedimento, matrimonium contrahant. Datum Lugduni, VIII Idus Martii, anno octavo.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man, the senior steward of Alzei. We rejoice in the Lord for the laudable testimonies which we have gladly received about you, namely that in the sincerity of faith towards God you maintain the purity of Catholic devotion to His church. To make others participants in your merits by sharing in your goods, we earnestly ask and command your nobility to lead the noble man, the Duke of Bavaria, to the devotion of the church with diligent exhortations and to bring him back, aiming for both your progress and his. But if he hardens his heart against your wholesome advice, spurning divine judgment, withdraw your favor and distance yourself from the man who stubbornly turns away from God, knowing that those who forsake God for man have never prospered. Given at Lyon, on the Ides of February, in the eighth year.

To the noble man Louis, son of the Duke of Bavaria. If you wish to have successful progress and enjoy longevity on earth, learn to worship God in the sincerity of faith and to diligently honor His church with the service of devotion. Because, as the Psalm says, if you run without iniquity, you will be directed. Do not be led astray by false examples of others, for those who turn away from God have never succeeded in any endeavors. Listen therefore to our beloved son, brother Henry, our Penitentiary, and heed his sound advice. Given as above.

To the Duke of Bavaria. We have consented with gracious affection to your petition, which you have repeatedly urged upon us, so that the remedy of fitting counsel is not lacking for your salvation. We have decided to send to you our beloved son, brother Henry, our Penitentiary, to whom you should promptly assent, as he will discuss with you the remedy for your soul and the service of devotion that you owe to God and His church. Provide for him a secure conduct so that he may have safe access and retreat. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro dapifero seniori de Alzeia mandat ut ducem Bawarie ad devotionem ecclesiae inducat, et si renuit, auxilium suum subtrahat. Dat. Lugduni, Idibus Februarii, anno VIII.

**Translation to English:**

To the illustrious King of the Romans, W. Although, after the Lord, moved by the cries of His humble servants, willed to appoint you as His anointed to liberate His devoted children from the yoke of miserable servitude, the Apostolic See, your mother, has unceasingly and diligently watched over your progress with continuous meditation, as the clear testimonies of deeds have proven: now, however, we intend to support you with timely aids and favors for the greater promotion of your person and the happy completion of your state, as the divine right hand promotes the prosperous progress of the church and empire, a matter which had previously languished despite the fervent efforts of many. Therefore, dearest son, we exhort your serenity in the Lord: work diligently on your behalf and collaborate with the exalted right hand, promote the faithful in the task, strive with due wisdom to bring the unfaithful back to faith, from which you will more gloriously proceed to the diadem of the Roman Empire, with which we aspire with all our heart to adorn you by God's grace. Nor should your royal excellence lend an ear to the deceitful speeches of some, who might perhaps suggest contrary things to you and attempt to mix some poison of the old serpent's cunning with your sincere affections, diminishing or weakening the charity you have for the Roman Church and with which it sincerely embraces you, and rendering your magnificence negligent in pursuing the imminent matter. Guard your heart with all diligence against such individuals, and hedge your ears with thorns against flattering whispers, always striving to grow in devotion to the Church, which has purely loved and loves you, and with motherly affection does not cease to love you, will soon, with God's favor and life's companion, elevate you to the crown of the Empire. Given at Lyon, on the 15th Kalends of March, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa illustri regi Romanorum W. hortatur, ut Ecclesiae devotione crescat et ad Romani imperii diadema perveniat, monens ne praviloquiis credat. Datum Lugduni, XV Kalendas Martii, anno pontificatus octavo.

**Translation to English:**

A part of the letter has been described, which, although it matters little to him, yet since it has not been printed elsewhere, we thought it should be added. Potthast, Reg. 10974. To the Archbishop of Lund and his suffragans. Man, created in the likeness of God and made in His image, when he was in honor and could see the invisible things of God understood through the things that were made, His eternal power and divinity, so that he would have no excuse: because he did not understand, he was compared to the senseless beasts, and became like them, and his foolish heart was darkened, changing the glory of the incorruptible God into the likeness of the image of corruptible man and birds, quadrupeds, and serpents, he chose to serve the creature rather than the Creator. And although Almighty God, lest he perish entirely whom He had exalted above other creatures with the privilege of dignity, rising up for the misery of the needy and the sighing of the poor, set forth Jesus Christ as a propitiation through faith in His blood for the remission of past sins, yet the prince of this world has so blinded the minds of some unbelievers that the illumination of the gospel cannot shine upon them, but still, wrapped in the darkness of unbelief, they not only refuse to call upon the Lord, who is near to all who call upon Him in truth, for whoever calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved, but also, just as formerly the son according to the flesh, born of the bondwoman, persecuted him who was born according to the spirit of the free woman among the children of Abraham, so now the children of Hagar, that is, the unbelieving people, who still walk in darkness and have not yet merited to see the great light, do not cease to persecute us, who are no longer children of the bondwoman but of the free woman, by which freedom Christ has set us free, who have thus become vain in their thoughts, that they refuse to acknowledge Him who came to break the yoke of their captivity as their redeemer, He Himself tolerating them by the counsel of His ineffable providence, so that either they may return to Him, more happily using the freedom of will, or, at last, may have no just complaints against Him, having been so long mercifully awaited, and also that they may exist for the faithful as an exercise of virtue, obtaining from there the fruit of their labors which does not perish. Since those who in the parts of Estonia are converted by God's grace to the faith of the Christian name are greatly harassed by the surrounding barbarians and therefore ask to be aided by the faithful of Christ: we admonish and exhort your brotherhood in the Lord and enjoin upon you for the remission of your sins, that you should attentively and effectively exhort and induce the peoples subject to you, that hastening to the reward of such great happiness and placing the sword on the thigh with Moses, they may run against these idolatrous nations and murmuring people in the splendor of the Lord's arms, girded for the battle of Him who promises a crown to those who strive lawfully. For we, relying on the mercy of Almighty God and the authority of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul, grant to all truly penitent and confessed, both those in your dioceses who, having taken the cross for the aid of the Holy Land, wish to commute their vows to this kind of assistance, and others of the same dioceses who shall go against the enemies of our faith to those parts, staying there at least for a year in this service of Jesus Christ, the indulgence which is granted to those going to the aid of the Holy Land. Given at the Lateran, December 14, in the fourteenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Lundensi et suffraganeis suis mandat ut subiectos populos inducant ad defendendos conversos in partibus Estonie a barbaris. Indulgentiam concedit pro huiusmodi conferentes. 1239, Dec. 14. Latere.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Paris. By the authority of these presents, we grant you the power to, having heard the confession of our dearest daughter in Christ, B., the illustrious Queen of France, regarding her having written to the late Emperor F. as if he were the Emperor after the sentence of deposition had been passed against him, and having received letters from him, and concerning her other sins, to grant her, in our stead, the benefit of absolution as often as necessary, and to impose upon her a salutary penance. Given at Lyon, 9th Kalends of April, in the eighth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Parisiensi concedit ut reginam Franciae B. absolvat et penitentiam iniungat pro litteris ad F. imperatorem post depositionis sententiam missis. 1251, Mart. 24, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the scholastic of the church of Saint Andrew of Cologne. William, a canon of the church of Saint John of Utrecht, has presented a petition to us. He showed that, when we decided to grant indulgence to clerics who had adhered to the former emperor Frederick against the people of Aachen, allowing them to receive the revenues of their benefices during their absence for a period of three years, a certain John called Xancis, also a canon of that church, took the cross against the people of Aachen. However, he did not participate in the expedition against them but redeemed his vow for a certain sum of money, not exceeding the value of three Tours pounds. Under the pretext of this concession, the heirs of this John are unjustly claiming the revenues of the prebend which he held in the said church and which has been canonically assigned to the said William, to William's prejudice and detriment. Therefore, he has humbly petitioned us to provide paternal provision for him in this matter. We command you to summon those who need to be summoned, etc., until the matter is observed. Witnesses etc. Given at Lyon, the fifth day before the Kalends of March, in the eighth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa scholastico ecclesiae sancti Andreae Coloniensis mandat ut vocatis evocandis litem dirimat super iure proventuum praebendae inter Willelmum canonicum Traiectensem et heredes quondam Iohannis Xancis, qui crucem suscepit sed votum redemit. 1234, Febr. 25. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble men Pepon and Nepoleon, viscounts of Campilio?, devoted to the Roman Church, of the diocese of Chiusi. Sometimes, by the heavenly disposition of counsel, it is provided that scandals arise in the kingdom of the church so that those who are tested may become manifest to the reprobates who have been reproved, because, just as the undevoted and reprobate receive due punishment, so the devoted and chosen obtain worthy rewards, with different rewards to each according to their merits. Therefore, although it has been proposed to us on your behalf that you, as devout to the Roman Church, strive magnanimously for its defense against its persecutors and enemies, for which we rejoice in the Lord and commend the fervor of your devotion with worthy praise and thanks, so that, encouraged by apostolic exhortations and fortified by the protection of the church, you may the more readily and effectively endeavor to assist the church in its necessity, where true friends are known, and so that it may be known to you more certainly that by this you will earn grace in the present and glory in the future, we beseech, admonish, and exhort your nobility in the Lord, enjoining you for the remission of your sins, that, strengthened by the spirit of courage and receiving the fortifications of a steadfast mind, you may persist immovably in the faith and devotion of the church, your mother. For we receive your persons, remaining in the devotion of this church, with your family and all goods which you reasonably possess at present, under the protection of blessed Peter and us, and we strengthen you with the patronage of this written document, wanting you to hold it for certain that the church will make no peace or truce with its enemies unless it expressly includes you in them, provided there is someone on your part who requests this. For your greater security, we have deemed it right to grant you these letters as testimony. Therefore, let no one infringe our protection. Given at Lyons, on the seventh Ides of December, in the eighth year [of our pontificate]. In the same manner to the noble men Bulgarello, Pepon, Rembotto, and Manenti, brothers, sons of the late Tancred, and to Raynaldo and Bernardino, brothers, sons of the late Rembotto, counts of Sarciano, devoted to the Roman Church, of the diocese of Chiusi. In the same manner to the noble men Cacciacomito and Radulf Ildebrandin and Comito, his sons, devoted to the Roman Church, of the dioceses of Siena and Arezzo.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobilibus viris Peponi et Nepoleoni vicecomitibus de Campilio, Clusine diocesis, scribit, eos commendans pro defensione ecclesiae Romanae contra persecutores et inimicos, eosque sub protectione beati Petri et sua recipit, promittens nullam pacem cum hostibus sine eorum inclusionem fieri. 1234, Dec. 7, Lugduni.

To whomsoever each part of the verses is cut. The words that are missing have been supplied in brackets from S. Priest, Hist. de la conqu. de Naples by Charles d’Anjou, vol. IV, appendix p. 254, who published a letter of the same tenor addressed to the authorities and people of Siena on the 30th of August in the second year from the Florentine Archive, no. 914, but erroneously attributed it to Pope Gregory X (Potthast, Reg. 8254). — We propose the letter anew, because this form, as it appears from the address to your brotherhood, is directed to the bishops.
