To the podestà, council, and community of Viterbo. It is not indicative of weakness in a fair arbiter of evils to be lenient, but rather commendable charity that prudently addresses the great maladies of illness, whenever, with the worthy fruit of repentance redeeming the sin, around those who, having turned from impiety, cease to be what they once were, mercy exalts over judgment, restraining the zeal of discipline. Indeed, though against those who, having broken the bond of faith with which they were bound to the Apostolic See, wickedly joined the persecutors of the Church in the present turmoil, we intend to be so severe in punishment that no leniency of indulgence from our merciful heart should proceed to them, which would give future generations confidence in similar impunity or an incentive to sin: it has been seen as useful and necessary for the peaceful reformation of your city and its common benefits that, to strengthen the good of peace, which, according to the desire of our heart and the paternal affection of our intention, the Lord has brought about between you and your fellow citizens, who were until now exiles, separated from the city's community by the malice of an enemy, the rigor that apostolic justice had extended against stubborn resistance should be softened by the counsel of piety. In this we indeed imitate the example of Him whose place we unworthily hold on earth, not only blamelessly but also commendably, who, over the evil of punishment which He justly considers to be inflicted on sinners, changes the severity of punishment to the clemency of mercy if they humbly reflect on repentance for the evil of their sin. We, therefore, firmly hoping that your members, which you once showed as weapons of iniquity to sin, will henceforth be shown as weapons of justice through the constancy of faith and fidelity to the Roman Church, your mother, and preferring rather to suffer the accusations of many from mercy, through which your reintegration is advised, than to exhibit the constancy of severity, which would instill terror in endeavors and bring about a pernicious example of impunity, sometimes paving the way for committed excesses: behold, we have gladly received you with open arms, returning filially to the Church's communion, and in your recollection, we open wide the bosom of paternal grace, knowing not to close to those humbly returning. So that where sin is known to have abounded, grace may abound much more, and the renewed devotion of sons may rejoice, and as a perpetual indication of excellent charity, the humble conversion to the father may find the forgiveness of many sins with him, inclined by your supplications, retaining almost all the simplicity and integrity of the words in which your petitions were conceived and put into authentic writings for your motion, recited in our hearing and that of our brothers, we do not wish that the crimes or indignation you committed against the Roman Church in past times should be retained as blame or indignation, we grant, remit and release to you collectively and individually to each one all and singular offenses, faults, penalties, and injuries, and whatsoever other crimes or offenses, presumed by word or deed until today from times past against us or the Roman Church or its cardinals or anyone from our court or family, or even any university or special persons then adhering to the Church by the community of Viterbo or by any or some Viterbans in any manner or cause or occasion of discord held formerly between the Church and the late Emperor Frederick, because you joined Frederick or his envoys against the Church, and all damages and penalties, which you incurred collectively or individually due to the foregoing or anything of the foregoing. To this end, all and singular sentences and commands, processes and all contracts, held or celebrated in Viterbo or anywhere by the Viterbans so far, we wish to obtain full force, so that they cannot be annulled or invalidated by reason of the excommunication under which you were then held. The possession or holding which Peter Bonus and his sons currently possess in the property of Fracta and all its appurtenances, as well as the holding or possession which the sons of the late Roland Peter Alexander have of the house, palace or tower, which are located in the district of Saint Peregrinus next to the public road and water stream, are to be preserved for them entire and unharmed, without prejudice, however, to the right of ownership of anyone wishing to assert their action against the possessors on these matters. All customs, usages, and liberties of the community of Viterbo and any citizen of Viterbo we wish to be preserved entire. We further will and command regarding the officials of the commune, judges, and all and singular officials of the same, that each in their offices shall continue until the completion of their term, and of the aforementioned officials, the commune of Viterbo may freely dispose of the office in the future

To the Archbishop of Mainz. Compassionately considering the burden of debt on the Church of Mainz, as we have learned from your communication, we grant you by the authority of these presents that you shall not be held responsible for the payment of the debts of the said church, unless it is proven that they have been converted to the benefit of the mentioned church, notwithstanding any contractual letters, renunciations, confessions, or even oaths. To the abbot of the monastery of Farfa, which belongs directly to the Roman Church, without intermediaries. Since, according to canonical sanctions, retribution is sometimes extended not only to the perpetrators of crimes but also to the progeny of the condemned, we strictly prohibit you and your successors by the authority of these presents, from admitting any of the offspring of those monks who fortified themselves against you and your monastery in its castles, as well as those who received wages from the enemies of the Roman Church, into the monks or familiars of the said monastery henceforth. Given at the Lateran, on the 5th day before the Kalends of December, in the 11th year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

To the Archbishop of Milan. Gregorius IX papa mandat officiali, ut dispenset cum Iohanne marchione Brandeburgensi et Theoderico marchionis Misnensis filio super matrimonio impedimentum consanguinitatis quarta linea contrahente. 1236, Mai. 2. Assisii.

**Translation to English:**

To the men of the village of Pingu in the diocese of Mainz. Since, as was put forward on your behalf before us, you cannot leave your village without danger to your persons due to the disturbance of the current time, we, moved by the supplication of our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Mainz, on your behalf, wishing to grant you favor, by the authority of these presents, grant that, in the face of such danger, none of you can be summoned to judgment outside of the village by letters of the Apostolic See or its legates, without a special mandate from the said See, making full mention of this indulgence. Therefore, let no one infringe on our concession, etc. Given at Perugia, the 6th day before the Ides of September, in the tenth year [of our pontificate]. The dean and the scholasticus of St. Peter of Mainz have been appointed as conservators for this matter.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa hominibus ville Pinguensis Maguntine diocesis indulget, ne, imminente periculo, ad iudicium extra villam trahi possint sine mandato speciali sedis apostolice. 1236, Sept. 6, Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To the archpriest of Mantua. To prevent individuals who adhere to the persecutors of the Church from being appointed to prelatures or any dignities or ecclesiastical benefices in the city or diocese of Verona, especially through deceitful means, we declare null and void any elections, postulations, provisions, and collations of prelatures, dignities, and benefices, both secular and regular, of the churches of the aforementioned city and diocese, made by those who adhered to the late Emperor F., who was bound by the chain of excommunication due to the present discord. We also declare void any future appointments undertaken by them, as long as they support E. de Romano, even if perhaps confirmed by the patriarch of Aquileia of blessed memory or the bishop of Verona. We command you to publicly announce this wherever you deem it expedient. Given at the Lateran, November 8, in the eleventh year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archipresbytero Mantuano mandat, ut electiones, postulationes, provisiones, et collationes beneficiorum ecclesiae in civitate et dioecesi Veronensi per eos, qui excommunicato imperatori F. et E. de Romano favent, factas, cassas et irritas denunciet. 1237, Nov. 8. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble Duke and the commune of the Venetians. Although, as we have learned from your reports, our venerable brother, the Bishop of Tusculum, legate of the Apostolic See, has decreed under penalty of excommunication that goods are not to be carried by Christians to the Saracens who inhabit eastern regions, because, however, as you assert, this causes no prejudice to anyone and results in not a little inconvenience to you, we, considering the purity of faith and the sincere devotion with which you render yourselves worthy of the special grace and favor of the Apostolic See, by the authority of these presents grant you permission, notwithstanding such prohibition, to send or convey your ships with goods to these parts until it pleases our will, without meanwhile incurring the sentence of excommunication, if the said bishop has pronounced any for this reason, provided you do not carry prohibited items to the enemies of the faith. Given at Assisi, June 7, in the tenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro duci et communi Venetorum concedit, ut non obstante prohibitione sub pena excommunicationis edita a Tusculano episcopo, naves cum mercimoniis ad partes orientales Saracenorum transmittere possint, dummodo res vetitas inimicis fidei non portetis. 1236, Iun. 7. Datum Assisii.

**Translation to English:**

To the provost and chapter of the church of Castellane, of the order of Saint Augustine. A petition presented to us on your behalf stated that the late Otto IV, Emperor of the Romans, in the first year of his reign, among other immunities and liberties with which he fortified you and your church by imperial authority, specifically granted to your church that no prescription of time unless it be a hundred years could be opposed against it, as we have seen fully contained in the privilege of that emperor, sealed with his own seal. Therefore, inclined by the prayers of your devotion, we, holding this grant of the hundred-year prescription, valid only against laypersons, as approved and acceptable, confirm it with apostolic authority, etc., up to: we fortify. Therefore, let no one — our confirmation, etc. Given at Perugia, on the 7th of the Ides of December, in the 10th year. An archpriest from Cortona, of the Arezzo diocese, is appointed as their conservator for this matter.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa preposito et capitulo ecclesie Castellane ordinis sancti Augustini significat se, petitionibus eorum inclinatus, concessionem Ottonis IV imperatoris de prescriptione centenaria contra laicos valituram auctoritate apostolica confirmasse. Datum Perusii, VII Idus Decembris, pontificatus nostri anno decimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man, the podestà, and the community of the castle of Montefusco in the diocese of Benevento. As we have understood, Conrad, the son of the late Emperor of the Romans, a manifest persecutor of the Church, is assailing you with hostile attacks while you persist in your devotion to the apostolic see, and he has resolved with all his might to proceed to the depopulation of your territory. Therefore, it is necessary for you to fight bravely against him and his supporters for the defense of your liberty and the preservation of fidelity to the Roman Church. We, in order that you may be strengthened with more resolute spirits to resist him, and that others may arm themselves with a more secure purpose, from the grace of Mother Church, provide healthier support in this matter, grant to you and to all who offer appropriate assistance in this, full indulgence for all sins, of which you have been contrite in heart and confessed with your mouth. Given at Assisi, the 11th of May, in the tenth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro potestati et communi castri de Montefusco mandat, ut contra Conradum, persecutorem ecclesiae, pro defensione libertatis et fidelitatis Romanae ecclesiae viriliter dimicent, plenam indulgentiam concedens. 1237, Mai. 11. Asisii.

**Translation to English:**

To the community of people of Rocca de Foce, in the diocese of Fermo. When a request is made to us, etc., to its effect. Your petition, indeed, presented to us, stated that the late R., cardinal deacon of Santa Maria in Cosmedin, then legate of the apostolic see, considering the sincere devotion you bear to the Roman Church and the dangers and damages you incurred by resisting the envoys of the late Emperor Frederick, took you under the protection of this same see. He granted you the right to form a commune and enjoy the same rights and liberties as those enjoyed by other communes of castles and places in the March of Ancona, who persist in devotion and fidelity to the Roman Church, as is more fully contained in the letters drawn up about this matter. Therefore, inclined by your supplications, we acknowledge and approve what the cardinal has providently done regarding this matter, confirming it with apostolic authority, etc., to our protection. Therefore, let no one—our confirmation, etc. Given at Assisi, on the 26th of May, in the tenth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa universitati hominum Rocce de Foce Firmane diocesis, acta a R. cardinali de Sancta Maria in Cosmidin, quondam legato apostolico, qui eos sub protectione sedis apostolicae suscepit et iura communantia concessit, auctoritate apostolica confirmat. 1236, Mai. 26. Assisii.

**Translation to English:**

To the Abbot of Saint Drupert, Diocese of Constance. Considering that when the head suffers, the members share in its suffering, we deem it proper and fitting that subordinates should aid their superiors in times of necessity. Therefore, since our beloved son, the abbot of the monastery of Reichenau, of the Order of Saint Benedict in the Diocese of Constance, which pertains directly to the Roman Church, has informed us that the monastery is heavily burdened with debts due to the dangers of wars, we, sharing his distress with paternal affection as is appropriate, command you to compel, by means of ecclesiastical censure, all those who hold offices or obediences of the said monastery, to provide, from their own resources, suitable yet moderate assistance for the alleviation of these debts, after due warning and with no allowance for appeal, notwithstanding if they or some of them etc. as above. Given at Assisi, the fourth of the Nones of September, in the eleventh year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati Sancti Druperti Constantiensis diocesis mandat ut omnes, qui officia vel obedientias monasterii Augensis obtinent, ad exonerationem debitorum subsidiis moderatis ab eorum facultatibus provideant per censuram ecclesiasticam, appellatione remota. Datum Asisii, IIII Nonas Septembris, anno pontificatus eius undecimo.

**Translation to English:**

To H., Cardinal Priest of the title of St. Sabina, legate of the Apostolic See. Although the union of the conjugal bond in the fourth degree of consanguinity or affinity is forbidden by sacred canons, the Roman Church, however, sometimes wisely dispenses from them, especially when urgent necessity or evident utility demands it. Therefore, since, as was proposed before us on your behalf, the noble men Henry, Count of Luxembourg of the Treverensis diocese, and Gerard, his brother, Lord of Dolbois of the Liege diocese, have shown themselves obedient and devoted to you in the affairs of the Church, we, intending to pursue them with grace and favor on this account, command that you, having received from that same Gerard a fitting guarantee of adherence to the Church and to our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, W., may freely dispense, by our authority, for him and the noble woman Mahadi, his future wife—notwithstanding the fourth degree of consanguinity by which they are related to each other—to remain in contracted marriage, as you see fit. Given at Assisi, the Kalends of July, in the eleventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Henrico tituli Sancte Sabine presbytero cardinali, apostolicae sedis legato mandat, ut Girardo de Dolboi et Mahadi uxori eius, non obstante quarta consanguinitatis linea, auctoritate sua in matrimonio remanere libere valeant dispenset. Datum Assisii, Kalendis Iulii, anno undecimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Albano, legate of the Apostolic See.

Since the city of Anglona is said to be temporarily subject to our beloved son, the noble man John of Montefuscolo, we desire and by the authority of these presents, we command you to appoint a suitable person, acceptable to the same nobleman, as bishop and shepherd of the currently vacant church of Anglona. You are to ensure that the chapter and the subjects of this church show due obedience and reverence to him as the father and shepherd of their souls. Any contradictors are to be disregarded, notwithstanding if it has been granted to some persons by the apostolic see that they cannot be interdicted, excommunicated, or suspended by letters of the same see, unless in those letters there is an express mention of such an indult and its full tenor word for word. Given at Perugia, on the 14th of May, in the ninth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Albanensi mandat ut ecclesiae Anglonensis vacanti personam idoneam, acceptam Iohanni de Montefusculo, in episcopum praeficiat, et obedientiam ac reverentiam a capitulo et subditis exhiberi curet. 1235, Mai. 14. Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Tournai. Since, as your fraternity has informed us, both your predecessors and you have deemed it necessary, according to canonical sanctions, to appoint certain public witnesses, commonly called synodal witnesses, in each parish within your city and diocese, the aldermen of the town of Ghent in the same diocese, appointed to this office, are obligated to denounce to you or to one appointed by you for this purpose, any individuals accused of assorted crimes. Nevertheless, they refuse to testify against those noted for fornication due to a certain wrongful custom, which should more accurately be called a corruption, as if fornication should not be considered a criminal sin. Since it is necessary to punish this crime with more diligence the more frequently it is committed by many, we command that, if this is the case, you compel the aforementioned aldermen, by prior admonition and, if necessary, by ecclesiastical censure, notwithstanding the aforementioned custom, to report the truth regarding fornication as well as other crimes, as they are obliged to do, removing any appeal. Given at Perugia, on the 15th of January, in the tenth year (of our pontificate).

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Tornacensi mandat ut scabinos ville Gandensis compellat ad testificandum de fornicatione ac aliis criminibus, consuetudine prava non obstante, per censuram ecclesiasticam. 1227, Ian. 15. Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To Henry, Duke of Lorraine and Brabant. Desiring fervently that the matter of the Roman Empire be brought to a laudable conclusion with the Lord as its author, we ardently wish that all the sons of the Church, especially the magnates of the empire, rise vigorously and steadfastly to promote this endeavor, and we gladly urge them to do so with our admonitions and prayers. Therefore, we earnestly advise, request, and exhort your nobility, and through apostolic writings, we command, by the remission of sins, that you, pursuing the aforementioned matter already prosperously begun by God's grace with fervent spirit, effectively and powerfully support our dearest son in Christ, W., the illustrious King of the Romans, against any of his adversaries. For neither in the life of the same king nor after his death, if it should happen that he is called from this world in the meantime, shall we in any way abandon you, your heirs, and others adhering to you in this matter, nor shall we restore peace with the aforementioned adversaries without placing you and them in peace. Given at Perugia, 11th March, in the tenth year of our reign.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Henrico duci Lotharingiae et Brabanciae mandat ut Romanorum regi W. contra adversarios eius assistat, promittens se eum et heredes eius in hoc negotio non deserturum. 1237, Martii 11. Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Piacenza. The sincere affection of devotion, which you are known to have towards us and the Roman Church, rightly induces us to favorably grant your petitions, as much as we can with God. Therefore, since you have presented to us, in our presence, that due to a grave discord that has arisen among the citizens of Piacenza, you cannot comfortably reside in the city at present, we, moved by your devoted supplications, grant you the faculty, by the authority of these presents, to adjudicate causes among your subjects either in our court or elsewhere, to commit those causes to others subject to your diocesan law, and to make decisions and arrangements concerning the churches, and to institute and remove clerics of the city and diocese of Piacenza, as it pertains to your office, according to what you judge to be more useful and expedient, without requiring the chapter of Piacenza, as if you were personally residing in that city, until you can safely return and reside there comfortably. Let no one, therefore, violate our concession, etc. Given at Perugia, on the 7th Ides of February, in the 10th year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Placentino significat se concedere facultatem cognoscendi de causis inter subditos suos, comitendi eas aliis subiectis, et statuendi de clericis Placentine civitatis, donec secure redire possit. Datum Perusii, VII Idus Februarii, anno decimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Henry, Duke of Brabant and Lotharingia. The sincere affection of devotion, which you are known to have towards us and the Roman Church, leads us to favorably grant your requests, by which the grievances of your subjects are addressed. Therefore, inclined by your devoted supplications, we grant you by the authority of these presents that no one, whether clerics or laymen, may be summoned individually or collectively concerning any matters or goods they hold in your land outside of it, nor be called to judgment by letters of the Apostolic See or its legates, without a special mandate from the same See, explicitly mentioning this indulgence; present letters valid for two years etc. Let no one etc. our concession etc. Given at Assisi, on the third day before the Nones of July, in the thirteenth year. The dean and the treasurer of the church of Leuven in the diocese of Liège are given to you as conservators for this matter — notwithstanding if anyone is granted or conceded by the aforesaid See that they cannot be interdicted, suspended, or excommunicated, nor called to judgment outside their diocese by apostolic letters, unless they make express mention of such an indulgence, or any other indulgence of the same See, by which this could be impeded or delayed. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro Henrico duci Brabancie et Lotharingie indulget, ut nullus clericorum aut laicorum terre eius possit extra eam evocari ad iudicium sine mandato speciali sedis apostolice. Datum Assisii, III Nonas Iulii, anno XIII.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Tallacocius of Monte Marano, of the Benevento diocese. Since you are said to be devoted to God and the Church, it is fitting that you should rejoice in finding us favorable concerning those things you justly desire. Therefore, we, acceding to your supplications, return and confirm to you by the authority of these presents, the small castle of Soro and the castle called Massafra, which pertain to you by right of succession as the closest relative of the late Rizardus and Troisius, lords of the aforementioned small castle and castle, who died intestate without children, as you assert. This is notwithstanding the fact that the late Emperor Frederick wickedly seized them after the death of those lords and his offspring still unlawfully hold them. We restore and confirm them to you by special grace, especially since the kingdom of Sicily is currently without a king, on the condition that you are bound to perform an oath of fidelity and render due and customary services to the Roman Church or its future king. Therefore, let no one infringe upon this restitution and confirmation of ours, etc. Given at Perugia, on the third day before the Kalends of February, in the tenth year (of our pontificate).

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro Tallacocio de Monte Marano castellucium de Soro et castrum Massafra, iure successionis ut proximus consanguineus Rizardi et Troisii, restituit et confirmat, Friderico imperatore ea post mortem dominorum occupante, regno Siciliae rege carente. 1237, Jan. 30. Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To all clerics and laity of Aachen in the diocese of Liège. Since your return to the devotion of the Church, both in faith and in the service of our beloved son in Christ, W., the illustrious King of the Romans, we have understood that you are fervent, we wish to honor your persons for this reason and at the request of the same king, who earnestly supplicates on your behalf, by granting a special grace. Therefore, to those of you who persist in the devotion to both the Church and the king, we, by the authority of these presents, grant that none of you, collectively or individually, may be summoned to court by letters of the Apostolic See or its legates on any matters outside the walls of Aachen without a special mandate of the same See, provided that full and explicit mention of this indulgence is made word for word. Let no one contravene our grant, etc. Given at Perugia, on the Kalends of March, in the tenth year. The abbot of the monastery of Roda, of the order of Saint Augustine in the diocese of Liège, has been appointed as the conservator over this matter; notwithstanding if it has been granted to some from the Apostolic See that they may not be excommunicated, etc., until mention is made.

**Regesto in Latin:**

**Gregorius IX papa** universis clericis et laicis Aquensibus Leodiensis diocesis concedit gratiam specialem, ne extra muros Aquenses evocari possint in iudicium sine mandato speciali sedis apostolicae, persisting in devotione ecclesiae et regis. **Datum Perusii, Kalendis Martii, anno decimo.**

**Translation to English:**

To the provost, dean, and chapter of Würzburg. Due to the merits of your devotion, we willingly accede to your desires and favorably hear your petitions as much as we can with God. Therefore, granting your requests with kind approval, we concede to you by the authority of this letter that, if it should happen that your church becomes vacant, you may freely proceed to the election or postulation of a bishop — notwithstanding any reservations or prohibitions made by the authority of our general or even special letters, whether already made or to be made in the meantime, even if in those letters it is stated that any indulgence of the Apostolic See should not hinder those seeking them, provided they have not made full and express mention of them. For we entirely revoke any sentences which might have been pronounced by the authority of those letters or which may be done in the meantime. Let no one etc. of our concession etc. Given at Assisi, the fourth day before the Kalends of September, in the eleventh year. The abbot of St. Stephen of Würzburg is appointed as the conservator for this matter; notwithstanding if some in those regions have been granted by the Apostolic See that they cannot be excommunicated, suspended, or interdicted or brought to judgment outside certain places.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa preposito, decano et capitulo Herbipolensibus concedit, ut, ecclesia vacante, ad electionem seu postulationem episcopi procedere possint, reservationibus vel inhibitionibus non obstantibus; abbas Sancti Stephani Herbipolensis super hoc conservator datus est. Dat. Asisii, IIII Kalendas Septembris, anno XI.

Translation to English:

To the noble man Patutius of Concesio, podestà, council, and community of Novara. We trust in God’s favor that an increase of devotion will come to you if we extend the grace of appropriate goodwill towards you. Therefore, having agreed to your supplications, we have decided to absolve you, your assessors, knights, and all your family members, son podestà, from strictly observing the statutes of your city with the authority of these presents, under the condition that you are bound to observe them not precisely as they are enacted, but according to the will of the entire council of the same city or the greater part of it. And you, son podestà, can seek and receive the absolution of those statutes from the aforementioned council, provided that such absolution is directed not to the detriment but to the advantage of the Church of Novara. Therefore, let no one — of our absolution, etc. Given at Perugia, VI Kalends of October, in the tenth year.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro Patutio de Concesio, potestati Novariensium, scribit se ipsum et assessores, milites, ac familiares suos a stricta observatione statutorum civitatis auctoritate absolvere, ita ut secundum voluntatem consilii civitatis vel maioris partis observentur, dummodo absolutionem non in dispendium sed in profectum ecclesiae convertatur. Dat. Perusii, VI Kal. Oct., anno X.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz. Since rewards are granted by merits, so that we may invite the subordinates to merits through rewards, we wish to honor our beloved son, the elected Bishop of Speyer, with a special grace; his proven devotion and purity of faith have shown themselves in necessity, where friends are known, such that he has rendered himself worthy of the special grace and favor of the Apostolic See. Therefore, wishing to honor his person and gratify him, we have ordered that he be provided with some archbishopric or bishopric of his choosing in the kingdom of Germany; although we trust that, because of the kinship, by which he is said to be related to you, and also because it befits you to align your will with the Apostolic See, you ought to present yourself favorably to him in this matter without our intervention or that of anyone else, we nonetheless embrace him with sincere affection and earnestly desire his promotion. We earnestly ask and admonish your fraternity to show yourself favorable and gracious to this elect for the reverence of us and the Apostolic See, so that he may rejoice that your favor has been present, and we, knowing the diligence of your zeal through the result, may commend your dedication with thanks. Given at Perugia, on the fifth day before the Ides of January, in the tenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino mandat ut electum Spirensem, propter probatam devotionem et puritatem fidei, favore et gratia prosequatur, ut in archiepiscopatum vel episcopatum in regno Alamanie promoveatur. 1237, Ian. 9. Datum Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Freising. We are induced by the merits of your probity and devotion to embrace you with the arms of sincere affection, and to favorably grant your petitions as much as we are able with God. Since, as we understand from the tenor of your petition, the revenues and incomes of your church have been so diminished by the noble man, the Duke of Bavaria, and other enemies of the church, that you are entirely unable to sustain yourself from them, especially since you must bear heavy burdens of expenses for the custody and defense of the castles of the said church, we, deeming it right and proper that you should find in us an opportune remedy for this, grant you by the authority of these presents, that you may freely retain the revenues of the benefices of your city and diocese that are vacant for one year out of three years for your sustenance and the defense of those castles — notwithstanding any indulgences granted to any persons by the Apostolic See — provided that in the meantime these benefices are not deprived of their due services. Let no one etc. of our concession etc. Given at Assisi, 10th Kalends of July, in the tenth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Honorius III papa episcopo Frisingensi concedit ut proventus beneficiorum vacantium civitatis et diocesis suae per unum annum retinere possit pro sustentatione sua et defensione castrorum ecclesiae, non obstantibus indulgentiis ab apostolica sede concessis. Dat. Asisii, X Kal. Iulii, anno pontificatus nostri decimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Freising: On your behalf, it was humbly requested of us that, since the noble man, the Duke of Bavaria, has devastated the temporal goods of your church so severely through plunder and fire that you are not only unable to provide victuals for the keepers of its castles from its revenues, but also unable to sustain yourself in any way, we might care to assist you with the benevolence of the Apostolic See. Therefore, in a fatherly affection, we are granting you the authority through these present writings to retain in your hands the churches of Ehuige, Pacharn, Eutuige, and Vetent of your diocese, which you propose fall under your patronage and are now vacant, whose revenues, as you assert, do not exceed the annual value of forty marks of silver, and to collect these revenues in full until you have regained peaceful possession of these goods, left in the tranquility of peace and restored to their rightful state. We also grant you the power to restrain objectors through ecclesiastical censure, removing any appeal. Provided, however, that in the meantime you provide suitable vicars to serve these churches. Given at Assisi, June 4th, in the tenth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Episcopo Frisingensi auctoritatem concedit ad retinendum et percipiendum proventus ecclesiarum diocesis suae, videlicet de Ehuige, Pacharn, Eutuige et Vetent, donec pacificam possessionem bonorum temporalium suae ecclesiae recuperet, et potestatem dat compescendi contradictores per censuram ecclesiasticam. Datum Assisii, IV Nonas Iunii, anno decimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Tusculum, legate of the apostolic see. As your fraternity has informed us, certain individuals marked with the sign of the cross, who by adhering to and favoring C., the son of the late Fr., who was posing as emperor at that time, and his brothers and their supporters, and some who were serving Wathacius, others as well who, by breaking into churches, committing thefts and arsons, and many others who incurred sentences of excommunication issued against them by their ordinaries or judges delegated by the apostolic see or its legates, because when legitimately cited by them they contemptuously did not care to appear before them within the set peremptory term, have shown manifest contumacy, come to you humbly requesting to be absolved from these sentences. Therefore, having full confidence in your prudence in the Lord, we grant your fraternity by the authority of these presents, that you may absolve the same excommunicated individuals, from wherever they may be or come, from such sentences according to the form of the church on our behalf, provided that these contumacious individuals pledge to stand by justice and satisfy the expenses for their contumacy to the other party, and that the mentioned robbers, church-breakers, and arsonists pledge to restore what they took and satisfy those to whom they caused damage by such breaking and arson, within a suitable term to be set by you, providing sufficient and suitable security, otherwise, by the very fact, they will incur the same sentences if they neglect to fulfill the aforementioned conditions. Given at Perugia, on the 12th of February, in the tenth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Tusculano, apostolicae sedis legato, concedit ut excommunicatos, qui ad eum veniunt absolutionem postulantes, ab excommunicationis sententiis absolvat, sub conditionibus satisfaciendi et praestandi cautionem. 1237, Feb. 12. Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To Frederick, parish priest of Vico, our chaplain. We remember having previously instructed you through our letters, in a specific form, to ensure that our beloved son, the elected bishop of Feltre and Belluno, would be provided up to the sum of one thousand Bolognese pounds by our venerable brothers, the archbishops and bishops of Lombardy, Romagna, and the province of Grado. We have learned that you diligently executed this task, with those archbishops and bishops generously opening the bowels of charity to the aforementioned elect, thereby increasing their reputation among men and their merit before God. Wishing to grant even greater favor to the elect in this matter, we command that, for the coming year, you ensure he is provided for by the same archbishops and bishops up to the said sum, by our authority, according to the contents of the previous letters—notwithstanding that we have subsequently decided to commend the spiritual and temporal administration of the Church of Concordia to the same elect, since he has not yet fully acquired possession of it. Given at Assisi, on the 9th of September, in the eleventh year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa (Frederico plebano de Vico, capellano suo mandat, ut electo Feltrensi et Bellunensi ab archiepiscopis et episcopis Lombardie, Romaniæ et Gradensis provincie usque ad summam M librarum Bononiensium providentiam extendat, iuxta priorum litterarum continentiam. 1237, Sept. 9. Assisii).

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot and convent of the monastery of Casanova of the Cistercian order, in the diocese of Penne. Your petition presented to us stated that John, called Morus, chamberlain and manifest supporter of Conrad, the son of the late Frederick, former emperor, was gravely harassing your monastery over a certain grange of yours, called Luceria. He was prepared and threatening to have you immediately dispossessed unless you received it from him through a contract under an annual rent. You were forced by the fear and power of the said chamberlain, against whom you could not resist, as you had all your goods under the power of the said Conrad, to accept from John the aforementioned grange under a certain rent, paying it to him annually. Since things done under such force and fear should lack the force of law, we, inclined by your supplications, wishing to safeguard the indemnity of the said monastery with paternal care, decree by apostolic authority that the contract concerning the said grange made between you and the aforementioned John, and whatever has been or will be done on account of it, lacks the force of law. Gregorius IX papa Iohanni episcopo Sabinensi mandat, ut redemptiones et obventiones votorum crucesignatorum in subsidium Terrae Sanctae per regnum Alamaniae colligat et conservet, absolutis a voto crucis pauperibus et inhabiles, remissionem peccatorum eis concedens. 1237, Aug. 13, Assisii.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Mediolanensi mandat ut contra potestatem, assessores, officiales et consules Mediolanenses, qui ad usuras persolvendas compellunt, procedat secundum litterarum continentiam. 1236, Oct. 11. Perusii.

Gregorius IX papa Fratri Henrico Barensi electo mandat ut omnes confirmationes electionum et collationes beneficiorum per Conradum seu alium post mortem archiepiscopi Barensis factas irritas decernat et plenam potestatem ad revocandas eas habeat. 1237, Martii 7. Perusii.

Gregorius IX papa Marino de Ebulol comitatum Acerrarum, quem Henricus Romanorum imperator iniuste avus uxoris privavit, restituit et de novo concedit. Perusii, VII Kalendas Decembris, anno X.

Our beloved son, the nobleman William, lord of Strin, of the diocese of Utrecht, has informed us that, having once left his former wife Matilda, he adhered to another woman, whom he defiled through adultery, and promised her that if his lawful wife were to predecease him, he would marry her. We, therefore, command that, unless it is found that the nobleman or Matilda (or either of them) conspired in the death of the aforementioned wife, you should act with our authority to dispense on these matters with him, as you see fit according to God for the salvation of his soul. Gregorius IX papa episcopo Sambiensi mandat ut cum Willelmo de Strin, qui uxore defuncta mulierem cum qua adulterium commiserat in matrimonium duxit, dispenset, si in mortem uxoris machinatio non fuerit, promitto eum militare in expeditionibus regis Romanorum. 1236, Iunii 11, Assisii.

Gregorius IX papa H. tituli Sancte Sabine presbytero cardinali mandat ut, non obstante revocatione priorum litterarum, in provisione Everardi praepositi ecclesiae Sancti Georgii Coloniensis secundum priorum litterarum continentiam procedat. Dat. Perusii, V Idus Ianuarii, anno X pontificatus.

Otherwise, we command our beloved son, the provost of the church of Cremona in the diocese of Piacenza, by our letters, to execute the apostolic mandate concerning this matter; those who oppose are... **Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa preposito ecclesie Cremensis Placentine diocesis mandat, ut Daniusio de Osenago civi Mediolanensi silentium imponat super procurationibus ab eo repetitis, si legati terminos egressi sunt, et statum debitum restituat. Alioquin preposito Cremensi mandat exsecutionem mandati apostolici. Datum Laterani, VI Idus Novembris, anno XI.

To the noble man, the Marquis of Este. The devotion inherited from your ancestors, continued through you, justifiably earns that the Apostolic See receives your petitions with favorable ears, when they become known to it through anyone. We believe that your actions are moderated by such a judgment of discretion that you seek the fulfillment of your desires only as the rule of equity suggests. Indeed, we have received with customary kindness your envoys, men truly prudent and discreet, who came into our presence and attentively listened to what they wished to propose before us and our brothers. Among other things, they requested that we deign to restore the March of Ancona to you, which you claim pertains to you, granting you such favor in law that you might obtain this restoration without the noise of a trial. However, although we hold your person in the bowels of charity and intend to anticipate you with blessings of sweetness as a devoted son, at present, given the cautious times and circumstances, it does not seem easy or entirely free to us to grant you the requested favor in this matter, concerning a territory so often defended by the labors of the Church, so often snatched from the hands of invaders at great expense. Nevertheless, because we are debtors to all in justice, not only to you, who have made yourself fit for the due of justice and suitable benefits of grace through merits of devotion: if you believe you have some right over the mentioned March and decide to pursue it at the Apostolic See, which by principal privilege judges its own causes, we will, God willing, ensure that just judgment is rendered to you. For other princes of the world, especially those who recognize no superiors in temporal matters, use the prerogative of power to adjudicate such fiscal questions in their own courts and appoint judges over such matters when they have no temporal judge in this matter. Given at Perugia, on the Nones of December, in the tenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro marchioni Estensi mandat, ut si super marchia Anconitana ius aliquod habere confidit, illud prosequatur apud sedem apostolicam, quae iustum iudicium exhiberi faciet. 1236, Dec. 5. Perusii.

Given at the Lateran, on the 4th Kalends of January, in the 11th year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Magistro Alberto notario et apostolicae sedis legato mandat ut legationis sibi commissae honorem tueatur et insignia consueta exerceat. Datum Laterani, 1244, Dec. 29.

To Henry, Bishop of Strasbourg. Because the merits of your devotion deserve that we follow you with gracious benevolence, we further grant you by the authority of these presents, that after the period mentioned in these letters has ended, you may collect the revenues of the first year of the prelatures and benefices that become vacant within the two-year period in the same city and diocese, to be used for the payment of such debts. This is granted notwithstanding any indulgences granted by the Apostolic See to any persons, which would require full or explicit mention in our letters, word for word, and by which the effect of these presents might be hindered or delayed. Gregorius IX papa Henrico episcopo Argentinensi concedit, ut in exonerationem debitorum, prosecutioni negocii ecclesiae generalis contractorum, per biennium percipere possit proventus prelaturarum et beneficiorum in civitate ac diocesi Argentinensibus vacaturorum; et postea proventus primi anni vacaturorum infra biennium idem percipere, pro debitis solvendis convertendos, auctoritate presentium indulget, proviso interim per ydoneos vicarios servitium. The devotion that our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Magdeburg, and our beloved sons, the noble men, Count Ernest of Gleichen, Otto of the same diocese, and the advocate of Gera in the diocese of Naumburg, along with their followers, have towards the Roman Church, has been diligently expressed to us through your letters. Gregorius IX papa H. tituli Sanctae Sabinae presbytero cardinali mandat, ut cum archiepiscopo Magdeburgensi et nobilibus, si utilitati ecclesiae et imperii necnon regis Romanorum videatur expedire, dispenset, ut in matrimoniis contractis, non obstantibus quartae affinitatis et consanguinitatis lineis, permaneant. Datum Perusii, XIII Kalendas Februarii, anno X (1237).

To Master Albert, our notary, legate of the Apostolic See. Although your person is distinguished by office and merit, the magnitude and nature of the affairs entrusted to you by the Apostolic See demand that they be conducted with a more solemn envoy than of the same See, however great and meritorious he may be. Therefore, after prudent deliberation with our brothers, we have provided, by their counsel, that you take on the legation to conduct these affairs more solemnly and usefully. Thus, having fuller confidence in the Lord regarding your prudence, fidelity, and industry, and holding for certain that you will pursue the said affairs more diligently and vigilantly, as you have been distinguished with a more celebrated title, and that you will be attended to all the better by everyone the more gracious you can be to them. Therefore, we command your discretion through apostolic writings, that you strive to exercise this legation laudably according to the grace given to you by the Lord, so that you may gain merit before God and a good name among men, and we may commend the diligence of your endeavor with worthy praises in the Lord. Given at Assisi, 7th Ides of June, in the tenth year.

Gregorius IX papa Magistro Alberto notario nostro mandat, ut legationis officium in regno Francie, Provincia, Guasconia aliisque partibus adjacentibus plene exequatur, cum potestate evellendi, destruendi, dissipandi, disperdendi, aedificandi et plantandi. 1236, Iun. 7. Assisii.
