Your petition, presented to us, stated that our beloved son, brother Jacob, our doorkeeper, who previously traveled to your parts for certain affairs of the Roman Church, forgave, in our name, all the faults, injuries, and offenses you have committed against us and the same Church up to now. He did this by our special mandate on behalf of your commune and its people. Moreover, he released to you the revenues and rights that the Church used to have and receive in your city, from the time you adhered to the enemies of the Church until the time you returned to the bosom of the same Church, your mother. And although ten thousand pounds of Sienese currency were requested from you in our name for the remission of such offenses, since you, as it is said, paid two thousand pounds of Sienese currency to our beloved son P., Cardinal Deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, then legate of the Apostolic See, and offered us three thousand generously, the same brother Jacob, content with these three thousand pounds in our name, promised to absolve you from all the aforementioned matters and any other condemnations, as is more fully contained in the public instrument made thereof. We, therefore, in recognition of your devoted service, admit you to the full grace of the Apostolic See, and wishing to preserve both you and your city in customary rights and freedoms, hold as valid and acceptable the remission, release, and promise, and confirm them with apostolic authority, along with what was done by the same brother concerning these matters, up to the point of: we strengthen. Therefore, let no one violate our confirmation. Given at Perugia, 10th Kalends of August, in the tenth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa potestati, consilio et communi Interampnensibus remissionem culparum et iniuriarum, cum relaxatione iurium ecclesiae Romanae, confirmat et ratificat. 1236, Iul. 23, Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To the judges, aldermen, and other citizens of Cologne. Your and your ancestors' steadfastness in the faith of Saint Peter has always been so firm and your and their loyalty to the Roman Church, your mother, so proven, that there has never been any reason to doubt your and their constancy towards her. You have always closed your ears to the words of others and have followed no one's footsteps but those of the universal church's shepherd and father. Therefore, we gladly accede to your requests and, as far as possible with God's help, strive to protect you from future burdens. Inclined by the written petitions of your devotion, we grant you by the authority of these presents that through letters obtained from the Apostolic See or its legates, by which no process has yet been initiated, or even letters to be obtained, you may not be summoned universally or singularly to judgment outside the city of Cologne for any private or common cause without a special mandate of the same See, making full and explicit mention of this indulgence word for word. Let no one, therefore... Given at Perugia, 9th December, in the eleventh year of our Pontificate.

To the judges, aldermen, and other citizens of Cologne. Your steadfastness, etc., as far as we can through God, we fulfill your petitions. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, inclined by your devoted prayers, we confirm by apostolic authority the liberties, immunities, and rights reasonably granted to you by the emperors and kings of the Romans, as well as the archbishops of Cologne and other faithful princes, and also your laudable and ancient customs, as you justly and peacefully hold them, we confirm for you and through you for your city and its citizens, etc. Let no one, therefore... our confirmation, etc. Given at Perugia, 12th December, in the eleventh year of our Pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa iudicibus, scabinis et ceteris civibus Coloniensibus concedit, ut absque speciali mandato sedis apostolicae, de verbo ad verbum faciente de indulgentia mentionem, ad iudicium extra Coloniam non evocentur, et confirmat libertates, immunitates, iura et consuetudines ab imperatoribus et regibus Romanorum et aliis fidelibus concessas. Datum Perusii, V et II Idus Decembris, anno undecimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of St. Gall in the diocese of Constance. Since, as was presented to us on your behalf, we had previously ordered, through a certain executor and in a certain form, that provision be made for you concerning the bishopric of Constance when it should become vacant, and fearing that waiting for this provision might prejudice you as we recently ordered the revocation of provisions to archbishoprics, bishoprics, abbeys, and priories to be made by our letters: you have humbly requested us to provide for you regarding this matter. Indeed, those merits of your devotion, which have rendered you worthy of such grace with us, have led us to ensure that no prejudice is generated against you by those letters, so that provision can be made for you regarding the aforesaid bishopric according to the tenor of our mandate, we grant you this indulgence by the authority of these presents. Let no one therefore violate our concession, etc. Given at Perugia, III Kalends of September, in the tenth year. In the same manner for the provost of the monastery of St. Gall in the diocese of Constance, but where it says concerning the bishopric of Constance, let it be said concerning the abbey of St. Gall, as far as: merits of your devotion and at the request of our beloved son, the abbot of St. Gall, your cousin, by which worthy etc. up to Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati Sancti Galli Constantiensis diocesis mandat ut, non obstante recenti revocatione provisionum, nulla tibi preiudicium generetur, quominus de episcopatu Constantiensi iuxta mandati tenorem tibi provideri possit. 1236, Aug. 30, Perusii.

Translation to English:

To Master Ysembar, our notary. Our beloved son, the elected Wlteranus, has humbly petitioned us that, since he desires to recover the castle of Monteriggioni belonging to the church of Wlteranus with all its rights and appurtenances from the hands of Scott Dominici and his associates, Sienese merchants, to whom it is said that Fr. of Antioch, son of the late Frederick who once posed as emperor, pledged it; and to mortgage his houses and silverware, except for the jurisdiction and other revenues of the same castle, which he wishes to retain in his own hands, for six thousand silver marks of the weight of the same castle to our beloved sons Bonifacio and Rollando Bonsegnoris, our familiar brothers, and Bartholomeo Christofori and their associates, citizens and merchants of Siena; and to recover the castle itself and other castles and possessions of the same church, which are known to be detained by some against justice, as well as to relieve the aforementioned church from debts that the same elect has so far contracted for the recovery of his bishopric, and also to absolve Scott and the aforementioned associates from the proceeds of the fruits which they have so far received from the said castle, and to renew likewise the instrument of a certain pension which the commune of the city of Siena annually receives from the aforementioned castle, that we might mercifully grant him the license to do the aforesaid. Therefore, having full confidence in your circumspection in the Lord, we entrust to your discretion that, if you see it as beneficial to him and the aforementioned church, you grant him the requested license by our authority—notwithstanding if the chapter of the same church does not give its assent to this. Given at Perugia, 25 February, in the tenth year.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa magistro Ysembar notario mandat, ut electo Wlterano licentiam tribuat castrum Monterii et alia possessiones recuperandi ac debita ecclesiae Wlteranae exonerandi, non obstante assensu capituli. 1237, Feb. 25, Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To all patriarchs, archbishops, bishops, abbots, priors, and other prelates, as well as chapters, convents, and church colleges. The nature of the time, which was mostly to be redeemed in these days due to their wickedness in various ways, and the importunate insistence of some, has compelled us to command through our letters that provisioning be made for archbishoprics, bishoprics, abbeys, and priories in various regions. But considering it wiser to provide for churches, especially when it concerns their governance, rather than individuals, we grant by the authority of these presents the free power to those to whom the election, ordination, collation, or provision of the aforesaid belongs, to canonically provide and ordain concerning all the aforementioned — notwithstanding any general or special letters in any form of words obtained or to be obtained regarding the promotion or provision of anyone from the apostolic see or its legates, or any reservations, prohibitions, or nominations. We decree that anything done or presumed to be done by anyone due to the occasion of such letters against the tenor of this our concession and the freedom of your rights or power in this matter, is null and void, releasing the sentences of interdict, suspension, and excommunication, if any have been declared under the pretext of those letters so far, and considering any that may be promulgated hereafter to be completely null, with the inhibitions by us and our legates regarding not electing prelates in churches of rebellious cities and dioceses to the Roman Church, when they fall vacant, to remain in full force. Given at Perugia, on the 10th Kalends of June, in the ninth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa universis patriarchis, archiepiscopis, episcopis, abbatibus, prioribus, et aliis praelatis necnon capitulis et conventibus ecclesiarum mandat, ut potestatem canonice providendi et ordinandi de archiepiscopatibus, episcopatibus, abbatiis ac prioratibus concedat, non obstante litteris specialibus vel generalibus super promotionibus vel provisionibus impetratis. Dat. Perusii, X Kal. Iun., anno IX.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of Mezano, legate of the Apostolic See. Although the office of the apostolate makes us debtors to all, it is fitting that we should come to the aid of those who are known to be subject to the Apostolic See without any intermediary, in a more special and effective manner. Therefore, since it was proposed to us on behalf of our dear sons, the noble princes of Poland, that their ancestors, after they acquired the knowledge of the Christian faith, were subject solely to the same See, as they still are, and as a sign of this subjection, they and the inhabitants of Poland have paid and continue to pay annually to the same See the tribute known commonly as the denarius of St. Peter: we command that you, through yourself or another, effectively assist with the defense and not allow them to be molested by anyone. If you find that any infeudations, distributions, or occupations of the land of Poland have been made by our dearest son in Christ, W., the illustrious king of the Romans, or by others, you shall declare by our authority, through yourself or another, that they are null and void, restraining molesters and contradictors, should there be any, by ecclesiastical censure, setting aside any appeal. This is notwithstanding any letters obtained or to be obtained from the Apostolic See regarding this matter, or if there has been a grant from the same See to anyone from those regions that they cannot be excommunicated or suspended or their lands subjected to interdict by apostolic letters, unless such letters make full and express mention, word for word, of this grant, and notwithstanding the constitution concerning two days promulgated in the general council. Given at Assisi, on the 16th day before the Kalends of June, in the tenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati de Mezano, apostolicae sedis legato, mandat ut principibus et habitatoribus Poloniae defensio praestetur, et infeudationes de terra Poloniae factas a rege Romanorum aliisque denunciet non valere. 1237, Mai. 17. Assisii.

Translation to English:

To the Prior of Fontisboni and Brother Jacob, a monk of the hermitage of Camaldoli of the Camaldolese order in the diocese of Arezzo. The noble men Tegrinus and Guido of Mutigliano, his son, palatine counts in Tuscany, have informed us that they, though unwillingly, upon the order of the late Emperor Fr. of the Romans, to whose dominion they were then subject, caused our venerable brother, Saxena, bishop, to be captured and handed over into the power of the said Emperor. Therefore, they humbly requested from us that since they feared they might have incurred the bond of excommunication by the pretext of the said bishop, although he has been restored to his former liberty, and since they cannot conveniently approach the Apostolic See due to dangers on the roads, to obtain the benefit of absolution, we should mercifully provide for them regarding this matter. Trusting fully in your discretion in the Lord, we therefore, by the authority of these presents, entrust you to grant the benefit of absolution to these nobles, when they humbly request it from you for this reason, with the consent and will of the aforementioned bishop, according to the form of the Church, in our stead, and furthermore, to enjoin upon them a salutary penance. If not both, etc. Given at Perugia, on the 11th of July, in the tenth year.

Latin Regesto:

Gregorius IX papa Priori Fontisboni et fratri Iacobo monacho Camaldulensi mandat, ut Tegrinum et Guidonem de Mutilliano, comites palatinos, auctoritate sua absolvant, consentiente episcopo Saxenate, poenitentiamque salutarem iniungant. 1236, Iul. 13. Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To the illustrious William, King of the Romans. It is fitting that sentences solemnly pronounced by royal decree should remain inviolate and should not lack the support of apostolic firmness. Indeed, your narration, dearest son, presented to us stated that you, in the general court recently held at Frankfurt according to the ancient custom of the empire, through a definitive sentence, by the common consent of the faithful princes of the same empire present there, have deprived all those of whatever goods they held in fief from the empire, who did not care to receive investiture from your highness within a year from the day you were crowned King of the Romans at Aachen by divine favor, as is more fully contained in the authentic letters made thereof and sealed with the royal seal. Therefore, inclined by the prayers of your highness, we hold what you have done in this regard as valid and pleasing, and we confirm it by apostolic authority, etc., up to: we fortify. Let no one therefore — our confirmation etc. Given at Perugia, 2nd December, in the 10th year. To the abbot of Fulda, of the diocese of Würzburg. It is fitting etc., up to: is contained, with words competently modified. Wherefore we command, that you should cause the same sentence to be inviolably observed by you or others by our authority — notwithstanding if it has been granted by the apostolic see that some cannot be excommunicated or their lands subjected to ecclesiastical interdict without etc., up to: mention, even if it is contained therein that any indulgence of the said see should not stand in the way of the petitioners of said indulgences, or any indulgence of the aforesaid see, by which the effect of your jurisdiction in this matter can be impeded or delayed, or the constitution concerning two diets etc. —; contradictors [etc.]. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Willelmum regem Romanorum rogat et auctoritate apostolica confirmat sententiam per eum in generali curia apud Frankforte promulgatam, qua omnes qui investituram a regno infra annum a coronatione sua non receperunt, bonis privavit, et mandat ut sententia inviolabiliter observetur, non obstantibus quibuscumque indulgentiis apostolicis. 1236, Dec. 2. Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Strasbourg: The pleasing services of the devoted are rightly to be compensated with a gratuitous reward, so that their rewarded devotion may rejoice and others may be encouraged by their laudable example to serve faithfully. Therefore, as we have learned, the beloved son, the noble man Eberhard, lord of Landesbert, fighting for the defense of ecclesiastical liberty and purity of faith, was captured by the undevout of the Church, supporters of the late Frederick who claimed the title of emperor, and has been long afflicted in the distress of imprisonment, suffering other grievous damages: we, on account of this and your supplicant intervention, wishing to graciously support the beloved son Lemprid, a cleric and son of the same noble, who is said to hold no ecclesiastical benefice, command that you provide for the same L. with some suitable ecclesiastical benefice under the authority of the abbess and convent of Hohenbourg of your diocese of the order of Saint Augustine, which is usually assigned to secular clerics, which the same L. chooses to accept, even if it involves the care of souls and is currently vacant, or as soon as the opportunity arises, by your authority or another's — notwithstanding if we have directed our writings to the aforementioned abbess and convent for others, which we do not wish to prejudice by this, or if we have otherwise written for the same, or if the same abbess and convent have been granted by the apostolic see that they cannot be compelled to provide for anyone or be excommunicated, suspended, or interdicted, or that provision for benefices belonging to their collation cannot be made for anyone by letters of the said see unless a full and express mention of such indult is made, word for word, or by any deficiency which the same L. is said to suffer of orders and age —; those contradicting — Given at Assisi, the 14th day before the Calends of September, in the eleventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Argentinensi mandat ut Lemprido, clerico et filio Eberhardi de Landesbert, pro defensione ecclesiasticae libertatis capto, provideat de beneficio ecclesiastico ab abbatissa et conventu de Hohemburci assignando, non obstantibus quibuslibet praemissis. 1238, Aug. 19. Assisii.

Translation to English:

To the schoolmaster of the church of Liège. Previously, our beloved son Jacob, dean of the church of St. John of Liège and chaplain of our dear son Peter, cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, complained to us that our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Mainz, was not keeping him unharmed regarding the debts he had incurred on behalf of the late Archbishop of Mainz, his predecessor, while managing the affairs of him and the church of Mainz at the Apostolic See, and in Liège, while the Archbishop was besieging Aachen. He was not compensating the aforesaid dean for the services rendered to the Archbishop himself. We initially directed our writings to the Archbishop under specific terms, and then, when the Archbishop, despite being admonished by our mandate and by our venerable brother, the Bishop of Mantua, then Provost of Parma and our chaplain, did not heed these admonitions, we appointed the late Bishop of Sabina, then cardinal priest of the title of St. Marcellus, as auditor for the aforementioned dean. Although the cardinal sent letters to the Archbishop urging him to compensate the dean for the above matters, or else within two months, which he specified as a peremptory term, send a suitable procurator to the Apostolic See, the Archbishop did neither, as the petition exhibited to us by the dean showed. We also arranged for the Archbishop to be cited in the usual form. However, because this citation did not proceed due to certain impediments, as we have learned, we command you to peremptorily cite the Archbishop of Mainz by our authority, either personally or through someone else, so that within four months after your citation, he appears before us in person or through a suitable and fully instructed procurator for the entire case, to do and receive what reason dictates. The day of the citation etc. until: to intimate. Given at Assisi, 27th September, in the eleventh year.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa scolastico ecclesiae Leodiensis mandat, ut Maguntinum archiepiscopum auctoritate apostolica peremptorie citet, quo infra quatuor menses post citationem compareat coram papa in causa debitorum et satisfactionis decano Leodiensi. 1237, Sept. 27. Assisii.

**Translation:**

To Brother H., presbyter cardinal of the title of Santa Sabina, legate of the apostolic see. Our venerable brother Arnold, Archbishop of Trier, has earnestly requested from us that he be granted the revenues of benefices, dignities, and ecclesiastical offices which may fall vacant once within three years in the city and diocese of Trier, to be freely received by him for one year after their vacancy, as he is said to have previously received there for some time by our indulgence. Since we have learned that the same archbishop is devoted both to us and to the Roman Church with a readiness to serve in this general matter, we, intending to graciously support him in this and other matters as much as we can with God's help, command that you grant this to him by you or another with our authority, merited by his devotion; objectors [etc.] — notwithstanding if it has been granted to anyone by the apostolic see that they should not be excommunicated etc. up to: mention. Given at Assisi, on the 4th Ides of July, in the eleventh year. To the same. Our venerable brother Arnold, Archbishop of Trier, due to the sincere devotion he is known to have towards us and the Roman Church in the general matter, wishing him to enjoy a special prerogative, we command that you grant to the same archbishop that he may retain the ecclesiastical benefices and dignities he obtained before his promotion, as he is said to have hitherto held by our indulgence, until our good pleasure, by you or another with our authority, merited by the devotion of the same archbishop; objectors [etc.] — notwithstanding any letters or indulgences prejudicial to truth and justice obtained or to be obtained from the apostolic see, or processes had by the same, or if it has been granted to anyone by the same see that they should not be excommunicated etc. up to: mention. Given as above.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa fratri H. tituli Sancte Sabine presbytero cardinali, apostolice sedis legato mandat ut Arnoldo Treverensi archiepiscopo concedat proventus beneficiorum et personatus post vacationem per unum annum percipere. Dat. Assisii, IIII Idus Iulii, anno XI.

**Translation to English:**

To the entire people of Massa. Since he is cursed by God who provokes his mother, you can greatly fear the danger of eternal damnation, having inflicted severe injuries on your mother, the Church of Massa, who, regenerating you in Christ through baptism, supplies milk to infants and solid food to the advanced, and, what is more, refreshes you with the most holy body of Christ. You have inflicted grievous harm upon her. For, while your city belongs to this church by full right, both spiritually and temporally, you, who as sons and faithful ought not only to keep her rights inviolate but also defend them from violators with all your might, have contemptuously dismissed divine fear and human decency, and wickedly withdrawn yourselves from her dominion. You have presumed to despoil her of possessions and other goods and to hand them over to others, and what is more dreadful, you have sometimes sacrilegiously captured bishops. Thus you have reduced this church to such poverty that it seems utterly unworthy of the episcopal dignity, being so overwhelmed with the intolerable burden of debts that it can scarcely satisfy the abyss of usury with all its revenues, as our venerable brother, the bishop of Massa, recently lamentably explained before us. Since it is deemed not only impious but also abusive that such an honorable seat, which boasts singular privilege, is exposed to such contempt, we earnestly ask, advise, and urge your community, firmly commanding that you provide for your own salvation and honor, at least in this matter appeasing your mother, by presently relieving the aforementioned church from the burden of debts, so that you make amends for past offenses and earn merit with God and men. Otherwise, as Matthew 21:43 says, "The kingdom of God will be taken from you and given to a people producing its fruit," we have commanded by our letters to the same bishop, to transfer the episcopal seat from your city and establish it in a suitable place where it seems more expedient. Given at Perugia, on the Nones of May, in the ninth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa universo populo Massano mandat, ut ecclesiam Massanam, quae gravissimis damnis affecta est, ab onere debitorum relevetis, alioquin episcopalis sedes transferetur. Perusii, Nonis Maii, anno nono.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishops of Castellano, Urbinati, Ariminensi, Feretrano, Bobiensi, Cesanatici, Foropopuliensi, Liviensi?, Faventino, Imolensi?, Cerviensi, Clomaclensid, and to the elected of Ravenna and Arezzo, as well as abbots, priors, parish priests, and other prelates of churches established in those cities and their dioceses. Considering with paternal care the state and tranquility of our beloved faithful from Massa Trabaria, we have appointed our beloved chaplain Huguition, a prudent and discreet man, accepted by us and our brothers for his meritorious qualities, as their rector with the full office of legation committed to him. We have decided to earnestly request and admonish your community, by apostolic writing, to receive and honor him with respect due to the apostolic see and to us, treating him joyfully and honorably, and to humbly heed him as your legate, so that he may be more strongly bound to your love because of this, and we may rightfully commend your devotion. Otherwise, [the sentence] as mentioned: to be observed. Given at Assisi, on the 12th day before the Kalends of August, in the 11th year of our pontificate.

To Huguition of the Marquises, our chaplain, legate of the apostolic see in Massa Trabaria. Since we have deemed it right to entrust you with the office of legation in Massa Trabaria, being inclined by your supplications, we grant you full authority by the present [letters] to freely exercise the jurisdiction, which Quintus of blessed memory, a chaplain of the apostolic see, and others who were legates of the same see in Massa at various times, are known to have had and exercised there and elsewhere, in both temporal and spiritual matters. Given at Assisi, on the 2nd day before the Ides of July, in the 11th year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopis Castellano, Urbinati, Ariminensi, et aliis, et electis Ravennati et Aretino, aliisque ecclesiarum praelatis per civitates et dioceses constitutis mandat, ut Huguitionem Marchionem capellanum, legatum apostolicae sedis in Massa Trabaria, honorifice recipiant et humiliter obediant. 1237, Iul. 14. Assisii.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of the Holy Trinity of Mileto, the prior of Saint Stephen of Bosco in Squillace, and Egidio, canon of Mileto. We have learned from trustworthy sources that the late Richard, chamberlain of the late Emperor Frederick, caused Benevenuto, a cleric and nephew of the said Richard, who had not yet reached the age of twenty and was not in holy orders, to be elected as bishop of Squillace by the chapter of the church of Squillace, not without secular influence. He subsequently improperly procured the confirmation of this election by the chapter of Regina, the metropolitan church of Squillace, while the church was vacant. Furthermore, the said Benevenuto wickedly sold chalices, crosses, silver thuribles, silk cloths, and ornaments of the Squillace church, dilapidating and enormously consuming its goods. After a deposition sentence was pronounced against him, he favored the said Emperor Frederick and ordered the celebration of divine services by priests and clerics of the city and diocese of Squillace against the interdict issued by us in the kingdom of Sicily. He also, under lay habit, unlawfully took up the administration of the spiritual and temporal affairs of the church, to the peril of his soul, the prejudice and scandal of many of the church's devotees, and the contempt of ecclesiastical discipline. Therefore, we command that if this is true, you annul the proceedings concerning the said election and confirmation by our authority, declare both the election and confirmation invalid, and expressly forbid the chapter of Squillace to elect anyone as their bishop without the special mandate of the Apostolic See, pronouncing a sentence of excommunication against those who oppose and rebel, setting aside any appeal. We also decree that anything attempted against this prohibition shall be null and void. If not all of you can carry this out, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the Ides of October, in the eleventh year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati Sancte Trinitatis Militensis, priori Sancti Stephani de Bosco Squillacensis, et Egidio canonico Militensi mandat ut processum electionis et confirmationis Benevenuti in episcopum Squillacensem cassent et irritum denuncient, necnon capitulo Squillacensi inhibeant ne aliquem sine mandato sedis apostolice eligant. 1237, Oct. 15. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To H., cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina, legate of the apostolic see. The petition presented to us by our beloved son, the nobleman Count Harcimann of Grueningen, stated that the author of discord had sown such a matter of disagreement between him and the nobleman Count of Veringen of the diocese of Constance, that from it not only followed the destruction of their properties, but also great perils of body and goods threatened the inhabitants of neighboring places and all those passing through. Thus, to put an end to this discord and to reform a bond of peace between them, the Count of Grueningen swore to take as his wife the noblewoman Hedwig, daughter of the said Count of Veringen, and even betrothed her. However, since the aforementioned Count of Grueningen is related to the woman in the fourth degree of consanguinity, he did not proceed to the consummation of this marriage until recourse was had to the apostolic see on this matter, humbly beseeching us to provide a salutary remedy, since nothing works so effectively for the restoration of peace between these counts and the avoidance of many dangers as the consummation of this marriage. Therefore, considering that urgent necessity and evident utility call for a dispensation, we command that, having diligently considered all the circumstances, if you see it to be expedient for the utility and the matter concerning our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious king of the Romans, you grant dispensation to the said Count of Grueningen and the woman by our authority, through yourself or another, so that, notwithstanding such an impediment, they may, if they wish, proceed to the consummation of the aforementioned marriage and lawfully remain together. Given at Perugia, on the sixth day before the Nones of October, in the tenth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa H. tituli Sancte Sabine presbytero cardinali mandat, ut comiti Harcimanni de Grueningen et mulieri Hedewigi de Veringen, consanguineis in quarta linea, dispensando concedat, ut ad matrimonium consummandum procedant ad pacem inter comites reformandam. 1236, Oct. 2, Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To Master Albert, our notary, legate of the Apostolic See: Since, as we have recently learned from the letters you sent us, there are certain difficulties posed by the counselors of the noble man, our beloved son, Charles, Count of Provence, regarding certain articles expressed in the conditions to be appended in the grant of the Kingdom of Sicily to be made by you: although the same count is content with these conditions, in order to gain their favor and thus more easily bring them to agreement, he asks that these articles be clarified and restricted by us upon the advice of some, as contained in your schedule, not, however, to be enacted, but to be used as an excuse towards the same counselors. Therefore, we command that you promise the same count on our behalf, as an excuse to the said counselors, that we will do concerning these articles whatever two prelates and one knight, whom this count will name, shall advise us, provided that the same count first produces his open letters to you, stating that such a promise is utterly null and void and does not bring any benefit to the said count nor loss to us or the Roman Church, and that we are not bound or obliged by it to anything, except only to those matters contained in the letters directed to you by us through our beloved son, Master Paganus, our chaplain, Provost of Saint Savior of Lavania. Furthermore, it seems to us that the same count, after the grant and investiture of the said kingdom is made to him by you, should call himself king. Given at Assisi, 11th of July, in the 11th year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Magistro Alberto, notario et apostolicae sedis legato, mandat ut comiti Provinciae super articulis in collatione regni Siciliae per eum faciendis promittat quod faciet quae duo prelati et unus miles consulent, nullo tamen emolumento dato dicto comiti, et post investituram se regem nominet. Dat. Assisii, V Idus Iulii, anno XI.

**Translation to English:**

To the Elect of Capua. Concerning the purity of devotion and faith toward God and the Church, and also concerning the life, morals, and knowledge of our beloved son, Brother Placidus, the provost of the monastery of Saint Benedict of Capua of the Order of Saint Benedict, laudable testimony is given by many trustworthy witnesses, especially by our beloved son, the noble man, the Count of Caserta and Alife, devoted to us and the aforementioned See. Because of these merits, and also because the aforementioned count has affectingly commended the provost to us through his special letters, we command your discretion, in which we have special trust in the Lord, through apostolic writings, that you, with our authority, appoint the same provost, if what is proposed about his probity is supported by truth, as abbot of the monastery of Saint Vincent of Volturno of the same order, which pertains directly to the Roman Church, either through yourself or another. You are to ensure that he is shown due obedience and reverence by his subjects and that the blessing is conferred upon him, and afterward, you are to receive from him the customary oath of fidelity for us and the Roman Church, according to the form we send enclosed under our seal. As for the form of the oath, etc.; opposition, etc. Moreover, once you have fulfilled our mandate concerning the aforementioned provost, you shall appoint our beloved son, Brother Andrew, a monk of the aforementioned monastery of Saint Benedict, a man, as asserted, of reverence, prudence, and honesty, whom the aforementioned count and beloved sons of the commune of Capua favor with special benevolence for his laudable merits, as provost of the said monastery of Saint Benedict with the aforementioned authority and proceed similarly in other matters concerning him, setting aside the oath, as expressed above regarding the aforementioned Brother P. However, we wish no prejudice to be generated henceforth to the monastery of Monte Cassino, to which the aforementioned monastery of Saint Benedict is said to be subject. Given at Perugia, on the sixth Ides of November, in the tenth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Electo Capuano mandat ut fratrem Placidum, prepositum monasterii sancti Benedicti Capuani, in abbatem monasterii sancti Vincentii de Volturno ordinis Sancti Benedicti constituat, si eius probitas vera est, et fratrem Andream in prepositum monasterii sancti Benedicti Capuani praeponat, servatis formis mandatis. Ne generetur praeiudicium monasterio Casinensi. Datum Perusii, VI Idus Novembris, anno decimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Basel. Your faith, proven and approved during the time of disturbance around us and the Apostolic See, by clear signs of praiseworthy works, deserves gratitude, so that the Church of Basel, which you preside over, may feel the effective grace of the same See through you. Indeed, your petition presented to us stated that the castle of Rinvelden, situated in the middle of the Rhine in the diocese of Basel, which the late Fr., while he was still alive and acting as emperor, acquired not for the empire but for himself and his heirs, is now being used by the noble man Conrad, the son of the said Fr., and the inhabitants of the place to gravely offend God, the Church, and men. Through substantial labor of yours and your relatives and heavy expenses of your church, you have taken possession of it and are having it guarded for the Church of Basel. Therefore, commending your vigilant diligence in this matter to the Lord, and moved by your devotion, we grant by apostolic authority that you and your successors, the bishops of Basel, may lawfully retain the said castle with all its appurtenances, villages, and hamlets in the name of the Church of Basel in perpetuity. Let no one, therefore, etc., regarding our concession. If anyone, however, etc. Given at Perugia, 5th day before the Kalends of August, in the tenth year. A conservator was appointed for this matter, namely the provost of the Church of Olemberc of the order of Saint Augustine in the diocese of Basel—notwithstanding if it has been granted to some by the Apostolic See that they cannot be excommunicated, interdicted, or suspended. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Basiliensi concedit ut castrum Rinvelden cum omnibus pertinentiis, villis et viculis, quod Conradus cum incolis offendebat, ipse episcopus et successores nomine ecclesie Basiliensis perpetuo retinere possint. Perusii, V Kal. Augusti, anno decimo.

**Translation to English:**

To all the faithful of Christ who will inspect the present letters. Although we have previously deemed it necessary to set a definite term for the nobleman Ezzelino da Romano to personally come to the Apostolic See to face the charge of heresy imprinted upon him and to receive what justice dictates, otherwise we would proceed more severely against him from that time onwards. However, prompted by the counsel of prudence, we wish to remove from him any harmful grounds for excuse, so that he cannot cover himself with any semblance of impossibility of obedience or danger of appearing before us. Let it be clear to all, as we pursue the matter of the Catholic faith with as much restraint as we can towards him, that the pious mother of all the faithful does not attack him with unjust animosity, but seeks his salvation with sincere desire of charity. Therefore, we modify the form of the aforementioned citation for the said nobleman to come personally to the aforesaid See with this balance of equity: if, before the upcoming Feast of the Assumption, he finds a certain and suitable place in Lombardy, or the March of Treviso, or Friuli, or even in Germany, or any other conveniently adjoining region, provided that the place is under the full power of the Church or its faithful, we permit him the option; and we are prepared to provide him full security there, so that he may personally fulfill what is incumbent upon him in the aforementioned matters. We are ready to send persons to that place who will receive the nobleman there on our behalf, humbly doing what he ought in this part. We wish this to come to common knowledge, so that reason may prove the action and what is publicly conducted in the matter of faith, concerning all faithful, may be known to public ears. Given at Perugia, the 9th day before the Kalends of July, in the ninth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa universis Christi fidelibus scribit, quod terminum Ezelino de Romano ad sedem apostolicam veniendi prius statutum moderatur, permittens ei locum tutum in Lombardia aut marchia Tervisina vel regione alia eligere, ubi in fidei negotio compareat; et hoc ad communem notitiam pervenire vult. Datum Perusii, VIIII Kalendas Iulii, anno nono.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Siena. Concerned about the well-being of your subjects, you humbly asked us to grant you the permission to absolve certain individuals from the sentence of excommunication, which they often incur by engaging in trade with the people of Pisa. Inclined by your supplications, we grant your fraternity, by the authority of these presents, the full and free faculty to absolve, according to the form of the Church, all those from the city and diocese who have incurred such a sentence of excommunication and who will incur it within the next two years, and to impose on them salutary penance. Given at the Lateran, on the 11th of February, in the eleventh year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Senensi facultatem concedit absolvendi, iuxta formam ecclesiae, omnes civitatis ac diocesis Senensis, qui sententiam excommunicationis propter commercia cum Pisanis incurrerunt vel in biennio incurrerint, iniungendo eis poenitentiam salutarem. 1254, Februarii 11, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To Brother H., cardinal priest of the title of St. Sabina, legate of the apostolic see. On behalf of our beloved son, the noble man, the Duke of Brabant, it was humbly requested to us that we should care to grant, from the special grace of the apostolic see, to the noble man Godefrid, lord of Perwez and Grimbergen, his kinsman and counsellor, who, as he asserts, desires to devote himself to the Roman Church and to the service of our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious king of the Romans, the tithes of lands which have come to be newly brought under cultivation in the dominion of Godefrid, with a third part of those tithes reserved for the rectors of the churches in whose parishes they are situated, or for those personally serving there. Wherefore, we commit to your discretion by the authority of these presents, that you act on our behalf in this matter, as you see fit for the affair of the church and the utility of the aforementioned king. Given at Perugia, the 11th of March, in the tenth year of our pontificate. 

To the same. On behalf of our beloved son, the noble man Henry, Duke of Brabant, it was humbly requested to us that since he has remained bound by heavy debts since the death of his father and for this reason has not been able to assist the Roman Church and our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious king of the Romans, as he has desired and still desires to do, in the relief of these debts, by which he might become more powerful to aid the same king, the tithes of lands which have come to be newly brought under cultivation in his dominion, etc., as above in all things. Given as above.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa, fratri H. tituli Sanctae Sabinae presbytero cardinali, apostolicae sedis legato mandat, ut tithas terrarum, quae in dominio Godefridi de novo ad culturam redactae sunt, cum tertia parte rectoribus ecclesiarum reservata, ex parte ducis Brabantie concedat; et eundem modum pro Henrico duce Brabantie, qui ob debitorum gravamina non potuit Romanam ecclesiam adiuvare, decimas concedendi auctoritatem tribuit. Datum Perusii, V Idus Martii, anno decimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the council and community of Lübeck, devoted to the Roman Church. The Apostolic See is accustomed to condescend to the prayers of the devoted and to grant favorable support to their wishes. Therefore, as has been explained to us on your behalf, the emperors of the Romans of clear memory, who were in office for the time being, remaining in the devotion of the Church, deemed it appropriate to grant you privileges, such that you could not be alienated, enfeoffed, or pledged by anyone, as you are directly subject to the empire, as is more fully contained in such privileges. We, inclined by your devoted prayers, hold what has been providently done by these emperors as confirmed and pleasing, and by apostolic authority, we confirm and strengthen it. Let no one, etc., oppose our confirmation, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the 13th day before the Kalends of February, in the 11th year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa consilio et communi Lubicensibus, devotionem erga ecclesiam Romanam exhibentibus, privilegia a Romanorum imperatoribus concessa, quibus ab imperio immediate subiecti alienari vel infeudari seu pignori obligari non valeant, auctoritate apostolica confirmat. Datum Laterani, XIII Kalendas Februarii, anno XI.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Modena. Our beloved son, Brother Rufinus, the minister of the Friars Minor of the Bolognese administration, our penitentiary, is said to have instructed you on our behalf to present a certain sum of money to our beloved sons, the citizens of Modena, who were once exiled for the freedom of the Church, as compensation for the damages they had sustained, from the twentieth of ecclesiastical revenues of the provinces of Lombardy, the March of Treviso, and Romagna, which we had previously commanded to be collected through our letters by you. However, as the same citizens have taken care to explain to us, you have paid them only a part of that money. Hence, we command you with our letters to diligently collect the said twentieth as is expedient and carefully, and pay the remaining amount of the aforementioned money to the same citizens from the collected and to be collected twentieth. If, however, the said twentieth is insufficient for this, you shall diligently and fully collect this twentieth in the Patriarchate of Grado from the city of Treviso for three years and in Romagna for the coming year, either by yourself or by others, and from this twentieth satisfy the same citizens up to the named sum of money. Since certain things, which we can scarcely believe, have reached our ears concerning this collection, we want you to faithfully inform us through your letters, of what and how much and from whom you have collected in each church and monastery, and other places and dioceses of those provinces on the occasion of the said twentieth, and how much and to which persons you have assigned the same, also sending a certain messenger to us, who will make a full and clear account of all and singular the above to our beloved son, our chamberlain. Otherwise, indeed, we do not wish you to have any power in collecting the said twentieth for the future. For we decree, if you do anything contrary, that it is null and void. Given at Perugia, 30th May, in the ninth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Mutinensi mandat, ut de vicesima proventuum ecclesiasticorum provinciarum Lombardie, Marchie Tervisinae et Romaniolae olim collecta, pecuniam civibus Mutinensibus exulantibus solvat, et de gestis suis plenam rationem per nuntium camerario referat, alioquin potestatem colligendi amittat. Datum Perusii, III Kal. Iunii, anno VIIIIo (1235).

**Translation to English:**

To John, elected Bishop of Turin. Desiring to address your grievances, we grant you by the authority of these presents that for the past and future, as long as you manage the care of the Church of Turin with our permission, you shall not be obliged to render an account of the administration of temporal matters to anyone. No one is to etc. our concession etc. Given at the Lateran, on the 4th day before the Ides of March, in the 11th year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Iohanni electo Taurinensi concedit, ut rationem administrationis temporalium nulli reddere teneatur, quamdiu de licentia apostolica ecclesiae Taurinensis curam gerat. Dat. Laterani, II Nonas Martii, anno XI.

**Translation to English:**

To Henry of Vinstingen, cantor of Verdun, our chaplain. On behalf of our beloved son Conrad, canon of Strasbourg and brother of the noble man, the lord of Liechtenberg, advocate of Strasbourg, our devoted one, it was presented before us that when we had previously directed our letters concerning the provision to the late Simon, his brother, canon of Strasbourg, for some prelature or dignity then first to become vacant in the city or diocese of Strasbourg to a certain executor under a certain form, eventually the provostship of the church of Surbourg in the diocese of Strasbourg, which by right was owed to Simon, became vacant. Anselm of Fleckenstein, our chaplain, by the authority of certain letters from the apostolic see, unbeknownst to us, as the father and brother of Anselm opposed themselves strongly and openly to the business of the general church, later procured it to be conferred upon himself to the prejudice of Simon. But our dearest son in Christ, William, the illustrious king of the Romans, and our venerable brother, the archbishop of Mainz, then-elect, informed us that the father and brothers of Anselm adhered to Conrad, the late son of Emperor Frederick of the Romans, and his supporters, and that they occupied and held occupied castles and fortifications of the empire. We, therefore, instructed our venerable brother, the bishop of Metz, through our letters, to admonish and effectively induce the aforementioned father and brothers, that within a certain time expressed in our letters after the admonition, they should return to the devotion of the church and restore the castles and fortifications to the mentioned king, otherwise to remove Anselm from the provostship with the counsel of our beloved son H., cardinal priest of the title of Santa Sabina, legate of the apostolic see, and to strive to confer and assign it by our authority to Simon; contradictors —. When the said bishop began to proceed in this matter, Simon passed away. However, subsequently, at the insistence of the said cardinal, and the elect of Speyer, as well as nobles of Swabia supplicating us on behalf of Conrad, we decided to transfer all graces obtained from us concerning Simon's provision to Conrad. Therefore, we command that you proceed in the same matter for Conrad according to the contents of our letters directed to the bishop of Metz regarding Simon. Given at Perugia, 7th Ides of April, in the 10th year of our pontificate.

**Regesto:**

Honorius III papa Henrico de Vinstingen, cantori Virdunensi, mandat ut procedat pro Conrado canonico Argentinensi iuxta continetiam litterarum directarum ad episcopum Metensem pro provisione Simonis. 1226, Perusii, die 7 Idus Aprilis.

Translation to English:

To the Bishop of Utrecht. Intending to favorably support your person, which we have understood to be zealous in the affairs of the universal Church and devoted to the Apostolic See, we grant you the authority, by the authority of these presents, to receive for one year the revenues of ecclesiastical benefices, dignities, and offices which may happen to be vacant for up to three years in your city and diocese. You may fully convert these revenues for expenses incurred for the service of the Roman Church and our beloved son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, W. You are also empowered to restrain any contradictors by ecclesiastical censure, disregarding any appeals — notwithstanding if some have been granted by the Apostolic See that they cannot be excommunicated, interdicted, or suspended without special mandate of the same See. However, it is provided that during this time, such benefices, dignities, and offices are not deprived of their due services, and the care of souls to whom it pertains is in no way neglected. Given as in another place.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Traiectensi facultatem concedit percipiendi proventus beneficiorum vacantium et contradictores compescendi. Datum ut in alia, anno pontificatus ?.

**Translation to English:**

To Conrad, scholar of Strasbourg. It was presented before us on your behalf that, when we had previously sent our letters to various executors concerning the conferring of a prebend or other ecclesiastical dignity in the regions of Germany to you and 25 other clerics under various forms, and eventually, upon the vacancy of the Strasbourg prebend, each of you had it conferred upon yourselves by executors appointed to you. However, Gebehard, brother of the noble men, Counts of Freiburg, our chaplain, believing himself to have canonically obtained the prebend thus conferred upon him, and asserting that Walther of Gorolske, canon of Strasbourg, to whom the prebend had been conferred, did not allow him to enjoy peaceful possession of the prebend, obtained that he be summoned to our presence. But since the same Walther was absolved from the accusation of Gebehard by our authority through our beloved son Andrew, our nephew and chaplain, and because of this, Walther, considering himself the provost of Strasbourg, claims to have canonically obtained the prebend, you, fearing that prejudice might be generated against the right you believe to have in the same prebend, since it has not been discussed, requested that we provide paternal remedy for you in this matter. Although a matter conducted between others does not regularly prejudice another, we, inclined by your prayers, grant by the authority of these presents that no prejudice be generated to you in your right, if you hold any in the same prebend, by the process held between the aforementioned Gebehard and Walther and the sentence pronounced or by the apostolic confirmation, as is said, or by the fact that you have hitherto delayed to pursue your right in this matter. Given at Perugia, IX Kalends of August, in the tenth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Conrado scolastico Argentinensi indulget, ne aliquod praeiudicium in iure suo circa praeposituram Argentinensem generetur per processum inter Gebehardum et Waltherum habitum aut sententiam latam, etiamsi detulerit prosequi. Datum Perusii, IX Kalendas Augusti, anno decimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected bishop of Augsburg. The sincere devotion that our beloved sons, the noble men H. and H. of Kiburg, and other counts and nobles of Swabia bear towards the Roman Church induces us to extend our benevolent favor to their just petitions. Therefore, as you yourself have been and are diligent and fervent in magnificently promoting the affairs of the Church together with them, we, at the request of these nobles and in view of your merits, by the authority of this present letter, grant you a special grace, allowing you to receive for one year the revenues of prebends and benefices, even those involving the care of souls, that may become vacant in the city or diocese of Augsburg for up to three years, to be converted to the aid of said affairs. However, it is required that from the mentioned revenues so much be reserved that service may meanwhile be carried out by suitable vicars in the churches where such prebends or benefices are held. To no one, etc. of our concession, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the Kalends of January, in the eleventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa electo Augustensi concedit, ut proventus prebendarum et beneficiorum in civitate vel diocesi Augustensi vacantium per unum annum percipere valeat ad subsidium ecclesiastici negotii, tamen reservatis ad interim deserviendum per vicarios ydoneos. 1238, Kal. Ian., Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop and chapter of Constance. A grave crime and horrible deed, deserving of the wrath and hatred of God, which the noble man Walter of Klingnau of the Constance diocese did not fear to commit, capturing and detaining you, brother bishop, his own father and the pastor and lord of the souls of others in the city and diocese of Constance, without laying hands on him, and holding him captive for a long time, to the grave offense of God and the Apostolic See and to the shame of the entire clergy. Whenever this comes to our memory, it embitters our heart and grievously wounds and disturbs our soul. Although we have deemed it worthy to wield the sword of our power to avenge such injuries inflicted not only on you, brother bishop, but on us in you and on the Apostolic See, and to punish the audacity of such temerity and presumption, yet because we seek the life of sinners, not death, and desire repentance rather than vengeance, in the patience of our gentleness, we wish to test whether the aforementioned nobleman, coming to his senses and touched by repentance, is willing to exhibit amends of worthy satisfaction with humility of spirit and contrition of heart for such injuries. We command by our letters to our beloved son, the abbot of Kempten of the Constance diocese, to diligently warn and induce the nobleman on our behalf, that he should not delay making full satisfaction to you for all damages, injuries, grievances, and offenses inflicted upon you and the church of Constance within two months after his admonition. If the aforementioned nobleman does not care to obey the admonitions of the same abbot within the said time, we have determined by the authority of these presents that, wishing to avenge not only in the person of the nobleman but also in the persons of his own progeny, that no one of his lineage up to the fourth generation shall be admitted as a canon or cleric in the Constance or any other collegiate church of any city. And if it is presumed otherwise, we decree it null and void. Therefore, let no one violate our decree, etc. If anyone should, etc. Given at Perugia, the ninth of the Ides of July, in the tenth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo et capitulo Constantiensibus mandat, ut Walterum de Clingena ad plenam satisfactionem infra duos menses inducant pro iniuriis episcopo Constantiensi illatis; et si noluerit obtemperare, descendentes eius ad quartam generationem a beneficio ecclesiastico arcet. 1237, Iul. 11, Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To H., cardinal priest of the title of Santa Sabina, legate of the Apostolic See. On behalf of our dearest son in Christ, W., the illustrious king of the Romans, it was proposed before us that although we have given letters to some prelates of the kingdom of Germany and other ecclesiastical persons, mandating that they should admonish and effectively induce certain nobles of the same kingdom, who are supporters of C., the son of the late Fr., emperor of the Romans, to, within a certain period expressed in those letters, return to the devotion of the Church and restore to the aforementioned king the castles and fortifications of the empire they occupy, otherwise, they should deprive the sons, brothers, and relatives of the same, clerics and our chaplains, of prelatures, dignities, and other ecclesiastical benefits which they possess by our authority. However, certain indulgences have been presented by the aforementioned clerics and chaplains before the same prelates and persons, which allegedly were granted to them by the apostolic see, stating that the disloyalty of their fathers, brothers, and relatives should not impede them from retaining prelatures, dignities, and ecclesiastical benefits. Therefore, the apostolic mandate concerning these matters could not be executed as intended. For this reason, the same king humbly requested us to take care with apostolic diligence to provide for him in this matter, as this causes not a small impediment to the promotion of the Roman empire and the general business of the Church in those parts. We, therefore, inclined by the requests of the same king, mandate through apostolic writings to your discretion, that against such clerics and chaplains, especially those who provide support from ecclesiastical revenues and income to such relatives of the same king rebelling in this matter, you or another should proceed according to the content of the same letters, as you see fit. Given at Assisi, June 4, in the tenth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa H(umfredo), tituli Sanctae Sabinae presbytero cardinali, apostolicae sedis legato mandat, ut contra clericos et capellanos, qui consanguineos regis Romanorum ecclesiasticis proventibus adiuvant, procedat, indulgentiis apostolicis non obstantibus. 1236, Iun. 4, Assisii.

**Translation to English:**

Concerning the renowned kingdom of Sicily, which has long been subjected to dire and most severe servitude, we have often poured forth deep groans and bitter sighs. We constantly bear in mind the aim to restore, with the Lord's assistance, the ecclesiastical liberty there, which has been almost entirely obliterated, to its former state. This is especially urgent since the kingdom, being under the legal right and ownership of the Apostolic See, is currently without a king and has no hope of revival except through God and the Church. Therefore, after careful consideration with our brothers and upon their counsel, we decree that all laws, constitutions, statutes, ordinances, dispositions, commands, and all similar acts issued by Frederick, the former emperor and persecutor of its liberty, either before or after his deposition, as well as any customs introduced against these by him or his predecessors, kings of Sicily, or anyone else within the said kingdom, are null and void. We fully restore to each church of the kingdom, whether secular, regular, cathedral, or otherwise, as well as religious houses, the cities, castles, villages, lands, estates, possessions, people, vassals, and other goods and rights of which they were unjustly deprived by him or any of his sons or officials through inquiries, grants, sales, or exchanges, or by any other means, to be possessed by them henceforth entirely with all their rights and appurtenances. We also grant these churches and houses, and their prelates, the free power to repair and rebuild anew the cities, lands, villages, and castles destroyed or partially destroyed by the command of the same Frederick or his sons or supporters, and to have them repopulated. Furthermore, to ensure that the chosen and beloved city of Benevento, indeed the special treasury of the Apostolic See, which the perversity of the same Frederick, eventually overthrown by the mighty arm of divine virtue, destroyed with impious ferocity, may rejoice in deserving consolation through the help of the same See, we render it equal and akin to the aforementioned kingdom in all the preceding matters and all other liberties, nonetheless remitting all security obligations it is known to have previously made to anyone without the authority of the Apostolic See in prejudice of its ancient liberty. We strictly enjoin those who received such securities to release them without any delay or difficulty and not to presume to demand them henceforth. Therefore, let no man at all dare to infringe upon our statutes or contravene them in any way. If anyone presumes to attempt this, let him know he will be punished with severe retribution. Given at Perugia, August 23, in the tenth year.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa omnibus Christi fidelibus declarat omnes leges et constitutiones per Fridericum imperatorem in regno Siciliae contra libertates ecclesiasticas editas irritas esse, ac bona ecclesiarum restituit. Civitatem Beneventi specialem protectionem et libertates aequales cum regno Siciliae largitur. 1236, Aug. 23. Perusiae.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Lübeck. Before we transferred you from the Church of Sambia to the Church of Lübeck, we entrusted certain matters to your diligence, specifically regarding preaching the crusade in aid of our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, W., and some other affairs to be handled. We wish and command you through apostolic writings that you faithfully and prudently execute these matters as they were entrusted to you at that time; [disregard] contradictors, etc., notwithstanding if it has been granted by the Apostolic See to some from those parts that they cannot be excommunicated, suspended, or interdicted. Given at the Lateran, on the Nones of April, in the eleventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Lubicensi mandat, ut sollicitudinem super predicanda cruce in subsidium regis Romanorum et alia negotia sibi commissa fideliter exequatur, non obstantibus quibusdam exemptionibus concessis. 1237, Apr. 5, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Sambia, from the order of Friars Minor. The sincerity of the devoted of the Church is especially brought to fruition when the kindness of the Apostolic See is found ready and favorable in fulfilling their desires. Indeed, the beloved daughter in Christ, a noble woman M., widow of the late C., count palatine of Tuingen, as she has explained to us, entered into marriage with our beloved son, the noble man R., lord of Durne, who is devoted to the Roman Church, unaware, however, that this nobleman was related to the aforementioned count in the fourth degree of consanguinity. Therefore, on behalf of these noble persons, it was humbly requested from us to provide for this issue with the kindness of the Apostolic See. Thus, trusting in your discretion, we assign to you, who are said to be a close associate of our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious king of the Romans, W., by the tenor of these presents, that, having carefully considered all the circumstances, if you see it to be expedient for the business of the Church and the benefit of the said king, you may dispense with our authority with the aforementioned nobles, so that they may freely remain in the marriage thus contracted, notwithstanding such an impediment. Given at the Lateran, 10th December, in the eleventh year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Sambiensi de ordine fratrum Minorum mandat, ut, si negocio ecclesie ac utilitati W. regis Romanorum id videatur expedire, cum nobilibus M. et R. de Durne auctoritate sua dispenset, ut in matrimonio sic contracto non obstante consanguinitatis impedimento libere valeant permanere. 1237, Dec. 10. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Trani, 

The beloved son Palermus, archpriest of the church of St. Felix and canon of Murano, has shown us in his petition that some time ago, before the Kingdom of Sicily was subjected to ecclesiastical interdict by us, the church of Murano was without a pastor. The archpriest and the chapter of the said church, on the day appointed for the election, convened in the chapter house, having called all who were obliged, willing, and able to conveniently attend, as is customary, and having invoked the grace of the Holy Spirit, they canonically and unanimously elected him as their bishop and pastor. But Nicholas, called de Patrice, a cleric of Taranto, occupying the said church by mandate of the late Emperor F. of the Romans after a sentence of deposition was pronounced against him, got himself consecrated as bishop of the said Murano church, and presumed to hold it in such a manner to the detriment of his own salvation, the prejudice of the archpriest, and the scandal of many. Since the Consana church, to which the said Murano church is known to be subject by metropolitan right, is said to be vacant at present, he humbly petitioned us to confirm his election and mercifully grant him the gift of consecration through the apostolic see's benevolence.

Therefore, we command you to diligently inquire into the manner of the election, the qualifications of the electors, and the merits of the elected, and if you find that the election was canonically conducted for a suitable person, confirm it by our authority and confer upon him the gift of consecration. Ensure that obedience and due reverence are shown to him by his subjects, removing from the said church the aforementioned cleric or any other unlawful occupier. Otherwise, if the election is found to be invalid, make provision as necessary. We wish, however, that no prejudice be generated in the future against the said Consana church by this; notwithstanding the constitution concerning two days issued in the general council. 

Given at Assisi, 12th June, in the tenth year.

He has granted and gifted to you the stronghold of Camaranico in the diocese of Theatina, along with all its rights and appurtenances, as a fief.
