We, thus, moved by the sincere devotion that he has shown towards the apostolic see for a long time, incline to his supplication, and we grant you, by apostolic authority and special grace, the dispensation so that you may lawfully and freely hold the aforementioned stronghold and whatever your said father has legitimately granted or gifted to you, notwithstanding the aforesaid defect. No one, etc. of our dispensation — Given at Assisi, 19th May, in the eleventh year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Adenulpho de Luczenardo significat se, supplicationibus patris sui Conradi inclinatum, dispensare cum eo, ut Roccam de Camaranico a patre in feudum concessam, defectu natalium non obstante, licite obtinere possit. 1237, Mai. 19, Assisii.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishops and beloved sons, abbots, priors, deans, archdeacons, and other prelates and rectors of churches, and their chapters and colleges established in the lands of the noble man, the Margrave of Meissen. Since in the palace of the supreme King, the glorious Virgin continually acts as our advocate, gently pleading for us with her felicitous patronage for pardon, whom human excess sometimes gravely provokes to vengeance, her tongue of flesh should not be silenced from offering praises, but rather rise to the due gratitude for such a pleasant gift, so as to cautiously avoid the harm of destructive ingratitude. Indeed, our beloved son, the noble man, the Margrave of Meissen, reflecting in his mind with the appropriate sincerity, that he might openly express the devotion he holds towards her and honor her with fitting services as much as he is able, has composed a new chant for "Kyrie Eleison" and "Gloria in Excelsis Deo" for the clerics of his chapel to use during solemn masses in honor of the same Virgin; and because the chant presented to us on behalf of the Margrave, which we had performed in our presence, was found to be pleasing to God and acceptable to men, we have decided to approve it due to the inventor's devotion, which, when led by the Spirit of God, is not constrained by the rules of music, granting you the free faculty to sing it and have it sung in the aforementioned solemnities. For greater assurance, we enclose to you the "Kyrie Eleison" and "Gloria" under this chant, sealed with our bull. Given at the Lateran, on the tenth day before the Kalends of February, in the eleventh year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX episcopis, abbatibus, prioribus, decanis, archidiaconis et aliis prelatis ecclesiarum in terra Marchionis Misnensis facultatem concedit cantandi novum cantum in Missarum solemnitatibus pro Virgine Maria compositum a Marchione Misnensi. Dat. Laterani, X Kalendas Februarii, anno XI.

**Translation to English:**

To Jacob, Bishop of Metz. Since, as your brotherhood has informed us, you have so far undertaken such heavy burdens of debts for the affairs of the universal church as well as for receiving legates and envoys of the apostolic see, that the revenues of your bishopric are said to be insufficient to relieve them, we, inclined by your devoted supplications, wishing to support you with some solace of relief in this matter, by the authority of these presents, grant you that you may freely collect the revenues and incomes of dignities, prebends, and other ecclesiastical benefices, even those with the care of souls, within the city and diocese of Metz, for up to three years, once they become vacant, for one year, converting them to pay off such debts, with a suitable portion reserved from those revenues and incomes for the service of the said churches, notwithstanding the contrary custom or statute of the said churches, or any oath or confirmation by the apostolic see or any other established firmness, or any indulgence granted to any person, dignity, or place by the same see, which, if not expressly mentioned word for word in these presents, might impede or delay the effect of our grace in this matter. To no one etc. our concession etc. Given at the Lateran, 2nd of the Kalends of February, in the eleventh year. The schoolmaster of Toul was appointed as conservator for this; notwithstanding if any persons from those parts have been granted by the said see that they cannot be compelled to provision or be interdicted, suspended, or excommunicated by apostolic letters etc. up to: mention.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Iacobo episcopo Metensi, qui propter debitorum onera ex negotiis ecclesiae generalis et legatorum receptione gravatus est, concedit ut proventus et redditus dignitatum et beneficiorum ecclesiasticorum Metensis civitatis et diocesis per unum annum percipiat ad debita solvenda, non obstante contraria consuetudine vel statuto. 1238, Ian. 31, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the clergy and people of Pontis Curvae,

By the experience of your works, we are certain of the purity of faith and devotion you bear towards your mother, the Roman Church. Hence, we have rightly favored you with special grace, which brings honor to you and prosperity to your land. Therefore, as your presented petition contained, the late Fr., once Emperor of the Romans, had demolished a certain castle situated near the main church of Pontis Curvae, which was very harmful to the same church. Inclined by your devoted prayers, and wishing to provide for your peace with paternal solicitude, we strictly forbid by the authority of these presents that any castle or fortification be constructed there or elsewhere in your land by anyone in the future. Let no one, etc., violate our prohibition, etc. Given at Anagni, 10th Kalends of September, in the 12th year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa clero et populo Pontis Curvie mandat ne castrum vel aliqua munitio in terra eorumdem construatur. Anagnie, XII Kalendas Septembris, anno XII.

**English Translation:**

To the Bishop of Strasbourg. Although the marriage contract of union in the fourth degree of consanguinity and affinity is prohibited by sacred canons, the Apostolic See has been accustomed to grant dispensations in such a degree to those who have deserved well, when necessity or utility advises it. Indeed, after having read the petition presented to us on behalf of our beloved son, the noble man Walter of Eschibach, of the diocese of Constance, it contained that since once there were mortal enmities between his relatives and those of the noble woman Kunegunde, his wife, daughter of the noble lord, Count of Sulza, to put a final end to the innumerable evils that arose from the source of such hatred, Walter and Kunegunde, although they were related in the fourth degree of consanguinity, contracted marriage and have remained together in this marriage, having produced children. Since our dearest son in Christ, our illustrious king of the Romans, you, our venerable brother, the bishop of Constance, and our dear son, the abbot of Saint Gall have asserted through their letters that the aforementioned Walter is devoted to the Roman Church and can and wishes to be fruitful to the business of the general church and empire, we command that, at the request of the same king, you dispense with the aforementioned Walter and woman so that they may lawfully remain in this marriage thus contracted, and that their offspring may legitimately succeed to their goods — notwithstanding the impediment of such consanguinity —, with our authority, as you see according to God for the salvation of their souls and the aforesaid business. Given at the Lateran, on the Nones of January, in the eleventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Argentinensi mandat ut, ad petitionem regis Romanorum, dispenset Walterum de Eschibach et Kunegundem, uxorem eius, ut in matrimonio contracto licite permaneant et proles eorum in bonis legitime succedant, non obstante consanguinitatis impedimento. Datum Laterani, Nonis Ianuarii, anno XI.

**Translation to English:**

To Maria, formerly Empress of the Romans, widow of the illustrious memory of Otto, Emperor of the Romans, and beloved daughter of the noble man, Duke of Brabant, her uncle. When, as you have proposed to us, our most beloved son in Christ, W., the illustrious King of the Romans, has, out of royal munificence, granted you the right to make a testament and disposition over the fruits of all goods you possess in Holland and Zeeland, so that the fruits of these goods for one entire year after your death may be entirely converted to settle your debts, such that those whom you choose to obligate them to may receive them in full for the same year as if you were alive and possessing them: we, inclined by your supplications, holding what has been provided by the same King as worthy and agreeable, confirm it with apostolic authority. We fortify it up to the point: our confirmation, etc. Given at the Lateran, the fifth day before the Kalends of April, in the eleventh year. The abbot of the monastery of Fliderbeke, of the diocese of Liège, is appointed as conservator over this matter; notwithstanding if it has been granted by the Apostolic See to some that they cannot be excommunicated, suspended, or interdicted by letters of the same see, unless mention is made fully and expressly, or word for word, of this grant. Given at the Lateran, the fifth day before the Kalends of April, in the eleventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Mariae quondam Romanorum imperatrici, relictae Octonis imperatoris Romanorum, confirmat concessum ab W. rege Romanorum ut de fructibus bonorum in Hollandia et Zelandia testamentum condere possit, fructus illos post mortem ad solutionem debitorum convertendos, auctoritate apostolica ratificans. Dat. Laterani, V Kalendas Aprilis, anno XI.

**Translation to English:**

To Henry, Bishop of Hildesheim. You have asserted that you had to endure great burdens of debt for the defense of the rights of the empire and the Church of Hildesheim. Therefore, we, wishing to grant you a special favor because of this and at the request of our dearest son in Christ, W., the illustrious King of the Romans, who implores apostolic grace for you, grant you by the authority of these presents the free faculty to receive all the incomes and revenues of the first year of all ecclesiastical benefices that may become vacant within three years in the city and diocese of Hildesheim, to be applied to the payment of such debts, and also the faculty to restrain the contradictors by ecclesiastical censure with appeal set aside— notwithstanding if it has been granted by the apostolic see to some that they cannot be interdicted, etc. —; provided that in the meantime those benefices are not deprived of their due services. Given at Assisi, on the 12th of May, in the 11th year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Henrico episcopo Hildesemensi concedit facultatem percipiendi redditus primi anni beneficiorum ecclesiasticorum vacaturorum in civitate et diocesi Hildesemensi ad solvendos debitos, et contradictores per censuram ecclesiasticam compescendi, non obstante indulto ab apostolica sede. Datum Assisii, II Idus Maii, anno XIo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Sambiensis and the beloved sons, the preachers of the word of the cross in the kingdom of Alamannia. Since it is forbidden by the sacred canons that those who, going to tournaments to gather and recklessly display their strength, and die there, be given ecclesiastical burial, we do not intend to open a way for anyone to go to such tournaments, but we utterly detest them. However, if it happens that some, whom we despise, go to them, we are willing to provide a special grace remedy for those who have offered some assistance, according to their means and your prudent discretion, to our dearest son in Christ, W., the illustrious King of the Romans, in the common cause against Conrad, son of the late Frederick, former emperor of the Romans, and his supporters, or who have taken the sign of the cross in support of the same king against the aforementioned C. and his supporters for themselves or their predecessors. Desiring to provide in this matter, for the favor of the king and the general business which he pursues for the peace of the Christian people, we grant you authority by these presents that if it happens that any of them die there, you may, by our authority, grant through yourselves or others suitable for this purpose, that they or those for whom the heirs of such or their relatives and friends have provided this assistance, provided that manifest signs of penance appear in all of them, be given ecclesiastical burial; these presents to be valid for no more than three years. Given at the Lateran, on the thirteenth of the Kalends of March, in the eleventh year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Sambiensi et praedicatoribus verbi crucis in regno Alamanniae concedit auctoritatem, ut illis, qui in torneamentis decedunt et subsidium praestiterint regi Romanorum contra Conradum et fautores eius, si signa poenitentiae manifesta apparuerint, ecclesiastica sepultura concedatur. 1237, Feb. 17. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbots of Malumbrunens and Uterine Valley of the Cistercian Order, of the diocese of Speyer. Considering the sincere devotion, purity of faith, and merits of probity of our beloved son, the elect of Speyer, who, being a man noble in birth and manners, has made himself worthy of the grace and favor of the Apostolic See, to you, Abbot of Uterine Valley, and our venerable brother, the bishop of Constance, we directed our letters, as informed by him, concerning the provision to be made for him regarding some archbishopric or bishopric which he would deem acceptable in the kingdom of Germany under certain conditions. Although later, concerning what we commanded to be provided through our letters regarding archbishoprics, bishoprics, abbeys, and priories in various places, we have more prudently determined that churches, when it concerns their governance, should be provided for rather than individuals, and we have granted under certain conditions by apostolic authority the free power to provide and canonically ordain concerning all the aforementioned matters to those to whom the election, ordination, collation, or provision of the aforesaid pertains. This is notwithstanding any general or special letters obtained from the Apostolic See or its legates regarding any promotions or provisions, or any reservations, prohibitions, or nominations made or to be made by the authority of these letters, or processes carried out or to be carried out in the future by them, all of which we wish to be entirely devoid of force. We decree null and void anything done or presumed contrary to the tenor of our concession or the freedom of the rights or powers of patriarchs, archbishops, bishops, abbots, priors, and other prelates, as well as chapters, convents, and church colleges in this matter, by reason of any such letters. We also relax the sentences of interdict, suspension, and excommunication if they have been imposed by pretext of these letters hitherto, and which may hereafter be promulgated, considering them to be utterly null. Because, however, the same elect, advancing from virtue to virtue, ought to be deservedly promoted from grace to fuller grace, not wishing any prejudice to arise to him concerning the provision to be made by reason of this concession, statute, relaxation, and decree, so that when an archbishopric or bishopric becomes vacant in the kingdom of Germany, he may be provided for from it. We command you to proceed with making the said provision for the aforementioned archbishopric or bishopric for the same elect — notwithstanding the aforesaid concession, statute, relaxation, or decree — when they become vacant. If both cannot act, etc. Given at the Lateran, the Ides of November, in the eleventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbatibus Malumbrunensi et Uterine Vallis ordinis Cisterciensis Spirensis diocesis mandat ut, non obstante concessione, statuto, relaxatione aut decreto, provisionem de archiepiscopatu vel episcopatu in regno Alamannie vacante faciant electo Spirensi. 1237, Nov. 13. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Lübeck. On behalf of the noble man Gebehard, Count of Rothnech, from the diocese of Regensburg, it was humbly requested of us that, since he had previously entered into marriage with a noble woman, the widow of a certain H. de Randecht, unaware that H. was related to him in the fourth degree of consanguinity, and had subsequently had children with her, we should, out of the benevolence of the Apostolic See, grant dispensation for him to lawfully remain in the contracted marriage with the aforementioned noblewoman, especially since the separation of said marriage could not occur without causing serious scandal to many. Therefore, trusting fully in the Lord in your prudence, and inclined by the prayers of the count himself and of the noblewoman A., senior Duchess of Bavaria, of whom the count is said to be a special advisor, we commit to you by the authority of these presents that you may dispense in this matter by our authority, as you see fit according to God, if it pleases our beloved son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, W. Given at Anagni, on the Kalends of July, in the twelfth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Lubicensi mandat ut, precibus Gebehardi comitis de Rothnech et nobilis mulieris A. ducissae Bawariae senioris inclinatus, et si W. regi Romanorum illustri placuerit, auctoritate sua dispenset super matrimonio cum consanguinitate quarta contracto. 1238, Kal. Iul., Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the schoolmaster of the New Church outside the walls of Huxar, of the Paderborn diocese. Our beloved son, John, a canon of Lübeck, a cleric, and the beloved son of our dear in Christ, W., the illustrious king of the Romans, and brother-in-law of the noble man, the duke of Brunswick, is known to be distinguished by his praiseworthy conduct and life, and should be supported with the grace of our favorable kindness. Therefore, we, wishing to honor the said duke and our venerable brothers, the archbishop of Livonia and Prussia and the bishop of Roskilde, as well as the counts of Holstein, who have earnestly implored apostolic grace for him through affectionate letters, command that you provide for the said canon in one of the churches of the province of Bremen, whether cathedral or other, in a position of office or dignity, even if involving the care of souls, to whichever collation it pertains, if it is currently vacant or as soon as the opportunity arises, by our authority, or ensure through another that it is provided — notwithstanding if we have directed our letters for others in the church where provision is made for him, which, etc., as far as: generated, or if by order of the legates of the apostolic see some have been received there, to whom we wish him to be preferred in the acquisition of such office and dignity, as he ought to be by law, or that he is otherwise beneficed, or that we have otherwise written for him, or any indulgence granted in any form or expression of words by the apostolic see to any persons, places, or dignities of those parts, that they cannot be suspended or interdicted or excommunicated or compelled to receive any, etc., as far as: mention is made, or the constitution about two diets established in the general council, so that beyond the third or fourth, etc. — ; opposers —. For we nonetheless declare null and void whatever may be attempted contrary to the aforementioned. Given at the Lateran, on the fifth day before the Kalends of February, in the eleventh year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa (scholastico Nove Ecclesie extra muros Huxarienses Padeburgensis diocesis mandat, ut Iohanni canonico Lubicensi in aliqua ecclesiarum Bremensis provinciae provideat de personatu vel dignitate, vacantibus, auctoritate sua provisurus. 1228, Jan. 28, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Sambia. With all our desires focused on the advancement of the church's cause and the Roman Empire, we vigilantly and continuously care, and to ensure that, with the Lord's guidance, it may laudably succeed, we apply the utmost diligence, providing whatever efforts we can and also requesting the assistance of others. Therefore, trusting fully in the Lord in your fraternity, we grant you by the authority of these presents, that throughout the kingdom of Germany you may preach the word of the cross to the faithful of Christ, and to all who take up the sign of the cross for the aid of the church or our beloved son in Christ, W., the illustrious king of the Romans, against C., the son of the late Frederick, the Roman emperor, and his supporters, to grant them the remission of sins and the same privilege and immunity customarily granted by the apostolic see to those signed with the cross for the aid of the Holy Land, and to take them under the protection of the same see, and to appoint them protectors according to the usual form of the said see. Furthermore, you may grant ecclesiastical persons, who are marked with the sign of the cross against C. and his supporters, the license to pledge their ecclesiastical revenues and income up to three years, according to the indulgence of those signed for the support of the aforementioned land — notwithstanding any custom or statute fortified by any firmness — and also to summon parish priests, rectors, and clerics of the churches of the same kingdom with their congregations for the said cause, whenever you see fit, and, if necessary, to coerce them to attend your summoning by ecclesiastical censure — by no means hindered by any privileges or apostolic indulgences. And so that a greater multitude of people may gather to hear the aforementioned word, we mercifully relax twenty or forty days from the penances imposed on all truly penitent and confessed who attend your preaching. Given at the Lateran, on the 14th of the Kalends of March, in the eleventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Episcopo Sambiensi auctoritate dat facultatem proponendi verbum crucis in regno Alamannie et concedendi indulgentias consuetas crucesignatis ob succursum Terre Sancte, tum pro auxilio ecclesie et Wfillelmil regis Romanorum contra C! filium condam Frederici et fautores suos; cum facultate convocandi clerum et plebem et relaxandi penitencias. Datum Laterani, XIIII Kalendas Martii, anno XI.

Translation to English:

To the Commune of the city of Basel. The sincerity of your devotion and the readiness of your faith deserve that, as we pursue you with apostolic favor, we protect you from burdens as much as we can with God's help. Therefore, since, as our venerable brother the bishop of Basel has made sure to inform us, you have stood by him with all your strength, in his indefatigable efforts for the cause of the universal Church and the Empire against the former emperor Frederick and his son Conrad and their supporters, and continue to support him in pursuing this cause, for which you are known to have incurred the hatred of many, such that you cannot safely leave your city for any great distance: we, wishing to protect you from future burdens, and inclined by the prayers of the bishop, grant you by the authority of these presents that you cannot be summoned to judgment outside the city of Basel, either collectively or individually, by letters of the apostolic see or its legates, as long as you persist in the devotion to the Church, unless such apostolic letters make a special and express mention of this indulgence word for word. Let no one etc. of our concession etc. Given at Assisi, the 24th of May, in the 11th year. The bishop of Basel has been appointed conservator over this matter; notwithstanding if some, by apostolic grant, cannot be excommunicated, interdicted, or suspended. Given as above.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa communi civitatis Basiliensis indulget, ne extra Basiliam ad iudicium trahi possint per apostolicas litteras, pro devotionis ecclesie perseverantia, nisi huiusmodi littere specialem mentionem faciant. 1237, Maii 24, Assisii.

**Translation to English:**

To Master Jordan, our subdeacon and notary, governor of Campania and the Maritime Province. If we apply our vigilant care regarding other churches so that their rights do not suffer losses but remain intact, we could certainly be justly noted for excessive negligence if we did not extend all diligence to the Roman Church, the mother and mistress of all others, which we specially administer by the will of the Lord, to ensure that its goods are not diminished by any occasion or occupied by any rash detention. Truly, because many of its rights, under the pretext of grace granted sometimes concerning some of them, are known to be considerably diminished, some even suppressed and vastly obscured, and some almost entirely lost, we, taking necessary caution from past losses for the future and instructed by previous losses, as to how we should subsequently avoid similar issues, because certain revenues, incomes, and rights, which the said Church holds in Campania and the Maritime Province, have been granted by us and our predecessors as grace, but not perpetually, to some individuals, to prevent the detriment of the same Church in this matter, having held a provident deliberation with our brothers and upon their counsel, we revoke all concessions, donations, commissions, and graces regarding the revenues, incomes, jurisdictions, dominions, and rights of the said Church in those parts of Campania and the Maritime Province, or in the castles of Trevi, Anticoli, Guarcino, Vico, and Collepardo, or in the cities of Ferentino and Veroli, or in other places of the aforesaid regions, made by us or the same predecessors or by governors who have been in those parts at any time, to any persons, barons, knights, or others, whether they are Romans, Campanians, or Maritimans or others, either for their lifetime or for a certain time or until our pleasure or otherwise, completely under apostolic authority, declaring those and any apostolic letters and letters of those governors concerning them to no longer be valid, and commanding firmly that to you and the governors who after you shall be in the same parts, full responses be made regarding the aforesaid revenues, incomes, jurisdictions, dominions, and rights — notwithstanding the aforementioned concessions, donations, commissions, and graces and letters — and full attention be given in all these matters. To no one etc. let anyone infringe the page of our revocation, constitution, and command etc. Given at Assisi, on the sixth day before the Nones of July, in the eleventh year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Magistro Iordano subdiacono et notario suo, Campaniae Maritimaeque rectori, mandat ut omnes concessiones, donationes, commissiones et gratias de proventibus, redditibus, iurisdictionibus, dominiis et iuribus ecclesiae Romanae in Campania et parte Maritima, factas ab ipso vel predecessoribus suis, revocet, et plenarie de iisdem respondeatur. Datum Asisii, VI Nonas Iulii, anno XI.

Translation to English:

To the bishop of Eichstätt. On behalf of our beloved son, the noble man Godfrey, lord of Sulzbürg, of your diocese, it was presented before us that he, while striving with all his might for the promotion of the general church affair against C., the son of the late Frederick, former emperor, and his supporters, had managed to bring back to the church's devotion the noble man W., butler of Clingenburg, of the Würzburg diocese, who had been a known adversary. To be better able to fight the church's enemies with this butler, he had sworn a bodily oath that his son Ulrich, still in the cradle, would take the younger daughter of the said butler as his wife when he reached lawful age. However, since the said butler, like a dog returning to his vomit (Prov. 26:11), has become, as it is said, a public persecutor of the church, committing worse deeds than before by damnably adhering to the supporters of said C., it was requested of us that we should absolve the aforementioned Godfrey from such an oath, especially since the said boy has not yet reached the age of five. Therefore, we command that, if it is so, you, by our authority, or another, should absolve the same Godfrey from the said oath and declare him absolved from it. Given at Assisi, on the Ides of May, in the eleventh year.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Eistetensi mandat ut Godfridum, dominum de Solzburch, ab iuramento dato de matrimonio filii sui Ulrici cum filia pincernae W. de Clingenburch absolvat, cum hic ecclesiae persecutor factus sit. 1237, Mai. 15, Assisii.

**Translation to English:**

To the provost of the church of Saint Arbogast outside the walls of Strasbourg. Eberhard, Cunrad, and Otto of Entrugen, canons of Strasbourg, have shown us through their petition that our beloved son, the deacon cardinal of Saint George at Velum Aureum, and later our venerable brother, the archbishop of Cologne, while serving in the office of legation in the regions of Germany, issued various sentences of interdict, suspension, and excommunication against the prelates and clerics of those parts who would receive someone into their churches for vacant prebends on their own initiative or have them as canons so received, as well as against many executors concerning certain provisions and sub-delegated by them, and also against conservators appointed by the apostolic see, and generally against all who would oppose those to whom they were appointed. However, the same canons, fearing they might have incurred some of these sentences, humbly petitioned us to provide for them with paternal care concerning this matter. Therefore, we command that, after receiving from the same canons a suitable guarantee to obey the mandates of the church, you absolve them, by our authority and according to the form of the church, from such sentences as a precaution, and dispense with them concerning any irregularity they may have contracted from it, as you see fit according to God for the salvation of their souls. Given at the Lateran, on the 16th Kalends of April, in the 11th year.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa preposito ecclesiae Sancti Arbogasti extra muros Argentinenses mandat, ut Eberhardum, Cunradum et Octonem de Entrugen, canonicos Argentinenses, ab interdicti, suspensionis et excommunicationis sententiis auctoritate ecclesiae absolvat et cum eis super irregularitate dispense, postquam idoneam cautionem de parendo mandatis ecclesiae receperit. 1237, Mart. 17, Laterani.

**English Translation:**

To Brother Willelmus de Eika of the Order of Preachers, chaplain of our most beloved son in Christ, W., the illustrious king of the Romans.

With all our affections and constant diligence, we strive to promote the cause of the universal church and the Roman Empire, and so that this endeavor may reach the desired completion, we apply diligent and careful effort, providing as much assistance as we can and also seeking the help of others.

Therefore, having full confidence in your discretion in the Lord, we command you by the authority of these presents, that through yourself or others, both religious and secular, whom you deem suitable for this, you propose to the faithful in the kingdom of Germany the word of the cross according to the prudence granted to you and those you entrust this to by God. Encourage them with diligent and earnest exhortations to courageously take up the sign of the cross against Conrad, the son of the late Frederick, formerly emperor of the Romans, and his supporters.

For we, relying on the mercy of Almighty God and the authority of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul, and from the power of binding and loosing granted to us by God despite our unworthiness, grant to all those who undertake this labor usefully and effectively in their own persons and at their own expense, and to those who, not in their own persons but at their own expense according to their means and abilities, send suitable warriors, as well as to those who, even if at others' expense, assume this burden in their own persons, the remission of their sins, of which they are truly contrite in heart and confess with their mouth. We desire them to enjoy the same privilege and immunity granted in the general council to those who aid the Holy Land. We also grant this remission to all those who, commensurate with their means and the devotion of their hearts, provide or contribute suitable counsel and assistance against the same Conrad and his supporters from their own goods.

Given at Perugia, on the fourth day before the Ides of February, in the tenth year [of our pontificate].

To the same. So that the talent of the word entrusted to you by the Lord may be multiplied in His service when He asks you to account for it, we have decided to entrust to your discretion the preaching of the cross against Conrad, the son of the late Frederick, formerly emperor of the Romans, and his supporters, persecutors of the church, throughout the kingdom of Germany by apostolic authority. You are authorized to carry out this preaching through yourself or others whom you find suitable, to grant crosses to those who sign up for this cause, and to bestow the privileges and indulgences that are given to those crossing into the Holy Land for aid. You also have full authority to grant a remission of forty days to all truly penitent and confessed who come to your preaching or that of those to whom you entrust it, and likewise to impose ecclesiastical censure on those who perhaps dare to impede you or them in these matters.

Given as above. In the same manner, [addressed] to John of the Order of Friars Minor, bishop of Sambium.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Fratri Willelmo de Eika ordinis Predicatorum mandat per auctoritatem presentium ut in regno Alamanie verbum crucis proferat, fideles contra Conradum, natum condam Friderici imperatoris, et suos fautores incitans, cum indulgentia simili illis qui Terre Sancte succurrent; dat. Perusii, IIII Idus Februarii, anno decimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Salerno:

As we have learned, you appointed Benedict, who acts as the abbot of the monastery of Saint Leonard of the Salerno diocese of the order of Saint Benedict, as the abbot of the same monastery due to the favor or command of the late Conrad, son of the late Frederick, former Emperor of the Romans. We order that if this is true, you remove the said Benedict entirely from that monastery and appoint our beloved son, Brother Raone, prior of the monastery of Saint Stephen of the small island of Ventotene, a man indeed prudent and discreet and circumspect in spiritual and temporal matters, as the abbot and pastor of the aforesaid monastery of Saint Leonard by our authority. Ensure that he receives due obedience and reverence from the prior, convent, and subjects of his monastery, as to their spiritual father and pastor. Those who oppose this order shall be dealt with accordingly.

Given at Anagni, on the 11th of September, in the 12th year of our pontificate.

---

**Regesto in Latin:**

*Gregorius IX* archiepiscopo *Salernitano* mandat *abbatem monasterii Sancti Leonardi* amovere Benedictum et *instituere fratrem Raonem* abbatem ex auctoritate apostolica. *Dat. Anagnie, III Idus Septembris, anno XII.*

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Basel. You have informed us that sometimes using the authority of the Apostolic See and its legates, and at other times by those to whom the granting belongs, certain prelacies and clerics are given prebends, dignities, and other ecclesiastical benefices of your city and diocese. The relatives of these prelacies and clerics, supported by their counsel, assistance, or favor, grow stronger against the devout members of the church, thus frequently impeding the business of the church. Therefore, you have requested an apostolic remedy for this matter.

Hence, we command that, if this is indeed the case, you, in our authority, or another designated by you, should remove such prelacies and clerics from their dignities, prebends, and ecclesiastical benefices. You should ensure these dignities, prebends, and benefices are entrusted to suitable and devout persons for the church by those to whom their presentation belongs, provided they are devout to the church. However, if those to whom their presentation belongs are not devout to the church, you should, under our authority, provide for these dignities, prebends, and benefices to suitable persons and those devoted to the Roman Church, by you or another, placing them in physical possession and defending them once inducted, notwithstanding if there have been any indulgences granted by the Apostolic See preventing excommunication, suspension, or interdict, or any provision of these dignities, prebends, or benefices by letters of the said see without full and express word-for-word mention of such an indulgence, or any indulgence of the said see that could impede or delay this being not fully expressed or inserted herein; those opposing this should be dealt with accordingly.

Given at Assisi, on the eighth of the Kalends of June, in the twelfth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Basiliensi mandat ut, si veri sunt, prelatis et clericis suae civitatis et diocesis, quorum consanguinei adversus devotos ecclesiae invalescunt, dignitates et beneficia ecclesiastica auctoritate apostolica adimat et personis idoneis conferat, non obstantibus quibusdam privilegis. Datum Assisii, VIII Kalendas Iunii, anno XII.

Translation to English:

Bishop, newly elected but yet unconfirmed, legate of the apostolic see. Since our dearest son in Christ, Otakar, the illustrious king of Bohemia, as we have learned from his own indication, desires to be crowned with the diadem of the kingdom, and because the Archbishop of Mainz, from whose hands the king ought to receive the crown, is said to be bound by the chain of excommunication through our beloved son H., Cardinal Priest of the title of St. Sabina, then legate of the apostolic see, we wish and command you by the authority of these presents, that you ensure the benefit of absolution is granted to the same archbishop, so that he might freely proceed to the coronation of the same king, provided that he satisfies regarding those matters for which he is held excommunicated, according to the form of the Church. But if he refuses to make satisfaction, you shall, by our authority, instruct the beloved sons, the chapter of Mainz, that they should, in the place of the archbishop and in the name of the Church of Mainz, have the same king crowned by someone from among the suffragans of his church. And if the aforementioned chapter is unwilling to accomplish this, you shall commit this task by the same authority to one of his suffragans or to another bishop whom you recognize as suitable for this purpose, to execute the office or ministry of the coronation in the place of the same archbishop. Given at the Lateran, on the 8th of April, in the 11th year of our pontificate.

Regesto in Latin:

Pope (Name of the Pope not specified) B. electo, legato apostolicae sedis mandat, ut Otacharum regem Boemiae per Maguntinensem archiepiscopum, vinculo excommunicationis innodatum, coronari permittat, dummodo satisfaciat. Quod si archiepiscopus recusaverit, praecipit capitulo Maguntino, ut per aliquem de suffraganeis regem coronent, vel alii idoneo pontifici hoc committat. Datum Laterani, VI Idus Aprilis, anno XI.

**Translation to English:**

To the provost of the church of Saint Mary in Erfurt of the Mainz diocese. Our beloved son Wigger, dean of Halberstadt, has explained to us that, at the request of the late, esteemed Henry, King of the Romans, we directed our letters to the dean and schoolmaster of the church of Paderborn so that they might provide for the said dean some dignity, prebend, or office in one of the churches of the city or diocese of Halberstadt, cathedral or otherwise, if it was vacant or as soon as the opportunity arose, despite any opposition, etc. However, the same dean has not yet obtained any benefit from such grace. Therefore, not wishing the said dean to be disappointed in the hope he has conceived from this grace, we command you to proceed with the execution of our mandate concerning this matter, either by yourself or through another, according to the content of the letters directed to the said dean and schoolmaster. For we decree null and void anything that may be attempted contrary to the tenor of our mandate concerning this matter. Given at Anagni, 23rd of August, in the twelfth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa preposito ecclesiae sanctae Mariae in Erfordia mandat ut Wiggero decano Alberstadensi in aliqua dignitate aut officio provideat, decretans irritum quidquid contra mandatum fiat. 1238, Aug. 23. Anagnia.

**Translation to English:**

To Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. Since our venerable brother, the archbishop of Prussia, to whom we long ago commended the bishopric of Lübeck for his support, has established, as we have learned, his seat in a suitable place where he can reside and be comfortably sustained from the archiepiscopal revenues: We, wishing to provide for our venerable brother L. de Diesta, of the Order of Friars Minor and bishop of Samland, for whom we have already written at the request of our dearly beloved son in Christ, the illustrious King W. of the Romans, as stated more fully in the letters composed on this matter, command you to revoke the commendation or concession made to the said archbishop and absolve the same bishop from the obligation by which he is bound to the church of Samland. You are to appoint him by our authority as bishop and pastor to the church of Lübeck, granting him full administration of the spiritual and temporal affairs of the said church, and moreover, granting him the license to transfer himself to the said church. You shall ensure that the obedience and due reverence by the chapter and clergy of the city and diocese of Lübeck are rendered to him, either by yourself or through another. Let those who oppose this be silenced, notwithstanding any concessions by the apostolic see to the contrary, such as exemptions from excommunication, suspension, interdiction, or being called to account outside certain locations, or the constitution of two days' journey established in the general council. Given at the Lateran, 4th day before the Nones of March, in the eleventh year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Petro Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali mandat, ut commendationem episcopatus Lubicensis a Prussiae archiepiscopo revocet et episcopum Sambiensium, L. de Diesta, ad Lubicensem ecclesiam transferat, plenam administrationem ei concedens, 1238, Mart. 4, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To Master Henry of Nicasell, canon of the church of Saint German of Speyer. Having appeared in our presence, you reported that, due to your devotion and pure faith towards the Apostolic See, you have endured severe labors and expenses with a manly spirit and constancy, thereby incurring a considerable amount of debt. Therefore, you humbly requested us to mercifully provide for you in this matter. We, therefore, considering the request of our beloved son Brother Theoderic, master of the hospital of Saint Mary of the Teutons in Germany, who earnestly sought apostolic grace on your behalf, his companion, agree to your supplications. We grant you the authority to pledge the revenues of your prebend of the church of Saint German of Speyer beyond the year of grace, which is traditionally due to the canons of the said church upon their death, so that you may bind these revenues for a period of two years in such a way that if you resign or pass away, these revenues may be fully converted to the payment of your debts — notwithstanding any contrary custom or statute, secured by any degree of firmness — by the authority of these presents. Let no one etc. of our concession etc. Given at Anagni, 15th June, in the eleventh year. The provost of the church of Worms is appointed as conservator in this matter; — notwithstanding if it has been granted by the Apostolic See to some that they cannot be suspended, interdicted, or excommunicated unless a full and express mention is made of this indult granted to them, either word for word or in our letters. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Magistro Henrico de Nicasell, canonico ecclesie sancti Germani Spirensis, concedit facultatem obligandi proventus prebende sue ad solvendum debita, non obstante consuetudine contraria. 1237, Iun. 15, Anagnie.

Translation to English:

To G., Cardinal Deacon of Saint Eustace, legate of the Apostolic See. Since we have deemed it necessary to entrust to your prudence the matter of the kingdom of Sicily as something most dear and foremost, choosing your robust shoulders to bear the weight of such great responsibility, we commit to you our duties in the same kingdom with the full office of legation, so that you may be able to execute this matter more freely and effectively, being fortified with increased authority regarding it. Thus, in the said kingdom, concerning the aforementioned matter and all others, both spiritual and temporal, you may act, dispose, ordain, establish, and command as our vicar and legate of the Apostolic See, as we could ourselves if we were present there in person. You have full power to restrain any detractors and rebels with spiritual and temporal censure— notwithstanding any apostolic privileges or indulgences, which we do not wish to confer any benefit to anyone in this matter, with appeals postponed. Therefore, be vigilant, effective, and diligent in the execution of this matter, so that through your tireless diligence, with the assistance of the Most High, it may advance to desired success and reach a prosperous conclusion. Thus, you will deserve great reward in heaven, multiple honor from the universal church, and sublime praises of laud from the faithful peoples. Given at Anagni, on the 17th day before the Kalends of October, in the twelfth year [of our pontificate].

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa G. Sancti Eustachii diacono cardinali, legato apostolicae sedis, regni Siciliae negotium cum pleno legationis officio committit. 1238, Sept. 15. Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To Master John of St. German, our subdeacon and chaplain. Our beloved daughter in Christ, Marotta, abbess of the monastery of St. Mary of Capua of the order of St. Benedict, sister of the noble man Aymon of Aquino, devoted to us and the Roman Church, has presented to us that our venerable brother, the bishop of Alatri, by mandate of our beloved son, P., deacon cardinal of St. George at the Golden Veil, then legate of the Apostolic See in the kingdom of Sicily, appointed her as abbess to the then vacant monastery. We, approving and ratifying what was done by the bishop in this matter, confirmed it by apostolic authority, instructing the same legate through our letters to bestow the gift of blessing upon her. The aforementioned bishop, at the legate's mandate, conferred this gift upon her. Subsequently, however, Altruda of Preturo, a nun of the same monastery, claiming to have been elected abbess by the convent and having her election confirmed by the chapter of the church of Capua, a dispute arose over the abbacy of the monastery between Marotta and Altruda. Initially, we assigned this matter to be heard by the bishop of Sabina, of blessed memory, and then, after his death, to our beloved son, Master Martin the Spaniard, our chaplain. Although there was litigation over the abbacy for some time, eventually, while the dispute was still pending, Altruda departed from this life. Therefore, Marotta humbly petitioned us to extend our usual kindness in this matter. We, thus inclined by her supplications, wishing the provision made for the monastery by the authority of the legate to stand firm, instruct you to confirm the provision by our authority and to correct any defect, if any existed, from the fullness of our power, removing any unlawful holder from the monastery, and to induct her, either by yourself or another, into possession of the abbacy, defending her once inducted, and ensuring that due obedience and reverence are rendered to her by the persons of the monastery; opponents are to be ignored. Given at the Lateran, 6th of the Kalends of February, in the 13th year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Magistro Iohanni de Sancto Germano subdiacono et capellano suo mandat, ut provisionem Marottae in abbatissam monasterii sanctae Mariae de Capua, factam auctoritate legati, confirmet et defectum, si quis extitit, suppleat, eamque in possessionem inducat, contradictores non obstantibus. Dat. Laterani, VI Kalendas Februarii, anno pontificatus XIII.

**Translation to English:**

To Nicholas, the minor, Roman citizen, son of the late Nicholas Perini of Anagni, Roman citizen. It was proposed on your behalf before us that between Pandulf, your brother, a Roman citizen, and Andrew, son of Roger the scribe, a citizen of Anagni, concerning the matter that Pandulf claimed to be your legitimate tutor, while Andrew claimed to be the appointed tutor, a dispute was brought before Gerard Filocari, the palatine judge and vicar of our beloved noble son, the senator of the city. The said judge, having understood the merits of the case and observed the legal order, issued a definitive sentence in favor of the said Pandulf; although an appeal was made on behalf of the said Andrew, Bartholomew Angeli of Rome, a Roman citizen judge, reasonably confirmed the said sentence with the authority of the senator, as it is more fully contained in the public documents drawn up on this matter. Therefore, you humbly petitioned us to fortify the said sentence with apostolic authority. Therefore, we, inclined by your entreaties, considering the sentence as just, approve and confirm it with apostolic authority, and fortify it, addressing any deficiency in it because Andrew is said to be under paternal authority and his father's consent in the said matter was not obtained, supplementing from the plenitude of power without prejudice to others' rights. To no one etc. of our confirmation and supplementation etc. Given at the Lateran, on the 11th day before the Kalends of May, in the eleventh year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Nicolao pupillo, civi Romano, sententiam de tutela inter Pandulfum fratrem eius et Andream filium Rogerii, a Bartholomeo Angeli iudice confirmatam, auctoritate apostolica roborat et confirmat, plenitudine potestatis interveniente defectu supplens. Datum Laterani, XI Kalendas Maii, anno XI.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Philip of Acerno, a spirit of wiser counsel. Since, as has been proposed on your behalf before us, you intend to return to the devotion of the Mother Church, we, greatly commending your praiseworthy intention and wishing to strengthen your position with appropriate favors and increase it with due graces, are inclined by your supplications to confirm by apostolic authority the city of Acerno and its castle, and the castles of Rotunda, Castro Novo, and Viario, half of Vetri with its castle, as well as the fiefs and possessions you hold and possess in Gifono and Campania, and the castles of Consane, Salerno, and the diocese of Acerno, with all rights, honors, men, and appurtenances thereof, and all other goods you currently hold and possess, to you, returning to and persevering in the devotion of the Church, and to your heirs in perpetuity, etc., as far as: we confirm. Let no one etc., our confirmation etc. Given at Anagni, August 17, in the twelfth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro Philippo de Acerno civitatem Acerni et roccam eius, castra Rotundae, Castri Novi, Viarii, medietatem Vetri cum rocca eius, feuda et possessiones in Gifono et Campania, et in castris Consane, Salernitanae et Acernensis diocese, cum iuribus, honoribus, hominibus et pertinentiis confirmat, ad ecclesiae devotionem redeunti et in ea manenti, in perpetuum. Dat. Anagnie, XVI Kal. Septembris, anno XII.

**Translation to English:**

For perpetual memory and observance. Against the grievances inflicted upon subjects by prelates in the matter of visitations, due to the burdens associated with procurations, canonical institutes have wisely provided regulations regarding the number of attendants and the excess of provisions, the immoderate feasting, and other extravagances, by establishing that due moderation should be observed, so that prelates would not excessively demand, nor subjects be unduly burdened in offering, and that the visitation might be conducted for the salvation and joy of souls, and not for the affliction and annoyance of the subjects. Nevertheless, because some complaints are still being heard regarding such procurations, we, wishing to provide with pastoral solicitude that any occasion for burdens may be entirely removed and that any cause for murmuring may cease, by apostolic authority decree that procurations should be provided moderately in victuals and other necessities to archbishops, bishops, archdeacons, and other prelates visiting personally from the churches and places visited, so that these, according to the common estimation of things in each place or the expenses incurred for these, may not exceed the sum or value of four marks of silver in any procuration, provided that according to the greater or lesser number of attendants and persons appointed for the greater or lesser prelates in the Lateran Council, expenses of these procurations may be made up to that sum or less. But in places where there is greater fertility or abundance of things and where the revenues or ecclesiastical resources are lesser, less should be expended according to the greater abundance of necessities and the smallness of revenues in these procurations. If, however, more has been expended in such procurations, the prelates receiving them will be compelled to restore them for the benefit of the churches from which they have received them, and those who have provided them will be compelled to give from their own to the poor double what has thus been expended beyond, with another penalty imposed if it seems necessary; nevertheless, all other statutes generally made for such visitations and procurations shall remain always in effect. To no one, etc. our constitution, etc. Given at the Lateran, February 28th, in the eleventh year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa universis ecclesiarum prelatis mandat, ne procurationes ratione visitationis onerosae fiant, statuens ut expensae in victualibus et necessaries quatuor marcarum argenti summam non excedant, et quod superflua restitui debeant ecclesiis aut pauperibus erogari. 1238, Feb. 28, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Albric of Romano. Those who suggest to you or publicly declare among the people that we have engaged in reconciliation negotiations with Ezzelino of Romano, which would derogate from the honor of the Catholic faith, the honesty of the Church, and the benefits of the devoted, strive to weaken the strength of your spirit and violate the constancy of your devotion. Therefore, son, notice the cunning ways of men exercising their methods for the subversion of the faithful, and recognize that neither with that man nor with another on his behalf do we have nor will we ever have, by the grace of God, such negotiations. Be confidently assured that if ever he, which we scarcely believe, should strive to deserve any mercy through fitting penitence of humility, he will never be able to reach any point through our clemency or any scheme of his cunning or simulation that what has been granted to you by us or by our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, William, or established for your benefit and confirmed by the Apostolic See, might be changed in any way. We decree by the authority of these presents that all these shall remain perpetually valid and unchangeable, notwithstanding any contrary concessions, constitutions, or remissions. For which reason, we have judged it fitting to grant you these letters as a token of our constitution and promise. Given at Anagni, on the Ides of August, in the twelfth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro Albrico de Romano scribit, negans se cum Ezelino de Romano tractatus reconciliationis habere, et confirmat omnia concessa vel constituta pro eius commodo a sede apostolica confirmata manere perpetuo firma. Anagnie, Idibus Augusti, anno XII.

**Translation to English:**

To the diocese of Penne. Due to the merits of your devotion and purity of faith, we gladly consent to your requests and hear you. Considering, therefore, the steadfastness of your loyalty and the sincere devotion you have had and still have towards us and the Roman Church, as we have learned, and because of this, you are said to have suffered many damages and dangers to your persons and properties from the late C., son of the late Emperor Frederick, and his brother Frederick of Antioch. Therefore, we deem it worthy that those who are oppressed by various persecutions should find solace in the comfort of our grace. We receive your persons, along with the castle, possessions, rights, appurtenances, and other goods, under the protection of the Apostolic See and ours, securing them thus. We keep the castle and its possessions always in our dominion, granting you by the authority of these presents that you enjoy the same liberties and immunities known to be held by the cities and castles of our domain in the Kingdom of Sicily. Let no one violate this protection and concession of ours. Given at Anagni, on the 4th day before the Kalends of September, in the 12th year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa diocesim Pennensem sub protectione apostolica suscipit propter fidelitatem et devotum affectum erga Romanam Ecclesiam, confirmans libertates et immunitates similes iis quae civitates et castra regni Siciliae habent. 1255, Aug. 29, Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Sambiensis. On behalf of our dearest son in Christ, W., the illustrious King of the Romans, it was proposed before us that our beloved son, Hlugol, Cardinal Priest of the Title of St. Sabina, then a legate of the Apostolic See in those regions, had dispensed with some nobles of the Kingdom of Germany regarding the collection of tithes, which according to the custom of the country, they held in fief or as allodial or quasi-hereditary right from ancient times, allowing them to retain the fruits thus far received and to be received from them for as long as they lived, provided they took up the sign of the cross for the common aid of the said king and the church, as it is said to be fully contained in the letters drawn up to this effect and sealed with the cardinal's seal. Therefore, inclined by the prayers of the king, we have deemed what was providently done by the cardinal in this matter to be valid and pleasing, and we have decided to confirm it by apostolic authority. Furthermore, we grant you the faculty, by the authority of these presents, to dispense with such persons in the same manner, as you and the said cardinal shall determine to be expedient for the support of the same king, with such dispensation lasting only until he has obtained the imperial diadem. No one, etc., of our confirmation and concession, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the sixth day before the Nones of March, in the eleventh year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Sambiensi mandat ut, inclinatione precibus regis Romanorum, dispensationem quam cardinalis Hugolinus super perceptione decimarum nobilium Alamannie fecit, confirmet et ipse dispensandi facultatem tribuit, dummodo in subsidium regis et ecclesiae signum crucis assumant, dispensatione durante usque ad adeptum imperii diadema. Datum Laterani, VI Nonas Martii, anno XI.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of the monastery of Liess, of the order of Saint Benedict, in the diocese of Cambrai. The merits of the devotion with which you are known to venerate the Roman Church, and the eager willingness with which, as we have heard, you are said to have rendered yourself favorable to our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious king of the Romans, W., intercede on your behalf. Therefore, it is fitting that you be protected by apostolic favor against the troubles of harassment, which sometimes do not proceed from charity. Hence, we, by the authority of these presents, grant you that no ordinary may pronounce a sentence of excommunication, suspension, or interdict upon you without a manifest and reasonable cause and a special mandate from the apostolic see, containing the full tenor of this indulgence word for word. For we declare that any sentences, processes, or anything else attempted against the content or intention of this present indulgence by any ordinary or delegate, subdelegate or executor shall have no force. No one is permitted to infringe upon our grant, etc.; these presents shall remain valid for a decade, etc.! Given at Anagni, the eighth day before the Kalends of August, in the thirteenth year of our pontificate. The prior of Saint James in Liège is appointed as the conservator for this matter.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa (nomine non indicato) abbati monasterii Liessensis ordinis sancti Benedicti dioecesis Cameracensis indulget, ut nullus ordinarius in eum absque manifesta et rationabili causa excommunicationis, suspensionis vel interdicti sententiam sine speciali mandato sedis apostolicae valeat promulgare, et sententias aut processus contra indultum attentatos vires non habere decernit. Anagnie, VIII Kalendas Augusti, anno tertio decimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the community of the city of Münster. Due to the merits of your devotion, etc., we hear you. Since, as was presented before us on your behalf, it is not safe for you to venture to remote parts from your city because of the dangers of wars and the incursions of robbers and enemies, without peril to your persons and possessions, we, inclined by your devout supplications and those of our venerable brother, the bishop of Münster, wishing to provide beneficially for your peace in this matter, by the authority of these presents, grant you that you cannot be summoned to appear in judgment, collectively or individually, beyond the district of the city of Münster during such perilous times by letters obtained or to be obtained from the apostolic see or its legates, unless the said letters to be obtained make full and express mention of this indulgence. Let no one, etc., infringe upon our concession, etc. Given at Anagni, on the 8th of September, in the twelfth year. The provost of the church of Münster has been appointed as conservator concerning these matters; notwithstanding if it has been granted to anyone by the apostolic see that they may be interdicted, etc., unless mention is made.

**Regesto (in Latin):**

Gregorius IX papa communitati civitatis Monasteriensis indulget, ut, durante discrimine guerrarum et incursionum, extra districtum Monasteriensem in iudicium evocari non possint sine expressa mentione indulgentiae. 1238, Sept. 8, Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To Berthold, Abbot of St. Gall in the diocese of Constance. Since, in the establishment of peace made by us between you and our venerable brother, the bishop of Constance, we have ordered, among other things, that all sentences of suspension and excommunication pronounced against you by the same bishop by his own authority be lifted, and because you fear that the privileges, indulgences, liberties, and immunities granted to you and your monastery by the apostolic see might be undermined, we, inclined by your supplications, desiring to protect in the future with paternal care your and your monastery's indemnity, decree by the present authority that no prejudice shall be generated against those privileges, indulgences, liberties, and immunities by the relaxation of these sentences, and that nothing shall be added to the rights of the same bishop. We grant this to you and the same monastery by the authority of these presents. Let no one etc. of our concession etc. Given at Anagni, on the 14th of July, in the twelfth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Bertholdo abbati Sancti Galli Constantiensis diocesis mandat ut, non obstante relaxatione sententiarum suspensionis et excommunicationis ab episcopo Constantiensi promulgatarum, privilegiis et immunitatibus concessis a sede apostolica nullum preiudicium generetur. Anagnie, II Idus Iulii, anno duodecimo.

**Translation to English:**

From the copies of the archive, which we have compared with the Registers, we present letter III from Perteius's copy. H., Cardinal of Santa Sabina. In the responsibilities of the pastoral office, our heart is greatly troubled and nothing makes our daily urgency in the concern for all churches more burdensome than when the necessity of the times and sometimes the demand for public utility requires that these same churches must be burdened with us in the support of the common task. For if it were possible in nature for the whole body to be governed by the head without the aid of the members, it would be our greatest wish that we could bear the common labors for the universal church in such a way that the individual parts were not burdened by any share of the impending troubles, but that from the frequent inconvenience of our disturbance only the advantage of peaceful leisure would result for others. However, since the ability given to us is not sufficient for everything, we are compelled to call upon the shoulders of others for their support in the task, lest the lack of strength, without which the effort of the undertaken labor cannot be effective, paves the way for danger and causes harmful detriments. But while we are compelled to share the burdens incumbent upon us with other churches, since pressing necessity drives us, not willingly but unwillingly, where a completely safe part does not offer a way to decline, we devise whatever remedies we can, so that whatever must be imposed on them for the support of the common cause can be borne more lightly by others, lest, as we have said, due to a lack of strength, ecclesiastical utility perishes.

To the Archbishop of Mainz. We have learned that certain letters, said to be ours, contain, among other things, that several prelates and chapters in Germany, following an ancient custom, have promised to provide certain clerics with ecclesiastical benefices, in response to the request of our beloved son in Christ, W., the illustrious King of the Romans. For this reason, inclined by his supplications, we have granted that each cleric for whom benefice provision has been promised or will be promised by virtue of these requests, should be preferred in the attainment of provisions over all others for whom we or our legates have written, without prejudice to them regarding other matters. Gregorius IX papa Adenulpho, fratri episcopi Troiani, castrum Airole cum iuribus in feudum perpetuum concessit et investivit. Anagnie, 1240, Aug. 12.

To the Podestà, council, and commune of Florence. Among all our endeavors, we recognize this as paramount: to contemplate peace among those who share the Christian name and faith. We know that the author of peace is not duly venerated in discord, that faith wanes through dissent and schisms, that moral discipline deteriorates, and that souls do not prosper. Therefore, we who desire peace among both distant and near peoples, must especially foster reconciliation where the tranquility of the Roman Church is disturbed by their proximity and the bowels of charity are moved by compassion. Indeed, after returning from the regions of Gaul and observing Tuscany torn by internal strife, rampant violence, and mutual hostility, we were deeply troubled, our hearts pierced with grief. We, along with our brothers, earnestly turned our thoughts to devising remedies to quell these evils. To this end, hoping that the joy of peace might arise from our mediation, we summoned the discordant parties to our presence, so that through suitable representatives with full powers to negotiate, they might participate in discussions aimed at common concord, complying with the Church's guidance, and uniting the peoples of the province, whom the enemy had divided through schisms and seditions, in one bond of love. However, by divine judgment, as we believe, the ears of those summoned were closed to our voice, and they despised the word of peace with obstinate spirit, refusing to send emissaries to the Apostolic See who might accept the salutary words of our mouth. While these parties were long gathering their forces against each other near Montaia, with camps set up in plain sight for battle, Mother Church was filled with fear and horror at the slaughter of bodies and ruin of souls that could occur. Striving to prevent such tragedies and confident that fear of impending ills might support the pursuit of peace, we urgently dispatched our beloved sons, R. of St. Angelo and I. of St. Nicholas in Carcere Tulliano, distinguished cardinals of the Church of God, as messengers of peace to the discordant. Yet the law of sin, disobedient to reason, hardened both parties to resist wise counsel, salutary advice, and paternal commands, so that the angels of peace were despised on both sides. They found no one on whom their peace could rest, bringing back no fruit of their labor except the merit of their pious intention. What evils followed our repulsed efforts, which our diligence would have remedied had they not been spurned, are testified by the spilled blood, which we believe cries out to heaven against those who with their counsel thwarted our and our brothers' efforts for peace, by the groans of the bound, moving the tribunal of the eternal judge against those who through evil counsels of war prevent the breaking of their bonds of captivity, and finally by the sorrow of the region, laid waste by frequent depredations, which proclaims the futility of labors and sterile expenses. But the reckless heat of anger, provoked by furies and stirred by impulses of hatred, prevents even those who suffer these things from perceiving them, because while the desire to conquer or avenge leads them to rash precipices, they do not heed the father who calls them back nor recognize the mother who shows them the breasts of mercy. But they trample on both, following the warlike impulse, and think it prudent to pursue recklessness as their sound judgment. Moreover, if the fortunes of Mars sometimes favor one of the combatants, he should not raise himself in security and exclude the mediator of peace until the final outcome of war is known, for the fortune of battle is still in the balance and has not pledged its gifts to either side such that they cannot be recalled and turned upon him who envied them to his rival. An invisible observer above indeed plays with human affairs, as with his permission or hidden judgment victory and defeat are exchanged, and ultimately, unexpectedly, the one who had won is overcome, for as the sage says: "The battle is not to the strong," since chance and time work unforeseen events in all things. If, however, one of the combatants happens to be cast down by chance, appearing inferior to the adversary in some respects, he sometimes counsels himself worse by immediately rising against the victor from his fall and expending opportunities for necessary restoration of his condition in opposing the standing adversary, whereas the times for reviving strength should precede those for revenge, and it often happens that one who too fiercely pursues his own disgrace incurs heavier reasons for vindication. Hence, despite the repulses of both our words and those of the aforementioned cardinals, it might have been necessary to desist from healing those who repelled us; but we are persistent towards our children and the invincible affection of paternal piety, knowing not how to desist from their reproaches, exhortations, and importunate rebukes until they return to better counsel and the perniciousness

We promise to uphold you as special and dearest sons with the shield of protection and defense against the attacks of anyone wishing to disturb your peace, in your persons, goods, and rights possessed and to be possessed by just title in the kingdom of Sicily, Germany, and Italy, in any way whatsoever, and to cherish you at all times. Let no one etc. of our protection and promise etc. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa eisdem mandat sub protectione apostolica admitti, promittens defensionem contra insultus in regno Sicilie, Alamania et Ytalia. Datum ut supra.

Given at Naples, on the fourth day before the Kalends of February, in the first year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Alexander IV papa Fratri Rufino de ordine fratrum Minorum mandat vices O. cardinalis de Sancta Maria in Via Lata, legati apostolici in regno Sicilie, in partibus Sicilie ac Calabrie gerendas, concedens ei potestatem committendi negotia personis idoneis si quando fuerit occupatus. Datum Neapoli, IIII Kalendas Februarii, anno primo.

**Translation to English:**

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Nicolao, Petrucio, Iacobo et Frorino pupillis, filiis et heredibus quondam Iohannis Morene de Siracusio, fidelibus suis, confirmat absolutionem ab onere rationis officiorum patris eorum, quam Manfredus princeps Tarantinus concessit. 1231, Ianuar. 30, Neapoli.

Albert, son of the noble Marquis of Meissen. Although the union of conjugal bond etc. until: persuades. **Regesto in Latin:**

Clemens IV papa nobili viro Iohanni Moro, fideli suo, officium camerariatus regni Siciliae, quod tempore condam C. nati condam Fr. olim Romanorum imperatoris obtinuit, auctoritate apostolica confirmat et de novo concedit, ut illud pleno iure vita sua habeat et exerceat. O. To the Cardinal Deacon of Saint Adrian. Innocentius IV papa O. Sancti Adriani diacono cardinali donationem domorum et bonorum Petri de Vinea a sorore eius Granata factam confirmat, et facultatem possessionis concedit, detentos exinde amovendos decernens. Neapoli, XII Kal. Ian., anno I.

Therefore, the same See deems it fitting and appropriate to extend gracious favor towards the city of Messina and its citizens, and to distinguish it, a city that shines with the fame of ancient power and nobility among the cities of the Kingdom of Sicily, with notable privileges and to honor it particularly with the prerogative of grace, especially since through it and its citizens great and agreeable benefits may accrue to the Holy Roman Church. Gregorius IX papa nobili viro Petro Ruffo de Calabria et civitati Messanensi privilegia et protectionem sub beati Petri et suae auctoritatis tutela concedit, statuens ut sint de demanio ecclesiae Romanae, similiter ac Neapolitani et Capuani vivant. 1238, Nov. 3. Neapoli.
