To the archbishops and bishops and beloved sons, abbots, priors, provosts, deans, archdeacons, archpriests, and other prelates of churches and their chapters and convents or colleges, whether exempt or not exempt, and patrons, clerics, or laymen who will inspect these present letters. Since divine providence has willed that we, though unworthy, should preside over the governance of the universal church, we have always held it in our heart to maintain honesty and order in all things and to exercise a mode of providence in making provisions, through which honor and benefit may arise for churches, monasteries, and other pious places. However, that sometimes the opposite has occurred, due to the malice of the times and the excessive impropriety of petitioners, has often brought us sorrow and burdened our heart with sighs, especially when, after many delays and contrived resistances, we have been compelled to make certain provisions quite unwillingly, which we would have considered a great joy to avoid.

Therefore, having remained vigilant in mind for a long time to be able to apply an appropriate remedy to these issues, we have decided to decree, for our peace of mind and for the welfare of the aforementioned churches, monasteries, and places, that each of you may confer, elect for, confirm those elected, or present and admit those presented to canonries and prebends, as well as benefices or personates and dignities, whether with or without care, revenues, and even pensions, pertaining to your collation or election or presentation, which are held by anyone originating from outside the kingdoms in which these canonries and prebends and other aforementioned exist, whether they remain at the Apostolic See or reside elsewhere, from now on to suitable persons, having God before your eyes. 

And from then on these persons may have full and unshaken right in those same canonries and prebends and benefices or dignities and personates, revenues, and pensions. However, they shall not meddle in these matters before they become vacant, but shall acquire them as soon as they become vacant by law, and they shall have free faculty to enter and retain them without anyone's consent being required, provided that those who currently hold them may have them peacefully and quietly by full right until they resign or pass away and shall suffer no prejudice absolutely on account of the statute.

We wish, however, that if some have been received under the expectation of prebends in the churches where provisions have been made for the said persons, or if they have obtained apostolic letters concerning their provision in them, as in reception or obtaining, thus in acquisition of prebends the persons are preferred. If any of these persons for whom provision has been made by virtue of the same statute or who by your liberal grace happens to be provided for according to the mode noted below, resigns or dies in the meantime, you may as soon as possible substitute another suitable person in their place and continue to do this successively upon the resignation or death of any of these persons.

Under the invocation of divine judgment, we command that these persons shall plot no treachery or fraud or cause any disturbances or any other inconvenience against the holders of the said canonries and benefices and prebends or personates and dignities, revenues, or pensions; otherwise they shall lose all rights acquired for them by this provision, since it is fitting that as grace is granted for virtue, so penalty should be recompensed for vice. Also, to restrain evils that might possibly arise from this statute in the minds of the perverse, we decree that if it happens that anyone who has been substituted under the benefit of the same statute is killed in any way, God forbid, the person so substituted shall not have nor even seize possession of their provision unless they first obtain public letters from the apostolic or ordinary and some religious men fearing God, that they are in no way suspected of the murder of the person thus killed.

Moreover, because it might result in grave tedium for these persons to wait for the vacancies of the canonries and prebends and other aforementioned for long periods, let your intention strive to provide liberally and without delay for them from the canonries and prebends and benefices or personates and dignities, revenues, and pensions pertaining to your collation or election or presentation, which, beyond this provision of yours, are presently vacant or happen to become vacant, as long as they are not by right the possession of someone else, and afterward, in place of these, as soon as possible, you shall substitute other suitable persons.

To the archbishops, bishops, beloved sons, abbots, priors, deans, archdeacons, and other prelates of churches and chapters established in Hungary, Bohemia, Austria, Styria, and Moravia. It is evident by example that the dissension's author, accustomed to deceit, strives to impel or rather utterly uproot the affection that God has naturally implanted in the flesh. This same aged inciter of all evils, by providing a catalyst for hatred and rancor between Cain and Abel, the first brothers, provoked one to the destruction of the other by violating the bond of brotherhood. And even now, weaving continuously the fabric of such a dangerous discord, he has sown a most hostile and ill-fated discord between our dearest sons in Christ, the illustrious kings of Hungary and Bohemia, joined by kinship, as you know well. From this lamentable situation, great sorrows, dangers to souls, and bodily harm continually arise, as churches are desolated, orphans are oppressed, the poor and widows are open to plunder, and, what is more grievous to us, the faithful, whom Christ redeemed with His precious blood, are subjected to the harsh dominion of the pagans, lamentably shackled in bondage. 
Therefore, it is incumbent upon us to provide the wisest counsel in these matters so that the seed of such dissension is led to destruction before it can further take root through negligence. For if we continue to permit it to blossom through our dissimulation, it will be difficult to cut it down even with the scythe of prudent forethought. The devouring fire may reduce the lands of these kings to desolation, and the raging sword may bring, if (God forbid) they come to battle, a miserable massacre and ruin, as the number of those assembling from the lands subject to their dominion is known to be plentiful on both sides.
Therefore, lest these perils add to the sorrow of our soul, which we have already conceived greatly from what has occurred, if a prompt remedy is not applied, but so that at least our carefulness within the body of Christendom receives a welcome tranquility, whose body we observe daily being heavily attacked by pagans at its extremities with bitterness of mind: for the reintegration between these kings, with the matter of discord removed by love of sincerity or at least by entering into truces which customarily precede peace, so that through their intervention a more suitable negotiated settlement may thereafter be had, we have deemed it worthy to dispatch our beloved son B., the elected Neapolitan, our chaplain, a man endowed with the gift of knowledge, outstanding in integrity of life, and accepted by us and our brothers for the merit of his probity, by committing to him the office of legation, so that he may build and plant, uproot, scatter, and destroy, as it shall seem expedient according to the prudence given to him by God, with the counsel of the same brothers. We have proposed to ourselves the hope that, with the Author who made our peace, uniting both into one, who joined two walls into Himself, He will unite those kings in a pleasing bond of reconciliation, whom the enemy of the human race has maliciously separated by his deceitful schemes.
Therefore, we earnestly ask, admonish, and urge all of you, through apostolic writings, commanding that you receive him, or rather us in him, cheerfully and honorably, and that you faithfully attend to and humbly and devotedly obey his salutary counsels and commands, which he shall consider necessary to establish peace or truces of this sort or otherwise, ensuring they are inviolably observed. Otherwise, the sentence he shall rightly render against the rebellious, etc., should be observed. Given at the Lateran, 4th Nones of April, in the 11th year.

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro Lodoico comiti Cotronensi, germano dilecti filii nobilis viri B. marchionis de Hohemburch, comitis Montis Caveosi, regni Sicilie senescalci, concessionem predecessoris, qua comitatum Cotronensem in concambium pro baronia Argentie et Montisfortis concessit, apostolica auctoritate confirmat. Gregorius IX papa nobilibus viris I. Molendinario, V. Sculteto, B. de Hottingen, H. Brunoni, C. Wellensi, C. Wicensi militibus ceterisque de Turego reconciliationem et impunitates a Constantiensi episcopo concessas confirmat. 1227, Feb. 12. Neapoli.

To the archbishops and bishops, and beloved sons the abbots, priors, deans, archdeacons and other prelates of churches, and the noble men counts, barons, justiciars, vicars and other officials, knights, burghers, the commune of Messina, and all those established throughout Sicily and Calabria, faithful to us and to the Roman Church. The benevolent mother church gladly joins in the common desire of her faithful, rightly elevating those who humbly submit to her with sincere faith and dutiful devotion by apostolic favors and magnifying them with abundant gifts of benefits. Therefore, so that the fullness of exultation and joy may arise for you from the desired governance, for which long sighs have been drawn, we receive you, and all churches and religious places of Sicily and Calabria, and all your and their goods under the special protection and defense of blessed Peter and ourselves. Moreover, wishing to keep always inviolate the liberties and immunities, usages, and commendable customs granted to you and to the aforementioned churches and places by regal or other munificent donations of any faithful, we confirm these to you and to these churches and places by apostolic authority from special grace. We further decree that the aforementioned Sicily and Calabria shall perpetually be part of the domain of the Roman Church and ours, and that they along with their appurtenances, districts, and rights and with all the people shall always remain under the dominion of the Apostolic See, nor shall it be permitted to grant anything to anyone that would diminish the true dominion remaining with the Roman Church or to alienate or transfer it in any way to illustrious or any other persons, with the said people always remaining under the power, jurisdiction, and protection of the said See and enjoying the desired benefits of freedom. Let none etc. of our protection, confirmation, and constitution etc. Given at Capua, the 13th Kalends of November, in the 12th year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopis, episcopis, abbatibus, prioribus, decanis, archidiaconis et aliis ecclesiarum prelatis, comitibus, baronibus, iustitiariis, vicariis, militibus, burgensibus, communi Messanensi et universis in Sicilia et Calabria constitutis. Confirmat libertates et immunitates ecclesiarum et locorum religiosorum Sicilie et Calabrie sub speciali protectione et defensione beati Petri et sua, statuens eadem perpetuo esse de demanio ecclesie Romane. Datum Capue, XIII Kalendas Novembris, anno XII.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Ministro fratrum Minorum Alamanniae ac diffinitoribus capituli provincialis in Ezzelingen celebrati significat se concessisse, dum erat Ostiensis et Velletrensis episcopus, ut, exceptis claustris Argentorati, Constantiensis, Ulmae et Phullingeni ordinis sancti Damiani, nullam curam gerere teneantur de claustris eiusdem ordinis in Alamannia constructis vel construendis, et nunc apostolica auctoritate confirmat. To the noble men Berthold, Oddo, and Lodoico, brothers and marquises of Hohemburch, our faithful followers. Since Manfred, Prince of Taranto, after withdrawing from Teano without permission due to the death of the late Burellus of Anglona, has embraced a spirit of rebellion, he has inflicted and caused to be inflicted many damages upon you, who persist in devotion, loyalty, and service to the Roman Church, and he continues to attempt further harm, as has been fully reported to us and our brothers. To this end, we and the Roman Church, by the counsel and agreement of our brothers, are bound. Let no one etc. of our promise and obligation etc. Given as in the immediately preceding.

Innocentius IV papa Bertholdo, Oddoni et Lodoico fratribus marchionibus de Hohemburch scribit se promisit per consilium et assensum fratrum suorum curare ut Manfredus Tarentinus princeps satisfaciat eis pro damnis illatis, si ad fidelitatem ecclesiae redierit. 1254, Dat. ut in proxima superiori.

To the Commune of San Flaviano, in the Diocese of Aprutium. Reason demands and equity persuades that we pursue the devotion of our faithful with the favors of apostolic kindness and indulgences of grace. Therefore, so that you may rejoice in the blessed times of your free condition and prove henceforth how sweet and how light is the burden to which the faithful of the Church submit their necks, we, favorably assenting to the supplications of your devotion, grant you by the authority of these presents and decree that you and your land of San Flaviano, both the new borough and the old, with its territories, possessions, and all its appurtenances, remain in the immediate and perpetual demesne and ownership and governance of the Roman Church, just as it is known to have been in the demesne of the kings of Sicily, to be wholesomely defended by the same Church as its pure and mere demesne from any oppressors or molesters, and never to be transferred into the dominion of another at any time. We furthermore revoke any concessions, donations, and submissions to the commune of the city of Ascoli and Fermo, or any cities or places of the March of Ancona or elsewhere, made by our beloved son P., deacon cardinal of Saint George at the Golden Veil, then legate of the apostolic see in those parts, concerning the aforesaid land either totally or partially, decreeing that you and your land are free and exempt from any submission, transaction, agreement, and convention, as well as from any alliances formed by you with the communes or men of the cities of Ascoli or Fermo or elsewhere, through which your liberty might have been impaired or any burden of service or subjection imposed upon you. Let none etc. of our concession, revocation, and constitution etc. Given at Naples, November 17, in the 12th year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa communi Sancti Flaviani Aprutinae diocesis terram suam cum pertinentiis in demanio Romanae ecclesiae manere concedit et a quibuslibet oppressoribus defensare constituit, concessionibus aliis revocatis. 1238, Neapoli, XV Kalendas Decembris.

**Translation to English:**

... to the Bishop of Würzburg. Our beloved sons, the dean, the scholasticus, Henry of Drondorf, and Heidenric of Zangenbere, along with certain other canons of the Halberstadt church, have taken care to inform us that when our venerable brother, Bishop M. of Halberstadt, once requested resignation for certain reasons from our beloved son, H., presbyter cardinal of the title of Saint Sabina, then a legate of the apostolic see in those parts, the said legate, understanding that such a resignation would not be beneficial to the church itself, did not accept it at all. He nonetheless instructed the dean, provost, and chapter of the church to ensure that no one would attempt to elect a bishop for that church before the resignation of the said bishop was properly accepted by us or by him; he declared that if it were done otherwise, it would be null and void. However, Ludolf of Sladein, a canon of the aforementioned church, desiring ambitiously to ascend the pastoral chair through cunning deceit, along with certain other canons of his church, his supporters, sent two fraudulent messengers to the same legate for the resignation of the said bishop. And although the legate did not accept the resignation even then, the aforesaid messengers, upon returning, falsely suggested to that bishop that the resignation had been accepted by the legate, as they had been instructed. The said bishop, too credulous to such lies from the messengers, without receiving any letters on this matter from the legate, simply resigned from the dignity of the pontifical office. The said Ludolf, publicly revealing the poison of his deceit, procured his election as pastor of that church, or rather as usurper, and having deceitfully obtained confirmation of the election from our venerable brother G., Archbishop of Mainz, the metropolitan of the place, while making no mention to him or to the said king about such an unseemly process. The said legate, fully aware of the above, declared the process of such an election and whatever followed from it to be null by definitive sentence, and he had this declared publicly, binding L., for retaining the castles and goods against the cardinal's mandate and for contumaciously refusing to appear before him when lawfully summoned, with the bond of excommunication. He absolved the prelates and clergy of the city and diocese of Halberstadt from obedience to him, and the barons, nobles, ministerials, vassals, and other men of that church from any allegiance they might owe to the said canon. He had this announced by our venerable brothers G., Archbishop of Mainz, and the Archbishops of Magdeburg and Bishops of Hildesheim, Nuremberg, and Merseburg, declaring them not bound by any such allegiance. The collation of dignities, personates, and other benefices and goods of that church, made by the said canon, was declared by him null and void, and he ordered the excommunication of him to be publicly declared by ringing bells and lighting candles on every Sunday and feast day by the said archbishops and bishops. Therefore, the said dean, scholasticus, and other canons of the same church have requested us to approve these acts and confirm the sentence of excommunication with apostolic authority. Therefore, having the definitive sentence of the said legate as confirmed and approved, we command you through apostolic writings to enforce that the sentence of excommunication, as reasonably pronounced, be observed inviolably by our authority until condign satisfaction is made, removing any appeal; contradictors, etc., notwithstanding any letters obtained or to be obtained from the apostolic see that might prejudice truth and justice. We do not wish that any prejudice against the illustrious Roman King W. arises from these letters. Given at the Lateran, III Kalends of December, in the eleventh year [of our pontificate].

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Erbipolensi mandat ut sententiam excommunicationis in Ludolfum de Sladein, canonici Halberstadensis, inviolabiliter observet, confirmans sententiam cardinalis tituli Sanctae Sabinae. 1237, Nov. 29. Datum Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble men Philip de Gaudio, Jacob, and John, brothers of Caleno. We have received from the tenor of your petition that although your ancestors held and peacefully possessed all the forests, marshes, and mountains of the district of Calinia and the rock of Mount Dracon in the diocese of Calinia, as well as the military constabulary in Caleno and the aforementioned rock, for a long time and even during the time of the renowned memory of King William of Sicily, eventually the late Emperor Frederick, at the request of the esteemed memory of Pletril of Capua, Cardinal Deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, granted and no less confirmed these possessions to your father John Capice, brother to him, of whom you are the sons and heirs, as it is more fully said to be contained in a privilege drawn up by the same Frederick and sealed with his seal. But because you have been unable to freely use your right over these matters due to the wickedness of the time that came afterwards, and you were even forced to be exiled far from your native land, you requested to be given help in this regard with paternal benevolence. We, inclined by your supplications, grant and also confirm by apostolic authority the same forests, marshes, mountains, and constabulary, as your aforesaid ancestors reasonably and peacefully possessed them, and as it is also contained in the privilege of the said Frederick, and as these matters are known to rightfully belong to you, to you and your heirs persisting in the devotion of the Apostolic See. We grant and also confirm them and protect them with the support of this present document. Let no one etc. dare to infringe our concession and confirmation etc. Given at Naples, on the 11th of January, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobilibus viris Philippo de Gaudio, Iacobo et Iohanni fratribus de Caleno concedit et confirmat silvas, paludes, montes et comestabuliam in dicto districtu Calinia et monte Draconis, sicut a progenitoribus suis detentis et in privilegio Friderici imperatoris contentis, auctoritate apostolica. Dat. Neapoli, III Idus Ianuarii, anno primo.

Translation to English:

To the elected Bishop of Aquileia, a spirit of wiser counsel. Our beloved sons, the dean and chapter of the Church of Trieste, have informed us that, as the same church was deprived of the solace of a pastor, they convened together, having called those who should and could conveniently attend, and, invoking the grace of the Holy Spirit, canonically elected our beloved son Arlongus de Woisperch, their fellow canon, a man indeed learned, endowed with knowledge and distinguished by the honesty of his manners, as bishop and pastor of that church. They humbly requested us to confirm this election with the kindness of the apostolic see, since nothing should be an obstacle to just appointments. Although the aforementioned church is subject to the metropolitan law of the Church of Aquileia, because you are known to be bound by the bond of excommunication, lest the same church suffer harm from prolonged vacancy, we have entrusted by letter our venerable brothers, the Bishops of Pola, Pedena, and Koper, that unless you are absolved from this bond in the meantime, after diligently investigating the manner of election, the diligence of the electors, and the merits of the elected, if they find that this election was canonically celebrated for a suitable person, they should confirm it with our authority and ensure that the elected receives due obedience and reverence from his subordinates. Also, one of them, with the others standing by, should bestow the consecration upon him, receiving from him the customary oath of fidelity in our name and in the name of the Church of Aquileia, so that no future prejudice may be generated against the aforementioned Church of Aquileia. Therefore, we command that if you happen to be absolved from the aforesaid bond in the meantime, you should confirm the election, if it is canonical, within eight days after being requested to do so, without any difficulty, and then at a suitable time, ensure that the consecration is bestowed, unless something reasonable prevents it. Otherwise, we enjoin the aforesaid bishops by our letters to proceed to such a confirmation without delay after the lapse of the said days in accordance with the contents of the prior letters directed to them. Given at Naples, VIII Kalendas December, the twelfth year. Written to them: What if not all, etc.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa electo Aquilegensi mandat ut, si a vinculo excommunicationis interim absolvatur, electionem Arlongi de Woisperch in episcopum Tergestinum intra octo dies confirmet et munus consecrationis impendi faciat, alioquin id praescripserit episcopis Polensit, Petenensi et Iustinopolitano. 1238, Nov. 24, Neapoli.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected Archbishop of Magdeburg. Since the pallium, the insignia of the pontifical office, was requested from us on your behalf with due insistence by your envoys, the beloved sons Heydenric of Zangimberch, a canon of Nuremberg, and Master Henric of Kirberch, our subdeacons, we, acceding to your supplications, have decided to send it, taken from the body of Saint Peter, through the same envoys to our venerable brother, the Bishop of Merseburg, to be assigned to you by him. He is to assign it to you according to the form enclosed under our bull, and he shall receive from you, in our name and that of the Roman Church, the oath of fidelity in the form we also send under the same bull. You, however, may use it within your church on those days specified in the privileges of the same church. Therefore, so that the sign may not differ from the thing signified, but what you bear outwardly you may also maintain inwardly in mind, we attentively admonish and exhort your discretion to strive to preserve humility and justice, granted by the Lord who gives gifts and bestows rewards, which preserve and promote their guardian, and to carefully work to augment, both spiritually and temporally, your spouse, the Church of Magdeburg, with God's guidance. Given at the Lateran, January 23, in the eleventh year of our pontificate.

To the Bishop of Merseburg. Since the pallium, the insignia of the pontifical office, was requested from us on behalf of the beloved son, the elected Archbishop of Magdeburg, through the beloved sons Heydenric of Zaugimberch, a canon of Nuremberg, and Master Henric of Kirberch, our subdeacons and his envoys, we, acceding to his supplications, have decided to send it, taken from the body of Saint Peter, through the same envoys to you, to be assigned to him by you. Therefore, we command you to assign it to him according to the form enclosed under our bull, and to receive from him, in our name and that of the Roman Church, the oath of fidelity, following the form which we also send under the same bull. Given as above.

III. Form of presenting the pallium. For the honor of Almighty God, and of the Blessed Virgin Mary, and of the blessed Apostles Peter and Paul, and of Our Lord Pope Innocent and the Roman Church, as well as the church entrusted to you, we present to you the pallium, taken from the body of Saint Peter, the fullness of the pontifical office, to be used within your church on certain days, which are specified in the privileges granted by the Apostolic See.

IV. Form of the oath. I, Rudolf, Archbishop of Magdeburg, from this hour forward will be faithful and obedient to Saint Peter and the Holy Apostolic Roman Church and to my lord Pope Innocent and his canonically entering successors. I will not be in counsel or consent or deed, that they lose life or limb or be captured by evil capture. The counsel that they will entrust to me by themselves or by their envoys or by letters, I will not reveal to anyone to their detriment, with me knowing it. I will be a helper to retain and defend the Roman papacy and the regalia of Saint Peter, saving my order, against every man. I will treat the legate of the Apostolic See honorably in coming and going and will aid him in his needs. Called to a synod, I will come, unless I am prevented by a canonical impediment. I will visit the thresholds of the Apostles every two years, either personally or through my envoy, unless I am absolved by apostolic license. I will not sell or gift or in any way alienate or pledge or newly infeudate possessions belonging to the table of my episcopate without consulting the Roman Pontiff. So help me God and these Holy Gospels.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius III papa electo Magdeburgensi mandat, ut cum pallium, insigne pontificalis officii, per nuuntios suos postulatum sit, illud per episcopum Mersburgensem sub certa forma accipiat et iuramentum fidelitatis praestet. Hortatur ut ecclesiam Magdeburgensem spiritualiter et temporaliter augeat. Datum Laterani, X Kalendas Februarii, anno XI pontificatus.

To John of Dist, Bishop of Lübeck. Although, by that general privilege which the Lord granted to the Church of Rome through Blessed Peter, the translation of bishops rightfully pertains to the Roman Pontiff and should not be done without his permission, this should only happen when urgent necessity and evident utility require it. Indeed, having understood that our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Prussia, to whom we are said to have previously commended the bishopric of Lübeck, then deprived of a pastor’s comfort, for his sustenance, had established his seat in a suitable place where he could reside and be comfortably sustained from the archiepiscopal revenues, and having prudently considered that the care of places should be entrusted to certain persons and that the ministries of persons should be provided for certain places, so that from the industriousness of persons the utility of places may grow and from the opportunity of places, persons may have greater capacity to engage more usefully in the things of God: We recently sent letters to our beloved son, Cardinal P. of St. George at the Golden Veil, instructing him to revoke such commendation or concession made to the said archbishop and to absolve you, then Bishop of Sambia, from the bond by which you were bound to the Church of Sambia, and to appoint you to the Church of Lübeck as bishop and pastor, granting and committing to you full administration of its spiritual and temporal affairs, and also granting you the license to be transferred to the same Church of Lübeck, and to have exhibited to you by the chapter and clergy of the city and diocese of Lübeck the due obedience and reverence: contradictors etc. Since the same cardinal, by the authority of this mandate, revoked the commendation itself and any concession made to the said archbishop, absolved you from the bond of the same Church of Sambia, and appointed you as pastor and bishop of the said Church of Lübeck, as is more fully contained in the letters of the cardinal made concerning this matter: We, inclined by your supplications, approving and ratifying what has been done by the same cardinal in this matter, confirm it by apostolic authority, etc., securing it, supplementing from the fullness of power any defect if any existed in this part, and causing the tenor of these letters to be inserted word for word in these presents. Complying with the petitions of the magnificent prince, Lord William, illustrious King of the Romans, by the providence of the Apostolic See, intending to show munificence to you in consideration of him, sent us letters in this manner: Innocent, etc., to our beloved son P. Cardinal Deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, greetings, etc. When our venerable brother, etc., as in n. 267 up to: Given at the Lateran, 4th Non-March, in the 11th year. Innocentius IV papa Iohanni de Dist episcopo Lubicensi mandat ut, revocata commendatione archiepiscopo Pruscie concessa, ab episcopatu Sambiensi absolvi et episcopum Lubicensem constitui, plenam administrationem spiritualium et temporalium eiusdem ecclesiae committat. Dat. Lateran., XV Kalendas Aprilis, anno XI.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man B., marquis of Hohemburch, count of Montis Caveosi, great seneschal of the kingdom of Sicily, our faithful subject. The clear services of your loyalty, by which you render yourself agreeable in our eyes and in the eyes of our brothers, urgently suggest to our mind that we not only preserve your rights intact and unharmed, but even increase them. Therefore, as you proposed in our presence, our predecessor, Pope I., of blessed memory, confirmed to you and your heirs the grants of the county of Montis Caveosi and of the castle and barony of Castri and its honor, and of the castles of Policori, Montispilosi, Caurati, and Cilii de Gualdo, once made to you by the late C., son of the late Fr., former emperor of the Romans, notwithstanding that Conrad was then bound by the chain of excommunication, which otherwise did not have the power to confer or grant in such a manner, and any sentence of deprivation of dignity, honors, and other rights pronounced against you by the same predecessor — with the advice and consent of his brothers, supplying any defect that might otherwise be in those grants, by the fullness of apostolic power. Moreover, he newly granted and gave the county, barony, and other aforementioned items with cities, castles, villages, hamlets, men, honors, rights, jurisdictions, the right of patronage of conventual (and non-conventual) churches, pastures, woods, hunting rights, meadows, possessions, cultivated and uncultivated lands, waters and their courses, justices, and with all their reasons and appurtenances, and with those things pertaining to absolute and mixed rule, namely, those that are of demesne to demesne and those that are of service to service, to you and your heirs forever, with the advice and consent of his brothers, from certain knowledge and special grace, as is more fully contained in the apostolic privilege obtained on this matter: we, inclined by your supplications, considering what was done by the same predecessor in this matter as ratified and pleasing, confirm it with the advice and consent of our brothers by apostolic authority, etc., up to: we fortify. Let no one, etc., our confirmation, etc. Given at Naples, 17th Kalends of February, in the first year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Ioas papa nobili viro B. marchioni de Hohemburch mandat, ut concessiones factas a predecessore suo de comitatu Montis Caveosi et aliis, de novo confirmat. Neapoli, XVII Kalendas Februari, anno primo.

To the same. The exceptional merits of your devotion and constancy are so prominent and illustrious that, when we consider their excellence and clarity, we deem them so worthy of graces and benefits that hardly any means of recompense appears by which we can suitably reward their greatness. Therefore, we are diligently attentive and vigilant, and our constant thought is engaged in this matter, so that for such and so great merits we may support your persons with appropriate graces and exalt you with fitting honors. Since, as you have stated in our presence, certain goods have been confirmed, granted, and given to you in the kingdom of Sicily both by our predecessor Pope I of happy memory and by us, with the counsel and assent of our brothers, as is more fully contained in the apostolic privileges obtained on this matter, we wish and, with the counsel and assent of the aforementioned brothers, we grant to you by the authority of these presents, that if any one or more of you dies without legitimate offspring, the remaining one or ones shall succeed and have those goods, just as they are known to have been confirmed, granted, and given to you by the apostolic see, except for the office of seneschal of the said kingdom and the fifteen hundred ounces of gold annually, which have been granted to you, son Berthold, by the same see for as long as you live. Let no one therefore etc. of our confirmation etc. Given as above.

Gregorius IX papa (eisdem) significant, quod bona in regno Siciliae ab apostolica sede confirmata, concessa et donata, in eventu quod aliquis eorum sine legitimis liberis decedat, reliqui succedant, excepto officio senescalciae et mille quingentis unciis auri annuis Bertholdo concessis. Anno pontificatus (pontifical year), Datum ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishops, abbots, and princes established throughout the duchy of Swabia. Our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious king of Castile and León, along with his ancestors, are recognized among other Catholic princes for their sincere devotion and faith towards the Roman Church in past times. Therefore, embracing him and his merits with the arms of special affection, we earnestly desire that he progresses continually in honor and grace, and we willingly and liberally extend the fullness of our favor to him in matters concerning his advancement. Since, as we understand, the same king is eagerly intent on acquiring the duchy of Swabia and certain other rights in those parts due to him by maternal succession, with due circumspection and power, we, considering your honor in this and the prosperous state of the same duchy, earnestly ask and exhort your devotion, commanding you through apostolic writings, that you assist said king and his envoys, out of reverence for the apostolic see and for us, in obtaining those same duchy and rights powerfully and openly with all your strength, offering them faithful counsel and effective assistance in the pursuit of this matter, which is beneficial to you and the duchy. Thus, supported by the power of your influence, the same king may achieve what he intends, and you, proving through the effect of your actions that you love those who love the Church, may more abundantly deserve our grace and favor. Given at Naples, February 4, in the first year of our pontificate. In the same manner to the noble men, counts, barons, knights, and officials established throughout the duchy of Swabia. In the same manner to the rectors, castellans, and communities of cities and castles established throughout the duchy of Swabia.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopis, abbatibus et principibus per ducatum Suevie constitutis mandat ut regi Castelle et Legionis acquirendi ducatum Suevie et iura materna adiutorium praebeant. 1228, Febr. 4, Neapoli.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbots of the Cistercian order of Saint Galgano and the Camaldolese order of Saint Salvatore de Rardingis, of the dioceses of Volterra and Arezzo. The beloved sons, the abbot and convent of the monastery of Saint Eugene, of the order of Saint Benedict in the diocese of Siena, have humbly petitioned us, claiming that their monastery, which belongs directly to the Roman Church, is so burdened by debt due to the war between Florence and Siena, the imposts and exactions by the commune of Siena, and the recovery of the fence of a certain mill, that unless swift provision is made, it would suffer irreparable harm. They seek permission to sell some of the less useful immovable goods up to the sum of one thousand Sienese pounds to settle these debts, as they have no other means to lift this burden from their shoulders. Trusting fully in your prudence, we order you to grant this requested permission, having considered the necessity and keeping only God before your eyes, insofar as the utility or necessity of the monastery requires. It should be ensured that the money is entirely used for settling the debts, and if it exceeds the amount of the debts, the surplus should be converted for the monastery's benefit, under your supervision and testimony. If not both of you, then etc. Given at Naples, the 9th day before the Kalends of April, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa (Honorius III) abbatibus Sancti Galgani Cisterciensis et Sancti Salvatoris de Rardingis Camaldulensis mandat, ut abbati et conventui monasterii Sancti Eugenii Senensis dioecesis, propter graves debitorum causas, licentiam alienandi bona immobilia minus utilia concedant. 1226, Mart. 24, Neapoli.

**Translation to English:**

To all the people of Amalfi and Atrani. Reason demands and justice persuades that we should pursue the devotion of our faithful with the favors of apostolic kindness and indulgence of grace. So that you may rejoice that happy times of noble condition have dawned upon you, and having been brought into the freedom of children, you may prove how sweet and light is the yoke which the faithful of the Church willingly bear. We, inclined by the prayers of your devotion, grant by the authority of these presents that you, your cities, and places under your jurisdiction may remain immediately and perpetually in the domain and property and governance of the Roman Church, never to be transferred to the dominion of another at any time, and that you may be free and entirely exempt from tolls, commerce, and exactions. Furthermore, you may have a court anywhere in the Kingdom of Sicily where you may be judged in civil matters, as it is known to have been observed during the times of the late illustrious memory of Roger and William II, Kings of Sicily, proposed by you to be judged by Amalfitans only. 

Moreover, as you have taken care to expose to us, that the men of Tramonti and Agerola of the Amalfitan diocese have been accustomed of old to be under your district and jurisdiction, when once the late Emperor Frederick received the imperial diadem: we restore you to that status concerning these men in which you are known to have existed during the times of the aforementioned kings, determining nonetheless upon your supplication that — notwithstanding the custom which you propose to have been observed among you, that the lesser would be punished more severely than the greater for equal injury — in judicially resolving actions of injury, the equity of common law should prevail among you, with the aforementioned custom abolished. Moreover, we confirm by apostolic authority your laudable and ancient customs, as well as the liberties and privileges, which you have used up to now in Romania and the overseas parts by the grant of the kings and princes of those parts, and also the privileges reasonably granted to your community by the named kings, for you and through you to your successors, and we protect them. Let no one etc. violate our concession, constitution, and confirmation etc. Given at Naples, the 9th day before the Kalends of December, in the 12th year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa (Universis hominibus Amalfie et Atrani) declarat eos, cum civitatibus et locis subiectis, in domanio Romanae ecclesiae perpetuo mansuros, immunes a doanis et exactionibus; restituit eos in statum circa homines Tramonti et Agerolo sicut temporibus regum Rogeri et Guillelmi II; confirmat consuetudines et privilegia eorum. 1238, Neapoli, IX Kalendas Decembris.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man John Mero, our faithful. We are inclined, as in the privilege of Henry of Rivellis, to favor the donations and concessions made to you by the late Conrad, son of the late Frederick, former Emperor of the Romans, regarding the castles of Calatamauri, Thermarum, Colatabaturi, Gulisan, Biccari, and Calatabian. We hold these favorable to you and your heirs, including the estate of Carbonaria, which you propose to possess, notwithstanding that said Conrad was at that time bound by the bond of excommunication and otherwise did not have the authority to donate or grant in such a manner, and any deprivation in you devolved, as in the same. So that your devotion towards us and the same church may grow more, we newly grant to you and your heirs the aforementioned castles and estate in fief with the advice and consent of the brothers, as a special favor, so that you and the said heirs may hold the aforementioned castles and estate with the men, both feudal and non-feudal, pastures, woods, cultivated and uncultivated lands, waters and watercourses, and with those things pertaining to mixed and merum imperium, of which we have invested our beloved son, the notary John of Rocca Imperiali, your familiar, in your name, recognizing no other superior or lord from there except the Roman church, in perpetuity. We wish that whenever the aforementioned church for the defense of that kingdom gathers or summons a general army, you and the said heirs are bound to provide seven knights suitably equipped with arms and horses to serve for forty days at your own expense, with the words competently changed. No one is to infringe on our confirmation and concession. Dated at Naples by the hand of William, master of the schools of Parma, vice-chancellor of the holy Roman church, on the third day before the Nones of November, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord's incarnation 1254, in the twelfth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Innocent IV. In the same manner for the beloved son John of Rocca Imperiali for the land of Canteabi with the service of one knight and for a certain house with an orchard situated in the city of Palermo, except that this phrase is not to be added: with those things pertaining to mixed and merum imperium.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa nobili viro Iohanni Mero castella Calatamauri, Thermarum, Colatabaturi, Gulisan, Biccari et Calatabian, necnon casale Carbonarie, in feudum cum heredibus suis concedit, non obstantibus excommunicationis vinculo Conradi donatoris. Eundem obligat ad septem milites pro ecclesiae Romanae defensione. Dat. Neapoli, III Non. Nov., anno Domini MCCCLIV, pontificatus Innocentii IV anno XII.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Novara. A petition presented to us by our beloved son, the elect of Asti, stated that the temporal jurisdiction, control, lordship, vassalage, and other rights that the Church of Asti is known to have over the castles, towns, and people of the Asti bishopric have been so unjustly and violently occupied by the communities of certain cities and castles, as well as other surrounding nobles, and, more nefariously, by the commune of the city of Asti itself—who ought to honor the Church as a mother and defend it from the oppressions of others—that little benefit and much loss and effort are derived from them. Therefore, the said elect humbly beseeched us that, as the Church is completely insufficient to recover the aforesaid rights against such people—having already lost much money due to this issue—we might grant him the license to sell these things back to the Asti ones, especially since they claim they are willing to release the castles of Govone, Vezza, and Rocchetta of the bishopric freely and quietly to him and the Church, and to purchase large properties near the aforementioned city at their own expense, so that from both the peacefully remaining possessions of the said castles and those to be purchased, the Church may receive equal or greater incomes than it used to receive when it had all things in peace. Therefore, trusting in your prudence more fully in the Lord, we command that, after carefully investigating the circumstances of this matter, if you see it as beneficial to the Church and if the chapter of the same Church or its greater and sounder part unanimously agrees, you grant the said elect the requested license by our authority, prudently ensuring that what is granted for the benefit of the Church cannot turn into its detriment, and that it may be sought from the Lord from your hands. Given at Naples, the Ides of February, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Novariensi mandat, ut, si ecclesiae Astensi expedire videatur et capitulum eius consenserit, licentiam vendendi iura temporalium ei tribuat, proviso ne in detrimentum redeat. 1227, Feb. 13, Neapoli.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble men Berthold, Odo, and Ludwig, brothers and margraves of Hohemburch, our loyal subjects. It is fitting and proper that the merits of the devoted and the subjects be weighed with due consideration, so that the worthy may be distinguished from the unworthy, and the deeds of each be prudently discerned according to how each has conducted themselves. And because there are diverse and various ways of earning merit, it should be clearly recognized who has served more and better, so that each may receive a fitting reward based on what they've earned. And because where great service is rendered, a substantial reward should follow, the one who has expended more in service should receive a greater reward. Truly, how greatly your loyalty shines towards us and the Roman Church needs not be explained with a multitude of words or lengthy oracles, since it is sufficiently manifest and is demonstrated more by deeds than it could be revealed by narratives. For this reason, we propose to appropriately increase apostolic favors towards you and to enhance your status with deserved generosity. Therefore, as you have expressed in our presence, our predecessor Pope Innocent of blessed memory confirmed, granted, and donated certain counties, baronies, cities, many castles, villages, and other goods in the Kingdom of Sicily to you and your heirs, with the counsel of his brothers, from certain knowledge and special grace, as is more fully contained in the apostolic privileges and letters obtained on this matter. We, moved by your supplications, holding these confirmations, concessions, and donations as valid and pleasing, confirm them with the counsel and assent of our brothers by apostolic authority, etc. up to: we fortify. No one, therefore, etc. of our confirmation etc. Given at Naples, on the 10th of February, in the 13th indiction, in the year 1254 of the Lord's Incarnation, but in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander IV.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Alexander IV papa nobilibus viris Bertholdo, Odoni et Lodoico fratribus marchionibus de Hohemburch, fidelibus suis, confirmationes, concessiones et donationes a predecessore suo I. papa factas, auctoritate apostolica confirmat. Datum Neapoli, die 10 Februarii, anno 1254, pontificatus anno primo.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Berthol, marquis of Hohenburg, our faithful one. Since you have completely committed yourself to our and the Roman Church's protection, recognizing it as your mother and mistress, and since you have devoted not only your lands and other goods but also your very person to its service, we, wishing to provide for your indemnity with apostolic concern, promise you with the consent and advice of our brothers, by the tenor of these presents, that if you are deprived by the noble man Manfred, prince of Taranto—who, after departing from Tiano due to the death of the late Burellus of Anglone, took up the spirit of rebellion—or by any other adversary of the Church, while you remain in the devotion, fidelity, and service of the said Church, of the county of Montescaglioso, the baronies of the Castle and its honor, as well as Flumeri, and of Policoro, Montepeloso, Caurato, and Cilio de Gualda castles and other lands, which you are known to possess in the Kingdom of Sicily by the grant and confirmation of the apostolic see, or if, God forbid, you might be deprived of them in the future, we will provide you with appropriate compensation in the same Kingdom of Sicily, and for this, we bind ourselves and the said Church with the counsel and assent of our aforementioned brothers. No one, etc., of our promise and obligation, etc. Given at Naples, 15th Kalends of March, in the 13th indiction, the year of the Lord's incarnation 1254, and in the 1st year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander IV.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Alexander IV papa nobilis viro Bertholdo marchioni de Hohenburg, fideli suo, promittit providere ei de convenienti concambio in regno Siciliae si fuerit destitutus a terris quas obtinet in eodem regno ex concessione sedis apostolicae, et obligat se et ecclesiam Romanam ad hoc. 1254, Feb. 15. Neapoli.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man John the Moor, great chamberlain of the Kingdom of Sicily, our faithful one. Since you have taken as your wife the beloved daughter in Christ, the noble woman Clementia, daughter of the noble man Henry of Principatu, with our and our brothers' good pleasure, and the same Henry has given and ceded all the rights he had in the counties of Conse and Principatu to you and your heirs, such that if it happens that you do not have offspring from the aforementioned Clementia, you and the same heirs shall nonetheless have the aforementioned counties with all their rights and appurtenances, as is more fully contained in the public instrument drawn up on this matter: We, inclined by your supplications, holding what has been done by the same Henry in this matter as ratified and pleasing, by the counsel and assent of our brothers and by apostolic authority, confirm it, etc., up to: we strengthen. And so that your devotion towards us and the Roman Church may grow more, we grant the aforementioned counties to you and the said heirs as a fief anew, under the due and customary services, by the counsel and assent of the same brothers, of special grace, so that you and the said heirs may hold the same counties with barons and other men, enfeoffed and not enfeoffed, woods, pastures, cultivated and uncultivated lands, waters and water courses, and with all their rights, justices, jurisdictions, and appurtenances, directly from the Roman Church, recognizing no other superior or lord besides it, in perpetuity. And so that you may consider this grace more gracious, we wish to inform you that we and the aforementioned Church will maintain you and the same heirs in possession of the aforementioned counties, and we shall care to provide you with necessary defense against all who would trouble, challenge, or disturb you concerning those counties; and if any complaints regarding castles or other lands of those counties have been granted by us or by the late Emperor Frederick of the Romans or by his son Conrad to anyone or any persons to the prejudice of the same Henry, we, revoking such grants, will strive to provide them with suitable exchange in the Kingdom of Sicily. Let no one diminish our confirmation, concession, and revocation, etc. Given at Naples by the hand of William, master of the schools of Parma, vice-chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the 16th Kalends of December, in the 13th indiction, etc., in the 12th year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro Iohanni Moro, magno regni Sicilie camerario, concedit ut comitatus Conse et Principatus cum omnibus iuribus et pertinentiis, quos Henricus de Principatu sibi et heredibus suis donaverat, ab Ecclesia Romana in feudum teneat, et promittit eos in possessione dictorum comitatuum manutenere. Dat. Neapoli, XVI Kal. Decembris, anno XII.

**Translation to English:**

To Gregory, abbot of the monastery of Saint Theodore of Gaeta. Due to the merits of your devotion, we gladly assent to your vows and favorably hear your petitions, as much as we can with God. Therefore, since our beloved son, brother Egidius, our penitentiary, has been directed to dispense with you by special mandate of the late Pope John, our predecessor, regarding the fact that you are known to have been elected in your monastery with the consent of the late Emperor Frederick, as is more fully contained in the letters of the same penitentiary drawn up on this matter, we, inclined by your supplications, confirming the same dispensation, hold it as valid and pleasing, and confirm it by apostolic authority, etc., as far as; we ensure. However, the tenor of those letters is as follows: To the venerable father in Christ, by the grace of God, bishop of Gaeta, brother Egidius, penitentiary of the Lord Pope, greetings in the Lord. We wish to inform your fatherhood that the religious man, Lord Gregory, abbot of the monastery of Saint Theodore of Gaeta, the bearer of these presents, has shown us by his confession that, when the said monastery was vacant by the death of Oderisius of good memory, the abbot of that monastery, the convent of the same monastery, with the consent of the late Emperor Frederick, who was not yet deposed but bound by the chain of excommunication, unanimously elected him as their abbot, and the canons of the Church of Gaeta, to whom the confirmation of such election then pertained, having confirmed the same election, the same Gregory, as elected and confirmed, managed the care of the said monastery as abbot and ministered both spiritually and temporally; who, finally, being weighed down by infirmity and having a remorseful conscience regarding the said election, by the advice of his confessor resigned the administration of the same monastery for nearly six years. Concerning which he approached the clemency of the Apostolic See, humbly supplicating to be mercifully provided for. We, therefore, by special mandate of the Lord Pope, through the venerable father Lord Raynald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri, having been made to us, dispense with the aforesaid abbot, that he may minister in his orders and govern the said monastery as abbot, according to the grace given to him by God, notwithstanding that he was elected with the consent of the said Frederick and, by reason of such election, acted as abbot of the aforesaid monastery. Given at Naples, 4th Nones of November, in the twelfth year of the pontificate of Pope Innocent IV. No one, etc. of our confirmation, etc. Given at Naples, 4th Nones of January, in the first year. 

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Gregorio abbati monasterii sancti Theodori Gaietani dispensat et electionem ipsum abbatem confirmat, auctoritate apostolica, non obstante consensu quondam Friderici imperatoris. Datum Neapoli, die 2a Ianuarii, anno primo.

**Translation to English:**

To the podestà, council, and all the people of Genoa residing in the city and district of Genoa. While the Church of God suffers multiple and very grave persecutions, you have shown a most firm and clear steadfastness in faith and devotion to it, so that, by resisting its enemies with all your might, you have incurred many losses of goods and dangers to your persons. Many are amazed at how you have stood out with such firmness of mind amidst so many adversities, and finally, by God's grace, you have been recognized with a famous and glorious victory. To these great merits, you have added other magnificent deeds with tireless spirit; namely, in overseas regions, those matters which seemed to concern the honor of the Church, the strength of ecclesiastical liberty, and the defense and expansion of the Catholic faith, you have promoted with great diligence and vigilant care under countless expenses and labors. 

Indeed, the pile of the aforementioned merits, shining like a certain star before the Apostolic See, has often prompted it to be concerned with exalting you with such honors and fostering you with an abundance of graces, so that henceforth a source of perpetual joy may be brought forth for you and your descendants. Since our predecessor, Pope Innocent of happy memory, personally passing through your city with his brothers, was informed by hearing and sight about many of these merits and was pleased to have recognized through evident work how sincere and obedient devotion was held towards the said See in you, he deemed it fitting to provide that, according to your desire, he should fortify you with the privilege of that grace through which affection for that reverend See may always grow in you, and it be brought to general knowledge that among the dear ones, the Church considers you most dear to itself, and that it is especially in its interest to repay those who have suffered for it with the greatness of the rewards they have longed for. 

Therefore, the same predecessor granted you this through his letters, and we, inclined by your prayers, which we deem worthy of the fullness of favor, by the authority of these presents, grant to your community, in the likeness of his predecessor, that you may be entirely free and immune in perpetuity from dues, levies, and collections, or tolls pertaining to us and any burden of servitude in the Kingdom of Sicily, which belongs to the right and property of the same See, and in the Duchy of Spoleto, the March of Ancona, the Patrimony of Saint Peter in Tuscany, and all the lands of the Roman Church. Let no one violate etc. our concession etc. Given at Naples, on the 8th day before the Ides of January, in the first year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa potestati, consilio et universis Ianuensibus mandat, quod, ob merita eorum in defensione ecclesiae et fidei catholicae, immunes sint in perpetuum a datis et oneribus in regno Siciliae et aliis terris ecclesiae Romanae. 1228, Jan. 8. Neapoli.

**Translation to English:**

In the name of the Holy and Undivided Trinity. Henry VI, by divine clemency, ever august Roman Emperor and King of Sicily. The unfailing grace of imperial liberality is accustomed to bestow the worthy rewards of merits to his faithful subjects, especially those who have never deviated from the path of loyalty, but have frequently remained devoted to our service, exposed to the loss of possessions and bodily dangers. Therefore, on this account, considering and keeping in mind the manifold services that our faithful Lucani and all the men of all Tuscany have diligently and frequently rendered to our majesty, and especially many of them in the kingdom of Sicily, we, together with our most illustrious consort Constance, illustrious Roman Empress and Queen of Sicily, grant to the men of Lucca and other men of Tuscany, our faithful subjects, the same right in the custom duties through all the ports of our kingdom, both in entry and exit, as the Pisans possess. We therefore decree and strictly command that no person whatsoever, high or low, ecclesiastical or secular, dares to burden or in any way disturb our aforementioned faithful subjects in this our grant. Whoever does so shall pay a penalty of 40 pounds of gold, half to our chamber and the remaining half to those who suffered the injury. For the memory of this matter, we have ordered the present page to be written and sealed with the seal of our majesty. Witnesses to this matter are: Matthew, Archbishop of Capua; William, Archbishop of Reggio; Bernard, Archbishop of Messina; John, Bishop of Cephalù; William, Marquis of Montferrat; Conrad, Duke of Spoleto; Marquard, Seneschal, Marquis of Ancona and Duke of Ravenna; Count Albert of Spanheim; and many others. I, Conrad, Bishop of Hildesheim, Chancellor of the Imperial Court, along with Lord Walter, Bishop of Troia and Chancellor of the Kingdom of Sicily, have recognized this. These acts were carried out in the year of the Lord's incarnation 1197, in the first indiction, in the reign of the most glorious Lord Henry VI, Roman Emperor and most powerful King of Sicily, in the 28th year of his reign, the 7th of the empire, and the 3rd of the Sicilian kingdom. Given at Messina by the hand of Albert, Protonotary of the Imperial Court, on the 27th day of the month of September. No one etc. of our confirmation etc. Given at Naples, 5th Kalends of February, in the first year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Urbanus IV papa consilio et communitati Lucanis confirmat privilegium concessum a Henrico VI Romanorum imperatore et Constantia uxore illius, quo ius in tholoneo per omnes portus regni Siciliae sicut Pisani habeant. Datum Neapoli, V Kalendas Februarii, anno primo (1262, Jan. 28).

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot and convent of the monastery of Lucelle, of the Cistercian order, in the diocese of Basel. It is customary, indeed, etc., up to: bestow. Your petition, indeed, read before us, contained that, etc. Inclined by the prayers of the said bishop and chapter, as well as yours, we, therefore, hold as ratified and pleasing what has been providently done by the aforementioned bishop, chapter, and count, and we confirm it by apostolic authority, etc., up to: strengthened, causing the tenor of those letters to be inserted word for word into the present ones; which is as follows: In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. Berthold, by the grace of God, bishop of Basel, to all Christ's faithful viewing the present page, forever. We likewise consider it pleasing and acceptable that we will firmly render service to the divine majesty when we diligently watch for the honor of His and the adornment of our mother Church by reforming deformed churches or transforming them for the better. Therefore, when we came to the convent of Michelbach, formerly of the nuns of the order of St. Benedict of our diocese, exercising the office of visitation by the authority of both the supreme pontiff and ourselves, and it was clearly evident that the said place, along with the persons living there, was so deformed that there was no hope of restoring it to its former state: using the counsel of wise men, especially Henry the provost, William the dean, and all our chapter, as well as some religious persons of the orders of the Friars Minor and Preachers and other God-fearing ones gathered there, with the consent and free will of Ulric, Count of Ferrette, our brother, and his sons, whom we induced to this, for they had been advocates of the same convent, we subjected the said convent with all its possessions, albeit few at present, to the monastery of Lucelle of the Cistercian order of our diocese, in full right, decreeing that hereafter the persons living there should serve the Lord under the obedience of the abbot of the said monastery of Lucelle, whoever he may be at the time, and under the rule of the Cistercians. We also provided and caused to be provided for the nuns of the said convent in food, clothing, and other necessities for their sustenance, as long as they live, competently, if they do not fall from the aforesaid provision through their own fault. Once they have departed from this life, the aforementioned convent will be governed by both monks and clerics, through whom divine service and pleasing service to God may be manifestly increased. And lest by this our ordination there be generated less prejudice to the Church of Basel, to which the aforementioned convent was immediately subject, by the required and nonetheless obtained consent of the same Henry the provost, William the dean, and our chapter, we further decree that the abbot and convent of the monastery of Lucelle shall pay to the dean of the major church of Basel forty solidi, to the other canons sixty, and to the chapel, which we have founded for God in the court in which we reside, whose collation we wish to pertain to the dean, also sixty, annually on the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary. And lest any scruple of doubt or matter for question may arise hereafter concerning the foregoing, we have caused the present charter to be strengthened with our and our chapter's seals. Done in the year of the Lord 1253, the tenth Kalends of December. To none etc. of our confirmation etc. Given at Assisi, on the eighth Ides of May, in the eleventh year.

**Regesto:**

Innocentius IV papa abbati et conventui monasterii Lucelensis ordinis Cisterciensis Basiliensis diocesis confirmat subiectionem cenobii de Michelenbach cum omnibus eius possessionibus monasterio de Lucela, auctoritate apostolica, et providet monialibus in victu et vestitu. Datum Assisii, VIII Idus Maii, anno XI (1254).

**Translation to English:**

To Master Albert, canon of Pisa, residing in Paris. Jacob de Scala, Jacob Giberti, and their associates, citizens and merchants of Florence, have submitted their petition to us, stating that they lent a certain sum of money to Master Thomas of Cambrai and Arnold called Digant, canons of Liège, who were procurators of the noble lady, the Countess of Flanders and Hainaut, by mandate from the Countess herself to contract a loan, to be repaid at a certain place and time, as is more fully contained in a public instrument drawn up thereon. Therefore, we command that the said Countess and her sons, her successors, whom we have caused to be bound by the chain of excommunication through our beloved son William, Master of the Schools of Parma, our Vice-Chancellor, and their lands to be placed under ecclesiastical interdict, as is more fully contained in the letters made on this matter sealed with the seal of the said Vice-Chancellor, if they do not satisfy the said merchants within fifteen days after the appointed term for the money according to the terms of the said instrument, once the said fifteen days have elapsed, you publicly announce them as excommunicated and their said lands as placed under ecclesiastical interdict until the said merchants are fully satisfied concerning the money with just and moderate expenses and due restitution of damages, entirely ceasing interest, by others who will announce it, contradictors etc. — notwithstanding if any have been granted by the same See that they cannot be interdicted, suspended, or excommunicated by apostolic letters, which have not made full and express mention of such an indulgence word for word, or any other indulgence granted by the said See to any person or place under any form of words, of whose full tenor it is necessary to make mention in our letters and by which the effect of these presents may be hindered or delayed, and the constitution on two diets issued in the general council. We have also caused the tenor of the letters of the said Vice-Chancellor to be inserted verbatim in these presents. Which is as follows: To all who shall inspect the present letters, William, Master of the Schools of Parma, Vice-Chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, greeting in the Lord. We make known to you by these presents that, since Jacob de Scala, Jacob Giberti, and their associates, citizens and merchants of Florence, lent a certain sum of money at the Apostolic See to Master Thomas of Cambrai and Arnold called Digant, canons of Liège, procurators of the noble lady, Lady Margaret, Countess of Flanders and Hainaut, by mandate from the said lady Countess to contract a loan, to be repaid at a certain place and time, as is more fully contained in a public instrument drawn up thereon, by the special mandate of the most holy father, Lord Innocent, the supreme pontiff, made to us orally, having seen and diligently considered the tenor of the letters of the same lady Countess made concerning the aforesaid business and the aforesaid public instrument, we hereby bind the said lady Countess and her sons, her successors, from now on by the chain of excommunication, placing their lands under ecclesiastical interdict, if they do not satisfy the said merchants within fifteen days after the appointed term for the money according to the terms of the said instrument. Once the said fifteen days have elapsed, by the mandate of the said lord, we have decided and commanded by these presents that the said Countess and her sons shall be publicly announced as excommunicated at the request of the said merchants, namely in the places the said merchants shall choose, and their said lands placed under ecclesiastical interdict, until the said creditors are fully satisfied concerning the money with just and moderate expenses and due restitution of damages, entirely ceasing interest. To the noble man Manfred, prince of Taranto, our faithful subject. The Mother Church, always merciful and gentle in its actions, maintains a mode of kindness towards its sons and subjects, choosing to preserve gentleness over rigor and to forgive rather than to be harsh. For it recognizes that true retribution is best achieved through magnanimous forgiveness. Through you, in whom conspire nobility, power, industry, and many other praiseworthy attributes, honor, advantage, and the exaltation of the Church can be effectively and abundantly procured. We have decided to elevate your person with magnificent gifts and to adorn your status with distinguished honors, so that, rejoicing in the abundance of benefits poured upon you, you may burn with greater love and devotion towards the Church.

Moreover, extending apostolic favor towards you, we fully confer anew, by the counsel of our brothers, all the aforesaid granted by Frederick to you and your heirs in perpetuity as a special grace.

Additionally, we have graciously decided to grant you the county of Andria in exchange for the county of Monte Caveoso, which the noble man Berthold, Marquis of Homburg, now holds, so that you and your heirs may hold the principality, honor, and counties with their cities, castles, towns, ports, baronies, and infeudated and non-infeudated men, cultivated and uncultivated lands, forests, waters, and watercourses, pastures, with honors, dignities, and rights pertaining to full and mixed jurisdiction, directly from the Roman Church, acknowledging no superior or lord other than it in these matters in perpetuity.

The great kindness of Mother Church maintains that affectionate care towards her children, so that she bestows great benefits on those who revere her with due devotion as a mother, and does not reject others who, after a period of irreverence and disobedience, return to her good pleasure and command; to the former, she gladly extends the hand of benevolence, and from the latter, she does not withhold the hand of mercy, diligently nurturing the former in the bosom of goodwill, and kindly admitting the latter to the embrace of propitiation, rightly replenishing the former with the milk of sweetness and offering the consolation of her breasts to the latter. Since you have fully committed yourself to the arms of the Church, recognizing her as mother and lady, and your will has been firmly established for her commands and service, we, with great joy conceived from this, receive you into our grace and the grace of the Apostolic See, remitting to you all injuries and offenses that you have inflicted upon us and the same See and Church. We take your person, your beloved wife the noblewoman Countess of Catanzaro, and all your nephews, along with all your relatives and kin, as well as with all the goods that you reasonably possess at present or may justly acquire in the future with the Lord's help, under our protection and that of the same See, and we fortify you with the protection of this present writing, strictly prohibiting any ecclesiastical or secular person from daring to inflict injury, trouble, or grievance upon you in person or possessions. And because the Kingdom of Sicily, with all its districts and appurtenances, pertains fully to the aforesaid See and is wholly devolved to its dominion, we, wishing to honor you manifoldly in it, inclined by your supplications, hold ratified the concessions and donations both of the County of Catanzaro and of the Castle of Mesoraca and the fief of Rende, made to you by the late Frederick, once Emperor of the Romans and King of Sicily, and by Conrad his son, and decided, by the counsel of our brothers with apostolic authority, to confirm them and fortify them with this writing's protection, notwithstanding any sentence of deprivation or deposition pronounced against the aforementioned Frederick by apostolic authority, and that both Frederick and Conrad were then bound by the chain of excommunication, and that they otherwise did not have the faculty of granting or conceding such things. Moreover, so that your devotion towards us and the aforementioned See may grow more, we confer anew to you and your heirs in perpetuity, by the counsel of the same brothers, the county, the castle, and the fief aforesaid granted by the same Frederick and Conrad, and if any are lacking to you pertaining to the same county, with special grace, so that you and those heirs may hold the county, castle, and fief aforesaid, of which we have invested your noble nephew Fulco in your name, with castles, towns, baronies, cultivated and uncultivated lands, men enfeoffed and not enfeoffed, woods, waters and watercourses, and pastures, with honors, dignities and with those things which pertain to pure and mixed imperium, with their rights, jurisdictions, and other appurtenances, immediately from the Roman Church, recognizing no other than it as superior or lord thereof, granting you moreover that you may lawfully and freely establish some of your nephews or their sons as your legitimate heirs in the aforesaid if you shall not have legitimate offspring. We and the same Church will also maintain you and those heirs in the possession of the aforesaid county, castle, and fief, and will take care to assist you with suitable defense against all who shall have molested, attacked, or troubled you concerning them.
