To the noble man Thomas, knight of Anagni. The prompt faith and devotion you have shown in the faithful custody of our castle of Fumone towards the Roman Church, commendably in effect, rightly deserve that, pursuing your person with special benevolence, we favorably accede to your supplications. Therefore, we, while we were constituted in a lesser office, and of blessed memory the priest of the title of Saint Mary in Trastevere and our beloved son, R., cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo, vicars in Campania and Maritima by the authority of the Apostolic See, considering all expenses, labors, and costs which your brother, Stephen, our chaplain, and you have undertaken for the support of the said castle and fort, granted to you and your heirs in perpetuity, freely and wholly, the fief or holding of John Obtinelli, a traitor, with what he held and possessed of the goods of Richard, his father-in-law, in the castle of Fumone and its territory, which the same John Obtinelli had been deprived of due to his faults, with all its rights and appurtenances, by the authority of Pope I., our predecessor, which we exercised at that time, so that you may hold it as other knights of the same castle are known to hold, as is more fully contained in our and the said cardinals' letters made thereon: you humbly supplicated that we would care to confirm this grant by apostolic authority with our accustomed kindness. Therefore, inclined to your supplications, having the same grant as agreeable and ratified, we confirm it by apostolic authority and strengthen it, causing the tenor of those letters to be inserted verbatim into the present document; which is as follows: By divine mercy, R., Bishop of Ostia and Velletri, priest of the title of Saint Mary in Trastevere and R., cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo, vicars in Campania and Maritima of the Apostolic See, to the beloved in Christ... archpriest of Saint Mary of Fumone, greetings in the Lord. Since grace should be bestowed upon merits and the diligence of the obedient should not lack due reward, it is fitting and reasonable that those who devote themselves with all their strength and heart to the services of the Roman Church should be recompensed with the rewards due to them. Therefore, considering the purity and constancy of our dear discreet man Stephen of Anagni, chaplain of the lord pope, as well as his diligence, concern, and solicitude, which he has shown and continues to show with prompt devotion for the custody of the castle and fort of Fumone, having also weighed and inspected the burdens, expenses, labors, and costs which he has undertaken for the support and service of the said castle and fort, we grant to the said Thomas, knight, and his heirs in perpetuity the fief or holding of John Obtinelli, traitor, or by whatever other name it is called, with what he held and possessed of the goods of Richard, his father-in-law, in the aforesaid castle and its territory, with all its rights and appurtenances, by the authority of the lord pope, which we exercise, freely and wholly, with certain knowledge to hold, as other knights of the same castle are known to hold. Therefore, by the authority of the present, we command and mandate to you that, upon seeing these letters, you should endeavor to invest the same Thomas in the said fief or holding, as stated, with the appropriate solemnity, introducing him into corporal possession thereof. Dated at Anagni, in the year of the Lord 1245, in the third year of the pontificate of Pope Innocent IV, in the third indiction, in the month of September, on the third day of its beginning. So that you, Stephen, and your legitimate sons, Jacob, whom you now have, may fully claim the right in the aforesaid fief or holding for yourselves in the future, we grant it with all its rights and appurtenances anew to you and the same Stephen and Jacob and their heirs in perpetuity of special grace. To no one etc. of our confirmation and concession etc. Dated at Naples, five days before the Kalends of February, in the first year [of our pontificate].

To the noble men Berthold, Odo, and Ludovic, brothers and marquises of Hohenberg, our faithful ones, greetings, etc. The mother church, always clement and mild in its actions, holds a manner of kindness towards its sons and subjects, in such a way that, as it exults greatly in works of piety and considers it delightful to show mercy, it chooses more to maintain gentleness rather than rigor and to forgive rather than to be severe. Hence, if it finds fault or offense in anyone, as it finds it delightful and pleasant to forgive the sinner by remitting or moderating the penalty, it more willingly spares than strikes and shows itself more gracious than severe; for indeed it recognizes that true and noble vengeance is taken when one is magnanimously forgiven. The church especially seeks and desires that those gathered in its kind bosom may prosper in love and devotion and continually delight in the sweetness of its abundance, which we willingly exhibit in gifts and favors, so that by our benevolence and liberality, they may be more strongly fortified in our goodwill and that of the church. Since you have totally committed yourselves to the arms of this church, acknowledging it as mother and mistress, and have healthily fixed your will on its commands and services, we have conceived great joy from this. Because through you, in whom nobility of birth, power, industry, and many other praiseworthy things come together, the honor, advantage, and exaltation of the church can be effectively procured, we have provided to honor your persons with worthy gifts and to magnify your state with magnificent graces, especially since you have long and diligently labored to draw our former Roman Emperor and his son to its devotion and to reform the bonds of peace between them and the church. Therefore, since the kingdom of Sicily with all its districts and appurtenances fully belongs to the apostolic see and has been totally devolved to its dominion, we, wishing to elevate you in that by the prerogative of benefits, grant and give to you and your heirs, in perpetuity, by the counsel and assent of our brothers, the duchy of Amalfi with its cities, castles, villages, hamlets, namely Amalfi, Plaiano, Vetita Maiore, Vetita Minore, Rufforore, Casanova, Loretto, Toboli, Scala S, Ravello, Tramonte, Agerula, Pogerula, Pinot, Pigmonte, Atrano, Maiori, Minori, the island of Capritana and Pasitana, as well as with their men, honors, rights, jurisdictions, the right of patronage of conventual and non-conventual churches, pastures, woods, meadows, possessions, cultivated and uncultivated lands, waters and watercourses, justices and with all their rights and appurtenances, and with those things that pertain to full and mixed empire, namely those that are of domain in domain and those that are of service in service, except for the city of Licterensi and the castle of Graniani, by certain knowledge and special grace — notwithstanding any constitution promulgated or to be promulgated, by which this our concession or donation could be invalidated or in any way derogated — so that no justiciar nor any other official of the court, greater or lesser, except a legate of the apostolic see, may seek or demand or ordain or establish anything in the duchy, cities, castles, villages, hamlets, and other aforementioned, nor use any power or jurisdiction, but you and your heirs may hold and possess all those things, of which we have invested you in the presence of the aforementioned brothers with a ring, in fief directly from the Roman Church, acknowledging no superior or lord from it except itself. To the Dean of Saint Savior of Metz. Since our venerable brother, the Bishop of Metz, was bound by a sentence of excommunication by apostolic authority due to debts he owes to certain Sienese merchants, and an arrangement was subsequently established between him and the said merchants through the mediation of our beloved son Hugh, Cardinal Priest of the title of Saint Sabina, under a certain form, we command your discretion, with the assent and will of the procurators of the said merchants, through apostolic writings, to grant the said bishop the benefit of absolution concerning the same sentence. Considering the vigilance, diligence, and solicitude you have shown in the defense of the city of Otranto, as well as the tireless efforts you have undertaken for the governance of the said city, and wishing to extend to you the hand of apostolic generosity on this account, we, inclined by your supplications, grant to you and your heirs, who remain in the devotion of the same church, the hamlet of Specchia de Minerum, which formerly belonged to Berard of Luco, traitor to the Roman Church, with all its men, rights, and appurtenances, as a fief with due and customary services, by special grace. To the elected archdeacon. Due to the merits of your devotion, we gladly grant your requests and favorably hear your petitions, as much as we can with God. Since, because of the tyranny of the treacherous Ezzelino, you do not dare to remain in your church, we, inclined by your supplications, supplement this: we grant you the authority, by these present letters, as an apostolic see legate, to know and decide on causes and other matters pertaining to your office and to exercise them at the apostolic see or wherever you may be, as if you were residing personally in the aforesaid church. **Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Tricarico. Since, in response to the urgent and insistent request of our dear sons, the provost and chapter of Regensburg, we have decided to entrust you with the task of conducting an investigation on various charges against our venerable brother, the Bishop of Regensburg, by our letters under a specific form, we command you, once you have proceeded in this matter according to the form given to you, to ensure by our authority that both parties are cited peremptorily, so that within two months after your citation, they may appear before us in person or through suitable procurators, to receive a just sentence, God willing. To the Bishop of Tournai: On behalf of the beloved sons, the aldermen and the citizens of the town of Bruges in your diocese, it was brought to our attention that some bigamists and husbands of widows, bearing the clerical tonsure, under the pretext of this, unjustly refuse to be subject to the statutes of the country and to contribute to the taxes, collections, and other burdens of the said town, like other laymen, to the detriment and grievance of the citizens. To the elect of Alba. **Translation to English:**

To John, rector of the church of Saint Christopher outside the walls of the city of Liège, and to the beloved daughters in Christ, the Beguines, living in the parish of that church. We gladly consent with a benevolent affection to your desires in these matters, through which the removal of grievances will ensure the tranquility of your state. Hence, inclined by your supplications, we, by the authority of these presents, grant you, dear rector, or any of you, daughters Beguines, that you cannot be brought to trial outside the city of Liège by letters of the Apostolic See or its legates unless the letters of the same See have made full and express mention of this kind of indulgence; these presents will be valid for no more than five years. Let no one etc. of our concession. Given at Viterbo, the 7th Ides of August, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Iohanni rectori ecclesiae sancti Christofori et Beghinis in parrochia eiusdem ecclesiae concessit, ne extra civitatem Leodiensem trahi possint in causam, nisi hoc expressum sit in litteris apostolicis; quinquennii spatio valitura. Dat. Viterbii, VII Idus Augusti, anno quarto (1246).

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Cambrai. Your fraternity has informed us that several clerics, both secular and regular, as well as some nobles subject to your diocesan law, have obtained from the Apostolic See the indulgence that no one could issue a sentence of interdiction, suspension, or excommunication against their persons, nor place their lands under ecclesiastical interdict. However, since because of this, you cannot take action against them, your jurisdiction is considerably weakened, you have requested appropriate remedy for this matter to be granted to you. Therefore, by the authority of these presents, we grant to your fraternity that — notwithstanding these indulgences — you may freely exercise your jurisdiction over them. For it does not seem plausible that our predecessors wished the jurisdiction of ordinaries to be weakened by such an indulgence, nor do we wish that such an indulgence be extended to them in any way. Given at Naples, the 11th of the Kalends of May, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto (in Latin):**

Innocentius IV papa (episcopo Cameracensi concedit, ut, non obstantibus indulgentiis clericis et nobilibus diocesis concessis, iurisdictionem suam libere exerceat. 1244, Apr. 21, Neapoli.

**Translation to English:**

To the archpriest of Padua, vicar in Calabria of our beloved son O., cardinal deacon of Santa Maria in Via Lata, legate of the apostolic see. Since our beloved son O., cardinal deacon of Santa Maria in Via Lata, legate of the apostolic see, has decided to appoint you as his vicar in Calabria, we want to make it known through the content of these presents that the promises which you may make to counts, barons, knights, or communities of cities, castles, or other places, for the promotion of the Church’s business in the same Calabria, committed to you by the same legate, as well as the agreements which you may decide to establish with them or some among them for this reason, will be held as ratified and firm by us. Given at Naples, on the Calends of April, in the first year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archipresbytero Paduano, vicario in Calabria dilecti filii O. Sanctae Mariae in Via Lata diaconi cardinalis, promissiones et conventiones cum comitibus, baronibus seu communitatibus in Calabria pro ecclesiae negotio factas ratificaturum se esse significat. 1227, Apr. 1. Neapoli.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Metz. The unbearable burden of debts, under which your church is heavily weighed down, prompts us to give special attention, among other duties of our vigilance, to supporting it with suitable help and assistance, so that it may be relieved from such burdens of debt and breathe amidst the distressing pressures of usury. Therefore, feeling compassionate towards its and your needs with a kind heart, we have decided to grant to your fraternity, by the tenor of these presents, the authority to receive, up to the amount of a thousand marks sterling, in the payment of such debts and not for other uses, from usuries, robberies, and other ill-gotten gains, provided those to whom restitution ought to be made cannot be known or found at all, as well as from any bequests left indistinctly for pious uses, provided the assent of their executors is obtained, and from the redemption of diocesan vows previously made, except for those related to Jerusalem. This concession is granted on the condition that, if you have not otherwise obtained such grace from us for the reception of similar things, nothing of the said thousand marks shall be left, restored, or given to those from whom they were received, and whatever is thus left, restored, or given shall not benefit the liberation of those debts, nor shall they be considered in any way absolved in respect of it. Let no one—our concession etc. Given at Viterbo, on the tenth day before the Kalends of July, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Metensi concedit facultatem recipiendi usque ad summam mille marcarum sterlingorum ad solutionem debitorum ex usuris et aliis male acquisitis, sub conditionibus specificatis. Datum Viterbii, X Kalendas Iulii, anno tertio.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected Bishop of Speyer, Chancellor of the Imperial Court. Due to certain reasons, you claim not to have the conscience to receive the orders and the office of consecration from our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Mainz, your metropolitan. We grant you, by the authority of these presents, the faculty to receive the aforementioned orders at the appointed times and the office of consecration according to the custom of appointed bishops from whichever archbishop or bishop holding the grace and communion of the Apostolic See you prefer, provided that no prejudice is generated against the Church of Mainz in the future. Given at the Lateran, on the 11th of December, in the second year of our pontificate. To the same. Deserving of your devotion's affection, we gladly accede to your wishes and favorably hear your petitions as far as we can with God's help. Therefore, inclined by your devoted supplications, we have deemed it proper to exempt your person from the jurisdiction of our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Mainz, for up to three years by the authority of these presents. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa electo Spirensi cancellario aule imperialis concedit facultatem recipiendi ordines et munus consecrationis ab archiepiscopo vel episcopo gratia et communione Apostolicae Sedis habente, et ab iurisdictione archiepiscopi Maguntini per triennium eximit. Datum Laterani, III Idus Decembris, anno secundo.

**Translation to English:**

To William, illustrious King of the Romans. As we have received from the contents of your petition, men from the parts of Frisia, who you have long considered disobedient and rebellious, have submitted themselves to your dominion as they are obliged to do, and have granted to you and your heirs in perpetuity the tithes of all their possessions, from which no one has received them up till now, in view of your county of Holland. Therefore, we, inclined by the devout supplications of your exalted status, having ratified and approved the same concession, grant you the authority by the present document, that you and your heirs may freely and lawfully receive and retain the revenues of these tithes for a period of five years, so that the places and persons to whom these tithes are legally owed may freely receive them after the aforementioned five-year period. Let no one etc. of our concession etc. Given at Anagni, on the 12th Kalends of October, in the first year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Guillelmo illustri regi Romanorum concedit ut decimas omnium possessionum in Frisia, a subditis olim contumacibus concessas, usque ad quinquennium percipere ac retinere possit. 1243, Sept. 20. Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the illustrious King of England. Since our beloved son, Wlteranus, elected by the mandate of our predecessor Pope John of happy memory, has gone to serve the Church for the pressing business of the Kingdom of Sicily, taking with him a honorable and valiant company of knights, and has therefore had to bear many expenses, so much so that besides the losses he is known to have incurred on this account, these expenses amount to the sum of four thousand and eight hundred Touraine pounds, to which the Roman Church is indeed bound to him, and you are obliged to pay all debts contracted for the promotion of the aforesaid business until a certain term, as is more fully contained in the apostolic privilege which we have sent to you through our venerable brother, the Bishop of Hereford. We earnestly ask and exhort your Highness that, diligently considering that the said elect fervently pursues this business and vigorously insists on its promotion, you pay this money to him or to his procurator in his name, especially since this money is included in the sum contained in the aforesaid privilege, before the aforesaid term, out of reverence for us and the Apostolic See. For we will consider ourselves and the said Church to be fully satisfied by you regarding this money. Given at Anagni, on the 4th day before the Ides of July, in the first year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa illustri regi Anglie mandat ut pecuniam Wlterano electo, in negotio regni Sycilie, ante terminum solvat, secundum apostolicum privilegium. 1227, Jul. 12, Anagnie.

Translation to English:

"To the noble men Zacharias, Nicholas, and Bibulus, brothers, sons of the late Sergius de Bibulo, citizens of Brundusium. The Apostolic See has customarily, like a pious father, had among its desires to willingly bring gifts of prosperity and joy to those who suffer losses for its sake, and to offer the grace of comforting consolation. Therefore, carrying the entrails of paternal compassion towards you, whose father was condemned to a most disgraceful death for the purity of faith and for maintaining loyalty to the Roman Church, and who have suffered many losses in your possessions, and wishing to favor you with the grace of special favor, we grant to you and your heirs forever, as a special grace, all movable and immovable goods of Ayroldus de Ripalta, an infidel of the Church who betrayed the city of Brundusium into the hands of the late Manfred, Prince of Tarentum, and who procured the killing of your said father and other honorable men of the city, as well as the house called Margariti located in Brundusium with all its rights and appurtenances, belonging to the domain of the court. We grant this to you and your heirs in perpetuity. Let no one etc. Our concession etc. Given at Viterbo, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of December, in the third year."

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa Zachariae, Nicolao et Bibulo fratribus, civibus Brundusinis, bona Ayroldi de Ripalta, infidelis ecclesiae, et domum Margariti in Brundusio cum omnibus iuribus et pertinentiis de gratia speciali concedit. 1230, Nov. 21. Viterbii.

**Translation to English:**

To the illustrious King W. of the Romans. Since we are obliged to embrace certain devout followers of the Apostolic See with greater affection due to their greater merits, we appropriately show ourselves kind and gracious to them, and are found to be more benevolent and favorable; indeed, so that our fruitful affection towards such individuals does not contain any lack in effect but rather abounds to their benefit, it is fitting that we strive to raise them with appropriate honors, not only by extending the hand of our grace to them munificently, but also by diligently procuring their advantages with others. Therefore, since our beloved son, Marrolinus, a knight and former castellan of Rocca Sorella, who is devoted to us, rendered great and devout services in the matter of the kingdom of Sicily to our predecessor of happy memory, Pope Innocent, and subsequently to us, whereby he deservedly earned the grace and favor of the Apostolic See, we, wishing that he may feel your serene goodwill on this account, earnestly request and encourage your excellency that, having him, Marrolinus, and his noble wife Agnes, specially commended for our sake and the reverence of the Apostolic See, you may be favorable and kind to them in all their affairs, so that they may rejoice that they have been devoted to us and the aforementioned See, and so that we may deservedly commend your serenity with worthy praises in the Lord. Given at Anagni, October 14, in the first year (of our pontificate).

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa W. regi Romanorum illustrissimo commendat Marrolinum militem et Agnetem uxorem eius, ut in suis agendis favorabilem se exhibeat. 1227, Oct. 14, Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Ademar of Poitiers, Count of Valentinois. Our beloved son H., cardinal priest of the title of St. Sabina, has informed us that if you and the noble woman Margaret, Marchioness of Montferrat, were to enter into marriage with each other, it would resolve serious discord and prevent spiritual dangers. Therefore, we, who act in the place of the peaceful king on earth, desiring to procure peace for all and each, inclined by the prayers of the cardinal, dispense with you by apostolic authority to lawfully contract marriage with the said noblewoman — notwithstanding that your former wife Sibyl was related to the said noblewoman within the line of consanguinity, one of them being related in the third degree from one side from the root and the other in the fourth degree from the other side. Let no one [impede] etc. our dispensation etc. Given at the Lateran, 26th January, in the second year [of our pontificate]. To the noble woman Margaret, Marchioness of Montferrat. II. Our beloved son etc. [repeating the same details]: that if you and the noble man Ademar of Poitiers, Count of Valentinois, were to enter into marriage etc. [as above]. Given at the Lateran, 26th January, in the second year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro Ademaro de Pictavia comiti Valentinot et nobili mulieri Margarite marchionisse Montisferrati concedit dispensationem ad matrimonium contrahendum, non obstante consanguinitatis linea quae cum Sibilla, prior uxore Ademari, intercedit, ut graves discordiae sopiantur. Datum Laterani, VII Kalendas Februarii, anno secundo.

Translation to English:

To the Bishop of Hildesheim. Your submitted petition stated that due to the dangers of wars, which the noble man, the Duke of Brunswick, did not hesitate to bring upon you and your church by devastating the goods of the said Hildesheim church through plundering and fire, you have been compelled to contract such a burden of debts that unless support is provided to the said church by the Apostolic See, it cannot be alleviated in any way. Therefore, you humbly requested us to deign to assist you with paternal care in this matter. We, thus inclined by your supplications, grant you by the authority of these presents, that for the relief of these debts you may receive for one year the proceeds of ecclesiastical benefices which are vacant in your city and diocese within three years, provided that they are converted solely to the payment of these debts, and to compel the contradictors and rebels by ecclesiastical censure, provided that these benefices are not defrauded of their due services and the care of souls is in no way neglected in them, where it is incumbent. To no one etc. of our concession etc. Given at the Lateran, the 5th Kalends of February, in the second year.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Hildesemensi concedit ut ad debitorum relevationem per annum unum proventus beneficiorum vacantium in civitate et diocesi sua infra triennium recipiat et contradictores per censuram ecclesiasticam compellat. Datum Laterani, V Kalendas Februarii, anno secundo.

**Translation to English:**

To the people of the city of Palermo, our faithful. Since your city, the first among others in Sicily, has risen from vile subjugation — to which an impious hand had long pressed it down — to the joy of desired freedom, having unfurled the banner of pure devotion with the fervent vigor of spirit, bringing to fruition the long-conceived and laudable intention of submitting to the sweet and gentle dominion of the Roman Church upon gaining the opportunity: We, considering these things with diligent reflection and wishing to honor the city itself with fitting graces from the Apostolic See, inclined by your supplications, confirm to you and your city by apostolic authority all the liberties, dignities, honors, and any other rights pertaining to you and your city from any concession whatsoever, whether of kings, emperors, or princes, or Roman pontiffs, as well as the reasonable customs long approved and peacefully observed in that city in the time of the late William II, King of Sicily. Additionally, we confirm the right of minting coinage, as you are known to have had during the times of the illustrious memory of Roger, William I, and the aforementioned William II, Kings of Sicily, up to the time of the late Frederick, former Emperor of the Romans. We confirm and fortify these for you and the aforementioned city by apostolic authority, etc., continuing: We strengthen them. Let no one, etc., our confirmation, etc. Given at Anagni, on the Nones of September, in the 10th year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa populo civitatis Panormi omnes libertates, dignitates, honores, et iura, ac consuetudines rationabiles tempore Willelmi secundi regis Sicilie observatas, nec non ius cudendi monetam, auctoritate apostolica confirmat. 1236, Sept. 5, Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To Henry, Bishop of Strasbourg. Your petition read before us contained that, for defending ecclesiastical freedom and for effectively promoting the business of the church and empire being conducted in those parts, you have incurred such grave enmities that it is not safe for you and your relatives and associates to litigate outside your diocese. Therefore, you humbly requested from us to mercifully address the disadvantages faced by you and them in this matter. Thus, considering your person worthy of special grace and inclined to your supplications, we grant by the authority of these presents that you, and our beloved sons, the noble Alexander your brother, Henry the rector of the church of Ebersheim, his son, your nephew, and also Olttol, the schoolmaster of the church of Honau, your special cleric, who faithfully stood by you in the said business, outside the said diocese cannot be summoned or brought to trial through apostolic letters obtained, through which citation of the parties has not been processed, or even to be obtained, which have not made full and express mention of these presents, for up to two years, provided that within the said diocese you are prepared in the meantime to exhibit the fullness of justice to those complaining against you before a competent judge. We grant this indulgence. To none etc. of our concession etc. Given at the Lateran, 16th Kalends of January, in the first year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Henrico episcopo Argentinensi concedit indultum, ne extra diocesim per biennium conveni possit, propter inimicitias quas pro ecclesiastica libertate tuenda incurrit. Laterani, XVI Kal. Ian., anno I.

**Translation to English:**

To James, canon of Padua, son of the noble man Manfred of Lobia, devoted to the Roman Church. The Apostolic See is accustomed to grant a benevolent favor to the pious wishes and honest prayers of those who ask. Your petition presented to us stated that our beloved son O. Cardinal Deacon of Santa Maria in Via Lata, then legate of the Apostolic See in the Lombard province, had instructed our venerable brother, the bishop of Adria, through his letters, to deprive Peter Abbatisse, once a canon of Padua who dared to adhere to Ezzelino of Romano, an enemy of God and the Church, of the canonries and prebends he held in the major and St. Michael's churches of Padua, and to confer and assign them to suitable persons devoted to the Roman Church, compelling objectors through ecclesiastical censure while disregarding any appeals. The same bishop, having lawfully examined and found the aforementioned circumstances, deprived Peter of the canonry and prebend he then held in the church of Padua by the authority of those letters, and canonically conferred them upon you, who persist in devotion to the Apostolic See, investing you likewise with the same, as is more fully contained in the public instrument drawn up thereof. We, therefore, inclined by your supplications, having ratified and approved what was providently done by the same bishop concerning this matter, confirm it by apostolic authority and provide it with the protection of the present writing. Let no one etc. Our confirmation etc. Given at the Lateran, on the second day before the Calends of May, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Iacobo canonico Paduano, filio Manfredi de Lobia, devotioni Romanae ecclesiae persistenti, canoniam et praebendam in ecclesia Paduana ab episcopo Adriensi canonice collatam, auctoritate apostolica confirmat. 1229, Apr. 30, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To Bernerius, Bishop of Cremona. As it was presented to us on your behalf, due to the devotion you bear towards us and the Apostolic See, you have been forced to live in exile outside your own seat by the Marquis Pelavicino, an enemy of God and the Church, after being expelled from the city of Cremona along with your relatives and associates by the same perfidious man. Stripped of your episcopal goods by him, you do not have other means to sustain yourself: therefore, inclined by your supplications, we grant you full authority by these presents to contract a loan for this purpose up to the sum of one hundred marks of silver, and to bind yourself, your successors, and the goods of your bishopric and the said bishopric to creditors, as well as to renounce the constitution regarding the two diets established in the general council and the benefit of complete restitution, and even the agreement of judges, should apostolic letters of any tenor happen to be obtained in the name of those creditors in the future. However, you and your successors are obliged to pay this money to those creditors, as well as damages, expenses, and interest, should you fail to pay the mentioned money by the deadline set by you, and the creditors should not be burdened with proving that the money has been used for the benefit of the said bishopric by virtue of any canonical or civil constitution, or any privilege or indulgence. Given at the Lateran, on the Ides of February, in the third year [of our pontificate].

---

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Bernerio episcopo Cremonensi auctoritatem plenam concedit ad contrahendum mutuum usque ad centum marcas argenti, et ad obligandum se, successores suos, et bona episcopatus creditoribus, necnon ad renuntiandum constitutionibus et privilegiis, pro damnis per marchionem Pelavicinum exulans perpessis. 1229, die 13 Februarii, apud Lateranum.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Chiusi. Formerly, a dispute arose between you and your church, the provost of the church of St. Mustiola of Chiusi, and the chapters of both churches on one side, and the authority, council, and commune of Chiusi on the other, over the temporal jurisdiction of the city of Chiusi, including houses, vineyards, woods, and various other matters. Because of this, much turmoil arose, and due to this dispute, as well as the fact that the same authority, council, and commune once adhered to Frederick, the former Emperor of the Romans, against the church, it is said that various sentences of interdict and excommunication were proclaimed against them by apostolic authority. Therefore, as it is believed that an amicable agreement between you and the people entrusted to you concerning these matters could be achieved, we, desiring that mutual charity be maintained and preserved among you, command that once a solemn agreement has been made by both parties according to our mandate with our beloved son, the abbot of the monastery of Spineto, of the order of Vallombrosa in the diocese of Chiusi, and guarantees have been given to abide by the decision or judgment of the said abbot, you may relax the said sentences according to the form of the church by our authority, imposing upon them nonetheless what you see fit to impose. This is notwithstanding any privileges granted to you and the said provost and chapters by the apostolic see that these sentences cannot be relaxed by the letters of this see without making full and explicit mention of such a privilege or any other indulgence of said see of any kind, by which this could be prevented. Given at Viterbo, on the Ides of December, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Clusino mandat, ut sententiis interdicti et excommunicationis, pro controversiis temporalium cum communi Clusino promulgatis, relaxatis arbitrium abbatem Spineto, Vallis Umbrose, observetur. 1230, Dec. 13. Viterbii.

Translation to English:

To the podestà, council, and commune of Milan. Although our ever-watchful care compels us to maintain general peace and the peaceful state of Italy, we must ensure an even more diligent watch over your city, as it is recognized as the nobler part of its province, has shown sincerer loyalty to the Roman Church since ancient times, and would cause a greater loss to the body of the community if such a significant member were harmed. We have learned that although a discord that had arisen among you was once prudently settled through the mediation of U. de Vialta, your then-podestà, and for more than forty years, peace and harmony, established by oath and agreement, were maintained, now, however, with the devil rekindling the extinguished coals of old disputes and striving to bring back abolished maladies to the peril of relapse, that peace is being disrupted under the pretext of certain statutes later enacted there, and is being violated, not only to the city's detriment but also to the jeopardy of the entire region. Therefore, because more careful counsel must be vigilant where the danger of the cause needing care is more apparent and the efficacy of health is more certain, we have decided to send our venerable brother, the Bishop of Bologna, a prudent man, and respectful in the eyes of us and our brothers, to you, so that from our behalf he may diligently and persistently urge you to observe this peace and oath, inducing you effectively through exhortations and entreaties according to the wisdom granted to him by God. Therefore, we command your community through apostolic writings to humbly and devoutly attend to this bishop in this matter, so that through his efforts, with your agreement, the fruit of beneficial harmony may arise, granted by the Lord. Given at Naples, on the Kalends of May, in the first year.

Regesto:

Gregorius IX papa potestati, consilio et communi Mediolanensibus mandat, ut ad observationem pacis et iuramenti reformati adhortationibus episcopi Bononiensis assentiant. 1227, Mai. 1. Napoli.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble woman M., Countess of Flanders and Hainaut. The effective devotion of your affection merits that, loving your person with sincere charity in the Lord, we shield you with the protection of the apostolic authority. Hence, we, inclined by your devout supplications, receive you, who persist in the devotion to the Church, along with the counties, towns, lands, rights, and jurisdictions you reasonably possess at present, under our protection and that of the apostolic see, and we fortify it with the protection of this present writing. Let no one etc. Given at Anagni, on the sixth day before the Kalends of February, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili mulieri M. comitisse Flandrie ac Hayonie, personam eius cum comitatibus, villis, terris, iuribus et iurisdictionibus sub protectione ecclesiae recipit et communit. Anagnie, VI Kal. Feb., anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Brandenburg. On behalf of our beloved sons, the noble men I., Margrave of Brandenburg, and P., Duke of Poland, it was humbly requested of us that, in order to settle the severe discord and enmities that had arisen between the aforementioned margrave and duke long ago, a noble man Conrad, son of the margrave, and our beloved daughter in Christ, the noblewoman Constance, daughter of the duke, may be joined in marriage. We should take care to dispense, with apostolic kindness, with Conrad and Constance, allowing them to enter into marriage freely, notwithstanding the fact that they are related in the fourth degree of consanguinity. Therefore, we command you that, if it is hoped that through such a marriage peace and concord might arise between the aforesaid duke and margrave, homicides may be avoided, and calm and tranquility may be ensured in those regions, and if it becomes clear to you that this pleases our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, William, then authorize them to contract the marriage freely, notwithstanding the aforesaid impediment, by our authority, as you see fit according to God. Given at the Lateran, on the 14th day before the Kalends of January, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Brandeburgensi mandat, ut, si speratur per matrimonium inter Conradum, marchionis Brandeburgensis filium, et Constantiam, ducis Poloniae filiam, pacem et concordiam provenire, cum illis auctoritate apostolica dispenset, non obstante consanguinitatis gradu. 1227, Dec. 19. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the dean and custodian of the church of St. Leonard in the diocese of Strasbourg. On behalf of our beloved sons, the provost of Strasbourg, born of the noble lord of Gevolseke, and Conrad, a cleric, his cousin, brother of the lords of Litoměřice, in the diocese of Strasbourg, it was proposed before us that our beloved son, P., cardinal deacon of St. George at the Velum Aureum, then legate of the apostolic see in those parts, admitted them as his chaplains at the request of the same nobles, who personally, while pursuing the business of the general church in those parts, faithfully exposed their persons and goods for his promotion. However, because later certain constitutions were issued by us concerning the revocation of certain provisions and receptions of canons expecting prebends beyond the number of four to be vacated, the same chaplains, lest they be prejudiced by these constitutions, implored the grace of the apostolic see. We, therefore, making special favor to the said chaplains at the request of the same nobles, command that you restore them in the churches from which they have been excluded by these constitutions to the right that pertains to them by the grace made to them regarding such provisions or receptions, by our authority, and proceed to their provision in the same churches by you or another or others — the aforesaid constitutions notwithstanding — according to the forms delivered to their executors in the aforementioned matters; contradictors, etc. Given at Viterbo, the ninth day before the Kalends of March, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa decano et custodi ecclesiae Sancti Leonardi Argentinensis mandat, ut prepositum Argentinensem et Conradum clericum, capellanos a cardinali legato admissi, restituant ad ius in ecclesiis, a quibus constitutionibus exclusi sunt, et procedant ad eorum provisionem. 1230, Feb. 21, Viterbii.

**Translation to English:**

To the dean and chapter of Besançon. We are led by the merits of your devotion to pursue you with the special favor of grace and to fulfill with paternal benevolence what you rightfully request. Indeed, a petition presented to us on your behalf stated that although we have previously decreed by our constitution that receptions of canons expecting prebends in churches, except certain ones, are null and void, nevertheless, we have restored, by various letters out of special grace, the right of canonry to twenty-five and more of your church's canons, whose receptions were nullified by the same constitution, which had been acquired by them in the same church from the aforementioned receptions. It is said that you have admitted eight of these canons by the authority of such letters, who have not yet obtained prebends in the same church. Since it is not our intention to burden the aforementioned church with the restoration of so many canons, but rather to preserve it from future burdens as much as we can with God: so that beyond the aforementioned eight, you are not obliged to admit any more under the pretext of such restoration by letters obtained or to be obtained from the apostolic see, unless they make explicit mention of this indulgence and its tenor and the number of canons expecting prebends therein to become vacant, we grant you by the authority of these presents. We also decree void and null any sentences of excommunication, suspension, and interdict, if any have been promulgated against you or any of you contrary to the tenor of this indulgence. Let no one infringe upon our concession and constitution, etc. Given at Anagni, January 25th, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa decano et capitulo Bisuntinis indulgentiam praebet ne ultra octo canonicos ex receptionibus cassatis admittant nisi de huiusmodi indulto et numero canonicorum mentionem faciant, constitutiones contra tenorem indulti irritas decernens. 1231, Jan. 25, Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

Wernher, abbot of the Herfeld monastery of the Order of Saint Benedict in the Mainz diocese. When a request is made to us, etc. Truly, your petition presented to us contained that, when you had previously willingly resigned from the administration of the Hersfeld monastery for certain reasons, the prior and convent of the same monastery, prudently considering that due to the same resignation the monastery suffered not a little detriment both spiritually and temporally, reinstated you to the administration of the said monastery. To prevent any doubt from arising in their minds, they obtained letters from the abbot of Mount Saint Peter and his colleagues in Erfurt, of the Mainz diocese, from our beloved son P. cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, then legate of the Apostolic See in those parts, so that unless it was evident to them that you had resigned the administration of the aforementioned monastery due to some notable or probable fault, they would ensure what was done by the prior and convent regarding you was confirmed by his authority. By the authority of this mandate, the aforementioned abbot of Mount Saint Peter and his colleagues diligently inquired into the truth of the premises, and because it was evident to them that you had not resigned the administration of the monastery due to any notable or probable fault, they took care to confirm what was done by the aforementioned prior and convent concerning your reinstatement by the authority of the legate. Therefore, inclined by your supplications, we approve and confirm by apostolic authority what was providently done by the same abbot and his colleagues concerning this matter, etc., up to: we solidify. To no one, etc., our confirmation, etc. Given at Naples, on the 11th day before the Ides of May, in the first year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Wernhero abbati monasterii Herfeldensis ordinis Sancti Benedicti Maguntinae diocesis concessionem administrationis eiusdem monasterii, postquam ipse administrationi cessisset, ab abbate Montis Sancti Petri et collegis Erfordensibus confirmatam, auctoritate apostolica ratam et gratam habet. 1227, Mai. 11, Neapoli.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble woman Clara, daughter of the late Jeremias de Polenta, of the Ravenna diocese. When a request is made to us, etc., to the effect. Therefore, beloved daughter in Christ, we willingly consent to your just requests, and we take your person, along with all the goods that you reasonably possess at present or may acquire in the future through just means, under the protection of Saint Peter and our own. Specifically, we protect the estate of Burgandentum, Frassenetum, Casacutulam, and other properties located in the diocese of Luni, which, as you assert, were granted by our predecessor Pope Gregory of happy memory to the ancestors of the late Guido de Polenta, your grandfather, in recognition of their devotion to the Roman Church, and which Pope Innocent III of happy memory, our predecessor, confirmed to the said Guido, whose heirs you, Guido Rizutus, and Guido de Polenta, your cousins, are, under an annual rent of twelve Lucensian shillings. We confirm by apostolic authority for that portion which pertains to you, as you justly and peacefully possess it, under the specified part of the rent proportionate to this portion, and we secure it with the protection of this document—notwithstanding that your said cousins, concealing the truth and making no mention of you, procured the confirmation of all the above in full for themselves, as is said, by the apostolic see, or any other letters obtained concerning these matters by suppression of the truth from the see. No one is to infringe our protection and confirmation etc. Given at Viterbo, on the 13th day before the Kalends of April, in the fourth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorii IX papae nobili mulieri Clarae, filiae quondam Ieremiae de Polenta, diocesis Ravennatis, concedit ut personam suam cum bonis suis, et praesertim fundi in Lunensi diocesi, sub protectione beati Petri et apostolica confirmatione recipiat, notwithstanding quae consobrini sui per sedem apostolicam sine eius mentione procuraverunt. Datum Viterbii, XIII Kalendas Aprilis, anno quarto.

Translation to English:

To the Bishop of Regensburg. It has come to our attention that although the castle of Hohenburg with its appurtenances has from ancient times belonged to the church of Regensburg by title of ownership, Diepold, the margrave of Vohburg, and his heirs have held the castle for several years, having occupied it by force. When Berthold and his brothers later succeeded the margrave and held the said castle with its appurtenances, Berthold finally acknowledged the right that the church had in the said castle and its appurtenances, and he received the castle with its appurtenances in fief from the late Siegfried, the Bishop of Regensburg, your predecessor. In compensation for this fief, he donated his own castle of Rohrbach with its appurtenances to the aforementioned church and received it back in fief from the same bishop under the condition that, upon the vacancy of the fief, the said castles with their appurtenances would remain perpetually with the aforementioned church, not to be alienated under any title. However, as we have learned from some reports, the said castles with their appurtenances have recently reverted to the aforementioned church, and you intend to alienate them with their appurtenances, to the grave detriment of the same church. Therefore, wishing to prevent such injury, we strictly forbid, by the authority of these letters, that the aforementioned castles or either of them, or their appurtenances, be transferred by you or your successors to others under any title of obligation or alienation, to the detriment of the said church, decreeing that anything attempted contrary to our prohibition shall be null and void. Given at Viterbo, on the Ides of August, in the third year of our pontificate.

Regesto:

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Ratisponensi mandat ne castra de Hohemburcht et Rorbach cum suis pertinentiis alienet, decreta auctoritate apostolica, ut quicquid super hoc contra prohibitionem fiat, irritum sit et inane. 1229, Augusti 13. Viterbii.

**Translation to English:**

To the clergy of the diocese of Aquila in Furconensis. If you had prudently considered, as is appropriate, how the vice of disobedience is regarded, you would have strived to obey and attend humbly and devoutly to our venerable brother, your diocesan bishop of Furconensis. But, as we have learned from the same bishop's report, you, not considering that, like the other clergy of the Furconensis diocese, you are bound to obey the same bishop as your diocesan, have, with a spirit of rebellion, unjustly refused to show due obedience and reverence to him and to render an account of episcopal rights, which has caused not a small prejudice and grievance to him and the church of Furconensis. Therefore, wishing to test whether the crime of your disobedience can be abolished by the sweetness of kindness, we earnestly beg, admonish, and exhort your community, making an imperative command by apostolic writings, that redeeming past disobedience through subsequent obedience, you attentively and humbly respond in all matters pertaining to his office to the same bishop as the father and shepherd of your souls; and that you render an account of episcopal rights fully to him, providing him with the due satisfaction for those withheld, fulfilling our plea and command in such a way that we may not undeservedly commend your devotion thereafter. Otherwise, we will consider the sentence, which he duly pronounces on the rebellious, confirmed and will cause it to be enforced, with the Lord as our guide, until satisfaction is achieved. Given at Anagni, 8th of July, in the second year [of our pontificate].

---

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa clero diocesis Furconensis mandat ut obedientiam debitam episcopo suo exhibeant et iura episcopalia plene respondeant, alias sententiam in rebelles latam ratam habebit. 1238, Iul. 8, Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Sergio Siginulfi, citizen of Naples. Both reason and justice persuade us to favor the devotion of our faithful with apostolic kindness. Indeed, a petition presented to us on your behalf stated that our beloved son Octavian, cardinal deacon of Santa Maria in Via Lata and legate of the apostolic see, considering the merits of your devotion, decided, with our special mandate and by the authority of his legation, to grant to you and your heirs in perpetuity the fief that the late John Thesonus, a knight from Aversa, held in Aversa and its appurtenances, which had reverted to the court due to escheat, along with all its rights and appurtenances, and made you enter into physical possession of this fief, as is more fully contained in the letters drawn up regarding it. Therefore, inclined by your devoted prayers, and holding such a concession as ratified and pleasing, we confirm to you, who remain devoted to the church, by apostolic authority the said fief— notwithstanding that the late Conrad and Manfred, sons of the late Emperor Frederick, are said to have granted the said fief to Bartholomew de Bursis, a knight from Aversa, who, due to his lack of devotion, is detained in prison by mandate of the apostolic see, and that our predecessor, Pope Innocent of happy memory, confirmed the castles, fiefs, and other things that the said Frederick and Conrad are said to have conferred on the same Bartholomew, when the same Bartholomew remained in devotion to the church, for he did not remain in devotion to the church—up to the point: we secure. No one, etc., of our confirmation, etc. Given at Anagni, the 11th Kalends of July, in the 1st year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa nobili viro Sergio Siginulfi civi Neapolitano feudum in Aversa, quod Iohannes Thesonus tenuerat, auctoritate apostolica confirmat, non obstantibus concessionibus factis a Conrado et Manfredo Bartholomeo de Bursis. 1243, Iun. 21. Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the podestà and commune of Forosimphroniensis. The sincerity of your devotion prompts us to favor you in many ways with apostolic support and to honor you with a special gift of grace. Therefore, inclined by your supplications, we grant you full authority by the power of these present letters to freely hold and receive as your citizens, without prejudice to the rights of others, those men who have come or will come in the future to reside in your city. Let no one, etc., infringe on our concession. Given at Anagni, on the 8th Kalends of November, in the second year (of our pontificate).

To the podestà and commune of the city of Forosimphroniensis. The sincerity of your devotion and the steadfastness of your pure faith deserve that we pursue you with apostolic favor in many ways and honor you with a unique privilege of grace. Therefore, inclined by your supplications, we receive your persons, city, and all your goods, which you currently hold reasonably and which you will be able to acquire in the future with the Lord's help, into the special domain of the Roman Church and under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves, etc., until: we protect. Let no one, etc., infringe on our protection. Given at Anagni, on the 14th Kalends of November, in the third year (of our pontificate).

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa potestati et communi civitatis Forosimphroniensis, quos devotionis sinceritas commendat, auctoritatem concedit, ut homines in civitatem eorum advenientes in cives recipere possint, sub protectione apostolica et beati Petri. Dat. Anagnie, VIII Kalendas Novembris, anno secundo.

Gregorius IX papa potestati et communi civitatis Forosimphroniensis, devotionis et fidei constantiam laudans, personas, civitatem et bona eorum sub speciali dominio Romane ecclesie et protectione beati Petri et sua suscipit. Dat. Anagnie, XIIII Kalendas Novembris, anno tertio.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Besançon: The petition presented to us by our venerable brother, the bishop of Strasbourg, and our beloved sons, the prelates and clergy of the city and diocese of Strasbourg, stated that the master, consuls, and the community of citizens of Strasbourg have recently decreed, at their own will, that no one from the city shall transport grain or wine. Thus, under the pretext of this statute, they presume to prevent the aforementioned prelates and clergy from exporting their grain and wine from the said city for their own benefit. Furthermore, if any of the prelates or clergy sell their grain or wine within the city, the aforementioned masters, consuls, and community unjustly demand and extort a certain sum of money from them, in violation of ecclesiastical liberty and to the detriment and grievance of the prelates and clergy. Therefore, the bishop, prelates, and clergy humbly implored us to provide them with paternal care in this matter. Wherefore, we command that, if this is the case, you shall compel the same master, consuls, and university, to allow the prelates and clergy to freely remove their grain and wine from the city, as they have been accustomed to do from time immemorial, and to let them sell their grain and wine without any monetary exaction, through prior admonition, by means of excommunication against individuals and interdict against the city, with the removal of the option of appeal — notwithstanding any privileges granted to them or any of them by the apostolic see, or any apostolic letters which do not make full and express mention of such an indult, and notwithstanding the constitution of the two diets issued at the general council. Given at Anagni, 10th June, in the second year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Bisuntino mandat, ut, si verum sit quod magistri, consules et universitates civium Argentinensium prelatos et clerum Argentinensis civitatis prohibent ne bladum et vinum suum extra civitatem educant et ab eis pecuniam contra iustitiam exigunt, eosdem magistrum, consules et universitatem compellat, ut prelatos et clerum bladum et vinum extrahere et sine exactione vendere permittant, sub poena excommunicationis et interdicti. Anagnie, 10 Iunii, anno secundo.

**Translation to English:**

To Master Siger, canon of the church of Saint Stephen of Mainz, envoy of our venerable brother Gerhard, Archbishop of Mainz. Since, as you have proposed in our presence, you need to bear the expenses for the affairs of our venerable brother G., Archbishop and the church of Mainz, and to prevent these matters from remaining unresolved due to lack of funds, we, moved by your requests, grant you full authority by the present letters to contract a loan up to the sum of four hundred and fifty new sterling marks, and to bind the aforesaid archbishop and his successors, as well as the goods of the said church, to the creditors, renouncing the constitution of the two diets established in the general council and the benefit of full restitution and all apostolic letters and indulgences obtained and to be obtained, as well as the convention of judges, should apostolic letters of any tenor be obtained in the future in the name of those creditors. Yet, the archbishop and his successors are to pay such money and also damages, expenses, and interest if the money is not paid by the term set by you. Additionally, the need to prove that the said money was turned to the benefit of the said church shall not fall upon the creditors due to any canonical or civil constitution or any privilege or indulgence, full and express mention of which ought to be made in our letters, by which the archbishop and his successors might further protect themselves in some way. Given at Anagni, on the fourth day before the Nones of January, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Magistro Sigero, canonico ecclesiae S. Stephani Maguntinae, facultatem concedit contrahendi mutuum ad summam quadringentarum et quinquaginta marcarum sterlingorum pro negotiis ecclesiae Maguntinorum expediendis, et onera archiepiscopi et successorum eius et ecclesiae bona creditori obligandi. 1229, Jan. 2, Anagnia.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Lucca. Since the authorities, council, officials, and the commune of Pisa, asserting themselves ready to comply with the mandates of the Church, urgently requested from us absolution from all excommunication sentences pronounced against them for any reasons, we have instructed you, by our letters, that if you wished to oppose them in your name and that of the Church of Lucca regarding these matters, you were to ensure your appearance before us, either personally or through a sufficient procurator, with all your documents and reasons, by a certain day which we assigned to you as a peremptory term. When you personally and our beloved son, Master Hugo, rector of the Church of Saint Fabian of the Pisan Fabricii, procurator of the aforementioned authorities, council, and others, appeared in our presence, and the same master petitioned for the relaxation of the aforementioned sentences according to the form of the Church, you opposed and stated that since the same sentences had been pronounced for a manifest offense, namely the occupation and detention of castles of the Church of Lucca, they could not and should not be relaxed by right before the restitution of the aforementioned castles was made. To support your intention in this matter, you produced several apostolic letters and other legitimate documents, copies of which we had exhibited to the said procurator through our beloved son, Johannes, Cardinal Deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere Tulliano. Finally, after hearing and diligently examining the documents, letters, allegations, and other things you and the said rector presented before us and our brothers concerning the aforementioned matters, by the counsel of those brothers, we pronounced that the named rector in the procuratorial name of the aforementioned authorities and others, and through him, they were not to be admitted to the requests and nothing should be innovated in this matter. Given at the Lateran, on the 4th day before the Kalends of May, in the second year.

---

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Lucano mandat ut, occasione petitionis a potestate Pisana factae pro absolutione excommunicationum, coram ipso compareat cum documentis; post auditas partes, refutat petitionem Pisani. Datum Laterani, IV Kal. Maii, anno secundo.

**English Translation:**

To the abbot in Lennin of the Cistercian order in the diocese of Brandenburg and to the provincial prior of the Dominican brothers in Germany. On behalf of the beloved sons, the noble men, the Duke of Saxony and John, the Margrave of Brandenburg, it was humbly requested from us that we grant the margrave and the noble woman, the daughter of the said duke, the license to contract marriage with each other, to confirm the contract, and to lawfully remain in it, notwithstanding that they are united in the third degree of consanguinity. Although the canons strictly prohibit the marriage contract between such parties and the apostolic see rarely, if ever, removes such an impediment by the grace of dispensation, unless for reasons of great utility and necessity, nevertheless, several reasons were proposed before us, due to which the clemency of the same see can honestly incline towards granting the aforementioned grace, especially the prompt offering of useful and great services by the same nobles in the general cause of the church and our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans W., the extinction of the fuel of past hatreds in those regions as a salutary measure, and the caution by which future evils are said to be prevented. We, being intent on extending to these nobles all the grace we can with God, persuaded by their merits, command your discretion, in which we have full confidence in the Lord, by apostolic writings, that you, after diligently inquiring into and carefully considering these proposed causes of services and other necessary utilities, grant them the requested license by our authority, dispensing them concerning the impediment of consanguinity as your circumspection shall deem expedient according to God. If not all, etc. Given at Naples, on the Nones of May, in the first year.

**Latin Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati in Lennin Cisterciensis ordinis Brandeburgensis diocesis et priori provinciali fratrum Praedicatorum Alamanniae mandat, ut, post diligentem inquisitionem causis propositis, licentiam contrahendi matrimonium inter ducem Saxoniae et Iohannem marchionem Brandeburgensem ac filiam dicti ducis, non obstante tertia consanguinitatis linea, concedant. 1227, Mai. 7, Neapoli.

**Translation to English:**

To Caziacomo, cleric of the diocese of Arezzo. The Apostolic See, as a pious mother, does not repel her children even if they have gravely sinned, but rather, welcomes them back with a joyful embrace and the kiss of reconciliation, when they return in the spirit of humility after their transgressions. Indeed, we have read your petition which stated that, while your late father Aldebrandino Caziacomo, and your late brothers were aligned with the late Roman Emperor Frederick and his son Conrad, one of your brothers obtained for you the archbishopric of Cosenza from Conrad by fact, which you accepted and from which you received income for a time. Later, when you were in the throes of death, you were absolved by a priest from the sentence of excommunication which you incurred because of this, in accordance with the form of the Church, as was fully attested to us by a public instrument. Therefore, with the stain of the aforementioned sin cleansed by the washing of virtues, you have adorned the nobility of your lineage with the honesty of morals and have aided in obtaining the grace of the aforementioned See with the gift of knowledge and praiseworthy testimony from trustworthy individuals. We, inclined by the prayers of your devotion, approve this absolution and, with the authority of these presents, dispense you from the irregularity you are known to have contracted, so that — notwithstanding this — you may lawfully retain the ecclesiastical benefice you hold and be elected to any episcopal dignity, which you may lawfully receive, and that on account of these or any graces obtained or to be obtained from the same See, no obstacle may be interposed against you; nor shall you be bound to restitution of the aforementioned income or to make satisfaction for them to anyone, nor can you at any time be compelled to do so by apostolic or any authority. We grant this concession to your devotion. Let none — of our dispensation and concession etc. Given at the Lateran, 9th of February, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorii IX papa Caziacomiti clerico Aretinae dioecesis scribit, absolutionem eius approbans et super irregularitate dispensans, ut non obstante huiusmodi irregularitate, beneficium ecclesiasticum licite retinere, ac ad episcopalem dignitatem eligi possit, nec ad restitutionem reddituum compelli valeat. Datum Laterani, V Idus Februarii, anno tertio.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Cambrai. The Apostolic See, as a kind mother, mercifully assists the oppressed and moderates the oppressors with its authority, thereby aiding not only the salvation of the injured but also of those causing the injury. For when the suffering of injuries leads to temporal loss, the act itself can lead to eternal harm. It is more beneficial to restrain the one acting from fault than the one suffering from discomfort or violence. Indeed, the aforementioned See has been known to grant certain letters, indulgences, and privileges commonly to the churches and prelates of the most Christian kingdom of France for the protection of their rights, possessions, goods, and freedoms, as well as for the suppression of injuries inflicted upon them by secular persons, at the supplication of the chapters of the cathedral churches of that kingdom. Therefore, considering that the Church of Cambrai and its subjects, although located within the boundaries of the Roman Empire, belong to the province of Reims and are said to observe the rite of the Gallican Church, they rightly ought to rejoice in the same immunity. We extend these letters, indulgences, and privileges to you, the aforementioned Church of Cambrai, and your subjects by the authority of this present document. We grant you and the Church of Cambrai the same power that executors or judges, commonly appointed by the said See for the prelates and churches of that kingdom, have in all respects for the protection of you, your church, your subjects, and your goods, and for the suppression of injuries if any are inflicted upon you by secular persons, as if you and your injurers were within the limits of the said kingdom and the aforementioned privileges, indulgences, and letters had been sought for you equally with those prelates and churches. This is granted notwithstanding the constitution on two diets issued in the general council, as long as no one is brought to judgment beyond the third or fourth diet outside their diocese by the authority of these letters, indulgences, and privileges. We grant this. Let no one violate our concession, etc. Given at Viterbo, 18th July, in the third year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Cameracensi mandat, ut litteras, indulgentias et privilegia sedis apostolicae, quae ecclesiis regni Franciae concessa sunt, ad ecclesiam Cameracensem et subditos eius proroget, non obstante constitutione de duabus dietis. 1229, Iul. 18. Viterbii.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Roger Finecte of Lentino, our faithful servant. The exceptional merits of your devotion and constancy stand out and shine so brightly that, when we consider their excellence and clarity, we deem them so worthy of graces and benefits that hardly any means of recompense comes to mind for us, through which we might adequately reward their greatness. Therefore, we are attentively and diligently considerate and often ponder how we might support your person with opportune gifts and exalt you with appropriate honors for such great and considerable merits. Since we presently intend to provide you in the Kingdom of Sicily with certain goods belonging to the demesne or falling to the court, from which you may annually receive income amounting to around two hundred ounces of gold, and inclined by your supplications, we grant to you and your heirs, remaining in the devotion of the Roman Church, the castles of Bizini, Modicet, Sicli, and Palatioli in the Syracuse diocese, as you assert that their revenues or proceeds amount to the aforesaid sum of ounces annually, with the enfeoffed and non-enfeoffed men, cultivated and uncultivated lands, forests, meadows, waters, and watercourses and with all rights, honors, justices, jurisdictions, and appurtenances pertaining to the aforesaid castles, from the counsel and agreement of our brothers, in fealty, by special grace. We also wish that whenever the Roman Church assembles a general army, you and your heirs are obliged to provide ten knights suitably equipped with arms and horses to serve the same Church for three months within the borders of the said kingdom at your expense. No one, etc. Given at Anagni by the hand of William, master of the schools of Parma, vice-chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Ides of September, in the thirteenth indiction, the year of the Lord's Incarnation 1255, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander IV.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Alexander IV papa nobili viro Rogerio Finecte de Lentino castra Bizini, Modicet, Sicli et Palatioli in diocese Syracusana cum omnibus pertinentiis in feudum concedit, servitium decem militum imponens. Anagnie, Idibus Septembris, pontificatus anno primo.

**Translation to English:**

To the provost, dean, and chapter of the greater church of Liège. Those things which are established by judgment or agreement, etc., up to: to be confirmed. Indeed, your petition presented to us stated that although no one should and ought to order concerning the saleable goods of the city of Liège without your consent, nonetheless, the bishop of Liège, of blessed memory, on his own initiative, against justice, decreed that a certain sum of money should be paid over and above the fair price given for them, to your prejudice and burden. And when subsequently, concerning this and various other articles, a question was long debated before the bishops of blessed memory, the bishop of Tusculum and P. of San Nicola in Carcere Tulliano, and Rainerius of Santa Maria in Cosmedin, cardinal deacons, whom Pope Gregory of happy memory, our predecessor, appointed as judges over the aforementioned parties, and the same judges had ordered this statute of the bishop of Liège to be revoked, finally, concerning the remaining articles, by the consent of the same judges, the matter was voluntarily and unanimously submitted to arbitration by both parties to the beloved sons, the abbot of Villers of the Cistercian order and the abbot of Floreffe of the Premonstratensian order, and Master G. of Laon, a canon of Reims; two of whom, the third being lawfully excused, as they had from such submission, revoked the said statute according to the mandate of the same judges, and proceeding rightly in the said matter, gave a just decision between the parties, as is more fully contained in the letters patent made thereof; which you have requested to be strengthened by apostolic authority. We, therefore, inclined by your supplications, holding the said decision, as it is just and accepted and approved by the parties and hitherto peacefully observed, as valid and firm, confirm it by apostolic authority and fortify it with the endorsement of this document. No one — our confirmation, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the 4th day before the Nones of May, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa Honorius III praeposito, decano et capitulo maioris ecclesiae Leodiensis arbitrium inter partes super rebus venalibus civitatis Leodiensis, ab arbitris revocatum et ab auditoribus approbatum, auctoritate apostolica confirmat. Datum Laterani, IIII Nonas Maii, anno tertio.

**Translation to English:**

To Henry, abbot of the monastery of Fulda of the order of Saint Benedict, in the diocese of Würzburg. From your petition and that of the beloved sons, the dean, the provost, and the convent of the monastery of Hersfeld of the order of Saint Benedict, in the diocese of Mainz, we have learned that when Wernher, once abbot of the same monastery, first voluntarily resigned from the governance of the abbey and later occupied it by force, our beloved son H., priest cardinal of the title of Saint Sabina, then apostolic legate in those parts, had him removed from there as demanded by justice. Observing that the said monastery, due to the malice and negligence of the aforementioned Wernher, had considerably collapsed in spiritual and temporal matters, and considering that through your diligence it could be happily reformed in both, he entrusted you with the care and administration of that monastery in both spiritual and temporal matters by the authority of his legation, until our will should decide otherwise. When the aforementioned Wernher again occupied the monastery through lay power, we instructed the beloved sons, the abbots of Slutere and Arnespurch, by our letters under certain conditions, that if this were so, they should remove Wernher from the said monastery, contradictors notwithstanding. The abbot of Slutere and the beloved son, the dean of the church of Saint Mary in the Fields of Mainz, to whom the abbot of Arnespurch had entrusted his full authority on this matter from the benefit of our said letters, upon legally establishing these matters, removed the aforementioned Wernher from the same monastery by sentence, according to the tenor of those letters. Therefore, at the request of the said dean, provost, and convent, it was humbly petitioned to us that since the same monastery can be more effectively governed and reformed by you than by another according to the demands of the present time and defended against the incursions of the wicked, we should care to strengthen the commission regarding the said monastery made to you by the aforementioned cardinal with apostolic authority. Thus, inclined by their and your petitions, we ratify and confirm this commission by apostolic authority, and we support it with the protection of the present writing. Let no one infringe on our confirmation. Given at Anagni, on the third day before the Ides of December, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa confirmat Henrico abbati monasterii Fuldensis ordinis sancti Benedicti commissionem administrationis monasterii Hersfeldensis, ex auctoritate cardinalis H. tituli Sancte Sabine, ab Wernhero contra legem occupati. 1230, Dec. 11, Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Malta. The Apostolic See, after careful deliberation considering the merits of individuals, rewards those whom it knows to be deserving and devoted with the grace of special beneficence. Since our beloved son, Master John Spata, our subdeacon and chaplain, by special mandate and authority of our predecessor of happy memory, Pope Innocent, deprived our venerable brother, Master Matthew of Palermo, then a canon of Syracuse and now bishop, of his personate, dignity, prebends, and all ecclesiastical benefices because he had rendered himself unworthy by serving the former Emperor Frederick even after his deposition, and conferred all these by the same authority of special grace and mandate of the same predecessor to our beloved son John, called Sacco, canon of Palermo, and that same predecessor confirmed them to him, and we subsequently approved and accepted what was done by the same chaplain and predecessor in this matter—notwithstanding any collations, confirmations, and letters obtained or to be obtained from the Apostolic See or its legates in prejudice to this—since you have been appointed executor on these matters in the manner of the aforementioned predecessor, yet have delayed executing the apostolic mandate to the notable prejudice and grievance of John, we therefore, not wishing what we have commenced regarding the aforementioned canon, whom we pursue with the favor of special grace due to his extraordinary devotion to us and the Apostolic See, to be left in any way incomplete: we firmly and strictly command you by apostolic writings, in the power of obedience, that you do not delay in executing the apostolic mandate on these matters according to the contents of previous letters—notwithstanding any suspensions, revocations, objections, or lapses of any times.
