For we decree null and void anything that has been or may be attempted henceforth to the prejudice and grievance of the same John, and we wish you to declare it void and null; those who oppose etc. Given at Viterbo, October 30, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Maltensi mandat ut mandatum apostolicum de collatis beneficiis Ioanni dicto Sacco canonico Panormitano exsequi non postponat, decernens irritum quicquid in eius praeiudicium et gravamen attentatum sit. 1230, Oct. 30, Viterbii.

**Translation to English:**

To the archdeacon of Brescia. Gerard, a canon of Cremona, son of the late Andrew of Trecio, presented his petition to us, stating that our predecessor Pope Innocent, of blessed memory, considering with piety that his father had been ignominiously slain by the former Emperor Frederick for his devotion to the Church, had sent letters to the chapter of Bergamo regarding his reception and provision. However, these letters were not presented to the said chapter due to the dangers of war, although the provost, archpriest, and many other canons of Bergamo, to whom these letters were shown individually, received the said Gerard as a canon and brother. Nonetheless, the prebend that later became vacant in the Church of Bergamo was conferred upon another. But because Gerard, due to poverty and the power of the opposing party, is unable to litigate over the prebend with its holder, he humbly requested us to provide for him with paternal care. Therefore, not wishing that what was piously begun regarding him should remain incomplete, we command that, if the truth supports these claims, you ensure that the aforementioned Gerard is received as a canon and brother by the canons of Bergamo who did not accept him, and that a prebend be conferred upon him, should there be one presently vacant in that church or as soon as one becomes available, notwithstanding that he may be otherwise beneficed, as he currently derives no benefit from his benefices, or any statute about a fixed number of canons, oath, or confirmation of the Apostolic See, or any other reinforcement, or if we have directed writings to others in the same church. Opponents are warned. Given at the Lateran, on the 12th of February, in the second year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archidiacono Brixiensi mandat ut Gerardus, canonicus Cremonensis, a canonicis Pergamensibus qui eum non receperunt, in canonicum recipiatur et ei conferatur prebenda in ecclesia Pergamensi vacans, cum pater eius pro ecclesiae devotione occisus fuerit. 1229, Februarii 12, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the Abbot and the convent of the monastery of Fontis Laureati of the Florensian order, Tropensis diocese. The petition presented on your behalf stated that our predecessor, Pope Gregory of happy memory, having understood that the monastery of Saint Angelus of Militin, then of the order of Saint Basil, Rossanensis diocese, was so deteriorated both spiritually and temporally that hardly any vestiges of religion remained in it, instructed, through his letters, the bishop of Bisinian of good memory and his colleague to personally visit the monastery and reform it within a certain time according to the regular observances of the order of Saint Basil, if possible, otherwise to entrust it to the abbot of your monastery of the Florensian order for reformation, saving the rights of the diocesan in all things. They, following the apostolic mandate, personally visited the place and, performing the office of visitation there, since the monastery could not be reformed in its own order, entrusted it to your abbot to be reformed according to the Florensian order, which even the brothers who remained there accepted, making a profession to this abbot by promising henceforth to observe the Florensian order in all things. But afterwards, not only were you unjustly dispossessed of that monastery, which you had possessed peacefully for some time, by the officials of the late brother, formerly the Roman Emperor, but this brother also recalled into his dominion the greater part of the possessions of your monastery according to his own will, because of which you are suffering a significant lack in temporal matters. We, therefore, inclined by your supplications, confirm and approve what was providently done by the aforementioned bishop and colleague with apostolic authority, and strengthen it by the support of this present writing, revoking entirely whatever has been presumed to your detriment in the aforesaid matters, and mandating that the aforementioned monastery of Saint Angelus should be restored to you and committed to your disposition and held in your hands until, having obtained full possession of it and its goods, it can be conveniently reformed by you in the said Florensian order. No one shall etc. concerning our confirmation, revocation, and mandate etc. Given at Anagni, II Kalends of November, in the second year.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati et conventui monasterii Fontis Laureati ordinis Florensis confirmat reformationem monasterii sancti Angeli de Militin per episcopum Bisinianensem et collegam suum factam, et mandat restitutionem eiusdem monasterii cum plenaria possessione ad reformandum. Anagni, 30 Octobris, anno secundo.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of the monastery in Urowe, of the Order of Saint Benedict, in the diocese of Würzburg. Our beloved sons, the abbot of Fulda, the dean, the provost, and the convent of the monastery of Hersfeld, of the Order of Saint Benedict, have shown us through their petition that Wernher, the former abbot of the said monastery, which pertains directly to the Roman Church of the Mainz diocese, had forcibly taken over the abbey, whose governance he had initially willingly resigned. Our beloved son, H., Cardinal Priest of the title of Santa Sabina, then legate of the Apostolic See in those regions, removed him from there, as justice required, and recognizing that said monastery, which had fallen considerably in spiritual and temporal matters due to the malice and negligence of Wernher, could be successfully reformed in both aspects through the industry of Henry, the abbot of the monastery of Fulda, entrusted the care and administration of the same, both spiritual and temporal, to the abbot of Fulda by the authority of his legation until the Apostolic See's pleasure was known.

Subsequently, when the aforementioned Wernher again seized the aforementioned Hersfeld monastery through secular power, we had entrusted to the abbots of Sluthere and Arnspurg, of the Mainz and Würzburg dioceses respectively, by our letters under a certain form, to remove Wernher from the Hersfeld monastery if it was indeed so, vanquishing opposers through censure, etc. The abbot of Sluthere and the dean of the church of Saint Mary in the Fields of Mainz, to whom the abbot of Arnspurg had entirely delegated his role in this matter by virtue of the said letters, found the charges legitimate and removed Wernher from the aforementioned Hersfeld monastery by definitive sentence.

Since we have decided to confirm the commission and sentence of the cardinal by apostolic authority, we command that if it is indeed so, you should install the said abbot of Fulda into the physical possession of the aforementioned Hersfeld monastery by our authority, through yourself or another, according to the tenor of the aforesaid commission, and protect him once installed in this manner, as is just; and vanquish opposers, etc. Given at Anagni, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of February, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati monasterii in Urowe ordinis Sancti Benedicti mandat ut abbatem Fuldensem in corporalem possessionem monasterii Hersfeldensis inducat, Wernhero praeoccupante amoto. Dat. Anagnie, XIII Kal. Feb., anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To Iringo, Bishop of Würzburg. Once a dispute arose between you and our beloved son Henry, the elected Bishop of Speyer, regarding the bishopric of Würzburg and other matters. Finally, our beloved sons H., Cardinal Priest of the title of Santa Sabina, R., Cardinal of Saint Angelus, and P., Cardinal Deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, amicably settled the dispute by arbitration, ordination, and definition. Among other things, they decreed that the same elect should henceforth not raise or cause to be raised any question against you, secretly or publicly, regarding the said bishopric. Indeed, he was to ensure, without any difficulty, that the city of Würzburg, the castles, villages, and whatever he might hold or possess through himself or others, which pertained to the said bishopric, be delivered and assigned to you or your messengers, to the extent it was within his power. And you were to subsequently pay him a certain sum of money within specified terms for the expenses and damages he incurred because of the said bishopric, as fully described in a public instrument drawn up and sealed by the said cardinals. But the same elect, it is asserted, does not care to abide by this settlement according to his own whim; a remedy was thus sought from us. Since it is right that a promise not kept should not be binding, inclined by your prayers, we allow you by the authority of this document, that if the said elect does not keep the arbitration, ordination, and definition as he is bound, you shall in no way be bound to the payment of money to which you are otherwise committed by oath, although we have deemed it appropriate to confirm the arbitration, ordination, or definition. Let no one infringe upon our concession, etc. Given at the Lateran, the day before the Kalends of April, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX episcopus Iringo episcopo Herbipolensi significat, quod si Henricus electus Spirensis arbitrium, ordinationem et diffinitionem super episcopatu Herbipolensi tenere neglexerit, Iringo ab obligatione solutionis pecuniae eximeretur, quamvis arbitrium confirmandum duxerit. Datum Lateran., II Kalendas Aprilis, anno tertio.

**Translation to English:**

To Angelo Bisantii of Risobaroli, devoted and faithful to us and the Roman Church. The steadfastness of your faith, through which you have merited the special benevolence of the Apostolic See, proclaims itself in our ears and those of our brothers by the praiseworthy testimonies of your works, which have become especially evident in recent days, not allowing your petitions to be denied the grace of a hearing. Indeed, it was made known to us through your report that our beloved son O., Cardinal Deacon of Santa Maria in Via Lata, then the legate of the Apostolic See in the Kingdom of Sicily, in his letters encouraging you in the matter of the recall of Baroli to the devotion of the Church, among other things, promised firmly that the Church would restore to you all that you might lose on this account from the goods of the said kingdom, as we have clearly seen contained in the same letters. And because, as we learned from the same cardinal’s reporting, through your diligent efforts, Baroli returned to the devotion of the Church and set himself openly against Manfred, the late prince of Taranto, and other enemies of the Church, these same M. and their enemies and supporters later seized the opportunity to strip you of all your movable goods and inflicted other serious damages upon you, which are known to have reached the sum of 1,140 ounces of gold. Thus, inclined by your supplications, we hold and approve what the aforementioned cardinal has done in this part, confirming it by apostolic authority, and we decree that all the revenues and proceeds which the court of the said kingdom is known to have in the said Barolo and its appurtenances are to remain obligated to you for the restitution of the aforementioned losses and damages, so that full satisfaction may be owed and provided to you from these same revenues and proceeds. Let no one etc. of our confirmation and constitution etc. Given at the Lateran, on the Ides of March, in the second year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Angelo Bisantii de Risobaroli, devoto et fideli, confirmat restitutionem omnium bonorum amissorum in regno Sicilie per mediantiam Octaviani cardinalis in reversione Baroli ad ecclesiam. Dat. Laterani, Idibus Martii, anno secundo pontificatus sui.

**Translation to English:**

To the Podestà, council, and community of Aquila, our faithful subjects. Your land, conspicuous with the clarity of pure faith, flourishes with luminous and magnificent deeds, offering a manifest example of praiseworthy liberty for other cities of the Kingdom of Sicily to follow. Therefore, this land, noble from the foundation of its walls and the nobility of its deeds, is rendered laudable for its progress in the eyes of both near and far, and worthy of being elevated with special favors and greater graces from us and the Apostolic See. Its praise resounds not only through the cities of the kingdom but its fame extends even further. We and the said See are led by all our affections to elevate it with appropriate honors and exalt it with fitting graces. Considering the steadfastness of sincere devotion and the firmness of unyielding faith for which your land is known towards the Roman Church, and desiring to show a full measure of our affection through action, also weighing the fact that almost all the inhabitants from Furconium and Amiternum are said to have moved their residence to your land, and considering that you, as orthodox worshippers and lovers of the faith, have commendably begun to endow the Church of Saints Maximus and George of Aquila, which you are building anew and seek earnestly to have erected into a cathedral by apostolic authority, with your temporal goods, according to your means, by liberally granting one and a half mills and two other sites for building two more mills, as we have seen stated in full in the public instrument drawn up for this purpose; we, moved by your supplications, take the aforementioned land of Aquila under the protection of Saint Peter and ourselves, and upon the advice of our brethren and the plenitude of our power, we decree it henceforth to be a city, granting it episcopal dignity, and transferring the seat of Furconium with all its rights, dignities, and honors to the aforementioned Church of Saints Maximus and George of Aquila, which we henceforth decree to be a cathedral, thus establishing that the bishop of the place shall henceforth be called not the bishop of Furconium but of Aquila. Let no one etc. of our protection, constitution, concession, and transfer etc. Given at the Lateran, on the 11th day before the Kalends of January, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa potestati, consilio et communi Aquilensibus significat se terram Aquile sub protectione beati Petri et sua suscipere, eamque civitatem cum dignitate episcopali constituere, sedem Furconensem ad ecclesiam sanctorum Maximi et Georgii de Aquila transferendo, ita ut exinde episcopus Aquilensis nominetur. 1229, Dec. 22. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the perpetual memory of the matter. Since men, equal by nature, have been made subject by the bondage of sin, it indeed seems just that those who abuse the dominion granted to them by Him, from whom all power in heaven and on earth comes, should, by the merit of ingratitude, be deprived of the power over the servants entrusted to them. And those who, obeying God rather than men, scorn to follow the wickedness of their lords against Christ with zeal for the faith, so that they may truly be free, should be exempted from all human servitude as a reward. Thus, by this example, the persecutors of the Church and the Catholic faith might be urged by the sting of deserved punishment to, if possible, turn back from their perversity and convert themselves to the pursuit of due devotion and recognize the way of truth. And it should bring joy to the faithful to attend to the cultivation of virtues, while they perceive that the reprobates are cast down for their wickedness and entirely deprived of the abundance of good things. Indeed, Ezzelinus of Romano has long been cut off as a heretic from the unity of the Church, and Albericus, his brother, has been bound by us with the chain of excommunication as a supporter and defender of heretics and deprived of all indulgences and privileges granted to him by the Apostolic See. But they, with their hearts hardened, like an anvil under a hammer, as if boiling like the sea, and with a spirit hardened in pride, do not cease to attack the Church and its devout as enemies and persecutors of the Catholic faith. Since it is fitting that the aforementioned Ezzelinus and Albericus should grieve for their iniquity, having suffered some loss, we, with the counsel of our brethren, by apostolic authority, fully release all their male and female slaves, along with their children and descendants of the same condition, who have returned or will return to the unity of the Church and remain in its obedience and devotion, to complete liberty, and we decree that they are free, so that they might retain their possessions freely and enjoy that liberty as if they were born free. Let no one infringe upon our decree and constitution, etc. Given at Viterbo, on the 5th day before the Nones of July, in the fourth year. 

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa declarat omnes servos et ancillas Eczelini de Romano et Alberici, qui ad ecclesiae unitatem redierint, liberos esse. Dat. Viterbii, V Nonas Iulii, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of the monastery of Amelungesborn of the Cistercian order in the diocese of Hildesheim. Since, by the duty of the apostolate entrusted to us, we are obliged to care for and be concerned about all churches, we willingly, as far as we can with God's help, attend to their needs and guard against their detriments. Indeed, a petition presented to us by our venerable brother, the bishop, and our beloved sons, the dean and chapter of the church of Hildesheim, contained that the late Henry, bishop of Hildesheim, predecessor of the aforementioned bishop, mortgaged the said church to several creditors for a substantial sum of money, because of which it is heavily burdened with debt. Its revenues have been so reduced due to twelve years of war in those parts that not only can the bishop not satisfy the creditors, but he also cannot sustain himself from the said revenues. However, since the chapter of the church of St. Maurice of Hildesheim, by ancient and approved custom peacefully observed until now, is bound to elect someone from the chapter of the said church of Hildesheim as their provost when the position becomes vacant, and the said provostship and treasurership of the same Hildesheim church are said to be vacant due to the promotion of the said bishop to the aforementioned Hildesheim church, which he previously held, we, moved by the supplications of the same bishop, dean, and chapter of the church of Hildesheim, bearing a pious feeling of compassion towards the same church, command that you, taking into your hands the revenues of the provostship, if the consent of their chapters is obtained, and also of the treasurership of the aforementioned, if it pleases the said bishop, dean, and chapter of Hildesheim, convert those revenues in full to the payment of such debts for five years, contradictors etc.; provided that the provostship and treasurership are not deprived of their due services and the care of souls, if any is incumbent upon them, is not neglected. Given at Viterbo, III Kalends of May, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati monasterii Amelungesbernen Cisterciensis ordinis mandat ut, si capitula consentiant, proventus prepositurae et thesaurariae ecclesiae Hildesemensis per quinquennium recipiat et eos in solutionem debitorum convertat. 1229, Apr. 29, Viterbii.

Translation to English:

To the noble woman Margaret, Countess of Flanders and Hainaut. The effective devotion, which you are known to have towards us and the Apostolic See, deserves such affection that we favorably accede to your petitions, through which your peace is sought. Since the title of the County of Flanders is so distinguished that it is scarcely believed by those who obtain apostolic letters against you to be omitted without malice, we, desiring both to counteract their deceits and to ensure your peace, inclined by your supplications, grant by the authority of these presents that you cannot be sued by such letters which do not mention the aforesaid county. Let no one violate our concession, etc.; null after three years, etc. Given at Anagni, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of December, in the fifth year.

Regesto in Latin:

Honorius III papa nobili mulieri Margarite comitisse Flandrie et Haoniev indulget, ut per litteras de comitatu Flandrensi non mentionem facientes conveniri nequeat. 1220, Nov. 20. Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To Master Jacob of Castiglione, our relative, Bishop-elect of Reggio. Since due to the adverse power of Manfred, formerly Prince of Taranto, who calls himself King of Sicily, you are unable to approach the Church of Reggio entrusted to you without endangering your person and cannot exercise the pastoral office therein, we are inclined by your supplications to grant you a special grace, that you are not obliged to be promoted to the orders of the diaconate and the presbyterate or to receive the consecration, until you have obtained peaceful and quiet possession of the same church — notwithstanding the constitution we issued against the elected of cathedral churches, that they are obliged to receive the gift of consecration within a period of six months. Let no one infringe upon our concession, etc. Given at Anagni, on the second day before the Nones of May, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Magistro Iacobo de Castellione, consanguineo suo, electo Regino, concedit ut non teneatur promoveri ad ordines diaconatus et presbyteratus neque recipere consecrationem donec pacificam possessionem ecclesiae Reginensis obtinuerit, constitutione edita non obstante. Anagniae, II Non. Maii, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the illustrious King of England. In order to reform the business of the Kingdom of Sicily, which the Roman Church undertook with you and our most beloved son in Christ, Edmund, your son, the illustrious King of Sicily, and to restore it to the state of prosecution from which it seemed to fall due to omissions and various delays, we have decided, with the counsel of our brothers, to send our beloved son, Master Arlotus, our subdeacon and notary, in whom we have full confidence, granting him express authority in a specific form over the reform of this business until the first day of June next, through other letters of ours.

However, since we have deemed it necessary to ensure, at the insistence of your messengers and also through our own diligence, that you have not incurred any sentence of excommunication or any penalties contained in the privilege of concession, renewal, and confirmation, which we made on behalf of the aforementioned Edmund concerning the said kingdom, due to any faults committed by you related to the aforementioned business, and that your kingdom is not subject to ecclesiastical interdict: we decree, with the authority of the present letters, that you are fully protected against these penalties, concerning your conscience and reputation, so that you are not considered tainted by guilt or the mark of perjury.

Moreover, to ensure that you are safeguarded against these penalties in the future and that the opportunity for the reform of the aforementioned business is so timely that it does not result in great harm to the Church or the ruin of the kingdom itself, we suspend all penalties contained in the aforementioned privilege until the said first day of June, so that, in the meantime, due to any faults committed by you in this business, you do not incur any sentence of excommunication or guilt or the mark of perjury, nor is your kingdom subject to ecclesiastical interdict, nor do we annul, invalidate, or announce as annulled or invalid the aforementioned renewal, concession, and confirmation, nor do we in any way dispose of the kingdom differently during this time, but the right that was acquired by the aforementioned King of Sicily through the renewal, concession, and confirmation made by us concerning the said kingdom remains intact and unharmed for him and his heirs until then, as it was after the same renewal, concession, and confirmation were made by us in the aforementioned privilege. For the irrefutable testimony of this suspension, we decree that these present letters be effective. Given at Viterbo, December 12th, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa regi Anglorum mandat, ut ad negotium regni Siciliae reformandum magistrum Arlotum subdiaconum mittat; interim suspendit omnes poenas in privilegio concessas, ut rex Angliae excommunicationis sententiam vel notam periurii non incurrat. Datum Viterbii, II Idus Decembris, anno III (1230).

**Translation to English:**

For the future memory of the matter. Because human actions are arranged according to the nature of the times, it happens that they change with the mutability of those times. Hence, what was once prudently acted upon out of necessity, is sometimes, with the same necessity, prudently revoked. Indeed, some things that were once pleasing later displease their own actors as time progresses, and sometimes what once seemed easy is perceived as very difficult. This is caused by the unstable state of time itself, which is continuously altered by various events concerning temporal and earthly matters; for, considering the necessity of time and the condition of places, it is necessary to direct and arrange ongoing affairs accordingly. For this reason, our predecessor, Pope Innocent of blessed memory, compelled by the harshness of the time, was known to have done many things, perhaps unwillingly, which he intended to change to utility when the opportunity arose. To many persons, both ecclesiastical and secular, he granted, due to the importunate insistence of the petitioners at that time, that they could not be interdicted, suspended, or excommunicated by delegates or conservators or executors appointed by the apostolic see, or by their subdelegates, nor could their entry into the church be interdicted, nor their lands subjected to ecclesiastical interdict, some for a certain time, others without a time limit. We, therefore, carefully considering that from such a grant or indulgence much boldness for malignancy can arise, as this indulgence openly arms against ecclesiastical censure and authority, encourages audacity, loosens modesty, arms insolence, and weakens judicial power, also considering that full justice cannot be exhibited against those protected by such an indulgence, as jurisdiction cannot be freely exercised over them, it is altogether expedient to apply a suitable remedy concerning these matters. Therefore, we revoke all such indulgences granted by the same predecessor or even by us, with apostolic authority, to any persons whether ecclesiastical, prelates and others, regulars and non-regulars, or seculars, namely princes and other lesser persons, and to chapters, colleges, convents, and communities or communes of any places, unless those princes are kings or the wives or sons or brothers of kings or great and distinguished men who have anciently had similar grace from the aforesaid see, so that henceforth they may obtain no strength or vigor, nor may the aforementioned benefit or protect themselves by them any further. No one, etc., of our revocation, etc. Given at Anagni, 18th August, in the first year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa universis ecclesiasticis et secularibus personis, preterquam regibus et magnatibus, indulsa per predecessorem aut ipsum concessa, quae ab ecclesiastica censura et auctoritate immunitatem praestabant, auctoritate apostolica revocat, ne ulterius vim habeant. 1227, Aug. 18. Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected of Conventry and Lincelfeld and Master Berard of Nimpha, our chaplain residing in England. On behalf of our beloved son, the noble man Richard, Earl of Cornwall, dear brother in Christ of our illustrious son, the King of England, it was proposed before us that our predecessors, the Roman Pontiffs of blessed memory, Gregory and Innocent, generously granted to the same Earl, then a crusader and later returned from overseas, legacies intended indiscriminately for the aid of the Holy Land and the redemption of crusaders' vows in the Kingdom of England, made before the Earl returned from the said parts, appointing various executors over this matter. Wherefore, he humbly petitioned us that since some of these executors have moved to distant parts and others have passed away, preventing the final resolution of this business, we should care with our accustomed kindness to provide for him in this matter. Therefore, unwilling to leave unfinished what was graciously begun regarding the same Earl, we command you that if this is so, you proceed effectively in the aforementioned business either by yourselves or by others, according to the directives of the letters of our predecessors directed to whichever executors on this matter — notwithstanding any apostolic permissions granted to crusaders and other persons of the same kingdom, that they cannot be interdicted, suspended, or excommunicated, or brought into cause outside their dioceses or other specific places or summoned to judgment through apostolic letters, without making full and explicit mention of such permission, and the constitution of two diets published in the general council. However, if there are any contradictors or rebels, you shall restrain them after a warning by our authority, removing any obstacle of appeal. We do not wish, however, that by this any prejudice arises against the graces we are known to have granted to the aforesaid king regarding redemptions, legacies, and others, or to the jurisdiction committed by the apostolic seat to our beloved son Master Rostan, our chaplain and nuncio in England over these matters. If not both, etc. Given at Viterbo, on the 11th Kalends of July, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Conventrensi et Lincelfeldensi electo et magistro Berardo de Nimpha, capellano suo in Anglia commoranti, mandat ut in negotio legatorum et redemptione votorum crucisignatorum regni Angliae ad subventionem Terrae Sanctae ex parte Riccardi comitis Cornubiae procedant, non obstante exemptione personarum et constitutione de duabus dietis. Viterbii, 21 Iunii, anno tertio.

**Translation to English:**

To patriarchs, archbishops, bishops, abbots, priors, deans, archdeacons, and other prelates of churches, as well as noble men, marquises, counts, barons, knights, and other faithful Christians who will inspect the present letters. Let it be known to all of you that we, considering the purity of faith and the fervor of devotion of our beloved son, the noble man Philip de Sancta Cruce, protontinus of Barletta and Monopoli, have decided, with the counsel of our brothers, to make donations, grants, or confirmations of the lands of Cannarum, Caurati, Terlicium, and Arricarium, and of the castles or hamlets situated in the land of Bari, as well as of the smelting house in Barletta and the house of the court which Ribaldinus held, for a time assigned in the smelting house, and of the vacant land outside the gate of Saint Leonard of Barletta, whose revenues are said to amount to four hundred ounces of gold annually, and of the office of protontinus of Barletta and Monopoli aforesaid. We have decided to do this because we saw it to be expedient, as the utility of the services which he rendered in the affair of the kingdom of Sicily, returning to the devotion of the church, demanded this, and necessity suggested it, because it was then promised to him in the name of the Roman church that he would be indemnified for all damages he incurred for that devotion concerning the goods of the aforesaid kingdom. Since we promised him that such donations, grants, and confirmations would be inviolably observed by him and his heirs by the kings holding the said kingdom from the aforesaid church, as is more fully contained in the apostolic privileges granted to him on this matter, and since this was done with the knowledge of the noble man Robert de Baro, who remained as the procurator at the apostolic see for our most beloved sons in Christ, Henry and Edmund, illustrious kings of England and Sicily, as was clearly evident to us, we desire that it be observed in perpetuity. Therefore, let no one at all infringe upon our donations, grants, confirmations, and privileges of this kind, etc. Given at Anagni, on the second day before the Kalends of September, in the second year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa patriarchis, archiepiscopis, episcopis, abbatibus, prioribus, decanis, archidiaconis et aliis ecclesiarum prelatis ac nobilibus viris marchionibus, comitibus, baronibus, militibus et aliis Christi fidelibus notum facit se donationes, concessiones et confirmationes terrarum Cannarum, Caurati, Terlicii et Arricarri, necnon domorum et officiorum in terra Bari dilecto filio Philippo de Sancta Cruce, protontino Baroli et Monopoli, fecisse, promittens eas inviolabiliter observari. Anagniae, II Kalendas Septembris, anno secundo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Sambia and William, canon of the church of Saint Denis of Liège. Our beloved son, P., cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, has informed us that while he was previously carrying out the office of legate in parts of Poland, several prelates and clerics, both secular and religious, of those regions refused to fulfill their obligations for his expenses according to their whims. Although the same cardinal has pronounced a sentence of excommunication against many of them for this reason, the aforementioned prelates and clerics, shamelessly persisting under the guise of an appeal — which they are said to have launched to us — still refuse to pay the same expenses, nevertheless presuming to involve themselves in divine offices while still bound. We, considering the aforementioned sentence as valid and agreeable and wanting it to be observed inviolably until suitable satisfaction is made, and considering the appeal frivolous, command you to admonish or have admonished the said prelates and others, of whatever dignity or order they may be, that within a time limit you deem appropriate to set for them, they should pay the said expenses in full to you and others whom you may appoint for this purpose, on behalf of the same cardinal, compelling the dissenters, against whom the same sentence had not been promulgated, to do so by ecclesiastical censure, dismissing any appeal. Furthermore, ensure that these and other contumacious individuals are cited peremptorily, either by you or others on our behalf, so that within two months after your citation, they present themselves personally before us to receive what their contumacy merits. If they should happen to disdain to comply with the summons out of a defect of disobedience, you should publicly declare the same prelates excommunicated and have them avoided more strictly by all until they come to our presence, ready to obey the apostolic mandates in the aforementioned matters. As for the others, you should deprive them of their ecclesiastical benefices, which they hold in the aforementioned parts, and confer them to suitable, obedient, and devoted persons whom you deem fit, repressing the dissenters with similar censure, removing any obstacle of appeal — notwithstanding if some of the said regions have been granted by the Apostolic See that they cannot be excommunicated or interdicted or suspended, and excepting the constitution regarding two days promulgated in the general council. You should faithfully inform us of the day of the citation and whatever else you do through your letters containing the details of this matter. If not both, etc. Given at Anagni, 30th June in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Sambiensi et Guillelmo canonico ecclesiae Sancti Dionisii Leodiensis mandat, ut prelatos et clericos Poloniae procurationes cardinali satisfaciant et contumaces excommunicatos declaret, beneficiis privet et obedientibus conferat. Anagniae, II Kalendas Iulii, anno I.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of the monastery of Vallis Umbrosa in the diocese of Fiesole. Our beloved sons, the abbot and convent of the monastery of Saint Apollinaris in Classe of the Camaldolese order in the diocese of Ravenna, have shown us through their petition that we had instructed them, along with the houses and obediences subject to them, to support our beloved son, the elect of Ravenna, with a thousand and one hundred Sienese pounds for the expenses he had incurred while personally pursuing the affairs of the Kingdom of Sicily. We had commanded the abbot and convent through our letters to pay this money to the aforementioned elect by certain deadlines, appointing specific executors for this task.

However, due to the monastery suffering great losses from the dangers of wars, provisions, pensions, and procurations imposed and exacted by the Apostolic See and its legates, the said abbot and convent were compelled to endure the penalties of exile outside the monastery for nearly three years, losing a great part of their goods, and they are otherwise burdened by heavy debts. They humbly petitioned us to mercifully moderate the aforementioned sum and absolve them, along with the monastery, houses, obediences, and members mentioned, from the remainder.

Therefore, we have reduced the sum to two hundred pounds and absolved the abbot and convent, along with the monastery, houses, obediences, and members mentioned, from the remainder of nine hundred pounds by special grace. We command you, by apostolic writings, to compel the elect and executors not to demand more than the aforementioned 200 pounds from them or their monastery, obediences, houses, or members, by means of a warning issued by our authority, removing any appeal, and to relax any sentences of excommunication, suspension, or interdict that may have been promulgated against them or any of them due to this matter without any difficulty, declaring any that may be passed in the future as null, and to dispense with any irregularity they may have incurred because of this.

Given at Anagni, on the 2nd day before the Kalends of September, in the second year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati monasterii Vallis Umbrose mandat ut electum Ravennatem et executores compellat, ne ab abbate et conventu monasterii Sancti Apollinaris et subiectis domibus ultra CC libras Senenses exigant, moderans summam in ducentis libris et absolvens abbatem et conventum a residuo nongentorum librarum. Anagnie, II Kalendas Septembris, anno secundo.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop and chapter of Paderborn. It has come to our attention that our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Cologne, and some of his accomplices sacrilegiously seized you, brother bishop, offending the clerical order and the dignity of the pontificate, keeping you captive in their camps until you and you, dear sons of the chapter, were forced to enter into a certain ordinance and composition with them. Through this, several castles, places, rights, jurisdictions, revenues, possessions, and other properties of yours and of the Church of Paderborn must be ceded to the right and ownership of the said archbishop and the Church of Cologne, with some of the aforesaid castles and places being completely subjected to destruction. Additionally, you renounced your rights, which belonged to you concerning several castles, villages, churches, lands, possessions, and others, expressly promising that you would not seek any letters from the Apostolic See or its legates or from the emperor, who might be in power at the time, against such a composition or ordinance, with it being enacted in the said composition and ordinance that such letters, if obtained, would have no validity. In this matter, letters, instruments, and public documents were given, penalties were added, sureties and various guarantees were exhibited, faith and even bodily oaths were interposed, with some of your vassals promising by oath that they would not stand by you against the archbishop and the aforementioned accomplices if you did not keep the same ordinance. Therefore, we, wishing to provide a beneficial remedy concerning these matters which are said to lead to a serious injury to the said Church of Paderborn, absolve you and the sureties given by you, as well as the vassals and any others named for you in the aforesaid ordinance and composition, from the obligations, promises, renunciations, agreements, guarantees, and assurances, the exhibitions of faith and oath, and any other matters included in the aforesaid composition and ordinance, with these premises being true, by the authority of these presents, restoring the said Church of Paderborn to the state it was in before the time of these compositions, ordinances, and such captivity. Let no one harm our absolution and restoration, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the 17th of the Kalends of April, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo et capitulo Padeburnensibus mandat eos absolvi ab obligationibus et promissionibus illis, quae coacti fuerunt inire cum Coloniensi archiepiscopo; et ecclesiam Padeburnensem ad statum pristinum reducendam decrevit. Datum Laterani, XVII Kalendas Aprilis, anno tertio.

**Translation to English:**

To the Scholastic of the Church of Strasbourg. It has been brought to our attention by the beloved sons, the prelates, religious, and clergy of the city and diocese of Cologne that, following a dispute between the venerable brother, our Archbishop of Cologne, on one side, and the noble men, the Count of Monte and Walram, brother of the Count of Jülich, along with some other nobles of the same diocese concerning various matters, these nobles have inflicted such grave damages upon the churches of the said city and diocese, both regular and secular, through arson and plunder and other means, that many from the said clergy and monasteries, having no means of sustenance, are compelled to miserably live outside the aforementioned churches, while the nuns, driven by hunger, turn to illicit acts, and the churches themselves are deprived of proper services. Since the divine preeminence has entrusted the care of all churches to us, though unworthy, we, moved by the supplications of the aforementioned prelates, religious, and clergy, command you, that if the truth supports the aforementioned claims, you diligently admonish and induce the said nobles and all others known to have inflicted such damages upon the aforementioned churches and monasteries, and their prelates and clergy, to make full satisfaction for the said damages within a suitable period, which you shall determine. Otherwise, as is just, you shall pronounce sentences of excommunication against these wrong

**Translation to English:**

To the Chapter of Magdeburg. We gladly add the firmness of apostolic protection to those things which are prudently arranged by church persons for their benefit, so that what has been fortified by our protection may remain unblemished. Indeed, your petition presented to us stated that, although Pope Innocent, of happy memory, our predecessor, and we ourselves, after pronouncing the sentence of deposition against Ludolph, who then pretended to be the bishop of the Halberstadt church, declared all alienations, infeudations, leases, and contracts made or held by the same Ludolph concerning castles, towns, possessions, and other goods belonging to that church and to its detriment, to be null and void, we deemed it proper to restore all these to the rights and ownership of the church. Nonetheless, the same Ludolph presumed to give in fief the county called Sehusen and three castles belonging to the said church to the noble men John and Otto, Margraves of Brandenburg, receiving from them three thousand and four hundred marks of silver, without the consent of the chapter of Halberstadt, converting these marks to his own use. However, our venerable brother, the bishop of Halberstadt, and the same chapter, acknowledging that they were unable to recover the county and castles from the hands of those nobles due to their power, although the same nobles had been diligently admonished under apostolic authority to restore the county and castles, transferred the said county and castles to your church, having provided the necessary oaths and securities from both sides, and receiving from you and your church, in the name of the Halberstadt church, two other castles and an annual income, as well as four thousand five hundred marks of silver, which the said bishop and chapter converted to settle the debts of the aforementioned Halberstadt church, which was engulfed in the voracity of usury. We, therefore, inclined by your supplications, ratify and approve what has been providently done in this matter, confirming it by apostolic authority and fortifying it with the protection of this present letter. Let no one infringe on our confirmation, etc. Given at Viterbo, on the 11th Kalends of January, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa [Gregorii IX] Capitulo Magdeburgensi mandat, ut confirmat transferentiam comitatus et castrorum Halberstadiensium ad ecclesiam Magdeburgensem, auctoritate apostolica, ob rerum ecclesiae Halberstadiensis debitis oppressae solutionem. Dat. Viterbii, XI Kalendas Ianuarii, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Siena. Since we are placed, albeit unworthily, on a lofty watchtower, we are bound to more diligently ensure the peace of the churches and guard against damages, as we rest more securely in their peace and take delight in their undisturbed state. Indeed, we have received with astonishment and are justly moved by the news that the Podestà, the Captain, and the councillors of Siena have established certain ordinances, statutes, and regulations, confirmed by oath, against ecclesiastical liberty, frequently imposing numerous burdens and unusual services on the clergy and churches as well as on the properties of the churches. This situation seems to make the priesthood under them in a worse condition than it was under Pharaoh, who had no knowledge of divine law. Therefore, unwilling, as we ought not to be, to overlook such actions by the Podestà and others with closed eyes, which cannot be committed without peril to salvation, we command you by apostolic writings, if it is so, to admonish and earnestly persuade the Podestà and the aforementioned others that — notwithstanding the aforesaid oath — within two months of your admonition, they remove such ordinances, statutes, and regulations from their records completely and do not observe or allow others to observe any customs introduced against ecclesiastical liberty, and moreover, to cease henceforth from such grievances. Otherwise, you shall publicly proclaim them excommunicated on each Sunday and feast day with bells tolling, and ensure they are more strictly avoided by others; contradictors, etc. Given at Anagni, the 10th day before the Kalends of April, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Episcopo Senensi mandat, ut potestatem, capitaneum et consiliarios Senenses moneat et inducat ad removenda ordinamenta contra ecclesiasticam libertatem, alias eos excommunicatione innodet. Datum Anagnie, X Kalendas Aprilis, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Pamplona. On behalf of our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of Navarre, it was proposed before us that after the death of the late king of Navarre, T., his father, several nobles of his kingdom presumed, not without the mark of treachery, to oppose the king, who was still in his youth, regarding the acquisition of the rights to the said kingdom. This same king, in order to redeem the royal right, was forced to pay certain stipends to such nobles and to do some other things to them, to which he was previously bound only voluntarily, and he bound himself with an oath to the detriment of the same kingdom. Over time, the nobles of the kingdom, with his mother and all the advisors he had brought with him from the region of Champagne, being excluded both from the king and the kingdom, procured through certain manipulations that he, who at that time had barely reached the fourteenth year of his age, enter into some illicit alliances with our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious king of Aragon, who was at that time in a dispute against our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious king of Castile, not without the detriment of the aforementioned kingdom, and that he should confirm them by his own oath. But when this king later withdrew the aforementioned stipends from the said nobles, as he was allowed to do before the said oath, and made an agreement with the aforementioned king of Castile, thereby withdrawing from the alliance of the king of Aragon, as the state of his kingdom justly required, he is said to have violated the sanctity of his oaths. He humbly asked us to provide for him in this matter for his well-being. Therefore, desiring to counsel the honor and reputation of the said king of Navarre, we command that you should earnestly exhort and induce those to whom the said king is believed to be obligated by reason of these oaths, in our name, to release these oaths without any difficulty. Otherwise, you are to relax the oaths and declare that he is not bound to observe them, providing for him regarding the violation of these oaths. Given at Viterbo, on the 6th of November, in the third year.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Pampilonensi mandat, ut monitionibus et inductionibus suis nobiles, quibus rex Navarre per iuramenta obligatus creditur, hortetur ad relaxanda iuramenta; aliter iubet ipse episcopus iuramenta relaxet et regem non teneri denuntiet. 1229, Nov. 6, Viterbii.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop, Dean, and Chapter of Besançon. The measures taken for those dedicated to God, aimed at curbing the insolence of those who are hostile to the clergy, are all the more worthy of apostolic support, as it is safer to prudently address issues beforehand than to find a remedy after an offense has been committed. Your petition presented to us indicated that you, dear sons Dean and Chapter, recognizing that the nobles of neighboring regions, and especially the vassals of your church, have wickedly conspired against you and the same church, and have extended sacrilegious hands against some individuals of your and other churches, daringly capturing and imprisoning some of them, have wisely decided, with careful counsel, that if any layperson, regardless of status or rank, kills, wounds, or rashly captures any of the canons of the aforementioned church, his male descendants up to the fourth degree shall not be able to obtain a position or benefit in your said church, with your consent, brother Archbishop, as you assert more fully in the letters made and sealed by you. We, therefore, moved by your supplications, hold this statute as valid and pleasing, and we confirm it by apostolic authority and support it with the protection of this present writing. No one is to infringe on our confirmation etc. Given at Anagni, April 28, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo, decano et capitulo Bisuntinis confirmat statutum quod si aliquis laicus clericum ecclesiae vulneraverit seu ceperit, filii eius usque ad quartum gradum non possint in eadem ecclesia beneficia obtinere. Datum Anagnie, IIII Kalendas Maii, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Patriarch of Aquileia. On behalf of the beloved sons, the provost, the dean, and the chapter of the church of Bamberg, it was presented before us that the said church, which pertains directly to the Roman Church without any intermediary, has been deprived of pastoral governance. They, as is customary, gathered together, invoked the grace of the Holy Spirit, and canonically and unanimously elected the beloved son, Berthold, a canon of the same church, a man indeed prudent and discreet, and circumspect in spiritual and temporal matters, as their bishop and pastor. They humbly petitioned us that, since the same church, whose possessions and goods are held by some, is so burdened with debt that the same elected cannot personally visit the Apostolic See to obtain the confirmation and consecration due to the great detriment of the church, we might confirm this election and grant the consecration to the elected — notwithstanding the constitution issued by us, which demands that the elect of churches, which pertain directly to the Roman Church, must personally visit the same see for their consecration — in those parts. We, therefore, considering the merits of the same elected and the devotion and fidelity his forefathers held towards the Roman Church, and pursuing them with the favor of special grace, mandate by the authority of these presents, with the counsel of our brothers, to your fraternity, that after diligently inquiring into the manner of the election, the diligence of the electors, and the merits of the elected, if you find the election to have been canonically celebrated concerning an appropriate person, you confirm it by our authority and, with a legitimate number of bishops summoned to you, grant the consecration to the elected, ensuring that obedience and due reverence are shown to him by his subjects. Afterward, you will receive from him, on our behalf and that of the Roman Church, the usual oath of fidelity according to the form we send you enclosed under our seal. Otherwise, if the election is annulled, you are to instruct the said provost, dean, and chapter to provide for the Bamberg church by canonical election of a suitable person; contradictors, etc. You should diligently ensure that the form of the oath he is to swear is sent to us word for word through his open letters, sealed with his seal, by his own messenger as soon as possible. Given at Anagni, the 11th of January, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX Papa Patriarchae Aquilegiensi mandat, ut post diligentem inquisitionem de electione Bertholdi canonici Bambergensis ecclesiae, si electionem invenerit canonice celebratam, eam auctoritate sua confirmet et electo consecrationis munus tribuat, fidelitatis iuramentum recepturus. 1230, Jan. 11, Anagniae.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Tricarico. After many grievous reports that have deeply troubled our hearts, which the procurators of the chapter of Regensburg have repeatedly brought to us concerning our venerable brother, the Bishop of Regensburg, he was finally summoned to our presence and that of our brothers. It was alleged that this bishop is stained with the most vile vice, for which the wrath of God descends upon the children of unbelief, and is heavily defamed. Since the detestation of such a vice is not only abhorrent to hear but also dreadful to contemplate, and since the fragrance of a good reputation, which ought especially to emanate from a bishop, compels us to obtain clear knowledge and manifest understanding of this matter, we command you to personally proceed to the city and diocese of Regensburg and, after informing the bishop of these charges, to diligently investigate the truth concerning this vice from credible witnesses of the same city and diocese and others whom you deem necessary and through whom this can best be known, without obstruction by any evasion or appeal. If the aforementioned bishop wishes to challenge the witnesses you have deemed admissible against him, you are to prudently receive and carefully examine those whom he produces on his behalf concerning such challenges within two months from the time you admit the aforementioned witnesses, as well as others whom the chapter might produce concerning the challenge of the bishop's witnesses within two further consecutive months. You are to bring to us in person what you discover concerning this affair and the written testimonies of all the witnesses produced. The witnesses, who, etc., up to: to testify. Moreover, lest the truth of the said crime be concealed under the pretext of excuses, which we can rightfully avoid, we desire that all those whom you deem necessary or useful for testimony should they perhaps have been excommunicated by the bishop from the time he was appealed to the apostolic see by the chapter, or will be in the future while the matter is pending, you or another on our behalf shall absolve them in this respect, provided that they first make suitable satisfaction for their notorious excesses for which they are bound by such excommunication and provide adequate assurance concerning doubtful matters about adhering to the law. Given at Viterbo, on the fifth day before the Kalends of May, in the fourth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Tricaricensi mandat ut personaliter ad civitatem et diocesim Ratisponensem accedat, veritatem de nefandissimo vitio episcopi Ratisponensis a testibus fide dignis diligenter inquirat, et omnia scripta fideliter nobis personaliter praesentet. Viterbii, V Kalendas Maii, anno quarto.

### Translation to English:

To the Bishop of Cambrai. The petition of our beloved sons, the noble man Eustace the Younger of Rœulx and the noble woman Agnes of Trasegnies, his wife, of your diocese, was presented to us. It stated that our predecessor, of happy memory, Pope Innocent, had commissioned our beloved son, H., cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina, then apostolic legate in the kingdom of Germany, to dispense with a certain nobleman of Hainaut so that he might marry a noble woman related to him in the fourth degree of consanguinity, if he saw it to be expedient for the church and our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious king of the Romans, William. The same cardinal commissioned Brother Michael of the Order of Preachers of Lille to dispense in this matter according to the said form. But since Brother Michael delayed proceeding in this matter and our predecessor departed from this world, the cardinal, by our special mandate given to him verbally, again commissioned Brother Michael by his letters to proceed in the aforementioned matter according to the form given by the cardinal. Brother Michael then dispensed with Eustace and Agnes, who are from Hainaut, so that they might lawfully marry, notwithstanding the fourth degree of consanguinity. Thus, by the pretext of such a dispensation, they contracted marriage between themselves through words of the present, followed by carnal union. However, you or your official, to whom it is asserted this matter was reported, summoned them to your presence because the marriage was alleged not to be valid. Wherefore, the said nobles humbly implored us to provide for them with paternal care. We therefore, wishing that what was done by Brother Michael under the pretext of the commission given by the cardinal by our authority have the strength of permanence, have deemed it appropriate to confirm the process conducted by Brother Michael by our letters, nonetheless dispensing with the same nobles by apostolic authority as a precaution, so that — notwithstanding the said degree — they may lawfully remain in the marriage thus contracted. Therefore, we mandate that you do not further trouble these nobles regarding this matter. Otherwise, we grant our venerable brother, the archbishop of Reims, by our letters the mandate to restrain you from such harassment, having first admonished you and with the impediment of appeal removed by our authority. Given at the Lateran, on the 13th day before the Kalends of February, in the second year (of our pontificate).

### Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Cameracensi mandat, ut Eustachium de Rodio et Agnetem de Trasegnies, coniuges ex dispensatione facta a fratre Michaele auctoritate cardinalis, non molestet, confirmans matrimonium et dispensans auctoritate apostolica. 1229, Ian. 20. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

Wolrad, elected Bishop of Halberstadt. As informed by you, it has come to our attention that our predecessor, Pope Innocent of blessed memory, having been informed of the invalid election of Ludolf of Sladen, a canon of the said church, declared the election entirely null and instead confirmed your canonical election with the counsel of his brothers. However, the said predecessor, by granting many graces and benefits to Ludolf to persuade him to comply with his mandates, instructed him through letters not to interfere with the administration of the bishopric of Halberstadt. He was to surrender peacefully all that pertained to you, including the bishopric, the city of Halberstadt, castles, towns, and other related matters, along with any benefits reaped in the interim. The same predecessor also mandated the provost of the church in Germorode of the Mainz diocese that if Ludolf disobeyed the apostolic mandate, the provost should revoke those graces and benefits and declare Ludolf deprived of them as ungrateful. Furthermore, commands were issued to the abbot of the monastery of Ballenstedt and the provost of the church of St. Mary in Erfurt to excommunicate Ludolf and any adherents and place their lands under interdict if they resisted the apostolic mandates, enforcing these sentences until proper satisfaction was achieved. Despite these measures, Ludolf not only disobeyed but compounded his wrongdoing by having the messenger carrying the letters blinded and e

**Translation to English:**

To the same. The difficulties of the past times and the shameless ambition of those requesting have greatly constrained our predecessor of happy memory, Pope I, to grant many and various things which he would perhaps not otherwise have conceded. Indeed, he was frequently compelled to issue concessions that did not align with his intentions, due to circumstances of place, persons, and the perilous nature of those times. It is said that this predecessor granted general and even special letters, in various tenors and forms, regarding archbishoprics, bishoprics, abbeys, and priories, stipulating that when they became vacant, they would be conferred upon those specified. Concerning lower benefices as well, such as deaneries, archdeaconries, and other prebends, parochial churches, and other benefices with care, designated by proper names or equivalent indications, it is reported that he granted these so that, upon vacancy, they would be assigned to certain persons for whom he had specifically directed his writings. These grants seem offensive due to the vice of ambition, which is an insatiable anxiety of harmful will, and because they involve plotting for another's death, being full of divine judgement's reproach and most sorrowful outcome, as it makes one seem to desire the death of the neighbor, whose place and benefit they believe they will succeed to, and it places hope for future succession on the possessions of the living. Therefore, wishing to swiftly remedy this disease, since the expectation of future succession should not claim a place in the Church of God, which even the Gentiles condemned in their laws, we, with the counsel of our brothers, decree that the letters obtained under any form concerning the aforementioned archbishoprics, bishoprics, abbeys, and priories, whether general or special, and the other lower benefices mentioned above obtained in the expressed form, and such grants, and whatever has followed from them or because of them, unless those procuring them have already acquired such dignities, benefices or other aforementioned items through those letters and are in possession of them, shall be void and not valid in the future. Especially since we have learned that the same predecessor intended to apply a wholesome remedy to this issue and was planning their revocation before his death. Given at Naples, the 5th of April, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX, omnibus quibus interest, declarat litteras super archiepiscopatibus, episcopatibus, abbatiis et prioratibus, necnon inferioribus beneficiis, sub diversis formis a felicis memoriae Papa Innocentio III concessas, nisi iam in possessione eorundem impetratores sint, esse nullius roboris. 1227, 5 Aprilis, Neapoli.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbots of Hottenburg and the hermits of Keremitari, as well as the abbot of Novillaren, of the Benedictine Order, in the dioceses of Augsburg, Constance, and Strasbourg. Our beloved son, Master Sibatto, a canon of Chur, acting on behalf of the greater and more prudent part of the convent of the monastery of Maioris Augiae, of the Benedictine Order in the diocese of Constance, which is said to belong directly to the Roman Church, has informed us that Abbot Burchard of the said monastery, having completely forsaken regular observance, is entangled in the sins of simony, perjury, and waste of the monastery's goods, and is otherwise insufficient in age, morals, and knowledge to govern the aforementioned monastery. Due to his negligence and dissolute life, the monastery is so deteriorated in spiritual and temporal matters that unless a speedy remedy is provided by the Apostolic See, it will incur irreparable harm. Furthermore, the same abbot, guilty in his own conscience, has caused the capture and imprisonment in iron chains of the provost and the custodian of the same monastery, because they oppose his nefarious actions, with the help of his armed brethren. Since, according to the Apostle 2 Corinthians 11:28, our daily concern is the continuous care for all the churches, we command you, if it is established to you that the greater and more prudent part has appointed its procurator, Master Sibatto, to seek an inquiry against the said abbot and that the said abbot is publicly defamed regarding these matters or any of them, to personally go to the same monastery and, with God alone before your eyes, to correct and reform by our authority what you know needs correction and reform, both in the head and in the members, removing from their offices those whom you see fit to remove due to their faults. Otherwise, do not proceed with such an inquiry. Furthermore, ensure the provost and the custodian are restored to liberty and received back in the same monastery, according to regular discipline, and that two or three persons on behalf of the said convent pursuing this business are provided necessary expenses from the goods of the same monastery, with the alienation of the goods of the aforementioned monastery completely forbidden to the named abbot. To the contradictors, etc. If not all, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of June, in the second year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbatibus Hottenburon et Keremitarum ac Novillarensi ordinis sancti Benedicti in diocesibus Augustensi, Constantiensi et Argentinensi mandat, ut si constiterit partes conventus monasterii Maioris Augie ad inquisitionem contra abbatem Burchardum constituisse procuratorem, ad monasterium accedant et corrigant auctoritate apostolica, amoventes indignos ab administrationibus. Dat. Laterani, XV Kalendas Iunii, anno secundo.

**Translation to English:**

To the dean and chapter of the church of Hamburg of the Bremen diocese. When it is requested of us, etc., up to: to the effect. Indeed, the petition you presented to us contained that in your church, by ancient and approved custom, it has been peacefully observed until now that those from the canons of the same church who hold lesser prebends should be promoted to greater ones when they become vacant, provided they are deemed more worthy and appear more beneficial to the church itself. But if by chance any greater prebend happens to become vacant there and none among them is considered suitable for it, you, to whom the conferment of prebends in the mentioned church pertains, bestow such a prebend on a suitable person and receive them as a canon and brother at the same prebend, the aforementioned canons meanwhile waiting for the greater prebends until they, due to their merits, are promoted to them. Therefore, on your behalf, it was humbly requested of us that we should strengthen this laudable custom, from which not a little increase in divine worship proceeds, with apostolic protection. Thus, inclined by your supplications, we consider the custom, as it has been reasonably obtained and peacefully observed until now, valid and firm, and we confirm it with apostolic authority and strengthen it with the protection of this writing. Let no one... of our confirmation, etc. Given at Anagni, on the 12th of May, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa decano et capitulo ecclesiae Hammenburgensis Bremensis diocesis confirmat consuetudinem, qua canonici minores ad maiores prebendas promovendos sunt, et si nullus idoneus invenitur, prebendam vacantem alii persone ydonee conferri, auctoritate apostolica corroborat. 1231, Maii 14. Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the clergy of the city and diocese of Lucania. We willingly and with a benevolent affection accede to your desires, by which the tranquility of your status is procured by removing the cause of your grievance. Indeed, your petition presented to us stated that we, by our letters, instructed our beloved son, Master Dalfinati of Naples, our chaplain, to ensure that our venerable brother, the Bishop of Monopoli, is provided by you with one hundred and ten pounds of Provencal currency annually, until he can return to his church and remain there safely; contradictors, etc.; and you have provided for the said bishop with such funds for one year. Wherefore, you humbly petitioned us that, since you are burdened by excessive poverty and your revenues and income are greatly diminished due to the dangers of wars, and you are often burdened by the procurations of legates and envoys of the Apostolic See frequently passing through your parts, we would take care to provide for you with paternal solicitude on this matter. We, therefore, inclined by your supplications, absolve you from such provision by the authority of these presents, out of special grace. Let no one — our absolution etc. Given at the Lateran, on the 9th day of December, in the sixth year. From the Register of Urban IV.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Urbanus IV papa clero Lucane civitatis et diocesis supplicationibus inclinatus, eos ab onere provisionis centum et decem librarum Provisinorum annuatim episcopo Monopolitano faciendi speciali gratia absolvit. 1268, Dec. 9, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the illustrious King of the Romans, W.

The duty of our office requires that amidst our concerns, etc., we strive for growth. Our intention, thought, and all our efforts are directed towards this: to call upon those who are entrusted with the Lord's flock and who are knowledgeable not only in the doctrine of words but also in deeds, to prudently guide and direct them in the way of wholesome commandments, and who desire not to rule over their subjects but to benefit them and to govern the churches entrusted to them in a peaceful and tranquil state.

Since our venerable brother, the Patriarch of Jerusalem, has been divinely transferred from the Verdun church, over which he previously presided, to Jerusalem, we, who are bound by the yoke of apostolic service to all churches, recognizing that if the provision for the aforementioned Verdun church is delayed, it would be subjected to many dangers and suffer serious spiritual and temporal losses, wish to promptly provide the Verdun church with a suitable shepherd. Therefore, with the counsel of our brothers and the fullness of apostolic authority, we have appointed our beloved son, Master Robert, elected of Verdun, then chamberlain of our beloved son, Cardinal I. of St. Nicholas in Carcere Tulliano, a man indeed learned, conspicuous for the honesty of his morals, prudent in counsel, and circumspect in spiritual and temporal matters, acceptable to us and our brothers by the merit of his probity, as bishop and pastor of the aforementioned Verdun church. We hope that through his commendable caution and circumspect providence, that church will prosper in both spiritual and temporal matters by the grace freely bestowed by the Lord.

However, because the same elected one is occupied with many and arduous matters of his church at the apostolic see and cannot presently come in person to your presence to receive from you or your officials, as is customary, the regalia of the aforementioned church, we have decided to earnestly request and exhort your serenity to, upon receiving the oath of fidelity from the messenger or procurator of the elected one in his name according to the custom of your kingdom, liberally grant these regalia to the said messenger in the name of the elected one for the reverence of us and the apostolic see, and also for the regard of the same elected one, who through the merits of his probity can be manifold fruitful for you and your benefits, putting aside any delay. Also, extend to him your favor and appropriate assistance. Let your royal magnificence fulfill our request in this regard in such a way that the aforementioned church, on the occasion of these regalia, does not incur any loss or detriment in temporal and spiritual matters, and that the same elected one is thereby more strictly bound to your service, and that we may rightly commend your excellence with due praises in the Lord.

Given at Anagni, 3rd day before the Nones of November, in the first year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa illustri regi Romanorum W. commendat electionem magistri Roberti in episcopum Virdunensem et rogat ut regalia ei liberaliter conferat. 1227, Nov. 3. Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Bremen, and to John of Lübeck and Henry of Hamburg, scholars, canons, and procurators of the Church of Bremen. Since, as you have presented in our presence, it is necessary for you, brother Archbishop, to bear the costs of expenses for carrying out your business and that of the Church and chapter of Bremen, lest these matters remain unresolved due to lack of funds, we, inclined by your supplications, grant you full authority by the present letters to contract a loan up to the sum of 2,500 marks sterling. This includes obliging you, brother Archbishop, and the said chapter, and your successors, and the goods of the same Church to the creditors, renouncing the constitution of two days established in the General Council, and the benefit of full restitution and all apostolic letters and indulgences obtained or to be obtained, as well as the agreement of judges, should any apostolic letters of any tenor be obtained in the name of those creditors in the future. However, you, brother Archbishop, and the said chapter and successors must pay the creditors this money, as well as damages, expenses, and interest if the money is not paid to the said creditors within a term set by you. Under the pretext of any canonical or civil constitution or any privilege or indulgence, which would need to be fully and expressly mentioned in our letters, and by which you, brother Archbishop, and the chapter and successors might otherwise defend yourselves, there is no necessity for proving that the said money was turned to the benefit of the Church. Given at Anagni, on the 14th Kalends of July, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Bremensi et Iohanni Lubicensi et Henrico Hamburgensi mandat, ut mutuum usque ad summam duorum milium et quingentarum marcarum sterlingorum contrahant, ecclesia Bremensi pro negotiis expediendis obligata. Anagniae, XVIUI Kalendas Iuli, anno quinto (1231).

**Translation to English:**

To the Patriarch of Jerusalem. Once, Pope Innocent III of happy memory, our predecessor, granted to the beloved sons, the master and brothers of the Order of the Temple of Jerusalem, the right to receive from the redemptions of the vows of those bearing the cross for the aid of the Holy Land, when poverty or probable personal weakness or a dispensation obtained from the Apostolic See excused them from personally fulfilling their vow, as well as from usuries, plunders, and other illicit acquisitions which the faithful ordered to be restored in their last will or even while they live, if they enjoy good health and are ready to restore them, provided those to whom restitution should be made cannot be found. They could also receive from the testaments of these faithful, which are bequeathed for the aid of said land without specifying any places or persons, up to a sum of ten thousand marks of silver wherever outside the kingdom of Germany, with certain executors appointed over this matter.

We, afterward, before the master and brothers as they claimed, had received such sums from the aforementioned, sympathizing with your needs and expenses with paternal affection, deemed it fit to grant you under certain conditions that you would receive the redemptions of vows and the aforementioned legacies in the kingdom of Jerusalem; and not wanting to stir up any cause of disturbance between you and the said master and brothers, we, induced by your prayers, in recompense for this grace granted to them in the said kingdom of Jerusalem, allowed the same master and brothers by our letters to receive all aforementioned things included in their predecessor’s grant wherever outside the said kingdom of Jerusalem, until they fully received what remained outstanding from the sum mentioned above.

However, since, as you claim, the aforementioned master and brothers are prepared to cede to you the receipt of usuries, plunders, and such illicit acquisitions, from which they still, as they assert, have not received anything in the aforesaid kingdom of Jerusalem, we, considering that, as we have learned from your notification, besides being greatly burdened with debt, you fear the advent of the Tartars and have to endure heavy burdens of expenses for the defense of the Church and your subjects, as well as for the aid of the Holy Land, to which the slender and feeble revenues of your patriarchate are said to be insufficient, and thus, out of the prerogative of love and grace, which your merits demand we extend to your person, wishing you to enjoy the solace of some relief, we grant to your fraternity by the authority of these presents that you may receive from the aforementioned usuries, plunders, and illicit acquisitions to the extent that the said master and brothers were to receive, and under the same form, so that if you remit or restore anything from the aforementioned or give to those from whom you received them, such remitted, restored, or given shall not benefit them at all towards their liberation nor shall they be considered absolved in any way concerning that amount. No one is to infringe upon our concession, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the 12th of February, in the third year.
