**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Patriarchae Hierosolymitano concedit ut usuras, rapinas, et illicite acquisita, quae fratres Ordinis Templi in regno Hierosolymitano recipere poterant, ipse percipiat, ob graviora onera et Tartarorum adventum, quae subire oportet. Datum Laterani, II Idus Februarii, anno tertio.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Henry, Count of Chastel, and the noble woman, daughter of our beloved son, the noble man Louis, Count of Oettingen, of the dioceses of Würzburg and Augsburg.

Although the sacred canons prohibit the contract of marital union in the fourth degree of consanguinity or affinity, the Apostolic See has customarily dispensed with such cases when necessity or utility has been considered, especially with devoted and meritorious individuals. Therefore, since, as you assert, you are united by the fourth line of consanguinity, we, considering your devotion and the steadfastness of faith of your ancestors towards God and the Church, and being inclined by the devout prayers of your father, daughter, with these presents, by our special grace and the plenitude of our power, we dispense that you may lawfully contract and consummate marriage with each other, and also remain in that state, notwithstanding the impediment arising from the aforementioned consanguinity, for the good of peace and the tranquil state of your country. Let no one infringe on our dispensation, etc.

Given at Anagni, on the Ides of July, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Henrico comiti de Chastel et nobili mulieri, filiae Ludovici comitis de Ottingen, dispensat ut, non obstante consanguinitatis impedimento in quarto gradu, matrimonium contrahere et consumare possint. 1232, Iul. 15. Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man John, Margrave of Brandenburg, and the noble woman Jutta, his wife, daughter of the noble Duke of Saxony. Once, when you petitioned us that, despite being related to each other in the third degree of consanguinity, you might be permitted to contract marriage and lawfully stay in it, we eventually dispensed you by our authority in this matter, and you subsequently contracted marriage with each other, with the carnal union having followed. However, because between you, daughter Jutta, and the late Otto, son of the noble Duke of Brunswick, who was related to you in the fourth degree of consanguinity and was your nephew, there had been a betrothal by words of future, about which no mention was made in our letters, by whose authority this dispensation arose, you had a scrupulous conscience regarding this matter. Our beloved son, H., presbyter cardinal of the title of St. Sabina, by our special mandate made orally to him, dispensed you to lawfully remain in the thus contracted marriage notwithstanding this impediment, as is more fully contained in the letters of the cardinal drawn up and sealed with his seal. Therefore, inclined by your supplications, we have ordered the tenor of the cardinal's letters to be inserted word for word in these presents for caution; which is as follows: Hugo, by divine mercy presbyter cardinal of the title of St. Sabina, to his beloved in Christ, the noble man John, Margrave of Brandenburg, and the noble woman Jutta, his wife, daughter of the noble Duke of Saxony, greetings in the Lord. It has been proposed on your behalf before us that when the lord pope instructed the religious men, the abbot in Lennima of the Cistercian order of the diocese of Brandenburg, and the provincial prior of the Friars Preachers of Germany, by his letters to see to it that you might be able to contract matrimony with each other and consummate the contract and lawfully remain in it, despite being joined in the third degree of consanguinity, by his authority, the same abbot, to whom the said prior had committed his place in this part, dispensed you in this matter by the authority of these letters, and by the pretext of such dispensation, you contracted marriage with each other, followed by carnal union. However, since between you, Jutta, and the late Otto, son of the noble Duke of Brunswick, related to you in the fourth degree of consanguinity, there was said to have intervened betrothal by words of future form, which by law could not have occurred, and the same Otto was your nephew, margrave, concerning which no mention is made in these letters, you have humbly requested to be providently relieved by the Apostolic See in this matter. Therefore, by the Lord Pope’s special mandate orally made to us, whose penitentiary care we manage, we dispense you to lawfully remain in the thus contracted marriage, notwithstanding this impediment. Given at the Lateran, January 12, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III. Given at the Lateran, January 21, in the second year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Alexander III papa Iohanni marchioni Brandeburgensi et Iuttae uxori eius, natae ducis Saxoniae, concedit dispensationem ut, non obstante tertia consanguinitatis linea, et sponsalibus inter Iuttam et Ottonem Brunswickensem non memoratis, in matrimonio contracto licite maneant. 1164, Jan. 21, Lateran.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Guido, Marquis, and others, who are commonly called the Guelphs, of the City of Castello, devout to the Roman church. We pursue you with special grace. Therefore, we, inclined by your supplications, the sincerity of your devotion towards the Roman church deserves that we receive you, persisting in the devotion to the Roman church, with all the goods that you reasonably possess at present, under the protection of Saint Peter and our own, etc., up to: we confirm. Therefore, let no one - our protection etc. Given at Orvieto, on the third day before the Kalends of December, in the second year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobilibus viro Guidoni Marchioni et aliis qui Guelfi appellantur, devotionem erga ecclesiam Romanam exhibentibus, protectionem sub beati Petri et sua auctoritate confirmat. 1228, Nov. 29. Apud Urbemveterem.

**Translation to English:**

To the illustrious kings Henry of England and Edmund of Sicily. Our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Tarantaise, and our beloved sons, the elected bishop of Salisbury and the abbot of Westminster, your envoys, humbly petitioned us to extend the deadline given to you, King of England, which had been fixed and approved by you, to send a suitable force to the Kingdom of Sicily and to pay a certain sum of money to us and the Roman Church for expenditures made in that kingdom, as outlined in the papal privilege granted to you, King of Sicily. We, therefore, inclined by their supplications, extended this deadline first to the octave of the aforementioned feast, and then, after consulting with our brothers, to the Wednesday after the octave, as the apostolic letters granted to the same envoys more fully detail. However, since your envoys presented your petitions to us and our brothers, having carefully heard and fully understood those petitions and deliberated with our brothers, we extended the said deadline at their insistence, as far as the sentences and penalty mentioned below are concerned, from the said Wednesday to six months from the first of December next, provided that the money from the tithes of ecclesiastical revenues, granted to you, King of England, by the apostolic see, both already collected and to be collected, is not spent or withheld but is freely paid to merchants for the relief of the debts of the Roman Church without any hindrance. And if any of this amount has perhaps been spent by you or on your order, it is to be fully repaid by you within a month after the knowledge of the extension reaches you, as mentioned above. With the counsel and consent of our brothers, we thus extend as follows: during this time, King of England, you and your kingdom shall not incur the sentences of excommunication and interdict, nor shall you incur the penalty regarding the money borrowed by our venerable brother, the Bishop of Hereford, your procurator and envoy, and for the prosecution of the cause of the Kingdom of Sicily, and which you have paid and may pay in the future, namely that you and your heirs shall have no claim against us and the church or anyone else regarding this money, nor any action, but shall completely forfeit it, regardless of any oaths you may have sworn concerning this matter. No one therefore shall contradict our extension. Given at Anagni, 6 October, in the second year [of our pontificate].

To the Archbishop of Messina. Our venerable brother, etc., until: it is fully repaid, we have thus extended with the counsel and consent of our brothers, namely that in the interim the same King of England, etc., until: notwithstanding, they do not incur. Since we intend to send you specifically for this matter, we grant you the free power, with the counsel of our brothers, to extend the deadline still further according to the prescribed form, if you see fit, for another three subsequent months. Given at Anagni, 10 November, in the second year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa Henrico regi Anglie et Edmundo regi Sicilie, petenti prorogationem termini ad mittendum militiam in regnum Sicilie et solvendum pecuniam, concedit extensionem ad sex menses a Kalendis Decembris, dummodo pecunia decime ecclesiasticorum proventuum non impendatur, sed mercatoribus solvatur, et plenarie satisfiat de quantitate expensa, nec sententias excommunicationis et interdicti incurrant. Dat. Anagnie, II Nonas Octobris, anno II.

Translation to English:

To the Archbishop of Besançon. Our venerable brother, the bishop, and our beloved sons, the chapter of Strasbourg, and all prelates and clerics of the city and diocese of Strasbourg have shown to us by their petition that certain citizens of Strasbourg, sons of perdition, have inflicted various injuries upon clerics and ecclesiastical persons, namely of the order of Preachers. Some were gravely beaten, one was thrown from a bridge into the water, another was hanged, and another was afflicted with various kinds of tortures. The bishop, seeing that the fear of God did not deter them from evil, decided, with the counsel and consent of the chapter, prelates, and clerics, that if any layperson of the said city or diocese presumptuously kills or mutilates any cleric or ecclesiastical person, they shall lose any offices and fiefs held from the churches or ecclesiastical persons of that city and diocese, and nothing shall pass to their heirs. He also added that such offices and fiefs should be conferred to others within fifteen days from the day of the crime by those to whom the collation of these belongs. The bishop also, with the counsel and consent of the aforementioned, issued certain other honest statutes consonant with law against the laypeople of the said city and diocese who perpetrated such crimes, which contribute to the enhancement of ecclesiastical liberty. The bishop, chapter, prelates, and clerics have bound themselves to the observance of these statutes by oath. However, the master, consuls, and community of Strasbourg, along with some nobles and knights of the city and diocese, have conspired against these prelates and clerics, attempting to compel them by capturing and seizing their goods to break these statutes, to the detriment of ecclesiastical liberty and the prejudice and grievance of the said bishop, prelates, and clerics. Therefore, the bishop, chapter, prelates, and clerics have humbly implored us to care for them with paternal solicitude in this matter. Wherefore, we command you, if this is so, to compel the master, consuls, community, nobles, and knights aforesaid to desist entirely from their injuries, by means of a monition and by the sentences of excommunication against their persons and interdict against their lands, the appeal being removed. You shall announce these sentences publicly until proper satisfaction is made, on every Sunday and feast day, with bells tolled and candles lit, and cause them to be announced by others in all places where you deem it useful — notwithstanding any indulgence granted by the apostolic see that might prevent the said community or any others from being taken outside their city or diocese in a case by apostolic letters that do not make full and express mention of such an indulgence, and notwithstanding the constitution of the two days promulgated in the general council. Given at Anagni, June 11, in the second year [of our pontificate].

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Bisuntino mandat, ut magistrum, consules, universitatem, nobiles et milites Argentinenses, qui contra clericos et personas ecclesiasticas ordinis Predicatorum deliquerunt, monitione premissa per excommunicationis et interdicti sententias compellat, ut ab iniuriis desistant, in augmentum ecclesiastice libertatis. Dat. Anagnie, III Idus Iunii, anno secundo.

Translation to English:

To the noble woman Marchisina, daughter of the late Paan.di, Duke of Venice, wife of the noble man Marco Baduarius of Venice, greetings, etc. Because sometimes the devoted become more devoted and others are more easily drawn to devotion when we respond to the merits of the devoted with worthy retribution, the fullness of our munificence in the gifts of graces fittingly abounds in those who, adorned with the clear nobility of lineage, have shown forth with full constancy of devotion and purity of faith towards the Roman Church. It has indeed been intimated to us on your behalf that the county of Andre once belonged to your late grandmother and that the late Emperor Henry of the Romans unjustly dispossessed her of it. Our predecessor Pope John of happy memory once fully restored that county, which is in our kingdom of Sicily, with all its rights and appurtenances, to your late brother Marco Ziano and granted him special favor concerning it, as is more fully contained in the letters of our predecessor regarding such restitution and favor. And since the said Marco is said to have left no son or descendant who could legally succeed him in the said county, it seems that the said county should rather belong to you by hereditary right, since Marco was your full brother from both parents. The said predecessor, recognizing the devotion that you and yours have shown towards the Apostolic See, desires not only that your rights be preserved but also augmented. Therefore, transferring to you and your heirs the favor previously granted by him to Marco, he fully restored and newly granted to you and your heirs the said county with all its rights and appurtenances, as he had restored and granted it to Marco, as a fief out of liberal grace— notwithstanding if the noble woman Alberia, Countess of Mudigliano, your aunt, daughter of the same grandmother, or her sons claim to have a right in the said county, since they adhered to the late Emperor Frederick against the Church, thus rendering themselves utterly unworthy of the grace and favor of the same Church, or if the said Frederick or his son Conrad granted the county to anyone else to your or Mark's prejudice. However, the letters of the said predecessor were never sealed with a bull, because he was prevented by death. Therefore, we, wishing to pursue this favor, fully restore and newly grant to you and your heirs the said county with all its rights and appurtenances in the same manner as our predecessor narrated above, notwiths

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Roger of Paris, our faithful [greetings, etc.]. The great benevolence of the Mother Church maintains such a feeling of compassion towards her children that she does not reject those who return to her. Therefore, considering your devoted return to the Church, being concerned for your welfare and humbly submitting yourself to her sweet and gentle dominion, we receive you into our favor and that of the Apostolic See. We completely forgive you all injuries and offenses you have caused to us and the same See and Church, as we wish to confirm you in this devotion with appropriate favors and grace. Inclined by your supplications, we confirm by apostolic authority, with the counsel of our brethren, the castle of Castelluccio of the Slavs and the estate of Saint Peter of Castelluccio, which you claim to hold by right of succession, and the grants of Dragonaria and the estate of Plantilliano and of the castles of Saint Julian and Petra of Mount Corvin, formerly made to you by the late Frederick, once Emperor of the Romans. Also, the sale and grant of the castle of Clusano to you by the noble woman Gemma, your kinswoman, as well as the grant of the castle of Saint Mark of Catula by the late Conrad, son of the aforementioned Frederick, and of the estates of Casalorde and Bisselleti by the noble man Manfred, then Prince of Taranto, acting as regent of the Kingdom of Sicily—despite Frederick, Conrad, and Manfred being bound by the chain of excommunication at the time and lacking the faculty to confer or grant in such a manner—following the precedent of the happy memory of Pope Innocent, our predecessor. We confirm them to you and your heirs by apostolic authority with the counsel of our brethren. And so that your devotion towards us and the same Church may increase, we grant to you and your heirs the aforementioned castles and estates anew as fiefs, with due and customary services, along with the castle of Rizze, such that you and your heirs shall hold the said castles and estates, with all men enfeoffed and not enfeoffed, woods, pastures, cultivated and uncultivated lands, waters, and watercourses, and all rights, jurisdictions, and appurtenances thereof, directly from the Roman Church, recognizing no superior or lord therein other than her, in perpetuity. To make this grace even more gracious to you, we wish you to know that we and the same church will maintain you and your heirs in possession of the aforementioned castles and estates and will provide necessary defense against all who trouble or challenge you regarding these matters. If it is established that anyone has a right to the aforementioned castles and estates, we shall endeavor to provide them with appropriate compensation in the Kingdom of Sicily. Let no one infringe on this our confirmation and grant. Given at Naples by the hand of William, master of schools of Parma, vice-chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Kalends of May, in the thirteenth indiction, the year of the Lord's incarnation 1255, and the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander IV.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Alexander IV papa nobili viro Rogerio de Parisio castrum Castellutii de Sclavis et alia bona confirmat et in feudum concedit. 1255, April. 24, Neapoli.

**Translation to English:**

To Henry, dean of Metz, our chaplain. A petition presented to us by our beloved son Folmar of Riste, a cleric, stated that he was formerly received into the church of Strasbourg as a canon and brother by the dean and chapter of the church, with the authority granted to them by our beloved son H., cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina, then legate of the apostolic see in those regions, through their letters. However, since we have decreed that the receptions of prebends expected to become vacant, with only four exceptions, are null and void, his reception has been annulled. Therefore, he humbly requested us to provide for him with paternal care in this matter. Therefore, at the request of the aforementioned Folmar, made to us through the intervention of our beloved son, the dean of Metz, our chaplain, we intend to show him special favor and restore the right which belonged to him in the said church by such reception, notwithstanding the constitution we have issued on this matter, and we do not wish that any prejudice may arise to him concerning his reception in the aforementioned church, nor concerning his right and acquisition of a prebend therein due to the same constitution. We command, therefore, that if it is so, you should ensure that Folmar is provided with a prebend, not lawfully owed to another, either currently vacant in the aforementioned church or as soon as the opportunity arises, either by yourself or another — notwithstanding if we have granted similar favor to others in the aforesaid church —; contradictors, etc. Given at Anagni, on the fourth day before the Nones of February, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Henrico decano Metensi mandat, ut Folmaro de Riste clerico de prebenda in ecclesia Argentinensi provideat, receptione eius quam constitutione irritam fecerat, in pristinum statum restituta. 1232, Feb. 2. Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the beloved son R., cardinal deacon of St. Angelo. Our beloved son Oliver, the castellan of Rocca Lariana, has informed us that you have recently received three hundred pounds of Provencal currency from the people of Velletri as compensation for certain injuries they caused to the inhabitants of the same Rocca in the territory of Lariano, while vigorously pursuing the rights of the Roman Church. Since the said Rocca is known to be in need of repair due to its walls threatening ruin from excessive old age, we command your sincerity through apostolic writings to have this money assigned to the aforementioned castellan for the repair of the said Rocca. Given at Orvieto, on the 4th of the Nones of February, in the second year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa dilecto filio R., Sancti Angeli diacono cardinali, mandat ut pecunia a Velletrensibus recepta pro iniuriis incolas Rocce Lariane illatis, castellano eiusdem Rocce ad reparationem murorum assignetur. 1229, Feb. 2, apud Urbemveterem.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Cologne. On behalf of you and the beloved sons of the chapter, priors, judges, aldermen, councilors, jurors, and the entire community of Cologne, it was presented to us that the money changers or masters of the mint of Cologne, commonly called "husgenoeten," along with the masters of the citizens and aldermen who were in the city of Cologne, where you hold temporal jurisdiction, and certain other officials known as the brothers of the aldermen, were publicly infamous for the following: the said money changers or masters of the mint were counterfeiting money, and others were fraudulently and unjustly carrying out their entrusted duties, condemning the innocent and absolving the guilty. You, having legitimately ascertained this and as was your responsibility, removed the money changers, masters, aldermen, and others mentioned, except for one of their aldermen, namely Bruvon of Kranz, who had faithfully and commendably executed the office of alderman, from their entrusted offices by your own authority as justice demanded. The beloved son, the noble man Guillielmus, judge of Arborea, as we have heard, due to his fidelity and devotion to the Roman Church, of which he stands as a foremost supporter, has courageously assembled an army, as befits his nobility, to liberate the Kingdom of Torres from the hands of Manfred, the former Prince of Taranto, who has occupied and continues to hold it. Further, use the prudence granted to you by God to encourage others throughout Sardinia, either personally or through others, both religious and secular, whom you find suitable, to preach the word of the cross against Manfred in aid of the said nobleman and to grant it to those willing to accept. Bestow upon those who proceed against Manfred and his supporters in the same kingdom, in person and at their own expense, and on those who go in person but at the expense of others, and on those who send suitable warriors there at their own expense, the remission of their sins, provided they are truly contrite in heart and have confessed with their mouths, as you see fit; restrain those who oppose, etc., as necessary. Given at Orvieto, 14th of July, in the second year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Arborensi mandat ut Guilelmo, iudici Arboreae, in recuperatione regni Turritani contra Manfredum principem Tarentinum auxilium praestet, verbo crucis per Sardiniam predicando. Dat. apud Urbemveterem, II Idus Iulii, anno secundo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz and his suffragans, and to our beloved sons, the abbots, priors, deans, archdeacons, provosts, archpriests, and other prelates of churches established throughout the province of Mainz. It is not without sorrow of heart and great disturbance that we have learned that in many places ecclesiastical discipline is so relaxed and the severity of canonical sentences so weakened that religious men, and especially those who have been granted greater liberty by privileges of the Apostolic See, suffer injuries and robberies from their wrongdoers without finding anyone to provide them with proper protection or to stand as a wall of defense for upholding the innocence of the poor. Specifically, our beloved daughters in Christ, the prioress, and the sisters of the monastery of Blessed Mary in Wnnental of the Order of Saint Augustine in the diocese of Constance, living according to the rules of the Friars Preachers, have complained about frequent injuries and the very daily lack of justice, and have requested through apostolic letters that the entirety of your community be roused so that you should rise with ready magnanimity in their tribulations against their wrongdoers, so that they may breathe a sigh of relief from the distress and pressures they endure through your protection. Therefore, we command and enjoin you by apostolic writings that you admonish those who have irreverently seized or unjustly detained the possessions or goods or houses of the aforementioned sisters, or who have presumed to promulgate a sentence of excommunication or interdict against these sisters or any of them contrary to the indulgences granted by the Apostolic See, or to extort tithes from the sustenance of their animals by disregarding the privileges of the Apostolic See. If they are laypersons, each of you, in your dioceses and churches, shall strike them with the sentence of excommunication with candles publicly lit; if they are clerics, regular canons, or monks, you shall suspend them from office and benefice, with appeal removed, not relaxing either sentence until full satisfaction is made to the aforementioned sisters, and both lay and secular clerics who are bound by the chain of anathema for the violent laying of hands upon these sisters or any of them, coming with the letters of the diocesan bishop to the Apostolic See, may deserve to be absolved from the same bond. Given at Anagni, on the tenth Kalends of November, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino et eius suffraganeis, et aliis ecclesiarum prelatis in provincia Maguntina constitutis mandat, ut possessiones et res abbatissae et sororum monasterii beatae Mariae in Wnnental ordinis sancti Augustini contra Apostolicae Sedis privilegia invasas restituant, et iniuriarum auctores excommunicatione vel suspensione puniant. Anagniae, X Kalendas Novembris, anno quinto.

To Henry, Bishop-elect of Speyer. We confirm the matters judged, etc., up to: we strengthen, having the tenor of the same instrument inserted verbatim in these presents; which is as follows: To all who will inspect these present letters, Brother Hugo, by divine mercy presbyter of the title of Saint Sabina, Riccardo of Saint Angelo, and Pietro of Saint George at the Golden Veil, deacons and cardinals, send greetings in the Lord. Since the eye of the heavenly judge looks upon justice and His face desires equity, it is known that it concerns the judges of earthly matters to likewise look upon and desire them, to overturn detestable injuries, and to give to each his own with righteous judgment. Indeed, between the venerable father Lord Iring, Bishop of Würzburg, and the venerable man Henry, Bishop-elect of Speyer, a question arose before the venerable father Lord Stephen, Bishop of Palestrina, appointed as judge by the Apostolic See, concerning both the bishopric of Würzburg and damages, injuries, expenses, captives held on either side, and other matters. At last, our lord Pope Alexander, understanding that the church of Würzburg was collapsing in many ways due to this discord, fearing it might fall into the deepest pit of ruin due to the duration of the litigation, entrusted us with the authority to hear the cause briefly by word of mouth, to order and dispose of the damages, expenses, captives, and injuries, and all other matters concerning the case, with the intervention of the consent of both Lord Iring, Bishop of Würzburg, on one side, and Master Diter, the procurator of the same bishop-elect of Speyer, having a special mandate for this, as is evident from the bishop-elect's patent letters.

We, by the authority of our aforesaid lord and of this compromise, having seen, heard, and understood what both the bishop for himself and Master Diterus in the procuratorial name of the said bishop-elect wished to propose in our presence, invoking the name of God, by ordering, arbitrating, and declaring by sentence, adjudge the said bishopric of Würzburg to the aforementioned Bishop Iring, imposing perpetual silence on the said bishop-elect regarding the same bishopric, and commanding the bishop-elect that he should not henceforth raise or cause to be raised any question secretly or publicly against the aforementioned bishop concerning the said bishopric, but should deliver and assign the city of Würzburg, its castles, its villages, and whatever he holds or possesses by himself or by others, which pertains to the said bishopric of Würzburg, to the aforementioned bishop or his messengers without difficulty, as much as lies in him, and absolve the clerics and laity of the same bishopric from all oaths of loyalty and any others he received from them, from which we also absolve those clerics and laity who are known to have sworn such oaths.

Furthermore, we annul, and declare null and void, whatever the said bishop-elect has done as if he were the bishop or prelate of Würzburg by binding, enfeoffing, leasing, donating, or alienating in any way any goods of the said bishopric of Würzburg, decreeing that such obligations, enfeoffments, leases, donations, or alienations, by whatever name they are called, lack any strength of firmness. And because the aforementioned bishop-elect of Speyer, believing he had a right in the said bishopric, personally labored at the Apostolic See and endured many labors and expenses, and some of his friends and relatives were captured and detained in prison due to the discord, we commend and order by pronouncement that the same bishop should free or cause to be freed and procure the freeing of the said captives, otherwise, to aid in their redemption, he should henceforth pay the bishop-elect one thousand marks of pure silver at the weight of the land within one year without reduction.

Since both the bishop-elect and the church of Speyer have borne great expenses in this matter, we, wishing to provide for them, likewise commend and order that the bishop should pay the same bishop-elect and the church two thousand marks of pure silver at the aforesaid weight, one thousand marks to the church and as many to the bishop-elect, in recompense for such expenses. We have ordered the payment of the said two thousand marks to be made in this manner: that from the day of payment of the aforesaid one thousand marks, which should be made, as aforesaid, in this current year for the aid of the redemption of captives, the said bishop should pay the same bishop-elect and the church or their messengers at Mainz in full over the seven consecutive years immediately following, so that each year on the same day, namely, on the octave of the Innocents, three hundred marks and in the last year two hundred will be paid.

To the Bishop of Squillace, residing in Germany. Our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Salzburg, has informed us that John of Ocra, a cleric claiming to be an envoy of the Apostolic See, had ordered the said archbishop to arrange for the payment of four thousand marks of silver to the Roman Church, a debt owed by the archbishop, within one month. In response, the archbishop, having presented legitimate exceptions to John within this period, appealed to the Apostolic See, requesting that no action be taken against him by John. However, John, disregarding the legitimate appeal of the archbishop, pronounced a sentence of excommunication against him. Furthermore, the venerable bishops and beloved sons, our presbyters and deacons, cardinals of the Holy Roman Church, to whom the archbishop had appealed during the vacancy of the see, sought to provide a salutary remedy for the archbishop and the Church of Salzburg. They sent you to those parts with letters under a specific form. Since, as we have learned, you have begun to proceed according to the mandate of the said cardinals, we, wishing this to be brought to its proper effect, and confirming what you have done with the authority of such letters, command you by apostolic writ to proceed in this matter according to the content of the letters directed to you by the said cardinals. Furthermore, you are to compel any wrongdoers against the archbishop, regardless of their order, dignity, or condition, to cease all injuries, and to admonish the prelates and clerics of the city and diocese of Salzburg, as well as the vassals, ministers, and people of the said Church, to obey and attend to the archbishop, under ecclesiastical censure and without appeal. This is notwithstanding any indult from the said see that might prevent or delay the effect of these presents, unless such indult is fully and expressly mentioned in apostolic letters. Moreover, ensure that the archbishop satisfies the said sum of money to the Roman Church by the upcoming Feast of the Purification of the Blessed Virgin Mary, according to the tenor of the cardinals’ letters. Otherwise, we decree that the sentence of excommunication shall be incurred by the archbishop, which you should promulgate as you see fit. Given at Viterbo, 10 Kalends of November, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Urbanus IV papa episcopo Squillacensi in Alamania commoranti mandat, ut in negotio contra Iohannem de Ocra excommunicationem proponentem procedat et archiepiscopum Salzeburgensem ab iniuriis defendat, praestituta satisfactione pecuniae ecclesiae Romanae. Dat. Viterbii, X Kal. Novembris, anno primo.

To the Archbishop of Trani. Due to the devotion, which the nobleman Philip of Santa Croce, the protontinus of Barletta and Monopoli, has towards the Roman Church, and because of the merits of his pure faith, we gladly grant his requests and show ourselves favorable to him in those things he worthily asks. Having come into our presence, he reported that the late Emperor Frederick, while he still persisted in devotion to the Holy See, had granted him and his heirs in perpetuity the castles or hamlets of Terlizzi and Aricci, located in the jurisdictions of the land of Bari, with all their men, rights, and appurtenances, as belonged to him, with generous and provident liberality. We, therefore, moved by his devoted supplications and holding what was done by Frederick and the bishop as confirmed and ratified, have seen fit to confirm it with apostolic authority. And so that he may burn with greater devotion towards us and the Roman Church, although in recompense for other damages he has suffered for the faith of the Roman Church—both in his stable properties in Monopoli and in other movable goods, estimated to the value of 1,500 ounces of gold—and for the services rendered to the same Church, we have granted the land of Cannarum and the castle or hamlet of Caurati, located in the land of Bari, as well as the court house once held by Ribaldinus and the vacant land outside the gate of St. Leonard in Barletta, as is openly contained in the privilege made for him by the Holy See. To the authorities, council, and community of the city of Foligno, our faithful ones. Since, as we have learned, people from various places in the mountains, above Foligno, and at the upper Palo towards Camerino and Mevania, are intending to form or establish some sort of alliance with your favor, we, considering that such an alliance, if it were to occur, would result in prejudice to the Roman Church and its rights, and unwilling to allow this, strictly command you under the obligation of loyalty, which you owe to us and the aforementioned Church, and under penalty of five hundred marks of silver, that you, as you hold our and the Apostolic See's grace dear, do not provide any counsel, assistance, or favor to the aforementioned people in this matter, and presume not to effect any change from the place called Pali upwards towards the aforementioned Mevania, knowing that if you presume otherwise, we, with the Lord as our authority, will proceed to collect the aforementioned penalty and otherwise proceed against you and your land more harshly and severely, spiritually and temporally, as we see fit. Given at Orvieto, December 10, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa potestati, consilio et communi Fuliginatibus mandat ne hominibus de montanis supra Fuligimr et Palo favorem prebeant ad communantiam faciendam, sub pena quingentarum marcarum, et minatur duriter procedere si contrarium fecerint. 1229, Dec. 10, apud Urbemveterem.

**Translation to English:**

To Brother John of Châtillon, of the Order of Friars Minor, our envoy in England. Since our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious king of England, is annually obliged to pay us and our brothers, the cardinals of the Holy Roman Church, a certain sum of money as a tax, and is known to have delayed in this payment for a long time, we command you by apostolic writings to effectively admonish and induce the king on our behalf, so that he may, without difficulty, pay the money for the period in which he has delayed to the beloved sons Rucho Cambii and Raynerio Abbatis, citizens and merchants of Florence, associates of Jacobi de Scala, their fellow citizen, or to either of them, in our name and that of the same cardinals, within a suitable period, which you shall assign peremptorily for this purpose. Otherwise, you shall place the king's chapel under ecclesiastical interdict, notwithstanding if the same king has been granted by the apostolic see that his chapel cannot be interdicted through apostolic letters, unless full and explicit mention is made of such a grant, word for word. Given at the City of Viterbo, the 8th day before the Kalends of August, in the second year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Fratri Iohanni de Cantias ordinis Minorum mandat, ut regem Anglorum moneat ad solvendum pecuniam debitam Rucho Cambii et Raynerio Abbatis mercatoribus Florentinis, alioquin capellam regis supponat interdicto ecclesiastico. Datum apud Urbemveterem, VIII Kalendas Augusti, anno secundo pontificatus nostri.

Translation to English:

To William of Waltmanshuse, guardian of the Friars Minor of Wezele in the diocese of Trier, and Brother Robert of Warnesperg of the Order of Friars Minor in the convent of Trier. Due to the requirement of pastoral care, which the divine dispensation has entrusted to us, we wish to investigate various articles against Henry, the elected of Trier, and have appointed certain persons for this task, in whose diligence and steadfastness we had firm confidence. However, since these persons were less diligent than we hoped in pursuing the assigned task, we have deemed it necessary to entrust the execution to you in the virtue of obedience and under the penalty of excommunication in a certain form, not doubting that what seemed to fail with those persons should succeed in your hands, as your noble lineage, holy religion, and zeal for the divine name promised, inducing the Apostolic See to have firm certainty about you in this matter. But behold, just as with those persons, our confidence seems to be defrauded by you, since, as we have learned, you have committed the matter not to memory but to neglect, as they did. Therefore, we strictly command you, by reiterated letters, in the virtue of obedience and under the aforesaid penalty, which we wish you to incur if you neglect to fulfill our mandate in this matter, that you proceed in this matter now with such diligence according to the form delivered to you, so that you may prove to have cleansed your preceding disobedience through subsequent obedience, and we may not be compelled to write to you otherwise concerning this matter. If not both, etc. Given at Orvieto, on the 30th of November, in the second year.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa Guillelmo de Waltmanshuse guardian fratrum Minorum de Wezele et fratri Roberto de Warnesperg, mandatum iteratum mandat, ut inquisitionem contra Henricum Treverensem electum diligenter exsequantur, sub poena excommunicationis, ad purgandam inobedientiam priorem. Datum apud Urbemveterem, II Kalendas Decembris, anno secundo.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishops of Pavia and Mainz, and the prior of the Friars Preachers in Pavia. Considering the mercies and compassions of the Lord, which are above all His works, and the abundance of His kindness towards the human race, we delight joyously in His praises. We render devout and due thanks to Him, from whom every good and perfect gift comes, and we exult with great jubilation at the newly conceived joy, that the merciful and compassionate Lord, who hates none of the things He has made and desires not the death of sinners but that they may convert and live, has mercifully called back to the devotion of the Mother Church the noble man, the podestà, council, and commune of the city of Pavia, who had, for a long time, strayed damnably from her devotion, as if they had made a pact with death.

For the podestà, council, and commune, who had gravely offended God and the Roman Church by adhering to the former emperor of the Romans and his sons and supporters to their own detriment, have returned to their senses, illuminated by divine grace. Desiring to return humbly to ecclesiastical life, from which they had been cut off due to excommunication, they earnestly sought absolution from such sentences through their beloved sons, the prior and brothers of Domus Nova of the order of Humiliati in Pavia, who were their procurators and special envoys, offering humbly to obey our commands and those of the Church.

We, therefore, though unworthy, entrusted as vicars of Him who most manifests His omnipotence in forgiveness and mercy, have commanded that, after taking a public oath from the podestà and syndic of the council and commune to obey our mandates and those of the Church (an oath we have also received from the aforementioned procurators for greater firmness), and after enjoining on the podestà, council, and commune in our name, under the obligation of the given oath, that they adhere to none against the said Church in the future, and that they accept as king or emperor of the Romans the one whom the provision of the Apostolic See shall approve, you shall absolve both the podestà, council, and commune, and all others, individually and collectively, from the district of the said city from the aforesaid sentences of excommunication by our authority, according to the form of the Church, through you or others. You shall also lift the interdict under which the city and district had fallen due to the aforementioned reason, allowing them to ordain officials and personages, when vacant, as pertains to them. You shall declare and have declared in places where it seems fitting that the aforesaid podestà, council, and commune, and others mentioned above, are absolved. Other matters which we may see fit to impose on the aforementioned podestà, council, and commune according to God, we reserve to our prudence. If not all, etc. Given at Anagni, April 30th, in the fifth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopis Papiensi et Mainensi et priori fratrum Predicatorum Papiensium mandat, ut potestatem, consilium et comune civitatis Papiensis, qui ad devotionem ecclesiae Romanae redierunt, ab excommunicationibus absolvatis et interdictum canonice relaxetis, cum praestito iuramento de obedientia. Dat. Anagnie, II Kal. Maii, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

Urbanus, etc., to our beloved son, Master Albert of Parma, our scribe, greetings, etc. Since our venerable brother, the Bishop of Bamberg, as we have learned from the report of our brothers, the cardinals of the Holy Roman Church, promised to pay one hundred marks of silver in the Roman court, and has not yet satisfied them of the same, we command your discretion by apostolic writings to admonish the said bishop to deliver the sum to you in the name of the same cardinals within the space of one month after your warning, without any delay or difficulty, either personally or through another or others; and if he does not comply with your warnings within the aforesaid term in this matter, you, by our authority, shall pronounce against the said bishop the sentence of excommunication, with the appeal set aside, and shall publicly announce him as excommunicated on all Sundays and feast days with bells ringing and candles lit, and ensure that he is avoided by all in all places where it seems necessary, until he has ensured the full assignment of the aforesaid money to you. If, however, the aforesaid bishop presumes to endure this sentence for one month, you shall then suspend him from the administration of spiritual and temporal affairs, summoning him peremptorily nonetheless, that within two months after your summons, he shall appear personally before us thus suspended to receive what he merits — notwithstanding if an indulgence has been granted to the same bishop by the Apostolic See that he cannot be interdicted, suspended, or excommunicated through apostolic letters not making full and express mention of such an indulgence, or any other indulgence of the same see by which the effect of these presents could be hindered or delayed, and the constitution on two diets issued in the general council —; restraining opposers through ecclesiastical censure, with appeal set aside. You should diligently inform us by your open letters containing the series of these matters the day of the summons and the form, and whatever you have done concerning it. Given at Viterbo, on the 10th Kalends of November, in the first year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Urbanus IV papa Alberto de Parma scriptori mandat, ut episcopum Bambergensem moneat ad solvendas centum marcas argenti cardinalibus, et si non paruerit, excommunicet et post mensem suspendat ab administratione spiritualium et temporalium. 1261, Oct. 23, Viterbii.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Beauvais. Our venerable brother, the Bishop of Cambrai, has shown to us by complaint that the noble man Engelram, Lord of Coucy in the Diocese of Laon, has unjustly and hostily entered the land of the bishop and the Church of Cambrai, presuming to inflict grave damages and injuries upon the bishop and his people through arson, robbery, and other means. Therefore, the aforementioned bishop humbly supplicated us to provide for him with fatherly concern in this matter. We thus command your fraternity, if it is clear to you without judicial process that these things are so, to compel the aforementioned nobleman, once admonished, to make due satisfaction to the bishop and the aforementioned people for such damages and injuries and to desist completely from inflicting them, by the removal of any appeal and through the sentences of excommunication upon his person and interdict upon his land — notwithstanding any possible apostolic indulgence granted to the nobleman that he cannot be excommunicated or his land subjected to ecclesiastical interdict through apostolic letters that do not make full and express mention of such an indulgence, or any other indulgence of the said see, of which the tenor must be fully and expressly mentioned in our letters and by which the effect of justice in this matter could be impeded or delayed. Given at Orvieto on the Nones of November, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Belvacensi mandat, ut nobili Ingerramo domino de Coziaco, qui in terram episcopi Cameracensis iniuste intravit, iniurias resarcire et ab eis committendis desistere compellat, excommunicationis et interdicti sententia. 1229, Nov. 5, apud Urbemveterem.

Translation to English:

To Master Gualo, our notary, envoy of the Apostolic See. We have learned, though we can scarcely believe it, that the commune of the city of Lucca is fervently negotiating with the vicar in Tuscany of Manfred, former prince of Taranto, about submitting the city to his dominion. Therefore, we will and strictly command you by the authority of these presents, to keep your eyes open and ears attentive in this matter, and if you perceive that they are faltering in the faith of the Roman Church and that such negotiations are to be consummated by them, you should ensure to save and preserve the six thousand marks sterling, which we command to be assigned to you or to your procurator or messenger from our beloved son, Master Milo, our writer and messenger in the kingdoms of France and England for the defense of the said city, in such a way that... 

Given at Urbeveteris, January 25, in the third year of our pontificate.

Regesto in Latin:

Urbanus IV papa magistro Gualoni notario et legato mandat ut, si commune Lucanum cum vicario Manfredi tractatum de subiectione civitatis consumatum sit, sex milia marcarum pro defensione civitatis a magistro Milone sibi assignata salvo custodiat. Datum apud Urbemveterem, VIII Kalendas Februarii, anno tertio.

**Translation to English:**

To Master Raynerius of Viterbo, our chaplain. Having complete trust in your faithfulness and loyalty in the Lord, we assign you the guardianship of our fortress of Orcla by the authority of these presents, to be carried out by you until our will is otherwise. Therefore, we command you to diligently and carefully guard the fortress so that you may be commended by us for your great diligence. Given at Orvieto, on the Nones of April, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Magistro Raynerio de Viterbio capellano nostro custodiam rocce de Orcla committit. 1229, Apr. 5, apud Urbemveterem.

**Translation to English:**

To Everard, cleric, brother of the noble man... count of Irsuti, in the diocese of Worms. Although actions done by our mandate have full firmness in themselves, we willingly strengthen them with apostolic authority to ensure they remain unblemished when fortified by our protection. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, we confirm and strengthen with apostolic authority the arrangement made by our special mandate through our beloved sons H., cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina, and P., cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, concerning the dispute that arose between you and our venerable brother... bishop of Worms, as is more fully contained in their letters drawn up on this matter. We have confirmed it and fortified it with the protection of this present writing, inserting the content of those letters word for word into these presents; which is as follows: By divine mercy, we, brothers Hugo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina, and Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, greet all who will inspect the present letters in the Lord. Between the venerable father... bishop of Worms and Everard, cleric and brother of the noble man... count of Irsuti, a matter of dispute concerning the bishopric of Worms, to which the same E. had been elected, once arose. This dispute was eventually resolved by a certain arrangement through the mediation of the late lord W., king of the Romans, to whom both parties had agreed to submit as arbitrator. Subsequently, our lord Pope Alexander IV, deeming the arrangement invalid due to the inappropriateness of the compromise, nevertheless decreed by the authority of his letters that the terms established in the form of the arrangement, especially since they proceeded with the will of the same bishop who bound himself to it by an oath, should be observed anew. However, when the aforementioned bishop personally approached the apostolic see and, explaining to our lord the modesty of the revenues of the same bishopric, implored grace regarding the moderation of the said arrangement, the same lord verbally charged us to arrange between the same bishop and Everard on these matters as we deemed pious and fitting. Therefore, having carefully considered the state and condition of the parties and desiring to provide for their peace, so that any discord between them may rightly be resolved by our arrangement, we command and ordain, with the special consent of the same bishop intervening in these matters, that the same bishop shall pay one hundred and fifty pounds of the currency of Worms, or of another currency of equivalent value if it should perhaps be changed, annually in Worms at the terms specified below; namely, half of the said one hundred and fifty pounds on the feast of All Saints, and the other half on the Sunday on which "Rejoice, Jerusalem" is sung, to the same E. or his designated messenger, intact and without difficulty, for as long as he lives, and that the said cleric shall be content with this, so that if the same cleric should hold any ecclesiastical benefices or dignities, only so much shall be deducted from the sum of the said one hundred and fifty pounds as he shall annually receive from the fruits of those benefices and dignities. We also decree that if the same bishop should happen to resign or pass away before the death of the same cleric, the said cleric shall be provided for in the aforementioned one hundred and fifty pounds from the goods of the same bishopric by the successors of the same bishop, who will be in office at the time, or by others into whose hands the revenues of the same bishopric shall fall, for as long as he lives. We further add that if the aforesaid bishop should fail in the payment of the same money at the specified terms and places and, when requested by the same E. or his messenger, does not satisfy him fully within three days after such request, he shall be suspended from entering the church by the very fact. Subsequently, our beloved son, Cardinal Hlugol, presbyter of the title of St. Sabina and at that time legate of the apostolic see in those parts, because it was suggested to him that the said Abbot W. had resigned the governance of the said monastery into the hands of the king, and that the king had therefore committed this administration for a certain time to the aforesaid abbot of Fulda, instructed, by his letters, the abbots of St. George and of Billedhausen, that if this were the case, they were to compel the aforementioned Wernher to resign the governance of the said monastery by ecclesiastical censure, and, having received his resignation, to commit the administration of said monastery in spiritual and temporal matters to the said abbot of Fulda until the cardinal or the supreme pontiff decided otherwise. However, the abbots of St. George and Billedhausen, not having investigated these matters, and since nothing had been established, committed the administration of the monastery to the abbot of Fulda. 

Later, when the prior and convent realized that the administration of the monastery could be conducted more conveniently and usefully by Wernher than by another, they reinstated him to the administration. This was then confirmed by both Cardinal Pletril of St. George at the Golden Veil, who was then exercising the office of legation in those parts, and by the authority of our letters. Although Wernher then managed the administration of the monastery peacefully and quietly for over four years after this reinstatement and confirmation, the abbot of Fulda, reportedly with the prior and convent’s instigation, forcibly deprived him of the abbacy of the said monastery, which he had canonically obtained and possessed for some time, without litigation, and he holds it to Wernher's detriment and grievance. 

Since those unjustly stripped should be aided with the remedy of restitution, we command you, having summoned those who must be summoned, to restore the same Wernher to the abbacy as is just, hear the case, and resolve it canonically without appeal. Ensure that justice is observed — notwithstanding any letters obtained from the apostolic see prejudicing truth and justice on the part of another concerning this matter. To the people of Guarcino, of the Diocese of Alatri. It is always fitting to keep in our affections that we preserve the rights of the Roman Church completely intact, and if anything from them is ever taken away, we should promptly strive to restore it to its former state, especially since we are continually vigilant to effectively assist all churches, both collectively and individually, in maintaining their rights. For we, nonetheless, by the authority of these presents, revoke the letters of our said predecessor directed for the same noble to you or to any executor, and any concession made by them or any other letters concerning the aforesaid matters and any other rights pertaining to us and the said church in the aforesaid castle, and we wish them to have no force. Datum Viterbii, III Kalendas Iulii, anno primo.
