To Manfred, elected of Verona, captain and rector of the duchy of Spoleto and the march of Ancona. We have learned that the monastery of St. Victor of Clusis of the order of St. Benedict in the diocese of Camerino is without a pastor. Some monks of this monastery have requested our beloved son Andacondeus of St. Angelo of Monte Nucerino, while others have requested Gratianus of St. Antimo of the same order from the Clusis dioceses to lead the monastery of St. Victor in their discord. Since the land of Clusis, where this monastery of St. Victor is located, is said to align with Manfred, formerly prince of Taranto and a known persecutor of the Roman Church, we have previously, upon the counsel of our brothers, prohibited all chapters, colleges, and convents of churches and monasteries existing in lands adhering to or favoring the aforementioned Manfred from proceeding in any way to provide pastors to these churches and monasteries through election or request when they become vacant, declaring null and void anything attempted against our prohibition. Therefore, it is clear that these requests, made contrary to and after this inhibition, and whatever has followed from or was done because of them, are utterly null and void. We wish and by the authority of these presents command you that, once these requests have been annulled by our authority, rather, declared null and void, you proceed by apostolic authority to provide for the said monastery of St. Victor, so that it does not incur grave spiritual and temporal losses from prolonged vacancy, whether by appointing the aforementioned Andacondeus, whose firm devotion to us and the Roman Church has been laudably attested to us, or another suitable person who is fitting for such responsibility and honor, as you see fit for the good state of the said monastery and the honor of the Church. Ensure that he, whom it happens to be provided for this monastery of St. Victor, is shown due obedience and reverence by the monks and other subjects of this monastery as their father and pastor of their souls; constraining opposers, etc., up to: restraining— notwithstanding any commission made by us in any form to anyone or some concerning the ordination or provision of an abbot for the said monastery of St. Victor or if some persons have been granted by the apostolic see that they cannot be interdicted, suspended, or excommunicated by apostolic letters unless full and express mention is made word for word of such privilege. For we declare null and void whatever may be attempted against the tenor of this our mandate concerning the provision of the said monastery of St. Victor. Given at Urbemvetus, 14th Kalends of April, in the second year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Manfredo Veronensi electo, capitaneo et rectori ducatus Spoletani et marchiae Anconitanae mandat ut, post cassationem postulationum discordantium de abbate monasterii Sancti Victoris de Clusis, provideat de Andacondeo vel alia persona idonea ad regimen monasterii, auctoritate apostolica procedens. Datum apud Urbemveterem, XIV Kalendas Aprilis, anno II.

**Translation to English:**

To Cardinal Priest of the title of St. Cecilia, legate of the Apostolic See. Regarding the affairs of the Kingdom of Sicily and the Senate of the city of Rome, which are conducted between the Roman Church and our beloved son, the noble man Charles, Count of Anjou and Provence, we have recently defined, among our brothers whose counsel we had sought on these matters, in this form: "Urban, bishop, servant of the servants of God, for the perpetual memory of the matter. Jeremiah says etc. as in the previous part until the end." Therefore, since we have full confidence in the Lord in your discretion, circumspection, and diligence, we send you to the Kingdom of France for these affairs, with the full office of legation entrusted to you upon the counsel of our brothers. We grant you full authority by these presents to act and promise concerning the aforesaid matters, as contained in the definition we delivered to you under our seal, with the form and tenor of that definition to be observed. Let no one therefore violate our concession, etc. Given at Orvieto, on the 6th day before the Nones of May, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Urbanus IV papa Cardinali presbytero tituli Sancte Cecilie, legato apostolico, plenam auctoritatem concedit agendi promittendique super negotiis regni Sicilie et senatus Urbis cum Carolo Andegavensi, secundum formam diffinitionis sub bulla traditae. Datum apud Urbemveterem, II Nonas Maii, anno tertio.

**English Translation:**

To the bishops of Prague and Olomouc. Since it is necessary for one singular and distinguished leader to preside for the sustenance of many and governance, as plurality in leadership would induce division and disrupt the firm governance, there are singular thrones of rulers and singular powers of leaders for each kingdom and province of the world. For when kings command the people and the people respectfully heed the kings, when these serve humbly and those lead kindly, when these lead with suitable commands and those obey with devoted minds, there thrives among these people a harmonious unity of minds, mercy and truth meet together, and justice and peace embrace each other. Therefore, temporal power of the sword has been given by that supreme king, through whom individual kings reign and princes govern, to earthly kings for the punishment of evildoers and the praise of the good, so that having taken up the duty of ruling, they may judge the people with equity and direct the nations subject to them in righteousness, so that their will may be in the execution of justice, their meditation in the law of uprightness, and their observance in holy peace. To exercise these duties more perfectly, these kings receive the gift of a greater grace through the virtue of sacred unction, which they receive according to ancient custom through the venerable ministers of Christ, so that they may be strengthened in the pursuit of just governance and be directed both in themselves and in their subjects with a wiser and holier spirit. For although the unction of a prince differs from that of a pontiff, as the pontiff is anointed on the head, while the prince is anointed on the arm or shoulder, where authority is fittingly designated, because the pontiff’s head is consecrated with chrism, yet the arm of the prince is anointed with oil, there is a powerful efficacy of this sacrament in the kings themselves, as when Saul was anointed, the Spirit of the Lord came upon him and he was changed into another man, and when David received the unction, the Spirit of the Lord guided him. Furthermore, to signify that kings should possess fullness of virtues and that in them is complete authority of temporal dominion, an honorable and venerable diadem is placed upon the head of the prince in a circular form; from this prince, thus adorned and distinguished with such insignia and titles, as from a head, a mode of right living is prescribed to the subjects as to members, and a rule of moderation is set and dictated. Truly, our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of Bohemia, a most devoted son of the Church, diligently considering the above like a Catholic prince and hoping to be enriched by the dew of spiritual grace through such unction, humbly supplicated us that, since his predecessors, the Kings of Bohemia, were anointed and crowned as kings by the Archbishops of Mainz, who were at the time, and since he cannot be anointed and crowned by the beloved son, the Archbishop-elect of Mainz, because his election has not yet been confirmed by the Apostolic See, we should arrange for him to be anointed as king and have the royal diadem placed upon his head. We, therefore, considering the manifold devotion of the said king and recognizing that he succeeds his ancestors, who were zealous champions of the Catholic faith, not only by bloodline but also by imitation of purity and goodness, and wishing, on this account, to honor him specially in these matters, being graciously inclined to his supplications, we command your fraternity that you or one of you, with a suitable number of bishops attending, both for the king's honor and out of reverence for the sacrament, take care to anoint him with such unction by our authority and place the royal diadem on his head. Moreover, we will and ordain that nothing shall hereafter prejudice the Archbishops of Mainz and the Church of Mainz, who will be at the time, in that they may freely undertake what pertains to them regarding the successors of the said king in this matter. What the said king would have presented to the Archbishop of Mainz, if he were to anoint and crown him, you shall receive in full from the same king, faithfully transmitting it to the said elect, should he happen to be confirmed, or otherwise to him who will preside over the governance of the said Church of Mainz. Given at Anagni, on the 4th of October, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopis Pragensi et Olomucensi mandat, ut regem Boemiae auctoritate apostolica inungant et coronent, servato honore archiepiscoporum Maguntinorum. Dat. Anagnie, II Non. Oct., anno sexto (1232, Oct. 4).

Translation to English:

For the perpetual memory of the matter. Recently, we instructed the noble man Peter de Vico through our letters to ensure that the castles of Blede and Civitatis Veteris, along with other goods formerly belonging to Peter, the Prefect of the City, which are known to pertain to the right and property of the Roman Church, and which the same nobleman unjustly occupied after the death of the said Prefect, be delivered and assigned to us and our envoy within eight days after the receipt of the said letters. Otherwise, he was to appear before us, either personally or through an appropriate procurator, within fifteen days following those eight days, to show the rights he claims in the said castles and goods and to receive what justice would advise in these matters.

However, since Peter did not care to hand over the castles and goods to us or the said envoy, Bonus John, his familiar and procurator, appeared before us at the appointed time and, among other things, proposed before us that since the nobleman himself was a Roman citizen, he was not obliged to litigate these matters at the Apostolic See. Nevertheless, when we assigned another date to Bonus John for these matters, he, having been awaited for a long time and repeatedly summoned in public audience, did not appear before us.

Moreover, so that the truth in the aforementioned matters might not be concealed through any subterfuge, we decreed, by way of interlocution, that the same nobleman — notwithstanding this — should submit to our jurisdiction in these matters and that proofs for the aforementioned Church should be admitted concerning the castles and goods. Nonetheless, to overcome the malice of the nobleman, we commanded through our letters that he be summoned again, to appear before us on a certain day, either personally, if he wished, or otherwise through an adequately instructed procurator with all his instruments, reasons, and rights, to explain the right he claims to have in the premises, to see the rights of the Church, to inspect its legitimate proofs, and finally to hear the sentence.

Indeed, when the said procurator of the aforementioned Peter appeared before us, and the procurator specially appointed by us requested in the name of the Roman Church that the matter proceed, on behalf of the same nobleman it was requested that a libellus be presented to his aforementioned procurator and that the solemn and usual order of judgments be observed in the case itself. Therefore, we, considering that the aforementioned castles and goods are part of the patrimony of the aforementioned Church, and recognizing that we who are debtors to all in justice must render to each their due right, so that the same Church is not harmed in its rights, and that we are bound to maintain and preserve these rights so that we do not do injury to anyone, considering also the commendable custom of the Roman Church, which has been observed by our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs, in such past times: we decree, with the counsel of our brothers, that the matter should proceed by way of inquisition from our office, bypassing the presentation of a libellus and the solemnities of such judgments, and that the rights of both the Church and the aforementioned nobleman should be diligently investigated. After these rights have been inquired into, seen, understood, and fully discussed, we will, with the Lord's guidance, proceed to pronounce or judge upon these matters as justice, fully understanding the rights and reasons of both the Church and the aforementioned nobleman, shall direct.

Given at Urbemveterem, VIII Kalends of May, in the second year.

Regesto:

Innocentius IV papa Petro de Vico mandat restitutionem castrorum Blede et Civitatis Veteris et bonorum quondam Petri prefecti Urbis ad ius ecclesiae Romanae pertinentium curare, et si non, coram se comparere iussit. Dat. apud Urbemveterem, VIII Kal. Mai., anno secundo.

**Translation to English:**

To the venerable brothers, archbishops and bishops, and the beloved sons, abbots, priors, provosts, deans, archdeacons, archpriests, or parish priests, and other prelates of churches and their chapters and convents, exempt and non-exempt, of the Cistercian, Cluniac, Premonstratensian, Saint Benedict, Saint Augustine, and other orders, as well as the masters and preceptors of the houses of the Knights Templar and the Hospital of Saint John of Jerusalem, Calatrava, and Velez, to whom etc.

Since we are sending our beloved son, Master Albert of Parma, our secretary, in whom we and our brothers fully trust for his known faith and discretion, to various parts of Gaul, Germany, England, Scotland, and Spain for certain affairs of the Roman Church and the aforementioned brothers, we earnestly ask and exhort your community, through apostolic writings commanding you, to kindly receive and treat the said master with three horsemen and four of his household, when he passes through your places, for the reverence of us and the Apostolic See, and to make sure that he is honestly and liberally provided for in his needs or those of his companions, if, due to the situation of place or time, he prefers, with twenty sous of Tours each day and also with safe conduct in going, staying, and even returning. 

However, if the same master must stay in any place for a longer time, so that the churches of that place are not overly burdened for his and his companions' needs, or he himself is not forced to endure loss or shortage, each other church of the neighboring places should supply such needs, when requested by him, in the aforementioned amount of money, so that the provision for each day does not exceed the said sum, and the number of provisions, whether in victuals or money, does not exceed the number of days he stays or travels.

And lest he demand or receive anything in money or clothes or any goods from anyone beyond or besides that under any pretext or manner, or anything be given to him or any of his household or anyone on his behalf or theirs by anyone, or offered under the guise of any gift, we strictly forbid it, unless perhaps it happens that one of the aforementioned number of horsemen is deficient or hindered for some reason; and then in such necessity, those who are asked by him are bound to assist with the suitable supplement of the same number without any difficulty, and the same master is to provide his open letters to the one assisting, by which it may appear that he has received such a horseman; otherwise, the one requested shall not be bound to give him such a horseman at all.

You shall fulfill our command in such a way that when the same master returns to us, he may be able to report favorably and pleasingly about you to us, and we may, therefore, deservedly commend your sincerity. Otherwise, we will consider the sentence he pronounces against the rebellious as ratified and, with the Lord as our witness, will have it inviolably observed until full satisfaction is rendered, appeal being removed—notwithstanding if it has been granted by the Apostolic See to anyone that they are not bound to provide or contribute any provision to the legates or envoys of the same See, or that they cannot be interdicted, suspended, or excommunicated by apostolic letters, which do not make full and express mention of such a grant and its entire tenor, or any privileges or indulgences granted by the Apostolic See to any persons, places, or orders under whatever form of words, of which and their entire tenors it is necessary to make full and express mention in our letters, and by which it might in any way be hindered.

Given at Viterbo, the fifth day before the Kalends of November, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa universitatem archiepiscoporum, episcoporum, abbatum ac militum ordinis Templi et Hospitalis rogans mandat ut Albertum de Parma, scriptorem suum, in iter ad Galliam, Germaniam, Angliam, Scotiam, et Hispaniam destinatum, benigne suscipiant et ei necessaria annua viginti solidis Turonensium cottidie provideant, prohibens ne ultra id quicquam exigat. Dat. Viterbii, V Kal. Novembr., anno primo.

**Translation to English:**

To the presbyter cardinal of the title of Saint Cecilia, legate of the apostolic see. Since in our definition, which we recently issued among our brothers regarding the affairs of the Kingdom of Sicily and the Senate of Rome, and which we handed to you sealed, it is explicitly stated that authority should be granted to you by us concerning the modifications requested on behalf of our beloved son, the noble man Charles of Anjou, Count of Provence, and since we have determined that these modifications should be included in our other letters, we grant to your discretion, in which we have full confidence in the Lord, full and free authority by these presents to proceed freely to make those modifications with the counsel of our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King Louis of France, as you see fit for the honor of the Roman Church and ours, and for the successful promotion of the business entrusted to you. 

Given at Orvieto, on the Nones of May, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa S. tituli Sancte Cecilie presbytero cardinali, apostolice sedis legato, potestatem plenam ac liberam concedit ad modificationes pro regno Sicilie cum consilio regis Francorum faciendas. 1239, Mai. 7, apud Urbemveterem.

**Translation to English:**

To Louis, dean of Mainz and our chaplain. If the most holy law of Christ, according to the Apostle, is fulfilled in this: that each should strive to bear one another's burdens, it is fitting and worthy that the needs of prelates should be relieved by the support of their subjects, especially since nature itself dictates that members should sympathize with the suffering head. Our venerable brother, the archbishop of Mainz, has informed us that the Church of Mainz, both because it has stood faithfully and powerfully alongside the Roman Church against the former emperor Frederick, and because it has endured hostile incursions for a long time, is so diminished in its temporal revenues and goods and is burdened with such debts that unless aid is swiftly provided, it can scarcely hope to recover, with the voracity of usury consuming a large part of its remaining goods and revenues. Therefore, the said archbishop has humbly requested us to ensure that at least a thousand marks of silver, which he owes to us and the Roman Church, be provided for him and the Church of Mainz by their subjects. Hence, we, moved by a paternal feeling of compassion towards the same archbishop and Church of Mainz, command you by apostolic writings — in whose diligence we have special confidence — to impose these thousand marks on the monasteries and churches of the city and diocese of Mainz under the authority of our archbishop, collecting from each what you impose according to their means, either by yourself or through another trustworthy person. Whatever is collected should be deposited intact in the house of the Hospital of Saint Mary of the Germans in Mainz in the name of us and the Roman Church, in the presence of sufficient witnesses, not omitting to restrain objectors by censuring them, etc., notwithstanding any indulgence granted by the Apostolic See that might exempt someone from being compelled to such contributions or from being suspended, interdicted, or excommunicated, or any other indulgence of the same See that might impede or delay the execution of our mandate on these matters, and which should be mentioned word for word in our letters. Moreover, diligently and prudently considering that we chose to entrust you with this business above many others who are faithful and devoted to us, carry it out wisely and faithfully, so that no suspicion or detraction may arise against you over time, but rather that your diligence might be commended. You should also inform us as soon as possible, with open letters bearing your seal and that of the master of the aforementioned house, of the amount of money deposited, when, and before whom. We wish you to receive whatever is collected under your or your delegates' or envoys' authority in the presence of two or three trustworthy persons and to provide your open letters sealed with your and these persons' seals, stating where, when, and how much you have received from each, to the individuals and places that give you these funds. Otherwise, no one is obliged to pay you or your delegate or envoy anything of the above-mentioned money; by such letters granted to the persons and places, the truth of which we will diligently make inquiries through our envoy coming to Germany, more certain and clearer assurance will be provided to them. Given at Orvieto, 22nd November, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Lodevico decano Maguntino mandat ut mille marcas argenti a fidelibus ecclesiae et monasteriis Maguntinis colligat et ad domum hospitalis sancte Marie Theutonicorum in Maguncia deponat, ut ecclesiae Maguntine debita allevientur. 1239, Nov. 22. Apud Urbemveterem.

**Translation to English:**

To Ludwig, dean of Mainz, our chaplain. Our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Mainz, has informed us that although several of his predecessors, who held the position in times past, collected tolls and duties from certain castles and the church of Mainz, he himself, after collecting these for some years, has carefully considered that these tolls and duties have caused great scandal in the surrounding region. He fears that the imposition of these, which he suspects to be newly established, caused him to fall under the penalty of an enacted canon, thus accumulating sins daily. To pacify his conscience, remove the scandal from those parts, and out of reverence for God and the Apostolic See, which rejects and abhors such unjust exactions, he has relinquished these tolls and duties. Therefore, he humbly requested us to mercifully provide him, the clerics, and the laity who participated in or otherwise communicated with him during this period, and clerics who received benefices and orders from him, with the benefit of appropriate absolution and dispensation. Therefore, acknowledging the pious and prudent consideration of the archbishop, which is pleasing to God and us, and desired by many faithful of the aforementioned region, we commend you, in whom we have special confidence in the Lord due to your discretion, with the tenor of these presents. If the said archbishop has thus relinquished these tolls and duties, upon receiving an oath from him or another on his behalf, that he will not exact nor cause them to be exacted in the future, you shall absolve him and the aforementioned persons, when requested by them, from the sentences of excommunication they have incurred on account of the aforesaid matters, by our authority and according to the form of the Church. You shall also dispense with them concerning any irregularity they are known to have incurred due to this, imposing upon them suitable penance for their salvation, as you deem appropriate for the health of their souls according to God. Furthermore, grant the same clerics that they may serve in the orders thus received and retain such benefices, provided nothing else canonical obstructs this. Given at Orvieto, on the Ides of March, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Ludeguico decano Maguntino mandat, ut, si archiepiscopus Maguntinus thelonea et pedagia remiserit, eum et alios a sententiis excommunicationum absolvat et super irregularitate dispenset. Dat. apud Urbemveterem, Idibus Martii, anno tertio.

Translation to English:

To Master Guala, our notary, legate of the Apostolic See. On behalf of our venerable brother, the Bishop of Pavia, and our beloved sons, the clergy of the city and diocese of Pavia, it was presented to us that the Church of Pavia had been afflicted with many troubles by the late Emperor Frederick and his officials. The clergy at times paid the greater part of their revenues, and sometimes six thousand pounds of Pavia currency annually, with much heartache. Later, when Ubertus, Margrave Pelavicini, presided over the same city, he extorted four thousand pounds of the same currency annually from the clergy. Because of these extortions, some of the clergy were forced to sell their movable and immovable goods, even the tiles of their churches. Indeed, when that one who, after the storm, gives calm and after cloudiness gives serene, brought the city back to the devotion of the Apostolic See, the bishop and clergy hoped to live quietly under its protection. But they are severely burdened by the legates and envoys of the said See in the provisions to be given to them. For you, as they claim, imposed three hundred pounds of the said currency in the first year of your legation, and as much in the second, upon the bishop and clergy, which they paid you liberally. Nevertheless, you now demand from the bishop and clergy two hundred pounds of the said currency. Therefore, they humbly implored us to provide for them with paternal care in this matter. We, therefore, compassionately sympathizing with them with paternal affection for the afflictions they suffered from the aforementioned Frederick and Margrave, wish you to be content with the sum of one hundred pounds of the two hundred pounds you demand from them. For, once they have paid you that amount, we have decided to absolve them from the remainder. We therefore command that, once you have received these hundred pounds from them, you do not trouble them about the rest, and that you release any sentences of excommunication, suspension, or interdict that you or someone else may have pronounced against them or their churches due to the aforementioned two hundred pounds, without any difficulty. Otherwise, we give a mandate through our letters to our beloved son, the prior of the Dominican Friars of Pavia, that after the bishop and clergy have paid you or your agent or messenger the said one hundred pounds, he should, with the removal of any obstacle of difficulty, strive to release these sentences by our authority. Given at Orvieto, on the Nones of February, in the third year.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa Magistro Guale notario, apostolicae sedis legato, mandat ut pro ducentis libris a clero Papiae requisitis contentus existat centum libris solvendis, et absolvat episcopum et clerum a reliquo, necnon relaxet sententias excommunicationis, si quae sunt latae. 1230, Feb. 5, apud Urbemveterem.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Liège. The excessively unrestrained audacity of the citizens of Cologne, if the reports are true, has not only disregarded the debt of fidelity they owe to the Archbishop and the Church of Cologne. They have presumed to detain him in strict custody. When this reached your knowledge, you, showing due compassion to your metropolitan archbishop, personally traveled to Cologne. There, with our venerable brother, the Bishop of Münster, and the noblemen, the Counts of Cleves and Geldern, along with many others assembled, you exerted diligent efforts towards the liberation of the same archbishop. However, the obstinacy of the wrongdoers could not be softened or turned by any means until the archbishop himself swore an oath that neither he nor anyone else on his behalf would lodge a complaint against them or inflict or cause to be inflicted any harm upon them due to this, and he would even work faithfully for their absolution. Furthermore, you, the bishop and the aforementioned nobles, and others were also compelled by necessity to swear that if the aforesaid archbishop did not keep what he had promised under oath, you would support those same citizens against him with all your might, obligating yourselves to this with your open letters and other guarantees; for which the Lord of Falkenberg is said to have similarly obligated himself. We, who are concerned with the offenses and wrongs of our brothers and co-bishops until... absolved. Hence, since it is clear that the archbishop is permitted to proceed according to the prescribed form to pursue this right, it would be unlawful for you, the aforementioned bishop and nobles, to support the sacrilegious people against the said archbishop pursuing this right under the pretext of the oaths, guarantees, and obligations made by you. We, wishing to specially provide salutary counsel to the aforementioned Church of Cologne and likewise to you, have decided that you, the bishop, and the aforementioned nobles, should be absolved from the oaths you made — and with the same authority, we annul and declare void the aforementioned guarantees and obligations — so that you may not be bound to support the aforementioned citizens against the said archbishop in these matters. We further strictly prohibit you and the same bishop and nobles, under penalty of excommunication, from presuming to support the same citizens in these matters in any way. Given as above.

---

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Leodiensi mandat, ne ipse episcopus ac episcopus Monasteriensis et comites Clevensis et Gellerensis iuramentis, cautionibus et obligationibus civibus Coloniensibus contra archiepiscopum Coloniensem datis, obtemperent, sed ab eis absolvuntur, et districte prohibentur sub pena excommunicationis, ne eisdem civibus in premissis assistant. Datum ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the Master and brothers of the Hospital of Saint Mary of the Teutons of Jerusalem. It is fitting that we provide assistance to prevent religious places or any other spaces dedicated to divine worship, which we perceive have fallen into a detestable decline or ruin displeasing to God and men, from complete destruction, and that they may achieve the effect of pious restoration with divine help. Indeed, on behalf of the beloved sons, the canons of the church of Saint Leonard of Lamabolaria, which directly belongs to the Roman Church and follows the order of Saint Augustine in the diocese of Siponto, it was previously presented before us that although this church of Saint Leonard, while vacant of a prior, used to flourish in spiritual and temporal matters from ancient times, it has been known to have fallen into such a state due to the malice of the times and the incursions of the Saracens from Lucera, which is nearby, and also due to the neglect of some priors who were in charge, that there is no hope that it can rise by itself. For this reason, the aforementioned canons previously petitioned us that since you are intent on observing regular discipline and pious works and are endowed with such power in those parts that the said church of Saint Leonard can soon be restored to a healthy state through your brothers stationed there, we should take care to reform it by incorporating it into the order of your hospital and committing its governance to the brothers of the said order in perpetuity. Since we could not then be certain of the premises, we, relying on the discretion of our venerable brother.. the bishop of Melfi and our beloved son.. the prior of the brothers of the Dominican order of Barletta in the diocese of Trani, directed our letters to them, instructing them to personally go to the place and diligently investigate the truth concerning both the exemption of the church of Saint Leonard and the other aforementioned matters and their circumstances, and to faithfully report their findings to us by their letters. Now, as we have received from their letters, the said bishop and prior personally went to the place and, after carefully examining several privileges of the Apostolic See, found concerning the aforesaid church that it is directly subject to the said See and is so enormously deformed in spiritual and temporal matters that it is no longer called a house or hall of God but is considered by almost everyone as a den of thieves; it sits miserable, despised, stripped of riches, and lacking servants and ministers, and it has no possibility or capacity to assume the robe of joy and the adornment of its ancient state, having cast off the reproach of desolation and the garment of sadness, unless this comes to it by the kindness of the said See. Therefore, on behalf of the said canons, it has been humbly requested of us, as once and again, that applying a salutary remedy to the great deformation of the church, we would mercifully take care to provide for the reformation, union, and commission as mentioned. Therefore, led by firm confidence that the same church will by your prudent discretion and careful diligence and by that of your brothers soon resume a praiseworthy and happy state with God's favor, we have decided by the authority of these presents to unite it with its rights and appurtenances to your order in perpetuity to achieve such reformation, ordaining that it shall always be subject to the governance of the brothers of the same order and be governed by them in all things and through all, and that it shall be liable to the Roman Church for an annual census of one ounce of gold as a sign of exemption, as it once was; provided that you supply the necessary means of life to the same canons, if they conduct themselves regularly and honorably, for as long as they live, and that no substitution from the order of the said canons shall be made in the aforementioned church after their death, but that you shall establish there as soon as possible a suitable college from the brothers of your order for the service of divine praise. Let no one infringe upon our union and constitution etc. Given at the Lateran, on the 6th day before the Kalends of December, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa magistro et fratribus Hospitalis Sanctae Mariae Theutonicorum Hierosolymitanae mandat ut ecclesiam Sancti Leonardi de Lamabolaria, propter lapsum et incursum Sarracenorum collapsam, ad ordinem eorum in perpetuum uniant et reformandam curent. 1232, Nov. 26, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the Cardinal Priest of the title of St. Cecilia, legate of the Apostolic See. Since the advancement of the affairs of the Holy Land and the Empire of Constantinople is known to largely depend on the affairs of the Kingdom of Sicily, we, considering that the liberation of both the land and the empire will be easier if the business of that same kingdom is effectively promoted by God's favor, grant to your discretion, in which we have full confidence in the Lord, the full and free power by the authority of these presents to absolve our beloved son, the noble man Alphonse, Count of Poitiers and Toulouse, from the vow of the cross which he is said to have taken for the aid of the said land, and to commute it to the assumption and execution of the business of that same kingdom. For we wish that the same count, with such a commutation of the vow, enjoy that indulgence and that privilege and immunity which have been granted to those aiding the aforesaid land in the general council. Since the promotion of such a great matter requires a person whose diligence, exceptional prudence, and considerable experience match its magnitude, we have appointed you, possessing full and firm confidence in your circumspection, industry, and maturity among our other brothers, the cardinals of the Roman Church, as our special envoy to the Kingdom of France for this matter. Gregorius IX papa universis Christi fidelibus communicat, plenam potestatem magistri Egidii camerarii ad exigendum et recipiendum redditus et debita Manfredi Veronensis electi, captivati ab hostibus ecclesiae, concedens. Dat. apud Urbemveterem, II Kalendas Iulii, anno pontificatus tertio.

**Translation to English:**

Innocent, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the noble duke and the commune of the Venetians, greetings and apostolic blessing. By the disposition of divine counsel, it is often provided that scandals arise in the kingdom of the church, so that those who have been tested may become manifest among the reproved, as indeed the unfaithful and the reproved receive deserved punishment, while the faithful and the elect obtain worthy rewards, each receiving different rewards according to their merits. For your devotion has been proven in necessity, in which the devout are tested, so that you are deservedly considered not just devout but especially as sons of the church, who, during the time of trouble, have shown yourselves stable in faith and effective in action, resisting the enemies of the church out of devotion to it. We, wishing to show you grace and favor for this, want you to know that if it happens that the Roman church comes to peace with the noble man Conrad, son of the late Frederick, the former emperor, we will expressly include you in that peace, if we are requested by you at that time. Given at Perugia, the Ides of August, in the tenth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa duci et communi Venetorum nuntiat se, si pax inter ecclesiam Romanam et Conradum filium Friderici quondam imperatoris fiat, Venetos in ea nominare, si ex parte Venetorum requisitus fuerit. 1253, Aug. 13. Perusiae.

Translation to English:

For the perpetual remembrance of the matter. Since our beloved son Manfred, the elected of Verona, has been captured by the enemies of the Church and is held in harsh imprisonment, we, justifiably fearing that should this elected one happen to die in the said prisons, which God forbid, or possibly resign from the governance of the Veronese Church, some person suspected by the Roman Church might be appointed to the governance of the same Veronese Church, and wishing to provide healthily in this regard, we reserve the provision of the said Veronese Church to ourselves this time by apostolic authority, should it become vacant through his resignation or death or in any other way whatsoever. We prohibit the beloved sons of the Veronese chapter from presuming to proceed to the election, nomination, or petition for a pastor in any way while the said Veronese Church is vacant, and declare null and void whatever might be attempted by them or by anyone else against the tenor of our reservation and inhibition. Let no one therefore violate our reservation, prohibition, and constitution, etc. Given at Orvieto, September 8, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa provisionem ecclesiae Veronensis, si vacaverit, sibi reservat et capitulo Veronensi prohibet ne ad electionem pastoris procedant. 1230, Sept. 8, apud Urbemveterem.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man William of Massa in the diocese of Fermo, the spirit of sound counsel. We have heard that you are holding in chains the noble man Maynard, Count of Panigo, a devoted servant of the Roman Church, who, while valiantly fighting against its enemies, occupiers of the March, was captured by an adverse fate. However, if you were to consider carefully and with appropriate attention, you would note that by this detention you are violating the duty of loyalty you owe to the same Roman Church. You involve yourself in serious danger to your soul, infamy, and many transgressions. You would not wait for us to admonish you regarding his release but would instead anticipate our admonitions in this matter. Since the release of the aforementioned count is highly desired by us and our brothers, we strictly command under the aforementioned obligation of loyalty and under penalty of all goods you hold from the same Church in the aforementioned March or elsewhere, which penalty you will incur automatically if you neglect to fulfill our command in this matter, that you release the named count, captured in service of the aforementioned Church as stated, from his chains and allow him to freely return to his liberty within eight days after receiving these presents. Given at Perugia, on the seventh day before the Kalends of March, in the first year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro Guillelmo de Massa mandat, ut Maynardum comitem de Panigo, captum dum in servitio ecclesie Romane decertabat, infra octo dies absolutum a vinculis libertati restituat. 1228, Feb. 23. Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To the authorities, council, and community of the castle of Ripatransone in the diocese of Fermo. When a request is made to us, etc., up to: effect. Truly, your petition presented to us contained that our beloved son Simon, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Martin, then rector of the March of Ancona and legate of the apostolic see in those regions, considering the devotion you bear towards the Roman Church and that you resisted the undevoted citizens of Fermo to the best of your ability, and that you suffered many damages and personal losses from those citizens on account of this devotion, out of special grace absolved you and your castle, as well as individual persons of that castle, from all condemnations, bans, fines, and sentences which you incurred by reason of rebellion against the same church by supporting the late Manfred, formerly prince of Taranto, or on account of any warning or even the castle of Marano, decreeing that you should never at any time be held liable for the payment of such bans, penalties, fines, and condemnations, as is more fully contained in the letters drawn up and sealed with the seal of the same cardinal. Therefore, we, inclined by your supplications, affirm and ratify what was done in this matter by the same cardinal, confirming it by apostolic authority and strengthening it with the support of this present writing. Let no one therefore — of our confirmation, etc. Given at Viterbo, 27 February, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa potestati, consilio et communi castri Ripetransonis Firmane diocesis significat se absolutionem et decreta ab Slimone, tituli Sancti Martini presbytero cardinali, concessa confirmasse; mandat ut nulla condemnpnationum, bannorum, mulctarum obligatione teneantur. 1257, Febr. 27, Viterbii.

**Translation to English:**

To S., cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia, legate of the apostolic see. Since the promotion of the affairs of the Holy Land and the Empire of Constantinople is known to depend largely on the affairs of the Kingdom of Sicily, and considering that the liberation of both the land and the empire will be easier if the affairs of this kingdom are effectively promoted with God's favor, we grant to your discretion, in which we have full confidence in the Lord, the authority to absolve, by yourself or through another, all those from the Kingdom of France and other lands under your legation who have taken or will take the vow of the cross to aid the aforesaid land, from such a vow, and to convert it to undertake and execute the aforementioned affairs of the Kingdom of Sicily, with full and free authority, similar to that granted by our predecessor Pope Urban of happy memory. We add that you may proceed to such absolution and conversion notwithstanding the oath by which such individuals are said to have bound themselves to cross over within a certain term to aid the aforesaid land. For we desire that those who have thus had their vows converted shall enjoy the same indulgence, privilege, and immunity that were granted in the general council to those aiding the aforesaid land. Given at Perugia, on the Nones of March, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa S. tituli Sancte Cecilie presbytero cardinali legato concedit potestatem absolvendi et commutandi vota crucesignatorum de regno Francie et aliis terris ad negotium regni Sicilie, cum indulgentiis et privilegiis eis concessis. 1227, Perusii, Nonis Martii.

**Translation to English:**

To O., Cardinal Deacon of St. Adrian, legate of the Apostolic See. As we send you to the provinces of Mainz, Trier, and Cologne, fully entrusting to you the office of legation for great and arduous affairs therein, we gladly endow you with the power which we consider useful and effective for the accomplishment of the duties committed to your care. Therefore, wishing that you be held in the greater esteem in the aforesaid provinces, as you will be able to bestow greater favors upon their inhabitants, we grant you the full authority, by the power of these presents, to dispense two noble persons from those provinces, so that they may, notwithstanding the impediment of the fourth degree of consanguinity, either contract marriages or lawfully remain in marriages already contracted, provided they assume the cross and pursue the affairs for which you are sent, as you shall see fit according to the prudence granted to you by God. Given at Perugia, on the 13th of May, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa O. Sancti Adriani diacono cardinali, apostolicae sedis legato mandat plenam facultatem dispensandi cum duabus personis nobilibus provinciarum Maguntinensis, Treverensis et Coloniensis, ut, impedimento quarto consanguinitatis gradu non obstante, matrimonia contrahere vel in contractis remanere possint, si crucem assumpserint et negotia pro quibus mittitur prosequantur. 1227, Mai. 13, Perusii.

**Translation to English:**

To the Podestà, council, and commune of Orte, our faithful. Since the army of that tyrant, the principal persecutor of the Church, Manfred, the so-called former prince of Taranto, intends, as we have learned, to proceed through your regions towards other lands of the Church closer to you to the detriment of the Roman Church and its faithful, we, considering the merits of your ancient fidelity, confidently hope and trust in you that you will stand firmly for the Church, for freedom, for your country against enemies and will set your faces steadfastly against the aforementioned Manfred, who is disturbing the Church these days with the pestilent breath of his iniquity, we earnestly admonish, request, and exhort your community, through apostolic writings, under the debt of fidelity which you owe to us and the aforesaid Church, strictly ordering that you might resist mightily and openly, since by God’s grace you have the ability to do so, and not allow that army or any of Manfred’s soldiers to pass through the said regions. Behold, we have decided to send to you our beloved son, Master Claudius of the City, our chaplain, a man indeed prudent and discreet and multiply gracious in our eyes and those of our brethren, to whom you should humbly and effectively heed his warnings and commands, so that we may justly commend the promptness of your devotion with due praises in the Lord and pursue the zeal of your faith with deserved thanks. Given at Orvieto, 10th July, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa potestati, consilio et communi Ortanis mandat, ut exercitui Manfredi non permittant per partes suas transire, et ad hoc gerendum magistro Claudio de Urbe mittit. 1255, Iul. 10, apud Urbemveterem.

Translation to English:

Alexander, Bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons, the preceptor and brothers of the Hospital of Saint Mary of the Teutons in Bolzano and Legemmo, of the Diocese of Trent, greetings and apostolic blessing. When a request is made to us that is just and honorable, both the force of equity and the order of reason demand that it be carried into due effect through the diligence of our office. Your petition, indeed, presented to us, contained that the late Frederick, Emperor of the Romans, before the sentence of deposition was pronounced against him, granted to you with pious and prudent liberality the right of patronage over the church of Slanders in the Diocese of Chur, which then belonged to him, as is more fully stated in a public instrument drawn up regarding this matter. We, therefore, inclined by your supplications and holding what was prudently done by the same Frederick in this matter as valid and firm, confirm it by apostolic authority and fortify it with the protection of this present writing. Therefore, let no one at all infringe upon this page of our confirmation, etc., under penalty of incurring the stated consequence. Given at Viterbo, the 9th of November, in the third year of our pontificate.

Regesto in Latin:

Alexander papa preceptori et fratribus hospitalis sancte Marie Theotonicorum in Bozano et Legemmos Tridentine diocesis confirmat ius patronatus ecclesie de Slandres Curiensis diocesis, quod Fredericus imperator eis donaverat, auctoritate apostolica. 1255, Nov. 9, Viterbii.

**Translation to English:**

To the Cardinal Priest of the title of St. Martin, legate of the Apostolic See. Formerly, Pope Urban of happy memory, our predecessor, entrusted the governance of the Duchy of Spoleto, the March of Ancona, and the cities and dioceses of Massa Trabaria, Perugia, and Castellan with their districts, both in spiritual and temporal matters, to your discernment with apostolic authority. He granted you the free power to exercise there whatever you deemed to be for the honor of the Roman Church and the benefit of the faithful residing in the aforementioned places, regarding both spiritual and temporal matters. Moreover, in the duchy, march, cities, dioceses, and districts mentioned above, as well as in Romagna, the patriarchates of Grado and Aquileia, except those cities and their dioceses and districts which are part of the province of Lombardy, he decided to commit the full office of legation to your care. He also granted you several special privileges and entrusted many other matters to your care, as is more fully contained in the letters of the same predecessor. Therefore, we, confident in the industry of your sincerity in the Lord, and having considered as valid and firm what was done concerning these matters by the same predecessor and approving it with similar authority, grant you free power by the tenor of these presents to freely pursue these commissions, utilizing the aforementioned concessions and privileges according to the tenor of the aforementioned letters of the same predecessor. Given at Perugia, 11 March, in the first year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa S. tituli Sancti Martini presbytero cardinali, apostolicae sedis legato, facultatem confirmat prosequendi commissiones et gratias a predecessor suo Urbano papa concessas in ducatu Spoletano, marchia Anconitana et aliis locis. 1227, Mar. 11, Perusia.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Luni. You have informed us that the people of the castles and villages belonging to the see of Luni incurred the sentence of excommunication pronounced by the apostolic see because they showed favor to the late Manfred, formerly prince of Taranto, and his supporters. Indeed, when the late Bernard, marquis Malaspina, who acted as Manfred's vicar in those parts, forcibly occupied those castles and villages, the noble men Isnard, brother, and Jacob, son and heir of the marquis, after his removal, presumed to transfer some of those castles and villages into the power and commune of Pisa, de facto, even though they could not do so legally. Thus, the said power and commune unjustly hold those places occupied, to your prejudice and significant detriment of the same see of Luni. However, because we have recently caused the power and commune and the men of their district to be absolved from the sentence pronounced by the apostolic see against them for having attacked the city of Lucca and for other offenses, the aforementioned men of the castles and villages belonging to the same see of Luni, which the mentioned power and commune still hold occupied in such a manner, falsely consider themselves absolved from the excommunication sentence they incurred for the favor shown to the said Manfred and his supporters, although they have not otherwise been absolved from it. Therefore, you humbly requested us to take care to provide an appropriate declaration on this matter. Although such a declaration would not be necessary for those who think rightly, we declare to dispel their malicious persistence that they are not in any way absolved in the aforementioned case. Given at Viterbo, on the Kalends of March, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Lunensi significat homines castrorum et villarum ad sedem Lunensem spectantium, qui propter favorem Manfredo olim principi et fautoribus eius latam per sedem apostolicam excommunicationis sententiam incurrerunt, non esse exinde absolutos, etsi se malitiose tales reputent. Datum Viterbii, Kalendis Martii, anno tertio (1229).

**Translation to English:**

To the podestà, council, and commune of Corneto, our faithful. Since the time is said to be approaching when you must provide for yourselves a podestà and captain for the coming year, we, considering the current condition of the times and desiring that a faithful person devoted to the Roman Church be assumed for the governance of your land, strictly forbid your community, under the obligation of fidelity which you owe to us and the aforementioned Church, and under penalty of one thousand marks of silver by the authority of these presents, from presuming to elect or appoint anyone as your podestà or captain unless you have first informed us of the person upon whom your minds are set, and unless the devotion and loyalty of the electors and the elected has first been approved by us. For if you presume otherwise, we declare it null and void, and we command you under the aforementioned penalty not to admit such an elected person at all, as we have decided to reserve to ourselves the approval of your future podestà or captain at this time. Given at Orvieto, 9th September, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Clemens IV papa potestati, consilio et communi Cornetanis sub pena mille marcharum argenti inhibet, ne potestatem vel capitaneum eligant, nisi prius personam significaverint et fides electorum electique per ipsum approbata fuerit. 1268, Sept. 9, apud Urbemveterem.

Translation to English:

To Circulus Oliveri Circuli, citizen of Perugia and Florence. Although our predecessor, Pope Alexander of happy memory, had bound Manfred, former prince of Tarentum and manifest adversary of the Roman Church, with the chain of excommunication along with all his supporters and followers, since the citizens of Florence adhered to him with nefarious audacity in disturbing the peace of Tuscany and in presumptuously seizing the rights and goods of the Roman Empire, thereby strengthening the same Manfred in his obstinacy as a perfidious and sacrilegious invader of the patrimony of Saint Peter, and entangling themselves in the snares of the aforementioned sentence, we, following the manner of a devoted father who diligently invites offending sons to return from the path of perdition to the way of salvation, sometimes by entreaty, sometimes by threat, made various threats at the recent feast of the Lord’s Supper against the Florentine merchants regarding the arrest of their persons and the seizure and detention of their goods, and the imposition of other penalties, unless they took care to return to the mandate of the church by the forthcoming feast of the Lord’s Ascension. However, as you humbly came to our presence on behalf of yourself, your brothers, and their sons, and by the venerable brother, our bishop of Ostia and Velletri, to whom we entrusted this duty by word of mouth, you have deserved to obtain the benefit of absolution from the aforementioned excommunications and due reconciliation, by taking an oath to comply with our mandates and those of the church. Therefore, we do not wish you to incur the penalties of the said threats or be bound by them, granting you this letter of ours as testimony concerning this matter. Given at Orvieto, on the 5th day before the Kalends of June, in the third year of our pontificate.

Regesto:

Gregorius IX papa Circulo Oliveri Circuli Perusino et Florentino civi, qui se excommunicationis laqueis involuerat ob adhaesionem Manfredo, absolutionis et reconciliationis beneficium concedit, pœnis comminationum liberans. 1230, Mai. 28, apud Urbemveterem.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Bologna. We wish and by the authority of these presents, we strictly command you in the virtue of obedience and under the penalty of excommunication, to diligently admonish and persuade our beloved sons - the podestà, council, and commune of Bologna on our behalf - that they return and surrender the towns of Medicina and Argile, which belong to the Roman Church and which they currently occupy, within eight days after your warning, to our beloved son Master Helias Peleti, our chaplain, whom we have sent to them for this purpose, in our name and that of the Roman Church. But if they should perchance refuse to comply with your – or rather, our – admonitions in this matter, you shall, by our authority, pronounce a sentence of excommunication against the podestà of Bologna and ensure it is solemnly published where and when you deem it expedient, disregarding any contradiction. This is notwithstanding any indulgence granted by the Apostolic See to the said podestà, that he may not be excommunicated by apostolic letters, unless there is full and explicit mention of such an indulgence. Moreover, we desire that you have a public instrument drawn up regarding your process in this matter, secured with your seal, and faithfully transmitted to us. Given at Orvieto, on the Nones of August, in the third year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Bononiensi mandat ut potestatem, consilium et commune Bononienses moneat, ut villas Medicine et Argelate ecclesiae Romanae restituant, alioquin in potestatem Bononiensem excommunicationis sententia promulganda sit. 1230, August 5, apud Urbemveterem.

**Translation to English:**

To Manfred, elected of Verona. Son, when we think about the distress and hardships you suffer at the hands of the enemies of the Church, when we somberly reflect on the unusual sufferings you endure in the squalor of prison, we are moved with deep compassion for you and willingly consider ways and means by which we might be able to provide you with some remedies of consolation. Therefore, considering that you do not have the means to sustain yourself comfortably in that prison at this time, and wishing to extend the right hand of apostolic generosity to you, we confer upon you by apostolic authority all rights and jurisdictions, fruits, revenues, and proceeds and others which the Roman Church holds in the castle of Carpo and its territory or district of the Diocese of Modena, and which once Bertolinus Tabernarius, citizen of Parma, while he lived, held from the same Church, investing your beloved cleric Anthony by our ring with these, so that you may hold, possess, and enjoy them for your lifetime and thereafter they may freely return to the aforementioned church. Let no one infringe upon our grant and investiture. Given at Orvieto, the 8th of September, in the fourth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Manfredo Veronensi electo, captivo in carcere, iura et iurisdictiones, fructus et redditus, in castro Carpo et territorio Mutinensi diocesis, quae Romana ecclesia obtinet et quondam Bertolinus Tabernarius tenebat, auctoritate apostolica conferens, ut per clericum suum Antonium investitus teneat et possideat vita sua, et post mortem ad ecclesiam redeant. 1230, Sept. 8, apud Urbemveterem.

**English Translation:**

These are the articles brought by the envoys of the Apostolic See to the Emperor. The envoys should propose that the lord pope and his brothers desire, as much as it is within their power, to have peace with the prince and with all men, and they are prepared, as much as they can, to offer peace and tranquility to him and to the whole world; and may it please the prince, or at least not obstruct it! Because it is a great and useful preamble to the peace negotiations if the prelates and all the captive clerics, whom he detains, and all both clerics and laymen captured in galleys, are restored. They ask and request that he ought to restore them, as he and his envoys promised before our promotion. Moreover, they propose that they are prepared to listen and negotiate on our behalf about peace and to hear the satisfaction that the prince wishes to make for all the reasons he was excommunicated. Furthermore, they offer that the church, if it has harmed him against its duty, which it does not believe, is ready to correct and restore it to its proper state; and if the prince says that he has not harmed the church against justice, or if he claims that we have harmed him against justice, we are prepared to summon kings, prelates, and princes, both secular and ecclesiastical, to some safe place, so that they may come there in person or through solemn envoys, and with the counsel of the council, the church is ready to satisfy the prince if it has harmed him in any way and to revoke any unjust sentence passed against him, and with all gentleness and mercy, as much as can be done with God and the honor of the church, to receive from him satisfaction for the injuries and offenses inflicted upon him and his. Moreover, let the prince know this, that the church wishes to place all friends and adherents of the church in peace and for them to enjoy full security, that never on this occasion...

**Regesto (in Latin):**

Gregorius IX papa nuntiis sedis apostolicae mandat, ut imperatorem exhortentur ad pacem, captivos prelatos et clericos restituat, et pacis condiciones audiat; ecclesia parata est satisfactionem recipere et, si opus sit, iniustam sententiam revocare. 1231, Perusiae.

**Translation to English:**

I. To Master Gaufridus de Bellomonte, our chaplain, legate of the apostolic see. Since we desire that all who have been cut off from the congregation of the Church return to ecclesiastical unity, by the authority of these presents, we grant you that if the citizens of Brescia, who are known to have adhered to Manfred, the former prince of Taranto, and Pelavicino and their followers against the Church, wish to return to the mandates of the Church, you shall, after having received from them and others of their company an oath and other suitable security, as you see fit, that they will not in the future provide aid, counsel, or favor against the Roman Church to the aforementioned Manfred, Pelavicino, and others, absolve them in our stead according to the form of the Church, and, having lifted the interdict of their city and county, enjoin upon them salutary penance. Given at Perugia, on the 12th day before the Kalends of November, in the first year. 

II. To the same. Since we are sending you to Lombardy for certain arduous business of the Church, so that the city of Mantua may rejoice at your cheerful arrival, we grant you, by the full authority of these presents, the faculty to suspend the interdict of that city and its county until the upcoming feast of the purification of the Blessed Virgin. Given at Perugia, on the 10th day before the Kalends of November, in the first year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Magistro Gaufrido de Bellomonte, capellano suo, mandat ut, si cives Brixienses ad ecclesiae mandata redire voluerint, receptis cautionibus, eos vice sua absolvat et interdictum relaxet; itemque concedit facultatem suspendendi interdictum civitatis Mantuanae usque ad festum purificationis B. Virginis. Datum Perusii, XII et X Kalendas Novembris, anno primo.

**Translation to English:**

To Wolrad, bishop of Halberstadt. It has come to our attention that the church of Halberstadt, which among other churches of the province of Mainz was accustomed to flourish in spiritual matters and abound in temporal ones, has been brought to near destitution due to the dispute that arose long ago between you and the late Ludolf, former bishop of Halberstadt, over the bishopric of Halberstadt. Indeed, with the barons and nobles of those regions rising against it, you, having no relatives or close connections in those parts, cannot resist them or defend the aforementioned church from such attacks. The people of that church are also said to be so malicious that it appears utterly impossible for the same church to be healthily governed by you. Thus, it can not unjustly be feared that it may incur irreparable harm in spiritual and temporal matters unless it is swiftly aided by the provident care of the Apostolic See. Since there is a strong belief among some that you, due to the aforementioned reasons, desire with a humble heart to resign from pastoral governance, we have deemed it appropriate to advise your fraternity through the content of the present letter that you carefully explain to us the aforementioned dangers to the said church, and also whether such a desire for resignation persists in your will, through your special letters, so that being sufficiently informed by your report on these matters, we may at last, with the Lord's guidance, provide for these issues as we see expedient for your welfare and the benefit of the same church. Given at Orvieto, on the Nones of June, in the third year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Wolrado episcopo Alberstadensi suadet ut discrimina ecclesiae Alberstadensis et voluntatem cedendi nobis exponat, ut de his informati providere possimus. 1230, Iun. 5. Apud Urbemveterem.

**Translation to English:**

To the dearest son in Christ, Charles, illustrious King of Sicily. Among the conditions agreed upon between the Roman Church and you regarding the matter of the Kingdom of Sicily, and confirmed by your oath, it is contained that you were bound to come to these parts within a certain period to pursue the said matter and to have a determined number of soldiers, crossbowmen, and other warriors equipped with certain horses and other arms and war supplies. Now, since the same matter has been happily concluded by the grace of God, we declare, by the authority of these presents and with the counsel of our brothers, that you have fulfilled these conditions regarding the prosecution of the said matter and the provision and number of warriors. Let no one therefore violate our declaration, etc. Given at Viterbo, on the Ides of May, in the second year. To the same. Among the conditions, etc., as in the above, it is contained that you were bound to render personal homage for the same kingdom to the Roman Pontiff. Therefore, since you have rendered the aforesaid homage to our venerable brother, the Bishop of Albano, and our beloved sons, Anchero, Cardinal Priest of the Title of St. Praxedes, Riccardo of St. Angelo, Goffredo of St. George at the Golden Veil, and Matteo of St. Mary in Portico, Cardinals Deacons, having special mandate from us for this, we declare, by the authority of these presents and with the counsel of our brothers, that you have fulfilled this condition in your person. Let no one therefore violate our declaration, etc. Given at Viterbo, on the Ides of May, in the second year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Carolo regi Siciliae illustri declarat ipsum condiciones inter Romanam ecclesiam et se super regno Siciliae initas, quoad prosecutionem negotii et numerum bellatorum, atque homagium personale Romano pontifici praestitum, implevisse. Dat. Viterbii, Idibus Maii, anno secundo pontificatus.

**Translation to English:**

To ensure the memory of this matter. Among the various concerns that keep our mind vigilant, our thoughts are particularly focused on preserving the province of Campania, a cherished region of the Apostolic See, in a prosperous state. For the more we perceive this province to be closely connected to the heart of the said See, the more diligently we contemplate its tranquility, which we enjoy with due dignity. Therefore, to prevent anything from arising through the castle of Monte San Giovanni in the diocese of Veroli, which is near the enemies of the Roman Church, that might lead to harm for this castle or the aforementioned province, we strictly forbid by apostolic authority that the noble man, the Count of Acerra, or any of those who have a share in the lordship of the said castle, dare to introduce, retain, or in any way harbor any troop of soldiers, crossbowmen, or footmen of Manfred, the former prince of Taranto, or any other disloyal individuals to this Church. For we deprive those who dare to act otherwise, by apostolic authority, of all goods, rights, and lordship they hold in the same castle, confiscating these, moreover, to the Roman Church by our plenitude of power. We command all men of the said castle to respond to our beloved son, the noble man Aymon of Aquino, who persists in devotion to this Church, with the goods, rights, and lordship of those to whom the sentence of such deprivation shall apply, and to fully obey him in these matters in the name of the aforementioned Church. Thus, the guilty will find their own fault turning into punishment, and the good will be known to achieve the rewards of their merit. Given at Orvieto, 8th day before the Ides of July, in the third year.
