**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Aymoni de Aquino mandat, ne comes Acerrarum vel alii in castro Montis Sancti Iohannis masnadas Manfredi vel hostium ecclesie introducant aut retineant, et si secus fecerint, bonis et dominio privantur, illa Romanae ecclesiae confiscando et Aymoni tradendo. 1239, Iul. 8, apud Urbemveterem.

**Translation to English:**

To the beloved daughter in Christ, the noble lady S., widow Countess of Caserta,

Since you are said to be devoted to God and the Church, we wish to extend to you a gracious exhibition of favor. Therefore, as the cities and places to which it happens that Manfred, the former prince of Tarento, Richard of Caserta, and Thomas of Acerra, the counts, and Galvano and Frederick Lancea, the brothers, come, are subjected to ecclesiastical interdict by the Apostolic See due to their faults, as long as they remain there: we, not wanting that under this pretext divine services should sometimes be hindered, in response to your devout supplications, by apostolic authority grant you that—in spite of this—you may, within such cities and places subject to you or your son, the said Count of Caserta, even while Manfred, the aforementioned counts, and brothers, or any of them, are staying there, if it happens that you arrive there or perhaps reside in them, hear divine services in religious places where they are celebrated by indult of the Apostolic See, or in your chapels by your own chaplains or other regulars with five honest women, and may allow these chaplains and regulars to celebrate them together or separately, and also that you and these women may receive and be administered ecclesiastical sacraments by them, and if it happens that you pass away, to be buried in an ecclesiastical cemetery, provided that these divine services are celebrated in the same places and chapels with closed doors, without ringing bells, with the excommunicated and interdicted and all others excluded, and with suppressed voice, and that neither you, nor the aforementioned chaplains, regulars, and women have caused the interdict, nor does it happen that it is specifically imposed on you or them.

Let no one, therefore, dare infringe our concession or oppose it, under penalty of incurring divine wrath; these presents shall be valid for no longer than three years.

Given at Orvieto, on the tenth day before the Kalends of July, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Urbanus IV papa nobili mulieri S. Caserte comitisse vidue indulgentiam concedit, ut in locis interdicto suppositis, ubi illa vel filius eius Casertanus comes degant, divina audiendi ac sacramenta recipiendi facultatem habeat, clausis ianuis et aliis exclusis. 1261, Iun. 22, apud Urbemveterem.

**Translation to English:**

To Master Renerus, schoolmaster of the Church of Tongeren, Diocese of Liège. As it was presented to us on behalf of our venerable brother Henry, Bishop of Liège, certain barons, nobles, knights, and laymen of the cities and dioceses of Liège and Utrecht are known to have improperly acquired or held certain things through wars, exercises, tournaments, and other means. However, because those to whom these should be returned, or their heirs, cannot at all be known or found, the same bishop humbly asked us to provide paternal care over this matter. Therefore, inclined by his supplications, we entrust you with the authority in these presents, to grant to those among the aforementioned barons, nobles, knights, and laymen who, having taken up the sign of the life-giving cross, will travel with the same bishop to aid the Holy Land – to which the bishop intends to go, as he asserts – that by our authority you allow them to use what has been acquired and held, provided that those to whom restitution should be made, or their heirs, cannot at all be known or found, after a public declaration and diligent care and concern have been taken for discovery in those parts where the said nobles are accustomed to reside and elsewhere, as you see fit, to expend them in support of the said land and not to be held liable for further restitution. Given at Orvieto, 6th July, in the third year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Magistro Renero scolastico ecclesiae Tungrensis mandat, ut baronibus, nobilibus, militibus, et laicis Leodiensis et Traiectensis, qui cum episcopo Leodiensi in subsidium Terrae Sanctae proficiscuntur, concedat ut indebita acquisita in subsidium destinetur, si heredes ad restitutionem non inveniantur. 1245, Iul. 6, apud Urbemveterem.

**Translation to English:**

To Gregory, parish priest of the parish of Marmoraria in the diocese of Siena. Recently it has come to our attention that Adota, who presents himself as the abbot of the monastery of Insula, belonging directly to the Roman Church of the order of Saint Benedict in the diocese of Vulturara, has reached such a state of mental excess that he has rashly dared to swear an oath of fidelity to Jordan, supporter and then captain or messenger of the late Manfred, former prince of Taranto and persecutor of the Church, in the lands of Tuscany adhering to him, and he has wickedly caused the people of Cortino, vassals of the aforesaid monastery, to swear a similar oath. Moreover, Adota, being unlettered and insufficient or less suitable for the governance of the aforementioned monastery, so enormously dilapidates and consumes the goods of the said monastery that unless aid is promptly provided by the Apostolic See to the same monastery, it will hardly or never rise again. Therefore, since it is proper to providently employ our counsel on this matter, we, trusting in your circumspection, command you that if you ascertain that the said Adota is publicly infamous concerning the aforementioned matters or any of them, you procure to summon him peremptorily by our authority through yourself or another, so that within fifteen days after your summons, he personally appears before us to receive what is due for his actions. Whatever you shall do and find out regarding this, and the day and form of the summons, you shall not omit to faithfully report to us through your letters containing the tenor of the present. Given at Orvieto, on the fourth day before the Nones of September, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Gregorio plebano plebis Marmorariae mandat, ut Adotam, abbatem monasterii de Insula, si infamia publica super negotiis quibusdam laborat, auctoritate pontificia citet ad comparendum coram papa. 1238, Sept. 2, apud Urbemveterem.

**Translation to English:**

To the Podestà, council, and commune of Perugia, our faithful subjects. Because that tyrant and principal persecutor of the Church, namely Manfred, the former Prince of Taranto, not content with the various forms of persecution with which he has hitherto harassed the Roman Church, intends to gather all the forces of his power and assemble troops from everywhere against us and the Roman Church, as well as the city of Orvieto, where our entire court resides, to the disgrace of the Church and the harm of its faithful, we, intending to resist the reckless endeavors of the same Manfred with your counsel and help, as well as that of other faithful of the Church, not only in the territory of the said city but also elsewhere in the lands of the said Church, have decided to exhort, request, and urge your community through apostolic letters, strictly commanding you under the obligation of faithfulness by which you are bound to us and the Roman Church, that, after deliberate counsel, you send solemn ambassadors and syndics with full authority to our presence before the forthcoming feast of Saint Mary Magdalene, to discuss these matters with us and to hear and carry out what shall be ordained by us and our brothers, with the Lord’s guidance, in this matter. Given at Orvieto, on the 6th day before the Ides of July, in the third year of our pontificate. In the same manner to the Podestà, captains, councils, and communes of Todi, Spoleto, Narni, and Assisi; and singularly to those of Foligno, Bevagna, Spello, Montefalco, Nocera, Interamna, Rieti, Cagli, Gubbio, Orte, Amelia, Bagnaia, Viterbo, Tuscany, Corneto, Monte Alto, Vetralla, Montefiascone, Castrum, Sutri, Civitavecchia, Nepi, Radicofani, and Centumcellae.

**Regesto (Latin):**

Urbanus IV papa potestati, consilio et communi Perusinis mandat, ut legatos cum pleno mandato ad suam praesentiam mittant ad tractandum de resistentia contra Manfredum. 1264, Iul. 10, apud Urbemveterem.

**Translation to English:**

To the Patriarch of Jerusalem, legate of the Apostolic See. In support of the Holy Land, the hearts of the faithful should be ignited, and Christians are especially urged to rise to its liberation with whatever aid they can provide. This is particularly encouraged because God's only begotten Son, Jesus Christ, chose to mercifully assist those continuously oppressed under the yoke of the ancient enemy, liberating them from perpetual servitude by the precious price of His blood. Considering that the walls of the city of Jerusalem are completely destroyed, with only their foundations remaining, it is both worthy and highly expedient among other aids to this land, that such a venerable city, stained with Christ’s blood, be fortified with strong walls. We have decided to earnestly admonish, request, and exhort our venerable brothers, the archbishops and bishops, and beloved sons, the other prelates of churches and their chapters, as well as the masters and brothers of the military orders of the Temple, the Hospital of Jerusalem, and St. Mary of the Teutons, and other religious and noble men, barons, and other faithful of Christ in the overseas territories, imposing upon them remission of sins, that they lend their effective aid and effort to the repair of the city's walls, which can be done more freely and efficiently now due to the discord among the sultans, through which the Lord seems to have specially provided for this land. We also intend to earnestly induce, through our letters, the Catholic princes of the world and all other Christians to honorably extend the hand of charity to this cause. We command you to make an appropriate taxation, as you are the one to whom we direct this letter, to ensure a certain assistance from each of them, both in soldiers and workers and other necessities for the same work, according to their capabilities, without any difficulty. Therefore, we order that you make this taxation according to the prudence attributed to you from above, keeping only the Lord in mind, and insistently demand the named subsidy, according to what you have assessed and expressed. Given at Anagni, the Nones of August, year 1.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa Patriarchae Ierosolimitano, legato apostolico, mandat ut taxationem pro reparatione murorum civitatis Ierosolimitanae faciat, et subsidium necessarium instanter exigat. Anagniae, Nonis Augusti, anno primo (1227).

**Translation to English:**

To the knowledge of the present and memory of the future. As obstinate sons, the citizens of the City of Castello, who currently hold the city, have hardened their spirits in pride, such that, showing neither reverence for God nor the apostolic see, they contemptuously disregard our and the same see's mandates, persisting stubbornly in their usual rebellion. Although we have publicly excommunicated them and subjected the city and its district to ecclesiastical interdict, and have deprived them of their privileges, graces, rights, and jurisdictions through various other processes conducted against them, they, nevertheless, disdain all these measures and perniciously persist in their contumacy. Therefore, intending that the aggravation of sentences and the severity of penalties may grant understanding to those whom our previous kindness did not lead back to the path of truth, we renew these processes and sentences. We again bind the powers, captains, councilors, judges, and any officials of the said city with the sentence of excommunication due to the aforementioned reasons and subject the city and district to a similar interdict, exposing their persons (excepting danger of death or mutilation) and their movable goods to the faithful to be seized freely and with impunity. We also warn them that unless they return to our and the church's mandates within one month from now, we shall proceed, as we see fit, to the deprivation of the episcopal dignity of the Church of Castello due to their obstinate malice, with the Lord's assistance. Thus, our process should be made known, etc., as in the previous letter of Conradinus, etc., up to: to be published, so that the citizens and commune of the City of Castello and others whom the process pertains to, etc., until: it is published. Done in our palace in Viterbo, on Maundy Thursday, in the year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa civibus Civitatis Castelli, propter eorum pertinacem rebellionem et contemptum mandatorum, excommunicationis sententiam et interdictum ecclesiasticum renovat, eisdem personis et bonis mobilibus exponendis fidelibus impune capiendis. 1235, Apr. 14, Viterbii.

**Translation to English:**

.. to the podestà, captain, and commune of Sassoferrato in the diocese of Nocera. For the merits of your sincerity and constancy, rewards of special benevolence are to be granted to you by the Apostolic See, so that by its favor you may, with God's help, achieve increases in prosperity and be burdened by no unworthy losses, especially at times when some traitors of the same church might try to trouble you for that reason, because their condemnable guilt is seen to have been punished by you at the command of the said church. Indeed, your exhibited petition stated that when the noble men Fildismidus de Castaneo, Guillelmucius Uffreducii, Peter and Bonaventura Mercatantis, Ventura Petri, John Inge, Abrazolus Radiconis, Favarellus de Podio, Carpinellus the Judge, Bovecellus, Aldebrandinus, Gentilucius born to the noble man Severus, and several others, formerly inhabitants of the castle of Sassoferrato, manifest traitors to the Roman Church, with a spirit obstinately inclined to rebellion, presumptuously adhered to the persecutors of that church and inflicted serious damages upon you who remain in the devotion of the same church, you eventually at the command of our beloved son M., the elected of Verona, former rector of the March of Ancona and the Duchy of Spoleto, demolished the houses of those traitors completely. Therefore, so that any opportunity for those traitors to challenge you on this matter might be removed in the future, we, acceding to your devoted supplications, grant by the authority of these presents that, if the above-mentioned facts are true, you or any of you, as long as you remain in the devotion of the Apostolic See, are in no way obliged to restore the aforementioned traitors or their heirs or any of them to rebuild the said houses or to compensate for the damages they claim to have incurred because of the demolition of those houses. Therefore, let no one — challenge our concession etc. Given at Orvieto, 9 June, in the third year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa potestati, capitaneo et communi Saxiferratin Nucerine diocesis indulget, ut proditoribus Romanæ ecclesiæ domos reficere vel dampna restituere non teneantur. 1229, Iun. 9. Apud Urbemveterem.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man, the Podestà of Rieti. Know that it has come to our attention that Bonconte of Pendentia, who unlawfully occupies the Church of Pacto, having been installed there by the late Manfred, former Prince of Taranto and a manifest persecutor of the Roman Church, holds it to the peril of his soul, causing great prejudice to our venerable brother, the Bishop of Pacto, and insult and contempt to the Roman Church itself. He has bought large and extensive possessions in the territory and district of the city of Rieti with the revenues of the aforementioned Church of Pacto. Frequently visiting the same city and staying there publicly at his leisure, he presumes to partake in certain perverse dealings with some citizens of Rieti, acting as a pestilent man and a public supporter of the same persecutor, and secretly does not hesitate to commit other acts there which might lead to the subversion of the same city and cause considerable harm to the Roman Church. Hence, it is absolutely indecent that, while the said Bonconte revels among the faithful of the Roman Church in the goods of the aforementioned Church of Pacto, the aforementioned Bishop of Pacto, who is compelled to live in exile from his church due to his devotion to the same Roman Church, has nothing from which he might sustain himself. Therefore, we have deemed it necessary to earnestly request and exhort your nobility, commanding that you take into your hands, in the name of the said bishop and the Church of Pacto, all the goods, both movable and immovable, which are known to have been thus acquired by the aforementioned Bonconte in the said territory and district, and hold them until we decide otherwise about them. So fulfill our request and command in such a way that we may rightfully commend your devotion with worthy praises in the Lord. Given at Orvieto, on the third day before the Nones of July, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro potestati Reatinos mandat ut bona, quae Boncontus de Pendentia, occupator ecclesiae Pactensis, in civitate Reatina contra animam suam ac detrimentum Romanae ecclesiae adquisiverit, retineat et custodiat nomine episcopi Pactensis, donec aliter disponatur. Datum apud Urbemveterem, III Nonas Iulii, anno III pontificatus.

TRANSLATION TO ENGLISH:

To the Bishop of Camerino and the Abbot of San Severo in Urbevetanus. After due deliberation, etc., as stated above in letter LXVII to the end.

REGESTO IN LATIN:

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Camerinensi et abbati Sancti Severi Urbevetani mandat ut, post diligentem deliberationem, sicut in LXVII littera supra dictum est, agant. Datum apud Urbemveterem, anno pontificatus (specific year needed).

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Ferrara. Our venerable brother, the Bishop of Saxena, has shown us by his petition that the power, councilors, and commune of the city of Cesena, having utterly cast aside the fear and reverence of God, gathered a general army and approached the city of Saxena, where the aforementioned bishop and the Church of Saxena hold temporal jurisdiction. They inflicted grievous harm on the same bishop, the church, and the people of the city of Saxena, committing vile crimes in the church itself and its cemetery. Nevertheless, they rashly occupied the city and continue to occupy it to the prejudice and grave detriment of the same bishop and church. Therefore, the named bishop, having diligently warned them to make amends for these matters and they having neglected to do so, pronounced the sentence of excommunication against the said power, councilors, and people of the city of Cesena, and against all those who provided them counsel, aid, and favor regarding the aforementioned issues, because these acts were so notorious they could not be concealed by any subterfuge. Therefore, the said bishop humbly petitioned us to make the same sentence obtain the strength of due firmness. Wherefore, we command that you cause the sentence, as it has been reasonably pronounced, to be observed inviolably by our authority, removing any appeal, until suitable satisfaction is rendered. And if after two months from when it is clear to you that the sentence was properly passed, the aforementioned power, councilors, and people, and others mentioned above, endure it with hardened hearts, you shall then publicly announce them excommunicated on every Sunday and feast day with ringing bells and lit candles, wherever and whenever you shall see fit, and have them announced as excommunicated by others and strictly avoided by all until suitable satisfaction is rendered. Given at Viterbo, the fifteenth calends of February, in the third year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Ferrariensi mandat ut sententiam excommunicationis contra potestatem, consiliarios et commune civitatis Cesenatis, a G. episcopo Saxenas prolatam, auctoritate apostolica inviolabiliter observandam curet, cum eisdem post duos menses publice nuntiet excommunicationem, nisi satisfaciant. 1229, Jan. 18, Viterbii.

**Translation to English:**

To Cardinal M. of Saint Mary in Porticu, rector of the patrimony of Saint Peter in Tuscany, legate of the apostolic see. Desiring that the business of the Roman Church, which we have entrusted to your industry, may receive increases of desired prosperity through the diligence of your effort, we grant to your discretion, in which we have full confidence in the Lord, the full and free authority by the present letters to settle by judgment or agreement the disputes or lawsuits which are said to have arisen between the powers, council, and commune of Spoleto on one side, and the noble men, lords of Arrone and of Castro Lacus on the other side. You are also granted the authority to restore to the Spoleto people the castle of Peroculi in the diocese of Spoleto, which we hold in our hands, and to remit to them the penalties and bans, into which the said Spoleto people are known to have incurred due to past rebellion attempted against us. Moreover, you are given the authority to establish, dispose, order, command, and do anything concerning the aforesaid matters that you see expedient for our honor and that of the Roman Church, and for the peaceful state of those parts. For whatever you do regarding the aforesaid matters, we shall consider it ratified and confirmed. Given at Orvieto, on the 6th day before the Ides of August, in the 3rd year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa M. Sancte Marie in Porticu diacono cardinali mandat, ut lites inter potestatem, consilium et commune Spoletanos ex parte una et dominos de Arrone et de Castro Lacus ex altera componat, castrum Peroculi Spoletanis restituat, et penas remittat. 1229, Aug. 6. Apud Urbemveterem.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Albano, legate of the Apostolic See. Our venerable brother, the bishop of Nola, has shown us by his petition that, although he, then the bishop of Angelis, was compelled by necessity to go to the city of Palermo — not as a prelate but as a familiar of the noble man, the count of Acerra, because he and his relatives were liegemen of the said count — he did not attend the presumed coronation of the late Manfred, prince of Taranto, but remained distant from the place where the said coronation took place. However, after the said Manfred was crowned, he went to the church of Palermo to have a mass celebrated there, or rather, to profane it, the said bishop was present in the church and could not leave due to guards stationed at the church's doors who allowed no one to exit. There, a silk cloak was sent to him by the archbishop of Bari, and although he refused to accept it several times, he was eventually compelled under threat of death from Manfred to wear the cloak and attend the celebration of the mass with the aforementioned prelates. Thus, the bishop, forced by such fear, attended the celebration clad in the cloak but did not participate in the divine rites, nor did he sign or seal the documents concerning the said coronation, nor did he swear allegiance to Manfred. Furthermore, our predecessor of blessed memory, Pope Alexander, having been informed by trustworthy persons about how the bishop was in Palermo at the time of the said coronation but did not attend it as mentioned, did not consider him excommunicated. Instead, as indicated by his gracious translation, he benevolently admitted him to the grace of the Apostolic See and transferred him to the see of Nola, then vacant, with full power and special grace. Therefore, on behalf of the said bishop, it was humbly requested of us to admit him to our grace and that of the said See, and to declare by our letters that he may freely administer temporal and spiritual matters and exercise the execution of pastoral office. Therefore, we command you, if it is established as true and nothing canonically stands in the way, to provide for the said bishop concerning these matters with your circumspection by our authority, as you deem expedient. Given at Viterbo, the fourth day before the Kalends of June, in the second year of our pontificate.

**Latin Regesto:**

Honorius III papa episcopo Albanensi mandat, ut si sibi constiterit episcopum Nolanum tempore coronationis Manfredi in civitate Panormitana fuisse, sed coronationi non interfuisse, ipsum ad gratiam apostolicae sedis admittat et declarare possit eum in temporalibus et spiritualibus libere administrare et officium pastorale exequi. Datum Viterbii, die IIII Kalendas Iunii, anno secundo pontificatus nostri.

**Translation to English:**

To the archpriest of Perugia, our chaplain. After careful deliberation, my brothers and I have deemed it appropriate to send you to promote the honor of the Church in the Duchy and the patrimony of Saint Peter in Tuscany. Therefore, fully trusting in your prudence, we command you to receive full information from our beloved son, Cardinal R. of Santa Maria in Cosmedin, to whom we are sending our letters regarding this matter, about what is necessary for this business. With Christ as your guide, proceed to the aforementioned patrimony and Duchy, acting so diligently and prudently in all things that you will be deservedly commended by us and our brothers. Given at Anagni, on the 7th day before the Kalends of September, in the first year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archipresbytero Perusino mandat ut, informationem plenam a cardinale R. Sanctae Mariae in Cosmedin accipiens, ad patrimonium et Ducatum beati Petri in Tuscia dirigat, ad honorem ecclesiae promovendum. 1227, Aug. 26. Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Cosenza and the Abbot of Monte Cassino. Having full confidence in the prudence of your discretion in the Lord, we hereby commit to you by the authority of these presents that if any of those who are bound by the chain of excommunication on account of the late Manfred, former Prince of Taranto, or his late brother Conrad, or their late father, wish to return to the mandates of the Church, you and each of you may grant them the benefit of absolution according to the form set forth below, which we diligently wish to be observed. This form is as follows: namely, that the said excommunicated persons shall, before all else, swear bodily an oath of adherence to our mandates and those of the Roman Church, and additionally provide surety as caution under the penalty you deem necessary. They shall also swear that henceforth they will offer no favor, counsel, or aid whatsoever, either publicly or secretly, to the said Manfred or any of his supporters or followers, and that they will neither receive nor send any letters, messages, or gifts, small or large, from or to him as long as he remains rebellious against the aforementioned Church or persists under the excommunication pronounced against him by the Apostolic See; nor will they provide him with any aid, counsel, or favor in the meantime. Furthermore, they shall completely withdraw from all confederations, promises, or pacts by which they have hitherto bound themselves to Manfred, even if they have sworn to uphold them, from which you may have the authority to absolve them by our permission. Regarding these oaths and promises, all of which we wish to be done publicly, you shall cause public instruments to be made and faithfully sent to us by you. For we wish you to proceed with all these matters, saving other mandates of ours concerning what we have deemed necessary to be done. Once these have been duly executed as stated above, you shall grant the aforementioned excommunicated persons the benefit of absolution from the said excommunication according to the form of the Church. Given at Perugia, the Ides of November, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto:**

Author: Innocentius IV papa  
Recipient: Archiepiscopus Cusentinus et Abbas Casinensis  
Abstract: Innocentius IV mandates the absolution of those excommunicated due to association with the late Manfred, Prince of Taranto, upon their adherence to specific conditions, including oaths of obedience to the Church's mandates and renunciation of support for Manfred.

Place: Perusii

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Jacob Gantelmi, vicar in the City of our beloved son Charles of Anjou, Count of Provence, senator of the City. Son, we rejoice, we rejoice in the Lord, and we give abundant thanks to Him, for He has turned the hearts of the Roman people so unanimously and concordantly to the wishes of us and the Roman mother church, that the same people under your diligent leadership and the fortunate banners of your lord, proceed with a united and universal army to prosecute and avenge the injury of the same church against that treacherous betrayer of the church, namely Peter de Vico, against whom we have proceeded both spiritually and temporally by the demand of his iniquity. Having entered powerfully into the territory of the castle of Vico, where indeed the same traitor was accustomed to weave the webs of his treachery and iniquity against the church, they set victorious camps in that territory and besieged the castle with a noble siege at our persuasion and prayers. We have decided that your diligence, which you are known to have applied to attract and induce the aforementioned people to honor and benefit the same church in this matter, which is ours and that of the same church, should be exalted with worthy praises, intending to respond to both you and the same people with gratitude for those things that pertain to the good and prosperous state of the City, with the Lord's favor for place and time. However, because you have faithfully informed us that the said castle could easily be captured if two thousand livres of Provence were at hand for constructing machines and other war instruments and were sent to you by us for such prosecution of the matter, we, desiring that the aforementioned Roman church may effectively obtain its intended purpose concerning the castle to the praise and glory of the divine name, behold, we have decided to specifically send to you our beloved sons, masters Helias our chaplain and Sinisius, clerk of our chamber, to whom you should give firm faith in those things which they will say to you on our behalf concerning this matter. Given at Urbisveterem, 30th May, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro Iacobo Gantelmil, vicario in Urbe Caroli Andegavie comitis, gratias agit pro studio eius et Romani populi in prosequenda iniuria ecclesie contra Petrum de Vico; promittit subsidium pecuniae pro machinis bellicis ad castrum de Vico capiendum. Datum apud Urbemveterem, III Kal. Iunii, anno tertio.

Translation to English:

To R., Bishop of Avignon. We gladly and with a ready affection attend to your and the church committed to you for their advancement, as your clear merits demand and because we hold both you and the same church with a special kind of affection more sincerely in the heart of our charity. Indeed, as the petition recently presented to us on your behalf stated, certain nobles, knights, and other laypeople of those parts are known to hold some villages, lands, possessions, and other temporal goods, which have, from long past times, come to the church of Avignon established within the borders of the Roman Empire by imperial grant, in fief from the same church. However, an imperial privilege has decreed that in such fiefs, which arise from these goods, only the sons or grandsons of those who temporarily hold them, or others descending directly from them, or their fathers or mothers may succeed to them for their lifetime, so that after the death of their fathers and mothers, the same fiefs should totally devolve to the aforementioned church. Therefore, it sometimes happens that the aforementioned nobles, knights, and laypeople, who are vassals of the same church, having no heirs to whom, according to the tenor of the aforementioned privilege, such goods held in fief should pass, neglect to manage these goods as would be expedient, thus causing considerable loss to that church. Therefore, you have humbly requested us to intervene with an appropriate remedy since it seems very useful to the same church that another arrangement concerning the succession of these fiefs be made with the said vassals. Therefore, inclined by your supplications, we have decided to grant to your fraternity by our authority — notwithstanding the aforementioned constitution — that you may, with the consent of your chapter or the greater part of them, negotiate and even arrange as you see most expedient for the utility of the same church with the aforementioned vassals concerning these matters; provided that what accrues to you from such negotiation or arrangement be entirely converted into the purchase of some possessions or otherwise for the benefit of the same church. Given at Viterbo, 9th December, in the third year of our pontificate.

Regesto in Latin:

To the bishop of Prussia. Understanding with spiritual rejoicing the deeds accomplished in the regions of Prussia by the beloved sons, the brothers of the Hospital of Saint Mary of the Teutons, and other faithful of Christ, through the favor of divine power, and considering the vastness of the land acquired there by the grace of God, we have deemed it appropriate to entrust to our venerable brother, formerly the bishop of Modena and our penitentiary at the apostolic see, the full office of legation in the regions of Prussia and Livonia, granting him full authority, with the counsel of our brothers, to delineate dioceses and divide the land of Prussia into parts.

Indeed, the bishop established three dioceses in Prussia and one in the land of Culm, and divided the land of Prussia into three parts. Of these, he assigned two parts to the aforementioned brothers, who bear the burden of battles and expenses and must enfeoff many with land, in such a way that, whether there be one bishop or several, they shall hold two parts of the land entirely with all revenue, and the bishop or bishops shall similarly hold the third part entirely with all jurisdiction and rights, saving for the bishop in the two parts of the brothers all those things which cannot be exercised except by a bishop.

Since we have determined that this limitation and division should be confirmed by apostolic authority, we command by decree that you should be content with one of the dioceses of Prussia, as you prefer, and with the third part of the land of that diocese, and that you should not presume to enfeoff, alienate, or give lands or rights pertaining to the part of the diocese you choose without special mandate from the apostolic see. Know that whatever you have alienated from the land of Prussia or the land of Culm or their revenues, we revoke as null, and we decree it void if you attempt any further alienation against our prohibition.

Moreover, you shall receive the temporalities that rightfully belong to you by the law of the bishopric from the hand of the legate in the name of us and the Roman Church, rendering yourself in all things as such, as pontifical dignity and religious propriety require, so that it may be to the glory of God and the Church, may bring merit to you, and may come to the progress of the faithful of Christ in Prussia. You propose, with the favor of divine clemency, to convert them to the worship of the Christian faith, and that our venerable brother, the Bishop of Olomouc, having assumed the sign of the life-giving cross, intends to join you in this cause to promote this work of faith. To the beloved sons, the abbots of the monasteries of the Cistercian order in Lucka and Novali of St. Mary, within the dioceses of Minden and Hildesheim. By the Lord's disposition, we have been undeservedly appointed to the governance of the universal church. We raise our eyes around us, and since the care of all churches falls upon us as a duty of our pastoral office, considering what is expedient for each of them, we strive to preserve them from harm and, as much as is permitted to us from on high, procure their advantages. However, concerning the state of those which lament the inconveniences of widowhood, we are more vigilantly stirred, so that we may appoint such persons to their governance, who, by their diligence, may govern them healthily in spiritual and temporal matters, and defend them in opportune times by their power. Indeed, with the Hildesheim church being vacant, the beloved sons, the dean and chapter of the same, having called all who wished, ought and could conveniently be present, gathered together in one for the substitution of a future pastor, as is customary, and considering that the same church placed amidst a perverse nation needed the powerful protection of a defender, and that the beloved son Otto, their fellow canon and a brother of the noble man, the Duke of Brunswick, was considered more useful than others for the defense and governance of the same church, they unanimously and concordantly, invoking the grace of the Holy Spirit, requested him, despite his deficiency in age, to be appointed as bishop of Hildesheim, humbly beseeching us to deign to admit such a petition. We, therefore, having duly considered the state of that church, the quality of the time, and the condition of the person, not wishing that the same church should incur the disadvantages of a prolonged vacancy, command your discretion by apostolic writings, that if such a petition is found to have been concordant and otherwise canonically celebrated, and that the same church can be defended by the said Otto as is expedient, and that he is already of such age as to be able to govern and direct the said church usefully, you appoint him, notwithstanding the aforesaid defect, especially since, as it is reported, he is competent in letters, endowed with the grace of discretion and circumspect providence, as procurator there by our authority, grant him the general care and administration of the spiritual and temporal matters of the same church, and ensure that all its subjects, vassals, and officials fully obey him as its procurator and respond concerning the rights of the same church, restraining opposers by censure. Whatever you shall have done concerning these matters, you shall faithfully intimate to us by your letters, containing the series of these events. Given at Orvieto, the tenth of the Kalends of September, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbatibus Lucka et Novali monasteriorum Cisterciensis ordinis mandat, ut si postulatio Ottonis subdiaconi in episcopum Hyldesemensem concorditer et canonice facta fuerit, ipsum, non obstante defectu etatis, in procuratorem constitutant, concedendo ei administrationem spiritualium et temporalium, et faciant eum ab omnibus obediri. 1239, Urbemveterem, X Kal. Sept.

To the Prior of the Dominican Order in Confluentia, Diocese of Trier. No gem shines more brightly in the adornment of the supreme pontiff than humility, the queen of all virtues and the radiant crown of the elect, and most pleasing in the eyes of the Divine Majesty, deserving of eternal clarity. For indeed, the loving kindness of the celestial Lamb has rendered this—a glory of heaven and an ornament of earth—so amiable to us through His grace, and has bound it to our affections with the emblems of sincere charity, that we have removed the thorn of all hatred or rancor from our heart and have firmly established the love of those who once afflicted our innocence with slanders and at times grievous losses. Indeed, at the time when our predecessor of blessed memory, Pope Innocent, was residing in Lyon, we, who were then serving in the office of archdeacon of Laon, were sent by the special mandate of the same predecessor to parts of Germany for certain affairs of the Roman Church. Thereupon, Hermann of Willemsdorp, the elder knight, along with Hermann the younger and Conrad, his brothers from the same place, and Eccheard of Bicken, laymen with certain of their accomplices from the Diocese of Trier, sacrilegiously captured us, stripping us of some horses, a certain sum of money, and very many other goods, and held us in captivity for some time. Yet, by the merciful intervention of the most clement queen of heaven, we were liberated from this captivity through the assistance of her power. Now, however, Hermann the younger, Conrad, and the aforementioned Eccheard, as they have taken care to inform us, have, by the inspiration of the Lord, returned to their senses and are prepared to make satisfaction to us for that part of the aforementioned goods which came into their possession and also for the inflicted injuries, according to the demands of their capability. Therefore, they humbly asked us to take care to provide for them suitably in this matter, since they claim to have incurred deadly hostilities and cannot come into our presence due to the greater dangers of the roads, and because we have already had the aforementioned Hermann the elder absolved by you out of a certain feeling of compassion. Since we have, albeit unworthy, received the dignity of that office by divine provision, in which we are bound to love even our enemies and to assist our persecutors with the aid of prayer, we commit to your discretion, by the authority of these presents, that you should completely absolve, on our behalf, Hermann the younger, Conrad, and Eccheard from the sentence of excommunication which they are known to have incurred because of the aforesaid matters, according to the form of the Church, once they have humbly requested this from you, and to impose upon them a salutary penance. Furthermore, after they have obtained such absolution according to the aforementioned form, kindly announce to them that we remit all injury and offense inflicted upon us by them and, with a view to divine piety, liberally release them from the need for restitution of money or goods for the damages they are known to have caused to our person, imposing upon them nonetheless, by virtue of the oath taken, that they henceforth abstain from such injuries and plunder. Given at Orvieto, on the 9th of July, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa priori fratrum ordinis Predicatorum in Confluentia mandat ut Hermannum iuniorem, Conradum et Eccheardum a sententia excommunicationis absolvat et iniungat eis poenitentiam salutarem, iniurias et damna nobis illata remittendo. 1229, Iul. 9, apud Urbemveterem.

Gregorius IX papa Potestati filio ac dilectis filiis Guasta et Seraphina nuntiis promittit expensas in obsidibus, quos Romana ecclesia apud Urbemveterem custodiri fecit, cum facultas obtulerit, resarciri. 1227, Oct. 3. Anagnie.

To the Bishop of Bologna and the abbots, priors, archdeacons, and other prelates of churches, chapters, and ecclesiastical persons, both secular and regular, whether exempt or not, established throughout the city and diocese of Bologna. Manfred, once Prince of Taranto, an imitator of paternal wickedness and tyranny, by plundering the kingdom of Sicily, is wounding, nay, tearing apart the Roman Church at its core, and from such depredations is disturbing nearly everyone from sea to sea and from the river to the ends of the earth. The Apostolic See, which had long been forbearing in the hope that he would return to his senses and repent his actions, seeing that he was only getting worse day by day, accumulating worse upon past deeds, has chosen our beloved son in Christ, the illustrious King Charles of Sicily, to counter his wickedness and restore peace to the lands and tranquility to the peoples. Therefore, as a great military force is coming from beyond the Alps to assist this king, not pursuing his own cause but that of the Church and the entire Christian people, we earnestly ask, admonish, and exhort your community, firmly ordering you by apostolic writings, to obey and support our beloved son, Master Geoffrey of Beaumont, our chaplain, whom we send to the province of Lombardy with full authority of legation assigned to him, with the advice of our brothers, in all matters concerning the movement of the aforementioned military force through Lombardy and its conduct and support for the royal cause. Otherwise, the sentence he will pronounce against the rebellious shall be observed. To the podestà, council, and commune of Assisi. The Apostolic See especially regards their devotion and records their fidelity in its book of memory, opening to them the bosom of special grace and favor, as it finds them steadfast in its fidelity and not separated from its side by any adversity or evil suggestion. Therefore, since, when the storm of persecution rose against the Roman Church, your mother, you endured grave afflictions and pressures for the defense of ecclesiastical liberty, with men from the Duchy, especially from Foligno and Spello, devastating your villages, trees, vineyards, woods, and also the works of your lands, we, recalling your constancy and sincere devotion with careful meditation and inclined by your supplications, grant you by the authority of these presents that you may freely reclaim full restitution for such damages from the people of Foligno, Spello, and others mentioned above, and summon them regarding these matters both in the Roman Church and elsewhere, wherever you wish. Given at Anagni, on the 4th of October, in the first year.

Gregorius IX papa potestati, consilio et communi Assisinatibus permittit, ut damna a Fuliginatibus, Spellanis et aliis illata repetere possint et illos convenire. 1227, Oct. 4, Anagnie.

To Master Geoffrey of Belmont, our chaplain, legate of the apostolic see. Since from the lands beyond the mountains, where we are having the cross preached against Manfred, the former Prince of Taranto, and the Saracens of Lucera, a great military force is coming to the aid of our dearest son in Christ, Charles, the illustrious King of Sicily, pursuing a cause not so much his own as that of the Church and the entire Christian people: because this same Manfred, through Pelavicino and other enemies of the Church, is trying by all means to hinder the passage of this military force, we, considering that it is of no less benefit and merit to ensure the passage of such a great army than to go to Apulia against the aforementioned Manfred and Saracens, will and by apostolic writings command you, that in the lands of your legation and the city and diocese of Bologna and other neighboring areas, you should preach and have preached the cross to procure the safe and free passage of this military force. For we grant to all truly penitent and confessed, who having taken up the sign of the cross go to procure this secure and free passage of the army, the same indulgence from their sins as was granted to those signed with the cross who crossed over to the aid of the Holy Land in the general council. And so that the faithful of Christ may more willingly run to hear the word of God, you grant an indulgence of one year and forty days, and those to whom you have entrusted the preaching, forty days, to all truly penitent and confessed who come to hear such preachings, whenever they happen to be made. Given at Perugia, on the 18th day before the Kalends of November, in the first year [of our pontificate]. 

To the priest cardinal of the title of Saint Martin in the Mountains, legate of the apostolic see. Since from the lands beyond the mountains, etc., as in the previous letter, up to: we command you, that prudently considering that the sum and state of the whole business depends on this, you immediately turn your whole mind and strength to it, and through all the lands of your legation and all your friends and relatives, with every diligence and care according to the prudence given to you by God, you watch over and labor to ensure that this same army passes freely and safely through the doubtful places of Lombardy, having about this the same urgency, since it does not admit delay, and concern so that we, who place firm hope in you on this matter, may not be disappointed in the trust conceived of you, but rather we may extol your name and you may therefore be justly commended before God and men. Moreover, you should know that by these letters, as we have arranged to be expressed in them, we do not derogate from nor intend to derogate from your legation. ### Translation to English:

To the Archbishop of Milan. Through your humble letters, you have beseeched us that, since we have previously decided that Uberto, the Marquis Pelavicino, due to his grave offenses, along with all who offer him counsel, aid, or favor, whether public or secret, should be bound by the chain of excommunication, and since the noble Marquis of Montferrat desires to be absolved from such excommunication, which he incurred by supporting the same Pelavicino, we should command the granting of the benefit of absolution to the said marquis. Therefore, having full confidence in your prudence in the Lord, we have decided to entrust this matter to you, commanding your fraternity by the authority of these presents to diligently observe the following form concerning the absolution of the Marquis of Montferrat: namely, that the said Marquis of Montferrat should first of all swear corporally to adhere to the mandates of the church and also provide a surety under penalty, as you deem appropriate; you shall command him under the obligation of the given oath that henceforth he shall neither receive letters, messages, nor gifts, large or small, from the same Pelavicino nor send any to him, as long as Pelavicino persists in the excommunication pronounced against him by the apostolic see. Moreover, he shall completely withdraw from all alliances, oaths, promises, or pacts, if any, made with the said Pelavicino until now. Concerning these mandates and their acceptance, all of which we wish to be done publicly in the presence of many ecclesiastical persons, religious and secular, and many laymen as well, you shall have a public instrument drawn up and faithfully transmitted to us. We want you to proceed with all these matters, saving other mandates of ours that we have ordered to be done concerning this same Marquis of Montferrat, either once or several times, by us or others. Once these things, as previously mentioned, have been duly completed, you shall grant the benefit of absolution regarding the sentence of excommunication to the said Marquis of Montferrat according to the form of the church. Given at Orvieto, II Kalendas Iunii, in the third year.

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Mediolanensi mandat ut marchionem de Monteferrato, qui propter favorem Uberto marchioni Pelavicino excommunicationem incurrit, sub conditionibus determinatis absolvat, praesertim si iuret stare mandatis ecclesiae et ab omni communicatione cum Pelavicino abstineat. 1229, Mai. 31, apud Urbemveterem.

To R., Cardinal Deacon of Santa Maria in Cosmedin, legate of the apostolic see. We have heard that those who render service of devotion to God and the Church in aid of the Viterbians desire to obtain remission of sins. Therefore, considering that it is fitting for the Church’s kindness to correspond to the worthy merits of its children with appropriate rewards of grace, we grant you, by the authority of these presents, the discretion to bestow such indulgence upon those who come in aid of the said Viterbians, either personally or at your call, as you see fit according to the measure of their support and the fervor of their devotion. Given at Anagni, on the fifth Ides of October, in the first year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa R. Sancte Marie in Cosmidin diacono cardinali, apostolicae sedis legato, concedit ut auxiliatoribus Viterbiensium indulgentiam largiatur. 1227, Oct. 11. Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the Guild of the Guelphs of Siena. The steadfastness of your devotion deserves to be cherished under the grace of apostolic favor, and we are more inclined to shield you from harm, the more we see the propriety of favorably supporting you with appropriate protections. In the recent feast of the dedication of the Basilica of the Apostolic Prince, having reviewed our past proceedings regarding the internal citizens of Siena, as well as the apostolic efforts and labors we have undertaken for their welfare through our various envoys, we recounted them before a multitude of faithful in the greater church of Viterbo. Observing that they have wickedly turned back and violated the oaths and promises made under certain monetary penalties to follow our commands, and further, by accumulating greater malice upon their grave excesses, they turned their eyes towards the remnants of the condemned seed, calling Conradin, the nephew of the former Emperor Frederick, into their protection by sending envoys to him. They have also rebelliously refused to admit our dearest son in Christ, Charles, the illustrious king of Sicily, whom we had sent to the Tuscan territories as a promoter of public peace. Instead, recklessly and stubbornly opposing him, they presumed to offend both him and us in many ways through him, and attempted as much as they could to do so. Therefore, lest their audacity remain unpunished, we, having previously bound them in the chain of excommunication for contemptuously disobeying our mandates, now declare them excommunicated again on the counsel of our brothers, as they have fallen into the sentence passed upon Conradin and his supporters. We declare that their persons, without danger of death or mutilation, and their movable goods, whether in France, England, or elsewhere, may be taken freely and with impunity by all. We also revoke all indulgences and any graces obtained from the apostolic see by any Sienese, as well as letters issued to them for the recovery of debts, except those that they might obtain anew from the grace of the apostolic see within three months from henceforth. However, as you have endeavored to show prompt devotion and effective faith towards the same Roman church, demonstrating it through deeds at appropriate times and places, so that we rightfully consider you devout and faithful to the same church, we are inclined to your supplications. We entirely exclude and declare you and each of you, as devoted to the aforesaid church, not to be bound by these sentences and processes by certain knowledge. We decree that the privileges, indulgences, and graces, as well as the letters concerning the recovery of your debts granted to you by the same see, shall persist in their former strength and validity for you, remaining devoted to the Roman church, without hindrance from the aforementioned sentences and processes. Let no one, therefore, violate our exclusion, declaration, and constitution, etc. Given at Viterbo, on the 12th of February, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Universitati Guelforum Senensium scribit, eos ab excommunicationis vinculo exclusos decernens, et privilegia eorum ab apostolica sede concessa pristino vigore duratura confirmans. Datum Viterbii, II Idus Februarii, anno tertio (1230).

**Translation to English:**

To the perpetual memory of the matter. With the Church of Würzburg being left without a pastor, two elections were discordantly held there: one for Boppo the provost and the other for Bartholomew of Hennemberg, a canon of the same church. These elections were then presented to our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Mainz, the metropolitan of the place. Each party petitioned him to confirm their election and reject the other, with a legal contest taking place on the matter. After various presentations and responses were exchanged, the said provost and the party that had elected him claimed to be wrongfully aggrieved by the archbishop and appealed to the apostolic see. However, the aforementioned archbishop, ignoring this appeal, confirmed the election of the said Bartholomew according to his will, ordained him a priest, and consecrated him as bishop.

Indeed, the procurator of the said provost and the party that had elected him, adhering to the constitution issued on this matter by Pope Innocent, our predecessor of happy memory, approached the apostolic see and earnestly requested us to nullify and declare void all actions taken by the archbishop regarding Bartholomew after the aforementioned appeal. We entrusted our beloved son, Master Peter Rostandi, our chaplain and general auditor of the palace, to hear what the said procurator wished to propose before him. The said chaplain summoned the opposing party to public hearings repeatedly and peremptorily, waiting beyond the period established by the constitution. As no legitimate procurator appeared on behalf of the opposing party, he diligently listened to the proposals of the procurator of the said provost and party, and later faithfully reported them in our presence and before our brethren. Having fully discussed these, it became clear that this matter had been rightfully referred to the apostolic see by the said appeal and ought to be dealt with there.

With the said procurator pursuing the matter on his party’s behalf and the other party’s obstinacy necessitating our proceeding, we found that the same archbishop, after the aforementioned appeal by which the matter had been rightfully referred to the apostolic see, had confirmed the election of the said Bartholomew improperly when the matter was entirely beyond his jurisdiction, and conferred the consecration on Bartholomew. Having summoned the party of Bartholomew to a public hearing under our mandate to hear the definitive sentence, and with them absent through obstinacy, we, with the counsel of our brethren, declare the confirmation of the election of Bartholomew attempted by the archbishop after the appeal, and anything Bartholomew presumed to do by virtue of this confirmation or attempted as bishop of Würzburg, to be null, void, and of no validity. Moreover, as far as they proceeded in fact, we nullify and annul them, decreeing that through this nullification, annulment, and declaration, no prejudice shall be generated against Bartholomew in law, should anything have been acquired for him from the election held about him. Nevertheless, it shall remain in the state it was at the time of the said appeal. Therefore, let no one… our declaration, nullification, annulment, and constitution, etc. Given at Viterbo, 9th day before the Kalends of June, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Maguntino archiepiscopo mandat ut electionem de Bertoldo de Hennemberch post appellationem ad sedem apostolicam attemptatam irritam decernat. 1239, Mai. 24, Viterbii.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man ..., the podestà, council, and people of Assisi. Maternal affection for her children always thrives, and barely a day passes without thoughts of their miserable state or reflections upon it. Indeed, this is what happens concerning you, special sons of the Church, placed under the distress of continuous persecution, whom the Church frequently holds before her eyes with sorrow, sighing because at present no help can come from it to provide you with the comfort you desire. But she hopes from the abundance of divine mercy that it will soon open the eye of compassion toward you and others suffering for the Church and kindly grant the grace of the expected end to your anxieties. Therefore, beloved sons, who wished long ago to endure many dangers as soldiers of Christ so that the privilege of ecclesiastical freedom might not be broken in you, until the day of hoped-for tranquility arrives and the shadows of present discord diminish. Remain strong in spirit and steadfast in mind in the faith and devotion of your mother Church, believing that since the great quantity of your merits can never be erased from the memory of the Church, the pious affections of the Apostolic See will, at the right time, be most ready to reward you with the deserved grace and favor for bearing the penalty of such a struggle, especially since its gracious kindness often overflows so much that it pursues with maternal affection not only those sons placed, as it were, in its bosom but even those for whom the merits of devotion intercede in distant places. Given as above.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro potestati, consilio et populo Asisinatibus significat ecclesiam, quamvis ob angustias praesentis temporis auxilium praestare non possit, de divina clementia sperare ut cito consolationem afferat, hortaturque ut in fide et devotione fortiter persistant. Datum ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To G., Cardinal Priest of the Title of St. Lawrence in Lucina, Legate of the Apostolic See. 

Instructed by the teaching of the Supreme King, who, though stable, allows all things to be moved, makes His spirits angels and ministers, and, descending from the height of the heavens to redeem mankind, became man. He sent the disciples He chose to preach the Gospel to the entire world. Entrusted, despite our insufficient merits, to the ministry of the Apostolic See, which God founded as the mother and teacher of all the faithful upon Himself, the cornerstone, we must lift our eyes and consider the children coming from afar, whom we cannot visit in body. The affection increases for what sight is denied, educating them to salvation through others in whom we have undoubted confidence, exercising such care, desiring to preserve the offspring of adoption, whom the Church, the bride of Christ, has borne, in safety, that she may glory in her fruitfulness in the Lord. 

Although we, undeserving as we are, have been set by the Lord, according to the prophecy of Jeremiah, over peoples and kingdoms to manage the universal care of the entire earth wherever the name of the Lord is invoked, among all the desires of our heart, we chiefly yearn for the salvation of souls, the growth of ecclesiastical freedom, the benefit of peace, and the good of quiet in all places of the faithful. We vigilantly labor with zealous care and apply what effort we can, so that these may, with the removal of any impediments, laudably come to fruition according to the fullness of our desire with the Lord's help. 

However, that spiritual advancement may come about in the provinces of Bremen, Magdeburg, Salzburg, and Gniezno, and that peace, tranquility, and ecclesiastical freedom may be nurtured, we desire all the more fervently as we have a special affection for those parts. Therefore, so that these provinces may advance more in the devotion to God and the Roman Church, feeling themselves specially encouraged by the presence of a legate of the Apostolic See sent from our side, behold, we have appointed you, a great and honorable member of the Church, a man conspicuous in religion, adorned with honesty of morals, endowed with knowledge of letters, and circumspect in prudence, whom among our other brethren we hold in great esteem due to your meritoriousness, to the aforementioned provinces, committing to you the full office of legation in them, with the counsel of our aforementioned brethren. So that, as laborers in the eleventh hour of the day, we are appointed in the vineyard of the Lord, you may in our place, as a diligent worker, uproot and destroy, scatter and disperse, build and plant, as the Lord will provide you with opportunities. 

From you, indeed, since purity of conscience assists you and the judgment of reason is readily available, we firmly hope that, guiding the straightforward and directing the indirect, you will turn the rough into smooth. Wherefore, we earnestly beseech and exhort your discretion, enjoining you in remission of your sins, that you willingly accept in the name of God and ours the office of this legation committed to you, and strive to execute it with diligence according to the prudence given to you by God, so that you may thereby merit divine grace and glory, and that we may boast in the Lord of having sent a faithful and useful vicar, and that the clergy and people have received an angel of salvation and peace from your legation. 

Given at Perugia, on the 8th day before the Ides of June, in the first year of our (pontificate).

This is especially true since there is clear evidence that peace and security will prevail if that wild nation, a minister of destruction, can be crushed by the triumph of the divine right hand or driven from the borders of the defeated.
