For we, that we may joyfully and easily see come to pass what we so piously and justly desire, grant to all those who, having taken the sign of the cross in Germany, proceed into Hungary against the Tartar ferocity, the same indulgence and privilege that is granted in the general council to those going to the aid of the Holy Land. However, so that the matter of such great salvation, by which many are touched by remedies, may receive the desired increase of prosperity, we grant you and those whom you appoint to preach the cross, by the authority of these presents, that you may impart the benefit of absolution according to the form of the Church to those marked with the cross who have incurred the bond of excommunication for arson and laying hands on clerics or other religious persons, provided they make competent satisfaction to those who suffered injury and damage, and their excess is not so grave and enormous that for this reason they should be sent to the Apostolic See. But you, brother patriarch, when the truth about the return of the Tartars has been made known to you at the suggestion of the said king, may cause all those marked with the character of the cross to proceed promptly and swiftly to Hungary with the angel of salvation as their guide. Given at Anagni, on the 12th day before the Kalends of August, in the first year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa patriarche Aquilegensi mandat ut fideles Christiani in Theutonia constituti contra Tartaros crucem suscipiant et in Ungariam proficiscantur, concedens indulgentias sicut pro subsidio Terre Sancte. Dat. Anagnie, XII Kal. Aug. anno primo (1227).

**Translation to English:**

To Wlodizlaus, Archbishop-elect of Salzburg. Considering the multiple and grave afflictions, distresses, and oppressions that our venerable brother, Ulric, the former Archbishop of Salzburg, has endured since the time he was transferred to the archbishopric from various causes, and that he was never able to fully possess the archbishopric or enjoy its revenues and goods, nor was he able to benefit himself or others from it, and that he complained of spending empty months and laborious nights, feeling he had run in vain, being exhausted by harsh troubles and shaken by various floods of disturbances, and that because rest was not given to the weary, he finally resigned the governance of the archbishopric through a procurator especially appointed for this purpose in our hands: we sympathize with him regarding these tribulations and are affectionately moved, deeming it fitting and due to mercifully extend a hand of grace to him, thereby advising him with the gift of our providence so that, relieved from his distress, he might breathe in the kindness of the Apostolic See. Therefore, since, as the petition of the aforesaid Ulric presented to us contained, he was bound by the bond of excommunication due to the debts he owed to the Roman Church, we, wishing to act kindly with him concerning this, command that you absolve the said Ulric from the bond of such excommunication without any difficulty, by our authority, through yourself or another, according to the form of the Church, publicly declaring and having him declared absolved at all places where it shall be expedient, and also dispensing with him concerning any irregularity he may have incurred by celebrating divine offices while so bound, appointing him as bishop and pastor to the Secovian Church, from which he was transferred to the aforesaid archbishopric and which our predecessor Pope Alexander of happy memory granted him to retain together with the same archbishopric by the counsel of his brothers, until he should peacefully acquire full possession of the archbishopric, by the same authority; providing him with the same, so that he may enjoy its peaceful possession, and ensuring that due and devoted obedience and reverence be shown to him by his subjects. We also wish and command that the Church of Piber, in the diocese of Secovian, which, as we understand, the aforesaid Ulric by virtue of a concession made by our predecessor Pope Innocent of happy memory, held and still holds together with the aforesaid Secovian Church, by the grace of such concession be lawfully retained by him with the aforesaid Secovian Church as long as he lives, notwithstanding any constitution of the general council or any other contrary decree, or that Warner, the vicar of the Church of St. George of your diocese or anyone else has obtained apostolic letters concerning the provision for him of the said church, which we declare null as regards the same Church of Piber, or if it has been granted to anyone by the Apostolic See that they cannot be interdicted, suspended, or excommunicated or drawn outside certain places by apostolic letters which do not make full and express mention of such indulgence or its full tenor verbatim, or any other general or even special indulgence granted by the Apostolic See in whatever form or expression of words, of which it is necessary to make special and express mention in our letters, and by which the effect of the present letters might in any way be hindered or delayed; restraining the contradictors by ecclesiastical censure, appeal being set aside. Given at Perugia, on the third day before the Calends of December, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa Wlodizlao electo Salzburgensi mandat ut Ulricum quondam archiepiscopum Salzburgensem ab excommunicatione absolvat et eum praeficiat in episcopum ecclesiae Secoviensis; dat. Perusii, III Kalendas Decembris, anno primo.

**Translation to English:**

To O. Cardinal Deacon of Saint Adrian, legate of the Apostolic See. In the matter of the empire, in which our dearest sons in Christ, A. the illustrious King of Castile and León, and Richard elected as King of the Romans, claim the right through elections, which they assert were held for them, a citation was issued some time ago by Pope Urban of blessed memory, our predecessor, under a certain form, that the same elects should appear before the same predecessor through suitable procurators at a certain term. And finally, within that term, our venerable brother Martin, Bishop of León, and our beloved sons, Master John Alfonsi, our chaplain, Archdeacon of Compostela, and Radulf de Podio Bonizi, appearing before the same predecessor for the named king, from whom they had sufficient mandate concerning this, among other things, requested that the same king be summoned to receive the imperial diadem from the hands of the same predecessor, and to proceed in the aforesaid matter according to other petitions presented by them and then repeated in the presence of the same predecessor and brothers, notwithstanding the absence of the opposing party. However, our beloved sons Master William, Archdeacon of Rochester, William de Corneria, our chaplains, and Robert de Baro, who had previously prosecuted this matter for the same elect, presented certain letters of excuse for him, excusing the absence of the same elect, whose causes, namely the turmoil of the Kingdom of England and others, they claimed to be notorious, alleging in many ways that it was not appropriate to proceed in the said matter with him absent and thus impeded. The aforesaid predecessor, having fully understood these and other things proposed on both sides and having discussed them thoroughly with the aforesaid brothers, decided, after deliberation with the same brothers, to suspend his process in the said matter, concerning the matters contained in the aforesaid citation, for the aforesaid and other just and evident reasons. And therefore, the rights of the parties and the matter itself remaining entirely in their previous state, he extended the term up to a year, to be calculated from the forthcoming feast of Saint Andrew the Apostle. And although in the term thus extended by the same predecessor and even after it, the named Master Radulf, notary, envoy, and procurator of the aforesaid king, appeared before us, urgently requesting, as he had requested before, that we proceed in the said matter, we, however, more diligently considering that although the entire number of edicts had been finished by the said predecessor, it is nevertheless proper and in accordance with law that at least one edict should emanate from us, have decided not to proceed in the aforesaid matter at present, and have suspended it until the Friday following the forthcoming feast of the Epiphany of the Lord, immediately following, and have determined that the same elects should be assigned this day as a peremptory term according to the prescribed manner contained in the extension of the said term made by the aforesaid predecessor as mentioned. Therefore, we command that you, on our behalf, cause the aforesaid R., elected as King of the Romans, to be peremptorily cited by you or by another, so that he may present himself before the apostolic see by the aforesaid day, in person or through a suitable procurator sufficiently instructed for the aforesaid matters. You should strive to inform us of the day and form of the citation and whatever you may do in this regard through your patent letters containing the series of these matters. Given at Viterbo, 2nd Kalends of May, in the 11th year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa O. Sancti Adriani diacono cardinali, apostolice sedis legato mandat, ut Riccardus in Romanorum regem electus citetur, ut se vel procuratorem idoneum ad diem peremptorium coram apostolica sede repraesentet; diem citationis et quidquid inde fecerit nuntiare studeat. Datum Viterbii, II Kalendas Maii, pontificatus anno undecimo.

**Translation to English:**

Innocent, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son, the noble man Alberico of Romano, greetings and apostolic blessing. Since your brother, Ezzelino of Romano, for many reasons and probable arguments, has long been held suspect of heresy, we have deemed it necessary to proceed with an inquisition against him by religious men. These investigators, having diligently inquired and discovered that he deserved to be considered suspect in this matter, finally sent messengers to the Apostolic See, to whom we appointed our venerable brother, the bishop of Sabina, as a listener. Before him, they offered to swear on Ezzelino's soul that E. believed in God and the Catholic faith according to what the Roman Church holds and teaches should be believed. But since this purgation was not accepted by the said bishop or by us, because such a purgation for so great a crime should be made not through a messenger but in person before us, we set a specific deadline for him to present himself to the apostolic presence to take action according to the order of reason, with full assurance of personal safety in coming and going.

However, because he neither came nor sent anyone within that period, nor afterward, he, being already ensnared by the chains of multiple excommunications, and justly suspected of erring in regard to the Catholic faith, we have resolved to bind him with the bond of anathema, assigning him another deadline to appear in our presence, to obey the mandates of the Church concerning the aforementioned matters, publicly declaring that unless he did so by the deadline, we would proceed more severely against him according to canonical and legitimate sanctions.

Since, therefore, he has despised to come or send, although waited for beyond the term, with damnable obstinacy, and now for not only a year but for two years he has endured the mentioned anathema, despising the keys of the Church, we should not further delay canonical judgment against him, whom such a long evasion and such hard obstinacy render guilty of such a crime: considering the aforementioned Ezzelino as a heretic, we have decided, with the counsel of our brothers, that he should be subjected to the sanctions promulgated against heretics unless he takes care to appear before us by the forthcoming Kalends of August, precisely to obey our and the Church's commands and decisions, a term which we have deemed to grant him from the great kindness of the Apostolic See, since we prefer him to be saved rather than perish.

In order that your always pleasing and prompt devotion, which you have always shown in the Church's affairs, may be rewarded, and that the impious labors of the same E. may be justly punished, all the goods that have legitimately come to him, which he now renders himself unworthy of, we grant and donate to you— notwithstanding any sales, donations, or alienations made by the same E. to the late Emperor Frederick, even when he was not excommunicated, or to his familiars or any other persons, after he adhered to the excommunicated F., or by will or any last testament in which he would intend to leave the aforementioned goods to another than you, or that he obtained your goods adjudicated to him by the same F.— if the aforementioned E. does not appear before us by the aforementioned Kalends to obey our commands and decisions, we grant and donate from special grace by the authority of these presents. Let no man whatsoever infringe this page of our concession and donation, under penalty of incurring divine wrath. Given at Lyon, the fifth day before the Nones of July, in the eighth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Alberico de Romano mandat ut, si Ezelinus de Romano frater eius, suspectus heresis, ad Kalendas Augusti non comparuerit coram sede apostolica pariturus mandatis ecclesiae, omnia bona Ezelini sibi concedat et donet. Lugduni, V Non. Iulii, anno octavo pontificatus.

**Translation to English:**

To G. de Montelongo, our subdeacon and notary, legate of the Apostolic See. By the tenor of these presents, we wish to inform you that, since recently the prince has requested us through solemn envoys and letters concerning the restoration of peace between the Church and himself, because we truly cherish peace and sincerely desire the unity of concord among Christians, lest we seem to reject the negotiation of this peace and thereby the prince might seize the occasion to defame the Church as usual, we have sent special envoys to him, offering him that form of peace through them, which seemed to be expedient for the Church and its devoted followers and even for the said prince. But the same prince, not accepting this form, sent envoys again to the Apostolic See, whose petitions, wherein neither the honor of the Church nor the welfare of its faithful appeared to be procured, we did not think fit to agree to, they departed from our presence with the matter of peace entirely unresolved. Wherefore, we command that you endeavor, as you see fit, with earnest inducements to encourage the faithful and devoted to the Church established in the regions of Lombardy to steadfastly persevere in their usual devotion and to persist in their services, informing them on our behalf that we intend to restore peace between the Church and the aforementioned prince with them and other devoted to the Church, as it seems expedient to the Church and them, and not otherwise. Given at Anagni, 23rd of September, in the first year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa G. de Montelongo, subdiacono et notario suo, sedis apostolicae legato, mandat ut fideles et devotos ecclesiae in partibus Lombardie animet, ut in devotione solita perseverent, significans eis intentionem reformandi pacem inter ecclesiam et principem memoratum. 1230, Sept. 23. Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Siena. Desiring to preserve intact the rights of our beloved son, the noble man William, Count Palatine, our loyal subject, and to guard against any harm to the merchants of Siena, we command that you expressly prohibit on our behalf both those same merchants and all under your jurisdiction from accepting any castle or revenues of the County of Ildebrandisci from the prince or his envoys or deputies as a pledge for any sum of money. You are to pronounce a sentence of excommunication by our authority against those who act contrary, and to ensure that they are publicly declared excommunicated throughout your city and diocese. Furthermore, we declare null and void any actions attempted by those same prince, envoys, and deputies against this prohibition concerning the lands and revenues of the said county to the prejudice of the aforesaid count. Given at the Lateran, 16th January, in the first year. In the same manner, to the Bishop of Florence against the Florentine merchants.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Senensi mandat, ut mercatoribus Senensibus et subiectis iurisdictioni suae prohibeat accipere castra vel redditus comitatus Ildebrandiscit a principe eiusque nuntiis pignore, sub poena excommunicationis, decernens irritum quidquid contra hanc inhibitionem agatur. 1227, Ian. 16, Laterani.

Translation to English:

To G. de Montelongo, our subdeacon and notary, legate of the apostolic see. The reverend brother of ours, the patriarch of Aquileia, is bound to assist the devoted sons of the apostolic see more effectively, inasmuch as the same see, treating him with greater grace and favor like a pious mother, has entrusted some persons to him as part of his care, preferring him confidently among others as a noble member of the church. But, as we have heard with amazement and report with distress, he, who ought to have stood as a wall for the defense of ecclesiastical liberty, distrustingly attacked the beloved sons of Treviso, devoted to the church, according to his own will and invaded their district with hostilities, not without a multitude of armed men, inflicting on them serious damages and not insignificant injuries. However, as it is unworthy for those who, inflamed with zeal and devotion, valiantly and powerfully oppose the enemies of the church, to be wickedly attacked by those who are bound to defend them from the incursions of others, we earnestly request, admonish, and exhort the same patriarch, giving him our letters of mandate, to cease henceforth from all harassment of the Trevisans out of reverence for the apostolic see and ourselves. Wherefore, we command you that if the said patriarch neglects to fulfill our mandate, you compel him to do so, by our authority and without appeal, after a warning has been given to him—notwithstanding the constitution concerning the two [warnings]. Given at the Lateran, 7 Ides of November, in the first year [of our pontificate].

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa G. de Montelongo subdiacono et notario suo, apostolicae sedis legato, mandat ut, si patriarcha Aquileiensis ab molestatione Tervisinorum non desistat, eum ad id auctoritate apostolica compellat. 1227, Nov. 7, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To ensure the certainty of these presents and the memory of future events. On the feast of the dedication of the Basilica of the Prince of the Apostles, in the third year of our pontificate, we have deemed it necessary, with the advice of our brothers and in accordance with justice, to proceed against the city and commune of the Firmans, their podestà, captain, councilors, and other rulers at that time, and the citizens of the same city, due to their various notorious excesses and manifest contumacies, to sentences of interdict and excommunication, as well as to the imposition of penalties and various threats under certain conditions. Among other things, we assigned them a peremptory term within which they were to return to our and the Church's commands, openly warning them that if they did not heed our admonitions, we would proceed against them more severely both spiritually and temporally. However, they, continuing their usual stubborn rebellion, contemptuously ignored the command to return to our and the Church's mandates according to the aforementioned edict of our process; for this reason, we declare the aforesaid podestà, captain, councilors, and others by whom the said city is governed, and its citizens, to be under the sentence of excommunication, and the city and commune themselves to be subject to the interdict due to the aforesaid causes. Nonetheless, due to these same reasons and also because of their increased stubbornness, we newly pronounce s

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz. The wickedness of certain iniquitous men, like a consuming fire, blinds their counsel to such an extent that, unable to behold the sun of justice, they not only fail to desist from things that are hostile to the Bride of Christ, the Church, but also sharpen their tongues against her, arm their hands, and shamelessly unleash their strength, challenging the defenders of the faith with hostility. Therefore, not giving preference to man over God, you have pronounced sentences of excommunication and interdict upon their lands, even declaring some deposed. So that their immense audacity does not incite others to sin through the ruinous example, if it remains unpunished, we, confirming these sentences with apostolic authority, command that you solemnly renew them every Sunday and feast day with bells ringing and candles lit throughout the neighboring regions; those who oppose, etc. Given at the Lateran, 11th of April, in the first year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino mandat, ut sententias excommunicationis et interdicti, auctoritate apostolica confirmatas, sollempniter innovari faciat dominicis et festivis diebus. 1228, Apr. 11. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the knowledge of the present and the memory of future generations. We recount with public voice and not without bitterness of mind the nefarious and horrible crime perpetrated in recent days in the regions of Tuscany by men of bloodshed, and we proceed to punish it with the most fervent attention, as the graver penalty is scarcely sufficient for revenge, because the commission of such a crime has redounded to the greater insult and offense against God, the injury of the Apostolic See, and the scandal of many. For when the bishop of Silves of blessed memory and our beloved sons, the dean and the archdeacon of Salamanca, the late knight Arnaldus, and several others from their company and households, both clerics and laymen, were traveling through Tuscany to approach the same see for certain business, Raynerius de Paczis, a son of damnation, and Scarcalupus de Safena, along with many accomplices and followers, both horsemen and foot soldiers, suspected their arrival and ambushed them along the path, setting aside the fear of God and entirely devoid of the duty of humanity. They violently attacked the bishop and the others mentioned, and apart from a few who either escaped by flight or were left as if dead having been severely wounded and some taken captive, they cruelly slaughtered them, miserably plundering their spoils.

Therefore, so that the harshness of vengeance may equally weigh upon the perpetrators of this extremely pernicious and detestable crime,

**Translation to English:**

To the subprior of the Order of Preachers at Paris. We bear sincere affection towards our beloved son, the noble man T., Count of Flanders, so that we may willingly and graciously heed his petitions, whom we pursue with the prerogative of favor and special grace. Therefore, as was proposed before us on behalf of the count, he had formerly acted in a hostile manner against certain of his enemies, not as if against devout men of the Church, with Hentius, intending to avenge serious offenses that had been inflicted upon him by the same. Our beloved son G. de Montelongo, subdeacon and notary, legate of the Apostolic See, is said to have pronounced a sentence of excommunication against him on this basis alone. Wherefore, he humbly requested us to order that he be absolved from the aforesaid sentence of excommunication by some discreet persons. Therefore, seeking from a purer heart what pertains to the status and honor of his person, we command that you bestow upon him the benefit of absolution according to the form of the Church on our behalf. For we wish and command that the letters which the aforementioned count obtained from us shall have their due force, notwithstanding this excommunication. Given at the Lateran, on the Ides of January, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa subpriori ordinis fratrum Praedicatorum Parisiensium mandat ut T. comiti Flandriae, a G. de Montelongo legato excommunicato, absolutionis beneficium impendat. 1228, Ian. 13. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To Roland of Cremona, of the Order of Preachers. We have learned from trustworthy reports that Ezzelino da Romano, an enemy of virtues and a persecutor of the faith, offends God and the Apostolic See in many ways, but especially in that he scorns the keys of the Church, harbors heretics, and associates with them indiscriminately, such that he is suspected of and publicly notorious for the stain of heretical depravity. However, lest such a horrid and harmful pestilence should, God forbid, lead to the peril of the faithful unless the authority of the Apostolic See promptly applies an appropriate remedy, we command you through apostolic writings, by virtue of obedience, to diligently investigate the truth concerning this matter, having God alone before your eyes, and to faithfully report to us what you have found in your letters. Moreover — notwithstanding the constitution of two days’ edict issued in the general council and the personal absence of the same Ezzelino — because he is known to be terrible and powerful, you should publicly summon him in nearby places where it can be done more safely, with the people standing by. Given at the Lateran, March 4, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Rolando Cremonensi de ordine fratrum Predicatorum mandat, ut de crimine heresis Ezelini de Romano diligenter inquirat et eum publice citet. 1227, Mar. 4, Laterani.

On behalf of the beloved sons, the abbot and convent of the Liessies Monastery of the Order of Saint Benedict in the diocese of Cambrai have brought before us that our predecessor, Pope Urban of blessed memory, requested prelates, chapters, colleges, convents, and other ecclesiastical persons both secular and regular, exempt and non-exempt, who resided in the territories of the beloved daughter in Christ, the noblewoman, Countess of Flanders, by reason of her dominion and fiefs within the same diocese and the Tournai diocese, among others in the kingdom of France and certain other provinces, to provide a tithe of all their ecclesiastical revenues for the aid of the kingdom of Sicily, through letters issued in a specific form, with your authority as executor granted by letters of the same predecessor. **Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Tarantasia and the Bishop of Maurienne. Since our beloved daughter in Christ, the noblewoman I., Countess of Flanders, with the spontaneous and legitimate consent of her sister, the noblewoman M., Lady of Dampierre, who is to succeed her if she outlives the former, has decided to grant to our beloved son in Christ, the nobleman T., Count of Flanders, her husband, an annual income of six thousand pounds of Artois, to be received from certain possessions and revenues of hers, for as long as he lives, through a provident liberality, as is more fully contained in the letters drawn up by these noblewomen, the tenors of which we have copied word for word into our letters. We, considering what these noblewomen have done in this matter to be pleasing and valid, have decided to confirm it with apostolic authority. We command that you do not allow the aforementioned count to be unduly harassed by anyone against the tenor of our confirmation concerning the aforementioned matters, and that you restrain such harassers. — not withstanding the constitution concerning two days' journey established in the general council. If not both, then one of you, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the eighth day before the Ides of December, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Tarantasiensi et episcopo Maurianensi mandat, ut non permittant comitem Flandrie super annuo sex milium librarum Artisiensium redditu ab aliqua persona indebite molestari, confirmationem apostolicam concedens actis comitissae Flandrie et dominae de Dampetra. 1227, Dec. 8, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man... Landgrave of Thuringia. We give thanks to the giver of all graces, for, as we have learned and indeed accepted, with Him mercifully inspiring your mind with the fear of His name and love, acknowledging your power of greatness from Him alone, who has the power in the kingdom of men, you venerate His bride, the Church, and ecclesiastical persons. Offering and exposing yourself to the apostolic see and our good pleasures with eager faith and ready devotion, you desire to please us with both will and action. Therefore, embracing your person with the prerogative of love and grace, and inclined by your devout prayers, we confirm with apostolic authority all the feuds that you are known to hold from the churches of Germany, as you now possess them reasonably and peacefully, and we protect them with the patronage of this present writing. Let no one, therefore, infringe our confirmation, etc. If anyone, however, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the Ides of April, in the first year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro Landgravio Thuringiae confirmat auctoritate apostolica omnia feuda quae ab ecclesiis Germaniae tenet, sicut ea nunc rationabiliter possidet et quiete. 1227, Apr. 13. Laterani.

Translation to English:

To the elected of Cologne. A petition sent to us on your behalf contained that certain prelates and other clerics of the city and diocese of Cologne have taken arms against you alongside the noble man, the count of Jülich, at the time of your capture. You, due to such an excessive act, have pronounced a sentence of excommunication against them by your own authority, which, demanding justice, you requested to be fortified by apostolic support. Wherefore, we command that, if it is so, these sacrilegious individuals are to be avoided until they have satisfactorily compensated you and the Church of Cologne for such great injury. And should they persist in their obstinacy for a year, deprive them of their personates, dignities, and other ecclesiastical benefits and prebends, ensuring that they are conferred to suitable persons by those to whom their bestowal is known to pertain; contradicters, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the second Ides of January, in the first year.

Regesto in Latin:

Innocentius IV papa electo Coloniensi mandat ut, si prelati et clerici Colonienses cum comite Iuliacensi armati contra eum insurrexerint, sententiam excommunicationis confirmet et, si per annum in pertinacia persistunt, eos ab ecclesiasticis dignitatibus privet. 1244, Jan. 12. Laterani.

To G. de Montelongo, our subdeacon and notary, legate of the apostolic see. Above all other devotees of the Roman Church, your famous city has frequently made itself agreeable and pleasing to it through the purity of faith, fervor of devotion, and firmness of constancy; from these, you gain the merit of eternal glory, human praise, and continuous gratitude from the Apostolic See. To the illustrious King of Castile and León, elected as King of the Romans. Although the multitude of great affairs continuously surrounds us, and although various concerns frequently invade our heart, their constant anxiety often demands us to resolve those pressing matters that fall within the duty of our office. Nevertheless, the urgency of the matter concerning the governance of the empire, due to its nature and our pursuit of it, demands immediate attention and causes us greater anxiety and distress, as the delay poses a severe danger to nearly the entire Christian populace, and we would hope for greater benefits from a swift resolution of the empire's organization.

Indeed, we observe and almost daily experience the countless and vast dangers that, as asserted by you and our beloved son in Christ, R., elected as King of the Romans, claiming the right to this empire acquired through various elections, the instability of the empire brings about. From such instability, the Church is deprived of the imperial defense, and the empire's enemies, not without risk to the Christian faith, attack more boldly. They wrongfully seize the rights of the empire with violence, and as the subjects of the empire engage in mutual injuries among themselves, no usual remedy of secular judgment is available.

These, beloved son, and other dangers not easily recounted, which the prolonged delay in the provision of the empire brings about, urgently call upon us and frequently trouble our mind, so that we may finally and swiftly focus on resolving the aforementioned matter with full dedication. Recently, within the term set by us for this purpose, the aforementioned R., elected, with his firstborn son Henry, and some other envoys and procurators, appeared before us, and for you, our beloved son, Master Radulf of Podio Bonizi appeared. With various issues proposed on both sides, both in fact and in law, the procurators of the said R., elected, presented various documents to support their intention and argued that Master Radulf, or anyone on your behalf, should not be admitted to oppose their petition, as it was evident that you had no interest, especially since the said Master relied solely on unsupported assertions and did not present any letters or other evidence.

The said Master, replying that the form of summons issued by us did not compel him at that time to prove anything in your name, especially since during the time of our predecessor Pope Alexander, of happy memory, full faith in your right, which he also asserted to be notorious, had been established through the decree of your election and various other letters, nonetheless, upon our instruction to state whether he wished to further substantiate your right, he stated that he would prove his assertions, on which he also presented certain articles, in Germany, France, Spain, and Italy, as well as in our court within delays appropriate for such a significant matter.

We, although surprised that you, a prince of such discretion, had sent a messenger to such a difficult matter so unprepared, namely without presenting any form of evidence regarding your right, nevertheless, wishing to show paternal kindness to you, decided to admit the aforementioned articles, as well as others presented by the opposing party. We set a definitive term after the feast of the Annunciation of the Blessed Virgin, the first one to come, with the advice of our brothers, whereby you and the opposing party, with your procurators, may present to the apostolic presence all the testimonies that may be produced on these articles and all other actions, reasons, documents, and rights.

We shall then proceed, whether you send such procurators or not, whether you pursue proving your intention or perhaps omit it, as we do not wish this matter to become immortal to the great harm of the entire world, finally to its resolution, as justice may suggest and we shall see fit, with divine favor granting clemency. To prevent any further delays requested by you on account of the witnesses to be produced, we desire that in Germany at Frankfurt, in France at Paris, in Spain at Burgos, in Italy at Bologna, and also in our aforementioned court before those we shall designate, on the eve of the feast of All Saints to come, which we have set as a definitive term for the production of witnesses to commence on both sides, both you and the opposing party strive to produce the witnesses you wish to produce, and to see them sworn in by suitable procurators. Given at Viterbo, on the 7th day before the Ides of May, in the third year.

To Simon, cardinal priest of the title of St. Martin, apostolic legate. In carrying out the office of apostolic service entrusted to us by the Lord, although unworthy, we shake off the slumber of lethargy from our eyes, as granted to us from above, and raise them to vigilant watchfulness all around. Thus, considering what is necessary for the diligent care of the flock entrusted to us, we might devote attention to the prosperous state of its parts with attentive solicitude. Our mind is particularly stirred by this, and our intentions and desires revolve especially around the fact that, when we see the Holy Roman Church, mother of nations, illustrious bride of Christ, afflicted by her persecutors with grave injuries, subjected to various insults and struck by enormous losses, we pass sleepless nights and do not indulge in leisure by day, diligently endeavoring and striving with laborious effort to care for that same Church and her faithful and children, who experience the discomforts of maternal persecution and share her pains and anxieties, to be liberated from the imminent storms of tempest with God's favor.

However, due to the variety of countless tasks incumbent upon us and the storm of persecution growing stronger against the boat of Peter, whose helm we hold as the Lord has pleased, although our mind is drawn in various directions by care, we cannot be present everywhere, for we cannot exceed the limits of human capability to execute the power given to us by the Lord simultaneously in different regions. Following the example of Him who, exercising the office of legation committed to Him in the region of sinners, sent the disciples He had chosen into the whole world, instructing His vicar to sometimes call others to share His care, when the duty of His office is prevented by bodily absence, we confidently call upon those to bear our burdens with us, whom we hope, based on the experienced industry we have observed in them, to be very useful and of whose virtues given by the Lord we have full confidence.

Therefore, in matters of great importance, we choose the best persons for their execution, so that with God's guidance, they may be directed usefully and beneficially according to our hearts. Thus, directing the gaze of apostolic consideration to your person and duly observing the virtues with which the Lord of virtues has adorned it, we firmly hold in hope and trust that, with Him guiding your actions and making your way prosperous, even crooked paths will be made straight and rough places plain through your ministry of diligence. Therefore, obtaining full confidence in the Lord from your sincerity, we commit to you by the authority of these presents the governance of the duchy of Spoleto and the march of Ancona and Massa Trabaria, as well as the cities and dioceses and their districts of Perugia, Castellan, Todi, Narni, Terni, and Rieti, both in spiritual and temporal matters, granting you the full authority to do whatever you know expedient for the honor of the Roman Church and the benefit of the faithful residing there in both spheres. Moreover, in the duchy, march, cities, dioceses, and districts mentioned, as well as in Romagna, the patriarchates of Grado and Aquileia, except for those cities and their dioceses and districts which are part of the province of Lombardy, we have decided to fully commit to your circumspection the office of legation, so that, according to the prudence given to you by God, you may uproot and destroy, build and plant, as you see fit. Therefore, we command that, receiving this burden of legation and governance with devotion and endeavoring to bear it patiently, you diligently strive to exercise the aforementioned governance and office in such a praiseworthy manner that you may find God more propitious to you as a result and us more strongly bound to your benefit. For we will uphold the sentences and penalties which you impose spiritually and temporally on the rebels of the duchy, march, cities, dioceses, and districts mentioned, and the sentences which you impose on other rebels of the legation committed to you, and will ensure with the Lord’s help that they are inviolably observed.

Let no one therefore etc. violate our grant etc. If anyone etc. Given at Lyon, 24 January, in the second year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Leodiensi indulget, ut generalibus litteris impetratis seu impetrandis non possit procedi ad conferenda beneficia vel prebendas ad suam collationem pertinentes in Coloniensi provincia vel sua civitate et diocesi. 1245, Ian. 24. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the citizens of Cologne and all townspeople established throughout the province of Cologne. If children, whom human nature has produced to their mothers, show themselves to be obedient so that they may always deserve to be blessed by them, then with even greater reason should the children of spiritual mothers, from whom they receive spiritual gifts, be bound to serve and alleviate the burdens of their spiritual mother with appropriate assistance, since spiritual things are more worthy than corporeal or natural ones. Therefore, since the Church of Cologne, your mother, as we have learned from the report of our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Cologne, is pressed by the heavy burden of debts, we have deemed it necessary to earnestly request and exhort your community, commanding you by decree to prudently consider that it is in some way in your interest that the resources of that church are not swallowed by the abyss of usury. For the reverence of the Apostolic See and ourselves, you should strive to offer such assistance from your goods to the said archbishop for the payment of the mentioned debts, so that he may be more strongly encouraged towards your advantages and that we may commend your devotion for this reason. Otherwise, we give mandate by our letters to our beloved sons, the dean of the Apostles Peter and Andrew, the provost, and Master John, canon of Paderborn, that they compel you to this with prior admonition through ecclesiastical censure, removing any appeal. Given at Lyons, the 11th day before the Kalends of January, in the second year. It was written to them with the provision that neither the people of Cologne nor any town community should be struck with a sentence of excommunication or interdict, etc. What if not all, etc. Given as in the previous one.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa civibus Coloniensibus et universis opidanis per Coloniensem provinciam mandat, ut ob gravia debitorum onera ecclesiae Coloniensis, bona sua in subsidium praebeant. 1239, Dec. 22. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man, the Duke of Saxony. Although the union of marital bond in the fourth degree of consanguinity or affinity is forbidden by sacred canons, the Roman Church sometimes provides dispensation, especially when urgent necessity or evident utility demands it. Since, as was presented before us on your behalf, you desire to marry the noble woman Helena, daughter of our beloved son, the nobleman O., Duke of Brunswick, who is related to you in the fourth degree of consanguinity on both sides, for the purpose of restoring peace between you and the Duke, with whom you are known to have had a serious war for a long time, we, considering the good that can arise from this, as we have learned from trustworthy sources, and the great tranquility that would be brought to those parts, inclined by your prayers and those of the aforementioned Duke, grant you full authority by the present letters to enter into marriage legitimately with her, with whom you are said to have already contracted a betrothal, the aforementioned consanguinity notwithstanding, and to lawfully remain in the contracted marriage. Let no one... of our concession... Given at the Lateran, on the Ides of May, in the first year. II. To the noble woman Helena, daughter of our beloved son, the nobleman, Duke of Brunswick. Although the union, etc. as above until: demands it. Since, as was presented on behalf of our beloved son, the nobleman, the Duke of Saxony, before us, etc. inclined by your prayers and those of the aforementioned Dukes of Saxony and Brunswick, your father, etc.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius III papa nobili viro duci Saxonie concedit facultatem plenam matrimonialem cum Helena, filia ducis de Brunsvich, licet in quarto consanguinitatis gradu contingant, ad pacem inter eos reformandam. 1216, Mai. 15. Datum Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the authority, council, and people of Narni. Because it is fitting that appropriate rewards are given to everyone according to their merits, it is right to reward the faithful and devoted to the Church, especially those whom the necessity of the present time has tested, with worthy prizes, and to punish with due penalty the inconstancy of the unfaithful and disloyal. Thus, the reward of the former may lead others to serve the Church, and the punishment of the latter may deter the rest from daring to sin. Therefore, since the citizens of Interamna, having abandoned their fidelity to the Roman Church like degenerate sons, have inflicted grave damages on your camps and other properties, while you remained unswayed by any evil suggestion or adversity from your devotion to the Church, we, by the counsel of our brothers and by the authority of the present document, decree that all such damages inflicted upon you by the Interamnenses or on their behalf, and any that may be inflicted in the future as long as they persist in infidelity, as well as all belongings taken from you, shall be fully restored to you by the commune of Interamna. The aforementioned Interamnenses are not to be admitted to the grace of the Church until they have completely satisfied you concerning the aforementioned matters. And because these same Interamnenses do not cease to attack and offend you and other faithful of the said Church, we grant you by the same authority that you cannot be sued by anyone for the offenses inflicted or those that may be inflicted on these rebels on your behalf, from which we deem you absolved. Moreover, so that the purity of your faith may shine ever more clearly, resist vigorously, fortified in spirit, against them and other rebels of the Church, remaining stable in the devotion to the Church, which seeks to raise you among its children with special favor and grace, as you have accustomed. Given at the Lateran, on the tenth day before the Kalends of May, in the first year.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa potestati, consilio et populo Narniensibus mandat ut omnes damni ab Interamnensibus illati eisdem Narniensibus integra restituantur, nec ad gratiam ecclesiae admittantur donec plenarie satisfecerint. Concedit eisdem auctoritate ut de offensis illatis a rebellibus non conveniantur. 1227, April 22, Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

Desiring to bestow upon you, due to the devotion you have shown towards our venerable brother, the Archbishop, and our beloved sons, the chapter of Mainz, and consequently towards us, a gift of singular grace, we are inclined by your prayers to grant you, by the authority of these presents, that you may not be brought to trial outside the city of Mainz by apostolic letters during the discord between the prince and the church, as long as you are prepared to submit to the law before delegated or ordinary judges of yours. Therefore, let none, etc., of our concession, etc. If anyone, etc. Given as in the next [document].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa capitulo Maguntinensi concedit ut, dum discordia inter principem et ecclesiam viget, extra civitatem Maguntinam ad iudicium non trahantur, dummodo coram iudicibus delegatis vel ordinariis stare parati sint. Datum Anagnie, anno secundo.

**Translation to English:**

To Master de la Curre, archpriest of Padua. Sharing in the anguish and hardships that our beloved sons, the citizens of Treviso, suffer from surrounding enemies, we have sent prayers and mandates to our venerable brothers, the Patriarch of Aquileia, the Bishops of Feltre and Belluno, and also to the noble Duke and council of the Venetians, that the Patriarch and Bishops cease their hostilities, and that they, along with the aforementioned Venetians, strive to assist the citizens in their needs, especially with food and money, and show themselves favorably disposes, allowing them to freely transport foodstuffs through their territories to the city of Treviso. Therefore, we command your discretion to personally approach those parts and effectively advise and persuade the aforementioned Patriarch, Bishops, and Venetians to follow through with these requests, compelling them to do so, if you see fit, with the appropriate strictness by our authority, removing any obstacle of appeal. Given at Lyon, on the 7th of the Ides of January, in the second year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Magistro de la Curre archipresbytero Paduano mandat, ut patriarcham Aquilegensem, episcopos Feltrensem et Belunensem, atque Venetos moneat ut civibus Tervisianis a circumstantibus hostibus pressis, auxilium in victualibus et pecunia praebeant, et eos permittant victualia libere transportare. Lugduni, VII Idus Ianuarii, anno secundo.

**Translation to English:**

To G. de Montelongo, our subdeacon and notary, legate of the apostolic see. So that you may exercise the office of the legation entrusted to you more effectively and better manage the affairs of the church, we, having deemed as valid and confirmed what has been done by you concerning the reception of cities, barons, and other nobles under the protection of your legation for the church, grant you full and free power to receive others of the same legation under such protection, as you see fit. Given at Lyon, on the 7th day before the Kalends of June, in the second year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa G. de Montelongo subdiacono et notario, legato apostolice sedis, concedit potestatem recipiendi civitates, barones et nobiles sub protectione ecclesiae. 1244, Mai. 26, Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To the abbots of the Cistercian order of the dioceses of Salzburg and Passau, namely of Sancta Crux and of Zwetil and of Rune. Since our beloved son, the noble man, the Duke of Austria, desires to establish and endow bishoprics in his land, which is extensive, we command you to diligently investigate the places where it would be most appropriate to do this, and the nature and amount of the revenues that the same Duke proposes to assign for this purpose, and to faithfully report to us what you have discovered, so that we may make arrangements as we see fit. If not all can be present, etc. Given at Lyon, 8th Ides of March, in the second year.

Latin Regesto:

Papa [Name] abbatibus monasteriorum Sanctae Crucis, Zwetil, et Rune ordinis Cisterciensis, Salzeburgensis et Pataviensis dioecesum, mandat ut diligenter investigent loca idonea ad episcopatus creandos et dotandos in terra ducis Austriae, nobisque de inventis fideliter rescribant. Datum Lugduni, VIII Idus Martii, anno secundo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Cologne. Your brotherhood has informed us that the Bishop of Osnabrück, your suffragan, has turned his back, not his face, to the Roman Church, being ungrateful for the benefits he is known to have received from it contrary to everyone's opinion. He has long since taken up the horns of rebellion because you were then held in chains, adhering at that time to the enemies of the same Church, whom he still does not cease to favor. He has devastated the goods of the Church of Cologne, to which he was bound to render aid as to his mother, with plunder and fires. Not content with this, but aspiring to tear at its sides like a viper, he dared to construct a certain castle in the heart of it, on land pertaining to the right and property of the same Church of Cologne, for the benefit of Th., his nephew, born of Frederick, Count of Isenburg, the murderer of your predecessor of good memory, Engelbert, Archbishop of Cologne. Since indeed we neither wish nor should pass over such matters with closed eyes, lest, if the said bishop were to bear such excesses with impunity, he would glory in it and others would be given access to commit similar acts, we command that you send him to our presence to receive what he deserves for his merits. Given at Lyons, on the eighth day before the Ides of January, in the second year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa archiepiscopo Coloniensi mandat ut, cum episcopus Osnaburgensis rebellionem contra ecclesiam Romanam fecerit et bona ecclesiae Coloniensis devastaverit, ipsum ad praesentiam suam mittat pro meritis recepturum. Datum Lugduni, VIII Idus Ianuarii, anno secundo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz. Since, as you have taken care to inform us, you have excommunicated Frederick the custodian, Gerard the cantor, Master Philip, Frederick Grifinclawe, of the major church, and Berthold called Mort, canons of Saint John's in Mainz, for adhering to the persecutors of the Roman Church and attacking it, and subsequently, as their contumacy increased, deprived them of the benefices they held and decided that they should be degraded from their orders by the council's advice held at Fritzlar: we, inclined by your prayers, have decided by the authority of these presents that any letters obtained or to be obtained from us by them, in which they appeal as clerics, are to be of no consequence unless they make express mention of such degradation or deposition. Given at Lyon, on the 5th of May, in the second year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa archiepiscopo Maguntino declarat quod litterae a Friderico custode et aliis clericis impetratae, nisi de eorum degradatione expressam mentionem fecerint, nullius sint momenti. 1245, Mai. 5. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man, the Duke of Lotharingia and Brabant. Although the union of conjugal ties in the fourth degree of consanguinity or affinity is forbidden by sacred canons, the Roman Church sometimes wisely dispenses with these, especially when necessity or evident utility demands it. Therefore, since you have contracted marriage with the noble woman Sophia, the daughter of the late saint Elizabeth, who is related to you in the fourth degree of affinity, and you have begotten children with her, we, taking into consideration that many dangers would arise from the divorce of this marriage, are inclined by your devotion to dispense with you by the authority of these presents, so that you may lawfully remain in the same marriage, notwithstanding the aforesaid affinity, declaring the same children legitimate. Let none therefore etc. But if anyone— Given at Lyon, March 31, in the second year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro duci Lothoringie et Brabantie, qui cum Sophia in quarto affinitatis gradu matrimonio iunctus est, dispensat ut in eodem matrimonio remanere possit, liberis ex eo natis legitimis declaratis. 1228, Mart. 31, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the dean, Bartholomew the archdeacon, and John the canon and procurators of the church of Olomouc. A humble supplication was made to us on your behalf, that since you, concerning the matter of the election which was held in the church of Olomouc for the beloved son William, have come to the apostolic see and, having spent a long time there, have incurred heavy expenses to the point that your funds are entirely exhausted, we would, with fatherly care, provide for you in this matter so that the aforementioned business would not remain unfinished for lack of necessities. Inclined by your prayers, we grant you, by the authority of these presents, the freedom to contract a loan for the necessary expenses to promote the said business, using the goods of the same church as collateral up to the sum of four hundred and sixty marks sterling and to pledge those goods for this reason. Given at Lyon, 4th day before the Nones of March, in the second year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa decano, Bartholomeo archidiacono et Iohanni canonico ecclesiae Olomucensis, concedit ut pro expensis electionis Guillielmi usque ad summam quadringentarum et sexaginta marcarum sterlingorum mutuum contrahant et bona ecclesiae obligent. 1245, Mart. 4, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot and prior of Saint Theodoric and Hugh, canon of Reims. Our venerable brother, the bishop of Liège, presented before us, stating that several nobles of the diocese of Liège and other dioceses, who are vassals of the Church of Liège, are using the frivolous excuse that the bishop did not receive the regalia from the prince, since he is bound by the chain of excommunication, and thus refuse to obey him and offer the due homage according to their will, causing not a small injury to him and his church. Therefore, he humbly beseeched us to provide paternal care over this matter. Thus, not wishing to bear the loss of the bishop, whom we intend to support and assist, we command you to compel all the vassals of the Church of Liège to render the due homage and usual services to him as they are bound to do, by means of ecclesiastical censure, with an admonition given beforehand and disregarding any appeal, notwithstanding any privilege or indulgence granted to some of them by the Apostolic See, claiming that they cannot be excommunicated or their lands placed under interdict. If you cannot achieve this with all of them, etc. Given at Lyon, the second day before the Calends of February, in the second year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati et priori Sancti Theodorici et Hugoni canonico Remensi mandat, ut feudatarios ecclesiae Leodiensis ad debita homagia et servitia episcopo Leodiensi praestanda compellant. 1238, Jan. 31. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Cambrai. Our beloved son, John of Avesnes, humbly petitioned us, since he seeks to have his legitimacy declared concerning his birthright before us, and fears that meanwhile the opportunity to prove this might be lost due to unforeseen circumstances, that we might provide for him with paternal care in this matter. We command you to prudently receive and diligently examine the suitable witnesses, whom the said John will bring before you regarding this matter, if their death is reasonably feared due to their imminent illness, and send us their statements enclosed under your seal, ensuring that you notify the noble man William, his brother, whom this matter also concerns, with your prudent notice, so that he may be present at the reception of the witnesses if he wishes, and make an authentic instrument about the notification made. If he also presents witnesses concerning this same matter on his behalf before you, do not neglect to receive and examine them carefully and to send us their statements under the same seal. Given at Lyon, on the Nones of April, in the second year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Cameracensi mandat ut testes de natalicio Iohannis de Avesnes recipiat et examinet, atque eorum dicta sub sigillo transmita, notificato Willelmo fratre eius. 1245, Apr. 5, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz. It was humbly presented before us that there had long been deadly enmities between the noble men Henry of Eberstal and Albert of Niffen of the diocese of Augsburg, from which various dangers and perils had arisen on both sides. Finally, in order to bring about a commendable resolution to these issues, the aforementioned Henry took to wed the daughter of the said Albert, who is related to him in the fourth degree of consanguinity, in matrimony. As a result, firm peace is now held between them, and stable friendship is maintained. Therefore, a humble petition was made to us on behalf of Henry, asking that we deign to dispense with this marriage by special grace, especially as, if a divorce were to occur between them, it would give rise to grave and dangerous conflicts. Thus, we command your Fraternity, in whom we have special trust for your prudence, by apostolic writing, to dispense concerning this marriage thus contracted by our authority, as you deem expedient. Given at Lyon, on the eighth of the Ides of May, in the second year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Archiepiscopo Maguntino mandat ut auctoritate apostolica super matrimonio inter Henricum de Eberstal et filiam Alberti de Niffent, in quarta consanguinitatis linea, contracto dispenset, ad pacem firmandam inter eos. 1230, Mai. 10, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Cologne. Due to the merits of his praiseworthy conduct and life, our beloved son Henry, canon of the Church of Saint Denis in Liège and rector of the Church of Horsmale in the diocese of Liège, is said to be worthy of receiving a special grace from us. Therefore, on account of his merits and at the request of our dearest daughter in Christ, M., widow of the late Otto, former Emperor of the Romans, who is said to have lifted him from the sacred font and is considered beloved for her merits of devotion, we grant you the authority by these presents to dispense with him, so that he may freely retain two benefices without cure, which he claims to have canonically obtained, alongside the said church with the cure of souls — notwithstanding the constitution of the General Council — if you see it as expedient, provided that he personally serves in the aforesaid Church of Saint Denis, the other church is not deprived of its due services, and the care of souls is in no way neglected. Given at Lyon, February 15th, in the second year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Coloniensi mandat, ut Henrico canonico ecclesiae sancti Dionisii Leodiensis et rectori ecclesiae de Horsmale, duas praebendas sine cura, quas se canonice adeptum proponit, cum ecclesia curam animarum habente, retinere permittat, constitutione concilii generalis non obstante, dummodo ipse personaliter deserviat et cura animarum non negligatur. Datum Lugduni, XV Kalendas Martii, anno secundo.

**Translation to English:**

To Arnold, the elected of Trier. Given both the promptitude of your devotion and the purity of your unwavering faith, you are considered among the special devotees of the Roman Church. We have deemed it fitting to pursue you with special prerogative of favor and grace, and to favorably grant your petitions as much as we can in accordance with God. Since, as has been proposed on your behalf before us, the revenues of your mensa have been so diminished due to the dangers of wars that they are insufficient to sustain the burdens incumbent upon you for the defense of your church and also of ecclesiastical liberty, we, granting a benign assent to your devotion's prayers, by the authority of these presents, allow you to freely retain the ecclesiastical benefices which you held at the time of your election, excepting only those which have been assigned to others by our mandate, until our will indicates otherwise. Let no one, therefore, etc., our concession etc., if anyone etc. Given at Lyon, on the 10th of May, in the second year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Arnoldo electo Treverensi indulget, ut beneficia ecclesiastica, quae tempore electionis suae obtinebat, libere retinere possit, donec aliud decernatur, propter diminutos mensae redditus ex bellorum periculis. 1245, Maii 10, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the archbishop of Rouen, the former bishop of Modena, and the abbot of Saint-Facundus, envoys of the Apostolic See. We have kindly received your letters and have fully understood their content. Among other things contained in those letters, we have learned that the prince is complaining about certain matters concerning us and is also urgently requesting something from us. However, if the truth of the matter and the quality of the time are carefully considered, neither his complaints nor his requests seem appropriate at present. For, since the Roman Church, bearing the care of all the faithful, frequently sends legates to various parts of the world to ensure the welfare of the absent, it had previously sent a legate to Lombardy for the common benefit of that land. However, this same prince, after we were elevated to the highest apostolic office, did not cease to attack the remnants of the patrimony of the same church, which during the time of our predecessor, Pope Gregory of happy memory, he almost entirely occupied. Rather, he afflicted them with a heavier hand of oppression. Therefore, it is not fitting for him to request the recall of the aforementioned legate, nor should we grant him an audience on this matter, especially because the hope of consolation desired by the Lombards, who have long been troubled by wars, would be removed by the absence of the same legate, and it would open the way to greater dangers for them. The Church would be branded with betrayal if it abandoned them in this manner without first obtaining a remission from the same prince or entering into a truce with him regarding the injuries which he claims they inflicted upon him on account of the same church. Furthermore, the cardinals of the Roman Church did not promise him the recall of the aforementioned legate while the church was vacant. But when there was a discussion about liberating our venerable brother, the bishop of Palestrina, and others who were captives, and when it was requested from the same cardinals, on behalf of the prince, to recall the legate, some of them responded that they would fulfill his requests as much as they could with God when the opportune time came. It is indeed much to be rejoiced by the prince that he restored the said Bishop of Palestrina and some others to freedom, and it is greatly to be lamented that he still holds others captive, since the restoration of those brought him salvation and honor, while the detention of these is known to have brought him the opposite. He should also carefully consider whether he reveres the church, which he often calls mother, as is fitting, and whether he honors its faithful as is proper. For how does he assert with words that she is his mother if he denies being her son by his deeds? Or how does he pretend devotion towards her in word if he shows himself undevoted to her in deed? Regarding the release of Salinguerra, about which we have now first understood the prince's will, it is incongruously requested from us, since we neither detain him nor do we cause him to be detained in any way. If he were indeed held by us, since he had stirred up the city of Ferrara, a special seat of the Apostolic See, as can clearly appear from the privileges of the same prince and his predecessors, for which the same Salinguerra was a vassal of that seat, against the Roman Church and was captured in rebellion of that same city, the prince himself could not be justly moved with admiration on this account. However, if it can be shown to us that he ought to be released by reason of some pact or promise, we will do what we should in this matter. Moreover, the prince's complaint is that we have assigned the office of legation in those parts to the elected bishop of Avignon in hatred of him and in favor of our dear son, the noble man, the count of Provence. But, with God as witness, we do not remember making any mention of the prince at that time, since we specifically entrusted the same legation against heretics and their supporters at the urging of the friars of the Order of Preachers, who had come to the Apostolic See from those parts for this reason. Nevertheless, we are prepared to do even greater things for the same count, due to the merits of his devotion. Nor can we justly be accused of proceeding against distant heretics, omitting those nearby, namely in Lombardy and Tuscany; for, as almost everyone knows, the Roman Church steadfastly pursued heretical depravity everywhere in the world before the discord between the church and the same prince arose, and the more so in the vicinity, because by reason of proximity it could more easily and fully exercise the force of its authority there. But after the same prince began to oppress the same church, he so restrained its strength and blocked its paths everywhere that it could not, as it ought, combat that depravity and promote the growth of the

Translation to English:

To the commanders and brothers of the Hospital of Saint Mary of the Teutons and to all the faithful Christians established in the land of Culm and the regions of Prussia. Our heart is troubled by anything impiously presumed against God and wickedly attempted to the detriment of His faithful, for whom we, although unworthy, have been appointed as fathers by the Creator of all. We must apply the diligence of that providence, which may both rescue them from the danger of perdition and procure prosperity for them. Indeed, through your labors and the sufferings of pilgrims in the regions of Poland, the Christian religion flourishes and advances, which once almost suffered ultimate destruction, being exposed to the swords of the Prussians. Although they have been greatly worn down by you, triumphing through the power of divine help, yet, with the enemy of the human race stirring up scandal, so that the fruits of your work may suffer loss, some who are Christians in name only, persecuting Christ in you, as we have heard, oppress you savagely with the deadly people of the Letts and Prussians, and strive to withdraw the land acquired by the price of your blood from divine worship. However, since it is fitting that the impiety of such should be suppressed by all virtue, and that your congregation be preserved from the danger of invasion, we wish and command, enjoining you for the remission of your sins, that you diligently strive with watchful care to subdue these treacherous Christians and the same Letts and Prussians, who so damnably persecute the cause of God, with a powerful arm and to break their horns, so that you and the other faithful of the land of Culm and Prussia may always, with God's favor, prosper in those things which pertain to your salvation and the increase of the Christian religion, and may finally obtain the reward of everlasting glory. Given as above in the next.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa preceptoribus et fratribus hospitalis Sancte Marie Theutonicorum mandat ut perfidos Christianos ac Letoinos et Prutenos, qui cum eis feraliter agunt, potentia reprimant, ut in fide et religione Christiana proficiant. 1231.

**Translation to English:**

To Master Bertram, schoolmaster of St. Andrew of Verdun. To show you special favor and due to your merits of probity, for which you have been given commendable testimony, and the pleasing acts of devotion and service, which you commendably provided to the late I., bishop of Palestrina, then legate of the Apostolic See, to whom you were a cleric, in the affairs of the Roman Church, and also the persecutions you are said to have faithfully endured by adhering to the same bishop, justly persuade us. Therefore, by the authority of these presents, we grant you permission to freely retain the school of St. Andrew of Verdun and the church in Greve, having the care of souls, which you propose to have canonically acquired and whose revenues, as you assert, do not exceed the value of sixteen marks of silver annually, together with the prebend, which the aforementioned legate conferred upon you in the church of Osnabrück — notwithstanding the constitution issued by the general council on this matter — provided that such benefices are not defrauded of their due obligations, etc., as far as: it is neglected. Therefore, no one etc. our concession etc. If anyone however etc. Given at Lyons, on the first of April, in the second year.

**Regesto (Latin):**

Innocentius IV papa Magistro Bertrammo, scolastico Sancti Andree Verdensis, indulget, ut scolastriam Sancti Andree Verdensis et ecclesiam in Grevem, curam animarum habentem, cum prebenda in Osnaburgensi ecclesia possit retinere, non obstante constitutione concilii generalis. 1244, Apr. 1, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the knowledge of the present and the memory of the future. The bowels of the mother church, agitated by grave unrest and wounded by unusual turmoil in these days, compel us to devise a new plan against our heart, which dire necessity demands, beyond the bounds of benevolent will which paternal affection preserves. For although the fertility of the mother church nourishes all peoples professing the Christian faith with the milk of her breasts and is solicitous for their well-being, she carries the Roman citizens particularly, whom divine disposition has ordained as her special sons, in her innermost bosom of charity. We indeed deem it fitting and proper that the City and its inhabitants be endowed with magnificent graces and adorned with sublime gifts, since heavenly clemency has established it as the head of the world, consecrated by the blood of the apostles, with the principal foundations of the apostolic see established therein. These are the inhabitants, accustomed to venerate the see with due reverence, to bestow upon it the fruits of their devotion, and to fervently assist in adversities as vigilant and tireless defenders of ecclesiastical liberty, considering it their own benefit to promote its cause at opportune times. Consequently, the more generous increments of gifts have been bestowed upon the sons by the mother's liberality, the more gravely and indecently it appears in the judgment of truth if they return reproach for honor and offenses for benefits, from whose graces the provident mother has not withdrawn her hand, but rather liberally adds new ones and fortifies the old with the strength of confirmation.

Who, therefore, could admire a city so magnificent, endowed with such prudent men, conspicuous for devotion, men of lofty counsel, thus imprudently, thus irreverently, thus inconsiderately fallen away, that it not only scorns to avoid offense to divine majesty or the injury and danger to the said mother, but even does not notice the detriment to its own reputation, whose glory is proven to receive an inextricable stain through this, miserably led into error under a certain vehicle of blindness.
