Raimundi of the Order of Preachers, appointed by the authority of the Apostolic See as inquisitors against heretics, which the same count claims to be null, we have caused to be relaxed for caution, before he approached our presence, according to the custom long observed in the Roman Church, having first received from him the obligation of his land to comply with the mandates of the Church concerning these matters and an oath of caution; for the full observance and satisfaction to be rendered to those for whom the aforesaid sentences were pronounced, if they appear to have been justly pronounced, we send apostolic letters to certain persons, in whose providence we have undoubted confidence. And when the same count, absolved, subsequently approached our presence in a spirit of humility and devotion, we received him with a serene face, and treating him with our usual benignity of meekness, we have deemed it right, at your intervention, also considering that he, holding no small place among other princes of the world, can be useful and very fruitful to the Church by his strength, power, and industry, to admit him to the grace of the Apostolic See with the counsel of the aforementioned brothers. Wherefore, we deemed it right to ask and exhort your royal excellence that you should pursue the same count, reconciled to the Church by your intervention, with the favor of your magnificence in such a way that he, remaining perpetually in the devotion of the Apostolic See and yours, may be more strongly encouraged to serve your majesty. Given at the Lateran, on the Kalends of January, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa illustri regi Franciae mandat, ut comitem Tolosanum, reconciliatione ecclesiae per intercessionem regiam facta, favore prosequatur. Datum Romae, apud Lateranum, Kalendis Ianuarii, anno primo.

**Translation to English:**

To the authorities and community of Treviso. As your petition presented to us contained, the city itself, once many nobles were handed over to the strict custody of prison by the late Emperor Frederick, surrounded as if by enemies and exposed to their endeavors, unable to further endure the heavy damages, countless pains, and immense distress with which they did not cease to oppress it, surrendered itself to Frederick, not without sighs of the heart and fear of imminent or future danger; who, without opposition from you or your ambassadors due to fear for your possessions and body, whether from your concession or that of the ambassadors, claims to have created a public instrument in your presence declaring that the aforesaid city was henceforth his, or that a new right was thus created for him in it. Wherefore you, fearing that prejudice might be generated against you in the future from this, humbly petitioned us to restore your city to its former liberty, notwithstanding such concession. We, considering that things done under duress or fear ought to lack the strength of validity, decree by apostolic authority that if the mentioned fear was so great and such, that it might and should rightly fall upon a steadfast person, you are absolved from all concessions or contracts thus initiated with the said Frederick or his envoys. Given at Lyons, 4th day before the Kalends of August, in the third year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa potestatem et commune Tervisinis absolvit ab omnibus concessionibus seu contractibus cum Frederico imperatore eiusque nuntiis metu coactis, et civitatem ad pristinam libertatem restituit. Datum Lugduni, IIII Kalendas Augusti, anno tertio.

Translation to English:

To the Archbishop of Mainz. Desiring to be found inclined to grace, we willingly extend it to those who seek to claim it as due to them by their own merits and those of their relatives. Therefore, as we have learned, our beloved son Berthold, cantor of Speyer and once a relative of the late bishop of Speyer of blessed memory, and our beloved son, the noble man C. de Scarphenberg, his brother, along with other relatives and allies, are mightily assisting you in the affairs of the Apostolic See both openly and powerfully. Intending, therefore, to pursue him with the prerogative of special grace, we grant you by the authority of these presents, that you may, in accordance with his nobility and devotion, dispense by our authority, as you see fit, that in addition to the benefices he currently holds having the care of souls, he may lawfully receive other benefices, although one of them may be a prebend or an ecclesiastical dignity, even if they also have the care of souls, and freely retain them along with those already obtained—notwithstanding the constitution of the general council; provided that the same benefices, etc., up to: be neglected. Given at Lyons, 15th September, in the third year.

Regesto:

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino concedit, ut cum Bertholdo cantore Spirensi et C. de Scarphenberg fratre eius super pluralitate beneficiorum auctoritate apostolica dispensare possit. 1229, Sept. 15. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the podestà, council, and people of Ancona. The steadfastness of your faith and sincere devotion, which you hold towards your mother, the Roman Church, induce us to agree to your honorable petitions, as far as we can with our integrity. Hence, being inclined by your supplications, by the authority of these presents, we grant you that the merchants of the city of Ancona may freely buy and sell throughout the city of Acre and the Kingdom of Jerusalem and extract goods therefrom without any payment of customs duties. Let no one, therefore, etc., our concession, etc. If anyone, etc. Given at Lyon, the fifth day before the Kalends of August, in the third year. 

To the podestà, council, and people of Ancona. The steadfastness of your faith, etc., as above, up to: to buy and sell throughout all of Apulia and the Kingdom of Sicily, as well as through all the lands and waters of the Roman Church, and extract goods therefrom without any payment of customs duties. Let no one, therefore, etc., our concession, etc. Given at Lyon, the fifth day before the Kalends of August, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa potestati, consilio et populo Anconitanis concedit, ut mercatores Anconitani libere emere et vendere possint per civitatem Acconensem et regnum Ierosolimitanum, nec non per totam Apuliam et regnum Sicilie, ac terras et aquas ecclesie Romane, sine solutione doane. 1245, Jul. 28. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Pisa. Since there is greater joy among the angels of God over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons who need no repentance, and we sincerely desire the conversion of our erring children, it has been brought to our attention by your report that the citizens of Pisa wish to return to the unity of the Church, ready to comply with its mandates and ours concerning the capture and despoiling of prelates and others who were once coming to the council of the Apostolic See, and the detention of strongholds of the Lucan church, for which the same citizens are bound by the chain of excommunication and their city is subjected to ecclesiastical interdict. To your fraternity, in whom we have sincere trust in the Lord, we commit and command through apostolic writings that if the said citizens provide you, in our name, with a sufficient guarantee of precisely and absolutely complying with the mandates of the Church and ours concerning the capture and despoiling of prelates and others mentioned, and that they will adhere to the Apostolic See with other faithful followers, and if they assign those strongholds of the aforementioned Lucan Church which they hold to some Roman Church cardinal whom they choose, to be held by him until it is legally determined whether they pertain to the aforementioned Lucan Church or to themselves, you shall grant the aforementioned citizens the benefit of absolution concerning the previous excommunication according to the form of the Church and lift the aforementioned sentence of interdict. Given at Lyon, August 16, in the third year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Pisano mandat, ut si cives Pisani cautionem sufficientem praestiterint ad standum mandatis ecclesiae et assignaverint castra ecclesiae Lucanae cardinali eligendo, beneficium absolutionis eis impertias et sententiam interdicti relaxes. Datum Lugduni, XVII Kalendas Septembris, anno tertio.

**Translation to English:**

To the Patriarch of Jerusalem, legate of the apostolic see, and the bishop of Sidon. Our beloved son, the noble man William of Dampierre, humbly petitioned us that when our beloved noble son John of Avesnes asked us to declare his legitimate birth, William, who is involved in this matter, appeared before us and intends to present certain witnesses against John who are in those parts. We should arrange for those witnesses to be received in those regions. Therefore, so that the truth may not be hidden, we command that you prudently receive within nine months those suitable witnesses whom the aforementioned William or his appointed procurator sends to you for this purpose, to be produced before you regarding the articles that our venerable brother, the Bishop of Porto, and our beloved son Giles, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, send to you enclosed with their seals. Whether John or anyone else on his behalf may attend this reception or not, ensure their diligent examination, and faithfully transmit their statements to us enclosed under your seals. As for the witnesses, etc. If not both, then one, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 8th of August, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Patriarcham Ierosolimitanum et episcopum Sindoniensem mandat ut testes quos Willelmus de Dampetra contra Iohannem de Avesnis producere intendit prudenter recipiant et examinent, eorumque dicta sub sigillis suis ad sedem apostolicam transmittant. 1245, Aug. 8. Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To the provost of the Church of Strasbourg. It is fitting that the grace of the Apostolic See should extend more abundantly to those who endeavor to earn it through their own merits. Therefore, since our beloved son Berthold, a canon of Strasbourg and son of the noble lord, the Count of Wilperce, has humbly petitioned us that, besides the ecclesiastical benefits involving the care of souls, which he currently holds, he may be granted a dispensation to receive other benefices or positions or dignities, even if they similarly involve the care of souls, and to freely retain them along with those he already holds — notwithstanding the constitution issued by the general council on this matter — we, considering that although the constitution of the sacred council prohibits the holding of multiple churches or ecclesiastical dignities to curb the ambitions of some, Berthold's knowledge of letters and noble conduct and birth, of which he is known to excel, make him worthy of obtaining special grace, and trusting fully in your discretion in the Lord, by the authority of these presents, grant you the authority to dispense with him concerning the above matters, as you, having weighed the circumstances and his nobility and merits, see fit according to God. Given at Lyon, on the 11th of October, in the third year [of our pontificate].

Regesto:

Gregorius IX papa præposito ecclesiæ Argentinensis concedit facultatem dispensandi cum Bertoldo canonico Argentinensi, filio comitis de Wilperce, super recipiendis et retinendis aliis beneficiis vel dignitatibus, etiam si curam animarum habeant, constitutione concilii generali non obstante, consideratis meritis et nobilitate eius. 1239, Oct. 11, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Prague and the Abbots of Brno and Hradec in the dioceses of Prague and Olomouc. Presented before us by John, the dean, Bartholomew, the archdeacon, and Master John, canon and procurator of the Church of Olomouc, was the case that Conrad, a canon of Hildesheim, had attempted to intrude himself into the Church of Olomouc and was acting as its bishop. He was summoned by our authority to present himself or a suitable procurator before us to respond to these charges according to justice. However, since he has not thus far cared to appear, though he has been awaited for a long time, we command you to summon him again by our authority, peremptorily, so that he may personally appear before us on the forthcoming feast of St. John the Baptist to do and receive what the order of reason dictates. You are to report faithfully to us what you have done regarding this. If not all of you can do this, etc. Given at Lyon, the 11th of March in the second year [of our pontificate].

To the same. Presented, etc., as above, up to "present himself." But since he, having been awaited for a long time, has arrogantly refused to appear, we, wishing to safeguard the indemnity of the same church, have decided to sequestrate it and its properties, along with all goods pertaining to it and the bishopric, and to suspend the aforementioned Conrad from the administration of spiritual and temporal matters on account of the suspicion of dilapidation and the infamy of intrusion arisen against him, and to prevent scandal among the people of the Lord. Therefore, we command you to receive and diligently preserve these properties by our authority until our will is satisfied, repressing opponents, etc. If not all of you can do this, etc. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa (Episcopo Pragensi et abbatibus Breunovensi et Gradicensi mandat, ut Conradum, canonicum Ildesemensem, qui se in Olomucensem ecclesiam intrusit et gerit pro episcopo, auctoritate sua citent et suspendant ab administratione spiritualium et temporalium propter suspicionem dilapidationis et infamiam intrusionis. 1238, Mart. 11, Lugduni.)

**Translation to English:**

To the Patriarch of Jerusalem, legate of the Apostolic See, and to the bishop of Sidon. Recently, at the supplication of our beloved son, the noble man William of Dampierre, we have instructed you by our letters to prudently receive, within nine months, suitable witnesses whom the same William or his procurator might produce against our beloved son, the noble man John of Avesnes, in the case concerning John's birth that is being contested before us, on certain articles before you. Let the discretion of your wisdom be known by the tenor of these presents, that it is our intention for the aforementioned months to be counted from the time we issued those letters. Furthermore, we desire that whichever party first comes before you shall not be held to wait for the other party for more than one month. If indeed John's party wishes to produce some witnesses before you to refute those received on William's behalf, you should prudently receive and carefully examine them within one month, if they are suitable, and then faithfully send us their statements enclosed under your seals. What if not both, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 11th of August, in the third year [of the pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa patriarchae Hierosolymitano, apostolicae sedis legato, et episcopo Sydoniensi mandat, ut testes idoneos quos Willelmus de Dampetra contra Ioannem de Avesnis in causa natalium produxerit, infra novem menses recipiant, et mensium initium a data litterarum computetur. Item, altera pars quae primo adierit non expectet plus quam mensem. Si Ioannis pars testes contra Willelmi partem produxerit, illos infra mensem recipiant et dicta sub sigillis transmittant. Datum Lugduni, III Idus Augusti, anno tertio.

**Translation to English:**

We have received the documents concerning the Rhenish matters, which Perteius did not describe, because they show that certain nobles and prelates were aligned with his sides at that time. Berger 1447. Although the union of the marital bond in the fourth degree of consanguinity or affinity is prohibited by the sacred canons, nevertheless, the Roman Church sometimes grants a dispensation regarding these matters, especially when urgent necessity or evident utility requires it. Therefore, as proposed before us on behalf of our beloved son, the noble man Ulrich, the Margrave of Burgau, this nobleman has taken as his wife a noblewoman, the sister of the noble men Conrad and Heinrich, Counts of Urach, from the diocese of Constance, who is related to him in the fourth degree of consanguinity, after many preceding wars, for the purpose of restoring peace, and has procreated offspring from her. Because we have learned that if a divorce were to occur between them, many dangers would follow, we, moved by the prayers of our venerable brother, the Bishop of Freising, and our beloved son, the Elect of Seckau, decree that, as long as they persist in devotion to the Roman Church, you may dispense them by our authority, if you see it as expedient, so that they may remain in the contracted marriage — notwithstanding this impediment. Given at Lyon, 27 August, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Frisingensi et electo Secoeensi mandat, ut Ulricum marchionem de Burgau cum uxore sua, consanguinitatis quarto gradu coniunctam, auctoritate sua dispensare possint, ne impedimento huiusmodi matrimonio separentur, urgente necessitate pacis. Lugduni, VI Kal. Septembris, anno tertio.

**Translation to English:**

To John of Dunpirre, canon of the church of Saint Denis of Liège. Although the constitution of the sacred council prohibits anyone from having multiple churches or ecclesiastical dignities due to the ambitions of some, the benevolence of the Apostolic See, prudently weighing the merits of individuals, sometimes grants greater favor to those who, born of noble lineage, are otherwise endowed with greater gifts. Therefore, because of both your nobility of birth and the merits of your virtue, regarding which you are given commendable testimony, and the request of the noble man of Los and Ceni, count, and noble women, the countess of Auvergne and the lady of Monitore, who have interceded for you, we are led to grant you, by the authority of this document, that besides the ecclesiastical benefices you currently possess, one of which involves the care of souls and from whose revenues you cannot, as you assert, comfortably sustain yourself according to your personal status and local custom, you may—despite the aforementioned constitution—accept a single benefice or dignity or prelature, even if it involves the care of souls, if it is canonically offered to you, and freely retain it along with those already obtained; provided that the same benefices are not neglected in their duties, etc. Therefore, no one may etc. infringe upon our concession etc. If anyone should etc. Given at Lyon, on the Nones of September, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Iohanni de Dunpirre, canonico ecclesiae Sancti Dionysii Leodiensis, concedit ut, praeter beneficia ecclesiastica quae nunc obtinet, unum beneficium vel dignitatem seu praelaturam, etiam curam animarum habentem, accipere et retinere possit, constitutione non obstante, intercedentibus nobilibus personis. Datum Lugduni, Non. Septembr., anno tertio (1245).

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop and the abbot of the monastery of Brennoweai and the provost of the greater church of Prague. On behalf of the beloved sons, the dean and chapter of the church of Olomouc, it was presented before us that, when the church was previously vacant of a pastor, they, as is their duty, convened to discuss the appointment of a future bishop, so that the church would not languish in prolonged vacancy. They all unanimously agreed, by means of scrutiny, to elect Master William, their fellow canon—a learned, honorable, and prudent man, circumspect in spiritual and temporal matters, by whose diligence the church was expected to be reformed for the better—as the bishop of Olomouc. Although he consented to the election upon their persistent urging, Conrad, a canon of Hildesheim, by lay power, managed to intrude himself into the bishopric of Olomouc. Having plundered their houses, he expelled them from the church, broke its doors, and ravaged its properties. Therefore, the procurators of the dean and chapter humbly petitioned us, since full faith could be placed in the Apostolic See regarding these matters, to provide paternal care for the church and its canons, who, having been stripped of all their goods by Conrad, were forced into the disgrace of mendicancy, suffering imprisonment and chains, an insult to the clerical order. 

The procurator of the opposing party, whom we admitted with his oath regarding his procuratorship, as he claimed he feared to carry the procuration letters with him due to the dangers of the roads, argued oppositely that Robert, the former bishop of Olomouc, despite frequent admonishments, did not care to correct the excesses of his canons, leading the venerable brother, the Archbishop of Mainz, Metropolitan of the place, to visit the church of Olomouc by metropolitan right. After a prior inquiry, he suspended the dean and other canons of the church for evident cohabitation with women and other various offenses and evident crimes, and eventually, with their increasing malice, he passed a sentence of excommunication on them. Later, with the dean and canons of the church of Olomouc remaining bound and neglecting to seek absolution, and meanwhile, the church being deprived of a pastor's comfort, the archbishop, believing them unworthy of the right of election after the lapse of time had already devolved the power of providing a pastor to him, appointed Conrad, the canon of Hildesheim, a truly prudent and discreet man, to the church of Olomouc, having him consecrated as bishop of the church. To whom the chapter and all the clergy of the city and diocese of Olomouc humbly obey as their bishop both spiritually and temporally.

Since it is our desire to aid the difficulties of churches through appropriate provision, we command that you give the said Conrad, who acts as the pastor of the church, a peremptory period of three months, within which, after your citation is issued, he must present himself, personally or through a sufficient and suitable procurator, with his reasons and documents pertaining to the matter, before our presence, to do and receive what the order of reason dictates—notwithstanding the apostolic letters obtained for the archdeacon of Wrocław and his co-judges regarding this matter, through which it is claimed that it was impossible to proceed due to the wickedness of the times and the power of the same Conrad. Whatever you do concerning this, communicate faithfully to us in your letters. If not all of you can act—then you, brother bishop, etc. Given at Anagni, September 11, in the first year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa mandat episcopo et abbati monasterii Brennoweai et praeposito maioris ecclesiae Pragensis, ut Conrado, qui se gerit tamquam pastor ecclesiae Olomucensis, terminum trium mensium praefigant, infra quem personaliter vel per procuratorem sufficientem se coram papa repraesentet, facturus et recepturus quod ordo rationis dictaverit, non obstantibus litteris ad archidiaconum Wratislaviensem super hoc negotio impetratis. Anagniae, III Id. Septembris, anno primo.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of the monastery of Mezano. Since serious discord has arisen between our venerable brother, the bishop of Cuiavia, the brothers of the House of the Teutonic Order in Prussia, and the noble men of Poland and the dukes of Kamien on one side, and the noble man, the duke of Pomerania and Prussia, on the other, and we have not been able to fully ascertain the truth regarding the matters proposed by either party before us: we, desiring to extinguish the flame of such dissension and to bring the discordant parties to the unity of concord, have decided to specially choose your person, in whom we have firm confidence in the Lord due to your diligence and circumspection, to carry this out, directing you to those parts as an angel of peace. Therefore, we command you, with our authority, to summon the parties before you and to diligently and prudently negotiate the making of peace between them, and if possible, to restore it according to the skill given to you by God. But if you cannot reconcile them, you should diligently inquire into all the articles of discord and faithfully report to us whatever you discover, setting a suitable peremptory term for the same parties to present themselves before us through suitable representatives to receive what we shall decide regarding these matters, using our authority against any contradictors, etc. Given at Lyon, 12 October, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati monasterii de Mezano mandat, ut auctoritate apostolica partes discordes, scilicet episcopum Cuiaviensem, fratres domus sancte Marie Theutonicorum, nobiles viros Polonie et Caminensem duces ex una parte, et ducem Pomeranie ac Pruscie ex altera parte, ad concordiam deducat aut veritatem discordiae articulorum nobis referat. 1239, Oct. 12. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishops of Mainz and Cologne and the Abbot of Hemeroth of the Cistercian Order in the Diocese of Trier. On behalf of the Chapter of Trier, it was presented before us that, while their church was deprived of the solace of a pastor, having convened on the appointed day to deliberate on the substitution of a future bishop, with all those summoned who ought and could conveniently attend, the greater and healthier part of the chapter canonically and unanimously elected our beloved son Arnold, then the major provost of the same church, as Archbishop of Trier. Some members of the chapter, albeit few, directed their votes towards a former provost of Saint Paulinus of Trier. Although the same provost of Saint Paulinus initially pursued his claim, he eventually recognized he had no right in such election and voluntarily withdrew his claim. Subsequently, when the same provost of Saint Paulinus and his electors, reviving a dispute against him that had been resolved, obtained our letters directed to the Abbot of Mont Frigid in the Diocese of Beauvais and his colleagues concerning the matter of the election, and after some litigation on both sides before them, the cause was finally brought to us upon the death of the aforementioned provost through appeal, and the procurators of the parties were presented before us. You are to ensure that obedience and due reverence are exhibited to the elected by his subjects, who shall later take the customary oath of fidelity to us and the Roman Church, in the form we send you enclosed under our bull. You shall ensure that the form of the oath, which he shall take, is sent to us as soon as possible by his own letters patent sealed with his seal through his own messenger. Otherwise, having duly annulled it, you shall ensure that the aforementioned church is provided with a pastor through a canonical election, restraining any dissenters or rebels by ecclesiastical censure, dismissing any appeal. Dated at Lyon, January 23, in the second year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa archiepiscopis Maguntino et Coloniensi necnon abbati de Hemeroth mandat ut Arnoldus, electus in archiepiscopum Treverensem, a suis subditis obedientiam recipiat, posteaque iuramentum fidelitatis praestet sub forma Romanae Ecclesiae. Si vero non ita, electionem canonicam de pastore fieri curent. Datum Lugduni, X Kalendas Februarii, anno secundo.

**Translation to English:**

To the dean of the church of St. Mary and the officials of Tournai. When our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Cologne, was collecting a fifth part of the ecclesiastical revenues of his province for one year by grace granted to him by the Apostolic See for paying the debts of the church of Cologne, an appeal was made to the Apostolic See on behalf of our venerable brother, the Bishop of Liège, and the clergy of the city and diocese of Liège because of this. We, having the Archbishop and Bishop present before us, relaxed the sentences of suspension and excommunication pronounced by the Archbishop against the clergy on this occasion and dispensed with those who incurred some irregularity, and for the sake of peace, we have decided to ordain thus: that the same clergy pay three thousand marks of silver to the Archbishop or his procurator in our name within the octave of the coming Pentecost, provided that they consent to our ordinance. The said Bishop shall distribute this money among the churches of the same city and diocese, considering their resources and also the burdens they have borne for the church of Liège, as he sees fit, with the Archbishop restoring or accounting for in payment according to your judgment what he is known to have received from them on this occasion. If the aforementioned clergy refuse to consent to such an ordinance, after it has been explained to them by you, he may freely use the grace granted to him, and those against whom the said sentences were pronounced shall know themselves to have been returned to the same sentences. If they consent, but the said money is not fully paid to the Archbishop within the specified term, he shall have the free power, with our permission, to proceed according to the tenor of the same grace against those who do not pay, the others being completely absolved. Therefore, we command you to go personally without delay to the church of Liège and, having convened the clergy of the whole city and diocese, diligently explain the aforementioned ordinance to them, and present their written response, fortified with your seals, to the said Archbishop and Bishop or their procurators. If such clergy consent to this ordinance, you shall compel them to pay the said money by ecclesiastical censure, with prior warning and setting aside any appeal. If not both, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 8th of February, in the second year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa decano ecclesiae beatae Mariae et officialibus Tornacensibus mandat ut clerum civitatis et diocesis Leodiensis ad solvendam summam tria milia marcarum argenti archiepiscopo Coloniensi, pro pace obtinenda, ecclesiastica censura cogant. 1229, Feb. 8, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the podestà and the commune of Vercelli. Both reason and equity demand that we repay the merits of the devoted with a gracious consideration, rendering a fitting reward for their services, so that they may be encouraged to serve the apostolic see more fervently and invite others by their example. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, recognizing that it is fitting to attend to the constancy you have shown in devotion to the apostolic see, a constancy that neither loss of goods nor dangers to persons could divert from the faithfulness to the Church, and considering it right to favorably accede to your petitions, we, inclined by your supplications, take under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the city of Vercelli, your persons remaining in devotion to the Church and in the defense of the Catholic faith and ecclesiastical liberty, as well as your castles, villas, and other possessions, jurisdictions, and all other goods which you were known to possess at the time when Frederick the prince was excommunicated by the apostolic see, and which you reasonably possess at present or may acquire in the future by just means. We also protect these with the support of this present document. Moreover, we revoke by the authority of these presents any sentences, bans, statutes, ordinances, penalties, confiscations, privileges, and concessions made concerning the goods of the said city or its citizens or their men or any of them by the same prince or anyone else in his name after the sentence of excommunication had been pronounced against him by the same see, notwithstanding any oaths taken on these matters. We also order that the fairs, which were customarily held from ancient times in the aforesaid city and its district, and those specifically called the fairs of All Saints and Saint Eusebius, be celebrated freely and without any contradiction in their accustomed places and times, notwithstanding the fact that the aforementioned prince, after he was excommunicated by the same see, is said to have ordered their transfer to the city of Turin. Let no one, therefore, etc. infringe on our protection, revocation, and constitution, etc. If anyone, etc. Given at Lyons, on the 5th of May, in the second year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa potestati et communi Vercellensibus civitatem Vercellensem cum bonis illorum sub protectione beati Petri et sua suscipit, et revocat sententias et concessiones a Friderico post excommunicationem latas, statuitque ut nundinae antiquo more celebrentur. 1239, Mai. 5. Lugduni.

**Translation to English**:

To the noble man Swantopolk, Duke of Pomerania, the spirit of sound counsel. You should particularly test the strength of your power in that which is pleasing to God and would bring forth the growth of the Christian religion. But you, as we have heard with astonishment, strive to accomplish the opposite, not without grave insult to the Creator, by afflicting with dire troubles the faithful and beloved sons of His, the brothers of the Hospital of Saint Mary of the Germans established in the land of Culm and parts of Prussia, and, what is more grievous, by often attacking them together with the pagans. Those who hear of the enormity of such error are astounded, especially since it surpasses all tyranny and barbarity to assail the family of the Redeemer along with the Letts and Prussians and to incite the sword of a damned people against innocent pilgrims, destroying thus the cause of faith, for which both the Church has been greatly concerned for long past times and the Christian people have endured multiple labors with the shedding of their own blood. You must see to it, noble man, that you do not provoke against yourself the wrath of God because of this and give the Apostolic See reason to presume that you lack the purity of faith, and that it might be to your joy to bring the keys of the Church into contempt, as such an assumption is taken from the fact that for your affliction of the clergy, the manifold desolation of churches, and many excesses of horrendous impiety, you have, as it is asserted, been bound by excommunication for eight years, not caring to return to the mandate of the Church. Therefore, we beseech you by the cross and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, that, putting aside all delay and excuse, returning to the merciful bosom of Mother Church, you may effectively commend the cause of Christ being carried out in Prussia, rendering yourself affable to the aforementioned brothers and the same faithful, and providing them with favorable support for divine and our reverence, so that from this the King of Heaven may be made favorable to you and the Apostolic See, which is known to have received the land of Culm and the acquired territories of Prussia into the right and property of Blessed Peter, may be bound to you for special graces. Otherwise, since we cannot neglect the cause of God, Whose right we strive to preserve for everyone, we will proceed against you, God forbid, persisting in such excesses, in such a way, with the Lord's help, that you will necessarily perceive how the Church is touched in its heart, because the cause of faith is being disturbed by you in such a damnable manner. Given at Lyons, on the Calends of February in the second year (of our pontificate).

**Regesto in Latin**:

Gregorius IX papa nobilis viro Swantopolco, duci Pomeraniae, monet eum ne per perseverantiam in iniuriis contra fratres hospitalis sanctae Mariae Theutonicorum in terris Culmensibus et Prussiae, iram Dei provocet et causam fidei perturbare pergat, sed potius ad ecclesiae mandatum redeat. Dat. Lugduni, Kal. Febr., anno secundo.

**Translation to English:**

To the king and people of the Tartars, to recognize the path of truth. Since not only men but even irrational animals and the very elements of the world are joined by a sort of natural bond of unity, following the example of the heavenly spirits, whose ranks the Creator God has distinguished with the perpetual stability of peaceful order, we are rightly amazed to hear that you, having entered many regions both of Christians and others, have devastated them with horrible desolation, and still, continuing your fury, extend your ravaging hands to further lands, having dissolved the natural bond of kinship, sparing neither sex nor age, raging with the sword of indiscriminate slaughter upon all. Therefore, we, desiring all to live in the unity of peace under the fear of God, following the example of the peaceful King, admonish, beseech, and earnestly exhort you to cease entirely from such attacks and especially from the persecutions of Christians; that you may appease the wrath of the Divine Majesty, which you have undoubtedly provoked severely by such great offenses, through fitting satisfaction of penance. Nor should you gain audacity to further rage from the fact that the Almighty Lord has so far allowed various nations to be laid low before your advancing sword, for sometimes He permits the proud to go unpunished in this world for a time so that if they refuse to humble themselves, He might not delay to punish their wickedness temporally and nonetheless avenge it more severely in the future. And behold, we have decided to send to you our beloved son Brother I.! and his companions, bearers of these presents, men conspicuous in religion, adorned with honesty, and endowed with the knowledge of sacred scripture. You should kindly receive and treat them honorably, giving faith to what they shall tell you on our behalf, and having a fruitful discussion with them concerning the aforesaid matters and especially about those that pertain to peace, you shall inform us fully through the same brothers what has moved you to the extermination of other nations and what you intend further. You are to provide them with secure conduct and other necessities for their journey to and from, so that they may safely return to our presence. The aforementioned brothers, whom etc. as in the next until: we sent others. Given at Lyons, the 13th of March, in the second year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa regi et populo Tartarorum mandat ut a persecutionibus abstineant et monitos per fratres ad pacem convertantur, plenam intentionem suam renuntiare iubens. Datum Lugduni, XIII Martii, anno secundo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Basel. The customary kindness of the Apostolic See distinguishes the merits of individuals with prudent deliberation so that those who excel in knowledge of letters and noble character and lineage may be elevated with greater favor and honored with more significant benefits. Hence, for our beloved son Eberhard, archdeacon of Strasbourg, brother of our dear son, the nobleman, the count of Sulz, of whom a commendable testimony is given to us, we command your fraternity by the authority of these presents, that if he is a noble and learned person, he may lawfully receive other benefices, even if they have the care of souls annexed, provided their revenues do not exceed the annual value of one hundred marks of silver, if they are canonically offered to him, and he may freely retain them along with the archdeaconry of Strasbourg and others already held—notwithstanding the constitution of the general council—by our authority you should grant him dispensation; provided that the mentioned archdeaconry and benefices are not defrauded of their due, etc., until: neglected. Given at Lyon, 18th October, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Basiliensi mandat ut Eberardum archidiaconum Argentinensem, fratrem comitis de Sulze, in recipiendis et retinendis beneficiis cum cura animarum, dummodo proventus non excedant centum marcas argenti annuatim, canonice offerendis, auctoritate apostolica dispenset. Lugduni, XV Kal. Novembris, anno tertio.

**Translation to English:**

To the suffragans of the church of Besançon. The unfathomable depth of divine wisdom, which established the Holy Roman Church in such breadth, has so arranged its governance and administration with unchangeable foresight that, although one holds the fullness of power for the consolidation of the unity of the Church, several are assumed to share the responsibility of its wholesome governance. For it willed that sons be born for its fathers, who would be set above all princes, mindful of their name and renowned heralds of the evangelical truth. Hence, we, who despite our insufficient merits have been placed on the high watchtower of the same Church, intend, with divine assistance, to carry out the ministry entrusted to us concerning nearby churches, so that we should not lack appropriate providence even for those from which we are distant by the positioning of places.

Since, therefore, the church of Besançon had been without a shepherd for a long time, and the provision for it had devolved upon us, we, wishing to provide it with such a person who, excelling in the merits of life, pleasing to God and men, powerful in word and deed, should shine like a star, illuminating the subjects with the light of the word of God, since the lamp should be placed on the candlestick of the church of Besançon, widowed by the death of its shepherd, to recall the errant from the wandering of truth with the light of doctrine and to be ignited with the zeal of justice in the spirit of judgment and fervor against the guilty without respect of persons, we have deemed it appropriate to appoint our venerable brother W., formerly bishop of Chalon, a man truly after our heart, of celebrated fame and known wisdom, freed from the bonds of the church of Chalon, as the archbishop and shepherd of the church of Besançon, firmly hoping that under his governance it will receive welcome increase in the Lord both spiritually and temporally. We command you to render him the due and devoted obedience and reverence as members obedient to the head, so that mutual grace among you may produce pleasing results, and we may justly commend your devotion in the Lord. Given at Lyon, the 21st of March, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa suffraganeis ecclesiae Bisuntinae mandatum dedit ut venerabili fratri W., olim episcopo Cabilonensi, in archiepiscopum et pastorem ecclesiae Bisuntinae praeficiendo, debitam obedientiam et reverentiam exhibeant. 1230, Mart. 21, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of Frigidus Mons of the Cistercian order in the diocese of Beauvais, the archdeacon and the penitentiary of Beauvais. Werricus, the dean, John, the cantor, and several other canons of the church of Trier have shown us through their petition that when the church was without a pastor, the chapter, with all those present who wanted, should, and could conveniently attend, convened to discuss the substitution of a future bishop. The treasurer and certain other canons of the same church, although they were suspended and bound by the chain of excommunication, should not have taken part in the discussion of the election, nevertheless, presumptuously usurping to themselves the right of election, presumed to elect A., then provost of the same church, who held many dignities and ecclesiastical benefices with the care of souls without an apostolic dispensation, when they could not do so by law. And although the said dean, cantor, and others adhering to them, to whom the right of election legally belonged, canonically elected the provost of the church of St. Paul of Trier as pastor of the said church of Trier, the said provost of Trier, trusting in his own power, does not fear to intrude into the administration of the spiritual and temporal affairs of the same church of Trier and to behave wickedly with its goods, to the peril of his soul, the great harm of the church, and the grave scandal of many. Wherefore, the aforementioned dean, cantor, and others have humbly begged us to provide, with fatherly care, for the indemnity of the same church regarding these matters. However, the procurator of the aforementioned A. proposed in opposition that, when the aforesaid church of Trier was vacant, all those who should, wanted, and could conveniently attend, convened on the day appointed for the election to discuss the substitution of a future bishop. The treasurer, Terricus, Arnold, and Henry, the archdeacons, with the greater and sounder part of the chapter of Trier, after the scrutiny had been undertaken and immediately published, and diligent deliberation had been held, canonically elected the aforementioned A., a noble, learned, prudent, and discreet man, circumspect in spiritual and temporal matters, as archbishop of the already mentioned church of Trier, who gave his consent to the election made of him. But Werricus, who acts as dean, and John, who acts as cantor of Trier, with some adhering to them, although they are not the greater and sounder part of the same chapter, presumed to elect the aforementioned provost of the church of St. Paul of Trier, less suitable and holding many dignities and ecclesiastical benefices with the care of souls without an apostolic dispensation, as archbishop of Trier de facto, when they could not do so by law. Having received the regalia from secular authority, he made homage be forcefully exhibited to him by the men of the already mentioned church of Trier in its towns and villages, intruding into the administration of the temporal affairs of the same church to the notable prejudice and grievance of the said A. and the same church. Finally, coming to his senses with his supporters, he yielded to this question, recognizing the right to be acquired by the other party. Wherefore, the aforementioned procurator has urgently requested us to provide a salutary remedy to the same church against so many dangers imminent to it because of this. Since our daily concern is the continual care of all churches, we command you, having summoned those who should be summoned, to diligently inquire with our authority into the aforesaid matters and others concerning this business, faithfully informing us by your letters of what you have found, assigning the parties a suitable, peremptory term when they should personally or through suitable procurators present themselves to our sight, to receive what justice shall dictate by the gift of the Lord; provided that nothing is attempted in prejudice of the canons and others prosecuting this business on this occasion, and if anything is presumed otherwise, to restore it to the proper state with the obstacle of appeal removed, contradictors, etc. — notwithstanding the constitution concerning the two days issued in the general council, provided that no one is brought to judgment beyond the third or fourth day outside their diocese by authority of these presents. What if not all, etc. Given at the Lateran, on the third Nones of December, in the first year.

Gregorius IX papa abbati Frigidi Montis Cisterciensis ordinis Belvacensis diocesis, archidiacono et penitentiario Belvacensibus mandat, ut, vocatis evocandis, super electione controversia in ecclesia Treverensi veritatem inquirant, partibus terminum assignantes quo se nostro conspectui repraesentent. 1227, Dec.

**Translation to English:**

To the illustrious King of Hungary. The prompt devotion of your royal majesty, with which you honor Christ and His Church, the bride, with due reverence, rightfully requires and laudably merits that we grant your petitions as much as we are able with God, considering it rightfully owed to you that we bestow upon your excellence whatever grace and favor we can. It was indeed proposed on your behalf before us that, when the kingdom of Hungary was formerly ravaged by barbarian nations and almost completely devastated by the tyranny of the Tartars, by the permission or command of the Lord, fearing that the kingdom might come to utter ruin, and desiring that its remnants might be saved, you rendered the oath of homage to the late Emperor F. under the condition that he would powerfully come to your kingdom to defend it against the aforementioned Tartars or send his son there within a certain time. The same Emperor F., long expected, neither came after the term nor sent his son as he had promised. Therefore, you have humbly petitioned us to ensure that, on this account, nothing can be claimed from the Roman Empire against you or your kingdom in the future, and that we should, with fatherly care, look after your indemnity in this matter. Therefore, considering that whenever something is granted under a condition and the condition is not fulfilled, it should be regarded as if it had not been granted, and also considering that a bruised reed is not to be broken nor should affliction be added to the afflicted, but rather human solace should be provided to those who urgently need others' compassion, so that a greater abundance of merits may accrue to the merciful, and especially since the aforesaid Emperor F., like other Christians, was bound to this by the dictate of nature, and was not to be hired for a reward: we, by the counsel of our brothers, declare by the authority of these presents that you are not bound by such an oath and homage, so that on this account nothing can ever be claimed against you or your successors or your kingdom at any time by anyone. Let no one, therefore, etc. of our declaration, etc. If anyone, etc. Given at Lyons, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of September, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa regi Hungariae illustri declarat eum non teneri iuramento et homagio prestito quondam imperatori F., cum condicione non extante, ita quod nichil in eum vel successores eius aut regnum possit vendicari. Dat. Lugduni, XII Kal. Septembr. anno tertio.

**Translation to English:**

To the master and brothers of the Hospital of Saint Mary of the Teutons of Jerusalem. We commend the just petitions, etc., to the consent, the limitation of the dioceses of Prussia and the adjoining land of Culm, and the division of the lands of Prussia, which were made with prudent deliberation at the Apostolic See by our venerable brother, formerly Bishop of Modena, our penitentiary, and legate of the Apostolic See in those parts, as contained more fully in the letters drawn up by him concerning this matter. We hold them ratified and firm, and we confirm them with apostolic authority and fortify them with the protection of this present writing. We have had the tenor of those letters recorded word for word in these presents, which is as follows:

William, by divine mercy formerly Bishop of Modena, legate of the Apostolic See, to all who inspect the present letters, greetings in the name of Jesus Christ. Let your entire community know that the most holy father, Lord Pope Innocent IV, among other things pertaining to the office of legation, entrusted to us in his presence, so that we might limit the dioceses within the terms of our legation and institute bishops in the same. By this authority, concerning the already converted regions, we thus limited the dioceses in Prussia. For the first diocese, we limited it from the land of Culm, as it is bounded by the three rivers Vistula, Drwęca, and Osa, so that Lubovia is included in the same diocese. However, in the land of Culm, it pertains only to the bishop who will be in office at the time, what was arranged by the common consent and will of the bishop of Prussia and the brothers of the Hospital of Saint Mary of the Teutons and the men dwelling in the same land of Culm, when men first entered to inhabit that desert, namely one measure of wheat and one measure of rye from each plow and one measure of wheat from each harrow, and in addition six hundred manses of land in appropriate or appropriate places of the same land of Culm.

Furthermore, we limited the second diocese as the Osa, Vistula, and Drusnia lake enclose it, ascending through the Passaluc river, so that the islands of Quidino and Santerii are within the same diocese. We also limited the third as it is enclosed by the Baltic Sea from the west and the river Pregola or Lipza from the north, and the aforementioned Drusnia lake from the south, ascending through the aforementioned Passaluc river towards the east up to the borders of the Letts. Concerning the unconquered land adjoining the aforementioned diocese, we limited the fourth diocese as it is enclosed by the salt sea from the west and the Memel river from the north and the Pregola river from the south, towards the east up to the borders of the Letts, so that all the aforesaid rivers are shared by the dioceses which are bounded by those rivers.

Moreover, because the aforementioned brothers bear the entire burden of expenses and wars and it is necessary for them to enfeoff many lands, we divided the lands of Prussia in such a way that, whether there is one bishop or several, the brothers shall have two parts entirely with all revenues, and the bishop or bishops the third part entirely with all jurisdiction and right; however, reserving to the bishop in the two parts of the brothers all those things which cannot be exercised except by the bishop. But that this division of lands may freely obtain its due effect, it shall be done in the name of Christ first according to the will and consent of the bishop and the brothers of the same hospital. And if concord cannot be reached, then they shall choose common friends through whom such a division may be made, and if they cannot even concord in such a manner, then those brothers, because the land is more known to them, shall divide the diocese into three parts and the bishop shall have the choice of one of those parts. Or if perhaps he does not wish to choose, which part out of those three parts shall belong to the bishop, as the lots may decide, it shall be determined. In witness whereof, we have caused the present writing to be strengthened with the protection of our seal. Dated at Anagni, in the year of the Lord 1243, on the fourth day of the month of July, in the first indiction, in the first year of the pontificate of the same lord pope.

Therefore, let no one infringe upon our confirmation, etc. But if anyone should, etc. Dated at Anagni, on the 8th of the Ides of October, in the first year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa magistro et fratribus Hospitalis Sanctae Mariae Theutonicorum

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz. God has established the fullness of ecclesiastical power in the apostolic see so that the Roman pontiff, who received the keys of power and discretion through blessed Peter, can sometimes exercise strictness and sometimes prefer leniency. Indeed, by considering all circumstances and leaving neither aside, he sometimes tempers strictness with leniency such that its force is not weakened, but wisely takes into account not only the persons but also the matters with which and in which he intends to dispense, lest he dispense in such a way as to dissipate, or dissipate as he dispenses, as the diversity of cases may require different modes of dispensation. It has been made known to us by our beloved son, Count Henry of Anhalt, that once one of the vials of God's wrath was poured out by the angel who was given power to harm, grave wars and enmities arose between his late father of blessed memory and the noble lords, the Margraves of Brandenburg. The cause of dissension sowed the seeds of discord, leading to human slaughter and various dangers on both sides. Thus, since peace could not otherwise be restored between them, except that the said Margraves swore to give the noble woman Mathilda, daughter of the noble Duke of Brunswick, to him in marriage, the count humbly petitioned us that, since he and Mathilda are known to be related in the fourth degree of consanguinity and he had not yet sought confirmation of this marriage, we might apply a salutary counsel to settle the aforementioned enmities. Therefore, considering that urgent necessity and evident benefit demand a dispensation, we command you that, if the truth supports these premises, you are to dispense them by our authority so that they may contract marriage if they wish, notwithstanding this impediment. Given at Lyon, on the 18th of May, in the second year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa archiepiscopo Maguntino mandat ut, urgente necessitate et evidenti utilitate, dispenset cum Henrico comite de Anchalt et Mathilda de Bruneswich, ut, impedimento consanguinitatis non obstante, matrimonium contrahere possint. Datum Lugduni, XV Kalendas Iunii, anno secundo.

**Translation to English:**

To the provincial prior of the Order of Preachers in Germany. 

We extend prompt favor to the just causes of men, and we ought with vigilant care to pursue the pious works of Jesus Christ all the more willingly, as it is known that God must be preferred by man and all reverence is due to Him. Therefore, since, as we have learned with joy from the report of trustworthy persons, the Creator of all things has been exalted manifoldly in the regions of Livonia and Prussia by the triumphant hand of our beloved sons, the brothers of the Hospital of Saint Mary of the Teutons of Jerusalem, and other faithful, and there is hope that the glory of His name will be further extended there, if we provide support to His planting in those parts, which we can in Him, by devoted aid of the Church: we beseech and exhort your devotion in the Lord, through apostolic writings, commanding and enjoining the remission of sins, that you make an effort to assign the priors and brothers of your order established in the provinces of Magdeburg and Bremen, dioceses of Regensburg, Passau, Halberstadt, Hildesheim, and Verdun, to such business, disregarding any difficulty, and exhort them earnestly to take on the duty of holy preaching for God's sake, to diligently and carefully instruct the faithful of the said provinces and dioceses with pious exhortations, according to the wisdom given to them by God, that they regard and return something for all that He has given them, having been redeemed at a glorious price, in whom it should fall as men who are Christians and Catholics to bear the reproaches of those reproaching Christ, that they gird themselves vigorously and mightily, having the zeal of God to expand the glory of the Crucified and to deliver their neighbors from the hands of pagans, proceeding and acting according to the counsel of the aforesaid brothers, so that eternal reward may be due to them, and infidels may not boast that they have impugned the name of Christ with impunity. Those from the said provinces and dioceses who, marked with the sign of the cross for the aid of Livonia or Prussia, cannot personally proceed there due to poverty or weakness, may be absolved from the vow of the cross, provided they offer a suitable contribution from their goods according to their abilities, to be converted to the same aid through the hands of the same brothers. For we, to complete what is so worthily sought for the name of the Redeemer with easy effect, admitting all those from the said provinces and dioceses who will proceed with the sign of the cross for the support of the same faithful, as well as their family and all their goods, under the protection and defense of the Apostolic See until their return or death is most certainly known, grant to them and others, who according to their capacity and status, will send suitable warriors there at their own expense, or who will supply a suitable contribution from their own goods to the aid of the said Livonia or Prussia, or who will go there at others' expense, to serve for at least a year's time, the same indulgence and privilege as are granted to those crossing over and supporting the aid of the Holy Land. Moreover, that the aforementioned business, which can be helped by many remedies, may receive the desired increase of prosperity, we grant by the authority of these presents to the priors and brothers assigned by you to the aforementioned business, that to those of the same provinces and dioceses who come to their solemn preaching, they may relax twenty days from the enjoined penance, and to each of them who proceed with the character of the cross taken up for this purpose, who have incurred the snare of excommunication for arson and violence against clerics or other religious persons, they may extend the benefit of absolution according to the form of the Church, provided that they satisfactorily compensate those who have suffered losses and injuries, except for those whose excesses are so grave and enormous that they must justly be referred to the Apostolic See. Given at Anagni, on the ninth day before the Kalends of October, in the first year of our pontificate.

In the same manner to the provincial prior of the Order of Preachers in Poland for the kingdom of Bohemia, Poland, and Pomerania. In the same manner to the provincial prior of the Order of Preachers in Denmark.

Gregorius IX papa priori provinciali fratrum ordinis Praedicatorum in Alemannia mandat ut fratres ordinis in variis provinciis constituti ad subsidium Livoniae et Prussiae exhortentur, indulgentias concedens et protectionem sedis apostolicae promittens. Dat. Anagnie, VIIII Kal. Octobris, anno I.

Considering previously that our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Mainz, had undertaken many burdens of expenses and had to endure them for the cause of the church, which he pursues with all his might, fearing neither the dangers of things nor of people, we gave you our letters instructing you to liberally provide him with a fifth of all your revenues. We, not wishing that the payment of this fifth be delayed by any evasions, have deemed it necessary to exhort and admonish you more attentively again, firmly commanding you by apostolic writings that, prudently considering that you benefit yourself in this assistance, you pay the said fifth liberally, willingly, and completely to the Archbishop without any difficulty. Do not place any trust in the letters or envoys of the prince, who promise to render you completely unpunished from the offense against the Apostolic See. **Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa eis qui remissi sunt in solutione quintae reddituum suorum ad subventionem archiepiscopi Maguntini, mandat ut quintam sine difficultate persolvant et sententias in rebelles latas observeant. 1238, Mai. 11, Lugduni.

Translation to English:

I. To the Archbishop of Sens. The power and wisdom of God, Lord Jesus Christ, to whose ineffable majesty all things are subject, from the beginning of creation has illuminated His Church with the splendor of virtues and endowed it with the unique privilege of power, so that through its ministry His justice may be achieved and, with the storm of wars calmed, peace may come to the world. Considering with reverence the preeminence of this dignity, we, who by divine providence, though unworthy, preside over the government of the universal Church, are made anxious in heart that the horror of the tempest, by which the Church itself is troubled and the Christian religion is shaken, may be averted by the aid of our provision with the help of heavenly mercy. Hence it is that we, so that the Church itself may have the beautiful order of its due state through the healthy counsel and fruitful assistance of the faithful, and that aid may be swiftly brought to the lamentable peril of the Holy Land and the afflicted empire of Romania, and a remedy found against the Tartars and other despisers of the faith and persecutors of the Christian people, and also for the matter that is in dispute between the Church and the prince, have decided to call the kings of the earth, the prelates of the churches, and other princes of the world. We therefore earnestly ask and exhort your fraternity, commanding by our authority that, having postponed every other consideration, you make an effort to come personally to our presence by the next feast of St. John the Baptist, so that the Church itself may receive spiritual joy from the honor of your visit and gain beneficial counsel from your industry; knowing that we have summoned the said prince in our proclamation, that he may appear in person or through his envoys at the council to be held, to answer to us and others who may have anything to propose against him, and to offer suitable satisfaction. As for the moderate number of persons and conveyances, you will ensure, when you come, that it is not excessively burdensome to your Church. Furthermore, we wish and command that you do not delay to instruct your suffragans to attend to our presence for these matters by the same date, and to instruct their chapters to send prudent and faithful envoys who may, on their behalf, offer us useful counsel. Given at Lyon, 3rd of the Nones of January, in the second year.

II. To the Chapter of Sens. The power of God, etc., up to: send prudent and faithful envoys by the feast of St. John the Baptist, so that the Church itself may receive spiritual joy from the honor of such a visit and from their industry, etc., as in the other, up to: to offer suitable satisfaction. Given as in the previous.

III. To the illustrious King of France. The power of God, etc., up to: to call. We therefore earnestly ask your serene Highness, and exhort you attentively, that you send prudent and faithful envoys to our presence by the next feast of St. John the Baptist, etc., up to: to offer suitable satisfaction. May you, son of blessing, fulfill this our desire in such a way that, rejoicing in you as a zealous defender of the honor of the Church, we may respond to what we shall perceive to be pleasing to God in your future, with paternal affections. Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa, archiepiscopo Senonensi mandat, ut ad suam praesentiam usque ad festum sancti Ioannis Baptistae veniat, ut ecclesia ex visitationis suae honore gaudium spirituale percipiat, et consilium utile pro negotiis ecclesiae praebeat. Dat. Lugduni, III Non. Ian. anno secundo.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Raymond, Count of Toulouse. Recently, we have decided to admit you, reconciled to the Church, into the fullness of the grace of the Apostolic See and our own. We gladly agree to the wishes of your nobility and devotion, and we aim to honor and support you with the prerogative of our favor in those things you request worthily, demonstrating favor to you as much as we can with God. You have proposed in our presence that Brothers Ferrarius and G. The immense kindness of God the Father, looking upon the fall of the human race which had been brought down by the sin of the first man, with ineffable compassion and wishing to mercifully restore what had been prostrated by the deceitful suggestion of diabolical envy, sent His only begotten Son, consubstantial with Himself, from the high throne of heaven to the lowly ground of the earth. Human nature, being rational, was to be nourished by eternal truth as its best sustenance; but restrained by the bonds of mortal punishment due to sin, it was reduced to such a state of lack that it could only strive to understand the invisible through conjectures of visible things. **Latin Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Magdeburgensi mandat ut personaliter ad eius praesentiam accedat infra mensem ad respondendum super omnibus quae contra eum proposita sunt. Datum Laterani, anno pontificatus III.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz. Since, as it was proposed to us on behalf of our beloved son, the elected Bishop of Strasbourg, it is necessary for the same elected bishop to incur expenses for the urgent business of the church, we command that you grant him, if you see it fit, the free authority by our mandate to contract up to a certain sum and to pledge the possessions of the church of Strasbourg to those with whom he has contracted; any objectors, etc. Given as above at the nearest date.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino mandat, ut electo Argentinensi, propter expensas negotii ecclesiae subeundas, auctoritate apostolica facultatem concedat possessiones ecclesiae Argentinensis obligandi. Datum ut supra proxima.

**Translation to English:**

Bishop of Cambrai. Your brotherhood has informed us that some clerics in your city and diocese...

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorii IX papae episcopo Cameracensi scribit de querela, quod nonnulli clerici in civitate et dioecesi Cameracensi agunt. Datum ... (incomplete date), pontificatus nostri anno (incomplete year), loco ... (incomplete place).

(Note: The provided text, "Berger 1920. .. episcopo Cameracensi. Tua nobis fraternitas intimavit, quod a nonnulli clerici in civitate ac diocesi tua," is incomplete both in content and details necessary for a complete regesto. Thus, placeholders (...) have been used for missing information.)

Translation to English:

To the bishop-elect of Ferrara. Having received your letters with affection, etc., as above in the previous [letter] until: he should pursue it vigorously, explaining to him how steadfastly the Church intends to support him, considering in this both the increase of royal honor and the strengthening of the Catholic faith and the defense of ecclesiastical liberty. Regarding the provision of the promised aid by us, etc., until: we arrange. Given at Lyon, on the 10th of June, in the third year [of the pontificate].

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa electo Ferrariensi mandat, ut quam constanter ecclesia sibi assistat, cum haec regii honoris augmentum et catholicae fidei robur consideret, exponat. Lugduni, 1239, Iun. 10.

**Translation to English:**

To the same recipients. Through special letters, we have previously instructed you not to grant prebends or ecclesiastical benefices in the Kingdom of Sicily, so that you can more appropriately defend yourselves against the undue insistence of petitioners. Since it is our desire to honor your persons in all matters that we can do so worthily, we wish that if it ever seems opportune to you to grant some benefices, you should explain it to us in your letters, for we are ready to grant what appears to you to be expedient for the honor of the Church or the benefit of the business entrusted to your prudence.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa eisdem mandat ut, licet prohibuerit ne in regno Siciliae beneficia conferant, tamen si eis expedire visum fuerit, id sibi per suas litteras exponant, quia paratus est concedere. Datum Laterani, anno undecimo.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected bishop of Ferrara, legate of the apostolic see. By the authority of these presents, we command you to earnestly advise and induce our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of Bohemia, to powerfully and openly assist our dearest son in Christ, H., the illustrious King of the Romans, for the honor of God and the Church, compelling him to do so with our authority, if necessary. Given at Lyon, on the third day before the Nones of July, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa electo Ferrariensi, apostolicae sedis legato mandat, ut regem Boemiae moneat et inducat, ut regi Romanorum assistat, necessario etiam auctoritate compellendo. 1246, Iul. 5, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the same. Since we have heard certain grievances concerning our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Magdeburg, which could provide us with just grounds for proceeding against him, we wish and by the authority of these presents command you to carefully admonish and induce the said archbishop to assist our beloved son in Christ, H., the illustrious King of the Romans, in such a powerful and manifest manner to the honor of God and the Church that he may be seen to fully absolve himself of his guilt. Inform him that if he should be negligent in this matter, we will not be able to overlook the unfavorable things we have heard about him. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa eidem mandat ut archiepiscopum Magdeburgensem moneat et inducat ad assistendum regi Romanorum, ne neglectis culpis auditis procedatur. Datum ut supra.

Translation to English:

... to the Archbishop of Mainz. Since, as has been reported to us, the monastery of Reinherisbrun of the Order of Saint Benedict in your diocese, which is said to have been founded by the progenitors of our beloved son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, H., is gravely deformed in spiritual matters, we, by the authority of these presents, command your fraternity to diligently investigate this matter. If you find it to be so, you are to reform the aforementioned monastery in its order if possible, otherwise in another order as you see fit, by our authority, with the monks of the same monastery being placed in other monasteries of their order; contradictors, etc. Given as above.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino mandat ut, monasterio Reinherisbrun ordinis sancti Benedicti in spiritualibus depravato, diligenter inquisito, si rem ita esse invenerit, illud auctoritate apostolica reformet, monachis in aliis monasteriis collocatis. Datum Laterani, anno pontificatus sexto.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Tusculum, legate of the Apostolic See. We wish and by the authority of these presents command you, that you do not hesitate to instruct those to whom you have entrusted the preaching of the cross throughout Germany for the aid of the Holy Land, so that they may refrain from such preaching at these times. This is especially because it is said to be now of little efficacy in those parts, and we have ordered the word of the cross to be preached in those same parts against Frederick, the former emperor of the Romans. We also wish that you keep this matter confidential, not to be revealed to anyone. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Tusculano mandat ut in Theotonia predicationem crucis pro Terra Sancta intermittant et eam contra F. quondam imperatorem Rom. predicant. Datum ut supra.

Translation to English:

To R., Cardinal Deacon of Saint Angel. Restored by the fragrance of devotion, which your letter presented to us, we have confidently decided to admonish you through the tenor of these presents that, considering with a diligent mind how abundantly God pursues His Church with mercy, you might turn your affection from the heart to this, that through the help of those whom you know are devoted to the Apostolic See, and particularly through the power of your house, the honor of the Church may advance according to your desire and its persecutor, the perfidious and impious Frederick, may succumb with the Lord’s right hand prevailing, and that from this you may gain an increase of renowned name among men and eternal reward with the Most High.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa R. Sancti Angeli diacono cardinali mandat ut, per auxilium fidelium Apostolicae Sedis eiusque domus potentiam, ad ecclesiae honorem promovendum et Fridericum impium deprimendum animum convertat. Datum anno pontificatus primo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Arborensis. On behalf of our beloved daughter in Christ, Adelasia, judge of Torres and Gallura, it was humbly requested that, since Henry, the son of the late Emperor Frederick, has stained the marital bed with the crime of adultery after contracting marriage with her against the prohibition of the church, we order a divorce to be celebrated between them. Therefore, we command that, after diligently inquiring into the truth of this matter, if it is established to you regarding the adultery, you separate the marriage to the extent that is just concerning the separation of the bed, by our authority. Given at Lyon, 21st of June, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Arborensi mandat, ut inter Henricum, filium Friderici quondam imperatoris, et Adelasian, iudicissam Turritanam et Gallurii, matrimonium dirimat, si adulterium constiterit. 1230, Iun. 21, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the same. We grant to your discretion the free authority, by the authority of these presents, to grant our beloved son in Christ, the illustrious king of the Romans, H., some religious men of any order from the parts of Germany, whom the same king shall have decided to request to stay with him, and also to designate some for the present business, whom the aforementioned king shall have chosen for this purpose, and to restrain the opposers of this matter by ecclesiastical censure, setting aside any appeals. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa discretioni destinatarii concedit potestatem eligendi religiosos ex partibus Theutonie, quos rex Romanorum H. secum retinere velit, et quosdam pro negotio destinandi, contradictores per censuram ecclesiasticam coercendo. Datum ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Liège. Since, as we have learned from your communication, you are obliged to bear heavy expenses for the imminent business of the church, we, inclined by the prayers of your devotion, grant you full authority by the present letter to contract a loan, with the advice and consent of our beloved sons, the prior of the Dominicans and the guardian of the Franciscan brothers of Liège, up to the amount that you deem necessary. Additionally, you are granted the power to pledge some possessions of your bishopric to those with whom you contract. Given at Lyon, the 10th of July, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Leodiensi mandat, ut ob necessitates ecclesiae mutuum cum assensu prioris Prodicatorum et guardiani Minorum fratrum Leodiensium contrahat, possessiones episcopatus obligando. Datum Lugduni, X Iulii, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the same. On behalf of our dearest son in Christ, H., the illustrious King of the Romans, it has been requested of us that since the nobleman Frederick of Drivorte, his advisor, has sworn that he would not act as a guarantor for anyone as long as he lives, and this might result in a disadvantage for the said king, we should kindly absolve the nobleman from such an oath and consider his salvation if he has perhaps not kept it thus far. Therefore, we command that you take care, by our authority, concerning the rash violation of the aforementioned oath — which pertains to the nobleman's soul's salvation — and concerning the relaxation of the same oath, which you shall determine to be expedient after weighing necessity or benefit.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa eidem mandat, ut Fredericum de Drivorte, consiliarium regis Romanorum, ab iuramento fideiussoriae obligationis absolvat, si necessarium aut utile videatur. Anno 5, Datum Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected bishop of Speyer. As we have received through your information, some individuals from the city and diocese of Speyer, who had once adhered to the former Emperor Frederick, wish to return to the embrace of the Church.
