Inclined by your prayers of devotion, we grant you by the authority of these presents, the full faculty to absolve them according to the form of the Church from the excommunication which they are known to have incurred, and also from any oath, if perchance they have made any regarding this matter, provided that they remain in the service of the Church in the regions of Germany for as long as they should have remained in the overseas regions according to our statute, for the duration they remained in service to the aforementioned Frederick. Given at Lyon, 30th of July, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa electo Spirensi concedit facultatem absolvendi nonnullos Spirensis civitatis et diocesis ab excommunicatione, si ad gremium ecclesiae redire concupiscant. 1246, Iul. 30, Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To the same. As we have ordered the preaching of the word of the cross to the faithful of Christ throughout Germany against Frederick, the former Roman emperor, we wish and by the authority of these presents we command you to ensure that what these faithful will contribute from their goods for this matter be diligently collected and faithfully preserved, to be expended later for the promotion of the same matter according to our mandate. Given at Lyon, 4th of the Nones of July, in the fourth year [of our pontificate].

Regesto in Latin:

Innocentius IV papa mandat ut in Theotonia, contra Fridericum quondam imperatorem, fideles Christi verbum crucis praedicent, et ut contributiones eorum diligenter colligantur et serventur pro negotii promotione. Datum Lugduni, II Nonas Iulii, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz. Since we know you to be a key promoter among church prelates of the affairs of the Church and the Roman Empire, we confidently and trustingly direct writings to you regarding matters we believe to be expedient for these affairs. Hence, we have entrusted to you and to our beloved son, the elected bishop of Ferrara, legate of the Apostolic See, the case that has arisen concerning the elections held in the church of Regensburg. As we have learned, the noble man, the Duke of Bavaria, is quite disturbed by this. Therefore, we wish and, by the authority of these presents, command your brotherhood to consider how useful the said duke can be to the aforesaid church and empire and to endeavor to suspend the case. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino scribit de causa electionis in ecclesia Ratisponensi, quam sibi et electo Ferrariensi commisit, monens ut, considerata utilitate ducis Bavariae, causam suspendat. Datum ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Alfonso, the firstborn son of our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious king of Castile and León. We are rightly and gladly attentive to the increase of your honor, as it is frequently recognized by renowned indications that you are diligently and effectively found to be magnanimous in works of virtue. Since, as you assert, your intention is directed towards having the right that the late Beatrix, queen of Castile and León, your mother, is said to have had in the duchy of Swabia, come to you, her heir, we want you to have full confidence in the benevolence of the apostolic see, that if you have legitimately undertaken to pursue the said right or if its acquisition comes to you by just means, the aforesaid see, as far as it can be done with God and honesty, will grant you the assistance of its favorable support in this matter. Given at Lyon, on the 5th of May, in the third year.

**Regesto:**

Innocentius IV papa Alfonso, primogenito regis Castellae et Legionis, suadet ut fiduciam habeat in auxilio sedis apostolicae pro iure ducatus Sueviae persequendo, si legitime id agere vel adquirere poterit. 1245, Mai. 5. Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To the noble men Pandulf of Fasanella, Jacob of Morra, and William Francis. We give thanks to divine mercy, which has rescued you from the hand of Pharaoh and brought you safely to the bosom of the Apostolic See. You, however, as sons of blessing, should take on the strength of a steadfast spirit and wait with confidence, for the power of the Most High will soon establish you and others afflicted in the Kingdom of Sicily under joyful liberty, especially since, after consulting with our brothers, we have decided to provide for the safety of said kingdom by appointing solemn legates and appropriate aid, hoping from their diligence that the cause of God and the Church should soon, with God's favor, come to the glory of triumph.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa nobilibus viris Pandulfo de Fasanella, Iacobo de Morra et Willelmo Francisco significat gratiam divinam eos a periculis liberasse atque spem firmam exprimit de liberatione regni Siciliae, consulto de legatis et subsidiis necessariis ad salutem regni procurandam. 1230, Roma.

**Translation to English:**

To the same. On behalf of the noble man G. of Wassenberg, it has been requested of us that, since he has taken as his wife the noble woman Elisabeth, the widow of the former firstborn of the noble man, the count of Cleves, related to him in the third degree of consanguinity, we might mercifully arrange a dispensation for them so that they may lawfully remain in the marriage thus contracted. However, as we have understood from several reports that a serious scandal would arise if a dispensation were not granted for such a marriage, we entrust to your discretion by the authority of these presents that you may, by our authority, grant a dispensation in this matter, if you see that it is expedient for the pressing business of the church and the empire. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa discretioni recipientis committit, ut dispensationem auctoritate apostolica concedat pro matrimonio inter G. de Wassenberg et Elisabeth, viduam primogeniti comitis Clevensis, in tertio consanguinitatis gradu coniunctos. Datum ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To all brothers of the Order of Friars Minor established throughout Germany. Since the Apostolic See regards your order with special affection among others and has honored it with many privileges, and always intends to strengthen it with manifold favor, it holds a fuller confidence in you as it hopes you, among other religious groups, will burn with greater devotion towards it. Therefore, we earnestly admonish and exhort your entire community that, once the election of the King of the Romans to be later promoted to Emperor has taken place, you encourage the faithful of Christ residing in Germany, whenever you have the opportunity, with diligent exhortations both in private and public, according to the prudence given to you by God. Instruct them, granting remission of sins, to faithfully and effectively support him who has been elected, and to stand by him manfully and steadfastly. Dated as above. In the same manner, to all brothers of the Order of Preachers established throughout Germany.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa universis fratribus ordinis Minorum per Theutoniam mandat, ut post electionem regis Romanorum in imperatorem promovendum, fideles per Theutoniam constitutos exhortentur ad fideliter assistendum electo, remissione peccaminum iniuncta. Datum ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected bishop of Ferrara, legate of the apostolic see. Since, as we have learned, our venerable brother, the bishop of Hildesheim, intends to resign from the governance of the Church of Hildesheim, we wish and by the authority of these presents command you, that if this bishop indeed happens to resign, you, receiving his resignation on our behalf, should instruct the chapter of that church to provide themselves with a suitable shepherd within a certain term set by you, with your counsel and agreement. But if perchance they do not see fit to make such provision, you shall then, by our authority, appoint a prudent and honest person as pastor to that church, as you see fit, ensuring that the aforementioned chapter and the subordinates of that church render him the due obedience and reverence; contradictors etc. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa electo Ferrariensi, apostolicae sedis legato mandat, ut in casu cessionis episcopi Hildesemensis, cessionem recipiat et capitulo praecipiat de pastore idoneo providere, et si non providerint, ipsum ipse praeficiat. Datum ut supra.

Translation to English:

To the elected Bishop of Ferrara, legate of the Apostolic See. With our letters, we have given a mandate to our dear sons, the noble men, all the princes, counts, barons, and other nobles established throughout Germany, instructing them for the remission of their sins, to assist clearly in the matter of the Roman Empire, as in the forthcoming...; and through these letters, we promise them that neither in the life of this king... nor will we reform peace without them. We wish and by the authority of these presents command you, with diligent effort, to labor so that the aforementioned princes and others likewise promise us, having received letters from them on this matter and other firm assurances, if you can obtain it. Given as above.

Regesto:

Gregorius IX papa electo Ferrariensi legato mandat ut principes et nobiles Theotonicos inducat ad promittendum auxilium in negotio imperii Romani, promissionibus et cautionibus receptis. Datum Lateranis, anno pontificatus primo.

**Translation to English:**

To our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, H. We have received with the appropriate joy and kindness the beloved sons Walter, Count of Atinstein, Theoderic of Gruningin, and Henry, brothers of the Hospital of Saint Mary of the Germans, your special envoys whom you have sent to the apostolic see. We have diligently listened to what they have presented on your behalf, accepting their petitions with favorable benevolence. We wish your magnificence to know that if, by chance, we do not grant the requests made to us on the royal behalf, it is not because we intend to be difficult concerning these matters, particularly since we wish to honor you above all other rulers of the world in this and other matters, but rather because we believe they are not expedient. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa illustri regi Romanorum H. scribit se nuntios eius benigne recepisse et petitiones suas benivolo favore admisisse, sed non semper eas concedere quia non expediunt. — Datum ut supra.

Translation to English:

Since, as we have received from your report, you cannot enter the diocese of Olomouc without fault on your part, so that this may not be to your prejudice and to the detriment of your subjects' salvation, we grant you by the authority of these presents the faculty of calling both religious and other secular clerics of the said diocese to the place where you are outside of it, and of enjoining upon them those things they owe to you — notwithstanding the constitution concerning the two days' journey issued in the general council. Given at Lyon, 16th Kalends of May, in the third year.

Regesto in Latin:

Innocentius IV papa recipienti facultatem concedit vocandi religiosos et clericos saeculares Olomucensis dioecesis extra eam, non obstante constitutione de duabus dietis. 1245, Apr. 16, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected bishop of Ferrara, legate of the Apostolic See. As we sternly charge our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Magdeburg, through our letters, to not delay in personally coming into our presence within the span of one month after receiving them, we desire and mandate you by the authority of these presents, that unless perhaps the same archbishop is diligently and openly assisting our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious king of the Romans, H., in such a powerful manner that, considering the usefulness of the ongoing matter, it may be justly permitted that he remains in those parts, you compel him, within the said span, to come to the Apostolic See to respond to all that has been proposed against him, by ecclesiastical censure, removing any appeal — notwithstanding any indulgence of the same See, if he has any, that he cannot be interdicted, suspended, or excommunicated without a special mandate of the same See, making mention of this indulgence. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa electo Ferrariensi, apostolicae sedis legato, mandat ut Magdeburgensem archiepiscopum personaliter ad sedem apostolicam veniendi, nisi forte regi Romanorum assistat, compellat. [Pontificatus anno VIII] [Datum Laterani].

**Translation to English:**

To the rectory and brothers of the hospital of St. Mary at St. Gall in Florence, of the order of St. Augustine, pertaining to the Roman Church without intermediary. We impart benevolent favor to those things which are piously and prudently requested from us for the love of divine worship. Therefore, we grant you the authority of these presents, so that when it happens that the city of Florence is placed under ecclesiastical interdict, you may celebrate divine offices in the church of your hospital, with doors closed, bells not rung, and excommunicated and interdicted persons excluded, in a subdued voice, provided that you have not caused the interdict and it has not been specially pronounced against you. Let none etc. of our concession etc. Given at Lyons, on the 13th day before the Kalends of January, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa rectoriae et fratribus hospitalis Sanctae Mariae ad Sanctum Gallum Florentinum ordinis Sancti Augustini concedit, ut sub interdicto Florentiae divina officia clausis ianuis, non pulsatis campanis, exclusis excommunicatis et interdictis celebrare possint. 1245, Dec. 20. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the mayor, aldermen, sworn officials, and people of Metz. Since those who serve the Apostolic See are deemed worthy of special grace, we, considering your consistent devotion towards this See, which we know you have demonstrated continuously, do not regard this unfavorably. Desiring, therefore, to grant you special grace, we are inclined by your petitions to grant you, while you persist in the devotion to the Church, the authority through these presents, that no delegate of the Apostolic See, or subdelegate or executor or even conservator appointed by the same See, may be able to pronounce the sentence of excommunication or interdict against your community without the special mandate of the same, mentioning this indulgence. Therefore, let no one etc. of our concession etc. If anyone etc. Given at Lyon, on the 9th of November, in the third year.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa maiori, scabinis, iuratis et populo Metensibus concedit ut nullus delegatus sedis apostolice sententiam excommunicationis vel interdicti valeat promulgare sine mandato speciali, in devotione ecclesiae persistentibus. Datum Lugduni, V Idus Novembr., anno tertio.

**Translation to English:**

To Master Henry, rector of the church of Wegosteton in the diocese of Basel. In order to grant you a special favor due to your knowledge and integrity of character, for which you are given commendable testimony, and also considering the petitions of our dear sons, the noble men Conrad and Henry, counts of Freiburg and Urach, who have interceded for you, we, by the authority of these presents, grant you permission to receive one benefice, even if it has the cure of souls attached, in addition to the parish church of Wegosteton which you currently hold, should it be canonically offered to you, and to freely retain it along with the ones you already hold—despite the constitution issued by the general council on this matter—; provided that the said benefices are not neglected in their due duties, etc. No one, therefore, etc., of our concession, etc. If anyone, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 3rd day before the Nones of February, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Magistro Henrico, rectori ecclesie de Wegosteton Basiliensis diocesis, auctoritate presentium indulget, ut, preter ecclesiam de Wegosteton, unicum beneficium, etiam si curam habeat animarum, recipere ac retinere possit, constitutione concilii generali non obstante. 1245, Febr. 3, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To all the princes of Germany. Since we believe that you are, among the princes of the world, especially zealous for the honor of the Church and the Roman Empire, we more confidently inspire your steadfastness to procure its augmentation through our advice and mandates, hoping that you will comply promptly and effectively with our apostolic suggestions. Therefore, we admonish, beseech, and earnestly exhort you, mandating, by way of remission of sins, that you assist our dearest son in Christ, H., the illustrious King of the Romans, powerfully and openly against any of his adversaries, continuing the matter of the aforementioned empire, which has already been laudably begun by the Lord, with steadfast minds so that it may come to a successful conclusion. For we will not abandon you in any way in this matter, either during the life of this king or even after his death, if he should happen to be called from this world in the meantime, nor will we reform peace with those same adversaries without you. Given as above. In the same manner to the counts, barons, and other nobles established throughout Germany.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa universis principibus Theotonice mandat ut regi Romanorum H. contra adversarios suos potentibus auxiliis assistant, promittens se ipsos in hoc negotio non deserturum. Datum anno pontificatus sui, ex Laterano.

**Translation to English:**

To G. de Montelongo, our subdeacon and notary, legate of the Apostolic See. Since it is of great importance to the universal Church, especially at this time, to appoint as shepherds and leaders those who are pleasing to God and acceptable to men, who revere the Roman Church, we command you by the authority of these presents to instruct the chapter of Verona and all others to whom the election of the bishop of Verona is known to pertain, that if it should happen that the Church of Verona becomes vacant of a pastor, they must not presume to proceed to the election of anyone without a special mandate from the Apostolic See. You shall impose this prohibition generally by our authority and, if you deem it necessary, specifically, declaring null and void anything that might be attempted against your prohibition; contradictors, etc. Given at Lyon, 2nd of September, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa G. de Montelongo subdiacono et notario, sedis apostolicae legato mandat, ut capitulo Veronensi et aliis, ad quos Veronensis episcopatus electio pertinet, interdicat ne absque mandato apostolico electionem fiant; decernens irritum quod contra fiat. 1229, Sept. 2, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the king of Bohemia. Because among the other princes of the world, etc., as above up to: we believe it will produce. Therefore, we admonish, request, and earnestly exhort your serenity, imposing upon you the remission of sins, that you, considering piously how Frederick, the former emperor of the Romans, once afflicted the Church of God with harsh persecution and still, as a pursuer of his conceived malice, does not cease to afflict, and with what great disturbance of wars, like a fervent enemy of peace, he has shaken and incessantly shakes many Christian provinces, also considering that if the aforesaid empire is providentially bestowed by divine clemency with a Catholic and devoted emperor, the tribulation of that church will cease and tranquility of peace will be restored to the Christian peoples, you should take every diligent care to ensure that the election of the king of the Romans, to subsequently be promoted to emperor, is celebrated unanimously without the delay of postponement, so that you may deserve to obtain great reward from God and greater favor from the Apostolic See. Given as above. In the same manner to the bishop of Würzburg.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa regi Boemiae mandat, ut omnem diligentiam adhibeat, ne mora intercedente, electio regis Romanorum promovendi ad imperatorem unanimiter celebretur, quo ecclesiae tribulatio cesset et pax Christianis reddatur. Datum ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Frederick, Count of Bichekagebi, of the diocese of Mainz. Since the Supreme Pontiff, with the keys of the heavenly kingdom entrusted to him in the person of blessed Peter by Him who, with eternal providence, governs both celestial and earthly matters, holds the pontifical power of binding and loosing, and sometimes, dispensing above the law, loosens the bonds of necessity by which all are bound to observe the law, wisely from the fullness of his power in certain cases, when urgent necessity demands or clear, especially public, utility advises, without any unjust favoritism, for it is not considered to favor a person when something is granted for the sake of public rather than private good, and especially out of consideration for divine service, without injury to the law. Therefore, since, as we have learned, you, who have been and can in the future be of manifold benefit to the Roman Church, have contracted marriage in the face of the Church with the noble woman Adewic, who is related to you in the fourth degree of affinity, we, inclined by your supplications, grant by the authority of these presents that you and the said woman may lawfully remain in the marriage thus contracted, notwithstanding such degree. Let no one, therefore, etc. Given at Lyon, VIII Kalends of May, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro Frederico comiti de Bichekagebi indulget, ut cum nobili muliere Adewic, quarto affinitatis gradu contingente, in matrimonio contracto licite remanere possit. 1229, Apr. 24. Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To the noble man Egidio, lord of Gaeta, Roman citizen. Having read with joy the series of letters you sent, we extend full gratitude to your nobility for being diligent in repressing the wickedness of the impious Frederick to the honor of God and the Church. However, since your courage and that of other devotees of the Church should and can already be increased in this matter, because we have provided solemn legates and other necessary assistance for the procurement of the safety of the Kingdom of Sicily, we have thought it right to affectionately implore and advise your sincerity, imposing upon you for the remission of sins, that just as you have commendably begun, you and your companions should maintain unwavering determination against the treachery of that tyrant, hoping that the Church, which holds the merits of the devoted in the secret of its heart, will compensate you and your companions with appropriate favor and grace at the opportune time.

Regesto:

Gregorius IX papa (nobili viro Egidio, dominae Gaite, civi Romano, gratias agit pro diligentia in reprimendo Frederici nequitiam ad honorem Dei et ecclesiae, et monet ut constantiam habeat cum sociis contra tyranni perfidiam, promittens opportunam compensationem meritorum; 1231, ex Urbe.

**Translation to English:**

To all counts and other nobles established throughout Germany. Since you are obliged to diligently and carefully maintain the honor and good state of the Roman Empire among the nobles of the world, we confidently encourage you through our letters, believing that you are more willing to execute our wishes in this matter. Therefore, with the beloved son, the noble man... Landgrave of Thuringia, having been elevated to the position of King of the Romans by the working of God, who inspires and assists His followers' desires, we admonish, implore, and earnestly exhort your nobility, commanding you, under the remission of your sins, to pursue this king with all due honor and to assist and support him promptly, faithfully, and vigorously, removing any obstacle of contradiction and difficulty. Otherwise, we instruct our beloved son... the elected bishop of Ferrara, legate of the Apostolic See, through our letters, to compel you to do so with spiritual or temporal strictness, as he sees fit. In the same manner, to the communities of the cities.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa universis comitibus et nobilibus Theotoniae mandat ut novo regi Romanorum, lantgravio Thuringiae, omnimodam fidelitatem et auxilium impendant, sub paena coactionis a legato apostolico exercenda. Anno pontificatus X, s.d.

**Translation to English:**

To the podestà and commune of the Milanese. Since, as we have learned from your reports, you have, with sound deliberation, convened and communicated counsel at the sound of the bell, as is customary, to deal with certain pestilent individuals from your city, who, commonly called malexardi, were once incited by a diabolical spirit to adhere treacherously to Frederick, the late emperor, and his followers, intending to bring ruin upon your city, and have decided to confiscate their goods and subject them to perpetual banishment: we, inclined by your supplications, since it is fitting that the unfaithful suffer loss for their infidelity, approve what you have prudently done in this matter, confirm it by apostolic authority, and support it with the protection of this letter. Therefore, let no one etc. of our confirmation, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 13th day before the Kalends of August, in the fourth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa potestati et communi Mediolanensium notificat confirmationem per apostolicam auctoritatem bonorum confiscationis et perpetuae bannitionis in malexardos, qui Friderico imperatori proditorie adhaeserant. 1246, Jul. 20, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected bishop of Ferrara, legate of the apostolic see. Desiring to appoint worthy persons to vacant churches, we wish and by the authority of these presents we command you to ensure that, throughout all the regular and secular churches of Germany, it is generally prohibited for their chapters or convents, when they happen to be vacant, to presume to provide themselves with a pastor or prelate through election or postulation without our or your counsel and consent, decreeing that if they should act contrary to this, it shall be null and void. Given at Lyons, 9th September, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa electo Ferrariensi, apostolicae sedis legato, mandat ut universis Theutoniae ecclesiis inhibeat ne capitula vel conventus sine consilio et assensu apostolico vel legati de prelatis sibi provideant; si secus egerint, actus irritos decernit. 1245, Sept. 9. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of Steinvelt of the Premonstratensian order in the diocese of Cologne. Our regard should be directed with favor towards the provision for those whose desire is that their humility be ascribed to divine praises. Hence, we command that, for our beloved son Thelemannus, a scholar from Echternach who desires to be enrolled in the clerical order, and about whom a laudable testimony is given to us, at the request of our beloved sons, the aldermen and community of Echternach in the diocese of Trier, who have earnestly petitioned us on his behalf, you are to accept him as a canon and brother in one of the churches of the city or diocese of Trier, excepting only the cathedral, and to provide him with a prebend as soon as the opportunity arises. This is notwithstanding any fixed number of canons established by oath or any other binding agreement, or if we have directed our writings for others in the church where you decide to assign him, which we do not wish to prejudice by the authority of these presents. Let those who contradict this be dealt with accordingly. Given at Lyons, 9th July, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa abbati de Steinvelt, ordinis Praemonstratensis, mandat ut Thelemannum scolarem Epternacensem in ecclesia civitatis vel diocesis Treverensis, excepta cathedrali, in canonicum recipiat et de prebenda provideat, non obstante numero canonicorum fixo. 1247, Iul. 9, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To all vassals and faithful of the Church of Verdun. By the authority of these presents, we strictly command you to render homage and the due oaths of fidelity to our venerable brother, the Bishop of Verdun, without any delay, since there is currently no emperor or king in Germany from whom the regalia of the Church of Verdun can be received. Otherwise, we will ratify the sentence or penalty, either spiritual or temporal, that the bishop rightfully imposes on the rebellious, etc., up to: to be observed. Given at Lyon, on the 12th day before the Kalends of April, in the third year. In the same manner, to all citizens of Verdun. II. To the primicerius and chapter of Verdun. By the authority of these presents, we firmly command you to assign the regalia of the Church of Verdun to our venerable brother, the Bishop of Verdun, without any difficulty or delay. Given as above.

**Regesto:**

Innocentius IV papa vassallis fidelibusque ecclesiae Virdunensis mandat, ut episcopo Virdunensi homagium et fidelitatis iuramenta sine dilatione exhibeant, et primicerio et capitulo Virdunensibus, ut regalia episcopo assignent. 1245, Mart. 21, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Frederick, rector of the church of Ostra, in the diocese of Constance. To grant you special favor and due to the merits of your probity, of which you are given laudable testimony, and in consideration of our beloved son, the nobleman H., count of Luperc, brother-in-law of the late C., bishop of Porto, who petitioned us on your behalf, we are moved to grant you by the authority of these presents, the permission to freely retain the church of Beirchheim along with the church of Ostra, which you are canonically proposed to have acquired with the care of souls, notwithstanding the constitution issued by the general council on this matter; provided that these churches are not neglected in their duties, etc. Given at Lyon, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of June, in the third year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Friderico rectori ecclesiae de Ostra indulget, ut ecclesiam de Beirchaima una cum ecclesia de Ostra libere retinere possit, constitutione concilii generali non obstante. 1245, Mai. 21. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Cardinal Priest of the Title of St. Mary in Trastevere and the Cardinal Deacon of St. Mary in Cosmedin, legates of the Apostolic See. If the all-seeing Lord, graciously hearing the laments of those afflicted in the Kingdom of Sicily, provides in His mercy that you have a successful entrance for the general welfare of those remaining there, it is reasonably presumed that you may have to endure the pressure of excessive importunity concerning the granting of ecclesiastical benefices. Therefore, to ensure this is done with honor to the Church and to yourselves, we grant you by the authority of these presents that if both or one of you enter the said kingdom, you or one of you may, in each church where it seems expedient, confer a single benefice or prebend to worthy and devoted persons suitable for the business of the apostolic grace or promotion, with the condition that the church in which one of you has provided shall not be burdened by the other without our special mandate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa presbytero S. tituli Sancte Marie Transtiberim et diacono cardinale Sancte Marie in Cosmidin, legatis apostolicae sedis, permittit conferre unicum beneficium vel prebendam in ecclesiis regni Sicilie, si ambo vel alter regnum intraverit, sub conditionibus statutis. Rieti, 1230, [date based on the calculated pontifical year].

**Translation to English:**

To the bishops established in Frisia. To ensure that those who have vowed, according to the eminent words of the prophets, fulfill their vows to the Lord, we command, by the authority of these presents, your fraternity to diligently admonish and induce the cross-bearers and those who shall yet take the cross in your dioceses in Frisia, destined for the aid of the Holy Land. If necessary, compel them by sentences of excommunication upon their persons and interdict upon their lands, with all evasion set aside, except for those who encounter such an impediment that their vow should be changed or deferred by the provision of the apostolic see. They should prepare themselves so that from the coming March until the following year they may set out on the journey, crossing the passage with our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of France, with the Lord's assent, for then their steps can be directed more usefully and successfully over the sea. Given at Lyon, on the 5th day before the Nones of August, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopis in Friscia constitutis mandat, ut crucesignatos ad iter faciendum in Terram Sanctam a Martio proximo usque annum sequentem cum rege Franciae inducant, si necesse fuerit, per excommunicationis et interdicti sententias compellendo. 1232, Augusti 3, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Trier. Since we aim to serve the honor of the Most High and its increase, we must especially grant special favor to those through whom His honor is increased and benefit is procured. Therefore, since our beloved son Wericus, a canon of Trier and your cleric, has shown himself to be helpful and devoted in the matters of the Apostolic See, we, intending to pursue him with the favor of special grace on this account, command that you ensure he is generously provided for in the Trier church with an archdeaconry or dignity, if any is currently vacant or as soon as an opportunity arises for it — unless we have specifically directed our writings otherwise to you concerning others on this matter — notwithstanding that he already holds a benefice, or if we have generally ordered others to be provided for in the city, diocese, or province of Trier, or if others have obtained positions in the same church by our authority, or if an indulgence has been obtained from the Apostolic See which could impede such grace; any objectors, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 19th of June, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Treverensi mandat ut Werico canonico Treverensi, clerico suo, in ecclesia Treverensi in archidiaconatu vel alia dignitate provideat, non obstante beneficiis vel mandatis aliis. 1229, Iun. 19. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Ostia, the presbyter of the titular church of Santa Maria in Trastevere, and the cardinal deacon of Sant'Angelo. We have received great joy in our hearts because the founder of the Church, Lord Jesus Christ, seems to have provided remedies for the sadness by bringing the persecutor of faith to a state where he sees obstacles from the nobility of the kingdom of Sicily, whom he once had as promoters of his wicked will. Following the commendable advice of our brothers and in accord with your prudent reflection, we have decided to apply vigilant diligence to advancing the matter of initiated salvation, in the hope of divine mercy, believing that this will yield great benefit to the honor of the Church through your industrious cooperation. Furthermore, since it is fitting that the hearts of the kingdom's nobility, who have fled the darts of the said persecutor and sought refuge with the Church, should be supported by firm attention, let your wisdom ensure that you nurture them with kind affections in the future as you have laudably done in the past. Also, ensure that the cause of God is advanced through their service and that of other devotees of the Church, as worthily as possible, providing help and effort.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Ostiensi, S. tituli Sancte Marie Transtiberim presbytero et R. Sancti Angeli diacono cardinalibus mandat, ut vigilantiam diligentem ad promotionem salutis inchoate impendant, nobiles regni Sicilie benignis affectibus sustineant, et causam Dei per eorum ministerium promoveant. 1234, Datum Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of the Monastery of Saint Bernard of the Cistercian Order in the Diocese of Cambrai. Having full confidence in your prudence in the Lord, we command you by the authority of these presents to ensure that a twentieth of the revenues of all possessions and goods from churches and ecclesiastical persons, whether exempt or non-exempt, in the land of our beloved son, the noble man, the Duke of Lorraine and Brabant, be assigned to you for three years and deposited in a suitable place, to be converted at our mandate into aid for the Holy Land; contradictors are to be ignored; you are to faithfully report to us in your letters the amount collected; notwithstanding any indulgence, if there be any granted to some by the Apostolic See, that may prevent them from being interdicted or excommunicated through apostolic letters, which have not made full and express mention of said indulgence. Given at Lyon, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of August, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati Loci Sancti Bernardi Cisterciensis ordinis Cameracensis diocesis mandat ut vicesimam proventuum possessionum ecclesiasticarum in terra ducis Lothoringie et Brabantie per triennium colligat et ad subsidium Terre Sancte convertat. 1240, Jul. 21, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Ostia and the presbyter of the Holy Title of St. Mary in Trastevere, and to R., deacon cardinal of St. Angel. The beloved sons, the consuls and the commune of Ferentino, have taken care to present to us that, although we have given you letters with instructions to compel the guarantors, whom the people of Alatri had given to the people of Ferentino for maintaining peace made between them, to observe this agreement, you have so far neglected to do so. Therefore, we command you, if this is the case, to endeavor to execute the apostolic mandate on this matter according to the contents of the previous letters. Given at Lyon, July 18, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Ostiensi et presbytero tituli Sancte Marie Transtiberim et cardinali diacono Sancti Angeli mandat, ut fideiussores, quos Alatrini Ferentinatibus pro servanda pace dederant, ad eius observationem compellant, iuxta priorum litterarum continentiam. 1230, Iul. 18, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of Bebrahusin in the diocese of Constance. On behalf of our beloved son Walter, rector of the church of Mont in the diocese of Constance, it was humbly petitioned to us that we might care to dispense grace concerning him, so that he might obtain ecclesiastical benefices up to the value of one hundred marks of silver, including the aforementioned church which he holds, were they to be offered canonically. Although therefore, etc., up to: prohibits, yet due to the devotion and purity of faith which he is said to have shown in the affairs of the Roman Church, exposing himself and his possessions to many dangers, and also considering the request of our beloved sons B. count of Hürach and Radulf, brothers of the late C. bishop of Porto, our loyal followers, petitioning us on his behalf, by the authority of these presents we entrust to you, that you may, considering the circumstances and merits of the same rector, dispense with him concerning the aforesaid matters up to the extent that you may see fit according to God: provided, etc., up to: neglected. Given as above in the next. 

**Regesto in Latin:**

Honorius III papa abbati de Bebrahusine Constantiensis diocesis mandat ut cum Walterio rectore ecclesiae de Monte super obtinendis beneficiis ad centum marcarum dispenset, ob devotionem et fidei puritatem eius ac postulantibus comite de Hurach et Radulfo. Datum ut supra in proxima.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected Bishop of Vercelli. Since, as you assert, it is necessary for you to fortify the castles of the church of Vercelli due to the war and the persecution of the enemies of the church, and you do not have the means to do so, we grant you by the authority of these presents that you may, for this purpose, contract a loan up to the amount of one hundred marks of silver and pledge the goods of the said church to the creditors. Given at Lyon, on the seventh day before the Calends of July, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa electo Vercellensi concedit ut propter necessitatem munitionis castrorum ecclesie Vercellensis, usque ad centum marcas argenti mutuum contrahere possit et bona ecclesiae creditoribus obligare. 1245, Jun. 25. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

On behalf of the community of citizens of Strasbourg, it was humbly requested of us that, with our dear son John, canon of Saint Thomas in Strasbourg, regarding the holding of multiple ecclesiastical benefices, including those involving the care of souls, should they be offered to him canonically, up to the sum of eighty marks of silver, we might deign to make a special dispensation. Although, therefore, the constitution of the holy council prohibits the holding of multiple churches or ecclesiastical dignities to curb the ambitions of some, considering the appeals of the said citizens and the merits of the probity of the canon himself, of which commendable testimony is given, we are moved to grant to your discretion, in which we place full confidence, the authority by these presents to dispense with him, notwithstanding the aforementioned constitution, regarding the foregoing matters, up to the amount that you, weighing the circumstances and his merits, see fit according to God; provided that the same benefices are not neglected in their duties, etc., up to: be neglected. Given at Lyon, March 20, in the third year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa discretioni tuae concedit, ut cum Iohanne canonico Sancti Thomae Argentinensis super pluribus beneficiis ecclesiasticis, etiam curam habentibus animarum, usque ad summam octuaginta marcarum argenti, auctoritate sua dispenset. 1229, Mart. 20. Datum Lugduni.

Translation to English:

Summons made in a public audience of the abbot of St. Prospero of Reggio and certain others. Lord Marinus, vice-chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, by mandate of the Lord Pope, on the 11th of September, in the fourth year of the pontificate of the same Lord Pope, in a public audience summoned under threat of deposition the abbot of St. Prospero of Reggio, the provost of St. Prospero of the castle of Reggio, the archpriest of Campiliola, a canon of Reggio, Philippus de Saxo, the archpriest of Herberia, Guillielmus de Apulia, a canon of Reggio, the archpriest of Monatius, the archpriest of Fabrica, Hugo called Papa, the archpriest of Bibiano, the archpriest of St. Vitalis, the archpriest of Bartolo, the archpriest of Sucaria, the abbot of Caranna of the diocese of Parma, to present themselves before the said Lord Pope on the upcoming feast of St. Martin. They were again summoned in a public audience on the 2nd of October, and for the third time summoned in a public audience on the 12th of October.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa Marinumm vicecancellarium mandat, ut abbatem Sancti Prosperi Regini et alios varios ad se in festo sancti Martini citet. 1230, Sept. 11, Romae.

**Translation to English:**

To G. de Montelongo, our subdeacon and notary, legate of the apostolic see. Our venerable brother, the bishop of Piacenza, has humbly petitioned us that, since frequently many legates and envoys of the apostolic see, to whom procurations are due, pass through the city of Piacenza, he bears not a light burden of expenses, which, if divided among many, can be more easily borne, or that contributions be made to him according to the means of other prelates of the churches and clerics of the same city, or that this ministry of charity be fulfilled by each of them in turn according to their abilities. We instruct you to provide for this matter with our authority, as you see fit in accordance with God; those who oppose, etc. Given at Lyon, 14th Kalends of August, in the fourth year.

---

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa G. de Montelongo subdiacono et notario suo mandat, ut onus expensarum procurationum in civitate Placentina, quod frequenter a legatis et nuntiis apostolicae sedis per ipsam transeuntibus exigitur, dividatur inter plures vel contribui debeat a prelatis ecclesiarum et clericis civitatis. 1246, Jul. 19. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Master Ulric, rector of the church of [Rectineuwee?] in the diocese of Constance. The benevolence of the Apostolic See so prudently discerns the merits of individuals through careful deliberation that it elevates those who excel in the knowledge of letters and nobility of character with the grace of greater favor and seeks to honor them with greater benefits. Therefore, considering your worthiness, and at the request of our beloved daughter in Christ, the noblewoman, the Countess of Kiburch, whose cleric you are, and wishing to bestow upon you a special favor, we are inclined by your supplications to dispense with you, by the authority of these presents, allowing you to lawfully receive one other benefice, office, or ecclesiastical dignity, even if it has the care of souls annexed, and to freely retain it along with those you already possess, even if they also require similar care, notwithstanding the constitution of the general council; provided that these benefices, offices, or dignity are not defrauded of their due obligations, etc., until: neglected. Therefore, let no one, etc., of our dispensation, etc. If anyone, etc. Given at Lyon, on the fourth day before the Ides of January, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Magistro Ulrico, rectori ecclesiae in diocesi Constantiensi, concedit dispensationem ut unum aliud beneficium vel dignitatem ecclesiasticam cum cura animarum accipere et cum obtentis retinere possit, rogatu comitissae de Kiburch cui clericus est. Datum Lugduni, die X Ianuarii, anno tertio.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Tusculum, legate of the apostolic see. Since our beloved son, the noble man, the Duke of Lorraine and Brabant, desires, as he asserts, to be marked with the character of the cross, intending to set out for the aid of the Holy Land, we, commending his laudable intention with worthy praises in the Lord, and intending to support him with grace and favor both from this and from the strength of his devotion, command you, that from the goods of those who have taken the cross in his land, and especially those who will be in his company, which they leave behind when dying on the way, returning, or staying there, or that may otherwise come into your hands, you should suitably provide for the expenses to be made for this aid, so that the same duke may be supported by these with suitable aid and become more devoted from the devotion. Given at Lyons, on the 14th day before the Kalends of August, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Tusculano mandat, ut de bonis crucesignatorum terre ducis Lothoringie et Brabantie, in subsidium Terre Sancte profecturi, congrue provideat ad expensas faciendas, ut ipse dux debito subsidio fulciatur. Datum Lugduni, XIIII Kal. Augusti, anno quarto pontificatus nostri.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected bishop of Ferrara, legate of the apostolic see. By the authority of these presents, we mandate you to effectively ensure that all, both the prelates of secular and regular churches as well as princes and other clerics and laypeople established throughout Germany, show loyalty to our beloved son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, H., by swearing oaths of fidelity and performing all duties traditionally rendered by them to the kings or emperors of the Romans. You are to compel the said prelates and clerics, after issuing a prior admonition, through the penalty of suspension from office, dignity, honor, and benefice, and the aforementioned princes and laypeople through spiritual or temporal penalties, if necessary. Furthermore, strictly enjoin those prelates and clerics whom you have suspended to personally present themselves before the apostolic see within a certain peremptory term that you shall set for them, to receive a sentence of deposition or other penalty, as the nature of their offense may require. Inform them that if they fail to appear by the specified term, we will nonetheless proceed against them to deposition or other penalties — notwithstanding their physical absence — as we shall see fit. Given at Lyon, on the 4th of July, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa electo Ferrariensi, apostolicae sedis legato mandat, ut universos per Theotoniam constitutos ad fidelitatem et oboedientiam erga regem Romanorum H. per iuramenta fidelitatis et alia consueta compellat, sub poenis suspensionis vel aliis, et ad apostolicam sedem comparere iubeat. 1230, IV Non. Iulii, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Basel. The beloved son, Henry, known as Suelle, rector of the church of Muzeche in the diocese of Strasbourg, humbly petitioned us in our presence that, besides the ecclesiastical benefices involving the care of souls which he holds, he might be permitted to receive other ecclesiastical benefices— even if they entail similar care— up to the sum of one hundred marks of silver, accounting for the aforesaid, if they are canonically offered to him, and to freely retain these along with those already obtained. We were asked to take care, by the kindness of the Apostolic See, to grant such dispensation. Although the constitution of the sacred council prohibits anyone from having multiple churches or ecclesiastical dignities to curb the ambitions of some, yet, due to his merits and at the request of the beloved sons, the noble man Ulric, Count of Ferrette, nephew of the late Conrad, bishop of Porto, of good memory, and Hermann, our subdeacon, son of the noble man, the Count of Wilperc, who have petitioned us regarding this matter on his behalf, we grant to your fraternity by the authority of these presents, that, notwithstanding the aforementioned constitution, you may dispense with him by our authority up to the amount which, considering the circumstances and his merits, you deem expedient according to God; provided that the same benefices are not neglected concerning their obligations, etc. Given at Lyon, 14th Kalends of September, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Basiliensi mandatum dat dispensandi Henrico dicto Suelle, rectore ecclesiae de Muzeche Argentinensis diocesis, ut alia beneficia ecclesiastica, ad summam centum marcarum argenti, recipere possit, constitutione sacri concilii non obstante. Datum Lugduni, XIIII Kalendas Septembris, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Cologne. The accustomed benevolence of the Apostolic See is such that it discerns the merits of individuals in a way that it elevates those who excel in the knowledge of letters and nobility of character with greater favor and strives to honor them with greater benefits, because it is not inappropriate to give to one what would suffice for many, etc. Hence, we, considering not unworthily the integrity and nobility of our beloved son, the provost of the Church of St. Mary ad Gradus in Cologne, and wishing to grant him a special favor, at the behest of our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, command that you provide him in the city or diocese of Cologne from ecclesiastical revenues, whether in prelatures or other ecclesiastical benefices, prebends or others, as long as the income from these, besides the benefices he currently holds, does not exceed the annual value of two hundred marks of silver. This is to be done by our authority, notwithstanding if in the churches where you decide to provide him, there is a fixed number of canons bound by oath or any other firmness, or if by our mandate the same churches are burdened with the provision for others, or if the same provost holds other benefices elsewhere; those who oppose, etc. Given at Lyon, on the Ides of June, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Coloniensi mandat, ut dilecto filio preposito ecclesie sancte Marie ad Gradus Coloniensis de redditibus ecclesiasticis in civitate vel diocesi Coloniensi, dummodo non excedant valorem ducentarum marcarum argenti annuatim, provideat. 1239, Idus Iunii, apud Lugdunum.

**Translation to English:**

Although we gladly extend grace to all who ask for it, it is appropriate for us to show greater favor to those who have merited the favor of the Apostolic See through praiseworthy acts of devotion. Since, therefore, our beloved son, Master Theoderic, the scholastic of Trier, has suffered many losses for the faith and devotion he has towards the Apostolic See, as we have learned from your testimony and that of others worthy of trust, we intend to pursue him with a special prerogative of grace. We command, therefore, that you provide him with or see to it that he is provided with another equivalent benefice or office or dignity in any church of your province by our authority, given that he is prepared to resign his benefices which he cannot enjoy because of the men of the empire — notwithstanding any indulgence of the Apostolic See which might impede this grace, or if we have directed our writings for others in the church where you will see fit to provide for him, which we do not wish to prejudice by the present authority; contradictors, etc. Given at Lyon, 17th Kalends of December, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa mandat ut magistro Theoderico scholastico Treverensi, qui dampna plurima pro fide et devotione ad sedem apostolicam perpessus est, provideatur in alio equivalenti beneficio seu dignitate in aliqua ecclesiarum provincie eius, renuntiatis beneficiis suis. 1239, Nov. 15. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Cambrai. Since our beloved son, the noble man, the Duke of Lorraine and Brabant, desires, as he asserts, to be marked with the sign of the cross, planning to proceed to the aid of the Holy Land, we, wishing to favor him, command that whatever has been collected by our mandate, or is bequeathed from the tithe or redemptions, or the offerings of those who have taken the cross in his land, either by your hand or that of anyone else for the aid of the aforementioned land, be restored and returned to our beloved son, the abbot of the Monastery of Saint Bernard of the Cistercian Order in the diocese of Cambrai, to be reserved in our name; contradictors, etc.; you are to faithfully report to us the amount of these in your letters; notwithstanding the indulgence, etc., up to the mention. Given at Lyons, on the 14th day before the Kalends of August, in the fourth year. To the same. Since our beloved son, the noble man, the Duke of Lorraine and Brabant, asserts that his land is considerably burdened due to the tithe collected for the aid of the Holy Land by our mandate, we command that you cease the collection of the aforementioned tithe in that land. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Cameracensi mandat, ut collationes de decima et obventionibus votorum crucesignatorum in terra ducis Lotharingie et Brabantie restituat abbati Loci Sancti Bernardi; et iubet ut cesset collectio decime in terra eiusdem ducis. 1246, Iul. 19, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Worms. Since we aim for the honor and increase of the Church, we ought to especially favor those through whom its dignity is enhanced and its utility is promoted. Therefore, since our beloved son Henry, a canon of Trier and son of the noble man, the Count of Altimont, does not have benefices from which he can be sustained according to his nobility and the custom of the land, which due to the hospitality prevalent there requires great expenses, we command your brotherhood with the authority of these letters, at your request, to provide him in the Church of Worms a prebend, if there is any currently vacant or as soon as an opportunity arises, and a position or other ecclesiastical dignity in the city or diocese of Worms that befits both the recipient and the donor, by our authority — notwithstanding that he may already be a beneficiary elsewhere, or if we have directed our letters regarding others in the churches where you decide to make provision for him, which we do not wish to prejudice by the authority of these presents, nor by any statute concerning the fixed number of canons, whether strengthened by oath, confirmation of the Apostolic See, or any other firmness —; to any objectors, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 14th day before the Kalends of January, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Warmaciensi mandat ut Henricum canonicum Treverensem, filium comitis Altimontis, in ecclesia Warmaciensi cum praebenda et alia dignitate ecclesiastica provideat, non obstante quod alias beneficiatus sit. 1245, Dec. 19. Datum Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the elect of Ferrara, legate of the Apostolic See. Since we have commanded our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Mainz, by our letters to suspend the cases arising from the elections held in the church of Regensburg, which we had committed to you and him, we desire and by the authority of these presents mandate you, that unless one of those elections is found to be canonical, concerning which we want you to diligently inquire the truth, as we do not intend to take away anyone’s right, you appoint a suitable person as pastor to that church by our authority, as you know to be expedient for the pressing affairs of the church and empire, ensuring that the due obedience and reverence are shown to him by his subjects, restraining the opposers by ecclesiastical censure with appeal set aside. Given at Lyon, 5th July, in the fourth year (of our pontificate).

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa electo Ferrariensi mandat ut, postquam cum Maguntino archiepiscopo causas super electionibus in ecclesia Ratisponensi suspenderit, nisi electiones canonicae inveniantur, personam idoneam in pastorem ecclesiae Ratisponensi auctoritate apostolica praeficiat; contradictores per censuram ecclesiasticam compescat. Datum Lugduni, III Non. Iulii, anno quarto (1241).

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of Wiblingen in the diocese of Constance. On behalf of our beloved son S. of Gudilingin, a canon of Speyer, it was humbly requested of us that we would grant him dispensation to hold multiple ecclesiastical benefices, even those with the care of souls, if they are lawfully offered to him, up to the value of two hundred marks of silver, in addition to those he already possesses. Although the constitution of the holy council prohibits anyone from holding multiple churches or ecclesiastical dignities due to the ambitions of some, we are nonetheless inclined by the nobility of his character and lineage, for which he is highly recommended, and by the request of the noble man, the count of Helfstein, his uncle, who has petitioned us in this matter through his letters. By the authority of these presents, we commit to you the power to dispense with him regarding the aforesaid matters by our authority, notwithstanding the aforementioned constitution, up to the extent that you, considering the circumstances, his nobility, and merits, see fit according to God: provided that the same benefices, etc., are not neglected. Given at Lyon, on the 21st of May, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati de Wibilingun Constantiensis diocesis mandat, ut S. de Gudilingin canonico Spirensi dispensare possit super plura beneficia ecclesiastica, etiam curata, usque ad ducentarum marcarum argenti valentiam, constitutione sacri concilii non obstante, consideratis circumstantiis, nobilitate et meritis. Datum Lugduni, XII Kal. Iunii, anno tertio.

**Translation to English:**

To the prior of Bonarcanto in the diocese of Arborea. Bencivenni, a cleric from the diocese of Perugia, has shown us through his petition that, although we had previously instructed our venerable brother, the bishop of Civitanova in Sardinia, by our letters to provide him a suitable ecclesiastical benefice in one of the churches of his city or diocese, as he claims not to have obtained any ecclesiastical benefice, certain contradictions arose. Because Enzo, the son of the late Frederick, Roman Emperor, prohibited the transport of apostolic letters through his land, the said cleric could not benefit from the favor granted to him. Therefore, not wishing the said cleric to be frustrated in his hope for our grace, we command you to ensure that the church of Saint Peter in Silanoi in the diocese of Arborea, if it is said to have been vacant for such a time that its collation has devolved to us, is conferred to the said cleric by our authority. You are to induct him into its possession and defend him while inducted; contradictors, etc. Given at Lyon, June 22, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa priori de Bonarcanto in diocesi Arborensi mandat, ut ecclesiam Sancti Petri de Silanoi, si vacavit et ad Sedem Apostolicam collatio eius est devoluta, clerico Bencivenni de diocesi Perusina conferat, ipsumque in possessionem inducat et defenset. 1239, Iun. 22. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of San Giorgio Maggiore in Venice. The kindness of the mother church is accustomed to open the bosom of mercy to needy children and especially to support those with the benefit of timely assistance who, exposing themselves to bodily dangers for ecclesiastical liberty, are known to have suffered multiple afflictions on this account. Therefore, since our venerable brother, the bishop of Fermo, was long ago expelled from his bishopric by the officials of the late Emperor Frederick and had all his episcopal goods confiscated, has remained for a long time in Venice and has borne heavy expenses: we, wishing to pursue him with apostolic grace so that he may be comforted by some kind of pleasant consolation, command that you make a suitable annual provision for him, so exiled, from some of the churches of the Patriarchate of Aquileia, which are less burdened by a similar provision from apostolic mandate, so that he, together with six persons staying with him, may be able to sustain themselves adequately; any contradictors, etc.— notwithstanding the constitution concerning two days issued in the general council. Given at Lyon, on the fourth year, 14th of July.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati Sancti Georgii Maioris de Venetiis mandat, ut episcopo Firmano, exulanti apud Venetias, provisionem annuam ex ecclesiis Patriarchatus Aquilegensis exhibeat, non obstante constitutione de duabus dietis. 1230, Jul. 14. Lugduni.

Translation:

To the noble man, the Count of Savoy. Although the continuous pressure of arising matters persistently attacks our mind, which, by the disposition of the Lord, we undeservedly preside over the universal governance, yet the care for all the churches, incumbent upon our shoulders, urges us with daily meditation all the more intensely as we have been specially, indeed principally, appointed to this by virtue of the office of apostolate assigned to us. Therefore, having recently received the resignation of our venerable brother, the former archbishop of the Church of Tarentaise, we, hoping that the Church of Tarentaise might be prosperously governed through the industrious diligence of our beloved son R., elected of Tarentaise, who is considered pleasing to God and acceptable to men, endowed with natural goods and adorned with gratuitous virtues, have, with the advice of our brothers, appointed him as archbishop and pastor for the Church of Tarentaise, granting him full administration of both temporal and spiritual matters. Therefore, we have deemed it appropriate to earnestly ask and advise your nobility, commanding that you, pursuing him with special favor and grace, assist him out of reverence for the Apostolic See and for us in matters that concern the good state of the aforesaid church, effectively and powerfully, so that said church, supported by his ministry and your backing, may receive an increase in prosperity, and we may commend your devotion with worthy praises in the Lord. Given at Lyon, 6th day before the Nones of March, in the third year.

Regesto:

Gregorius IX papa nobilis viro comiti Sabaudie commendat electionem R. ad ecclesiam Tarantasiensis in archiepiscopum, mandans ut favore speciali ipsum prosequatur et adiuvet in bonum statum ecclesiae promovendo. Datum Lugduni, VI Nonas Martii, anno III.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble woman, the Countess of Flanders and Hainaut. Sometimes the Roman Pontiff, to whom divine providence has entrusted the duty of binding and loosing, grants a dispensation for what the laws completely deny, especially when great necessity or evident utility demands it. Therefore, as you have taken care to present to us, there are few noble women in your regions with whom your sons can decently unite in marriage according to their noble status. It is very necessary and highly useful for your and your sons' prosperous and peaceful state, as well as for the counties, that they may marry some from their own kindred or affinity. We, therefore, favorably supporting your petition and wishing to grant you special favor, dispense with apostolic authority that one of your sons, whom you prefer, may lawfully contract marriage with a noble woman who is related to him in the fourth degree of consanguinity or affinity. Let no one, therefore, etc. of our dispensation, etc. If anyone, etc. Given at Lyon, 11th May, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobilis mulieri comitisse Flandriae et Haynonie concedit dispensationem, ut unus filiorum eius matrimonium cum nobili muliere, quae in quarto gradu consanguinitatis vel affinitatis ei sit coniuncta, contrahere possit. 1239, Maii 11, Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To the noble men Theobald Francis and all others in the kingdom of Sicily who have returned to the devotion of the Roman Church, may the spirit of wiser counsel guide you. The Lord has shone His face upon you, delivering you from the dominion of Pharaoh and directing your efforts towards those works which promote the honor and peace of the Church in the salvation of the kingdom of Sicily. Having received full joy from the Comforter of the grieving, the Lord Jesus Christ, and with the counsel of our brothers, we have provided in such a way that we undertake all diligence for the redemption of this kingdom. Therefore, to successfully promote this pious endeavor, we have decided to appoint solemn legates, namely our beloved sons, S., priest of the title of St. Mary in Trastevere, and R., cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Cosmedin, indeed men distinguished for their wisdom and renowned for their diverse virtues, and have likewise provided them with the necessary support. Through their industry, with God’s favor, we believe it will come to pass that the enemy will quickly fall into the pit he has made. Therefore, having been made warriors of the Lord Jesus Christ from the soldiers of the tyrant, strive with steadfast spirit and unwavering mind to expand the illustrious fame of your name in the sight of the nations. Rise firmly in the hope that, if the power of the Most High, with your service and the cooperating support of the Church's devotees, ends the lamentations of the afflicted, the apostolic see will consistently hold you as special among its dear sons, as noble in both lineage and virtue.

Regesto:

Gregorius IX papa nobilibus viris Theobaldo Francisco et universis aliis regni Sicilie, qui ad devotionem ecclesie Romanae redierunt, mandat, ut operibus ad honorem et tranquillitatem ecclesie promovendis intendentes, sub legatis S. tituli Sancte Marie Transtiberim et R. Sancte Marie in Cosmidin, strenue laborent, promittens eos inter caros ecclesie filios habere. Datum Laterani, anno pontificatus nono, die VI Idus Aprilis.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz. Having affectionately received your letters, we have gathered from their content that our beloved son, the noble lord Landgrave of Thuringia, has been elected King of the Romans by the common consent of the princes and publicly conducts himself as king. For this, we give due thanks to Him who inspired such desires in their hearts and assists in fulfilling them. Truly desiring with ardent zeal that the affairs of the Roman Empire be directed towards prosperous outcomes, we have committed ourselves with all our mind and steadfast purpose to the promotion of him whom the same Landgrave has chosen, and wish to persevere in this with prudent counsel, strong support, and vigorous favor. We intend to support the said king more through deeds and assistance in this matter than through promises. Therefore, we earnestly ask and exhort your fraternity, commanding you to diligently admonish, effectively guide, and strongly encourage this king to, trusting in divine virtue and the favor of the Apostolic See, vigorously and bravely pursue the matter which he has already undertaken with courage. Furthermore, you should use the wisdom given to you by God to inspire other German princes, both ecclesiastical and secular, to fully and faithfully support the aforementioned king, offering him strong and open assistance, so that, with the Lord's favor, this matter, which has been started so promisingly, may be brought to a laudable conclusion with His grace cooperating. Regarding the provision of the promised aid from us, there shall be no lack on our part, as we intend to even greater efforts to complete this matter. To the aforementioned king, however, we have not yet written because we await his formal envoys with whom we will fully arrange what is necessary for this matter. Given at Lyons, June 9, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino mandat, ut lantgravium Thuringiae, electum regem Romanorum, monere et confortare studeat, necnon principes Theutoniae ad eius auxilium excitare. 1239, Iunii 9, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To S., presbyter of the title of Saint Mary in Trastevere, and R., deacon cardinal of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. The Apostolic See holds a particular concern regarding the kingdom of Sicily, that God in His mercy might bring it from distress to peace, and from the disgrace of servitude to the honor of freedom through the ministry of the same See, so that its inhabitants may rejoice, having found in us and our brothers the efforts of wise providence and the results of due circumspection. Hence, we wish to rightly provide that the Church may remain free from scandal and untainted concerning matters that need to be addressed in the kingdom, and indeed that you may more freely pursue the office of the legation entrusted to you, being more fully informed about what should be omitted or done. We desire and by apostolic writing command you that, without our special mandate, you make no alterations whatsoever concerning the state of the aforesaid kingdom; do not grant any temporal matters—be they villages, castles, cities, estates, lands, possessions, or houses—nor any spiritual matters—be they prebends and ecclesiastical benefices; nor ordain any vacant churches until, with the grace of God, the aforesaid kingdom is established in a peaceful and free state, at which time we will decree, with the counsel of our brothers, what we see will favor the honor of the Church and its benefit. Concerning these and other matters, may your prudent foresight act in such a way that the honor of the Apostolic See is augmented with the praise of your name.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa S. tituli Sancte Marie Transtiberim presbytero et R. Sancte Marie in Cosmidin diacono cardinalibus mandat, ne circa regni Sicilie statum, sine speciali mandato, aliqua immutent aut beneficia concedant, donec regnum in tranquillo et libero statu per Dei gratiam constituatur. Datum apud Lateranum, anno IV.

**Translation to English:**

To the archbishops and noble men, other princes of Germany, having the power to elect the king of the Romans, to be later promoted to emperor. Since among the other princes of the world you are especially bound to procure the honor of the Church and the Roman Empire, and we firmly hope that you, as distinguished in faith and sincere in devotion, are diligently and fervently aiming for the exaltation of both, we more confidently request and urge you to this end, as we believe you will more willingly and promptly comply with our wishes in this matter. Therefore, since the beloved son, the noble Landgrave of Thuringia, is prepared to undertake the task for the honor of God and the Church and the protection of the said empire, we earnestly admonish, request, and urge your community, commanding in the remission of sins, that, trusting in the grace of the Holy Spirit, you elect the said Landgrave unanimously without delay as the king of the Romans, to be later promoted to emperor, since it is known that the aforementioned empire is currently vacant, faithfully and steadfastly assisting him, and vigorously supporting him to the praise and glory of the Lord Jesus Christ, the increase of the Catholic faith and the liberty of the Church, and the tranquility of the entire Christian people. For we will, with the help of the Lord, indefatigably strive to promote the affairs of that empire and yours, and those of the other princes of Germany. Given at Lyon, 11th day before the Kalends of May, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopis et nobilibus viris principibus Theutonie mandat ut lantgravium Thuringie in Romanorum regem eligant. 1239, Apr. 21. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Worcester, abbots, priors, and other prelates and clerics of the churches established in the city and diocese of Worcester. In the matter of providing the subsidy once requested by our predecessor of blessed memory, Pope Gregory, from the prelates and clerics of England for the needs of the Apostolic See, the contribution is said to have proceeded not so much according to the resources of the churches as according to the disposition of the contributors, with some promising and paying more, others less, as dictated by greater or lesser devotion and as was more diligently admonished and effectively induced by the bishops among the clergy. We understand that the present subsidy, which we recently deemed necessary to request from the English Church, was distributed by our beloved son, Master Martin, a cleric of our chamber, who was then in those parts, more by example of the aforementioned contribution than by regard for ecclesiastical revenues. However, since your contribution in the previous aid, as we have been given to understand, was more abundant than others due to greater devotion, and a portion of the present subsidy has been assigned to you corresponding to the amount of the previous contribution, you, feeling a loss where you have deserved grace, and fearing that this might set a precedent, have requested that the burdens on your churches be precluded by the providence of the Apostolic See in the future. Therefore, inclined by your devotion's prayers, we do not wish that by the example of such a distribution of the subsidy any prejudice may be generated against you or your churches in future times. Given at Lyon, the 18th of May, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Wigorniensi, abbatibus, prioribus et aliis ecclesiarum prelatis Wigorniensem ad preces devotionis eorum declarat, ne in futuris temporibus ex distributione subsidii ecclesiis suis preiudicium generetur. 1245, Mai. 18. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected bishop of Ferrara. Desiring to promote the matter of the Roman Empire commendably with the support of divine grace, we grant to your discretion the authority that, once the election of the Roman king to be later promoted to emperor has been held, you may effectively compel all secular and regular church prelates, as well as princes and other clerics and laity established throughout Germany, to give their attention to the one who has been elected, to swear oaths of fealty, and to perform all that they are accustomed to provide to Roman kings or emperors. This should be done by first issuing a warning to said prelates and clerics, and if necessary, by imposing sentences of suspension from office, dignity, honor, and benefice, and to said princes and laity through spiritual and temporal penalties. You should strictly command those prelates and clerics whom you have suspended for this reason to personally present themselves before the apostolic see within a certain peremptory period that you will set for them, to receive a sentence of deposition or another punishment, as the gravity of their offense might require. You should also notify them that if they fail to appear within the set period, we will proceed against them to deposition or other penalties — notwithstanding their bodily absence — as we see necessary. Given at Lyon, on the 10th day before the Kalends of May, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa electo Ferrariensi mandat ut post electionem regis Romanorum in imperatorem promovendi, ecclesiarum praelatos et principes per Theutoniam constitutos compellat, ut electo fidelitatis iuramenta praestent et consueta exhibeant. 1238, Apr. 22. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

... to the prior of Santa Maria outside the gate of Lucca. Our beloved son, Andreas, a cleric of the Church of St. John of Gaeta, has shown us through a petition that although we previously gave a mandate by our letters to our beloved son, the parish priest of Pugnan, to provide him with a suitable ecclesiastical benefice in some church of the province of Pisa, restraining any opposers, the same parish priest, although he ordered the parish priest and chapter of the church of Bluiti in the diocese of Pisa to receive him as a canon and brother of the same church, in which there is neither a certain number of canons nor are there distinct prebends, to provide him with a suitable benefice or to appear before him and show cause why they should not do so, did not proceed further in the matter, being deterred by the fear incited because the Pisan authority prohibited under a certain penalty anyone from the city and diocese from using the letters of the Apostolic See or its legates. Moreover, not wishing that the provision for the aforementioned cleric, who has been exiled from the city and diocese of Pisa by the same authority because he refused to obey its mandates, be delayed in any way, we command you to proceed in the matter according to the content of the letters directed to the same parish priest, notwithstanding that the same cleric is already beneficed elsewhere. Given at Lyons, 9th September, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**
