Innocentius IV papa priori Sancte Marie foris portam Lucan mandat ut, non obstante prohibitione potestatis Pisane, provideat in beneficio clerico Andree de ecclesia sancti Iohannis de Gaeta secundum mandatum litterarum directarum ad plebanum de Pugnan, etsi idem clericus alias beneficiatus sit. 1246, Sept. 9, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected Bishop of Ferrara, legate of the Apostolic See. Following the example of the One, though unworthy, constituted as vicar, who for the salvation of the human race descended from the heights of heaven to the depths of the world, and sent the disciples He chose to preach the gospel to every creature, we, instructed by His example, sometimes call upon prudent and discreet men to share in the care of our great affairs, as we cannot be present in all places physically. These men, by turning the crooked into straight and the rough into smooth, make the paths of our God straight and render the people acceptable to Him. Therefore, we have decided to commit to you, of whose providence and discretion we have firm confidence in the Lord, the full office of legation in the parts of Germany, granting you the free power to root out and to destroy, to overthrow and to scatter, to build and to plant, as you see fit according to God. Thus, we command you to strive to exercise this legation with commendable effort according to the grace given to you by the Lord, so that you may gain merit before God and a good name among men, and we may commend your diligence with worthy praises in the Lord. Given at Lyon, on the 5th of July, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa electo Ferrariensi apostolicae sedis legato mandat ut legationis officium in partibus Theotonie plene exerceat, concessa libera potestate evellendi, destruendi, dissipandi, dispergendi, aedificandi et plantandi, prout secundum Deum expedire viderit. 1247, Jul. 5, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of Uterine Valley, of the Cistercian order, in the diocese of Speyer. The Apostolic See is accustomed to condescend to the prayers of the devoted and, for their sake, to grant special favor to others, especially to those through whom the honor of the Church is increased and its utility is ensured. Therefore, granting a kind assent to the requests of our beloved son, the noble Duke of Lorraine, who earnestly pleaded with us for our beloved son R., the provost of St. Simeon at Trier, we command that you provide for the said provost, on whose behalf the knowledge of letters, moral integrity, and noble lineage intercede more evidently before us, in a prelature, dignity, or office of any church in the province of Trier, if any are currently vacant or as soon as an opportunity arises, by our authority — notwithstanding, if in the church where you decide to provide for him, we have directed our letters for others, which we do not wish to prejudice by the authority of these presents, or the fact that he is already beneficed elsewhere, or any indulgence by which this kind of favor might be impeded —; contradictors, etc. Given at Lyon, the 6th day before the Kalends of January, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa abbati Uterine Vallis, ordinis Cisterciensis, diocesis Spirensis mandat ut dilecto filio R., preposito Sancti Symeonis Treverensis, in aliqua ecclesiarum Treverensis provinciae in prelatura, dignitate vel personatu provideat, non obstantibus scriptis pro aliis directis vel beneficiis iam existentibus. 1245, Dec. 27. Datum Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

It is established that the chronological note at Ripen is falsely ascribed. Potthast, Reg. 11957; Perlbach, Preuss. Reg. 245; Berger 1871. ... to the archbishop of Prussia, Livonia, and Esthonia. It is fitting that through the providence of the Apostolic See, those who are aided by the merits of a commendable life, virtuous deeds, and knowledge, should be preferred for the governance of churches, and especially so when honor is bestowed upon such persons who also promote the glory of the Roman Church. Given that it is clearly known from evident indications regarding our beloved son, Brother Guarner of the Order of Preachers, that he eagerly applies himself to the love of virtues and diligently strives in the pursuit of a religious life, being earnestly committed to the cause of God and the Church, we, deeming it fitting and proper that he should be honored for these merits, and considering the regard of our beloved son, the noble man, the Landgrave of Thuringia, to whom Brother Guarner is known to be both familiar and dear, command by this precept that you appoint the same Brother as bishop of the land of Courland or Pomerania, removing any obstacle of delay or difficulty, and having summoned two or three bishops, confer upon him the gift of consecration, ensuring that the due reverence and obedience are rendered to him by his subjects; as for those who oppose, etc. We declare from now, if anything contrary to our command is attempted regarding this, it shall be null and void. Given at Lyon, on the third day before the Nones of May, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa archiepiscopo Pruscie, Livonie et Estoniet mandat, ut fratrem Guarnerum ordinis Praedicatorum in episcopum Curiensis seu Pomezani constituat et ei munus consecrationis impendat, subditis revenerentiam et obedientiam exhibere iubens. 1245, Mai. 5, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

Considering that we have shown liberality and kindness to several ecclesiastical persons of your city and diocese, by granting them our letters of grace concerning benefices and other special favors, hoping that they, as beneficiaries of the Apostolic See, would exhibit grateful devotion to us and the Church, especially in times of need, and labor diligently to promote its affairs: we wish and by the authority of these presents, we command you, that you should not hesitate to completely deprive all those whom you find ungrateful and lacking devotion in this regard, of such graces. You shall instruct the executors, to whom we have entrusted the execution of these graces, not to proceed with any apostolic letters obtained concerning them, and revoke any actions, if any have been initiated by them; contradictors, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 5th Nones of October, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa mandat ut omnes ecclesiastici civitatis et diocesis, qui ingrati et indevoti erga sedem apostolicam reperiuntur, beneficiis et gratiis apostolicis priventur. 1247, Oct. 3, Lugduni.

To the provosts of Salzburg and Pechtersgaden of the Order of St. Augustine in the diocese of Salzburg. Gregorius IX papa provostis Salzeburgensi et Pechtersgardmensi mandatum tradit, ut archiepiscopo Pruscie, Livonie et Estonie administrationem episcopatus Chimensis vacantem committant, donec aliud decernatur. 1229, Mar. 30. Datum Lugduni.

**Regesto:**

Innocentius IV papa archiepiscopo Prussiae, Livoniae et Estoniae legato mandat, ut controversiam inter Caminensem ex una parte et Misnensem ac Brandenburgensem episcopos ex altera super episcopatuum limitibus, auditis rationibus, concordia vel iustitia dirimat. 1251, Dec. 23. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To our knowledge, as reported by our beloved son, the nobleman Gerbert, Count of Stoltenbroke, although he has cohabited with his noble wife for eight years and has had offspring with her, he is related to her within the fourth degree of consanguinity. Therefore, he and, on his behalf, our venerable brothers, the bishops of Münster, Osnabrück, and Minden, along with our beloved sons, the counts of Tecklenburg and Oldenburg, have humbly petitioned us to allow the count, who offers himself with his knights and household to maintain and defend the justice of the Church by adhering to our dearest son in Christ, Henry, illustrious King of the Romans, to be marked with the sign of the cross, to remain in the marriage contracted with his wife by our grace. Although we wish the canonical constitutions, which bind all, to be inviolably observed by everyone, we do not wish to stretch their string so much that it should either break or be entirely abandoned, because God has established the fullness of ecclesiastical power in the Apostolic See so that the Roman Pontiff, who has received the keys of power and discretion in blessed Peter, may sometimes exercise rigor, sometimes prefer leniency, as the diversity of causes, considering all circumstances, requires different dispensations. Therefore, inclined by the devoted supplications of the said bishops and counts, we entrust to your devotion by the authority of these presents that, the aforementioned Count of Stoltenbroke faithfully fulfilling what he offers, you may dispense with him and his said wife by our authority so that, notwithstanding this impediment, they may licitly remain in the marriage thus contracted, declaring the offspring born of them to be legitimate. Given at Lyon, on the Nones of July, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa mandato electo Ferrariensi dispensat cum Gerberto comite de Stoltenbroke et uxore sua, quarta consanguinitatis linea coniunctis, ut in matrimonio contracto permaneant, legitimando prolem susceptam, propter oblationem in servitium ecclesiae, annuente rege Henrico Romanorum. Datum Lugduni, Nonis Iulii, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected Bishop of Ferrara, legate of the Apostolic See. We are greatly disturbed and moved when some presume to inflict troubles upon churches and ecclesiastical persons, but we are justly provoked to greater anger when our officials and associates, especially those whom we favor with greater grace and favor due to their nobility and probity, are offended by some. The more they are engaged in the service of us and the Apostolic See, the more they should be honored by others, and their injuries affect us more acutely. Therefore, since our beloved son, the Provost of Utrecht and Xanten, our chaplain, as we have learned from his report, is greatly troubled by some concerning the benefices he holds in the kingdom of Germany, and it is burdensome for him to have to recurr to the aforementioned See whenever he suffers injuries concerning the rights and revenues of those benefices, we, wishing to provide an appropriate remedy for the aforementioned chaplain, command that you, or his procurators, whenever requested by them, ensure by our authority the fulfillment of justice concerning the aforementioned rights and revenues against any wrongdoers of the said chaplain; contradictors etc.; notwithstanding the constitution concerning two days' journey issued in the general council. Given at Lyon, 27th September, in the fourth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa electo Ferrariensi, apostolicae sedis legato, mandat ut, contra iniuriatores dilecti filii praepositi Traiectensis et Xanctensis, capellani sui, super beneficiis in regno Teutoniae, iustitiae complementum exhibeat. 1230, Sept. 27. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Canterbury. Since the benignity of the apostolic see embraces some in the sweetness and gentleness of its discourse, pursuing them with the prerogative of favor and special grace, we have deemed it fitting to favorably extend the hand of our beneficence to persons distinguished by nobility of birth, knowledge of letters, and good morals, whose appointment benefits and honors the utility of churches. Considering therefore the commendable testimony that is borne concerning our beloved son William, cantor of Lausanne, born of a noble man, the count of Gruyère, and being thereby induced, we wish to favor him with special grace. We firmly command you, by apostolic writings, to provide for him in the kingdom of England with an ecclesiastical benefice that is worth sixty marks of silver annually, by our authority—regardless of whether the church in which you decide to provide for him has the care of souls, or if by oath or confirmation of the apostolic see, or by any other firmness, a certain number of canons has been established, or if for others in the same we have directed our writings, which we do not wish to be prejudiced by the authority of the present, or if it has been granted by the apostolic see that its rector or chapter cannot be compelled by apostolic letters to provide or receive anyone, not mentioning this indulgence expressly, or any other privileges, indulgences, customs, or constitutions, by which this provision of grace might be impeded—; contradictors etc. Given at Lyon, the 16th day before the Kalends of September, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Cantuariensi mandat ut Guillelmo cantori Lausannensi in regno Anglie beneficium ecclesiasticum annuatim sexaginta marcas argenti valens provideat. 1240, Aug. 17, Lugduni.

Therefore, let no one etc. of our concession etc. If anyone etc. Given at Lyon, 22nd November, in the fourth year.

Gregorius IX papa nobilibus viris Manegoldo comiti de Wilperce et filiis eius indulgentiam concedit ne sententia excommunicationis contra eos ab aliquo delegato vel subdelegato Apostolicae Sedis absque speciali mandato promulgetur. 1230, Nov. 22, Lugduni.

To the Archbishop of Lund. Innocentius IV papa archiepiscopo Lundensi mandat, ut, sicut prius iussum est, episcopum Sleswicensem moneat et inducat, ut regi Datie homagium et fidelitatem praestet, aut causam nobis rescribat, cur id fieri non debeat. Datum Lugduni, XV Kalendas Novembris, anno quarto.

Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, inclined by your supplications, we have decided to absolve you all, collectively and individually, from any obligation which you owed to the late Emperor Frederick or to anyone on his behalf for any reason, and especially for the expenses made for the defense of your city, at the time when the city came into the hands of the Church, by the authority of these presents. To the Archbishop of Trier. We have perceived you to be so fervent regarding the affairs of the Church, which you have undertaken boldly and courageously, that we consider it fitting, indeed necessary, to grant your requests with swift favor. Therefore, as you have taken care to explain to us, you have decided to confer upon our beloved son, the senior provost of Cologne, the Transrenal archdeaconry of the Church of Trier, which falls under your donation and in which you hold a certain highly fortified and renowned castle against the enemies of the Church. Venerable Cardinal Priest of the title of Saint Mary in Trastevere, our vicar in the City. Through the strength of the Lord’s right hand, Frederick, the perfidious persecutor of the Church, is justly rejected and wounded by those whose ministry he attempted to diminish and overthrow other ministers of God. From this, there emerges full confidence that as the impious one soon approaches his downfall, a desired consolation will come to the desolate realm for the honor and tranquility of the Church. Having held a solemn deliberation with our brothers, we have resolved that we should diligently labor with alert minds for the advancement of such a great matter. **Gregorius IX papa** venerabili cardinale tituli Sancte Marie Transtiberim et R. By the authority of these presents, we grant you the power to pronounce sentences of excommunication against all those who, by their counsel, assistance, or favor, hindered you from capturing the aforementioned castle, unless they return the said castle to you after being warned. This is to be done notwithstanding any privilege granted to them by the Apostolic See, which would prevent such sentences from being pronounced against them or their lands. Given at Lyon, 19th February, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Argentinensi auctoritatem concedit, ut in personas eorum qui castrum de Keisersperc capere impedierunt, excommunicationis et terrarum interdicti sententias promulgare possit, nisi moniti castrum restituant, privilegiis apostolicis non obstantibus. Datum Lugduni, XI Kal. Martii, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbots of Kaisham and Wibilingin and the prior of Kaisham of the Cistercian order and of the order of Saint Benedict, of the dioceses of Augsburg and Constance. Although we propose that everyone, and especially bishops, take on the part of the concern as much as we can with God, when we perceive offenses in them that offend the eyes of the divine majesty and are examples of destruction to others, it is understood to be within our concern to apply that remedy which we believe to be opportune in the Lord. Since certain nefarious acts of the Bishop of Trent have been reported to us that we cannot and ought not to overlook with God and our honor, we, wishing to provide for this from our office, command you to diligently inquire into the life and merits of that bishop and concerning the matter that he is said to have illicitly alienated the goods of the Church of Trent and to have given counsel, help, and favor to the late Emperor Frederick after he was bound by the sentence of excommunication. Diligently ascertain the truth, and faithfully send to us in writing what you find, under your seals, by a trustworthy messenger, setting a suitable peremptory term for that bishop, by which he shall personally present himself before our presence to answer for his deeds, with the alienation of the goods of the Church of Trent forbidden to the aforementioned bishop in the meantime, as he is suspected of dilapidation. But if the said bishop, without waiting for the outcome of the inquiry, chooses to resign, wishing to counsel his honor and safety, receive his resignation by our authority, reserving the provision of the aforementioned church to the Apostolic See. For we decree that it is void and null if anyone attempts anything concerning the provision of that church without our special mandate. Given at Lyons, the 27th of April, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbatibus de Kaisham et de Wibilingin necnon priori de Kaisham mandat ut inquirant de vita et meritis episcopi Tridentini, qui bona ecclesiae Tridentinae illicite alienasse et consilium F. quondam imperatori post excommunicationem praestitisse dicitur, et quae invenerint sub sigillis suis ad sedem apostolicam transmittant, interdicta interim alienatione bonorum ecclesiae eidem episcopo suspecto de dilapidatione. Si episcopus cedere voluerit, cessionem auctoritate papali recipiant, provisione ecclesiae sedem apostolicam reservante. 1230, Apr. 27, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected representative of Ferrara, legate of the Apostolic See. The proven devotion of our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Mainz, shines brightly, especially in times of need when true friends are recognized, such that he should be considered not only a legitimate but also a special son of the Apostolic See. He has fully demonstrated to it, like a son to a mother, what is due from filial affection, standing by it vigorously and powerfully in times of necessity. For this reason, we, esteeming him with a special prerogative of charity, wish to pursue him with the sweetness of affection, and we desire to show our love for him through action to those dear to him as well. Therefore, considering not only the great but also pleasing and useful services that the Archbishop and, through him, his people have faithfully and effectively rendered to the Roman Church, and wishing to honor him through his nephew, our beloved son Brother Henry, from the Order of Friars Minor, whom we also wish to favor and support due to his religious life, honesty, and integrity, we command that if there is any bishopric within the bounds of your legation that is currently vacant or will soon become vacant, from which he and his nephew can and should be duly provided for, you should make arrangements for him by our authority concerning this brother. Opponents, etc. Given at Lyon, 16th December, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa electo Ferrariensi, apostolicae sedis legato, mandat ut, ob merita archiepiscopi Maguntini et nepotem suum fratrem Henricum honorandum, si episcopatus vacet infra fines legationis, de eo provideat. 1230, Dec. 16, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man John of Montfort of the diocese of Bari. We, applying diligent effort to relieve the burdens of subjects, and especially nobles, willingly bring to effect what we cherish in our hearts concerning them, so that oppressors may feel the shame of confusion, and the oppressed may hence take joy and material for devoted service. Therefore, when you appeared in our presence and proposed that the late Richard of Montfort, your uncle, of the Benevento diocese, had donated all his goods to you while alive, and the late Frederick, former Emperor of the Romans, had stripped you of these goods at his whim, we, swayed by your supplications, restore them to you and your successors by special grace, especially since the Kingdom of Sicily currently lacks a king, provided that the said goods do not belong to another who persists in the devotion to the Church. Given at Lyon, on the seventh day before the Kalends of November, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa nobili viro Iohanni de Montefusculo Barensis diocesis, bona quae quondam Riccardus de Montefusculo, patruus eius, ei donaverat et quae Fridericus quondam imperator Romanorum abstulerat, restituit, dummodo ad alium in devotione ecclesie persistentem non pertineant, cum regnum Sicilie rege careat. Datum Lugduni, VII Kalendas Novembris, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Cluj. The benevolence of the Apostolic See is accustomed to favor with kindness the desires of the faithful who sincerely obey and to adorn the persons of the devoted, whom it finds eager and fervent in their devotion, with suitable titles. Therefore, so that you may feel that the apostolic favor has increased for you due to the special devotion which you are known to have towards us and the Roman Church: we grant by the authority of these presents that no delegate or subdelegate, conservator, or executor by the authority of the Apostolic See or its legates may pronounce sentences of excommunication, suspension, or interdict against you or your church without the special mandate of the same See, making full mention of this indulgence. Therefore, let no one etc. of our concession etc. If anyone etc. Given at Lyons, 14th day before the Kalends of March, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Clugiensi mandat, ut propter devotionem specialem quam habet ad sedem apostolicam, nullus auctoritate apostolica vel legatorum eius sententias excommunicationis, suspensionis aut interdicti in eum aut suam ecclesiam sine mandato speciali promulget. Datum Lugduni, XVI Kalendas Martii, anno quarto (1247).

**Translation to English:**

To the dean and chapter of Verdun. As we send our beloved son, P., cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, to the regions of Germany with the full office of legation entrusted to him, we wish and by the authority of these presents command you not to proceed with the election in your church before the arrival of this legate. You should ensure the provision of a suitable pastor for the church with his advice and consent, or receive as bishop the one whom he will decide to provide for that church. For we decree that anything attempted against our mandate in this matter will be null and void. Given at Lyon, March 17, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa decano et capitulo Virdunensibus mandat, ne procedant ad electionem in ecclesia eorum ante adventum legati, sed cum consilio eius provideant de pastore idoneo. 1231, Mart. 17. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Gurk and the elected Bishop of Seckau. Inclined by the prayers of our beloved son, the elected Archbishop of Salzburg, we command you by the authority of these presents, that you decree with our authority that the collations of churches and prebends, and other ecclesiastical benefices made by the late Archbishop of Salzburg, while he was bound by the chain of excommunication, as well as any alienations of the goods of the Church of Salzburg, if he presumed to make them against the statutes of the canons without the consent of his chapter, are entirely invalid. Given at Lyon, on the Ides of March, in the fourth year (of our pontificate).

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Gurcensi et electo Secowiensi mandat, ut collationes et alienationes a quondam archiepiscopo Salseburgensi, dum erat excommunicatus, factas, irritas decernant. 1247, Mart. 15. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

We have received it as proposed below, neither collated with the Regesta nor supplemented from them. Since the Vatican Archive cannot be accessed now, we present the letter thus truncated so that our work is not excessively delayed, especially since what is missing is probably not of great importance. Berger 2362.

To the abbess and chapter of the secular church of Seconia in the diocese of Constance. Since our beloved son, the noble man Harmann, Count of Hircberc, as we have learned, is diligently and faithfully pursuing the business of the church, we, at his request, have decided to grant a special favor to our beloved son Suiger, priest of the church of Keinz. We have deemed it appropriate to exhort and encourage your community, instructing that you ensure to provide him with a suitable ecclesiastical benefice or prebend that pertains to your collation.

Given at Lyons, the 8th of January, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbatisse et capitulo ecclesie secularis Seconiensis mandat ut Suigero plebano ecclesie de Keinz in beneficio ecclesiastico vel prebenda competenti providere studeant, postulatione Harmanni comitis de Hircberc. Datum Lugduni, VI Idus Ianuarii, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the patriarchs of Aquileia and Grado and the archbishops, bishops, abbots, etc., established throughout Lombardy and Romagna. The balance of rightful consideration is weighed carefully when the merits of the subjects are assessed with just estimation, so that a worthy reward corresponds to the devotions of the faithful and the punishment of perpetual disgrace presses upon the necks of the unfaithful, etc., as above in the letter of the legation of P. of St. George, etc., up to: with the counsel and good pleasure of our beloved son, O. Cardinal Deacon of St. Mary in Via Lata, legate of the Apostolic See, you are to ensure; contradictors, etc. Otherwise, we enjoin the same legate by our letters to execute the apostolic mandate concerning this matter. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Octaviano Sanctae Mariae in Via Lata diacono cardinali, apostolicae sedis legato in Lombardiam et Romaniolam destinato, varia mandata, ad exercendum legationis officium spectantia, dat. 1247, Mart. 8.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz. The providence of the Roman pontiff, with the power to bind and to loose given by the Lord, enhances the grace of dispensation especially when evident benefit or necessity suggests it. Therefore, as you have explained to us, the beloved son, the noble man Conrad, Count Hirsutus, has taken as his wife the beloved daughter in Christ, the noblewoman Junot, daughter of Count Silvester, and afterwards discovered she is related to him in the fourth degree of consanguinity, and the dissolution of this marriage could not occur without the risk of wars and danger to many. You have humbly pleaded with us to allow the aforementioned count and the said Junot to remain in the contracted marriage, considering the nobleman's readiness and usefulness to the Church, and to avert the aforementioned dangers, granting permission from the customary mercy of the Apostolic See. We, therefore, moved by your supplications, grant you the authority by the present letters to dispense with them in this matter. Given at Lyon, on the 30th of January, in the fourth year.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa Archiepiscopo Maguntino mandat, ut dispensationem concedat nobili viro Corrado comiti Hirsuto et Iunotae uxori eius, in quarto consanguinitatis gradu sibi attinentibus, ut in matrimonio remanere possint. 1230, Jan. 30, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the archbishops and bishops, abbots, priors, deans, archdeacons, and other prelates of the churches, and to noble men, counts, barons, knights, and the people of the cities and castles and places established throughout the kingdom of Sicily. Our affection eagerly aspires to this, that the divine power of majesty may deliver you from the yoke of servitude and that all of you may breathe under tranquil abundance. In order that such affection may be happily and easily directed to the goal of completion, we have decided to entrust the full office of legation to our beloved sons, S. cardinal priest of Santa Maria in Trastevere, and R. cardinal deacon of Santa Maria in Cosmedin, men indeed preeminent in the church, endowed with much wisdom and virtue, granting them the free power to relax the sentence of excommunication, which you may have incurred intending against Frederick, the enemy of God and the church, or any others, and to remit each offense you have inflicted upon the church itself, and to admit you into the grace of your mother, the apostolic see, and to gather an army against the said Frederick and his adherents, and to do all things both spiritual and temporal which they see as expedient for the honor of God and the church and for your salvation in this matter. We will consider it valid and pleasing, whatever they or either of them shall see fit to do regarding the aforesaid. Therefore, we affectionately ask and command your community to devoutly and cheerfully admit these legates, in whom we wish to receive our person and be treated with filial reverence, and to reverently and effectively attend to their mandates and admonitions concerning all the aforesaid and others which they shall impose upon you on our behalf. Otherwise, the sentence or penalty, whether spiritual or temporal, which shall have been imposed upon the rebellious by them or either of them, shall be ratified, etc., until: to be observed.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopis, episcopis, abbatibus aliisque praelatis ac nobilibus in regno Siciliae constitutis scribit, legationem committens cardinalibus S. Sanctae Mariae Transtiberim et R. Sanctae Mariae in Cosmidin, cum potestate relaxandi excommunicationes et congregandi exercitum contra Fridericum, atque hortatur ut eos devote admittant et mandata sua reverenter exequantur. 1239, Anagniae.

**Translation to English:**

To the dean and chapter of the church of Colmar in the diocese of Basel. It is fitting for us to have paternal care in the provisions for clerics, so that they may find worthy gifts of grace in us, advance in the increase of virtues, and grow in the frequent praise of God. Hence, on behalf of our beloved son Ulrich, rector of the church of Turckheim in the diocese of Basel, who is said to be supported by the merits of a laudable life and conduct, we have decided to request and admonish your community, instructing that you admit him, for the reverence of the Apostolic See and us, as a brother and canon, in whom we wish to honor the persons of our beloved sons, the noble men of the house of Ferrette and of the house of Petite Pierre, devoted to us and the Roman Church, providing him with a prebend as soon as the opportunity arises, — notwithstanding any oath or agreement confirming a certain number of canons, or that he is otherwise beneficed, or if we have sent letters to you on behalf of another, to whom we do not wish to cause prejudice by this authority, or any indulgence of the Apostolic See, of which mention must be made in our letters —; executing our mandate in such a way that your sincerity may be held in worthy favor by us because of this. Otherwise, we charge our beloved son, the treasurer of the church of Saint Peter in Strasbourg, through our letters, to execute the apostolic mandate concerning this matter; any opponents etc. Given at Lyon, 27 November, in the fourth year. It is written without error.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa decano et capitulo ecclesiae Columbariensis in diocesi Basilensi mandat ut Ulricum rectorem ecclesiae de Turincheme in fratrem et canonicum admittant, eumque de prebenda provideant. 27 Novembris, anno quarto. Datum Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

The text discusses various issues related to the registration and annotation of papal letters and councils held with cardinals, focusing on discrepancies and errors in the inscriptions and the addition of certain phrases in the letters of recommendation for legates. The specific letter mentioned, which entrusted Peter with the office of legation, does not survive, but it is believed to have been written around the time when all related documents to the legation were dated between March 14 and 18. The Pope addresses a nobleman regarding the appointment of the cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil as a legate to Germany, advising him to receive and treat the legate honorably and to trust the messages conveyed on behalf of the papal authority.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobilitati cuidam mandat ut dilectum filium suum P., Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diaconum cardinalem, in legationem Alamanniae missum, honorifice recipiat et mandata eius ex parte sedis apostolicae fidei plenissime habeat. Datum, ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the schoolmaster and Landulf, canon of the Church of the Holy Apostles Peter and Andrew in Paderborn. Inclined by the requests of the beloved sons, noble men of Everstein and of Waldeck, counts, we have deemed it proper to request and admonish the dean and chapter of the New Church of the Diocese of Paderborn, by our letters, commanding them to receive the beloved son Conrad, a cleric of Paderborn, devoted to these counts, who, as he asserts, has not obtained any ecclesiastical benefice, into the canonry and brotherhood out of reverence for the Apostolic See and ourselves. They are to generously confer upon him a prebend if any is presently vacant in their church, or as soon as the opportunity arises — notwithstanding a certain fixed number of canons secured by oath or confirmation of the Apostolic See or by any other firmness, or if we have directed our writings for others, by which the authority of those letters we do not wish to generate prejudice. Therefore, we command that, if the said dean and chapter neglect to fulfill our mandate, you ensure its execution, opposing any contradictors, etc. Given at Lyon, 17th Kalends of December, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa scolastico et Landulfo canonico ecclesie Sanctorum Apostolorum Petri et Andree Padeburgensis mandat ut decanum et capitulum Nove Ecclesie Padeburnensis diocesis instruant ad recipiendum Corradum clericum in canonicum et in fratrem et conferendum prebendam, si vacet. Si mandatum neglexerint, illud exequi procurent. 1230, Nov. 15, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the elect of Ferrara, legate of the Apostolic See. It is pious and almost demanded by a certain debt of law that clerics, who are chosen to the lot of the Lord, should be admitted to participate in His inheritance and be sustained by the stipends of His patrimony, to whose service they are assigned. Therefore, since our beloved son Henry of Vetericuria, a cleric of the diocese of Cologne, whose life and moral integrity are attested to us with commendable testimony, does not have means for sustenance according to the merits of his probity, as he declared in our presence, we, who desire to do good universally, inclined by the prayers of the noble man Henry, lord of Isenburch, devout to the Roman Church, and our beloved daughter in Christ, the noble woman Mettildis, his wife, sister of our venerable brother, the archbishop of Cologne, by the authority of these presents, command you, that to this cleric, who as he claims has not obtained any ecclesiastical benefice, in any of the churches of your legation — notwithstanding if in the church where you deem he should be provided, there is a certain number of canons established by oath or any other firmness, or if for the provision of others we have directed our writings, which we do not wish to be prejudiced by these present letters, or if it has been granted by the apostolic see to the church itself that no one should be provided therein — you should provide or have provided a prebendal benefice, if it is currently vacant or as soon as the opportunity presents itself; contradictors, etc. Given at Lyon, October 12, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa electo Ferrariensi, legato apostolico, mandat ut Henrico de Vetericuria clerico Coloniensis diocesis, cuius probitas commendatur, in beneficio prebendali provideatur. 1230, Oct. 12, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the powers, councils, and people of the cities and places established throughout the March of Ancona, invoking the spirit of sounder counsel. Through human industry, it was previously impossible for you to return with due devotion to the bosom of Mother Church, as the sword of the treacherous Frederick weighed upon your necks. But now, with the right hand of our God, known for triumphing over the proud and wicked, having miraculously removed the imperial diadem from the head of a wicked man, and many being drawn away from his side, who sought to trample the Church of God with him, it is known that a way has been prepared for your community, afflicted by many losses and wounded by damages, to return to the Apostolic See, to be cherished by its sweet embrace. We therefore ask for your devotion and beseech you in the Lord Jesus Christ, strictly commanding you under the obligation of fidelity and imposing upon you in remission of your sins, that you may not let slip the joys of liberty, which are known to have been prepared for you, from your hands, but rise unanimously with ready spirits to attack him, the enemy of God and despiser of the Catholic faith, who has damnably alienated you from it, with all the strength you can, trusting in the aid of divine assistance. Especially since we have deemed it prudent to provide, through solemn legates, as well as having offered necessary aid, namely our beloved sons, S., Cardinal Priest of the title of Santa Maria in Trastevere, and R., Cardinal Deacon of Santa Maria in Cosmedin, that the impiety of that man may soon be overthrown, pursued by the angel of the Lord, and the kingdom of Sicily may be rescued from his hands, with the hope proposed to us that, as they are known to have been more fully endowed by God’s wisdom with the insignia of virtues, they may more easily accomplish things of salvation and grace. Moreover, let your sincerity so fulfill our prayers that, as you can now pretend no shadow of excuse nor assume a veil of fear, it may be fixed in our heart to favor and grace you as special sons of the Church, forgetting the faults of past deeds with the passage of time. In the same manner, to the powers, councils, and people of the cities and places established throughout the Duchy of Spoleto, invoking the spirit of sounder counsel. In the same manner, to the powers, councils, and people of the cities and places established throughout the patrimony of Saint Peter in Tuscany, invoking the spirit of sounder counsel.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa potestatibus, consiliis et populis civitatum et locorum per Anconitanam marchiam, ducatum Spoleti et patrimonium beati Petri in Tuscia constitutis mandat, ut ad gremium ecclesiae redeant et Fredericum, hostem Dei et fidei contemptorem, impugnent. 1239, Anagnia.

**Translation to English:**

Finally, it was reported, described by the distinguished scholar A. Mau. Berger, 2882. To the noble woman Maria of Pisa, daughter of the noble man Raynerius, count of Travara. Inclined by the prayers of our beloved son Uguicion, the Marquis' chaplain, we grant you by the authority of these presents that it may be permitted to you, along with four noble and honorable women accompanying you, to hear divine services in places where it is permitted by the apostolic see during times of interdict, excluding those excommunicated and interdicted, without ringing bells, with closed doors, and in a low voice, provided that neither you nor these women have caused the interdict, nor has it been specially declared against you. Let no one, etc., of our concession, etc. If anyone, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 11th of March, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili mulieri Mariae de Pisis, concedit ut, associatis quatuor mulieribus nobilibus, possit audire divina in locis interdicti tempore, certis condicionibus observatis. 1230, Mart. 11, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the dean of Concordia. Although the Apostolic See is accustomed to open its bosom of compassion to any in need, it is more obliged to readily and willingly assist those who, in defense of ecclesiastical freedom, suffer continuous persecutions from the enemies of the Church, having nearly all their goods destroyed. Therefore, as we have heard that the goods of the Church of Treviso have been so devastated by the late Emperor Frederick and his adherents that the resident canons there have nothing whereby they can be sustained, we, bearing a compassionate affection toward them, command you to provide for six canons, the primicerius, and as many chaplains continuously serving in the same church, with our authority, in the amount of one hundred marks of silver for their sustenance this time from certain churches or monasteries in Carinthia and Styria — notwithstanding if these churches and monasteries, where you decide they should be provided for, have been burdened by our authority with a similar provision, or some indulgence of the Apostolic See granted to them, that they cannot be compelled to receive or provide for anyone through apostolic letters unless they have made express mention of that indulgence, or any other by which such grace could be impeded or even delayed, or the constitution of two diets established in the general council —; provided that the brothers of the military orders of the Temple and the Hospital of Jerusalem are not compelled to such provision. Given at Lyon, on the third day before the Nones of November, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa decano Concordiensi mandat ut sex canonicis, primicerio et totidem capellanis ecclesiae Tervisinae, cuius bona destructa sunt a Friderico imperatore quondam, in centum marcis argenti pro sustentatione provideatur ab ecclesiis vel monasteriis Carinthiae et Styriae. 1246, Nov. 3, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the provost of the monastery of Augsburg of the order of Saint Benedict in the diocese of Constance. The beloved son Berthold, parish priest of the church of Seckingen, procurator of the beloved son, the abbot of Saint Gall, humbly requested us to favor him with special grace, that we might cause him to be received in the church of Episcopal Cell, diocese of Constance. Therefore, at the request of the same abbot, whom we intend to honor, along with his followers, and wishing to grant a special favor, we command that the aforementioned parish priest be received by our authority as a canon and brother by the beloved sons, the provost and chapter of the above-mentioned church, and be granted a prebend if any is currently vacant in that church, or as soon as an opportunity presents itself, notwithstanding a certain number of canons secured by oath or other firmness, or if we send our letters for others, by which we do not wish to generate prejudice with the present authority, or because the same Berthold is otherwise beneficed; supporters of the opposite view, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 3rd Nones of December, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa preposito Augensis monasterii mandat, ut Bertoldus plebanus Seconiensis in canonicum et fratrem ecclesiae Episcopalis Celle Constantiensis diocesis recipiatur et sibi conferatur prebenda vacans, non obstante numero canonicorum iuramento firmato. 1230, Dec. 3, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the deacon cardinal of Santa Maria in Via Lata, legate of the Apostolic See. Since we are sending you to Lombardy, with the full office of legation entrusted to you, as an angel of peace by the advice of our brothers, we grant you the full authority by these presents to reform peace or concord among the cities, counts, barons, and other nobles of the march of Treviso. For we will hold as ratified and firm whatever you consider necessary to do, establish, or even ordain with the aforementioned or some of them, together with our brothers. Given at Lyon, the 11th of April, in the fourth year [of the pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa O. Sanctae Mariae in Via Lata cardinali diacono, legato apostolicae sedis, mandat ut pacem inter civitates, comites, barones et nobiles marchiae Trivisinae reformet, plenam concedens potestatem. Datum Lugduni, III Idus Aprilis, anno IV.

Translation to English:

To the Bishop of Regensburg. Having learned that our venerable brother, the Bishop of Friuli, is so afflicted with severe and incurable bodily infirmity that he is unable to carry out his pastoral duties, we, to prevent the Friulian church from suffering spiritual and temporal harm due to this, instructed our venerable brother, the Bishop of Cracow, through our letters, to appoint a coadjutor to the aforesaid bishop if the situation was as described. Although the same Bishop of Cracow appointed Brother Pontius, prior of the Dominican brothers of Marseille, as coadjutor by this mandate's authority, the prior refused to undertake this burden, and the said Bishop of Cracow subsequently did not provide another assistant, as was recently reported to us by our beloved son Otto Fornari, provost of the aforementioned church, explaining the serious detriment to the same church. Therefore, wishing to prevent any harm to the church with fatherly care, we order your brotherhood to personally go to the aforementioned church and, if you find the situation as described, to appoint a prudent and discreet man as coadjutor to the aforementioned Bishop of Friuli in spiritual and temporal matters. If the said Bishop of Friuli, prudently considering his soul and honor, wishes to voluntarily resign from the episcopate, which seems to be for the best, you should accept his resignation on our behalf and ensure that he receives a suitable and decent provision from the episcopal goods for his sustenance and enjoys the peaceful possession of this provision; opponents, etc. Given at Lyons, on the Ides of December, in the fourth year.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Regensit mandat, ut, si episcopus Foroiuliensis propter infirmitatem nequiverit officium pastorale exercere, coadiutorem ei deputet; et si episcopus cedere voluerit, cessionem recipiat et provisionem honestam ei assignet. Datum Lugduni, Idibus Decembris, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the patriarchs of Grado and Aquileia, and to the archbishops, bishops, abbots, priors, etc., established throughout Lombardy and Romagna. Since we have dispatched our beloved son, O., cardinal deacon of Santa Maria in Via Lata, a man indeed endowed with knowledge and adorned with honesty, as previously mentioned in the letter of legation of P. of Saint George, etc., until: we urge and exhort the entirety of you earnestly, commanding that you assist the churches and their goods for the purpose of promoting this matter, etc., as stated throughout the letter. Given as above. Similarly, to the noble men, marquises, counts, barons, and other nobles established throughout Lombardy, until: we dispatch, we earnestly urge and exhort your nobility, commanding that you devoutly receive him, indeed rather us in him, etc., as stated throughout, promising that whatever you decide or arrange with him concerning all matters related to the aforementioned affair, etc., as stated throughout.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa patriarchis Gradensi et Aquilegensi, archiepiscopis, episcopis, abbatibus, prioribus per Lombardiam et Romaniolam constitutis mandat, ut ecclesiarum bona ad promovendum negotium subveniant; etiam marchionibus, comitibus, baronibus et nobilibus, ut cardinalem O. suscipiant et negotia cum eo ordinent. 1231, [locum non specificatum].

**Translation to English:**

To the dean and chapter of Winpina, diocese of Worms. The merits of the praiseworthy conduct and life of our beloved son Reinard, rector of the church in Schlettstadt, diocese of Speyer, are said to commend him, so that he might obtain special grace from us. Therefore, moved by these merits and at the request of our beloved daughter in Christ, the noblewoman A., Countess of Levenstein, who is devoted to us and the Roman Church, and whose person we wish to honor in him, we earnestly ask and exhort your assembly, commanding you to admit him as a brother and canon for the reverence of the Apostolic See and ours, providing him liberally with a prebend as soon as the opportunity arises, notwithstanding any fixed number of canons secured by oath or any other firmness, nor the fact that he may already hold another benefice, or if we have directed our letters for others, which by the authority of these presents we do not wish to be prejudiced, or any indulgence about which special mention in our letters would be necessary; ensuring that you fulfill our mandate in such a way that your sincerity may be deemed worthy of our favor due to his rejoicing in what he hopes to obtain. Otherwise, we have directed through our letters to our beloved sons, the provost, the treasurer of the major church, and the dean of St. Germain in Speyer, to execute this apostolic mandate; contradictors etc. Given at Lyons, 24th November, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa Innocentius IV decano et capitulo de Winpina, Warmaciensis diocesis, mandat ut Reinardum, rectorem ecclesiae in Sceltburnen Spirensis diocesis, in fratrem et canonicum admittant, de prebenda providentes. 1246, Nov. 24, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Conrad, rector of the church in Buesingen, diocese of Würzburg. On behalf of our venerable brother, the Bishop of Bamberg, it was presented before us that when Rudeger, a canon of the church of St. John in Houge, freely resigned the church in Buesingen, Würzburg diocese, which was first of the late Henry, your father, you, having been dispensed by the apostolic see to hold all orders and ecclesiastical benefices, even if they had the cure of souls, subsequently lawfully obtained the said church and have peacefully possessed it for many years. Therefore, the same bishop, of whom you are said to be a cleric, humbly petitioned us that since the defect of hereditary succession, which is reprobated in ecclesiastical benefices, is purged by the intervention of a third party, and because you are commended for the merit of your life and praiseworthy conduct, we should care to confirm the said church to you out of the benignity of the apostolic see. Inclined by the prayers of the said bishop, we confirm the church to you by apostolic authority, as you justly and peacefully possess it, and we strengthen it with the support of this present writing. Let no one etc. of our confirmation etc. If anyone etc. Given at Lyons, on the 21st of January, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Conrado rectori ecclesiae in Buesingen diocesis Herbipolensis ecclesiam quam iure et quiete possidet auctoritate apostolica confirmat. Datum Lugduni, XII Kalendas Februarii, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man, the margrave of Meissen. The greater the power and strength you are believed to hold, the more it befits and is proper for you to refrain from causing harm and offenses to churches and church persons, since in their sufferings, the Lord Jesus Christ Himself is offended and seems to be persecuted. Therefore, as we have learned from our venerable brother, the bishop of Naumburg, you have attacked him and the church of Naumburg with many damages and oppressions, incited by a seditious instigator. We, desiring your honor and well-being, earnestly ask, admonish, and exhort your devotion, commanding that you wisely consider how grave and indecent it would be to be called a persecutor of the church, and how much this would detract from your nobility and honor. Out of reverence for the eternal King, the Apostolic See, and ourselves, cease entirely from oppressing the said bishop and church. Otherwise, do not find it burdensome or distressing if we administer justice to the bishop, which we neither can nor should deny him, since we are indebted to everyone in this regard. Given at Lyon, January 22, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro marchioni Misnensi mandat ut ab iniuriis et offensis in episcopum et ecclesiam Nuemburgensem abstineat, alias iustitiam episcopo administraturus. 1230, Ian. 22, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz and the Bishop-elect of Ferrara. Be it known to you that it has come to our attention that when the church of Regensburg was recently deprived of its pastor, the dean and chapter of the same church, having called together all those who wished, ought, and could conveniently be present, met to discuss the appointment of a future bishop. After due deliberation, they unanimously entrusted the matter to the aforementioned dean and Albert, a fellow canon, granting them full authority to choose three other trustworthy persons from their college, with whom they were to provide for a suitable candidate either from the body of the church or elsewhere for the widowed church. The aforementioned chapter solemnly promised before all who were present to accept as pastor the person whom these five would unanimously elect. After receiving this commission, the dean and canon associated themselves with three others according to the terms of the commission. These five, after diligent deliberation among themselves and invoking the grace of the Holy Spirit, unanimously elected Bertold, the provost of Speyer, a prudent and discreet man, circumspect in spiritual and temporal matters, as the bishop of Regensburg. They placed both themselves and the election they had made under the protection of the Apostolic See to prevent any attempts against their rights. However, because later S. and some other canons of the same church rashly opposed the aforementioned election and presumed to elect the provost of Regensburg in fact, although they could not do so legally, the aforesaid provost of Speyer delayed consenting to the election until he could understand our will on this matter. Therefore, not wishing the provision for the aforesaid church to be delayed on account of this, we command you to diligently inquire into the truth of these matters, and if you find that the election of the aforesaid provost of Speyer was canonically conducted for a suitable person, you shall confirm it once the provost consents to the election, nullifying the other election, and you shall induct him into the corporal possession of the bishopric of Regensburg and defend him so inducted. Ensure that all and singular subjects of the church of Regensburg exhibit due obedience and reverence to him, and that the neighboring bishops bestow the consecration upon the elected. As for the expenses to be reimbursed, determine what is just between the parties, and ensure compliance with your decrees, etc. Witnesses, etc. — notwithstanding the constitution concerning two diets, etc. Given at Lyon, on the Ides of June, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa archiepiscopo Maguntino et electo Ferrariensi mandat ut electionem Bertoldi praepositi Spirensis in episcopum Ratisponensem, si canonice celebrata sit, confirment, cassata alia electione. 1253, Idibus Iunii. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Fulco, count of Lavagna, son of the late Ravascherius, count. Although the union of marital bond is prohibited by sacred canons in the fourth degree of consanguinity or affinity, the Roman Church nevertheless sometimes provides a dispensation in these cases, especially when urgent necessity or evident utility demands it. Therefore, hoping that you and yours will be fruitful in many ways to the Roman Church, inclined by the prayers of your devotion, we dispense with you by apostolic authority so that you may freely take Alda, called Pastorecta, a woman related to you in the fourth degree of consanguinity, as you claim, as your wife, notwithstanding the aforementioned consanguinity. Let no one, therefore, etc. Given at Lyon, on the Nones of April, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Fulconi comiti Lavaniel, nato quondam Ravascherii comitis, concedit dispensationem apostolicam ut Aldam dictam Pastorectam, consanguineam in quarto gradu, uxorem accipere possit, non obstante consanguinitate. 1239, Apr. 5, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

The petition submitted on your behalf stated that, due to your unwavering loyalty and devotion to the Roman Church, you have suffered damages and losses from the men of the castle of San Severino, in the diocese of Camerino, who are supporters of Frederick, the former emperor and enemy of the Church. You humbly requested protection through the providence of the Apostolic See regarding these matters. Therefore, in order that the faithful of the Church, by virtue of their steadfastness, may obtain the proper remedy of relief, and that the unfaithful, through their inherent malice, may at least recognize the consequences of their actions as instructed by punishment, we are inclined to your pleas. We declare that the men of the said castle are obligated to you for the full and proper compensation of your damages, which you have suffered on behalf of the Church, provided you persist in your devotion to the Apostolic See. We decree that these men, notwithstanding any contrary edict or any other obstacle, must fully restore to you such damages. Let no one, therefore, etc., infringe our constitution, etc. Given at Lyon, February 15, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Paganello de Camerino et fratribus suis mandat, ut homines castri Sancti Severini Camerinensis diocesis pro debita recompensatione dampnorum, quae propter ecclesiam passi sunt, obligati sint et dampna integra resarcire debeant. 1247, Feb. 15, Lugduni.

**English Translation:**

To the Archbishop of Cologne. On behalf of Otto, provost of the church of Aachen, it has been reported to us that, previously between the late... Valentine, the elected, and him, a dispute arose concerning the election of him and the postulation of the aforementioned elected one in the church of Liège. While the case was still pending, and after his election was annulled, our venerable brother, the bishop of Tournai, and our beloved son, the provost of the church of Saint-Quentin, claimed that they had admonished him by apostolic authority not to make any decisions regarding the revenues of the episcopal see of Liège. Although he had been summoned by them to their presence, he contumaciously refused to appear, and they deprived him of all his ecclesiastical dignities and benefices by sentence, and pronounced a sentence of excommunication against him. However, as soon as he learned that proceedings had been taken against him in this manner, he sought through a suitable procurator from them that such proceedings be revoked, especially since he was prepared to provide suitable security to stand trial before them. This, however, they entirely refused to do. Hence, he humbly petitioned us to order that the aforesaid dignities and benefices be restored to him by special grace, and since he had, in the meantime, conferred some benefices pertaining to his donation by reason of his provostships of Aachen and Saint Servatius of Maastricht and his other dignities on certain individuals, we might, with paternal solicitude, provide counsel to these individuals concerning the said benefices. Therefore, we command you, if this is indeed the case and the said provost wishes to confer these benefices anew to the same individuals, you, unless they have been conferred to others by our mandate, confirm his collation by our authority. Given at Lyon, 28 October, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Coloniensi mandat, ut, si Otto prepositus Aquensis beneficia nova conferre velit, collationem suam auctoritate apostolica confirmet, nisi ea aliis de mandato papali iam collata fuerint. 1229, Oct. 28, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

The letter of the Venerable Cleric A. Mau, written in the month of May, was finally recorded in the register. Berger 2597. To the parish priest of the church of Licigniano in the diocese of Siena. Those admitted to the clerical militia should be provided for from ecclesiastical goods, so that, being made partakers of the reward and burden, they may effectively apply themselves to laudably achieve their desire. Hence, we, wishing to grant a special favor to our beloved son Peter Guarnaldi, cleric of the diocese of Perugia, who, due to an impending discord, along with his brothers, has suffered losses and detriments to their goods, command that you provide him, by our authority, with one of the churches of the city or diocese of Grosseto, even if it has the care of souls, or with a suitable ecclesiastical benefice, if it is presently vacant or as soon as it becomes possible, notwithstanding if in the church, where you decide to provide for him, there is a fixed number of canons established by oath or confirmation of the apostolic see or any other firm rule, or if we have directed our letters in it for others, to which we wish, etc., up to: generated, or any indulgence or privilege that has been granted to the church by the apostolic see, by which such provision could be hindered or delayed, or that we have otherwise written for the same; opposers, etc. Given at Lyon, 16th Kalends of March, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa plebano ecclesiae de Licigniano mandat, ut Petro Guarnaldi clerico Perusinae dioecesis de ecclesia vel beneficio ecclesiastico in dioecesi Grossetana provideatur. 1229, Feb. 14. Lugduni.

Translation to English:
To O. Cardinal Deacon of Santa Maria in Via Lata, legate of the Apostolic See. Although all those distinguished by the Christian religion are bound to defend the Catholic faith and ecclesiastical freedom, ecclesiastical men, both religious and secular, and especially prelates of churches, etc., as above in the document addressed to P. Cardinal Deacon of San Giorgio in Velabro, legate of the Apostolic See, up to: defeating the faithful. Therefore, we command that you attentively admonish and induce all the prelates of the churches of Lombardy and Romagna to carefully consider how many tribulations and troubles Frederick has inflicted not only on churches but also on almost the entire Christian populace, etc., as in the same document up to: providing necessary support. Given at Lyon, on the 9th of April, in the fourth year.

Regesto in Latin:
Innocentius IV papa O. Sancte Marie in Via Lata diacono cardinali, apostolicae sedis legato mandat, ut prelatos ecclesiarum Lombardiae et Romaniole moneat et inducat ad resistendum tribulationibus a Friderico illatis. 1246, Apr. 9, Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To the abbot of the monastery of Saint Gall in the diocese of Constance. We, inclined by your prayers, grant you by the authority of these presents the license to sell and to enfeoff possessions and other less useful goods of your monastery for the purpose of promoting the business of the Church and the Empire — notwithstanding the oath you made not to alienate the possessions of the said monastery. Therefore, let no one etc. Given at Lyon, on the 10th day before the Kalends of May, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

Regesto in Latin:

Innocentius IV papa abbati monasterii sancti Galli Constantiensis diocesis licentiam elargitur vendendi ac infeudandi possessiones pro negotio ecclesiae et imperii promovendo, non obstante iuramento de non alienandis. 1247, Apr. 22. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the former Queen of the Romans. As we have learned, our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Mainz of clear memory, bound himself to your husband, the King of the Romans, for ten thousand marks of silver, as is said to be contained in the letters drawn up on this matter. And since you are said to have these letters of obligation, we earnestly ask and urge your Highness to not delay in returning those letters to the aforementioned Archbishop. Given at Lyon, on the 5th of May, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa reginam quondam Romanorum hortatur, ut litteras obligationis, quas habere dicitur, archiepiscopo Maguntino restituat. 1230, Mai. 11, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected Bishop of Ferrara, legate of the apostolic see. Since we have instructed our venerable brother, the Bishop of Gurk, and our beloved sons, the elects of Regensburg and Seckau, through our letters, to compel all the suffragans of the Church of Salzburg, the clergy, and the people of both the city and diocese of Salzburg, as well as the counts, barons, and other nobles who are vassals and officials of the said church, to devoutly receive our beloved son Burchard, the elected of Salzburg, as the father and shepherd of their souls and to effectively carry out his beneficial admonitions and commands, by our authority, removing any appeal: we wish and by the authority of these presents command you that you compel the aforementioned Bishop, and the elects of Regensburg and Seckau, if necessary, to execute our mandate in this matter, by the same authority, removing the impediment of appeal. Given at Lyon, 5th day before the Kalends of March, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa electo Ferrariensi, apostolicae sedis legato mandat ut, si necesse fuerit, Gurcensem episcopum ac Ratisponensem et Secowensem electos appellatione remota compellat ad Burchardum Salseburgensem electum tanquam patrem et pastorem a Salseburgensibus suscipiendum. 1230, Feb. 25. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

... to the provost of the Church of Saint Peter in Viniali, Diocese of Furcone. It is unworthy for us to leave without our grace those whose devotion we experience through continuous services, while sometimes we make participants of our benefits those whose merits are unknown to us. We therefore rightly pursue the known with grace, while at times we may even anticipate the unknown with it. Hence, since Gualterus, called de Ocra, the notary of Frederick, the former emperor of the Romans, is said to hold the Church of Saint Eusanius in the Diocese of Furcone, we, intending to pursue with special favor our beloved son Berardus de Furconio, our clerk and scribe, whom we hold in great esteem and accept immensely for the many services rendered to us and to the Roman Church, command that, once the aforementioned Gualterus is removed from the church, having rendered himself unworthy of it, you should ensure that it is conferred upon the aforementioned Berardus by our authority. You are to induct him into possession of the same church and defend him once inducted, and ensure that he or his procurator on his behalf is fully answered concerning its revenues; contradictors etc. Given at Lyons, Kalends of February, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa proposito ecclesiae Sancti Petri de Vinialibus Furconensis diocesis mandat, ut amoto Gualtero de Ocra, qui ecclesiam Sancti Eusanii obtinere dicitur, Berardo de Furconio clerico eam conferat et in possessionem inducat. Datum Lugduni, Kalendis Februarii, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To all archbishops and their suffragans, abbots, priors, deans, archdeacons, provosts, archpriests, and other prelates of churches, whether exempt or not exempt, established throughout Germany. The care entrusted to us by the universal Church, the fullness of ecclesiastical power granted to us, continuously stirs our hearts with urgency, constantly excites us with the goads of thought, so that we may fulfill the duty of solicitude towards all Christ’s faithful, near and far, directing our attentive eyes upon each, extending the focus of consideration to each, as long as we live under the yoke of apostolic servitude imposed upon our shoulders, as befits the salvation of their souls. However, while we thus approach as debtors to all, while we consider ourselves set over the governance of all, we are rightly terrified by intense fear and shaken by great tremor not without reason, lest we fail to sufficiently fulfill the office of apostleship we have undertaken, lest we omit anything through negligence concerning the care of the Lord's flock entrusted to us, especially since we are powerless in ourselves to bear the weight of such a burden and cannot, due to the diversity of places, be present with our bodily presence at the same time to the sheep to whose custody we are appointed. Since the condition of human nature does not allow that while one is confined to one place, he can be captured in another at the same time, having a just excuse from this, we sometimes call upon prudent and discreet men, as it behooves us to be attentive to all churches and to be present personally to each at the same time, lest we neglect those absent, instructed by the example of Him who descended from the heights of heaven to the depths of the world for the salvation of the human race, sent his chosen disciples into the world to preach the gospel. Therefore, thinking with paternal diligence about your salvation, we have decided to entrust the full office of legation in your regions to our beloved son, the elected bishop of Ferrara, a man endowed with knowledge of letters, adorned with honesty of morals, circumspect in counsel, a zealot of the Catholic faith and indefatigable defender against the machinations of ecclesiastical liberty, acceptable to us and our brothers by the merit of his probity, granting him etc. as above: to expedite. Since we pursue this elected person with the prerogative of grace and favor, we earnestly admonish, exhort, and command your community that, receiving him kindly and treating him honorably as the legate of the apostolic see, indeed us in him, offering him counsel, aid, and favor, you devoutly and humbly attend to his healthful admonitions and commands. Otherwise, the sentence which he shall rightly pass upon the rebellious, etc., shall be observed. Given as above. In the same manner to all princes, counts, barons, castellans, and other nobles, rectors, bailiffs, and other Christ’s faithful established throughout Germany.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa universis archiepiscopis et prelatis ecclesiarum in Theotonia constitutis scribit se dilecto filio electo Ferrariensi legationis officium commisisse, hortaturque eos ut eum tanquam legatum sedis apostolicae honorifice recipiant et eius monitis obediant. Datum Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

The Pope (presumably Gregory IX based on the context) addresses the faithful Montanario, canon of Esino, Manetti Baligano and Guidoni brothers, sons of the late Uguicione, Symonetto, Bartholomeo, Captio Cavalco, Fantibono Gifredi, Bonifatio Transmundi, Raynaldo Mainardi, Marino, Symonib Cerlongi, Iacomello the notary, Lombardello and Laurentio de Ripise, citizens of Esino, and Phylippo de Longan from Racanate. 

The letter expresses that the Church, like a caring mother, strives to assist all those who are oppressed by cruel injustice, especially those who suffer heavy losses for the Church's sake, so that the cause of their ruin might become the source of their salvation. A petition presented to the Pope on their behalf explains that they have suffered grave damages and losses for the faith and freedom of the Roman Church from both the envoys of the late Emperor Frederick and their fellow citizens, as well as other enemies of God and the Church, such as Montefeltrano de Bissazon, Palmerio Palmerii, Accurrinbonae Gisserii, Guillielmo Gottiboldi and his brothers, the Count of San Pietro, Iacobo de Marto, Octaviano Philippi, Dominico Buccanigra, Acto de Massacio, Boninsigna de Presbytero, Todino Iacobelli, Barnaba the notary, Arimino Recuperi, Accurribona Palmerii, Matheo Scotti, Alberto Fantolini, Matheo the brother of Judge Paul, Adammo Fuite, Compagnono, Blasio dompni Azonis de Ruvellian, Corrado son of Francucius, from the city and diocese of Esino, and Philip of Lady Aigane from the Senogallia diocese. They humbly requested that the Apostolic See ensure their indemnity for these matters.

In view of this, to ensure that the faithful of the Church receive proper relief due to their steadfast loyalty and that the traitors learn the penalty of their malice as they gratuitously hate and harm the Church's children, the Pope, heeding their supplications, wants the goods of the aforementioned enemies to be pledged to them as full compensation for the damages they suffered for the Church, by the authority of this present letter, stating that they should be fully compensated for such damages, notwithstanding any contrary edict or statute. Therefore, none may infringe upon this concession and constitution of ours. If anyone does, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 6th of the Nones of July, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Montanario canonico Esino et aliis fidelibus nuntiat, se eorum petitioni inclinatum bona proditorum ad integrum dampnorum recompensationem obligare, quae propter ecclesiam passi sunt, mandans ut illi dampna resarcire teneantur. Datum Lugduni, VI Non. Iuli, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

Potthast, Reg. 12479; Berger 3001. To the Archbishops of Split, Zadar, and Dubrovnik and their suffragans. As we cannot be physically present in each place, etc., as above in letter 53 up to: preaching the gospel. Therefore, considering your salvation with paternal diligence, we are sending our beloved son, Cardinal O. of St. Mary in Via Lata, a man endowed with knowledge and adorned with moral integrity and prudent in counsel, to your regions, etc., as in the same letter up to; to be observed inviolably. Given at Lyon, on the 15th day before the Kalends of May, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa archiepiscopis Spaletensibus, Iadrensibus et Ragusinis eorumque suffraganeis mandat, ut evangelium praedicari curet per dilectum filium cardinalem O., et inviolabiliter observent. 1251, April. 17, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Strasbourg. By the providence of the Roman pontiff, with the power of binding and loosing granted by the Lord, the grace of dispensation is especially extended in certain cases when evident advantage or necessity persuades. Since, as you have taken care to explain to us, our beloved son, the noble Radulf of Usemberc, in order to settle grave discord and great enmities that have long been agitated between himself on one side and our beloved son, the noble Louis, advocate of Litemberc, and the late Henry, his brother, of the Strasbourg diocese on the other, desires to take as his wife our beloved daughter in Christ, the noblewoman Helica, daughter of the aforementioned Henry, and has contracted a betrothal with her, yet the marriage cannot be consummated because they are related to each other in the fourth degree of consanguinity and affinity, and cannot withdraw from it without grave and great danger to many, you have humbly petitioned us to, in order to avert these dangers, grant them the permission to consummate the marriage so contracted and to remain in it, from the customary mercy of the Apostolic See. We, therefore, considering that unless the aforementioned marriage is consummated, grave dangers might arise, and that these nobles, as you assert, have shown themselves ready to handle church matters and to assist vigorously and powerfully our beloved son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, for which they have deserved the favor and grace of the Apostolic See, inclined by your prayers, grant you the authority, if you see fit, to dispense Radulf and Helica so that they may consummate this marriage and licitly remain in it, notwithstanding the aforementioned impediment, provided the aforementioned nobles persist in their devotion to the Church. Given at Lyon, the Nones of January, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Argentinensi mandat ut dispenset cum Radulfo de Usemberci et Helica, nata Henrici de Litemberc, ut, impedimento quarto consanguinitatis et affinitatis gradu non obstante, matrimonium contrahant et in eo maneant. Datum Lugduni, Nonis Januarii, anno IV.

**Translation to English:**

To the archbishops and bishops, abbots, priors, and other prelates of churches established throughout Germany. With the scales of right consideration balanced, the merits of subjects are weighed with just estimation, so that worthy recompense answers the devotions of the faithful, and the perpetual penalty of disgrace oppresses the necks of the unfaithful. Thus, many are raised to the merits of virtue by the benefits granted to the good, and the boldness to sin is prevented among others by the penalties of the wicked. Therefore, as we have learned that several clerics and laypeople holding fiefs and ecclesiastical benefices from you and your churches have adhered and still presume to adhere to Frederick, the former Emperor of the Romans, and Conrad, his son, manifest persecutors of the Church, we wish and by the authority of these presents strictly command you to remove the said fiefs and benefices from them and to bestow them upon other faithful and devoted to the Church, with the advice and consent of our beloved son P., Cardinal Deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the Apostolic See. Those who oppose, etc. Otherwise, we have instructed the same legate by our letters to carry out this apostolic mandate. Given at Lyon, on the 17th day before the Kalends of April, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa archiepiscopis, episcopis, abbatibus, prioribus aliisque ecclesiarum prelatis per Alamaniam constitutis mandat, ut clericis et laicis Friderico quondam imperatori et Conrado eius filio adhærentibus feuda et beneficia auferant, eaque aliis fidelibus conferant, sub consilio P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum cardinalis legati. 1246, Martii 16, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

...to the abbots of the Cistercian and of the Saint Benedict orders, and to the provost of the church of Weirenhusen of the dioceses of Augsburg and Constance.
