The more we love and intend to honor those who have been called to share in our responsibilities with sincere affection, the more we are troubled by great sorrow when reports of their deeds are brought to us that offend God and scandalize men. Indeed, among other matters that have been conveyed to us about the nefarious actions of the elected Bishop of Brixen, it has been reported that he has, for over six years, shamelessly disregarded the sentences of suspension and excommunication pronounced against him by Master Albert, the archdeacon of Passau, with apostolic authority, out of necessity of justice, contemptuously defying the keys of the church, and without obtaining confirmation of his election, impudently interfering in the spiritual and temporal administration of the church of Brixen. He has granted the county and district, indeed, the whole duchy of the same church with its castles and officials to the late Emperor Frederick and his supporters, to the great detriment of the aforementioned church and significant prejudice and burden to the princes of Germany, because of which the passage from Germany to Italy is closed to these princes, as well as to pilgrims and other faithful of Christ. Furthermore, he has so squandered and consumed the goods of the same church, which once used to flourish with the abundance of its spiritual and temporal wealth, that it is to be feared that unless quick remedy is applied, it will incur irreparable harm. Since we cannot and should not overlook these matters with God and our honor, we, wishing to proceed on this from our office, mandate that you diligently investigate the truth concerning the aforementioned matters and regarding the report that he offered counsel, assistance, and favor to the said Frederick after he was bound with the sentence of excommunication, and also about his life and merits, and faithfully write down your findings and transmit them to us under your seals as soon as possible through a trustworthy messenger, setting a competent peremptory term for the said elected bishop to present himself personally before us to receive according to his merits, forbidding in the meantime the alienation of the goods of the church of Brixen to the aforementioned elected bishop, since he is suspected of squandering them. However, if the often-mentioned elected bishop, prudently consulting for the safety of his soul and honor, wishes to prevent the conflagration of the investigation by resignation, you, having received his resignation by our authority, should provide for the aforementioned church with such a person through whom the loss of past time may be compensated and future advantage conferred, and who may be clearly faithful and devoted to us and the Roman Church, invoking, if necessary, the assistance of secular arm; contradictors, etc. If not all of you, etc., any two of you, etc. Given at Lyons, on the 4th of June, in the third year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbatibus Cisterciensis et Sancti Benedicti ordinum et preposito Weirenhusen ecclesiae Augustensis et Constantiensis diocesum mandat inquirere de actibus Brixinensis electi, qui sententias suspensionis et excommunicationis vilipenderit et bona ecclesiae dilapidaverit, et eum citare ad se personaliter representandum; alienationem bonorum interim prohibet. 1236, Iun. 4, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the treasurer of Saint Thomas of Strasbourg. As we have learned, our beloved son Henry of Geroldseck, a canon of the church of Speyer, does not dare to reside safely in the city of Speyer because he openly opposed the supporters of the late Emperor Frederick. We command you that if this is so, you should ensure that the income from his prebend of that church is provided to Henry in full for up to three years, wherever he may be, notwithstanding any contrary custom or statute: those who oppose this, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 12th day before the Kalends of May, in the fourth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa [Innocentius IV] mandatum thesaurario Sancti Thomae Argentinensis, ut Henrico de Geroldiseck, canonico ecclesiae Spirensis, qui urbem Spirensem propter oppositionem fautoribus quondam imperatoris Friderici securo morari non audet, proventus prebendae suae usque ad triennium ministrari faciat. Datum Lugduni, XII Kal. Maii, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the dean and chapter of St. John's in Osnabrück.

It is fitting and in accordance with equity that those who find the benevolence of the Apostolic See favorable in provision rejoice, and he who is deemed worthy of favor by laudable reputation should be glad to receive the grace he intends through our support. Therefore, for our beloved son Segucard, a priest of the diocese of Osnabrück, commendable to us for his life and manners, and in whom we wish to honor the persons of our venerable brother, the bishop of Osnabrück, as well as the noble man L., count of Ravensberg, and our beloved daughter in Christ, the noble lady, countess of Wloton, niece of our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, we earnestly request and urge all of you, commanding that you admit him, who is said not to have obtained any ecclesiastical benefice, as a brother and canon for the reverence of us and the Apostolic See, and provide him liberally with a prebend as soon as the opportunity arises—notwithstanding any oath or firm agreement concerning a certain number of canons, or if we have sent any letters to you regarding others, which we do not wish to be prejudiced by the authority of these presents, or any indulgence for which special mention must be made in our letters. Thus, you should fulfill our request and mandate in such a way that, by him rejoicing in obtaining what he desires in this matter, the sincerity of your devotion may be worthy of the increase of our favor. Otherwise, we give instructions by our letters to our beloved sons, the schoolmaster, the treasurer, and Bertram, canon of St. Ansgar in Bremen, to carry out the apostolic mandate in this matter; to oppose etc. Given at Lyons, February 22, in the fourth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa decano et capitulo Sancti Iohannis Osnaburgensis mandat, ut Segucardum, presbyterum diocesis Osnaburgensis, in fratrem et canonicum admittant et ei provideant de prebenda. 1230, Feb. 22, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the senator and people of Rome. The horrendous prideful betrayal of Frederick has ascended to such an extent against the gentle and humble-hearted Son of God, the Lord Jesus Christ, that it has repelled him from the dignity of the empire and provoked the hearts of those who fear God to his ruin. As is clearly acknowledged by us and you through the rejoicing, many of the noblest and most powerful of the kingdom of Sicily, fleeing his deceptions and snares, oppose him with all the strength of their soul. Since, through this clear miracle of God, the honor and dignity of the Apostolic See, your mother, is raised, it consequently acquires glory and increased utility for you, its special sons: we beseech and entreat you in the Lord Jesus Christ, imposing upon you for the remission of your sins, that, presenting to the eyes of your minds how and by what means this traitor has long disturbed the Church of God and you, his most beloved, with injuries and harm, you might rise against him with all the affection of your heart, so that through the victorious supports of your strength, the enemy of faith may fall, the afflicted Church may breathe with you, tranquility may come to the Christian people, and the kingdom of Sicily, oppressed by the yoke of misery, may hasten to attain the joy of redemption. Let there be for us, as we desire, a swift possibility, that we who have been forced to leave our seat by the savagery of such a dreadful tyrant, may happily return to it, led by the angel of salvation. To ensure that the compassion of this desire may more easily be fulfilled with God's favor, we have decided to entrust the full office of legation to our beloved sons, S. of the title of Santa Maria in Trastevere as presbyter and R. of Santa Maria in Cosmedin as deacon cardinals, as noble and distinguished members of the Church, conspicuous in wisdom and renowned for a diversity of virtues. May your devotion diligently attend to them in all things as to us, so that over time we may be bound to you for special graces; knowing that, for the promotion of so great a matter as magnificently as befits, we are presently sending the appropriate assistance we deemed necessary. Moreover, support those nobles of the kingdom who have sought your protection with the fullness of honor and goodwill, so that rejoicing at having found refuge with you, affection may arise in others of the kingdom to refuse to submit to the damned man and to resist his raging wickedness according to the quality of their strength. In the same manner, to the powers, rulers, councils, and peoples of the cities, castles, and places established throughout Campania and Marittima. To the gentle, etc., up to: sons to secure evident utility: to all, etc., up to: traitor has disturbed the Church of God with injuries, etc., up to: special. In the same manner, to the powers, rulers, councils, and peoples of the cities, castles, and places established throughout the patrimony of the blessed Peter in Tuscany with a spirit of sound counsel! In the same manner, to the powers, rulers, councils, and peoples of the cities, castles, and places established throughout the Duchy of Spoleto with a spirit of sound counsel. In the same manner, to the powers, rulers, councils, and peoples of the cities, castles, and places established throughout the March of Ancona with a spirit of sound counsel.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa senatori et populo Romano mandat ut contra Fridericum, qui superbia et perfidia sua ecclesiam Dei perturbavit, consurgant, ad promovendum honorem et utilitatem sedis apostolicae ac regni Sicilie liberationem. 1241, Datum Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the dean and chapter of Verden. It is fitting for us to have a fatherly devotion in the appointments of clerics, so that they may rightly rejoice in having found the gifts of grace in us, and progress with the increase of virtues, and become strong in the praise of God. Hence, for our beloved son Alvericus of Bederekesa, a cleric, who is known to be aided by the merits of a praiseworthy conversation and life, so that he may obtain special grace from us, we earnestly ask and exhort your community, commanding that you admit him, in whom we wish to honor the person of our dear son, the noble man, the Duke of Saxony, devoted to us and the Roman Church, into your brotherhood and canonry, and provide him liberally with a prebend as soon as the opportunity arises—despite any fixed number of canons secured by oath or any other firmness, or if we have sent you our letters on behalf of others, which we do not wish to be prejudiced by the authority of these presents, or any indulgence that needs special mention in our letters. You shall so fulfill our command that from this your sincerity may merit an increase of favor with us. Otherwise, we instruct our beloved sons, the dean and the treasurer of Osnabrück, by our letters, to execute the apostolic mandate in this matter; against any contradictors. Given at Lyon, on the Ides of March, in the fourth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa decano et capitulo Verdensibus mandat, ut Alvericum de Bederekesa clericum, intuitu ducis Saxonie, in fratrem et canonicum admittant et prebenda provideant. 1247, Mart. 15. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To P., cardinal deacon of San Giorgio in Velabro, legate of the Apostolic See. So that we may not seem to take upon ourselves the fault of the Bishop of Augsburg, which is well-known enough, if we leave it uncorrected, we command that you have certain discreet individuals diligently investigate his heinous acts, and proceed with his perpetual suspension by our authority, if the gravity of his offenses demands it, writing back to us about what you have done regarding this matter. Given at Lyon, the 6th of May, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali, legato sedis apostolicae mandat, ut de nefariis episcopi Augustensis actibus inquiri faciat et, si merita exigant, ad eius perpetuam suspensionem procedat. 1247, Mai. 6, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Gerard, a layman, the son of Gerard, known as a knight of Brabant, a messenger of the noble man, Duke of Brabant. The Apostolic See, which by the Lord’s arrangement is the mother and teacher of all, wisely considering that the fault of the parents should not be imputed to the children, lest contrary to the edict of divine law, the sons bear the iniquity of the father and the teeth of the sons be set on edge when the fathers eat sour grapes, as stated in Jeremiah 31:29, has sometimes, after inspecting various causes, dispensed with certain illegitimately born individuals, allowing them to be admitted to spiritual acts. Since greater fitness is required for spiritual matters than for secular ones, there is no doubt that the same authority can legitimize such individuals for secular acts, especially those who, during the vacancy of the Roman Empire, have no other authority among men holding such power except the Roman Pontiff. Indeed, considering more closely the devotion of your father, who asserts he has no legitimate offspring, and inclined by his devoted supplications, we grant you, whom your father, being unmarried, is said to have begotten from an unmarried woman, that — notwithstanding this defect — you may be called to successions and admitted to legitimate acts, by the authority of these presents. To no one etc. Given at Lyon, on the 11th of April, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Gerardo, laico, filio Gerardi militis Brabantiæ, dispensat ut defectu natalium non obstante ad successiones et actus legitimos admittatur. 1231, Apr. 11, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Master Jacob, canon of the church of St. Paul in Trier. We believe it is worthy to act, if we sometimes extend the affection, which we particularly have towards the devoted sons of the church among others, to their familiar ones, by offering them the hand of beneficence, so that those who attend to our and the Roman Church's services, may merit the grace of the Apostolic See not only for themselves but also for others. Therefore, the noble count T.'s request, devoted to the Apostolic See, inclines us to command that you cause the beloved son, Andrew, rector of the church of Triconville, his cleric, of whom commendable testimony is borne to us, to be received as canon and as a brother in some church of the province of Trier by our authority, and to provide him with a prebend as soon as the opportunity arises — notwithstanding if in the church, where you deem him to be provided, a certain number of canons is established, fortified by oath or any other firmness, or if it is burdened by our mandate for only two, or if the same church has been granted an indulgence by the See that it is not obliged at all to provision or reception of anyone, or that its canons cannot be excommunicated or interdicted by apostolic letters unless they make express mention of such indulgence, or that the same cleric holds another benefice elsewhere —: resistors etc. Given at Lyon, on the 8th day before the Ides of March, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Magistro Jacobo canonico ecclesiae Sancti Paulini Treverensis mandat, ut Andream, rectorem ecclesiae de Triconvile, in canonum fratremque in aliqua ecclesiarum provinciae Treverensis recipiat et de prebenda provideat, non obstantibus certis statutis et indultis. Datum Lugduni, VIII Idus Martii, anno quarto (1230).

**Translation to English:**

To the illustrious King of France. Your ancestors are known to have been fervent in their devotion to the Church, so much so that, among the world's princes, they were distinguished defenders of the Church, striving not only to preserve its freedom but also to greatly enhance it. Therefore, as you, by bloodline succession and in imitation of their devotion, fervently seek to honor the aforementioned Church and prove your commitment through your deeds, we extol your exalted status with due praises in the Lord, and we offer you our deepest gratitude. Indeed, our venerable brother, the Bishop of Senlis, and our beloved son, G., the custodian of Bayeux, your envoys, whom you recently sent to our presence, have taken care, among other things, to propose to us on your behalf that you desire peace to be reestablished between the Church and the late Emperor Frederick. You are ready, out of zeal for God and reverence for the Church, to earnestly mediate for this cause, which obliges us to hold you in high regard. However, we want you to know that we and our brothers worked tirelessly with all our ingenuity and diligence—from the time we were appointed to the governance of the universal Church until the time of the Council of Lyons—to achieve this peace, albeit in vain. Hence, based on previous efforts, we do not hope to succeed in negotiations. But because the Church does not customarily close its arms to the returning, we, following the example of Him whose unworthy vicars we are constituted, who does not wish the death of a sinner but rather that he turns back and lives, earnestly desire the salvation of the aforementioned Frederick and wish to receive him if, perhaps divinely inspired, he wants to return to Church unity. Due to the particular affection of grace we have towards your person and our hope that you would not allow the Holy Church, your mother, to be deceived in any way, we will act as gently and kindly as we can with God and the honor of the Church, without sin, in dealing with him. Concerning the matter of aid for the Holy Land, your envoys will convey our response to you in person. Given at Lyons, November 5, in the fourth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa regi Francie illustri significat desiderium suum recipiendi Fredericum, si redire velit ad unitatem ecclesiasticam, et commendat zelum regis in pace reformanda inter ecclesiam et Fredericum. Responsionem super subsidio Terre Sancte nuntii regis referent viva voce. Datum Lugduni, Non. Novembr. anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To Master James, Canon of the Church of St. Paulinus in Trier. So that virtue may be profitable not only to its possessor but also to others, we sometimes grant grace to some through the intervention of the virtuous, which they might perhaps not obtain by themselves. Hence, we, moved by the prayers of our devoted son, the noble man, the Count of Luxembourg, command that you provide or have provided to our beloved son Peter, his familiar, the rector of the church of Nanthort in the Diocese of Toul, in the province of Trier, with an ecclesiastical benefice that is due to him, as soon as the opportunity presents itself, by our authority — notwithstanding if in that church the number of canons is established by oath, confirmation of the Apostolic See, or any other firmness, or if we have directed our writings to others in it, which we do not wish to generate any prejudice, or if it has been granted by the aforesaid See to that church that it is in no way bound to provide or accept anyone through apostolic letters unless they make express mention of such indulgence; objectors etc. Dated at Lyon, 13th of April, in the fourth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Magistro Iacobo canonico ecclesiae Sancti Paulini Treverensis mandat, ut provideat Petro, rectori ecclesiae de Nanthort Tullensis diocesis, de beneficio ecclesiastico, non obstantibus quibusdam statutis, auctoritate apostolica. Datum Lugduni, Idus Aprilis, anno quarto [1246].

**Translation to English:**

To the procurator of the Church of Asti. The foolish heart of many in the cities and dioceses of Alba, Asti, and Turin has become so darkened that, having cast aside the fear of the divine name, they almost willingly perish under another Pharaoh's dominion, persecuting at his command not only the freedom of the church but also oppressing its sons, striving to please the Lord of virtues through works of sincere devotion. Therefore, desiring to exercise the power granted to us from above against the excesses of such reprobates in a manner that they may perceive it to be to their disgrace, because they do not fear to damnably persecute the Church of God, we grant by the authority of these presents to all in the said cities and dioceses who remain in the devotion of the same church the faculty to lawfully retain in perpetuity for their own use as their own goods all that they have taken from the goods of their persecutors, so that they cannot be convened concerning these matters by apostolic letters unless they have made full mention of this concession. No one, therefore, may infringe upon our concession, etc. Given at Lyon, 27 March, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa procuratori ecclesiae Astensis auctoritate presentium concedit facultatem omnibus in civitatibus et diocesibus Albensi, Astensi, et Taurinensi ecclesiae devotis, ut bona persecutorum ecclesiae in usus proprios perpetuo retinere possint. Datum Lugduni, VI Kalendas Aprilis, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

Innocent IV to the bishop and citizens of Strasbourg. So that, in the business of the Church, which you have undertaken with spirit and for which we give you our thanks, you may remain steadfast without any hesitation, inclined by your devotion, we want you to know for certain and hold that if it happens that peace is re-established at any time between the Church and Frederick, the former emperor, which will never be while he remains emperor or king, you will place the Church in the same peace. Given at Lyon, 5th day before the Kalends of February, in the fourth year of our pontificate. Innocent IV, the Pope, grants Henry IV the bishop of Strasbourg the faculty to absolve the citizens of Strasbourg, who proceeded against the supporters of Frederick, the former emperor, during the truce. Inn. IV Reg. Vol. I, 359; Lib. IV, 378. We compared the Pertsius copy with Schoepflin, Alsat. dipl. 1247, Jan. 28. Vol. I, p. 395, n. 523, which was transcribed from the city library of Strasbourg, 14th century. (S.). Potthast, Reg. 12403; Berger 2374. To the bishop of Strasbourg. Since, as we have received from your report, your citizens, during the truces established and confirmed by oath between them on one side and certain supporters of Frederick, the former emperor, on the other, did not observe these truces, but proceeded gravely against them, for which they fear they have incurred the guilt of perjury, we, inclined by your devotion, grant you full faculty by the authority of these presents to absolve them from these acts. Given at Lyon, 5th day before the Kalends of February, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Henrico IIII episcopo Argentinensi mandat facultatem absolvendi cives Argentinenses, qui durantibus treugis contra fautores Friderici quondam imperatoris graviter processerunt, concedit. Datum Lugduni, V Kalendas Februarias, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Strasbourg: Since, as we have learned, the Bishop of Chur received a certain sum of money from the late Emperor Frederick to be spent against the Church and has been suspended and bound by the chain of excommunication due to his disobedience by our beloved son, the elected bishop of Ferrara, then a legate of the apostolic see: We command you by the authority of these presents to set a fixed and peremptory term for him, within which he must present himself before our presence, also informing him that if he perhaps scorns to come into our presence, we will proceed to a sentence of deposition against him. Given at Lyon, on the 18th of April, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Argentinensi mandat, ut episcopo Curiensi, qui pecuniam a Friderico quondam imperatore contra ecclesiam accepit et excommunicatus est, terminum prefigat peremptorium ad presentiam papalem se conferendi, sub poena depositionis. Datum Lugduni, XIIII Kal. Maii, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

The Most Illustrious and Noble A. Man. Berger 2572. To the bishops of Ploaghe and Empúries. As we, like a devout father, desire to bring back to the fold the wandering sons, we authorize you by these presents to absolve all Sardinians, who, having left the company of the persecutor of the church, turn to the right hand ready to obey the command of the church, from the bond of excommunication, to which they are bound due to the favor shown to the aforesaid persecutor, according to the form of the church. Each of you may freely do this by himself, whenever both of you are unwilling or unable to be present. Given at Lyon, on the second day before the Kalends of May, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopis Ploacensi et Empuriensi mandat, ut omnes Sardos, qui relicto persecutore ecclesiae ad ecclesiae mandatum paratos se convertunt, ab excommunicationis vinculo absolvatis. 1231, Apr. 30, Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To the abbot of Pomposa, in the diocese of Comacchio. If mercy should be extended to all those in need, so that the merciful may obtain mercy in the reward of the just, greater care and more abundant assistance should be given to those whose nobility is revealed by their modesty, and who have fallen into poverty or exile without fault of their own. Since our beloved son, the noble Bernabeus of the cities of Palude Regina and Parma, of which he is a citizen, has been expelled and stripped of all his possessions by the late Emperor Frederick and his envoys, we command that provision be made for him in the amount of twenty-five imperial pounds annually from some churches in the diocese of Bologna, which are not already burdened by a similar provision at our command, until he can return to his possessions and recover them—notwithstanding any indulgence of the apostolic see, by which such provision might be hindered—and those who resist, etc. Given at Lyon, on the Ides of April, in the fourth year.

Regesto in Latin:

Innocentius IV papa abbati de Pomposa mandat ut Bernabeo de Palude Regina et Parmensi civitatibus, expulsus et bonis spoliatus a Friderico imperatore, provisio fiat in viginti quinque libris imperialium annuatim ab ecclesiis Bononiensis diocesis, quae non sunt simili provisione gravate. 1247, Apr. 13. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Trier. Although the injuries from any prelates are grievous to us, we are more strongly urged by the grievances of our venerable brothers, the Archbishops of Mainz and Cologne, because we embrace them with the arms of more sincere affection. Therefore, as these archbishops have taken care to explain to us, you burden and harass their people by extorting tolls and customs duties from them with undue exactions. Wishing to prevent the losses both to you and to them in this matter, and to avert grievances so that no cause of dispute may arise between you and them, we have deemed it necessary to earnestly ask and admonish your fraternity to prudently consider how disgraceful it is to add affliction to the already afflicted people on the occasion of the impending discord. Cease completely from vexing these people henceforth, and do not delay in restoring what you have taken from them. You should heed our requests in such a way that, commending your devotion for this reason, we are not forced to provide otherwise, because we can in no way fail those archbishops in their rights, as indeed we ought not to do. Given at Lyons, on the second day before the Kalends of February, in the fourth year.

To the Archbishop of Mainz. Although the injuries, etc., as in the previous letter until "we embrace them." Therefore, as you have taken care to explain to us, our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Trier, extorts tolls and customs duties from your people, etc., until "as indeed we ought not to do," with the words competently changed. Therefore, we wish to make you certain by the tenor of these presents, that if the said archbishop does not care to obey our mandates, we will compel him to do so by the appropriate severity. Given as in the previous letter. In the same way to the Archbishop of Cologne, as to Mainz.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Treverensi mandat ut ab iniustis exactionibus hominum archiepiscoporum Maguntini et Coloniensis desistat et ablata restituat; aliter, eum ad oboedientiam compellet. 1244, Ian. 31, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Patriarchs of Aquileia and Grado, the Archbishops of Milan, Ravenna, and Genoa, and their suffragans, abbots, priors, etc., both exempt and non-exempt, prelates of the churches. Desiring with all our hearts the good and prosperous state of your regions, the exaltation of the Church, and the honor of the Roman Empire, we send our beloved son, Cardinal O. of Santa Maria in Via Lata, a man endowed with knowledge, adorned with honesty, and prudent in counsel, to those regions, etc., as above in the letter written concerning the legation of P. of St. George at the Golden Veil, and so forth: to be observed inviolably. Given at Lyon, on the Ides of April, in the fourth year. In the same manner, to the marquises, counts, barons, and other nobles established throughout Lombardy and Romagna.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa patriarchis Aquilegensi, Gradensi, archiepiscopis Mediolanensi, Ravennati, Ianuensi, eorumque suffraganeis, abbatibus, prioribus ecclesiarum praelatis mandat ut dilectum filium O. Sanctae Mariae in Via Lata cardinalem ad exaltationem ecclesiae et imperii Romani honorem suscipiant. Datum Lugduni, Idibus Aprilis, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the archbishops, bishops, abbots, priors, deans, and other prelates of the churches established throughout Lombardy and Romagna. The only begotten Son of God descended from the heights of the heavens to the depths of the world to free man from the snare of servitude, etc., as mentioned above in the letter sent to all the dukes, marquises, and other princes and nobles established throughout Germany, until: they felt refreshed, behold, we have chosen to send our beloved son, O., deacon cardinal of Santa Maria in Via Lata, a man truly endowed with knowledge, adorned with moral integrity, and distinguished by maturity of counsel, to these regions as an angel of peace by the counsel of our brothers, with the full office of legate entrusted to him, so that he may uproot and destroy, scatter and disperse, build and plant, as he sees fit to do. Therefore, etc., as in the same until: to be observed inviolably. Given at Lyon, the Ides of April, in the fourth year. In the same manner to the marquises, counts, barons, and other nobles established throughout Lombardy and Romagna.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa archiepiscopis et episcopis, abbatibus, prioribus, decanis et aliis ecclesiarum prelatis per Lombardiam et Romaniolam mandat dilectum filium suum O., diaconum cardinalem Sanctae Mariae in Via Lata, virum scientia praeditum, ad partes illas legationis officio pleno destinandum ut pacem restituat. 1247, Apr. 13. Datum Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the illustrious King Henry of Cyprus. We gladly respond to the plea of the mother church, under whose protection you seek peace, as you, whose mind was once influenced by the contagion of the late Emperor Frederick, now humbly return like a devoted son. We more willingly, with paternal affection, endeavor to ensure that you may enjoy tranquility in both spiritual and temporal matters. Indeed, a petition read on your behalf before us stated that you once swore an oath of fealty and homage to the same Frederick. Therefore, implanting the fear and love of the Lord in your heart and desiring to separate yourself from all his participation, you have humbly fled to the Apostolic See, to which you desire to be subject alone. You earnestly ask us to consider absolving you from such an oath and to receive your kingdom under its protection. Since Frederick, who became a persecutor of the church from being its patron and, degenerating from a son to a stepson, strives with all his might to enslave the mother church, which nourished him from the cradle and exalted him above all the princes of the world, and who, bearing the name of Christ in vain, attacks the Catholic faith, was deposed by us in the sacred council of Lyon, with the deliberate counsel of all the prelates present there, from the empire, kingdoms, and all other dignities, with all those bound to him by an oath of fealty or any other title being generally absolved: we, moved by the prayers of your devotion, embrace you with the arms of sincerity as a most dear son. We have decided to absolve you especially from any oath by which you were bound to Frederick and receive you and the kingdom of Cyprus, which you hold, under the protection of the Apostolic See and our own. Henceforth, we decree, by the authority of these presents, that you are subject only to us, especially since, as you assert, your predecessors were subject to no secular power by reason of the aforesaid kingdom. Let no one therefore infringe upon our absolution, protection, and constitution. Given at Lyon, on the 5th of March, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Henrico illustri regi Cipri mandat, ut ab iuramento fidelitatis Friderico quondam imperatori prestito absolvendus sit, et regnum Cipri sub protectione sedis apostolicae suscipitur. 1247, Mart. 5, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To P., cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, legate of the apostolic see. Since, as we have learned, the monastery of Saint Martin of Glandières in the diocese of Metz is subject to our venerable brother, the bishop of Metz, in spiritual and temporal matters, we, desiring that this monastery, which is said to be currently vacant, may thrive commendably in both, command you to, if this is the case, assign the administration of the said monastery to the same bishop, through whose diligence and capability it can receive the desired increases in both spiritual and temporal matters, if you see it as expedient, by our authority; contradictors, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 8th of May, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali mandat, ut si monasterium Sancti Martini Glandariene Metensis diocesis subiectum sit episcopo Metensi, administrationem eiusdem monasterii eidem episcopo committat. 1230, Mai. 10, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot and convent in Würzburg of the Order of Saint Benedict in the diocese of Speyer. Because we aim for the honor and increase of the Church, etc., as above, so that utility may be secured. Since our beloved son, the nobleman E. of Grendorf, as we have heard, has shown himself to be diligent and devoted in the affairs of the Church, we, wishing to reward him and his kin with grace and favor on account of this, ask and earnestly admonish your community, firmly mandating you to ensure that his son, the cleric H., is provided with an appropriate ecclesiastical benefice, which pertains to your grant and has been accustomed to be assigned to secular clerics, as soon as the opportunity offers itself — notwithstanding any writings we may have previously sent to you in regard to others, by which we do not want to generate any authority, nor any indulgence obtained from the Apostolic See, by which such grace might be delayed or even hindered. Otherwise, we give our venerable brother, the bishop of Strasbourg, the mandate by our letters, etc., to execute this; contradictors, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 18th of April, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa abbati et conventui in Woizeburc ordinis sancti Benedicti Spirensis diocesis mandat, ut H. clerico, nati E. de Grendorf, provideant in beneficio ecclesiastico competenti, cum facultas se obtulerit, non obstantibus litteris pro aliis directis. 1247, Apr. 18. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Arles and his suffragans, abbots, priors, deans, archdeacons, provosts, and other prelates of churches, whether exempt or non-exempt, established in the province of Arles. We, though unworthy, bear the role of Him on earth who renders to each according to their merits with due recompense, compensating both the worthy and unworthy according to the demands of their actions, thus imparting to each the rewards of their merits. Therefore, so that those who, due to the enormity of their sins, have deserved to be struck by the sword of malediction and marked by the Church, may teach others to avoid being involved in such malediction by avoiding their company, and thus, with them delivered according to the Apostle "for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved on the day of the Lord," these may be preserved immune from punishment: we command all of you to solemnly publish the sentences of excommunication against Frederick, the former emperor, his supporters, and other violators of the peace made by the legates of the Apostolic See, and also the interdict declared against the lands adhering to and favoring them, both from the same See and by others with its authority, in your cities, dioceses, and respective places on Sundays and feast days. You are to observe these decrees by our authority, setting aside any appeal, until proper satisfaction is rendered, and to ensure they are inviolably observed by your subjects, providing mutual counsel, aid, and support against the aforementioned. Given at Lyon, on the 13th day before the Kalends of January, in the sixth year of our pontificate. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Vienne and his suffragans, abbots, priors, deans, etc., established in the province of Vienne. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Aix and his suffragans, abbots, priors, etc., as above, in the province of Aix. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Narbonne and his suffragans, abbots, priors, deans, etc., as in another, in the province of Narbonne. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Embrun and his suffragans, abbots, priors, etc., as above, in the province of Embrun.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Arelatensi et suffraganeis eius, praecipit ut excommunicationes et interdicta contra Fridericum imperatorem et fautores suos publice promulgent et observent. 1230, Dec. 20, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

G. de Montelongo, subdeacon and our notary, legate of the apostolic see. It was intimated to us by our beloved sons, the dean and chapter of the churches of Feltre and Belluno, that, some time ago, the church being deprived of the comfort of a pastor, they, having called all who wished, should, and could conveniently attend, convened in chapter to discuss the substitution of a future bishop. Proceeding by way of scrutiny, they elected three trustworthy members from the said chapter; these diligently and secretly inquired individually for the votes of all and immediately published them in writing in common. After this consideration, the aforementioned dean and chapter unanimously consented to appoint our beloved son Tison, a canon of Ceneda, born of the noble man Biaquino de Camino, devoted to the apostolic see, a truly prudent and discreet man, circumspect in spiritual and temporal matters, by whose industry and foresight the same church, it is hoped, might receive growth. They petitioned for him as bishop; when they presented this petition to you, for you to admit it, you instructed our beloved sons, the elect of Ceneda and the abbot of San Vallis through your letters, that having inquired and known the truth concerning the aforesaid matters, if they found the petition to have been made concordantly, they should procure its admission. Having personally approached the said church and conducted a diligent inquiry on the aforementioned, they admitted the petition according to the form given to them. Wherefore, the said dean and chapter humbly petitioned us that since the aforementioned T. suffers from a defect of orders and age, we should deign, from the apostolic see's benevolence, to dispense with these and confirm what was done by the elected and the abbot in this matter, committing to T. the free administration of the aforementioned church, both in spiritual and temporal matters. Therefore, since you might be able to have fuller knowledge of this business and its circumstances, we entrust to your discretion, by the tenor of these presents, to provide for the administration of the same church to be committed to him by our authority, as you see fit; contradictors, etc. Given at Lyons, January 15, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa G. de Montelongo, subdiacono et notario suo, apostolicae sedis legato, mandat ut super administratione ecclesiae Feltrensis et Bellunensis dilecto filio Tisoni canonicum Cenetensem, electo consensu decani et capituli, auctoritate apostolica provideat, non obstante defectu ordinum et aetatis. 1246, Jan. 15, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Podestà and commune of Vercelli. The sincere affection of devotion, which we know you have towards us and the Roman Church, and the necessity of the present time justly lead us to grant you favor and grace. Therefore, being inclined by your devout supplications, we grant you by the authority of these presents that no delegate or subdelegate appointed by the apostolic see as executor or conservator can, through letters obtained from the same see, even if the matter has already been initiated through those letters or might be obtained in the future, pronounce sentences of excommunication upon you or interdict upon your city, without a special mandate from the same see making mention of such indulgence. Therefore, let no one, etc., of our concession, etc. If anyone, etc.; with these presents to last for three years, etc. Given at Lyons, on the Nones of May, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa potestati et communi Vercellensibus indulget, ut nullus delegatus vel subdelegatus a sede apostolica deputatus possit excommunicationis et interdicti sententias in eos sine mandato speciali promulgare. Datum Lugduni, Non. Maii, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Diatalmo de Graviata. Since we are sending our beloved son, O., the cardinal deacon of Santa Maria in Via Lata, as a legate of the Apostolic See for the pressing business of the church, we have deemed it necessary to inform your nobility through the tenor of these presents, that we have granted him full and free authority to promise on our behalf to you and all prelates of the churches, marquises, counts, barons, communities of cities and other places, and all others within his legation, that neither we nor our brethren will abandon you and them in this matter, nor will we in any way negotiate peace with the former Roman Emperor Frederick, such that he or any of his sons might exist as king or emperor. Given at Lyon, on the fourth day before the Nones of May, in the fourth year [of our pontificate]. In the same manner to the noble man Henry de Villa Alta.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa nobili viro Diatalmo de Graviata mandat, ut eum certiorem faciat quod cardinalem O. Sancte Marie in Via Lata legatum mittat cum plena potestate promittendi ex parte apostolica quod nec cum Friderico nec cum filiis eius pacem reformabit. 1246, Mai. 4, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To P., Cardinal Deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the Apostolic See. Even though the union of the marital bond, etc. Therefore, as it was proposed before us on behalf of the noble man Gotfrid, Count of Calw, of the diocese of Speyer, the same count has taken as his wife the noble woman Berta, who is related to him in the fourth degree of consanguinity, and has begotten several children with her. We command that, notwithstanding the aforementioned impediment, you use our authority to dispense them to lawfully remain in this marriage, if you see that it is expedient for the business of the Church. Given at Lyon, on the 8th Ides of May, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa P. sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum cardinali, apostolicae sedis legato mandat, ut Gotfrido comiti de Calwe et Berte eius uxori, quarta consanguinitatis linea contingenti, dispensationem concedat ut in matrimonio remanere possint, si ecclesiae negotio expediat. 1247, Mai. 8, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Constance. Since several clerics have obtained grace from the Apostolic See in regard to personates, dignities, prelatures, prebends, canonries, and other ecclesiastical benefices, we command you that, if you find them or those through whose intercession they have obtained this grace to adhere to the late Emperor Frederick or his son, you should, by our authority, deprive those clerics, as ingrates, of all the aforementioned benefices and confer them upon those devoted to the Church whose relatives and friends are willing and able to assist in the business currently at hand; those who oppose, etc. Given at Lyons, on the third Ides of May, in the fourth year.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Constantiensi mandat, ut clericos, qui F. quondam imperatori vel eius nato adhaerent, ab omnibus beneficiis ecclesiasticis privet. 1240, Mai. 13. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the prioress and convent of the monastery of Hecgebolxhen, diocese of Strasbourg. The kindness of the Apostolic See must pursue with more earnest love the prudent virgins who prepare to meet the bridegroom with their lamps lit, in proportion to the greater need they are known to have for support due to the weakness of their sex. Therefore, as has been stated on your behalf before us, you, enclosed in body within the confines of your cloister, yet freely serving the Lord with a devoted mind, have laudably chosen to observe those constitutions of the Order of Preachers that are applicable to you, and wish to be entrusted to the master and prior of the Teutonic province of the same order. We, commending your pious intention in the Lord, are moved by your prayers and the consideration of the noble man, the count of Montfort, our devoted follower, who has interceded for you before us, to commit you and your monastery by the authority of these presents to the aforementioned master and prior. By the same authority, we likewise decree that you shall henceforth remain under the guidance and teaching of the master and provincial prior of the Teutonic province, who shall be in office at the time, enjoying the privileges that have been granted or will be granted in the future by the Apostolic See to the said order. The master and prior themselves — notwithstanding any contrary custom of the order or indulgence obtained or to be obtained from the Apostolic See — shall take care for the well-being of your souls and provide you with such constitutions of the order that are applicable to you without any difficulty. They shall provide, either personally or through other suitable brothers of their order, the office of visitation to the monastery as often as needed, correcting and reforming in both head and members whatever they know needs correction or reformation. They shall also institute, depose, change, and organize as is customary in other monasteries of nuns of the same order. They shall hear your confessions and administer the ecclesiastical sacraments to you. However, the election of the prioress shall freely belong to the convent. And lest the lack of a priest should present a danger due to the brothers of the order not being required to reside continuously in your monastery, the aforementioned master and prior shall appoint some discreet and prudent chaplains for you to hear confessions in cases of necessity and administer the aforesaid sacraments. Furthermore, you are permitted to receive and freely retain revenues and possessions, notwithstanding any contrary custom or statute of the same order confirmed by the Apostolic See or established by any other firm authority. Let no one, therefore, etc., dare to infringe upon our commission and constitution, etc. If anyone, etc. Given at Lyon, the 12th of the Kalends of May, in the third year [of our pontificate]. In the same manner throughout for the prioress and convent of the monastery of Merinbrunne, diocese of Strasbourg.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa priorisse et conventui monasterii de Hecgebolxhen Argentinensis diocesis mandat ut sub magisterio et doctrina magistri et prioris provincialis Theutonie ordinis Predicatorum maneant, gaudentes privilegiis concessis, cum libertate electionis priorisse et facultate recipiendi retinendique redditus. Dat. Lugduni, XII Kal. Maii, anno tertio.

**Translation to English:**

To P. St. George at the Golden Veil, deacon cardinal, legate of the apostolic see, and to the archbishop of Mainz. Since the beloved son, the elected bishop of Speyer, who is devoted to the service of the apostolic see, does not possess the means to sustain himself honorably due to his goods being seized by the enemies of the Church and some being obligated by the mandate of the apostolic see, we command you to ensure, in Germany, in places where it seems expedient, that a certain sum of money is provided annually according to your discretion, until the persecution of the Church ceases. This mandate is to be carried out notwithstanding any general or special indulgence obtained or to be obtained from the apostolic see that might impede or delay this grace. Opponents, etc. Given at Lyon, on the Nones of May, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa mandat P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum cardinali et archiepiscopo Maguntino ut electo Spirensi in Germania annuam pecuniae summam providere faciant, donec cesset persecutio ecclesiae, rebus suis ab ecclesiae inimicis occupatis. 1246, Mai. 7. Datum Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To P., deacon cardinal of St. George at Velum Aureum, legate of the Apostolic See. Since, as was proposed before us on behalf of the nobleman E., lord of Eicheum, the nobleman Ulric of Risinspurc of the Diocese of Augsburg, who had previously been betrothed to this man's daughter, married her and had several children with her, we command that you, with our authority, dispense with them so that they may remain lawfully in the marriage thus contracted, notwithstanding such impediment, if you see it fit. Given at Lyon, 8th day before the Ides of May, in the third year of [our] pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali, apostolicae sedis legato, mandat ut cum Ulrico de Risinspurc et coniuge eius, non obstante impedimento, auctoritate apostolica dispenset, ut in matrimonio remanere valeant. 1245, Mai. 8, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Constance. We are moved to grant special favor to your cleric, Master Henry, by the devoted prayers of Frederick, knight, messenger, and agent of our beloved sons, the noble men, the counts of Swabia. Therefore, considering his knowledge of letters, his honorable morals, and praiseworthy conduct, for which he is given commendable testimony, and for these reasons, as well as out of regard for you and the aforementioned knight, we pursue him with favorable benevolence. We grant you the free authority, by the present letters, to dispense with him so that he may freely receive other benefices with the care of souls, up to the amount you consider expedient, if they are canonically offered to him, and to retain them along with those he already has — notwithstanding the constitution of the general council — provided that the same benefices are not neglected in their due duties, etc. Given at Lyon, May 9th, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Constantiensi mandat ut dispensationem concedat magistro Henrico clerico, ut, non obstante constitutione concilii generalis, alia beneficia cum cura animarum, una cum iam obtentis, recipere et retinere possit. Datum Lugduni, VII Id. Maii, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Pandulf of Phasanella, from the Capua diocese. The Apostolic See, with its usual providence, examines the merits of its subjects with a careful deliberation and rewards those which are deemed most worthy by reason's judgment with greater rewards, pursuing these with more abundant favors and elevating them with fuller benefits. Hence, since you are fervent in your devotion to the Roman Church and strive to maintain steadfastness towards it, so that you are especially marked with the title of faithfulness among its other sons and deserve to be honored in many ways by it, we, considering these things not unworthily and wishing to attend to your interests and diligently seek the increase of your honor, grant to you and your successors the castle of Gifoni in the Salerno diocese with its domain, rights, honors, and all other appurtenances, especially since the Kingdom of Sicily is currently without a king and the noble man Oddo de Laviano has renounced all rights he had in the said castle, as a special favor in fief, provided that the said castle does not belong to another who persists in devotion to the same church. We wish, however, that after you have taken corporal possession of the same castle, both you and the same successors are obliged to perform homage and the oath of fidelity for the same castle to the aforesaid church or to the king who, through it, will be in the said kingdom for the time being, which other vassals of the same kingdom are obliged to exhibit for the castles or fiefs they hold. Therefore, let no one etc. violate our concession etc. Given at Lyon, 14th March, in the fourth year of our pontificate. In the same manner, we grant in special favor to the same for the castle of Campagna in the Salerno diocese as above until the king is now absent, as a fief, provided etc. as above in another until the end.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro Pandulfo de Phasanella castrum Gifonis et castrum Campanie in diocesi Salernitana in feudum de gratia speciali concedit, dummodo castra dicta ad alium devotionem Ecclesiae Romanae persistentem non pertineant, et mandat ut postquam possessionem corporalem habuerit, ipse et successores eius pro castris homagium et iuramentum fidelitatis ecclesiae vel regi praestare teneantur. 1230, Mar. 14. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To this edition, Collect. Laporte du Theil Bibl. Paris. was applied. Potthast, Reg. 12187; Berger 1993. Although all those whom the Christian religion distinguishes are bound to the defense of the Catholic faith and ecclesiastical liberty, ecclesiastical men, both religious and secular, and especially the prelates of the churches, are more strictly bound to this, as they are called to the participation of the Lord's lot more specially, and should be more deeply moved by the injuries of Jesus Christ and against the persecutors of the Church, His bride. Above all, the tyrant F., formerly Emperor of the Romans, incessantly and openly wields the arms of persecution against God and the said Church, as he, who previously shone by the dignity granted by this Church, now rages against it with greater cruelty, turning the forces of his power against it with nefarious perversity of mind, sharpening the sword for its destruction, which he had received from it to wield against its enemies. However, so that his wicked intention may be utterly thwarted by the Lord's authoring and the strength of his power broken, we must especially resist the efforts of his malignancy and thwart his attempts, from where he is accustomed to be superior due to the excellence of his name and to be feared even more for the greatness of his power. Therefore, we earnestly warn, beseech, and exhort all of you, commanding that, considering how much the same F. has scourged not only the Church but also nearly the entire Christian population with the hammers of tribulations, and how long he has poured out the venom of his ferocity upon ecclesiastical men, and that he continually rages against them with harsher fury, an effective remedy needs to be applied to these matters. Rising with fervent spirits to defend the aforementioned faith and liberty against his treachery, especially since another has now been elected as King of the Romans, to be promoted to Emperor by the Lord's authoring, we urge you to assume the sign of the cross against the same F. and all his supporters, hoping for divine and our assistance, and to propose the word of the cross through your cities and dioceses, both by yourselves and by others, religious and secular, whom you know to be suitable for this purpose. Urge them with diligent and zealous exhortations to gird themselves quickly and manfully against him, taking this sign, considering attentively the detestable wickedness and execrable purpose of the aforementioned F.
