**Translation to English:**

To the archbishops and bishops, abbots and priors, deans, archdeacons, and other prelates of churches, as well as to the noble counts, barons, knights, and the people of the cities, castles, and places established throughout the kingdom of Sicily. The sound of your tribulation has gone out into all the earth, and your groans, most worthy of compassion, have reached the ends of the earth, leading many to marvel greatly, that, oppressed by the disgrace of such dire servitude and burdened by the manifold loss of persons and goods, you have neglected to take counsel, by which, as with other peoples, some solace of freedom might come to you. Truly, the Apostolic See has often endeavored, with the ingenuity that maternal affection is accustomed to suggest, so that through its help some remission of your pains might be made or the full joy of redemption might come about. For this reason, our predecessor, Pope Gregory of pious memory, endured the anguish of heart until he passed through the span of temporal life, and for this reason, we ourselves, even while holding a lesser office and after we were, though unworthy, elevated to the office of pastor of the universal Church, have poured out deep and bitter sighs, crying out with the voice of the heart to the Lord, that He might make you in our days worthy to become numbered among the free. But when the extension of our desire became too long, so that Frederick, the minister of deceit, the disturber of the age, the despiser of the Christian faith, the persecutor of the Church, and your continual oppressor, might be made alien to his usual works of perversity, we chose to go to distant places under the experience of many labors and pains, where, after the long delay of expectation, knowing that the said persecutor sought only to destroy the Church or to bind it with its children to tearful necessities, we, with the approval of the holy council, rightly deprived him of the dignity of the kingdoms and the empire, having conceived confidence in divine mercy that a path of salvation should be given chiefly to your afflictions and to those of many others. With the world stirred against the impious one and many nobles of the kingdom opposed to him, who desire consolation of freedom for themselves, for you, and for posterity, we beseech all of you by the mercy of God and in remission of your sins, that you would grant swift joy to us and our brothers lamenting over your affliction, by rejecting the dominion of the condemned man, to whom you are bound in nothing whatsoever, and by returning to the bosom of holy Roman Church, your mother, from which you are special sons, ceasing all evasions, especially since we, as much as we can in God, are always ready to assist you, having determined to appoint two solemn legates, namely, our beloved sons, the cardinals S. of the title of St. Mary in Trastevere and R. of St. Mary in Cosmedin, men indeed endowed with wisdom and distinguished by various virtues, to promote this business, having granted them the full office of legation, as you will gather more fully from other letters we are sending to you concerning this matter, knowing that we, for procuring your general salvation, are sending the aid we believe to be expedient for the present. Behold what is expedient for you, who groan under the weight of penal labors and bemoan the depletion of your substance through constant exactions and collections, what our soul desires for you, you clearly see and manifestly feel. Consider, therefore, with vigilant heart, that the chain of your servitude may fall from your neck and that your whole community may bloom again in the joy of liberty and peace, and let there be rumor among the nations, that just as your kingdom is conspicuous for its great nobility and wonderful abundance, so, with the favor of divine power, it may be secure in liberty. Given at Lyon, the 6th day before the Kalends of May, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto:**

Gregorii IX papae ad archiepiscopos, episcopos, abbates, priores ac nobiles regni Siciliae, exhortans ut a dominio Frederici, quem ab imperii dignitate deiecit, se absolvant et ad Ecclesiae Romanae gremium redeant. Datum Lugduni, VI Kal. Maii, anno tertio.

**Translation to English:**

To the archbishops and bishops, abbots, priors, and other prelates of churches, both exempt and non-exempt, established throughout Germany. Since we are sending our beloved son P., cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, a man indeed endowed with knowledge, adorned with honesty, and circumspect in counsel, to the regions of Germany with the full commission of legation for the business of the Church and Empire, we earnestly ask and urge your entire community, instructing that you commit your churches and their goods to the promotion of the same business without any difficulty, whenever you are requested by the aforementioned cardinal. By the tenor of these presents, we promise that we will keep you and the same churches completely unharmed in this matter and, together with our brothers, we will hold firm and acceptable whatever you decide or arrange with the aforementioned cardinal, and we have granted him full power to promise this to you. Given at Lyons, on the 15th before the Kalends of April, in the fourth year. In the same manner to all noble men, dukes, marquises, counts, barons, and other nobles established throughout Germany: we earnestly ask and urge your nobility, instructing that you devoutly receive and honorably treat him, indeed rather us in him, and firmly believe him regarding all matters he conveys to you from us. By the tenor of these presents, we promise that whatever you decide or arrange with him concerning both the creation of the king and all other related matters, together with our brothers, we will hold firm and acceptable, and we have granted him full power to promise this to you. Given at Lyons, on the 15th before the Kalends of April, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopis et episcopis, abbatibus, prioribus aliisque ecclesiarum prelatis per Alamaniam constitutis mandat, ut ad promotionem negotii ecclesiae et imperii ecclesias et bona eorum sine difficultate obligent, cum dilectum filium P., Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diaconum cardinalem, eo fine destinet. Lugduni, XV Kalendas Aprilis, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishops, abbots, priors, deans, archdeacons, and other prelates of the churches, as well as to the noble men, counts, barons, magistrates, rectors, councilors, peoples, and communities of the cities, castles, and places throughout the patrimony of Saint Peter in Tuscany, the Duchy of Spoleto, and the March of Ancona, wishing them the spirit of wiser counsel. 

The Church has long awaited with an anxious heart that the mercy of the eternal Father would receive with a kind ear the groans of the afflicted, caused by the impious and detestable Frederick, and would come to their aid with the fullness of consolation. This expectation now seems to be realized through divine mercy, which was the desire of the Christian people. For the Son of God, in whose presence it pleased Him to strike down Frederick, who had been granted power by Him though us undeserving, for his countless acts of wickedness from the dignity of the Empire, seems willing to finally crush him under the burden of eternal disgrace, as is presumed with great exultation of spirit from the fact that many of the sons of tears in the kingdom of Sicily, abhorring the deadly dominion of the treacherous tyrant, stand against him, with the hope conceived that together with others, through the help of the mother church, they might attain the longed-for joys of freedom.

Since it was paramount to our predecessors and remains a primary affection of ours that the same kingdom, which is of the right and property of the apostolic see, would shake off the shackle of servitude and gain some possibility of repose, and now this miracle, glorious through God, begins to shine through its effect, with all the affection of our mind and in consultation with our brothers, we have taken steps to apply our strength and diligence to the redemption of the same kingdom. However, since the nature of such a business demands that its execution not suffer any delay, behold, for the successful procurement of the same redemption, while providing the necessary assistance of support, we have deemed it proper to appoint as solemn legates our beloved sons, the cardinals S. of the title of Santa Maria in Trastevere and R. of Santa Maria in Cosmedin, men indeed renowned for their wisdom and endowed with diverse virtues.

We therefore ask and urge your whole community in the Lord Jesus Christ, commanding that you be eager to show through the effect of your deeds how great in you is the purity of faith toward God and the sincerity of devotion towards the apostolic see, raising them up with continual honors worthily. We wish them to be received as our own person, having fully the office of legation, and to be treated with filial reverence, admitting them devoutly and joyously, and striving to honor them in all the ways you know and are able, intending effectively to them or either of them on those matters which pertain to the glory of God, the honor of the Church, and the increase of ecclesiastical liberty, and especially the initiated salvation of the kingdom, believing that through this you will acquire the reward of heavenly grace and obligate our spirit to compensate your deeds of graces. Otherwise, the sentence which they or either of them shall pronounce against the rebellious, we shall hold ratified, etc., until it is observed. In the same way to the archbishops and bishops, abbots, priors, deans, archdeacons, and other church prelates, as well as to the noble men, counts, barons, magistrates, rectors, councilors, peoples, and communities of the cities, castles, and places throughout the patrimony of Saint Peter in Tuscany, the Duchy of Spoleto, and the March of Ancona, health and apostolic blessing.

**Regesto (in Latin):**

Gregorius IX papa ecclesiarum prelatis et nobilibus viris per patrimonium beati Petri in Tuscia, ducatum Spoleti et Anconitanam marchiam constitutis mandat, ut legatos S. tituli Sanctae Mariae Transtiberim et R. Sanctae Mariae in Cosmidin cardinales devote admittant et eos honore prosequantur ad redemptionem regni Siciliae. 1230, Asisii.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz. On behalf of our beloved son, the noble man Warner, Duke of Bavaria and seneschal, devoted to the Roman Church, it was humbly requested to us that, since he has founded and endowed the monastery of Syon in your diocese on his own land and from his own resources, and since nuns are soon to reside there, it being a new establishment, we might, with paternal care, grant them the Order of Saint Benedict according to its original institution, so that they are not bound by the constitutions that were made later in that Order. Therefore, we command you, by our authority, to make arrangements as you see fit in God. Given at Lyon, on the 11th of May, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino mandat, ut monasterium Syon, a Warnerio duce Bavarie fundatum, ordinem Sancti Benedicti secundum primam institutionem suam observet. 1230, Mai. 11. Datum Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbots in Alchingen and Ahusena, and the provost of Wetenhysen, of the order of Saint Augustine in the diocese of Augsburg. Since, as it was proposed to us on behalf of our dear son, the noble man H., Count Palatine of Tübingen, devoted to the Roman Church, we had directed our writings to the abbot and convent of the monastery of Blaburen of the order of Saint Benedict in the diocese of Constance concerning the provision of several matters, appointing certain executors for this task: we, wishing to grant a special favor to the said abbot and convent at the request of the aforementioned count, command that you expressly prohibit these executors, who have not yet proceeded with this provision, from proceeding further in this matter. 

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbatibus Alchingen et Ahusena necnon preposito Wetenhysen, ordinis sancti Augustini, mandat ut executoribus provisione ad abbatem et conventum monasterii Blaburen pertinentibus pro intercessione comitis palatini de Tuwinghen ne procedant, inhibentes. 1241, Maii 7, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Anselm the bailiff and all the people of the town of Pingue. Since those who show themselves to be endearing to the Apostolic See through the pleasing zeal of devotion deserve to obtain the favor of the same See more especially, we, mindful of your services which you have freely and liberally rendered to us and the Roman Church up to now and continue to provide incessantly, wishing therefore to honor you with a special gift of grace, moved by the supplications of our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Mainz, and yours, grant you with the authority of these presents, that as long as you are prepared to present full justice before your ordinary to those complaining about you, you or any of you cannot be dragged to judgment outside your town by apostolic letters, unless they make explicit mention of this indulgence: these presents will cease to be valid after three years. Let no one etc. of our concession etc. Given at Lyon, 4th day before the Nones of May, in the fourth year.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa Anselmo villico et hominibus oppidi Pinguensis concedit, ut dum parati sint iustitiam coram ordinario suo exhibere, extra oppidum suum per litteras apostolicas ad iudicium non trahantur, nisi expressa fiat mentio de indulgentia. 1229, Mai. 4, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Ancona. Some undevoted to God and the Church from the city of Osimo, after having wickedly adhered to the former Emperor Frederick, have especially sought to manifest their cruelty by grievously injuring and enormously damaging the Church of Ancona. However, since the said church, as we have learned, has been almost reduced to nothing because of this, we, wishing to apply remedies of proper consolation to it and to suitably compensate the persecutors with the merits of reward, have decreed by the authority of these presents that the said Osimans are bound to restore to the same all that has been consumed from the goods of the said church by them or through their instigation by the army of the aforementioned Frederick, from the time he occupied the March. Let no one, therefore, etc., of our constitution etc. Given as above? In the same manner, to the Archdeacon and Chapter of Ancona.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Anconitano mandat ut Auximani omnia consumpta de bonis ecclesiae Anconitanae a tempore occupationis Marchiae per Fredericum imperatorem restaurare teneantur. 1234, ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man A., Marquis of Este. Since at the time when Frederick, the former emperor, occupied the city of Vicenza, you were exercising the office of podestà there, and you claim that you were not paid the salary promised to you due to this occupation: we, considering the damages to property and persons that you are known to have incurred during that occupation, by the authority of these presents, grant you the right to demand from the commune of the aforementioned city the said salary whenever the opportunity presents itself, and we decree that the said commune remains obligated to make full payment to you or your heirs. Therefore, let no one etc. violate our concession and decree etc. Given at Lyons, on the Ides of May, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa nobili viro A. marchioni Estensi concedit, ut salarium sibi promissum tempore occupationis Vicentinae a Friderico quondam imperatore, a communi civitatis postulare possit, et comune ad solutionem plenariam obligat. 1246, Maii 15, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

When our beloved son, the noble man .. I. Count of Burgundy and Lord of Salins, as we have learned upon his information, hesitates to go in support of the Holy Land, and it is fitting that he should have an appropriate subsidy from his land for that purpose, we command that when requested by the same count, you faithfully collect the twentieth part of the ecclesiastical revenues of his land and keep it until it pleases our will; notwithstanding letters obtained by others regarding the said twentieth in that land. Given at Lyon, on the fourth day before the Kalends of June, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa .. mandat, ut cum a comite Burgundiae et domino Salinensi requisitus fueris, vicesimam partem reddituum ecclesiasticorum terre sue fideliter colligi et servari facias usque ad beneplacitum papae. 1230, Mai. 29. Datum Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To P., Cardinal Deacon of St. George at the Velum Aureum, legate of the Apostolic See. Since, as we have learned from trustworthy sources, our venerable brother, the Bishop of Augsburg, already worn out by old age, has become incapable of carrying out the pastoral office, and as a result, the Church of Augsburg is known to be harmed in spiritual matters and diminished in temporal ones, and the business of the universal Church is greatly hindered: we command you not to delay in admonishing and effectively inducing the same bishop on our behalf to resign freely into your hands. Once his resignation is received, you should ensure that the chapter of Augsburg is prohibited from proceeding with an election, postulation, or nomination without a special mandate from the Apostolic See, decreeing by our authority that any such attempt shall be null and void if they proceed otherwise. Given at Lyon, on the 11th of May, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali mandat ut episcopum Augustensem, propter senectutem officium pastorale exsequi inutilem, ad renuntiationem inducat, et capitulo Augustensi sine speciale mandato sedis apostolicae actiones in electione prohibet. 1230, Mai. 11. Datum Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Constance. Your brotherhood has informed us that when C., the son of the late Emperor Frederick, pledged the advocacy of the monastery of Reichenau in your diocese, which the same Frederick had purchased from the nobleman Diethalm of Chreinchigen and his heirs, to the same nobles as a pledge, after a sentence of deposition had been passed against him, the abbot of the monastery, incited by a diabolical spirit, presumed to deliver the bridge over the Rhine and the tower on the other side, by which the island of the monastery was enclosed, to the said nobles, causing great harm to the monastery, and knowingly associated with those bound by the chain of excommunication. Therefore, wishing to assist the monastery, we grant you the authority through these presents, that, if it is so, you should diligently labor for its recovery, and you must remove the same abbot from the governance of the abbey for such a great excess, and fully receive its revenues and proceeds, ensuring that, while taking care of the monastery, you provide the convent with all necessary things from these revenues and proceeds, and that the remainder be converted, by our authority, to the support of the business of the church, as you see fit, contradictors, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 4th of the Nones of May, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Constantiensi mandat ut abbatem monasterii Renaugensis propter excessum amoveat et eius redditus recipiat, providens de necessariis conventui et residuum in subsidium ecclesiae convertat. Datum Lugduni, IIII Non. Maii, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man A., Marquis of Este. It is neither new nor unusual nor even unfamiliar that Frederick, the former emperor, frequently spreads entirely false and unfounded rumors throughout the world; for this reason, the devoted to the Church should not be disturbed nor lend credence to such words if he makes certain things be said that might weaken their hearts, but, as steadfast men whom we will by no means forsake, they should remain more firmly in their usual steadiness. Therefore, since the aforementioned Frederick causes it to be spread that there is a negotiation for the restoration of concord between the Church and himself, you should know that although we desire the salvation of his soul, as well as that of any Christian no matter how perverse, and that he may return to his senses and repent of his sins, there is no negotiation whatsoever regarding peace or the restoration of concord, nor has there been any since the time when the sentence of deposition was pronounced against him in the general council. Given at Lyon, 12 May, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro A. marchioni Estensi significat Fredericum quondam imperatorem rumores falsos de tractatu pacis cum ecclesia disseminare, sed nullum tractatum post depositionem in concilio generale habitum esse. 1239, Mai. 12. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot and convent of Swarzahe, of the Order of Saint Benedict, in the diocese of Strasbourg. To offer a special grace to our beloved son Nicholas, a cleric of Strasbourg, we are prompted by the requests of our beloved son, the noble lord, the count of Württemberg, and by the merits of the said cleric, about whom laudable testimony is provided. We therefore earnestly request and instruct your community, mandating that you provide this cleric, for the reverence of the Apostolic See and ours, with a suitable ecclesiastical benefice, which pertains to your collation and has customarily been assigned to secular clerics, as soon as the opportunity arises, generously — notwithstanding if we have sent you other letters for others, which we do not wish to hinder this grace, or any indulgence obtained from the Apostolic See, which might delay or impede this grace. Otherwise, unwilling that our word should return to us void, we give our venerable brother, the bishop of Strasbourg, a mandate in our letters to execute this apostolic mandate; those who oppose, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 10th of May, in the fourth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati et conventui de Swarzahe ordinis sancti Benedicti Argentinensis diocesis mandat, ut Nicolao clerico Argentinensi, ad preces comitis de Wirtemberch, beneficium ecclesiasticum competens assignent. 1231, Mai. 10, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the archbishops and bishops, abbots, priors, and other prelates of churches, both exempt and non-exempt, established throughout Poland and Pomerania. Since we cannot be present in person to every place, we sometimes send those whom we have appointed with full authority to share in our concern, following the example of Him who descended from the highest heavens to the lowest parts of the world for the salvation of mankind and sent the disciples He chose into all the world to preach the gospel to every creature. Therefore, thinking with paternal diligence about your salvation, we have decided to send our beloved son P., cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, a man endowed with knowledge, adorned with moral integrity, and circumspect in counsel, to your regions, with the full office of legation committed to him, so that he may uproot and destroy, build and plant, as he sees fit. Since we embrace him with the arms of special affection among other brothers, we command and charge all of you to receive and treat him kindly and honorably, or rather us in him, as the legate of the Apostolic See, humbly and devotedly attending to him, and effectively fulfilling his admonitions and commands, which he shall deliver to you on our behalf. Otherwise, the sentence, etc., as far as: by the authority of the Lord, until full satisfaction is observed inviolably. Given at Lyons, on the 14th of March, in the fourth year. In the same manner to the archbishops and bishops, abbots, priors, etc., both exempt and non-exempt, established throughout the kingdom of Dacia. In the same manner to the bishop of Cambrai and the abbots, priors, etc., established throughout the city and diocese of Cambrai. In the same manner to all counts, barons and nobles throughout Poland. In the same manner to all counts, barons, and other nobles established throughout Pomerania.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa archiepiscopis, episcopis, abbatibus, prioribus aliisque ecclesiarum praelatis per Poloniam et Pomeraniam mandat ut P. cardinalem, legatum apostolicae sedis, benigne recipiant eiusque mandata ex parte papae efficaciter impleant. 1247, Mar. 14, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Cardinal Deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, legate of the Apostolic See. Our venerable brother, the Bishop of Halberstadt, has requested through his letters that, as he intends to assist his mother church honorably and powerfully in its affairs, by providing aid and showing the duty owed to filial affection, we grant him the permission to contract a loan and pledge the goods of his church to creditors for this purpose. Therefore, entrusting this matter to your prudence, in which we have full confidence in the Lord, we command your discretion to grant him the requested permission if you deem it expedient. Given at Lyons, on the tenth day before the Kalends of June, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Sancti Georgii ad Vellum Aureum diacono cardinali, apostolicae sedis legato, mandat ut, si expedire visum fuerit, licentiam concedat episcopo Halberstadensi contrahendi mutuum et obligandi bona ecclesiae suae. 1247, Mai. 23. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Peter of Savoy. Since the supreme pontiff, endowed with the keys of the heavenly kingdom in the person of the blessed Peter by Him who, through eternal providence, arranges heavenly and earthly matters alike, holds the authority to bind and to loose, sometimes, exceeding the law while observing justice, foresees to relax the bond of necessity, to which everyone is bound for the observance of the law, from the fullness of his power concerning certain individuals, when urgent necessity demands or evident utility, especially public, advises it, without any undue partiality of persons intervening, for it is not to be considered favoring a person when something is granted without injury to the law for the sake of place and time, especially with regard to divine service. Therefore, as we have learned from your report, you have contracted marriage with a noble woman, daughter of a noble man, the lord of Fulciniaco, related to you in the fourth degree of consanguinity. Inclined by your supplications, wishing to prevent the dangers that might arise, as you assert, if a divorce were to occur between you and the said noblewoman, we grant by the authority of these presents that you and the said noblewoman may lawfully remain in the marriage thus contracted, notwithstanding such a degree. Let no one therefore etc. infringe our grant etc. Given at Lyon, on the Nones of May, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa nobili viro Petro de Sabaudia concedit, ut cum nobili muliere, in quarto consanguinitatis gradu sibi coniuncta, matrimonium contrahere possit et in eo remanere, non obstante consanguinitatis gradu. 1246, Mai. 7. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

... to the provost and chapter of the secular church of Grandisvallis in the diocese of Basel. As we have heard from our beloved son Bertold, the messenger of the noble woman Margaret, once the daughter of the late ... Duke of Austria, Master Cuno of Lucerne, chaplain of our venerable brother, the Bishop of Constance, and your fellow canon, wishes to freely resign the prebend he holds in your church. We have deemed it necessary to more earnestly ask and warn your entire community, firmly ordering you by this mandate that, since the conferral of prebends of the same church pertains to you, you should liberally grant this prebend, once his spontaneous and free resignation is accepted, to our beloved son John of the monastery of Grandisvallis, a cleric who has not yet obtained any ecclesiastical benefice, and to whom his knowledge of letters, honesty of morals, and purity of life provide support, in honor of the Apostolic See and our reverence, admitting him to the same prebend as a canon and brother — notwithstanding any previous letters we might have directed for others, by which we do not wish etc. until: generated. Given at Lyon, on the 11th of May, in the fourth year.

**Regesto:**

Innocentius IV papa preposito et capitulo ecclesiae Grandisvallis mandat, ut prebendam, quam magister Cuno Lucernensis resignare velit, Iohanni de monasterio Grandisvallis clerico conferant. 1246, Mai. 11. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the illustrious king of Cyprus and lord of the kingdom of Jerusalem. Those who hold greater power ought to exercise such care and solicitude over their subjects, that through their prudent governance, peace and concord may be increased for them, and their condition may be directed towards prosperity, so that when the benefits of fortunate times come to them, they may boast not merely of being subject but of reigning under their superiors. Therefore, dearest son, if you carefully consider and rightly ponder the fact that you preside over the land where Jesus Christ wished to be born, live, and die for the redemption of humankind, you will sweetly endure and pleasantly bear the burdens of any labors, cares, and concerns that may arise, in order to restore it — beset by various adversities due to sins — to a better state. We ask and urge you more willingly and confidently because we know and recognize that this is expedient for your benefit and honor, the exaltation of the Church, and the salvation and benefit of the entire Christian people. Let, therefore, the strength of your power arise, fortified and secure in the grace of the King of Kings, which will not fail you if you direct your steps to Him, and strive to govern and administer the aforesaid kingdom with careful prudence, and the mark of virtue and power, unafraid of toil or expense, such that, through your agency, peace may arise for the people of that kingdom, tranquility may be strengthened, Christian devotion may flourish, and may be encouraged for your support and that of the land. Thus, let it be done, so that besides the reward of eternal beatitude which you will thereby achieve, a heap of perpetual praise may increase for you, and you may be commended by us also, whom you will always find favorable and kind to your advantages, with worthy praises in the Lord. Given at Lyon, April 17, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa regi Cipri et domino regni Ierosolimitani mandat, ut regnum, quod Iesus Christus inhabitatum voluit, cum prudentia et virtute regere studeat ad pacem et devotionem Christianam promovendum. 1231, Apr. 17, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Brixen: Lest the wicked may boast when they have done evil, we grant you the authority by these presents, that you may remove and deprive from their prelatures and benefices the prelates and clerics of your city and diocese who offer or will offer counsel, aid, or favor to the late Emperor Frederick, or who have scorned to obey you concerning the business of the Church, and that you may freely confer the aforementioned prelatures and benefices to suitable persons who persist in devotion to the Church, as you see fit; any opposers, etc. Given at Lyon, on the Nones of June, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Brixinensi concedit auctoritatem amovendi et privandi prelatos et clericos civitatis et diocesis, qui Friderico quondam imperatori favorem exhibent, et conferendi beneficia personis idoneis. 1247, Iun. 5. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

Our beloved son, the noble man Stephen, son of the late and esteemed King Andrew of Hungary, has shown us by his petition that, when of old our predecessor of happy memory, Pope Gregory, had instructed our beloved son G. de Montelongo, our subdeacon and notary, legate of the apostolic see, to ensure that his mother, the late Queen Beatrice of Hungary, would be provided for annually from the monasteries and churches of his legation as he saw fit, the legate having executed this apostolic mandate, and with our aforementioned predecessor having passed away, we first instructed our beloved son, the elected bishop of Ferrara, under certain conditions, and then, after the said queen had passed away, we ordered him by our letters to continue the provision which certain prelates of churches, monasteries, and other places of his legation had been commanded by apostolic authority to make for the said queen. This was notwithstanding any indults granted by the said see to some of these prelates, monasteries, churches, or places exempting them from being bound by apostolic letters to make provision for anyone, without mentioning such indults, to ensure this provision was made by our authority, notwithstanding any opposition. The provision was ordered to be paid by you and our venerable brothers, the bishops of Trieste and Concordia, and some other prelates of churches, according to the apostolic mandate. And because you refused to comply with the mandate according to your own will, we commanded you by our letters to ensure the portion of the said provision imposed on you was paid to Stephen, the legate being appointed to oversee this matter. And although the legate has ordered you to satisfy Stephen for the arrears and to pay him the aforementioned portion, threatening you with the sentence of interdict if you disobeyed in this matter, you nevertheless have not cared to comply, despising such a sentence. Therefore, we ask, admonish, and earnestly exhort your fraternity, commanding you that, if this is so, you redeem your former disobedience by subsequent obedience, so that Stephen may not be compelled to labor further in this matter, and we may rightly commend your devotion. Otherwise, we have instructed our beloved son, the provost of Ferrara, by our letters to compel you to do this, having given prior warning and with our authority, removing any appeal—notwithstanding the constitution regarding two days' travel, etc. Given at Lyons, on the third Ides of March, in the fourth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo mandavit, ut provisionem pro Stephano, filio regis Andreae Hungariae, exolveret, quae ab ecclesiarum prelatibus et locis sub legatione olim mandata fuit matri suae, reginae Beatrici. 1247, Mart. 13, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Venerable Abbot of Santa Maria di Portonovo, of the Order of Saint Benedict, Diocese of Ancona. When our venerable brother, the Bishop of Ancona, was called to the Council of Lyon and had prepared himself for the journey to the Apostolic See, certain members of his household, compelled by necessity, arrived at Porto Recanati. Instead of being met with the reverence and kindness due to the Apostolic See and ourselves, as they should have been, the residents of that place, presumptuously and with reprehensible boldness, as we have been informed, robbed them of a certain palfrey belonging to the bishop and other goods through violence. Therefore, we command you, if it is found to be true, to compel the commune of that place, after due warning and through ecclesiastical censure, setting aside any appeal, to restore these things to the bishop as they are bound to do. Given at Lyon, on the Ides of May, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati Sancte Marie Portus Novi ordinis Sancti Benedicti mandat ut, si constiterit quod familia episcopi Anconitani a communi Portus Racanatensis violenter spoliata sit, commune illud monitione premissa censura ecclesiastica cogat ad restitutionem. Datum Lugduni, Idibus Maii, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the schoolmaster and treasurer of the church of Verdun. By commendable conduct and life, our beloved son Henry, a cleric born of our beloved son Vologard, consul of the city of Bremen, is said to have made himself worthy so that by the kindness of the Apostolic See, which delights in favoring the deserving, he may receive special grace. Therefore, considering his merits and the request of our beloved sons, the noble man, Count of Ravensberg, and the commune of Bremen, who are devoted to us and the Roman Church, and who sent us special prayers and letters regarding this, we command you to provide the said Henry, who claims not to have acquired any ecclesiastical benefice, with a prebend in one of the churches of the city or diocese of Bremen, excepting the cathedral, if a vacancy presently exists or as soon as one should occur, by our authority — notwithstanding if the church in which you decide to provide him has a certain number of canons bound by oath or any other binding agreement, or if we have issued letters for another in the same church, which we do not wish to be prejudiced by the authority of these presents, or any indulgence, about which full mention ought to be made in our letters —; contradictors, etc. Given at Lyon, 12th of the Kalends of May, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa scholastico et thesaurario ecclesiae Verdensis mandat, ut Henrico clerico, filio Vologardi consulis Bremensis, qui nullum beneficium ecclesiasticum assecutus est, in ecclesiis Bremensis civitatis vel diocesis, cathedrali excepta, de prebenda, si vacet vel vacare contigerit, auctoritate apostolica provideant. Datum Lugduni, XII Kalendas Maii, anno quarto pontificatus nostri.

**Translation to English:**

From Potthast, Reg. 12514; Berger 2698. To P., cardinal deacon of San Giorgio in Velabro, legate of the Apostolic See. On behalf of our beloved son in Christ, the illustrious king of Bohemia, we were humbly petitioned that since Conrad, whom we had long removed from the church of Olomouc, was willing to freely resign the castles and other properties he held from the goods of the bishopric of Olomouc, we might, out of customary kindness, grant to the same Conrad, who is noble and powerful in those parts, the village of Cholso and the possessions of Opava and Gelz, with their appurtenances, up to the value of three hundred marks of silver annually, which belong to the bishopric of Olomouc. Therefore, we command that with our authority you do what you see fit in this matter; against those who resist, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 11th of May, in the fourth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa, P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali, apostolicae sedis legato mandat ut, postquam Conradus possessiones Olomucenses resignare voluerit, villam Cholso et possessiones de Opavia et Gelz cum earum pertinentiis Conrado concedat, si id expedire videatur. Datum Lugduni, V Idus Maii, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To all provosts, priors, and other prelates of the churches subject to the Fulda Abbey. As our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Mainz, has explained to us, he is compelled to make heavy expenses from his own resources for the recovery and defense of the lands and possessions of the Fulda Abbey, which have been entrusted to him by us. He found the goods of the abbey so encumbered that even the monks of the abbey barely have what they need to sustain themselves. It is fitting that the members should assist their head and that the subjects should support the burdens of the prelates. Therefore, we command all of you to provide the Archbishop with a moderate subsidy, according to your own means, without any difficulty or delay, to alleviate the burden of these expenses he is compelled to undertake for the recovery of these goods. Moreover, we desire that from these goods, once they have been recovered through the assistance of your contribution, no one shall receive anything until such time as this subsidy has been repaid to you from their revenues. Otherwise, we instruct our beloved son, the Abbot of Eberbach in the diocese of Mainz, with our letters, to compel you to do this by ecclesiastical censure, with an admonition made beforehand and without possibility of appeal. Given at Lyons, on the fifth day before the Nones of May, in the fourth year (of our pontificate).

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa universis praepositis, prioribus et aliis praelatis ecclesiarum monasterio Foldensi subiectis mandat, ut archiepiscopo Maguntino subsidium moderatum ad expensas recuperandi terras monasterii Foldensis conferant, cum obligationes gravent monachos eiusdem. Si defuerint, abbas Eberbacensis per censuram ecclesiasticam eos compellat. 1231, Maii 3, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

Innocentius IV papa Sancte Marie in Via Lata diacono cardinali, apostolice sedis legato mandat, ut, cum Massa Trabaria infra fines legationis eius sit, si expedire viderit, ei provideat de rectore. 1247, Iun. 12. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbess and convent of the monastery of Saint Mary Magdalene of Alexandria. The prayers of your devotion and the fervor of your religion, which, though enclosed in body, you offer to the Lord of virtues with a free mind, prompt and induce us to look after your needs. Since the whole community of Alexandria is annually obligated to pay a certain sum of money to the Roman Church and has not paid for several years due to the misfortunes of the times, we, inclined by your prayers, grant you by the authority of these presents the free faculty to demand and fully receive the aforementioned money for the past five years to be converted to your own uses. Given at Lyon, on the 8th of June, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa abbatisse et conventui monasterii sancte Marie Magdalene de Alexandria concedit facultatem petendi et recipiendi pecuniam Alexandrie ecclesie pro quinque annis elapsis. 1246, Iun. 8, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Cardinal Deacon of Santa Maria in Via Lata, Legate of the Apostolic See. Since we are sending you for the urgent business of the Church, we grant you the discretion to provide benefices in Tuscany, such as canonries, prebends, and other ecclesiastical benefices, whether they have the care of souls attached or not, to three or four suitable persons, as you see fit. You are to ensure they are received as canons in the churches of Tuscany and provided with prebends or dignities or other benefices, if they are vacant, or as soon as they become vacant. You may freely restrain opposers through ecclesiastical censure, setting aside any appeal—the statute regarding a fixed number of canons, and any other customs of the churches, both cathedrals and others in the province, even if reinforced by oath or any other firmness, notwithstanding. Even if these churches have been burdened by the Apostolic See or its legates with the provision for others, or if they have an indulgence from the same See that their prelates or chapters are not bound or cannot be compelled to make provisions for anyone, and that they cannot be interdicted, suspended, or excommunicated without a special mandate from the aforesaid See making full mention of such indulgence, and any other apostolic indulgences by which they might perhaps defend themselves, or if the aforementioned persons are perhaps beneficed elsewhere—none of these are to hinder you. We have decided to grant this by our present authority. Given at Lyon, 4th day before the Nones of May, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa, cardinali diacono Sancte Marie in Via Lata, apostolice sedis legato, mandat ut in Tuscia, de personatibus, canoniis, prebendis aliisque beneficiis ecclesiasticis tribus vel quatuor personis idoneis provideat, contradictores per censuram ecclesiasticam cohibendo. Datum Lugduni, IIII Nonas Maii, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To P., deacon cardinal of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the Apostolic See. The proven devotion of our beloved son, the elected bishop of Speyer, has become so evidently clear in times of necessity—times when the devoted are tested—that he is to be considered not only a legitimate but also a special son of the Apostolic See. He has fully demonstrated to it what is owed to a mother with filial affection, by diligently complying with its mandates and seeking to please it with his will and actions, totally committing himself for its sake. Therefore, loving him with a special prerogative of charity, we propose to treat him with the sweetness of paternal affection, sincerely aspiring to his advancement. Thus, so that he, whom his merits render graceful, may reap the fruits of his devotion and endeavor to progress with even more effective efforts, being preemptively gifted with the grace of special favor, he sees the reasons for gifts growing with increasing gifts. We command you to ensure, by our authority, that he is provided with some archbishopric or a more opulent bishopric than that of Speyer, should it currently be vacant or as soon as it happens to become vacant. Given at Lyons, on the Ides of May, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa P. diacono cardinali Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum, apostolicae sedis legato, mandat ut de archiepiscopatu vel episcopatu opulentiori Spirensi, si vacat vel vacare contigerit, dilecto filio Spirensi electo, obedientiae et devotionis gratia, auctoritate apostolica provideat. Datum Lugduni, Idibus Maii, anno quarto pontificatus.

**Translation to English:**

To Brother Blancus of the Order of Friars Minor, our messenger. Since, as was proposed before us by our venerable brother, the bishop, and the beloved sons of the clergy of both the city and diocese of Avignon, you have imposed upon them the burden of paying money for the support of the Apostolic See, which by no means aligns with their capabilities: we command you by the authority of these presents, that, after considering their means, you moderate the amount of money imposed on them, which you have decided to impose on the surrounding bishoprics according to the proportion of their goods, so that they have no just reason to appeal to us. Given at Lyon, on the Kalends of June, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Fratri Blanco de ordine fratrum Minorum mandat, ut pecuniae quantitatem clero civitatis et diocesis Avinionensis pro subsidio sedis apostolicae impositam moderetur, consideratis facultatibus eorundem. 1246, Iun. 1. Datum Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Rector of Arezzo in the Marche of Ancona and the Bishop of Fermo. Know that it has come to our attention that, with the church of Jesi being without a pastor, the canons of that church, who remain there despite excommunication, not considering that those who are under excommunication cannot elect nor be elected, have presumed to appoint one of their own, namely Armannus, as their bishop in fact, while another, namely Montanarius, a canon of that same church and devoted to the Roman Church, who resides in Ancona due to fear of the late Emperor Frederick, elected Brother Gualterus of the Order of Friars Minor outside the fold of that church. Therefore, we command that, upon diligently inquiring into such elections, if you find them attempted thus, you completely annul them and, with our authority and the counsel of the aforementioned canon Montanarius—who, due to the devotion he bears to the church, does not dare to reside in Jesi—provide a pastor for that church; any contradictors, etc. Given at Lyon, the 3rd day before the Kalends of June, in the fourth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa rectori Aretino Marchiae Anconitanae et episcopo Firmano mandat ut electiones in ecclesia Esina diligenter inquirant et, si taliter attemptatae fuerint, eas cassent et de consilio Montanarii canonici, qui apud Esium residere non audet, de pastore provideant. 1241, Maii 30. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Würzburg. Since, as we have learned from your report, many clerics of your city and diocese, by favoring and adhering to Frederick, the former Roman Emperor, an enemy of God and the Church, have rendered themselves unworthy of the graces and ecclesiastical benefices granted to them by the Apostolic See: because it is fitting that the disloyal suffer loss for their disloyalty and the loyal gain benefit from their loyalty, we command you, by our authority, to deprive these unworthy individuals of the said graces and benefices, and to confer and assign them to suitable persons who are devoted to the Roman Church; those who oppose this decision, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 4th of June, in the fourth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Herbipolensi mandat ut clericos, qui Friderico quondam imperatori faventes se indignos beneficiis apostolicae sedis reddiderunt, ab eisdem beneficiis privet, eaque personis idoneis et ecclesiae Romanae devotis conferat. 1246, Iun. 4. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot and convent of the monastery of Saint Andrew in Vercelli. A petition presented to us on your behalf stated that some time ago, our beloved son G. de Montelongo, our subdeacon and notary, and legate of the apostolic see, had assigned the castle of Constanzana, belonging to you by full right, to the custody of the noble Henry of Advocates, a citizen of Vercelli. This was done under the false suggestion from him that your predecessor, the late abbot T., had turned against the church’s enemies and that the said castle rightfully belonged to the abbot. At that time, all goods you possessed there were entrusted to his custody. We later deemed it necessary to confirm this act of the legate with our confirmation page, at the request of the aforementioned noble, granted to our beloved son, the elect of Turin, appointed as protector to the noble. Therefore, you humbly petitioned us to ensure that no harm would befall you or the said monastery due to the legate's grant or concession, or even our confirmation. Thus, inclined by your petitions, we grant you by the authority of these present letters, that no further prejudice shall be generated against you or the monastery regarding the aforementioned matters due to the aforementioned grant, concession, or confirmation. Let no one, therefore, etc., infringe upon our concession etc. If anyone, etc. Given at Lyon, 18th May, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati et conventui monasterii Sancti Andree Vercellensis indulget ne per concessionem legati vel confirmationem suam preiudicium generetur. 1229, Mai. 18. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Prioress and convent of the monastery of Saint Agnes of Strasbourg. Since, as was proposed on your behalf before us, you, enclosed in body within the monastic enclosures but freely serving the Lord in spirit, have commendably followed the institutions of the Order of Preachers, we, at the supplication of our beloved in Christ sons, the noble woman Amicia, lady of Jouy, and Gualcher, her son, our familiar, inclined by the prayers of your devotion, incorporate you and your monastery into the aforesaid order. By the authority of these presents, we decree that you shall henceforth remain under the guidance and teaching of the Master and Provincial Prior of Germany of the said order, whoever they may be at the time, enjoying those privileges granted or to be granted to the said order by the Apostolic See. The Master and the Prior, with no contradiction from the constitution of the order or indulgence obtained or to be obtained from the Apostolic See, shall care for the salvation of your souls and take responsibility, etc., as stated in the letter of the third chapter up to: as they see fit. Let no one, therefore, etc., violate our incorporation and constitution, etc. If anyone, etc. Given at Lyon, Kalends of June, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa priorisse et conventui monasterii sancte Agnetis Argentinensis mandat, ut eos et monasterium eorum ordini fratrum Predicatorum incorporat, sub magisterio et doctrina magistri et prioris provincialis Theutonie, cum privilegiis ordini concessis. 1231, Lugduni, Kal. Iunii.

**Translation to English:**

To the beloved son P., cardinal deacon of St. George at Velabrum, legate of the Apostolic See. Although all who are distinguished by the Christian religion are bound to the defense of the catholic faith and ecclesiastical liberty, ecclesiastical men, both religious and secular, and especially prelates of churches, are more strictly obliged to this due to their special calling to participate in the Lord's lot, and they must be more vehemently provoked against the injuries of Jesus Christ and the persecutors of the Church, His bride. Among all tyrants, F., the former emperor of the Romans, incessantly and openly wages the arms of persecution against God and the aforementioned Church. The higher dignity he previously shone with, operating by the Church, the more cruelly he has raged against it, wielding the sword, which he received from it to be brandished against its enemies, with impious perversion of mind to its destruction. However, so that his wicked intention may be completely nullified by the Lord's help, and the strength of his power shattered, his wickedness must be resisted with efforts, and his attempts must be thwarted everywhere by the faithful of Christ. Therefore, we command that you earnestly admonish and induce all the prelates of the churches of Germany, Denmark, and Poland, that, considering diligently how many tribulations the same F. has not only scourged the churches but almost the entire Christian populace, and how long he has spilled the venom of his ferocity upon ecclesiastical men, and that he continuously rages against them with more severe madness, which necessitates an effective remedy to be applied, they may rise with fervent spirits to defend the aforesaid faith and liberty against his perfidy, assuming the sign of the cross against the same F. and all his supporters, hoping for divine and our aid, and through you, the prelates of churches, and other religious and secular individuals of the aforementioned Germany, Denmark, and Poland, whom you know to be suitable for this, proposing according to the prudence granted to you by God, the word of the cross to the faithful throughout the same regions, that considering attentively the detestable wickedness and execrable purpose of the aforesaid F., they may gird themselves quickly and manfully against him, having assumed this sign, do not delay in inducing them with earnest and diligent exhortations. For we, confiding in the mercy of almighty God and the authority of His apostles Peter and Paul, from that binding and loosing power given to us by God, though unworthy, etc., as in the letter XXIXP to the end. Given at Lyon, the 15th Kalends of April, in the fourth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa dilecto filio P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali, legato apostolice sedis, mandat ut universos ecclesiarum prelatos Alemannie, Datie ac Polonie moneat et inducat ad crucis signaculum assumendum contra F. quondam Romanorum imperatorem et fautores eius. Datum Lugduni, XV Kalendas Aprilis, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To O., Cardinal Deacon of Santa Maria in Via Lata, legate of the apostolic see. The city of the Venetians has continuously maintained a sincere affection for the Roman Church and preserved such constancy of heart that, distinguished with the special title of fidelity among other cities, it laudably encourages them by its example to the service of the same Church. For it has always been so solicitous and attentive in the affairs of this Church that it has shown itself ready in their reception, diligent in prosecution, and steadfast in completion. Therefore, as it excels in devotion, it deserves to be honored with greater favor and elevated with more grace by the Church itself. We, recalling such firmness of faith and purity of spirit, deem it worthy, indeed most worthy, to kindly assent to the wishes of our beloved sons, the noble Duke and the people of Venice, whenever we can with God's will, and clearly demonstrate our apostolic benevolence toward them through action. Therefore, inclined by their supplications, we command by apostolic writings to your prudence that you, by our authority, receive into the right and property of Saint Peter the churches of Saint Mark of Tyre and Saint Mark of Acre, pertaining to the church of Saint Mark of Venice, and firmly forbid anyone to exercise any jurisdiction over them without a special mandate from the apostolic see. Furthermore, establish a certain census, to be paid annually at a fixed term by our beloved sons, the primicerius and chapter of the church of Saint Mark of Venice, in the name of the churches of Saint Mark of Tyre and Saint Mark of Acre, as you deem expedient, as a token of this freedom. Given at Lyon, 6th May, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa O., Sancte Marie in Via Lata diacono cardinali, apostolice sedis legato, mandat ut ecclesias Sancti Marci Tyrensis et Sancti Marci Acconensis, ad ecclesiam Sancti Marci de Venetiis pertinentes, recipiat in ius et proprietatem beati Petri et inhibeat iurisdictionem absque mandato speciali sedis apostolice exercendam. Lugduni, II Non. Maii, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Constance. On behalf of the mayor and the community of the town of Freiburg in your diocese, we have been humbly petitioned that, since there is only one parish church in that town responsible for nearly forty thousand parishioners, it is essential for their salvation that they have a resident parish priest who can hear their confessions and otherwise attend to their spiritual well-being according to God. Therefore, we should ensure that, when the aforementioned church is vacant, a parish priest may not be appointed there unless he is a priest and willing to reside there. Wishing, therefore, to defer to you in this matter, who are the diocesan of that place, we command you to grant them what they have requested, as you see fit for their salvation and the benefit of the same church according to God. Given at Lyon, on the Nones of June, in the fourth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa [Name] episcopo Constantiensi mandat ut, pro utilitate ecclesiae et salute animarum in villa de Vriburc, plebanus non instituatur nisi sit sacerdos et velit ibi residentiam facere. Datum Lugduni, Nonis Iunii, anno quarto pontificatus.

**Translation to English:**

To the illustrious King of England. The noble man Bartholomew Pesce, your servant, and brother Radulf of the Order of the Holy Trinity, envoys of the noble man R., your brother, the Count of Cornwall, who recently came into our presence, humbly requested three things from us on your and the Count’s behalf: first, that we preserve inviolate the rights you and he have in the County of Provence, which, excluding the dowries due to you for your wives and him for his, and also the agreement or contract made between you and the late Count of Provence, contain half of the aforementioned contract; second, that we send someone from our side to prohibit the noble man Charles, brother of our dearly beloved son in Christ, the illustrious King of France, from further occupying the cities, towns, and castles of the County of Provence until a full discussion and rightful conclusion of this matter is made before us, so that by the grace of our prohibition, you and your said brother may be able to reclaim your rights, which, as the aforementioned envoys stated, were distanced by another, namely our dispensation granted to the said Charles; third, that we give no credence to the testament said to have been made by the aforementioned Count of Provence until we know its rights in judicial form, since the same Count revoked that testament and died completely intestate. 

Therefore, although your envoy, the beloved son Master Laurence, stationed at the Apostolic See and who has frequently pressed our ears on these and many other matters, omitting nothing of concern, might have conveyed our intent and what we have already done in these matters to your Serenity, we respond in such a way that, since by the office of apostolic administration received from the Lord we are obliged to support all who are considered of Christian profession in their rights, we are thus more than willing to preserve inviolate the things that pertain to your rights and those of your brother, not only from the obligation of pastoral care but from our own volition and desire, because we love you and the aforementioned brother of yours, devoted to us and the Roman Church with special affection, more fully in Christ. However, we have not seen fit to proceed at present to make the prohibition noted above, because on your and your brother’s behalf no one has appeared before us to request justice in judicial form concerning the aforementioned right, and indeed the aforementioned B. and R., in our presence, protested that they would not prosecute the pursuit of the right according to that form, and since the merits of causes are revealed by the assertion of the parties, we have not yet been able to know anything certain about that right; nevertheless, led by the zeal of paternal affection, by which we desire to promote and augment your and your relatives’ honor, we will earnestly and diligently induce the aforementioned King of France and Charles through prayers and admonitions to provide for the salvation of their souls by liberally granting the rights which pertain to your wives and those of your said brother, their kinswomen, in the aforementioned county. Moreover, we have not seen nor do we see, nor does it appear to anyone of sound mind, that the dispensation mentioned earlier derogates from your and your brother's right in any way, although the promoters of evil, enemies of truth and friends of falsehood, sometimes presume to pervert correct affections and lawful actions. And indeed, although we granted a dispensation to the aforementioned Charles so that he might be matrimonially joined to some woman related to him in the fourth degree of consanguinity or affinity, we did not expressly name in our letter of dispensation either the woman with whom he afterward made a conjugal union or any other woman; nor was it fitting for the Roman Church to deny such a noble man born of royal lineage the grace of dispensation at the last degree of prohibition of marriages, which it is accustomed to grant even to lesser persons in closer degrees. As for the testament that the aforementioned Count of Provence is said to have made, we neither believe in it nor will believe in it, except insofar as justice will persuade us. Considering these things, observing the purity of our heart and the sincerity of our affection, persist unwaveringly in the devotion of the Apostolic See, your mother, which has been and intends to be favorable and kind to you and yours in all matters according to God, as a blessed son, and do not listen at all to interpretations or suggestions of the wicked who strive to turn the firmness of your mind from the fervor of its devotion. Given at Lyons, the 1st of March, in the third year. In the same manner, to the noble man R., Count of Cornwall throughout, with appropriately changed words.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa regi Anglorum mandat ut iura sua et fratris in comitatu Provinciae serventur, prohibitionem contra Carolum Franciae regem non procedere, et testamentum comitis Provinciae

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Marseille. We believe that what is generously granted by the munificence of princes to the holy churches of God and ecclesiastical persons, through divine grace inspiring them, should be fortified with the firmness of apostolic authority, so that, being fortified with perpetual stability, their possessors, both present and future, may enjoy peaceful possession of those things. Therefore, we, assenting to your just petitions, confirm by apostolic authority and strengthen with the protection of this present writing, the liberties and immunities granted to you and the Church of Marseille by the late Frederick, Emperor of the Romans, of clear memory, with pious liberality, and afterwards confirmed by Frederick, his successor, then Emperor, as well as the possessions and rights expressed in their privileges, as you justly and peacefully possess them. To ensure greater caution and full firmness, we have caused the tenor of Frederick II's privilege, containing the entire series of the first, to be noted word for word in these presents. It is as follows: Frederick II, by the favor of divine clemency, Emperor of the Romans, ever august and King of Sicily, from the custom of imperial clemency, we aim for the peace and quiet of venerable churches and places, so that, fortified by the protection of the august power, they may enjoy peace and security both presently and in the future. Therefore, you, Peter, venerable Bishop of Marseille, our beloved faithful, coming to our presence, showed to our court a certain privilege of Lord Frederick, the most illustrious Emperor of the Romans, ever august, our dearest grandfather of renowned memory, which he had granted and conferred upon your Church of Marseille. You humbly and devoutly begged that, since the privilege itself seemed to have been consumed by age, we would deign from our grace to renew and confirm it to you and your church in perpetuity. Therefore, admitting your supplications favorably into the chamber of our hearing, and considering also the pure faith and sincere devotion you are known to have laudably and devotedly towards our majesty and the empire, we have decided to renew the privilege itself word for word, and as your church was accustomed to use it in the time of our aforementioned grandfather and later in the time of Lord Henry, our father, Emperor, we confirm it to you and your successors and the Church of Marseille in perpetuity. The tenor of which is as follows: In the name of the Holy and Undivided Trinity. Frederick, by the favor of divine clemency, Emperor of the Romans, august. The authority of our majesty and the tenor of ancient institution admonish that we should diligently provide for churches established under the Roman Empire, and that we should assist by the protection of imperial privilege so that their rights and possessions may be preserved without injury.
