To all dukes, marquises, counts, and other princes, as well as barons and other nobles established throughout Germany. The only-begotten Son of God descended from the highest heavens to the depths of the world, to rescue man from the snare of servitude into which the serpent's suggestion had cast him, clothed Himself in the garment of our mortality, wishing to extinguish the fires of eternal torment with the shedding of His own blood and to make His own, possessed by eternal death, possessors of everlasting life. Exercising the office of the mission entrusted to Him in the region of sinners, He sent the disciples He had chosen into the whole world to preach the gospel to every creature, instructing His vicar to sometimes call others to share the concern, where the debt of His office is prevented from being paid by bodily absence. Although the fullness of power has been committed to us, we cannot exceed the limits of human possibility, so that while we exercise the office entrusted to us in one part, we cannot execute it personally elsewhere, because the law of human condition does not allow the same person to execute the power entrusted to him by being simultaneously in diverse parts, nor does the law of nature permit one body to be encompassed in several places at the same time. Therefore, since the care of the governance we have undertaken constitutes us as debtors to all the faithful of Christ, lest we leave them unattended in negligence, we sometimes send suitable persons to them in our place, dispensing through them the remaining care, which we personally bear at present. Indeed, among other desires of our heart, ardently desiring the salvation of souls, the increase of ecclesiastical liberty, and peace to all the faithful of Christ, we diligently watch with zeal and employ the study of diligence as much as we can, so that laudably, with all impediments removed, they may come to fruition according to the fullness of our desire by the Lord's author, and the more fervently we desire the good state of those parts, the more ardently we desire that the progress of souls may come, that ecclesiastical liberty may thrive, and that the tranquility of peace may be preserved in your parts. Therefore, so that those parts may progress more in the devotion of God and the Church, because they have specially felt themselves to be refreshed by the office of visitation by the Apostolic See as a mother, behold, our beloved son, P., Cardinal Deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, a man indeed endowed with knowledge, adorned with honesty of morals, and distinguished by maturity of counsel, we have decided to send to those parts as an angel of peace, with the full office of legation committed to him, to uproot and destroy, to overthrow and scatter, to build and plant, as he shall see fit. Since we embrace him with the arms of special affection among our other brothers, we command and enjoin your community by apostolic writings, that you, kindly receiving him and treating him honorably, may humbly and devoutly attend to him, indeed rather to us in him, as the legate of the Apostolic See, by effectively fulfilling his warnings and precepts and whatever he shall command you on our behalf. Otherwise, the sentence he shall pronounce against the rebellious, we will hold firm and, by the Lord's authority, will make it be observed inviolably. Given at Lyon, on the Ides of March, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa universis ducibus, marchionibus, comitibus aliisque principibus per Alamanniam constitutis mandat ut P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diaconum cardinalem, legatum apostolicum, benigne recipiant et eius monitis pareant, cum plena potestate legationis ad partes illas destinatum. Dat. Lugduni, Idibus Martii, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot and convent of the Monastery of Morbach of the Order of Saint Benedict, of the diocese of Basel. Since, as we have learned, our beloved son, Master Johannes, canon of Lübenbach, has been captured and suffered grave damages by the enemies of the Church, we, wishing to favor him on account of this and at the request of our venerable brother, the bishop of Strasbourg, and the noble lord R. of Ufenberg, who have appealed to us on his behalf, have decided to kindly request and admonish your community, ordering that you provide for the said Master Johannes, out of reverence for the Apostolic See and ourselves, with a suitable benefice within your grant which is customarily assigned to secular clerics, if it is currently vacant or as soon as it becomes so. This is to be done notwithstanding any other letters we may have directed to you on behalf of others, which by the authority of these presents, etc., as in the next [document] up to: delayed. Otherwise, we give orders in our letters to our venerable brother, the bishop of Basel, to compel you to do so by ecclesiastical censure, the appeal being removed, after prior admonition. Dated as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati et conventui Morbacensibus mandat ut magistro Iohanni canonico Lubenbacensi, captivo et dampna perpesso ab inimicis Ecclesiae, in aliquo beneficio competenti, quod ad eorum collationem pertinet, provideant, sub censura ecclesiastica, si opus sit, compellendi. Dat. Lateran., anno III (1229).

**Translation to English:**

To P., Cardinal Deacon of St. George at Velum Aureum, legate of the Apostolic See. Our beloved son, the abbot of the monastery of Augia in the diocese of Constance, belonging directly to the Roman Church, has informed us through his petition that certain manifest adversaries of his, wickedly claiming that he has been disobedient and disrespectful to the Apostolic See, have contrived to require him to appear personally in our presence. This requirement has caused him great astonishment because, when previously he set out on a journey out of devotion to the aforementioned Church to visit the late H., King of the Romans, seeking his favor and support, he was captured and held by enemies of the same Church. Yet, his spirit did not wane but rather grew in strength to such an extent that, after being restored to freedom by God's grace, he did not and does not cease to resist the aforementioned enemies of the Church with all his powers through his relatives and friends. However, since he deserves gracious benevolence as recompense for such merits rather than injury, we command you to announce him restored to the grace of the Apostolic See and return him to his rightful state if, through diligent inquiry, you find that the same abbot is devoted to the aforementioned Church. Nullify any actions taken against him based on this false denunciation. But if you find him guilty, proceed with a mode of correction towards him that would provide us and the Church with suitable satisfaction. Given at Lyon, on the 16th day before the Kalends of June, in the fourth year (of our pontificate).

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali mandat, ut, si per inquisitionem constiterit abbatem Augensem ecclesiae devotum esse, eum ad gratiam sedis apostolicae restituat. 1246, Mai. 17. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

Desiring to gratify you for your devotion and through this favor to provide for others, we grant you, by the authority of these presents, the free faculty to confer upon suitable persons the prelacies, dignities, offices, prebends, and benefices of churches, both regular and secular, in the city and diocese of Parma, which are currently vacant or may become vacant in the future, regardless of any reservation or prohibition made or to be made by us or by others of any authority. You are also granted the power to forbid that anything regarding the aforesaid be presumed without your permission and to suppress opposers through ecclesiastical censure without appeal. This faculty is granted to you until the storm of persecution, which F., the former emperor, inflicts upon the Church, ceases — notwithstanding any letters obtained or to be obtained from anyone concerning these conferments or any indulgences granted by the Apostolic See to whomever, which might compel the acceptance of some individuals through letters that do not mention these matters and through which such favor might be hindered or delayed. For we declare null and void anything attempted by anyone in conferring or arranging the same without your permission or mandate. Given at Lyon, III Kalends of June, in the fourth year [of the pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa [Recipientis Nomen] facultatem concedit conferendi prelaturas, dignitates, personatus, prebendas et beneficia ecclesiarum civitatis et diocesis Parmensis idoneis personis, et prohibendi ne quid sine licentia eius fiat, donec persecutio F. quondam imperatoris conquiescat. 1246, Lugduni, III Kalendas Iunii, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Cervia. Hugolinus and Rolandinus, canons of the church of Prato in the diocese of Pistoia, have shown to us through their petition that after the passing of Zonchello, our chaplain and the provost of their church, other canons of the same church, although bound by the chain of excommunication for publicly celebrating divine services for F., son of the late Emperor Frederick, and other excommunicated individuals, presumed to elect Raynald, son of the noble Adelprandinus Cazacontis, a persecutor of the church, as the provost of their church through the abuse of secular power, even before the body of Zonchello had been buried. We command you, that if this is the case, to declare the election absolutely null, as it was rashly attempted by excommunicated persons, and to provide for the same church with a suitable candidate by our authority; contradictors etc. Given at Lyon, 22 June, in the fourth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Cerviensi mandat, ut electionem Raynaldi filii Adelprandini Cazacontis in prepositum ecclesie Pratensis, temere ab excommunicatis attemptatam, denuntiet nullam esse et eidem ecclesie de persona idonea provideat. Dat. Lugduni, X Kal. Iulii, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz. Although we are obliged to provide the aid of defense to anyone, we must particularly support those with the grace of our favor and defend them with the shield of apostolic protection from the attacks of the wicked, especially those who resist the tyranny of those raging against the mother church and oppose the efforts of its persecutors with all their strength and might, for the glory of the Redeemer. Indeed, your petition, read before us, stated that when the see of Hildesheim became vacant after the resignation of our venerable brother Conrad, the cantor and seven other canons of Hildesheim, not absolved from the sentences of suspension and excommunication which you had justly proclaimed against their chapter for denying you the payment of a fifth of their ecclesiastical revenues granted to you by us as a special favor, improperly requested H. of Gleichen, a fellow canon of theirs and minor in years, as bishop of Hildesheim, without convening the chapter or appointing a proper day for this purpose. However, afterwards, the aforementioned bishop and our beloved sons, the provost, dean, schoolmaster, treasurer, and sixteen other canons of the church of Hildesheim, having been absolved of the sentences which you had imposed on them, came together on a day legitimately appointed by them, and by invoking the grace of the Holy Spirit, canonically and concordantly elected their fellow canon, the prudent and honorable H., provost of Heiligenstadt, circumspect in spiritual and temporal matters, as their pastor and bishop. Once this election was duly confirmed by you under metropolitan authority, the elect, upon approaching the mentioned church, was honorably received by the entire clergy and people of Hildesheim, and obtained the castles and other fortifications of the same church. Nonetheless, the aforementioned H., improperly requested, supported by the power of noblemen such as the Duke of Brunswick, the Counts of Gleichen and of Kevernberg, and certain other supporters of the late Emperor Frederick, greatly disturbed the elected, by hostily invading the possessions of the Hildesheim church, to the detriment of the elect and the church. Therefore, wishing to provide for the peace of the aforementioned elect, who, as you assert, has steadfastly, beneficially, and powerfully supported you and the church in this matter, and to prevent grievances, we confirm and approve your process regarding this matter as prudent and just with apostolic authority. We command that you assist the elect with the aid of defense, and do not allow him to be unjustly troubled by the aforementioned H. or anyone else concerning the above matters, notwithstanding the aforesaid request. Given at Lyon, April 29, in the fourth year (of our pontificate).

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino mandat ut electum Hildesemensem ab indebita molestatione, per H. de Glichen et alios, defendat, electionem eius auctoritate apostolica confirmans. 1230, Apr. 29, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Ulric, archdeacon in Bevenhusen of the Church of Verden. As we have learned from our beloved daughters in Christ, the prioress and nuns of the monastery of Buostehuthe of the Order of Saint Benedict in the diocese of Verden, you have been appointed to the care and governance of the said monastery by our venerable brother, the bishop, and our beloved sons, the chapter of Verden, due to the merits of your integrity and honesty. We, moved by the devotion shown to this monastery by our beloved daughters in Christ, the noble women M., Margravine of Brandenburg, and M., Duchess of Brunswick and Lüneburg, who have implored us by their letters, grant you, by the authority of these presents, the faculty to receive your ecclesiastical revenues with the same integrity, except for daily distributions, for a period of three years while you are engaged in the care and governance of the same monastery, as if you were personally residing in the churches where you hold these revenues, notwithstanding any contrary custom of those churches. Given at Lyon, on the 13th day before the Kalends of July, in the fourth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Ulrico archidiacono Bevenhusen nuntiat se facultatem concessisse ad percipiendos proventus ecclesiasticos, etiam absente, dum monasterium Buostehuthe regit, non obstante consuetudine contraria. 1247, Iun. 19, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop and Chapter of Ravenna. It was presented before us on your behalf that, when you decided to grant a certain fief, which the late Ubertinus of Ravenna held from the Church of Ravenna, to the noble man Azzo, Marquis of Este, with the same agreements and conditions under which the said Ubertinus had held it, by our mandate, eventually, disputes and doubts arose between you and the said noble regarding these agreements and conditions. To resolve these doubts, twelve ancient and trustworthy men were jointly chosen by the parties, with an oath taken from both sides that the decision or declaration of these men would be inviolably observed by both parties. These men, guided by equity, reasonably clarified the aforementioned doubts. The parties jointly accepted this declaration as these matters are more fully contained in public instruments prepared on this matter. Therefore, inclined by your supplications, we, considering this declaration as reasonably made and willingly accepted by both parties, confirm it by apostolic authority and fortify it with the protection of this present writing. Let no one, therefore, etc., infringe our confirmation, etc. If anyone, etc. Given at Lyon, the 7th of the Kalends of July, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa archiepiscopo et capitulo Ravennatibus mandat ut declarationem per duodecim viros fide dignos de controversiis super feudo inter eos et Azonem marchionem Estensem factam, auctoritate apostolica confirmet. Datum Lugduni, VII Kalendas Iulii, anno quarto pontificatus.

**Translation to English:**

To the illustrious King of Cyprus, lord of the Kingdom of Jerusalem. We commend your diligent concern, which you have shown thus far in the conservation of the Kingdom of Jerusalem, with rightful praises in the Lord. As your efforts are highly necessary for the kingdom, we earnestly ask, advise, and encourage your majesty to labor with unwavering resolve in maintaining the good state of the kingdom, as you have done thus far, so that you may be deservedly commended by God and men. Know for certain that if peace is restored between the Church and its adversaries, who are also your enemies, we will ensure peace for you and your subjects, provided this is brought to our attention. Given at Lyon, on the 6th of July, in the fifth year. In the same manner to the noble lord of Beirut, bailiff of the Kingdom of Jerusalem.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa illustri regi Cypri, domino regni Ierosolimitani, commendat diligentiam in conservatione regni Ierosolimitani et hortatur ut in bono statu regni conservando perseveret. 1248, Iul. 6, Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To the provost and chapter of Basel. Since our beloved sons, the noble men C. and H., counts of Freiburg, have hitherto shown themselves devoted and obedient in the affairs of the Roman Church, we, wishing to show them the affection we have for them, have decided, inclined by their prayers, to request and admonish your entire community, commanding that you, out of reverence for the Apostolic See and for us, receive our beloved son Berthold of Horburg, a canon of Strasbourg and a relative of the said counts, into your canonry and brotherhood, and liberally confer upon him a prebend, should any be vacant in your church at present or as soon as the opportunity arises—despite any fixed number of canons fortified by oath or any firmness, or even if we have directed our letters to you concerning others, for whom we do not wish any prejudice to arise by the authority of these presents, or that the same Berthold is otherwise benefited, or any indulgence of the Apostolic See by which such a grace might be delayed. Otherwise, we have instructed our venerable brother, the bishop of Strasbourg, by our letters, to execute the apostolic mandate concerning this. Given at Lyon, on the Ides of June, in the fourth year.

Regesto in Latin:

Innocentius IV papa, preposito et capitulo Basiliensibus mandat, ut Bertholdum de Horburg, canonicum Argentinensem et consanguineum comitum de Vriburc, recipiant in canonicum et in fratrem, eique conferant prebendam vacuam. 1250, Iun. 13, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected Bishop of Olomouc. On behalf of our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of Bohemia, it was presented before us that, because you could not obtain peaceful possession of the bishopric of Olomouc, his land in Budsin had been placed under ecclesiastical interdict by our authority. The clerics of that land, fearing the king, recklessly celebrated divine services during the period of this interdict. Therefore, the aforementioned king humbly petitioned us to provide for them with paternal care, considering the multitude involved. Wherefore, we command that with our authority you grant a dispensation to those clerics, except for those who were the instigators of such transgression, regarding the irregularity they have incurred, imposing on them salutary penance. Given at Lyon, on the 6th of July, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa electo Olomucensi mandat, ut clericis Budsin, metu regis Boemiae interdicto ecclesiastico violato, auctoritate sua, exceptis transgressionis actoribus, super irregularitate contraxerunt dispenset. 1231, Iul. 6, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Tusculum, legate of the Apostolic See. 

We are beset by troubles on all sides, etc., as mentioned previously: it should be reconsidered. From this, it can be clearly understood how unfair and unreasonable it would seem if the honor of the Church, which is known to be endowed with such a great privilege of freedom, should be curtailed in those immunities which are known to be much less than the aforementioned ones in these times. If those barons, etc., as mentioned before: should be removed, we command by apostolic letter to your fraternity that you notify them, through yourself or another, after consulting with the prelates, to desist from such actions, explaining and urging them to do so more earnestly, and to attend the assembly of those prelates, who, as we have learned, must convene for this reason, removing any difficulties and delays, encouraging those prelates to stand firmly in defense of their liberties and rights, for which we offer them all possible counsel and aid, as it primarily concerns us as the head. Furthermore, since it seems that through the aforementioned actions attempted by the same barons not only ecclesiastical liberty but the state of the whole Church is being altered, and it is believed that this is being pursued by an enemy aspiring to subvert the faith, we wish and command with the counsel of our brothers that you should proceed in this manner: First, declare and have declared excommunicated all those who have enforced statutes made and customs, or rather abuses, introduced against the Church. Also, declare and have declared excommunicated those who made and wrote those statutes, as well as barons and lords of the lands and other nobles and powers, consuls, rectors, and councilors of places where such statutes or customs have been enacted or observed, as well as those who have presumed to judge or act publicly according to them. Also, declare and have declared that these statutes are of no effect and that the oaths taken to observe them are entirely unlawful and therefore those who have taken them are not bound to the oath of such an observation. Also, excommunicate all those who have entered or will enter the society of such a conspiracy or have procured or will procure the entrance of others unless they completely repent. Also, excommunicate all those who, for the observance of such statutes, will pay or collect or receive for themselves or another the hundredth part of their income, or who will induce or compel others to pay, or who have given or will give counsel, aid. Also, excommunicate all those who, on account of such a conspiracy, will hinder the prelates from exercising ecclesiastical jurisdiction in cases where it is their right by law or approved custom. Also, excommunicate all those who will impede, disturb, or harass those acting, responding, assisting, advocating, or judging in the ecclesiastical forum in the aforementioned cases, as well as those who will presume to harass their relatives in person or goods on account of this — notwithstanding any indulgences or privileges granted to any persons by the Apostolic See, that sentences of excommunication or interdict cannot be pronounced upon them or their lands without special permission from the said See. 

If some are found to be obstinate, let them know that they will be deprived of all privileges obtained from the Apostolic See and of any fiefs they hold from churches, and that their offspring will not be admitted to the clergy or ecclesiastical benefice or dignity. Clerics who remain with the aforementioned, unless they immediately after your public admonition withdraw from their service and counsel, will be stripped of all ecclesiastical benefits and even the privilege of clerical status. 

Given at [location].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Tusculano, apostolicae sedis legato, mandat ut barones et alii consuetudines contra ecclesiam introducentes excommunicentur et eorum statuta irrita nuntientur; clerici, si non secesserint, beneficiis priventur. Datum Anagniae, anno pontificatus nostri primo.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Ravenna. On your behalf, we have been humbly petitioned that, since certain possessions, which the monastery of St. Andrew in Ravenna holds from the Church of Ravenna, have been occupied by some citizens of Ferrara from the time of the outbreak of discord between the Church and the late Emperor Frederick, and from which the monastery has received nothing nor can receive anything since that time, we might grant you, from the benevolence of the Apostolic See, the fruits of those possessions which you believe can be extracted from the hands of those who currently hold them. We, therefore, inclined by your supplications, have decided to grant you, by the authority of these presents, the aforementioned fruits to be collected by you, as long as you can safely remain in your church once peace is restored in those parts by the grace of God — notwithstanding any simulated donation made concerning the aforementioned fruits. However, we do not wish that any prejudice may be generated in the future for the aforementioned monastery regarding these possessions through this concession. Let no one, therefore, etc., infringe our concession etc. Given at Lyon, 25 June, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa archiepiscopo Ravennati mandat, ut, ex parte sua supplicante, concedat ei fructus possessionum monasterii sancti Andreae de Ravenna ab civibus Ferrariensibus occupatarum, donec pace reformata in ecclesia sua secure possit commorari. Concessio facta nullo modo praeiudicium inferat monasterio. Datum Lugduni, VII Kal. Iulii, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Prefect of the City. Because it is fitting that due retribution be meted out to each according to their merits, it is proper that the faithful and devoted to the Church, particularly those tested by the needs of the present time, be rewarded with worthy prizes, and that the inconsistency of the unfaithful and disloyal be punished with due penalty, so that the reward of the former may encourage others to serve the Church and the punishment of the latter may deter others from daring to commit offenses. Hence, since the people of Tuscania, Vetralla, the lords of Vetulonia, and their men, having abandoned their allegiance to the Roman Church like degenerate sons, have inflicted grave harm on your castles, vassals, and other properties, we, in order not to leave these injuries against you unpunished, by the authority of these presents command that all such damages inflicted on you by the same people of Tuscania, Vetralla, and the lords of Vetulonia, or on their behalf, and whatever may be inflicted as long as they persist in infidelity, as well as all things taken from you by the aforementioned, be fully restored to you, and that they are not to be admitted to the grace of the Church until they have fully satisfied you regarding the aforementioned. And because the same people of Tuscania, Vetralla, and the lords of Vetulonia do not cease to attack and offend you and other faithful of the aforesaid Church, we grant you, by the same authority, that you cannot be sued by anyone concerning the offenses inflicted on the said rebels and also those you may inflict on them henceforth for this reason; from which we have determined to absolve you. In order that the purity of your faith may always shine more clearly, we admonish, urge, and exhort your nobility earnestly, commanding that you, armed with the promptness and strength of spirit, vigorously resist them and other rebels of the Church, remaining steadfast as usual in the devotion of the same Church, which plans to elevate you among its other sons with special favor and grace. Given at Lyon, 5th day before the Nones of May, in the fourth year [of our pontificate]. In the same manner to the noble men, the lords of New Vetulonia.

---

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa prefecto Urbis mandat, ut dampna ab infidelibus Tuscanensibus, Vetrallensibus, et dominis Tulfe veteris illata, integre restituantur; et concessit eum ab omnibus huiusmodi offensis absolvi. Lugduni, anno pontificatus quarti, Nonis Maii.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot and convent of St. George in the Black Forest of the order of St. Benedict, in the diocese of Constance. Desiring, at the request of the noble man Count Burkhard of Henneberg, who has petitioned us on behalf of his beloved cleric Walter, to provide said cleric with an ecclesiastical benefice, we have decided to exhort and admonish your community, instructing that out of reverence for the Apostolic See and ourselves, you should ensure that the aforementioned Walter is liberally provided with one of the churches under your collation, which are customarily assigned to secular clerics, should any be vacant at present or as soon as you have the opportunity, notwithstanding any similar provision we may have directed to you for others, or any indulgence of the Apostolic See that might obstruct such a favor. Otherwise, you are to know that we have instructed our beloved son Berthold of Bussnang, canon of Constance, through our letters, to compel you to do so, after a prior warning, by ecclesiastical censure and without appeal. Given at Lyon, on the seventh day before the Kalends of July, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati et conventui Sancti Georgii in Nigra Silva mandat ut Waltero clerico, precibus comitis Burkardi de Henneberg, de beneficio ecclesiastico provideant; alioquin mandatum est canonico Bertholdo de Bussnang ut eos per censuram ecclesiasticam compellat. Datum Lugduni, VII Kalendas Iulii, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To P., Cardinal Deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the apostolic see. Since, according to the diversity of times and places, ecclesiastical censure must sometimes be aggravated beyond the usual measure, as the quality of the excess and the malice of the day require, you should know that we have received from the report of some trustworthy persons that it would greatly benefit the business of the church, which is currently at hand, that in parts of Germany, in public places and other locations where people usually gather, certain religious persons should, by apostolic authority, impose excommunication on all those who, having once adhered to the church and sworn an oath in this regard, have turned back to serve Frederick, the former emperor, and his son Conrad, with nefarious audacity. Furthermore, their lands should be placed under ecclesiastical interdict, and in these same stations and places, it should be expressly forbidden that they, and all others who adhered to F. or C. after the sentence of deposition was passed on F., be admitted as witnesses or to other legal acts, nor should they have the customary benefit of defense from the church if they seek refuge there, since it is in vain for someone who violates the law to invoke the help of the law. In the said places and stations, under the threat of anathema, it is forbidden to presume to communicate with the adherents or supporters of the aforementioned F. or C. by buying or selling or in any other way. Clerics who strive with their poisonous slanders either to hinder the church’s business or to defame it, as much as they can, are to be suspended from office and benefice in the aforementioned places and stations, and the suspension should be announced both there and elsewhere. Therefore, we command that you, by our authority, take care to proceed in these matters as you see fit; any objectors etc. Given at Lyons, the second day before the Nones of June, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali, apostolicae sedis legato mandat ut in partibus Theutoniae excommunicationem et interdictum auctoritate apostolica imponat illis qui ad obsequia Friderici quondam imperatoris et Conradi nati eius reversi sunt. Dat. Lugduni, anno pontificatus quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Count of Artois. The Church of God has always held a firm and unwavering belief that it would find you ready and willing to provide great assistance whenever you deemed it necessary. Indeed, with much joy, we and our brothers have learned that this belief has reached the grace of fulfillment, as with a devout heart, upon hearing of the Church's necessity, you have committed yourself to its personal service, swiftly assembling a great military force through which both the cause of God may advance and the honor of the Church may be preserved. However, blessed son of grace, while this brings you increased renown and earns you eternal merit before the King of Heaven, the Church remains diligently concerned to pursue you and yours with gracious goodwill. We earnestly urge your nobility, imposing for the remission of sins, that you steadfastly maintain your pious intent, as inspired by divine grace, and with all your heart be vigilant for the glory of God, so that you may resist with courage those who despise and persecute the Church, causing them to feel ashamed and regretful for attempting to overthrow the state of ecclesiastical freedom. Furthermore, since we desire assistance to come to us in a way that is fruitful without burdening the provider, we wish that you neither embark on a journey nor send an army for the Church’s defense until you have understood the will of the Apostolic See through our envoy or special letters. Given as above. In the same way to the Count of Poitiers. In the same way to the Count of Anjou.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa comiti Atrebatensi mandatum dat, ut promptus sit ad resistendum persequentibus ecclesiam et ut, antequam se ad iter accingat, votum sedis apostolicae per nuntium aut litteras intelligat. Datum ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To John of Beaumont, chamberlain of the Kingdom of France. The renowned rectitude of your heart and the laudable purity of your mind, with which the Lord of virtues is known to have illuminated you, have been so manifestly revealed in recent days concerning the business of the Church, that we bear full joy in our heart, and plan to compensate you and yours with the grace of full favor at an opportune time, especially since, with God inspiring you, you have diligently endeavored with all your strength that a magnificent and triumphant aid may be provided by our dearest sons in Christ, P., the illustrious king, and .. the queen of France, and the noble men, the king’s brothers, to the troubled Church in its persecution. However, since through the greatness of this merit a future reward of eternal glory shall be your gift from the divine clemency, we have thought it fit to affectionately ask and admonish your nobility in the Lord, enjoining it upon you for the remission of your sins, that you may strive to so conduct the devotion that has been infused into you from above towards the Church, so that you may rejoice at the advancement of the Church to a prosperous state through the support of your devotion as time progresses, and that the Church may be obliged to you and your descendants for all things that are for your convenience and honor, the tyrant facing true shame for having unjustly thought to persecute the Church and nullify the glory of the faith, which the only-begotten of the living God established in his blood. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Iohanni de Bellomonte, camerario regni Franciae, gratias agit pro auxilio ecclesiae tributo et hortatur ad perseverandam devotionem in remissionem peccaminum, promittens futuram retributionem gloriae sempiternae. Dat. ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot and convent of Corvey of the order of Saint Benedict in the diocese of Paderborn. We have diligently read and inspected the privilege of our predecessor Pope Leo of happy memory, and we have caused its text to be transcribed and sealed, which is as follows: Leo, servant of the servants of God, to Charlemagne, Emperor of the Romans. Rejoicing entirely in your pious petition, we do not delay to grant what you request. Therefore, we decree that this Mount Eresburg, which you have conquered and offered to God along with all of Saxony, and which you have consecrated through us to Saint Peter, is to be free from all human power and subject only to the authority of the brothers gathered there for the service of Christ. So that they may not suffer any hindrance in this and so that no invaders of your kingdom may prepare any confidence for rebellion, we forbid, under the anathema of Saint Peter and by our authority, that anyone may ever place military garrisons on this mount or dare to seize the lands or tithes granted by you around the mount within the two Saxon realms that you have assigned there. To those who preserve this, let there be peace from God the Father; to those who violate it, excommunication and eternal separation from the company of the blessed. Given at Eresburg by the hand of John, librarian and chancellor of the Roman Church, on the 24th of December, in the fourth year of Lord Leo III, the seventh indiction, on the day of the dedication of the chapel in Eresburg. Given at Lyon, on the 11th of June, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa abbati et conventui Corbegensibus privilegium Leonis III papae pro monte Eresburg confirmat, ut sit liber ab omni humana potestate et sub anathema sancti Petri defendatur. Datum Lugduni, III Idus Iunii, anno IIII.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Strasbourg. It has been presented to us on your behalf that we have instructed, through our letters, the abbess and convent of the Monastery of Seckingen, of the Order of Saint Augustine in the Diocese of Constance, to provide our beloved son Walter, a cleric and nephew of our beloved son, the provost of Speyer, and a canon of Strasbourg, whose relatives and even he himself are said to have labored beneficially in the affairs of the church, with a suitable ecclesiastical benefice that belongs to their granting and is customarily assigned to secular clerics, with certain executors appointed for this purpose. However, disregarding our mandate, these abbess and convent ignored it, and the executors, using apostolic authority, granted the Church of Ulm, which belongs to their granting and is customarily assigned to secular clerics and is known to have become vacant, to the same cleric, having him inducted into the corporeal possession of the same church by the archdeacon of the place. Since the aforementioned abbess and convent are said to have rashly granted the same church to Albert of Habsburg, a canon of Strasbourg, whose brother and uncle and several other relatives adhered to the late Emperor Frederick against the church, we, holding what was properly done by the aforesaid executors as valid and agreeable, command your fraternity that, if it is so, you make the said Walter enjoy possession of that church—notwithstanding that the aforementioned abbess and convent presumed regarding the said church, with no letters prejudicial to truth and justice having been obtained from the apostolic see by the same Albert with the truth concealed—contradictors, etc. Given at Lyon, June 3, in the fourth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Argentinensi mandat, ut Walterum clericum, cui executores ecclesiam de Ulmon contulerunt, in possessione eiusdem faciat gaudere, non obstante quod abbatissa et conventus Seconiensis ecclesiam eidem Alberto de Hebesburc temere contulerunt. 1246, Iunii 3, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of Saint Gall in the diocese of Constance. Wishing to pursue with special grace and favor our dear son, Henry, a cleric from Schaffhausen, considering the nobleman Rudolf of Hewin, who was recently captured by Conrad, son of the late Emperor Frederick, due to his devotion to the Apostolic See and is still detained in Conrad's prison, as well as Rudolf's brother, who humbly petitioned us on his behalf, and also in recognition of Henry’s own merit, who is said to be assisted by his honorable conduct and knowledge of letters to obtain the grace of the same See, we command that you, with his supporting merits, grant him dispensation by our authority so that he may freely and lawfully receive and retain personates, dignities, and other ecclesiastical benefices, even if they have the care of souls and are offered to him canonically, notwithstanding the constitution of the general council, up to the extent that you consider expedient according to God and his merits require; provided that personates, dignities, and benefices are not neglected in what is due, etc. Given at Lyons, 4th of July, in the fifth year. In the same manner to the same abbot for Walter of Kilthein, cleric.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati Sancti Galli Constantiensis diocesis mandat ut Henrico clerico de Schaffhausen dispensationem concedat, ut personatus, dignitates et alia beneficia ecclesiastica recipere et retinere possit, constitutione generalis concilii non obstante. 1231, Iul. 4, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Patriarch of Jerusalem, legate of the apostolic see, the Archbishop of Tyre, and the Bishop of Sidon. Our venerable brother, the Bishop of Acre, has shown us by his petition that the late Theobald, Bishop of Acre, his predecessor, at the insistence of the Pisans who were residing in the city of Acre at that time, elevated the chapel of Saint Peter of the Pisans in Acre to the status of a parish church and made all the Pisans residing in the said city parishioners of that church, causing great harm to the Church of Acre. Since the Pisans, due to their adherence to the late Emperor Frederick against the church, should be deprived of all ecclesiastical privileges, grace, and honor, we command that, notwithstanding any compositions or agreements made between them and the Bishops of Acre, whoever they were at the time, and any confirmations, indulgences, or privileges obtained from the apostolic see, the said church should be reduced to a chapel, as it was before, and that you inform the same Pisans, who are deprived of all these things, that they should receive ecclesiastical sacraments from the Church of Acre and obey and attend to the bishop as their ordinary, compelling them, having given prior warning, by ecclesiastical censure, notwithstanding any appeal. If not all, then at least two of you. Given at Lyons, June 10, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa patriarche Ierosolimitano, archiepiscopo Tyrensi et episcopo Sydoniensi mandat, ut capellam sancti Petri Pisani Acconensem in statum pristinum reducant, Pisanosque, qui Friderico quondam imperatori contra ecclesiam adheserunt, privatos omnibus privilegiis, sacramenta ab ecclesia Acconensi recipere compellant. 1246, Iun. 10, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Constance. Since, as we have received from your report, some abbots and abbesses, provosts, and other prelates of both religious and secular churches in your diocese presume to offer certain procurations and other services to Conrad, son of the late Emperor Frederick, by the authority of these presents, we grant you the power to punish them for this with sentences of excommunication and suspension and other censures as you see fit, as well as removal from monasteries and prelatures and deprivation of their benefices. You may also institute others whom you recognize to be zealous in the devotion to the Church and not inept in its business in the same abbeys, prelatures, and benefices, and freely excommunicate, suspend, and place under ecclesiastical interdict the persons of Cistercians and other religious, as you see fit for this business, notwithstanding any privileges or indulgences obtained from the Apostolic See; contradictors, etc. Given at Lyon, 10th June, in the fourth year [of our pontificate].

To the same. Your fraternity has informed us that certain Hermits and some other abbots of your diocese, because they are not immediately subject to Conrad, son of the late Emperor Frederick, although they are known to be subject to his supporters in temporal matters, refuse to observe the interdict in their monasteries and churches and other places belonging to them, according to the arbitrary will of their own, withdrawing themselves from the support of the general business. Therefore, we grant your fraternity the authority of these presents to compel them to observe such interdict and to offer obsequies and other services for this business by sentences of excommunication, suspension, and other means, as well as removal from their prelatures, setting aside any appeal, and to freely institute in their abbeys persons suitable and useful for the business of the Church, as you see fit for this business, notwithstanding, etc. Given at Lyon, 10th June, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Constantiensi mandat, ut abbates et alii prelati diocesis suae, qui Friderici nati quondam imperatoris fautores sunt, per excommunicationem et alias censuras puniat, et personas ecclesiae devotas in eorum loco instituat; insuper, ut ipsos Hermitas et abbates interdictum observare cogat. 1230, Iun. 10, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the archbishops and bishops, abbots and priors, and other prelates of churches, and to all who have gathered in Paris or elsewhere for the honor of God and the Church.

We are surrounded by distress, as we consider the cruel impiety of the persecutor of the Church and his efforts to devour it with all his might, both through himself and his members. What pierces us more deeply is the sting from those whom we, as Catholics, placed great trust in, believing that both faith and devotion flourished among them, and whose ancestors, fervent in faith and sincere in devotion, not only defended the Church from others but also enriched it with wealth and many privileges of liberty. These are now conspiring against the Church with new and utterly unprecedented inventions. It is no wonder we feel this pain, particularly because of the harmful example it sets for other nations and because the offenses of friends wound more deeply, as the Lord testifies through the prophet: "If my enemy had reviled me, I could have borne it."

Indeed, the current afflictions, insults, and disturbances the Church endures are sufficient, as it is continually troubled by the enemy sowing weeds everywhere. There was no need for certain barons of France to add affliction to affliction, disturbing it with new regulations or rather derelictions. As we have heard with pain and wonder, they seek to reduce the Church, which regenerated them as sons from the womb of holiness and continually offers the spotless lamb to God the Father for their salvation, into servitude. They no longer wish to be called sons of the free woman but of the bondwoman, attempting miserably to enslave the spouse of the eternal King, who freed them with His own blood from perpetual servitude. By common conspiracy and conspiracy against its liberty, they have established, it is said, many grave and enormous statutes that swallow the law and custom of said liberty, diminish the Church's honor, cause scandal, and generate dangers for souls.

If the nature of the business is carefully considered, if the state of affairs is weighed with any thought, it was not expedient for the honor or valor of these barons to attack the holy Church at such a critical juncture. For the noble, when unbounded by divine fear, are accustomed from a certain magnanimity to assist the oppressed, even if past wrongs were strong, and offer a helping hand in necessity. However, if the said barons had carefully considered that Charlemagne, wishing to honor the Church from which he received all honor, decreed by perpetual law that all subject to its jurisdiction should inviolably observe the statute issued by Emperor Theodosius for the Church's liberty—that is, that anyone having a dispute, whether the petitioner or at any stage of the process, or when an affair is being argued, or when judgment has begun to be pronounced, if they choose the judgment of the sacred see's bishop, should immediately, without any doubt, even if the opposite party objects, be directed to the bishops' judgment with the litigants' speech, and all cases treated by praetorian and even civil law should be concluded by the bishops' sentences, and the matter settled by their judgment should never again be reconsidered by anyone—they might discern for themselves, based on sound reasoning, how unjust and absurd it seems if the honor of the Church, known to be endowed with such a great privilege of liberty, should be diminished in our times in those immunities known to be much lesser than the previously mentioned ones.

If these barons were to consider that all who presume to establish statues against ecclesiastical liberty are by that very fact bound by the sentence of excommunication, perhaps they would not have proceeded to such actions nor persisted in them. But because perhaps knowledge of this did not reach them, to remove all excuse of ignorance and that they were not warned, we wish it to be announced and explained to them by some of you whom you consider suitable, and to induce them diligently with solicitous admonitions and exhortations to desist from such actions. If, by chance, the aforesaid barons cannot be swayed, retaining something of the leaven of wickedness blown into their ears, since it is written: “Let not prosperity lift you up nor adversity cast you down,” you, hoping in Him who dissolves the bands of wickedness and the bundles that weigh down with His power, and considering that the Church, against which even the gates of hell shall not prevail, is accustomed to be expanded in tribulation according to prophetic word, fortify yourselves in the defense of ecclesiastical liberty, as the prophet exemplifies a fortified city and iron column, fearing nothing at all; but armed with the steadfastness of heart, which no arrow of persecution can penetrate, manfully oppose yourselves as a wall for the house of the Lord, confidently using that liberty which you have hitherto possessed and used, and proceeding against rebels as appropriate, proclaiming the statutes attempted against eccles

**Translation to English:**

To the provost and chapter of the church of Grandeval in the diocese of Basel. It should be a heartfelt desire that what is pleasing to us may also bring you the reward of special grace. Indeed, our beloved son, the noble lord, the Count of Newcastle, is said to be earnestly dedicated, along with his men, to increasing the honor of the church through their service. Because of this, we, pursuing his person with a benevolent affection, have deemed it appropriate to admonish and instruct your community, commanding that you admit our beloved son H. de Rinach, the special cleric of the said count, who is commended for his noble lineage, morals, and knowledge, and who is said to have deserved the gift of our gracious favor through the sincere devotion of his service, as a brother and canon out of reverence for the Apostolic See and for us. This is to be done as stated above in the 40th chapter, without hindrance arising from any preexistent benefice or any special indulgence that should be mentioned in our letters. You should fulfill our request and command in such a way that, as he rejoices in obtaining what he desires in this matter, the sincerity of your devotion will be worthy of praise and favor in our eyes. Otherwise, we have instructed our beloved son, the abbot of Capella in the diocese of Constance, through our letters, to execute the apostolic mandate in this matter; dissenters, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 16th day before the Kalends of August, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa preposito et capitulo ecclesiae Grandevallensis Basiliensis diocesis mandat ut H. de Rinach, clericum comitis Novicastri, in canonicum admittant. 1247, Jul. 17, Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To O. de Falke, Bishop of Tusculum, legate of the apostolic see. Since at present the Holy Land is in need of the aid of warriors, and our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of France, not by human agency but rather by divine operation, having taken up the sign of the life-giving cross, is preparing powerfully and valiantly to come to its aid: we, wishing to favorably assist and profit him in this endeavor, command that through the cities and dioceses of Cambrai, Liège, Toul, Utrecht, Metz, and Verdun, on our behalf, you prohibit and have prohibited that no one presume to absolve anyone from those regions from the vow of the Jerusalem cross by the authority of our letters, or to alter that vow to something else, compelling those who presume otherwise to wholly desist from such presumption by ecclesiastical censure, with an admonition given and appeal removed, and nonetheless decreeing null and void whatever may be attempted otherwise by the presumption of anyone — notwithstanding any letters obtained or yet to be obtained from the apostolic see in general or special form, by which this might be impeded, even if express mention of them is not made here. Given at Lyons, July 5, in the fifth year [of the pontificate].

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa O. de Falke episcopo Tusculano mandat ut in civitatibus et diocesibus Cameracensi, Leodiensi, Tullensi, Traiectensi, Metensi et Virdunensi prohibeat absolutionem vel commutationem voti crucis Ierosolimitane. 1234, Iul. 5. Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To the Bishop of Basel. As your fraternity has informed us, the priory of Abelchilche of the Order of Saint Benedict in your diocese, which in the past used to flourish with an abundance of spiritual and temporal goods, has now fallen into such poverty due to the malice of the noble man Ulrich, Count of Ferrette, who, adhering to the late Emperor Frederick and being a known supporter against the Church, has enormously squandered and consumed the goods of the same priory, illegally converting them for the expenses in service of the said Frederick, to the detriment of his own salvation and causing significant harm to the aforementioned priory, that now the people residing there, although they are fewer than before, are unable to be provided for from its goods. Therefore, you have requested from us an appropriate remedy for this situation. Having full confidence in the Lord in your discretion and desiring with paternal care to prevent the loss of the said priory, we command that you assign the governance of the same priory to such a person who is willing and able to recover and protect its goods and to diligently and vigorously maintain it in good condition; those who oppose, etc. Given at Lyon, the 16th day before the Kalends of August, in the 5th year of our pontificate.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX episcopo Basiliensi mandat, ut prioratum de Abelchilche ordinis sancti Benedicti, ab Ulrico comite Phiretarum enormiter dilapidatum, tali persone committat gubernandum, quae bona eius eripere et tueri possit. Datum Lugduni, XVI Kal. Augusti, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Chapter of Salzburg. We, having been raised to the highest office of the Apostolic See, presume to govern the universal church as the vicars on earth of Jesus Christ, the only begotten Son of God, who reigns eternally in heaven. Although we are unworthy, we carry out His duties on earth. This, however, fills us with great fear, and as we consider the burden of the responsibilities that weigh upon us, our mind is indeed struck with awe. For the duty we have taken upon ourselves demands the constant diligence of the pastoral office, and since we are aware of our own insufficiency, we have reason to fear that we may not execute the fullness of the power entrusted to us as completely as we should. Although we strive diligently to protect the flock of the Lord entrusted to us, dismissing the slumber of negligence from the eyes of our hearts, we maintain firm hope and trust that He who willed us to become His vicars will continually grant us the grace of his strength to carry the burden laid upon our shoulders effectively. We tirelessly endeavor to care for all churches, attending to their needs and safeguarding their welfare, especially by ensuring that their governance is entrusted to those who will lead to spiritual and temporal growth. This is particularly true for those churches known to be directly subject to the Roman Church, since, the more closely they are subject to it, the more diligently we are bound to consider them.

Indeed, as your church is without a pastor, acknowledging its prominence and influence among other churches in that region, we do not wish it to remain without a prelate for long, as its vacancy would be more perilous due to the greater care required for the many subjects under its temporary pastor's charge. Therefore, desiring to provide it with a bishop whose industry and diligence match the weight and honor of such a position, especially since we have already instructed all cathedral chapters in Germany, both through our letters and through our beloved son, the elected Bishop of Ferrara, the apostolic legate, not to presume to elect pastors for their churches without our counsel and consent when they happen to be vacant, we have, with the advice of our brethren and the fullness of our power, appointed our beloved son, Bruccard, the elected Archbishop of Salzburg, formerly the Provost of Friesach, a man of proven life, great knowledge, and known circumspection, much dearer and more acceptable to us and our brethren due to his merits of probity and devotion, as archbishop and pastor of your church. We decree null and void anything else that you may have attempted concerning the provision of the same church, firmly hoping and trusting that, with the Lord's help, he will laudably increase the well-being of the said church in spiritual and temporal matters through his diligent care.

Therefore, we command you to humbly receive the said elected archbishop as a brother and pastor of your souls, rendering him due obedience and reverence by effectively implementing his salutary warnings and mandates. Otherwise, the sentence which he may duly pass, etc., shall be observed. Given at Lyon, February 25, in the fourth year of our pontificate. In the same manner, the clergy of the city and diocese of Salzburg. In the same manner, all the suffragans of the Church of Salzburg. In the same manner, all the counts, barons, castellans, and other nobles, vassals of the Church of Salzburg, we command, with suitable modifications, that they humbly render their due service to the said elected archbishop, implementing his salutary warnings and mandates effectively. Otherwise, the sentence, etc., as above. In the same manner, the people of the city and diocese of Salzburg. In the same manner, the elected bishops of Gurk, Regensburg, and Seckau, as above, with suitable modifications. Hence, we enjoin all the suffragans of the Church of Salzburg, the chapter of Salzburg, the clergy of the city and diocese of Salzburg by our letters to execute the above mandate. Therefore, we command that if the said suffragans, chapter, and clergy neglect to execute our mandate, you, with prior admonition, compel them to do so by our authority, removing any appeal. If not all, etc., two of you, etc.: In the same manner, to the elected Bishop of Ferrara, apostolic legate. In the same manner, to the elected bishops of Gurk, Regensburg, and Seckau, as above. Hence, we enjoin all the counts, barons, castellans, and other nobles, vassals of the Church of Salzburg, as well as the ministerials of the same church by our letters, to execute the above mandate. Therefore, we command that if the said counts, barons, castellans, other nobles, and ministerials of the Church of Salzburg neglect to execute our mandate, you, with prior admonition, compel them to do so by eccles

**Translation to English:**

To the archbishops and bishops established throughout Ireland. Amidst various difficulties etc. as above in letter LXXXI up to: may rise from tranquility. Therefore, with the counsel of our brothers, we have resolved to ordain that from the incomes and ecclesiastical pensions of Italian clerics, which they have in Ireland up to a hundred marks and below, a fourth part, and of those more than a hundred marks sterling which they possess in the same place, half for one year, counting from the next feast of the Nativity of Blessed John the Baptist onwards, may be assigned to the aid of the aforementioned church: we earnestly request and encourage your community, by giving a directive, that each of you should ensure that a fourth and a half of the said incomes and even pensions held by the said clerics in your bishoprics are collected into your hands in the name of the aforementioned aid according to the form noted above. If it happens that any of you doubts whether those who are known to hold incomes or pensions in his bishopric have other incomes or pensions in the bishoprics of others, he should ensure that only those incomes and pensions established in his own cities and dioceses are collected, so that the church may not be deceived in this matter, and it would be better for him to resign the surplus than to demand a deficiency; and, if there be any contradictors or rebels etc.; — notwithstanding any indulgence, even if the present letters do not explicitly mention it —; you are to report back to us as soon as you can the amount of what has come into your hands from the aforesaid incomes and pensions, faithfully. Given at Lyons, the 3rd day before the Calends of June, in the fourth year. In the same manner, to the bishops established throughout the kingdom of Scotland up to: which they hold in the kingdom of Scotland etc. In the same manner, to the archbishops and bishops established throughout the kingdom of England up to: which they hold in the kingdom of England etc. In the same manner, to the archbishops and bishops established throughout the kingdom of France, as in the kingdom of France etc. In the same manner, to the archbishops and bishops established throughout the kingdom of Germany, as in the kingdom of Germany etc. In the same manner, to the archbishops and bishops established throughout Provence, as in Provence etc. In the same manner, to the archbishops and bishops established throughout Gascony, as in Gascony etc. In the same manner, to the archbishops and bishops established throughout Burgundy, as in Burgundy etc. In the same manner, to the archbishops and bishops established throughout Spain, as in Spain etc.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopis et episcopis in Ybernia constitutis mandat, ut quartam vel medietatem redditibus et pensionibus Italicorum clericorum accipiant ad subsidium ecclesiae deputandam, et de his quantitatem fideliter rescribant. 1230, Mai. 30, apud Lugdunum.

**Translation to English:**

To the Margrave of Meissen. We are greatly amazed and disturbed that, although the iniquities and crimes of the late Emperor Frederick are known to all, both to those nearby and those far away, and have reached all corners of the world due to his cunning, cruelty, and deceit, you, who as a wise and learned man should not ignore all this, wish to taint your house and descendants with his accursed blood, being a Catholic prince and one of the great ones of the world. However, although, out of regard both for you and for our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious king of Bohemia, your father-in-law, who has highly recommended you to us, we wish to grant you special favor, we direct our letters under specific form to our beloved son, P., cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the Apostolic See, regarding the relaxation of certain sentences passed on this occasion, as you requested. Yet, embracing your person with special favor and grace, we consider you to be a great and principal defender of the Church, and we sincerely counsel you, since you are dear to us, we ask and beseech you prudently to consider that your ancestors steadfastly adhered to the devotion of the Apostolic See, to whom you ought to succeed, as much in the imitation of devotion as by the propagation of blood. And consider that the aforementioned Frederick aspires, by whatever means he can, not only to the subversion of faith and the Church, against which he continually plots with nefarious dealings, but also to completely destroy or at least to reduce to extreme or vile servitude all the nobles and powerful. Therefore, do not hesitate to send back his daughter, with whom your son is said to have contracted marriage, in fact, to him who sent her, for the sake of divine and Apostolic See and our reverence. Be assured that, however much we intend to pursue your person with the prerogative of special favor, we could not tolerate the aforementioned marriage with good conscience. Therefore, strive to fulfill our requests quickly and effectively, so that merit and praise in the eyes of God, in whose injury and to the grave detriment of his name such a marriage would proceed at this time, may grow, and so that you may bind the Apostolic See and the universal Church more closely to you and yours. For we, who desire your salvation and progress, if you conform to our good pleasure and commands in this matter, have decided that you should be absolved from any promise or pecuniary obligation or any other made to the aforesaid Frederick or to anyone else in his name on account of the aforementioned betrothal. Given at Lyon, on the Nones of May, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa marchionem Misnensem monet et rogat, ut filium ab infausto coniugio cum filia Friderici quondam imperatoris revocet, ne domum suam scelerato sanguine inquinet, promittens eum ab obligationibus foederis absolvere. 1241, Mai. 7, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Morinensis. On behalf of the beloved sons, the aldermen and the community of the town of Ypres, it was brought before us that in the town itself, where nearly two hundred thousand people reside, there are only four parish churches, whose regular canons hold the care of souls, and in each of them, only one canon customarily stays overnight. As a result, they suffer not a little spiritual detriment and request that both the number of churches and clergy in the town be increased.

They also complained to the Apostolic See about certain grievances, namely that the dean of Christianity and the rectors of the churches in the same place of the Morinensis diocese, seeking their own gain, not those of Jesus Christ, do not allow multiple marriages to be celebrated at the same time and on the same day under one mass celebration, so that they might extort more offerings. If people from different parishes of the same town want to marry each other, they never allow such marriage to be consummated unless they first receive from each contracting party a certain amount of money in the name of offerings. If three consecutive holidays happen to occur when weddings should be celebrated, they maliciously prohibit the banns from being announced during these solemnities unless it is according to their own will, to the prejudice and grievance of the people.

They also, putting no limit on their greed, do not allow, if several men die at the same time in the same town, their bodies to be given ecclesiastical burial under one mass celebration, due to a certain pernicious custom, unless an offering is made for each one, to the peril of their souls and the scandal of many. Furthermore, the said people asked that a remedy be provided for some of their needs, for with the mills of the town of Ypres unable to grind without wind, which, even if they had favorable wind every day for grinding, would scarcely suffice for the multitude of people, they sought to be allowed to grind whenever the wind would be suitable for grinding.

Moreover, if they happen to be bound by a sentence of excommunication for the same offense, they wish to be obligated for the payment of only one penalty, if a penalty must be paid. Furthermore, since there is a certain custom for weddings in the same town called "kergankeh" in the vernacular, for which both poor and rich exhaust themselves in vain glory through labors and expenses, so much so that some spend more on such things than they receive as a dowry for the woman, they asked that they not be compelled to perform this custom anymore.

Wherefore, they humbly petitioned us to provide for them in these matters with the kindness of the Apostolic See. Therefore, wishing to consult their benefit in such a way that the justice of others is not harmed, we command you to diligently inquire into the truth of all the above-mentioned matters and faithfully report to us what you find, so that instructed by your report, we may do what is just. Given at Lyon, 11th Kalends of June, in the fourth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa (Honorius III) episcopo Morinensi mandat, ut super querelis scabinorum et universitatis ville Yprensis de augmentando numero ecclesiarum et clericorum, avaritia decani et rectorum ecclesiarum, et aliis gravaminibus diligenter inquirat et nobis fideliter rescribat. Datum Lugduni, XI Kalendas Iunii, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the illustrious Queen of France. We trust that the Queen of Heaven intercedes for the lamenting voice of the Church, and so the kindness of the eternal King has inclined His ear, such that our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious king, and our beloved sons, your noble sons the counts, have resolved to magnificently aid the Church personally. Inflamed with the fire of the Holy Spirit, you have resolved from your royal heart that you yourself wish to take up the journey with an army to magnificently support the Church. **Translation to English:**

To the same (recipient). Since it is very expedient for the pressing business at hand that peace and concord be restored among the faithful of the empire, we command that you intervene with the counsel of our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, whose concern it is, to restore peace between our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Mainz, and the noble Duke of Brabant, so that we may justly commend your effort and diligence in this matter. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa [recipienti ignoto] mandat, ut cum consilio regis Romanorum inter archiepiscopum Maguntinum et ducem Brabantie pacem reformet, ita ut studium et sollicitudinem ipsius commendari possit. [Datum ut supra].

Translation to English:

To the same. By the authority of these presents, we command you to publicly announce and cause to be announced, in all places where it seems expedient, that all those who have presumed or will presume, publicly or privately, to assist Frederick, the former emperor, or his sons or their party, after the sentence of deposition was pronounced against Frederick, are excommunicated. This announcement should be made with bells ringing and candles lit on every Sunday and feast day; those contradicting, etc. Given as above.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa eidem mandat ut omnes, qui post sententiam depositionis in Fredericum imperatorem quondam eiusque filios aut partem eorum adstiterint, excommunicatos publice nuntiet. Datum ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the men of the castle of Cassia, our faithful ones, of the diocese of Spoleto. The earnestness of your devotion deserves that we favorably accede to your requests. Hence, being inclined by your devoted supplications, we grant you by the authority of these presents that you may be exempt from the payment of fodrum, which you owe annually to the Roman Church, for up to six years. Therefore, let no one etc. of our concession etc. Given at Lyon, on the 8th day before the Ides of January, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa hominibus castri de Cassia Spoletane diocesis concedit ut a prestatione fodri, quod ecclesie Romane annuatim debent, usque ad sex annos sint immunes. 1248, Jan. 6. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To P., Cardinal Deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the Apostolic See. Since our beloved daughter in Christ, the noblewoman, the Duchess of Austria, has sought our approval for contracting a marriage, we, wishing her to be matrimonially united with someone suitable for her and devoted to the Roman Church, command that you provide effective help and effort for contracting a marriage between her and our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, or another suitable and devoted to her and to us. Given at Lyon, January 21, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali mandat, ut opem ferat ad matrimonium contrahendum inter ducissam Austrie et regem Romanorum vel alium idoneum. 1231, Jan. 21. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To O. de Falke. Berger 3340. To .. the abbot of the monastery of Indensist in the diocese of Cologne. By the authority of these presents, we command you to absolve our venerable brother .. the archbishop of Cologne from all sentences of excommunication, both of canon and of man, on our behalf. Given at Lyon, on the 16th day before the Kalends of November, in the 5th year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa O. de Falke mandatum mittit, ut archiepiscopum Coloniensem ab excommunicationibus absolutum faciat. 1257, Oct. 17, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz. Since a matter of discord, as we have learned, has arisen between you and our beloved son, the noble man, the Duke of Brabant, concerning a certain land, we have deemed it appropriate to earnestly request and urge your fraternity, commanding that for the reverence of us and the Apostolic See, you should do what our beloved son, P., deacon cardinal of Saint George at Velum Aureum, legate of the Apostolic See, has decided to ordain, and do not make yourself difficult in this matter for the honor of the Church. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino mandat ut, ob reverentiam Apostolicae Sedis, faciat quod P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diaconus cardinalis, legatus sedis apostolicae, ordinaverit super discordia cum duce Brabantie. Datum ut supra, anno pontificatus.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Bamberg. Inclined by the prayers of your fraternity, we grant you the authority by the present letters to absolve, according to the form of the Church, the treasurer of Bamberg and others to whom you have entrusted the management of the affairs of the Bamberg church, from the sentence of excommunication, if they have incurred or will incur it by associating with the supporters of Frederick, the former emperor, for the purpose of handling matters and obtaining truces for the benefits of the said church. Given at Lyon, on the third day before the Nones of October, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX episcopo Bambergensi scribit, quod facultatem absolvendi thesaurarium et alios ab excommunicationis sententia, pro utilitatibus ecclesiae Bambergensis communicando fautoribus Friderici quondam imperatoris incurrenda, concedit. 1231, Oct. 5. Datum Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To the same (recipient). Desiring to impose ecclesiastical censure against those who show contempt for the keys of the Church, we command that in all cities of Lombardy, which sided with the late Emperor Frederick or his sons, after the sentence of excommunication was pronounced against him and his supporters, you ensure that baptism for infants and ecclesiastical burial for the deceased be prohibited, as long as these cities persist in such obstinacy. However, you shall establish an appropriate place outside these cities to which infants to be baptized may be brought, as you see fit; those who oppose this, etc. Given as above.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa mandat episcopo Mediolanensi ut in omnibus civitatibus Lombardiae, quae cum quondam imperatore Frederico vel eius filiis se tenuerunt, baptismum parvulis et sepulturam ecclesiasticam decedentibus prohibeat, dum in pertinacia perseverant, tamen locum idoneum extra civitates statuat pro baptizandis parvulis. 1238, Datum ut supra.

Translation to English:

To John of Hunoldisburch and Conrad of Wissinohrn, brothers of the Order of Preachers. Since it was proposed to us, on behalf of our beloved sons, the noble men of Swabia, devotees of the Church, that you have incurred the animosity of some, both religious and others, while you have diligently pursued the affairs of the universal Church in the regions of Germany, we, not wishing you to suffer loss where you have deserved benefit and honor, grant you the full authority by these presents to move to another region where the rule of the blessed Augustine is observed, upon the completion of these affairs, should your brothers wish to impose any burden upon you—notwithstanding any letters or indulgences granted or to be granted to your order by the Apostolic See. Therefore, let no one etc. of our concession etc. Given at Lyon, on the Nones of October, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa Iohanni de Hunoldisburch et Corrado de Wissinohrn, fratribus ordinis Praedicatorum, facultatem concedit transeundi ad aliam regionem post negotia ecclesiae in Theotonia peracta, si fratres onus eis imponere voluerint, non obstantibus indulgentiis Apostolicae Sedis. Datum Lugduni, Nonis Octobris, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishops of Schwerin and Ratzeburg. Since we have decided to entrust the church of Lübeck to our venerable brother, the archbishop of Livonia, Estonia, and Prussia, we mandate you by the authority of these present letters to diligently inquire whether it is expedient for the same or the Cammin church to be elevated to a metropolitan status, and to faithfully report back to us what you find. Given at Lyon, on September 4, in the fifth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Zwerinensi et Raceburgensi episcopis mandat, ut diligenter inquirant an expediat Lubicensem vel Caminensem ecclesiam in metropoliticam erigi, et de inventis fideliter rescribant. 1248, Sept. 4, Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To the Abbot of Cava of the Salerno diocese. The customary kindness of the Apostolic See easily shows favor, etc., up to: the devoted ones. Hence, concerning our beloved son Riccardo de Trentenaria, a layman of the Capua diocese, whose father was despoiled of all his goods by the late Emperor Frederick of the Romans, and whose brother is in exile, and who himself suffers hardships due to his devotion to the Roman Church, we command that you endeavor, by our authority, to provide for him in the Valley of Grace or Calabria from the revenues of two military fiefs, etc., as previously stated: ability; those who oppose, etc. Given at Lyon, the 9th of August, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

Regesto:

Innocentius IV papa abbati Cavensi mandat, ut Riccardo de Trentenaria laico Capuae de duobus feudis militaribus in Valle de Grati seu Calabria provideat. 1247, Aug. 9. Lugduni.
