**Translation to English:**

To P., Cardinal Deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the Apostolic See. Since our venerable brother, the Bishop of Augsburg, as he has informed us by his letters, desires to resign, being now unable to perform the pastoral office, we command you to accept his resignation on our behalf and to provide for him from the episcopal goods, from which he may be suitably supported. Furthermore, appoint a suitable person to the pastoral office of the Church of Augsburg or entrust its care to our beloved son Hartemann, a canon of the same church, born of the noble Count of Dikkingen, a devoted servant of the Roman Church, who is known to have merited the favor and grace of the Apostolic See by the esteem of the late H., King of the Romans, and other kinsmen. Those who oppose, etc. Given at Lyon, the 5th day before the Kalends of October, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali mandat, ut episcopi Augustensis cessionem accipiat et episcopalibus eum bonis sustineat, atque ecclesie Augustensi personam idoneam vel Hartemanno canonico eius curam committat. 1231, Sept. 27, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the same. Since in the empire many have taken or received the sign of the cross for carrying out various pious works: because we consider it a most pious work to currently assist our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious king of the Romans, against the treachery of Frederick, who longs for the destruction of the faith, we grant you full authority by the present letters to change the vows of those who have taken the cross to assist the aforementioned king, except for those who have received the cross for the support of the Holy Land. Given as above.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa (eidem) mandat, ut vota crucesignatorum, qui in diversis operibus pietatis versantur, in auxilium regis Romanorum commutentur, exceptis his qui pro subsidio Terræ Sanctæ crucem acceperunt. Datum ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Constance. Since the noble man, the Count of Montfort, is said to hold certain fiefs from the churches of Chur and St. Gall, and the same, by adhering reprehensibly to the late Emperor Frederick, does not cease to persecute the Roman Church and consequently those churches, and it is fitting that the disloyal suffer loss from their disloyalty and the loyal gain advantage from their loyalty: we command your fraternity, that if the matter stands thus, depriving the said count of the same fiefs by our authority, you confer and assign them to our beloved son, the noble man F., brother of the said count, who persists in loyalty to the Church; any opponents, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 4th Kalends of October, in the 5th year (of our pontificate).

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Constantiensi mandat ut, si comes de Monteforti, Friderico imperatori quondam adherens, res ecclesias Curiensis et Sancti Galli persequitur, ipsum feudis privet et ea fratri comitis ecclesiae devoto conferat. 1247, Lugduni, 28 Septembris.

**Translation to English:**

To the provost and chapter of Neweburg. Since, as we have learned, our beloved daughter in Christ, the noble lady, the Duchess of Austria, has taken refuge and resides in the castle of Obalenberch, which is said to belong to your church, for its fortification: we earnestly ask, admonish, and urge your community, strictly ordering you, that you should not presume to make any exchange of this castle with anyone else except with her, who, as she asserts, is prepared to assign you an equivalent exchange for it. Given at Lyon, 10th Kalends of February, in the year of our Lord.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa preposito et capitulo Neweburgensibus mandat ne permutationem castri de Obalenberch cum aliquo alio praeterquam cum ducissa Austrie faciant. 1239, Jan. 23. Datum Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Brothers of the House of the Teutonic Knights of Starkemberg and Gotenstein, who are holding the castles. By the authority of these presents, we firmly command you, in the virtue of obedience, to take care with all diligence and solicitude to guard the castles of Starkemberg and Gotenstein, which the late duke of Austria fortified as impregnable for a long time, so that they may not come into the hands of the late Emperor Frederick or his supporters; fulfilling our mandate in this matter in such a manner that we, rightfully commending your effort, may thus owe you deserved thanks. Given at Lyon, on the 11th of October, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa fratribus domus Theutonicorum de Starkemberch et de Gotenstein mandat ut castra Starkemberch et Gotenstein diligenter custodiant, ne ad manus Friderici quondam imperatoris vel fautorum eius perveniant. Datum Lugduni, V Idus Octobris, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

"...to the elect Parmense and Regino. Since, as we have learned, certain citizens of Cremona have offered and continue to offer counsel, aid, and favor to the late Emperor Frederick after the sentence of deposition was pronounced against him, we, not wishing that the audacity of such presumption should be an example to others, command that you, by our authority, deprive these citizens perpetually of all fiefs they hold from monasteries or churches, and confer them upon the Cremonese knights devoted to the Church, who are eager to promote the business of the Church; those who oppose, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 13th of March, in the fifth year."

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Parmensi et Regino electis mandat, ut cives Cremonenses, qui post depositionem Friderici imperatoris eidem favorem praestiterunt, feudis ecclesiasticis priventur et haec militibus Cremonensibus ecclesiae devotis conferantur. Datum Lugduni, III Idus Martii, anno quinto.

Translation to English:

To the citizens of Aachen, a spirit of sound counsel. We believe you should know, etc., as above up to: assumed; from which all should rejoice, and you especially, as you are closest to him and his kind, and in his aid, etc., up to: to be done. Therefore, we earnestly ask, admonish, and encourage your community, commanding that, wisely considering that the same king, by himself and through his followers, by whom you are surrounded, will favorably keep you and your land in liberty, grace, and honor, you should immediately and completely withdraw from the service and condemned devotion of Frederick, deposed from imperial and royal dignity and bound by the sword of anathema, and steadfastly and powerfully support the same king, so that you may deservedly be commended before God and men for this and that the aforementioned king may be strongly bound to your honors and benefits and we may duly pursue your devotion with worthy acts of gratitude. Given as above.

Latin Regesto:

Gregorius IX papa civibus Aquensibus mandat ut a Friderico deposito recedant et regi assistentiam praestent, promittens gratiam et honorem a rege et seipso. Datum Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the Cardinal Deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the apostolic see. Since, as we have learned, you have promised to the beloved son, the noble man, the Duke of Brabant and Lotharingia, to make all the prelates of Germany promise by their open letters that they would stand by him as allies to allies and friends to friends vigorously and openly in the matter of the church against Frederick, the former emperor of the Romans, and his sons and supporters and adherents: we, considering that such a promise is worthy of favorable prosecution and that with the combined strength of the same, they will be able to confidently pursue the cause of the church, which is not individual but common, and not fear the attack of the enemies, we command that you effectively admonish and induce the said prelates to this end and, if necessary, compel them by our authority, removing the impediment of appeal, as you see fit to expedite. Given at Lyons, on the 12th day before the Kalends of December, in the fifth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali mandat, ut prelatos Alamannie moneat et inducat ad promissionem faciendam duci Brabantie in causa ecclesie contra F. quondam imperatorem et filios eius, et si necesse sit, auctoritate apostolica compellat. 1247, Nov. 20. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Alexander, canon of Verona, son of our beloved Albertinus de Belude, knight of Padua. In consideration of the beloved sons, noble men, the Marquis of Este and Alberic of Romano, who have earnestly petitioned us on your behalf through their letters, we grant you, as much as we can with God’s approval, favor and grace. Since, as your request presented before us, our venerable brother, the bishop of Verona, has deemed it appropriate to assign to you a place and benefice in the church of Verona, should one be vacant or become vacant soon, by our authority, we, appreciating what has been prudently done by the said bishop in this matter, confirm it by apostolic authority and strengthen it with the protection of this present document. Let no one, therefore, etc., dare to infringe upon our confirmation, etc. Given at Lyon, on the Ides of February, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Alexandro canonico Veronensi, filio Albertini de Belude militis Paduani, favorem et gratiam ob supplicationem marchionis Estensis et Alberici de Romano impertitur, confirmans auctoritate apostolica assignationem loci et beneficii in ecclesia Veronensi per episcopum Veronensem factam. 1230, Feb. 13, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the illustrious King of Hungary. Since, as we have heard, etc., up to: the noble [of] Austria, inflamed with zeal for faith and devotion, intends to oppose the enemies of the Church, we earnestly ask, admonish, and encourage your royal serenity, that considering the said noble as more commendable for our and the apostolic see's reverence, you assist her in her time of necessity, when you are requested by her, both in her rights and against those enemies, so that she may feel that our prayers have been profitable to her with you, and that we may rightly commend the zeal of your sincerity. Given at Lyons, the 5th day before the Kalends of February, in the fifth year of our pontificate. In the same manner, to the illustrious King of Bohemia.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa illustri regi Ungariae mandat ut nobili Austriae, fidei et devotionis zelo accensae, in tempore necessitatis assistat, tam in iure suo quam contra inimicos ecclesiae, V Kal. Februarii, anno quinto, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the same. Desiring that our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, be devoutly and humbly obeyed by all within the empire, we command that you do not hesitate to compel, with the appropriate strictness and setting aside any appeals, all and each, of whatever order or profession they may be, to firmly obey and attend to the king's salutary commands—notwithstanding any indulgence of the Apostolic See. Given at Lyon, on the 12th Kalends of December, in the fifth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa [recipienti ignoto] mandat, ut universos et singulos ad obediendum regis Romanorum mandatis compellat, non obstantibus indulgentiis apostolicis. 1235, Nov. 20, Lugduni.

### Translation to English:

To the Bishop of Augsburg. Since, as we have learned, some laypeople of your diocese, for the reason that they adhered to the late Frederick, former Emperor of the Romans, along with the noble man, the Count of Savoy, against the Church and our beloved son, O., Cardinal Deacon of St. Mary in Via Lata, the legate of the Apostolic See, when he was passing through those parts, are known to have incurred the sentence of excommunication: we, inclined by the supplications of our beloved sons, the noble men Goffrid the Viscount and James of Quinto of the same diocese, grant to your fraternity the free authority by the present letters to absolve their men, who have incurred the bond of such excommunication, provided that they take a corporal oath that they will precisely obey the mandates of the Church and will never adhere in such a manner to the said Frederick. Given at Lyon, 9th December, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

### Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Augustensi mandat, ut laicos diocesis, qui excommunicati sunt propter adhaesionem cum quondam imperatore Frederico et comite Sabaudiae contra ecclesiam et Cardinalem legatum, absolvendi facultatem habeat, dummodo iuramentum praestent parendi ecclesiae mandatis. Datum Lugduni, V Idus Decembris, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble men H., elder, and H., younger, counts of Kiburch. From the purity of faith and the integrity of devotion, by which you are proven to be zealous for our honor, by avoiding the company of F., the former emperor, and C., his son, and adhering to the part of the Church, we have deemed it worthy, or rather we consider it our duty, to exalt you with every excellence of grace and honor as special sons of the Church. Therefore, so that you may persist with firm and stable constancy and unwavering resolve in the service of the Roman Church, indeed more truly of Jesus Christ, we are benignly inclined to your worthy supplications, not devoid of grace or favor, and by apostolic authority, we have decided to absolve you from all faith, fidelity, and general or special obligation, oath, or other firmness, by which you are bound or obligated in any way or for any reason to the aforementioned F. and C. Therefore, no one etc. of our absolution etc. Given at Lyon, on the 11th of February, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobilibus viris H. seniori et H. iuniori comitibus de Kiburch absolutionem ab obligationibus erga F. quondam imperatorem et C. nati eius, auctoritate apostolica, concedit. 1234, Febr. 11. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man, Philip de Vicedominis, Podestà of Parma. We willingly grant the support of apostolic authority to those things done for the good state of the city of Parma, so that they may remain unblemished when they have been fortified by our protection. Therefore, as was presented to us on your behalf, our beloved son G. de Montelongo, our subdeacon and notary, and legate of the apostolic see, at the request and supplication of the council of Parma, deemed it appropriate to absolve you from the oath which you are known to have sworn to observe its statutes for the good state of the said city. We, moved by your supplications, considering this absolution as valid and agreeable, and supplementing any defect that might exist in it, from the fullness of our power, we confirm it with apostolic authority and strengthen it with the support of this present writing. Let no one therefore etc. of our confirmation and supplementing etc. Given at Lyon, on the Nones of March, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro Philippo de Vicedominis, potestati Parmensi, scribit de absolutione ab iuramento a G. de Montelongo subdiacono et notario apostolicae sedis legato concessa, confirmans eam auctoritate apostolica. 1236, Martii 7, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Peter, Cardinal Deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the apostolic see. On behalf of our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, it was humbly petitioned to us that we might, with paternal providence, arrange for certain nobles, who have taken the cross both from the kingdom of France and Germany and wish to assist against his adversaries, to exchange their vow of the cross in aid of this king. Since this king, who champions the cause of the faith and the church, is in need of warriors' support, we command that you exchange the vow of the cross into aid for the king for these cross-bearers, five of whom are from the kingdom of France and fifteen from the empire; any objectors, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 12th day before the Kalends of December, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Petro Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum cardinali mandat ut quibusdam nobilibus, crucesignatis de regno Franciae et Alamanniae, votum crucis in subsidium regis Romanorum commutet. Datum Lugduni, XII Kal. Decembr., anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Bamberg. Because you have been almost entirely despoiled of your goods by the enemies of God and the Church, to the point that you lack the means to sustain yourself comfortably, we sympathize with you with paternal affection and extend our hand of provision in this time of such great need. Although the former Bishop of Chiem (Kimensis) voluntarily resigned his position for the sake of his church, and although this resignation might not have held firm, yet in detestation of his person, we have deemed it right and agreeable to accept the same resignation. We have decided to entrust you with the administration of that church until it pleases our will, granting you full administration over its spiritual and temporal matters. Therefore, we command that you diligently and faithfully undertake its care, doing all that you know to be necessary for the duties of this administration and caretaking, notwithstanding any opposition, etc. Given at Lyon, the 19th of October, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Bambergensi administrationem ecclesiae Kimensis, tam in spiritualibus quam in temporalibus, committit usque ad beneplacitum suum. 1248, Oct. 19. Datum Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the dean of the church of Saint Gengulphus of Toul. We briefly respond to your consultation regarding the collection of the twentieth part from the churches and ecclesiastical persons, both exempt and non-exempt, of the city and diocese of Toul according to the form of the letters directed to you on this matter by the Apostolic See. We do not understand or intend that the abbots and monks of the Cistercian order, who use the offerings given to them out of piety almost entirely for works of charity, nor the Templars, Hospitallers, or the brothers of the Teutonic Order of Saint Mary, who dedicate themselves and their goods to the service of the Redeemer without fearing the loss of their goods or dangers to their persons, should be included under such a general classification of persons. Given at Lyon, on the Ides of January, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa decano ecclesiae sancti Gengulphi Tullensis respondet consultationi de vicesima exigenda ab ecclesiis et personis ecclesiasticis, non includens sub generalitate abbates et monachos Cistercienses, Templarios, Hospitalarios et fratres Theutonicorum. Datum Lugduni, Idibus Ianuarii, anno pontificatus nostri quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the illustrious King of the Romans. We willingly assent to your desires and favorably hear your petitions, as much as we can with God. Thus, inclined by your supplications, we grant by the authority of these presents to your chaplains, notaries, and clerics, that as long as they remain in your service, they may fully receive the revenues of their benefices, except for the daily distributions, as if they were personally residing in the churches where they hold these benefices,—notwithstanding any contrary custom or statute, oath or confirmation of the apostolic see, or any other reinforcement of any firmness, or any indulgence of the same see, by which such grace can be delayed or impeded and of which it is necessary to make special mention in the present. No one, therefore, etc. of our concession etc. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa regi Romanorum illustri concedit, ut capellani, notarii et clerici eius, quamdiu in servitio suo permanserint, proventus beneficiorum integre percipiant, non obstante aliqua consuetudine vel statuto contrario. Datum Laterani, anno pontificatus nono.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man, Conrad, Count of Handek. We hold in gratitude and acceptance, commending your devotion with due praises in the Lord and pursuing actions of thanks, because, as we have learned from our beloved daughter in Christ, the noblewoman, the Duchess of Austria, you have stood by her vigorously in the prosecution of her rights and especially against the enemies of the Church, and you continue to assist her. Therefore, so that you may pursue even more laudably what you are known to have commendably begun through our exhortations, we earnestly advise and encourage your nobility, enjoining in remission of your sins, that you assist and powerfully aid the said duchess in her rights, and especially against the supporters of the late Emperor F., against whom, inflamed by zeal for faith and devotion, she proposes to stand, so that she, etc. as above in the next, until the end.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Conrado comiti de Handek commendat devotionem eius, quod ducissae Austriae in iuribus suis et contra inimicos ecclesiae adiuvit, hortaturque ut eidem contra fautores F. quondam imperatoris, quos ipsa oppugnare intendit, viriliter assistat; et remissionem peccaminum ei promittit. Datum anno pontificatus VII, apud Urbem.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Metz. The content of your petition has shown us that after the abbot of the monastery of Saint Martin of Glandières, of the Order of Saint Benedict in the diocese of Metz, resigned from the governance of the abbey due to being considered unable and useless because of old age, the dean of the church of Saint Savior of Metz, by the mandate of our beloved son P., Cardinal Deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, legate of the apostolic see, entrusted the administration of the mentioned monastery, in both spiritual and temporal matters, to your discernment. This was done so that with the aid of your favor, it may quickly rise back to a state of prosperity, from which it had greatly fallen due to the impotence of the former abbot. Therefore, we, considering the benefit of this action and also favoring your person with due honor, have been moved by your requests. We hold what has been providently done by the said dean to be valid, and we confirm it with apostolic authority and strengthen it with the protection of this present writing. Let no one, therefore, etc., of our confirmation etc. Given at Lyons, on the Nones of November, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Metensi administrationem monasterii Sancti Martini Glandariensis, ab decano Sancti Salvatoris Metensis commissam, auctoritate apostolica confirmat. 1226, Nov. 5. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the master and brothers of the Teutonic House in the regions of Prussia. Since we are sending our letters to the illustrious King Daniel of Ruthenia and to his brother and the noble man Alexander, Duke of Suzdal, instructing them that if it becomes evident to them that the Tartar army is directing its steps towards Christianity, they should inform you, so that when this becomes known to us through you, we can more promptly plan how to resist these Tartars vigorously with God's help, because dangers can be more easily avoided if we are armed against them with the shield of providence: we command you, as soon as this becomes known to you through them or any of them, to endeavor to inform us without delay. Given at Lyons, 22nd January, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa magistrum et fratres de domo Theotonicorum in Pruscie partibus constitutis mandat, ut si per Danielum regem Ruscie vel fratrem eius vel Alexandrum ducem Susdaliensi intellexerint Tartarorum exercitum versus Christianitatem dirigere, hoc quam primum pontifici notificent. 1241, Jan. 22, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Master William of Saint-Amour, canon of Beauvais. To make a special favor for you, the affectionate requests presented to us by our beloved sons, the elected bishop of Tarentaise and the noble man Thomas of Savoy, count, and also your merits of probity induce us more earnestly. Therefore, considering the laudable testimony given to you regarding your knowledge of letters, honest life, and good morals, and intending to further pursue you with the prerogative of favor and greater grace: so that besides the church of Gareville, which has the care of souls that you hold, you may freely receive one ecclesiastical benefice or personate, or dignity, even if it has similar care, if it is offered to you canonically, and may lawfully retain it with those you already hold – notwithstanding the constitution of the general council – we grant you by the authority of these presents; provided that the same benefices, etc., until: is neglected. Let no one, etc., of this concession, etc. Given at Lyon, 11th Kalends of September, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Magistro Willelmo de Sancto Amore canonico Belvacensi indulget ut, praeter ecclesiam de Garevilla, unicum beneficium ecclesiasticum vel dignitatem, etiam si curam animarum habeat, recipere ac retinere possit, constitutione concilii generalis non obstante. 1248, Aug. 22. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Peter, Cardinal Deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the apostolic see. Since the current matter at hand pertains to the general church, to whose complete destruction there is an aspiration, we are exceedingly troubled by the prelates who, as pillars, ought to support the church if they oppose this matter. Therefore, we command that if you find any prelates in the lands of your legation who do not obey our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, as they are obliged, you are to summon them peremptorily on our behalf, so that within the term you have established for each, they may appear before us to hear the sentence of deposition. You are also to inform them that whether they come or not, we will nonetheless proceed to the sentence of deposition against them. Meanwhile, you are to entrust the administration of their churches, both spiritual and temporal, to some discreet persons, as you see fit. Those who contradict, etc. Given at Lyon, November 16, in the fifth year of our reign.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Petro Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali legato mandat, ut prelatos in legationis terris reperiatos, qui regi Romanorum non obediant, citet ad comparendum coram se depositionis sententiam audituri et interim ecclesiarum administrationem committat discretis personis. 1247, Nov. 16, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To P. Cardinal Deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the Apostolic See. It is said that our venerable brother, the Bishop of Constance, received a mandate from you to collect a certain amount of money from the churches and monasteries of his city and diocese, both exempt and non-exempt, for your benefit. However, the said bishop, under the pretext of this mandate, instructed the beloved sons, the abbots of the Cistercian order of the said diocese, under penalty of excommunication and even deposition, to procure payment of a certain sum of money within a specified term, as we have learned from their own report. Since pecuniary procurations for legates of the Apostolic See are not usually demanded from the aforementioned order, we order that you no longer permit such money to be demanded from them, and that you ensure any proceedings against them for this are revoked. When you visit their monasteries or other places of the same order, be satisfied with what is customarily provided to legates coming from the side of the Roman Pontiff. Given at Lyon, 15th day before the Kalends of March, in the year five.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa, P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali apostolicae sedis legato mandat, ne episcopus Constantiensis ab abbatibus Cisterciensis ordinis pecuniam ad opus suum exigat, et ut revocetur, si quid contra ipsos actum est. 1236, Feb. 15, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected bishop of Liège. The careful consideration of the Apostolic See, appropriately weighing the changes of times, sometimes grants certain things from the fullness of its power, which it would not otherwise bestow, and sometimes denies certain things, which it might grant at other times, dispensing the gifts of its grace appropriately according to the needs of the time, now kindly bestowing them, now rightly denying them, having considered both sides of the temporal circumstances, so that it always acts in accordance with what it perceives to be useful and beneficial. Hence, since it is known that you must diligently and effectively work for the promotion of matters concerning the Church in parts of Germany, and as we recognize that for this reason you cannot attend to the affairs of the church committed to you as thoroughly as is necessary, we, inclined by the supplications of your devotion, grant you by the authority of these presents that no one shall compel you to receive any sacred order without our special mandate explicitly mentioning this indulgence, even if you have taken an oath to receive orders, so that you may more freely pursue these affairs. Therefore, let no one etc. Given at Lyon, 15th November, in the 5th year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa electo Leodiensi concedit, ne ad suscipiendum aliquem ordinem sacrum sine mandato apostolico cogatur, ut negotia ecclesiae in partibus Alamannie diligentius prosequi possit. 1231, Nov. 15. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Deacon Cardinal of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the Apostolic See. In order that those who strive for the Church against its persecutors may obtain a reward that does not perish, we desire and command with the authority of these presents your devotion, that you grant, with apostolic authority, full remission of their sins to our beloved son, the noble man, the Duke of Brabant and Lotharingia, who, by himself and his followers, stands firmly and openly with us and the Roman Church against Frederick, the former emperor of the Romans, and his sons, and their supporters and allies, and to all others assisting the said duke in this matter, provided they are truly contrite and have confessed. Given at Lyon, 20th November, in the 5th year of our pontificate.

**Regesto:**

Innocentius IV papa P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali, apostolicae sedis legato mandat, ut duci Brabantie ac Lotharingie et aliis sibi assistentibus remissionem peccaminum, si vere contriti et confessos, auctoritate apostolica largiatur. 1251, Nov. 20. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Gerard of Peis, archdeacon of Liège. On behalf of our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Cologne, it was presented before us that, since we have decided to grant him a fifth part of the ecclesiastical revenues of the province of Cologne for a certain period, and since we have appointed the provost of the church of Tiel and his colleague as executors in the diocese of Utrecht, these executors have pronounced a sentence of excommunication against certain abbots and other clerics, both secular and regular, of Friesland in the aforementioned diocese, because they stubbornly refused to pay the said fifth part to the Archbishop from their ecclesiastical revenues, as demanded by justice. Therefore, the aforementioned Archbishop requested us to ensure that this sentence is upheld with due firmness. We thus command you to have this sentence publicly proclaimed, where you see fit, by you and others, with bells tolling and candles lit on Sundays and feast days, and to ensure that this sentence, as it was reasonably pronounced, is inviolably observed until proper satisfaction is made; opposers, etc. Given at Lyon, 17 October, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Gerardo de Peis, archidiacono Leodiensi mandat, ut sententiam excommunicationis contra clericos Frisiae, qui quintam proventuum ecclesiasticorum archiepiscopo Coloniensi solvere recusabant, publice proclamet et inviolabiliter observari faciat. 1231, 17 Oct., Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot in Hersedchusen of the Paderborn diocese. Our venerable brother, the Bishop of Hildesheim, has informed us through his petition that Hermann of Glichen, a canon of the Hildesheim church, supported by the favor of certain followers of the former Roman Emperor, holds the episcopal house, cities, towns, fortresses, and goods of the same church by force, causing considerable harm and grievance to the bishop and the church. Because of this, our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Mainz, following the demands of justice, has pronounced a sentence of excommunication against the aforementioned Hermann with apostolic authority. However, Hermann, disregarding this sentence, presumes to retain these goods, to the peril of his soul and to the scandal of many. Therefore, the aforementioned bishop has humbly petitioned us to provide paternal care since he cannot find justice in those parts due to Hermann's malice and power. We command you to summon Hermann by our authority to appear before us within two months after your summons, to address and resolve these matters as dictated by reason and order. You are to report back faithfully to us whatever you decide to do regarding these matters. Given at Lyon, 2nd day before the Kalends of February, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius Papa IX abbati in Hersedchusen Padeburnensis diocesis mandat Hermanno de Glichen canonico Hildesemensis ecclesiae, qui bona eiusdem ecclesiae vi occupat, auctoritate apostolica citare peremptorie, ut infra duos menses compareat coram papa. Datum Lugduni, II Kal. Februarii, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To Brother Franco of the Order of Friars Minor. Inclined by the devoted prayers of our beloved daughter in Christ, the noble woman, the Duchess of Austria, we grant you by the authority of these presents, that you may hear confessions of her and others of her household, both men and women, as often as it is opportune, and impose upon them salutary penance for their sins, granting to them, the duchess and the women, if necessary, the benefit of absolution on our behalf, with these present letters being valid for no longer than a year. Given at Lyon, on the 10th day before the Kalends of February, in the fifth year. In the same way, to the same for the noble man Conrad, Count of Handek, and...

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Fratri Franco de ordine fratrum Minorum concedit, ut confessiones ducissae Austriae et aliorum de familia sua audiat et eis penitentiam salutarem iniungat, cum beneficio absolutionis, si necesse fuerit. Dat. Lugduni, X Kal. Februarii, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz. Since, as we have learned from your report, you have incurred significant expenses for the promotion of the affairs of the Roman Church, and you must still undertake great expenditures, we grant you the authority, by the power of these presents, to retain for two years the revenues of all ecclesiastical benefices, even those with the care of souls attached, which may happen to become vacant within the city and diocese of Mainz for up to five years. You are also given the authority to restrain any objectors through ecclesiastical censure, disregarding any appeals, provided that sufficient resources are reserved from these revenues to ensure that suitable vicars can serve comfortably in the churches where such benefices are held. Given at Lyon, 14th day before the Kalends of January, in the fifth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa archiepiscopo Maguntino concedit facultatem retinendi per biennium proventus omnium beneficiorum ecclesiasticorum in civitate et diocesi Maguntina, quae usque ad quinque annos vacare contigerit, et contradictores compescendi. 1250, Dec. 19, Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To the abbot of the monastery of the Scots at Wina in the diocese of Poitiers. We have learned with great disturbance of mind that you and some of your monks, not without your knowledge, are conducting divine services with open doors and in loud voices in front of the supporters of Frederick, the former emperor, who are excommunicated. Since this, if true, greatly deviates from the regular decency and could bring confusion to your honor and soul, not unworthily, we strictly command you by the authority of these presents, that if the matter is as reported, you should abstain yourself and make your monks abstain from such celebrations in front of the same excommunicates, and rather strive to avoid them more strictly and make them be avoided by your subjects, if you wish to escape the penalty of canonical punishment. Given at Lyon, January 23, in the fifth year [of our pontificate].

Latin Regesto:

Gregorius IX papa abbati monasterii Scothorum de Wina Pitavensis diocesis mandat, ut, si divina officia coram excommunicatis fautoribus Friderici quondam imperatoris celebrentur, ab huiusmodi celebratione abstineat et monachos suos abstinere faciat, ultionis canonicae poenam effugere cupiens. 1231, Ian. 23. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To P., Cardinal Deacon of San Giorgio in Velabro, legate of the Apostolic See. When the late H., King of the Romans, promised a certain sum of money to the noble men, H. and H., Counts of Kimburg, to assist him against the former Emperor F., the matter could not be completed due to the king's death. However, since the same counts, who are influential in those regions, can greatly advance the affairs of the empire, we command that you diligently and carefully, using the prudence given by God, strive to ensure that our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious W., King of the Romans, endeavors to pay the money promised to the counts by the aforementioned king, so that they may assist him bravely and powerfully against the former F. Given at Lyon, on the 14th of October, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

**Gregorius IX papa** P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali, apostolicae sedis legato, mandat ut operetur, ut W. rex Romanorum pecuniam H. et H. comitibus de Kimburcha a rege H. promissam solvat, ut ei contra F. assistent. 1231, Oct. 14, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To P., Cardinal Deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the Apostolic See. As our venerable brother, the Bishop of Bamberg, proposed before us, he has bound himself as a guarantor at the behest of the late H., King of the Romans, to the noble Duke of Moravia and some other nobles from those regions. We direct our writings to our beloved son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, W., so that he may, by whatever means he can, assist and ensure that the bishop is released from this obligation. Therefore, we command you to favorably commend the same bishop for the reverence of the Apostolic See and ourselves, and to diligently advise and induce the king to this end, and to apply your effective effort according to the prudence given to you by God, so that we may commend your diligence in this matter with worthy praises in the Lord. Given at Lyon, on the 8th of November, in the fifth year. In almost the same manner, to our beloved son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, W.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali legato mandat ut regem Romanorum W. moneat et inducat ad liberandum episcopum Bambergensem a fideiussione; commendat episcopum. Datum Lugduni, VI Idus Novembris, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble men Hugolino Raynerii and Hugolino Bonicomitis, citizens of Camerino. The customary providence of the Apostolic See examines the merits of its subjects with careful deliberation and rewards what is judged by reason to be superior with greater remunerations, pursuing these with more abundant favors and raising them with fuller benefits. Hence, because you are fervent in your devotion toward the Roman Church and strive to maintain constancy regarding it such that you deserve to be specially honored by her among her other sons with the title of fidelity, we, considering these things not unworthily and wishing to attend to your interests and diligently secure the increase of your honor, inclined by your supplications, grant you by the authority of these presents the mountains of Nursia, Cassio, Cerreto, and other surrounding castles of the diocese of Spoleto, as well as the land of Arnulphs and their revenues and profits, to be retained by you until our good pleasure. Therefore, let no one etc. of our concession etc. Given at Lyons, on January 12, in the 5th year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa nobilibus viris Hugolino Raynerii et Hugolino Bonicomitis civibus Camerinensibus montana Nursie, Cassii, Cerreti et alia castra Spoletane diocesis cum terra Arnulphorum et eorum reditibus concedit retinenda usque ad beneplacitum suum. 1248, Ianuarii 12. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the citizens of Mainz. It will never fade from our and the apostolic see's memory how much you have endured for it, and the steadfast devotion you have shown, as we have learned from experience, in the affairs of the church, and still show; for which we give you as much gratitude as we can. Although we are secure in your unwavering firmness, in order to fulfill our duty of exhortation and not omit anything in our power concerning matters at hand, we earnestly ask, advise, and urge you all, and for the remission of your sins we enjoin you, to continue in the established devotion and customary constancy to the aforementioned see in the person of our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, so that you may assist this king vigorously, and thereby, gaining divine, apostolic, and royal favor and the praise of men, you may prove yourselves more virtuous through action day by day and stronger in such a great matter. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa civibus Maguntinis gratias agit pro devotione constanti et hortatur eos ad assistendum regi Romanorum. [1227–1241], Dat. ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the same (recipient). Wishing to assist with paternal care the devoted of the Church, against whom proceedings are known to have been initiated by their persecutors, we declare null and void all conspiracies, guarantees, promises, and grants or assignments of feuds, made or to be made regarding the persons or goods of these devoted ones by the late Emperor Frederick, his sons, or any other of their supporters, after the sentence of excommunication was pronounced against Frederick and those adhering to him, by the counsel of our brothers. We strictly prohibit such things from being presumed in the future. Those who presume to give counsel, help, or favor to these actions shall know they are subject to the sentence of excommunication. We command that all the aforementioned be carried out, etc., as above until the end.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa omnibus christifidelibus notum facit se, post sententiam excommunicationis in Fridericum imperatorem eiusque adherentes latam, consilio fratrum suorum irritare omnes coniurationes, securitates, promissiones, et feudorum dationes devotis Ecclesiae adversus persecutores factas, et talia de cetero fieri districtius prohibere. Quicumque consilium, auxilium, vel favorem ad haec praebuerint, excommunicationi subiciuntur. [Datum anno X, Anagniae, 1236.]

Translation to English:

To the noble man W., born of our beloved daughter in Christ, the noblewoman, the Countess of Flanders. The careful consideration of the Apostolic See, rightly weighing the changes of the times, sometimes grants to some individuals from the fullness of its power certain things that it would not otherwise concede, and sometimes denies certain things that it might grant at other times, aptly dispensing the gifts of its grace according to the necessity of the time, sometimes bestowing them kindly, and at other times rightly denying them, considering the nature of the time on both sides, so that it always acts in what it perceives to be useful and beneficial. Therefore, since, as we have learned from your communication, you have entered into a marriage with our beloved daughter in Christ, the noblewoman Maria, born of the noble man, the Duke of Brabant, whom you claim to be related to in the fourth degree of consanguinity, we, inclined by your supplications, dispense with you by apostolic authority to lawfully remain in the marriage thus contracted, notwithstanding the aforementioned degree. Let no one, therefore, etc., of our dispensation, etc. Given at Lyon, on the sixth day before the Kalends of December, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro W., filio comitissae Flandriae mandat ut cum nobili muliere Maria, cuius quarti consanguinitatis gradus est, in matrimonio remanere possit, auctoritate apostolica dispensans. Dat. Lugduni, VI Kal. Decembris, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Cardinal Priest of the title of St. Mary in Trastevere, our Vicar in the City. As we have learned, Walter of Ocre presumes to hold the Church of Valva, which belongs directly to the Apostolic See, on the occasion of a certain election said to have been conducted or rather attempted for him there, supported by secular power. We command, therefore, that the election itself, which we declare void, be completely nullified, and that, in our stead, you appoint as bishop and shepherd of the said church our beloved son, the Archpriest of St. Lucy in the City, who seems suitable for a bishopric, if it can be done without scandal. Otherwise, appoint another suitable person, ensuring that due obedience and reverence are shown to him by his subjects. Dated at Lyon, 5th of the Nones of October, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa presbytero cardinali tituli Sancte Marie Transtiberim, vicario suo in Urbe, mandatum dat ut electionem Walterii de Ocre in ecclesiam Valvensem irritam nuntiet et archipresbyterum Sancte Lucie de Urbe, vel aliam idoneam personam, in episcopum instituat. 1231, Oct. 3, Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To the Archbishop of Prussia, legate of the apostolic see. It has been fervently requested of us by our beloved son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, that since many Frisians, who are inheritors of the County of Holland, have taken up the sign of the cross for the aid of the Holy Land, we might, in our customary benevolence, allow them to exchange this cross for the king's assistance and grant them the pardon of their sins as if they had personally crossed the sea. Therefore, we command that you arrange and dispose this matter, which we have verbally communicated to you, with the counsel of our beloved son Peter, cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the apostolic see, and with the king or another of them. Given at Lyons, 15th day before the Calends of December, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

Regesto in Latin:

Innocentius IV papa archiepiscopo Pruscie, apostolicae sedis legato mandat ut Frisones, qui signum crucis pro Terra Sancta susceperunt, convertant hoc in subsidium regis Romanorum, remissionem peccatorum obtinentes perinde ac si personaliter transfretassent. Datum Lugduni, XV Kalendas Decembris, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To P., Cardinal Deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the Apostolic See. Remembering the clear memory of Henry, King of the Romans, that our venerable brother, the Bishop of Bamberg, being a man of great circumspection and probity, is useful for exercising the office of the Imperial Chancellery, and that it cannot be better or more usefully exercised by anyone other than him, appointed him as his chancellor and invested him with the same office, as the said bishop has made known to us by explaining. However, as he asserts, the one to whom such an office is granted should hold it for the duration of his life. Hoping that the aforementioned bishop will also be useful to him, we order you to carefully advise and induce the one who will happen to be promoted as king, by the grace of God, not to grant the aforementioned office to anyone else, but to allow the bishop to remain in it. Given at Lyon, on the 4th day before the Nones of September, in the fifth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Petro Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali, apostolicae sedis legato, mandat ut Henrici regis Romanorum consilium sequens, episcopo Bambergensi officium cancellarii concessum sit et in eo permaneat, monens regem futurum ut nulli alii concedat. Datum Lugduni, II Non. Sept. anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of Santa Mustiola of Torri, of the Order of Vallombrosa, in the diocese of Siena. Since, as we have learned, the church of Massa is vacant of a pastor, and the authority of that place, F., a former supporter of the emperor, has forced the canons of that church, against their will, to elect someone as their bishop and pastor, we command you, that if this is the case, to declare such an election null and void by our authority, and to instruct these canons on our behalf not to proceed with any election, but to send some from among themselves to our presence with full authority to do what we shall decide regarding this matter. Furthermore, you shall declare null and void by our authority anything attempted to the contrary. Given at Lyon, on the Ides of February, in the fifth year (of our pontificate).

---

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati Sancte Mustiole de Turri ordinis Vallis Umbrose mandat, ut electionem coactam episcopi in ecclesia Massana irritam decernat et canonicis praecipiat ad nostram praesentiam mittere cum mandato pleno. 1234, Feb. 13, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the dean and chapter of Halberstadt. The supplications of our beloved son, the noble man Odo, Margrave of Brandenburg, and the merits of the same provost, about which a laudable testimony is given, persuade us to grant a special favor to our beloved son Albert, provost of the church of Stindar, chaplain of the said margrave. Therefore, we have thought it proper to earnestly request and admonish the whole of your community, commanding that you receive the same provost, out of reverence for the Apostolic See and ourselves, as a canon and brother, and liberally bestow upon him a prebend, if any is currently vacant in your church or as soon as an opportunity presents itself, notwithstanding that he is already beneficed elsewhere or if we have directed our writings to your church on behalf of others, or any statute regarding a fixed number of canons, confirmed by oath or confirmation of the Apostolic See or by any other firmness. Otherwise, we mandate our beloved sons, the abbot and the prior in Ulse of the diocese of Verden, to execute the apostolic mandate regarding these matters; opponents, etc. Given at Lyon, 16th August, in the fifth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa decano et capitulo Halberstatensibus mandat, ut Albertum prepositum Stindarensis ecclesiae in canonicum et fratrem recipiant, eique prebendam conferant, non obstantibus aliis beneficiis aut statutis. 1247, Aug. 16, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To H. de Klingemberc, canon of Chur. We are moved to extend to you the gift of grace due to the devoted prayers of our beloved sons, the noble men H. the elder and H. the younger, counts of Kiburg, of whom you are the counselor. Therefore, as you have taken the care to explain, since you often need to communicate with the noble man, the count of Raprethtiswiler, son-in-law of the aforementioned younger count, to whom you are frequently sent by these same counts for matters concerning the church, as well as with some other supporters of the late Emperor Frederick, we, wishing to ensure your safety in this matter, and inclined by the prayers of the said counts, grant you by the authority of these presents that, in communicating with the aforementioned individuals for such occasions, as long as you diligently give aid and effort so that they may return to the mandate of the church, you shall not incur the chain of major excommunication. Let no one, therefore, etc., infringe our concession, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 9th of February, in the fifth year.

---

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa H. de Klingemberc canonico Curiensi concedit, ne in communicatione cum comite de Raprethtiswiler et fautoribus quondam imperatoris, dummodo eos ad ecclesiae mandatum revocare studeat, excommunicationem maiorem incurrat. 1231, Feb. 9, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To G. de Montelongo, our subdeacon and notary, legate of the apostolic see. It is fitting and reasonable, etc., as stated above in the 654th chapter, up to: persecuted, and they have presumed with reckless boldness to devastate the goods of those who, leaving the city of Cremona, adhered to the same church: we, intending to avenge such an excess at its appropriate time according to its enormity, bind with the sentence of excommunication the authorities, judges, and commune of Cremona, and all those who gave counsel, aid, or favor towards the devastation of those goods, by the counsel of our brothers, from which they cannot be absolved unless they first make full satisfaction to those whose goods have been devastated, for all damages and expenses known to have been incurred on this account. We mandate that you solemnly publish and cause to be published all the above in all places where you see fit; contradictors, etc. Given at Lyon, March 9th, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa G. de Montelongo subdiacono et notario apostolicae sedis legato mandat, ut sententiam excommunicationis in potestatem, iudices et comune Cremonensium, qui bona fidelium devastaverunt, publicet, et ut absolvi non possint nisi prius plenarie satisfaciant. 1247, Mart. 9. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Gregory de Montelongo, our subdeacon and notary, legate of the Apostolic See. It is fitting and reasonable that those who, putting aside divine fear and the salvation of souls, do not hesitate to resort to violence, should be punished with due retribution, so that their punishment may instill fear in others. Since the commune of Cremona, with some exceptions of loyal and devoted members of the Church, has been known to have persecuted the Church and its faithful more aggressively than before, clinging almost inseparably to the deposed Frederick, the former emperor, after the sentence of deposition was pronounced: we, intending to punish such excesses according to their enormity in due time, invalidate all dowries and marriage contracts or promises made for any marriage by the disloyal of Cremona, either within or outside the city, whether they were made fraudulently or willingly accepted by the parties. We command that you solemnly publish and have published all of the above in all places where you see it to be expedient; contradictors etc. Given at Lyons, 9th of March, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa Gregorio de Montelongo subdiacono et notario, legato apostolice sedis, mandat ut omnes dotes et contractus matrimoniorum a Cremonensibus indevotis factas irritas pronuntiet et publicet. 1231, Mar. 9, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Passau. On behalf of the noble women M., widow of the late H., son of F., formerly Emperor, and G., widow of the late W., son of our dearly beloved in Christ, the illustrious King of Bohemia, a complaint was presented to us that the brothers of the Hospital of St. Mary of the Germans in Starkemberg in the diocese of Passau unjustly hold certain privileges, by which they ought to inherit in the duchy of Austria by hereditary right, and refuse to return them. Therefore, we command that, if this is so, you compel the said brothers, with a prior warning and without any appeal, using ecclesiastical censure, to restore these privileges to the said women, as they are obliged to do, according to justice. Given at Lyon, 3rd day before the Nones of September, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Pataviensi mandat, ut fratres Hospitalis Sancte Marie Theutonicorum in Starkemberch compellat, ut privilegia, quae nobiles mulieres in ducatu Austrie iure hereditario succedere debent, eis restituant, si contra iustitiam detinent. 1248, Sept. 3, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of Luzela of the Cistercian order of the diocese of Basel. Our beloved son, the noble man Diethalmus, son of the late count of Toggenburg, complained in our presence that the noble man, the count of Montfort of the diocese of Chur, unjustly detains Elisabeth, his niece, the wife of the said Diethalmus, and is said to have forcibly betrothed her, resisting and unwilling, to another man. We command that, if this is the case, you should diligently admonish and induce the said count to either return the woman to her husband Diethalmus, as he is obliged, without any difficulty, or place her in a safe location accessible to both parties, so that the count or anyone else may, if they wish, make and prove any reasonable objection against the marriage contracted between the aforesaid Diethalmus and the woman. If necessary, compel him to one of the aforementioned actions by the sentences of excommunication upon his person and interdict, removing any appeal. Given at Lyon, on the Nones of October, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa abbati de Luzela Cisterciensis ordinis Basiliensis diocesis mandat, ut comitem Montisfortis moneat et inducat, ne neptem suam Elisabeth, uxorem Diethalmi, contra iustitiam detineat, sed eam viro suo restituat aut eam in loco tuto ponat, ut matrimonium cum Diethalmo contractum impugnari possit. Si necesse fuerit, per excommunicationis in personam et interdicti sententias compellat. 1247, Oct. 7. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To P., Cardinal Deacon of San Giorgio in Velabro, legate of the apostolic see. Although the constitution of the sacred council prohibits contracting marriage within the fourth degree of consanguinity and affinity, the apostolic see is accustomed to dispense with this prohibition when evident necessity and utility require it. We mandate, therefore, that if you ascertain that knights Walter of Ekoven and Arnold of Ranste, who are said to be in the fourth degree of consanguinity with their wives, and Arnold called Amas, who is said to be in the same degree of affinity with his wife, are beneficial to our beloved noble son, the Duke of Lorraine and Brabant, in ecclesiastical matters, and you see it as expedient, and if they have taken the cross against the former Emperor F., to which they offer themselves ready, you may dispense with them by our authority, having received sufficient caution from them on this matter, so that they may freely remain in the marriages thus contracted. Given at Lyon, on the second day before the Kalends of September, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali mandat ut, si necessitas et utilitas exposcat, cum militibus Waltero de Ekoven et Arnoldo de Ranste, qui cum uxoribus suis in quarto consanguinitatis et affinitatis gradu sunt, auctoritate apostolica dispenset ad matrimonia contrahenda. Dat. Lugduni, II Kalendas Septembris, anno quarto.

**Translation to English:**

To the provost of the church of Newcastle, in the diocese of Lausanne. Our beloved son, the noble man Conrad, advocate of Freiburg, has complained to us that the noble man, the lord of Valkenstein, and certain other laymen of the dioceses of Basel and Constance, are causing him injury regarding lands, debts, and other matters. Therefore, since he cannot obtain the fulfillment of justice in those parts before a secular judge, as he asserts, because the people of those regions oppose our beloved son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, W., to whom the dominion of that country pertains, adhering to the persecutor of the church, he has humbly petitioned for the remedy of the Apostolic See to be provided for him in this matter. Therefore, in order that the aforementioned wrongdoers do not benefit from their malice in this matter or that the rights of the aforementioned nobleman do not perish for this reason, we command you to summon the parties, hear the case, and, with the appeal removed, observe the prescription of use, etc., ensuring that it does not impact the land of the said noble, etc. Witnesses, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 10th of February, in the fifth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa preposito ecclesiae Novicastri Lausanensis diocesis mandat, ut partes convocet et causam inter Conradum advocatum de Friburch et laicos Basiliensis et Constantiensis diocesum audiat. 1248, Feb. 10, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the dean of Regensburg. On behalf of our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Salzburg, it has been brought to our attention that although we had instructed Philip, provost of the church of Visegrád, not to harass the aforementioned archbishop concerning the presumed election of himself in the Salzburg church, and had given our letters to the chapter and clergy, as well as to all the counts, barons, officials, and people of the city and diocese of Salzburg, to humbly and devoutly obey him as their archbishop, we had appointed our venerable brother, the Bishop of Gurk, and our beloved son, the elect of Regensburg, as executors in this matter: since the same bishop has been imprisoned and the said elect is away, our mandate could not be executed in this matter. We command you to proceed to execute it according to the content of the previous letters—notwithstanding if bishops or other prelates or religious, subject to the metropolitan jurisdiction of the Salzburg church, have been granted by the Apostolic See that they cannot be interdicted or excommunicated without special mandate of the same See, mentioning such indulgence. Given at Lyon, on the 12th of August, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa decano Ratisponensi mandat, ut mandatum suum pro exequendo electionem archiepiscopi Salzeburgensis exequatur, non obstante indulto a sede apostolica episcopis vel aliis prelatis subiectis. 1231, Aug. 12, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, legate of the apostolic see. No one of sound mind is unaware that since F., the former emperor, a member of the devil, minister of Satan, and the unfortunate herald of the Antichrist, aspires to the destruction of the orthodox faith, the trample of the nobles and other faithful, and the total annihilation of the Church, it is more expedient and pleasing to our God and Lord Jesus Christ, against whom he does not fear to presume such things, to aid at present our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious king of the Romans, against the treachery of his wickedness, rather than even to the Holy Land. For to that land, whose temple the same wicked man has made defiled by the filth of the Saracens, as if damningly agreeing with them, aid cannot be brought from here, and the faithful of Christ could not hope for any help from there, however great the necessity might be. Therefore, we command you to preach the cross against the aforementioned F. and to have it preached throughout Germany, and to grant indulgence of their sins to those taking up the sign of the cross for this purpose, as you see fit for the urgent business that requires prompt assistance. Given at Lyons, on the 13th day before the Kalends of December, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Petro Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali mandat, ut crucem contra F. quondam imperatorem per Theutoniam predicet et indulgentias concedat. 1247, Nov. 19, apud Lugdunum.

**Translation to English:**

To the power and people of Camerino. It is fitting for us to look with a kindly eye upon those who have returned to the embrace of the mother church, from which they had departed by adhering to the enemies of the church, and to support them manifoldly with the grace of the Apostolic See. Since the city of Camerino has wisely returned to the bosom of the church, from which it had long strayed, and because you have suffered damages, burdens, and losses due to this, we, bearing a compassionate affection towards you, by the authority of these presents, grant that you are henceforth not obliged to pay tolls throughout the March, the Duchy, and everywhere through the patrimony of Saint Peter. Therefore, let no one etc. of our concession etc. Given at Lyon, on the Nones of December, in the fifth year of our pontificate. To H. .. prior of Saint Venantius of Camerino. Those who etc., as above until: they are not obliged, we have decided to grant through our letters. Wherefore we command that you do not allow them to be unjustly troubled by anyone against the tenor of our concession; such troublemakers etc. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa potestati et populo Camerinensibus concedit ut ad solvenda pedagia per Marchiam et Ducatum et patrimonium beati Petri non teneantur, postquam ad ecclesiam reversi sunt. Datum Lugduni, Nonis Decembris, anno quinto pontificatus.

**Translation to English:**

To P., cardinal deacon of St. George at Velum Aureum, legate of the Apostolic See. Our beloved son, the noble Albert, Count of Tyrol, and certain other nobles have informed us through their letters that the Church of Trent has collapsed severely, both spiritually and temporally diminished, its rights, possessions, and other goods having been oppressed for a long time by the late Emperor Frederick and almost reduced to nothing. They humbly beseech us in the same letters that the Church might be well governed and its rights defended by appointing Bruno, a canon of Magdeburg, a man they assert to be learned, prudent, and discerning, and who is of the greater adherents of the Church in the land of Swabia, as bishop and pastor. The said count, who is said to be the advocate of the aforementioned church, along with the same nobles, relatives, and friends of the said canon, as powerful men, pledge to unite their strength to effectively labor and strive toward the upliftment and defense of the church’s rights by the same canon’s promotion. Therefore, we command that if what is asserted about the aforementioned canon is supported by truth and you see other things converging toward this as well, and if the aforementioned church is presently vacant by right, you should provide for the same church through the aforementioned canon by our authority, either by yourself or through our venerable brother, the bishop of Würzburg, who is said to have knowledge of this matter; contradictors, etc. Given at Lyon, Kalends of October, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Honorius III papa P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum cardinali diacono, apostolicae sedis legato, mandat ut, si Brunonis canonici Magdeburgensis virtutes in veritate fundatae sunt, et ecclesia Tridentina iure vacat, eidem ecclesiae providet in episcopum. Datum Lugduni, Kal. Oct. anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz and his suffragans. Commending the diligence and care you are known to have exercised in the election of our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, with worthy praises in the Lord, we return to you the thanks we can offer. Since the more significant the undertaking, the more it requires greater assistance for its successful completion, we earnestly ask, advise, and exhort your fraternity, granting remission of your sins, that, prudently considering that in such an arduous task one must not be dormant, you should assist the said king with manly and powerful support, using the prudence given to you by the Lord, and giving your help and effort to those things which you see would benefit this matter. Given at Lyon, 19th November, in the fifth year. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Cologne and his suffragans. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Trier and his suffragans. In the same manner to the Archbishop of Bremen and his suffragans. In the same manner to the Bishop of Würzburg. In the same manner to the Bishop of Strasbourg. In the same manner to the Bishop of Münster. In the same manner to the Bishop-elect of Speyer. In the same manner to the Duke of Brabant. In the same manner to the Count of Guelders. In the same manner to the Count of Looz.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino et eius suffraganeis mandat ut, remissis peccatis, consueta constantia regem Romanorum illustrum adiuvent. 1230, Nov. 19, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Strasbourg. From the contents of your letters, we have learned that the beloved sons, the abbot and convent of the monastery of Gengenbach of the Order of Saint Benedict in your diocese, have been afflicted by many injuries and oppressed by serious harm due to the supporters of the late Emperor Frederick. One of these supporters presumed to capture the said abbot, who was girded for a journey to the Apostolic See, and held him in prison for some time. However, due to these losses, the said monastery is burdened with heavy debts and cannot easily be relieved without the cooperation of apostolic assistance. We, acceding to your prayers, commit to you by the authority of these presents, that you may grant the said abbot and convent the free faculty to retain for one year only, nine churches of those in which they hold the right of patronage, when they shall become vacant, and to convert their revenues entirely to the payment of such debts. However, the churches themselves must not be deprived of due services in the meantime, and a suitable portion of their revenues must be left to the ministers of these churches, from which they can reasonably sustain themselves. Given at Lyon, on the 2nd day before the Ides of December, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Argentinensi mandat, ut abbati et conventui monasterii Gengembacensis concedat facultatem retinendi proventus novem ecclesiarum ad solutionem debitorum. Datum Lugduni, II Idus Decembris, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Strasbourg. The noble sons H. and H., counts of Kiburc, presented before us that Renaud, a canon of Strasbourg and brother to the noble men Conrad and Henry, lords of Tengen, while being in the order of subdeacon, allegedly contracted a relationship with a certain widow and cohabited with her for some time, engaging in carnal relations. Eventually, returning to his senses, he completely cast away the widow and returned to the clerical order. Therefore, the aforesaid counts humbly petitioned us that, since the same canon, whom they hold in great affection and esteem, has vigorously assisted and continues to assist you in the affairs of the church, and his noble and powerful brothers are prepared to comply with our good pleasures and strongly oppose the adversaries of the church, we should kindly care to dispense with him on this matter as usual. We command you to dispense by our authority, so that the said canon may serve in minor orders, if you deem it expedient. Given at Lyon, on the Ides of February, in the 5th year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Argentinensi mandat, ut auctoritate sua dispenset cum Renaudo canonico Argentinensi, qui, relictis illicitis, ad clericalem ordinem rediit, ut in minoribus ordinibus valeat ministrare, si expedire videatur. 1248, Feb. 13, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To all the devoted and friends of the Church of the city and diocese of Cremona. In consideration of your steadfast faith, which is known to us towards the Apostolic See, and also considering the losses you have suffered on this account, we, with the advice of our brothers, take your persons with all the goods which you have peacefully and quietly possessed since the time of the Council of Lyon or which you may acquire in the future by just means, under the protection of Saint Peter and ourselves, and we safeguard them by the patronage of this present writing. We declare null and void any pacts, promises, pledges, obligations, donations, renunciations, or any other agreements made by principal persons or others on their behalf, as well as sentences, bans, confiscations, statutes, penalties, privileges, issued or pronounced against you by the late Emperor Frederick or Henry his son or the power of Cremona or their officials or bailiffs in the meantime. Therefore, let no one etc. of our protection and declaration of voidance etc. Given at Lyon, on the 11th of March, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa, universis devotis et amicis ecclesiae Cremonensis, personas suas cum bonis sub protectione beati Petri et sua recipit, et acta contra eos edita ab imperatore F. vel eius filio H. irrita nuntiat. 1247, Mart. 11, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected bishop of Volterra. To the Apostolic See, which, by the grace of the Lord, presides albeit unworthily, bestowing to each their due and never closing its door to those wishing to return to it, we grant by the authority of these letters to your devotion that you may absolve, in our place, those who have adhered to and favored the late Emperor Frederick against the Church and thus incurred the sentence of excommunication, should they wish to leave him and return with humility to the unity of the Church. This is contingent upon receiving sufficient and suitable assurance from them that they will no longer adhere to or favor the said Frederick. You should impose upon them what you see fit to impose according to God. Furthermore, to those adhering to and favoring the Church against the same Frederick, you may grant, as you see expedient, the pardon of their sins, of which they are truly contrite and confessed, with the same authority. As for your assertion that you cannot avoid those excommunicated, we leave it to you, for the benefit of the Church, to communicate with them so that you do not incur any sentence of excommunication by this. Given at Lyon, on the fourth day before the Ides of November, in the fifth year.

**Regesto (in Latin):**

Gregorius IX papa electo Vulterano concedit potestatem absolvendi, vice sua, eos qui excommunicationem incurrerunt ob adhaesionem Friderico quondam imperatori, si ad unitatem Ecclesiae cum cautione redeunt, et veniam peccatorum faventibus Ecclesiae largiendi. Lugduni, II Idus Novembris, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To P., deacon cardinal of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the apostolic see. Since, as was presented to us on behalf of the beloved daughter in Christ, the noble woman, the Duchess of Austria, the master and brethren, and brother Rasco of the hospital of the house of Holy Mary of the Teutons in Austria at Starthenberch and in Gentenstrinb and certain other castles, the treasure and other movable and immovable goods, which belong to her by a concession made to her by a former Duke of Austria, her uncle, by virtue of an imperial privilege granted to the said duke, are said to be detained: we command that you compel, by you or by others, through ecclesiastical censure, the said master and brethren to restore all these to the duchess in full and to satisfy her for the damages which she claims to have incurred on this account, as they are bound to do, after a prior warning, with appeal removed, after considering the case. And if the aforesaid master and brethren do not care to restore the above, if you see it fit, you should seriously admonish our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious king of Bohemia, that he ensures satisfaction is made to the aforementioned noble woman from the revenues that the said master and brethren hold in his kingdom. Given at Lyons, the 5th day before the Kalends of February, in the fifth year.

---

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali, apostolicae sedis legato, mandat ut magistrum et fratres hospitalis domus Sanctae Mariae Theutonicorum in Austria compellat ad res ducissae Austriae restitui et de dampnis satisfieri, eique in regno Bohemiae satisfieri curandum, si necessarium videatur. Datum Lugduni, V Kalendas Februarii, anno quinto pontificatus.

Translation to English:

To the eminent man O. de Falke, Bishop of Lausanne. We are willing to apply a healthy remedy against the source of hatred and causes of enmity, as we desire that peace may thrive and concord be maintained among the faithful of Christ from the innermost affection of the heart. Indeed, between our beloved son John, son of the noble man William de Gomens, and his own on one side, and the noble man Peter...d of the same place of your diocese on the other, mortal enmities have arisen, as we have been informed, instigated by the enemy of humankind, from which multiple dangers are feared to be imminent unless, by God’s grace, the balm of peace promptly intervenes between them. However, since our beloved sons, the noble men H. and H., counts of Kiburg, have earnestly petitioned us in our presence that we might deign to remove the matter of such a great danger by the aid of apostolic piety, we entrust to your fraternity’s diligence, in which we place special trust in the Lord, by the authority of these presents, to arrange with the aforementioned John, if he is faithful to the Roman Church along with his own, that he may be able to unite in marriage with Isabella, the daughter of the said Peter — notwithstanding that they are related in the fourth degree of consanguinity. Given as above.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Lausanensi mandat ut Iohannes, si est devotus ecclesiae Romanae, cum Ysabellam filiam Petri in matrimonium copulare possit, non obstante quarta consanguinitatis linea, ad pacem inter partes procurandam. Datum Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To Brother Bonefideus of the Order of Friars Minor. Presenting to the eyes of our mind the distress by which the beloved sons, the clergy and people of Benevento, faithful to the Roman Church, are wickedly afflicted by its enemies, we willingly seek to provide consolation to their hearts as we can rightly do. Since they, because they communicate and associate with the late Emperor Frederick and his officials and envoys, albeit unwillingly, are bound by the snare of excommunication and are almost daily compelled to be bound due to such association, we, acceding to their pious desires, entrust to you by the authority of these presents, that you may grant the benefit of absolution to the same clergy and people, when they have humbly decided to recur to you for this reason, according to the form of the Church, and impose salutary penance and administer ecclesiastical sacraments.
