Furthermore, if it happens that you are absent, you shall entrust your duties regarding this to two or three discreet and prudent brothers of your order with the same authority. Given at Lyon, on the 5th day before the Kalends of August, in the fifth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Fratri Bonefidei de ordine fratrum Minorum mandat ut clero et populo Beneventano, qui inviti cum Friderici quondam imperatoris officialibus communicant et excommunicatione laqueati sunt, absolutionem concedat et sacramenta ministret, vices suas fratribus commissurus si absens fuerit. Datum Lugduni, V Kalendas Augusti, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the procurator of the church of Salzburg. Since, as we have learned, our beloved daughter in Christ, the noble woman, the Duchess of Austria, inflamed with zeal for faith and devotion and inserting a masculine spirit into feminine thought, intends to oppose the enemies of the Church: we earnestly ask, admonish, and exhort your devotion, commanding that you show yourself favorable to her in this, and assist her vigorously and powerfully in her rights. Moreover, we will and command that you place the castles and places of your province and diocese, whose inhabitants have bound themselves by an oath against the Church to the late emperor Frederick, under ecclesiastical interdict, and proceed against those inhabitants both spiritually and temporally. Given at Lyon, January 23, in the fifth year of our pontificate. To the bishop of Olomouc. Since, as we have learned, our beloved daughter in Christ, the noble woman, the Duchess of Austria, inflamed with zeal for faith and devotion and inserting a masculine spirit into feminine thought, etc. as above in chapter 522 until: places of the duchy of Austria, whose etc. as above until the end. In the same manner to the bishop of Seckau.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa procuratori ecclesiae Salzeburgensis mandat, ut duci Austriae in iure suo assistat et loca, quorum habitatores se Friderico quondam imperatori astrinxerunt, interdicto ecclesiastico supponat. Datum Lugduni, 23 Ianuarii, anno 5.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Curonia. Although the matter of the Holy Land is very dear to our heart, the cause of the general church solicits us with even greater care, as a greater danger looms unless the distant matter progresses successfully. For the persecutor of God and men, the angel of darkness, with cunningly sustained machines of deceit and trickery, works to devote himself entirely to the subversion of both faith and the church. Therefore, since our beloved son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, has assumed this cause and it rightfully belongs to him, as he ought to be the advocate and defender of the church, yet he cannot pursue it by himself; we, considering that this cause is not individual but common and pertains to all Christians, and wishing to help this king as much as we can, command that throughout the empire, according to what our beloved son P. Cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the apostolic see, shall enjoin upon you, you preach and have preached the word of the cross in aid of this king. You are to grant the remission of sins with our authority to those who take up the cross to help the said king, which is granted to crusaders crossing to aid the Holy Land. Given at Lyons, 20th of February, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Curoniel mandat ut verbum crucis per totum imperium, secundum quod P. Sancti Georgii diaconus cardinalis iusserit, predicet, veniam peccatorum concedens crucem assumentibus ad regem Romanorum adiuvandum. 1240, Febr. 20, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the same. Bearing greater confidence in the prudence of your discretion in the Lord, we command that, diligently assessing whether our venerable brother, the bishop of Basel, requires an assistant, you provide an appropriate assistant for him by our authority, who is devoted to the Church and is able and willing to effectively advance the task at hand; any contradictors, etc. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa mandat ut, si episcopo Basiliensi coadiutor necessarius sit, idoneus coadiutor auctoritate apostolica provideatur. Datum Anagniae, anno tertio.

**Translation to English:**

To the citizens of Cologne. Just as it is the Lord's doing that a person not only worthy but most worthy has been unexpectedly elevated to the pinnacle of the empire, so we believe it is the Lord's doing that the city of Cologne, so famous and celebrated and in some way unique in the regions of Germany, excelling other cities in size, nobility, and power, has willingly chosen to receive and honor this person, namely our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious king of the Romans. For this, we extend to you many thanks, as you have bound us, the Apostolic See, and the king himself to you all the more, as it is known that through this, the king's progress is directed favorably and his status elevated prosperously. Since the crown is not for those who begin but for those who persevere to the end, although you have a reputation and omen for the virtue of constancy among others, it does no harm to urge the forward horse. Therefore, we earnestly ask, admonish, and exhort your community, offering you the remission of sins, that, considering wisely what is prudent—to progress in virtue—you persist in unwavering firmness and usual devotion to the king, so that, with apostolic and royal favor increasing for you, you may not undeservedly be commended for your perseverance in faith before God and men. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa civibus Coloniensibus gratias agit, quod regem Romanorum honoraverint, et hortatur eos ut in devotione eius perseverent, promittens remissionem peccaminum. Lugduni, anno quinto, die ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To P., deacon cardinal of Saint George at the Golden Veil, legate of the apostolic see. The proven devotion of our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Mainz, shines brightly in necessity, where friends are known, so that he is to be considered not only a legitimate but also a special son of the apostolic see. He fully exhibits to it, as a mother, what is due to filial affection, standing by and supporting it vigorously and powerfully in times of necessity. Therefore, we, loving him with a special prerogative of charity, desire to pursue him with the sweetness of affection in such a way that we also wish to show the love we have for him to his own through our actions. Considering, therefore, not only the great but indeed the pleasing and useful services which the same archbishop and through him his own have rendered to the Roman Church as faithfully as effectively, and wishing to honor him in his beloved nephew, Brother Henry, of the order of Friars Minor, whom we also desire to pursue with grace and favor in view of his religion, honesty, and probity, we command you that, if any bishopric within the boundaries of your legation is vacant at present or will soon become vacant, in which provision can and should be suitably made for himself and him, you should take care to provide for the same, by our authority, with regard to this brother; those opposing, etc. Given at Lyons, 24th of August, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa P. S. Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali mandat ut, si episcopatus infra legationis fines vacat, eum fratri Henrico, nepotem archiepiscopi Maguntini, ordinis Minorum, conferat. 1247, Aug. 24. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Lausanne. The presumptuous audacity of many who arrogantly oppose the Church, their mother, or rather against God, has grown to such an extent that, utterly devoid of the spirit of discretion and reason, they rush headlong like animals worse than brutes and eagerly engage in injuries and offenses against us, the Roman Church, and their Creator. It is fitting, necessary, and expedient that the proud necks of these individuals be humbled and subdued, lest their insolence becomes too rampant or their impudence gains further strength. Therefore, as our beloved sons, the noble men H. the elder and H. the younger, counts of Kyburg, have taken care to inform us, certain men of Bern and others in your diocese, with raised necks against God and supporting persecutors of His Church with all their might, have obstructed the path of our beloved son O., Cardinal Deacon of St. Mary in Via Lata, legate of the Apostolic See, and the soldiers proceeding in support of the Church. This is all the more grievous since rebelling against father and mother is a greater offense. We, wishing to break the bonds of their iniquity and restrain the impudence of their condemnable boldness, command you to assist the aforementioned counts, who have sincerely undertaken the cause of the Church, and their envoys, whenever requested by them, with a strong and outstretched arm against the aforementioned Bernese and other enemies of the Church. Do not hesitate to pronounce the sentence of excommunication upon all those who have communicated with the said Bernese and others by buying, selling, or any other means whatsoever, and to place their lands under ecclesiastical interdict, so that they may learn how hard it is to kick against the goad and foolishly raise horns against the father. Given at Lyon, on the 12th of February, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Lausanensi mandat, ut contra Bernenses et alios ecclesiae inimicos excommunicationis sententiam promulget et eorum terras interdicto ecclesiastico supponat. Dat. Lugduni, II Idus Februarii, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the princes, dukes, margraves, and messengers of other noble princes to be gathered at the forthcoming council in Aachen. We believe you are aware that our most beloved son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, whose person is recognized not only as worthy but most worthy of such great dignity, has been elevated to the pinnacle of the empire not through human agency but rather through divine mystery, almost unexpectedly; wherefore all, especially the devoted of the Church and the faithful of the empire, ought to rejoice and rise with ready magnanimity to support him, as it is undoubted that this has happened by divine inspiration or rather disposition. Since it is without doubt that the princes of Germany have been strengthened by this, considering that the progeny of the late Emperor Frederick, having been rejected, attempts to claim the empire as if by succession, we earnestly ask, admonish, and exhort your community, and enjoin upon you for the remission of your sins, that you might powerfully and manfully support the aforementioned king, providing him with counsel and necessary aid against the aforesaid Frederick, the manifest adversary of God, the Church, and the empire, so that you might deservedly be commended for this before God and men, and we, who share in the successes of the same king and thrive in his prosperity, might be obliged to your and your descendants’ benefits and honors. Given at Lyon, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of December, in the fifth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa principibus, ducibus, marchionibus aliorumque nobilium nuntiis apud Aquisgranum congregandis scribit, ut regi Romanorum contra Fridericum consilium et auxilium exhibeant. 1247. Nov. 20. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To P., cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the apostolic see. Since our venerable brother, the bishop of Augsburg, as he has made known to us through his letters, desires to resign, having become unable to perform pastoral duties, we command you to receive his resignation on our behalf and to provide for him from the episcopal goods so that he may be suitably sustained. We believe that it would be beneficial for the Church of Augsburg, provided you also find it suitable, to appoint the beloved son Hartmann, a canon of the same church and born of the noble man, the count of Dillingen, who is devoted to the Roman Church, as bishop and pastor, if he is suitable. Otherwise, entrust the administration of the Augsburg church, both in spiritual and temporal matters, to the same canon, who, by the favor of the late H. king of the Romans and other relatives, has deserved the grace and favor of the apostolic see; any objectors, etc. Given at Lyon, the 7th of October, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali, apostolicae sedis legato, mandat ut, episcopo Augustensi cessionem petenti, vice sua cessionem recipiat et eidem de bonis episcopalibus provideat; Hartmannum canonicum, si idoneus sit, in episcopum praeficiat, alioquin administrationem ecclesiae committat. 1231, Oct. 7, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of Wectingen of the Cistercian order in the diocese of Constance. Since the beloved sons, the citizens of Basel, have returned to the devotion of the Church, abandoning its persecutor, as Catholic and faithful men, we, intending to pursue them with grace and favor on account of this, command that you ensure their rights and customs, long owed to them, are preserved intact by our authority; [you shall act against] the contradictors, etc. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati de Wectingen mandat, ut iura et consuetudines civibus Basiliensibus ab antiquo debita illesa auctoritate sua faciat servari. 1234, ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the provost of the church of Minor Augia, of the Premonstratensian order in the Diocese of Constance. Beloved sons, the abbot and convent of the monastery of Wettingen of the Cistercian order have complained to us that although the nobleman, the count of Froburg, with the consent of the beloved sons, R. the provost of Boningen and the noblemen H. the count of Homberg and Hartmann, his sons, sold certain properties with their appurtenances and other goods in the village of Arneuestorfe, which belong to him, for a certain sum of money, the said Hartmann has violently occupied the aforementioned properties and goods according to his own will and unlawfully retains them, to their prejudice and grievance. Therefore, since it is fitting that religious places be relieved through apostolic favor in times of need, we command that, if so, you hear the case brought by the aforesaid abbot and convent, having first restored all the aforementioned goods as is just, and decide it to a due end without appeal, implementing what you have decreed, etc.; ensuring that nothing is done in the land of the said nobleman, etc.; no letters from the apostolic see prejudicial to the truth and justice obtained may stand in the way. Witnesses, etc. Given at Lyon, 11th of October, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa preposito ecclesiae de Minori Augia mandat, ut si vera sunt quae abbas et conventus monasterii de Wettingen queruntur de bona a comite de Froburg vendita et a Hartmanno iniuste occupata, restitutis bonis causam audiat et fine debito decernat, sublata appellatione, nullis obstantibus litteris apostolicis iustitiae adversis. Datum Lugduni, V Idus Octobris, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To Engelbert, a cleric of Strasbourg. Although those born from a union not justified by the bond of marriage are considered illegitimate, we readily extend mercy to those who strive to erase the stain of their birth with honorable conduct, as if they have received grace from the Lord, since where the Lord is generous, the servant should not be stingy. Therefore, since you, born of a priest and an unmarried woman, redeem the defect of your birth through the advancement of your merits, we, desiring to do good to the virtuous and intending this also through the petition of our beloved sons, the noble men of Dilgen, of Wirtemberg, of Gruningen, and of Calw, counts of Swabia, who earnestly interceded for you to us, grant you a special grace that, notwithstanding such defect, you may be promoted to holy orders and obtain an ecclesiastical benefice, even if it has the care of souls, by the authority of these presents, with the condition, however, that if you happen to be called to episcopal dignity, you shall by no means accept it without the special permission of the Apostolic See. Let no one, therefore, infringe our dispensation. Given at Lyon, on the Nones of February, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Engelberto clerico Argentinensi concedit dispensationem specialem, qua, non obstante defectu natalium ex sacerdote genitus et soluta, ad sacros ordines promoveri et beneficium ecclesiasticum cum cura animarum obtinere possit, sed ad dignitatem episcopalem sine apostolicae sedis licentia speciali non ascendat. Dat. Lugduni, Nonis Februarii, anno quinto.

Translation to English:

To the provost and chapter of Basel. We willingly treat with due honor the person of our venerable brother, the bishop of Strasbourg, who labors with indefatigable spirit for ecclesiastical liberty, especially in matters we perceive to be dear to his heart and contributing to the benefit of the Roman Church and its devotees. Therefore, at his intercession, who has earnestly requested apostolic grace through heartfelt letters for our beloved son Peter, canon of the church of Lutemburg and brother of the noble man Wezelon of Lapide, who valiantly assists him for the aforementioned liberty, we have decided to ask and admonish your entire community, ordering that you admit the said Peter in brotherhood and as a canon out of reverence for the Apostolic See and us, and that you liberally provide him with a prebend as soon as the opportunity arises — notwithstanding if your church has a fixed number of canons, confirmed by oath or any other firm means, or any indulgence requiring explicit mention in our letters, or which could hinder such grace, or if he is otherwise beneficed, or if we have directed our writings for others in the same church, which we do not wish to disturb, etc. —; fulfilling our requests and mandates in such a way that we may compensate you with favors and grace at the opportune times. Otherwise, we have ordered our venerable brother, the bishop of Basel, through our letters to execute the apostolic mandate concerning this; opponents etc. Given at Lyon, the 24th of February, in the fifth year.

Regesto in Latin:

Innocentius IV papa Basiliensi preposito et capitulo mandat, ut Petrum canonicum Lutembatensem, fratri Wezelonis de Lapidet, in fratrem et canonicum admittant et prebenda provideant. Si non, episcopus Basiliensis mandatump exequatur. 1258, Feb. 24. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the dean and chapter of Saint Nicholas in Magdeburg. At the apostolic see, our beloved sons, the noble men H. of Obdriborch and H. Ascarie, counts, and B. of Magdeburg, by the merits of their devotion and faith, have made themselves deserving of such favor that we, at appropriate times, willingly assent to their requests concerning matters of honor and grace. Indeed, the said nobles have affectionately requested us, through special letters, on behalf of their devoted son Arnold, a cleric from Magdeburg, that we extend some fitting grace upon him, as he is said to have not yet secured any ecclesiastical benefice. Since this cleric is commended to us with honest morals and praiseworthy conduct, we have deemed it appropriate to earnestly ask and admonish your community, commanding that you admit him into your fraternity and as a canon, and that you provide him with a prebend as soon as the opportunity arises, out of reverence for the apostolic see and ourselves — notwithstanding a certain number of canons bound by oath or any firm agreement, or if we have sent our letters to you on behalf of another, which we do not wish, etc., up to: to be generated, or any indulgence, about which special mention should be made in our letters —; you shall fulfill our request and mandate in such a manner that an increase in favor and grace may come to you from us as a result. Otherwise, we have instructed our beloved son .., the provost of the church of Saint Vitus of Niemborch in the diocese of Magdeburg, through our letters, to execute the apostolic mandate on this; those who oppose, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 13th day before the Kalends of January, in the fifth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto (in Latin):**

Gregorius IX papa decano et capitulo Sancti Nicolai Magdeburgensis mandat, ut Arnoldum clericum de Magdeburca in fratrem et canonicum admittant ac de prebenda provideant. 1230, Dec. 20, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the provost of the church of Rival of the Premonstratensian order in the diocese of Constance. Our beloved son, Conrad called Judaman, a knight who has taken the cross from Thurgau, has shown us in his petition that Conrad, the son of the former Emperor F., has presumptuously decided to outlaw him for a certain offense committed by the knight, over whom he has no jurisdiction. Our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans G., has decreed that such an outlawry is null since it was done by one who is not a judge, as is more fully contained in the letters drawn up about this matter. Egelolf of Asele, a knight, the father of Ita, the wife of the aforementioned knight and of the diocese of Constance, has, due to this matter, taken the said Ita, his wife, and certain homes, vineyards, possessions, and other goods pertaining to her dowry into his hands, and through violence, he retains and refuses to return the wife and the aforementioned goods. We command you, therefore, if this is true, to admonish and effectively induce the said Egelolf to restore the aforementioned wife as well as the homes, possessions, vineyards, and other goods, which he has recklessly occupied, along with the fruits received from the time of such occupation, not omitting to compel him to do this, if necessary, through ecclesiastical censure, with prior admonition and disregarding any appeal, once the truth has been established. Concerning the witnesses, etc. Given at Lyon, 4th February, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa preposito ecclesiae de Rival Premonstratensis ordinis Constantiensis diocesis mandat ut Egelolfum de Asele compellat ad restituendum Itam uxorem et bona eius, quae temere occupavit. 1258, Feb. 4, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Strasbourg. Since we address various letters to you concerning the appointment of a coadjutor for our venerable brother, the Bishop of Basel, and the granting of a captain or defender to the citizens of Basel, and since our beloved son, the provost of Grandivallensis, is deemed suitable due to his nobility, industriousness, and power, it seems expedient and agreeable to us that you should provide for him concerning these matters if you are to proceed with them, especially since he is agreeable to the nobles of that land and the aforementioned citizens and desires and is able, together with them, to promote the business of the church both vigorously and beneficially. Given at Lyon, 2nd of the Kalends of April, in the 5th year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Argentinensi mandat, ut, si ad procedendum sit, de preposito Grandivallensi, propter eius idoneitatem, ad conferendum coadiutorem episcopo Basiliensi ac defensorem civibus Basiliensibus provideat. 1231, Mart. 31. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbess and convent of the monastery of Scandensis, of the Order of Saint Benedict in the diocese of Chur. We are moved by the merits of our beloved son, the noble man Ulric of Clinginb, who, as we have learned, is earnestly intent on promoting the honor of the apostolic see, by his own efforts and those of his followers, with God's favor. Therefore, we consent to his desires in those matters where we can do so worthily. Hence, at his request and also considering the regard of our beloved son F., a canon of Beromünster, who, as we have learned, is devotedly and steadfastly promoting the honor of the said see, we have decided to exhort and admonish your community. We are commanding that you provide, as soon as the opportunity arises, for our beloved son Rudeger of Tundorf, a presbyter, devoted to the aforementioned noble and nephew of the same canon, with a suitable ecclesiastical benefice in any of the churches under your collation, which is accustomed to be assigned to secular clerics, for the reverence of the apostolic see and ourselves—this is notwithstanding any other letters we may have directed to you concerning others, which we do not wish, etc., up to: to be generated, or any indulgence about which a special mention must be made in our letters—so that you may fulfill our requests and mandate in such a way that your sincerity may be regarded by us with worthy praise and favor. Otherwise, we charge our beloved son, the abbot of Vrinilperc of the Cistercian Order in the diocese of Constance, by our letters, to execute the apostolic mandate in this matter; let those who oppose, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 5th Ides of October, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbatisse et conventui monasterii Scandensist ordinis sancti Benedicti Curiensis diocesis mandat, ut beneficio ecclesiastico Rudegero de Tundorf presbytero provideant, pro reverentia apostolice sedis. Dat. Lugduni, V Idus Octobris, anno Ve.

**Translation to English:**

To the same. Although the acts carried out by our mandate possess full authority in themselves, we willingly support them with apostolic protection to render them even more robust and unassailable, when they are fortified with our backing. Therefore, since we have sent directives to our venerable brother, the Bishop of Strasbourg, concerning the destruction of the house of our venerable brother, the Bishop of Basel, the election of consuls and judges, advocacy, and certain other matters in a specific form, we, inclined by your supplications, confirm and strengthen with apostolic authority whatever the same Bishop of Strasbourg has arranged or decreed in accordance with the terms of these letters, and we support it with the protection of this present writing. Let no one, therefore, etc., of our confirmation, etc. Given as above. A conservator was appointed for them regarding these matters, namely the Abbot of Wechtigen of the Cistercian order, diocese of Constance, under the same date.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Argentinensi scribit, confirmans et auctoritate apostolica communiens quae idem episcopus super destructione domus episcopi Basiliensis, electione consulum et iudicum, advocatia et aliis ordinavit. 1237.

**Translation to English:**

To the same. As we have learned, religious persons and others in the city of Acre are presuming to rent their houses to public prostitutes, which results in many scandals and dangers to souls. We command that you compel the aforementioned and others, by issuing a prior warning and using the appropriate severity, without allowing for appeals, to completely desist from such presumptuous acts in the future, and that the aforementioned prostitutes vacate those places. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa mandat, ut religiosi et cives Acconenses domos suas meretricibus locare desistant et meretrices loca dimittant. Dat. Laterani, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot and convent of the Novillarensis monastery of the Order of Saint Benedict in the diocese of Strasbourg: It was presented before us on your part that, although Master Gervalcus of Strasbourg, your cleric, has served you and your monastery faithfully and devoutly for a long time, you are unable to provide him with an appropriate ecclesiastical benefice, as you are bound by mandate to Santoro and Simon, the son of the noble man Lodewicus advocate of Liethenberc, and six other clerics, from us and our beloved son P., deacon cardinal of Saint George at the Golden Veil, legate of the apostolic see, concerning the conferment of ecclesiastical benefices. But because the beloved sons, the masters, consuls, and the entire community of citizens of Strasbourg have urged us by their letters to extend our customary kindness to him in this matter, we, inclined by their and your pleas, grant you by the authority of these presents, that after Santoro and the son of the aforementioned noble have been provided with the due benefices, you may, preferring him over the other six, as long as these benefices are not specifically assigned or reserved in special churches, provide the said master with a suitable ecclesiastical benefice which pertains to your collation and is customarily assigned to secular clerics— notwithstanding that he may already hold another benefice or that we have previously written on his behalf —, provided, however, that afterward, you provide for the said six clerics as you are bound to do, as soon as the opportunity presents itself. Therefore, no one etc. of our concession etc. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati et conventui monasterii Novillarensis ordinis sancti Benedicti Argentinensis diocesis concedit, post provisum Santoro et nati nobilis viri Lodewici de Liethenberc beneficiis, ut magistrum Gervalcum de Argentina, clericum suum, in ecclesiastico beneficio competenti, aliis sex praelatum, provideant. Datum Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Constance. Since, as we have learned, Master Frederick, the notary of the late Emperor Frederick, and rector of the church of Überlingen, openly supports the said Frederick: because he renders himself unworthy of this ecclesiastical benefice, we command that if this is so, you deprive him of the same church and confer it by our authority on our beloved son Eberhard, the provost of St. Stephen in Constance, your nephew— notwithstanding that he already holds another benefice— and that you assign and induct him into corporal possession of the same church and defend him as inducted; contradictors etc. Given at Lyon, the 5th of the Kalends of April, in the fifth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Constantiensi mandat, ut magistrum Fridericum, notarium quondam imperatoris Friderici et rectorem ecclesiae de Uberlingen, si favore F. manifeste faveat, ab eadem ecclesia privet et eam Eberhardo, nepoti suo et praeposito Sancti Stephani Constantiensis, conferat et in possessionem inducat. Datum Lugduni, V Kalendas Aprilis, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the same. Since, as we have learned, the Kingdom of Jerusalem is incessantly and variously troubled by the Saracens, we mandate that you arrange for the defense of this kingdom with the counsel of our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of Cyprus, and the barons of the same kingdom, as you see fit; any opposers, etc. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa destinat mandatarium ad regni Ierosolimitani custodiam disponendam consilio regis Cypri et baronum, ob infestationem a Sarracenis. Datum Laterani, anno XI, Idibus Aprilis.

**Translation to English:**

To the Abbot of the monastery of Augia of the Order of Saint Benedict, directly subject to the Roman Church without any intermediary. In order for the affairs of the church to advance in your hands, which cannot be achieved without a heavy burden of expenses, we grant you, with the authority of these presents, the free faculty to pledge some of the possessions of your monastery, with the advice of its convent, as collateral for your needs. Given at Lyon, 14th of the Kalends of June, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa abbati monasterii Augensis ordinis Sancti Benedicti concedit facultatem aliquas possessiones monasterii pignore obligare pro necessitatibus suis. 1247, Lugduni, 19 Maii.

**Translation to English:**

To the dean and chapter of Münster. We must duly honor those who are devoted to us and the Church, so that the grace of appropriate provision becomes a cause of joy for them. Indeed, our beloved son, Ernest, a canon of Osnabrück, commended to us for his honest character and laudable conduct, is said to be supported by the merits of our beloved son, the noble Lord L. of Steinford, and other relatives who are devoted to the Apostolic See, so that he may rejoice to have found the gift of special grace with us. Therefore, because of this and also at the behest of our venerable brothers, the Archbishop of Cologne, the Bishop of Osnabrück, and the Bishop of Paderborn, as well as our beloved son, the noble Lord B. of Lippe, who have sent us special letters on his behalf, we earnestly ask and exhort your community, commanding that you admit the same Ernest as a brother and canon out of reverence for the Apostolic See and ourselves, and provide him liberally with a prebend as soon as the opportunity arises—despite a fixed number of canons, any binding oath, or his already holding a benefice, or if we have directed other letters to you for others, with which we do not wish anything to interfere; nor any indulgence that needs to be specially mentioned in our letters—as our request and mandate should be fulfilled in such a way that you may rejoice to have merited an increase of favor and grace with us over time. Otherwise, we instruct our beloved sons, the dean, Hermann and Vromold, canons of the church of St. John of Osnabrück, by our letters to execute this apostolic mandate; any opposers, etc. Given at Lyon, October 30, in the fifth year of our reign.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa Innocentius IV decano et capitulo Monasteriensibus mandat et hortatur ut Ernesti canonici Osnaburgensis in fratrem et canonicum admittatur et de prebenda provideatur, non obstante numero canonicorum et aliis impedimentis. Dat. Lugduni, III Kal. Novembris, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the archpriest of San Fedele of Casate in the diocese of Milan. The devoted prayers of our beloved nephew, the noble man Jacopo, son of the late Bernardo Rubei, urge us to grant a special favor to our dear son Jacopo, called Musca, a canon of the church of Decumani in Milan. Therefore, being inclined by his prayers and wishing to grant him this special favor, we command you to provide him with some prelature in the city or diocese of Milan, worth at least twelve imperial pounds annually, using our authority, if there is any vacancy at present or as soon as a suitable opportunity arises; any opposition notwithstanding. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archipresbytero Sancti Fidelis de Casate Mediolanensis diocesis mandat ut Iacobo dicto Musce canonico ecclesie Decimanorum Mediolanensis provideat de prelatura in civitate vel diocesi Mediolanensi ad minus valente duodecim libras annuatim, si qua vacat. Datum ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To Bertold of Ortingen, cleric. The sincere devotion you are known to have towards us and the Roman Church encourages us to extend to you favor and grace, as much as we can with God. Therefore, since, as your petition presented to us stated, our beloved son, the abbot of the Campidonensis monastery of the order of Saint Benedict in the diocese of Constance, had canonically conferred upon you the vacant church of Rota with its appurtenances, which Henry, its former rector, was deprived of due to his faults by the authority of our beloved son P., cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, legate of the apostolic see, as was his right: we, moved by your pleas and the consideration of our beloved sons, the noble men E. de Eichem and his son E., who are devoted to us and the Roman Church, of whom you are a notary, supplicating on your behalf, hold what has been providently done by the aforesaid abbot as pleasing and valid, and we confirm it by apostolic authority and protect it with the safeguard of this written document. Therefore, let no one etc. Given at Lyons, on the Ides of March, in the fifth year.

**Regesto:**

Innocentius IV papa Bertoldo de Ortingen clerico ecclesiam de Rota cum suis pertinentiis, a Campidonensis abbate canonice collatam, auctoritate apostolica confirmat. 1248, 15 Martii, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To G. de Montelongo, our subdeacon and notary, legate of the Apostolic See. When we diligently consider and reflect in the chamber of our heart, on how many and what kinds of persecutions the Church and we ourselves have suffered, having faced dangers on land and sea, endured the risks and labors of the body, almost to the point of death, for the peace and salvation of the faithful: we deem it expedient for the universal Church, indeed necessary because of the prevailing malice of the times, that such persons be appointed to prelatures, dignities, honors, and other ecclesiastical benefices, especially in the regions of Italy, who are both pleasing to God and acceptable to men, governing their churches beneficially and healthily, honoring the Roman Church with the purity of faith, fervor of devotion, and zeal for righteousness, faithfully and steadfastly supporting its assistants and devotees. But because we firmly trust in the foresight of your discretion, which is guided by law and natural counsel, that you will execute our mandate faithfully and prudently as usual: we command by apostolic letters to your discretion, that in all the cities and dioceses of Lombardy, the March of Treviso, Romagna, and your entire legation, which adhere to or favor the late Emperor F. or his emissaries, you issue a general and, where it seems appropriate, special edict, forbidding the chapters, convents, rectors, or clerics of churches, cities, and dioceses of any condition or order from presuming to elect, request, receive, or nominate anyone as bishop, archdeacon, provost, abbot, or prelate of any dignity, canon, rector, cleric, monk, or lay brother, or for any ecclesiastical benefice, unless they have received a special mandate or license from us in this regard. And so that rash presumption or presumptuous audacity in this matter may profit no one, but rather be harmful, you shall decree that whatever is attempted against your prohibition shall be null and void and of no effect whatsoever, inflicting the penalty of due retribution on the transgressors of this matter nonetheless. Given at Lyon, on the 13th of March, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa mandat G. de Montelongo subdiacono et notario suo, apostolicae sedis legato, ut in civitatibus et dioecesibus Lombardiae, marchiae Tervisinae, Romandiolae et legationis suae prohibitionem edicat, ne alicuius dignitatis ecclesiasticae electiones vel nominations fiant sine licentia apostolica, et contra transgressores debitas poenas decernat. 1258, Mart. 13, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the same. Having full confidence in your discretion in the Lord, we command that if the citizens of Basel wish to have a captain or defender for the good state of the church and the city and diocese of Basel, and if our venerable brother, the bishop of Basel, is so impotent, negligent, or remiss that he is useless for executing the aforesaid, you are to grant them, by our authority, someone devoted to the church and powerful, who is willing and able to defend them and promote their and the church's business usefully. You are to ensure that he is provided for, considering his labors and expenses, from the goods of the bishopric and the collegiate churches, and other goods of the city and diocese of Basel by our authority, as is proper and expedient; those who oppose, etc. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa mandat episcopo ut Basiliensibus cives potestatem concedat eligendi capitaneum vel defensorem ob bonum statum ecclesiae et civitatis Basiliensis, si episcopus loci impotens sit, et ut de bonis episcopatus et ecclesiarum provideri faciat. Datum Anagniae, 1233, Kalendis Octobris.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Strasbourg. We have received a grave complaint from our venerable brother, the bishop, and our beloved sons, the chapter of Basel, that although the citizens of Basel are bound by oath to keep the rights of the bishop and his church intact, they nevertheless, in support of the former emperor Frederick, whom they assist to their utmost, have recklessly violated their oath and, turning from sons into step-sons, and impiously fighting against their mother, have completely destroyed the palace which the bishop had in the city of Basel, threatening to do worse to them and the clergy of the diocese of Basel. Therefore, the bishop, since they disdainfully ignored his diligent admonitions to make satisfaction for this and repent from their evil, has pronounced sentences of excommunication against them and interdict against the city, demanded by justice. They scornfully disregard these sentences, rejecting to return to the unity of the Church. Therefore, in order that a sharper punishment may sting those whom no penitence has yet pierced, we command that you ensure these sentences, as they were justly pronounced, are inviolably observed by our authority until proper satisfaction is made, with no appeal whatsoever. You are also to expressly prohibit, on our behalf, the Friars Preachers and Minors, Hospitallers, monks, and other religious of any order residing there, from celebrating or allowing the celebration of divine services in their churches and chapels for those citizens, notwithstanding any privileges or indulgences granted to these religious by the Apostolic See. Proceed further on this matter as you see fit. Given at Lyon, on the seventh day before the Kalends of August, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

---

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Argentinensi mandat ut sententias excommunicationis et interdicti contra cives Basilienses, qui in favorem quondam imperatoris F. iura ecclesiae Basiliensis violaverunt, auctoritate apostolica faciat inviolabiliter observari, et religiosis quibuslibet ne eis divina officia celebrent prohibeat. Datum Lugduni, VII Kalendas Augusti, anno sexto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Abbot of Saint Gall in the diocese of Constance. We ought to be especially ready to provide for those who are supported both by their own merits and by the prayers of the devout of the Church. Indeed, desiring to extend our grace and favor to our beloved son Walter of Rotemberc, a cleric and your kinsman, who is recognized for his gift of knowledge and nobility of character and lineage, and also at the request of you and our beloved son, the noble man, the Count of Habsburg, our devoted ones, we command that you provide or have provided for him a suitable ecclesiastical benefice, prebend, or another, if it is presently vacant or as soon as an opportunity presents itself, where you see fit, notwithstanding that the said cleric is already beneficed elsewhere, or if in the place where you will have decided to provide for him, there is a statute concerning a fixed number of canons fortified by oath or another assurance, or if we have sent our letters for others, to whom we do not wish any prejudice to be caused, or any indulgence of the apostolic see, by which the effect of our grace can be delayed or even hindered and of which special mention needs to be made in our letters; restrain those who contradict, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 14th of March, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa abbati Sancti Galli Constantiensis diocesis mandat ut Waltero de Rotemberc clerico, consanguineo suo, provideat in beneficio ecclesiastico, non obstantibus quibuscumque statutis. Datum Lugduni, II Idus Martii, anno V.

**Translation to English:**

To the Cardinal Deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the Apostolic See. Even though we are concerned with the provision of all churches, we are particularly urged by a greater care for the churches of Germany, so that suitable and devoted individuals are promoted to them at this time. Therefore, as was presented to us by the beloved sons, the provost, dean, and chapter of Worms, they, with your full mandate to elect, as they had received directions from you, sent four prelate canons of that church to your presence. With your will and consent, they unanimously agreed on our beloved son, Master Conrad, our chaplain, the Dean of Mainz, a man indeed endowed with knowledge of letters, adorned with the maturity of counsel, and distinguished by the honesty of character, and you afterwards likewise approved of this consent. Since it is fitting that no difficulty should hinder right dispositions, we command that you appoint the aforementioned dean, of whom we have probable reason to hope, by God's favor, that the church of Worms will advance in spiritual institutions and grow in temporal increments due to his effort, as bishop and pastor of the same church, making sure that obedience and due reverence are shown to him by the aforementioned provost, dean, chapter, and other subjects and ministers of the same church; contradictors etc. Given at Lyon, on the 11th of September, in the fifth year. To the same person. Since we have directed our letters to you concerning the appointment of our beloved son, Master Conrad, our chaplain, the Dean of Mainz, to the church of Worms: because the same church is said to be burdened with debt and it is not expedient for the business of the church that the Bishop of Worms lacks resources at this time, we mandate that you, by our authority, allow the same dean to retain, along with the bishopric of Worms, his dignities, positions, graces, and all other benefices with all their rights and appurtenances until our good pleasure of will. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa cardinali diacono Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum mandat ut magistrum Corradum decanum Maguntinum, capellanum nostrum, in episcopum Warmaciensem instituat et eum retinere sua beneficia auctoritate concedat. Datum Lugduni, XIII Kalendas Octobris, anno quinto.

Translation to English:

To the noble man, lord of Aucheim, of the diocese of Augsburg. Since you are said to have occupied some of the goods of Corradus, son of the late Emperor Frederick, and an enemy of the Church, who, being bound by the chain of excommunication, attacks the freedom of the Church and the Catholic faith, resisting him vigorously with your son E. and certain others adhering to you: so that you may retain those goods with a clear conscience, we, inclined by your devoted supplications, grant you this indulgence by the authority of these presents. Let no one infringe upon our concession. Given at Lyon, on the Nones of April, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

Regesto in Latin:

Innocentius IV papa nobili viro domino de Aucheim Augustensis diocesis indulget ut bona Corradi, inimici ecclesiae, quae occupavit, salva conscientia retinere valeat. 1258, Apr. 5. Datum Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Patriarch of Jerusalem, legate of the Apostolic See. Since, as we have learned, the Pisans and many others, when they arrive at the city of Acre, dare to carry the banners of the late Emperor Frederick and to place them in the churches during solemnities, to the peril of their souls and the scandal of many, we command that you absolutely prohibit this from happening. You shall restrain the aforementioned individuals and others from this presumption henceforth, after issuing a warning, through ecclesiastical censure, removing any appeal, and invoking, if necessary, the aid of secular authority. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa (patriarchae) Ierosolimitano mandat, ut Pisos aliosque prohibeat vexilla F. quondam imperatoris apud Acconem deferri et in ecclesiis poni. (Data non præcisa).

**Translation to English:**

To the provost of the church of Olimberg, of the Order of Saint Augustine, in the diocese of Basel. We have been informed by our beloved son, the noble lord Ralph the Elder, Count of Habsturch, our devoted one, that the people from the places of Suberitse and Sarnond in the diocese of Constance, who belong to him by hereditary right, have rashly withdrawn from their allegiance and lordship to him and wickedly adhered to the late Emperor Frederick after the sentence of excommunication had been pronounced against him and his supporters. And although, later, guided by wiser counsel, they swore an oath affirming that they would remain under the count's dominion and would not obey Frederick or anyone else against him, nonetheless, disregarding the sanctity of their oath and the sentence of excommunication pronounced against the adherents and supporters of the said Frederick, and rashly abandoning their allegiance, they have withdrawn from his dominion, assisting the said Frederick against him and the Church with all their might. Since it is fitting that those who love a curse should receive it, and those who refuse a blessing should have it withheld, we command you that, if these things are so, you should admonish the aforementioned people to withdraw from Frederick within a suitable period set by you, and not to obey or attend to him as emperor, and to return to the unity of the Church, and to strive to serve the said count as their lord with the devotion they owe, and also the people of the town of Lucerne, if it is confirmed to you that they have communicated and favored the said Frederick in these matters, to announce that they are subject to the sentence of excommunication, and to place these locations and the town of Lucerne under the sentence of interdict. You are to ensure that both sentences are observed inviolably, by our authority, without the obstacle of appeal, until they make worthy satisfaction, and proceed further on these matters as you see fit. Given at Lyon, the 28th of August, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa preposito ecclesie de Olimberc ordinis sancti Augustini Basiliensis diocesis, mandat ut homines de Suberitse et Sarnond, qui a comite Radulfo seniore de Habsturcb defecerant et F. quondam imperatori adheserant, excommunicationi subiaceant nisi ad comitem redeant, et villam Lucernensem interdicto supponat si eisdem communicaverint. 1247, Aug. 28. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz. The beloved son Theoderic of Molengassen, a citizen and magistrate of Cologne, appeared before us and stated that the late Emperor Frederick, noticing that he and his brother Henry were marked with the sign of the cross for the defense of the faith and the Church, and observing their fervent devotion towards the Roman Church, attempted to revoke them from their position by sending letters to the judges, magistrates, and all citizens of Cologne. These letters instructed them to exclude Theoderic and his brother from their company, not to admit them to any offices or judgments, and to declare any sentences pronounced by them null and void, thereby expelling them from the city of Cologne. However, our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Cologne, unable to tolerate such injustice against those he had taken under his protection and thwarting the wicked attempts of their persecutor, forbade the judges, magistrates, and citizens, under pain of excommunication, from proceeding with the election of magistrates and the organization of other offices without the legitimate involvement of Theoderic and Henry, whose interest was recognized. He declared that any contrary attempt would be null and void, and consequently, the right to elect magistrates and organize other offices devolved solely upon the aforementioned brothers. Therefore, Theoderic humbly petitioned us to confirm with apostolic authority what the Archbishop had done in this matter. Since it is fitting that the devoted receive fruits from their devotion and the undevoted suffer loss from their lack of devotion, we, having accepted the process of the said Archbishop as rightly conducted, command that you ensure it is firmly observed through ecclesiastical censure, with any appeal removed. Given at Lyon, on the 3rd day before the Kalends of August, in the fifth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino mandat ut processum archiepiscopi Coloniensis, quo Theodericum de Molengassen et fratrem suum Henricum in eorum iuribus contra voluntatem quondam imperatoris F. confirmavit, firmiter observetur, sublata appellatione. Datum Lugduni, III Kalendas Augusti, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected bishop of Liège. To further the church's cause against the former emperor Frederick and his supporters, who are persecutors of the same church, we, favorably assenting to your petitions, grant you by the authority of these presents the faculty to receive for one year the income of the benefices within the city and diocese of Liège that might become vacant within three years, and to restrain, if necessary, opposers by ecclesiastical censure with no appeal allowed, provided that enough of the income is reserved so that suitable persons may serve appropriately in the churches where these benefices are. Given at Lyon, on the 4th day before the Nones of May, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Leodiensi electo facultatem concedit percipiendi pro anno fructus beneficiorum vacantium in civitate et diocesi Leodiensi ad prosequendum ecclesie negotium contra Fridericum quondam imperatorem, contradictores ecclesiastica censura compescendi. 1254, Mai. 4, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Rufinus of Aramengo, castellan of the castle of Verrua in the diocese of Vercelli. The honor of promoting the Church should, with diligent care, justly receive from the Apostolic See the reward by which they may joyfully embrace an increase of sincere devotion toward it. Indeed, the tenor of your petition has presented to us that you, for the purpose of recovering the castle of Verrua from the hands of the late Emperor Frederick, who had once violently seized and held it, endured many labors and incurred very heavy expenses, not without much shedding of blood, especially since you restored the walls and rebuilt the houses of the said castle, which the Saracens then dwelling there had destroyed, and also because you must always be diligent for its conservation and bear the frequent burdens of expenses for the evident benefit of the people of Vercelli and other devotees of the Church, who obtain passage through that castle and acquire salt and other necessities. Furthermore, your family, devoted to God and the Church, placed themselves as a wall of strength against the attacks of persecutors for the defense of the liberty of the Church of Vercelli for long periods, and the same castle was faithfully preserved by some of your family members over many spans of time, you and they incurring such hatred from the said Frederick for such sincerity and constancy of your faith, that constant care for the protection of your persons is incumbent upon you. Therefore, since it is fitting that for such illustrious merits a fitting recompense should come to you, we grant to your nobility by the authority of these presents that you may hold the said castle under your custody for ten years and more, as long as it is with our good pleasure and will. Furthermore, we decree that full satisfaction be rendered to you for the expenses which you have previously incurred for the said castle and will incur in the future, and also that without our special mandate fully and expressly mentioning these presents, within the time of your custody, no sentence of excommunication or interdict may be promulgated against your person and the men of the said castle by reason of the same custody, and if by chance it has been issued, it shall obtain no strength of firmness. No one therefore is permitted to infringe our concession and constitution, etc. Given at Lyon, the 13th day before the Kalends of March, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa nobilis viro Rufino de Aramengo castellano castri Verruce Vercellensis diocesis concedit, ut idem castrum sub eius custodia teneat usque ad decennium cum plena satisfactione expensarum, et nulla sententia excommunicationis vel interdicti contra ipsum aut homines castri promulgari possit. Datum Lugduni, XIII Kal. Martii, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

Innocent IV granted the bishop of Strasbourg full authority to dispense with the noble man Conrad, Count of Freiburg, regarding his marriage to the noble woman Sophia, daughter of Frederick, Count of Zollern, who was related to him in the fourth degree of consanguinity and affinity. This was done to settle serious disputes and enmities between their families, which had been ongoing with much bloodshed. The marriage could not be dissolved without grave danger to many, and the Count of Freiburg remained devoted to the Church. Therefore, the bishop was authorized to allow them to remain in the marriage lawfully and ensure that the offspring from such a marriage would not be considered illegitimate, despite the mentioned impediment. Given at Lyon, on the 18th of May, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Argentinensi mandat, ut cum Conrado comite de Friburch, qui nobilem mulierem Sophiam, quartae consanguinitatis linea contingentem, in uxorem duxit, dispenset, ut in matrimonio remanere possint et proles legitima habeatur. 1247, Mai. 18, Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To R., Cardinal Deacon of Santa Maria in Cosmedin, legate of the Apostolic See. The Church seems to be guided by the spirit of counsel and piety, especially now, when it directs its efforts toward that which brings about the salvation of souls and the growth of ecclesiastical liberty. Therefore, since we have heard that some from Romagna wish to be freed from the yoke of servitude and, by returning to the embrace of the Apostolic See, desire to be cherished with the joy of liberty, we, trusting in your proven discretion, grant you by the authority of these presents the power to freely provide for the relaxation of sentences of excommunication, which these individuals have incurred by adhering to the enemies of the Church or any others, and to remit all offenses they have committed against it, as you see fit for their salvation and the honor of the Church. For we will hold as ratified and confirmed whatever you decide to do concerning these matters. Given at Lyon, 4th of the Nones of April, in the fifth year [of our pontificate].

Regesto in Latin:

Innocentius IV papa R. Sancte Marie in Cosmidin diacono cardinali, legato apostolice sedis, mandat ut in Romaniola, super relaxatione excommunicationum et remissione offensarum, provideat. 1248, April. 2, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Basel. Considering it a delight to endure many and frequent labors for the liberty of the Church, you have rendered yourself vigilant in all things for the glory of God, through which the Church may achieve an increase in honor. Therefore, we, enjoying to pursue your person with special favor for this reason, by the authority of these presents, grant you that if it happens out of evident necessity for the citizens of Basel to appoint a captain or some defender by our authority, he shall have no power whatsoever to dispose of matters pertaining to your office or the goods belonging to you or the churches of the city and diocese of Basel, nor shall you be obliged to supply him with necessities or provide any procurations, except for appropriate assistance, if perhaps our venerable brother, the Bishop of Strasbourg, judges it reasonable to impose something upon you and others for this purpose. Let no one, therefore, etc., of our concession, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 12th of April, in the 5th year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Basiliensi mandat ut, si necessitas evidens cives Basilienses duxerit capitaneum vel defensorem per auctoritatem apostolicam constituere, nullam habeat potestatem in bonis ad episcopum vel ecclesias Basiliensis pertinentibus. 1248, Apr. 12. Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To the Archbishop of Mainz. On behalf of our beloved son, the elected bishop of Liège, it was humbly requested to us that, since the noble woman, his sister, and the noble man, Count of Jülich, who, although they are related in the fourth degree of consanguinity, are matrimonially united, that we should take care to dispense them with apostolic authority so that, notwithstanding this impediment, they may remain in the marriage thus contracted. Therefore, at the request of the elected bishop, we command that, after first receiving from these nobles sufficient and suitable assurance of their dedication to the service of the Roman Church against Frederick, the former emperor, and his supporters, the persecutors of the Church, with vigor and openness, you dispense them with our authority so that they may remain in the marriage thus contracted. Given at Lyon, III Kalends of May, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa Maguntino archiepiscopo mandat ut, obtenta cautione de insistendo servitio ecclesie Romane contra Fridericum olim imperatorem, nobili muliere et nobili viro, in quarta consanguinitatis linea coniunctis, auctoritate apostolica dispenset, ut remanere valeant in matrimonio contracto. 1236, April 29. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Cologne. Through commendable conduct and life, our beloved son, Master Gerlacus, a canon of Osnabrück, is said to have rendered himself worthy of obtaining a special grace from the Apostolic See, which delights in showing favor to the well-deserving. Hence, we, in consideration of his merits and the effort of his relatives, as we have learned, striving to promote the honor of the Apostolic See, and also in consideration of our beloved son, the noble man Adolf, Count of Berg, your brother-in-law, who sent us earnest petitions in his favor through special letters, command you, by our authority, to receive him into the church of Fritzlar in the diocese of Mainz as a canon and brother, and to provide him with a prebend as soon as the opportunity allows, by our authority — notwithstanding if that church has a set number of canons, supported by oath or any other firm assurance, or any indulgence which in our letters needs to be fully or expressly mentioned, or if we have sent our writings to others in the same church, which etc. as far as: may be generated —; those opposing, etc. Given at Lyons, 23rd March, in the fifth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Coloniensi mandat ut magistrum Gerlacum in ecclesia Frizlariensi Maguntine diocesis in canonicum recipiat et de prebenda provideat. 1231, Mart. 23, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Abbot of Farfa. We take pleasure in pursuing with benevolent affection the just desires of the devout, especially those whom we know have endured hardships under the guise of ecclesiastical liberty. Therefore, since our beloved son Gualterus, a cleric of the parish of Vado in the diocese of Fiesole, along with his companions, has been oppressed by the supporters of Frederick due to their faith and devotion to the Roman Church, as we have learned, we, wishing rightly that he may rejoice in finding apostolic grace favorable to him, command that you confer and assign to him the church of Saint Felicitas of Augusta in the diocese of Tivoli, if it is indeed vacant by right at present, removing any unlawful occupant with our authority, ensuring that he may enjoy peaceful possession — notwithstanding any indulgence of the apostolic see which might otherwise impede or delay such grace —; those who oppose, etc. Given at Lyons, 2nd Kalends of April, in the 5th year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa abbati Farfensi mandat ut ecclesiam sancte Felicitatis de Augusta Tiburtine diocesis, vacantem de iure, Gualtero clerico conferat et assignet, amoto quolibet illicito detentore, ut pacifica possessione gaudeat, non obstante indulgentia sedis apostolice. 1248, Martii 31, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To James of Aspello, a cleric of our venerable brother, the Patriarch of Constantinople. Being present before us, you humbly requested that since you could not present the letters we granted you regarding your provision in the church of Saint Laurence in the diocese of Spoleto, due to the malice of the time, we might ensure that no prejudice could arise to you from others obtaining similar grace in the same church from us or legates of the apostolic see. We, thus inclined to your supplications, grant you by the authority of these presents that you be preferred in obtaining the prebend over all who have obtained similar grace in the same church after the date of your letters. Let no one therefore... of our concession... Given at Lyon, on the 26th of May, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Iacobo de Aspello clerico patriarche Constantinopolitani indulget, ut in assecutione prebende in ecclesia sancti Laurenti de Spello eos, qui post datam litterarum suarum similem gratiam impetrarunt, auctoritate presentium preferatur. 1231, Maii 26, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Brixen. So that the undevout may suffer loss from their lack of devotion and the devout may gain advantage from their devotion, we grant you the authority by our present decree to suspend from their offices and deprive of ecclesiastical benefices the prelates and clerics subject to you and your charge in the church of Trento, who have scorned to obey you. You are also granted the authority to confer these benefices on suitable persons devoted to the Roman Church, and to dispense with those among these prelates and clerics who, through their efforts of devotion and obedience, have reconciled themselves to grace, concerning the mark of irregularity, should they have possibly incurred it, and to restrain opposers, if necessary, by ecclesiastical censure, with appeal removed. Given at Lyon, the 8th day before the Kalends of June, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Brixinensi mandat facultatem suspendendi et privandi prelatos et clericos ecclesiae Tridentinae qui obedire contempserint, et conferendi beneficia personis idoneis, dispensandi cum eis qui se gratiae coaptaverint, compescendi contradictores per censuram ecclesiasticam. 1247, Mai. 25, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the dean and chapter of Osnabrück. The sincere devotion of our venerable brother, the bishop of Osnabrück, and our beloved sons, the noble men Otto of Tecklenburg, Henry of Oldenburg, and Wichold of Holte, towards our person and the Roman Church, induces us to grant their requests as much as we can before God. Therefore, being inclined by their supplications, we exhort, ask, and earnestly urge all of you, commanding you to receive our beloved son Wescelus, a cleric who, as he asserts, has not obtained any ecclesiastical benefice and about whom laudable testimony is given to us, into your community as a canon and brother, liberally granting him a prebend as soon as opportunity allows, notwithstanding a fixed number of canons established by oath or confirmation of the same see, or any firmness fortified by any means, or if we have sent our letters for others to you, which we do not wish, etc., up to the point: to be generated, or if the said see has granted you that you are not obliged to receive or provide for anyone, or that you cannot be interdicted, suspended, or excommunicated by apostolic letters, unless they make express mention of such indulgence, or by any other means by which such grace can be impeded or delayed. Otherwise, we have instructed the aforementioned bishop by our letters to compel you to do this, after prior admonition, through ecclesiastical censure, with appeal removed. Given at Lyon, on the 16th day before the Kalends of April, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa decano et capitulo Osnaburgensibus mandat ut Wescelum clericum, qui nullum ecclesiasticum beneficium assecutus est, recipiant in canonicum et in fratrem, prebendam conferendo, non obstantibus statutis seu indultis quibuscunque. Dat. Lugduni, XVII Kal. Aprilis, anno V.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Constance. Since we have directed our letters to you that when it happens that the Church of Basel is without a pastor, you should forbid its chapter from proceeding to the election or postulation of anyone without your advice and consent, we wish to mandate to your fraternity by the authority of these present letters that, when it is vacant, you offer your advice and consent so that our beloved son, the Abbot of Saint Gall, may be appointed to its governance. Given at Lyon, 5th Kalends of July, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV episcopo Constantiensi mandat ut, ecclesia Basiliensi vacante, consilium et assensum suum praebeat ad eligendum abbatem Sancti Galli in pastorem. 1248, (27 Iunii), Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble men, the Prefect of the City, Peter of the Bonifatii family, and others of the Prefect's council. The accustomed providence of the Apostolic See examines with diligent deliberation the merits of its subjects, and what it concludes to be superior by the judgment of reason, it rewards with greater remunerations of rewards, pursuing them with more abundant favors and fuller benefits. Hence it is, that since you, etc., as above in Chapter CXIII until: to procure, inclined by your supplications, we restore to you and your successors, by special grace, Bleda, Vicus, and other your castles with their dominion, rights, honors, and all other appurtenances, of which all the captains of the late Emperor Frederick had despoiled you because you adhered to the church against him, granting to you by the tenor of these presents, that you may freely enter into possession of all the aforesaid as soon as you have the ability. Let no one, etc., infringe our restitution and concession, etc. Given at Lyon, on the second day before the Kalends of April, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa nobilibus viris prefecto Urbis Petro Bonifatii et aliis Prefectanis scribit, restituens Bledam, Vicum et alia castra cum dominio et iuribus, quae a capitaneis Friderici quondam imperatoris ablata fuerant, speciali gratia. Datum Lugduni, II Kalendas Aprilis, anno quinto pontificatus sui.

**Translation to English:**

Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum, cardinal deacon and legate of the Apostolic See. Our dearly beloved son in Christ, W., the illustrious Roman king, has requested from us through special letters that, since it is necessary to magnificently advance the Church's business in the regions of Germany, we should convert the vows of the crusaders from Friesland, intended for the aid of the Holy Land, to support the aforementioned business. Therefore, trusting in your discretion, we entrust you with the authority of these presents, that, having considered all circumstances, you may absolve such crusaders from their vow of the cross up to a number that you deem appropriate, so that they may assist the aforementioned king in the promotion of his business vigorously and diligently until the term you shall decide, granting them, for this reason, the pardon of sins granted to those going to Jerusalem. Given at Lyon, on the 8th of April, in the third year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa, Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali et apostolicae sedis legato mandat ut vota Frisonum crucesignatorum, sub certis circumstantiis et usque ad numerum opportunum, in subventionem negotii ecclesiae in partibus Theotonicis commutentur, absolvens eos a voto crucis. 1239, April. 8, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of the Marbach monastery of the order of Saint Benedict, diocese of Basel. It pertains to the office of paternal kindness to favor the just desires of sons with support, yet with such attention to the dispensation, that he may follow with the gift of fuller grace the one whom he perceives to be greater in merits. Indeed, our beloved son Warner, a secular canon of the church of the Grandval monastery, whose relatives are said to be devoted to the Apostolic See, is declared to be supported by merits of honesty and knowledge, which he rejoices to be fostered by our gracious benevolence. Therefore, for this reason and also in consideration of our beloved sons, the noble men R., count of Neufchâtel, and H., lord of Harguel, who are devoted to us and to the Roman Church and have implored apostolic grace for him with special letters, we earnestly ask and exhort your devotion, instructing that you should liberally provide the said canon, out of reverence for the Apostolic See and ourselves, in the Lucerne monastery, which is said to be immediately subject to you, with a suitable prebendary benefice pertaining to your collation, which is accustomed to be assigned to secular clerics, as soon as the opportunity presents itself, provided that we have not yet written elsewhere for him — notwithstanding if we have directed our letters for others to you, by which, etc., down to: to be generated, or any indulgence, of which, in our letters, etc., down to: mention. Otherwise, we have instructed by our letters the abbot of Bellelay, diocese of Basel, to execute the apostolic mandate regarding this; opposers, etc. Given at Lyon, March 20, in the fifth year (of our pontificate).

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati monasterii Marbacensis mandat, ut Warnero canonico ecclesiae Grandisvallis de beneficio prebendali in monasterio Lucernensi provideat. Si vero non fecerit, mandatum exequatur abbas Bellelagii. 1231, Mart. 20, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz, the Archdeacon, and other prelates of churches established throughout the city and diocese of Mainz. It was presented before us on your behalf, Brother Archbishop, that although the nations of Thuringia and Hesse within your diocese have long been malicious and disobedient to you more than others, after the death of the late King of the Romans of blessed memory, H., there has been no one able to restrain them. Their malice has hence increased so greatly that, fearing neither God nor man, they engage in such tyranny against ecclesiastical liberty, devastating churches through arson, plundering and capturing clerics, and afflicting them with bodily torment until they are compelled to ransom themselves with money. As a result, clerics, fearing the aforementioned danger, dare only to dwell in fortified places, leading to many churches in various locations being left desolate and the care of souls neglected. Therefore, you, following in the footsteps of your predecessor, with the counsel and assent of your suffragans, have decreed in your provincial synod that to curtail the rage of these wrongdoers, all places to which clerics’ spoils are brought, or where clerics are held captive, or where the plunderers find refuge, should be placed under interdict if the culprits do not repent upon warning, until appropriate satisfaction is made to those who have been wronged. But since certain nobles of the same diocese claim to have obtained from the Apostolic See a concession that sentences of excommunication or suspension cannot be promulgated against them or their lands without our special mandate, by this statute, the clerics are little or not at all relieved on this account. Therefore, you have humbly implored us to apply a salutary remedy with paternal care. Not wishing, therefore, that this occasion should derogate the aforementioned statute, we command all of you that, notwithstanding the aforementioned indulgences, you ensure that this statute is inviolably observed by our authority; the contradictors, etc. Furthermore, to subdue the malice of the aforementioned wrongdoers, we grant you, Brother Archbishop, full authority by the present document to decree within your province that the children of those who do not release clerics they have captured without extracting money from them or resignation of benefices or some part of the revenues, shall in no way be admitted to the clergy or ecclesiastical benefices in the future, and if they have already been admitted to the clergy and benefices, they shall not ascend to personates and other ecclesiastical dignities. Given at Lyon, February 11, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino mandat ut statutum de interdicto locorum spoliatoribus clericorum receptaculum praebentium, non obstantibus indulgentiis quibusdam nobilibus concessis, inviolabiliter observetur, et plenam facultatem concedit statuendi ne filii malefactorum ad clericatum admittantur. Datum Lugduni, III Id. Febr. anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Patriarch of Jerusalem, legate of the Apostolic See, to the archbishops and bishops, and to the beloved sons, prelates, Templars, Hospitallers, and brothers of the Teutonic Order, as well as to all barons devoted to the Church in overseas territories. Since, as we have learned, Thomas, Count of Acerra, who is said to reside in the County of Tripoli on behalf of the late Emperor Frederick, is harming the devoted followers of the Church through methods and deceptions typical of his lord, we command your entire community to diligently work to ensure that this count departs entirely from those regions. And you, brother Patriarch, place under ecclesiastical interdict the places where he stays and any he may arrive at, by our authority; those who oppose this, etc. Given at Lyon, the 8th day before the Kalends of June, in the fifth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Patriarchae Hierosolymitano scribit se mandare ut Thoma comes Acerrarum a comitatu Tripolitano omnino recedat et ut loca ubi moratur ecclesiastico interdicto subiciantur. 1242, Mai. 25, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Peter, Cardinal Deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the apostolic see. The universal Church grieves and indeed ought to grieve, and we grieve much with it and for it, and are troubled when we hear that prelates, who ought to extinguish the flames of persecution which presently consume the Church, not only refuse to lend a hand to defend against the fires of persecution but in a certain way, even stoke the flames by multiplying persecutions against the Church.
