For when... the Archbishop of Magdeburg and... the Bishops of Passau and Friesland, as noble members of the Church, should be so consumed by zeal that they cannot bear the reproaches and the usurpation of its rights, they, to our heart's bitterness, not only fail to stand with the Church, their mother, against the malice of those persecuting it, as they should, placing themselves as walls against the adversaries, but also, having put aside divine fear and human shame, and neglected pontifical dignity and disrespecting the keys of the Church, they openly provide aid, counsel, and favor to Frederick, the former emperor, excommunicated, and an enemy of God and the Church; by which action, like public enemies, they persecute the said Church, with the same Archbishop of Magdeburg arranging the marriage between Frederick and the daughter of the Duke of Saxony. We have indeed learned that the Margrave of Meissen, the Dukes of Bavaria and Saxony, and the daughter of the Duke of Saxony, as well as the nobles of Austria and Styria, and H. of Eversstein, who acts as captain for these nobles in the name of said Frederick, noble men by birth but ignobling themselves by their wicked deeds and having been given over to a reprobate mind, vigorously and powerfully assist the aforementioned Frederick against God and the Church. Therefore, we command that you, citing the aforementioned Archbishop and Bishops with our authority, set a suitable peremptory term by which they must personally come into our presence to receive their due merits. And the other aforementioned nobles, that departing completely from said Frederick, they do not provide him aid, counsel, or favor, and that they return to the unity of holy mother Church, compelling them by ecclesiastical censure with appeal removed, if you deem it expedient. Given at Lyon, VII Kalends of November, in the fifth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Petro Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali mandat ut Magdeburgensem archiepiscopum et Pataviensem ac Frisiensem episcopos ad suam presentiam evocet, et nobiles quosdam ad reditum ad unitatem ecclesie compellat. Dat. Lugduni, VII Kal. Novembris, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the provost and chapter of Regensburg. A complaint has been presented to us on behalf of our venerable brother, the Bishop of Regensburg, that you presume to issue statutes, make appointments and dismissals, as well as other actions that legally pertain jointly to him and you, without his knowledge or request, to his considerable prejudice and harm. Therefore, since it is unfitting for you, as members, to separate from the bishop, who is indeed your head, we command that you make no such statutes, appointments, or dismissals without the consent of the said bishop. Otherwise, we declare them null and void. Given at Lyon, on the 9th day before the Kalends of October, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa (preposito et capitulo Ratisponensibus) mandat, ut sine consensu episcopi Ratisponensis statuta et institutiones non faciant, alioquin eas irritas decernit. 1248, Sept. 23. Datum Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the provost of the church of Dairago, Diocese of Milan. Our duty of office leads us to provide for those who are enlisted in the clerical militia. Therefore, since our beloved son, David, known as Bonaventus, a cleric of Milan, as he asserts, has not yet obtained any ecclesiastical benefice, we, induced by our dear son, the noble man G., count of Cavalliate, who has petitioned us on his behalf, command that you provide for the said cleric in some church of the city or diocese of Milan, except only the cathedral, with a suitable ecclesiastical benefice, even if it has the care of souls, if it is vacant at present or as soon as the opportunity arises — notwithstanding etc., as above in chapter 827 up to: preferred —; contradictors etc. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa preposito ecclesiae de Dairago mandat, ut clerico David dicto Bonavento in ecclesiis Mediolanensis civitatis vel diocesis, excepto cathedrali, provideat in beneficio ecclesiastico competenti, vacante ad presens vel cum facultas se obtulerit. 1236, ex urbe Roma.

**Translation to English:**

The duty of the apostleship imposed on us and our compassion persuades us to ensure that those chosen for the Lord's lot are provided with Christ's patrimony. Wanting therefore to grant a special favor to our beloved son Guerard, canon of the church of Saint Andrew in Worms, at the request of the noble man Emicho, Count of Leiningen, who has humbly petitioned us through his letters on behalf of the same, we command you, by our authority, to provide or cause to be provided for the aforementioned canon in the city or diocese of Worms with a suitable prebend or other ecclesiastical benefice, either with or without care of souls, if any is currently vacant there or as soon as an opportunity arises — notwithstanding if in the church where you decide to provide for him a statute exists concerning a fixed number of canons, whether by oath or confirmation of the apostolic see or any other firmness, or even if the same canon is already beneficed elsewhere, or any indulgence by which such grace could be impeded and which would require express mention in our letters, or if we have directed our writings concerning a similar grace for others in the same city or diocese, etc., as far as: be generated, —; let those who contradict, etc. If not all, etc. Given at Lyons, on the 8th of April, in the fifth year [of our Pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa decano, thesaurario et magistro Corrado canonico Warmaciensibus mandat, ut Guerardo canonico ecclesiae Sancti Andreae Warmaciensis provideant de beneficio ecclesiastico in civitate vel diocesi Warmaciensi. Datum Lugduni, VI Idus Aprilis, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To Gualteroni, canon of Pistoia. We consider ourselves especially obliged to provide for those who have suffered the loss of temporal goods for the sake of maintaining faith and ecclesiastical liberty. Therefore, since our beloved son Salmon de Ficeclo, a poor cleric of the diocese of Lucca, has been, as he asserts, deprived of all his possessions by the envoys of the late Emperor Frederick for maintaining faith and ecclesiastical liberty, as well as for the devoted services rendered to the Roman Church, and since he does not have a benefice from which he can comfortably sustain himself, we, intending to show him favor, command that you confer and assign to him, by our authority, the first vacant personate or prebend in the diocese of Lucca that he deems acceptable — notwithstanding the fact that our beloved son R., cardinal deacon of Santa Maria in Cosmedin, wrote concerning his reception in Prato, and our beloved son G. de Montelongo, subdeacon and our notary, legates of the Apostolic See, wrote concerning the churches in Faenza, although due to the disturbance of the present time no benefit has been obtained from such letters, or if in the place where you provide for him we have directed our letters for others, or any indulgence of the Apostolic See, by which the effect of our grace could be delayed or even impeded —; contradictors, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 8th day before the Ides of April, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Gualteroni canonico Pistoriensi mandat ut Salmoni de Ficeclo, clerico pauperi, personatum aut plebanatum primum in diocesi Lucana vacantem auctoritate sua conferat et assignet, non obstantibus impedimentis. 1231, Apr. 6, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To O. de Falke. Berger 4024, Bishop of Clusium.

Since we hold the beloved sons, the citizens of Perugia, in the bowels of charity due to their fervent devotion to us and the Roman Church, their mother, we earnestly desire the salvation of their souls with all the desires of our mind. Thus, we grant you, by the authority of these presents, the faculty of absolving them according to the form of the Church from the sentence of excommunication, which they are said to have incurred because they presumed to issue certain statutes against ecclesiastical liberty and to burden the churches and ecclesiastical persons of the city and diocese of Perugia with collections and exactions, after having received from them sufficient and suitable assurance that they will completely revoke those statutes and cease entirely from such collections and exactions henceforth. Given at Lyons, the seventh day before the Kalends of June, in the fifth year (of our pontificate).

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Clusino mandat ut cives Perusinos, excommunicationis sententia innodatos pro statutis contra libertatem ecclesiasticam et oneribus in ecclesias et personas ecclesiasticas impositis, recepta cautione, absolvendi facultatem habeat. Datum Lugduni, VII Kal. Iunii, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Strasbourg. We previously sent letters to your sincerity, stating that if our venerable brother, the Bishop of Basel, were unable, negligent, or remiss, you were to appoint our beloved son, B., provost of Grandval and canon of Basel, as defender or captain for the beloved sons, the citizens of Basel, by our authority. Provided that if the said bishop were restored by God's grace to such health that he could serve the citizens as captain and defender, you would arrange with the aforementioned provost that he should henceforth in no way interfere in such defense and other matters pertaining to the bishop. Indeed, what we initially approved regarding the same provost, we still approve. However, since the aforementioned bishop has in the past diligently shown himself fruitful in matters concerning the honor of the church, we desire and command your fraternity that if due to urgent necessity it happens that you wish to appoint the aforementioned provost or someone else as an assistant to the same bishop according to the form given to you, you should first ascertain the will of the bishop, so that you may appoint someone agreeable to him, who may be suitable for the office of assistant according to our intention. Given at Lyon, 14th April, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Argentinensi mandat ut si episcopus Basiliensis sit impotens, B. prepositum Grandivallensem defensorem deputet, proviso quod post convalescentiam episcopi de consensu eius coadiutorem eligat. 1248, Aprilis 14. Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To Master Radulf, rector of the church of Ringuigin, in the diocese of Constance. To show special favor to you, due to the merits of your probity for which laudable testimony is rendered, and at the request of our beloved son, the noble man H., the Count Palatine of Ciugin, who is devoted to us and the Roman Church and who has interceded on your behalf, we, by the authority of this present document, grant you the indulgence to receive and freely retain one additional benefice, even if it involves a similar care of souls, provided it is offered to you canonically, alongside the churches of Ringuigin and Laichingin, which you claim to have canonically acquired with the care of souls—despite the constitution issued by the General Council on this matter—, ensuring nonetheless that these churches and the benefice are not neglected. Let none, etc., of our concession, etc. Given at Lyon, on the third Ides of May, in the fifth year [of our pontificate].

Regesto in Latin:

Papa [Name] Magistro Radulfo rectori ecclesiae de Ringuigin Constantiensis diocesis concedit, ut preter ecclesias de Ringuigin et de Laichingin, beneficium unicum, etiam cum cura animarum, canonice sibi oblatum recipere et retinere possit, constitutione concilii generalis non obstante. Datum Lugduni, III Idus Maii, anno quinto.

Translation to English:

To the noble man Hermann, Margrave of Baden.

The devotion you hold for the Apostolic See merits that we grant your petitions the more favorably as they are found to fully express the debt of justice and the equity consonant with law. Hence, we, inclined by the prayers of your devotion, confirm to you by apostolic authority the duchy or principality of Austria, with all its honor, jurisdiction, and rights, rightly and liberally given to you during the lifetime of the noble woman G., Duchess of Austria, your wife, to whom the said duchy was said to be lawfully devolved by hereditary succession according to the ancient and approved custom of the land, and also as you assert, confirmed by the supreme pontiffs, emperors, and kings of the Romans. We also strengthen this confirmation with the protection of this present writing. Let no one therefore etc. our confirmation etc.

Given at Lyons, on the 18th day before the Kalends of October, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa Hermanno marchioni de Badone confirmat ducatum sive principatum Austrie, quem a nobili muliere G. ducissa Austrie uxore sua sibi donatum fuisse asserit, auctoritate apostolica confirmat et scripti patrocinio communit. Datum Lugduni, XVIII Kal. Oct., anno VI.

**Translation to English:**

To the Abbot of the Valley of Saint Lambert of the diocese of Liège. To bestow grace and favor upon our beloved son, the elected bishop of Liège, and in reverence of the cross with which he is marked against Frederick, the former emperor, and his supporters, persecutors of the Church, and being moved by the sincere devotion he is known to have towards us and the Roman Church, his mother, we command you to collect the redemptions of the vows of those signed with the cross against the same Frederick and his supporters, who are weak and unable to fight, as well as the legacies assigned to the aid of this undertaking in the lands, fiefs, castellanies, and domains of the said elected bishop, and to assign them to the same elected bishop. You are to absolve those signed with the cross from their vow and grant them the remission of their sins and the indulgence which was granted to those crossing for the aid of the Holy Land in the general council; contradictors, etc. — notwithstanding any indulgence, if any has been granted to some by the Apostolic See, that they cannot be interdicted or excommunicated by apostolic letters which do not expressly mention that indulgence, or any other, of which special mention should be made in our letters. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati Vallis Sancti Lamberti Leodiensis diocesis mandat ut redemptiones votorum crucesignatorum contra F. quondam imperatorem ac fautores suos colligat et electo Leodiensi assignet, absolvens crucesignatos a voto et concedens eis veniam peccatorum et indulgentiam. Datum ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the procurator of the church of Salzburg. Our venerable brother, the bishop of Bamberg, has shown us through his petition that, although we had granted him the bishopric of Chiemsee, which is vacant in the province of Salzburg, to be held until our pleasure is further known, you, compelling him to renounce this grace now through threats, now through flattery, and now through fear, which could affect even the steadfast, have unlawfully conferred the said bishopric on the provost of the church of Salzburg as a matter of fact, although you could not do so by right. Since acts done under duress or fear should lack the force of validity, we command that, notwithstanding this renunciation and collation, which we declare to be without legal standing, you reinstate the aforementioned bishop into the physical possession of the said bishopric, removing the said provost and any other unlawful occupant by our authority, and protect him once reinstated, ensuring he enjoys peaceful possession of the said bishopric. Otherwise, we entrust by our letters to our beloved son, the dean of Regensburg, the execution of the apostolic mandate regarding these matters; opposers etc. — notwithstanding any constitution concerning two diets etc., or any indulgence granted to you or the said opposers by the Apostolic See, protecting you from being excommunicated, suspended, or interdicted by apostolic letters or from being taken to court outside the diocese of Salzburg. Given at Lyons, 9th April, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa procuratori ecclesiae Salzeburgensis mandat ut episcopum Bambergensem in possessionem episcopatus Kimensis inducat, amoto praeposito Salzeburgensi, quibusdam minis et blanditiis renuntiationem extorquente. Dat. Lugduni, V Idus Aprilis, pontificatus nostri anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To Scoiggero, canon of Speyer. It is fitting that the grace of the Apostolic See be more abundantly extended to those who strive to merit it for themselves through their own offerings and the prayers of noble devotees of the Church. Therefore, to grant you a special favor, both in light of the nobility of your character and lineage, which you are said to possess, and at the behest of our dear son, the noble man Conrad, count of Wazeburc, who has petitioned us on your behalf, we, by the authority of these presents, grant you the privilege that, besides the ecclesiastical benefices you currently hold, some of which, as you assert, have the care of souls attached, you may receive and freely retain one additional benefice or dignity or office, even if it has a similar cure of souls, provided it is offered to you canonically, notwithstanding the constitution issued by the general council on this matter; provided that benefices, dignities, and offices, etc., are not neglected. Let no one, etc., our concession, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 13th of May, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Scoiggero canonico Spirensi concedit facultatem recipiendi et retinendi unicum beneficium vel dignitatem, etiam si curam habeat animarum, in additione ad iam obtenta, non obstante constitutione concilii generalis. 1247, Mai. 13. Datum Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Arnold, canon of Chur. The Apostolic See is accustomed to grant the requests of the devout more willingly when they render themselves dearer through pleasing and acceptable services. Therefore, as you have taken care to inform us, our venerable brother, the bishop of Chur, recognizing the purity of your faith and the integrity of your devotion, with which you have shown yourself prepared, eager, and diligent in the business of the church, not without great labors and expenses and the harsher confinement of imprisonment, has promised to provide for you, with the consent of his chapter, from a benefice under his gift, which you have deemed acceptable, as soon as he has the means to do so. He has bound himself to this through his letters, reinforced by the seals of himself and the said chapter. We, therefore, wishing to grant the requested favor, inclined by your prayers, having accepted and ratified this promise, confirm it by apostolic authority and strengthen it with the support of this present writing. Let no one, therefore, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 9th of June, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Arnoldo canonico Curiensi promissionem beneficii a Curiensi episcopo factam, auctoritate apostolica confirmat et scripti patrocinio communit. 1248, V Idus Iunii. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the citizens of Basel. The Apostolic See is accustomed to accede to the prayers of the devoted and sometimes grant them special favor. Therefore, inclined by your supplications, we grant you by the authority of these presents that you may freely convene against your wrongdoers or debtors concerning arsons, spoils, debts, and other matters before an ecclesiastical judge, with these presents being valid for two years only. Let no one, therefore, etc. infringe on our concession, etc. Given at Lyon, on the third day before the Kalends of April, in the second year of our pontificate. To the same. Since you have returned to the devotion of the Church and the command, having completely abandoned its persecutor, we gladly assent to your wishes and favorably hear your petitions as much as we can with God. Therefore, inclined by your supplications, we grant you by the authority of these presents that according to the statute of your city, the annual prescription among those present shall run over goods that you have possessed in good faith for a year and a day. Let no one, etc. infringe on our concession, etc. Given as above. To the citizens of Basel. Since you have returned to the devotion of the Church, having abandoned its persecutor as faithful and catholic men, we, intending to pursue you all and individually with grace and favor for this reason, grant you by the authority of these presents that you cannot be summoned in a cause outside the city or district of Basel for five years by apostolic letters. Let no one, etc. infringe on our concession, etc. Given at Lyon, on the third day before the Kalends of April, in the fifth year of our pontificate. The abbot of Wectingen of the Cistercian order, diocese of Constance, is appointed conservator for this matter on the same date.

---

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa civibus Basiliensibus indulget ut malefactores et debitores suos coram ecclesiastico iudice convenire possint, et annalis praescriptio super bonis secundum statutum civitatis currat, necnon extra districtum Basiliensem trahi non possint per quinquennium. 1250, Mart. 30, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Osnabrück. Desiring to honor your person and, through the honor shown to you, to provide for others, we commit to your fraternity by the authority of these presents that, along with your beloved brother, the provost of the church of Osnabrück, and two other clerics in your service, you may freely receive other benefices, even if they involve the care of souls, as long as they are canonically offered to you, and you may lawfully retain them along with the ones already obtained— notwithstanding the constitution of the general council— up to that amount, by our authority, as you deem conducive to their merits and the salvation of their souls; provided that those benefices are not neglected in their duties, etc. Given at Lyon, the 10th day before the Kalends of October, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Osnaburgensi mandat ut ipse cum germano suo et duobus clericis beneficia ecclesiastica, etiam cura animarum onerata, si canonice offerantur, recipere possint, constitutione concilii generalis non obstante. Datum Lugduni, X Kal. Oct., anno sexto pontificatus.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of the monastery of Saint Peter of Eboli, in the diocese of Salerno. The Holy Mother Church is accustomed to open the bosom of its mercy to needy sons and especially to support with timely aid those who are despoiled of their own goods and are forced to miserably wander in exile for its cause. Therefore, since our beloved son, John of Philecto, a knight from the diocese of Capua, has presented himself before us and has explained that he was long ago expelled from the Kingdom of Sicily, with all his paternal and maternal goods confiscated, suffering countless deficiencies and afflicted with the bitter pains of exile: we, sympathizing with his needs, command that you diligently provide to this knight and to his descendants a suitable military benefice, considering the merits of this knight, in the said kingdom as soon as the opportunity arises, by our authority; to any who may oppose, etc. Given at Lyon, 9th September, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa abbati Sancti Petri de Ebuloc, Salernitane diocesis mandat, ut Iohanni de Philecto militi exulanti in Regno Sicilie beneficium militare congruum provideat, consideratis meritis eius, cum facultas se obtulerit. Datum Lugduni, V Idus Septembris, anno sexto.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Amiens. Since the beloved son John of Riencourt, knight, and his son Hugh, both from your diocese, are driven by zeal for the faith and devotion and are ready, as they claim, to set out against the people of Aachen in support of the universal Church, we command that, if they do what they offer and bring with them suitable warriors for this purpose, you grant to them, based on our authority, the pardon of sins that is customarily given to those going in support of the Holy Land, for a suitable period of time according to your provision. Given at Lyon, 17th October, in the sixth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Ambianensi mandat, ut Iohanni de Riencourt militi et Hugoni filio eius, pro fide contra Aquenses proficiscentibus, veniam peccatorum concedat, quae consuevit dari euntibus in subsidium Terrae Sanctae. 1232, Oct. 16. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Strasbourg. Lest you incur damage from where you ought to have deserved benefit and favor, we willingly provide remedy and caution. Since, as is evident by the actions and was proposed on your behalf before us, you have taken the town of Gengenbach and the castles of Mulberg and Otemberg with their appurtenances, which the late Emperor Frederick held in fief from the Church of Bamberg, not without great expenses, we, wishing to safeguard your indemnity with paternal care, by the authority of these presents, grant you that you are not obliged to restore them, nor may the aforementioned places be alienated in any way by our venerable brother, the Bishop of Bamberg, or his successor or anyone else; and we declare any such alienation, should it be attempted, to be null and void unless you and your helpers and men have first been fully compensated for the damages and expenses you are known to have incurred for this reason. No one, therefore, etc., may infringe on our concession and decree, etc. Given at Lyon, 3rd day before the Nones of June, in the 5th year [of our pontificate]. Conservators have been appointed for this: the dean and treasurer of St. Thomas in Strasbourg.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Argentinensi concedit, ne oppidum de Gengenbach et castra de Mulberc et de Otemberce, capta cum magnis expensis, restituere teneatur, et alienationem absque compensatione damni decernit irritam. Data Lugduni, III Non. Iunii, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Calina. We, wishing to grant a special favor to your devotion, which we know you have shown towards the Apostolic See, and inclined by your supplications, by the authority of these presents, grant you that you may, with one of your clerics whom you know to assist you in character and knowledge, licitly receive and freely retain ecclesiastical benefices, even if they have the care of souls attached, if they are canonically offered to him, up to the sum of twenty ounces of gold — notwithstanding the general constitution of the council — by our authority, provided that these benefices are not neglected in their due obligations, etc. Given at Lyon, on the Nones of October, in the sixth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Calinensi concedit, ut cum uno clerico suo beneficia ecclesiastica usque ad viginti unciarum auri summam recipere et retinere possit, constitutione concilii non obstante. 1248, Oct. 7. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the podestà, council, and commune of the Genoese. In order that you may feel the apostolic favor has increased in you from the special devotion you have toward us and the Roman Church, we grant you by the authority of these presents, that no delegate or subdelegate, executor, or even conservator, by indulgence or apostolic letters, however full or explicit they may be, obtained or to be obtained, or processes had through the same, failing to make mention of this indulgence, may pronounce against you or your land sentences of excommunication or interdict. Therefore to no one etc. Given at Lyon, November 5, in the sixth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa potestati, consilio et comuni Ianuensibus concedit, ne quis sine mentione huius indulgentiae excommunicationis vel interdicti sententias promulget. 1248, Nov. 5. Datum Lugduni.

**English Translation:**

To the provosts of the churches of Neuerburg and Ardacher in the diocese of Passau. By the authority of these presents, we command you to induct the beloved son Kilian, elected for the monastery of Saint Mary of the Scots in Vienna, diocese of Passau, into possession of the same monastery and to defend him once he has received the blessing from our venerable brother, the bishop of Regensburg, according to the tenor of our mandate which we have sent to the said bishop. Opponents, etc., if necessary, with the aid of secular power invoked for this purpose. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa prepositis ecclesiarum de Neuerburg et de Ardacher mandat, ut Kylianum electum monasterii sancte Marie Scotorum in Wienna in possessionem inducant et defendant, adiuvantes, si opus fuerit, auxilio brachii secularis. Data ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Mantua. Our duty and piety compel us to provide for those who wish to serve the Lord in the clerical order. Therefore, at the request of our beloved daughter in Christ, the noble woman Mabilon, wife of the noble man, the Marquis of Este, who is interceding on behalf of Benedict, a scholar and the son of the late Richard Ponzeconi, a citizen of Bergamo, and wishing to grant this scholar a special favor, we command you, by our authority, to provide him or have him provided with a suitable ecclesiastical benefice in one of the churches of the city or diocese of Mantua or Ferrara, excluding cathedral churches, that is currently vacant or will become available as soon as the opportunity arises. This is irrespective of any statutes in the church about a fixed number of canons confirmed by oath or apostolic authority, or any indulgence that must be mentioned in our letters, or any of our writings directed to the church for others, which we do not wish to interfere with, etc. Opponents, etc. Given at Lyon, 3rd day before the Nones of July, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Mantuano mandat, ut Benedicto scholari, filio quondam Ricardi Ponzeconi civis Pergamensis, provideat in beneficio ecclesiastico competenti in aliqua ecclesiarum Mantuane vel Ferrariensis diocesis, cathedralibus exceptis; non obstantibus statutis vel indulgentiis. Datum Lugduni, III Non. Iulii, anno sexto.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of Saint Martin in Trier. On behalf of our beloved son R., the elected of Worms, it has been humbly requested that, since our beloved son P., cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil and legate of the apostolic see, has annulled the election which the chapter of Worms conducted de facto for Conrad, provost of the Worms church, and has decided to provide the aforementioned Richard to the same church as bishop, we should take care to confirm this provision with the kindness of the apostolic see. Although we strongly presume in favor of what has been done by the legate in this matter, yet wishing to be fully informed about the premises, whether all proceeded canonically, we command that you summon the aforementioned elect and any others who might wish to oppose the provision made for the said Richard, on our behalf, peremptorily, to appear before us within a suitable term to be assigned by you, with all their reasons and documents, either in person or through sufficient and suitable procurators, to do and receive what justice may dictate. Given at Lyon, on the 4th day before the Nones of August, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati Sancti Martini Treverensis mandat ut Ricardum, electum Wormaciensem, et alios qui provisioni eius contradicere volunt, citet ad comparendum coram sede apostolica, de actis legati cardinalis Placentini certificandum. Datum Lugduni, II Non. Augusti, anno VI.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of Augia Monastery of the Order of Saint Benedict, directly subject to the Roman Church, of the diocese of Constance. On your behalf, it was brought before us that several ministerials and vassals of your monastery, holding fiefs from you, have presumed to adhere, in a damnable manner, to C., son of the late Emperor F., and his supporters against you and the Roman Church, thus breaching their oath of fealty to you. Others, rising wickedly against you, do not fear to weaken and infringe the rights and liberties of the said monastery. Thus, hindered by their malice, you are unable to effectively attend to the matters of the apostolic see as you desire. Therefore, you sought from us that we take care to provide for you with paternal solicitude in this matter. Thus, inclined by your supplications, we grant you the authority, by the power of these presents, to restrain the aforementioned ministerials and vassals through the deprivation of their fiefs, so that, having abandoned the treachery of C. and his supporters, they may assist you in the affairs of the Church vigorously and powerfully, and desist entirely from molesting the said monastery. This permission is granted notwithstanding any contrary indult from the apostolic see. Given at Lyon, on the 13th day before the Kalends of June, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa abbati Augensis monasterii mandat ut ministeriales et vassallos, qui contra eum et Romanam ecclesiam agunt, per subtractionem feudorum compescat, concedens ei auctoritatem ad hoc faciendum. 1247, Mai. 20. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Abbot of Saint Vincent of Besançon. As it was presented to us on behalf of our beloved son, the abbot of the monastery of Murbach of the order of Saint Benedict, certain clerics from the cities and dioceses of Basel, Strasbourg, and Constance, falsely claiming that they and their associates have faithfully served us and the Roman Church in the affairs of the Apostolic See, have obtained our letters concerning their provision in churches fully belonging to his monastery and customarily assigned to secular clerics, with certain executors appointed for this purpose. However, these clerics have shown themselves to be not devoted but rather disloyal to us, openly supporting their relatives who adhered to the late Emperor Frederick against us and the same church. We, considering it unworthy for the aforementioned clerics to attain the grace of our provision, command you that, if this is so, you ensure that these executors on our behalf are prohibited, so that, refraining from the aforesaid letters obtained through such fraud, they do not proceed by means of them in any way. Given at Lyon, 19th June, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati Sancti Vincentii Bisuntini mandat ut, si clerici Basiliensis, Argentinensis et Constantiensis civitatum false impetraverint litteras provisionis, executoribus eisdem inhibeat, ne per illas procedant. 1229, Iun. 19. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To P., Cardinal Deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the Apostolic See. On behalf of our beloved son, Henry, knight of Limelate in the diocese of Liège, who has taken the cross, it was humbly petitioned to us that, since he had carnal knowledge of a certain woman and later, forgetful of this fact, married Aelidis, who is related to that woman in the fourth degree of consanguinity, we might mercifully grant a dispensation for them to freely remain in such a contracted marriage. Since the same knight is said to work loyally in the affairs of the Church and our beloved son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, for which he is deemed worthy of grace and favor, we command you, if this is so, to dispense with the said knight and his wife in this matter by our authority, as you see fit for the salvation of their souls according to God. Given at Lyon, the Ides of September, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali, apostolicae sedis legato mandat, ut cum Henrico milite de Limelate et Aelide uxore eius in quarto consanguinitatis gradu, super matrimonio contracto dispenset. Datum Lugduni, Idibus Septembris, anno sexto.

**Translation to English:**

To the governor of Spoleto,

From the book of our memory, oblivion has not erased, nor has the passage of time removed from the eyes of our mind, the sincere devotion that the late Manente Rainaldi of Spoleto had towards the Roman Church, and his fervent desire for the increase of its honor. Therefore, it would be unworthy if we, who are debtors to all in justice, were to neglect our beloved children in Christ, the noble woman F., his wife, and Manente, his son, who, because of his memory, are to be cherished by the same church, in their rights. Therefore, as they have shown us through their petition, since several goods and rights which the said Manente had and possessed were occupied by many after he left the city of Spoleto to remain faithful to the church, we command you to investigate these matters plainly and without the noise of judgment. Whatever you find to have been thus occupied or detained, by the power granted to you, you shall restore to them, and provide them with suitable satisfaction from the fruits and revenues received from these properties—notwithstanding any statute, oath, or any other firmness established to the contrary. Otherwise, we instruct the rector of the duchy of Spoleto by our letters to execute this apostolic mandate; let the opposers be aware, etc.

Given at Lyon, the fourth of the Nones of October, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

---

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa potestati Spoletano mandat ut bona et iura quondam Manentis Rainaldi, a multis occupata, restitui faciat. 1248, Oct. 4, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Agnes, a nun of the monastery of Saint Petronilla of Siena, sister of brother Grifo. Since we have granted you permission to transfer from the monastery in which you reside to the church of Saint Angel in Cuti, of the diocese of Gubbio, together with two nuns of the same monastery, so that you may serve the Lord there under regular observance along with them: inclined by your prayers, if any usurers from the city and diocese of Gubbio, extorted from anyone, and some from the same city and diocese, who have inflicted damages onto others, wish to voluntarily satisfy for the construction of the said church and its workshops in their own name or in the name of their ancestors or others related to them, we grant you the authority by these presents to receive up to one hundred pounds from such satisfactions, provided that those to whom such satisfaction is owed by law cannot be found. Moreover, we desire that those from whom satisfaction has been made to you, as mentioned, shall not be held to another satisfaction. Let no one, therefore, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 21st of August, in the sixth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Agneti moniali monasterii sancte Petronille Senensis mandat de satisfactionibus usque ad centum libras recipiendis pro ecclesiae sancti Angeli de Cuti fabrica, si usurarii et qui dampna intulerint voluntarie satisfaciant, dummodo creditores legitimi non reperiantur. 1249, Aug. 21, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Philip, procurator of the Church of Salzburg. Since, as your petition presented to us contained, the castles, vassals, possessions, revenues, and other goods, which the former Duke of Austria and Styria and the Count Palatine of Bavaria held in fief from the Church of Salzburg, have returned to the right of the same Church, with no legitimate heir remaining alive who should succeed to the fief, which you claim to have partially recovered not without great labors and expenses, and you trust in the Lord to recover the other part soon: we, wishing to provide for the benefit of the same Church in the future with fatherly care, by the authority of these presents more strictly forbid that you or any of the archbishops, who shall preside over the Church of Salzburg in future times, presume to enfeoff or otherwise alienate or dispose of the castles or other things aforementioned in any way without consulting the Roman Pontiff hereafter. For we decree null and void anything attempted against our prohibition by anyone regarding the aforesaid or any part of it. Therefore let no one etc. of our prohibition and constitution etc. Given at Lyon, the 8th day before the Kalends of October, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Philippo procuratori ecclesiae Salzeburgensis mandat ne castra et bona ab ecclesia Salzeburgensi recuperata sine consensu Pontificis Romani infeudare praesumat. 1248, Sept. 24, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Brother Henry of the Order of Preachers, our penitentiary. Since through you the resignation of our venerable brother, the Bishop of Chur, has been received, we order that our beloved son, the abbot of St. Gall, be appointed as bishop and shepherd of the Church of Chur. The devotion of the said abbot has been proven and is known to shine forth in such a way that, driven by the special prerogative of love in necessity when friends are revealed, we wish to pursue him with grace and favor. Therefore, we grant you the authority to dispense with him so that he can hold both the bishopric of Chur and the abbey of St. Gall until it pleases our will to decide otherwise. This is granted by the authority of this present document, notwithstanding the indulgence said to have been granted to your order by the Apostolic See, which states that brothers of the said order are not bound to be involved with cases or matters committed to them by the same See, nor are they to involve themselves through apostolic letters which do not expressly mention this indulgence. Given at Lyon, on the third day before the Ides of October, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa fratri Henrico ordinis Praedicatorum, penitentiario suo, facultatem concedit dispensandi cum abbate Sancti Galli, ut episcopatum Curiensis cum abbatia possit tenere. 1248, XIII Kalendas Octobris. Datum Lugduni.

Translation to English:

...to the Abbot of Saint John of Parma. Desiring to be found inclined towards grace, etc., as above until: to claim. Hence, on behalf of our beloved son, the archpriest of the church of Saint Vincent, son of our beloved nobleman Jacob Veltric of Valvisneria, who is preserving the fortress of the same place and other lands held in their mountains for the common good of Parma, to the honor of God and the church, not without great expenses and labors, we command that you have him received, by our authority, as a canon and brother in some of the cathedrals of Lombardy, except those of Parma, Genoa, Reggio, and Piacenza, and to liberally confer upon him a prebend, if one is presently vacant in that church, or as soon as the opportunity presents itself — notwithstanding if we have directed our letters for others in the same place, which, etc., until: to be generated, or if by the command of our beloved son G. de Montelongo, our subdeacon and notary, legate of the apostolic see, or by the chapter of that church by their own authority some have been received therein, to whom we wish him to be preferred, as he should be preferred by right, and notwithstanding the statute regarding a certain number of canons, strengthened by oath or confirmation of the apostolic see or any other firmness, or an indulgence perhaps granted by the apostolic see to some, which does not bind them to the reception or provision of anyone by apostolic letters, which would not make express mention of that indulgence —; contradictors, etc. — notwithstanding the constitution of the two. Given at Lyons, the Nones of April, in the fifth year.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorii IX papae abbati Sancti Iohannis Parmensis scribit ut archipresbyterum plebis Sancti Vincentii, natum Iacobi Veltric, in aliqua ecclesiarum cathedralium Lombardie recipi faciat et ei praebendam conferat, exclusis Parmensi, Ianuensi, Reginensi et Placentina. 1240, Apr. 5, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Fano. In the service of the Apostolic See, the late Bishop M. of Arezzo demonstrated such purity of faith and fervor that, while insisting on the defense of ecclesiastical liberty, he endured many hardships and ultimately did not fear to face the danger of death for it. Because of this, we are rightly moved with a solicitous heart to support, with benevolent affection, his dear ones and intimates in his time. Indeed, our beloved son Nicolaus Pecte, a citizen of Ancona and brother of the said bishop, has explained to us that for the work of the same bishop, while he was engaged in the aforesaid services, he bound himself to certain creditors for five hundred pounds of Anconitan and Ravennate money, etc., as stated in the next section with words suitably modified up to the term: expedited, we command that if these matters are confirmed to you, you ensure that the aforementioned citizen is paid in full from the goods of the Arezzo Church the said five hundred pounds, to be converted without delay into the payment of these debts, with interest completely ceasing; any opposing parties etc.—notwithstanding the constitution about the two diets etc. The witnesses however etc. Given at Lyon, 11 June, in the fifth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Fanensi mandat ut Nicolaus Pecte, civis Anconitanus, de bonis ecclesiae Aretine quingentas libras pro debitis fratris sui episcopi persolvi faciat. 1236, Iun. 11. Datum Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To the abbot of the monastery of Wectingen of the Cistercian order, in the diocese of Constance. Since, as we have learned, beloved son Brother Werner, your lay brother, has incurred the hatred of many because he has worked devotedly and faithfully in the affairs of the church, we command that you or anyone else of the same order must in no way presume to send him to other places at the suggestion of some; rather, treat him with kind affection and provide him with the necessities, and make the lay brothers, as they have been accustomed until now, obey him so that he may be able to promote the affairs of the church with them. This is notwithstanding any privileges or indulgences contrary to the Cistercian order granted by the Apostolic See or its legates, which would require special or express mention in these presents. Given at Lyon, 10th November, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

Regesto in Latin:

Innocentius IV papa abbati monasterii de Wectingen Cisterciensis ordinis mandat, ne frater Wernerus conversus, qui propter ecclesiae negotia laboravit, ad alios locos mittatur, sed ut benigno affectu pertractetur et in negotiis ecclesiae adiuvetur. 1250, Nov. 10, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected Bishop of Turin. On behalf of our beloved son, the noble Boniface, Marquis of Montferrat, it has been presented before us that he, along with the authorities, councils, and communes of the cities of Milan, Genoa, and Piacenza, have previously agreed to certain pacts and conditions regarding soldiers and crossbowmen to be granted to him by them, as well as other articles, in a friendly manner. However, despite being admonished by our letters, they refuse to observe them at their own discretion. Therefore, we command that if this is the case, you should earnestly admonish and induce the said authorities, councils, and communes to fulfill and observe the said pacts and conditions within a suitable term set by you. If necessary, do not hesitate to compel them through ecclesiastical censure, with any appeal or frivolous exception set aside. Given at Lyons, 8th day before the Kalends of October, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa [Taurinensi electo] mandat, ut potestates, consiliarios, et communia Mediolanensis, Ianuensis, et Placentine civitatum compellat, pacta et conditiones cum Bonifatio marchione Montisferrati facta, infra terminum impleant. 1230, Sept. 24. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

... of our concession etc. Given at Lyon, December 10th, in the sixth year of [our pontificate]. To the provosts of the churches of Saint Arbogast and of the Holy Trinity and to the dean of Saint Thomas of Strasbourg. As required etc., with words suitably changed up to: to be obtained. Therefore, we command that you do not allow the aforementioned sons, nephews, and relatives of the above-mentioned people of Strasbourg to be troubled; those who cause such troubles etc. If not all [of you can act] etc. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa praepositis ecclesiarum Sancti Arbogasti et Sanctae Trinitatis et decano Sancti Thomae Argentinensibus mandat, ne filii, nepotes et consanguinei supradictorum Argentinensium molestentur. Datum Lugduni, IIII Idus Decembris, anno sexto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz. It is fitting and reasonable that those who have received benefits from the Church should especially support it. Therefore, since both we and our legates have shown favor to many prelates, nobles, and others in the kingdom of Germany, we command you to compel all those in those parts who have received any favors from us or from the said legates to serve our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, by pursuing the business of the aforesaid church with due diligence, removing any appeals. This is notwithstanding any letters obtained or to be obtained from the Apostolic See, which might hinder or delay this, and about which special mention ought to be made in the present document. Given as above.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino mandat, ut omnes qui a se vel legatis suis gratias consecuti sunt, ad serviendum regi Romanorum illustri, negotium ecclesiae prosequenti, compellat. Datum ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

Having consulted the Registries, Potthast, Reg. 13111; Berger 4238. To the Archbishop of Mainz and the elected Bishop of Speyer. Trusting in the Lord with fuller confidence in the sincerity and steadfastness of your devotion, we command that the twentieth part of the ecclesiastical revenues, appointed for the aid of the Holy Land, be collected throughout the kingdom of Germany. Ensure that it is deposited in a secure place, not to be assigned to anyone without our special permission, notwithstanding any indulgences or letters obtained or yet to be obtained from the Apostolic See, which might impede or delay this collection and which need to be specifically mentioned in these presents. To those opposing, etc. If both cannot act, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 9th of December, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino et electo Spirensi mandat, ut vicesimam proventuum ecclesiasticorum pro subsidio Terre Sancte in regno Alamannie colligant et in tuto loco deponant, non sine licentia speciali assignaturi. 1232, Dec. 9, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishops of Regensburg and Meissen. Our most beloved son in Christ, the illustrious king of Bohemia, has informed us that, due to his fervor of devotion and purity of faith towards us and the Roman Church, he has strongly opposed the late Emperor Frederick and his supporters to defend ecclesiastical liberty. However, some barons and nobles of his kingdom, who had taken the sign of the cross against Frederick and other enemies of the Church, have returned to their former errors, like dogs returning to their vomit, and presume to offer counsel, help, and favor to Frederick and his followers, to the detriment of their own salvation. We command you to diligently admonish and strive to induce these barons and nobles to abandon Frederick’s treachery, return to the bosom of Mother Church, and to assist the Church and the king boldly and openly. If they do not heed your admonitions and claim they dare not due to fear of the king, to remove this obstacle, receive from the said king assurances that he will not harm them in their persons or property, and from them, guarantees and pledges that they will observe the aforementioned. By our authority, absolve them from the sentence of excommunication they are known to have incurred, according to the form of the Church. Otherwise, publicly declare them excommunicated and ensure they are strictly avoided by all, imposing an ecclesiastical interdict on their lands, so that no divine office or ecclesiastical sacrament is celebrated or administered there, except for the baptism of infants and the penance of the dying, invoking, if necessary, the help of the secular arm; contradictors, etc. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopis Ratisponensi et Misnensi mandat ut barones et nobiles, qui a F. quondam imperatore defecerunt, ad ecclesiae gremium reverti et regi assistere inducant, excommunicationis poena et interdicti terris impositis, si resipiscere recusaverint. Datum ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

Issued and compared with the Registers by the illustrious O. de Falke. Potthast, Reg. 12965; Berger 3967. To Hydo, the provincial prior of the Dominican brothers in Germany. In order that those who have taken vows, according to the eminent prophets, may render their vows unto the Lord, we charge your discretion, by the authority of these presents and in the virtue of obedience, that you exhort diligently and induce all the crusaders from Frisia, Holland, and Zealand, either through yourself or through some of your fellow brothers of your order whom you deem suitable for this task, and if necessary, compel them by ecclesiastical censure, with no appeal possible, to prepare themselves such that in the coming March they may embark on their journey in aid of the Holy Land. This is to be done notwithstanding that an indulgence has been granted to the same order by the Apostolic See, so that they are not compelled against their will to be involved in causes or affairs granted to the brothers of the said order by the same See, or any indulgence granted by the same See that they cannot be interdicted, suspended, or excommunicated by apostolic letters without a special mandate from the same See making full mention of this indulgence, or by any other regulation of which special mention must be made in our letters, or by the constitution regarding two days' notice issued in the general council. Given at Lyon, 10th Kalends of July, in the fifth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Hydo priori provinciali fratrum Praedicatorum in Alamania mandat, ut omnes crucesignatos de Frisia, Hollandia et Zeelandia moneat et inducat ad iter in Terram Sanctam mense Martio proxime futuro arripiendum, etiam per censuram ecclesiasticam, si opus fuerit, appellatione remota, compellendo. 1243, Iunii 22, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Strasbourg. Having understood previously that the citizens of Basel wanted to return under certain conditions to the mandate of the Church and our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, we are said to have directed our letters to you, containing among other things, that you should grant our beloved son B., Provost of Grandvaux and Canon of Basel, as a defender or captain for the aforementioned citizens, by our authority, as long as our venerable brother, the Bishop of Basel, is impotent, negligent, or remiss. You should promise them on our behalf that if they return to the Church's mandate according to the tenor of these letters and persist in its devotion, we will ensure that they are kept unharmed concerning the destruction of the bishop's house, and we will not allow them to be molested by the bishop or anyone else on this matter. However, it was never our intention, nor is it now, that the same provost should be an assistant to the aforementioned bishop in any matter, especially since he has been found to be so openly diligent and effective concerning matters that pertain to the honor of God and the exaltation of the Church, that he does not require the assistance of any coadjutor, as long as he is sufficient by himself for the execution of the care entrusted to him. For this reason, we rightly will and command your fraternity by apostolic writings that if the said bishop is deemed sufficient in any way for the execution of such matters, you should allow him to handle his imminent affairs according to his will, and with sincere affection, assist him in these matters when appropriate, according to custom. Furthermore, if the said bishop is, by God's grace, as asserted, so restored to health that he can be a captain and defender for the aforementioned citizens, arrange with the aforementioned provost that he should no longer interfere in such defense and other matters pertaining to the bishop. If there are any who contradict or rebel, restrain them by ecclesiastical censure, removing any appeal—no letters obtained or to be obtained from the Apostolic See, which do not make full mention of the present matters, should stand against this. Given at Lyons, March 24, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Argentinensi mandat ut, si episcopus Basiliensis ad executionem munerum suorum sufficiens habeatur, eum in negotiis suis agendis permittat; sin autem, cum preposito Grandivallensi disponat ut se de defensione civium Basiliensium non intromittat. Dat. Lugduni, VIIII Kalendas Aprilis, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Podestà of Spoleto. Since it was proposed to us by the beloved sons James and Andrew of Castel Litaldi, Hermann, Follis, Philip, and Giles, sons of the same James from the diocese of Spoleto, that our beloved son R., cardinal deacon of Santa Maria in Cosmedin and legate of the apostolic see, has condemned the people of Castel Litaldi to compensate for the damages inflicted by them and also for other losses they incurred in maintaining loyalty to the apostolic see, we mandate that you, with the power granted to you, execute this condemnation clearly and without the noise of judgment, from which could follow a prolongation of the cause, notwithstanding any statute, oath, or other firmness established by the city of Spoleto. Otherwise, we give our venerable brother, the bishop of Perugia, the mandate in our letters, so that he may carry out the apostolic mandate on this matter. Given at Lyon, on the Kalends of December, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa potestati Spoletano mandat ut condemnationem in homines Castri Litaldi latam ab R. Sancte Marie in Cosmidin diacono cardinali exequatur, non obstante statuto Spoletano. 1231, Dec. 1. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Brixen. Your fraternity has informed us that our beloved son, Cardinal O. of Santa Maria in Via Lata, legate of the apostolic see, has entrusted you with the administration of the Church of Trent, both in spiritual and temporal matters, by our authority, until it pleases us otherwise. He commanded the archdeacon and chapter of that church not to disturb you in any way in this administration, but rather to obey you in this matter, and if they acted otherwise, he threatened them with the sentence of excommunication. However, they, acting against this command, did not fear incurring the said sentence, and you, by the authority of this commission, pronounced the sentence of excommunication, as justice demanded, after a canonical warning, because they refused to obey and attend to you in this regard with obstinacy. Although they claimed to be aggrieved by the same legate, asserting that you summoned them to an unsafe place, and appealed to our hearing, the said legate deemed their appeal frivolous, as it indeed was. Nevertheless, the archdeacon and the aforementioned chapter, as despisers of ecclesiastical authority, remained in this contumacy, continuing to celebrate divine services and administer ecclesiastical sacraments, to the peril of their souls, your prejudice, and contempt of ecclesiastical discipline. Therefore, to teach them through punishment how rash it is to oppose apostolic commands, we order you, notwithstanding the aforesaid appeal, to publicly pronounce them excommunicated and to ensure they are strictly avoided by all as excommunicated until they offer suitable satisfaction. If they do not repent, you are empowered by our authority to suspend them from their offices and strip them of their benefits, and to confer those benefits on suitable persons devoted to the Roman Church, as well as to dispense with those of the chapter who, through devotion and obedience, have deemed themselves worthy of grace, concerning the note of irregularity, if they are known to have incurred it. Opposers, etc. Given at Lyon, May 22, in the fifth year of our reign.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Brixinensi mandat ut, non obstante appellatione, archidiaconum et capitulum ecclesiae Tridentinae excommunicatos publice nuntiet et arcius evitari faciat, eosque, si non resipuerint, ab officiis suspendat et beneficiis privet, illaque conferat personis idoneis et ecclesiae Romanae devotis. 1230, Maii 22, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Patriarch of Jerusalem, legate of the Apostolic See. Since, as was presented on your behalf before us, you have tolerated, albeit with prior protest, out of reverence for us, that our venerable brother, the Patriarch of Antioch, apostolic legate, when he was in Acre, presumed to display the insignia of legation, walk with the red [attire], and bless the people of Acre, although such acts are proper only to a legate appointed directly by us: we, inclined by your supplications, by the authority of these presents, grant you that through these actions, no prejudice shall be generated against your church. Let no one therefore etc. of our concession etc. Given at Lyon, on the 4th day before the Nones of December, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius Papa IX Patriarchae Hierosolymitano, apostolicae sedis legato, concedit auctoritate praesentium ut, ob gestum Patriarchae Antiocheni in Accon, insignia legationis gerens, rubro utentem et populum benedicentem, nullum ecclesiae suae praeiudicium generetur. Datum Lugduni, IIII Non. Decembris, anno sexto.

**Translation to English:**

To the master and convent of the Knights Templar of Jerusalem. As we have learned, certain individuals from your regions, both religious and others, are seditiously plotting how the kingdom of Jerusalem could come into the hands of Frederick, the former emperor, and his son Conrad, enemies of the Church. We earnestly ask, admonish, and exhort your entire community, firmly ordering you not to deviate from your steadfast devotion to the Roman Church and not to allow, as much as it lies in you, the dominion of that kingdom to be altered in any way. Otherwise, you and other privileged persons in those regions who act against this can rightfully fear that all privileges, liberties, and immunities granted to you and them by the Apostolic See will be permanently revoked. Given as above. In the same manner. To the vice-master and convent of the Hospital of Jerusalem. In the same manner. To the master and convent of the Hospital of St. Mary of the Teutonic Knights. In the same manner to the archbishops and bishops and abbots, priors, archdeacons, and other prelates of churches established throughout the kingdom of Jerusalem. In the same manner to all barons and knights of the kingdom of Jerusalem. In the same manner to the consuls and community of the Genoese in the kingdom of Jerusalem. In the same manner to the consuls and community of the Venetians residing in the kingdom of Jerusalem. In the same manner to the consuls and community of the Pisans residing in the kingdom of Jerusalem. In the same manner to the people of the city of Acre.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa magistro et conventui militiae Templi Ierosolimitani mandat ne in devotione Romanae ecclesiae immutentur et ne permittant regnum Ierosolimitanum in manus inimicorum ecclesiae pervenire, sub poena privationis privilegiis ab apostolica sede concessis. Datum apud Anagniam, anno pontificatus quarto (1230).

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Tripoli. We have recently learned that the Father of mercies and Lord, who chastises and corrects the son whom He loves, has visited you with the scourge of illness in these days in order to preserve your spirit. Therefore, doubting the recovery of your health, you wisely and prudently wish, while discretion is still with you, to arrange your movable goods for the salvation of your soul, and to provide for the needs of some of your relatives who, due to their steadfastness in faith and devotion to the Roman Church, have been forced into exile and stripped of their own goods by the supporters of the late Emperor Frederick. On your behalf, we were humbly petitioned to grant you the apostolic permission to do so. Therefore, we, who share in your difficulties with paternal affection, kindly consent to your wishes in this matter, granting your fraternity the free authority by the present document to dispose of the aforementioned goods and provide for your aforementioned relatives as your discretion sees fit, nonetheless permitting that these relatives of yours, to whom you have given or decided to give any of the aforementioned goods, may rightfully retain them. Given at Lyons, on the 17th day before the Kalends of December, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Tripolitano licentiam concedit ut, propter infirmitatem, de bonis mobilibus disponat pro salute animae et necessitatibus consanguineorum suorum, qui exulant propter fidem. Lugduni, XV Kal. Decembris, anno sexto.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Modena. Although the Apostolic See, like a loving mother, has often shown itself generous in granting provision even to strangers and unknown persons, its munificence in providing should not be absent for the devout and known. The more it finds such individuals proven through their deeds, the more it should rise in rewarding their merits. Therefore, since our beloved son Bartholomew, a canon of Reggio, the nephew of our former chaplain Master Philip, has been deprived of all his ecclesiastical goods by the supporters of the late Emperor Frederick, and with his father miserably imprisoned by the said Frederick, he has been expelled from his own land and home, we, wishing to console him with the grace of due provision, command that he be received, by our authority, as a canon and brother in one of the cathedrals throughout Lombardy, which he chooses to accept, except for Piacenza, Parma, and Genoa, and be provided with a prebend if one is presently vacant or as soon as it becomes available. This is to be done regardless of any statute in that church about a fixed number of canons, reinforced by oath or any other firm assurance, or if we have sent our letters for others in the same, which we do not wish to be hindered, or any papal indulgence that might impede such grace and for which special mention would be required in our letters. Opponents are to be disregarded. This is notwithstanding the constitution regarding two days, etc., as stated generally. Given at Lyon, 5th of June, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Mutinensi mandat ut Bartholomeum canonicum Reginum in una ecclesiarum cathedralium Lombardiae, Placentina, Parmensi et Ianuensi exceptis, recipi faciat in canonicum et provideri sibi de prebenda, ut consolationem habeat ob persecutiones a fautoribus Friderici quondam imperatoris passas. 1231, Iun. 5, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the priors of the Order of Preachers of Louvain and Antwerp in the dioceses of Cambrai and Liège. Having full confidence in your circumspection in the Lord, we command you to collect the redemptions and proceeds arising from any cause concerning the vows of those signed with the cross, both against the late Emperor Frederick and his son Conrad and their supporters, as well as for the aid of the Holy Land, who, being detained by just impediment, were unable to personally fulfill their vows. Also, collect the legacies designated for such aid in the province of Cologne and those parts of the dioceses of Cambrai and Tournai, known to be of the empire, and the twentieth of the ecclesiastical revenues of all Germany, either by yourselves or by others whom you see fit for this task. Assign what has already been collected to you and also keep it until our goodwill pleases, opposing any contradictors, and you shall faithfully inform us of their amount by your letters— notwithstanding any indulgence granted by the Apostolic See to your order or any other person to whom you may deem it appropriate to entrust this, which states that the brothers of the same order or the said person are not bound to know or involve themselves in causes or matters committed to them by the Apostolic See, or any other, which states that any persons cannot be interdicted, suspended, or excommunicated by apostolic letters, unless they make full mention of such indulgence. Given at Lyon, 13th Kalends of October, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa prioribus ordinis Praedicatorum Lovaniensium et Anwerpensium mandat ut redemptiones et obventiones a crucesignatis vota personaliter exequi non valentibus et pro subsidio Terrae Sanctae colligant, ac ea conservet usque ad beneplacitum suum. Lugduni, XIII Kalendas Octobris, anno VI.

**Translation to English:**

To all patriarchs, archbishops, bishops, abbots, priors, deans, archdeacons, and other prelates of churches, both exempt and non-exempt, established in overseas regions. Desiring with all our heart your safety and prosperity, the exaltation of the Church, and the liberation of the Holy Land, we have decided to send our venerable brother, the Bishop of Tusculum, a man endowed with knowledge, decorated with integrity, and circumspect in counsel, to those regions as an angel of peace, for the promotion of the business of the said church and the procurement of the utility of the said regions. We grant him the full office of legation and the free power to relax the sentence of excommunication, which some of those parts, adhering to Frederick, the former emperor of the Romans, and his supporters, have incurred or might incur against the church itself and any others in those parts, and to freely remit any injuries and offenses they have inflicted on the church itself, admitting them into our grace and that of the said church. Since we embrace him with the arms of special affection among our other brothers, we command and enjoin upon all of you that you receive him, or rather us in him, kindly and treat him honorably, as the legate of the apostolic see, in all the aforesaid matters. For whatever he decides to do regarding the above matters, we shall hold firm and acceptable. Otherwise, the sentence or penalty, whether spiritual or temporal, which he pronounces upon the rebellious, etc., shall be observed. Given at Lyon, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of August, in the sixth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa universis patriarchis, archiepiscopis, episcopis, abbatibus, prioribus, decanis, archidiaconis aliisque ecclesiarum prelatis in ultramarinis partibus mandat ut episcopum Tusculanum, legatum apostolicae sedis, honorifice recipiant et benigne tractent, cum plenis potestatibus excommunicationes relaxandi et in gratiam ecclesiae recipiendi. Lugduni, XII Kal. Augusti, anno VI.

Translation to English:

To the provost and chapter of Rimini. Since, as your petition read before us contained, our beloved son R., cardinal deacon of Santa Maria in Cosmedin, legate of the apostolic see, deemed that you should be absolved from the sentence of excommunication which you seemed to have incurred by favoring the late emperor F. or otherwise, by the authority granted to him generally by us on this matter, and also dispensed with you for the irregularities contracted from it: we, assenting to your devout prayers and considering what has been done by the same cardinal as valid and pleasing, confirm it by apostolic authority and strengthen it with the protection of this present writing. Therefore, no one, etc., of our confirmation, etc. Given at Lyon, 23rd December, in the sixth year. A conservator was appointed for them on this matter, the bishop of Fano.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa praeposito et capitulo Ariminensibus confirmationem concedit absolutionis ab excommunicatione et dispensationis a cardinali legato factarum propter favorem quondam imperatori F. 1236, Dec. 23. Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To the elected Bishop of Vercelli. Since you are known to currently need the help of your vassals due to the war against Frederick, the former emperor, and his supporters, and since those who do not assist their lords in times of need rightly deserve to be condemned to eternal shame and perpetual punishment: we grant you by the authority of these presents the full faculty to deprive perpetually all vassals of the Church of Vercelli, who within fifteen days after being required or admonished by you or your messenger in a general proclamation at Novara (as they cannot conveniently be sought out or admonished in their homes due to the war at this time), do not assist you and the said Church, as rebels of yours and the said Church, of the fiefs which they hold from it, and to enfeoff other suitable and devoted persons with these fiefs or to retain them for the use of the same Church, as you see fit to do, and to restrain the opposers, etc. up to: we grant you full authority. Therefore, let no one, etc. Given at Lyon, December 8, in the sixth year.

Regesto in Latin:

Innocentius IV papa electo Vercellensi mandat, ut vassallos Vercellensis ecclesiae, qui infra quindecim dies post requisitionem in generali predicatione apud Novariam, auxilium non praestiterint in guerra contra F. imperatorem quondam, perpetuo feudis privet et alios idoneos infeudet. 1248, Dec. 8, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the citizens of Aachen in the diocese of Liège. Although in returning to the devotion of the Church you have been more obstinate than was expedient, nevertheless, because you have returned and, as we have learned, you excel others in the strength of constancy and purity of faith, we, for this reason, wishing to count you among the special devotees of the Apostolic See, willingly accede to your wishes and favorably hear your petitions as much as we can with God. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, inclined by your supplications, we confirm by apostolic authority the privileges, rights, and freedoms granted to the inhabitants of your land by Charles of blessed memory and other emperors and kings of old, which our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, is said to have confirmed, as long as you persist in the devotion and favor of the Church, and we secure them with the protection of this present script. Therefore, let no one whatsoever etc. our confirmation etc. Given at Lyon, on the 12th of December, in the sixth year. A conservator was appointed for them on this matter, the dean of the church of Aachen in the diocese of Liège.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa civibus Aquensibus in diocesi Leodiensi privilegia, iura et libertates a Carolo et aliis regibus concessa auctoritate apostolica confirmat. 1248, Dec. 12. Datum Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Milan and his suffragans. Those whom the sweetness of maternal mercy does not recall to the bosom, the rod of paternal severity should subdue, lest it be an impious cruelty to let the sins of those who persistently offend go unpunished due to the weak leniency of soft compassion and to leave those who deserve hellish punishment free from temporal penalty. Indeed, the power and commune of Tortona adhered obstinately to the late Emperor Frederick against God and the Church, opposing God's counsel, by which the universal Church, for the sake of public salvation, has acted against him, and joining hands with him to undermine Catholic freedom and disrupt the state of Italy, they seem to have made a pact with hell and a covenant with death. For they do not respond to one mercifully calling them to salvation, nor do they regard the clemency extending a hand for their protection, but willingly perish under the condemned tyranny of the modern Pharaoh, following a blind leader to ruinous depths like the blind. Therefore, we, wishing still to use the moderation of apostolic see's gentleness towards them, which prefers to correct sins in subjects rather than punish, command that in the solemn assemblies of your people you publicly admonish these people of Tortona that they, ceasing from harmful dissipation, completely withdraw from the said Frederick, enemy of God and the Church, and by devoutly obeying our mandates, strive to be reconciled to ecclesiastical unity and join the communion of the faithful in obedience to God and devotion to the Church. Otherwise, they should know that we will proceed to deprive their city of the honor of episcopal dignity and to inflict more severe punishments on them, if their obstinacy demands, so that those whom the fear of God does not draw away from evil may be crushed by the worthy severity of vengeance. Given as above. In like manner to the Archbishop of Genoa and his suffragans.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Mediolanensi et suffraganeis suis mandat, ut Terdonenses, a Frederico quondam imperatore recedentes, ad ecclesiae unitatem reconciliari moneant, alioquin civitatem episcopali dignitate privaturum et graviores poenas infligendum minatur. 1237, dat. Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archdeacon of Todi. The purity of devotion and the constancy of fidelity, which our beloved sons, the noble men Hugolinus Bonicomitis, Rainerius, and Hugolinus Hugolini, our faithful ones, have maintained towards the Roman Church, their mother, like being set upon the rock of faith during their adversities, propose to us a firm hope of their perseverance and lead us to grant them special grace. Since the noblemen declare that they have received many damages for the sake of the same church from the people of Castrum Iuxi and Monte San Martino in the diocese of Spoleto, we command that you compel these people, by prior admonition and through ecclesiastical censure, straightforwardly and without the noise of a trial, as would be just, to satisfy the said noblemen for the aforementioned damages, removing any appeal. Given at Lyon, 18th December, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archidiacono Tudertino mandat, ut homines Castri Iuxi et Montis Sancti Martini Spoletane diocesis, qui nobilibus Hugolino Bonicomitis, Rainerio et Hugolino Hugolini dampna intulerunt, ecclesiastica censura compellat ad eadem dampna resarcienda. Datum Lugduni, XV Kal. Ianuarii, anno sexto (1241).

**Translation to English:**
