To the bishop of Châlons and the abbot of the Holy Sepulchre of Cambrai. Our beloved sons, the noble men John of Avesnes and Baldwin, his brother, have informed us that certain enemies of theirs maliciously seek to tarnish their legitimacy, so that over time they might be excluded from the goods that belong to them by hereditary right, spreading this accusation to many ears. Therefore, they have humbly petitioned us, since it would be very dangerous for them or at least for their heirs for this matter to remain thus unexamined, that we would provide for them concerning this matter with paternal solicitude. Therefore, we command that regarding the lineage of these nobles — notwithstanding that there was litigation and proceedings before us for some time on this matter between them on one side and their brothers on the other, with nothing having been concluded — you diligently inquire the truth, as plainly as you can, and decide what is canonical, setting aside any appeals, the question of the goods being reserved to the principal lord. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Cathalaunensi et abbati Sancti Sepulchri Cameracensis mandat, ut veritatem super natalibus Iohannis et Balduini de Avesnis inquirant et canonicum statuant. Datum Anagniae, anno pontificatus tertio, circa 1230.

**Translation to English:**

To the Abbot of the monastery of Augia, of the order of Saint Benedict, belonging directly to the Roman Church without intermediary, in the diocese of Constance. It has been intimated to us through the letters of our venerable brother, the bishop of Constance, and our beloved sons, the noble men Hartmann of Kyburg, Ludwig of Frohburg, Gottfried of Sigmaringen, and Hartmann of Grüningen, counts devoted to the Roman Church, that if you have hitherto seemed neglectful and remiss in the affairs of the Church, it proceeded from strategy, not from obstinacy or deficiency, namely so that by seizing the opportune time, you might be able to offend those resisting rather than be offended by them. Their assertion is manifestly supported by the fact that when recently C., son of the late emperor F., having gathered forces from all sides, not considering that victory in war does not depend on the multitude of the army but that strength is only from heaven, attempted to engage with these counts, you stood by them manfully and powerfully with a decent and honorable retinue of armed men, so that the persecutor of the Church, turning his back, nearly became captured by a strong hand, leaving behind many of his possessions. Therefore, they humbly supplicated us on your behalf, that we might admit you, as a devoted son of the Church, into our grace and favor and pursue you with the benevolence of special grace. We, indeed, hoping that henceforth the lamp will not be hidden under a bushel but will come into the light and into expected prominence, have seen fit to admit you into the grace and favor of the Apostolic See and ours, at the contemplation of the same bishop and the said noblemen, directing that you conduct yourself in the future in such a way that we may recognize through evident works that what they have intimated to our ears about you is true. Furthermore, we will favorably admit your petitions, as far as we are able with God. Given at Lyon, on the Ides of May, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa abbati Augensis monasterii ordinis Sancti Benedicti significat se in gratiam et favorem apostolicae sedis eum admittere ob servitia praestita contra persecutorem ecclesiae, monens ut in futurum operibus evidentibus se gerat. 1248, Mai. 15, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the archbishops and bishops, abbots, priors, etc., as mentioned above, to the prelates established throughout Lombardy, the march of Treviso, and Romagna. Since Ezelinus da Romano is rightly considered suspect of heretical depravity for many reasons and probable arguments, we have deemed it necessary to proceed with an investigation against him by religious men; these diligently investigating the matter, found that he should be considered justly suspect. Subsequently, he sent envoys to the apostolic see, to whom we appointed our venerable brother... the bishop of Sabina, as an auditor, before whom they offered to swear on his soul how Ezelinus believes in God and the Catholic faith according to the teachings of the Roman Church. But this purgation was not accepted by the said bishop or by us, since such a serious crime must be purged not through envoys but in person before us. We set a deadline for him to present himself before the apostolic see by the coming Kalends of August, to act in accordance with the dictates of reason, ensuring his personal safety with full security for his coming and going. And because neither by the deadline nor after he has made any attempt to come or send anyone, being already ensnared by the bonds of several excommunications and reasonably suspected of holding erroneous beliefs about the Catholic faith, we have deemed it necessary to bind him with the chain of anathema on the holy day of the past Thursday; and we have commanded and want it announced to him that unless he appears before us by the upcoming feast of St. John, to comply with the mandates and wishes of the Church regarding the above matters, we will proceed more gravely against him according to canonical and legitimate sanctions. Therefore, we command through apostolic writings to all of you that you publish and cause to be published all of the above and each individual item in places where you see it to be necessary. Given as above. In the same manner to the patriarch of Aquileia.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopis, episcopis, abbatibus, prioribus per Lombardiam, marchiam Tervisinam et Romaniolam praecipit, ut Ezelinum de Romano, suspectum de heretica pravitate et anathematis laqueo innodatum, publice denuntient, nisi coram apostolica sede usque ad festum Beati Ioannis compareat, mandatis ecclesiae pariturus. 1233, [locus non specificatus].

Translation to English:

To Manente, son of the late Manente Rainaldi, citizen of Spoleto. The gracious benevolence of the Apostolic See should always precede and follow you with full favor since the Roman Church has accepted you as its protégé. The meritorious actions of your father on our behalf advocate for this, as from the earliest days of his youth, he ardently aspired to carry out actions that were beneficial and honorable to the state of the aforementioned See and its community. He ultimately concluded his life’s journey in such a way that, while your mother was pregnant with you, he chose to leave his paternal home and transfer to the City to live under the protection of the Church, where he consequently died in exile, rather than deny his allegiance to the See and the aforementioned community. He foresaw their impending downfall, which the public persecutor of Italy at that time was nefariously pursuing to ruin his city and fellow citizens. Considering it fitting and proper that the Roman Church should in return bestow upon you a gratuitous reward of paternal blessing and grace, we have decided by apostolic authority to grant you the right to peacefully and quietly possess your men, vassals, castles, towns, and other goods, in the same manner and liberty as your father obtained for himself, free and exempt from all services, exactions, and collections of others, whether common or private persons. We decree that no one should dare to exercise any jurisdiction or exaction over the aforementioned matters in any way other than as during your father's time. Let no one, therefore, etc. of our concession and establishment, etc. Given at Lyons, on the Nones of November, in the sixth year. The bishop of Spoleto is appointed as a conservator over this matter.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa Manenti, filio Manentis Rainaldi civis Spoletani, concedit ut homines, vassallos, castra, villas, et alia bona sua, simili statu et libertate, quemadmodum pater suus pro se obtinuit, pacifice possideat et quiete. 1232, Nov. 5, Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To the beloved sons, brothers Henry of Ankesperge and Hermann of Botenbrunnen of the Order of Friars Minor, and to the Vicedomine of Regensburg. The beloved son, the noble man Conrad, Count of Wasserburg, presented before us that although the citizens of Höhnowe, his ministerials, and their wives and children, as well as Conrad, knight of Sebrucke of the Diocese of Freising, had been absolved from the sentence of excommunication which they had incurred through the Apostolic See against all adherents of the late Emperor Frederick by our beloved son, the elected Bishop of Ferrara, then legate of the Apostolic See, according to the form of the Church, by swearing corporally to persevere in the purity of faith and ecclesiastical devotion: nevertheless, they, like dogs returning to their vomit, do not fear to stand more boldly than usual with the enemies of the Church and to rebel against their lord, to the peril of their souls. Therefore, lest they boast of having gained from the vice of ingratitude and infidelity, we command that, unless they and others like them in this matter shall have returned to their senses and made satisfaction according to the Church's mandate before the forthcoming Feast of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary, you will subject them to the sentence of excommunication from that time and make known the excommunicated, at places where it shall seem expedient, on every Sunday and feast day with ringing bells and lighted candles until the

**Translation to English:**

... to the abbot and convent of Wettinhgen of the Cistercian order in the diocese of Constance. Since your monastery is among the supporters of Frederick, the former emperor, and because of this, you cannot easily avoid occasionally communicating with the excommunicated: we, inclined by your petitions, grant you by the authority of these presents, that if it happens that you communicate with the same supporters bound by the chain of excommunication, you may not be involved in the snare of major excommunication, provided you do not communicate in crime with criminals. Let no one, therefore, etc. of our concession etc. Given at Lyon, 12th Kalends of February, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa abbati et conventui de Wettinhgen, Cisterciensis ordinis, Constantiensis diocesis, indulgentiam concedit ne, cum fautoribus Friderici quondam imperatoris excommunicationis vinculo innodatis, communicare contingat, maioris excommunicationis laqueo involvantur, dummodo in crimine non communicent. 1249, Jan. 21, Lugduni.

### Translation to English:

To those concerned. Since we have commanded that the Bishop of Padua, deemed as ineffective, be admonished and induced to resign due to his bodily incapacity, which seems to have hindered his usefulness, and since we intend to provide the Church of Padua with a person who matches such a responsibility and honor, we command that if the aforementioned bishop should voluntarily resign or pass away, you expressly prohibit the chapter of the same church under our authority from proceeding to elect, petition, or nominate anyone without our special permission. For we decree that anything attempted contrary to this prohibition shall be null and void. Given as above.

### Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa capitulo ecclesiae Pataviensis mandat ne ad electionem seu nominationem episcopi procedant sine licentia apostolica. [Pontificatus anno XI].

**Translation to English:**

To Master Peter of Atino, our scribe, canon of Atino, rector of the church of Saint Marcian of Atino in the diocese of Sora. Since, as you have taken care to inform us, the late bishop L. of Aquino conferred upon you the church of Saint Marcian of Atino by the authority of our predecessor of happy memory, Pope G., pronouncing a sentence of excommunication against any contradictors or rebels, and you have long been in peaceful and quiet possession of it: we, inclined by your supplications, holding what was done by the same bishop as valid and agreeable, confirm to you the said church by apostolic authority and fortify it with the support of this present writing — notwithstanding that the canons of Atino are said to have, after this grant, invested one of their own and, together with I., nephew of Judge Peter de Vinea, who acted as their provost, recklessly assigned it to the common table by their own authority and confirmed this by oath; we decree that these acts and anything else presumed against you and to your prejudice concerning the church or its goods are of no validity. Therefore, let no one etc. violate our confirmation and constitution etc. Given at Lyon, the ides of October, in the sixth year. Conservators were appointed for this matter: the abbot of Casemari and the prior of Saint Dominic of the dioceses of Veroli and Sora, that they may not permit anyone to disturb him against the tenor of our confirmation and constitution. If not both, then etc. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Magistro Petro de Atino, canonico Atinensi, rectori ecclesiae sancti Marciani de Atino, ecclesiam confirmat et mandat ne permittant eum ab aliquibus contra confirmationis tenorem molestari. Datum Lugduni, Idibus Octobris, anno sexto.

**Translation to English:**

O. de Falke. Berger 3915. To the Bishop of Strasbourg. Having understood the purity of devotion and faith with which our beloved son, the noble man Eberard of Erendorf, strives to be found conspicuous in the services of the Apostolic See, boldly opposing the wicked and reprobate who attack the honor and dignity of the Church, we have directed our prayers and mandate to the dean and chapter of Strasbourg to receive the late Hermann, the cleric son of the said noble, as a canon and brother and to assign him a prebend. Similarly, we instructed the abbot and convent of the monastery of Weissenburg of the Order of Saint Benedict in the Diocese of Speyer to provide him with a suitable ecclesiastical benefice, which pertains to their collation and is customarily assigned to secular clerics. Indeed, the said dean and chapter are said to have received the aforementioned cleric as a canon, and the same abbot and convent, through their open letters, promised that as soon as an opportunity arose, they would provide him with a benefice according to the apostolic mandate. However, as it pleased the Lord, the same cleric has since passed away, and the said noble is said to continue his prior devotion with matters that redound to the honor of the Church. We, considering him worthy of special favor and wishing to console his grieving spirit with apostolic grace, for whom many noble and powerful men from Germany, devoted to the Roman Church, have sent us affectionate letters with you, command your fraternity to ensure that our beloved son Ulric, a cleric, the son of the same noble, in whom we wish to transfer the favor granted to his brother Hermann, be received as a canon and brother of the Church of Strasbourg and be assigned a prebend and be provided with a benefice by the same abbot and convent; those who object, etc. Given at Lyons, on the 3rd day before the Kalends of June, in the fifth year.

**Regesto:**

Papa Innocentius IV episcopo Argentinensi mandat ut Ulricum clericum, filium Eberardi de Erendorf, in canonicum et fratrem ecclesiae Argentinensis recipi faciat et ei prebendam conferat, secundum gratiam primo fratri Hermanno factam, datis litteris abbatibus et conventui monasterii de Wissenburch de provisione beneficii. Datum Lugduni, III Kalendas Iunii, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Treasurer of the Church of Saint Peter in Strasbourg. Our beloved son Hugo, a canon of the Church of Zurich in the Diocese of Constance and a cleric of our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King W. of the Romans, presented himself before our presence, stating that he fears some danger might be imminent for him, potentially due to the machinations of some of his rivals, because some of his relatives are offering aid and favor to Frederick, the former emperor, against the Church. Although he has worked with all his strength to bring them back to the service of the Church, he humbly implored us to mercifully provide him with protection, as he has always loved the Church to the best of his ability. Since Hugo has been devoted to the Roman Church, and the display of his good works is said to affirm this, and the said king protests as much in his letters, and since the wrongdoing of his relatives should not harm him who strives to benefit the business of the Church with all his might, we command that you do not allow Hugo, who persists in devotion to the Apostolic See, to be harassed by anyone concerning his benefices or the revenues thereof due to this matter, notwithstanding any letters of the same See or its legates obtained by him or yet to be obtained. Protectors of this kind, etc. Given at Lyons, on the second Ides of November, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa thesaurario ecclesiae Sancti Petri Argentinensis mandat, ut Hugonem canonicum ecclesiae Turicensis, qui contra molestias ob consanguineorum suorum fautores Friderici imperatoris quondam timet, tueatur, ne beneficiis suis praeiudicetur. Datum Lugduni, II Idus Novembris, anno sexto.

**Translation to English:**

To the same. Although unworthy, we fulfill the duties on earth of Him who does not wish the death of the sinner but seeks life, we are troubled with deeper sorrow the more noble the member that sometimes is harmed in the body of the Church. Hence, because a covered wound, if left untouched, tends to spread widely as a scandal to the body, we, seeing that Frederick, the former emperor, neglecting his own salvation, disgracefully scorned the sentence of excommunication which the Roman Church had pronounced against him due to his faults, and waiting for a long time for him to humbly return to the Lord of Hosts seeking Him, - indeed, we sorrowfully report - with a hardened heart despising the remedy and loathing the rebuke of discipline, as if considering the hammer to be mere straw, he not only did not correct himself with any repentance, but also audaciously provoked the Lord against him by adding sin to sins and gravely persecuting the Church in many ways, we have declared the said Frederick deprived of all dignity and honor, which he rendered himself unworthy of, and we have decreed that all those who were bound to him by oath should be perpetually absolved from such an oath. However, since in all these matters His wrath is not turned away, but His hand is still stretched out, so that his wound seems incurable, and it is fitting that those whom divine fear does not recall from evil should at least be restrained by temporal discipline, if perhaps affliction may give them understanding: we command you strictly, by virtue of obedience through apostolic writings, that each of you in your cities and dioceses proclaim to the peoples subject to you the word of the cross against said Frederick and his son Conrad and their supporters, diligently inciting the same peoples against them as subverters of the faith and destroyers of ecclesiastical liberty, granting by our authority to those who shall assume such a burden in their own persons and goods, that pardon and indulgence for their sins which was granted to those going to aid the Holy Land in the general council; you shall fulfill our command in such a way that the diligence of your zeal may shine through its effect, and the apostolic see may take evident proof of how much it should trust you in this, and that you may not be accused of disobedience or contempt. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa mandat episcopis, ut in civitatibus et diocesibus suis verbum crucis contra Fridericum quondam imperatorem eiusque fautores proponant, indulgentiam concedentes assumptoribus huiusmodi oneris. Datum ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble men, the Prefect of the City, Peter Boniface, Amato son of the late Gabriel of the Prefects, lords of Vico, and others of the Prefecture. Since it is fitting that everyone receives a reward appropriate to their merits, it is proper that the faithful and devoted to the Church, especially those whom the necessity of the present time has tested, be rewarded with worthy prizes, and that the inconstancy of the unfaithful and disloyal be punished with due penalty, so that the reward of the former may induce others to serve the Church, and the retribution of the latter may prevent others from daring to commit offenses. Therefore, since the men of Vico and Bleda, and of other lands of yours, your vassals, have abandoned the fidelity they owe to you, while you persist in devotion to the Church, and presumed to hand themselves and your castles, where they resided, over to the captains of the late Emperor Frederick of the Romans as traitors, nonetheless causing severe damage in other castles, to vassals and goods: we, to ensure that such offenses inflicted upon you are not left unpunished, by the authority of these presents, command that all such damages caused to you by the aforesaid vassals or on account of them, and any that may be inflicted as long as they persist in such infidelity, as well as all things taken from you by these vassals and the fruits and revenues of those castles thus lost, be fully restored to you, and that they not be admitted to the grace of the Church until they have fully satisfied the aforementioned matters. And because these same vassals do not desist from attacking and offending you and other faithful of the Church, we grant you by the same authority, that you cannot be summoned by anyone regarding the offenses inflicted by the rebels and other enemies of the Church, or those to be inflicted on you henceforth on this account; from which we decree that you be absolved. We further command that no community of city or castle, baron, or other person presume to defend these vassals of yours and their goods, who have committed such a crime against you, their lords, or to harass you in any way concerning their goods. To make the purity of your faith shine ever more brightly, we earnestly ask and encourage your nobility, commanding you to resist vigorously the same and other rebels of the Church, fortified with promptness and strength of spirit, remaining steadfast as usual in the devotion to the Church, which intends to elevate you among its other sons with special favor and grace. Given at Lyon, on the 2nd day before the Kalends of May, in the 5th year. 

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobilibus viris praefecto Urbis, Petro Bonifatii, Amatori filio quondam Gabrielis de Prefectis dominis de Vico, et aliis praefectanis mandat ne damna ab infidelibus vassallis illata impunita relinquantur, et ut omnia ablata plenae restaurentur. Lugduni, II Kal. Maii, anno V.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected bishop of Castrum. Although it is necessary to show mercy to anyone in need, so that those who are merciful to their neighbors may receive mercy in return from the Just, there should be a greater care and more substantial aid towards our brothers and fellow bishops, especially those who have fallen into poverty and exile without any fault of their own. Therefore, since our venerable brother, the bishop of Plovace, has been, as he asserts, miserably ejected from his own seat and stripped of all his goods by the officials and supporters of Henry, son of the late emperor Frederick, we, bearing the appropriate compassion towards him and desiring to assist him with suitable remedy so that, God forbid, he should not be compelled to beg, which would be a disgrace to the pontifical office, command you to provide for him each year with a hundred Genoese pounds, to be proportionally divided among individuals and ecclesiastical places in Sardinia, from archbishops, bishops, churches, and monasteries as you see fit, until he can return and safely reside at the Plovacian church. This should be done by our authority, notwithstanding the constitution regarding two days' journey, or if any persons of those churches and monasteries have been granted by the apostolic see that they cannot be compelled to give or provide, or be interdicted, suspended, or excommunicated by apostolic letters unless explicit mention of such indulgence is made, or any other obstacle which could impede or delay this grace; contradictors, etc. Given at Lyon, October 21, year 6.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa electo Castrensi mandat, ut episcopo Plovacensi, qui ab officialibus Henrici natus quondam imperatoris eiectus sit et bonis suis spoliatus, per ecclesias Sardiniae in centum libris Ianuensibus annue subveniat, donec ad sedem suam redire possit. Dat. Lugduni, XII Kal. Novembris, anno VI.

**Translation to English:**

To the podestà and people of Mevania, in the diocese of Spoleto. Since, as has been intimated to us on your behalf, certain citizens of Foligno, who, with a feigned devotion to the Roman Church, presume to adhere to its enemy, have lent money to some men of your land and have greatly offended you and other faithful of the aforementioned Church, and do not cease to offend: we, who must raise the faithful of this Church with apostolic favor and oppress the unfaithful with the severity of punishment, so that the former may gain advantage from their loyalty and the latter suffer loss from their infidelity, grant to all the men of your land and their successors, that they are not bound to repay such creditors the money, unless full satisfaction for all damages and offenses inflicted upon you by them has been rendered by the same, by the authority of these presents. Let no one therefore etc. of our concession etc. Given at Lyon, on the 3rd Ides of December, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa potestati et populo de Mevania significat se concedere, ut homines terre eorum creditoribus pecuniam solvere non teneantur, nisi plenarie eis satisfiat de dampnis et offensis illatis. 1232, Dec. 11, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Cardinal Priest of the Title of Santa Maria in Trastevere, our vicar in Rome. Although we are bound to attend to the provision of all who seek the grace of our provision, we ought to bestow special care on those who, born of noble lineage, are compelled to live in miserable exile for the defense of ecclesiastical liberty. Therefore, since our beloved son Matthew, a cleric, nephew of the late Theodinus of Amiternum, claims to have been deprived of all his goods and expelled from his own home and country by the enemies of the Church from the time of the first discord between the Church and the Empire, we, bearing a compassionate heart towards him on this matter and considering him worthy of the special grace and favor of the Apostolic See, command that you provide him with a prebend if any is currently vacant or will become vacant in the Church of Rieti, ensuring that he is then received there as a canon and brother. This is notwithstanding that the same cleric may already hold other benefices, or if we have written to others concerning the same church, which we do not wish, etc., up to: be generated, or any other indulgence granted to the same church by the Apostolic See, which might impede or delay such grace, and of which, etc., up to: mention. — Those who contradict, etc. Given at Lyon, 12th November, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa S. tit. Sancte Marie Transtiberim presbytero cardinali, vicario suo in Urbe mandat, ut Matheo clerico, nepoti quondam Theodini de Amiterno, de prebenda in ecclesia Reatina vacantem vel vacaturam provideat, non obstantibus aliis beneficiis a clerico detentis, contradictores coercendo. Datum Lugduni, II Id. Novembris, anno VI (1232).

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz, legate of the Apostolic See. Since we have deemed it necessary to entrust you with the full office of legation in the Kingdom of Germany, for the good of its state and for promoting the affairs of the Church and the Empire, upon the counsel of our brothers: we grant you, by the authority of these presents, the faculty to confer ecclesiastical benefices throughout the entire land of your legation, just as it would be permitted to a cardinal of the Roman Church if he were performing the office of legation there — by the established constitution. Given at Lyon, 24th February, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino, apostolicae sedis legato, facultatem concedit conferendi beneficia ecclesiastica per totam legationis suae terram, sicut cardinali Romanae ecclesiae liceret. Datum Lugduni, VI Kalendas Martii, anno sexto.

Translation to English:

To the Bishop of Constance. Desiring always to support your person in episcopal rights with usual kindness, we grant you full authority by the authority of these presents to freely receive and demand the condemnations or penalties, commonly called bannalia, reasonably imposed by the rectors and clerics of the churches of your diocese on your parishioners due to their offenses or excesses, as are known to have been decreed by you and your predecessor, the late Bishop Henry of Constance. Therefore, let no one etc. of our concession etc. Given at Lyon, on the Ides of March, in the sixth year of our pontificate. A conservator was given to him for this, the abbot of Faucibus of the Augsburg diocese.

Regesto in Latin:

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Constantiensi concedit facultatem plenam percipiendi et exigendi bannalia a rectoribus et clericis ecclesiarum diocesis suae impositas. 1249, Mar. 15. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the provost of the church of Rivi, of the Premonstratensian order, in the diocese of Constance. It was reported to us on behalf of our beloved sons, the abbot and convent of the monastery of Wetringhen, that the noble lords of Siteretelingen, in the diocese of Lausanne, had summoned them concerning certain possessions before Conrad, son of the late Emperor, after the sentence of deposition was pronounced against the late Emperor Frederick. We command you, if this is so and these noblemen proceed with the summons, to declare, by our authority, that they have completely fallen from any right they might have had in those possessions; contradictors, etc. Given at Lyon, the 5th day before the Kalends of February, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

**Innocentius IV papa** proposito ecclesiae de Rivi Premonstratensis ordinis Constantiensis diocesis mandat, ut nobiles de Siteretelingen, si citationem prosecutionem contra abbatem et conventum de Wetringhen fecerint post depositionem Friderici imperatoris, ab omni iure in possessionibus cecidisse denuntiet. **1249, Jan. 28, Lugduni.**

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of Saint Urban, of the Cistercian order, in the diocese of Constance. The noble men H. Senior and H. Junior, counts of Kiburch, have submitted a petition to us, revealing that Ulric of Saint Nicholas, a priest and canon of the church of Zurich in the diocese of Constance, has openly adhered to the supporters of the former Emperor Frederick, providing them counsel, aid, and favor against the church. Through our letters, we have instructed the abbot of Altaripa in the diocese of Lausanne to, if this is true, strip him of his canonry and prebend with our authority and to confer said prebend, by our authority, to Ralph, the cleric and notary of the said junior count, suppressing any opposition. However, since the same Ulric, as it is fully known to the same Ralph, has stayed in the city of Zurich, which is under ecclesiastical interdict and whose inhabitants favor the said F., with the permission of our venerable brother, the bishop of Constance, Ralph cannot derive any benefit from such favor: the said counts have humbly asked us to assist Ralph, who has worked faithfully and usefully for the affairs of the church alongside them, not fearing loss of goods or danger to his person, with our usual benevolence in this matter. Inclined by the prayers of these counts, we command you to assign and confer, by our authority, the prebend that Ulric holds in the church of Zurich, upon his resignation or death, and ensure he is received by the provost and chapter of the same church as a canon and brother for said prebend—with no regard to any oath or any firm agreement regarding a fixed number of canons, or if we have directed our writings for others, or that he is otherwise beneficed; suppressing any opposition. Given at Lyon, on the Ides of April, in the fifth year of our pontificate. To the same. The beloved sons, as above: understanding that Burcard, canon of Zurich, rector of the church of Mura in the diocese of Constance, is a supporter of Frederick, etc., to confer to Henry of Clinginberch, advisor of the same counts, etc., until the end.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa abbati Sancti Urbani Cisterciensis ordinis Constantiensis diocesis mandat ut Ulricum de Sancto Nicolao, presbyterum et canonicum Turicensem, privet canonicatu et prebenda ob fautorem Friderici quondam imperatoris, et prebendam Radulfo clerico conferat. Similiter, Burcardum canonicum Turicensem in ecclesia de Mura rectoratum privare et Henrico de Clinginberch, comitum consiliario, conferre iubet. Datum Lugduni, Idibus Aprilis, anno V pontificatus.

**Translation to English:**

To Otto, cleric of Truhendingen, of the diocese of Eichstätt. Considering the merit of your goodness and the sincere devotion of your beloved brothers, noble men Frederick and Louis, lords of Truhendingen, we willingly extend apostolic favor to you and honor your person with the special privilege of grace. Therefore, inclined by your and your brothers' supplications, we grant you the authority of the apostolic see, allowing you to be lawfully elected to the pontifical dignity, notwithstanding the defect you are said to suffer in orders and age. However, we desire that if it should happen that you are elected while such a defect persists, confirmation of this election is to be sought from the Apostolic See. Therefore, let no one etc. of our concession etc. Given at Lyon, 30th January, in the sixth year. To Albert, canon of Würzburg. Considering the merit of your goodness and the beloved sons, noble men Frederick and Louis, etc., as above until the end.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Ottoni clerico de Truhendingin Eistetensis diocesis, non obstante defectu ordinum et aetatis, auctoritate apostolica indulget ut ad pontificalem dignitatem eligi possit, electionis confirmatione ab apostolica sede petenda. Datum Lugduni, III Kal. Februarii, anno VIe (1250).

**Translation:**

...to the elected bishop of Liège. Due to the steadfastness of your devotion, which is affirmed by the purity of your faith, we have deemed it fitting that you be considered as special among the devoted to the Church, and it is proper that we pursue your petitions with favorable kindness, granting them as liberally as we can with God. From your indication, we have learned—and indeed, the clear works of your faith prove—that you, diligently and powerfully laboring for the affairs of the Universal Church as a noble member thereof, bear many burdens of expenses. And because the revenues of your bishopric scarcely suffice to carry out these affairs, you have requested that we aid you with some special grace for remedy. Therefore, that these affairs which are incumbent may reach the completion desired, we, willing to provide for both your person and these affairs, by apostolic authority grant you the indulgence that for two years you may retain the revenues of all ecclesiastical benefices, even those having the care of souls, which may become vacant within five years in your city or diocese, for your needs— notwithstanding any contrary provision by which this grace might be impeded, provided that enough is reserved from these revenues so that during the interim, suitable persons may serve in the churches where these benefices are held. Let no one, etc., of our concession, etc. Given at Lyon, 22nd December, in the sixth year.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa electo Leodiensi concedit, ut pro suis necessitatibus proventus omnium beneficiorum ecclesiasticorum vacaturorum infra quinquennium in civitate vel diocesi sua per biennium retinere possit. 1232, Dec. 22. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Ofreducius and Andreas, brothers, and Hugolinus, their cousin, lords of Alviano. A petition presented to us on your behalf stated that, because of your faith and unwavering devotion to the Roman Church, which you maintain with steadfast firmness, you have suffered severe damages and losses to your properties and those of your vassals from Henry of Pareimano, and through him from the envoys of Frederick, the late emperor, whom it still shames not to adhere to. You humbly requested the providence of the Apostolic See to provide some relief for you concerning these matters. Therefore, so that the Church's faithful, by merit of their steadfastness, may obtain the remedy of due relief, and its persecutors, having hated it freely and maliciously struck its sons, may at least feel regret through the sting of punishment, inclined by your supplications, we have decided, by the authority of these presents, to grant you the castle of Jupiter with its appurtenances in the diocese of Amelia, as a due and complete recompense for your damages suffered because of the same Henry or through him from others on account of the Church, to you who persist in the devotion to the Apostolic See, decreeing that the same Henry, notwithstanding any opposing decree or any other measure, must make reparation for these damages to you. Let no one infringe etc. our concession and decree etc. Given at Lyon, on the second day before the Nones of December, in the sixth year. Conservators for these matters are also appointed: the bishop and the abbot of the monastery of Saint Peter in Perugia.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Ofreducio et Andree fratribus ac Hugolino consobrino eorum dominis de Alviano castrum Iovis cum pertinentiis Ameliensis diocesis pro recompensatione dampnorum ab Henrico de Pareimano propter ecclesiam passo concedit. 1232. Dec. 4. Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To the podestà, council, and people of Parma. When we diligently consider and carefully reflect on the plots and types of traps Frederick, the former emperor and persecutor of the Church, sets for you, by what designs or means, deceits, and cunning he tries to draw the faithful of the Church to himself, so that he may bite them with a most bitter bite and impiously deliver them to death: it is expedient, indeed necessary due to the present wickedness of the time, that the rash presumption of those who, thirsting for your blood, turn for assistance to him either privately or publicly, be chastised with a deserved punishment and struck with a fitting penalty. Since, therefore, you have guided us to be requested in regard to the guidance of your state and that of all other devotees of the Church, we have intended to apply ourselves with all our ability and ingenuity, as we desire nothing more at present than that successful outcomes arise and happy events follow from the common undertaking that is being conducted, and that this may in no way come to pass, and our labor be useless if it happens that you labor to the contrary: we desire and command by apostolic writings, instructing you to set and swear henceforth to be observed by you unbreakably, that all those who are found to have acted or even to have planned in favor of the aforementioned Frederick and to the detriment of your city or the loss of the Lombard League, from the time you returned to the devotion of the Church, shall have all their goods confiscated and applied to your common use, they shall be permanently banned from your city and all other cities of the aforesaid League, and their sons and grandsons shall not be appointed to any offices or positions of power in your city or any city of the same League. Indeed, those who presume to appoint such individuals or even podestà in their city, shall know that they will be bound by the sentence of excommunication, and their lands subjected to ecclesiastical interdict. Given at Lyon, the 10th Kalends of May, in the fifth year of our pontificate. In the same manner to the podestà, council, and commune of Piacenza until: loss of the Lombardy League, from the time when we issued the sentence of deposition against him. In the same manner to the podestà, council, and commune of Novara. In the same manner to the podestà, council, and commune of Bologna. In the same manner to the podestà, council, and commune of Mantua. In the same manner to the podestà, council, and commune of Milan. In the same manner to the podestà, council, and commune of Brescia.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa potestati, consilio et populo Parmensibus mandat ut omnes qui in favorem Friderici quondam imperatoris et in detrimentum civitatis eorum vel societatis Lombardie tractaverunt, bona eorum publicentur et perpetuo bannituri sint, filii eorum ad officia non admittantur, et officiales qui tales assumant excommunicationi innodentur. 1240, Apr. 22, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of Saint Gall. Whereas we have previously excommunicated the bishop of Chur, or rather declared him bound by the chain of excommunication, because he favored the late Emperor Frederick and his excommunicated supporters and allies, assigning him a specific deadline to appear before us and comply with the apostolic commands, threatening him with the penalty of deposition unless he effectively fulfilled the aforementioned orders: although the same bishop later, through his messenger whom he sent to the apostolic see, swore before our venerable brother, the bishop of Albano, whom we appointed as an auditor for the matter, to obey our commands, and we sent word to the bishop of Chur both through the aforementioned messenger and special letters to ensure in the hands of our venerable brother, the bishop of Constance, that he would not provide any assistance to the said Frederick and would humbly obey our commands, the said bishop of Chur, however, before the same bishop of Constance, only offered an oath as security; for which reason we could rightfully pronounce a sentence of deposition against the same bishop of Chur. But wishing still to act mercifully with him, on the last Holy Thursday, in the presence of a public and general assembly of the faithful, we deemed it proper to enjoin him that by the coming feast of Pentecost he should offer and assign to the said bishop of Constance all the castles of the Church of Chur, which the same bishop of Constance would wish to hold, in the name of the Church of Chur, and that he should personally appear before us by that festival, ready to comply with our commands and good pleasure. Otherwise, without any further delay, we will, with the Lord's help, proceed to his deposition, whether he be present or absent, according to the custom of the apostolic see. We strictly command the canons of the said Church of Chur to send some of their number to appear before us by the said feast, who, if the bishop does not fulfill our command, shall have full authority regarding the provision of the aforesaid Church of Chur and also to execute our good pleasure. Therefore, we command that you make known all and each of the aforementioned matters to the same bishop in a place where he can be accessed without danger, and also publish them in all places where it seems expedient. Given at Lyons, 14th of the Kalends of May, in the fifth year. In the same manner to the bishop of Constance, with words suitably altered. In the same manner to archbishops and bishops and abbots, priors, deans, provosts, archdeacons, archpriests, and other prelates of churches established throughout Germany, with words suitably altered.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa abbati Sancti Galli mandat, ut episcopo Curensi excommunicationis causam notificet et ei praecipiat castra Curiensem ecclesiae assignare, necnon personaliter coram papa compareat. Si autem mandata non impleverit, depositionem minatur. 1248, Apr. 18, Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To R., Cardinal Deacon of Santa Maria in Cosmedin, legate of the apostolic see. So that the business of the universal church may progress all the more strongly through your mediation, as greater power has been granted to you by the apostolic see, we have deemed it appropriate to grant to your prudence by the authority of these presents, that you may be able to absolve all and each from the kingdom of Sicily who wish to return to the bosom of the church, whatever excommunication binds them and whatever sentence of law or judge entangles them, either by yourself or through another according to the customary form of the church, and to lift the interdict of cities and other places of the same kingdom that humbly return to the mandate of the church, for whatever cause and by whosever authority the said cities and places have been subjected to interdict. For we will hold ratified and firm whatever you shall decide to do concerning these matters. Given at Lyon, 18th January, in the sixth year. To the same. So that the business etc. as above up to: and each from the province of Tuscany? to the bosom of the church etc. to the end.

Regesto in Latin:

Innocentius IV papa R. Sancte Marie in Cosmidin diacono cardinali, apostolicae sedis legato, concedit potestatem absolvendis omnibus et singulis de regno Siciliae et relaxandi interdictiones civitatum et locorum redeuntium ad ecclesiae mandatum. 1249, Ian. 18. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the dean of the church of St. George in Cologne. To grant a special favor to our beloved son Giselbert, our subdeacon and canon of the church of St. Mary in Utrecht, the requests of our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious king of the Romans, and the merits of the said canon, for which laudable testimony is given to him, compel us. We command you, therefore, to provide, or to have provided, to the said canon a prebend and dignity in any of the churches of the city or diocese of Utrecht which he wishes to accept, by our authority, as soon as an opportunity presents itself— notwithstanding that he already holds other benefices, or if we or the legates of the Apostolic See have directed our writings for others in the same church wherein you intend to provide for him, which we do not wish to be affected, or the indulgence granted to some in those parts by the Apostolic See, that they cannot be compelled to provision for anyone through apostolic letters; oppose, etc. Given at Lyon, the Nones of January, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa decano ecclesiae Sancti Georgii Coloniensis mandat, ut Giselberto subdiacono et canonico ecclesiae Sanctae Mariae Traiectensis de prebenda et dignitate in ecclesiis civitatis vel dioecesis Traiectensis provideatur, non obstante quod alias beneficiatus existit aut indulgentiis quibusdam obstantibus. 1249, Non. Ian., Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To the Bishop of Regensburg. Our beloved sons, the abbot and convent of the monastery of St. James of the Scots in Regensburg, of the Order of St. Benedict, which pertains directly to the Roman Church, have presented a petition to us. They have shown that, since the convent of the monastery of St. Mary of the Scots in Vienna lacks an abbot, and considering that it pertains directly to the said monastery of St. James, they are unable to elect one at this time. This is because, in the town of Vienna, divine services have been rashly celebrated under an interdict imposed by apostolic authority. To prevent the monastery of St. Mary from suffering spiritual and temporal detriment due to prolonged vacancy, they have canonically and unanimously appointed our beloved son Kylian, a monk from Ebersberg, a man of eminent knowledge and circumspection in spiritual and temporal matters, to the vacant monastery, as pertains to them. They have humbly petitioned us that, since the Bishop of Passau, the diocesan of the place, is bound by the tie of excommunication by the aforementioned authority, we might grant the blessing to the elected one as he approaches the Apostolic See. Therefore, wishing to honor your person in this matter, since you steadfastly persevere in devotion to the Apostolic See, we command you to bestow the blessing upon the elected individual, and ensure that his subjects exhibit due and devout obedience and reverence to him; as for the contradictors, etc. We do not wish, however, that any prejudice be generated against the Church of Passau in the future because of this. Given at Lyon, on the Kalends of December, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Ratisponensi mandat, ut Kyliano monacho Eberspergensi, electo ab abbate et conventu monasterii sancti Iacobi Scotorum Ratisponensium monasterii sancte Marie Scotorum in Vienna, benedictionem conferat et obedientiam a subditis exhiberi curet, non obstante quod episcopus Pataviensis excommunicationis vinculo teneatur. 1232, Dec. 1. Lugduni.

### Translation to English

To the Bishop of Fano. We have received from our beloved son Boniface, a canon of Rimini and a cleric of R., Cardinal Deacon of the Holy Roman Church of St. Mary in Cosmedin and legate of the Apostolic See, an announcement that when the same church was vacant of its pastor and provost, the chapter of the church unanimously elected him as provost through a canonical election. However, to prevent this election from suffering any challenge due to the fact that the said chapter was under the sentence of excommunication at the time of the election—because the city of Rimini adhered to the late Emperor F. at that time—Boniface humbly requested that provision be made by us. Considering his devotion, as well as that of the said chapter and the community of Rimini, the noble man R. Malatesta of Verucchio, knight, and several others who petitioned us on behalf of Boniface through their letters, and wishing to grant him special grace, we grant you the authority through these present letters to confirm this election by apostolic authority and also to supply if by chance there was any defect due to the aforementioned cause. Those who oppose, etc. Given as above.

### Regesto in Latin

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Fanensi mandat ut electionem Bonifatii canonici Ariminensis in prepositum ecclesiae auctoritate apostolica confirmet, non obstante sententia excommunicationis qua capitulum tenebatur tempore electionis. Datum. 1235, ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Milan. We do not undeservedly bestow the support of apostolic favor on matters that contribute to the safeguarding of ecclesiastical freedom, whose progress you are known to earnestly cherish, as you diligently guard against those things that cause serious harm to it. It has indeed been reported to our ears on your behalf that, since it often happens that prelates and other ecclesiastical and religious persons, due to the laypeople of the city and diocese of Milan, deny the due tithes and first fruits customarily owed to the churches, which they hold back not without sacrilegious audacity and offense to the divine name, sometimes bring a complaint under your examination, sometimes even before your vicars. The noble man, the podestà, his assessors, and the consuls of the same city, rashly attempt to claim for themselves the judgment of these tithes and first fruits, preventing proceedings freely in the ecclesiastical court against the laypeople detaining them, as is known to pertain solely to it, publicly prohibiting this. Moreover, they presume to outlaw anyone who would act against such a prohibition. Because of this, ecclesiastical rights are enormously damaged there, and the authority of its ordinary jurisdiction is significantly weakened to the detriment of the Church of Milan. We, therefore, moved by your prayers, grant you, by the authority of these presents, the free power, both through yourself and through your vicars, to proceed as needed, equipped with both ordinary and apostolic authority, against the authors of such pernicious audacity, removing the impediment of appeal, and to restrain the contradictors or rebels, if there are any, with the appropriate severity, with the appeal removed. Given at Lyon, 17th December, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Mediolanensi mandat ut contra laicos, qui decimas et primitias ecclesiis negant, auctoritate ordinaria et apostolica procedat et contradictores compescat. 1232, Dec. 17, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Regensburg. As we have heard from your report, some priests and clerics of your city and diocese have dared to celebrate, indeed, as far as they could, even profane the divine offices in certain churches of the same city and diocese, despite the ecclesiastical interdict imposed by our beloved son, the bishop-elect of Ferrara, who was then legate of the apostolic see in those regions, due to a general discord. They did this by siding with the Duke of Bavaria and Conrad, the son of the former emperor Frederick, persecutors of the Church, and have not yet corrected themselves with appropriate satisfaction for this. To ensure that such presumption does not remain unpunished and serve as an example to others, we strictly command you, by apostolic letters and in virtue of obedience, to deprive, by our authority, the priests and clerics of the aforementioned city and diocese, whom you find to have exceeded in this manner, of their ecclesiastical benefits. You shall also ensure that the altars of these churches are stripped bare in detestation of such a crime and remain so as long as you see fit. Those who resist, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 5th of February, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Ratisponensi mandat, ut presbyteros et clericos civitatis et diocesis Ratisponensis, qui divina profanaverint dum ecclesiastico interdicto subiiciuntur, beneficiis ecclesiasticis privet et altaria ecclesiarum nudentur. 1232, Feb. 5. Datum Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected Bishop of Vercelli. Concerned about the indemnity of the Church of Vercelli, you humbly petitioned us that, since once our beloved son G. de Montelongo, subdeacon and our notary, acting as a legate of the Apostolic See, wished to recall the commune and people of the city of Vercelli to the bosom of the mother church and its devotion. However, he sold and granted them, adhering damnably at that time to the Roman Emperor F., temporal jurisdiction over certain towns, castles, villages, places, and people which the bishops and the Church of Vercelli have possessed since time immemorial, for a certain sum of money by the authority of his legation, at their insistence. You requested us to provide paternal diligence on this matter. Therefore, desiring to safeguard your indemnity and prevent the enormous injury to the said church with apostolic authority, we completely revoke, annul, and declare null whatever was done by the said legate in terms of sale, donation, or any other alienation or contract regarding the said jurisdiction and its appurtenances, by the counsel of our brothers. We decree that all documents drawn up concerning this are entirely void, notwithstanding that the consent of the chapter of that church, with you then being the provost, is said to have been given to such alienation. Let no one, etc., of our revocation, annulment, nullification, and constitution, etc. Given as above. A conservator was given to them on this matter, the Bishop of Novara.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX episcopo electo Vercellensi nuntiat quicquid a legato G. de Montelongo per venditionem vel alienationem de iurisdictione Vercellensi factum erat revocari et irritum nuntiari. Datum Laterani.

**Translation to English:**

To the elect of Constance. Due to the merits of your devotion, etc., as we hear you. Therefore, granting a kind assent to your supplications, we, by the authority of these presents, grant you the right to confer the provostship of the church of Constance, as soon as it becomes vacant, to any devoted member of the church whom you deem suitable — notwithstanding any letters obtained from the Apostolic See concerning similar provisions, provided they do not make special mention of this provostship, or any others by which it is generally ordered for dignities, prebends, or other ecclesiastical benefices to be provided to someone, or that the person to whom you confer it already holds other benefices, or that we have otherwise written for the same, or any indulgence of the same see, by which this might be impeded or deferred and for which special mention ought to be made in these presents —; objectors. Given at Lyon, on the 3rd day before the Nones of February, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa electo Constantiensi concedit, ut, vacante prepositura ecclesiae Constantiensis, eam alicui devoto conferre possit, non obstantibus litteris apostolicis vel aliis impedimentis. 1249, Feb. 3, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of Pruvening of the order of Saint Benedict in the diocese of Regensburg. Our beloved sons, the abbot and convent of Saint Emmeram of Regensburg of the order of Saint Benedict, have shown us by complaint that although the advocates of this monastery, having residences in different dioceses, are obliged to defend them and their goods, and to receive certain revenues from the goods of the same monastery, as has been established from ancient times, nevertheless, these advocates, not prudently considering that an advocate of the church ought to be understood as a defender, have turned from defenders into persecutors. Disregarding their duties, they extend their unlawful hands to the goods of the aforementioned monastery, tyrannically invading and seizing the revenues and incomes of the above-named monastery to its irreparable detriment. Therefore, wishing to safeguard the welfare of the aforementioned monastery with fatherly care, we command you, if this is the case, to compel those advocates, after giving warning, by means of justice, removing any appeal, through sentences of excommunication on their persons and interdict on their lands, that they remain content with their rights and restore what has been taken to the monastery, and that they desist completely from undue harassment, allowing them to freely manage, as pertains to them, the goods of the aforementioned monastery. Given at Lyon, on the Kalends of February, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati de Pruvening ordinis S. Benedicti Ratisponensis diocesis mandat, ut advocatos monasterii S. Emeramni compellat, ne bona monasterii invadant et ablata restituant, cessantes a molestatione indebita. 1232, Febr. 1, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz and the Elect of Speyer. The work of God and the Church, which our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, pursues with mighty strength, ought thus to be promoted through the providence of the Apostolic See, so that he may achieve an easy and happy outcome with divine aid. Therefore, we have deemed it worthy to commit to your discretion, by the authority of these presents, to faithfully collect, either by yourselves or by others suitable for this task, the redemptions of vows made by those signed with the cross against the late Emperor Frederick and his supporters, as well as any income arising from whatever source, and also legacies or bequests or in any other way granted for this purpose. You shall assign them intact to the aforesaid king as soon as possible, absolving from the vow of the cross those who redeem their vows through you or those you appoint for this purpose, granting them the pardon of sins which was bestowed upon those journeying to aid the Holy Land or providing assistance therein, as decreed in the general council — notwithstanding any privileges obtained or to be obtained from the Apostolic See, which could hinder or delay such a collection and for which a special or express mention needs to be made in our letters. Let any contradictors etc. If not both etc. Given at Lyon, January 2, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa archiepiscopo Maguntino et electo Spirensi mandat, ut redemptiones votorum crucesignatorum contra F. quondam imperatorem et eius fautores colligant et regi Romanorum assignent, cum absolutione votorum et peccatorum venia. Datum Lugduni, IIII Nonas Ianuarii, anno sexto.

**Translation to English:**

To Corrado de Savignano, canon of Mantua. Since, as contained in the petition presented to us by our beloved son, the archpriest of Prato in the diocese of Reggio, our beloved son G. de Montelongo, elected as the bishop of Tripoli and apostolic legate, deprived William, known as Apulus, then canon of Reggio, of his canonry and prebend in the church of Reggio by our authority, because he adhered in a damnable manner to the late Emperor Frederick and his supporters against us and the apostolic see, and canonically conferred them upon the archpriest, who is devoted to us and the Roman Church: we, inclined by your devoted supplications, supplementing any deficiency that might exist in the aforementioned collation due to the fact that proceedings were carried out in G.'s absence with legitimate caution being previously observed, and confirming by apostolic authority what was providently done by the said legate, command that you do not allow the said archpriest to be unjustly disturbed by anyone regarding the mentioned canonry and prebend; to deal with such molesters, etc. Given at Lyon, 19 February, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Corrado de Savignano canonico Mantuano mandat ne archipresbyter de Prato super canonicatu et prebenda in ecclesia Regina, a G. de Montelongo ei collatis, ab aliquibus molestetur, collationem auctoritate apostolica confirmans. 1249, Feb. 19, Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To the bishop of Tournai. Since, as your petition presented to us stated, according to canonical sanctions in your city and diocese, both your predecessors and you have deemed it necessary to appoint certain public witnesses, who are called synodals, in each parish, the aldermen of the town of Ghent in your diocese, appointed to this office, although they are obliged to report all crimes to you or to someone you choose as suitable for this purpose, nevertheless, due to a certain wrongful custom, which should rather be called corruption, they refuse to testify against those noted for fornication, as if fornication should not be considered a criminal sin. Therefore, since this disease must be more diligently addressed the more frequently it is committed by many, we command, if this is the case, that you compel the aforementioned aldermen to report the truth concerning fornication as well as other crimes, as they are obliged — the aforementioned custom notwithstanding — with a prior warning, through ecclesiastical censure, removing any appeal. Given at Lyon, 20th February, in the sixth year of (our pontificate).

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Tornacensi mandat ut scabinos villae Gandensis compellat veritatem de fornicatione et aliis criminibus referre, consuetudine prave non obstante, censura ecclesiastica. 1232, Febr. 20, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the consuls and the community of Strasbourg. Since those who present themselves to the Apostolic See with a devotion pleasing to us deserve to obtain the special favor of this See, we, mindful of your services which you have generously rendered and continue to render to the Roman Church, desire to exalt your city with multiple honors as much as we can with God, and to favorably grant your requests and to provide you a kind hearing in those things which you worthily request. Therefore, as you have taken care to explain to us, our venerable brother, the bishop, the dean, and the chapter of Strasbourg, following the example of the late bishop H. of Strasbourg and his predecessors, with the unanimous consent and will of the ministers, citizens, and their other faithful, decided to renew and firmly establish that the advocacy of your city with its rights and appurtenances may never be conferred upon any of the emperors, kings, dukes, or other illustrious persons or their descendants, nor be transferred by any title, means, or form by them or their successors, as we have seen clearly expressed in the letters crafted by the said bishop and chapter. Inclined by your supplications, we confirm by Apostolic authority what has been prudently done by the same bishop and chapter, and strengthen it with the protection of this document, declaring null and void any contrary attempts by them or their successors. The tenor of their letters, inserted here word for word, is as follows: Henry, by divine mercy bishop of Strasbourg, Arnold the provost, Berthold the dean, Frederick the cantor, Conrad the scholar, Conrad the chamberlain, and the whole chapter of the greater church make known to all the faithful of Christ who will inspect this present document that, just as it was once firmly promised by our chapter through the mediation of the venerable lord Henry of Veringen, of blessed memory, bishop of Strasbourg, under a corporal oath, so we, considering the benefit of our church, firmly and faithfully promise and renew the said promise for ourselves and our successors, namely, that we shall never grant the advocacy of Strasbourg with its appurtenances to any illustrious or most illustrious person, emperor, king, duke, or their progeny, nor permit it to be granted by the bishop under any title of infeudation, sale, pledge, exchange, commission, or any form of alienation. And if, God forbid, any of the bishops of Strasbourg should attempt this, we faithfully promise all together with all our strength and by all legal means to oppose this. On the other hand, the ministerials of the church and citizens of Strasbourg have faithfully promised to defend the person, goods, and possessions of Bishop Henry now residing, and also any of his successors who will or wishes to undergo the abovementioned oath on the article of advocacy, as well as all the canons of Strasbourg, both present and future, and all the clergy of the city who will ever exist, against any man. The consuls of the city, whenever they are changed and renewed, shall swear in good faith to defend and promote all those whom they perceive or believe to be beneficial for the preservation and stability of these agreements over time, or through whose counsel or assistance they can ensure the aforementioned agreements remain firm and steadfast, and likewise to defend and conserve the clergy in their honor and due freedom. Therefore, lest this action be recalled by the cavillation of posterity or the passage of time, this present document has been composed and solemnly confirmed with the seals of the venerable lord Bishop Henry, the chapter of the Greater Church, and the city of Strasbourg as testimony. These acts were done at Strasbourg in the bishop's palace, in the year of the Incarnate Word 1247, on the feast of the apostles Philip and James, in the presence of these witnesses: Henry of Ohsenstein, Berthold of Sultze, Reinald of Tengent, Conrad, Eberhard, and Otto, brothers of Entringen, Berthold of Thiesberc, Marcuald called Sunnelcap, canons of the greater church, Nicholas cantor of St. Thomas, lord Louis of Linthenberc, lord Alexander of Dike, brother of the lord bishop, Walter the marshal, William the vice-dominus, Albert Bagarius the White, Warner Cagone, Warner Bagarius, Conrad of Virvecorns and his sons Reinbold and Reinbold, Erbo the son of the judge, John of Kiungesoven, Burchard the Dispenser, John Vitulus, Rudolf of Vegersehim, Hugh Riplino, Frederick of Hagenowe, Siglin Bildell, Gozzo, Erbo and Reimbold sons of Nicholas, Frederick among the merchants, Wirico, Conrad of Zavernia, Rudolf son of Lontzelin, Rainbold Stumbelweck, Henry son of Marsilius, Hecelo of Ethevindesheim,

Translation to English:
To the prelates, chapters, and all clerics established in the city of Trier. Due to the requirements of your devotion, etc., until: we listen. Therefore, since, as was proposed before us on behalf of our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Trier, the city of Trier is surrounded on all sides by both its own and the Church's enemies, we, inclined by the supplications of the same archbishop and yours, grant by the authority of these presents to you who persist in devotion to the Church and to us, that, while these hostilities persist, you may not be summoned outside the aforementioned city or the district of the same archbishop in legal matters by apostolic letters or those of the legates of the Apostolic See, especially since you are ready to offer full justice to those complaining about you before your ordinary. Therefore, let no one, etc. Given at Lyon, 22nd February, in the sixth year. An executor was appointed over this matter for them, the abbot of St. Maximin in Trier.

Regesto in Latin:
Gregorius IX papa prelatis, capitulis et clericis in civitate Treverensi constitutis concedit, ut, inimicitiis circumdantibus, extra civitatem vel districtum archiepiscopi Treverensis in causam trahi non possint. 1232, Feb. 22. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Vicedominus of Regensburg. When previously, we had instructed you and our beloved sons, Brothers Hermann of Bothenkrimen and Henry of Honkespeh of the Order of the Friars Minor, by our letters, to strictly prohibit the Bishop of Passau, by our authority, from attempting to enfeoff, sell, exchange, alienate in any way the goods of the Church of Passau: because, as we have learned from your report, you alone, due to the other brothers being occupied with other matters, cannot execute the apostolic mandate in this regard. We, wishing to safeguard the integrity of the same church with fatherly care, command that you proceed with the execution of our mandate concerning this prohibition, according to the contents of the letters directed to you and those brothers, declaring any alienations attempted by that bishop null and void; those who oppose [etc.]. Given at Lyon, the 15th day before the Kalends of March, in the 6th year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa vicedomino Ratisponensi mandat ut, ob aliorum fratrum occupationem, solus exequatur mandatum apostolicum, ne episcopus Pataviensis bona ecclesiae alienet, et denuntiet alienationes nullas; actum Lugduni, XV Kal. Mart., anno VI.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Treviso. The careful consideration of the Apostolic See, duly weighing the changes of the times, etc., as above in chapter LVI up to: always act. Hence, we, inclined by the prayers of our beloved son, the nobleman John Theupulus, Count of Abson, born to a nobleman, the Doge of Venice, command that you, with the daughter of the same, may lawfully dispense with our authority so that she may contract marriage with the son of the nobleman, the Count of Arbon, notwithstanding that the said Count of Abson is said to have held the same son when he received the chrism of the forehead. Given at Lyon, 27th March, in the sixth year (of our pontificate).

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Tervisino mandat ut, non obstante spirituali affinitate per crismationem nata inter filium comitis Arbonensis et filiā Iohannis Theupuli comitis Absonensis, auctoritate apostolica dispenset ad matrimonium contrahendum. 1249, Mart. 27, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz, legate of the apostolic see. Those who are known to excel among others in honesty of life, knowledge of letters, and maturity of providence, should be raised with greater favor from the apostolic see and honored with the gift of more abundant grace. To them, also, the governance of churches can be entrusted more confidently, as a more secure hope is obtained that they, due to their clear merits, wish and can benefit themselves through a healthy way of life and others through their example. Hence, since our beloved son Conrad, provost of the church of St. Guido of Speyer, deserves to be greatly honored by the same see due to his devotion and probity, we, considering this with foresight and not wishing to leave his probity without suitable provision, command you to appoint him as bishop and pastor to some cathedral church in the kingdom of Germany, which he shall deem acceptable, as soon as the opportunity arises, by our authority, declaring null and void anything attempted otherwise regarding the provision of that church for which you will provide the aforementioned provost. Opponents will not be able to act against this—regardless of any privilege or indulgence of the apostolic see. Given at Lyon, February 4th, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino, apostolicae sedis legato, mandat ut Corradum praepositum ecclesiae sancti Guidonis Spirensis in episcopum alicuius ecclesiae cathedralis regni Almanniae auctoritate sua praeficiat. 1231, Feb. 4, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Prior of Saint Peter at Arenas of Metz. The sincere devotion and affection that the noble men, the burgrave of Nuremberg, and the count of Gruengue bear towards our person and the Roman Church induces us to lend them a gracious ear to their petitions and to liberally assent to them as far as we can in accordance with God's will. Therefore, being inclined by their supplications, we command that you provide or have provided to our beloved son, Renald of Filieres, a cleric, a suitable prebend or other ecclesiastical benefice in any of the churches of the city or diocese of Trier, except the cathedral, as soon as the opportunity arises. This is to be done notwithstanding that there may be a fixed number of canons established by oath or other security in the church where you decide to provide for him, or even if we have written previously regarding others in it, to whom we do not wish, etc., or if the church has been granted an exemption by the Apostolic See that it is not obliged to accept or provide for anyone, or that its canons cannot be suspended, excommunicated, or interdicted, or any other indulgence of the Apostolic See that may prevent or delay such a grace. Opponents, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 4th day before the Kalends of February, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa priori Sancti Petri ad Arenas Metensis mandat, ut Renaldo de Filieres clerico in civitate vel diocesi Treverensi, praeter cathedralem, de beneficio ecclesiastico competenti provideat, non obstantibus statutis canonicorum vel indulgentiis sedis apostolicae. Datum Lugduni, IIII Kal. Februarii, anno sexto.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected Bishop of Paderborn. The sincere devotion you and our venerable brother, the Bishop of Münster, and the noble men, Lord B. of Lippea, ... of Arnsberg and ... of Retberg, bear towards our person and the Roman Church induces us to lend a favorable ear to your petitions as much as we can with God’s will. Therefore, being inclined by your and the aforementioned bishop's and nobles' supplications, we command that you have our beloved son John, rector of the church of Yenhusen, who cannot be adequately sustained by the revenues of said church, as they do not exceed the value of three marks of silver annually, as he asserts, to be received in the church of the Holy Apostles Peter and Andrew of Paderborn as a canon and brother by our authority, and that you provide him with a prebend as soon as the opportunity arises. This is notwithstanding that he is beneficed elsewhere, and if a certain number of canons in the said church of the Holy Apostles is established by oath or any other firm agreement, or if we or legates of the Apostolic See have issued our writings for others there, which we do not wish, etc., up to: be generated, or the said church has been granted by the Apostolic See that it is not bound to receive or provide for anyone, or that its canons cannot be interdicted, suspended, or excommunicated by apostolic letters unless such mention of indulgence is expressly made, or any other by which such grace can be hindered or delayed and which needs to be expressly mentioned in our letters. Opponents, etc. Given at Lyon, January 8th, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa electo Paderbornensi mandat, ut Iohannem rectorem ecclesiae de Yenhusen in ecclesia Sanctorum Apostolorum Petri et Andreae Paderbornensi canonicum recipi faciat et de prebenda provideat. 1249, Ianuarii 8, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Brother John of the Order of Friars Minor. With all our efforts inclined towards the promotion of the business of the Church and the Roman Empire, we watch over it with diligence, and in order that it may proceed laudably with the Lord's guidance, we apply all our diligence, expending our efforts as much as we can for this purpose. Therefore, as it was presented to us on behalf of our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, some princes, loyalists, and officials of the empire have not yet rendered homage and loyalty to him as they are bound to do. By the authority of these presents, we command you to compel the said princes and others, by issuing a prior warning, to render homage and loyalty to the aforementioned king without any difficulty or delay, using ecclesiastical censure with appeal removed. Given at Lyons, 3rd March, in the sixth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Fratri Iohanni de Ordine Fratrum Minorum mandat, ut principes et alios imperii, qui regi Romanorum homagium et fidelitatem nondum praestiterunt, monitione praemissa per censuram ecclesiasticam sine appellatione compellat. 1232, Mart. 3, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the deacon cardinal of Santa Maria in Via Lata, legate of the apostolic see. Since, as our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of Bohemia, and our venerable brother, the Patriarch of Aquileia, have informed us, there has been a negotiation regarding the contracting of marriage between our beloved son, the noble man Ulrich, son of the noble Duke of Carinthia, and the noble woman Agnes, niece of the said patriarch, widow of the late Duke of Austria. Because the said Ulrich is related to Agnes in the third degree of affinity, they decided not to proceed to the consummation of the marriage before recourse was made to the apostolic see. Therefore, on behalf of the king and the patriarch, it was humbly petitioned to us that, given the marriage might greatly contribute to appeasing the grave enmities that, due to sins, have arisen among the relatives and vassals of both parties, and to restoring the bonds of peace between them, we might provide beneficial counsel.
