Considering, therefore, that urgent necessity and evident utility call for a dispensation, by the counsel of our brothers, we command that, after receiving from the said Ulrich and Agnes, as well as from others whom you see fit, a sufficient and suitable guarantee, both oath-bound and otherwise, of their support for the Roman Church and their steadfast devotion and faith in the same church against Frederick, the former emperor, and his supporters, you, by our authority, may dispense with the impediment, if you see it as expedient, so that they may contract marriage, if they wish, notwithstanding this impediment. Given at Lyon, 23rd December, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa legato apostolico, diacono cardinali Sanctae Mariae in Via Lata, mandat ut dispenset cum Ulrico, filio ducis Carinthiae, et Agnete, neptem patriarchae Aquilegensis, in tertio gradu affinitatis coniunctis, ad contrahendum matrimonium. 1232, Dec. 23, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Strasbourg. The Apostolic See, with maternal affection, attends to the services of its devoted followers, and willingly repays them with suitable rewards of favors according to the quality of their merits. Therefore, since our beloved sons, the noble men of Nuremberg and of Grüningen, counts, due to their pure faith and sincere devotion to the Roman Church, deserve to be honored in many ways, we, considering this not unworthily and wishing to do them a special favor, are inclined by their supplications and command you by the authority of these presents, that you ensure that Anna, a nun of the monastery of Walkirch, of the Order of Saint Benedict in the diocese of Constance, niece of the aforementioned counts, about whom we have received favorable testimony, be appointed as abbess of one of the nunneries of the same order in the cities or dioceses of Metz, Strasbourg, Toul, Constance, or Basel, which she chooses to accept, by you or another, with our authority, as soon as the opportunity presents itself, — notwithstanding any indulgence granted by the Apostolic See or its legates to the diocesan bishops or any persons, by which such a favor might be impeded or delayed and of which special or express mention should be made in our letters, —; those who object, etc. Given at Lyons, 27th January, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Argentinensi mandat ut Annam, monialem monasterii de Walkircheg ordinis Sancti Benedicti, neptem comitum de Nueremberch et de Grueningin, in abbatissam alicuius monasteriorum Metensis, Argentinensis, Tullensis, Constantiensis vel Basiliensis promoveat. 1233, Jan. 27. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the parish priest and chapter of the parish church of Saint Stephen in the diocese of Luni. Desiring to provide for the indemnity of your church, which, as you assert, is burdened with the reception of multiple individuals, with paternal solicitude, and inclined by your devout supplications and those of the beloved son, the noble man Barnabas, Marquis of Malaspina, who implores the grace of the Apostolic See on your behalf concerning this matter, we grant you by the authority of these presents that you are not obliged to the provision or reception in the parish of the same church of benefits or pensions obtained or to be obtained through letters of the Apostolic See or its legates, unless they make full and express mention of this indulgence. Therefore, let no one blah blah blah our concession. Given at Lyon, 4th day before the Kalends of April, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa plebano et capitulo plebis sancti Stephani Lunensis diocesis auctoritate indulget, ut ad provisionem vel receptionem in plebanatu beneficiis seu pensionibus non teneantur, nisi expressa huius indulgentiae mentione facta. 1231, Mart. 29, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz and the Bishop of Strasbourg. Your fraternity has informed us, brother bishop, that some time ago, at your request, we gave instructions to our dear son P., Cardinal Deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, who was then a legate of the Apostolic See in those regions, that he should provide a benefice from some episcopate in the German regions to our dear son Henry of Geroldseck, canon of the churches of Basel, Strasbourg, and Speyer, nephew of our dear son, the elected Bishop of Speyer. However, the same legate returned to our presence before this could be accomplished, and thus the said canon has not benefited from our favor. Therefore, wishing to bring to completion what we began regarding him, we command that you appoint the said canon as bishop and pastor in some cathedral church in those regions, except Basel, if there is currently a vacancy or as soon as an opportunity arises where you see fit, with our authority, according to the content of the previous letters, ensuring obedience and due reverence from the subjects of the church where you decide he should be provided for him — notwithstanding any indulgences or other letters obtained or to be obtained by anyone from the Apostolic See or its legates, which might impede or delay the provision for the said canon. Those who oppose, etc. If not both of you, then one among you. Given at Lyon, on the 15th day before the Kalends of January, in the 6th year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino et episcopo Argentinensi mandat ut Henricum de Geroldseke, canonicum ecclesiarum Basiliensis, Argentinensis et Spirensis, in aliquam ecclesiam cathedralem, Basiliensi excepta, in episcopum et pastorem preficiant. Datum Lugduni, XV Kalendas Ianuarii, anno VI.

**Translation to English:**

G. de Montelongo, our subdeacon and notary, apostolic see legate. You know well, as you were present, and we are also not ignorant, how great and significant the services that our beloved son, the elected bishop of Vercelli, has rendered to the Church, not avoiding damage to his possessions nor danger to his person, and how much loss he has therefore suffered. Lest detractors and rivals from those regions insult him, weakening the resolve of the faithful by saying that he acted imprudently, we wish to extend a generous hand to him in such a way that others may not be deterred by his example from the service of the Church, but rather encouraged to it. Therefore, we command that you ensure provision is made annually for the said elected bishop, who must bear great expenses at this time, from some of the churches and monasteries under your legation, both exempt and non-exempt, in a suitable and sufficient amount, as you see fit, for the duration of this discord, granting him conservators of this provision. This is to be done notwithstanding any privileges, indulgences, general or special letters obtained or to be obtained from the apostolic see, or their confirmations, constitutions, or statutes, oaths, or any other means by which these things might be hindered or delayed, and which would require special mention in the present document, nor by the constitution of two days' journey issued in the general council. Opponents, etc. Given at Lyon, 28 December, in the sixth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa G. de Montelongo, subdiacono et notario suo, apostolicae sedis legato mandat ut provideat annuatim electo Vercellensi, qui magna expensarum onera sustinere debet, sumptibus ab ecclesiis et monasteriis sub eius legatione, durante discordia, non obstantibus privilegiis et statutis. Datum Lugduni, V Kalendas Ianuarii, anno sexto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Mainz. Although the times are perilous and the world lies in wickedness, remedies of consolation for the bride of Christ are not lacking amidst the storms of any tempests. The impiety of Herodian persecution does not prevail, as the child Jesus, given to us from heaven as an inheritance for the nations, survives. The cunning of Pharaoh's purpose, striving to crush Israel among the males, does not reach its goal, as the holy offspring of those who see God multiplies. Behold, the fertility of the most holy mother church is ever renewed with fresh seed, from which the divine majesty continuously nourishes a larger number of the elect in the frequency of praise. We have indeed learned that in the field of the Lord, namely the breadth of the kingdom of Germany, a considerable grain taken from the heavenly nursery is being sown, destined to be raised into the height of a large and branching tree by the Lord who gives growth—a pious beginning of regular intent conceived in the mind by the noble man, the Count of Swilemberch, and certain other nobles and ecclesiastical men, aimed as a safeguard of Christian peace and a bulwark of faith. Strengthening approval was sought from the head, namely the supreme seat of Peter, from which whatever is of salvific growth in the members descends, so that the new structure may be solidified in the cornerstone, in which the whole building, constructed, is brought to completion into a holy temple in the Lord. However, since more abundant fruits are produced from the arrangements of good things which are planned with more mature counsel, and a happier outcome of completion is added to arduous matters when they are undertaken more judiciously through deliberation, we command you, with certain tested brothers of the Predicators and Minors in knowledge and religion taken with you, having before your eyes God and the liberty of the Catholic faith alone, to diligently examine the quality and number of persons who have conceived the said intention, as well as the rule of life according to which they desire to regularly serve the Lord, together with those brothers. After you have prudently assessed the undertaking from the persons and the intentions of the persons from the undertaking, if you see that from the institution of this new observance a great increase of faith, salvation for souls, and discipline for morals might result, you should guide and correct it, adding and subtracting as you know to be expedient from the counsel of the aforementioned brothers, sending its outline to the Apostolic See under your and the brothers' seals, so that we may decree upon it what seems expedient according to God. Given at Lyons, on the Nones of October, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa archiepiscopo Maguntino mandat, ut cum fratribus Predicatorum et Minorum qualitatem et numerum personarum, propositum a comite de Swilemberch conceptum ad fidem et pacem Christianam tuendam, examinet et corrigat, et seriem ad sedem apostolicam transmittat. 1248, Oct. 7. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the cardinal deacon of Santa Maria in Via Lata, legate of the Apostolic See. Considering more carefully the imminent persecution of the Church and the tyranny of the persecutor, we are compelled to seek remedies against those who provide cause for such persecution by deed or word, help or action. Therefore, since many from various regions adhere to the late emperor Frederick, forgetful of their salvation, we, unwilling to let this pass unnoticed lest, God forbid, others nearby take it as an example, command that you excommunicate the sons and grandsons of the aforementioned Frederick, naming them explicitly, as well as the marquises, counts, barons, prelates, clerics of any rank or order, and all others who presume to favor Frederick in any way or visit or send to his court or that of his sons or grandsons, whether invited or not. You shall announce and have announced their excommunication publicly in places you deem appropriate, with bells ringing and candles burning on every Sunday and feast day. Also, you shall place cities, castles, towns, and places adhering to Frederick under ecclesiastical interdict by name, depriving them, their judges, notaries, and all aforementioned individuals of all honor, office, dignity, and any ecclesiastical sacraments, except in cases permitted by law, excluding only the baptism of infants and penance of the dying; none are to be compelled to respond to them in court. Furthermore, specifically forbid that any of Frederick's supporters be elected or appointed to power, office, or dignity, under the sentence of excommunication for those who contravene. And because Ezzelino da Romano, as a limb of the devil and a vessel of iniquity, has damnably devoted himself to the service of the aforementioned persecutor against the Church, proceed against Ezzelino and his supporters in the same manner as described above; preach the crusade against all these in the lands of your legation, granting the sign of the cross to those assuming it against these, with the indulgence of their sins and the protections and privileges granted to crusaders crossing to aid the Holy Land. Given at Lyon, 5th Kalends of May, in the fifth year of our pontificate. In the same manner to Gregory of Montelongo, our subdeacon and notary, legate of the Apostolic See. In the same manner to Raynerius, cardinal deacon of Santa Maria in Cosmedin, legate of the Apostolic See.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa cardinali diacono Sanctae Mariae in Via Lata, legato apostolicae sedis, mandat ut excommunicet et interdicto supponat omnes fautores Friderici quondam imperatoris, et Ezelinum de Romano, prædicans crucem adversus eos, signum crucis sumpturis veniam peccatorum et privilegia concedens. Datum Lugduni, V Kal. Maii, anno quinto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Châlons and the Abbot of the Holy Sepulchre of Cambrai. Our beloved sons, the noblemen John of Avesnes and Baldwin, his brother, have informed us that certain of their rivals maliciously accuse them of illegitimacy, seeking thereby to exclude them from properties due to them by hereditary right, by spreading such accusations to many ears, and using certain letters obtained from the Apostolic See regarding this matter. Therefore, they have humbly entreated us to ensure, with paternal solicitude, that such a serious accusation does not remain unexamined, as it could be very perilous for them or at least for their heirs. We command you to diligently investigate the truth regarding the noblemen's legitimacy, notwithstanding the fact that there has already been litigation before us between them and their brothers for some time, as nothing has been conclusively settled therein. You are to determine what is canonical, setting aside any appeal, while reserving the main issue of the properties for the principal lord. Given at Lyons, 25th February, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Cathalaunensi et abbati Sancti Sepulchri Cameracensis mandat, ut super causa natalium nobilium virorum Iohannis de Avesnis et Balduini fratris eius veritatem diligenter inquirant et quod canonicum fuerit statuatis, questione bonorum principali domino reservata. 1232, Feb. 25. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishops of Freising, Passau, Regensburg, and Eichstätt, and to the beloved sons, the elected Bishop of Augsburg and the procurator of the Church of Salzburg.

When our beloved son, the noble Conrad, Count of Wazeburg, a crusader and devoted to the Roman Church, lamented before us that the noble Duke of Bavaria, his wife A., their sons, Rapoto, the Palatine of Bavaria, Berthold, Margrave of Hohenburg, Gebhard of Hirsperch, Otto of Bleiene, Albert of Miesbach, and other followers of theirs from your dioceses, supporters of the late Emperor Frederick, an enemy of God and the Church, have hostilely invaded his castles, towns, and possessions, occupying and retaining them, thus preventing the fulfillment of his vow:

We command you, if these allegations are true, to urgently and effectively admonish and induce the said Duke, his wife, sons, and the other nobles to restore to the said Count his castles, towns, and possessions along with the fruits obtained from those possessions since the time of their occupation. Moreover, they must cease from further harassment and grievances against him and his lands. Should they not heed your admonitions, you are to force them by applying sentences of excommunication against their persons and interdict against their lands, setting aside any appeal. Renew these sentences solemnly on every Sunday and feast day, in the places you see fit, with bells tolling and candles lit, if their stubbornness requires it. Furthermore, strictly forbid the celebration of any divine office or the administration of any ecclesiastical sacrament in those territories except for the penance of the dying and baptism of infants until they make full satisfaction.

This command remains, despite any indulgence granted to the Duke of Bavaria or any of the aforementioned individuals by the Apostolic See, stating that they cannot be excommunicated, their lands put under interdict, or be summoned to judgment outside their territories by apostolic letters without a special mandate making full mention of the indulgence. Otherwise, lest the Count suffers a loss of his rights due to your failure, we have given the friars Henry of Ankesberg and Hermann of Bodenbrunnen of the Order of Friars Minor and the Vicedominus of Regensburg our letters commanding them to execute this apostolic mandate. 

Given at Lyon, on the third day before the Nones of May, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopis Frisingensi, Pataviensi, Ratisponensi, Eistetensi, electo Augustensi et procuratori ecclesiae Salzburgensis mandat ut, si verum sit quod Conradus comes de Wazeburc conquestus est de duce Bawariae aliisque nobilibus possessiones suas invasisse, eos monendo et excommunicationis sententia cogant ad restitutionem. 1231, Mai. 5, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Strasbourg. We sincerely cherish in the Lord the persons of our beloved sons, the noble men of Gruningen and Nuremberg, and we gladly lend a favorable ear to their requests, especially admitting those that are known to particularly concern their honor. Therefore, inclined by their supplications, we command that you provide, or ensure provision is made, for our beloved son Henry de Vinstingen, a canon of Strasbourg and their relative, to a dignity in the church of Saint Arnulf in the diocese of Metz, when it shall happen to be vacant and which the same canon shall choose to accept, by our authority. This is notwithstanding that he already holds another benefice or if we or legates of the Apostolic See have sent letters to that church on behalf of others, for which he should be preferred in attainment of the same dignity, or if we or the legates have written elsewhere for him, or by any indulgence of the same See granted to the diocesan bishop and the chapter of that church or any persons whatsoever, by which such a grace might be impeded or delayed and mentioned in our letters, or if the canons of the same church have been granted by the same See that they are in no way bound to provide for anyone, or that they cannot be interdicted, suspended, or excommunicated by apostolic letters, or by any contrary or statute strengthened by an oath or any other firmness. We decree null and void anything attempted against our mandate concerning this dignity. Given at Lyon, 30th January, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Argentinensi mandat, ut Henrico de Vinstingen, canonico Argentinensi et consanguineo nobilium virorum de Gruningen et de Nuremberc, provideat in aliqua dignitate vacante ecclesiae sancti Arnualis Metensis diocesis. Lugduni, III Kal. Februarii, anno VI (1233, Jan. 30).

**Translation to English:**

To the same [recipient], 

The petition presented to us by your fraternity contained that several prelates of monasteries and churches in your diocese are striving to obtain exemption from the jurisdiction of the Church of Constance by the Apostolic See, to the detriment of you and that church. Therefore, you humbly requested that provision be made for this matter concerning that church by the providence of the Apostolic See. Therefore, desiring that you and that church be preserved unharmed in its rightful jurisdiction, we wish your fraternity to be assured of the benevolence of the Apostolic See, that we have not hitherto exempted anyone subject to you by diocesan law, nor is it our intention to do so. 

Given at Lyon, 16th March, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa [recipienti] significat, quod prelatorum nonnulli monasteriorum et ecclesiarum sue diocesis exemptionem a iurisdictione Constantiensis ecclesie petunt, et affirmat nullos eximendos esse, ut detrimentum huius ecclesie evitetur. Datum Lugduni, XVII Kalendas Aprilis, anno sexto.

**Translation to English:**

Innocent IV, the Pope, informs the prelates and other ecclesiastical persons of the March of Ancona and the Duchy of Spoleto that he assigns Peter, the cardinal, as a legate of the Apostolic See to reform the Kingdom of Sicily and liberate it from the tyranny of Frederick, the late emperor. He has also entrusted Peter with the governance and full legation duties in the March of Ancona and the Duchy of Spoleto. He commands them to humbly attend to him. Dated: April 7, 1249. Source from the registers: Inn. IV Reg. Lib. VI, f. 70, cur. n. 27.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa praelatis et ceteris ecclesiasticis marchiae Anconitanae et ducatus Spoletani mandat, ut Petro cardinali, legato sedis apostolicae, quem pro regno Siciliae reformando et a tyrannide Friderici quondam imperatoris liberando destinaverit, humiliter intendant. 1249, Aprilis 7. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the provost of the church of Faenza. Our venerable brother, the bishop of Cervia, has shown us by his petition that, while he is known to have certain churches in the district of Ferrara, the clerics of that same district, when anything is demanded from them in the name of procuration or for another reason by the legates or envoys of the apostolic see, burden these churches to such an extent that the bishop himself, when procurations of this kind are required from him and the clerics of his diocese by the aforementioned legates or envoys, cannot receive any aid from the clerics of the aforementioned churches. We command you, if this is the case, to compel the clerics of the mentioned district by ecclesiastical censure, with an admonition having been issued and without the possibility of appeal, that they may not presume to burden the mentioned churches or their clerics under the pretext of such procurations. Given at Lyon, on the 25th of February, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa preposito ecclesiae Faventinae mandat ut clericos districtus Ferrariensis compellat, ne ecclesias Cerviensis episcopi sub procurationis praetextu gravent. 1249, Febr. 25. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the dean of the church of Aachen, diocese of Liège. The vice of incontinence, which tarnished the reputation of the clerics of the city and diocese of Utrecht, was prudently addressed by our beloved son, P., cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, then legate of the apostolic see in those parts. It is said that he decreed that none of them should have public concubines henceforth, and that within twenty days of the time when such a constitution was promulgated, they should dismiss them and not attempt to have them or others thereafter. Otherwise, they would be suspended from office and benefice by the law itself, and if they persisted incorrigibly, after ten more days they would know they had incurred the sentence of excommunication, and their benefices would be vacant. However, as we have learned from information given by our dearest son in Christ, W., the illustrious king of the Romans, some of these clerics have incurred the aforementioned sentence and celebrated divine services while being bound by it, but later corrected themselves commendably. We, therefore, acting mercifully at the request of the same king, order that when they humbly come to you for this reason, you may grant them the benefit of absolution by our authority this time according to the form of the church, and dispense them from the irregularity incurred on this occasion. But for others who, having incurred the aforementioned sentence, presumed to celebrate or rather profane the divine services contemptuously ignoring the keys, unless they correct themselves humbly within ten days after your admonition, as they are bound to by the constitution itself, you shall punish with canonical discipline, and you shall try to confer their benefices, which according to the same constitution are found to be vacant, to suitable persons devoted to the Roman church; contradictors etc. Given at Lyon, December 31, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa decano ecclesiae Aquensis Leodiensis diocesis mandat, ut clericis Traiectensis dioecesis, qui sententiam excommunicationis propter concubinatum incurrerant sed se correxerunt, absolutionem et dispensationem super irregularitate tribuat; alios vero rebelles canonice puniat. 1258, Dec. 31. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the provost of the church of St. Mary of the Rotunda in Metz. We do not wish that our beloved son R., the elected bishop of Worms, concerning whom our beloved son P., deacon cardinal of St. George at the Golden Veil, then legate of the apostolic see, is said to have provided for the vacant pastorate of the church of Worms, be troubled by anyone regarding the benefices he held at the time of such provision, until the controversy arisen over the same provision has come to an end. We consider him worthy of the favor of the apostolic see due to his connection with our beloved son, the noble Wirricus de Dune, marshal of the royal court and his brother. We command you, therefore, declaring by our authority null and void anything attempted by anyone concerning the said benefices of the elected until the said elect has obtained corporal possession of the aforementioned church of Worms by right or favor, to ensure that the revenues of these benefices are fully provided to the elected wherever he may be, as if he were personally residing in the churches where he holds them, with only the daily distributions excepted, notwithstanding any contrary custom or statute, oath, or any other form of security, or any indult of the apostolic see, which needs express mention in these presents and by which this grace could be hindered or delayed. Against opposers, etc. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa preposito ecclesie sancte Marie Rotunde Metensis mandat ut nullus molestet R. electum Warmaciensem super beneficiis suis, donec controversia provisionis finem accipiat, et ut eidem electo proventus beneficiorum interim ministrentur. Datum ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbots of St. Emmeram of Regensburg and ... of Walerbarche in the diocese of Regensburg. As we have heard not without disturbance of mind, the church of Passau has gravely collapsed both spiritually and temporally due to the negligence and carelessness, or rather malice, of the bishop of Passau. Neither is there hope that the church, which once flourished with an abundance of goods, might be restored to its former state of splendour under him. Nor does the business of the universal church advance for the better through him, as he remains lukewarm and lax regarding this, although, unfortunately, it might not be getting worse. Thus, if the said bishop would consider with prudent reflection that if he does not fulfill the effect of the episcopal office, he may find reason to grieve, for he should expect confusion in the heavens due to the primacy he holds on earth: he would prudently consult for his soul and honor if he would withdraw from the episcopacy, which seems to have ceased to be beneficial to him. Therefore, lest the said church incur irreparable harm under his governance, we command that you prudently and effectively admonish and induce the said bishop to resign from his episcopacy, reserving to himself only the pontificals if he wishes, and ensure that, upon his resignation and the acceptance of this resignation by us, an honest and suitable provision from the episcopal goods be assigned for his maintenance, and that he may enjoy peaceful possession of it. Dated as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbatibus Sancti Emeramni Ratisponensis et de Walerbarche mandat, ut episcopum Pataviensis ad resignationem episcopatus inducant, provisione honesta sibi assignata. [Pontificatus anno XIII, 1239, ex urbe Roma.]

**Translation to English:**

To Master Philip of Assisi, our subdeacon and canon of Liège, collector of the twentieth throughout the city and diocese of Liège. Through their commendable devotion, the beloved son, the prior, and the convent of the monastery of Saint Lawrence of Liège, are known to deserve that they perceive us to be both benevolent in affection and gracious in action towards them. Since, as we have learned from our beloved son, P. Cardinal Deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, then the apostolic legate in those parts, they have been and are considerably diligent in matters pertaining to the honor of the Apostolic See, enduring many burdens of expenses during the siege of Aachen, we, considering them worthy of special grace for this reason, have decided to remit sixty marks of silver from the money they owe to us and the aforementioned see by reason of the twentieth of their revenues, which they have from the revenues of the abbot of the aforementioned monastery. We command that you should not trouble the aforementioned prior and convent over the exaction of these said marks in any way, nor allow them to be troubled by anyone, revoking anything that has proceeded against them in any way by you or by another; and about the molesters, etc. Given at Lyon, March 18, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Magistro Philippo de Assisio, subdiacono et canonico Leodiensi, mandat ne priorem et conventum monasterii Sancti Laurentii Leodiensis super exactione sexaginta marcarum argentii molestet, revocans in irritum processum contra eos. 1232, Mart. 18, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Master Adinulfus of Arpino, canon of the Church of St. Mary of Castello Scipione in the Sorana diocese. We, loving your person with sincere charity in the Lord, willingly lend a benign ear to your petitions, especially admitting those to the grace of hearing that are known to regard your honor and benefit particularly. Therefore, since our beloved son, Master Berardus Carazolus, our chaplain and professor of civil law, has conferred upon you the rural church of St. Peter of Campomayna in the Sorana diocese, which was vacant by the death of John de Gaydo, its rector, by our special mandate, as is more fully contained in the letters he made concerning this matter, we, inclined by your prayers, holding this collation as pleasing and acceptable, confirm it with apostolic authority, notwithstanding that the church may have been conferred by Frederick, the former Roman Emperor, or his officials, or that you may hold other benefices. We fortify it with the patronage of this present writing, decreeing that whatever might be attempted against this collation and our confirmation is null and void, ordering the tenor of those letters to be inserted word for word in these presents, which is as follows: To the prudent and discreet man, Master Adinulfus of Arpino, canon of the Church of St. Mary of Castello Scipione in the Sorana diocese, Berardus Carazolus, chaplain of the lord Pope, professor of civil law, greetings in the Lord. Since our lord and most holy father, Pope Innocent, wishing to bestow a special grace upon you, has enjoined us to confer upon you the rural church of St. Peter of Campomayna in the Sorana diocese, vacant by the death of John de Gaydo, its rector, by his authority — notwithstanding that the said church may have been conferred by Frederick, the former Roman Emperor, or his officials, or that you may hold other benefices —: we, by the special mandate of the aforementioned Supreme Pontiff, confer upon you the aforementioned church in the stated manner. For the memory of this matter, we have caused these present letters to be made and fortified with our seal. Done at Lyon, 24 October, in the sixth year of the same lord Pope's pontificate. Therefore, let no one etc. of our confirmation and constitution etc. Given at Lyon, 25 October, in the sixth year. .. to the abbot of the secular church of St. Peter of Canneto in the Verulan diocese. Loving the person of our beloved son, Master Adinulfus of Arpino, cleric of the Sorana diocese, with sincere charity in the Lord, we willingly lend a benign ear to his petitions, etc. as above with words competently changed up to: might be attempted. We command that you induct the same master into the corporal possession of the aforementioned church and defend him once inducted; contradictors etc. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa magistrum Adinulfum de Arpino in possessionem ecclesiae sancti Petri de Campomayna diocesis Soranae inducit et collationem factam a magistro Berardo Carazolo, capellano suo, auctoritate apostolica confirmat, iis non obstantibus quae per Fridericum imperatorem vel officiales fieri potuerint. Datum Lugduni, VIII Kal. Novembris, anno sexto (pontificatus).

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Strasbourg. Wishing to favor our beloved son Henry of Vinstingen, canon of Strasbourg, for his merit of probity and at your request, along with those of our dear sons, the noble men Ulrich of Wittenberg, Henry of Grutanger, Henry of Kleinstein, and Conrad of Freiburg, counts, who have pleaded with us on his behalf, so that he may more easily obtain the desired munificence of the Apostolic See through these numerous intercessors, we command that you provide the said canon in the city, diocese, or province of Trier, in the cathedral church or another church, with a prebendary benefit and a personate or ecclesiastical dignity, even if it has the care of souls, as Henry himself shall choose to accept. Whether it is vacant now or whenever the opportunity arises, you shall provide for him by our authority, either by you or another, and ensure he is received in the church where you have chosen to provide for him as a canon and brother—notwithstanding any fixed number of canons, oath, or other binding agreement, or if we or legates of the Apostolic See have directed our writings for others. Concerning the acquisition of the prebend or personate or such dignity, unless someone has acquired a special right to it, we wish this canon to be preferred, or that he is otherwise already benefitted, or if the bishop or chapter or any persons of the church where he shall be provided has been granted immunity by the Apostolic See, which prevents them from being excommunicated, interdicted, and suspended without the mandate of the same See, or any indulgence for which a special mention must be made herein and by which such provision could be obstructed or delayed, or that a legate of the said See has otherwise written for the same matter—contradictors, etc. For we decree as null and void anything rashly attempted against the tenor of this our mandate. Given at Lyon, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of February, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Argentinensi mandat ut Henrico de Vinstingen, canonico Argentinensi, in civitate vel diocesi seu provincia Treverensi provideat beneficio prebendali et personatu seu dignitate ecclesiastica, etiam si curam habeat animarum, non obstantibus quibuscumque. Datum Lugduni, XII Kal. Februarii, anno VI.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Prussia, Livonia, and Estonia, legate of the Apostolic See. We are said to have given you a mandate by our letters, that you should, without any delay or difficulty, appoint one of the clerical brothers of the Hospital of Saint Mary of the Teutons, who is suitable for the episcopal burden and honor, as bishop to one of the dioceses in Prussia, upon request from our beloved sons, the brothers of the said hospital residing there; and having summoned two or three brothers, you should confer the consecration upon him, and ensure that obedience and reverence are exhibited to him by his subjects, contradictors, etc. However, since no benefit appears to have arisen yet from such grace, we, wishing that it may become fruitful for them, strictly command your fraternity by apostolic letters, in the virtue of obedience, to promptly appoint our beloved son, Brother Henry of Stritherche, a priest of that order, a man indeed of praiseworthy conduct and life, and devoted to us and the Roman Church, as pastor to one of the mentioned dioceses, namely Warmia or any other that is currently vacant or will soon be vacant. And if something should happen to this brother in the meantime by human chance, you shall do the same for another suitable brother who is acceptable to the same brothers; you shall fulfill our command in such a way that your sincerity may be held in high regard by us, with worthy praise and an increase of favor. Otherwise, we decree from now that any attempt made in this matter against our pleasure shall be null and void, and we instruct our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Cologne, by our letters, to execute the apostolic mandate concerning this matter according to the form given to you, contradictors, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 11th of February, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Pruscie, Lyvonie et Eustonie, apostolice sedis legato, mandat ut fratrem Henricum de Stritherche, sacerdotem ordinis hospitalis sancte Marie Theutonicorum, in episcopum unius ex diocesibus Pruscie preficial, alioquin archiepiscopo Coloniensi iniungitur mandatum exequatur. 1232, Feb. 11, Lugduni.

To the same. We wish and command you by the authority of these presents, that you strictly warn with our authority the chapters and convents of cathedrals and major monasteries of your legation, both specially and generally, not to presume to provide for bishops or abbots in these churches when they become vacant without our special permission, decreeing that if they act otherwise, it shall be null and void. Given at Lyons, on the Kalends of March, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Maguntino, apostolicae sedis legato, mandat ut ingratos ecclesiae privet gratiis et in provincia Coloniensi legationem non exerceat, et universis ecclesiarum capitulis vetet ne de episcopis seu abbatibus sine speciali licentia provideant. 1233, Feb. 24-28, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the illustrious King of the Romans. Although you are obliged by the power granted to you by the Lord to support everyone in their justice, it is appropriate for you to show more favor to high and noble persons through whom great benefits of utility are expected to come to your honor, especially in matters that have been granted to them by your predecessors. Therefore, since, as proposed before us on behalf of our beloved son, the noble man, the Margrave of Baden, it has been allowed by the Roman emperors of blessed memory, who were in power at the time, to the Dukes of Austria by special privilege that if the same Dukes died without male heirs, females could inherit in the duchy and other fiefs and goods by the right of males; and since he is prepared to take up the sign of the cross against F., the former emperor, and C., his son, and their supporters and to adhere to you faithfully with all his strength, as he claims, we, considering it worthy that he should be graciously pursued with royal munificence on account of this, earnestly ask and urge your majesty to liberally grant and invest the duchy, fiefs, and other goods, which the Duke of Austria of blessed memory is known to have held, to the noble woman, his wife, niece of the same Duke, to whom these ought to succeed both by kinship of blood and by the reason of the said privilege, so that the aforesaid noble man may be bound to your favor and we may rightly commend the zeal of your sincerity. Given at Lyon, on the second day before the Kalends of February, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa regi Romanorum commendat marchionem de Baden, hortans ut ducatum et bona ducis Austrie uxori marchionis conferat et eam investiat. 1249, prid. Kal. Feb., apud Lugdunum.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Genoa. The balance of right judgment is then adjusted with an even measure when it dispenses due rewards to virtues and fitting punishments to vices. Thus, by justice, which renders to each what is theirs by order—grace to services and retribution to injuries—examples of rewards stimulate the slow to merit good deeds, and sometimes fear of punishment curbs those prone to transgressions from the incitement of evil imitation. The clear services of proven devotion, by which the beloved sons, the power and commune of the Genoese, have pleased us not only in these days but also our predecessors in the needs of past times, come frequently to mind. On the contrary, the perverse insolence of the power and commune of Tortona, rebelling against the light with the sons of darkness, who, following the footsteps of the lost son F., the former emperor, deviate from the womb of the mother church and the fellowship of the faithful, provoke God with scorn and the Apostolic See with contempt and injuries, and thus treasure up wrath for themselves in the day of wrath with the hardened malice of their hearts. Weighing in the balance of equity the merits of each, we deem it fitting that the devout should taste something of the fruits of their ways, and the undevout should feel something, and that what is taken from the ill-deserving in punishment of their fault should be added to the well-deserving as an increase in their reward. Therefore, since the said power and commune of the Genoese have temporal dominion in several castles and places of the diocese of Tortona located beyond the yoke towards Lombardy, in which the church of Tortona is known to have ecclesiastical jurisdiction, we, wishing that the city of Tortona be taught by its own confusion to seek the name of God, having been stripped of a portion of its honor, which it does not seem to understand, and the city of Genoa, decorated with titles of honors due to its devotion, may be made more certain of the grace of the Apostolic See by manifest experiences, have seen fit, by the authority of these presents, to commit the spiritual jurisdiction in these same castles and places that by right or custom pertains to the aforesaid church of Tortona, to you and your successors until it pleases our will. We decree that you fully receive and exercise the episcopal rights according to both laws from them, being supported by the protection of the Apostolic See, notwithstanding any contradiction from our venerable brother, the bishop, and the church of the Tortonese. For we impose silence upon them concerning these matters with the tenor granted to you, and if the aforementioned bishop or his archdeacons or vicars or anyone else, by the authority of the said church, presume to pronounce any sentences of excommunication, suspension, or interdict against the aforementioned castles and places or the churches established therein or the ecclesiastical or secular persons residing there, we decree them to be utterly null and void. Let no one, therefore, etc., of our commission, imposition, and constitution, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 3rd of the Nones of June, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa archiepiscopo Ianuensi mandat, ut cum potestas et commune Ianuensium in nonnullis castris Terdonensium temporalem dominium habeant, iurisdictionem spiritualem in eisdem castris ad archiepiscopum Ianuensem usque ad beneplacitum nostrum committat, iniungens ut iura episcopalia exequatur, non obstante contradictione episcopi Terdonensium. Datum Lugduni, III Non. Iunii, anno V.

...to the Bishop of Bologna. The Holy Mother Church is accustomed to open her bosom to her sons, especially to those who strive to please us and the Apostolic See through the service of devoted offerings. Since, therefore, our beloved son Albert, a canon of the Church of St. Margaret in Modena of the Order of St. Augustine, and chaplain of our venerable brother, the Bishop of Sabina, is known for the devotion he holds towards us and the Apostolic See, and since he asserts that it is not safe for him to remain in the same church due to the fear of the late Emperor Frederick and his supporters, we, bearing towards him the due affection of compassion, command that you provide or arrange to provide for him from any of the churches within your city or diocese of the aforementioned order, until he can safely return and reside at the aforementioned Church of St. Margaret, with the necessary provisions for sustenance and clothing by our authority—notwithstanding if the persons of the church, where you may decide to provide for him, have been granted by the same See that they cannot be compelled, interdicted, suspended, or excommunicated by apostolic letters that do not make express mention of this kind of indulgence, or any other through which the effect of this provision might be impeded or delayed—; opposers, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 16th Kalends of April, in the 6th year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Bononiensi mandat ut Alberto canonico ecclesiae sanctae Margarite Mutinensis ordinis sancti Augustini, qui propter metum Friderici imperatoris quondam et fautorum eius in eadem ecclesia morari non potest, provideat de necessariis victus et vestitus ab aliqua ecclesiarum civitatis vel diocesis, donec ad ecclesiam suam secure reverti possit. We command, therefore, that you confer and assign to this provost the provostship of the church of Saint Amarian in the diocese of Basel, if it is currently vacant or as soon as it becomes vacant, by our authority — notwithstanding that the said provost has previously been beneficed elsewhere, or any indulgence which requires special mention in our letters and might otherwise impede or delay this grace, or if we have sent other letters regarding other benefices in the aforesaid church of Saint Amarian, which we do not wish to prejudice regarding other benefices, or if provision has otherwise been made for the said provost by our authority —; contradictors, etc. For we decree that whatever is attempted against the tenor of our mandate regarding the said provostship is null and void. Given at Lyon, on the second day before the Kalends of March, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa abbati Bellelagiensis ordinis Praemonstratensis Basiliensis diocesis mandat, ut dilecto filio praeposito ecclesiae Basiliensis, cuius devotio et fides erga sedem apostolicam cognoscitur, praeposituram ecclesiae Sancti Amarini Basiliensis diocesis conferat et assignet, si vacat vel cum vacare contigerit, non obstantibus beneficiis aut indulgentiis aliis. Dat. Lugduni, II Kal. Martii, anno VI.

To the provost of the church of Bugella in the diocese of Vercelli. Among those who deserve praise and those who do not, etc., as above, up to the word "gracious." Therefore, in order to exalt the praises of the righteous and to restrain the insolence of transgressors, justice has raised in the world dominions, thrones, principalities, and various other powers in the manner of the heavenly court. Since Peter, called Bicherius, a citizen of Vercelli, who, being exalted from almost nothing through ecclesiastical goods, should, if he were to think rightly, even lick the footsteps of the clergy, has been given over to a reprobate sense and impudently adheres to Frederick, formerly emperor, who has been rejected by us and a holy approving council, and openly, through which he persecutes and attacks God and the Church like a satellite of Satan: we, considering that it is fitting that those whom divine fear does not turn away from evil should at least be restrained by temporal punishment, and wishing to punish him at present in some ways, so that through this we may bring benefit to the devoted of the Church, command that you absolve our beloved son, the noble man Uberto de Bulgaro, a citizen of Vercelli, devoted to us and the Roman Church, from all debts, sureties, and obligations, to which he is bound for any reason, and from oaths made concerning these — notwithstanding sales, if any were made to him by the said Uberto on the pretext of any surety or obligation, which we wish to be regarded as not made — by the authority of these presents, and declare that he and his predecessors are not bound to the aforementioned Peter concerning the above matters henceforth, nor can they be summoned by him or others for the same at any time, strictly prohibiting, by our authority, any power, judges, consuls, or rectors, or the said Peter, from daring to compel him to pay those debts or to trouble him concerning the above matters in any way, and to bear the sentence of excommunication against them, if they presume to act contrary to your prohibition in any way, so that they are bound by this sentence ipso facto, from which they cannot be absolved until they have fully satisfied Uberto for the damages and expenses that he may have incurred on this occasion. Given at Lyon, on the Nones of January, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa praecepto ecclesiae de Bugella mandat absolvere Uberto de Bulgaro civem Vercellensem a debitis et obligationibus in favorem ecclesiae Romanae et excommunicationem in eos qui contraveniant imponere. Datum Lugduni, Non. Ianuarii, anno sexto.

To the Bishop of Tusculum, legate of the apostolic see. On behalf of our beloved daughter in Christ, the noble lady Mellisende, widow of the late B., Prince of Antioch, and daughter of the illustrious memory of Amalric, King, and Isabella, Queen of the Jerusalemites, it was humbly petitioned to us that, since she asserts herself to be most closely related by bloodline to C., son of the late Emperor F., heir to the Kingdom of Jerusalem, among his other relatives in those parts, and since by both law and the ancient custom of the same kingdom, the one closest to the heir should, in his absence, hold the dominion and guardianship of the kingdom, we might cause her to be inducted into the possession of the said dominion and guardianship through you, and having been inducted, to be defended against any unlawful possessor. We command you, having diligently inquired into and known the truth in this matter, if you find this to be the case, to execute it by our authority, as it is just, if it can be done straightforwardly and without scandal; as for the contradictors, etc. Otherwise, what you have done or could be done in this matter, you should strive to faithfully inform us by your letters. Given at Lyon, the 9th day before the Kalends of April, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Tusculano mandat, ut, si Mellisendis petitio de possessione dominii et baiulatus regni Ierosolimitani vera esse deprehendatur, eam in possessionem inducat et defendat. 1232, Mart. 24. Lugduni.

Therefore, acceding to your supplications, we grant to your fraternity by the authority of these presents, that no prejudice be generated against you and the church of Tyre concerning the aforementioned tithes and rights with respect to the oft-mentioned church of Saint Mark of Tyre by reason of this exemption. Innocentius IV papa archiepiscopo Tyrensi concedit ut super decimis et iuribus ad ecclesiam sancti Marci Tyrensis pertinentibus, nullum preiudicium fiat propter exemptionem ecclesiarum sancti Marci Tyrensis et Acconensis a sancto Marco Venetiarum. 1249, Ian. 12, Lugduni.

Gregorius IX papa electo Vercellensi mandat, ut abbates et clericos Vercellenses, pro delictis contra ecclesiam in favorem imperatoris defuncti commissis, ab officiis et beneficiis ecclesiasticis perpetuo privet et personas idoneas substituat. Lugduni, VII Idus Ianuarii, anno sexto.

To the archbishops, bishops, abbots, priors, deans, archdeacons, and other prelates of churches situated throughout Germany. Since we have previously summoned Frederick, the former emperor of the Romans, to personally or through messengers appear at the Council of Lyon to answer to us and others who wished to bring forth accusations against him, and to provide suitable satisfaction. Finally, in the same council, we discovered many things against him, among others, that were so certain and evident that there was no room for denial. Because of these, he was rightly to be held suspect of the sin of heretical depravity. Especially since after the sentence of excommunication pronounced by our predecessor, Gregory of happy memory, he was bound by the chain of anathema, and after the capture of cardinals, prelates, clerics, and others who had come to the apostolic see, he showed contempt for the keys of the church, causing divine offices to be celebrated, or rather profaned as much as he could, openly asserting that he did not fear the sentences of our predecessor. Moreover, he allied himself with the detestable Saracens, embracing their rites and keeping some of them in his daily service. After the Sultan of Babylon, with whom Frederick had a long-standing mutual friendship and perfect concord, had inflicted grievous harm and inestimable injuries on the Christians of the Holy Land and its inhabitants, he had the Sultan's envoys honorably received and magnificently provided for through the kingdom of Sicily with praises extolling the glory of that Sultan, misusing the pernicious and horrendous services of other infidels against the faithful, and procured to be united with those who, damnably scorning the apostolic see, had departed from the unity of the church by friendship and affinity.

In that council, for these and many other reasons contained in the sentence then pronounced against him, we declared him deposed and deprived by the Lord of all honor and dignity both of the empire and of the kingdoms, and we pronounced against him the sentence of excommunication solemnly for these and other causes. We have since had this sentence renewed annually on certain solemnities according to the custom of the Roman Church. But he, as if confirmed in his wickedness, has neither cared to provide satisfaction for such abominable and damnable suspicion nor to return to the bosom of mother church, although he has sent the archbishop of Palermo, the bishop of Pavia, and some others to the see, who presented to the venerable brothers, the bishops of Porto and Albano, and our beloved son H., cardinal priest of the title of St. Sabina, whom we assigned as auditors to them, an instrument of a certain notary and letters sealed with a golden bull, in which it was stated that when Frederick was held as suspect of heretical depravity in the said council, he, being interrogated and examined by them on the 45 articles contained in the creed and others pertaining to the catholic faith, declared that he firmly believed them and swore; in which also he appointed the examiners as his procurators to swear on his soul that he believed them, and to offer purgation also in our presence in an appropriate place on such suspicion. They reported these things to the same auditors viva voce, and that they were ready to swear thus, offering such purgation on Frederick's behalf.

However, we, having understood these things and considering such examination and purgation as presumptuous, with neither place nor subject nor before whom it should have been conducted, since the examiners themselves and their relatives are from his court or lands subject to his power or rather tyranny, deemed it illusory and frivolous, and with the counsel of our brothers and many prelates who were then present with us, we decreed it null and void, utterly rejecting the process presumed by those examiners concerning these matters. We have learned that the church of Passau, which used to flourish in the abundance of both spiritual and temporal goods, has now irreparably collapsed in both due to the malice of its prelates, especially the one in charge. This prelate, who in old age has become in mind like a child, besides being prodigal with his reputation and neglectful of his salvation, has enormously squandered and consumed the goods of the church. He has made himself a public enemy of God and the Roman church by not fearing to hand over the fortresses and strongholds of the church of Passau to the nobleman, the Duke of Bavaria, offering him and his other supporters counsel, aid, and favor against the church. In other matters, he is so lukewarm and remiss in managing the affairs of the church entrusted to him that under his governance, unless swift remedy is applied, the said church will suffer irreparable harm. The bishop, entangled in the bonds of excommunication by our beloved son P., cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, then apostolic legate in those parts, presumed to celebrate divine offices, indeed, to profane them more truly, and to consecrate churches and ordain clergy in lands and castles of the ministerials of Chunrinfe, which were subjected to ecclesiastical interdict by apostolic authority. Innocent IV, Bishop, servant of the servants of God, for perpetual observance and memory. From the days of Frederick, a foster child of iniquity and almost a precursor of the Antichrist, the kingdom of Sicily has suffered violence, and his ministers have violently plundered it. Indeed, this dragon, leaping from the narrow dwellings of manifold necessity, famished and thirsty, into the vast abundance of overflowing prosperity, began to ravage the aforementioned kingdom with a rapid mouth, consuming its flesh, that is, the abundance of its resources, as food, and draining its blood, namely the life of its people, as a drink; he thus blazed with insatiable rapacity against its goods and persons, that, lamentably wild more than any beast, he almost entirely devoured it in both respects, not sparing sex, age, or order. Oh, what a perverse ruler was entrusted with so great and such a kingdom, who, intent solely on his nefarious desires, wickedly rushed to its destruction, to satisfy his beastly spirit with the enormity of inhumanity, a guardian indeed pillaging, a governor dissipating, a defender offending, a leader deviating, a prince precipitating, and a king gnawing!

Alas, therefore, that the gracious and precious kingdom, specially blessed by the Lord in all things, has fallen from the heights of glory to the depths of misery, distressed by various tribulations under the dominion of hostile adversity, which once rejoiced in the abundance of blessings from the smile of friendly prosperity! Alas, that the beautiful kingdom is seen changed with such great alteration that it seems wholly different from its former self, and those who beheld it in its first form scarcely recognize it! Weeping has stolen its laughter, and its joy has ceased into lamentation. However, as we consider ourselves debtors to all, while we think ourselves more inclined to the governance of all, we are justifiably terrified with intense fear and we tremble greatly, not without reason, lest we inadequately fulfill the office of the apostleship we have undertaken, lest we omit something through negligence concerning the care of the Lord's flock entrusted to us, especially since we are powerless of ourselves to bear the weight of such a burden, and cannot in person be present at the same time because of the diversity of places, for the sheep to whose guard we have been appointed. Indeed, because the condition of human nature does not allow that while one is contained in one place, he can be captured in another simultaneously, having a just excuse from this, sometimes, when it is fitting for us to be attentive to all the churches and we cannot be personally present at the same time for each one, we call prudent and discreet men into a part of our solicitude, instructed by the example of him who descended from the heights of heaven to the depths of the world for the salvation of the human race, sent his disciples, whom he had chosen, into the world to preach the gospel. Innocent, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to our beloved son, the noble man Alberico de Romano, greetings and apostolic blessing. For the perpetual glory of your name, it has come, etc., as in number 755 up to: with grateful concurrence of assent, the privileges and concessions which our beloved son Gregory of Montelongo, our subdeacon and notary, legate of the apostolic see, is said to have granted to you for your devotion to the Church and defense of the Catholic faith and the liberty of the Church, as is more fully contained in the letters drawn up concerning this matter, we confirm by apostolic authority and fortify with the endorsement of this writing. Therefore, let no one, etc., of our confirmation, etc. But if anyone, etc. Given at Anagni, the 9th of October, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa dilecto filio nobili viro Alberico de Romano privilegia et concessiones a Gregorio de Montelongo, apostolice sedis legato, concessa, auctoritate apostolica confirmat. 1243, Oct. 9, Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To William of Lutira, cleric of the Diocese of Worms. To the just desires of petitioners, etc., to fulfill. Since, as your petition presented to us contained, the beloved sons, the dean and chapter of the church of Saint German of Speyer, have received you into their church as a canon and brother, even though no prebend was vacant at that time: we, inclined by your devoted supplications and those of the beloved son C., the envoy of our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, consider what has been prudently done by the dean and chapter to be valid and pleasing, and we confirm it by apostolic authority and support it with the protection of the present document. Let no one, therefore, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 6th year of our pontificate, May 6.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Guillelmo de Lutira clerico Warmaciensis diocesis mandat, ut receptio eius in canonicum et fratrem ecclesiae Sancti Germani Spirensis, quamvis sine vacante praebenda, a decano et capitulo facta, auctoritate apostolica confirmetur. 1249, Mai. 6, Lugduni.

Translation to English:

To the bishop of Gurk: On your behalf, it was humbly requested of us that, since many laypeople of your city and diocese have inflicted numerous damages through fires and plundering upon certain other churches for the defense of the rights and goods of the Church of Gurk, and since it is exceedingly difficult for them to approach the apostolic see to obtain the benefit of absolution from the sentence of excommunication they have incurred for this reason, we might order, out of our usual kindness, that they be absolved. Therefore, having full confidence in your discretion in the Lord, by the tenor of these presents, we entrust you to absolve these excommunicated individuals from the sentence of excommunication in our stead, according to the form of the Church, imposing on them what should be imposed by right, with the provision that they make proper satisfaction to those who have suffered damages. Given as above.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Gurcensi mandat ut laicos diocesis Gurcensis, excommunicatos propter dampna aliis ecclesiis illata, absolvendi facultatem habeat, iniunctis eis satisfactionibus pro dampnis illatis. Datum ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To P., Cardinal Deacon of San Giorgio in Velabro, legate of the Apostolic See. The desired benefit from the grace of the Apostolic See should be granted to the subjects so that they may persist more fervently in their devotion to it and its generosity might be extolled among others. Therefore, to our beloved son, the noble man Matteo of Amiterno, of the Diocese of Rieti, our devout follower, we have decided to concede that he succeeds freely in all goods and rights of the late Gentile of Amiterno, his father, and Theodinus his uncle, which the late Emperor Frederick holds unjustly occupied: we command that you, or his procurators on his behalf, enter him into physical possession of the aforementioned goods and protect him once inducted, quashing any opposers or rebels, should there be any, with spiritual and temporal penalties, bypassing any appeals. Given at Lyon, on the 15th day before the Kalends of June, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa P. Sancti Georgii ad Velum Aureum diacono cardinali, apostolicae sedis legato mandat ut Matheum de Amiterno in possessionem bonorum et iurium quondam Gentilis patris et Theodini avunculi inducat et tueatur, contradictores coercendo. 1248, Mai. 18, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of Saint Lazarus of Verona, residing in Mantua. Since, as proposed before us on behalf of our beloved son, the noble man, the count of Saint Boniface, it was stated that the former abbot of the monastery of Vangadicia, of the Camaldolese order in the diocese of Adria, with the consent of his convent, decided to grant certain possessions and other goods of the said monastery to the late William of Lendenaria, to whom Antonius and Petrus, brothers and sons, and Bartholomeus and Antonius, nephews and heirs, captains of Lendenaria, devoted to the count and the Roman Church, succeed in these goods, for a certain period under an annual rent, as it is more fully contained in the public instrument made thereon; we, inclined by the supplications of the said count, command you to confirm the aforementioned to the same heirs by our authority, provided that the condition of the said monastery is thereby improved; contradictors etc. Given at Lyon, on the Nones of June, in the sixth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa abbati Sancti Lazari Veronensis, Mantue commoranti, mandat ut possessiones et bona monasterii de Vangadicia, olim Willelmo de Lendenaria concessa, sub annuo censu confirmet heredibus, dummodo monasterii conditio melior fiat. Datum Lugduni, Nonis Iunii, anno sexto.

**Translation to English:**

**I.** To the Archbishop of Cologne. Since we have shown ourselves to be generous and kind to certain ecclesiastical and secular persons of your legation, etc., as above in the 412th chapter, up to: it was considered by them; dissenters, etc. Given as above.

**II.** To the same. We wish and by the authority of these presents command you, that to all both of cathedral, etc., as above in the 414th chapter, up to the end. Given as above.

**III.** To the same. Since, in the kingdom of Germany, we have decided, with the advice of our brothers, to fully entrust you with the office of legation for the good status of it and to promote the business of the church and empire: we, therefore, grant your fraternity, by the authority of these presents, the permission to confer ecclesiastical benefices throughout the land of your legation, as if you were a cardinal of the Roman Church, should you exercise the office of legation there, notwithstanding the constitution issued by us on this matter. Given as above.

---

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Coloniensi mandat eum habere potestatem conferendi ecclesiastica beneficia in regno Germaniae pro bono statu ecclesiae et imperii, sicut cardinales ecclesiae Romanae habent, non obstante constitutione prius edita. Datum ut supra.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot of Middelburg, of the Premonstratensian Order, in the diocese of Utrecht. In order that the apostolic favor may increase for both him and his followers, due to the devotion which our beloved son, the noble man H. called Buffelo, envoy of our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, is known to have towards us and the Roman Church, we command that you provide or arrange to provide, by our authority, for our beloved son Giles, canon of the church of St. Mary in Utrecht, the brother of the said nobleman, a position or dignity in the province of Cologne, even one involving the care of souls, should he choose to accept it, if it is vacant at present or as soon as it becomes vacant — notwithstanding if we have sent our writings there for others, or any other apostolic indulgence that would need to be mentioned and by which such grace might be impeded or delayed. Those who oppose, etc. Given at Lyons, the 4th of the Nones of May, in the sixth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa abbati Middelburgensi, ordinis Praemonstratensis, in diocesi Traiectensi mandat ut Egidio, canonico ecclesiae beatae Mariae Traiectensis et germano nobilis viri H. dicti Buffelo, provideat de aliqua praelatura vel dignitate in provincia Coloniensi, etiam curam animarum habente, auctoritate apostolica, non obstantibus aliis scriptis vel indulgentiis apostolicis. Datum Lugduni, die 4 Nonas Maii, anno pontificatus nostri sexto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Cologne. On behalf of our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, it was earnestly requested of us that, since Bastianus de Viseto, a knight of the diocese of Liège, had contracted marriage with Juliana de Fontanis, who was about seven years old, and was separated from her by ecclesiastical judgment because it was discovered by matrons that the woman would remain unapproachable even when she reached legal age, and because he subsequently contracted marriage with another woman related to the said Juliana in the third degree of consanguinity and had children with her, we might use our usual benevolence to dispense with this matter. Therefore, wishing to grant a special favor to the said knight at the request of the king, we command you to dispense with him by our authority, so that—despite this impediment—he may lawfully remain in the marriage thus contracted. Given at Lyon, 10th Kalends of May, in the sixth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopo Coloniensi mandat ut cum Bastianus de Viseto, miles Leodiensis diocesis, matrimonio cum alia muliere in tertio consanguinitatis gradu coniuncta et filios genitus, auctoritate apostolica dispenset, non obstante impedimento cum Iuliana de Fontanis, obtentu regis Romanorum, ut in matrimonio sic contracto licite remanere possit. 1232, Apr. 22, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Abbot of Saint Trudo in the Diocese of Liège:

On behalf of our beloved son Egidius, a canon of the Church of Blessed Mary in Maastricht, it was presented before us that he has canonically obtained a prebend, which once belonged to Frederick, a canon of the same church, who was a crusader. However, Gotfrid of Kut, a canon of the same church, and other executors of the testament of the said Frederick, are claiming the fruits of the said prebend for their own benefit, based on a certain indulgence. This indulgence was granted to clerics serving our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, for a period of three years by our beloved son P., cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, who was then the legate of the Apostolic See in those regions. This is causing prejudice and harm to the said Egidius. We order that, unless the aforementioned Frederick personally fulfilled his crusader vow by serving the said king, you are to ensure that the revenues of the said prebend are fully assigned to Egidius, notwithstanding this indulgence. Opposers, etc. Given at Lyon, 4th of the Kalends of May, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa abbati Sancti Trudonis Leodiensis diocesis mandat, ut proventus prebende, quam Egidius canonicus ecclesie beate Marie Traiectensis canonice adeptus est, ei assignentur, nisi Fredericus, quondam canonicus, votum crucis per se impleverit. Actum Lugduni, anno sexto pontificatus, die IIII Kalendas Maii.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble woman Sarracina, wife of Giffredo de Galluciol. To the just requests of petitioners, etc., to be fulfilled. Since, as your petition presented to us stated, your mother, the late Countess Cecilia, of good memory, granted and gifted to you all the goods that the late Pandulf of Aquino, her kinsman, had conceded and donated to her, as they pertained to her, as is more fully contained in the document drawn up on this matter: we, at the request of our beloved son, the noble man Roger of Gallucio, your father-in-law, acceding to your noble petition, considering valid and proper what has been done by that countess, by apostolic authority confirm these goods to you and strengthen them with the protection of this present writing. Let no one, therefore, etc., infringe our confirmation, etc. Given at Lyon, 16th Kalends of May, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa nobili mulieri Sarracinae, uxori Giffridi de Galluciol, bona a matre sua comitissa Cecilia sibi concessa auctoritate apostolica confirmat. 1248, Apr. 16, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the archbishops and bishops, abbots, priors, deans, archdeacons, and other prelates of churches, whether exempt or non-exempt, as well as to the chapters and the entire clergy established throughout the kingdom of Germany. The care of the universal Church entrusted to us, the fullness of ecclesiastical power granted to us, continuously stirs our heart with insistence and perpetually excites us with the spur of thought, so that we direct our attention to all the faithful of Christ, both near and far, etc., as stated in the 411th chapter, in the one which is addressed to the archbishops and other prelates of Germany concerning the legation of the Archbishop of Mainz, until: they may feel supported: behold, to our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Cologne, a man indeed endowed with knowledge, etc., as in the same, until: fulfilling. Otherwise, the sentence which he may rightly pass on the rebellious, etc. Given at Lyon, 2nd day before the Kalends of May, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopis et episcopis, abbatibus, prioribus, decanis, archidiaconis et aliis prelatis ecclesiarum per regnum Alamanniae mandat ut archiepiscopo Coloniensi auxilium praebeant in legatione sua perficienda, aliter sententiam in rebelles rite latam subeant. 1233, Apr. 30. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the parish priest of Milian in the diocese of Lucca. The devoted supplication of our beloved sons, Paul of Garfagnana, a clerk of our chamber, and William his nephew, along with the merits of the rector himself, induce us to grant a special favor to our beloved son Uguiccione, rector of the church of Saint Martin of Lauran in the diocese of Lucca. Therefore, moved by their supplications, we command that you provide the aforementioned rector with a certain parish or rectory that he deems acceptable, even if it involves the care of souls, should any such position currently be vacant in the diocese of Lucca or should such a position become available soon, under our authority — notwithstanding that the same rector holds another benefice, or if we have sent similar writings in the same diocese on behalf of others, for whom we wish etc., up to: to be generated, or by any indulgence of the apostolic see which could impede or delay the effect of our grace and up to: special mention; contradictors, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 10th of June, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa plebano de Milian Lucane diocesis mandat ut Uguicioni rectori ecclesiae Sancti Martini de Lauran plebanatum vel rectoriam vacantem in eadem diocesi concedat, non obstantibus beneficiis aliis. Datum Lugduni, IIII Idus Iunii, anno sexto.

**Translation to English:**

To the scholastic of Cambrai. Our beloved sons, the abbot and convent of the monastery of Saint Trudo in the diocese of Liège, have complained to us, showing that several prelates of churches, counts, barons, and other noble and powerful men burden and harass the said monastery with forced labor, unjust levies, and other undue exactions against justice. They also demand and extort undue money from certain estates of the monastery, which are commonly called allods, to the prejudice and burden of the monastery and its people. Therefore, we command that you compel the aforementioned prelates, counts, barons, and others, after a prior warning, to desist from such undue harassment of the monastery and its people, through ecclesiastical censure, with an appeal removed and reason being given—despite if any of these harassers have been granted an indulgence by the apostolic see, stating that they cannot be excommunicated, suspended, or interdicted without a special mandate of the same see mentioning such indulgence, and notwithstanding the constitution concerning two days, etc., provided it does not exceed the third or fourth day, etc. Given at Lyon, 4th of the Nones of May, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa scholastico Cameracensi mandat, ut ecclesiarum praelatos, comites, barones aliosque nobiles, qui monasterium sancti Trudonis indebite angariis et exactionibus vexant, ecclesiastica censura compellat desistere. 1251, Maii 4, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Gerard, a canon of Cologne, born of a noble man, Count Silvestrius. It was presented before us on your behalf that the late Archbishop of Mainz, of good memory, issued a sentence of deposition against you, who were then the cantor of the major church, and against Berthold, a canon of St. John's in Mainz, your cleric, depriving you both of the benefices you held at his discretion and, as much as it lay within his power, declared you ineligible by sentence to obtain ecclesiastical benefices. And although the same archbishop later admitted you to his grace, because through negligence and carelessness, while the archbishop was still alive, it was omitted that these sentences should be revoked, we, moved by the devout supplications of our dearest son in Christ, W., the illustrious King of the Romans, and yours, by the authority of these presents, grant you that these sentences shall not in the future impede you and the aforementioned canon in obtaining dignities, prelatures, and other ecclesiastical benefices. Let no one therefore etc. impugn our concession etc. Given at Lyons, on the 8th of the Ides of May, in the sixth year [of our reign].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Gerardo canonico Coloniensi mandat, ut sententiae depositionis latae per archiepiscopum Maguntinensem in ipsum et in Bertholdum canonicum Sancti Iohannis Maguntine nihil obsint ad dignitates, prelaturas, et alia ecclesiastica beneficia obtinenda. 1249, Maii 8. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Würzburg.
