On behalf of our beloved son, the provost of the church of Würzburg, it was presented before us that the dean, Yringus of Huimburch, Eberhard of Masbach, and certain other canons of the same church, not considering that the goods of his provostship have been significantly diminished by the enemies of the church and other sons of perdition, are demanding the revenues of their prebends and daily distributions with the same fullness as they used to be provided before the diminution of these goods, according to his will... and immediately suspend their services if they are not satisfied in this matter. Therefore, he humbly petitioned us to take fatherly care in providing him relief in this matter. Since you can have more complete knowledge of these issues, we command you, if the truth supports the aforementioned claims, to compel the said dean and other canons, through prior admonition and ecclesiastical censure, removing any appeal, to be content with what can be conveniently provided to them by the said provost, and to desist from harassing him on this account, provided that he provides for them according to his means — notwithstanding if any of them have been granted by the Apostolic See that they cannot be excommunicated, suspended, or interdicted through apostolic letters. Given at Lyon, 22 June, in the sixth year of our pontificate. 

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Herbipolensi mandat, ut decanum et canonicos ecclesiae Herbipolensis compellat, ne provostum bona sua minora molestent, proviso quod eis iuxta facultates ministret. 1232, Iun. 22, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble woman Sophia, landgravine of Thuringia, niece of the illustrious memory, the Roman king H., and widow of the good memory, the duke of Brabant. As we have learned, you are fervently devoted to being regarded as pleasing in the sight of God and the Apostolic See, as deduced from the fact that ecclesiastical freedom is laudably promoted in those parts through your favor's assistance. We, indeed, considering you worthy of the grace of honor and favor due to such merits, hereby receive your person with all the goods, which you reasonably possess at present or may justly acquire in the future, under the protection of Saint Peter and our own, strictly prohibiting anyone from daring to deceive, impede, or annoy you in your devotion to the Apostolic See regarding the aforementioned goods. Let no one therefore etc. of our protection and prohibition etc. Given at Lyons, on the 6th year [of our pontificate], 2nd day before the Nones of May. In the same manner to the noble woman, the widow countess of Sayn.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa [Nomen Papae] nobili mulieri Sophiae, landgraviae Thuringiae, nepti regis Romanorum H., et relictae ducis Brabantie, personam eius cum omnibus bonis sub protectione beati Petri et sua suscipit, et prohibet ne quis eam super bonis suis impediat. Datum Lugduni, II Nonas Maii, anno VI.

Translation to English:

We have included it in the Registers. Potthast, Reg. 13327; Berger 4604. To the noble man P., son of the noble man Pandulf of Aquino. Since the noble man Pandulf of Aquino, your father, presumed to adhere to the former emperor Frederick against the Church, we, prudently considering that he has deserved punishment for this, but you, due to your devotion, suffering exile for the Church, have claimed the grace of the Apostolic See for yourself, we grant to you and your successors the barony, castles, and other goods that he holds both in the Kingdom of Sicily and outside of it, freely and fully, just as he is known to hold them, by the authority of these presents — notwithstanding if he has decided to grant any of them to others —, yet if he returns to the devotion and command of the Church, he shall fully regain all those things as before. Let no one therefore etc. Given at Lyons, on the 3rd day before the Kalends of May, in the sixth year.

Regesto in Latin:

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro P. nato nobilis viri Pandulfi de Aquino indulget ut ipse et successores sui baroniam, castra ceteraque bona patris sui, quae in regno Siciliae et extra habet, plenarie habeant, si Pandulfus ad ecclesiae mandatum redierit, res suas integre recipiat. Datum Lugduni, III Kal. Maii, anno VI.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Henry Fraiapane, count of our sacred Lateran palace, your clear devotion, distinguished among other nobles towards us and the apostolic see, earnestly demands that we favor you continuously and elevate you with abundant honor, following the examples of our predecessors, who honored your ancestors with many graces and enriched them with generous gifts for the many great services they rendered to the Roman Church. Therefore, considering your noble lineage and proven worth, we wish to honor you with a special gift of grace. We have decided to grant you all the fruits, revenues, and proceeds from the jurisdiction of Arborea, except for the tax owed to the Roman Church for it, to be received by you or by those we shall appoint for this purpose, for as long as you live and until it pleases us otherwise, by the authority of these presents. Let no one, therefore, etc. Given at Lyon, on the fourth day before the Nones of June, in the sixth year.

The same. Since we have decided to grant you all the revenues from the jurisdiction of Arborea, except for the tax owed to the Roman Church, for as long as you live and until it pleases us otherwise: by the tenor of these presents we wish you to know that if you happen to incur any expenses to recover and receive these revenues and to preserve the rights of the church in this matter, we will never revoke this grant until you or your successors are compensated for these expenses from the proceeds of the jurisdiction. Given at Lyon, on the Nones of June, in the sixth year.

**Regesto:**

Innocentius IV papa nobili viro Henrico Fraiapane, comiti sacri palatii Lateranensis, omnes fructus, redditus et proventus iudicatus Arboree, excepto censu debito ecclesiae Romanae, quoad vixerit et usque ad beneplacitum, concedit et expensas pro conservando iure ecclesiae compensandas promittit. 1249, Iun. 2-5, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man Gentile de Rocca Accarina of the diocese of Spoleto. The sincerity of your devotion merits that we, pursuing your person with paternal benevolence, honor it with a special gift of grace. Therefore, we, inclined by your supplications and wishing to honor you with some provision, have decided to grant you fifty measures of wheat, to be received annually for your lifetime, from the fruits and revenues of the lands of the castle of Otricoli in the diocese of Narni, which pertain to the apostolic see, according to the measure of the city of Narni. No one therefore etc. Given at Lyon, the Nones of May, in the sixth year. S. II. P. To the deacon cardinal of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the apostolic see. With our beloved son, the noble man Gentile de Rocca Accarina of the diocese of Spoleto, concerning the fruits and revenues etc. as above until: granted, we command that the said measures be fully delivered to the said noble; objectors etc. Given as above.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa nobili viro Gentili de Rocca Accarina de Spoletana dioecesi quinquaginta raseria frumenti annuatim ex fructibus et proventibus castri Otriculi Narniensis dioecesis, ad sedem apostolicam pertinentibus, concessit. Dat. Lugduni, Nonas Maii, anno VI.

**Translation to English:**

To Brother William of Eika of the Order of Preachers, Diocese of Liège. Confident in the Lord regarding the sincerity and constancy of your devotion, we command that you faithfully collect and have collected by yourself and others, who are suitable for this task, the redemptions and revenues arising from any cause of the vows of the crusaders in aid of the Holy Land, who are poor and unable to cross over, as well as legacies or bequests or any other contributions granted for this purpose throughout the kingdom of Germany. You are to keep these under careful custody until our good pleasure, absolving those redeeming their vows through you or those you have appointed for this purpose, granting them the remission of sins that was granted at the general council to those going to the aid of the Holy Land or supporting it. This is notwithstanding any privileges or indulgences or any letters obtained or to be obtained from the Apostolic See or its legates, which might impede or delay such collection, and for which a specific or express mention must be made in our letters. Opponents, etc.; whatever you decide to do concerning these matters, you shall faithfully report back to us. Given at Lyon, on the 14th of May, in the sixth year of our pontificate. In the same manner, to Brother John of Disth of the Order of Friars Minor, Diocese of Liège.

---

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa fratri Willelmo de Eika ordinis Praedicatorum Leodiensis diocesis mandatum dat ut redemptiones et obventiones ex votis crucesignatorum pauperum per regnum Alamanniae ad subsidium Terrae Sanctae colligat et custodiat, absolutionem concedens. 1249, Mai. 14, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the dean of Saint Servatius in Maastricht, diocese of Liège. Our beloved son, the abbot of Saint Trudo of the order of Saint Benedict in the diocese of Liège, humbly petitioned us in our presence, requesting that since the same monastery is somehow burdened with an intolerable weight of debts, we, providing with fatherly concern, might, out of apostolic kindness, place some of the monks of the same monastery in other places to alleviate such debts. Since, therefore, it primarily pertains to us, upon whom the care and responsibility for all churches generally lie due to the office of the service undertaken, to counteract the burdens of the churches as much as we can with God’s help: we command you to place some of the monks of the aforementioned monastery by our authority in other monasteries or priories of the same order that are not burdened with a similar provision by apostolic mandate, and which have the resources for this, placing each in each location to remain there for up to three years. You shall compel the abbots or priors of the monasteries where you provide placements for them to receive them and treat them with fraternal charity, using ecclesiastical censure if necessary, removing any appeal beforehand— notwithstanding any indult granted to them or their communities by the apostolic see that they cannot be compelled to receive or provide for anyone by apostolic letters, or that they be excommunicated, suspended, etc., as above, up to: mention, and the constitution concerning two days, etc., provided that beyond the third or fourth, etc. Given at Lyon, 15th day before the Kalends of June, in the sixth year.

**Regesto:**

Innocentius IV papa decano Sancti Servatii in Traiecto mandat ut aliquos monachos ex monasterio Sancti Trudonis, propter debitoris sarcinam alleviandam, in aliis monasteriis ordinis Sancti Benedicti per triennium collocet. Lugduni, XV Kalendas Iunii, anno VI.

**Translation to English:**

Innocent, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son, the noble man Alberic of Romano, podestà of Treviso, greetings and apostolic blessing. We have received your letters of sincerity and devotion with paternal affection, and having more carefully understood their content, we acknowledge the zeal for faith and the ardor of charity, which you have for our person and the Holy Mother Church, as we have long recognized through experience and now fully understand through these letters. To you, for whose exaltation we will strive with all our efforts when the time comes, we give as many thanks as we can. Although an appeal or exhortation seems somewhat unnecessary for confirming your steadfastness, since fullness does not require addition, yet it does not harm to spur a willing horse. Therefore, we have deemed it fitting to attentively request and admonish your nobility, commanding through apostolic writings, that you, increasing from good to better in devotion to the Apostolic See, since it is wise to grow in virtue from strength to strength, persevere with your usual promptness, so that with the favor of the Apostolic See greatly increasing for you, besides the divine reward you will receive from the Rewarder of all good, you will render the Roman Church more firmly bound to your advantages, which does not forget its devoted followers. Given at Genoa, the 6th day before the Kalends of August, in the second year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius III papa [Alberico de Romano potestati Tervisino mandat, ut in devotione sedis apostolicae perseveret, promittens proinde favorem apostolicum et divinae retributionis mercedem. 1205, Iul. 27, Iannuae.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected Bishop of Liège. A beloved son, W., abbot of the monastery of St. Trudo of the order of St. Benedict in your diocese, presented before us that he, formerly a parish priest of Aachen and a chaplain of our beloved son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Romans, was induced by the diligent exhortations of many religious men to take the monastic habit in the same monastery. Within eight days, after having made his profession there, the monks of the same monastery, then without an abbot’s governance, believing that through his providence and the power of his friends, the monastery – whose goods had been gravely diminished by the negligence of its predecessors – could receive pleasing increase in spiritual and temporal matters, unanimously elected him as abbot of the monastery. Thereafter, our venerable brother Arnold, formerly Bishop of Semigallia from the Cistercian order, with your special license and mandate, conferred upon him the blessing of the abbot. Therefore, since a scruple of doubt has arisen in his conscience due to such promotion, he humbly begged us to provide a salutary remedy for him from the usual clemency of the apostolic see. We, therefore, inclined by the interceding prayers of the aforementioned king made on his behalf, command that you, by our authority, act dispensatively with him as your circumspection sees expedient for the salvation of his soul and the utility of the church. Given at Lyon, on the 4th day before the Nones of May, in the sixth year (of our pontificate).

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo electo Leodiensi mandat ut cum W. abbate monasterii sancti Trudonis auctoritate apostolica dispenset super electione sua in abbatem facta et benedictionis munus acceptum, prout videbit expedire. 1232, Mai. 4, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot and convent of the monastery of the Holy Spirit of Sennona, of the Cistercian order, in the diocese of Gaeta. Your way of life, commendable for its purity of intention, venerable for the goodness of your works, and approved by the pursuit of regular observance, has earned you favor with us and the Apostolic See. As you have withdrawn your steps from the slippery path of this world to the dwelling of cloistered solitude to avoid mortal ruin, we extend to you fitting favors and even arm you with apostolic privileges. We are especially diligent as a father in caring for you, so that, with peaceful and devoted minds, you may serve the King of Peace continuously, with the cause of scandal removed and the path to disputes blocked. 

Therefore, as your house, as we have learned from your communications, is obligated to pay an annual rent or tribute of three pounds of frankincense to the monastery of Saint Angel in Gaeta for the island of Sennona, and as we have recently subjected that monastery to the monastery of Pontian Island of the Cistercian order by the fullness of our power, we, wishing to entirely remove any occasion for discord between you and the abbot and convent of the aforementioned monastery of Pontian Island in this matter, and inclined by the supplications of your devotion, grant by the authority of these presents that you and your successors are no longer obliged to pay this rent or tribute in the future. Let no one, therefore, etc. Given at Lyon, the 5th day before the Kalends of May, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa abbati et conventui monasterii Sancti Spiritus de Sennona, ordinis Cisterciensis, in diocesi Gaietanae, tribuit ut non teneantur solvere censum annuum trium librarum olibani monasterio Sancti Angeli Gaietani pro insula de Sennona. Datum Lugduni, V Kal. Maii, anno sexto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Cologne, legate of the Apostolic See. Regarding matters that pertain to the honor of the Apostolic See, our beloved noble son Ulric of Minceberg, chamberlain of the imperial court, is said to be so diligent and fervent that he deserves a reward of gracious favor from the same See. Indeed, through the noble's report, we have learned that our beloved noble son Sibotho, his stepson, has married Lugard, the daughter of the noble man, the Count of Rostein, who is devoted to the Roman Church, although they are related in the fourth degree of consanguinity. Because through this marriage not only have certain deep enmities been resolved, but many dangers have also been safely ended, and because of this, it is said, pleasing services could also benefit the church: we, for the sake of the aforementioned chamberlain, have decided to commit to your fraternity by the authority of these presents, that, after considering all the circumstances, if you deem it suitable and expedient, you may dispense with Sibotho and Lugard so that they may freely remain in the marriage thus contracted, notwithstanding such an impediment. Given at Lyon, on the Ides of May, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa archiepiscopo Coloniensi mandat ut, si decens et expediens videatur, cum Sibotho et Lugard in matrimonio contracto, non obstante impedimento consanguinitatis, dispenset. Datum Lugduni, Idibus Maii, anno VI.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Gurk. The Apostolic See is accustomed to accede to the prayers of the devout and extend benevolent favor to their desires. Therefore, since, as you have stated in our presence, our beloved son Engelbert, your cleric, has served you faithfully and devotedly for a long time, we, wishing to grant him special favor at your request, by the authority of these presents, grant you the permission to provide or have provided for the said cleric a suitable prebend or other ecclesiastical benefice in Germany, where you see it to be expedient, even if it involves the care of souls. This is notwithstanding the fact that he already holds another benefice, or if we have sent our writings concerning others in those regions, which we do not wish to affect this grant, or despite any fixed number of canons confirmed by oath or by any other authority, or any apostolic indulgence granted to churches or persons in those parts that might prevent or delay the reception or provision of someone by apostolic letters, or any indulgence of the Apostolic See which might impede or delay this grant, and of which special mention would need to be made in the present letters; let any contradictors, etc. Given at Lyon, 18th May, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa episcopo Gurcensi mandat ut Engelberto clerico, qui fideliter et devote servivit, in Alamania provideat in beneficio ecclesiastico competenti, non obstantibus quibuscumque impedimentis. 1249, Mai. 18. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the chapter of the church of Saint Stephen at Capite Pontis of Florence. The kindness of the Apostolic See gladly adds the firmness of apostolic confirmation to those things which are prudently carried out by its authority. Indeed, your petition presented to us stated that, when we gave orders through our letters to the beloved son, the archpriest of Florence, to diligently admonish and induce the clerics of the city and diocese of Florence, who were favoring the late Emperor Frederick II, to return to the devotion of the Apostolic See within a span of one month after the archpriest's admonition, otherwise the same archpriest should deprive those clerics of ecclesiastical dignities, offices, and benefices. The said archpriest, having legitimately ascertained that Albert, who claims to have been elected prior of your church, favored the aforesaid Frederick, both personally and through his supporters, and having been diligently admonished by the same archpriest according to the form of our mandate, contumaciously despised to return to the devotion of the church. Therefore, he deprived him by sentence of whatever right he had in the priorate of the aforesaid church, as is stated more fully in the letters drawn up on this matter. We, therefore, inclined by your supplications, hold what has been rightly done by the same archpriest in this matter as ratified and acceptable, confirm it by apostolic authority, and protect it by the patronage of this present writing. Let no one therefore etc. Given at Lyon, the second day before the Kalends of June, in the sixth year (of our pontificate).

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa capitulo ecclesiae Sancti Stephani de Capite Pontis Florentinae confirmat sententiam ab archipresbytero Florentino contra Albertum latam, qui ad devotionem ecclesiae redire contempsit, eum prioratu privando. Datum Lugduni, II Kalendas Iunii, anno sexto (1253).

**Translation to English:**

To the archbishops and bishops, abbots, etc., situated throughout Sardinia. It is rightly measured by the scale of careful consideration, when the merits of the subjects are so weighed with just estimation that a worthy recompense responds to the services of the devoted, and the punishment of perpetual disgrace weighs upon the necks of the unfaithful. Thus, through the benefits granted to the good, many are elevated to the merits of virtues, and through the punishments of the wicked, the audacity to sin is prohibited in others. Therefore, as we have learned, certain clerics and laymen, who have obtained fiefs and ecclesiastical benefices from you and your churches, have adhered and still dare to adhere to Frederick, the former emperor, and to his sons, manifest persecutors of the Church. We wish and by the authority of these presents strictly command you that you take away these fiefs and benefices from them and confer the same to other faithful and devoted to the Church, with the counsel of our beloved son, the elect of Torres, legate of the Apostolic See; let the contradictors, etc. Otherwise, we have instructed the same elect by our letters to execute the apostolic mandate concerning this matter. Given as above. In the same manner to the archbishops, etc., situated throughout Corsica.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa archiepiscopis et episcopis, abbatibus per Sardiniam constitutis mandat ut feuda et beneficia ab infidelibus obtenta auferant et ea fidelibus de consilio electi Turritani conferant. 1237, Dat. Laterano.

**Translation to English:**

To the noble man R. de Gallucio, devoted to the Roman Church. The accustomed providence of the Apostolic See examines the merits of its subjects with skilful deliberation and distinguishes those which are superior by the judgment of reason, rewarding them with greater remuneration and advancing them with more abundant favors and fuller benefits. Therefore, since you are fervent in that devotion towards the Roman Church and strive to maintain constancy towards it, so that among its other sons you are specially distinguished by the title of fidelity and deserve to be honored by it in many ways, we, considering this not unworthily and wishing to provide for your advantages and diligently seek the increase of your honor, inclined by your supplications, restore and grant to you and your successors the castle of Vayrano in the diocese of Teano, which, as you assert, was liberally conferred to you by our predecessor of happy memory, Pope G., and from which you were despoiled by the late Emperor F. at his pleasure, with its dominion, rights, honors, and all its appurtenances, especially as the kingdom of Sicily currently lacks a king, by special grace, provided that the said castle does not pertain to another who persists in the devotion of the Church. However, we wish that once you have possession of the said castle, you and your said successors are obliged to render homage and fidelity and other duties to the aforesaid Church or to the king who through it will be in the said kingdom for the time being, which other vassals of the same kingdom are obliged to show for the castles they hold. Let no one, therefore, etc., violate our restitution and concession, etc. Given at Lyons, on the 10th day before the Kalends of May, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa nobili viro R. de Gallucio castrum Vayrani, in dioecesi Teanensi situm, cum dominio, iuribus et pertinentiis suis restituit et concedit, sub conditione homagii et fidelitatis praestandae, cum regnum Sicilie rege careat. 1232, Apr. 22. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the dean and chapter of Mainz. Having received your letters and envoys with usual kindness, we have diligently understood the contents of those letters and what the envoys reported on your behalf. You humbly requested us to entrust the church of Mainz, currently vacant of a pastor, to our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Cologne, an indefatigable defender of the church, so that he might take care of it, since he seems all the more capable of governing it as he would be better able to support its needs through the Church of Cologne. We commend your devotion in the Lord. However, because it is entirely unprecedented for two such honorable and exalted archiepiscopal churches to be entrusted to a single governance, and if it were to happen, it would seem utterly inappropriate, we have deemed it not suitable to agree to your request in this matter. Yet, because we do not wish for the aforementioned church of Mainz to remain without a pastor for a long time, lest it suffers severe spiritual and temporal detriment due to a prolonged vacancy, we command you to provide for the church with a suitable pastor with the counsel and consent of our venerable brother, the Bishop of Strasbourg, within a month after the said bishop informs you. Otherwise, we have instructed the said bishop by our letters, that at that point, he shall appoint a person suitable for such a burden and honor as pastor of the aforementioned church of Mainz by our authority. Opponents, etc. Given at Lyon, on the fourth day before the Nones of May, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa decano et capitulo Maguntinensibus mandat, ut, cum ecclesia Maguntina pastore vacet, eis praecipit, quatinus de pastore idoneo cum consilio et assensu episcopi Argentinensis infra mensem provideant, alioquin idem episcopus auctoritate papae pastorem instituat. Datum Lugduni, II Non. Maii, anno sexto.

**Translation to English:**

To the bishop of Ruthenensia. Our beloved son, the noble man John of Viridifolio, our faithful one, heir of the late John of Chabreira from the diocese of Utica, presented before us that Pope Adrian of blessed memory, our predecessor, took under his protection and that of Saint Peter the person of the same John of Chabreira with all his goods, both ecclesiastical and worldly. He received the castle of Viridifolio and half of the castle of Petra Sadula, which land he received from his hands and for which he showed loyalty, and also confirmed to him with apostolic authority all other things reasonably acquired or to be acquired, as it is contained in the privilege of our predecessor. At the request of the said nobleman, because it has begun to decay with age, we have had it transcribed and our seal affixed to such a transcript. Therefore, not wishing the same nobleman to be unjustly troubled by anyone regarding his goods, which he acknowledges to hold as a fief from the Roman Church, we command that if you ascertain that anyone has unjustly occupied these goods, you shall compel them, as well as those who hereafter occupy them, to restore them to the aforementioned nobleman with the fruits received from them, justice intervening through ecclesiastical censure, removing any appeal, and not allowing the said nobleman to be unjustly disturbed regarding these goods, contrary to the tenor of the aforementioned privilege. You shall admonish such disturbers or molesters, notwithstanding any indulgence granted by the apostolic see to any of them that they cannot be excommunicated or interdicted without a special mandate of the apostolic see making mention of this indulgence, and the constitution regarding two diets, etc. Given at Lyon, 15th June, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Ruthenensi mandat, ut si qui bona Iohannis de Viridifolio, quae ab ecclesia Romana in feudum tenet, iniuste occupaverint, eos compellat ad restitutionem cum fructibus perceptis, necnon prohibeat ne idem nobilis contra privilegii tenorem inquietetur. 1233, Iun. 15, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

Inclined by your devotion, we hold the concession ratified and pleasing, and we supplement any potential deficiency in its solemnity with our grace. We confirm it with apostolic authority and fortify it with the protection of this document. Therefore, let no one violate our confirmation, etc. Given at Lyon, on the eighth day before the Kalends of May, in the sixth year [of our pontificate]. To the same. Deserving, etc., as in the previous [letter], up to: shame. Inclined by the prayers of your devotion, we have decided to grant you the possessions and goods that Nepolionus Raynaldi was known to have in the castles of Antignano, Ciriano, and St. Mary of Laurent, which were destroyed by you because he opposed the Roman Church. We grant you the free faculty of entering their possession, especially since the inhabitants of those castles are, as you assert, now residents of your castle, provided that the rights of any devotees of the Church are not infringed by this concession. Therefore, let no one, etc. Given at Lyon, on the fifth day before the Kalends of May, in the sixth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa inclinat devotionis precibus, possessiones et bona quae Nepolionus Raynaldi in castris de Antignano, Ciriano et Sanctae Mariae Laurentii habebat, auctoritate apostolica confirmat et concedit, cum liberam facultatem possidendi tribuat, dummodo ecclesiae iura non ledantur. 1232, Apr. 27, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Brother William de Oika, of the Order of Preachers, of the diocese of Liège. We command your discretion by the tenor of these presents, that you collect, by our authority, through yourself or others suitable for this task, the redemptions of the vows of the cross-bearers of the Kingdom of Germany, both against the late Emperor F. as well as in aid of the Holy Land, and likewise legacies or bequests and other revenues, from whatever causes they may have been granted to the said land or to the general business of the Church — notwithstanding any concessions, indulgences or letters concerning these redemptions and others aforementioned granted by the Apostolic See to any persons or to be granted in the future, even if it is necessary to make mention of them in these presents. What may arise from the redemptions of the vows of the cross-bearers against the aforesaid F., or from other causes granted for this purpose, you shall procure to confer and assign to our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King W. of the Romans, as we are said to have already granted to him by our letters. But what may arise from the vows of the cross-bearers to the Holy Land or even from legacies owed for any other causes to the said land, you shall ensure is kept in safe custody in a secure place until our good pleasure. Opponents, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 11th of May, in the sixth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Fratri Willelmo de Oika ordinis Predicatorum mandat ut redemptiones votorum crucesignatorum regni Alamannie et alia subsidia colligat et ea regi Romanorum W. conferat, dum obventiones Terram Sanctam pertinentes conservet. 1232, Mai. 11, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbots of Casemarium of the Cistercian order and St. George of Grataraft in the dioceses of Verulanus and Cephaludensis, and to Master Paganus, canon of Trani, residing in the City and Campania. It is fitting for learned and good-doing men, etc., up to: rewards. Thus it is that we command, on behalf of our beloved son John Sacco, canon of Palermo, that you, as we intend to treat him with special grace and favor, confer and assign to him the chaplaincy of the major church of Palermo, which has been vacant for such a long time that, as it is said, its appointment has devolved to us — notwithstanding that the archbishop of Palermo, while he was bound by excommunication, is said to have conferred the same chaplaincy to another, and that the same canon holds another benefice — by our authority, to be retained by him along with the prebend which he holds in the aforesaid church. You shall induct him into possession of the same chaplaincy and defend him, removing any unlawful occupant; opposing parties, etc., calling upon, if necessary, the help of the secular arm — the constitution regarding two diets, etc. If not all, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 11th of May, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa abbatibus Casemarii et Sancti Georgii de Grataraft diocesum Verulane et Cephaludensis et magistro Pagano canonico Tranensi mandat, ut Iohanni Sacco, canonico Panormitano, capellaniam maioris ecclesiae Panormitanae, auctoritate sua conferant, quamvis archiepiscopus Panormitanus eam alii contulerit dum excommunicatus erat, et ipsum in possessionem inducant et defendant. 1248, Mai. 11. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Cardinal Priest of the title of Santa Maria in Trastevere, our Vicar in the City. Since, by other letters, we have instructed you to confer, by our authority, the church of Santa Maria de Cesis in the Marsican diocese, which is said to be vacant of a rector, upon Bartholomew, a scholar, the son of our beloved son Bontempi, our familiar, who wishes to be enrolled in the clerical militia. We command that if you are unable to confer it upon him due to a just cause, you should, by the aforesaid authority, provide him with another equivalent church or ecclesiastical benefice in the Marsican bishopric or other places in the Kingdom of Sicily, either by yourself or through another or others, and place him or his procurator in possession of the church or benefice, of which you have decided to provide him, and protect him once inducted; let any contradictors be dealt with appropriately, notwithstanding the constitution concerning the two days, or if we have directed our writings for the provision of others to the bishopric or the aforementioned places, which we do not wish to be hindered up to: be generated. Given at Lyon, 14th Kalends of July, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa S. tituli Sancte Marie Transtiberim presbytero cardinali, vicario suo in Urbe, mandat ut, si ecclesiam sancte Marie de Cesis Marsicane diocesis Bartholomeo, filio Bontempi familiaris sui, conferre nequit, de alia ecclesia vel beneficio ecclesiastico in episcopatu Marsicano vel regno Sicilie provideat. 1233, Iun. 18, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the archbishops and bishops to whom these letters shall come. It contributes to the glory and honor of God that such guardians are chosen in His vineyard who benefit themselves through a virtuous life and others through example. Indeed, as we have learned, our venerable brother, the archbishop of Livonia and Prussia, the legate of the Apostolic See, prudently considers the commendable conduct and merits of knowledge of our beloved son, Brother Henry of the Order of Preachers, who worked diligently and faithfully with him for the cause of faith and the Church. Moreover, he recognizes that the land of Jatwesonia can receive laudable growth in spiritual and temporal matters through the industry of this brother, with the Lord's guidance. According to the authority of our letters, which empowered the said archbishop, he appointed the same brother as bishop and pastor of the aforementioned land. However, since the same archbishop has been expelled from his province and is not permitted to consecrate the said brother as bishop in another's territory, we have been humbly entreated on behalf of the said brother to bestow upon him the office of consecration. Therefore, we earnestly ask, admonish, and exhort your fraternity, commanding that whichever of you is requested in this matter by the same archbishop through his letters, should bestow the office of consecration upon the aforementioned brother, having called some of the neighboring bishops. Given at Lyon, on the 11th of April, in the sixth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa archiepiscopis et episcopis mandat, ut fratri Henrico ordinis Predicatorum, a Livoniae et Prussiae archiepiscopo in episcopum Iatwesoniae electo, convocatis aliquibus vicinis episcopis, consecrationis munus impendant. 1249, Aprilis 11, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

We have consulted the Registers. Potthast, Reg. 13306; Berger 4606. To the abbot of the monastery of St. Peter of Villamagna in the diocese of Anagni. Desiring to grant a special favor at the request of our beloved son, the noble man P. de Fasanella, to our beloved son James called Squarsapella, a cleric of the church of St. Pancras in Anagni, we command that you provide or cause to be provided for him, by our authority, in the kingdom of Sicily, from ecclesiastical revenues up to the sum of thirty ounces of gold belonging to any benefice, and that he be received into the church or churches where provision is made for him, if they are collegiate, as a canon and brother—notwithstanding any fixed number of canons, oath, or confirmation of the Apostolic See, or any security thereof, or if we have directed our writings there for others, to whom, etc., until: to be generated, or if it has been granted to any person or church that they cannot be excommunicated, interdicted, or suspended or prohibited from entering the church, or by any indulgence of the same See, by which such a favor may be hindered or delayed, and of which specific mention should be made in our letters, and the constitution regarding two days' journey, etc.—; and those who contradict, etc. Given at Lyons, the seventh day before the Kalends of May, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa abbati monasterii sancti Petri de Villamagna mandat, ut Iacobo dicto Squarsapella, clerico ecclesiae sancti Pancratii Anagninae, in regno Siciliae de redditibus ecclesiasticis usque ad triginta unciarum auri summam provideatur et in canonicum recipiatur, non obstantibus quibuscumque impedimentis. 1249, April. 25. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To Rudolf, schoolmaster of the Church of Augsburg. When a request is made to us, etc., to the point of: effect. Indeed, when you previously informed us that the former schoolmaster of Augsburg had transferred to the Order of Preachers, intending to remain there permanently as was believed, we, at the request of the noble man C. of Waizeburg, instructed, by our letters, our beloved son, the dean of Eichstätt, that if it became clear that the aforementioned schoolmaster had professed to join the said order, leaving the schoolmastership of the Church of Augsburg vacant, he should confer and assign it to you, upon your resignation from the archdeaconry of Augsburg, by our authority. Once it had been fully verified regarding the said schoolmaster's profession in the aforementioned order, the dean conferred the said schoolmastership to you according to the tenor of our mandate, instructing nonetheless the elected, the provost, the dean, and the chapter of Augsburg to receive you into the position. He had you inducted into corporal or quasi possession of it, implementing excommunication sentences against opposers and rebels, as is more fully contained in the letters of the said dean. We, therefore, inclined by your supplications, ratify and approve the process conducted by the said dean as it is just and, by apostolic authority, confirm and protect it by this written document. Therefore, let no one, etc. Given at Lyon, April 30, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa Rudolfo scholastico ecclesiae Augustensis confirmat et apostolica auctoritate ratificat collationem scholastriae ecclesiae Augustensis, ei factam a decano Eistetensi, postquam illam vacare contigerat per professionem ordinis fratrum Praedicatorum a priore scholastico. Datum Lugduni, II Kal. Maii, anno sexto.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Cologne. The abundance of apostolic grace is so great towards those who have shown themselves worthy through their proven faith and works that they can feel its benefits extend to their natural kin. Truly, considering the purity of devotion and faith by which our beloved sons, the noble men C. and H., brothers and counts of Fribourg, and their ancestors, have pleased the Apostolic See, and recalling the commendable memory of C., Bishop of Portus, their uncle, we have decreed to honor our beloved son Gebehrard, our chaplain and their brother, with a special privilege of our grace. We command you to provide for this G. with an episcopal see in all of Germany as soon as the opportunity arises, and ensure that the subjects of the church to which you appoint him offer him due obedience and reverence, notwithstanding any indulgence granted or to be granted by the Apostolic See that could impede the execution of our mandate, or the constitution regarding two days' journey, etc. Given at Lyons, the 13th of April, in the sixth year [of our pontificate]. II. To the Archbishop of Cologne. For our beloved son Gebehrard, our chaplain and brother of the noble men C. and H., counts of Fribourg, we have directed our writings to you, that you should provide him with an episcopal see in all of Germany as soon as the opportunity arises. However, lest our grace becomes ineffective or unacceptable to him in any case: if the same G. should refuse the episcopate offered to him, when the opportunity arises, we do not wish that the authority granted to you by our letters should be diminished, so that you should fail to provide him with another when the opportunity arises. Given at Lyons, the 13th of April, in the sixth year [of our pontificate].

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa archiepiscopo Coloniensi mandat ut Gebehrardo, capellano suo ac fratri comitum de Friburch, de episcopatu in Alamannia provideat, sub conditionibus specificatis. 1250, April 13, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

Innocent, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son, the noble man Alberico de Romano, greetings and apostolic blessing. Considering the steadfastness of your faith, which you are known to have towards the Apostolic See, and also taking into account the damages you have suffered on this occasion, we receive your person, along with all your lands, castles, jurisdictions, and other goods, which you peacefully and quietly possessed at the time when the sentence of excommunication was declared on the prince, or which you may justly acquire in the future, under the protection of Blessed Peter and our protection, and we strengthen it with the safeguard of this letter. We declare null and void any pacts, promises, pledges, obligations, donations, renunciations, or any concessions made by you or others on your behalf to the said prince or others for him regarding the aforementioned goods prior to the said excommunication, under the condition that you withdrew from the will or command of that prince or acted against him, and also those made after the same excommunication, judgments, bans, confiscations, statutes, penalties, privileges, if any have been issued or pronounced against you or your friends by the same prince or his officials in the meantime, for the reason that you adhered to the Church afterwards. Let no one, therefore, etc., infringe on our protection and declaration of nullity, etc. If anyone should, etc. Given at Genoa, 23rd July, in the second year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa dilecto filio Alberico de Romano, nobili viro, personam suam cum bonis suis sub protectione beati Petri et sua suscipiens, pacta, promissiones et alia irrite nuntiat, quae contra eum post excommunicationem principis lata sunt. 1245, Iul. 23, Ianue.

**Translation to English:**

To Manasses, cleric of the Church of St. Andrew of Anagni. We, loving your person with sincere charity in the Lord, willingly grant a favorable hearing to your petitions, especially admitting those to the grace of hearing which are known to regard your honor and advantage. Therefore, since our beloved son Peter, called Gaetanus, our chaplain, has conferred upon you, by our special mandate, the church of St. Mary of Septimus located in the territory of Cosenza, which was vacant by right, as is more fully contained in his letters made thereon: we, inclined by your prayers, holding this conferment as pleasing and valid, confirm it by apostolic authority and strengthen it with the protection of this present writing, declaring null and void anything attempted against such conferment, inserting the tenor of said letters word for word in these presents; which is as follows: P., called Gaetanus, chaplain and subdeacon of the lord pope, to his beloved Manasses, cleric of the Church of St. Andrew of Anagni, greetings and sincere affection. Since the most holy father in Christ, lord Pope Innocent, has enjoined us to confer upon you the rural church of St. Mary of Septimus located in the territory of Cosenza, we confer it upon you with its rights and appurtenances and invest you with it by our biretta — notwithstanding if the said church had been conferred to another by mandate of the late Emperor Frederick. In testimony whereof we issue these letters to you with our seal. Done at Lyon, the Ides of March, in the sixth year of the pontificate of lord Pope Innocent IV. Let no one therefore etc. of our confirmation and constitution. Given at Lyon, the second day before the Nones of May, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Manassi, clerico ecclesiae sancti Andree Anagnine, confirmationem collationis ecclesiae sanctae Mariae de Septimo a Petro Gaetano facta auctoritate apostolica confirmat et communit, non obstantibus collationibus per F. quondam imperatorem. Actum Lugduni, II Non. Maii, anno VI.

**Translation to English:**

...to the dean of the Church of Saint Paulinus in Trier. Our beloved son Arnold, son of the nobleman A., lord of Disth, has shown us by his petition that Godefrid, lord of Bredal, the brother of the same A., bequeathed him a thousand pounds of Louvain currency in his last will, leaving the villages of Scothem, Marcon, and Ekecim, which rightfully belonged to G., pledged to him for this reason, to be retained by him until the heirs of the said deceased provided him with full satisfaction concerning the aforementioned matters, with the fruits of these villages, which he would receive in the meantime, not to be counted towards the principal, as is more fully contained in the letters drawn up thereon. Henry of Bredal, canon of Liège, who claims to act as the heir of the deceased, asserting that the said villages pertain to his fief, holds them on this account without any prior satisfaction being made, to the prejudice and grievance of the same Arnold; concerning which, the same Arnold seeks to be assisted by the providence of the Apostolic See. We command you that if you find the matter to be so, you compel Brother William of Eika of the Order of Preachers, the nobleman Henry called Berthold, and other executors of the testament of the said Godefrid, to place the same Arnold in bodily possession of the said villages, and that the aforementioned canon be compelled by ecclesiastical censure, having removed any appeal, after prior warning, to allow Arnold to enjoy peaceful possession of those villages until he has been fully satisfied concerning these matters — notwithstanding any indulgence of the Apostolic See, by which the execution of such a mandate could be hindered, or that the same Arnold is of deficient age. Given at Lyon, on the 16th of the Kalends of June, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto:**

Innocentius IV papa decano ecclesiae sancti Paulini Treverensis mandat, ut Arnoldo, filio nobilis viri A. domini de Disth, subveniat, fratrem Willelmum de Eika et alios executores compellendo, ut eum in possessionem villarum Scothem, Marcon et Ekecim inducant, Henricum de Bredal canonicum Leodiensem prohibendo, ne impediat, et monitione per censuram ecclesiasticam ad pacem et satisfactionem plenariam cogendo. 1248, Mai. 17, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the abbot and the prior of the Holy Spirit on the island of Sennenabi of the Cistercian order in the diocese of Gaeta, and to Nicholas de Littera, a canon of Salerno residing in Maritima. The merits of devotion that our beloved son John, called Saccus, a canon of Agrigento, has towards the Roman Church inspire in us a feeling to support him with special grace at opportune times. Truly, as he has humbly set forth before us, due to his aforementioned devotion, he has been stripped of all his goods and is forced to endure the penalties of exile. Since the prebend that he holds in the church of Agrigento has, due to the malice of the times, been so reduced in revenues that it does not reach an annual value of four ounces of gold, and since the benefice commonly called "tertiary" of Castronovo in the same church is said to have been vacant for such a long time that its collation has devolved to the apostolic see: we, bearing a paternal affection of kindness towards him, command that the benefice — notwithstanding that after its collation devolved to us, as we have learned, the bishop of Agrigento presumed to confer it to another, and that the same canon holds another benefice — be conferred and assigned to him by our authority to be retained with the aforesaid prebend, taking care to induct him into the possession of the same benefice and defend him inducted, removing any unlawful holder; any contradictors, etc.—notwithstanding the constitution concerning two diets, etc. If not all, etc. Given at Lyon, 28th May, in the sixth year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa abbati et priori Sancti Spiritus insule de Sennenabi Cisterciensis ordinis Gaietane diocesis et Nicolao de Littera canonico Salernitano mandat, ut Iohanni dicto Sacco canonico Agrigenti beneficio "tertiario" Castrinovi in ecclesia Agrigentina, postquam ad sedem apostolicam collatio eius devoluta fuit, conferant et assignent. 1249, Mai. 28. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the Archbishop of Cologne, legate of the Apostolic See. Although unworthy, we are established as vicars of Him who, for the salvation of humankind, descended from the heights of heaven to the depths of the world, and sent the disciples He chose into the entire world to preach the gospel to every creature. Often, following His example, we call upon prudent and discreet men to share in our concerns, as we cannot be present in every place in person, to address urgent issues. These men, by converting the crooked to the straight and the rough to the smooth, make straight the paths of our God and render the people acceptable to Him.

Truly, among the other desires of our heart, we most ardently wish for the salvation of souls, the increase of ecclesiastical freedom, and peace for all the faithful of Christ. We vigilantly and diligently strive so that, with all obstacles removed, these may come to pass laudably according to the fullness of our desire, with the Lord's help. We desire this even more ardently so that in the regions of Germany, souls may profit, the freedom of the Church may thrive, and the tranquility of peace may be maintained, to the extent that we fervently seek the good state of those regions.

Therefore, that these regions may more fully advance in devotion to God and the Church, knowing they are specially nurtured by the presence of the legate of the Apostolic See, behold, to you — in whose virtue and industry we have full confidence in the Lord — we have decided to entrust the full office of legation in the aforementioned parts, so that you may uproot and destroy, scatter and disperse, build and plant, as you see fit. We therefore command you to diligently exercise this legation according to the grace given to you by the Lord in such a commendable manner that you may earn merit before God and a good name among men, and we may commend your diligence with worthy praises in the Lord. Given at Lyon, March 14, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa archiepiscopo Coloniensi, apostolicae sedis legato, plenam legationis officium in Alamaniae partibus committit, ut animarum profectus, libertas ecclesiae, et pacis tranquillitas promoveantur, mandans ut legationem laudabiliter exerceat. Datum Lugduni, II Idus Martii, anno VI.

**Translation to English:**

It has come to our attention that some time ago certain citizens of Würzburg, sons of Belial, violently attacked our beloved son Glison, provost of the church of St. John in Houge, and certain other canons of the Würzburg church during the solemn mass on the feast of its dedication. They grievously wounded some of them and cruelly treated others, endangering their own souls and showing contempt for ecclesiastical discipline. As a result, both religious and other clerics of the city and suburbs of Würzburg ceased from divine services. However, the late Archbishop of Mainz and our venerable brother, the Bishop of Würzburg, wishing to restore peace among the aforementioned parties, took on this matter. They decreed that the entire clergy of the aforesaid city should resume their duties until the feast of the Purification of the Blessed Mary Virgin just past, and in the meantime, both the church and those who suffered injuries should be given appropriate satisfaction, and full security for the future should be provided. This was ensured by receiving an oath from the leading and powerful citizens to assist the aforementioned Archbishop and Bishop. However, if agreement could not be reached within the set term, they prudently decided that divine office should not be celebrated in the aforementioned city and its suburbs, as is more fully contained in the letters drawn up about this matter. But since this has not come to effect due to the malice and, as it is said, the connivance of the aforesaid citizens, it is unworthy that such audacity should remain unpunished. We command you, therefore, if this is so, to enforce the ecclesiastical interdict in the aforementioned city and its suburbs according to the ordinance of the aforementioned Archbishop and Bishop, until full satisfaction is made by these citizens. Opponents, etc. Moreover, those who laid hands upon them, who it will be established to you have obtained absolution from the apostolic see or its legate either by silence of truth or suggestion of falsehood, you shall nonetheless declare to remain subject to the original sentence of excommunication until they make fitting satisfaction. Given at Lyon, 30th May, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Latin Regesto:**

Gregorius IX papa decanis Sancti Stephani et Sancti Victoris ac cantori Sancti Petri Maguntinorum mandat, ut propter audaciam civium Herbipolensium in clericos, ecclesiasticum interdictum in ciuitatem et suburbia servari faciant donec plena satisfactio praestetur; iniectores manuum qui absolutionem impetraverunt, denuntientur subiacere excommunicationi. Datum Lugduni, III Kal. Iunii, anno VI.

**Translation to English:**

To the elect of Torres, legate of the Apostolic See. Although the bishop of the Apostolic See, having called others to share in his care, alone holds the fullness of power, he cannot, due to human imperfection, suffice to relieve the individual needs of the churches and bear all the burdens of the subjects. Thus, he is compelled to execute through others what he cannot personally accomplish by himself, following the example of Him who, having chosen the twelve apostles, sent them to preach the gospel across the entire world. For from Him, as ointment upon the head, which descends upon the beard and even reaches the hem of the garment, comes the bread of understanding and life, extending to others with the doctrine of faith and the saving water of wisdom. Therefore, we, considering that the island of Sardinia, which is known to belong spiritually and temporally to the Roman Church, is separated from us by a long stretch of sea and the onslaught of tempests, and because it has been inflamed by the fury of the wicked Frederick, the mutual affection of the mother towards her children and of the children towards their mother seems to have somewhat cooled. To extend to them the service of a gracious visitation, we have decided, on the advice of our brothers, to send you to those parts, in whose discretion and prudence we have firm and unwavering confidence, entrusting to you the full office of legation. Following the prophetic word, uproot and destroy, scatter and disperse, build and plant, as you see fit according to God. Therefore, we earnestly ask and exhort your discretion, commanding that, since we specially cherish these islands among the other parts of the world as a special patrimony of the Roman Church, you should strive to exercise this legation in those parts laudably according to the providence given to you by God. Through your diligent effort, let them recognize the affection we have had and continue to have for the clergy and people of those islands. Besides the merit you will receive from God and the good reputation you will acquire from men, let your diligence be worthy in the Lord. Given at Lyon, on the 10th of June, in the sixth year. In the same manner to the same, to the islands of Corsica.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa electo Turritano, apostolicae sedis legato, mandat ut, Sardiniae et Corsicae insulis visitationem gratam impendens, legationis plenam functionem exerceat, ut clerus et populus earum insularum affectum Romanae ecclesiae percipiant. 1249, Iunii 10, Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To all archbishops and bishops, abbots, priors, and other prelates of churches established throughout Sardinia. Since, according to the prophetic word, we are appointed over nations and kingdoms of the whole earth (Jeremiah 1:10), where the Lord is invoked, we are bound to hold general care. However, a certain natural obligation compels us to direct our focus of concern towards Sardinia, which is especially known to pertain to the Roman Church. But, because the nature of human condition does not allow us to be personally present in many places at the same time, lest we inadequately fulfill the office of apostolate we have assumed, we are compelled, following the counsel of Jethro, to choose prudent men, who fear God, love truth, and detest covetousness (Exodus 18), who zealously uphold our honor and that of the Roman Church, so that we may send them, as necessity demands and utility advises, to accomplish various tasks. Therefore, fearing that the enemy of mankind, who prowls around like a roaring lion seeking whom he might devour, may affect your parts, which are distant from us by a long stretch of sea, as stated above until, to the end that we may bestow diligent care, we have designated our beloved son, the elect of Torres, legate of the apostolic see, indeed a prudent and discreet man, distinguished by the integrity of his character and very dear and acceptable to us and our brothers due to his merits, to be sent to your parts, with full authority granted to him to uproot and destroy, to build and plant whatever he deems necessary to uproot and destroy, build and plant in the Church of God, according to the advice of our brothers. Therefore, we earnestly ask and admonish your entire community, strictly commanding that you receive and honor the aforementioned elect as the legate of the apostolic see, indeed as our own person, showing him the due and devout reverence, and that you heed with devoted minds his salutary admonitions and precepts, and that you hold firmly and observe whatever he deems necessary to establish among you as sons of devotion, assisting him with help, counsel, and favor, for he will endeavor to walk the straight path, as directed by the Lord, not turning aside to the right or to the left, according to the mandate we have given him by word of mouth. Otherwise, the sentence which he has duly pronounced, etc. Given as above. In the same manner to archbishops, etc., established throughout Corsica. In the same manner to judges, counts, castellans, and other nobles, rectors, bailiffs, and the rest of the faithful in Christ established throughout Sardinia. In the same manner to noble men, judges, etc., established throughout Corsica.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Papa [Nomen] universis archiepiscopis et episcopis, abbatibus, prioribus, aliisque ecclesiarum prelatis per Sardiniam et Corsicam constitutis mandat, ut electum Turritanum, legatum apostolicae sedis, tanquam personam suam recipiant et honorifice pertractent, eiusque monitis ac statutis obediant. Datum [Locus], [Data ex anno pontificatus].

**Translation to English:**

Innocent, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son, the noble man Alberico de Romano, greetings and apostolic blessing. It comes to the eternal glory of your name that resisting manfully those who persecute the Catholic faith and the Church, you show yourself as a zealous supporter of the orthodox faith and a son of the Church, while you do not omit to defend it with great praiseworthy proclamation; for which reason we do not deem it unworthy that the apostolic protection should guard you from the assault of persecutors, whom your devotion, exhibited in the repression of the perverse to the apostolic see, commend in manifold ways. Hence, responding with grateful assent to your just desires, we take your person, persisting in the devotion to the Church and in the defense of the Catholic faith and ecclesiastical liberty, along with the castles, towns, fortresses, and villages of Baxiano, Romano, Muxolente, Bursiano, Casale, the church of St. Lary, Cassanico, Poveno, Cordesino, Solanio, Sanaseto, Cismone, Arsedo, Rivaliis, Tonico, Yvano, Telve, Arnan, Ausugum, Mazanigo, Cartilano, Roxano, Cassola, St. Lucia, Frata, Fontaniva, Auguaro, Zerzono, Campese, Eneco, Galado, Foce, Vallis Resina, Vallis Rovina, Torre, Marostica, Cusano, Marsango, Castelletto, Planeza, Pedole, Muris, Caribolo, and Pauso, as well as 330 lands and possessions, jurisdictions, and all your goods, which you possessed of old at the time when the prince was bound by the sentence of excommunication by the apostolic see, and which you reasonably possess at present or may justly acquire in the future, under the protection of blessed Peter and Our own, and we fortify them with the protection of this present writing. Furthermore, we revoke by the authority of these presents the sentences, bans, statutes, penalties, and privileges, and the grants and concessions made concerning your goods by the same prince or any other on his behalf to any communities or persons whatsoever, as well as the agreements, securities, oaths offered to the said prince or anyone on his behalf, for whatever reason, and all other things which are said to be established against you and your goods generally or specifically. Therefore, let no one at all dare to infringe upon this page of our protection and revocation or oppose it with rash boldness. But if anyone dares to attempt this, let them know they will incur the indignation of Almighty God and his blessed apostles Peter and Paul. Given at Anagni, on the seventh Ides of October, in the first year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa Alberico de Romano, nobili viro, personam eius cum castris, villis et bonis sub protectione beati Petri et sua recipit et decreta a principe facta revocat. 1243, Oct. 9, Anagnie.

**Translation to English:**

To the dean and chapter of Cambrai. When the church of Cambrai was vacant, and the day for election had been set, the canons convened, and some of them, after due scrutiny, consented to elect our venerable brother Nicholas de Fontanis, then a canon among them, as bishop, with the solemnity of deportation following. However, realizing afterward that the election had not been conducted by the greater and wiser part of all, they returned to the chapter with the elected. Since the elected had renounced the election, the term for election was postponed to the following day. When the canons gathered for election on that day, some of them, claiming for themselves and their adherents that, since the previous election had been presumed against the form of the general council, those who participated in it were deprived of the power to elect on that occasion and should not proceed to elect, appealed to the Apostolic See. As they left the chapter and did not care to return, despite being repeatedly requested by the others, those who remained in the chapter unanimously elected the same bishop. When this election was presented to our beloved son P., cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, then acting as legate in Germany, those who had previously appealed appeared before him, objecting on the previous grounds and claiming the election had been attempted after their appeal, asked us not to confirm it, adding that the same bishop had a deficiency in literacy. But the cardinal, in the presence of our venerable brother the archbishop of Reims, metropolitan of the place, diligently examined the person elected and the process of election, found that the elected was sufficiently literate and that the previous appeal could not prevent those who remained in the chapter from canonically electing a suitable person as pastor, confirmed the election. Those who opposed the election having come to the Apostolic See, demanding its annulment for previous reasons and claiming it was conducted on a day not appointed for election, we decided, in justice, not to hear them. Finally, when one of them objected something against the elected's person, and the elected personally appeared before us, and, after a legitimate contestation of the case, with both parties swearing to tell the truth, positions and responses being made, witnesses produced and testimonies published, and the allegations of each party heard: finally, both parties submitted entirely to our arbitration. We, considering that the mentioned bishop, as established by the cardinal's report who examined him, is sufficiently literate, and that nothing of what was objected to him was proven, and recognizing that he is known to shine with a commendable life and maturity of manners, approved and supplied with apostolic authority, out of the fullness of power, for any defect there might have been in these matters, and appointed the same Nicholas as bishop and pastor of the church of Cambrai, with the counsel of our brothers, and later had the order of priesthood conferred on him, and we ourselves imparted the consecration. We command, therefore, that you receive the same bishop as the father and pastor of your souls with devotion, rendering him due obedience and reverence, humbly attending to his salutary admonitions and commands. Otherwise, the sentence, which he pronounces rightly, etc. Given at Lyon, on the 9th of April, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Innocentius IV papa decano et capitulo Cameracensibus mandat, ut Nicolaum de Fontanis in episcopum et pastorem Cameracensis ecclesiae recipiant, electionem eius confirmans et defectus supplens. Datum Lugduni, V Id. Aprilis, anno sexto.

**Translation to English:**

The texts are read, now we provide them in full, which A. Mau described from the Registers. In the same manner to the abbot and convent of the Cistercians, considering the weight of such great importance. Therefore, diligently considering as befits us from our own weakness Ps. 33, 18. to fail, and knowing that the prayer of the righteous is very powerful, because the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous and his ears on their prayers, we confidently implore your support and that of other spiritual men. Therefore, we ask, advise, and exhort you in the Lord, by apostolic writings mandating to you, that you, offering the incense of your prayers Hos. 14, sweetly to the Lord and presenting the calves of your lips, may earnestly beseech Him, that from the abundance of His mercy, which exceeds the merits and desires of supplicants, directing our actions in His good pleasure, the people committed to our governance may profit by our word and example, that He may watch over His Church with continuous mercy, and because without Him it cannot stand safe, may it always be governed by His gift. But Eccli. 18, because when a man has finished, then he begins, that you, through the merit of life, may benefit others laudably by example, forgetting what is behind and stretching forth to what is before with the apostle, emulating the better gifts, secure that the hand of our help will not fail you, but we will gladly impart grace and favor to you in every opportunity, believing that we thus please Him, who accepts your pleasing service. Furthermore, etc. as above to the end. In the same manner to the abbess and convent of the monastery of Ioeta up to: to their prayers, we confidently implore your support. Therefore, etc. up to: mandating that in your tears and groans, remembering us before God, whom it pleased to ordain us as minister of His holy church, although unworthy and servant of His servants, you may lift pious hands to Him, fervently praying that He, who knows that we are unable to stand amidst such dangers due to human frailty, may prevent us with His strength, to grant us to perform the ministry committed to us by Him worthily, so that it may come to His glory and joy of His angels and to the salvation of us and those committed to our governance. But because etc. as above up to: that it be suitably satisfied to Himself. Given as above. In the same manner to the king of Castile and León, considering the weight of such great importance. Observing the fervor of sincere devotion, which you are known to have towards the apostolic see from the innate custom of your ancestors, we have decided to send you the first fruits of our letters as to a special son of the Roman Church. Therefore, we earnestly request and advise your royal excellency, that you strive to honor and reverence your mother the holy Roman Church and all the churches of your realms in such a way that the affection of your devotion may not appear to have cooled in any way but rather to have increased, and that you may assist us, having been taken to the governance of the apostolic see by the disposition of the Lord, as befits a Catholic prince, humbly and devoutly. For we, in those things that pertain to your honor and advantage, as much as we can with God, gladly intend and hold your person with a special prerogative of love and favor in the bowels of charity. Given at Anagni, etc.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa regi Castelle et Legionis devotionem sinceram commendat, eumque monet ut matrem suam ecclesiam Romanam ac regnorum ecclesias honoret et revereri studeat. Dat. Anagnie, 1227, Mart. 23.

**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Meissen. The authority of paternal blessing elevates a devoted son to great heights and quickly eradicates one who is raised in opposition cruelly. Thus, Joseph is called the growing son, and Canaan with his progeny is subjected to servitude. Absalom is hanged on an oak, and Solomon receives the diadem of his father's throne. These, and what is read in the Holy Scripture: "Honor your father and your mother, that you may live long in the land" (Exodus 20:12), if the noble man, son of our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of Bohemia, would diligently heed, as is proper, he would honor his father, the king, as a son desiring paternal inheritance blessing, and would abstain entirely from offending him. But, as we have learned, led by the wicked persuasions of certain barons of the kingdom of Bohemia who hate the goods of peace and delight in the evils of discord, the same man, together with them, cruelly persecutes the said king and attacks him with hostile persecution, to the detriment of the king's person and status, forming a damnable alliance of friendship and society with Conrad, the son of the late emperor Frederick, Duke of Bavaria, and other persecutors of the Church. In all these actions, the hand of the Bishop of Prague and certain other ecclesiastical persons of the same kingdom is said to be involved. Therefore, to prevent such great evil from prevailing, if not countered, we command that you diligently admonish and induce the son and the same barons to desist entirely from such iniquity and to return to the devotion of the aforesaid king, from which they cannot withdraw without notable infamy and danger to their souls, and to attend to him as they are obliged. If they do not care to heed your admonitions, excommunicate them and all their supporters in this iniquity by our authority, removing the impediment of appeal, and place their lands under the strictest interdict, so that no divine service or ecclesiastical sacrament is celebrated or offered in them, except for the baptism of infants and penance of the dying, making the sentences of such excommunication and interdict publicly proclaimed on all Sundays and feast days, with bells ringing and candles burning in places you deem suitable, invoking, if necessary, the assistance of the secular arm. As for the same bishop, since he is excommunicated by our beloved son, brother Gottfried of the Order of Preachers, our penitentiary, sent by us to those regions, on account of our justice, for presuming, as is said, to celebrate—indeed, truly profane—divine offices and to conspire against the same king together with his son, cite him by the same authority and appoint him a peremptory term for him to personally present himself before our presence to receive what is deserved. Since, as has been intimated to our ears, some provosts, deans, canons, and rectors, as well as other canons of the churches of the aforementioned kingdom, by favoring and adhering to the aforesaid son of the king and barons, persecutors of the Church against it, have rendered themselves unworthy of ecclesiastical benefices, and it is fitting that the undevout suffer loss from their undevotion and the devout gain benefit from their devotion: we will and command that, if it is established to you that the aforementioned provosts, deans, and others are such, you deprive them perpetually of the prebendaries and dignities and benefices they hold from the churches, by the same authority, and have them conferred by those to whom their collation pertains, if they are devoted to the Roman Church. Otherwise, you confer them this time to suitable persons devoted to the said church; contradictors, etc. Given at Lyon, 10th Kalends of May, in the 6th year.

**Regesto in Latin:**

Gregorius IX papa episcopo Misnensi mandat, ut nobilem filium regis Boemiae et barones, qui ipsum regem persequuntur et cum persecutoribus ecclesiae foedus inierunt, excommunicet, nisi ad devotionem regis redeant; item, episcopum Pragensem et quosdam ecclesiasticos in regno, qui in hac iniquitate complices sunt, ad sedem apostolicam citet. 1232, Apr. 22. Lugduni.

**Translation to English:**

To the elected archbishop of Turris. Since we are sending you to the regions of Sardinia to promote the well-being and affairs of the Church there, on the advice of our brothers, we wish to grant you certain faculties for the salvation of souls. We grant you the authority to dispense with clerics in your legation who are impeded by the defect of birth, allowing them, notwithstanding this defect, to serve in the orders they have received, advance to higher orders, and obtain ecclesiastical benefices or offices, excluding only the episcopal dignity, even if they have the care of souls in the churches of your legation. Given as above. In the same manner to the same. In Corsica. III. To the same. Since we are sending you to the regions of Sardinia, with the full office of legation entrusted to you, we grant you by the authority of these presents that if you are prevented from entering the lands of your legation freely, or if for any reason you need to leave them and travel to other parts, as long as you stay in Genoa or its district or at Porto Venere or Bonifacio, and even while going and returning, you can exercise the office of legation in the aforementioned Sardinia. Given as above. In the same manner to the same. In Corsica. IV. To the same. Since we are sending you, etc. as above until: we grant you, to dispense with twenty religious persons suffering from the defect of birth in those parts, of whatever order they may be, so that notwithstanding this defect, they may be lawfully assumed to prelatures and administrations of their orders in the churches of your legation. Given as above. In the same manner to the same. In Corsica. V. To the same. Since we are sending you, etc. to appoint the same, we grant you authority to remove perpetually both prelates and others of your legation who are disobedient to the Church or rebellious or presume to plot against it and persist in their malice, from the administration of their spiritual and temporal affairs and to restrain the opposers, etc. notwithstanding any privilege or indulgence of the apostolic see — by the tenor of these presents, we grant you free power. Given as above. To the same. We grant you the authority of these presents, to dispense with ten ecclesiastical persons, both religious and secular, of your legation, who bound by the bond of excommunication have received sacred orders or ministered in them, concerning this irregularity, as you see expedient for the salvation of their souls. Given as above. VI. To the same. Since we are sending you, etc. as above until: we grant you the authority to freely exercise ecclesiastical censure on all, both of cathedral and other churches, etc. as above in the legation of P. cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, legate of the apostolic see. In the same manner to the same. In Corsica. VII. To the elected archbishop of Turris.
