**Translation to English:**

To the Bishop of Cambrai. A dispute arose between the canons who had taken the cross on one side and certain canons who had not taken the cross of the Church of Liège on the other, concerning the matter that the said cross-bearing canons were requesting to be given the revenues of their prebends of the said church without any reduction, as they claimed to be entitled to based on an indulgence granted to them due to assuming the cross. Eventually, after both parties were summoned to our presence, and some of those cross-bearing canons appeared personally, while others appeared through their procurators, and similarly, some of the non-cross-bearing canons appeared personally and others through their procurators at the apostolic see, we decided to entrust the resolution of this dispute to our beloved son P., Cardinal Deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil. The same cardinal, after having a careful deliberation, made the following arrangement between them under our special mandate: John of Appia and Gerard of Peis, archdeacons, Master L. the schoolmaster, G. the cantor, the provost of Louvain, the custodian of St. Denis, Master Gerard of Bohaing, John of Gothegni and Simon called Dagores, canons of the same church, who were residing in Liège at the time of taking the vow and executed their vows personally at Aachen, should receive from now on for three years the revenues of their prebends of the said church, wherever they may be, in full, whether in grain, bread, wine, money, or any other income, except for that part of the distributions, which consists in money that is given to canons serving in canonical hours and anniversaries. Indeed, the foreign canons and other residents, who were not residing in Liège at the time of taking the vow and executed their vows personally at Aachen, namely the provosts of Cologne, Aachen, and Reims, Hermann of Salmis, Anselm of Barbeneheroc, John of Kantemd, Jacob of Iacta, and Henry of Alois, who is said to have substituted his father Hugo the knight with the consent of the same cardinal, then acting as a legate in those parts, should receive the revenues of their gross prebend for the same period, wherever they may be, in a similar manner and be content with the same revenues; granting both the resident and foreign canons mentioned above the free faculty of selling, pledging, assigning, or otherwise disposing of these fruits during the same period, as they see fit. If it happens that the same canons serve or even reside in the aforesaid church, the revenues of their prebends of the aforementioned church should be fully administered to them as to the others serving and residing there; and the said cardinal decided this should extend to the above-mentioned canons, who made their customary residence in the aforementioned church before taking the vow. For those who did not make the said residence in the same church, as regards the revenues of benefices, they shall not obtain anything more from the indulgence of assuming the cross than that the time they were on the expedition to Aachen may, if they wish, be counted for them as residence of that year; except for Arnulf called Digant, canon of the said church, who, although he did not complete his customary residence in the same, may nevertheless absent himself during the same period, if he wishes, without prejudice of the contrary custom or statute or oath said to have been made about making residence there, receiving nothing in the meantime for his absence; the said cross-bearing canons shall not incur any penalty for having trusted in the benefit of assuming the cross and absenting themselves from the aforementioned church. Therefore, we command you to firmly observe this arrangement through ecclesiastical censure, removing appeals, relaxing by our authority any sentences that may have been pronounced against those who complied with the said arrangement on account of the aforementioned indulgence, and dispending with them about any irregularity they may have incurred, and making sure that all goods of the said church that were occupied or detained for this reason are fully restored to the aforementioned church; those opposing, etc. However, we do not wish this arrangement to be extended to the prejudice of the privileges and customs of the aforementioned church in the future — notwithstanding any custom or statute fortified by oath or any other firmness. Given at Lyon, the 9th of April, in the sixth year.
